name: Endless ocean

_childDocuments_.review: The beauty of Endless Ocean is that players can do as much or as little as they like. The relaxed and calm atmosphere of the game gives divers the freedom to explore special locations such as shipwrecks and underwater ruins, discover and interact with sea-life, complete fish logs or simply relax in the soothing environment. The game opens with players onboard a diving boat, with a crew member who provides advice and tips on finding the best locations for fish and helps players advance the storyline. Players must assume the role of the diver, opting to go into the water to explore sea-life at their own pace utilising tools such as a camera or fish bait. In the cabin on the boat, divers can access the fish log to check out the fish that have been spotted, as well as carry out missions like photographing marine life. These missions unlock content, such as new items to use underwater, or different diving gear that can be used to customize the diver. Navigating their way through the depths using the Wii remote, players guide their character using the pointer's cursor, visible as a bright blue dot. When players wish to interact with fish or plants they can highlight them with the pointer and press the A Button. By doing so, players discover new species and build up their fish log. What's more you can also befriend companions like a dolphin which will become your partner and with whom you can train and swim with. [Nintendo]

name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid
detailed_description: Notice 8/6/2024 update added English to the game language. About the Game A circus troupe comes to Yomogi Town, a rural town in Japan situated between mountains and the ocean. As the son of the circus ringmaster, enjoy a special summer filled with wholesome adventures! All of Yomogi Town and the nature surrounding it are an open world where you can enjoy your days to the fullest. Immerse yourself in nostalgic scenery filled with towering clouds, beautiful sunsets, and the sound of cicadas. You can chill in the shopping district, listen to live music in the afternoon, or go on a wild and exciting adventure. It's all up to you. Feel like climbing up a tall, steep cliff? Or hopping from one rooftop to the next? Maybe look for a hidden gem at a remote spot? No problem! Even if you drop from a very high place, you'll be perfectly fine because you're the protagonist of this game. You can spend time in an open field, quietly admiring the little flowers. Use the Acorn Shooter to catch bugs that are out of reach! Go fishing at a river or the sea! Donate rare bugs and fish to the museum for their exhibits! Have the fish you caught cooked into a delicious dish! Join the local detective agency, raise a wild pig, dig up fossils, ride a train, earn money, and write and draw in your picture diary! During the summer festival, fireworks and the Bon Festival dance liven up the night. You can even help run the Fireworks Show! And you'll be directing the performance of the circus troupe in the latter half of your summer vacation. What a huge responsibility! Are you up for it? Make your own, unforgettable memories during your summer vacation filled with unique experiences! This is the latest work by Kaz Ayabe, creator of several games themed around summer vacation and childhood nostalgia. Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid comes to Steam. About the Gameplay: Dive into a midsummer adventure in a vast open world! Experience the freedom and nostalgia of a small country town brought to life in stunning 3D. Our game offers a seamless open-world environment where you can explore without any interruptions or loading screens. Immersive Realism: Relive the magic of childhood adventures with lifelike 3D recreations of quaint shopping districts and charming single-car trains. Dynamic Environment: Witness the passage of time and changing weather conditions in real-time, adding depth and authenticity to your journey. Endless Exploration: Catch bugs, play detective, climb tall cliffs, even fly through the sky... Reconnect with the childhood joys of exploration, embark on adventures you dreamed about back then, and create new memories in a world brimming with possibilities.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The English translation is out! I do however still recommend the belowThe English translation does not come out until August, however, if you are studying Japanese this is maybe the best game you could get on Steam. A lot of everyday items, casual situations and a wide cast of characters who speak intermediate Japanese makes this the perfect choice for people who want their first game to play in Japanese.

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard about Boku no Natsuyasumi so decided to give this a shot as an English player with some basic Japanese comprehension. I had no idea what to expect, but after a few hours strongly recommend it.Stay with me here, but the closest game I can relate this to is probably Shenmue, as the game is broken up into days, and each day has a world clock that ticks away. NPCs all have their routine, so you'll see them go from A to B during the day and carry out their chores.The first thing you'll want to do is change the passage of time from "Normal" to "Leisurely" (nonbiri), as the game will only pause the world clock when on the map screen, so if you want to take time translating conversations or trying to figure out what you are supposed to do by trial and error, the slower clock means you can still relax and play the game without feeling like you are at a disadvantage. I wanted a chill game, and with the time set to this, it's very chill.The day starts with breakfast and ends with a 10 pm curfew (which you can skip, but you get in trouble), and what you do during this time is completely up to you. You have main story tasks, most of these are relaxed but some ask you to achieve criteria before a date, and smaller mini-tasks, such as solving puzzles left by a creepy ghost girl. Most of the tasks are charming and fun, and it also has a lot of slow-burning tasks like catching every type of fish, insect, mushroom etc, with milestone rewards along the way.The main limiting factor (other than time) is your stamina bar, which is made up of stars, you start with just four which means you cannot climb very high, and cannot run very far. But once you've earned a few more from the quests, you'll be climbing all sorts and running along roof-tops looking for the hidden items and rewards scattered about all over the place like a little parkour ninja.The game world is relatively big, I thought it would all just be set in the starting town but discovered otherwise when I wandered into a neighbouring town of equal size, plus it has plenty of cool landmarks off in the distance I've not reached in the first 8 hours, but it's one of those "if you see it you can visit it" games that rewards exploration.Now for a couple of negativesOn Steamdeck it's a fairly stable 60fps even up to 1080p. But the PC port is bare bones, you have one graphic mode setting with three options that range from "looks like the Switch version" to "it still looks like the Switch version but the draw distance is a bit better". It also has a 30/60fps toggle, but for some reason even if you disable vsync the game will lock itself to this framerate, it's not possible to go higher than 60fps.My other minor negative is that the main character huffs and puffs constantly due to all the running and climbing, it's just a bit much and should have been toned down.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: A 'Breath of the Wild' moment for 'Boku no Natsuyasumi' games!It's liberating when you're free to go anywhere, explore at your own pace, do your tasks as you see fit and in any order you like. Whether seeking new fishing spots or gathering collectibles on top of the roofs, it's all up to you. You can spend the whole in-game day doing these smaller things and no one would stop and handhold you to a next story related goal.Climbing is also in. Anything you see can be climbed on.In terms of freedom to explore the dev team was clearly inspired by BotW. In terms of visual style and overall level of polish it is closer to Wind Waker. The visuals are not as detailed as previous Natsuyasumi games, which had hand-drawn 2D backgrounds, but all the interactivity of the world and freedom of exploration easily makes up for it.One of the main gameplay features, that separates Natsu-mon from the crowd, is that this is one those games where every day you spend in this world is tied to the in-game calendar. You are living your day from 7am to 10pm, and once it's over it's over. It was your day and that's how you decided to live it.You have about 11 hours of daylight activity which can be spend on exploring the island to its fullest and then about 4 hours in the evening when you'll be restricted and won't be able to stray too far from the guest house where you pass a summer.Some may not like that you have to keep in mind that your hours are finite, and there's only so much you can do during the day. But that's part of the game's design and the story, as you're spending a last month of summer in these places.Think Pikmin where you have to take care of gathering fruits, battling enemies and discover new locations all in a timely manner. You have to plan and prioritize. It's not that stressful in Natsu-mon though, because it generally goes in a much more relaxed pace. But still, you have a clock ticking away with every route you take and every small activity that might get you sidetracked.And pretty much every day is a busy day here: be it some events popping up at different locations that you can attend, trying to catch rare bugs/fish and donating to a museum, investigating a local Edo period castle, climbing on some high spots in town or taking a hiking route into the mountains. Every day is filled with something new and exciting for a 10 year old boy.All in all, not only can I recommend Natsu-mon to every Boku no Natsuyasumi fan out there, but I can finally recommend it to pretty much anyone who just likes chill and cozy games with the emphasis on exploration and collecting. And surprisingly this game can even be thought provoking at some times.Millennium Kitchen outdid themselves this time around, effectively pulling themselves out of this niche genre. They made something that still carries these inherently unique qualities of the series and at the same time appeals to a much broader audience this time.In short: brilliant game. If you liked Breath of the Wild, Wind Waker, Pikmin, Psychonauts - get this game, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a while to grab Natsu-Mon on Switch. Thankfully the Steam ver. released today !I adore Millennium Kitchen's releases. They work so excellently as a window into each title's chosen time period. Culturally, historically, politically, and personally. There's a level of humanity in these works that you just won't find in other works. I'll always remember the scene in Bokunatsu where the characters say that they hope a person survived the war. Natsu-Mon is excellent. The art style is excellent and perfectly melds w/ the writing and sound. There's so much charm to Natsu-Mon, it's hard to put into words. The game speaks for itself so well.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: It's great to see Kaz Ayabe's Boku no Natsuyasumi series finally getting regular English-language releases. They're such fun, relaxing, wholesome games. This is the first in the series to leave the pre-rendered backgrounds behind in favor of a full-3D world. Longtime fans will miss how the backgrounds gave a picturesque vibe to the proceedings, but the world in these games has never felt more open to explore. If your a fan of games like "Harvest Moon" or "Animal Crossing," you should try this series out.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: Please note: This review comes from someone who bought Natsumon in Japanese on the Switch earlier this year with over 40hours gameplay completing it once, then getting halfway through 2nd play with the DLC there after.Natsumon is a game that combines Boku no Natsuyasumi with Zelda: Breath of the Wild gameplay.A fun wholesome and chill game following a boy on summer holiday making memories in a town he's never been to before, experiencing a nostalgic summer holiday full of the innocence of child-like wonder.Natsumon takes the idea of the chill BnN summer holiday fun and makes it its own thing with fully 3D environments that differ to the more fixed camera angled gameplay of BnN.This in turn makes the art style downgrade in comparison with BnN's real detailed backgrounds (which fans of the BnN have criticised upon) though it could be argued this compromise was made to incorporate the fully 3D gameplay. Despite this, I do find Natsumon's artstyle very charming and full of personality.The BotW mechanic of wall climbing and running is a big aspect of the gameplay traversing here and there on the massive island. Lots of things to find, such as insects and fish, and a healthy amount of whimsical characters to meet along the way making memories with the inhabitants of the island.There is a lot to do and uncover on the island on your one-month holiday at Yomogi Town and running around places to really get the views and discover new things is really fun, you receive stickers from completing missions that increase your stamina which makes the experience a lot more enticing.Although both main composers for the OST, Hideki Sakamoto and Ryo Shirasawa, did the music for this game, those who have played the other Millennium Kitchen title featuring Shin-chan will be glad to know that the two had also done music on the first game there as well.Real chill and fun music along with fitting tracks for certain scenes, the music also makes you enjoy the game more as well.Voice casting for this game is also pretty high-profile as well such as 3 VA's (for Satoru, Ryoko, and the Zashikiwarashi) casted as idols from THE iDOLMASTER CINDERELLA GIRLS series, Hideko's VA being Yui Ogura, Tobiyama's VA being Maaya Sakamoto, Kyoko's VA casted as Yuuko from Nichijou, and Jiroo's VA casted as Pikachu for the longest period.For those who want to put their Japanese skills to the test could attempt playing the game in Japanese as it can help a bit with the study and revision of the language, though do note this game does not contain furigana unlike a lot of Japanese titles targeted for a younger demographic does so it really does put you to the test at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great fun! Great entry point into the Natsuyasumi games, especially now that English text was added!You're a kid moving to a new town in the summer and you're, more or less, left to your own devices. Explore the countryside and make your way all through the towns while meeting the locals and getting to know and help them along the way. Fishing, bug catching, mountain climbing, and occasionally solving mysteries are some of the activities you can get into each day.If you're at all interested in the Natsuyasumi games, or just want to spend a fun summer in the Japanese countryside, this game is a winner!!It's a very easy game to get into...just hard to stop playing. Highest recommendation for anyone that enjoys exploration and finding out what's out there to be found!
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid is a heartwarming slice-of-life gem that transports players back to a simpler time in the Japanese countryside. As Satoru, you'll experience the nostalgic charm of a bygone era in the town of Yomogi, filled with friendly faces, heartwarming scenarios, and a cozy soundtrack.The game's beautiful crayon-like art style and vibrant colors create a visually stunning world that perfectly captures the essence of summer. Each day brings new opportunities to build relationships with the townsfolk through adventures and heartfelt conversations. You can also spend your days catching bugs and fish to complete the encyclopedia or donate them to the museum.Whether you're looking for a relaxing escape filled with nostalgic vibes or a heartwarming story about cherishing the last days of summer, Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid is a delightful experience you won't want to miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! I love the ease of play, the setting, the characters, the graphics, the soundtrack, and sense of exploration. I changed my settings to "Relaxed" so I could get the most out of my time throughout an in-game day and it was very beneficial. Kind of reminds me of Animal Crossing with the ease of catching bugs and fish but much more to the story. This game effortlessly recaptured the essence of childhood wonder—roaming freely, oblivious to time or duties, and only pausing when called back to reality (usually by an adult).
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: 1.3 million views on a 6 hour essay about , under a 100 reviews for , the world is a weird place... Anyway, this might be Kaz Ayabe's masterpiece. Yes, it doesn't have the painted pittoresque backgrounds of the past, and the 3D graphics are on the simple side, but what you get in actual freedom of movement is so cool. Today I had an itch to replay , but then I remembered I don't really like combat and ended up here instead.The boy you play is a bit of a little brat, and all the villager interaction are following suit, very snappy, sometimes even funny (sometimes also just silly), but not in that slightly disturbing Shin-chan way. Like in virtually every Kaz Ayabe game you gotta accept that your character will express crushes on older girls and women, personally I'm not a fan, but that's probably an essential part of his summer vacation memories... So yeah,  may not have the sweet sentimentality of  (or the Millenium Kitchen PlayStation games), instead it feels, set in 1999, more contemporary and livelier, you literally get to jump and run around a little open world and to waste some summer days in any way you like, guided by plenty of tasks and quests, and this is what I love: The freedom to do whatever I want on any day, but with enough context to not make it meaningless.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this. Gameplay-wise there’s a real joy to the movement and the exploration. You do feel like you’re on your own little adventure in this beautifully crafted world, which you can take at your own pace. The setting of Japan at the turn of the millennium is also well fleshed-out, with beautiful environments and a lot of attention to detail.I’d been wanting to try out a game in the Boku no Natsuyasumi series given its recent increase in popularity. This one seems to have modernized some of the gameplay, taking inspiration from games like “A Short Hike” or “Breath of the Wild” in terms of movement mechanics, but without losing any of its charm or core formula the series is known for.I played most of it on the Steam Deck. It runs really well and serves as a great cozy game for the platform. The shooting mechanic in the game automatically used the Deck gyro controls. It’s the first game I played that did this so I was surprised at first, but it’s a great fit and now I can’t imagine playing it any other way. I really appreciated this attention to detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: I've put about 15 hours into this game so far and I've got to say it's obvious a lot of love went into this project. The art style is amazing, the characters are interesting and well designed, the mechanics are tight and fluid, and it's got lots of things you can miss meaning it's a great game to replay. It's a very relaxing love letter to childhood summer vacations and it's a real shame that this game isn't getting more attention. It's a cozy experience set in a rural Japanese town and you get a whole month to do what you want. Go exploring and climb the tallest mountain, go fishing, catch bugs, discover side stories and watch the town change as time goes on. I strongly recommend this game if you want a fun and beautiful experience, but be aware that there is a time limit (you can adjust the length of the day to a certain extent).
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: I love Millennium Kitchen games, I was sooo excited when they announced this one was getting an official translation! Didn't expect it to take over my life as much as it did, but in saying that let me be clear: this game has such a relaxed pace that I could play one in game day, and put it down for the day, completely satisfied. I thought I would play something else at the same time, but I just couldn't get this one out of my mind. Was having some serious depression issues when I started, physically and mentally, and this turned out to be a perfect escape. Now I'm out the other end of what was going on, and I feel my life is overall richer for having experienced Natsu-mon.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: What if Animal Crossing minus the furniture, and Yakuza but only the side missions and city-roaming, had a 3d platformer baby in which you play as a 10 year old boy in 90's Japan who has just started his summer vacation in a beautiful port town with his circus family.  And also there are 200 bugs to collect.Genuinely on my GOTY shortlist so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing summer adventure game with cozy atmosphere. I've enjoyed exploring the map, climbing hills and mountains, collecting stuff and getting to know the colorful cast of townspeople. This virtual summer vacation in a small coastal town felt nostalgic even though I haven't really experienced summer like this before. The game has a great and cute art style and nice music too.This game deserves to be talked about more. And I wish more people would play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly well-done evolution of this series.  If you are even remotely interested in this game, you should buy it and play it.  This is an excellent port of the game and it looks gorgeous at 60 FPS- though I would recommend switching 30 FPS for the shooting and pachinko minigames, as it seems like they did not test them in 60 FPS and one of the games seems unwinnable at that framerate.   One of the best games of the year, and one of the most addictive games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I finish a session of this game, I speak aloud the words "this game is delightful." I do this whether or not there is anyone around to hear me and without even thinking. It's reflexive, and, in the same way the doctor's little hammer makes me kick, this game bypasses conscious thought and elicits that response. It's relaxing. It's wholesome. It lets you explore a place without any need for combat or even much conflict to speak of (at least, that's the case at the six-hour mark).I catch bugs and fish. I parkour around the rooftops looking for acorns and yellow diamonds. I solve mysteries. It's more than enough and it's all wonderful — delightful even.Buy this game and play it before bed as part of your sleep hygiene routine.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: Natsu-Mon is a wonderful experience. It's a very relaxing slice-of-life, and there's nothing that you absolutely have to do in order to progress, but there are interesting and fun things around every corner that will keep you exploring and collecting and meeting people. It's a beautiful game, and I hope we get more like it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: charming little game about one kid's summer vacation in the late '90s. the game marries the gameplay mechanics of the legend of zelda: breath of the wild with the gameplay loop of animal crossing, giving you a coastal valley within the japanese countryside to explore while catching fish, bugs, and developing friendships with the locals as their lives unfold. sweet, relaxing, and reminiscent of simpler times.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. This is the first in this series I've played, and I feel like many may hold off on it due to fear of not knowing much about Japanese culture, but don't let that stop you. I didn't either, and while I'm sure it will enhance some aspects, most of the game is about something we all did as kids , catch bugs, explore and relax on summer vacation. It's got an animal crossing feeling of just hang out and explore. Just like real life summer vacation as a kid, watching the calendar tick down to the final day filled me with a sense of dread, knowing my time with it would soon be over. Thankfully we can replay this.  I'm roughly the same age as the protagonist, so this hit me particularly hard. I'm not ashamed I almost teared up in the ending seeing summer vacation come to a close, and waving goodbye to all the friends made during the break.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: It is criminal to me that this game doesn't have more reviews. Beautiful game, amazing art direction and so much spirit in it. Never have I played a game that took me back to my own childhood quite like this one does, I can't seem to want to leave this little town I've grown to love and the people there that make it more special. Discovering how high you can climb and pushing the limits of your stamina meter only to discover a rare bug waiting for you is such a treat. You will want to do everything the townspeople ask of you and then some. The DLC ontop of all of that giving you hours more content is not really necessary to playing but is a very cool and welcome addition as well. Already closing in on my second playthrough since getting this game and loving it even more. Couldn't recommend this game enough if you just want to take a break from everything and feel some joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game. I loved the developers last game, Shin chan: Me and the professor on summer vacation the endless seven day journey, and I thought this was just as good. My only gripe is your stamina does not carry over to NG+. Would make things a lot less tedious for 100% if it did. Either way, i'll always be there for these devs' games.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

_childDocuments_.review:
A circus troupe comes to the the countryside. The protagonist is the ringmaster's only son. Enjoy a special summer vacation filled with nostalgic spectacles like thunderous clouds, evening sunsets, and the sounds of cicadas. After eating breakfast with everyone, do radio calisthenics in front of the shrine. Then, go fish in the ocean or river, catch rare insects in the hills and fields, and record everything in your picture diary.

During your vacation, you can help out the circus, or enjoy the summer festival to your heart's content. Enjoy fireworks and Bon Festival dances at night, or take the train over to the next town over. As you experience various things, the more you will be able to do. Whether you climb to the top of the mountain, swim in the ocean, or stroll around downtown, you will be able to make plenty of summer memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsu-Mon: 20th Century Summer Kid

name: Tomba! Special Edition
detailed_description: Tomba! returns in Tomba! Special Edition , the ultimate version of the legendary platforming masterpiece. As the titular Tomba, you leap, bite, and throw your way across stunning 2.5D landscapes on a quest to overcome a deplorable cadre of nefarious pigs. Along the way, you’ll explore ancient relics, discover fascinating characters, unlock thrilling quests, and unearth hidden treasures. It’s a platforming adventure that perfectly fuses linear and nonlinear gameplay styles. Tomba! was first published in 1997, and is back today in a vastly-expanded special edition packed with quality of life improvements, including: Save Anywhere! No more worrying about heading back to a checkpoint. Rewind - Stuck on a difficult challenge? Try again! Toggle for analog control A museum crammed with classic print advertisements, original packaging and manuals, never- before-seen dev documents, and high-res original artwork A new remastered soundtrack from original Composer Harumi Fujita (who also composed Ghosts 'n Goblins, Mega Man 3, Bionic Commando , and more!) Interview with Tomba! 's legendary creator, Tokuro Fujiwara (famous for Ghosts 'n Goblins, Resident Evil, Mega Man X , and more!)

Toggle for analog control A museum crammed with classic print advertisements, original packaging and manuals, never- before-seen dev documents, and high-res original artwork A new remastered soundtrack from original Composer Harumi Fujita (who also composed Ghosts 'n Goblins, Mega Man 3, Bionic Commando , and more!) Interview with Tomba! 's legendary creator, Tokuro Fujiwara (famous for Ghosts 'n Goblins, Resident Evil, Mega Man X , and more!)
short_description: In Tomba! Special Edition, leap, bite, and throw your way across stunning 2.5D landscapes in this vastly-enhanced update to a platforming classic!

_childDocuments_.review: i've done alot of speedruns of the original game on a PSP and it baffles me how much worse this release is.- text speed options from the original removed or hidden, which defaults to "FAST" when the good option is "AUTO" means fast text mashing is no longer possible- the Remastered OST is just overlaid by the front-end and starts during loading screens, in some situations it completely ruins the mood it was suppose to set (the water slide ost is suppose to run for a fixed amount of time, but loops over due to it starting during the loading screen!)- it actually lags on PC at some points (when running original OST you can hear the audio warp from lag)- it uses PCSX-ReArmed as an emulation base, are you serious??, cause it worked so well for the PS Classic :)- load times are comparable to the Playstation 1, just because you want accuracy doesn't mean we have to mimic CD loading times, they stopped doing that during the Playstation 2 era with the fast disk speed option, for most games this wouldn't be a huge problem, but the grating black screens between opening AND closing your inventory are ridiculous, a problem that was solved with a handheld console released in 2005!- Save Anywhere "feature" locks you to 3 save slots......memory cards for the PS1 gave you 15! how are we going backwards on this?!- Apparently Analog is a toggle (mentioned in the features list), but the Dpad is set to analog movement and i cannot change it, nothing in settings and no buttons to change it, what?these were all figured out within 25 minutes of play and i'm ready to refund, i'm so disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba (Tombi to us in PAL territories) is a good game. So good I'm surprised it's taken this long to get a rerelease on modern platforms. While this rerelease is competent, it doesn't offer any real advantage over the PS1 version. The FMVs haven't been touched, they're grainy and artifacted just like on the PS1. The in-game graphics are all 4:3, and the scaling is not the best. There's no widescreen support here unless you count borders or stretching, and you know we don't. The in-game menus didn't even get a 16:9 bump.This isn't a bad way to play the game, but I really just expected more for my AU$29. Nightdive Studios are out here remastering thirty year old games and frankly embarrassing Limited Run Games every time they do it, by giving us upscaled graphics, widescreen support, and mountains of cut content being finished and worked into the game, and that doesn't seem to have inspired LRG to step up their game at all. Nightdive's philosophy is "plays the way you remember, not the way it was", while Limited Run just gives us things the way they were. Up to you if you like that, but for me, I just wanted a bit more.As for Steam Deck compatibility, it works, but it only gives us 1280x720 graphics, while the deck's screen is 1280x800. This means those of us on the Deck will get letterboxing left and right, AND letterboxing top and bottom. I'm honestly considering, even though I've bought this, just playing the PS1 version in Duckstation.

_childDocuments_.review: - TOMBA CUT-CORNERS EDITION - Great game but let down by issues with a bad porting job.Tomba, or as I remember it as Tombi was an interesting platformer as it blended 2D and 3D together into 2.5D, but it also threw in some RPG elements like levelling up, side missions, a mission based structure like an RPG's storyline. And now 17 years later, we have the Tomba Special Edition, is it good? Well.....yes and no.===================================================================What I liked=======TOMBA'S BACKIt's Tomba on modern platforms, more people can play this and it's no longer considered dead media.Its the same game with all the bells and whistles and even achievements, it's short but sweet. (This also does go into a negative aspect, is the price justified at the game length? I personally think its fine but it might've been better if it were a little cheaper.)EMULATION QUALITY IS UP TO PAR!The graphical fidelity of the emulation is pretty much up to snuff with the likes of Duckstation so this is quite crisp and very clean (Some points in the game it will lag though from upscaling so just warning you.)REMASTERED TRACKS ARE VERY WELL COMPOSED MOSTLY!When you get to hear the remastered songs they truly do sound stunning and different from the original in a huge way, some songs however I prefer the original ones to give an example, I prefer the purified Phoenix Mountain from the original and the Underground Maze from the original over the remastered version. The Evil Pig Boss theme is always a bop and this is no exception, listening to it will have you tapping your feet.SAVING AND LOADING ANYWHERE FEELS FLUID AND FAIR.Saving and loading anywhere really is a lifesaver as you'll get into an area and have to go afk or something, you can save anywhere even in the middle of someone's dialogue which is super handy, the rewind function let me just say, you know, I know, we will use it on the motocross course to get the Gold Medal if we don't know the trick behind getting the time needed to get it.MUSEUM IS A LOVE LETTER TO FANSThe museum is a treasure trove of Tomba's history, love it and you'll love it too.Interviews, artwork and commercials await you in the museum.=======What I disliked=======THE LOOPS RUIN THE EXPERIENCEOh boy here we go, time to dig into why this port is not recommended despite me recommending it, I can't say I hate the game but I do feel let down by the plethora of problems it has.....starting with the in-game looping of tracks, to put it bluntly, they're terrible.Some songs lose their shine when they loop in a really bad way.Prime example is Mermaid's Singing Rock, this song is the most lullaby inducing and enchanting song, it truly was a beautiful piece of music, well its ruined in this game by the looping coming in way too soon only looping once and losing the whimsical feeling it has usually!Other songs like Village of All Beginnings loops too soon so it feels like you're not getting the full song as it doesn't sound quite like the original.Please fix this, this is a huge problem and comes from the fact the music is front-end.REMASTERED.....Sort of?Now you're asking, what does that mean?The remastered option allows you to listen to the remastered music during gameplay, well it's only PART true. Some cutscenes still use their original audio despite there being a clear rendition of a remastered version of the song in the games MUSIC PLAYER on the main menu. Very odd and strange, this might be a Carbon Engine issue as all they did was overlay the music over the top of the game and this has a strange side effect.....The music plays DURING the loading screens, so while it would otherwise be a surprise when you first hear that epic boss music, now you'll enter the Pig Gate and BOOM instant boss music.....It's kind of jarring.....and bad..... I really hope this is addressed!CUTSCENES LOSE THEIR CHARM!Cutscenes in the base game originally had sound effects that played like when you blow the fog away with the Furious Tornado (Spoilers wow, but come on guys its the first mission!) there are no wind sounds at all, no sound of the fog getting swept away....... It really is a shame.When you ride the Phoenix it also loses its charm as the Phoenix usually lets out a shriek when you are dropped into Baccus Village and now the sound is completely gone so this loses its touch.ALL the cutscenes use their original audio despite having remastered ones in the player, why? Why was it such a poor job?TWEENINGOh boy....here we go....the true way to be lazy is to use TWEENING instead of fluid animation.To put it bluntly the artwork on the titlescreens and menus.....all uses tweening.....and its a sign this was made for a quick buck and playing on our nostalgia. It's gross at times.===================================================================Verdict=======So we have come to the end of this review.Do I recommend this game to other players to purchase?If you're a die hard Tomba fan, you'll probably buy it anyway, like me, but I was met with disappointment.If you're not a tomba fan I cannot recommend this, but I can recommend you play the original, it is a masterclass in how to change up a platformers formula!Limited Run Games is known for delivering poor service as I've seen countless times about people buying collector's editions and not getting them for months or even years!If they're gonna release old games for the carbon engine, please refine it first.You've got the Gex Trilogy coming up, if this ends up being bad you will end up angering a lot of die hard Gex fans, and trust me they've been waiting a LONG time for another Gex Night..... Don't blow it.So yeah I say if you are a fan, buy it just to see the museum content and listen to the remastered tracks and give the game a go through on the original soundtrack only as the remastered one is mired by bugs and missing songs which hamper the experience.If you know nothing of Tomba, skip this, it's not worth your time or your money.Thanks for reading-Drax

_childDocuments_.review: When I was nine years old, I found a Tomba (although it was called Tombi here in Europe) demo disc in my box of cereals. I played that demo to smithereens, I loved it so much. I went to the local game store weekly, asking if they had Tombi, and was told weekly that they wouldn't even order it because it would not be popular over here and the copies would never sell. Disheartened, I kept playing my demo, and I kept asking the man from the game store every time I went there to browse. UIntil one day, I walked in there and he excitedly greeted me holding a little PS1 game box that would soon be my most prized possession. He could apparently not see me sad one more time so he had paid a little extra to order just one copy, for me. I don't think I've ever run as fast as I ran back home to start playing Tombi, and I don't think I've ever run as fast ever since. That's how much I love this game. It genuinely is my favourite childhood game, it holds a dear place in my heart and I have been looking forward to playing this again for SO long, I can't even express how much it means to me to see other adults hype over this game and love this game. I had never met anyone else irl who even knew about it, let alone shared my excitement.If you were a fan of the original Tomba, then this is just one big nostalgia trip for you. Buy it. Play it. Relive your childhood. Notice you have become much, much worse at platforming because you've been getting older, slower, less focused. Weep.Be informed that this is an emulator port, not a remaster. The game is 100% the same graphics- and gameplay-wise as the PS1 game, with a remastered soundtrack (that is on by default but can be toggled of in the settings for that full nostalgic experience) but it surprisingly still looks quite good.And to put your concerns to rest: I, too, was miffed it was "just a port" and not a full remaster, at first. I thought about how well done the Day of the Tentacle remaster was and I wanted something similar for Tombi. But now that I'm playing it... nah. The game *really* holds up. I'm not even listening to the remastered soundtrack, because the og is so great. This *definitely* was enough, and potentially even better than a real remaster.Keyboard controls are hardcoded on arrow keys and x and z which is... not ideal, if you're used to playing WASD, and they can't be remapped, so I recommend using a controller. Like it was intended to be played, one could argue.Not sure how the game would hold up with a new player who isn't riding the nostalgia, but if you like platformer games and the retro feel, and you lower your expectations to a 1997 frame of reference, it's definitely probably a good game for you, maybe. Yes.Looking forward to Tomba 2, Limited Run. Get on it!

_childDocuments_.review: I only bought this because of nostalgia, I own the physical disc for PS1 along with Tomba! 2 and have replayed these games more times than any other game I've played.This is a lazy, sloppy port of the original game, and sadly you would get a better experience for free with a modern emulator.The development art in the Museum is great, but there is plenty more cut content that could have been interviewed about and covered in the museum, which really, the Museum is the only reason I purchased this game on Steam.I played through the entire game with original soundtrack, partly because of the bugs with "remastered" audio being lazily overlayed over original audio, which causes issues with music starting at the loading screen, and looping issues which kill immersion, not to mention D-Pad being emulated as analog which messes with the game's movement in it's entirety.The game itself is very enjoyable and an absolute classic, it's just sad to see after waiting ever since my childhood, that the "remake" is essentially a cashgrab capitalizing on nostalgia.Ever since I was a young child I've hoped for a Tomba! 3, and played both games once a year or more, but really this is nothing more than a port of the original game, with more issues than you would find on an open source emulator for free.I hope the Tomba! 2 port is treated better, as that is the one I have the most nostalgia for, but this port has not given me much hope. I've always dreamed of a Tomba! 3 one day, but if this is how this amazingly unique title is going to be treated, I think it's best to leave it be, as Limited Run Games is not adding much beyond what was already there in the originals.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is good. The original was good too. This is easily worth your time. Can be speed-ran in 3 hours and may take up to 6-7 hours for someone playing blind with no looking up at wikis. IMO worth it at full price let alone at discount price.The long answer: There's something to be said about a good remaster. A good remaster can take the opportunity to go back and clean up bugs, prevent short-sighted decisions by the original team or patch out opportunities to lock yourself out of options that existed in the previous game.This is not a remaster, and does none of those things. So why do I recommend this?Tomba Special Edition is a no-frills graphical update to the original game, with emulator settings like save states, rewinding, upscaled cutscenes, and importantly display filtering. Adding the CRT filter does make the game feel back in it's retro home and with the cleaned up controls, feels more natural compared to the PS1 original copy that i broke out to side-by-side comparison.Buy this version if you would like to have an official, legal copy of the game without having to resort to downloading iso's and emulating, or buying expensive original disks on the secondary market.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes down to many of gaming’s most fascinating yet obscure franchises over the past several decades, the Tomba duology has to be by far a particularly great hidden gem of sorts that made its debut on the original PlayStation way back in 1997 as it offered a unique experience to many platforming enthusiasts at the time. Given that this was a period where many game development studios in their youth were experimenting to see which ideas worked for various genres of the time, with technology rapidly growing into the new fancy 3D realm, it stands within reason then that such a game as Tomba would eventually arise as the then-active company Whoopee Camp sought to take a shot at making their own mascot for the surprise hit console that was the original PlayStation.Though as fate would have it, sometimes being good and standing out with a fresh new take on the genre simply isn't enough where the world of business and marketing is concerned, seeing as the duology of Tomba games performed less than stellar when it was being sold to customers across the globe at the time. However, time and time again we see cult classics arise over the decades and I can say with confidence that Tomba deserves to be remembered as one of the hidden PS1 gems of its time, something that Limited Run Games thankfully agrees with as they have created this port of the first game here and made this creative title available on modern platforms.Although before delving into what this ingenious game is all about, one point of contention should be explored here as some Tomba fans have considered this to be an early adaptor of the now-popular ‘Metroidvania’ genre (many come to mind, though Terraria and Cave Story are two that easily encapsulate what a traditional Metroidvania is all about) whilst others firmly believe it to be more akin to a puzzle platformer, of which Oddworld: Abe's Odyssey is a prime example of what the genre has to offer.Whilst I personally believe it to have its roots firmly placed within the Action-Adventure genre, it is worth touching upon the two specific genres I mentioned earlier as Tomba sits somewhere in-between those two. To clarify, a Metroidvania game features a large area, many parts of which are locked off to the player initially, where collecting items can empower the player in ways of superior platforming abilities and new and improved weaponry to better deal with more dangerous foes alongside the usual health improvements and other nifty abilities. Meanwhile, puzzle platformers are games largely focused on overcoming various obstacles through the use of game mechanics that require the player to think outside of the box.After having played this game for myself and completed it fully, I can confidently say that Tomba Special Edition is a puzzle platformer with some Metroidvania elements incorporated into the gameplay. Since the puzzles themselves are often relatively straightforward and can be solved casually without too many headaches and the upgrades are, whilst handy and allowing for some especially neat tricks for shortcuts, mainly serve to make the platforming easier for the player and to ensure that they don't perish to later enemies too quickly; ultimately I find that Tomba strikes a nice balance between the two that ensures it won't be too confusing for players who dislike puzzles or too challenging for less combat-inclined gamers.With that being said, the gameplay of Tomba revolves around exploring the many areas awaiting the titular character himself as you start off with nothing but a jackhammer to stun enemies with. Given the above genres that I mentioned earlier, progress is made through discovering items either on the field or conversing with many of this game's inhabitants and completing events by many different means. Two such examples are using a miniature tornado you can hold onto to clear the fog that prevents access to the next area and using a new tool that doubles as an upgrade to your jackhammer to make your way up to a secret village atop a mountain, noting that this is one of several that has multiple methods of accomplishing the same goal.On the note of events themselves, seeing as most of them can be worked out by the player without too much effort, a few are fairly obscure and can prove tricky to solve for most players without a guide. Perhaps the most obnoxious example of this is with the 'Pump Rocks' event which, whilst I won't go into detail about where it leads to as far as gameplay or story goes, Even though some are complicated to complete, this isn't nearly as bad as a few of the game's events that can potentially be missed and softlock you out of 100% completion. I'll go into spoilers here for those who would rather explore Tomba blindly for themselves, but for those who want a heads-up here are the events you can end up missing outright:Unfortunately, due to the nature of these early games designed around such complex structures for gameplay, problems like these were bound to arise despite being a direct emulation of the PS1 game itself. Seeing how one would expect improvements for what could easily be perceived as a remaster of the sorts, I can easily understand why some potential fans would be put off when having to navigate carefully for those who care about 100% completion.On the subject of emulation, since this has been a controversial matter for some, whilst I can understand why it would be perceived as a 'lazy' approach to bringing back our most beloved games from decades past, I have to say that LRG did a fairly okay job with keeping the game's 'spirit' intact as far as general performance and emulation bugs go. However, the same can't be said for the original music soundtracks as I was quite disappointed to see that there was a noticeable slowdown that made some songs sound quite glitchy and generally unpleasant to listen to, unlike the remastered soundtracks.Now for those who have been paying attention, the word 'remaster' may sound a tad contradictory when I just mentioned this being an emulation port earlier. Whilst that's true for the game at large, LRG does offer a variety of new QoL improvements and provides players with a whole museum that hosts various artwork, both official and behind-the-scenes concepts, alongside some videos documenting interviews and development of the game itself. Alongside the ability to adjust the screen size and apply a CRT filter, it is very appreciated they included three save slots where you can save at any point (unlike the original where you needed to examine signposts spread across the continent to save) and a handy rewind function which enables players to go back in time by up to two and a half minutes for any problematic situations!It goes without saying that, despite some issues that I have with the game's archaic design and this emulation having its own technical mishaps, Tomba Special Edition is an overall bonus for those looking to get into retro gaming as well as older fans who once played the games back then and I would wholeheartedly recommend it to support the movement to provide games like these that are often overpriced due to scalpers and the retro collection market preventing many from enjoying these fantastic games!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the "Special Edition" part of the title fool you - this is very much a minimal viable product (e.g. "how little can we provide while still ensuring people will buy it") with extra steps, namely a mini-documentary on the original game's creation and high-res product assets, concept art, and video. The Carbon Engine isn't doing anything fancy here - it's just a frontend for those extra steps as well as the PCSX PS1 emulator for the game itself, with custom plugins for injecting new assets into the game. The "remastered" soundtrack, a mix of actually-remastered versions of the original music and poorly done remixes, is awkwardly faded into the game - which is made all the more blatant when you switch to using the original soundtrack and it syncs up perfectly with the game. And, as others have stated, .Furthermore, even though the game supports using DualShock 4 and DualSense controllers, both of which use the same button symbols as the PS1's OG DualShock and digital controllers and, thus, could use the original game's PlayStation button prompts, the game is now hardcoded to exclusively use Xbox button prompts. (To be fair, it seems the Carbon Engine only supports Xbox controller prompts, so they probably just decided to keep it consistent.)As as for the game emulation itself? It's good enough. It's not , and it can slow down in places the original game wouldn't, but it's not unplayable. Yes, it does have save states and rewinding, and yes it does have options for how the game outputs, but the first two are common in modern emulation releases like this, and the output changes are pointless as the game was never meant to be displayed in any aspect ratio other than 4:3, and even the downsampling mode, which very nicely smooths out the game's visuals, doesn't use 4:3 - it uses the unmodified output from the emulated PS1, meaning shapes that shouldn't be stretched are. Plus, those game output options are confusing themselves - the "fullscreen" mode in-game (not to be confused with the completely different "fullscreen" setting in the Carbon Engine's main menu) doesn't stretch the output to the entire screen, that'd be the "16:9" mode.Tomba - heck,  commercially-released emulated game - deserves better than the barebones product Limited Run Games has provided here.
