_childDocuments_.review: A blast from the past that I thought was long forgotten. You play as a wild child that's trying to hunt down pigs to get his Grandfather's bracelet back. The gameplay is a neat mixture of 3D characters on 2 separate 2D planes. This may in fact be the first game that I can remember that did this. Your primary form of attacking is jumping on your enemies, biting them, and chucking them at objects or better yet other enemies. Most of the quests is just a long series of fetch quests but it seems to do it in a fun way that isn't to hard to keep track of as long as you talk to everyone and explore everywhere. I really find it hard to review this game since I play through my copy every couple of years. What takes me 8ish hours to 100% will probably take a first timer near 12-13. I still adore this and the second game and hope to see that here eventually. Would probably say it's worth $15 to new people but I was happy to buy it for $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Back when you could become aware of new games through a few gamer magazines, which you usually never bought yourself and accidentally saw on the coffee table of an acquaintance or family member, or just explored the endless PSX covers in the store, Tomba!, (In my country this game was called Tombi! instead of Tomba!) was one of those games that I found in a gaming store where I spent half an hour looking at the covers, without knowing whether the game was actually good and fun, Tomba! was one that I bought by guessing, but I certainly did not regret it, it had a fitting atmosphere to play an adventure game in that era of gaming as a teenager.Also, 2.5D was still a bit newer to experience than pure 2D or 3D, which also invited me to play again more often. I admit that my expectations for this special edition were perhaps a bit higher than the final result, I was hoping for a bit of a graphical makeover so that the colors and lines would be more refined in the picture and would also be more striking in the eyes.The game feels more like an emulation of the original game. It feels like it, but that doesn't mean it is, it's still Tomba! for immortal platforms like the PC and I'm definitely happy with that!Now we have to wait until we can buy Tomba 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This review is hard for me to write. I grew up with , this has a lot of nostalgia value for me. At its core, it's still fundamentally a great game, and I would recommend anyone to play it. If anything, this game demonstrates the difficulty using the thumbs up/thumbs down rating system, because I would give  a thumbs up, but I would give  a thumbs down. The 90's were an interesting time to be alive, and a great time to be a kid. The pace of innovation was unbelievable. Within the span of 5-6 years, I went from playing the original Mario Bros. on the family NES, to the mind blowing graphics of  on the SNES (which I didn't think could be surpassed}, to playing in fully realized 3D worlds like  and on PlayStation. It was wild. The internet didn't exist for us at this time. My family didn't get a computer until 1999. Gaming news spread by world of mouth on the playground, magazines, and demo discs that were bundled with pizzas for some reason at Pizza Hut. It was a different time. Maybe a better time. Who's to say?I had a very little by way of games. Maybe 3-5 full games in total, but boy did I have demo discs. From demo discs I got to play:- Tomb Raider- Armored Core- Jet Moto- Einhander- Ninja- Grand Tursimo- Tekken - Cool Borders- Ape Escape- Tony Hawk Pro Skater- Final FantasyAnd of course, . These being demos, it was usually only one level, but I would play them over and over and over.  was a game that stood out. It was bright and colorful, weird and fantastical: There were pigs you could jump on and throw, and a peach that farted, and these weird accordion thingies just seemingly around, all set to an intoxicating steel drum score, that was bouncy and cheerful and just made me  things. Not to mention anything of the fact that you played as a shirtless boy with pink hair and green pants who carried a spiked ball on a rope. There wasn't anything normal here. It was so bizarre and attention grabbing. I needed to play it. I needed more than the demo. I needed the full game.I begged and pleaded with my parents to buy me the game, but it was so obscure that they just simply couldn't find it. Eventually a copy turned up, and one magical birthday, I was finally able to dive into the game I'd been pining for for what felt like years (given I was a child, it was probably a couple of months, but I digress). I finally had the full game, and it was beyond my expectations. The game only got weirder and weirder, and my love for it grew and grew. On the surface, you can just more or less run from left to right and get through most of the game. But there were plenty of places to get stuck. Plenty of challenges to put my 8 or 9 year old brain to the test. I played this game for hours, picking up quests (called Events), hunting down the Evil Pigs, and putting the world to right. God only knows how long it took me to finish this game as a child, but I did finish it. Did I get all 130 Events? No, but to be fair, many of them are so cryptic that without a guide, even an adult would easily miss some of them. In reality, if you know what you're doing, this game can be completed in an afternoon. But to a young me, this was an odyssey. I still would re-visit  on occasion. When my old consoles died, and when my physical copies were lost, I emulated it and played it usually once per year, just to get my nostalgia fix. I say all this to emphasize how much I love this game and how much I would recommend anyone play it. It is a magical experience. But this version...Unfortunately, this is a lazy cash grab. It's just an emulator with a wrapper. The original release had quite a few bugs, and they all carried over. In fact, this release has  bugs than the original. Yes, I think it's great the got the original composer to do a remastered soundtrack, but also I wouldn't recommend playing with it. Why? Because the sound font doesn't match the original aesthetic. Not only that, but the "remastered" soundtrack is bugged. Bad. Literally, and I cannot emphasize this enough,  But if you are looking for a *ahem* more legitimate way to play, then this version will do. It's just sad though to say that . is a wonderfully beautiful, mesmerizing cult classic that didn't get its day in the sun due to poor marketing. And now it's getting a second life and I want to be so happy, but once again  was done dirty... If this is your only way to play it, then maybe wait for a sale and pick it up. Switch on the original sound track and just let yourself experience this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I have such fond memories of this game from a child - I remember having the demo from a Playstation magazine and I played it over and over again but my parents wouldn't buy the game for me because it was too expensive!  Well, I couldnt believe reading a few years ago they were remastering it for re-release!  It plays just as well as I remember although I wouldn't say the game looks very much like a remaster, it looks like it did on an old emulator and you can rewind like you could on there.  I found the key bindings to be super annoying, I couldnt see if you could rebind them anywhere.  All in all, I highly recommend this game if you like puzzle platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Very happy with this Special Edition port of one of my favorite PS1 games growing up. Tomba! is a truly unique action adventure game with a creative world, fun characters, and game design that's taking inspiration from a lot of genres (RPGs, point-and-click adventure games, platformers, Zelda / Metroid style progression via finding new tools in an open world, and more), but manages to make it all cohere into an experience that's a joy to play.I spent my first hour just looking through all the awesome stuff in the museum, the handful of videos with the Director and Composer were especially cool. Gameplay-wise it's nice to be able to save anywhere and the rewind has been great for when I'm feeling impatient with some of the trickier platforming sections. I also installed Reshade and am using the crt-royale shader, which imo makes the game look real nice, definitely better than with the built-in CRT overlay.Maybe best of all is the brand new soundtrack, I was cautious about it before release because I enjoyed the original so much, but so far pretty much every track has felt like an improvement or at least of equal quality. I've yet to be disappointed upon hearing the music when I progress to a new area. The original soundtrack is also available to play with, remastered in CD quality in-game for the first time. There's also a music player in the main menu where you can listen to any track (I do wish it had more media controls than just pausing). I should mention that I've had a few moments of the music sounding tinny during gameplay, not sure if that's an issue with the emulation or what, hopefully it can be patched soon.I can definitely recommend this to old fans like me and newcomers who want to experience this PS1 gem for the first time!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Its probably my all-time favorite. Its so quirky, creative and hilarious. I still have the original PS1 game and have been playing it every few years. Nowadays it's difficult to find a tv with the right connection for 90's electronics and my playstation1 has been slowly giving up for years anyways. With a rerelease on Steam I have full access again. A shame they changed the intro song, tho. The original Nanana-song from the intro was catchy as H. They also removed some of the cartoon cut scenes? Other than that: I love that they haven't changed the graphics. It would have lost way too much charm, if you couldn't appreciate the character expressions like they were meant too, originally. Can't wait till they release the 2, but I do hope they update the graphics there a little. That game was soooo before it's time and I'm so impressed they could actually make such an advanced game on a ps1-processor. The 1st one is an ultimate classic, tho. I'm giving this to my nephew for his birthday and am very much looking forward to experience how it's recieved in the younger generation. Wish there were more games like this one. Buy it, play it, repeat <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: A great nostalgia hit that *MOSTLY* holds up even almost 3 decades after it released.Tomba! Special Edition is a little rough around the edges, but for FINALLY getting it on PC and only being around $20, it's certainly worth it if you ever played the demo back on the PS1. The rewind feature might seem like a little bit of a cop-out to some but it really does take the frustration out of things like the awful hit-stun mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game - I've owned it for ps1 since I was a kid, and the old demo disc got me started on it. So I had been looking forward to the remastered release.Unfortunately I'm a bit disappointed.I feel that I would have been happy with it if it had proper widescreen (or even better, ultrawide) support, and if the loading times had been addressed (thinking ahead to the haunted mansion and how much of a pain in the backside loading is there) but as it is, I may as well get my money back and use an emulator to play it again for now.Additionally, the movement feels a bit off somehow compared to running it on an emulator or back on the old ps1, and something about the remastered music in the village of all beginnings makes my brain unhappy?
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: While this rerelease leaves more to be desired, I still had a ton of fun playing Tomba once more. So much so, that I completed all in-game events in one single day without any bugs or problems. If you have missed Tomba like me, this release is definitely for you - but be aware, that some players experience problems so waiting for a sale might be recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this through and clearing all 130 events has been a wild ride! I've ever only played this on the demo disc multiple times but never got around to owning it myself until I heard of this release.  I've got a bit to criticise, but on the whole the game functions well. TL;DR Good game, would recommend if you want a legal digital copy of the game.An obvious issue was the sound design. The loop for some tracks are still having issues has the biggest issue where the music just stops once you go in one of the doors. Bit crushed wall climbing and chicks tweeting put me off right at the beginning.No life lost music (Though it's almost impossible to die with the emulator controls built in)Moving on from sound issues is gameplay, which is about 95% functional. The occasional slowed frame rate in some areas isn't a big deal IMO but just annoying.Love the ability to save anywhere, great feature on the one hand. However, rewinding on the other hand killed the challenge and made beating the game too easy. I would suggest that rewinding should be unlocked upon beating the game once.That's about it. Gonna work on speedrunning this game now. Shoutout to the other demo disk 1 players who found this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Just bought this game today and beat it 100%! This game stands out from a lot of platformers. It's a lot of fun, clearing events give that good dopamine rush and you get cool items as rewards. It's a criminally under rated platformer and this game deserves a second chance!As for the port job, It's not the greatest ever done but besides a few technical hiccups here and there, it does it's job at bringing Tomba to modern consoles and that's all that matters at this point (And by golly does it matter because have you checked the prices for an original copy?)
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba "Special Edition" is not so much a special edition, as it is just a solid port/emulation that comes with an optional remastered soundtrack that is a legitimate improvement over the original. The addition of saving anywhere and basically having a rewind feature is neat but ultimately unnecessary. It's still possibly one of the best games on the original Playstation,  I really can not say enough good things about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Just good as i remember it being during my childhood. Remastered the game once again on different platform. I can only wish that they eventually get rights to do same to Tomba 2 so i can get the entire set!EDIT: Seems like we will receive Tomba 2 to steam too after seeing some of the in game teasers. Cant wait!WARNING: 130 Events Achievement is bugged so you need to change to Remastered Soundtracks before the event screen pops up and you're all good. The Achievement wont currently pop if you finish the game with the original soundtracks.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba from the PS1 era was a great game, and now here we are years later to the Steam port of it. Now I love the original music in Tomba, the remastered is good, but nothing can beat the classic music. 130 Event's may seem like alot, granted you have to return after certain items, or requirement's have been met, but honestly, it's not all that bad. If you're going through the Bronze, Silver, and Gold Medal Event's, the time trial course can get a bit annoying to newcomers and old players alike, but with a little practice, you'll ace all three with no problems. Waiting on Tomba 2 now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba! Is one of the games that shaped my taste in the medium growing up, and to this day both it and Tomba 2 remain some of my favourite games of all time. It makes me really happy to see the franchise return, especially with the remastered tracks which I think sound phenomenal. I've been having a blast and most definitely will keep on having a blast for playthroughs to come. Can't wait for Tomba 2 next year!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on a demo disk many, many years ago, and always told myself I would buy the full game. Well, 27 years later, I finally fulfilled my promise to myself, and I'm thoroughly enjoying the experience. Now, admittedly, I've been abusing the rewind feature included in this Special Edition, but I don't really think it detracts from the experience. In fact, it helps keep me from getting *too* frustrated at the sometimes slippery controls, although a large part of that was from an ability/upgrade that I received from finishing an Event.All of that being said, I do wish I was able to control the volume in-game, and I can see where individuals using keyboard or PS controllers would have issue with the XBox control scheme, but honestly, I do not recommend playing with keyboard if possible. The game runs in a smaller 4:3 aspect ratio, but unlike most other games forced to play in that ratio, it doesn't change the native ratio of my monitor, and instead plays in a letterbox, which you can change the background (and color, depending on the background chosen). I closed the game once in the time that I've had it, and while my computer did save the volume setting and the game was running in fullscreen as opposed to the default windowed, it did switch the soundtrack from playing the original like I had set it to playing the remastered. Which is fine, because the remastered sounds good, but I just wanna play with the original soundtrack for now for the nostalgia, but I can't ignore that the setting reset.I have yet to run into issues running the game on my computer, and I read on the forums that the cloud saving "issue" was fixed, so I don't know what's causing some people the issues that have been reported. Additionally, I haven't noticed any marked performance issues while playing, either.This is very much targeting the older players, like myself, who played the original game or the demo disk, so I offer word of caution to those that have not played the game at all: The only thing remastered in this game is the soundtrack. The gameplay and the graphics remain true to the original so, if that isn't your cup of tea, then please pass this game up and don't buy/play it only to downvote it because it's not "modern". The gameplay is still very solid, and if one can see past the "outdated" graphics, the charm and fun of the game will be quite apparent.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, there is an easy way for me to dye my hair pink, run around half naked while jumping and biting pigs without society looking down at me.In all serious though, this was one of my favourite games growing up and I can't wait to replay it, yes even that damn Motocross section.There's a few issues I've noticed so far with the port, but it's a way to play Tombi / Tomba legally, which is the important thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best metroidvanias / platformers on the Playstation and one of my favorite games. It's a ton of fun!The boss battles are a bit lackluster, though, so this might not be the game for you if that's what you play games for. This is also more or less a straight port of the old game with little in the way of quality of life improvements. The only real changes to the gameplay is being able to save wherever you want and the rewind feature, and both of those are nice but it's still pretty much the same game that released on Playstation, for better or worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Still a very unique and extremely enjoyable. For the most part, you do get your childhood game that none of your friends have ever heard about back, but not without its imperfections, and I'll explain.-Sometimes, you can get wedged up against a floor and a wall and you won't be able to control Tomba properly (unless I'm just not remembering that little piece of jank).-Some of the sounds seemed glitched/bit-crushed, like when you're on a brown pig-nose plant (or similar object) and you rotate to the other side.-When using the Rewind feature, you're prone to loosing your music, especially when rewinding from another region or from a load screen-No feature to change button layout, which was a little annoying because I was using a Switch Pro controllerOTHER THAN MY LIST OF WOES, I love this game. I like the remastered soundtrack, the ability to save anywhere is great, rewind feature is always welcome, and I love the music player and museum.If they gave the same treatment to Tomba 2, I'd still buy it and be a happy costumer.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Help Tomba explore the island, defeat the evil anthropomorphic pigs and return his grandfather's golden bracelet.Gameplay:Tomba can run, jump, climb walls/rocks/plants, pick up and use objects, attack enemies with weapons (flails and boomerangs) and melee.He can jump on enemies' backs, bite and throw enemies.NPCs can give Tomba various quests (find an item, save a character or clear a path), for completing which he receives a reward.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba! (originally Tombi! in EU regions including Australia), is a great PS1 game, and a "hidden gem", if you've never played it.However, this is an odd port: some areas seem greatly polished/improved: new save feature, rewind functionality, remastered soundtrack, and then we have others like: odd control scheme, no way to remap buttons, and very few video scaling & filtering options. They've changed the text hints in-game to have X-input buttons, but even those buttons are not mapped correctly. For example, using keyboard input, it tells you to push 'A' to talk to people. What it doesn't tell you is that 'A' will  with an NPC, but then you need to push 'X' to advance the dialog.Feels very much like a wrapper around an emulator with the PlayStation ISO. I do wish there were some more filter options, a Bilinear blur might help smooth out some edges. Some of the text is super aliased too, especially on the orange Event name/Event Cleared popups. It would be nice if these textures had received at least a little bit of an upscale, even if the rest of the game didnt.All-in-all, if you're after a good little 2.5D RPG/Platformer, Tomba is a great game. Just don't expect it to be the best port/remastering ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Man.. I could go on and on about how beautiful Tomba was back on the PS1 when I was a kid. I never got to play the first one until late into my teens because the first game was a hard title to find growing up so my first introduction to Tomba! and Tomba! 2 was with the second game. I remember spending hours playing it at my grandparents house on the weekends and again when I would go spend time over at my aunt's house during the summer just so we could 100% the game back then.Going through and playing Tomba! felt like such a breath of fresh air when looking at games we have nowadays that I honestly felt relieved and relaxed... almost like I was having a cozy afternoon/evening of gaming. 10/10 recommend picking it up and if they give Tomba! 2 the same treatment, I highly recommend you picking it up as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to 100% in a few hours. I mainly play this game for nostalgia. It was one of my favorite games on the PS1 and I revisit it every few years. Cool to see it available for new audiences.The "remastered" music leaves some aspects to be desired and it repeats at awkward intervals, but I'm not playing that long for it to bother me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba is a cult classic that I grew up playing a demo for but was never able to finish the game until years later. This game is a great game that stood the test of time and this is a great port. The rewind system they've implemented is pretty nice, as well as being able to save from anywhere, but the only issue is the audio options. Not having volume control over the game is rough if you're in a call with friend and the default audio for the game is insanely loud. Other than that this is a great port
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten this game multiple times as a kid and it's just as good as it was then, besides the addition of extra developer stuff such as artwork, the process of composing the remastered tracks for this release and how whoopee camp started out. If you don't want to go through the process of emulating this game, I would definitely recommend this version as I personally had no issues for the entire play through. The rewind feature and option to save anywhere without using a sign was also a very welcome addition to this version and helped out a lot, specifically for the motocross section. I would hope to see "Tomba! 2: The Evil Swine Return" receiving the same features if we are able to get a steam release for that too.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Iconic game from the PS1 era, some consider to be a hidden gem!The story puts you in the shoes (or lack thereof) of Tomba, a feral jungle boy armed with a deadly blackjack and a sick mane of pink hair, quite possibly making him the only male to rock the color and not have preferred pronouns! He notices the local corrupt police bullying a caravan and goes to record them for Facebook, only to be knocked out and have his family heirloom wrongly taken from him: his bling.In anger, our hero sets out to rid the land of the corrupt police by turning them into sweet sweet bacon, all the while restoring the land to what it looked like before governments got involved, and eventually uniting the people of all shapes, sizes, and colors, against the common enemy!Rating: ACAB (All Cops Are Bacon)/10On a serious note: one of my favorites from my childhood. Looks and plays great on the deck, I just wish that they could have remastered the graphics alongside the newly revamped musical score as well. That being said, I personally have had no issues with performance. Looks and plays identical to its original release!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Very faithful, though this sadly extends to the res. If there is an option to truly get it to fullscreen, I couldn't find it, and had to play with borders.They do have playful artwork borders to choose from, but I just can't handle that personally. I'll be refunding, but I can definitely recommend for those who don't mind borders. Doubly so if they ever add an upscailing option.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's fine. Ignore the negative reviews whining about how this isn't a remaster; it was never advertised as one.Could they have quickened the loading times? Yes. Could they have made the game play in proper widescreen? Yes. Could they have added features that other retro PC releases received? Yes. Unfortunately, they didn't, which makes this a "fine" re-release as opposed to an excellent one. The game still looks and plays as great as it did when it originally came out.My recommendation is to buy this only if you're a hardcore Tomba!/Tombi! fanatic, who wants to own the game on every platform and/or wants to see all the museum content added in this specific release. Otherwise, stick to your emulated copy on DuckStation, which has all the options available that this release should have also received.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me but I have to give this version of the game a negative review. The game itself is AWESOME! But the port is terrible. First, I had issues booting the game up. I had to turn off Steam input to be able to boot. Second, the game flickered half my time into the game. Some weird graphics glitch. Still enjoyed the game and I like the ability to rewind and save wherever you want, but the fact that all the loading screens and blackouts between sections in the game were still there is terrible. Also, I would've loved for the graphics to have gotten an update (a la Duck Tales Remastered), but no nothing. Honestly, I'm now playing the game on DuckStation with RetroAchievements on and it runs more stable and the experience is way more solid than this "Remastered" version on Steam. Limited Run games, please step it up for Tomba 2...?!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first I bought this because i were never able to complete it as a kid (didn't understand English) and I was so happy that it got released on PC.But for some reason the game wont even start. I found out that it wont work at all when i have my controller plugged in, but even without it the game wont go past the Intro.. Also they have muted the sound effects and changed the music completely which is super disappointing.The visuals also seemed grainy from what i have seen, I was expecting somewhat of a remaster and not just a straight up copy paste (which I could have lived with if I was able to actually play it).This is the first review i have ever done, but i felt like it was needed from the inability to play the game and the sheer laziness from the developers/publishers., Refunding the game after posting this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a lot when I was a teenager. I have been waiting for it to drop on Steam for a while now. It really takes me back. Certainly not as great as I remember.A very simple game in many ways. It's pretty unique. It's mostly 2D, but you can interact with layers to give it the illusion of being 3D. Some areas actually are 3D, but you can only move around in 2 dimensions. One level rotates.The controls are a bit awkward. Movement is sluggish and doesn't allow for precise movements that easily, though you get used to it. The character doesn't always latch onto things just like you want. Load screens are too frequent and annoying. It would be nice if the quests told you where the quest giver was so you could remind yourself of what you are doing. The text of the quests in menu isn't super helpful. The map doesn't really help either and is confusing. Because of this, it's hard to know what to do next somtimes. I had to use a guide for a few of them, as I occasionally got stuck and wouldn't be sure what to do to progress the game. Areas that are clear will later have totally unrelated NPCs from other areas and you'd only ever find it by recombing over the entire game over and over again. It's no wonder I never beat this game when it came out. There wasn't much internet back then.One nice addition is the the game saves state, like an emulator would, every few seconds, so you can backtrack quickly as needed if you go in the wrong load zone or something.Don't be afraid to use your fast travel consumable. There is a way to get a reusable fast travel later on, though I believe you could miss it and not get it until much later. I wish this was a required quest much earlier, as travel can be a slog due to the confusing map, interwoven zones, and frequent load screens. I often forgot how to get somewhere because of how woven the zones are. There were paths that are obscure that I forgot were there until I came back out the other side again. It's really cool how intricate the design is, but confusing without a great map.I'd say the game is definitely worth picking up on sale if you played it when you were younger and want to be nostalgic. I'll give it a thumbsup, just because that was my case. If not, I still wouldn't give it a thumbs down, but I'd be more neutral towards it. It's not bad, it's just not great. It's a really great concept that could use some improvements. An actual remake would have been nice, instead of a port.Took me about 12 hours with 93% achievement completion. I wasn't going back and finishing all the quests to get 100% completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love Tomba and have fond memories playing the original release of the game when I was a child, however it's incredibly disheartening how barebones this "special edition" is. I was willing to put aside my grievances to support this release in hopes they re-release Tomba 2 and potentially revive the franchise from obscurity, but my goodness the lack of cloud saving implementation on launch for a $25,99 (CAD) game is ludicrous. Very disappointed many crucial QOL features are either poorly implemented or completely absent. At its current state it's hard to recommend the game unless you're a die hard fan and are playing it on a singular device.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me you'll have fond memories of playing this on the PS1 and think "Well damn, even in this age of remakes and remasters I wasn't expecting a Tomba! rerelease. Time to wallow in nostalgia." And then, like me, you'll steadily come to the realization that this remaster is lacking quality of life features, barely has any visual updates, kinda has crappy controls, and bugs out a fair bit, and think "Hang on, did I actually like this game or am I just nostalgic for 90s gaming?"Stay nostalgic, friends. _childDocuments_.review: Tomba (or Tombi as it was once known in Europe/Australia) is a great little 2.5~ish game. You play in a single 2D dimension but occasionally can move back and forth between the foreground and the midground. Some village areas are 2.5D style and allow you to talk to the inhabitants. The main focus of the game is to explore and help others out which will complete events (think quests) that can either help make game play easier, or are required to open up more areas to explore.Overall it's a fun game brought back from the dead from the PlayStation 1 days, although this update adds in some nice new features (rewind mode, re-imagined music, bonus vids) it sadly suffers from over the top load times when you move from area to area (understandable in "PS1 on a disc" days but really shouldn't be a thing with 2024+ hardware and storage)Good but could be loads better if they tried
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: As a child I remember endlessly playing Tombi! on a demo disk, it's nice to have the full game after all these years. I took me eight hours with a guide to wrap it up in a completionist way, and the behind the scenes art and photographs in this edition are super neat.Tomba is a platformer metriodvania, and deserves it's cult following. I cannot wait to 100% the sequel they're remastering soon, as  Tomba! 2: The Evil Swine Return is one of my all-time favourite games.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba is a franchise that I hold near and dear to my heart. When I was old enough to hold a controller I remember sitting on the floor in front of the TV and having my mom watch me try and complete the sequel, Tomba 2, albeit it took me several months to accomplish that feat. Ever since then I've had a special place in my heart for this little pink-haired caveman. With that being said, I was absolutely devastated to hear that Whoopee Camp shut down after their second release and that I would likely never see or play a Tomba game again.Despite all odds and about 20 years of waiting we're here with a "new" Tomba game and a dream fulfilled. So does it actually hold up?SUMMARY:Tomba is a "2.5D" platformer-adventure game where you traverse a whimsical and, at times, outright silly world in search of your grandfather's bracelet that was stolen by evil pigs. Along the way you'll visit towns that have also been cursed by these mischievous swine. Your goal is to help as many people as you can to unlock upgrades to both your gear and weapons—so it might not be a bad idea to help out everyone you can!PROSThis game is such a weird one in the nicest, and most positive way possible. This is the type of game that wasn’t afraid to be silly in an era of Castlevanias and Metroids. The visuals are a nice blend of 3D environments mixed with 2D spritework and it is honestly pretty amazing and ambitious for a game developer's first outing in the 90s. This whimsical atmosphere has stuck with me for 20 years and I still couldn’t help myself from just enjoying the visuals in my most recent playthroughs.One thing that I think is cool about this game, but I don’t want to go too much into detail about is the fact that once you “cure” and area of its curse you actually get to see that area as it was before the curse and you can even go back and interact with the villagers and inhabitants. I can’t think of another game that actively lets you do that! Most games will have you play straight through and then just give you a cutscene showing that you have saved the world (yippee!). Visually the game is very unique and the music and sound effects are right there with it. I didn’t learn until recently, but apparently some people did not like the original OST, which is what prompted the remastered soundtrack available with this version. I personally never minded it. The game itself is weird and the music I feel fits pretty well. There were some songs like Baccus Village that I thought were outright catchy even. The music of the Haunted Mansion encapsulates a very foreboding aura. It’s pretty good! CONSThe game is a tad bit challenging as some of the controls are dated as they were originally made with a D-Pad in mind. This paired with some tricky jumps and hard to reach collectibles can feel unfair at times. With enough practice, though, any obstacle can be overcomed. Outside of the platforming, there are a handful of quests that had me scratching my head to find out where exactly to go next. There were a few times where I would run around the entire world (literally) just to see if an NPC had a hint on where to go next. This, obviously, is only an issue your first or second time playing through, but it can still be frustrating to try and go for 100% and not have a clue on where to get the final events.Outside of issues relating to game design, this particular port does have its fair share of bugs that I’m sure the developers are hard at work to squash. I haven’t run into anything major outside of the occasional music track stopping when opening the “remaster windows”, but I have heard of some unfortunate souls having their games crash. My heart goes out to both you guys and your save files that I’m sure lost a fair bit of progress (SAVE OFTEN!).VERDICT:I am not a reviewer. I am just a very happy fan that was given another opportunity to support a game from my childhood, and now I am able to share my love for the game with people who have and haven’t played Tomba before. The game is not perfect, but it is filled with a lot of heart. Just scrolling through the dev blogs and early concept art you can really tell that the team at Whoopee Camp had a vision for this thing and they gave it their all. They believe Tomba could be one of the greats and I still think that he can be.If you enjoy games in the same vein as this one I’d recommend giving it a shot. I have loved this little weird pink-haired caveman for 20+ years now and I hope that you can find as much enjoyment as I have playing his game.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my childhood and it's a gift to video games. It was so ahead of its time and everyone should play it for sure. It's quaint and entertaining. _childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This entire game is great, even with some of its jank.do not go into this expecting polish. this is the same game as released on the original playstation, with all the jank that version had.it adds a rewind feature and a save anywhere option which really help it. but. other than that the game is left untouched.i'd reccommend first time players use a strategy guide. because there IS some obscure weirdness to it.with that in mind, even for all its jank and lack of polish, tomba gets by on one thing really well: it's charm. this, is a gorgeous game visually. and the tone of the game reminds me of very early dragon ball (when it was silly and lighthearted series about an adventerous boy with zero social skills), and tomba himself, despite not being able to speak, has a very great design and personality.just remember: do not break a rolling barrel (hit it to make it lose its spikes and then roll it into the water),  and you'll be fine.i heartily reccommend this game, despite its jank. and i hope this is a new lease on life for the lovable wild child with a ball and chain.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Great to see Tomba getting some recognition with a rerelease, can't wan't for Tomba 2! Overall an enjoyable experience, with some of the more annoying aspects of old design eased by the rolling savestates/rewind feature. Things like infinitely respawning enemies(but not quest barrels), blind jumps, insta-death pitfalls, no quick retry option on minigames, etc. Stuff I wouldn't normally forgive, but  it doesn't matter since I can roll the game state back. Music would sometimes cut out when using the rewind, but overall a solid way to experience this old game.Only complaint I have is I broke the barrel not thinking much of it in the early game, only to find out that's why I don't deserve 100% completion. Definitely really hits that vintage game design feel, and I'm cool with leaving it at that. Also Tomba 3, please?
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite literally just a copy of the original game. The original soundtrack is available but you have to manually switch over to it every time you boot up the game and certain steam achievements wont pop if you're listening to the original soundtrack which was annoying. For $20, I wasn't expecting massive changes or anything but it would have been nice if they had fixed some of the soft blocks (like breaking the barrel or certain events being missable if done out of order.) All in all, it was a great trip down memory lane and I can't wait for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: is a great game, this release is okay. I'll separate the review into parts dividing this specific release and the game itself. After a lot of thinking, I chose to make this a positive review, but with caveats detailed in the conclusion below.The bonus features are really cool, creator interviews and scans of all game-related material is perfect stuff to include in a re-release, and stuff like the dev documents being translated is great. That said, it's a very basic implementation of it all; no controls for video/audio playback in the museum or music player and not even a repeat/endless play toggle for music. At least you can watch the videos from within the game folder using a media player.I didn't listen to a lot of the remastered soundtrack due to its janky implementation. It sounded nice, but some tracks started their loops too soon, or the music would sometimes vanish completely until you did something to cause a track change.Being able to rewind the game and save/load anywhere is very useful if you're struggling, or if you need to quickly stop your session and aren't near any save points -- standard stuff for old game re-releases these days. Saving via signposts seems to now use the same system as the new save/load system, except signpost saves fail to generate a proper thumbnail.Performance-wise, it was playable. A couple instances of slowdown, don't remember if it happens in in the original too. The load times seem to still be stuck in 1997; I did a highly unscientific test where I started from the Y-crossing, visited all three rooms in the Iron Castle and returned. Of the 86 seconds it took, the screen transitions (Now Loading/black screen) lasted a collective total of over 50 seconds.Last couple notes, a general volume slider of any kind would have been nice, and I dunno if it's been fixed, but the achievement for completing every event would pop  if you reached the final results screen with the remastered soundtrack enabled.Tomba! is still a ton of fun. It's not without its flaws, but I still love playing it.Exploring the world, clearing events and hurling pigs around is as satisfying as ever. Tomba! has some bite to it with the occasional "gotcha" trap or a tricky platforming segment, but it's generous with its lives for those with the will to explore.Speaking of exploration, you'll be going from place to place to clear events . It's a blast, but without a guide, you might find yourself running in circles trying to figure out where exactly you need to go next. I beat it without a guide, but I ended up spending several hours aimlessly circling and backtracking all the areas trying to find events to do.The music is wonderful, I would deliberately mess around in a few areas just so I could hear it for a while longer. The dwarves must be sick of seeing my face around their village by now.It's great that Tomba! is finally available to people again, but the price is pretty steep. It's the same game, so you should temper your expectations accordingly. If you already own a copy of the game, you may want to weigh whether or not access to the museum and remastered soundtrack is worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Could it have been a remake? Sure. A remaster? Certainly. But it's Tomba! so all I've ever asked for from this timeless game is: a rerelease. And that's exactly what this is, with a remade soundtrack option as a cherry on top. Yes, this version has its flaws which other reviews have documented well, but for this game (and the promised sequel, fingers crossed) and at this price point I am willing to let those slide.Bought it, played it, loved it, and thus do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba! holds a special place in my nostalgic heart, being such a replayed game in my childhood. This version has remastered music (that you can also set to original music) and the ability to put a CRT filter on it so the graphics look a little smoother. The rewind is a nice touch, but serves as a reminder that this is essentially a port and not a remake of the game.The ability to miss an entire event in the game is still there from the original Playstation 1 version, which is frustrating to those who trophy hunt here on Steam. My only gripe is pretty minor, and that's if you're playing on a controller, you can't change the button display to anything other than Xbox inputs.Otherwise, I'm very pleased with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia definitely blinded me a bit in terms of quality. I have fond memories of playing this back as a kid on the PS1. Now, 20 years later, I understand why; the convoluted map and quest design and cut content has you travelling back-and-forth a ton to figure out where you need to go and when. That said, the game is still incredibly cute and fun, a great example of the attempted innovation of games of its time.This release is basically just a PS1 emulator with a pretty shell over it that adds some extra features that you can see outlined on the store page. I think the interviews and design stuff in the Museum section is really great to have collected in one spot.A lot of love went into making this game, and a lot of love went into making this remaster. Hope they give the second game a similar treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomba and its sequel are, to me, perfect video games. They encompass everything I want in a game, and I enjoyed them both since they released in the late 90s. They are at their core Metroidvanias. If I had to compare them to anything, maybe Super Adventure Island 2 on SNES. This remaster hits all the right notes and thee addition of achievements makes it even better. The controls are smooth although be patient as you learn the mechanics of biting enemies. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game with 100% achievement, the game is exactly the same as the PS1 counterpart. The only difference is the music players, demos, interview videos, rewind system, and the remastered soundtracks and the home menu. As someone who loves classic games, this brings back a lot of memories and the controls aren't that hard to navigate (I use controller). The only thing that needs improvement is the implementation of the remastered soundtracks used during game play, which some loops unusually compared to my other game play with the original sounds. The remastered BGMS play during loading screen, which is unusual for me for someone who played the PS1 counterpart. Overall, the game is fun and challenging. The only needed improvement is the remastered soundtracks implemented during loading screen or black screen transition.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: *ROG Ally verified* Unofficially. This game has brought me back to my childhood. It’s great that others who never had a chance to play it will get to experience this whacky adventure.  The rewind feature and save anywhere is welcomed for those who don’t have the time to find save points, or get frustrated having to  restart an area. It’s a unique game with odd mechanics including over 100+ mini events to do and some requiring using cryptic messages from NPC’s, finding items, acquiring an ability, solving minor puzzles or finding people. They are very random so just take this game as a classic slice of life. It has towns that switch to a traditional JRPG style which I love. They have also remastered the music and can switch it back to the old OST too. The NPC and story is typical classic old school style with simple messages like those classics in the 80’s and 90’s games with subtle clues so don’t go expecting a deep cast or story. The negatives- The game seems to have kept the load times from the PS1 version. They are not bad, but still could be reduced. I guess they did keep that nostalgia. - There is a slight delay when going to the items menu. Nothing major but it can be a little tedious when you go back and forth. - I don’t think it’s too much of a negative for me, but maybe others, as they have reduced the save files to only 3 max and not 15 as per memory card in the original. Overall this game is great fun. If you love classic old school platforming games with some quirky events, solving tasks and get back your bracelet from the seven evil pigs, this is worth a go. There is some backtracking but also items to fast travel places too. *If you have any issues with the LT and RT on the ROG Ally not registering in game mode, go into the steams input for control and change “Full Pull” to “Soft Pull” for both Left and Right triggers. This seems to occur with other games too and wanted to point out this tip to save others from the frustration of finding out why they failed to register*
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it for all the extras! The new soundtrack sounds just like the original, but fuller and brighter with much more instrumentation. The "museum" is like having an exclusive pass to explore Whoopee Camp's internal archives, with English translations of Japanese concept art. The interviews with Tokuro Fujiwara is video game history, in and of itself. The game plays just like the original (after all, it is just an emulation) without any obvious issues. I'm not sure why folks are upset that the graphics are unchanged from the original: nowhere in the store listing does it say the game is a remaster or a remake. There are even videos that clearly show the gameplay is visually unchanged and clearly an emulation. Plus, the price point should communicate to you what you're getting. You can play in a stretched widescreen mode, 4:3 mode, or a "regular" mode. A true widescreen mode would've been amazing, but then, the game would also have been double the price. I'm fine with playing at a regular resolution, with a choice of background (the bright pink logo background is, surprisingly, the best one!). Being able to save anywhere is a nice quality of life improvement. Some other reviews are unhappy with this being added, but you can simply choose to not save anywhere if you don't want to: save checkpoints still exist in-game and will correctly open up the save menu, if you choose to access these checkpoints. Controller glyphs have been replaced with Xbox/ABXY icons, but it would be nice to have the option to toggle these to PlayStation glyphs. Overall, this an appropriately priced port of a game that will bring back deeply held memories in so many. If you remember playing Tomba! (or, Tombi!) on the PlayStation, like me, this release will take you back in time!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of nostalgia this game brought me is insurmountable. I understand some of the frustration about the overlay, amongst other things, as this is a remastered version. But if you’re  a fan of the original and you enjoy this game for what it is, you won’t be disappointed.Hopefully Musashi gets the remaster treatment next!

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with many other of the reviews and comments saying that many things could have been improved for the current age.But I also think that this version still had a lot more added to it plus I am happy to play one of my childhood games on a PC hence it's positive - since I hope other people will also get to enjoy it now <: Everything is working - which is more than any other remaster manages to do in the first day. The only times I get a crash is if I am switching to the game scene in OBS. Personally I save over the same save, so for me it's perfectly fine - but I agree that it could have more save slots like we did back on PS1*Will write a full review once I finish the game
_childDocuments_.name: Tomba! Special Edition

_childDocuments_.review: If you do not have a way to play the original game, for $20 this is not a bad pickup. That being said, it is basically a port of the PS1 version of the game, with remastered music (choice of original), save states, and an updated remaster title screen. Outside of that it is basically the original game. I have noticed a few weird glitches were my character will float in a weird way when getting hit, almost like he is wearing the parasol and a gust of wind caught him. Outside of that it plays just like the original. There are also some weird audio issues where the cutscenes are super loud in comparison to the game volume.If you have the original and have a way to play it, unless you really just want achievements or want to be able to play it on the go on your steam deck it's not an immediate go out and grab like I was hoping it would be. It's not bad, but I was hoping for a remaster with upgraded graphics and new music (which the later we got). Overall it's still a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a little bit wonky, but I'm giving it a thumbs up.At the end of the day, it's still Tomba, just the way I (and everyone who played it) remeber it. And that's good.Yeah, it should have been a proper remake because these games deserve it, but it's good. Really, if this eventually gives us Tomba 3, it'll be worth it. I still love it to bits. One of my favorite games from the PS1 (along with Tomba 2).

A lot of people played the demo for this back on the demo discs you used to get with PS magazines and now finally everyone is able to play itAs for special edition, its still the same game you know and love from back in the day but with improvements to the soundtrack, menus and with a load of artwork extrasThere is a reason this is my favourite game of all time. Go get it, you wont be disappointed

About the Game ENGAGE IN SPECTACULAR NAVAL COMBAT Prepare for devastating battles by crafting a dozen different ships and equip your fleet with powerful loadouts. Unlock stronger weapons as you progress and customize your ships to reflect your unique pirate playstyle. SAIL INTO A DANGEROUS HELL IN PARADISE Voyage into the Indian Ocean and explore a vast open world teeming with cutthroat pirates, deadly sea monsters, supernatural threats, devastating storms, and more. TEAM UP WITH FELLOW PIRATES Sail the lawless seas solo or team up with two friends or other players to partake in shareable contracts and rewards. ENJOY EVER-EVOLVING CONTENT Each season, face a brand-new legendary sea lord and discover fresh content, limitless endgame opportunities, and new exciting features designed to enhance your pirate experience. Persistent internet connection and Ubisoft account required.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game for the first time at the beginning of 2024, during the Ubisoft free week. I then bought it on Steam for £20, only because it was on 60% sale. The game is not worth £50.The game is online-only. It’s like taking all the bad things from the MMO and adding them to a single player game. There is a lot of grind, crafting taking a real time (so that you have to log in to the game every 12h to restart your factories), and a lot of various popping timed events. But there are no big battles, nor a player-controlled market. In fact, you rarely even see other players. The lack of ability to pause the game really hurts.Add to it server side issues, desyncs, disconnects, kicks due to “inactivity”, and long loading times. Fast travel between two outposts frequently gets you stuck on the loading screen for 1-3 minutes.After playing the game for almost 200h, and observing all the different problems, I think that the game is fundamentally flawed by design. Every single action requires talking to the server - nothing is cached locally. So you open an inventory, and wait 3 seconds for the items’ icons to load. Or you open a map, and the background is all black with icons in front of it. Even when you press RMB to aim, you won’t see a crosshair until the game actually downloads it from the server. Conversations with NPCs get stuck between lines and cannot be skipped, probably because it downloads the text and audio from the server...And the servers? Each of them is messed up in a different way. On one you cannot complete a certain quest, on another enemies spawn in hundreds, on another chat doesn’t work, on another you get a half second game freeze every 5 seconds, and so on...A lot of people compare it to , but I actually haven’t played this one. However, I put 250 hours into , and my first impression was that it’s pretty much the naval combat part only. Seriously - take out the on-land combat, add some ship customisations, and that’s it. Bracing, holding the right mouse button to shoot, ramming, boarding - everything feels identical.In terms of UI/UX, the game is really poor. For example, the map is an absolute disaster. Cluttered with tens of flashing icons, no filtering, and different things shown at different zoom levels, you can never find what you are looking for... Some icons are not clickable, so you have no idea what they mean. Your currently tracked task is often not highlighted, or just gets lost in all this mess...There are at least 15 different currencies in the game, and you can only see their symbols. No idea what they are, how to get them, and where to spend them. Except 2-3 most obvious and basic ones, none of them are explained in the in-game knowledge base. Even  doesn't even mention most of them. Pretty much every trader I talk to uses different currencies...And the gem on top is how the inventory interface works - there can be two items selected at the same time. One selection is what you clicked, and the other selection is what you are currently pointing at. And now you use a keyboard shortcut to move the item from the ship cargo to the warehouse - which one gets moved? It took me a really long time to understand and get used to this interface.And there is a lot of other issues, and bugs, including game breaking bugs:

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game for 20 something euros on sale, as this made sense for a 20 something euro game (certainly not 60-80 euros). After having some time with it, no I cannot recommend this.Ignoring the lies from the CEO, the removal of most of the playability and the many bugs, I thought for a simple pirate-naval game, this might not be too bad.So it's a Naval game. How many ships do you get total. Twelve. Five of them are current "end-game". and that's your lot. In a AAAA rated game. As for customisation of said ships, its not plentiful either. Because of this, most players end up looking the same.Do you like PS1 Style loading screens that take a minute? Time for a nostalgia trip cos S&B has lengthy load screens everywhere. Even when doing a simple task like visiting a merchant.Your ship has stamina. That's right, your ship, can get tired.Your ship also has "Severe damage", which is damage you can only repair at docks. So if you get one-shotted by an enemy, or if you crew mutinies randomly, you can get sent back to the docks (with a minute or two load time) only to then be informed that you failed the boss battle because you moved away from it, when the game gives you no choice.The game also kills you for no reason. I have seen many times that I will be engaging an enemy, only to get killed by "Unknown forces" as the game calls themHonestly, hold your money for now and see if there is any grand improvements in the next 6 months. If you don't hear Ubisoft doing anything in the next 6 months with S&B, then just assume it's another RDR2O failure and that it has been abandoned as soon as it was released.So check again in March 2025. If this game has not had another 20 ships added and many bugs and load screens fixed, then it means that it is dead for good.

_childDocuments_.review: Ahoy, Mateys!I was ready to hoist the sails and plunder the high seas like it was Black Flag all over again, but instead, I found myself in a leaky rowboat with a couple of rotten oars. I mean, really—how do you go from the masterpiece that was Black Flag to this soggy biscuit of a game? It's like expecting a fine rum and getting watered-down grog instead.I barely survived the opening mission before I had to abandon ship. Naval warfare? More like a cartoonish water balloon fight! Cannons firing like machine guns? Ships doing donuts on the ocean with zero wind mechanics? Even SpongeBob's watery escapades have more realistic naval action!And let’s talk about those graphics—if this game had a face, it would be stuck in the awkward teenage years of the mid-2000s. The textures look like they were plundered from Davy Jones very own bilge tanks, and no amount of "ray-tracing" is going to polish this barnacle-encrusted mess.  I’ve played mobile games with better visuals and more authentic pirate action!Then, for absolutely no reason whatsoever, I was kicked from the server! Not disconnected, mind you—actually kicked! It’s like the game itself realized how bad it was and did me a favor by tossing me overboard. So thanks for that I guess. In short, if you're looking for a swashbuckling adventure, this ain't it, matey. Save your doubloons and sail far, far away from this one. Black Flag set the bar high—this game just walked the plank.Time for me to go grovel to the steamy pirate overlord and beg for my doubloons back!

_childDocuments_.review: The ship combat it kinda meh imo. Even at 24 dollars, I dont think there is too much fun to be had that cant be found in other games. Ships having a Stamina bar is crazy. And using items on the spot like a traditional rpg makes no sense to me. As I was not having fun with the first hour of the game at all I decided to refund it. I did not experience the mid to late game content like the boss battles or monster fights. But I imagine its more of the same with different cannons. _childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, the game is on sale for 24$ US. At this price it is a good game. Decent grind for ships, entertaining mechanics, and good/fun selection of ship weapons for different play styles.What this game is being compared to and what I compared it to is Sea of thieves. This game is not trying to be a pirating sim, where you have to manually control key aspects of the ship and combat of real pirating(?), instead you ARE the ship. If you want to compare it to a game, I would compare it to World of Warships. This game so far is just a naval combat game that has strong arcade elements just like WoW. In order for it to be full price, they should add FPS elements with personal weapons and abilities to grind for also. Depending on how old you are, this game reminds me of Pirates of the Caribbean Online which was F2P with a subscription wall. If they can replicate the decent story POCO had (which currently is generic pirate story I spam click through), actual ground maps to explore, FPS elements, gun rarity, sword rarities, abilities your character had, and GROUND world events (Ex: Jolly Roger would invade an island and the server had to defend it on land), i'd happily pay full price.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly fun yet very flawed game. It's clear that the developers weren't really sure what they wanted to make for a while, so it has remnants of an attempt at a survival game (but they've been mostly sanded off, thanfully). The naval combat reminds me of Black Flag, but it has slightly more depth to it (as most modern open world games do, it has a bunch of "RPG-lite" features, though in this case I don't think they detract from the experience)There's PvP and it seems like at some point it was considered a major part of the game, but I don't really like to PvP nowadays cause I'm old and grumpy, so I haven't really engaged with it. Thankfully there's also a lot of PvE stuff to do, between just going around attacking AI controlled vessels to plundering settlements, or doing quests and some light empire building.Overall, it's closer to Sid Meier's Pirates! than any other comparisons that would come to mind. It has a lot of modern junk like a battlepass, seasonal events that are timegated and stuff like that, but the core of the game is definitely inspired by Pirates! (and it reminds me of the sad fact that we haven't actually had a new Pirates! game in 20 years)Performance-wise, it runs surprisingly well, though it doesn't really look super amazing (it doesn't look terrible either, just middle of the pack, really).For full price I'd say it's not really the best purchase you could make, but at 60% off, it's a pretty fun timewaster if you are into Age of Sail ships and don't mind fantastical elements and weird anachronisms.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy.This is a mediocre game littered with bugs. Was unable to customise my character's clothing or my ships for hours. Turned out that it was required that in order to do either of those things I had to install 3 sets of cannons on my Cutter ship. Had to be cannons, the different types of projectiles I added did not count at all. There was nothing that stated that I had to layout my Cutter ship that way to get these customisations, it happened out of pure chance and time. The game play is fine. It's nothing special at all, just very basic: drive ship, aim gun, shoot gun. The map is small, character movement looks and feels dodgy and you can't jump. The icons on the map do not tell you what things they are icons for they are just small icons on a map.There are game-breaking bugs that they clearly do not care about. While doing coop, my friend and I were battling an enemy group of ships then at the same time we both were flashed with the "out of bounds" message and then our crews revolted. We were not out of bound at all, we were to the west of the Spice Islands. Upon respawning, my ship wreckage was placed out of bounds, thousands of metres from where I had originally been overthrown. Because of this I was unable to get hours of loot back. Same thing happened to my friend. Refund and support request was denied.This game is not worth the money it costs to buy it. _childDocuments_.review: It's far from perfect, but I do enjoy it. And for anyone into sailing ships in a very arcady way, yet nice graphics and decent combat, this maybe a fun game for you.The bad; It lacks depth, but that's not to say there isn't progression that can be fun for the first 20 or 30 hours. After that, you're doing the same stuff over again to slowly grind materials to get the last little stats and bonuses out of your ships.End Game or lack thereof is also a disappointment. It's not to say there isn't one. But what you have is a grindy slow paced logistics management system. It's been made easier in Season 2. But it doesn't change how slow and honestly boring the gameplay is.There is hard bosses to kill, over and over again for chests and it can be fun, even more so in a group of players. Just after doing the same 10 or so boss ships becomes boring after awhile.So after that, why would I ever recommend this game? And that is a good question. I find enjoyment here, and I look forward to what may come to the game down the road.The Devs have been fairly responsive over the last 6 months, taking our feedback and helping things get better. With the launch of Season 3, I can feel the games UI is far better now for PC players. When navigating or using items, it feels less like a console port.The map is large, but with fast travel it becomes smaller quick. And we've had no increase in map size since launch. We also lack Large class of ships, which is a major bummer.Devs say they are working on them, But until we can have a Corvette or Frigate I don't think players will be happy.This is mostly a PVE game, with a opt in choice for open world PVP. However servers are small, and PVP activities aren't very exciting. So if you enjoy ships, and can play with friends or a group, I do think you'll have some fun here for a discount. With hope that Devs will keep listening to feedback and give us the stuff players are wanting.It's not a AAAA game, nor is it a AAA game. But it's not a "bad" game.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon clicking play, I waited around 5 minutes for the third-party Ubisoft launcher to load and update. Then I had to sign in, and it asked for a product key. After canceling out of that menu, I had to click play again. This time, the game launched after BattleEye loaded. I loaded into the game quickly after that, only to be met with an unskippable cutscene. I then had to agree to a "play nice, play fair, play safe" prompt, or else I couldn't play.I clicked play on the main menu and had to sit through another unskippable cutscene. I was having a somewhat good time destroying the small enemy ships, but then I ran into the bigger boss ship that was as spongy as a Division boss. I got 6 minutes of gameplay before another unskippable cutscene. Then I got the longest loading screen yet, which led to another cutscene. During this tutorial phase, pausing did not actually pause the game, but if you paused during a cutscene, that cutscene would pause.After that 4 and a half minute cutscene, I got to a character creator that was less interesting than the Division’s. Don’t worry, you can put facial hair on your female character (icky). At least I could skip the dialogue now. When I entered the social hub, the players running around were super buggy—floating and flying all over the place.After running around and skipping dialogue for about 6 minutes, I finally got to edit my ship after another loading screen.You can't name your ship "c0ck_cruncher," "weiner_eater," or "UbiRichardRider." "Muncher" is a banned word in general. I settled for "Richard_Sitter." I accidentally disembarked three times while trying to sail away and had to wait through agonizing loading screens. I was shocked when I realized my ship had a stamina bar.I attacked NPC ships and "boarded" them, which just triggered a loot-box-esque menu where I could choose what generic items to take. At one point, some dolphins jumped out of the water next to my ship, and I thought it was another ship firing at me—I’m not sure if it was a player, but I sank it anyway. This gave me a wanted level that seemed like it was trying to imitate GTA, but nothing happened, and it just went away after a while.I then sailed across the sea to a big X on the map, only to find out it was my marker that I didn’t realize I had set, and not treasure. This game is AAAA in name (and maybe in a graphical sense? I didn’t play with the settings turned up all the way) only.It makes sense why they heavily discounted it for its Steam release (where it should have released in the first place). I’m on the fence about refunding it, as I got a bit of dopamine from sinking ships (a single, measly drop of dopamine is all I need in life), although the sinking animation is the exact opposite of Sea of Thieves—lifeless and emotionless. But I wouldn’t pay full price for this game in a million years, let alone consider the premium edition.Pirates: The Legend of Black Kat from 2002 for the Original Xbox and PlayStation 2 is more of a AAAA game than this. Also, if you ever need to contact Ubi support for help with any issue, you’d get better assistance letting your cat lick you clean with its sandpaper tongue.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave long reviews, but this game deserves some discussion.I got this game when it was on sale for like $30. I had extremely low expectations because of the poor launch and the ridiculous claim that it's a AAAA game. So I went into it thinking it'd be trash. However, it's... good. Not great, there's problems with it, but -- I've put WAY more time into this game than I thought I would.The gameplay loop is essentially what others described: you accept quests from a "kingpin," you sail around the Indian Ocean and blow up enemy ships, and you pillage towns. You primarily play as the ship, which is customizable, unless you're walking around in a town or on an island, in which case you play as your character, the captain, who is also customizable. The end-game involves upgrading your ships, crafting powerful weapons, and managing your smuggling empire. It's a multiplayer game, and servers contain usually like 15-20 other players, which is enough to make it feel like other people are around but not too crowded.The good: I cannot put this game down. Doing the "world quests" with other players is so much fun. Making a healer build or a strong glass cannon DPS build feels extremely satisfying. Taking down one of the bosses with other players is just so fun. Managing and upgrading the empire keeps me coming back daily. I had such LOW expectations, it's been shocking to me how much fun I'm having. Will the fun run out? Maybe, but for now, I'm enjoying it. AND it's runs on SteamDeck, which is huge for me.The bad: Like I said, it runs on SteamDeck, but I do have to keep the settings at their lowest point, which sort of sucks. No problems at all with quick and easy 'login and play' through Steam. Occasional crashes, though, which may be related to SteamDeck performance limitations. Also, beware of FOMO on the Store.If you like Sea of Thieves, you'll like this.

_childDocuments_.review: IF YOU ARE IN EU I urge you to read and sign this petition to fix games like these: BRIEFLY: Arcade sailing from A to B and shooting mostly easy NPC ships (due to you being way above their level). Matchmaking for Coop NPCs is sometimes dead so don't always expect help fighting "bosses". PvP also if you want challenge. Game is still occasionally obstructively buggy, so not bad idea to wait for sale if you want a fully working game and your money's worth. Bugs / glitches (I've encountered) can be fixed by restarting the game (reconnecting to server). Sometimes servers go unavailable for a while too.If this sounds like fun, you can give it a go.It is clear to me why this game was made: because there are so many who remember Assassin's Creed III, IV (Black Flag) etc. and their sea battles and enjoyed them. It was something fresh over 10 years ago. So Ubisoft thinks, "how can we make more money with as much old code, and as little work, as possible". So they take a small part of the code, put some new paint on it, and try selling it as a NEW full AAAA game. And result is like Fallout 76 was when it launched, trying to sell same stuff again and again. There is no new real game here, it is only a part of the decade old Assassin's Creed recycled and re-painted. World takes 20 hours to explore. Endgame is grinding same bosses over and over again for currencies to buy captain clothes and ship cosmetics, but also unique better weapons, armor etc.At this point I cannot recommend the game to all, because I don't feel it has content nor the mechanics to make it worth 60 or even 24 euros. It is same old sea battle from Assassin's Creed we've seen for a decade. Just a new map, multiplayer battles, some dialogue and repetitive end-game quests to keep you sailing back and forth.FYI: All bad reviews out there are not real. They haven't even played the game really. I unlocked trophies in 5 hours 95% players haven't unlocked. Many do not really try the game or even give it a chance. Bad review, refund and out of sight, out of mind, feeling good for bullying Ubisoft.Frustrations:- Constant bugs occurring every few hours. Some forcing to abandon quests, relaunch game.- Stacking boss fights. Many quests go through boss fight areas so while going from A to B you'll be forced to possibly die from stacking enemy occurences: bad weather damage, bosses (sometimes even 2 main bosses simultaneously) and their spawns firing at you, pirates spawning to loot your Helm coveted cargo etc.- Bounty Board Contracts: you need to constantly go to one of two main cities to pickup Bounty Board Contracts to get all money and rewards from fighting bosses, because, irritatingly, these quests "fail" after some time if you haven't done them already.
