_childDocuments_.review: A fun representation of the famous Quidditch game from the Harry Potter books and films. The core gameplay is fun and addictive, with online matches with friends being a particular highlight. Some features of the original game have been tweaked, such as the golden snitch now only granting 30 points and not ending the game. Personally, I think this is a great move by the developers, as the snitch now functions as a small boost to a teams points rather than rendering the efforts of the chasers useless. The base game is good, but does leave the player wanting for further updates. I understand that there is planned future content coming (with the likes of 6v6 and holiday events) which should hopefully keep the game engaging. One update I would like to see is the inclusion of online teams which you can create/name with friends and climb a global leaderboard (this would make the game feel more competitive). Although fun, I do agree with the criticisms that Quidditch Champions is reminiscent of a mobile game, mainly due to the way you unlock and purchase skins etc. I do want to state that as of this review, there are no microtransactions - all upgrades and skins are unlocked and purchased through playing the game. In conclusion, at its core the game is fun (especially with friends), but is wanting for small bug-fixes and large updates to keep engagement and draw out the competitive nature of Quidditch.
_childDocuments_.name: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions

_childDocuments_.review: This review will stay negative until they add 6v6.This game has a lot of potential, and it feels real good to not have a game with microtransactions that I paid full price for. Unfortunately, I think it's safe for me to say that the 3v3 just ain't gonna work for your target audience (which i'm assuming is for a younger group considering the cartoony graphics), if you do plan to release a comp mode it would work better as a 6v6 so people can be focusing solely on their role of choice to benefit the team. Hopping between the two and letting the AI (which is braindead btw) take over the one you aren't currently on is just way to much to juggle. I don't know why this wasn't implemented on launch. From what I can see is that's one of the main points people make when they are leaving negative reviews and I must agree. There definitely is a skill gap though, and I won't speak to much on that because I haven't played enough. I appreciate all the tutorials for players who know nothing about quidditch but this current system may still be too intimidating for most new players. Please expedite the process of implementing that into the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I am so hooked on this game already. It's been out for three days and I've hardly put it down. It's a small game at the moment, but given that it literally just launched and there's more content on the way, I'm not too bothered about it.The rules aren't quite to the book, but only so that it's... you know, actually playable. The snitch is a huge benefit but no longer an insta-win, there's only one Beater, but otherwise everything else is pretty comparable.The singleplayer campaign is easy and once you get the hang of the game I find Champion (the highest difficulty) not terribly challenging, which is where PvP comes in.PvP is a tad rough at the moment -- there doesn't seem to be any sort of ranking in the teammaking system so a level 45 might end up on a team with two level 5s while the other team is all around the lvl25 mark. It can get a little frustrating to be on a team with people who are of a very different skill level to you, but hopefully it'll be tweaked in the coming months.I was concerned about the 3v3 system for PvP initially because nowhere really explains it well, but after playing the mode it's a lot better than I had anticipated. That said, I am super psyched for the coming 6v6 so we can pick one role to play the whole match.Beyond upgrading brooms (and there are only four upgrades per broom) the currency is all sort of useless at the moment, but as they add things to the market they'll get more useful.I'm not a sports person, but if this game had a spectator mode I would sink hours in just watching other teams play and being able to boo or cheer them on.All in all, I'm already immensely happy about this game and am very excited to see where it's headed.

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I was born in 2002 and I did not play QWC.  Will that bring in some generational hate for this review? Idk probably.  Personally I think this game is really good, I won’t be comparing it to anything so if you’re expecting that go away.  I like the art style but I could also see a more realistic art style going a long way, either way I don’t think it looks bad at all.  The voice acting is great as well.  As far as gameplay, I think it’s extremely fun and definitely captures the fast paced feeling of quidditch that you see in the movies.  There is a 3v3 PvP mode which means you have to switch between two roles, personally I don’t mind it but I can understand people frustration.  In the bright side, a 6v6 mode is on the roadmap for this game so that won’t be a problem in the long run.  Ultimately if you are a fan of Harry Potter and you want to experience fun and fast paced broom mechanics, I think it’s safe to say this is your game.  I do think watching the game and playing the game are two different things.  Try it out, if you hate it refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for a nostalgia hit, revisiting the fond memories you had of the classic PS2 era World Cup game? Sorry pal, this isn't it. This is FIFA on broomsticks, with none of the tight controls, cinematic flair, and charm of the original game. Problems I had:- the flying mechanics are loose and floaty, imprecise, and convoluted. Switching to roles like the Keeper also changes the inputs.- the game requires a WB account to even get into the main menu, its always online DRM that uses their cloud saves not steam's, and on reboot it forgot all the settings I'd adjusted including graphics, FPS limit, and inverted controls. - for singleplayer the game requires you to play as the whole team. Swapping between chasers is fairly familiar to any soccer game, but trying to manage being a chaser, beater, and keeper, and then also keep an eye on the snitch and being a seeker occasionally is awkward. It's not like the original where the focus was on being a chaser with bludgers being call-ins, and seeker's being the end-game phase. - the rules of the game were completely altered for "online balancing", with the snitch appearing on a timer for 30pts bonuses throughout the game, and catching it doesn't end the game. - The animations and stages have none of the cinematic flair of the original game; tackles don't feel punchy, there's no cinematic team power moves or special moves, the levels all feel very generic. - The UI is a cluttered mess. Even on a 144Hz oled with its lack of ghosting and crisp clear visuals that helps in FPS games... this UI design just became a blur for me. It was hard to make out friendly vs enemy players, icons for grabbing the ball were small and hard to see, its hard to work out how close you really are to anyone and how close you need to be, there's so many magical trails covering the screen especially when close to other players that its difficult to focusOverall, the original World Cup game was leagues better. Tight controls, cinematic flair, stuck true to the lore, and felt much more playable. I was deeply disappointed that this was not just a polished up evolution of that game I loved.

_childDocuments_.review: A fast paced, mostly fun quidditch game. Smooth and intuitive controls make for a non frustrating learning curve and offers some really intense thrills towards the end of matches.It's a little oversimplified version of quidditch but the 7 minutes or 100 points works pretty well for this format.On the other hand there is a noticeable lack of consequences / weight to every action and score, especially due the absence of penalties. The game feels almost too focused on functionning as a pure esports offering and not working as a functional fictional sport. Features a welcomed but totally unremarkable quidditch world cup campaign / solo mode but the game doesn't offer a lot of gameplay content besides multiplayer. Very repetitive presentation as of now, from arenas to commentary to player equipment / cosmetics although the absence of micro transactions is refreshing and very heartwarming in 2024. Overall, it behaves quite well as an esport wannabe game even though it still feels really early in its growth.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so torn on this because I like the game, but I don't know if I can recommend someone pick it up at full price. I'm only 5 hours in and i've beaten all the cups on the hardest difficulty and there isnt a ton that the game has to offer. I'm not a huge fan of micro transactions but I feel that this game would have been better off as a free to play game with cosmetics you can earn and buy. I feel like they should have looked at league or Dota and taken some inspiration from them. There should be a ranked mode for people to grind and want to come back, and they should have made their money through cosmetics. I hate that the game is 3v3, i feel like that had changed during play testing and I personally dont like it. I wish that the boarder for the pitch was a little larger, I feel like when your going after the snitch you are just constantly hitting the border. I dont like that you have to customize 6 different characters, I would be more invested if I got to choose a role and just play as my personal character. I do like the art style, i dont think it'll be for everyone but I dont mind it. Mechanically the game is very simple to pick up and play. And I like that its a quidditch game, i've missed playing Quidditch World Cup and this scratches that itch. This is a fine game that could have and possibly should have been included in Legacy or been a DLC for it. As a stand alone game I'd say to maybe hold off until it's on sale or temper your expectations. I'd say at launch its a solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed playing Harry Potter Quidditch Champions! The game offers tons to grind, and I love that everything is free — you don't have to spend any money to enjoy the full experience. If you miss a season pass or just don't have time to play as much, you can still purchase previous season rewards with in-game currency in the following season, which is a fantastic feature.Personally, I'd love to see a more complex ranked mode, something similar to Rocket League’s ranking system, to give the competitive aspect a bit more depth. At launch, there were quite a few bugs and glitches, but they were addressed pretty quickly, and it’s easy to keep up with updates on the official Discord. It’s a nice touch that you can sometimes even chat directly with the devs there. The new 6v6 mode is a brilliant addition — for me, it’s actually more fun than the 3v3 mode! The only thing that frustrates me isn't the game itself but some of the community: many players don’t pass the Quaffle and tend to try to do everything solo, which can lead to unnecessary losses. But overall, this is a fantastic game, especially for fans of the Harry Potter universe. It's a blast to play, even after many hours, and offers a ton of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: If you come here expecting it to be like the Harry Potter Quidditch World Cup game from 2003 with better graphics, then curb your expectations. It is not. The single-player aspects are just....similar. I think if you like Harry Potter Quidditch, online competitive games, and sports games like FIFA, then you'll probably like this game. Of the things I listed, I only like one of those aspects, the quidditch. Not a big fan of online competitive games in general so I was disappointed by the heavy focus on that. The daily and weekly challenges, while fun for now, will become a chore later, coming from personal experiences. Not sure how long I'll keep playing this after beating the single-player stuff. Also, be prepared to make a WB Games account and HP Fan Club account and tie those to Steam if you want to get access to all of the cosmetics, another aspect I'm not fond of. I wish they allowed for a full 7-man team queue for online so everyone can focus on their roles, but it's currently a 3-man team where each player controls 2 roles. Losing because you have to keep juggle between Chaser-Keeper or Chaser-Beater is disheartening. There are ways to give each role more to do... Did I mention there's only 1 Beater per team? But since it's not a big role, I guess they felt there's only need for 1. I understand the rule changes to Quidditch to make it balance for online play, but it's not really the Quidditch you know and love from the series. I guess 1 change I like is that the snitch is worth a lot less (30 pts) and catching it doesn't end the match. It's first to 100 points. Lastly, mobile game level graphics. I don't care too much graphics so it doesn't bother me as much but if you do care, you should know. At least it's easy to run. No Microtransactions at least....for now. Update after a server disconnect, you need to be online just to play the single player parts. That's a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having fun and I'm pretty sure I'll keep having fun. It's not full OG Quidditch rules, however I'm sure they have put a good amount of thought into it and this is what they came up with.I should mention that I am not too much of a Harry Potter fan. Even since the Quidditch mode of Chamber of Secrets on the Gamecube I have been basically waiting for something like this.Of course these are my subjective Pros/Cons.Pros:- Personally I love the visual style- Nice music- Very good performance - So far every ingame purchase can be done using with ingame currency you gain- Fair implementation of the roles, I imagine this will be similar to games like Rocket League where you have a low amount of base mechanics, but people will find a way to play crazy (waiting for ceiling flip reset shots lol)- Match length feels good- players seem to be teamplayers I didn't encounter anyone that didn't pass me the ball- not too complex, but influencing skill system, including different brooms with different ability scores, I have some builds for different roles now and they feel like great improvements to my playstylesNeutral:- I had a bug where the wrong controller layout was shown I don't know if it's due to Steam input or if the game did it, but it made my tutorial almost worthless - With the battle pass I am worried about possible micro transactions in the future- Queue times for seekers are pretty long by now- Match Making for me got better, but can still be a bit random with who you're matched with, most matches are close matches for me thoCons:- Audio design could be better, some sounds cut in which makes it sound kinda cheap sometimes- Commentators definitely need more lines and enthusiasm, they sound like they'll fall asleep while commenting lol- I have now finished the... let's call it "Campaign". You play a few cups against bots only and I don't know who designed the difficulties, but there was no match I didn't win 100:0 even on the highest possible difficulty. I wish it was actually harder. The cutscenes for winning the cups are also disappointing 5-10 second videos with almost nothing to show unfortunately- bot players, but the 6v6 is on it's way if we can believe the roadmapUPDATE AFTER 17+ hours:I actually enjoy it even more. The game reminds me of the early days of Rocket League, where everyone was just playing and learning the game, getting better and better, finding out new mechanics etc. I personally don't care about battle passes, rewards or anything else. I'm just here to have fun and that is what works out for me. Most cons are even basically nitpicking, since they don't really influence the gameplay itself.The roadmap shows the wanted 6vs6 in development and an upcoming Season 1, I'm eager to see what's to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Over 20 years of waiting for the next Quidditch game and here it finally is. And it is good.+ The most important thing: the game is just . It's Rocket League on brooms. The gameplay is very fast-paced, smooth and fluid. Flying feels good, scoring goals feels amazing. Each role is different and rewarding in its own different way when you do well.+ You can customize each of your characters.+ You can advance in the game by playing both PvP and PvE, whichever you prefer.- A bunch of mostly minor bugs that will hopefully soon be fixed. Things like some achievements not counting, some changes in the settings resetting when relaunching the game etc.- The main mode is great, but there is room for some more content and modes, like 1v1s and private matches. _childDocuments_.review: This game has lots of potential. Do I agree with the sentiment that the snitch got "nerfed"? It's a hard no. Take this game at face value, and don't compare it to QWC.  That was decades ago, and the skill cap was very low back then.  The mechanics in this game are unique, and although not perfect in more than one way, can definitely be addressed. Pros: Customization is as on point as Hogwart's Legacy Graphics and rendering is solid; I would argue that I have a mid-tier build, but can comfortably run this game on Ultra Settings There are actual roles in this game, and you're free to chose whichever one you'd like to play. Sure you may be limited, but there really are just three roles. In game currency being the only source to buy customization.Cons: Someone said it before, and I agree, switching positions can sometimes become disorienting, The seeker role is also a bit disorienting since the snitch is insanely erratic, and cornering at both ends of the fields are not properly supported by the drifting mechanic.  Yes, the skill gap does get lower the more you upgrade your seeker skills. The keeper mechanics are not terrible by any means, but can use a little bit of work.Overall, this game plays well, and fairly well.  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up playing the Original Harry Potter QWC, this one surely seems to elevate the original's quirks and provides you a smooth traversal on the broom with better graphics and online multiplayer capabalities. _childDocuments_.name: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with the game, gives me that "just one more match" feeling every time I consider giving it a rest.The 3v3 multiplayer is really nice tbh, Just the fact that I don't get stuck as one single position and can switch to another, Like being chaser to help my mates score but then switch to beater(my favourite position so far!) to help defend, or even to knock out the opponents keeper for easy goals for a short while, and occasionally  chasing the opponent seeker with my bludgers to give my own an advantage. I've also seen teammates change to keeper on defense to great effect, then back to chaser on offence.I see a lot of people complaining about "having" to change positions... You don't HAVE to, but strategically speaking it's good to have the option to change to a more specialised position to give your team an advantage. That said I wouldn't mind an extra game mode for 1v1 and even 6v6, though I'm definitely loving the 3v3.I do feel a bit let down by the single player experience, thought it would be more interesting (along the lines of Fifa's career mode or something), instead it's just 4 short tournaments and that's it.The game runs smooth on max settings, had a couple crashes in the first few hours of release but that was it, no crash or noticeable bug yet since then. Annoying that I need an internet connection for single player stuff though. And of course... NO MICRO-TRANSACTIONS!!! It's been said and celebrated over and over, but it's never enough! A multiplayer game with customisation and no cash grab schemes? Bloody miracle!Ps: I do not agree or condone JKR's views, and even though it's all connected in one way or another, I prefer to keep politics separate from my gaming hobby

_childDocuments_.review: Very objectively it is what is advertised, a Quidditch game. Albeit with some changes to the OG rules, which make sense, if you think about it. (The game instead of ending with catching the Snitch and winning 150 points, it ends with the first team that reaches 100, catching the Snitch earns the team 30 points and resets the Quaffle at the center of the field. And instead of having 7 players, there are 6. There is only one Beater instead of the original 2).There are 4 game modes: Campaign, Multiplayer, Exhibition and Practice. Exhibition is just a quick local match, Campaign you can do solo or co-op. Where you control one position, but can change between all 6. Each position feels unique and quite satisfying, again just what one would expect of a Quidditch game. Campaign is also divided into 4 different ones. Weasley-, Hogwarts-, Triwizard- and World cup, each with 5 different difficulty levels. All start with some qualifier matches and then a bracket. Multiplayer mode, seems to be the main focus of the game, which imo makes sense (although I do hope they continue to add single player content in the future). Matches here at their current state are 3+3bots vs 3+3bots. Where a player in each team controls two positions. One Chaser (always) and either a Keeper, a Beater or a Seeker (my favorite). It's and interesting choice that, personally works well, involves quite a bit of strategy. You have to think and manage when to score points with the Quaffer, beat other players, defend or go after the Snitch. A game lasts for 7 minutes in total, and initially you focus on scoring points with the Quaffer, until the snitch is available, which is when you would switch to the Seeker and try and catch it to earn 30 points. Graphics are stylized, look good and work well for a multiplayer game (I imagine more realistic ones would have inherent costs to performance, which could hinder the multiplayer experience). To me they are reminiscent of panini sticker drawings when the first movie came out back in early 2000s. There is a season battle pass and a shop that uses in game currency. You can't buy this currency, this currency is obtain by completing daily, weekly and what they call career challenges, that can also earn you new cosmetics and Harry Potter characters. So if you purchase the game you end up having to play to earn these cosmetics items.You can edit the look of each position. You can edit basic physical aspects of the character, clothing (hat, glasses, body wear), emotes, wands, victory celebration, scoring vfx and the broom. The broom can be upgraded with points that you earn from completing challenges and leveling up your account. Each position has a "skill tree" where a maximum of ten points can be invested, so you can adapt the character to which ever style of play you prefer. To be honest I would have preferred the game to be free to play and then buying a battle pass for a moderate fee, with some cosmetic packs in shop (like for example for Hogwarts houses), just so there would be a chance to have more players. But this also works, since I have everything available (probably for a lesser fee than I would have if it were f2p) as long as I keep playing the game.All in all, the game is really fun, and I believe it is a good adaptation of Quidditch. And it does kill that little bug that I had for quite a while. (It's been 21 year more or less since the last game.)To those that say this should have been a dlc for Hogwarts Legacy: yeah I thought so as well when that game came out. That would have made sense if the goal was just to have a single player experience. But clearly the goal of this game is to have a multiplayer experience, and for that reason it wouldn't have made sense to download a 100gb game just to play Quidditch. So a standalone version is ideal.And to those that say 2003 was better here is a link to a youtube video showing the two: Being nostalgic is nice and all, but let's be real. There is no comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions is a high flying action packed sports game that is a wicked good time. I have always wanted to play a Quidditch game and this game is a delight to play and well worth the long wait. The game is very easy to pick up and learn while still having depth and giving you a lot to master. The controls are smooth and responsive which helps tight maneuvering around the pitch. The game is played 3 v 3 (6 v 6 with the included AI) and all of the four classes are fun to play. I enjoyed playing as the Keeper as it was the less picked class but also had a big role in the outcome of the match. Also playing as a Chaser is really fun when you are making a crazy winding run to the goal with the quaffle and having the entire opposing team chasing and breathing down your neck, its exhilarating and quite the adrenaline rush. Quidditch is competitive and fast paced, matches can last up to 7 minutes but usually end sooner. The graphics are on the cartoon side but they are charming none the less. There are currently 6 map locations which are unique and all look good however they could add more objects to the background and maps to bring them more to life. There is nice depth to the character customization and there are a ton of cosmetics to collect and apply to personalize your character. The in game currency you are awarded for completing matches is generous and there are many cool items you can unlock in the store as well. There isn't much of a story and its short but that is expected for a sports game. Also the AI on the hardest setting isn't very difficult. All of the classes can be upgraded which greatly enhances your performances and gives you added skills. In the story you have the freedom to switch between all of the classes on the fly while when playing online you are restricted to two classes. There is a lack in variety of game modes currently. A handful of extra game types would really help spice up the game play. However even with the lack of diversity there is still replay value and even more so when playing with friends. I did not encounter many bugs playing the game which was nice to see at launch. At times when things got really hectic there was a bit of lag and sometimes when switching back and forth between the classes the game would glitch a little, however these were minor issues. Overall I had a blast playing Quidditch Champions. The issues with the game are minor when compared to the magical moments you can create when playing. The concept is truly awesome and well executed. Even if you are not a Sports fan or a Harry Potter fan I would still recommend this game as its just pure fun.

_childDocuments_.review: SO! It's finally here. Before I start my review, I wanna touch on a few things. Firstly, these are my first thoughts. I've not played pvp, and have been mostly just playing the career mode. Second, there is a certain review that should honestly just be ignored, because the person only bought the game to leave a bad review, and they called Rowling, who has nothing to do with this game a "Terf" Kinda wish people would just get over it and not be so pathetic. But seeing that the review seems to be gone. Is what it is. Just remember that JKR Had nothing to do with this game.Alright, onto the review. I will edit this later to add more things when I experience the game more, but firstly let's start with the good. The game is beautiful, and while I'm not too big of a fan of the characters looks. The stadiums I have seen look amazing. I do like the art style, just not for the characters (I will get to them)Next I was seriously surprised with Beater. Idk what it is, but there is something sooo.. Satisfying about knocking people off their brooms and smacking them with the stick. I found myself having a ton of fun with it. Beater honestly surprised me. Chaser is also pretty fun to play, but tbh that was a given. It's kinda the main role in Quidditch. Flying feels great on mouse and keyboard, I haven't exactly tried controller as of yet, but it does feel pretty good. And so far, the career mode has been pretty good. It honestly feels kinda like QWC (Quidditch World Cup) but with some major changes such as the fact that you can actually play all the roles instead of just being stuck as Chaser (For the most part) and hitting buttons to summon Buldgers and well QWC never really let you play as Keeper. And yes I am a Huge fan of QWC and I saw a person mention in their review saying "This game isn't for QWC players" which tbh is both true and not in my opinion. This game does feel like the successor to QWC, to a point. I feel like those who have played QWC will enjoy the career mode.I will also say that being able to create your own OC's and play as them is something I like. However Character creation is a bad for me. See below. Another good thing is that the devs are taking in feedback from play testers and players. And this game has a ton of potential if done correctly, And one could even do tournaments or (In my case) use the game for RP reasons. Now for the bad.. and these are things I feel could be improved on, or I just do not like. To start, I feel like Character creation is very limited. There are only a few face options, hair color options, and even hair options in general. Now I am not asking for 100 hair styles or anything like that. I'm just saying it feels.. limited. The hair colors are kinda a disappointment, Specially for a game based in the HP Universe. And some of the faces just look ugly. Then there are the pronouns, and I've seen people whine about them. I legit just kinda rolled my eyes, shrugged, picked one and moved on. It's not a bad, but it did seem unnecessary. Keeping with the bad.. You can't name ANY of your OC's.. and that's a HUGE Disappointment for me. Specially since I love creating characters. I'm hoping we get a patch where we get more customization's, even just a few more hairstyles and faces would make me more happy. But character customization is a bit disappointing for me.Next well. I'm gonna be brutally honest. Seeker and Keeper are horrible. Keeper from what I've played just feels clunky and underpowered. Maybe I am just bad, but still it's disappointing. And seeker, a role I was gonna play is basically a waiting game and pretty much if you've played the older HP games (Chamber of Secrets on ps2) it's basically THAT mini game with some added tweeks. And speaking of Seeker.. The game does break established lore by making games only go up to 100 points, and the snitch is heavily nerfed. Only 30 points and the game continues. Now I get why they made this change, It's a game. And if they had remained the same I feel like people could abuse it, and it would make more people leave games. But not even having options for it is.. just another disappointment.And of course.. There is the fact that Multiplayer is 3v3 with bots. Everyone has talked about it and commented about it. and while we are getting 6v6 in the future, it's still a little frustrating. And I get why people who have play tested this game are super frustrated. but the devs are listening to feed back. Which is a good thing. But we have to see more. And on a final note. The game is repetitive. I can see people grabbing the game, playing it for a while and getting bored. You do gotta grind stuff in the game which isn't hard but I'm not the type who enjoys grinding stuff for hours. There's also the issue of the game being a live service game, soo if the game dies and servers get shut off. You are out of luck. I personally wish games would just make Live service an option instead of forcing it. But what can you do.In conclusion. As a huge HP fan, I think the game is good, but it's not great. It has a ton of potential, but with 6v6 coming who knows when, gameplay being kinda repetitive, and 2 out of the 4 roles just being meh. I'd give it a 6/10. It's good. Just not great. If you are a huge HP fan like me, grab it. Otherwise I'd say wait for a sale. and to be honest. I do think the game is worth it's price tag. It's not like it's a 70$ AAA game. Honestly? Just have fun with it!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and runs well, and being able to swap between players adds a fun complexity to the matches. My only issue is (and it's not just this game but ALL live service games) forced PVP. There is no shop for real money which is AMAZING, and you earn in game currency just by playing, but in instances like the current Legacy event you have to play 50 PVP matches to earn keys. So far 80% of my PVP experience has been a laggy mess making me not want to work towards the event rewards (Aside from the legacy characters which can be done in PVE and its obviously the high selling point) BUT The character's in the vault art 250 keys per bundle and you are limited keys per day. Now i get its a live service and you need to incentivize players to play PVP to keep the servers healthy but me having a mainly PVP background has completely dropped PVP all together a year ago due to sweaty players and the unfair advantages that come with Online play, and honestly i am a casual when it comes to games outside of fps/rpg's and me being a huge harry potter fan i wanted to be able to hop in a just have fun. This game DOES provide that, for me it's just having that feeling of missing out because i dread playing PVP especially in a game that requires prompt timing to dodge or tackle but most of the time i don't even get a prompt to tackle or dodge and will even go to score a goal with no one guarding the goal and the game tells me my shot was blocked when no one is even there. Another example is playing as a BEATER there are times when i try to throw the ball and it will either not throw or i don't get the prompt. When i can hop on and just play with the little time i have I LOVE this game but with this current event i more then likely will not bother aside from the characters. I neither have the time or patience to run 50 games where i'm stuck just sitting there and trying to not get kicked. ALSO if plenty of people leave the game it kicks anyone else out and if you are trying to complete games you gain no progress. I gave up on doing PVP weekly's during the week of launch because i had to practically double to amount of games just to finish it because every other game people left. Conclusion: If the devs could add an alternate challenge to earn the same rewards this game would be a 9/10 for me as of now though i would rate this game a 7/10 ultimately the PVP drags this game down. _childDocuments_.review: This game had the potential to be amazing, but the devs chose not to go that route. Instead, they decided to make it intentionally bad. The production quality shows tremendously in this game, and while I was a playtester in the game for over 250 hours + whatever you may now see on steam here, and I loved and supported this game, I have to be honest and write a clear and true review. TLDR will be posted at the end:Bugs - This game released in what honestly looks like a Beta or even Alpha state. Bugs that should never, EVER make it to a release copy of the game are present, and I promise you with as frequent as they are, it is not because they weren't aware. It's a complete disregard or interest for polishing the game. I've got a very, very long list but let me emphasize the most pressing ones: 1.) Matchmaking is broken. Sometimes you queue into 1v3 games. Sometimes your own party members get put on the opposing team. Sometimes their 3v3 mode accidentally puts more players on the team than intended and it can turn into a 4v2 or a 5v1. Beyond that, even getting a working party can at times be a challenge because the party screen likes to break and not permit people to be invited at times. 2.) The game resets, on repeat, all your audio settings whenever it restarts. 3.) Desync is unreasonably bad, making quaffle throws sometimes nonsensical, making seeker fights sometimes feel like a ping war, and making keeper saves sometimes get reconned. A title like this should not struggle to get the simple part of networking right.Time Wasters - This game has a tutorial that, if you actually go through it, takes WAY longer than necessary. Arguably by the time you get past the game's opening cutscenes, finish the tutorial, and complete your first real PvP game or even the first couple aspects of the SP game, you've burned through your refund timer. This seems pretty intentional, honestly. It's beyond obvious that the tutorial had no business being as long as it was, and it seems to me like its only purpose is to secure the purchase, not teach the player. Moreover to this point, it does not even go over core game mechanics for all roles, which is baffling since the most important mechanics in the whole game are never once discussed (such as the Seeker's ability to bump). This includes how the skill trees and broom stats function, which means you waste more time trying to figure that out, which funnels back to my original point.Stats - The skills and broom stats are VASTLY overtuned. You'll notice this immediately if you queue into anyone who already has points unlocked or a leveled broom. I comprehend that some games include this mechanic to enhance your skills as you play, but that is NOT what this does. Rather, a player with full skill points and a leveled broom (or heck, even only half that) will absolutely decimate a player without these unlocked. If I hadn't been part of the playtest to know that things get worse before they get better, I would have probably quit the game long before I leveled everything simply do to how insanely OP these are and how it basically makes what could be a balanced game into what amounts to free farm for higher tier players so that they don't get bored and quit immediately.Gameplay - Realistically, every role feels frustrating to play, and it doesn't have to. They should rename this to "Harry Potter: Quidditch Brawlers" because half the gameplay loop is just trying to spam-knockout your opponents and keep them from being allowed to play the game. This is especially bad for Seekers because, except for during their minigame for snitch-catching, they are locked to only 1 character at a time as opposed to other players that have 2. This means a seeker main might spend *literally more than half the game unconscious and not playing the game!!!* For specific roles though:Seeker - Your purpose is to be a punching bag. Every role in the game, even the opposing seeker, can hurt you. Which means you can be stunlocked and knocked out on repeat, if they so choose. And they choose, because the game is so unreasonably unbalanced that a double snitch catch (which is 60 out of the 100 points to autoend the game) invalidates the chaser entirely.Chaser - You want to score goals? Nah. Seeker wins the game because they score at such a rate that if you're playing against a competent team, the chaser score will NEVER decide the outcome of the game. Your purpose is to be a second, more valuable beater, because you can level stats in dealing damage and help stop the seeker from playing the game.Keeper - Enjoy not stopping quaffles, because that's not your role. This role is unbelievably nerfed and cannot reasonably win a 1v1 with a chaser, all things being equal. Your main purpose is to focus on kicking the seeker when they come by your end of the field, OR switch to chaser because that position actually means something.Beater - You're literal purpose is knocking players out, but chasers can arguably do that just as well. Yes, you deal more damage, and you have access to a bludger, but the bludger is easily dodge-able. You're better off staying Chaser most of the time so you can participate in the quaffle battle while also doing normal beater tasksBots - The AI is awful. I've seen better AI for games written by elementary schoolers who are learning rudimentary C++ for the first time. Keepers almost intentionally dodge the quaffle to permit scoring, and there are exploits that let you drag them away from the hoops so they become completely negated. Also, the keeper bot auto-passes to the closest player, even enemies. Chasers only sometimes pass when requested, fly in straight lines, and shoot in easy-to-predict ways so a chaser bot getting the quaffle helps the opposing team more than your own. Other bots simply are seemingly unable to dodge, so if you don't swap to them, the opposing team will just spam-knockout them when you aren't looking to gain an advantage over you. The only advantage to the bots in any way is that the Seeker bot can find the snitch in record time because #BotsCheat so there's no point in swapping to the "Seeker" until the snitch is found... its more of a "Chaser" than the actual chasers are. The only real reason to swap to the bot is to prevent the other team from knocking them out.Skill in Game - With most games, they start off rough and get better as you play. Not with this one. You go from being sad and 100-0'd by teams that are better, to learning how to play and realizing that the key to winning is mostly making your opponents rage and exploiting the game (Especially the forced-AI bots). If I wanted that, I'd go play League of Legends. As it stands, no role feels fun to play at higher levels except maybe chaser, and even that is a bit of a stretch.Future Promises & 6v6 PvP - The devs HAVE publicly stated that they intend to release a 6v6 all-player PvP mode, but that's not in the game at this time. There are also no custom matches, so you cannot play against friends (unless the match maker breaks and puts them on the other team!). There is no "All" chat, there is no Ranked mode, and there is no publicly visible MMR system. There is no world in which a competitive league can thrive under this environment, making this a purely-casual game until further notice. TLDR: I really, truly want to be clear that I loved this game. I looked forward to this game for over a year. I praised the devs and preordered the game and helped structure a competitive league (that was rendered mostly irrelevant) for the game in the time leading up to release. This review isn't just me lambasting a game that I feel stole my money. It's me spilling my heartbreak over a game that could've been so much better. Do yourself a favor: Don't buy it unless they completely overhaul it. I will update my review should any of this change, but my hopes continue to be thrown out the window by Unbroken and WB.

_childDocuments_.review: This really does feel like it should have been part of Legacy. It's just too small to feel like a full game, and with no real end goal minus progressing challenges for rewards. It would have had a much bigger impact as part of a larger storyline.That said, it is fun, at least for now. Going at this as a fully solo player, the AI isn't terrible. They have slightly changed the rules from the books/movie, However it isn't really a bad change, more one to make it work as a video game.You get the option to play as each position which you can switch between on the fly. There are options (On by default) to switch automatically as you pass the ball.  You can also switch to a teammate in your direct view with a key press. Or the default menu which allows a quick cycle between all of your team.Chasers - You'll spend time wishing the AI didn't seem faster. Your goal is to move the ball and score. Passes are pretty simple. As is dodging  bludgers (via a handy prompt) , not so much other people but you quickly find easy ways to confuse the ai and move downfield un-touched.Beater - Yep. Only 1. You can summon your bludger and then toss it at the other team to a)Knock the ball loose, or b) just do some damage. Enough damage and the person will fall off their broom.Keeper - As you'd expect. Stop the ball from entering the goal. AI does a fantastic job on it's own so it's the position I've played the least. It's rare that I even switch as the opponent is getting ready to take a shot.Seeker - This has the largest change. Your seeker will only pop up when the snitch is on the field. You'll want to quickly swap over and start hunting. It's not hard to spot as it makes a rather large golden sparkle cluster. Once it's spotted you'll chase after it. Staying close to it fills it's meter and it will spawn rings you'll want to fly through to keep your boost meter up. once it's full you can attempt a grab for a massive 30pts. (No instant wins here, sorry.) Then the players will reset and the game will move on.All in all it's not a terrible game. I should also point out, ZERO Micro Transactions (Even if the game feels like it was set up for some, they never made it in the game) you CANNOT purchase any type of currency, it's all earned via playing the game, completing daily, weekly, seasonal challenges. This currency will spend in the market for cosmetic unlocks (Outfits, Characters, Brooms, Broom Trails, Wands (For some odd reason), emotes, etc. So yeah, not terrible, but doesn't feel worth 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: The game stands out for its simple and accessible design. You don't need a high-end gaming PC to run it smoothly, which is a big plus, making it enjoyable for both hardcore and casual players.The controls are intuitive and easy to understand. It doesn’t take long to get comfortable with the game, making the initial experience very smooth. However, the leveling system is a bit of a drawback. The experience points (XP) are so low that it feels like you have to grind for days to make any real progress. This wouldn't be as frustrating if the rewards were worth it, but unfortunately, they aren't very motivating.Although the player base has noticeably shrunk, there are still no major issues when searching for multiplayer matches. The overall multiplayer experience remains intact, and playing with friends makes it even more enjoyable.All in all, it's a very good game with a lot of potential. With better adjustments to the leveling system, more rewarding incentives, and additional content, it could be even more successful. We'll have to see what the future holds, but for now, my friend and I are having more fun with it every day.

_childDocuments_.review: This game proves beyond a shadow of a doubt that there is a lot of toxicity to be found in the Harry Potter community. There are players who will praise this product to heaven and back without even knowing what the actual game is like. On the other hand, there are players who will claim this product is designed with the sole purpose of scamming Harry Potter fans with the promise of a good game. And in all that chaos and toxicity, it's difficult to have a nuanced discussion regarding what's good or bad about the game.Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions does things that no game before has done. It offers 4 singleplayer campaigns: the burrow cup (tutorial), the hogwarts house cup, the triwizard cup (between hogwarts, durmstrang and beauxbatons) and the world cup (with the possibility to play as any of 16 countries). It offers an online multiplayer mode (3v3 + bots), there's plenty of possibilities for character customisation and there's a wide range of in-game challenges.With that said, the game has a long way to go as well. There's numerous bugs, some even game-breaking. A 6v6 mode (without bots) has been announced, but has not yet been released. There's a lot more possibilities when it comes to customisation, there could be more maps in a wide variety of interesting locations and the devs may need to take a look at the keeper position, which currently seems to be rather unpopular due to its restricted range of possibilities. Lastly, the devs may need to be more clear and more communicative towards their passionate playerbase, as concerns over longevity of the game have been up in the air for a while now.That is, in my own humble opinion, the good and the bad that comes with this game. I hope that if you're reading this, at this point you will have a clear view of whether you'd like to buy this game or not, based on the information given thus far. Personally I have made the decision to buy it, because I'm a big Harry Potter fan. I've had a lot of fun with the game so far, and I believe I will have even more fun with the game in months to come, given the devs do their utmost to truly make this game as amazing as it has the potential to be.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. I'm a massive Harry Potter fan so I've mostly enjoyed it, but it needs more. I would say if you're not a Harry Potter fan, or a fan of Quidditch, don't bother.Campaign is fine, AI could be better but not terrible. You get to play a campaign at the Weasley's house (basically just the tutorial), one at Hogwarts between the school Houses, one between Hogwarts, Durmstrang and Beauxbatons (Triwizard Quidditch tourney), and the Quidditch World Cup where you can choose one of a bunch of countries. Like I said, it's fine, still relatively easy on the harder difficulties but it's pretty fun if you're a Quidditch fan. Not a ton of replay value though.Multiplayer has a ton of potential, and I think is where the game could have a future. Right now it's 3v3, each player controls two players. You always play as a seeker, and can also play as a beater/seeker/keeper. I understand they did this probably for server issues. The way it's implemented now is good enough, but man, if they implemented a full 6v6 mode (or maybe 5v5 and just have AI keepers) where you just play as one position, this game would be a blast. But right now PVP is easily the best part of the game, there is some skill gap and the different positions are pretty fun to play (besides keeper).Overall 7.5/10 because I'm a huge HP fan, if you're not a big fan it's probably lower.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for 13 hours so far, and overall feel I can recommend it! If you are a Harry Potter fan, fan of the 2003 Quidditch game, or want a competitive Quidditch experience that gives Rocket League vibes, this is the game for you. Some say the game is not worth the $30 price tag, which I was worried about going into it, but I strongly disagree. If you purchased Rocket League when it was for sale and you felt it was worth it, then this game will also be worth it from a perspective of what the game offers. You have single player with the various cups, each with a handful of unlockable cosmetics. As it has been emphasized, there are no micro-transactions, and aside from the season pass and the vault unlockables, all items and cosmetics can be obtained without it feeling grindy. Single player has been a good experience for getting used to the game and improving in a risk-free environment, but multiplayer is where this game shines.While the connection quality has not been perfect, I find 90% of my games play nearly perfectly, while occasionally I will experience lag followed by a crash. However, you do NOT receive any penalties for the game crashing, and since the games are short in duration, I never feel like my time is wasted. The developers are also listening to players, with a roadmap including events and adding 6v6, as many players have been desiring. I personally enjoy 3v3, as the roles of keeper and seeker are not full-time roles, so it allows me to play more flexibly. We will see how 6v6 goes though! I am sure I will enjoy it as well. At first I felt the game was a bit too fast and chaotic, but I learned I was the problem. This is a competitive game where people play very aggressively, and the coordination of a team really determines how the game feels. If beaters ignore the seeker and just sit targeting the keeper, the snitch is gone. If beaters are allowed to beat up on the keeper, goals are free for the enemy. Coordination is necessary, and luckily the more I have played the more I have realized verbal communication is not essential as long as you are paying attention to the field and your teammates. One fixable caveat: controls. Play with the control schemes, see what feels most natural, and what makes sense to you. I thought the controls were pretty good at the beginning, but after adjusting them for my own comfort, everything feels great. The expectations for video games nowadays is sky-high regardless of the price. I am nowhere near bored or burnt out from the game, and am excited to see what they continue to add going forward. Because of the niche audience this game is for, I believe the developers will continue to listen to player feedback and provide the best experience possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions is a sports video game set in the Wizarding World based on the fictional Quidditch game. It allows players to create their own unique Quidditch player and choose a specific position: Chaser, Seeker, Beater, or Keeper. Each position has its own unique skills and responsibilities, ensuring a diverse and strategic gameplay experience.Quidditch is a magical sport played by witches and wizards in the Harry Potter series. It takes place on a flying field, with players riding broomsticks. The game involves three types of goals, each worth 10 points: the hoops, the quaffle, and the snitch.Chasers are responsible for scoring goals by throwing the quaffle through the hoops.- Keepers defend their team's hoops.- Beaters use bats to hit Bludgers, magical balls that aim to knock players off their broomsticks.- Seekers search for the Snitch, a small golden ball worth 150 points. The first team to catch the Snitch wins the game.Harry Potter: Quidditch Champions features a variety of modes, including single-player campaigns, multiplayer matches, and challenges. Players can compete against friends or AI opponents in thrilling Quidditch matches, showcasing their skills and strategies. As they progress, they can unlock new spells, broomsticks, and customization options, further enhancing their game-play experience.--------------------------I fully recommend this game for any fan of the Harry Potter series.

_childDocuments_.review: After an hour of play, I gave it a positive review, wanting to be an ambassador of sorts for those who hesitate to buy it or are put off by the reviews focused on JKR hate or the need for a WB account.However, after two and a half hours, having completed two PvE cups and played a dozen PvP matches, I have to change my stance and give this game a hard no, unfortunately. The FIFA + Rocket League formula sounds exciting on paper but proves to be really broken or underdeveloped or both. Only two out of four roles are actually playable, and even then, they feel laborious. You end up doing the same thing over and over. PvP offers some excitement, yes, but PvE is just atrocious. WB marketed this as PvE-friendly, but in reality, the "campaign" is just an extended tutorial that can be completed in a couple of hours. It feels like I keep saying this about a lot of games these days, but this project, at this point, is a solid proof of concept and nothing more. And I will treat it as such. I won't return it, but I'll pretend it's an early access game and check back in 6-8 months to see how things have progressed.PS: Refunded after all. There's just no value in the game for money they ask.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected more out of this game because I am a huge HP fan and Quidditch World Cup was one of my favorite games as a kid. However, I was extremely disappointed with this game. For starters, the game play is fun in its own regard, with the player able to control all 4 roles in Quidditch: Keeper, Chaser, Beater and Seeker. Unfortunately, the tutorial feels rushed and thrown together and doesn't do a great job teaching the controls, so when you get into actual game play, it is a struggle to master.There are some weird, extreme changes to the rules of the game, like only including one Beater and the Snitch being worth only 30 points instead of 150 and does not even end the game when it's caught. It appears twice during a normal length game, but could appear a 3rd in overtime. The first team to 100 points or the team with the highest score after 7 minutes wins.The single player content is lackluster. Even though the AI becomes increasingly difficult as you level, once you learn how to play, the game becomes increasingly easier and it's almost insulting to play at that point. Overall, this game was such a massive disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: In today's day and age of gaming I'm very happy to see a great game finally be released among the sea of half hashed games in over done genres that dev's call triple A titles, Quidditch Champions is a shining example of making a good game the first time, content is on the low end right now, and is lacking a bit in game modes and non ranked matches, but for it's really pleasing graphics and fun audio and magical experience of flying brooms fighting over the ball sends rocket league down the drain in my opinion.A few pointers I wanna say regarding the majority of reviews for this game:(Start up and crashing problems) When it comes to new games there is always that odd individual problem that some users have not being able to start up or play long with out some crashes, sadly this happens to me to in every other game I play, but here, I have had no issues regarding playing the game and remaining in matches, it could just be some software updates that you may need or simple drivers updates to fix it, or even just a poor install, try verifying cache. Worst case the game needs a patch to cover some holes that may be leaking for some PCs that causes these issues, but I'm sure in due time it will be fixed soon.(Bots) People have been saying that 3v3s have bots, I think what they mean is 3v3 multi-player has AI that auto pilots your secondary role for you while you are handling your primary. which of course is chaser, this is a must in this mode other wise your other character would be sitting still the whole time making those positions worthless with out someone controlling them, so to help this, AI is in place to keep the game going, I see no issues with this design, how ever it would be cool to see a mode where all positions are filled and a whole game is played by independent roles, that would make for a really enjoyable match as well.(Micro transactions) I honestly think people are completely stupid about this one, there is not ONE SINGLE micro transaction in the freaking game what so ever. No currency's are purchasable in the market place, and the season pass is 100% free, and active on start up, all 3 currency's in the game is earned by the progressive seasonal pass (free) and leveling up and playing the story.Overall: I see this game being way better after some after-release content updates. Like new game modes, and limited time game modes and ideas to keep the community engaged. I love this game already and I hope for it's expanding growth, don't listen to every complaint and take it as the whole honest truth, people just like to complain, and aren't happy that some casuals get to enjoy a game for once. Just get it and give it go yourself, and make the judgment on your own.Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I played this game for a good amount of time and while I still think that for the price it's a decent buy and I've spent 30 dollars on worse, there's really no reason it shouldn't have been apart of Hogwarts Legacy besides the fact that then you couldn't have logically included characters from the main franchise. It's fun but it's not full blown regular quidditch1. Matches are 3v3 with characters choosing from two positions to swap back and forth between, usually Chaser and a specialty position like Seeker/Keeper. 2. You only play to 100 points but matches are super quick which I appreciate, I don't want to be in an hour long match.3. Catching the Snitch only awards 30 points. I actually really like this change, 150 points for the Snitch always seemed over the top to me but in the books/movies the field was huge and you didn't have a tracker on it once you found it. It logically does not make sense to award 150 points in a match that lasts less than 10 minutes. 30 is good and still keeps the match competitive. 4. There are 4 "Cups" Weasley Burrow, Hogwarts, Triwizard, and then Quidditch World Cup. It's a bracket style event. The "Campaign" is pretty short.5. I'm either really good at the game or the AI is just not hard because even the hardest difficulty AI was still very easy6. You complete challenges and earn in game currencies, there are three different currencies, coins, keys, and moonstone?. Moonstone is used to upgrade any of the brooms you unlock/have access to, Coins are used to buy cosmetic packs, and winged keys are used to buy rarer skins,7. THERE ARE NO MICRO-TRANSACTIONS, ALL IN GAME CURRENCY IS EARNED IN GAME AND CANNOT BE BOUGHT8. Multiplayer is multiplayer, same gameplay as campaign, but your teammates are either good or terrible, there's no inbetween.Overall there's not a lot of meat on this games bones. It's fun but you can finish the campaign in an afternoon and then it's pretty much just multiplayer to grind for skins.

Edit 3.Harry Potter World Cup came out 21 years ago not 11 i make that mistake alot so im not gonna fix it sorry. check out the link of the guy trying to gatcha - look at the crowd and look at the players faces - obviously the general graphics are better - but the crowd looks better in the 21 year old game and the faces of the big characters are more recognizable even with less polygons. So yes are a graphics downgrade thanks for the link loser.  (anyways the bar was raised with Hogwarts Legacy this is a huge downgrade from that.)The Review.First just wanna say that the game feels like an alpha build. If this was an alpha release this would be a positive review "great core game can't wait to see what they add and polish." But the devs feel as if this is good enough to release so let's review it as is. Imagine making a game that is only Quidditch and then it not getting the quidditch right. Catching the Snitch gives ya 30 points and doesn't end the game. Game ends after 5min or a team gets 100 pts. feels like HP Champs is the XFL where HP World Cup is the NFL. Similar but different rules which creates different vibes. Sure people might say "do you really want the game to end when someone catches the snitch" YES because that's quidditch. It makes the value and importance of catching the snitch. now it's more of an annoying interruption when your making a play. Also how is winning the House Cup more satisfying in a game made 11 years ago? The campaign in this game is a lazy bracket screen then you get a png of your opponent and one line. That's the entire vibe of this game, menus and directly into quidditch. No walking onto the pitch, no fan interactions (because the fans are literally downgraded from 11 years ago lol). Bracket -> Picture with 1 line-> Game -> Repeat. That's what I mean by the game feels lazy and lacks soul.The Arena's are shorter than what you'd expect going into them. Height restriction is just above the goals. often find yourself bonking your head off invisible walls. annoying and limits vertical play. Bots being in PVP feels really bad. so how the game works is it's 3v3 everyone controllers both a chaser and one of the other 3 roles. When you are playing as one of the characters the other is controlled by a bot. Overall Vibe feels like PVP lite. IDK when im Qued for PVP i don't wanna be passing to Bots and shooting a bot keeper. Feels like laziness or cheaping out on servers that can handle 6v6. let's talk start with the Seeker role because they wrecked it. After a certain period of time in the match the snitch will become available then the player can switch to the seeker and fly through rings behind the snitch to fill up a bar and once the bar is full then you can grab the snitch - doesn't feel like a race what so ever. maybe a race to collect rings but not a race for the snitch. then you get 30 points for catching the snitch and the quaffle gets reset to being thrown from center field. no ending the game no 150 points, nope 30 points and a center field toss up. Time wise the game seems to allow two snitch catches maybe more as player lvl gets higher. So the seeker player can play catch the rings for half the game and score 60pts. 8hr update: General Seeker tip. When you see the snitch fly into the corner don't chase it but setup to follow it as soon as it leaves the corner, the arena is small so the path is predictable and you can cut it off to get directly behind it. the rings will give you more catch rate the closer you are to the snitch when you grab them. so combine this with the skill that makes rings disappear after you fly through them, and you will be catching two snitches a game while the opposing seeker is struggling to catch a single ring. Wish the arena was bigger so the snitch could be more unpredictable but it essentially just flys in a loop. like the rest of the game it's so close to being good just needs more polish. Loved the Keeper role at first but with the inconsistency of the keeper not catching the quaffle thats flying under his armpit keeper has pretty much become kick the people in the face when they get close. because trying to block is a coin flip if you character will actually try to block. I recommend all the skills the improve the Keeper's kicks. Chaser's are alright can feel like getting bullied from time to time but that's quidditch baby. Beater's I never play, they just look boring to me but I assume that's a preference. Not everyone is gonna enjoy every role nothing wrong about that ill stick to keeper. Graphics look like a premium phone game and everything feels like this is a 5 year old mobile game ported over to PC. It''s evident that they were unable to use the likeness of the characters from the movies as Hermione and Ginny both look like their faces got smushed. Didn't even recognize Cho until i her name was underneath her. all the characters get a semi similar squished face. Really just looks like a fan made game that's trying to avoid copyright issues. Honestly the entire Vibe of the game feels soulless, doesn't feel like a harry potter game. alot feels lazy dev work, alot of visual bugs, mobile game graphics, 1/3rd of the cut scenes are animated while others are just talking pngs no consistency. House Cup is now just brackets with no other heart put into it. I Loved QWC. and the expectations for this game were raised when Quidditch wasn't in Hogwarts Legacy. So me like many other people were hoping for a Quidditch game with the quality or refinement of Hogwarts legacy. What we got was a slight improvement to graphics and an improvement on broom handling from the 11 year old game but a downgrade from broom handling and graphics from hogwarts legacy. just disappointing.We were shown the potential for a great game, what we got was a mediocre reboot that looks like it was made with the intent to port to mobile and I would not be surprised if we either see a micro transaction update within a year that or the servers will get shut down. hopefully the devs prove me wrong and pull a No Man's Sky but i doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: ⠀If you love Harry Potter, and or are fascinated by Quidditch, and or played and enjoyed Quidditch World Cup for PC or GC from 2003, this game will be your jam, your jelly, 100% your thing.⠀I tick all of the above, and I must say ALL my concerns were surprisingly resolved. The product is high quality, the price I think is fair for its contents, not even considering the updates yet to come, and no MTX! ⠀It's fairly well balanced for multiplayer play, the bar of entry is very low, and the skill ceiling seems to be satisfactorily high and I guess we're yet to see how high it can go, but how to improve isn't obtuse at all; in fact I haven't watched any tutorials yet I already feel pretty confident I'm good. All of the most tacky and quirky "tricks" and "techs" I've learnt usually came from being absolutely dominated by a very savvy opponent, observing their play carefully and trying to recreate it, so even losing can be quite fun.⠀It *almost* feels retro to play a multiplayer game of this scope, with matchmaking, and NOT having to worry about what cosmetics I'd be able to get... but there's a caveat.⠀While it's true there's no further purchases you can make once you buy the product (besides its deluxe pack ofc), the game's unlockeable conditions are very suspiciously designed in much the same way any other game WITH MTXs. That is to say, the game has 3 currencies, each of which allow you to buy different kinds of stuff; it's plain to see how easy it would be to implement a coin store with these, so the experience of unlocking stuff isn't quite retro, but uncannily pleasant. It's like playing a modern multiplayer as if you were a whale and able to acquire everything.⠀Unlocking stuff also doesn't feel awfully grindy, so as a GaaS it's quite the specimen in this regard. There is, for instance, a sort of "season pass", the typical step by step unlock sequence we usually have to pay for in any other game, yet here we all get them, and we can even advance it by just playing singleplayer matches. In fact, we can unlock virtually all the game has to offer just playing SP, but MP requirements do show up for the weekly/daily "challenges" which do accelerate progression substantially. ⠀It would be a shame if season pass items become totally inaccessible for future players, but we don't know yet. As of the writing of this review the very first pass is still active, so we have yet to see how they handle it.⠀ As you probably imagined, they modified much of the original rulebook, obviously; Champions is a first to 100 points game, with a 7 minute time limit and overtime golden goal for tied matches. Snitches now grant only 30 points, taken straight from Muggle Quidditch, and another change: there's now only 1 beater, composing teams of 6 players total, and making the field a bit more habitable, specially for chasers for which the game was schizo enough. ⠀This makes quite a neat team symmetry between the 3 chasers and 3 "unique" roles, which was very astutely purposed to reduce the player-clients required to compose PVP teams to 3, each player controlling both a chaser and their unique role of choice, swapping at their discretion between the two, take over one and the other becomes a bot.⠀In practice, they totally work and it made all roles feel equally relevant and present during a match. Do keep in mind 6 vs 6 was confirmed for November, so that'll also be cool.⠀Very well designed for the purposes of the game, with both full 3D navigation freedom and a well defined framework of limitations that makes teamwork imperative against serious players, yet still allowing individual performances to really carry a team's momentum. Everyone except the keeper plays exactly the same, with 1 or 2 different button mappings according to their role; with the same button a chaser passes the quaffle, a beater shoots their bludger and a seeker goes for the catch.⠀The camera is locked to broom orientation, so scanning around your peripherals is actually quite inconvenient when your priority is catching up or racing towards your objective, since you'd have to actually change your forward trajectory towards what you're trying to look at. There is the option to look directly behind you, and there's also a button to focus on the quaffle, but it wont work if you yourself have it, obviously. ⠀This is where the *drift* mechanic comes in. Drifting sounds and, indeed, looks very cool; it allows you to keep a linear momentum for a moment while you look around, letting you aim without having to stay still, which is very useful to surprise a keeper last second, but take too long and you'll get gotten, since you're just going on a straight line.⠀Stealing quaffles from chasers, or clubbing them as a beater, is actually quite hard if the chasers know how to make their path unpredictable, sometimes even slowing down so you overshoot, or sacrificing a forward advance for spontaneous dives and varying their altitude such that your window of opportunity for a lunge is really tight, since when you lunge for a steal or a hit you can mostly just steer horizontally.⠀Quidditch's quaffle play is probably most similar to basketball, not even because of the "hoops", but rather in the sense of how players move and adjust their position on the field. Rebounds are quite common, and what defines a good goal opportunity is how quickly a team can carry the quaffle to the opposite side while maintaining wide positions, possibly leaving behind the previous attackers before they can do the turnaround and reach effective defensive positions and markings.⠀I like that, in a normal match, the snitch appears twice, so that ultimately seekers could "tie" and make Quaffle play the determinant factor to victory, and it's also cool because by the second snitch some matches can have scores coming close to the 100 mark, meaning there are situations where catching a snitch does end the match and makes that team win the game. I guess the hypest catch would be the *very* rare THIRD snitch that occurs in the case of tied overtimes, since you'd also need to catch it before the golden goal.⠀Since there's only 1 beater now, their role will be primarily offensive, as opposed to the possibility of having a beater play escort/patrol or other defensive roles. This is not too big of a lost opportunity, since the benefits of removing the one beater seem to hold way more weight than this unrealised beater pair potential, and also because dodging bludgers is actually quite easy, though it is a LOT more nuanced than a QTE.⠀Just so you know: the bludger tracks; of course it does, otherwise no one would ever hit anyone unless it was hitscan. The directional aileron dodge roll (or barrel roll in Starfox terms) is very efficient for both bludgers AND chasers trying to steal or hit you, but it does NOT have I-frames, so timing must be precise and choosing the right dodge direction actually makes all the difference. It's made so you actually have to think about the bludger's trajectory, and you could even dodge one by just free-flying a very tight curve.⠀Keepers move differently. Their orientation and camera is locked pointing towards the field, yet they have free movement on all 3 axes, though it is quite slower than the forward flying from the rest of the players. This allows you to maintain spatial awareness while effectively moving to steal and/or intercept the quaffle, or close in on a carrying attacker to reduce the goal. I personally think that good keepers can make the role feel OP, but it's not; you'll just need a good pass.BUY IT!
