_childDocuments_.review: Originally I marked my review as not recommended, but now that season 1 has released, I have changed my mind. Season 1 has added ranked and a 6v6 gamemode (meaning there are no bots in the game). This gamemode is everything the game was meant to be: a fast paced, chaotic but competitive quidditch game that is faithful to how it was described in the books. I still agree with my other critiques and the player base is still not that large, but the game as a whole is honestly great fun and worth your money.My original review is shown below:Although I think this game is a fun take on Quidditch, the small player base and lack of meaningful updates, make it hard to recommend it.For starters, the gameplay is fun, with the player being able to control all 4 roles in Quidditch (keeper, chaser, beater and seeker). All roles have fun mechanics and the synergy between the roles works well. Small, but needed changes are made to the rules of the game, like only including one beater and the snitch being worth only 30 points and not ending the game. The snitch appears two times during a normal length game, but may appear a 3rd time in overtime. First to 100 points or the team with the highest score after 7 minutes wins. The game contains most standard features that can be expected from a competitive game like this. It has a levelling system with a season pass, daily and weekly challenges and plenty of customisation in the form of trails, goal explosions, and player cosmetics. The game also features career challenges and achievements, so there is a sense of completion/progress in that regard.  The single player content is lacklustre. There are a total of 3 cups (house, triwizard and world cup) and all 3 follow a similar structure of a few placement matches followed by a knockout stage. Although the AI gets reasonably difficult on the highest difficulty, after a few hours it becomes easy to win consistently. Combined with the simple (and similar) format of the 3 cups, the single player does not take long to become repetitive.Although the single player content is simple in nature, it is enough to keep one busy for long enough to justify buying this game on sale and if the developers could flesh it out a bit more, it could be worth the full price tag of 30 euros. However, clearly the main focus of the game is the competitive multiplayer. And honestly, this is where the game dropped the quaffle.Firstly the game seemed to be marketed poorly and so far hasn't gotten a lot of attention. This creates a fairly small player base. During peak hours, finding a match is easy enough (taking roughly 1-5 minutes), but off-peak, searching for a game can easily take up more than 10 minutes. In addition, a lack of skill-based matchmaking makes it difficult to enjoy the PvP, as I am constantly matched up with people far above my skill level. These two factors alone make the moderate enthusiasm I had for the game thus far quickly die out and I wouldn't be surprised if more players feel this way. Speaking of dying out, the game hasn't really gotten a serious update since release as far as I can tell. Plenty of patches have rolled out and the developers are absolutely active in trying to improve the game, but the first season has felt more like a early-access release than anything else. There are only a few stations to play in and only a single multiplayer game-mode (which is probably due to the low player base). This makes me wonder about the future. When the first real season launches, and Christmas around the corner I believe the game really needs to start attracting more players and adding more content and skill-based matchmaking to keep those players active. Otherwise, I wouldn't be surprised that this game dies out, becomes free to play and eventually gets cancelled within a year of its release.

_childDocuments_.review: My Steam review required a yes or no on the recommendation. I'm going to click yes, BUT:YES: This is a quidditch game, and it's finally online multiplayerNO: THIS GAME DOES NOT FOLLOW CANNONICAL QUIDDITCH. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME IF YOU'RE EXPECTING HPQWC2. IT'S NOT THE SAMESo... it's not what i've been waiting for in terms of a quidditch game. THEY CHANGED THE BLOODY RULES!!!!Harry Potter Quidditch World Cup, PS2, Around 2002: Played exactly as you would expect quidditch would. 3 chasers, 2 beaters, 1 keeper, 1 chaser. Snitch awarded 150 points and ended the game, for better or for worse. Whether you'd scored. 160 points and got that 150 to win, or scored nothing and the opposing team scored 160 and didn't catch the snitch, the game ended at that point. Harry Potter Quidditch Champions: 3 chasers, 1 beater, 1 keeper, 1 seeker. The team is missing 1 full entity (a second beater), the game does not end when you catch the golden snitch. The golden snitch does not award 150 points, and instead awards 30, and the golden snitch does not end the game. This game, does not keep true to quidditch in it's entirety. It's actually a really decent game, but when you go into it after having been speedrunning and just enjoying HPQWC for well over 2 decades, the game is trash. It does not keep in the format of the previous game or the movies, and is just all together mediocre as a single player game, however, the new format does well specifically for multiplayer, and not for those of the fanbase. On top of that, each game only lasts 10 minutes tops (I think, might be shorter). Snitch spawns multiple times! only awards 30 points. doesn't end the game. (This is a great idea for multiplayer, but not for career).I really want to love this game. I've been waiting for this game since at least 2004 (around a year after the original game) and I genuinely think EA sports could have done better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game for a few hours now, and personally, I really like it. However, there are a few things the developers should consider:I think the game must become free-to-play over time, because a paid model simply isn't sustainable for a multiplayer game in the long run. This isn't like Overwatch, which can maintain its player base for a long time. This is a Harry Potter game, primarily for Harry Potter fans, which is already a niche group, and even smaller is the group of people who are both Harry Potter fans and gamers.If the game becomes free-to-play, there must be a paid store, battle pass, or something similar, because otherwise, it won’t be sustainable in the long term. Even the store design looks like this game will be filled with microtransactions. I don't understand why the game was advertised as having no microtransactions, because sooner or later, they will be necessary, and that will cause a major backlash.Obviously, during the first few weeks or 1-2 months, casual play will be enough, but if the developers truly want a committed player base, adding a ranked mode is essential so that players have something to strive for. Speaking of ranked: this can only be properly implemented with a 6v6 PVP mode.

_childDocuments_.review: No microtransactions, no fluff just straight forward quidditch with familiar characters as well as a good roster of international teams and the ability to have custom characters play throughout from tryouts to the world cup (I remade the 1999 japan team from the 2003 game). unlocks feel well spaced out and enough freedom to invest skill points where you want for your play style.First I want to address some common complaints I see in other reviews, The art style feels more a safe choice to avoid aging poorly plus feels like an homage to the 2003 game.It can be easy against bots but a decent challenge on harder difficulties, the multiplayer and unlocks are where its focus really is, clearly there will be seasons expanding the list of unlockables as well as daily's and such.The rules have changed, the snitch appears after a while in a match, is 30pts and does not end the game so can appear a few times (2-3 depending how fast it gets caught) at first yes this sounds like heresy but if you get a chance to play the 2003 game (Which I still do every few months) you will find that the alternative of a true 150pt snitch and game end means an even easier and faster game even on the hardest difficulty and against the best teams.I can feel that this change to the rules did not come easy or just out of nowhere, the games now last longer and some strategy is employed of whether you focus on being seeker or try and play chasers to negate the 30 from the snitch (Also forgoing bonus medals at the end of each match) or heck switch to beater and take their seeker out completely, all freedom of choice you did not have in the 2003 game, there is so much more here than its predecessor and claiming otherwise is at best nostalgia blinders or at worse deliberate misinformation.This game most definitely is not a "Mobile game" unless you run a gaming mobile with a controller paired. people need to actually go play some mobile games again because this is has been tossed around to new games a lot lately (AC: Shadows and SW: Outlaws).It's a sports game, like fifa/rugby/golf/f1 whatever have you, you hop on, play a few rounds, get some daily's feel good or bad about yourself and your skill lvl then logoff. there's no long story driven campaign or hidden depth. its Quidditch from start to end and how much fun you get out of it is how much you allow yourself to enjoy it.That all said, my complaints: Why Rita skeeter as a world cup commentator?? Where's my man Ludovic Bagman?

_childDocuments_.review: It was a brisk evening at Hogwarts, the golden light of the setting sun spilling through the high windows of the Gryffindor common room. Harry, Hermione, and Ron sat huddled around the flickering fireplace, each with a look of deep concentration on their faces. Harry had just returned from testing out the latest game to hit the wizarding world: Quidditch Champions.“So, how was it?” Ron asked eagerly, leaning forward in his chair. “Does it really feel like playing in the Quidditch World Cup?”Harry sighed, pushing his round glasses up the bridge of his nose. “It’s… alright,” he began, choosing his words carefully, “but it’s not exactly like flying on a real broomstick.”Hermione, ever the analytical one, narrowed her eyes. “What do you mean, Harry? The game was supposed to let you live out your Quidditch dreams!”Harry shrugged. “Well, you do get to play all the positions—Seeker, Chaser, Beater, and Keeper—but there’s something missing. For one thing, the character customization… it’s a bit underwhelming. You’re expected to create your entire team, not just one witch or wizard. It feels like they want you to be Madam Hooch, Professor McGonagall, and Oliver Wood all at once!”Ron snorted. “Blimey, that sounds like more work than Snape’s homework assignments.”Harry nodded in agreement. “Exactly. I just wanted to focus on my Seeker skills, but instead, I had to worry about the whole team. And don’t even get me started on the Battle Pass. Sure, it’s free, but it’s a grind like nothing I’ve ever seen—even worse than Professor Binns’ History of Magic lectures.”Hermione frowned. “A grind? But the game is supposed to be fun, not a chore.”“Oh, it is,” Harry said, though his tone was half-hearted. “At least, until you realize you have to play for hours on end just to unlock a new pair of Quidditch gloves. By the time you’ve unlocked everything, you’ll have spent more time playing than we did hunting Horcruxes!”Ron’s eyes widened. “No way! But what about the Snitch? Catching it must be the best part, right?”Harry winced. “Well, that’s the thing… Catching the Snitch isn’t what it used to be. In the books and movies, the match ends when you catch it, right? But in the game, it’s only worth 30 points. It doesn’t even end the match! You’re just left flying around, wondering why you bothered.”Hermione looked horrified. “They’ve changed the rules of Quidditch? But the Snitch is the most important part!”“I know,” Harry said, shaking his head. “I wish they’d included different game modes, too. It’s just the same thing over and over. I was hoping for a bit more variety, like a ‘capture the Snitch’ mode where everyone’s hunting for it. But no, it’s just the standard match with a few tweaks.”Ron slumped back in his chair, looking defeated. “So, you’re saying the only fun parts are playing as a Beater or Chaser?”Harry nodded. “Pretty much. If you’re into smashing Bludgers or scoring goals, you might have a good time. But as for the rest of it…” He trailed off, staring into the fire. “I wanted it to be something special—something that felt like Quidditch. But it’s just not the same.”There was a long silence as the trio sat, contemplating the game that could have been. Finally, Hermione spoke up, her voice filled with determination. “Well, maybe they’ll update it, improve things. Until then, we’ll just have to stick with the real thing.”Harry smiled faintly, glancing out the window where the Quidditch pitch loomed in the distance. “Yeah,” he agreed softly. “Nothing beats the real thing.”And with that, they left the common room, their thoughts already on the next Quidditch match, where no amount of digital wizardry could ever replace the thrill of the wind in their hair and the roar of the crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game has great potential, there are so many issues:1) There are little to no cosmetics. They have a shop dedicated to purchasing items but there are little to no items to purchase. After multiple weeks, no updates have been provided.2) They provided one major quality of life update, then revoked it when hardcore players complained. In this update, chasers were nerfed by having their turn radius slowed drastically. This was because keepers couldn't keep up with the turn speed of chasers while also dealing with the ONE CLICK OPTION THAT ALLOWED CHASERS TO ROLL TO THE OTHER SIDE OF THE HOOPS AND SHOOT AT THE SAME TIME. Because of this function, chasers could fake that they're moving to a particular direction then rapid move to another so quickly that the opposing player couldn't keep up before they were scored on. It offered no reaction time, only the hopes that the keeper *guessed* the direction of the incoming chaser and by chance moved in the direction that they were being pressured in,Now, you may ask yourself if I'm being an ass by posting this here? Well, yes it may come off that way. However, please note that I initially attempted to post this complaint in the actual discord correlating with this game itself. However, when I did so I was greeted with a user who has a self proclaimed SIX HUNDRED GODS DAMNED HOURS that told me that I was incorrect because his lack of bathing determined that I knew nothing about how the game was supposed to operate. His resources? The four (also self-proclaimed) pro player keepers that determined that what I was saying what incorrect and ill-informed. He argued that if the people I played with actually knew what they were doing, they'd have done just fine BEFORE the game was properly balanced and thus the only reason they did poorly was because they weren't good enough to deal with the state of the game.With all of this said, I hope dearly that the devs level out the game and grow enough of a pair to care about the mass majority of the player base instead of peeing their pants and folding to the one percent of players who have never heard of the word shower. As someone who has lost sleep to the idea of waking up to an owl taking them away from their abusive life, I wish this universe would for once be put in the hands of people who don't only care about making a quick buck.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is still in a very early state especially for $30 but has great roots to be an awesome game like Rocket League. The lack of micro transactions could lead to the game fading out before too long. If you aren't tight on money it is a truly unique experience and I do recommend you check it out!          The game has really strong roots and could become something great, a few notable pros are it is similar to a rocket league type play style which has great replayability. It doesn't spam your screen with micro transactions but we will get back to this later.  Another good thing is (at least for now) the developers seem to be updating very consistently and listening to feedback for the most part. Also it seems the AI bots are a lot better than you would think for a game like this, they can pose a fair challenge on higher difficulty and aren't completely stupid most the time (most). A not so good thing is upgrades on brooms and skills are very simple and once they are done and you have the "best build" you really don't need to worry about it anymore (becomes null), however not everyone dislikes this I just personally would like to see it have more depth. Now some bad things. The game is $30 and it's basically an Alpha build. This game was definitely released too early and needs some work. It lacks essential things like a ranked mode and a 6v6 mode (all players no bots). Also as stated before it has no micro transactions and as of right now everything can be earned in-game. This sound awesome and in theory it is, however for the longevity of the game this sucks. WB will not be able to make enough money off of the game to keep up with the servers and I really don't want to see that. If you come from rocket league and enjoy that or if you are just a fan of harry potter in general and don't even know what RL is, it would still be a good play.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original for what it was and I came with expectations to this game that it would feel different because it's been many years since and that at least is the one thing that should be said: despite being the same sport, this isn't the same game at all as the original. The main difference is that this is all about playing in multiplayer, playing all the roles while being fun and accessible for everyone. The original had local multiplayer but really at it's core it was about selling the fantasy of quidditch, teams had loud video sequences where they showcased their personalities and goals where highlighted like an event with a zoom in on the character and the teams had at times brutal attack moves to really show who dominated the skies, the bludger was never nice to the faces it crushed into even in the movies after all. You saw the players do athletic stunts on their brooms to get the quaffle, high five each other and do victory poses after each goal. This game in comparison feels like someone stripped the original of all it's personality, took the gameplay and tried to make it feel like you have more individual control over the role you play. In the gameplay aspect I feel like it mostly succeeded, you definitely feel more free in the sky than in the originals "on rails" fly paths... except when you crush into all those invisible walls all around the field that don't allow you to fly very high or around the towers like in the movies or books. The total lack of individual character is the real tragedy here though because the game has you ALWAYS play with your custom characters which means you create some neutral looking character in the beginning and suddenly you see that face fly for any house, any school and any national team you control... cool. also the teams basically are only different in looks because of their uniforms (unless you play in multiplayer where everyone looks like they want to), so if you play solo in the campaign it feels repetitive after like 4 games because for the most part it's the same arena against the same bland faces... and yea, sure... some are lookalikes from characters you might know, but they fly and act like everyone else while you play so they might as well all wear the hagrid ps1 mask.if you really love the gameplay and are big on team based sports games on a magical broom, all the lack of personality might not matter to you ofc. This game definitely has fun enough gameplay, but for the solo experience and selling the fantasy or immersion of playing quidditch this feels like the bare minimum you could do with it and it looks flat compared to the original game. This doesn't really feel like a thumbs up review but because it works at it's core, as team based multiplayer broom sports game, I give it to it anyway... but don't play this if you want the "campaign", it's really just the same match over and over against the same very weak AI with only the color of your outfit changing and really nothing else surrounding it, the teams don't even celebrate in different ways.

_childDocuments_.review: - I've been really enjoying the game. Like many others, I was initially disappointed about the bots, but I'm still finding the game strong even without 6v6 mode. - I love the rush of managing when to swap between roles. My favorite combo is chaser/seeker, but I also really enjoy playing chaser/keeper.- The skills you can unlock as you level up are really cool. For chaser, you can choose to focus on teamwork, handling, or tackling. As an example, Teamwork gives you a speed boost when following teammates and lets you give others a speed boost when you pass. It’s a lot of fun!- I realize this might put new players at a disadvantage, but you level up quickly in the beginning. After just 4 hours, I’ve already added a significant amount of skills to my seeker and chaser roles.- The announcers are fun and have great voice lines. The maps are really pretty, although I wish there were more, but I’m sure that’ll come in time. The cosmetics are fun too—I love the house hats, and the snake is super cute. Plus, all currencies can be earned by playing the game, which is a nice touch.- I haven’t played single-player yet, so I can’t comment on that.If you’re on the fence, I’d say grab it and try it out—you can always refund it if it’s not your jam. Overall, I’d rate the game a strong 8/10 as it stands, and once 6v6 is added, it’ll probably move up to a 9/10 for me.

But as I don't want to be all negative about this review I want to say that it is in fact, for its price, a nice game without many issues. - AZERTY keyboard users, you won't be able to change your role unless you change your keyboard language settings to QWERTY because there isn't an unbind option for the numbers (Seeker, Beater, Chaser and Keeper) - Character creation is a bit buggy, like I want to customise my characters but sometimes after I hit save, it just changes my character into Ginny Weasley for some reason?So, should you buy this game?If you are a Potterhead: yes. DO IT.If you aren't a Potterhead, but you still enjoyed Hogwarts Legacy: yes, try it out and if you don't like it just refund If you never heard of Harry Potter before and are unsure wth Quidditch even is: don't buy this game and go watch the movies first. _childDocuments_.review: You can really tell that this is made with love for the source material while still trying to provide as fun an experience as possible. You also know exactly what rewards you are working towards rather than lootboxes.Not played a huge amount of PVP, but from what I played it was quite fun.  Imagine a 6 v 6 would be more chaotic and looking forward to when that comes out, but the single players has had me hooked ever since I got it.Overall, this is the best quidditch experience in a game I've played, and I now do not care at all that it wasn't included in Hogwarts Legacy, since it having a standalone game allowed a much more fleshed out experience.

They can also knock out the opponents seeker when they are chasing the snitch. Cons:There isn't a whole lot to do in the game so far. You are given a tutorial in the beginning and then you can play a season. Your first season is at Hogwarts. Once you beat that you can play the Tri Wizard Cup scholols, then the world cup. The only other feature is PvP right now. The PvP is a 3v3 match where you queue up as 2 roles (seeker, keeper, beater, or chaser).

_childDocuments_.review: If there were a Quidditch match for how badly this game missed the mark, Quidditch Champions would be dead last, stuck in the Bludger’s path with no way to dodge it. I don't even know where to start—let’s talk about the controls. It feels like flying a broomstick made out of wet noodles. The mechanics are clunky, unresponsive, and the flying physics? A nightmare. Every time I try to line up a shot, it’s like my character suddenly forgets what a broomstick is supposed to do. Is this a game about Quidditch or a test of patience?The graphics look like they were designed for a 2003 mobile phone. The character models are stiff, and the animations look like something you'd find in a bargain-bin knockoff game. And don’t get me started on the soundtrack—it’s like they hired a guy with a kazoo and a synth to make the music. A major auditory assault.Now, the multiplayer? That’s a disaster. I’m not even sure the game is trying to make it work. I spent more time waiting in loading screens than actually playing. And when I did get into a match, it was like watching a car crash in slow motion, with random disconnects and lag ruining any semblance of fun.What’s even worse is the monetization. You can't even unlock all the teams and gear without forking over money—looks like this game's more about "Quidditch Champions" in your wallet than in your heart.Save your money. This isn’t a Quidditch game; it’s a money grab, a buggy mess, and an insult to the sport. Avoid at all costs. If I could give this game zero stars, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a hard decision to be honest, I really want to like this game and wanted to support it (especially since it has no microtransactions), but at the moment I am not sure whether to refund it and just wait till later or not.Let me start with the positives, or a positive anyway. The gameplay is quite fun, its responsive, impactful, sound effects are great and each position feels unique. I can definitely see this staying fun for at least a couple dozen hours when trying to master all the positions, especially in the multiplayer.With that out of the way, here are my issues, I know some of them will seem petty but thats just how it goes. Im also almost completely uninterested in the multiplayer personally so I look at this from a single player point of view and what I expected when comparing it to other more modern sports games.My biggest dissapointment is the career mode, it isnt done like how I expected (and the trailers didnt clarify as far as I saw) like how it is done in fifa for example (not that those games are any good anymore). You dont create your own character and play as him/her, trying to be the best you can be and reach the top, you cant even name your character, you create an entire Quidditch team right off the bat and you have to manage all of them, in other words, its a manager mode rather than a quidditch player career mode.You could play as only one of them I suppose, at least when it comes to Chasers, Keepers and Beaters but you would be severely limiting yourself and likely resign yourself to unnecessary losses outside of the easiest modes. However the game clearly isnt meaning for you to do that, there is no personal story or hell even cutscenes that would take just your player character, like I said, you cant even name it. I was really hoping for the career mode to be simple from zero to hero story like how it sounded in the features trailer.My second biggest issue is the changes to the rules, now dont get me wrong I understand why they were made, at least some of them, but that doesnt mean they necessarily lead to a better game. We play with one fever Beater, likely so the 3v3 multiplayer can be as it is, catching golden snitch no longer awards 150 points or ends the match, instead we just play untill a 100, first team to score that wins.Needless to say this may be better for balance, but it makes for a lot less dynamic and interesting game. Yes catching the GS in the books usually ends in the win of whoever caught it, but in the Quidditch World Cup and even here, its doubtful that you couldnt score enough points to nullify that, especially if you, or your team are good and it obviously diminishes the seeker role as a whole, which tends to be one of the most played and enjoyed. More importantly, this game in particularly provides ample ways to disturb the seeker if you focus them in my opinion, with beaters being able to summon a bludger every few seconds and everyone being able to tackle means you can essentially stun lock anyone.Personally I dont find these changes necessary or welcome, yea quidditch is flawed as hell, but it was SO much fun to play in the Quidditch World Cup that I dont see any reason to change it.Now the more minute issues.Graphically the game goes for a very stylized graphic style and while it doesnt look bad where the characters are concerned, the enviroments beyond the immidiate vicinity look quite dreadful, trees and such being just outlined in the distance etc., this, coupled with the home screen where you are standing in your locker room with features and options arround you kinda makes me think this was meant to be a mobile game initially (I am glad it isnt btw).Which neatly leads me to my second annoyance, which is the body types and the they/them approach to commentary. This really makes the game feel like a cheaply made mobile game. There are three body types, none of which are recognizably female and it mostly relies on what face you pick. We get the small kid I guess, the middle one which I assume is meant to be female given that you cant pick the more "masculine" faces and the third one which are guys.I guess the thinking was that the first option is for younger students, second are women with not recognizable curvature, which includes the grown ups (aside for Molly who also plays quidditch for some reason) and then the male ones. I got used to that nowadays we just cant have gendered character creators "body types", but why does everything have to be blanketed in this uncrecognizable they/them approach, instead of just adding a third option. Same with the commentary, there is no he and she, and while I do not know if this was done of inclusivity reasons or budgetary restriction reasons, it is an annoyance either way. For one, its not inclusive, I am not a they/them and 90+% of anyone playing this isnt either, its actively exclusive of the largest playerbase, and two, this game barely has any "gendered" dialogue whatsoever, like I said above, there barely is a career mode/story, voicing the few sentences where the player characters are directly adressed shouldnt be a big issue.Then the last minor annoyance, when exactly is this supposed to be set? I dont care for a timeline here but there are just straight up impossible scenarios here. Ginny mentions at the begining that she is now a retired player and became a renowned quidditch comentator, meaning everyone from the cast is an adult, yet we have Fred still around and commentating away, same with Molly just throwing quidditch moves around like nobody's business. Dont get me wrong its not a big thing and in the case of Molly its hilarious to see, but it would just be so easy to not mess with this.So thats it, for me, this is quite a dissapointment. I wont go as far as to say that Quidditch World Champion Cup was straight up beter, I have played it only a few years ago and while I adore it and finished it fully I do realise how limited it is in todays terms, but as it is, this game barely offers more. The biggest draw for me, a proper career mode simply isnt here, multiplayer, as far as I am aware, is also not exactly what many were asking for with the cut beater and only 3v3 (tho 6v6 is upcoming supposedly) and various other features being either barely better, or even more limited in scope, like the stadiums or countries available.Add to that the fact that the game is currently free with Playstation +, means that this can and should be a pass for now, the offering as it is, is just too meager and the annoyances too big, I can just go play something else for now. I hope that it improves, more content is added, more fleshed out career mode and not just new hero looks or accessories, but as it is now, I think I am going to refund and try again later.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Running on PC with KBM. Fantastic fun once you're good at it and winning often and still can be fun when you're getting stomped as a comeback can be just a few good quaffle goals and 1 snitch grab away. The gap between casual and serious is already widening. Do not listen to people that say it's hard to score with the Quaffle, I routinely drop 5 goals a game as a Chaser that secondarys as a keeper. The game has a great balance of being short rounds where chasers, seekers, keepers and beaters all play vital roles that, when done well, can turn the tide of a match. Needs: Ranked mode. This is definitely a competitive game. It needs 6v6 though I do quite enjoy 3v3. Better server region finding (Routinely play on 80-130 ping and for this game it affects a LOT of fast events dodging, shooting, keeping etc.) But I've had 16 ping so there must be good servers, it needs to prioritise those better pings.Has: Good flight movement with great dodge manoeuvre system. Even with a bad keeper or seeker you can take over a game as chaser and drop 5-7 goals. Hitboxes can be a bit iffy, sometimes I'll see the ball in my arms after a steal but then its back to the opposing player, this is probably ping related though. Broom stats are cool, as well as plenty of character options. Overall, a really solid game that should probably use the Rocket League model of Free to play with cosmetics, ranked competitive and nightly tournaments. I believe a lot of my game related concerns are due to server region and ping and with good prioritising and more of an Oceania playerbase (Playing from Aus) this would be mitigated.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world flooded with overmonetized live-service PVP slop, this one is refreshing. This is not a game that you will be stuck playing for hours after you come home from work in order to avoid battlepass FOMO. This is not a game that needs you to think much. This is not a game that will demand you open your wallet every week. You just play Quidditch and earn cosmetics. As someone who is easily angered by competitive PVP games, this one makes me happy. It feels fair. If you like Harry Potter, you will feel right at home with the sound and level design. The developers have done a great job creating the wonderous and magical atmosphere you associate with the franchise. Yes, it's nowhere near as detailed as Hogwarts Legacy, but I promise you, at the pace you will be playing, it won't matter to you even if you're a graphics snob. This game is a sharper, snappier, more exciting version of the old Quidditch World Cup game from years and years ago. That game aged well, and so will this one if the servers stay online. There is a campaign built into the game and several offline modes. If this is how it starts, I can only wonder what new maps and game modes Unbroken may add to the game as it goes on. Fingers crossed.Pick up this game. Pick it up for your friends. I think you'll have a fun time. At the very least, it's a great game to play when you aren't sure what to play next in your library. Support developers not attempting to gut your wallet in exchange for hollow satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super entertaining game, and it runs pretty smoothly in both single and multiplayer. It's essentially just Sky Rocketleague. Quick and Intuitive to learn as well. However, this is a Neutral review, certainly not a positive one.Here's the deal; if youre a multi player focus gaming looking for something new and quick, youll love it pretty much right off the top. However, if youre a single player focus gamer, Especially one with Childhood QWC nostalgia, its suuuper mid. Im not going to launch into a rant about the Snitch rules as everbody else already has. That said, its unfortunate the rules just one of several pretty massive blown opportunities for immersion, lore and nostalgia bating. With Hogwarts Legacy coming out so recently and doing so well, it just seems financially irresposible on the part of the Devs to not Play into it more. Again, the gameplay itself is great, but the game feels soulless after about 3 hours. The in game play by play during the world cup matches is provided by...Rita Skeeter? everyones favorite??? Super odd choice to make such a diliked character so prominant but *shrug* sure guys its your game.The player customization is super limited at a level 1-30 state, and somehow never includes the ability to name our players??? This along with all players on your team simply being reffered to by their positions makes everything feels so dry.The Commentary itself is actually probably the biggest weakspot in my opinion. Gone are the days of flourishing rants from an over excited Ludo Bagman about specific nations/players and their special skills.  You as the player get no sense of how good or bad your opponent is before matches.  The voice actors themselves are great, but theres actually only about 20 spoken scenario lines in the game across all 4 narators. The opening presentations of every match in every stadium in QWC Felt like a massive deal, unique to that slice of happiness in that corner of the wizarding world. I'm sure fans on all sides of the harry potter spectrum were hype asf for modern redone cultural  intros  and special for each country. Why can't japan do cool ninja ♥♥♥♥? Why arent the americans Dunking on people?? Why isnt Sweden throwing Ice at people?? What in the actual Cirque Du Soeil F**** did the French Chasers just do???unfortunaly those are gone too. Boooooring.We do however get to see Beauxbaton and Durmstrag castles and environments in a offical capacity though, which is a nicee touch. The other teams definitely feel super hallow, especially with so few characters and "real" teams  from the books and movies that could have been included. No Ireland Or Bulgaria in the world cup? cmon guys, seriously which countries did you think old fans would look for first?  It would have been great if this game had given quidditch some real structure as a culture and part of the wizarding community instead of just a flash in the pan of lore. Listen, If youre looking for QWC 2, or maybe imagining a full out FIFA/Madden/2k/NHL25 style sports game youre going to be massively dissapointed, but other than that its worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I was really itching for a Quidditch game since the previous one on the old Xbox, I wasn't really expecting much more than a half-baked cheap game I'd play once or twice and then drop, especially in this gaming climate.The game is a very pleasant surprise and feels a lot like a less nit-picky and technical Rocket League. I sort of hoped for a 6v6 where each role was filled by an individual player, but I'm honestly okay with how they made the 3v3 work.Everyone plays a Chaser (you can pass, tackle and score) while you're also tied to one of the three sub roles that you can freely swap* to:- Keeper (you guard the three goal rings while you can also put booster rings on the map for your chasers to speed through);- Beater (essentially you smack other players with an iron ball or tackle them down, you're the main disruptor);- Seeker (*this role isn't available to swap to until the Golden Snitch appears, which can happen at certain points throughout the match because grabbing one only grants you a large sum of points as opposed to winning the entire game at once, meaning you're also most likely the main person in charge of controlling the Chasers until that winged prize comes zooming in - you find the Golden Snitch and then start a chase scene where you try to stay as close as possible while bumping heads with the opposing Seeker).All in all it's a great game to play with a friend or two, even if you aren't that big on the HP universe but do enjoy the occasional arcade sports game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick info about the game: It's a lite Rocket League like game. The controls and mechanics are easier to learn, and (So far) easy to master. The controls are extremely responsive and ''Feel good''. But if you are NOT someone who's used to competitive sports game, do NOT buy this you WILL have a bad time. Aka: If your main games are Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing and you found Hogwarts Legacy's ''Normal'' difficulty a bit too harsh, this is not a game for you. If you fit the very specific player archetype this game targets (Enjoys Harry Potter universe, is a decent gamer, enjoys competitive/sports games) I do recommend this game, but can only partially recommend it. The lack of a true ranking system (bronze/silver/gold etc.) Is clearly a big minus. A competitive game of this nature NEEDS a ranking system. Players need a way to measure how they compare to others and whether or not their game is improving. Overall, this game is a 'Play it when you remember you have it, wake up the next day and forget it exists' kind of game. It is enjoyable in short bursts, but it lacks the feeling of personal skill progression that other games in the genre bring due to it's lack of "deep" game mechanics. Just temper your expectations. This is close to the Quidditch game the me from 15 years ago wished for, but it just isn't quite there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game at the present time. I think the game itself has a really good model and is actually pretty good, however, the problems outweigh the good currentlyFirst off, keep in mind this game, unlike others that you pay for, is 100% internet needed. What I mean is that 100% of the time you will need to be connected to the internet. If at any point the internet flickers you will be kicked out of the game at that precise second and will not be allowed back in until you restart the game with internet. Also, it's stated if you are connected to the WB server 100% of the time you will also have the same. This means that if the WB server flickers, and it's no fault on the players side, you will not be able to play this game.I know this first hand because I was about to win an advanced diffculty world cup mode game when it kicked me back to the opening screen and wouldn't allow me in, despite finding that the internet flickered for only a moment. That's the big one, and I can't recommend the game alone for that as players are going to want to play this offline quite a bit. There is hours and hours worth of single player content, from learning to play to playing the different houses and gaining skills. The only content that should be online is multiplayer and maybe the shop, if WB needs it that way. Basically there's an easy way to do this, dividing the online content from the offline content. Not difficult. Players know well if they don't have internet they can't play the online stuff and they accept that. There's a lot of offline players out there that are not looking to do multiplayer or otherwise.2. Lack of features: I'll say for this one the game honestly should've been put on early access in Steam first before hitting the market as a 1.0 steam game fully released. Yes, there was an alpha and beta but we all know how those go, and they barely listen to the players, only taking game code feedback so they can see "we need to fix glitches." If even that sometimes in the game industry. For this one I don't see glitches really so they did a good job there. Biggest notables on things they would've got feedback on to do and didn't:- Putting an option for traditional play: currently the game is setup with a max score of 100 pts, ending when that's reached or a timer runs out. Fans of HP who know quidditch obviously want the traditional experience, being able to catch the snitch for 150 points and ending the game when it's caught. They don't want a timer, and they want to play the game to the fullest in its traditional form. Why? Because they loved the game and history from the books and movies.                                  * the 100 points idea is a good one in the way they use it, making the snitch worth 30 and the game more focused on playing the quaffle, the keepers, and the beaters. This way everyone enjoys. It's a good formula and it works. Just pointing out a second mode should be made for traditional players. Probably just make the snitch much much harder to spot or only appearing for short periods at certain points where seekers really have to be on their toes. There are ways to make this all work- Being able to play as a country's, or school's, teammates: currently the game is setup where you make your own people to play as, depicted as you would personally like, and i do like that. The only thing I don't like is you have to play as them EVERYWHERE. No offense, but if I'm playing Durmstrang being able to use their teammates would be GREAT! cause I want to play Durmstrang, not my random mii character, same for Japan, or England, or any other country. There should be an option for this. Being able to take your own players everywhere is great, but a bit of customization on what teammates you take and don't also I think is where things would be better.                         Like, allow for one main of yours to be who you use on the team and the rest of your mii creations be left behind. Why? cause like Hogwarts Legacy the idea of creating your own character is more to make yourself feel like your experiencing and winning/losing vs an entire team of yous. No offense, but...I don't know if anyone else like me really wanted a whole bunch of yous running around, we just wanted one of us.Things to be aware of: - Seekers: There's a bit of rubber banding put in where even if they aren't doing the necessary things to build up their meter they are still keeping up with you and can be winning. At higher difficulty it's been more natural, but in the hogwarts schools be aware that if you play against Hufflepuff, Cedric Diggory, they for some reason build up the meter extra quick and there's nothing you can do to beat them at catching the snitch. A bit of game favoritism there I'm afraidSteam deck users be aware: Beaters cannot really use bludgers on steam deck, for some reason targeting does not work so basically beaters become useless except with the clubs. On PC there's some issues still there as well so be awareRegarding Chasers: when you start out tackling will be a pain, one thing that will help is there's a skill that helps targeting. Get close to a chaser before tackling and it will automatically line up your targeting for you.TLDR peeps: internet 100% needed to play this game, there should be options to play traditional quidditch, there should be an option to just take one of your players into a hogwarts team or any other rather than your whole mii team, seeker Cedric Diggory is glitched so you will lose just about every time, beaters cannot target on steam deck and there's slight issues on pc, chasers you need to get close to tackleEnding positives: the formula for this game actually is really well done, I will give them the credit that's due. It truly does feel like your experiencing each player position as you would on the field fully, and you can play as that player position the entire time, except the seeker.Review stupidities: Please for the love of everything do not bring up DEI. I've played through basically everything in this game, there is no DEI, so unless your that caught up in needing to see it, it doesn't exist here, your being an idiot for bringing it up. There is nothing political or otherwise in this gameNote specific towards WB: I got this game as one of the first players to play the game on steam literally right when it came out. There were a lot of negative reviews that came out causing the review meter to show mixed. WB deleted over 100 reviews in order to make the game look better. Don't care how WB feels about my review, it's true, if they don't like it they shouldn't have done stupid stuffEdit: Checking into countries we may be missing I found there aren't too many more teams they could do. The only missing ones I know of are Bulgaria and France from the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a Rocket League/Fifa Street/Mario Strikers type of game that you can jump on in to play a quick and fun match with brooms flying all around following the basic rules of Quidditch with the obvious Harry Potter theme in all aspects and background.The match has 6v6 players either on campaign/skirmish or PVP, at the moment when going to PVP 3 positions on each team will be AIs (planned on the roadmap for the future to add proper 6v6 with all humans), so you can queue and play as any of the game positions and you will have the option to switch to a Chaser at any time:■  Your aim is to grab the ball and pass it through your mates to score in one of the three rings to get +10 points for a goal;■   You can swap to defend the goal when it's getting pressure by the enemy team and thus dangerous by trying to intercept the ball or just straight kick it out of the goal (including kicking players out of there);■  Your objective will be to knock down key positions (e.g. Seeker almost getting the snitch, Chaser getting close to the goal with the ball) by either tackling them or throw a bludger■  Your aim will be to seek the snitch and follow its quick movement to catch it on time, which if you are able to do so you will get +30 points (instead of the book/movie rule of +150 and the match ending)The graphics and effects are good including when in fast motion and you have the option to create your own character for each position or you can also select on of the "hero" type skins that you can unlock as you play to use characters such as Harry, Ron, Hermione and even other like the members of the Weasley Family, Malfoy and so on.At the moment there are no micro-transactions and all items are only cosmetic and available directly to unlock aside from the cosmetics contained in the Deluxe pack and Twitch Drops, which of those you can get similar in the game and everything is unlockable through just playing and acquiring the in-game Gold currency as you play (which is not purchasable with real money aside from the 2000 gold that comes with the Deluxe but that just gives you a tiny head-start to buy be able to get some cosmetics from the start) as old school games would do - these go from different wands, brooms, headwear, eyewear, clothes, insignias, broom trails, goal score explosions, etc.As a note whether the game is a success and reaches its potential or straight up doesn't reach the height markers that it needs to, most likely this will be the last time that we will have the chance to get a proper Quidditch game since we had to wait 21 years for this one, so if you are interested at all try to give it a spin and see how you find it (it's free on PS+ this month for those that might have those services) and hopefully the devs will keep supporting the game and adding even more things to it as it was said in the roadmap (the aforementioned 6v6 with All humans since tactically that will be more interesting than the current 6v6 with 3 being AI, more stadiums, customizations, characters, etc).

_childDocuments_.review:
Your next chapter takes flight! Immerse yourself in the enchanting world of Quidditch by playing solo or sharing the magic with friends and family.

LIVE YOUR QUIDDITCH FANTASY
Take to the sky as one of the classic positions—Chaser, Seeker, Keeper, or Beater—each with their own unique play style. Soar into legendary Quidditch arenas, as well as maps that showcase never-before-seen areas of the wizarding world.

MULTIPLE WAYS TO PLAY
Career Mode: From backyard battles in the Weasley Burrow to high-stakes showdowns at the Quidditch World Cup, rise to become a champion either solo or in online co-op with teams of up to 3 friends.
Exhibition Matches: set your teams, map, and difficulty and play alone or on teams of up to 3 in online co-op.
Player vs Player: Test your skills in competitive online matches against other Quidditch teams.

YOUR QUIDDITCH YOUR WAY
Customize Your Approach: Level up and use skill points to tailor your play style for each role. Change your flight style by switching between and leveling up different brooms.
Play As Yourself or as Iconic Harry Potter Characters: cosmetic customization options and classic character designs allow you to express your game-time personality.

Everything costs money in the game, and they "turn the servers off" in order to force you to buy a new copy. So I played 22 until it was disabled (just as I made the NBA final series after 2 seasons after 2 years of 48 minute games). So, I hate 2K and what they do to basketball just because they have a monopoly. They turn basketball into some kind of garish Las Vegas casino. And it smacks you in the face as soon as you start 2K25. Everything is flashing and going kaching and there's strip malls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with go carts and funny shaped cheerleaders everywhere. You have 80,000 quests and 26 messages on your phone, and you are running around in a brown shirt because a t-shirt is the equivalent of 10 games' salary. It's just gross. If they didn't waste so much time trying to suck every dollar they can out of everyone, my avatar might not look like he just caught the short bus to a Mike Tyson fight. When Giddey hit 7 threes I couldn't suspend my disbelief any longer. The free throw difficulty is ridiculous for some reason. But so far it's good. I bought the $120 version so my guy started at 75 which made it a lot easier. I reckon 70 would be the sweet spot. All up I'm not unhappy with my decision to finally cave and buy this one after three years.*edit* ok, so I feel compelled to come back to this review. I found myself walking into the stadium all like "F^&*^ a Caldwell-Pope. And then I realised my emotions were being manipulated and I laughed. On the other side, the coach/player relationship is so cringe. 2K, just send me the script next time. I just can't understand how a company raking in THAT MUCH MONEY can't afford someone to head off the cheesy crap before its too late. I'll do it. _childDocuments_.review: My review is admittedly biased because I am an NBA junkie.  Solid 8/10.  Runs exceptionally well on the Steam Deck and on my aging i9 9900 system.  My only gripe with the game so far is that it feels as though it were optimized for the Steam Deck and not PCs.  An example being there is no way to run the game in 144hz, nor are there any exclusive full screen options.  I'm a big fan of the gameplay tweaks.  Now it feels as though your player is actually making hard cuts when on offense on/off ball.  Shooting is similar to the previous title, but the shot gauge is uglier and takes a bit to get used to.  Ball handling is more fluid, it feels as though there are more animations and cancels into different animations which makes for some fun shake n bake scenarios.

_childDocuments_.review: WE FINALLY GOT NEXT GEN ON PC!!!Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Pros:Enhanced Visuals with TrueView Technology: NBA 2K25 introduces TrueView, a new graphics engine upgrade that brings even more realism to player models, lighting, and crowd dynamics. Faces and movements have an uncanny realism, and the enhanced court environments make each game feel like watching a real broadcast. Stadium lighting and even arena-specific details contribute to an impressive overall look.Fluid Gameplay with Refined ProPLAY: Building on last year’s ProPLAY, NBA 2K25 has expanded real-life animations across more player movements and interactions, making transitions between actions smoother and more responsive. The result is a fluid experience where dribbling, shooting, and defending feel polished and natural, giving players more control in every possession.Legends Mode - Celebrating NBA’s Greatest: This new Legends Mode allows players to control the greatest players from various eras in NBA history, from Larry Bird to Shaquille O’Neal, with era-specific teams and rivalries. It’s an in-depth, nostalgic experience for long-time fans and a great introduction to NBA history for newcomers, featuring challenges and storylines based on iconic games and moments.Balanced MyCareer Progression: This year’s MyCareer mode has made notable improvements in progression balance. While VC is still part of the system, the grind for badges and attributes feels less intense, allowing players to develop their character without relying heavily on microtransactions. The storyline includes deeper branching narratives and more impactful choices, adding a nice RPG element.Crossplay & Enhanced Online Stability: NBA 2K25 has refined its crossplay capabilities across PC, Xbox, and PlayStation, improving matchmaking and enabling friends on different consoles to play together seamlessly. Server stability has seen noticeable improvement, and disconnects are less frequent, making online games more enjoyable and competitive.MyTeam Seasons & Dynamic Events: MyTeam has introduced seasonal challenges and dynamic events that align with real NBA events, like special challenges during the All-Star Weekend. New weekly rewards and updated card themes keep things fresh, and the removal of contracts continues to make team management more streamlined.Cons:Microtransactions Still Prominent: While progression has been balanced somewhat in MyCareer, the game still includes a heavy emphasis on microtransactions. VC is still used in nearly every mode, and while it's now slightly easier to earn, it can feel difficult to stay competitive in online play without spending real money.Limited Innovation in Core Gameplay: Though ProPLAY improves animation fluidity, the core mechanics remain largely unchanged. Veteran players might feel the gameplay loop has become predictable, with only minor adjustments from NBA 2K24. More variety in play styles or strategies would have helped keep the experience fresh.AI Inconsistencies: While the game’s AI has improved, there are still occasional moments where teammates make questionable decisions or the difficulty curve spikes unexpectedly, especially in MyCareer. Opponents sometimes feel overpowered in certain game modes, which can disrupt the overall balance.Grinding in MyTeam: Despite the addition of seasonal events, MyTeam remains grind-heavy. Unlocking high-tier cards without spending on microtransactions requires significant time investment, which could deter more casual players who want to stay competitive in the mode.Minor Server Lag: Although server stability has improved, minor lag persists, particularly in high-stakes online matches. This issue can impact shot timing and responsiveness, which is crucial in competitive games.Verdict: NBA 2K25 pushes the series forward with stunning visuals, refined animations, and exciting new features like Legends Mode, which is a treat for fans of the sport's history. The balanced progression in MyCareer is a welcome improvement, although microtransactions are still prominent. With better crossplay and more stable servers, the online experience is also more reliable. NBA 2K25 is a solid upgrade for both returning fans and new players, but the lingering reliance on VC and the familiar core gameplay may leave some wanting more substantial innovation.

And yet, version after version, 2K leaves us hanging.You'd think with the amount of money we’re dropping on this franchise, they'd prioritize ironing out these problems, but no—same old story. And don’t even get me started on the bugs that never get patched, but hey, they sure know how to push microtransactions in MyCareer, right? The real MVP of 2K is probably the guy who handles the in-game store.The frustration is real. 2K, you’ve had enough time. People aren’t going to put up with this forever. It’s not that the backlash isn’t coming—it’s just waiting for the right moment to hit.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is great! Thank you 2K for finally bringing us the new gen to PC.  Good graphics, access to all the features, good animations, good customization options, all the best modes, decent VC earning potential. Some of the broadcasting is tired but I don't mind it, they just need to continue to add to what they've had over the past 15 years and clean up some of the triggers so it's more relevant to game activities. I'm not a fan of rhythm shooting or perfect release "green" mechanics, but real % is available in the SP modes for those of us that like the strategy more than the timing. Multiplayer is heavily focused and match making sucks. I don't know why they don't have better lobbies and queues. The squad finder has literally never found me a squad. Highlighting each person in REC to find out what and how they play is tedious. There is no focus in finding 1-3-5 or 1-2-4 or 2-3-5 balanced teams. And why the heck do I need to sit in REC waiting to be invited into a team, just let me queue with my preferences and then walk about the city buying stuff or racing (very cool side activity btw). We need more mini game activities (darts, billiards, squirt guns, find the hidden item) to waste time while queued. I have no interest waiting court-side burning my XP boosts. Too much focus on squads and not enough focus on no-squads. I would love to be in a pro-am team, but getting an invite never happens and I don't want to build my own team. Where is the draft board that let's people select others (in their region, low latency, etc) based on their player DNA/Ratings/playtime/etc. ? If you are going to focus on multiplayer, for the love, make the queues and lobbies better. Wasting time standing around is not fun and doesn't promote game activity, it promotes idleness. Too many times I'm in a REC game and we have an idler which then turns into an AI, which then is exploited because they don't seem to have the same shot mechanics problems the rest of us are forced to use in MP games. AI players should use the player DNA of those that it's acting for. I expect the idle cutting 3 to play like that, not hold the ball and try to run plays (which never happens in MP). MP (online) is kind of a crap show anyhow, because it's just Big C rebounder/blocker and stupid long transition passes that are either dunked or stolen. Again, not fun. At least it's 5v5 though, 3v3 and 2v2 modes are even less fun, but somehow doesn't seem to suffer from the transition passing as much. I have so much more to say, so I'll edit it later. Oh and BTW I had 111hrs in before ever buying any VC stuff and was at lvl 22 in the season. I'll give more on the VC stuff later but tldr, bonus MT is decent, HOF is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: While overall there are general improvements when comparing to 2k21 (last played 2k), still can not recommend this game due to various flaws the online play has.To list some of them:- Controller settings reset randomly, in result, you almost automatically lose the match;- Impossible to rebind buttons, it would always say that something is unbound when everything is obviously still bound to every recognized controller;- Hands up defence is weaker than running into people's faces or space, makes 0 sense;- Events and event courts are broken (too many issues to list here, plus do not forget about your controller settings resetting randomly during a streak). Overall poorly executed (minus the blackout one, but that also had some very tedious tasks, if you were unlucky). And you also have skill based matchmaking here, so the best strategy is to cheese the system by creating new characters which have 0 skill level, even 60 overall characters being strong due to bugged courts;- Skill based matchmaking is present in casual game modes (e.g. Rec, Theater), while missing in the more competitive ones (e.g. Pro-AM), in result, it is almost impossible to find matches in Theater, the same goes for Solo Rec;- There was an active VC glitch for at least 24 hours (or longer), not sure if anyone got any punishment for abusing it, but there was no public statement about it as far as I know.- Still missing crossplay, which would be a great improvement.- VC can be somewhat quickly acquired, if you know the best mycareer grinding method. But it is a mindless grind, and still you need to grind a decent amount to max out one character to 99. Online play modes offer really low VC rewards (maybe minus 3x3 Pro-AM). Also, the daily and weekly quests are almost impossible to complete, even for a regular player.Some positives or improvements noticed:- There is less blatant cheating present;- There are less connectivity or crashing issues;- The shooting change is overall a good change;- The steals are really good this year (but sometimes a bit inconsistent and illogical), idiots can no longer get away with really bad passes;- Badge progression and system is much better than in the older versions;- The new rebirth also is a good improvement for people who want to play more than a single build;- The city looks nice and is overall compact without much wasted space, plus the kartings are cool. The 1 mil first place VC prize in the track is not though, should give something to top10 instead, maybe a bit more for top3.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good, the Bad, the UglyStarting off, just like to say i was excited about this game taken its been years since I played my last 2k game back 7-8 years ago. Starting the game needed patience. The download is HUGE... by huge I mean 150g worth of download and even with high speed internet it will take close to an hour. Then you think ok, its done lets start.... WRONG. Wait another 20-25 min for the shaders to download. (apparently everytime you re-start the game the shaders need to re-download again and again (quicker then the first time but you still need to wait).Game Start -  First big no-no. The quick succession of rapid flashing lights and colors while you wait for My Team or other parts of the game to load will make people who don't have epilepsy suddenly feel they are about to acquire it. The guy who did this should be fired IMMEDIATELY. (no joke, I have to look away every time this script starts and I don't have any epileptic issues).Moving on: Way too many moving parts, menus upon menus and micro-transactions for everything ($)There are so many parts you literally wont have a clue where you need to go unless you are a seasoned veteran in NBA 2k.I have to spend time watching online videos so I could familiarize myself with every part of the game because nothing in the game will explain things to the extent needed.Bugs - there are a few but I think the most annoying one is the one where you cant exit My Team. It says press (A) to exit but nothing. You need to shut down the whole game ( good luck with any progress you made till then cause it will all be lost ). Honestly, rolling out a $100 game where the save & exit from game doesn't work is beyond insane, its comical.Then the music ... not going to get into that but lets just say latin-rap isn't my go-to.The good: After all the bad things, it was very hard to get excited about anything really, but i will still mention some things I liked. The game is smooth (maybe a little too smooth with alot of animations kicking-in when you do some moves. (I have a high-end PC so not sure if its smooth with all users especially on different platforms), but I had no issues with lag or anything else. Although I must say when transitioning to different highlighted parts of the game there is a small delay. (est 10-15 seconds at most which i did not expect accompanied by the rapid flashing lights and colors and annoying music!).Therefor, overall I cannot give this game a passing grade at this point in time. I will keep playing it and hope some things will get fixed and the game experience is at least enjoyable. Im optimistic, while also realistic that this could be the worst +$100 game I ever bought.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but the same innate issues that have plagued 2k for over half a decade still plague the game today. (This will fully be going from a MyCareer/Park perspective)This game feels in the range of decent to pretty good in terms of gameplay. Not great or amazing, but decent/pretty good. If you don't have experience playing 2k before, I could see this game being tedious and more of a hassle than a basketball game. Unless you spend $100 more to max out your character (and a cool fit is another $20 lol)Also a big question people have is, do people play the game? So far in 3 weeks. Yes. But if you want games fast/consistently you can really only play park. Rec takes a good 5-10 minutes for a game. Proving Grounds is inconsistent but in 1v1/2v2 it's pretty fast. In 3v3 it's around 2-3 mins. 5v5, impossible. Not many people go to the theater. And starting 5? Good luck with that.  I also see people complaining about optimization issues? I run an i7-8770k and a 1660super and run 90 frames no problem, yea it's at lowest settings but there's really been no issues. But I wanted to address that here. ALSO THE TRACK HAS BEEN BROKEN FOR 2 WEEKS, CAN WE PLEASE FIX?-------------GAMEPLAY-------------The shooting is definitely a problem this year, however if you use rhythm shooting/pro stick shooting the results get a lot better. Although a learning curve, I became a lot more consistent in park after switching to this setting. (54% 3p -> 62%3p). I also recommend REALLY optimizing your custom jump-shot, your release speed at the end doesn't matter as much. Your base and release 1/2 matter much more.On-top of that, in controller settings, change your shot/layup timings. For whatever reason, the game autos to difficulty-based so no matter how good your jumpshot timing is, the fate is determined by the difficulty of the gamemode you are playing. I recommend "normal-risk timing" as it's the most relative to older 2k games. Why don't they tell you any of this? I DONT KNOW!!!The finishing feels iffy, at least on lay-ups. It seems no matter how high your layup is this year, your player will just smoke wide-open layups once in a while. I know it happens in real life, but in game it happens a lot more than i think an NBA player (especially our myplayer who's supposed to be the goat) would actually allow. Dunks/alley-oops seem pretty strong this year. Not overpowered, but if you want your player to dunk and they have really good dunk ratings, as long as you have animations your player will just yam it if you have the space. It's pretty nice. Dribbling feels nice (if you're annoyed with constant hand switching, turn off passive dribble hand switching in controller settings) it seems a lot more authentic at least in the way you are able to chain together/combo moves. However speedboosting is still an innate problem that never seems to go away, so "meta" dribble moves will always be used the most/have most value. However, I've tried plenty of dribble sets with a 90 ball handle and gotten value in park/rec/proving grounds/etc with unique stuff I made on my own. If you have lower than a 60 ball handle, be ready to get the ball stolen A LOT. Defense matters this year, I mean it when I say it if you don't have AT LEAST an 80 perimeter defense going against a 95+ ball handling guard, you are going to get blown by, ankles took, you name it.The same applies to the interior, I'd say if you aren't at AT LEAST a 75 (you get a good amount of defense badges at this spot) your contests and interior defense will just be wildly inconsistent.Block/steal matter a good amount too, you can notice your character get better animations if you have a 75 block comparing to say a 93 block. Same applies to steal, bronze interceptor with 67 steal will never get the same value as 87 steal with gold interceptor. (Last I played in 2k20, it really didn't matter if you were good enough)No matter how skillful you are, your badges/attributes will hold you back. Your physical attributes matter too, I've seen a 5'9 guard with 70 strength body a 6'5 guard that clearly had no strength while dribbling and it was hilarious. So i'd at least say have decent strength, you don't need to max it out but don't have it at 25. Agility matters if you're someone who likes fade aways, step-backs, creative shots in general, while also helping your perimeter defense A LOT (pick dodger) Speed matters for dribbling, and vertical matters for interior finishing/defense (rise up, posterizer, pogo stick)-----------------------CORE OF THE GAME-----------------------2k is still the same, microtransactions that make you want to refund soon as you open the game, cheesy dribble moves behind screens, your player getting a stupid animation, it's almost impossible as a no money spent player unless you spend 60+ hrs a week. Microtransactions have actually gotten WORSE over the years, much worse actually. Watch "NBA 2k Really Needs a Competitor" by Fireplace Gaming on Youtube to truly gain some more insight on how awful it's gotten. Cheesy animations will always be in the game, it's not really a complaint. It's a video game in 2024, people will always use the best things they can use. People have been using the best things in 2k since 2k15 park when everyone was a 7'0 demigod, so this aspect will just never change. I will say, sometimes your player gets forced into a dribble animation, bump animation, drive animation, and as much as you want to pass or shoot at a certain point, you get delayed SO much. Not being able to have control over your player when you want to sucks, especially because these delays have so much variance. Sometimes it's .25 seconds, .5, 1, 2, sometimes even 3 yes THREE seconds. Finally, if you're going to go into mycareer being no money spent. You will genuinely lead a one person journey into the deepest depths of hell. I am not overexaggerating. I will say there are A LOT of ways to make VC this year. Complete your quests, if your player averages crazy stats you can sim mycareer to progress in the goat/dynasty stuff for a bunch of VC/awards ontop of shoe endorsement every season, free wheel spin prizes have been pretty good this year i've made 30k VC alone in only 3 weeks from it. Do the track every week, it's a free 2500 VC. MAKE SURE TO CLAIM YOUR SEASON PASS AWARDS. Even if you're a free to play player, the very first tier gives you 15000 VC straight out the gate. After completing all the entry stuff + redeeming the 15k, you can start the game pretty much at around a 70 overall. Regardless of all these methods to acquire VC, once you reach around 85 overall things REALLY slow down. Just for reference, you will need around 450k VC (accounting for attributes AND animations) to fully max out a player. That is $100, and if you spend that out the gate your player is still only maxed out at 85 because you haven't done your MyPlayer caps yet from playing the game. I will say at least badges are super easy this year. -----------------CONCLUSION-----------------Genuinely if the game took a step-back on microtransactions and actually had more of a "grind" system in place it'd be more fun. Realistically no rookie going into the league that's some prodigy is going to be a 60 overall, can we at least start at an 80 so we can play the game somewhat without spending money? I kinda wish MyCareer games had a bit more purpose. The game is fun, I like a lot of the experiences I've had playing both guard and center but the fact there's so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with microtransactions and settings could make it some of the worst experiences for first time players. Experienced players expect it, but that's a whole other problem in its own.
