_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I've played 2K on PC since 2K13, have every game but 22 and 24, but my most recent is 23 so most comparisons will be 23 vs 25. I've only played a game in MyCareer but I've played a few in MyNBA/League, which is my most played mode across all 2Ks. Will potentially update review as time goes on.So far this has been a love/hate relationship. I'd say I probably recommend the game 55/45 to those who want to buy a new 2K title. If you're content with the current title you own, wait on sale to purchase 25.I am loving that PC finally gets Next Gen, the mechanics/movement feels like I have more control over my individual player than previous titles. The floaty feeling you get when controlling your player feels more momentum based this year. The animations look more clean/fluid and less like a programmed animation. Dribbling has more of a learning curve than in previous titles, at least in my opinion, but that's mostly the "new" player movement and different Pro Stick configuration than in 23. Timing your shot has more of an effect, feels less RNG, and make the visual gameplay look more immersive. Having access to Next Gen also brings the new animations that PC never had access to, making the game feel more like an actual NBA game. More detailed signature moves from dribbling to shooting.I am also loving the added customization options to players. More body types and physical trait editing (neck length, "trunk" length lol), the option to now add tattoos to created players, makes the rosters feel more accurate to life with less bland/generic 2K created players that are just bald/close cut with no tattoos.Now for the undesirable/hate part. The HUD is not visually pleasing to me. It's a bit too "busy" while trying to stay minimalistic. Everything is crammed into one location (shot feedback, score, time, and stats) are on one banner/ticker at the bottom of the screen that isn't very big. The in-game play calling menu (plays, sets, freelance, etc. menu) is difficult to get used to. In previous titles, it was a bigger menu with good contrast to the floor so it's noticeable. In 25 it's smaller with a transparent background, making it a bit of an eyesore to use. There are simultaneously more and less options as well. Some options that were in previous games, like "Set Screen" are no longer a default option, so you have to add it in the coaching menu, but you can now call specific plays for said player in the same menu section instead of having two separate menus for actions. My biggest issue with it is that there is no in-game menu on defense, so you have to pause the game to adjust the defense "on the fly". The only options on D now are full/half court sets and individual player settings (who to guard, defensive pressure).The menu HUD in MyNBA is not great. Visually it is a bit different since it's one small menu that pops up and isn't an entire screen of it's own. The main issue though is the moving between options. It'd be easier to use if you could maneuver through the option with directional input, but you can only progress or backtrack with A/X and B/O. Furthermore, if you enter a menu option and back out, you have to re-enter the menu again from the start. It will remember your last option, and automatically highlight the last option entered, but it's just a small QOL change if you could move through the menu more fluidly. VC is horrible, but that's to be expected in 2K. I made a save file to see how bad the VC rates are this year, and to my non-surprise, it's grindy as all get out. Still the standard 1k~ VC for a game played in MyNBA, but only gives you one or two upgrades in MyC. Took me 550-ish VC to upgrade my 60 OVR player from a 55 3pt to a 56.Lastly, and my biggest gripe, is the graphics/performance. I don't have the beefiest PC (RTX 3060, Ryzen 5 3600X, 32 GB RAM) but from some digging it seems even beefy PCs struggle. High vs Medium setting didn't make much of a difference besides making the game look visually worse. Menus I get 120-144 FPS, cutscenes are 30, and in game I average around 58-70 FPS. My frames are never stable so the game looks a bit janky at times. VSYNC doesn't help because it actually syncs with your monitor (like it should, crazy 2K got this right) instead of the basic 60 FPS most devs program. Fluctuating frames and no way to stabilize them makes the game hard to play at times, whether it be making my motion sickness act up or just getting the timing down for movements. Close up the details really pop and look good, but all together the game looks like an earlier PS4 title. There's no solid anti-aliasing, which can definitely be seen when you're viewing more than just half-court.If they fix the FPS/performance issues, I'd rate the game a solid 7.8/10, but until then I'll have to give it a 6.5/10. A real improvement over previous titles that unfortunately has it's own issues still. If you can wait until a sale to purchase, I would, but I'd also say this is a 2K definitely worth getting on PC if you have the desire.Edit: Set all the setting to high, but most optional. Went into NVidia Control Panel to set the anti-aliasing on, capped FPS to 60, maxed performance. Helped the visual performance a lot. Arena's, at least for MyNBA, have been consistently at around 35-40% capacity for the first 3 and a half quarters, only filling up to 60-80% at the last half of the 4th if the game is close.Edit: Seems like they fixed the arena capacity issue. Most games are now the appropriate attendance level.

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all : I've played 2K forst the first time in 2011 with 2K12, I bought it every year until 2K17 on console. I came back on PC when 2K23 was on sale, but it was old gen that was just to play offline and enjoy it alone.As 2K25 is finally next-gen on PC, I bought it day one, as I wanted to experience another full year of 2K since day one, and honestly I'm not surprised but still disapointed about ONE thing : 2K has the worst playerbase in all sports game industry.2K has finally worked on gameplay, and not just a little bit, they made the pro-play, which is a huge improvement, and even more if you play offline, that thing makes the game much more enjoyable as players really have their own style of dribbling.You may think this is the biggest addition gameplay-wise but it's not, in recent years, 2K have struggled with cheaters, and not just on PC but also on consoles with something called " Zen " which was basically an shooting-bot that was based on the timing of your shot, cheaters couldn't midd an open shot. Since the timing was always the same, a cheater could never get banned as the cheat was litterally coming from their modded controller.So 2K said " **** that " and made 6 different shot timings depending on your shooting form, and made a new way of shooting called " Rhythm shooting " that's where the true game changer is. It's a new way of shooting based on your skill level and instead of releasing the shot based on a timing that you'd know by heart, it forces you to release the shot based on your shooting animation. Rhythm shooting is a new way to shoot with stick that makes the game much more skill based, old sweaty players in the majority hate it cause they hate that they have to learn something new, but they got what they finally asked for which is the end of cheaters using third party controllers, and also a new shooting system that creates a skill gap and that FEELS like shooting instead of just mechanically repeating the same shot with the same timing. You can still shoot with the button press, it's still possible and to this day, I think most players still shoot with this, but mostly because they're not accepting to change their habits ( Proof that they didn't want a new game from 2K since whenever they make a major change, they just ignore it ) If you're a new player I recommend you getting used to Rhythm shooting as you'll be rewarded with a larger " green window " and a funnier way to play.For us, PC players, we also received some recognition. During the first days of playing I did encountered some cheaters in park ( Not zen users ) with 60 overall players that suddenly had all the badges once the game started. I thought " **** the game is already plaged with cheaters " not even one week after day one, 2K released a patch, that ban-waved a lot of cheaters, and I never met any cheaters since then ( Let's hope it continues that way ) and I think SOME of the negative reviews are actually some of the cheaters that got banned, I've seen some reviews saying they were ban for " nothing " ( Sure we all get banned for nothing )On the negative points, yes I would add that indeed, in MyCareer, grinding VC can feel long, especially since nowadays a lot of people accepted the idea of micro-transactions and are willing to pay to max their player even if their build is failed, so it can feel frustrating if you're not willing to pay for VC but still wanna play Park or other online MyCareer related modes.I didn't have any regular crash as some of the other reviews says, I have no idea why or if I'm " lucky " I didn't even touch any settings related to performance and everything was set to maximum in graphics. I'd say that if you feel like your PC won't handle the game don't buy it or you can still refund if you crash during your first 2 hours, but I have a feeling this kind of reviews are from either people who think they can play on potato or those who have been banned from the banwave for cheating.So to make everything short : This playerbase will complain if the game don't change, but will also complain when the game changes and forces to change their habits. Make your own opinion, if you're a player from previous editions, open your mind and accept to play a different way, if you're a new player have fun, and play the tutorial before everything.

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K25, the latest installment in the long-standing basketball simulation series, unfortunately falls short of the high expectations set by its predecessors. Despite the game’s potential, it emerges as a disappointment for both longtime fans and newcomers to the franchise.From a technical standpoint, NBA 2K25 struggles with several persistent issues that undermine the overall experience. The game suffers from noticeable bugs and performance inconsistencies that detract from its realism. Frame rate drops and stuttering, even on high-end systems, are frequent and disruptive. Additionally, the AI behavior, which is crucial for a sports simulation, remains problematic. Opponent and teammate logic often feels erratic and unrealistic, leading to frustrating gameplay scenarios that detract from the immersion.The graphical enhancements, which were anticipated to be a highlight, fail to deliver a significant upgrade. The player models and animations, while detailed, do not exhibit the level of refinement one would expect from a modern release. Furthermore, the presentation elements, including the commentary and in-game visuals, lack innovation and feel recycled from previous versions. This stagnation is particularly disheartening given the rapid advancements in gaming technology.NBA 2K25’s MyCareer mode, a fan-favorite feature, is marred by a convoluted progression system and an excessive focus on microtransactions. The monetization strategy employed within this mode feels particularly intrusive, overshadowing the enjoyment of the core gameplay. Similarly, the MyTeam mode’s reliance on card packs and additional purchases has shifted the focus away from skill-based play, which diminishes the overall satisfaction.The game's attempts at introducing new features and modes fall flat, as they often feel underdeveloped or poorly integrated. The lack of substantial innovation and the failure to address longstanding issues contribute to a sense of stagnation rather than progress.In conclusion, NBA 2K25 does not meet the expectations of a franchise known for its attention to detail and commitment to delivering a high-quality basketball simulation experience. Its numerous technical issues, outdated graphical presentation, intrusive monetization practices, and lack of meaningful innovation render it a disappointing entry in the series. Fans of the NBA 2K franchise may find themselves disheartened by this release, which fails to advance the series in a meaningful way.

_childDocuments_.review: Next gen finally came to PC. I refunded the game last year and made a negative review. Feels like our combined efforts paid off. This means city access, shootaround pregame, entering arena via the tunnel,.MyCourt is back with a ball machine by default. After being fed the exact same game basically 4 times in a row, there's a significant difference in the way this feels. I dont feel helpless starting out. My guy can actually make shots without having 3-point shot maxed. Players move and collide more realistically. Ball hits the rim more realistically with large variety of possibilities, physics-wise. There's also a new more-dynamic camera setting that players might actually use, instead of being stuck with default 2K camera. Quality of life improvements galore. Too many to list, but they finally changed the half-time shows and music. Finally took that goofy jingle out of the game with the dancing little kids. You're able to skip sooner during time-outs, half time, and free throws. Exiting games is also lot faster. Ingame simulation actually works while you're on the bench. Doesn't get stuck. I might change my mind later on if I run into some bad business practices, but as someone who mostly does MyCareer, this is easily the best 2k in the last 5 years easy, especially if you've been on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Jumping from the ps4 port thats been the last few years of 2k on PC to the supposed next-gen version was exciting at first. It would go without saying that we would finally get an update to the molasses netcode thats plagued online play since 2k14, finally get an anti-cheat since obviously cross-play would be a thing, finally get a visual overhaul to the wax statue character models and ps3 era crowds. Only half of one of those things came true. The Gameplay in this game is 1 step forward and 18 steps back. Everyone has hated the RNG jumpshot timing that has gone along with the always inconsistent shot contests and how it made every player whos not Steph Curry feel like a freshman AAU player shooting the ball. In what i can only rationalize as trying to stop the cheesers and spammers online spamming broken jumpshot builds, 2k has now made all jumpshots with all players have randomly changing green windows throughout a game and even in practice. Whoever had this idea should be fired from the dev team. It makes the gameplay feel like you have even less control then before as you are at the mercy of RNJesus to make a wide open 3 with Kyrie Irving or Ben Simmons (both seemingly can shoot the same percentages now). While everything moves and flows more realistically now, it somehow feels more rng then ever. The game will slow your fastbreak player down if a defender is gonna get the chasedown block on you. When RNJesus decides that the offense is gonna grab 3 straight offensive boards and score on the third, theres nothing you can do no matter how good of a defense you play. Bigs still cannot finish in the post over small guards consistenly and havent been able to for 4 years now which is just maddening. You feel like you can only be effective as an aggressive downhill driving guard or a Wemby build bigman and everyone else may as well be a created player on the classic teams. Its just sad to watch the slow butchering of a once perfect gameplay foundation 2k had. This is the least amount of fun ive had with a 2k since 2k15 on ps3........real ones know.For being such an aggressive resource hog, this game really doesn't look very good. for 15 years now, 2k has been unable to make hair look at all realistic, and while the crowds and benches look better, the courts still look worse then 2k15-17 and the face scans range from decent to fugly. Menus are laggy, load times range from normal to 40 seconds with so many shutters and freezes i think its crashing nearly every time i load up a play now. MYEras is a good idea, just not done well at all. Why do i have to start a whole MyEras save file and choose to run every single team just to look at each team's rosters and practice with them? Is it because the majority of these teams have 6-8 real players and the rest are bum 56-68 ovr created players who are useless in a game? Why is it that when you go into practice you only see real courts in mygm and otherwise you get the boring and stale 2k practice court? Why do half the Myera courts stay in one style for 3 plus eras despite the real courts of the time looking nothing like the ones in game? If you are gonna do something like this do it right. Myteam is slop as usual, and with how frustratingly bad the gameplay has gotten, i have no desire to go deep into mycarrer. Its the same as its always been, only now with somehow even more cheaters and hackers. 2K refuses to give us cross-play because then they would have to develop and use a real anti-cheat and that would take time and effort. Its just sad that PC players are somehow treated worse then Madden PC players. this is the first 2k since 2k12 (my first) where i have no desire to drop any extra cash, play deep into a mygm or mycarrer, or do much of anything beyond the occasional casual game with buddies. Shooting is the worst its ever been, the spam online is somehow worse then ever, and myeras is half baked and pointless with how few teams have more then 6 players. You also cant just play a single season variant of MYGM which sucks for those of us who just wanna mess around with drafting different rosters from different eras and play without the annoying ownership and team whining nonsense. Add on top of that the always present 60-100 extra bucks you have to spend to be able to do much of anything in mycareer, and i think that may finally be tapping out of this series in a couple years. Its not the same anymore. I want to be able to go online and play with netcode that feels like it was made this decade, without cheaters, and actually be able to hit a wide open 3 with my own skill and not RNJesus. This game just makes me sad now when it used to be the most fun i had gaming with my buddies. What a shame.  3/10

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K25 highlights more than other 2K iteration the lack of care for any game mode other than the cash-grab, VC driven online modes. The fact that substitutions were broken on day-one and are still broken shows that not only are they in no rush to fix such a basic and blatant issue, but prior to release they didn't play test anything other than online. Either that or they were aware of the issue and were content to push out a broken product because their only concern is how much money they can rake in from online play.And this really is the tip of the iceberg. Player ratings are a joke with zero attention payed to defensive ratings that might actually reflect reality. Defensive AI also remains broken, and whilst people have claimed the offensive AI is better, multiple times a quarter I will watch isolation plays where the AI dribbles around like an idiot for 15 seconds before making the worst shot attempt you could imagine.You will also see players blatantly ignore an open player just to complete the running of a set-play. 2K talked a lot about how the players now act like people, and that might be true in online when they're controlled by people, but in any other mode they continue to function as ones and zeros, moving through a predetermined set of animations, showing very little 'intelligence'.Is dribbling better? Sure. But off-ball body contact animations are ridiculous. When moving your player will be pulled off the line you're running and forced into a body contact with a screener or just any random body that happens to remotely close to you. Not to mention watching players glide several feet across the court to somehow end up under the basket for a lay-up, or watching your defender glide several feet away from the attacking player giving them an open lane.You'll also take great pleasure in watching every NBA record fall because only one or two players on every team will actually take shots, rebounds or assists. This isn't helped by the lack of substitutions with but even on a per 36 minutes basis the teams key players average over 30 shot attempts per game, and centres will average 18 rebounds a game.These are only a few of the problems with playing 2K25 outside of the online 'arcade' mode.For those who aren't taken in by the online play and are looking for a realistic basketball game wait until the game is on sale and the community has released complete player attribute and tendency reworks along with MyNBA and gameplay sliders that actually make the game playable. Unfortunately it's on 2K to fix the substitution problem.In short, I load this game up cursing myself for liking basketball and being hooked into playing it despite how exceedingly mediocre it is. As usual our hopes now rest with the community of modders and testers who will manage to make another steaming pile of S**t from 2K playable.

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time the game on PC is Next-Gen, which means that all the new features are there. If you're an offline player or basketball enjoyer or both, then the game is awesome, I'm actually having a blast, which is something I didn't thought was possible again with 2k. The myNBA Eras feature is awesome, sure, it'd be better if one could start at any point in time and sooner in NBA history, who knows, maybe Kareem doesn't turn out to be the best scorer of All Time until LeBron or something like that, anyways, it's awesome. I played a couple of myCareer games and spent a total of one hour in front of loading screens for/in theCity which is horrible, but I don't play online anymore so I don't care that much, just know that it's a cash grab with very little improvements from the year before (except for the game-play, but I'll touch on it later).TheW my career (WNBA) is refreshing and a good idea of what an offline myCareer should be. No cutscenes, no wandering for an hour in the city to buy 10k VC Shoes, just playing games and growing your player the league, while having an eye on your legacy. (Kinda like the older Madden with the legacy ladder, you earn more legacy points by meeting requirements, stat lines and WNBA Records, pretty neat). TheW game-play really shines, it's slower and obviously less athleticism but they made it really fun and realistic. I didn't touch and most definitely never touch myTeam.Before I start on myNBA, let me say that the gameplay is awesome, easily the best NBA I've ever played, new animations that seamlessly integrate with the flow of the game, new players on the field scale, better spacing, defenders are smart and intercept passes playing the lane, they cut. You really can let the AI shine in this one. It is a beauty creating playbooks and playing as an offensive facilitator, spreading the ball around and setting up teammates for easy shots from the mid, three or making them cut to the rim for an easy oop. Really a thing of beauty. I saw Akeem Olajuwon get an offensive rebound near the rim and as soon as he touched ground he exploded back up for a dunk all in one motion, no hesitation, no animation to connect, no hitch, just jump, rebound, down and up again to bring the rim home and put in my bedroom type of beauty. Wonderful.  myNBA is where the game really shines, you can do everything here, from just simming years and years to see if MJ and the Bulls can dominate the 90s again, the 2000s Lakers and Spurs dynasties and the deadball era,to the 2010s and Lebron, Curry and KD. You can take control and rebuild teams, or watch it all unfolds, or play a multi-generation myCareer just like I'm doing. Your imagination is (almost all the times) the limit.For example:My dad was a basketball player, so it made sense to me to create him and follow his career by player-locking to him and sometimes play key games, then when his career will be set and done and he will retire, I'll sim until 2020 and I'll create and draft myself and a few years later my little brother, then we'll see how our careers unfold. Does this take time to set up and get it up and running? Hell yeah, sometimes it's a pain and I found out the hard way that it's better to download and import each year's draft class, otherwise non licensed players will be auto generated rookies which will break immersion. Luckily there's a custom draft class for every year of the sim with around 30-35 players created and curated so it's pretty good, sometimes you'll stumble into a 2nd round auto generated pick which plays 5 minutes a game but it's passable to me.There are some things to polish though, one important one is that injuries are too quick to recover. Players with a broken leg come back in 3 weeks when the estimate is 6 to 8 weeks, and there seems to be no final solution as of now, there's an injury length slider but it seems to not work, also, but this is something I've got to verify, it seems that when you force out of retirement some players they disappear (?). As I said, I've got to verify it, but Larry Bird and Magic are nowhere to be found in my record books which is really weird, since they both played until 39-40 years old. TL:DR: offline player? Game's good, maybe not worth full price but that'll be up to you, with mods the game will be awesome. online player? not worth full price, myCareer is a slog and it's full of bloat, same as myTeam.

The game looks much better and runs much better... most of the time. While I'm pleased with this change, I do not believe 2K earns any goodwill this change. I can excuse 2k21 since that was the transition game, but 2k22, 2k23, and 2k24 being Current Gen was an awful decision. It's inexcusable that it took until halfway through the PS5/XSX cycle to get it.Second: The gameplay and animations are overall much smoother. The stars feel a lot more like themselves than they ever have before. LeBron plays like himself, Jimmy plays like himself, KD plays like himself, and so on. That's not to say there aren't frustrating moments in gameplay like there is every year, but it's generally better than it has been in recent years.Third: I really do not like the changes made to shooting this year. I don't like that the green window is completely gone in many circumstances. Getting a "slightly early/late" when I shot at the right time is frustrating and it makes me doubt my timing- leading to me missing more shots trying compensate due to the false feedback. I don't like that you can do everything right- you can be wide open, you can have a high 3PT rating, and you can time your shot perfectly- but you still miss. That doesn't making the game more challenging. That makes the game something I don't want to play.Fourth and final: The bugs are killing this game. The substitution bug plaguing all modes is game-breaking. The bug makes it so you don't get subbed out in MyCareer (and neither do your teammates nor the opposing team's players) and your coaches won't make subs in modes in other modes while you play 5v5. This is likely done because the devs wanted to make it so you don't get benched while you're heating up, but they implemented it in the most obtuse way ever and broke the game.Defensive matchups are not saving. For example, if I put my SF to guard their PG, my PG will guard their SF. I I move my PG to guard their SG instead, then my SF matchup will be erased and somebody else will guard the PG instead. This was never a problem in prior 2Ks and I have no clue how the devs even managed to implement this bug.What were the game testers doing this year? How was this not caught and fixed before the release? Why are we still a week in and this isn't fixed? These bugs are enough for me to not recommend this game to other people. If they gets fixed, I'll revisit my review.

_childDocuments_.review: 2K finally updated PC to next gen and introduced a bunch of changes making the game much more accessible for offline and casual players like me. The WNBA modes are some of the best in the game. the W career mode is like the offline MyCareer that I would have wanted, similar to way back when before microtransactions became so invasive in the rest of the game. MyCareer was fun, having to only play key games which affect badges and your dynasty is a great idea. The offseason options helped keep the career mode interesting too. I managed to influence some trades by suggesting expendable players with high potential who could grow with me after my team aged up. It took me 5 seasons to get goat status and grind to 99 overall with no money spent on VC. I liked the city as it didn't affect performance much and we got the go kart early on. The streetball challenges were fun and prepared me for coop and park games even though usually stay away from multiplayer modes. MyNBA and Eras with the next gen upgrade are a welcome change and has kept things interesting. MyGM mode is arguably worse than before with just a minor design change. There's a lot to be done to make this mode even decent. MyTeam is still microtransaction heavy but its where I spend most of my playtime now as the auction house is back and helps to avoid the pack market. That said, the auction house is pretty empty and I don't think the time lag between transactions helps. I also tried a couple of multiplayer challenges which went smoothly except that the park was very empty whenever I logged in. Overall, one of the best NBA2K games in recent memory. Every mode is fun except MyGM. Great for offline or casual players. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: ***I was looking for a more arcade style game and that was my mistake.*** I am not the target audience for this game. I bought it to play with friends that were really into this franchise and what I bought was a game that will take hundreds of hours for me to get just average at it. Everything I am saying is my own perspective and will only be for those that don't usually play 2K games. My LARGEST issue is the cost to get into the game. You can either spend over $100 dollars (after purchase of the game) to increase your players stats buy buying skill points. OR you can level your character up by playing the game and earning points. So, it is kinda pay-to-win(ish). It will always have more to do with skill than stats and that is what keeps most people coming back, IMO. BUT in order to level up without spending real world money, you will be spending a very significant amount of time grinding out progress (probably 100+ hours). That is not a commitment I am willing to make. Some will be fine with that and actually enjoy it - different strokes.The HUB city area is just chaos to me. It seems like a terrible version of an open-world RPG. You have to walk from store to store (and other areas) in order to buy, train and practice. It is not something I appreciate. I would just prefer to purchase items in a menu that does not require that I memorize a specific store's location. The map and fast travel are poop-doodie and seem to ignore all of the clever ways RPGs have learned to make an open-world map. I also did not much care for the music library as a whole. There are some bangers, but there are also a lot of music I can do without. You can choose what songs play and can mute the music overall, which is good. I only have selected like 15-20 songs that I am willing to listen to and after hearing them 3-4 times in a play session, I am done with all of them.THIS IS NOT A VERY LEGITIMATE COMPLAINT (as much as it is just something that I would like to see)- with AI language technology being where it is, why do we still have to select from such a limited library of recorded names/nicknames? It reminds me of Fight Night and that game is 13 years old and Fight Night had many more nicknames available at that time. I h8 hearing my character called "MP" as default if I chose not to select from one of the available nicknames and have a name that isn't already recorded. BASICALLY: If you are a 2K fan, you are probably good with this game. Some of my friends are all about it. For a person that is a casual sports gamer I have to encourage you to stay away. You may get some playable hours out of the campaign and quick matches. But when you find yourself playing multiplayer it will not take you more than 2 matches before you realize the learning curve is as dramatic as playing the sport IRL. If you can get it on sale, give it a try. If you spend full price, you are just going to get a more expensive lesson in humility. Prepare to be faced with the choice to slog through the hundreds of hours it will take to "GIT GUD"; or get used to being clowned by some pretty "toxic" 2K-bros on how garbage you are.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, we can play 2k on PC without having to play an outdated version.For context on my review, I mostly do play-now at max rank and have at least 2000 games on every 2k since 2k18. My review is completely centered around the high level casual-competitive environment this game provides and is not related to the experiences on the MyCareer and MyTeam gamemode.This 2k has been really hit or miss so far.Through the attempt to nerf a consistent and overpowered meta that has existed since the inception of MyCareer, that being playmaking sharpshooters, they have severely crippled the overall game experience. In this 2k, they have taken many steps to stop even the best players from shooting consistently. Unless setting your game to the shot-profile that makes it impossible to hit non-green shots, you can not time your shot in a way that guarantees a green (shot with 100% chance of going in) without super-human consistency. Even on the high risk shooting profile you have 30m/s to guarantee a green shot. The rest of the green-window for your shot has an RNG % chance of coming out as a green or white shot. To add insult to injury, they have made it so shots this year choose between 8 different timings every time you go to shoot. While overall they are minor changes to timing, they completely shift the green window. Due to this system,  It is completely ridiculous and idiotic to change someone's shot timing randomly every time they shoot. This is all without mentioning that community testing has shown that after making too many shots in a row the game forces you to miss when in a live game.This system has been an overall negative to shooting, reducing it to a luck contest where even at the top level players struggle to green consistently. In my personal experience my play-style has been completely shattered and I don't even take 3's. I focus on creating high efficiency mid-range shots while creating threats in the paint. Even this simple and effective shot selection is completely ruined by the RNG shooting and it's very disappointing for anyone that likes to do anything other than dunk.However, it is important to note that while the RNG is a terrible and regretful decision to re-implement into the series, the poor shooting itself does create some fun in the game and if the game proceeds to heavily limit shooting while completely removing RNG the playstyle they are trying to cultivate can be very fun.Despite the flaws in the structure of the game, it is very refreshing for a more grit-and-grind style game, 3 pointers have become exciting and risky again rather than the go-to plan like it has been for so long. While some players still stick to and succeed in range-centered gameplay, the majority of the community has spent a lot more time playing physically and in the paint. It really is a refreshing experience for a 2k game and is not the overall negative the community makes it out to be. The only problem is the RNG.We should not be failing to green a wide-open corner 3 with Steph Curry because 2k rolled a green window that is significantly outside the normal timing of our shots. We should not be having the visual cue's on our player's jump shots completely desynced from the actual timing of our shots because 2k rolled a green window that is significantly outside the normal timing of our shots. We should not have a chance to get a white shot with perfect timing down to the exact millisecond.With my main team that I have spent thousands of games on and know everything about the timing of by heart, I am now afraid to take the same wide open fade-away mid range shots I have hit with 80-90% accuracy for years now. Let alone a stand-still mid range. Every shot is a risk forced by the game regardless of skill level.TLDR: A refreshing 2k experience with a focus on physical play that is marred down by a terrible RNG system meant to artificially limit player skill. Skill expression from range is tarnished and even smart and safe shots are interfered with by the game to make them virtually impossible to hit.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't pick up the last couple 2K's since they were still porting the obsolete version of the game to PC instead of the Next Gen version for PS5/XBSX. This move is so baffling to me since PC is where players have access to even *more* power than console players. Boneheaded move that hopefully cost them millions of dollars. But at last! We have the updated next gen fancy edition on PC! Rejoice! But is it a better 2k than last generation? Honest answer: probably?The simulation aspect of this game has always been the best in sports games and continues that tradition in 2k25. With the graphics cranked to max, my wife constantly double takes when she catches some gameplay. Movement and physics feel like they have weight to them unlike years past which felt more floaty. Dunks and tricky layups feel earned when you nail one in traffic and makes the game more engaging. The game just feels good to play and replicates what being Luka or Joker or Dame or Steph would feel like. Gameplay is solid and rewarding if you use your noggin instead of just driving or pulling up from 3 off an iso. Playing the point or main offensive facilitator is satisfying in a way unlike other 2k's. Passing and making plays are key to winning with smarter AI that can capitalize on your mistakes more often, creating a more complex game of getting guys open, making good passes, and spacing the floor.I've dabbled in MyTeam and MyEras a bit, and they're mid to pretty lackluster. MyTeam is still an absolute scam and a mini casino marketed to a player population filled with literal children. I don't know about you, but that is abhorrant to me. There's more of a reason to get into MT (MyTeam) with the addition of Triple Threat, where you can use your MT cards to hoop in PvP pickup games like you would in The City with your created character. It's honestly pretty fun and a good excuse to check out MT if you're interested. MyEras is very poorly integrated and the incomplete rosters hold back what could be an honest to God innovation in a sports game (!). Thanks to the community rosters, the mode is saved for the most part. Getting the rights to use players likenesses is always an issue, so this isn't really 2k's fault, but it always sucks seeing my 04 Pistons without that legendary starting 5. The franchise mode that boasts RPG elements is hollow and more of a rough outline than anything. It's just not fun. Not much to say other than that.MyCareer (MC) is...man I don't even know dawg. The revamped story is grounded and feels like a glimpse behind the scenes unlike every experience before. Heart of a Dynasty is fun to hone your skills in and connect to the larger story being told in the current day. It's not super deep, but it's fun and rewards you for doing light roleplaying in certain moments. There's incentive to keep playing the single player mode to the very end of your career with the promise of creating your own dynasty. The new streetball mode is a neat distraction if you want to step away from the grind of the NBA. I wish I could skip the intro Lil Wayne or whatever is annoying good golly. Online is...well...2k online. Nothing new to report. I love the player builder and the ongoing evolution towards a more accessible experience. It's been downright fun to cobble together a player that's tuned to play exactly how I want to play hoops. If progression was tied to gameplay, I'd put 3,000,000 hours into this mode. It is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame this mode is corrupted by the VC scam and a dystopian nightmare of a City to roam in. The amount of ads and product placement feels like a joke. Wow! I'm so excited to do the State Farm Challenge so I can look like Jake from State Farm! Time wear my American Express merch (that costs 10,000 VC) for extra XP! It sounds like a joke when I tell people who don't play 2K. VC should not be tied to stats anymore and the overall experience suffers heavily from the reliance on a purchasable currency. It costs over 20 bucks to get a usable character and it doesn't get cheaper from there. You don't earn VC in a fast enough fashion to justify this system and needs to change more than ever.This *feels* like a game worth $70 with the amount of stuff packed in here. You can lose hundreds of hours digging into every aspect of this game like always and feel like you weren't ripped off. It's so unfortunate that the game tries to nickle and dime every moment you are in it. I don't feel good spending money in this game because it doesn't feel like I'm willingly doing it. The return is the same as feeding quarters into an arcade cabinet or a slot machine: you pay to keep playing.

Honestly, it’s become a game of  rather than skill.Let’s talk about that VC grind because 2K did nothing to make it better. In fact, it feels even worse. _childDocuments_.review: My Review is for developers and fans of fighting games.Defense: Y/Triangle-Left Analog Away is a jumping hand contest meanwhile, Left analog-Towards/ Right Analog Towards is a bump/ Shot contest. The problem is your brain is already set that the right analog toward is hands up defense = Why would left analog back be hands up jump defense. That doesn't make any sense, and I know tekken combos.Fix: Both analogs toward during a shot = Hands up jump contest. See how easy of a fix that is? See how much more it makes sense? Both analogs toward = Both hands up?Alot of the time you swinging back and forth and you don't have time to press the triangle/Y button when you want to block- Let alone thinking about pressing Triangle/Y and Away on your movement analog to contest? Moving your movement analog away to contest a shot makes no sense from a gaming perspective of controls- and its not even the analog controlling your hands most of the time.Shot Mechanics: They brought in a system for shooting that relies on flicking the stick like a (Skate Game). It's alright except when in the paint, I don't think they implemented it into layups or dunks so both shot systems feel completely seperate whether you want to drop step or fade away and that makes it feel clunky, they should've added a dymamic layup/dunk system with the same type of releases.- And I don't think it works to double tap the right stick in a direction to hop step for a perimeter shot, Now you have to double tap x- While holding right stick in the direction you want, then flick your stick for a shot because shooting with x is completely incompetent? Fix: Let me drop step people and pound the right stick up for the rise and down for the dunk instead.Your physics engine is still trash but I've come to the conclusion they care more about recycling the same garbage than fixing stuff that should've been fixed 10 years ago. Its the one thing real fans always ask for you to fix, and its the one thing you always sell us short on.I've played enough videogames to realize this is far from beginner friendly, let alone logical. You'd have to dedicate yourself to 2k controls alone to understand them, and coming from someone who goes for achievements only 5% people have in other games, that's illogical and I don't see how the average person enjoys it. _childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game over 2k24, for the following reasons.1 - Foul out in co op multiplayer (6 fouls)?  Nope, doesnt matter your game performance or how much time is left in the game, you're immediately booted to the lobby.  If you're playing with one other person, the game ends outright and abrupt.  No VC earned at all.  Doesnt matter if the character you have fouled out has 7 points, or a 50 point quadruple double.  As an example, I received this game as a gift from a friend to mostly play co op with in quickplay.   The first time this had happened to me, I had a 35 point triple double and had an A player rating, and when I received my sixth foul with two minutes left in the fourth quarter, we were booted immediate. Whether it be two people on the same team, or two on one team one on another, if you foul out 6 fouls you are immediately booted to the lobby.2 - Unreasonably graphically demanding with long load times versus 2k24.  I REALLY enjoy formatting shaders every single time I launch this stupid game.3 - Server stability.  When doing quickplay, theres about an 85% chance at some point the game will encounter some error at some point or another and forcibly kick you back out to the lobby, indiscriminate of time in the game.  It could happen with 9 seconds left in the fourth quarter, or 2 minutes into the second quarter.4 - HUD does not apply changes you create.  First and foremost, there is no actual shot meter bar like in 2k24.  Now its all the arrow, or the dial, and even if you change them in the HUD?  Good luck getting them to apply for more than one game.  Yes, I have launched the game as administrator and attempted to apply settings to no avail.5 - The game boots you from the lobby for having a poor game performance.  This is absolutely atrocious for those of us just getting to learn the game and changes from 2k24, and basically promotes stat padding.  Not everyone wants to play as 85+ rated characters.With the above all being said, I could understand some of the changes being applied to rec or to pro am or to my career in general, or even to myteam.   And I'm all for that. But when you're playing co op with a friend in quickplay and you have 4 fouls in the third quarter and you arent allowed to play defense because of risk of fouling out and getting kicked to the lobby?  Absolutely sours the game in general.In short, would I purchase this game?  No.  I would ask for this game to be refunded if steam were to allow this.  If changes were fixed?  Sure, it could be warranted to buy the game.  The shot meter, yeah its a personal gripe but I could work around that.  Every year the shot meter changes to something different.  The instability, and the fouling out, and being kicked out for poor performance?  As someone who chooses to play only multiplayer co op? Absolutely not, and those are deal breakers for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first NBA game, and I'm thoroughly disappointed.ShootingIf you don't live near the servers, shooting feels like a gamble. I have to run the game on the lowest settings with an RTX 3080 and a Full HD display, yet I still get an unstable 60 FPS.BugsThe game is riddled with frustrating bugs. Shooting settings and animations can reset mid-game, often leading to lost matches. The racing track has been broken for two weeks now, causing the game to drop to 1 FPS when you enter. The only fix is to force quit with ALT+F4.SupportCustomer support is unhelpful and slow. Their solutions are generic, like suggesting to reboot my router. I spent 15 hours troubleshooting why I couldn't play, while support kept recommending changing my Ethernet cable.After hours of troubleshooting, I discovered that if you use an unsupported gamepad (with no list of supported ones available), you can play offline, but you'll be immediately kicked from online play with a generic error message that provides no useful information, not even for support.Maybe it's a great game for fans, but for someone who's never played NBA before, it's just a waste of time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: CPU: Ryzen 7 3700xGPU: GTX 1080RAM: 32gbStorage: 1000gb SSDI love NBA 2k25. I've played over 1000 hours of 2k15 alone, but I haven't been able to buy a version of 2k since 2k16 (I bought 2k20 and didn't refund it in time) bc it's unplayable on PC. This game is smooth and playable...when it works. The way you can make it work, is you take 40 minutes to an hour of time to start the game over and over again until the the second set of shaders load. This is not the Cyberpunk 2077 launch.What I did to make it work so far:1) Let the first set of shaders install. The game will crash. Reopen it and do it until they are at 100% because the first time they load is the slowest. I have an SSD so that helps but after they installed it only took a few seconds for them to load to 100% on launch2) Skip the second set of shaders by pressing "cancel" and go straight to the graphics settings3) Turn the setting to their lowest setting and put the game on "Windowed" *not* "Windowed Fullscreen" then close the game (if you don't it will crash inevitably)4) Reopen the game and let the second set of shaders load (it only loaded about 4% for me at a time, so yes, this is the longest step). The game will crash, reopen it and let the shaders load some moreFinal) Once the shaders get to 100% you should be good (If you leave the game idle or minimized, it will probably crash so if anything close the game in case you still want to refund it before you play it too much).Graphics settings:*Video Settings*Window Mode "Full Screen Windowed"Resolution Scaling Method "None"Vertical Sync "On"Dynamic Vertical Sync "Off"Texture Detail Level "High"Overal Quality "Custom"*Advanced Quality Settings* (The settings that aren't at the lowest setting)Player Detail Level "High"NPC Density "Medium"Reflections "High"Tempooral Anti-Aliasing "On"Max Anisotrpy "16"Conclusion:Overall, I wouldn't recommend buying this game. I don't appreciate the laziness and penny pinching companies have done over the last 4-6 years with massive AAA titles. For titles like 2k, the game needs to be ready at launch because there is a one year countdown forced on the players as soon as the game is launched, and once that countdown is over, the game is basically lost forever. 10/14/24 UpdateLower Texture setting to "Low" and lower overall setting to the lowest setting. (It only took me a week to figure this out)

_childDocuments_.review: Great game when you can play it. You know what to expect if you've played recent games. This is all of that, but finally next-gen and unfortunately, with a lot of crashing. 4K performance is great on top end hardware like the 4080 Super when it runs.Crashing is regular and reported by a lot of people, not recommended for $70. The main issue I see right now for myself and others, is crashing. Especially in The W, which is primarily what I play.I can play a game without any trouble and the game crashes loading back to The W. Other times, loading to The W crashes twice and then I can play a full game. It's pretty absurd for the price tag and all the talk about increased production costs. Unfortunately, The W is still the only experience for women. I don't mind The W, it's definitely a lot better than not being included at all. I do wish they would just make WNBA a main story and stop holding back what they obviously intend to do eventually.I can deal with all that. However, the mostly universal experience with crashing is completely unacceptable for this brand and a $70 price tag.. If they fix the bugs and crashes, would recommend. Until then, 2K25 seems like I'm paying more for a worse product just because layoffs were more important for the shareholders than quality. The game is the same great basketball sim we know, but the crashing makes it impossible to recommend.Performance is great with good hardware, but only if it doesn't crash. I get a stable 100fps at 4k Ultra with DLSS set to Quality. I get about 65fps average at 4k Native or with DLAA.That means you could typically expect a stable 60FPS at native 4K with max settings when using my hardware. I prefer using DLAA for anti-aliasing at 4K60, but to each their own there.I don't play The City, but it performed bad in the previous games and I hear it performs bad in this one too. I'd expect half the above performance in The City with frame stutter or lag spikes likely.Building ALL shaders is really important if you want to avoid stutters when playing. If a shader gets called that isn't cached, the game will hitch for a half second. I've not experienced any stuttering which others have complained about after building all shaders.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who only really plays the offline modes like MyNBA and MyGM, this is the most enjoyable NBA 2K I've played in a long time.MyGM is back, MyNBA has more eras than ever with the eras feature now being on PC, lots of little quality of life changes have been made to MyNBA such as the ability to actually offer rookies contract extensions, or actually play all 15-17 guys off of your bench, much improved coaching rotation and substitution AI, and more small but notable changes.The shooting this year is a little strange when you first get ahold of it, but it pretty quickly became my favorite shooting mechanic of any 2K that I can remember. Shooting just feels intuitive and I feel like I can get a better rhythm for it this time around than in years past. There are some quirks such to the overall feel such as the rim physics, which just seem a bit... off. A lot of shots seem to like bouncing all around the rim even when they're made shots, which always feels a bit bizarre and is not something I remember being so noticable in previous entries. Performance can occasionally be an issue as well. The halftime show with the Inside the NBA guys is locked to 30 fps and seems to have some sort of shader issues, unlike the rest of the game. Make sure to turn cloth simulation OFF in your settings for significant improvements to performance, although even with it off there is an occasional stutter when a timeout is called.Also worth mentioning that the game works pretty decently on the Steam Deck. The graphics and performance are obviously much better when running it off a proper gaming PC, but being able to take the game with you on the go and still get a passable experience is a really nice touch. At this point I've probably played a bit more on my Deck than on my machine.Haven't touched the Career mode yet as I usually play it sparingly, but it seems like multiplayer in the PC version has issues with cheaters and the like. I've never really cared for the multiplayer online stuff in 2K but it's clearly a very popular part of the game and it's a shame 2KSports hasn't addressed this and made this aspect of the game worthwhile for PC players. Please beware of this if you're looking to purchase the game for that stuff. However, all in all, really enjoy this game for the offline and single player content, and the mods being rolled out make it an even better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Next gen engine on PC.  Playing defense has improved drastically and the player movements are responsive.  Skipping halftimes and timeouts take a couple of button presses, but it does move forward without forcing you to watch or wait too much.  There are still situations where your player will get animation locked.  I.E. you go for a steal, but the reach doesn't register until after the animation is complete.  Same thing with other moments, but it's to be expected and you can often break the animation by moving your player away from the other player.  MyCareer has a similar grind as before.  Other reviewers have mentioned that the amount of MP points needed to be a star has increased a lot.  So far MyPlayer is a 75 OVR and we're halfway through the season.  He doesn't move like a superstar until a Badge is activated, but then his stats jump to the 90s in enough categories that you'll be able to make some good plays.  Practice increases your Badge level and Overall stat cap.  Unfortunately, once you've maxed a Badge in practice you can't play that mini game anymore.  You have to practice the badges that aren't fully upgraded yet.  At least this was the case for all my offensive badges.  I'm stuck practicing boxing out until I increase my rebounding stat high enough to go to the next badge level.  I like this game a lot and it's the best 2k I've played (most recent was 2k22; I've been waiting for next gen on PC).

The only way I can get close to smooth play is by setting the fps cap to 60fps on nvidia control panel. The game badly needs an optimisation update. My gpu usage fluctuates between 60-80% and cpu usage stays below 60% most of the time with 4k resolution, 120fps frame limit set to 117 in nvidia control panel and graphical setting maxed out.I was playing nba 2k24 last week on the same pc smoothly with 120fps 4k no stutter or lag.Looking at my hours played, I spend most of those hours debugging the substitution problem.So unless you are planning to play online vs other players only, I cannot recommend this game in its current state. 2k has not excuse as this problem would have come up during the testing stages if they had have played just one mynba era or mycareer or play now or any game mode where you play against cpu.This is a game that gets re-released every year with mostly roster and commentary update for players and some minor updates here and there using the same engine and charges us full price.Honestly at this point, I blame myself for buying it day 1. _childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever review for a game. And not surprisingly it has to be 2k. I would HIGHLY recommend you buy this game on sale. This is not a $70 game. It is at least $30 at best.As of right now, the shooting is horrific. I have spent hours toying with different releases, cues, animations, speeds, and nothing ever changes. The only difference that actually works is playing on rookie or semi-pro mode. This goes for both MyCareer and MyTeam. Shot meters for shots near the post and some layups will not work or be bugged totally throughout your matches. The delay for animations such as rebounds and steals is so delayed that it is not practical trying them in game. Getting caught on players whether on defense or offense is so bad that you have no choice but to play off the opponent as much as you can. The AI opponents in MyTeam have some of the worst advantages I have ever come across in 2k. The amount of layups and shots they make when you are actually playing good defense, yet the coverage feedback says they were "open" is nefarious to say the least. It is so difficult to be rewarded for playing great ball in this game for reasons I have no idea about. Pick and Rolls are at the best 40% effective. Teammates never "really" roll to the basket or fade off of a screen, they commit about half way and will either roll off of a fade or fade slightly off of a roll. Also, the "cut to basket" input is awful. Unlike previous 2ks, I remember distinctively holding down Y and your teammate will make a 100% full commitment to cutting to the basket. In this game, it is not feasible at all which sucks. The amount of issues with this game out weigh the purchase price/value of the game in total. Wait until is goes on sale, you are not missing out on anything. I know the game recently just released, but they do this every year it seems. I took a chance this year on the game after missing the last 3 years, but unless this game receives some MAJOR patches and fixes, this will be my last 2k purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the greediest game I've ever played. VC is harder to get than ever before, and attributes cost more than ever before. If you don't want to spend dozens of hours grinding, it will cost you $100 to make your MyPlayer viable for online play. You will NOT be able to make any tweaks to your build after creation, so any minor mistake in your build means creating a brand new character and spending another 60 hours / $100.The game has arbitrary attribute values that NEED to be met, otherwise your character will be missing out on crucial skills. for example, an 85 three ball rating is significantly more useful than an 84 three ball rating, or a 75 speed with ball unlocks animations that a 74 speed with ball will not have access to. this means that any small mistake in your build can have long reaching implications, and I believe it was done intentionally to push players to make new builds and spend more time / money. there are even bonuses that can be unlocked only by having multiple characters at 95 ovr.This game is probably a good pickup for like $30 or less. having next gen is cool. the game finally feels different. the graphics are definitely better. "high level" players just spam dribble moves behind screens until they get favorable animations. the game launched with the substitution system completely broken, and it somehow took over a week to fix. the contest system just doesn't work half the time. pressing the steal button either makes me teleport across court for a steal or sends me flying into the bleachers. _childDocuments_.review: I have been passionately playing basketball in all forms for almost 40 years now, i feel like i will never lose that love for the game itself, being in real life or in a digital form. Why am i not recommending it then? Well, 2k over the years has been trying REALLY hard to kill my love for the game in the digital form. But since there are actually more positives this year then there are negatives, i will start of with the positives. First of all, i should mention that even though i have 30+ hours in already,  there are certain modes i haven't tried (my gm, the W,...) as i have rarely played them in the past. My usual go-to games are the online games in my career. But that only speaks volume as to how many different kind of game modes there are. The amount of content across the game is ridiculous. I mean seriously, there would be absolutely no shame if the game was being released only once in like 4 years or so. I have started the game by only playing the play now and play now online modes and i went through the tutorial mode which is actually well done this time around. It will teach you practically everything you need to know about the core mechanics. Also all the "main menu modes" would probably be enough to keep anyone entertained for the whole year on their own.Then there's my career of course. The city is really well done, it's just small enough for all functions to be quite readily accessible and just large enough so exploration doesn't get an overextended welcome. There is A TON of content and game modes and the experienced players will be right at home with stores, items and progression even though it looks vastly different at first glance. I won't get into details about each game mode as it's all pretty self explanatory and everyone should just take the first day to get acquainted with everything on their own. I will say though, that even with the "next-gen" labeling, certain elements of the game are ancient and obsolete and just ridiculously bad. For example, visually creating your player is the least fun thing i've done this year. The generic faces available are just atrociously bad and ugly and facescan has never produced expected results either. And the hair is just extremely bad. No amount of directx candy can hide the age of the engine itself. Back to the game modes themselves, if you like competitive play, there is no doubt you will find something for you in The City, i have no doubts there. As for the mycareer itself and the story, well... I have to say the story always got on my nerves in previous years as it was a literal cringe-fest, but this is absolutely not the case this year. I mean it's not an oscar material but it's efficient, it's straightforward and ABOVE all...it's not trying to be "socially or politically pleasing" as so much content in movies and games is trying to be last few years. There are no "agendas", no one is trying to subtly convert you into a vegetarian or make you transform your gender or accept people identifying as flying pink pandas or anything like that. And that alone is worth an A+ to me (looking at you DISNEY for ruining Star wars for me). The career part of gameplay is pretty bad in certain elements but more on that later. As for the myplayer builder itself, it's probably the best it's ever been done, especially with the pre-made builds that it has available now and should make life easier for people who don't want to dissect every nuance the builder offers, or they just simply don't know what they're doing. Even though i made a completely custom build, i have yet to fully realize how good it will be. I am around 85 ovr for now. I never watch youtube videos on the "perfect archetype and build", because i believe this is part of the fun, to figure it out on your own. Even if you make a mistake or two. And i've never created more than 1 build per yer, so i'm not the right guy to judge how good the laboratory really. I was pleased with it. If you take your time you will see in real time how each single change will affect your badges. It's very intuitive but it's probably a good idea to have a basic understanding of yourself, how you like to play the game, what your basic basketball behavioral tendencies are, etc. As i've mentioned  certain aspects of graphics, let's continue with that note. I am running an i7 9700k which is starting to show its age, a 3080ti gpu and 32gb of ram and a samsung 980 pro ssd. While we have become used to 2k being riddled with bugs over the years and even more so with bugs that persist for MANY years, i would NEVER defend 2k just solely on pure fact how they've treated bugs over the years. But man, reading all these negative reviews here really is mind boggling as to what on earth people are doing with their machines. In my 30+ hours i haven't encountered A SINGLE (mark that word down!) bug, a SINGLE crash, not even a TINY little glitch for which i could hold 2k accountable. I am really sorry for people who are either unable to play or have constant problems, but i strongly advise those people to call someone who will be able to get their system in shape, perhaps even do a clean install of the OS. My system is neither high end, nor new, if it was really as bad as many people claim i should have ran into at least one crash or other problem. I have a 1440p monitor but i'm running the game supersampled to 4k resolution and DLSS enabled and set to DLAA which i didn't expect to produce completely fluid framerate but it is. Certain arenas are more intense so i lowered the resolution back to 1440p and i NEVER drop below 60fps in games. I have all graphic options set to maximum. The raytracing is not well optimized so the City has a pretty poor framerate if it's enabled but as soon as you get to any part where you actually play, the framerate is stable and high. The lightning and shadows and player models are actually pretty nice looking but i personally would not call them next gen. The game looks solid, but can't visually compare to modern graphics in AAA games, especially the unreal engine 5 games. However the motion of the game is amazing. 2k has never been this fluid before and that itself boosts the immersion immensley. I can't wait what modders will be able to do with the game this year as i have pretty high expectations in that regard. Now finally, let's touch on the gameplay itself. Letting all the hate of a typical long term 2k baller aside, i personally never had gripe with how the game is being played. The core of 2k games has always been a pretty solid blend of realism and arcade. And i don't want to sound like someone on 2k's payroll but man, i really like gameplay this year. I've not enjoyed digital basketball this much probably since 2k16. I was actually pleasantly surprised by 2k in that regard as i have lost all hope over the years. I won't go into specific details, but gameplay elements are top notch in my books. The only real gripe i have with the game is AI which is ridiculously bad and has always been. And i mean ridiculously bad. I will end off by saying that i've had my doubts if i should even buy 2k when i saw  it won't support cross play as it was instantly clear to me this means nothing has been done about the cheating issues (shocking, i know). However, going to next gen, i had my hopes that something has been done to the engine that will prevent cheating at least in the easiest form. Sadly, it wasn't. And this fact, coupled with the predatory MXT is still enough to never recommend this game to anyone. You WILL need to feed around 30-50 euros into the game minimally, if you want to actually have fun online. MXT that affect skills in a full priced game? I will NEVER EVER accept that. And the fact that 2k doesn't even protect you from cheaters after that is even worse, and it's just sad because of how good the game itself is. And until that gets addressed, i cannot recommend anyone buys their products. No matter how much you love basketball.

_childDocuments_.review: **Edit notes: I left the original review here for anyone who wants to read it, however I have placed the update at the top of the old review**Updated Review:  So after hours of being crushed in the MyCareer, I have finally found the solution. If you are a newer player, or someone who doesn't want to do the grind, do yourself a favor. Go into Settings > Controller Settings > Shot Profile, and change your profile to Real Player %. This makes the game lose the shot meter, and use your skills in game to determine the success of your shots. Believe me, this makes a world of difference. I wont ROTY, Finals MVP, NBA Cup, and NBA Championship with a 61 overall using this method. So normally, I'm not a review guy. But just in case anyone reads this review, and it helps them, then it is worth it.@k25, as an overall game, is great. MyNBA, WNBA, and MyTeam are all smooth as silk and same as ever. However, MyCareer seems to continuously stumble down this path, switching from one side to the other. I started playing 2k in 2016, back in the Orange Juice time frame. I loved that game, and if I could still find a way to play it, I would, because that MyCareer was the most fun, and most entertaining, out of any we have played since. However, even last qyear's last-gen MyCareer was better than the garbage sandwich we were handed this year.First, Heart of a Dynasty seems cool, until you jump in to what is effectively supposed to be a High School game, and yet the players on the opposing team are playing like NBA all stars (literally, P. Wells shot two three pointers, back-to-back, from beyond half court, and suck them both!? Name one NBA player who can do that consistently!?), you're teammates play like senior citizens, and if you haven't leveled up your character, you are as good as useless on defense. Then let's throw in the fact that badge progression in the practice facility has been made 1000% more difficult, as you cant repeat exercises, and the new drills are outright impossible for early leveled characters. Finally, the actual NBA games are mostly okay, but I still can't score consistently with my low level character, because I cant level up the badges that would normally help me. There are plenty of ways to make VC, but they require you be able to perform well with your character, which you cant do unless you can level them up. Long story short, if you are like me, and want a decent MyCareer, wait until this game goes on sale, then use the money you save to buy VC and get a huge starting boost on your character.Now on to the good stuff. First, there are plenty of ways to earn VC, and several of them are repeatable methods. However, none of them give enough VC to really feel worthwhile, unless you play on HoF difficulty. Both the Rec and Pro-am are pretty full right now, so it's a good time for those matchups. I also really enjoy the layout of the City, its far easier to navigate.Gameplay is fine, although I'm not a fan of the new shot meter.

_childDocuments_.review: Just avoid the online stuff, it's pure cancer. Play MyNBA Eras, it's by far the best mode. Want to recreate Jordan's dominance in the '90s, make it even crazier, or maybe prevent him from winning with Utah Jazz and the beautiful duo of Stockton and Karl Malone? Want to play the 76ers of Julius Erving and Moses Malone in the mid '80s and stop the Lakers - Celtics dominance? Maybe you want to convince the mediocre Bulls team to trade their exciting rookie in '84 and create an alternative reality where the '90s Bulls never existed? Or maybe you want to actually win an NBA title with that mediocre Bulls team in the '80s with just prime Jordan (with Hall of Fame difficulty lmao)? You could also try to trade Charles Barkley in '92 when he becomes a free agent and make an insane trio of Jordan - Pippen - Barkley (you'll probably need to trade half of your team to just manage the salary cap hahaha)Or play as Allen Iverson in early 2000's and actually win a title against the mighty Lakers' duo of Shaq and Kobe? Or more recently, stop Steph Curry from dominating? (impossible honestly lol)And yes, some rosters in some eras are not 100% complete, but you can load custom rosters made by the community and you'll have a greater experience (notably Charles Barkley and Blake Griffin are missing in the official roster due to some licensing issues). All in all, just this mode is fantastic honestly, no sports game comes close to recreating a historical era so well. It's quite immersive, including rule changes that actually happened in real life, teams relocating and actual historical drafts (witness a rookie Shaq, Kobe, Duncan, Iverson, McGrady, Irving coming into the league) and most importantly, team tendencies and styles being so different — if you play ball in the '80s era, there's almost no 3's, the game is slower, more inside baskets and intense defense and closer game; in the '90s there's some 3's being thrown but they are almost negligible compared to the current era, the pace though ramps up compared to the '80s. And the current era is just splashing 3's most of the time lmao which can be annoying but it's also much harder on defence in my opinion. Players are so well-rounded in the current era it's actually insane, before you had just a few well-rounded players and it was mostly about role specialists. Now you can have a center like Jokic that can do basically anything. Just having this sandbox of options is fantastic and worth getting the game. If you actually play like real basketball with pick and roll and calls (and broadcast camera) it's basically watching real ball, it can get very immersive. And again, I just don't care about online, tried MyCarreer a little and all the cutscenes and the low rating of your player (incentivizing you to buy currency with real money) is just cringe as hell, so I just avoid it. Pro tip: if you want to "simulate" a MyCareer like gameplay without all the predatory stuff just turn on the "player lock" setting and set it to a specific position (PG if you want to play Iverson in the 2000's 76ers, for example), it can get a bit annoying when subs are automatically done as you'll basically be forced to play another player temporarily, but you can manage that with manual subs. This way you can have a "MyCareer" without the flashy stuff and cutscenes that I mostly don't care about. Also, playing as a historical player is much more immersive than a random custom player you generated, but that may be just my preference.TLDR: play MyNBA eras, avoid online. Actual gameplay on the court is immersive, realistic and highly customizable.

My only issues are the odd antialiasing and crashes (but that just might be my rig). You can dominate the paint this year with no dunk and high layup. Being big/strong actually matters this year, but also diminishes you in other ways (slower, more stamina consumption). Being small may be a disadvantage on defense, but offensively, you are almost un-guardable. Shooting has been changed to combat "zens" so, even if they are cheating, they can no longer be prolific cheaters. The game has introduced elements that award team play and discourages one man shows. Although you can still dominate the game as a one man army, you will lose against a team of skilled team players.I have yet to run into a cheater, but if I did, I dont think I would know. The dribbling is easier, most dribble combinations will auto-play for you while still giving you the ability to be creative and add your own flavor.  If you like basketball, and 2K, I say 2k25 is a must have. Especially if you are able to find a discord group with people willing to run proam 5v5, 3v3 to filter out any cheaters. _childDocuments_.review: "NBA 2K25: A Love-Hate Slam Dunk (That'll Still Drain Your Wallet)"Okay, folks, let's talk about NBA 2K25. This game is like that ex you just can't quit, even though they keep asking to borrow money and "forgetting" to pay you back.  Yeah, the microtransactions are worse than a flagrant foul, but dang it, the gameplay is just so smooth.Look, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. 2K25 is a love-hate relationship. On one hand, you've got the MyPLAYER mode, which is basically basketball role-playing at its finest.  You create your own baller, grind your way to the top, and live out your NBA dreams (minus the million-dollar contracts, sadly).  And then there's Eras, which lets you relive the glory days of basketball with classic teams and legendary players.  It's like a time machine for hoops fans, and it's pure nostalgia gold.But on the other hand, you've got those microtransactions lurking in the shadows like a shady sports agent. They're everywhere, tempting you to spend your hard-earned cash on virtual currency (VC) so you can upgrade your player and dominate the court.  It's a slippery slope, my friends, and I've lost more money to this game than I care to admit. (Don't tell my wife.)So, why do I keep coming back for more?  Because when 2K25 is good, it's really good.  The gameplay is tight, the graphics are slick, and the atmosphere is electric.  When you're draining threes and breaking ankles, it's easy to forget about the predatory monetization.  But then you remember you need to grind for hours or shell out more cash just to improve your player's free throw rating, and the frustration comes flooding back.Here's the bottom line: If you're a die-hard basketball fan who can resist the siren song of microtransactions (or you have a trust fund), then NBA 2K25 is worth checking out.  But for the rest of us mere mortals, I'd recommend waiting for a sale.  Trust me, your wallet will thank you.Now, if you'll excuse me, I need to go beg 2K for some free VC.  Maybe if I write them a heartfelt poem about my love for the game...  Nah, who am I kidding? They'll just tell me to open my wallet.
