_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea where anyone that honestly thinks this is better than Payday is coming from.Yes this game is certainly inspired by Payday. There's some good mechanics here that had me going hmm why doesn't Payday have that. The ability to carry 2 bags of loot makes you slower and unable to use primary, UI and interaction for locks, and loot that dynamically fills bags are great simple adds. The graphics are good albeit a bit unoptimized atm. Campaign missions are somewhat interesting.AI teammates have good mechanics being able to give them commands like to help you bag loot and even switch to play as their character. Though it is a bit annoying how atm they can trigger the alarm when they roam by cluelessly walking into guards.Ofc Payday not only has a prestige and build system that make you want to maximize and try cool builds but also pull off perfect runs for XP bonuses and the most loot. Most importantly, it's also a strategy game at least when going stealth. Which guards will you take down? Will you have to drop an unexpected guard? Do you have enough time to page the guard? Will a guard unexpectedly check a room or did you soft alert a guard that will now investigate an area? The answer to all those questions in this game are no.Even if your impatient in stealth Payday gives strong value in just partially stealthing missions or even rushing stealth with risky moves thanks to it's strong gameplay. It has something for everyone.Guards are dumb as rocks here, yet the gameplay lacks the ability to rush stealth missions and pull risky plays in a similar way as Payday does. Guard and cam pings last forever meaning that a guard will never give you a surprise scare. In combo with the ability to just bonk infinite guards here makes stealth just a boring test of patience and a snooze fest.I don't like whatever the gun system is. Seems like there's no customization and you just have to find special versions of  a weapon even to get basic things like a suppressor. Granted if you've read up till here you know suppressors are useless anyways since this game is just bonking whatever guards you need/want to and easily slipping by.Same boring ass music everywhere. Seriously heist music in Payday is certainly a nice piece, and is nice in any kind of game like this.The reason I can't recommend this game are primarily 21.  While even Payday 3 lacks some simple neat mechanics this game has the same is true the other way around. Hostages serve no value here. It's not a strategy game at all. Many missions you stealth are a measure of your patience in just taking down as many guards as you want, which leaves no risk or fun and makes stealth just boring. It also makes mission design much lazier since they don't need to pay so much attention to patrol paths and tuning their difficulty. In short, this has potential in it's mechanics but is as shallow as a puddle. I can't understand how this is even in the same realm as being compared to Payday by many reviews.2. More importantly is the Coop truly sucks. The Coop missions are extremely repetitive and overwhelmingly short, basic, and boring. Bank heists are easily completed in 5min and armored cars can be done in a couple min as 2 examples. I'd have to imagine the positive reviews only come from campaign (which is not Coop) bc from the perspective of it as a MP game it's just bad. Ofc again the campaign seems decent here for solo but Payday has actual story line and plot in it's missions.This is besides the bugs and unoptimized graphics, which are playable but can sometimes partially break missions at least. The game ultimately has some potential with the mechanics and graphics it offers so there is some hope if they add Coop campaign or actually good MP missions. However, even if it improves in these areas it's hard to say it'll have close to the same longevity and replayability as Payday thanks to it's build and prestige system.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is fine. You really have to look at how much this game is costing you and using that as a way to gauge the value of your experience in this game. Most of the negative reviews make good points. But from what's here, and seeing that it's only going to improve with future updates, I don't see why we need to nitpick at it. (Other than technical issues like bugs or crashes, those make sense.)The one negative that I will say is that it's fairly easy to tell that stealth was  a big topic in development. While I think the strike system is really nice and forgiving, it just feels like there is too much going on for stealth to be a viable option in most cases. The RNG element of heists does give great replayability, but, sometimes it can set things up for stealth to absolutely not work at all. The biggest way to show this is by trying to solo stealth. It just doesn't work most of the time, which is a shame honestly. I think doing loud heists is fun, don't get me wrong, but I do want stealth to be an actual secure choice when I'm playing heists. I'm having fun with it personally. Good game, really fun with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is genuinely fun and immersive. The only Current issues i have with the game is it's mechanics such as movement, interactions, weapons, and armour. Movement is still fun and somewhat smooth only issue is A) you can slide to Paris and back on one slide sometimes making it difficult to stop where your trying to go like behind cover or to a cop or thug who had spotted you but you've underslide or overextended in distance giving them time to shoot you and alert nearby enemies. B) Leading into interaction such as trying to vault certain objects that aren't vaultable which should like fences or walls. For some reason npcs can but you cant. stopping or hitting npcs/cameras that are next to each other are extremely difficult as the game will get confused with what your trying to do example there is an npc under a camera so your trying to break the camera inorder to get the npc on the ground without being spotted, the game gets confused to instead of hitting the camera your character hits the npc under the camera which the camera will instantly picks up and everything goes loud (happened to me). second example trying to backslap two guards walking in a line if you attempt to hit one the other guy will instantly notice (makes a lot of sense as theyre behind each other) so then you attempt to hit the guy infront but the game still thinks that your trying to hit the previous guy you just knocked one the ground giving the guy infront enough time to let a shot go off alerting other guards in nearby area (happened to me). C) Weapons and armour in my personal opinion is the biggest issue, example there are captains of rival gangs who come and attack you mid gang skirmishes, I could be using an M4 that uses 5.56mm rounds and the enemy gang captain has a t-shirt with a vest on but can tank 50 rounds before dying, yes I understand that they are designed to be mini bosses because they're captains but at least give them some armour so it makes sense i could be sooking or rambling but I think these little thing's makes the game a little better.All in all the game is genuinely fun and would 100% recommend it, just hope some of these things get reworked or added on, hope this helps new players understand before they play the game so they got some insight.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't the faintest idea where Jupiter is from with the inscrutable accent, and I don't care, she's an absolute doll, my favorite character, the team's designated 6'5" tall, 3-loot-bag-holding, roided out hard carry and never needs to change. Her voice actress' performance was phenomenally and unironically endearing, and she should be brought back for more lines for her own personal DLC. Nothing about her should change.It's nearly impossible to play this game without making immediate comparisons to Payday 2, and CBRC comes out on top. The shooting mechanics are smoother, the user interface more friendly, the heists less BS, and even the DLC has more bang for your buck. The missions where I'm forced to go loud are few and far between. Network issues as described by other reviewers are anecdotal, as I've not had issues, but if it concerns you just hop into multiplayer immediately and figure out if you're one of the unlucky ones and need to return in the 2 hour window. Speaking as someone with nearly 300 hours in Payday 2 from its release, and has 90 hours as of review time, this is a must buy for any fan of Payday 2 looking for anything to soothe the sting of Payday 3's launch and monetization.There are some negatives - Chuck Norris' voice in game is either AI or one of the most stilted performances I've been forced to bear witness to since I had to watch my nephew have no lines in a 4th grade class rendition of Fiddler on the Roof. Danny Glover is better, he seems to only be sometimes AI instead of always. There could be more locations, but they just added some in the new update so they're on top of it. Guard and camera placements on Hardcore difficulty, during the high risk Warehouse on Watch mission specifically, can be so dense and overlapping that I can feel the devs sarcastically telling me to go ahead and stealth this bulls**t. Randomized elements in general are usually reasonable on each difficulty though, enough to keep things interesting, not so much that you're getting bodied by shockers every other mission. The highest level characters in the game each has a set of missions that detail their respective backstories, I love this. You have to do these missions within 3 days of them popping up, even if you've beaten the whole set of missions, or you won't have access to that high level character for the rest of the run, I hate this.Devs, I am begging you - I appreciate what you were doing with the big names, all huge names in the 90s when this game is taking place, it's thematic, most of them did a fine job. But please hire professional trained voice actors like you did for the iconic heisters, and use whatever money you save to hire more level designers for more heists, more modelers and artists for new ♥♥♥♥ to put on those maps, and more programmers for interesting mechanics. I will buy every damn DLC you put out so long as I'm getting new maps, weapons, and interesting characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A really amazing Payday side-grade.It takes a lot of the positives, and strips back some features, like the in-depth customization of guns and appearance.In trade, you get a ton of replayability, with more impactful pre-heist choices, as well as a full, roguelite, singleplayer gamemode.I do miss being able to equip what I want, and mod my guns how I want, but the flexibility in heisting, and all the different ways to experience the heists, grouped with an actual criminal empire campaign, make it a VERY unique, and fun package.There's no shame in being a fan of both, seriously, it's worth it.VERY recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a blast with this game. While the various jobs certainly lack the length and depth of Payday heists, the short and concise nature really complements the overall campaign. Makes for a really chill experience where you can kinda blow a stealth job and just power through the rest of the heist rather than have to start over and have blown like a half hour. Fairly fun in multiplayer to play random jobs, just disappointing that the campaign is not co-op.Big complaint is that there is no clear indication whether a mission starts quiet or loud, which can make it difficult to prepare accordingly. For example, there's one mission type where you're looting an armored cash transport, but there's no good indication whether you're crashing the convoy and looting it while shooting at cops, or just quietly intercepting it while its stopped at a motel. They should really just add a clear tag to all missions that start loud.Not really a complaint because it kinda falls into the "so bad its good" and in general plot for these kinds of games really doesn't matter but... Wow, the writing, voice acting, and just all around presentation for this game is pretty bad. I thought the actors were just randoms they brought in at first to pretend to be these big names like Chuck Norris, Danny Trejo, Danny Glover, and so on, but they're actually all the real actors. Just giving the absolute worst performances ever, for some reason.Really fun game despite that stuff, decent replayability and much more casual than Payday 2, which is a nice change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiplayer games seem to be going further and further down the drain, and this one is no exception.Playing this game was great so far and has filled the void that Payday 3 was supposed to, till I decided to check out the multiplayer, which was a mistake (a massive one). Just like Hell Divers 2 and Siege, being kicked for no reason is just as common here and proves just how immature and sad multiplayer gaming has become. My team and I finally loaded into a game and, unfortunately, were put with someone who was clearly a ticking time bomb, thinking he could 1v20, which wasn't the case. Eventually, he never learned and kept doing this several more times till he was out. Then, he decided if he can't have fun, no one can, and just as we were about to escape with a serious sum of money, he promptly kicked us. 25+ mins and over 1.5 million, gone. Poof.This, unfortunately, isn't the first incident and certainly won't be the last in my over an hour of time with this game. Frankly, this childish behavior won't do this game any favors, and it's why I'll be getting a refund. It's impossible to play or even enjoy this game because these people make it unbearable. If you still decide to buy this one, expect to be kicked over and over again for things that are not your fault.Even for the low price, sadly, I still can't recommend it, which is a shame, as this game does some great stuff that I wish Payday had and even some unique things up its sleeve. But unless people stop abusing the kick system (it's an insta-kick, by the way—no vote or anything, and the host can do it to everyone), it's not going to last even a month.

_childDocuments_.review: So you may be wondering what the heck is 'Crime Boss: Rockay City'?Well the short answer is: The Payday 3 we should of got.The long answer is a little more convoluted and in depth But bare with me, an hopefully I can clear some things up for you.If you are looking for something to fill that Payday 3 void. This may be the game for you. So first things first, lets get the obvious out of the way. do i need an epic account? I can very gladly say, No! you do not! Now onto the rest of the info. The game play is fairly simple and straight forward. You don't have to worry about complex trees/ builds like you did in Payday 2. But you can equip skills/weapons to make like pseudo builds. Different skills and different characters are better at different things. Just something to keep note of.The Stealth is easy to get into but hard to master at least from my short time playing it. Stealth was one of my favourite things of Payday 2 and here I can quite confidently say. This really scratches that same itch, sneaking around is pretty much the same. Cameras are just as scary but well executed shouts can take down crowds easily.  Bricks can be thrown to distract guards and help you get them into better positions to make your moves. Melee weapons are great early on because if you get detected you can melee a guard to death (if you don't have a silenced gun.) to save your self from going loud. Oh and there is a really cool lock pick mechanic and for the most part, doors can be opened and closed!Which may not sound like a big deal but if you have played as many hours in payday 2 as I have. There are many stealth heists where i wished i could do something as simple as that. Oh and levels are very dynamic, if you fail to complete some objectives in an allotted time or mess up stealth. Then the direction of the mission may change drastically, Which I found really cool. I wont spoil anything but I will move onto more mechanics.Drills and saws are always loud but never jam on there own. If you start one in stealth it will attract all the non tied down guards in a certain area. However for the most part Civvies don't give a ♥♥♥♥. You can Interact with said equipment to boost the cutting speeds but at the risk of over heating them. I can not tell you how good it is to not NEED to baby sit drills. No more  *insert PTSD broken drill beep noise from payday 2 here* unless you want them to go as quickly as living-ly possible. Loud is straight forward, Shoot the enemies dead. Try not to become the un-alived yourself and get the loot out. However I will say be prepared for some humbling experiences. You have a very watered down version of Payday 2's build system when it comes to combat. Combat is either ON or it is Off. Basically as you fight the meter on the screen will slowly increase showing the level of Police, that you will be facing. An 5 badges is *SPICY*. You will want to be well equipped and have levelled characters if you plan on wading through tier 5 combat. Thankfully most jobs can be completed well and truly before that. CB:RC works on haste more then drawn out gunfights with literal armies of cops like Payday. So you really want to be matching the flow of the game in your movements, work on looting and things while the cops retreat. Focus on defence and combat when they are attacking. Strong Team work and good choke points are key to holding your ground. Now on the topic of loud, most of the weapons feel decent to use. Shotguns in CB:RC are so good. Popping heads with the streetsweeper is just *chef kiss*. I will say there are some weapons that feel weak but that's usually on the lower grade tier any way. Now onto the things you may be wondering about in other reviews: The Rogue-lite Single player.So simply put the Single player is what it says on the tin. You are working on taking over Rockay City. A chunk of territory at a time. As you work through the campaign you will likely face odds you are ill-equipped to deal with. Usually causing you to fail and worse case loose a run. But the game in intended to be this way, You are supposed to level up your boss and your station to better improve your odds of your next run. It makes you work for the progress which I personally like, it also gives the campaign some replay-ability. Multiplayer can be fun, but honestly the game lacks a large player-base ATM. So quick-play will likely put you into lobby by yourself. But it is worth just playing side missions or skirmishes to better level your account so you will have the money and things to unlock characters or weapons. Even solo i would say it is worth doing.Other things I like about CB:RC:Your characters can carry TWO bags. Yes you read that right, two whole ass duffel bags. You want to know the penalty for this? you move slower and can only use your secondary weapon. But there is a skill that once levelled can help you move faster while carrying bags. But carrying one barely slows you down and you can still use your primary! No more running single bags all the way to the drop point just to run all the way back to the loot. *Don't get me wrong you still kind of have to do it But at least you can do it quicker.*Characters have animations so you can see NPC models actually doing things. Whether they are throwing bags, helping some one up, picking locks etc.Maps will reuse area's but have different structures to break up the similarity between area's an missions. You also often have a wide area to flank or manoeuvre to better get at objectives. Which is a real nice touch.Cars will explode if they cop enough fire. Yes i know, not super realistic but its a nice touch to have destructive terrain during combat.Now onto the things that I don't like:CB:RC, is a live service game. Which really *really* sucks. I hate live service games for all the obvious reasons.It is a little buggy, it has its issues. But nothing that has caused me to stop playing.Having civvies or guards panic over spotting nothing is a little frustrating. And losing the ability to shout down guards because the prompt bugs is also a little problematic.The Film-clips/Cut-scenes are REALLY cheesy and I find myself usually skipping them as I roll my eyes at the some what poorly delivered lines or questionable dialogue. I understand they are meant to be larger then life characters and things but it feels overdone. Payday 2 I think, had the in game dialogue nailed. For the most part, ya know... Bain never shutting up was standard fair. However the characters voice lines suited them and if you felt they were grating. You could just switch characters. The looping lines and the character dialogues in CB:RC however, I find quite grating and can be a bit much.Over all is Crime Boss: Rockay City worth it? I would say yes. If you are a fan of the Payday games you may like this. Also For the price point it's not a hard sell and if you can get it on sale, even better.Edit notes: I found this super handy guide which covers all the aspects of CB:RC. Hopefully this will help you out if there are parts you are struggling with.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: the game is really good and for the price, it's a bargain. Now I'm no veteran I bought it day one when it came out on steam and only followed the game through youtube videos and such, but the game improved so much and the devs put a lot of care and passion into the game. The game is a bargain, for 16 euro with all the DLC on sale, and 20 euro full price I definitely don't regret my purchase, you can certainly spend worse. Now the game isn't perfect, some of the levels run fine, and others run horribly, most of the voice acting for the characters is meh and some lines are downright cringy, the gunplay and the music while not horrible, can be a lot better. If you can stomach all of the game's faults that can honestly be looked over, well maybe except the performance issues, then you'll get a great cheap game that can be played solo, or multiplayer, so I'd say give it a shot. I'm really looking forward what the devs are in stores for us and hope they find more success in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I will admit. When I first saw this game exclusive to the Epic Games Store, I ridiculed it for what it was, but after having played it now on Steam I can right my premature joviality a bit. Because this game is actually pretty entertaining now.For one, I've heard that the game now has a much better sense of direction and progress compared to its launch, and I appreciate that there is actually some coherence to the story, even if it is "so badly voice acted that it is funny".Some of the story missions are absolutely hilarious, at times ridiculous premises, and have strangely high production value for what they are. The voice acting almost speaks for itself in ambition.While there are also smaller shorter heists and daily jobs that don't seem to vary as much, overall it is a positive experience to play through, if you don't mind smaller odd jobs between the big heists.-What has hampered my experience with the game is the performance, and ultimately I blame modern day Unreal Engine for a lot of it. I don't want to sit a whole minute or two in the main menu waiting for the shaders to build every single time. When I try to run the game at DX11, which I've always found to be most stable DirectX in the past, Unreal crashes whenever the cops show up and start shooting.I'm playing on a GTX 1660 SUPER, i5-10600K and 16 GB of RAM, and I get a very playable experience at Low settings. I feel like many of the Unreal Engine bells and whistles are not worth it on this game. If it was more approachable on lower specs, it would definitely find a bigger footing of players that host their own servers and have a good time, like other heisting games that are still alive today.-In summary, this game is worth it, especially with the pretty reasonable launch offer, but try to get a better PC (especially GPU) than mine before you purchase. I'm hoping that the devs can cut a lot of the unnecessary glitter out and in turn also make the game run better at lower specs, given how awful Epic has made the Unreal Engine nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just good old school fun. I've only played the singleplayer campaign so far, so I can't speak on the multiplayer. Having said that, this campaign has a suprising amount of depth and replayability. The cutscenes with their voice acting delivery, odd animations, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue has me laughing often. The gunplay is solid, not excellent, but servicable considering stealth is the optimal approach usually. Finding loot and robbing it is even more satisfying here than in Payday, which is the game that will inevitably draw the most comparisons with Crime Boss. The only thing Payday does better in my opinion is the cool mask mechanic, other than that Crime Boss is the superior heist game. Not to mention it costs less than most indie gamesDon't let the complaints about the friendly AI scare you off. For one, you can control your bot teammates and position them before/during a mission. And two, they're actually quite competent at gunplay and especially loot management. The pathfinding is manageable if you order them effectivelyMichael Madsen is the standout among all the great actors in this game, and they give him all the best dialogue. Not to mention he's probably who you'll play the campaign as most of the time, so it's just cool that we have a game where Mr. Blonde is the player character. The progression feels great, both within your campaign, and with the permabuffs you get as you advance rank. Overall this is just a solid package and it's the most fun I've had in an FPS in a long time. For it's price, I'd say definitely give it a shot

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't feature bloat like Payday, where you have several systems working together to make a character strong at loud or stealth missions while ruining them for the other kind. It is ok to fail stealth since you can take weapons off corpses and probably complete missions in under 5-10 minutes. Drilling goes by quickly since it doesn't break every minute.There are several game modes like roguelite, random mission set, and character missions where you use a preset crew to do a handful of missions. Roguelite is you actually taking over the city by fighting turf wars and doing random missions scrounging up money to support it. It's different from the other modes and has its own leveling system and is meant to be replayed with better gear each time. A solo effort.The money sink is being able to customize your character in appearance, weapons, perks, and colors. Your boss also has their own level where random items are introduced each level up. Those then appear in the other modes.

_childDocuments_.review: Observed pros and cons with a few hours of gaming, at least on the default difficulty:PROS:-You can play as Danny Trejo, up to four(4) Danny Trejos at once all using a Machete™.-Shooting stuff feels great, almost everything seems viable and thus boils down to what mood you're in. Also includes throwing bricks for caveman strategies.-You can pick up enemy weapons if you want to change gear, and ammo pickups seem generous.-You can carry up to two bags, and you can also carry half a bag worth of loot without penalties.-Seemingly infinite sprinting and generous sliding to move around, even while hauling two bags, so moving around isn't a slog.-Stealth works on a 3 strike system, so even if there's 2 mistakes you can still beat it in stealth instead of a one-and-done system.-You can blow up cars and kill a bunch of enemies in one fiery swoop.-Has an option for solo offline mode, and if playing solo, you can command or even swap bots. Handy if you fall down and you want to switch to another character that hasn't fallen down to keep a run going.-You can speed up the drilling/sawing with a simple timing minigame, so you always have something to do while waiting for doors to open up.-Price is attractive: $20 maximum, and a generous discount+DLC offer until July 11th, 2024.CONS:-Somewhat frequent and random stuttering/framerate drops, though this self-corrected after about 20 seconds later in-game.-Matchmaking was down for the first hour I played, but came back when I played again later. Unsure how frequent this is, likely due to the game running on epic game servers.-Suffered at least one unreal engine crash at the start of a heist.-Loadout customization is locked on random variant weapon drops. IE a Desert Eagle with a scope is a separate equippable item you can bring with you, but you cannot manually add a scope onto a regular Desert Eagle.-Most of the heists are quick smash-and-grab styles of missions, though this can be a pro if you want to cycle through a bunch of missions swiftly or just want a quick hit of action.-Sometimes enemies seem sparse and the heists seem empty because of it. Good for just getting through a mission, bad if you are itching to blast something.Ultimately, the pros outweigh the cons, especially considering the price, and this can be at least considered a Good Game™.

_childDocuments_.review: So for those who want a comparison to Payday--The gunplay, stealth, and general actions in my opinion is much better in this game than payday's; it feels a bit more realistic. The stealthing in this is 10x better without having to worry about zipties. You have 3x strikes on screwing up, ie. killing a guard/taking out a camera, but don't have to worry about the buzzer on guards. Easy to distract the attention and make them inspect a certain area to knock them out without being seen.However, stealthing is 100x easier than Payday, almost laughable. Love the mechanics, just everyone has some shotty short range vision for sure.It's less of a "puzzle management" to stealth, and just overall better--get in, and get out.However, the missions feel so...small. Especially if you play the single-player rogue-lite mode, which is a lot of fun, but stupid repetitive. Most missions you finish within 5-7 minutes at most (if not quicker), but it's largely the same 3-4 missions over and over until you get a big heist mission.If you're in it just to have fun in multiplayer, it's a bit better; you get to "select" your "boss", equipment, and the perks that you buy with the money you earn. However, the customization is severely lacking compared to payday.This game is totally worth $15-20, but does it beat Payday? Not exactly, better systems, just lack of content.Ignore the Voice Acting...it's just horrible all around...I thought there was an actual storyline, but not really. It's chopped up fast past where the "cutscenes" are just...random for the most part, just setting up a small story for the heist you're embarking on.I would have been upset paying anything more than $20 for this though.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Payday 3 but still heaps of wasted potential.Quick edit: on deeper thought I'd still overall recommend the game despite its incredibly goofy voice acting and writing. I think what I detail below is a big problem in the game's design, but the way that randomness is integrated even in events like bank heists (where you'll on occasion spawn in with some guards already pacified and the vault already open) does add a very fun level of RNG to this roguelite that I've not really experienced in other roguelites. That ultimately wins me over, I think.I don't know who thought throwing chess pieces from a jail cell into a laundry cart one story down was the kind of riveting gameplay I was expecting in this title, but they were very wrong. When I hire "experts" in these sorts of games, I really don't want to suddenly be put into their PoV and given a random mission that, if failed, completely wastes the resources I spent to use the supposed expert's services. _childDocuments_.review: Me and a few friends bought this game during the bundle deal, and we've been having a lot of fun with it.It's also one of the worst games I have ever played in my life.There is absolutely no excuse for this game to be in such an absolutely abysmal state after using Epic as an open beta for a year. In addition to running about as well as a dead raccoon that's had all four legs smashed into pieces by an aluminum bat, it's plagued by an overwhelming myriad of bugs, many of which are outright gamebreaking.In the short time me and my friends have played, we have encountered a bug that disables nearly every individual mechanic in the game, including but not limited to;-Losing the ability to fire weapon-Losing the ability to use ladders-Losing the ability to use equipment (Which I personally experience roughly every three to four games)-Losing the ability to move, turn camera, or really anything besides jump in place.And keep in mind, this is not one bug causing all of this at once. This is a multitude of different bugs occurring at different times under different circumstances, all fairly frequently. Not to mention the incalculable amount of smaller visual bugs, such as the van despawning when looked at from certain angles, frozen particles, elevators (visually but not mechanically) failing to move, doors (visually but not mechanically) failing to open, guns turning invisible, and your character turning pink for some reason?But wait, there's more! There's also plenty of awful game design that has nothing to do with bugs. For example, one mission begins with a cutscene of you hang gliding onto a roof. During this cutscene, you are actually already on the roof, and it is entirely possible for the game to spawn a guard directly in front of you, who will spot you while you are still stuck in the cutscene, and thus unavoidably fail stealth immediately before you even have control of your character. Me and one of my friends particularly encountered this at the end of a shuffle, which was especially frustrating considering said mission is arguably the hardest loud mission in the game.Oh, that also reminds me of a mission that starts you on a moving platform, in which I once spawned in late, the platform having already left, and resulting in me falling to my death the moment I spawned.Speaking of failing stealth, another bug we encountered was guards becoming fully "alerted" by nothing. They would remain like this until they actually saw something suspicious, at which point they would instantly, actually alert.Now, lets talk about the game closing. Yes, these devs somehow even managed to butcher closing the game, demonstrating a level of incompetence I wouldn't even expect from a rock that somehow acquired brain damage. In my personal experience, closing the game from the menu closes the window, but does not actually end the process, leaving it to eat thousands of megabytes in memory and bring my computer to a snails pace until I close it from Steam or the task manager.But why close the game when I can close my entire computer? Because upon leveling up after one match, my primary monitor died, my secondary monitor froze, and my computer completely locked up, all while the last sound to play from the game rapidly stuttered as is typical for a game crashing like a Boeing plane heading for a whistleblower convention. It didn't end there however, because upon manually restarting my entire computer and rejoining my friend ingame, I discovered my level had been reset to 1. What made this extremely interesting however is that I still had all of my money and unlocks. It had not reset my save, only my level. I cannot fathom how this even happens. Why is the level stored separate from the rest of the save? Why? Why? Why? Regardless, I initially believed this was a good thing, as it only meant I would unlock rewards faster due to my newfound lower level, but I was quick to learn that despite still possessing my unlocks, they were all also re-added to the drop pool, meaning many of my levels would effectively result in no reward due to being offered things I already have.In summary, the devs have somehow spectacularly fumbled in just about every possible aspect you could imagine to create one of the most horrendous games I have ever made the mistake of spending money on in my life. I genuinely cannot even begin to understand how some of these catastrophic errors even came to be, or how they are still in the game after so long. All I know is if I had to trust the building of a bridge between this dev team, or a headless chicken supplied only with a toothpick and a piece of string, I would ask where the dead raccoon from the beginning of the review had gone to, because they would clearly be a better option than either. This game is objectively garbage and frankly it's an insult they have the audacity to ask you to pay them for this atrocity.I can't wait to play more.

_childDocuments_.review: It really depends on WHAT you like about PD. Someone else pointed this out well; it's not a complete "heisting simulator" but rather a "gang going on a heist simulator". I'll start with the cons and end with the pros for a specific reason.Cons: - Horrible voice acting. Honestly, it doesn't even feel "so bad it's good" level to me, it's just painfully bad. The experience was actually degraded until I turned voices to 0% in options. The game then became way better.- There are definitely the occasional bugs, not the "this game just works a little differently" type, moreso the "I just outright can't use my throwable in this play session" type. However, for me and my friends, it hasn't been every session. - The game could definitely be waaayyy better optimized. 3060Ti shouldn't be at 5FPS on the main menu with a couple of characters and a map loaded, even if it's "max settings" by default, it doesn't look quite complicated enough for that.- Sometimes the AI does some very ridiculous things.Pros:- Very solid gameplay loop. "Multiplayer" and "singleplayer" are actually two different types of games. Singleplayer is a roguelite while multiplayer is just about the heists and making piles of money. It helps use the same gameplay for different mechanics and progression types, keeping the game feeling fresh (at least to me so far).- Game is pretty nicely balanced towards still keeping a good amount of pressure on the player, despite the time-regenerating health. I was concerned they'd be as bad as One Armed Robber is about it, but fortunately not.- Non-dumb AI pathing. AI actually does help with carrying bags and even deposits them for you. Not completely reliable but better than Payday's. - Bag system may be liked or disliked. Personally I like it though. Bags are just bags, you can hold one bag with little consequence, but holding a second bag prevents you from using your primary and slows you down a bit. I have my concerns on the longevity of the gameplay and whether the devs can update it to keep it well-maintained and listen to the right feedback. Hopefully they do well with it, though. I heard others say the devs are very pro-modding, but I don't know how much you can mod the game considering it's Unreal Engine (unfortunately). The game, while it has technically existed for a year, has only just now came to Steam, making it to where it'll actually start having attention. There's been a few simple UI and model change mods, so hopefully we can have some gameplay changing mods as well.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 10/31/24 - Unfortunately the devs have succumbed to the trend of using AI generated art in the new Rockay Rumble map, which screws over artists and their work. Hopefully something is done about the art and this does not become a trend for the game. A shame, because the game is still fun, and the new map/event is fun as well, but its hard to recommend in good consciousness knowing that the devs intend on using AI generated art. Until something is done about the art (or im just wrong about it being AI generated in the first place) ill be changing my recommendation to No, A real shame, because everything in my original review down below still stands.ORIGINAL REVIEW -This game is very silly but very fun. The roguelite campaign in the core of the game, and its fun to see how far you can get or how much money you can make. Some slight crust in regards to performance, both of the game and actors who appear in the game, who give performances ranging from chuckle worthy to bone chillingly cringe. It kinda honestly feels like a PS2 or early XBox game plucked from nearly two decades ago and dropped it into today.I bought and played the game while it was on Epic, and comparing the game from then to now, theres some things that have changed a little for the worse (each of the unique heisters used to have special perks that made them stand out from the generic goons you can hire) and for the better (new heists, new maps for the existing smaller jobs). There was also a decent amount of story cutscenes in the first few runs you did that are either cut or spread throughout multiple runs, which makes the story feel a little disjointed or clunky.Gameplay wise, it feels and plays more closer to an arcadey style shooter like Call of Duty, with sliding and regenerating health that requires you to use cover effectively, compared to the slower and more methodical gameplay that Payday 2 has to offer. Theres a fun risk reward mechanic with the drills and saws on heists that have them, where you can speed the drill up at risk of overheating the drill and needing to restart it. Your AI companions flip between being very useful friends and nearly sabotaging a stealth run when they decide to grab a bag or zip tie a civilian who isnt relevant.Overall, fun and worth some of your time, especially considering the price of the game at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I thought the game was going to be all memes when I got into the playtest, but I hyperfixated on it like a mother ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I have been craving a decent crime boss type game where you fight for control over city territory and work to protect your assets. This game really scratches the itch without needing to turn the whole game into an isometric turn based top town game. The game's mechanics do a pretty good job of letting you feel useful and capable without gating a bunch of skills or talents necessary for a particular heist type behind a lengthy grind (looking at you payday 3). You can stealth or play your missions aggro and you aren't punished by the game if you need to switch from stealth to aggressive. For the purposes of this review, I am going to assume that the devs intentionally love the cheesy over the top dialogue and the action movie tropes, so I won't be including that in my further breakdown. It's not the way I would write dialogue, but it's clear to me this game is a love letter from the devs.-The Good-The mechanics of the game are pretty good. They could use a little bit of responsiveness tweaks, like sometimes your bots will get confused or stuck, but largely, the systems work really well together in my experience.Looting things and packing bags feels satisfying. Something about the sound design and the visual of loot flying towards you while you gently caress it with your hand feels pretty damn satisfying. The sound design in general is really great. The guns, voices, music, etc it all sounds pretty good to me.The devs very clearly care about this game and want it to succeed. Prolific closed testing, good price point, and embracing the meme-ability of the game. The fact that it seems like people who bought the game on Epic and participated in the closed tests seem to have gotten steam copies for free is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool imo. The incentives to play the multiplayer function with random people, indicates to me that the devs care about fostering a good and respectful community. It seems to me that they want people to play together rather than alone. BUT they also empower you to play the game by yourself too if you prefer that! Which is such a nice change from all the controversies surrounding 'always online' style games. -The stuff that needs a little work-Some of the weapon animations, such as checking the revolver's cylinder every single time you pull out your sidearm, needs to go away. It is so frustrating to be in the middle of a fight for my life with a tiny sliver of health and for my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ character to open the weapon to check the ammo while in the middle of a life or death moment when he already knows it's loaded. One time when you first pull out the weapon would be good. No more than that. The animation team did a good job, but you don't have to beat me over the head with how sick your revolver animations look.Loading screen/skip jankiness. The loading screen/mission start up screen needs a little TLC imo. Not much to say about this other than sometimes the skip button doesn't work as intended or the start of a mission hiccups a little bit. Nothing game breaking but would be a nice quality of life improvement.The game runs a little hot. My computer is not top of the line and up to date right now by any means, however, I am not experiencing any of the stutters, freezes, or frame issues other people seem to be having. But, the game does use quite a bit of hardware resources and can sometimes make my pc chug a little bit.-What I would like to see-This part is very subjective to me, but I have been playing with and streaming for a discord full of my friends and they largely agree with many of these things.1. I want an endless difficulty for the campaign. I want the ability to toggle the campaign into an endless state so that I can make a run last as long as I possibly can. I'm honestly not sure exactly how that would work given the current way the campaign is structured, but man that would be so fun.2. In addition to the nice rogue-like mechanics of the campaign, let me get temporary buffs that affect only the next run. Let me buy something or unlock something that has mutator effects for my next run, like "20% more cash from heists next run, but the Cognali robots begin the campaign helping the police from the start" or "The boss starts with a weapon of your choice, but he only gets one weapon slot" or even "If you hit the green zone when speeding up a drill or saw for the first time, it stays sped up permanently, but when you alert the police they start at one star higher than normal" stuff like that.3. Let us make a custom boss for the campaign, and allow us to change the look of our unlocked characters in both multiplayer and single player. I want to spend my cash on dumb stuff like shirts and pants and hairstyles too in addition to weapons and perks. That about does it for me. I have to say I really love this game already and I have a blast while I am playing it. I easily get sucked into a campaign run and time just flies by while I'm focused on that. Thanks to the devs for making a good, affordable, well crafted game. Keep on working on this game, and I think it'll go down as one of the most legendary multi-genre games in recent history.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: You have to appreciate a certain kind of schlock to get a kick out of this concerning everything "Story" and theme-wise. But some people won't.We have Vanilla Ice and Danny Trejo fighting against you for control of the city, Chuck Norris giving the weirdest voice performance imaginable, Michael Rooker playing your gunked out LMG wielding enforcer, Danny Glover being your man for everything concerning the police, Michael Madsen playing the most Yankee cowboy crime boss imaginable, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wild honestly. Say what you will about performances, they are anything but forgettable. Hell out of all the songs in the world Bomfunk MC's - Freestyler is constantly playing, that should give you a good idea on what to expect.Gameplay-wise, it's definitely reminiscent of Payday, and that is a good thing. We don't have enough Heist-like games, and Rockay City does a few pretty great things that improve a lot about the gameplay-loop such as:There are a few other things i'll cover, but those two are the definite winners by far. But there are few things that could use a touch up or something of the sort.The game has such enormous potential, and with the release on steam, i really desperately hope it becomes the first real contender to compete with Payday 2. _childDocuments_.review: Updating to provide more info:When I first saw this game on steam I asked myself, why is it being advertised on the front page? "Rockay City" sounds like some sort of GTA ripoff, and the picture looked like the old "Mafia Wars" facebook game. Even the screenshots weren't very convincing. Then I found that it had actually released last year, but on to the black hole that is the epic games store, so no wonder why I never knew it existed.I watched a few youtube reviews that really painted a horrible picture, but I thought the gameplay looked half decent. Since the game has received numerous updates and a lot of TLC from the devs, I decided why not. Now I have little to no experience with "heist style" games such as payday, but it's a fun concept to me. I can tell the devs have put a lot of time and effort into updates, gameplay features, weapons, characters, etc. that it's worth my time. Plus the addition of all DLC released up to June 18 2024 is a no brainer. Original review below:Ignore any outdated reviews posted online before this Steam release. I'm having a ton of fun, it's simple but entertaining gameplay, and the dialogue is so bad it's hysterical. I've played some of the rougelike singleplayer which has been great, and a few short missions with bots for multiplayer. I can't stress how great it is to play with bots, and that they actually work well! I'm sure it's even more fun/easy with people but it works great for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I will be updating this review as I continue playing the game.So far I have to say this game is much more fun than I expected. The story driven elements of the game a cheesy but honestly the vibe of the game kind of fits it.Loving the fact the game has a progression system giving you a reason to want to come back and play.The gun play feels very good, the movement is a little strange at first but easy to get used to.Rogue-lite campaign is by far one of the coolest features in the game. This makes you play as a crime boss leader, there is a pretty big area that is cut into sections. Those sections are controlled by different crime bosses and your mission is to capture everything before the investigation gets finished in you. The investigation process length depends on how you do your heist mission and such. Because to be able to control the territories you need people and to be able to have people you need cash to get that cash you need to do heist and to be able to do heist you need a crew to be able to afford that crew they take a cut. All of the elements come together and while all this you need to make sure the boss does not die as that ends the run. This game mode has other elements to it as well like selling the stolen good, investing and ect.All around so far the game is awesome just having some fps issue and even had a part where my fps dropped to 25 and stayed there till I finished the mission.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss: Rockay City sounds like a cheap mobile game, but that couldn't have been farther from the truth. It got me seriously hooked with it's addicting gameplay loop. It brings a fresh take on the whole heisting formula with it's roguelite campaign which is unique every run you do. The game is packed with unlockables for you to unlock in a gacha-style level up system, which worked fairly well to keep me coming back to the game for more and more. The game will kick your ass the first few tries, but you'll keep getting better and better, and the game rewards you with permanent unlocks to make your next run slightly easier. It's all a learning experience, and I enjoyed all of it, it helped me get the most out of this game.The campaign has you taking over the city, turf by turf. To get turfs, you need money, that's where jobs come in. These are fairly varied and range from warehouses, compounds, armored trucks, banks, jewelry stores, malls, etc. And then you also get the BIG jobs which are more elaborate heists with greater rewards. The campaign has multiple options for a variety of aspects, such as making other bosses leave the city in alternative ways or capturing multiple turfs with 1 attack, in short the campaign provides enough variety for you to keep coming back to it.When you're done with the campaign, there's also multiplayer, which lets you experience the single player jobs in a more traditional, payday-style experience, with friends or with bots. Multiplayer has it's own progression system, and while it's a little bit on the grindier side, it also helped with providing content for me to keep playing to unlock.The devs have made great efforts to make this game as Single Player-friendly as possible, EVEN the Multiplayer mode of the game. I'm a Single Player type of guy, I very rarely play multiplayer, these days almost not at all, so this is greatly appreciated. The bots in this game, while they have their own quirks, are already pretty solid when compared with other games. They work as a team, do objectives, collect and deliver loot, among other things that make my experience as a single player that much more enjoyable.A big part of this game is the gunplay, and the gunplay in this game is TIGHT and PUNCHY! Enemies don't suffer from the spongy syndrome, and guns feel and sound STRONG! Animations are great, and so are all the other effects that complete the whole gunplay experience. Shotguns in particular are straight up porn, the devs made sure to not mess up the shotguns in this game. A FPS game with terrible shotguns is not a FPS game.The stealth in this game is fairly basic and braindead, but it's the kind of stealth that I enjoy. This is a game you're meant to replay a lot of times, so stealth doesn't need to be too complex.The game also has a very strong B-Movie feel, with it's cast of celebrities. The dialogue of this game is straight up cheese from the 90s, but in a good way (except Sheriff Norris' lines, which are straight up ASS). It makes the game feel unique and not take itself too seriously. The licensed soundtrack they've picked also complements this. The devs seem to have fully embraced the cheese.The glow up this game has had from it's almost-disastrous launch to the addicting fun experience that it's become today is to be commended. The devs have shown that they're very passionate about the game, they've listened to feedback and have implemented improvements with various updates, and they're still doing this today.Now I did mention that this game has issues, and boy does it have SOME issues! AI glitching out or getting stuck, optimization issues, softlock issues, the game still needs work. But like I mentioned above, the devs are actively listening to feedback and improving the game with each update they release. And I'm still tolerating these issues whenever they show up, just because of how damn fun this game is.

_childDocuments_.review: When Crime Boss released on the Epic Launcher awhile back I considered it and ultimately decided not to get it yet as I had other interests at the time but after seeing it release on Steam given my overplayed boredom of GTA5 along with the poor release of Payday 3 with the same repetitive nonsense as the first two games while I eagerly await GTA6 I must say that Crime Boss fills that void quite well as it is one hell of a fun game that doesn't disappoint! Here's why...+ PROS +++++++++++ Outstanding Visuals!+ Outstanding Audio!+ Outstanding Gameplay!+ Outstanding Characters and some based on Real Hollywood Actors!+ The Rogue-like Campaign gives the game infinite replay value!+ Fantastic Story and Plot+ Hilarious Moments+ Choice and Consequences+ Random Unexpected Events+ Increasing Mission Difficulty+ Singleplayer and Multiplayer+ Legitimate quick-join co-op and not some lame only join if you host and have friends+ Excellent Skills+ Excellent Equipment+ Excellent Upgrades+ Decently Open Maps+ Future Planned Roadmap from Dev Team+ Turn-based Events are very involving for players- CONS - ------------- The AI is questionable at times such as on Easier and Normal the AI can often easily be outgunned usually- Theres a lot going on in the game so it can be overwhelming at first even though the game does teach you- Buying more AI Soldiers at first isn't really taught very well other than needing them so this created some problems later for me until I realized I was supposed to be doing that all along during each turn- I wish that there was some more larger-scale open-world like missions such as actually Driving to a Mission, parking a Van in a suitable spot, getting out, and then going on the mission then later being able to drive off after completing a mission which would make the game feel way more immersive- I do kind of wish that the game was more real-time and not-so-much turn-based but I guess that is the only way to make it happen effectively as I am a huge fan of realistic dynamics- I'm currently halfway through my first campaign and that worries me slightly as I feel like I might beat it quickly which makes me question its full-replay value as to what will happen when I play again if I will be bored and stop playing= VERDICT ============== Crime Boss is an outstanding game with a lot of replay and value that delivers some serious fun and I can highly recommend it. I really hope to see some great updates in the near future as well as a sequel way down the road, it deserves a lot of attention and is a hidden gem in its own right!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An excellent co-op heisting FPS that's inspired by cheesy 80s/90s action movies and shares similarities with PAYDAY. I'd recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of the PAYDAY series or just wants to rob some banks with friends and listen to old Hollywood actors deliver cheesy lines. Also the game is bizarrely cheap, all the DLC is free to keep if you get it now, and future DLC will be the same way.The devs must've done a complete 180 because I recall people giving the game scathing reviews last year when I can't really find any major flaws with it now. The dialogue is very cheesy and Chuck Norris clearly did not care whatsoever when delivering his lines, but that made me laugh and every other celeb does a pretty good job (even Vanilla Ice!). Otherwise I don't see why this would've deserved being labeled one of the worst games of 2023.In some ways Crime Boss: Rockay City is like if you took the neat ideas from rough gems of the Xbox 360/PS3 era and polished them up. Overall the game is heavily inspired by 80s/90s action films like Heat, Lethal Weapon, etc. The campaign is a roguelite (permanent progression is available so it's not a roguelike), each time you start a run you'll be met with a different cutscene, a different main heist to work toward for that run, different missions, etc. etc.This aspect of the campaign is fun, though it does also feel like they had a normal-styled linear campaign during development and then chopped it up. The cutscenes that play feel totally random and confusing at first, there's no real "intro" to the campaign either (anymore, apparently when this first released on EGS there was a sorta-intro mission that's no longer available for some reason?). I'd like to see this fixed down the road, along with co-op support for it.The multiplayer on the other hand is very similar to PAYDAY, and I can see why so many other user reviews compare the two. I've played all three of that series and after the disappointment of PD3 I do think Crime Boss is scratching that itch nicely, but it feels different enough that it doesn't come off as a PAYDAY "clone," it's more like "we enjoyed PAYDAY but want to make our own game in that style."I like the 80s/90s movie vibes (including with some of the missions), stealth isn't obnoxious and limiting (infinite zipties!), and I think the gunplay feels really good and weighty.I only have a few bits of feedback at the moment, and the ones that are complaints/negative are pretty minor:

_childDocuments_.review: Its a bad game. But its a fun bad game.As a first person shooter its fun. Enemies aren't in anyway smart but neither am I so it equals out. It gets compared to Payday frequently and I suppose that's unavoidable. There is more here than just heisting though. Deathmatches in the streets for turf. Low scale store knock offs, crew and gang management. Its a full crime em up.But, and I say this without an ounce of hyperbole, this is the worst writing and voice acting I have ever heard. The devs got big name actors (from the 90s and before) and not actual VAs. Listen Chuck Norris has never been a good actor. VA or otherwise. The script is written like an edgy middle schooler learned a new swear word and that has become his whole life. This is not how people talk. Edit:I've played for a bit now and while I do say that this game is overall still fun, the cracks are showing. Lets start with the single player roguelike.Baker's battle is fun when it works. It doesn't always work and it makes even less sense. I have had multiple runs end due to various bugs. Had one where police robots showed up completely at random on low heat early in the run before they are introduced. Had another where I ended the day and it skipped multiple days in one go, timing out heists, skyrocketing my investigation and losing my territories. One time I hit 100% investigation and...nothing happened. Norris never showed up. Continued on with the game. The logic of this game is frustrating. This is due to the complete lack of it. For example, as you progress, one of your assistants comes to you with an offer to buy a new car to raise your rep. So you shell out six figures for one....then break into a DMV so its not registered as stolen. I DIDNT steal it. We bought it. Money exchanged hands. Next is during one of the heists we have to scout a port to see what boat is carrying a load of drugs into the city. After we discover when and where the boat will be, the worlds worst assistant goes "yes, looks like the usual boat in the usual port." IM SORRY? We already knew? It has a routine?  We gathered intel and spent money on info we already knew?This is due in part to the absolutely abysmal writing. It appears this game's budget went to hiring expensive actors instead of actual writers and VAs. Every line is off. Either it doesnt make sense in context, or goes on way too long or its being delivered by someone 3/4 of a way through a whiskey bottle. There is ONE exchange late in the game that sounds like two people having a convo. If you fail your run but survive and escape Madsen and Rooker will have talk about starting over. It feels (and sounds due to the sudden drop in mic quality) like this was a candid convo that just happened to get recorded. And if you read into what they are saying about "this is bad and a nightmare" following Madsen's disappointed sigh and Rooker's laughing, it almost comes off as they are making fun of the game candidly. Some lines go on way too long. Someone will make a point and then there will be another 3 or 4 shot and reverse shots of each character just making an awkward quip or saying something completely out of pocket and unrelated. Sometimes, especially with Madsen and Nasara, their lines will turn into complete gibberish. Just a random assortment of words. I think, I cannot confirm, but my headcannon is that the devs got these big name celebrities to say a line or two then used AI to do the rest. Including writing their script. There are so many moments where I had to stop and think "no human would say that." Overall though, its still fun. I like the combat. I like the more free take on stealth vs Payday. I do think the game is very easy. Early in the run you will blitz through missions. Even late game when you get a decent crew together, you'll chew through enemies. The only difficult part is the investigation meter, which I honestly really dislike, and turf wars. Turf wars are more difficult because you are playing as a random soldier. This means you cannot build them or choose their equipment. I do like the randomness of it but I am tired of spawning into a gunfight armed with only a knife. The investigation meter constantly ticks ahead and Norris for somereason only focuses on you. You can do nothing but stealth and keep under the radar but Norris will still find you and ignore everyone else. Its terrible and sucks.I do recommend it. Especially with all the free DLC. There is a surprising amount of game here given the price. Just be ready to put your head in your hands whenever Chuck Norris chokes out a line like a illiterate 3rd grader.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright here's the gist of it:It's far better than Payday 3, but no where near as good as Payday 2. It basically sits right in the middleHowever, unlike the current version of Payday 3, the game very much has a Soul, you can tell the studio actively WANTED to make this game.And quite frankly, after a year of constant love from the devs, it's in a very good place right now.Because here's the thing... this game, isn't just a cheap Payday clone, there are plenty of cool and unique ideas that makes this game stand out on its own 2 feet, like the rogue-lite campaign mode with character perma-death, the bigger heists having some pretty cool Cooperative mechanics that makes it easier to complete, the AI bot system actually being one of best in the entire genre.To me, this game went from a crappy 3/10 at launch to a solid 7/10 now, which is damn impressive considering it was achieves in the span of a single year.Overall, this thing went from a complete slop at launch to an actually enjoyable and surprisingly good coop experience, for 20 bucks, you're getting a very decent product that'll last you for a while, with more updates/DLCs on the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: What Payday 3 should've been. As an avid player of Payday 2 who was utterly disappointed at the outcome of Payday 3, I found this game on a whim a day before it dropped. I playtested it, not expecting much, but six hours went by and I was enjoying the hell out of the Baker's campaign. It has high replayability value due to nature of the turn-based mechanics, it's pretty, decently optimized, and the AI are actually capable of following instructions, looting, and being immersive enough to keep the game fun and fresh. For the price (which currently includes the DLC), it's highly worth it. Take it from someone who excitedly pre-ordered PD3's Gold Edition and has sunk in maybe ten hours total, if even that, this is much more fun. It can be quick, the combat mechanics are varied and fun, there's load out customization, weapon skins, the heists aren't tiresome or pointlessly elongated, there are drills and saws that you can choose to accelerate (if you screw up, that's on you), and a variety of different playing modes and heists of which there's more to come! Seems like the devs listened to everything that was mildly infuriating about Payday and turned it into something good. Find some friends, take it online, or play by yourself. Worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that launched what, a year ago, and was terribly received, it's actually really good. Now I didn't experience it at launch so I can't say whether it was as bad as it sounded and there has been massive fixes and changes, or if it was just review bombed by everyone and everything and it was fine from the start, but really what matters now is the state that it's currently in which I consider to be pretty amazing.First off, rougelites, I love em. Not only will the missions be similar to PD:2 where locations are randomized, but the city map and who controls what will be as well. The whole point of the original non-DLC campaign is simple, take over the city before the police have enough evidence to shut you down. Raise funds through large and small time jobs, take over and hold territory, eliminate entire enemy factions, all against the ever climbing investigation meter. You also have the daily heat meter which rises when things go south. If your first job of the day attracts the attention of the police, and you hold your ground or don't get out soon, this meter will begin to rise from 1 to 5 stars. Starting with normal patrol officers and ending with heavy units like shields, juggernauts, and special units. If you get jobs done quiet like, the police response will remain minimal. If every job of the day has been an extended shootout with the police, as soon as the alarm is raised special units will have boots on the ground incredibly quickly. When you advance the day, this meter will reset, unlike the overall investigation meter. Second, guns and gameplay. I really have no complaints here. The movement is solid and the guns feel punchy. The biggest issue I have is, where are the silencers? Although not strictly necessary, silencers can save you from going loud under certain circumstances. For hire characters come with their own gear, so I say, just keep a lookout for any with a silenced pistol just in case. Maybe there is a way to unlock a purchasable gun with a silencer that I could distribute to all team members that I just have not gotten to yet. The stealth system is also satisfying. One of the biggest plus sides here is the ability to holster your gun after taking it out. I don't even think these guys wear masks like our Payday crews, but it's apparent that the Payday crew applies their mask with Gorilla glue to ensure it can not fall off and their identities exposed during their heists. Here, you can unholster and holster your weapon as necessary during the stealth phase, which is great.AI: Pretty darn good. But keep in mind this game does have strictly single player modes as well as multiplayer so I would expect no less. They will come in and help gather loot, tie down civilians, and carry things to the van. You can order them to do specific tasks as well if needed. Bugs: Incredibly rare and thus far never game breaking. I think I've seen 2 civs kinda phased into a wall slightly but they came out and resumed normal behavior after being shouted down. There was also one mission about freeing a prisoner or something from a transport and once released he just kinda got stuck by the truck but it made no difference, mission still complete and everything was good. I'm assuming he should have run off of the map. Overall with the release here on Steam that kinda reminded us yes, this game exists, plus the low price for the base game and all current DLC, it's 100% worth it. I think it would be worth it even without a discount. And this game isn't over yet. There is still more to come. I'm not sure exactly what the devs plan for this game is, whether it be supporting it for a long time like PD:2 or a much shorter lifespan, but I'm here for it and definitely welcome new content and maybe one day a second entry in the series since now I do consider it a good game, worth the time and worth continuing to make. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I bought this game myself on EGS and all DLC and received a free Steam copy because I assisted with beta testing roughly a month prior to the Steam release. I am not affiliated with or paid by 505 or IGS.This game was good at launch on EGS, though lacking a bit of polish and content, as opposed to some of the games released in the same time frame that didn't even work for most players. Yet somehow those AAA title got better reviews than this game from 'influencers' and 'journalists'. I guess it doesn't matter as long as you get the clicks and views. Anyway, that's water under the bridge, so let's take a look at the Steam release!Fast forward from 2023 to 2024 and many updates and content updates later. The game is in a really great state at the moment, whether it's performance, content or balance. It's over the top, a bit cheezy, but good fun. Heisting in 90's Miami, euh I mean Rockay City! Single player roguelite campaign stays fresh replay after replay due to the well-implemented procedural generation and well-executed story and heist content. The expansions add major heists as well as new characters/skins and weapons. Playable offline too, none of that live-service stuff in here!Multiplayer offers a variety of heists and jobs and the unlock/progression system is well-thought-out. Did I mention Michael Madsen and Michael Rooker being amazing? (Can't say the same for Norris, but somehow it fits in with the cheese). The other characters are varied, with each their own character and voice lines, and when used as bots, work well to assist the player. Last, but not least: devs have been very committed with updates and new content and there's another year of that planned.Performance wise: it runs on Steam Deck and my ROG Ally has no problem with it too. Doesn't need a hefty PC to play.Anyway, if you're looking for a good heisting game, either single or multi player, and for a really nice price (at launch also includes ALL the DLC), then Crime Boss: Rockay City is a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant surprise. This is better at the Payday formula then Payday itself.That being said, don't expect Payday 3 going in. The game plays much like a rogue-like shooter with various objectives, ranging from gang shootouts, traditional Payday-style heists, and small jobs such as robbing compounds, gas stations, etc.There is also a management side to things as you hire soldiers to take over territory, as well as a small pseudo-market that you sell the goods you steal on - But be careful as the entire thing is permadeath.The multiplayer side of things plays much like normal Heist-'em-ups, with a persistent bank balance that remains between sessions/deaths, the missions are free-pick in the multiplayer. (Also features a server browser!) There is no real downside to playing multiplayer as a solo, as the bots and AI are competent most of the time, and you still progress if you private your lobby and fill it with bots. I highly recommend this to people who enjoyed Payday but were let down by 3, and are seeking a heisting game to fill that void.

This is probably due to the rough launch and notoriety this game had for being absolutely horrible on release. The lack of player base has made the multiplayer mode almost completely deserted, making it impossible to get a full squad match. As a result, you're often forced to play with bots, which becomes monotonous and feels no different than the campaign.Overall rating: 6.9/10. _childDocuments_.review: I put 20 hours into the play test and really liked it. I've played both Payday: The Heist and Payday 2 for over a hundred hours combined. Surprisingly, the bots in this game are more competent than my teammates in any Payday game (lol).This game is designed with solo play in mind. As a solo player, I can play solo with bots in both the campaign and solo multiplayer matches. I can switch and control them anytime, setting different loadouts for heists. Even if my main character dies in solo multiplayer, I can still switch to bots and complete the heist successfully. It's awesome.You can order the bots to loot, subdue guards, wait, follow, tie up civilians, break and loot stuff automatically, and take the loot to the van while you’re busy shooting cops.Weapon customization is limited; weapons come in presets. You can only choose primary, secondary, and equipment for your loadout. Weapons come in different colors and tiers as you level up. Similarly, urban legend heister bots are unique and have their own skills and play styles, but you can't customize them.I don't want to compare this too much to Payday, as it's more "inspired by" Payday, but Crime Boss: Rockay City is different in its own way. Heists are short, gameplay is more casual, weapon animation is good, and the visuals are stunning and stylized in a colorful way on ultra settings.Overall, I love this game. It's very affordable, with all free DLC on Steam launch. For $19 with another 20% off, it's really fun and worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Was very skeptical going into this game. However, I am very impressed with how it turned out. It's almost like the game is what Payday 3 should have been. It 100% feels like an addition to the Payday universe that takes place in Florida with some futuristic elements added.I was worried it would feel more like a cyber punk given from the footage and the trailer on the store page, but it only makes up a small fraction of the game. The rest of the game has a modern setting to it.The looting was very satisfying, and by far one of the biggest improvements in this game when comparing to Payday was the AI. The NPC companions are so smart and are actually useful. They help move bags and gather loot, and even just throwing a bag down a hallway, the NPC Heisters already know to go and grab it and move to the extraction point. One of the coolest features is the ability to switch to another companion mid heist and play as them or position them in a certain area for standby.The investigation bar that increases as you commit crimes and move throughout the days is sick. The heat system to make levels harder when committing too many heists in one day (in-game day) is also cool.The Turf War system was super interesting, and took up a bit too much of the game (more then I liked). Having to constantly go and defend turfs and take over other turfs was a very annoying and repetitive task.One of the biggest negatives with the game has got to be the voice acting, or atleast the animations for the characters when talking. It isn't synced pretty well with the audio and seems very off.The ability to pickup guns from dead bodies mid missions despite not owning them was a great idea.Lastly, the stealth was very cool, maybe a bit too easy. And the gunplay was some of the best I've every seen. The guns feel heavy but also smooth, and just has an immersive feel to them. The recoil with the guns is perfect.Amazing game. Needs some more missions though.And dammit, get a new logo for the game cuz my eyes bleed when looking at it during loading screens. Terrible logo.
