_childDocuments_.review: In case you, like many, were disappointed by Payday 3, Crime Boss: Rockay City is an extremely enjoyable, if very janky and silly heisting experience. The main emphasis is put on the singleplayer roguelite mode, which has strategic elements in between missions. There is a big variety of missions to take on, far, far more than Payday 3, however a majority of these are smaller robberies, though there are still a lot of the big high-stake heists like it's competition. Bot behaviour is, compared to every Payday game on the market, Highly advanced. You can freely swap between any characters you bring onto your mission in loud or stealth, and bots will help with most objectives, such as bagging loot, pacifying civilians, and even delivering loot to the escape for you. The voice acting and storytelling will either be a source of constant annoyance or endless entertainment, as the big hollywood actors they had hired for the main characters in cutscenes where likely given not very good acting direction, as most, if not all, voice lines are very poorly acted. The main two exceptions are Nasara, voiced by Payday's very own Damien  Potier, and Dollar Dragon, voiced by Danny Trejo. Overall, though, Crime Boss is very enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: Worth the price of admission, the team behind Rockay City has proven they understand what this genre means as well as how to make it (mostly) work without fuss.  It isn't perfect, but it's much better than most of the AAA games I've picked up in teh last year.  It isn't a Payday equivalent, but it has the same feel, similar gameplay, has a great singleplayer line along with various multi-player options, and in total gives me exactly what I want versus the unfortunate experiences from earlier titles.If you go in with an open mind, and don't expect a carbon copy replacement of other games existing in the same space, you'll hopefully be pleasantly surprised.  The actors and actresses alone in this game make it worth the price - especially on sale!  And getting every bit of DLC alongside the reduced price was an all-time high coming from a game purchase for something that launched in the last 6 months or less.Pros:* Familiar gameplay, missions, and overall flow* Great voice acting and characters* Gunplay doesn't feel too overworked - it just plain works* Multi-player drop-in/out works great, and having a pseudo-campaign in multi-player is a bonusCons:* Some NPCs feel a little canned in the voice line department* A couple minor bugs crop up occasionally.  Nothing deal-breaking, but can be a brief annoyance.* AI just got retweaked, but it had felt a bit braindead at times.  We'll hope it's moving in the right direction now!* Buying 'new things' can feel a bit grindy due to rewards vs. purchase price.  I don't mind it, but I understand statements in this space.* A few visuals seem aligned to 'only the Boss / leader' in multi-player, meaning that only the Boss sees and effect.  We've been attempting to verify this in group in multi, and seem to have verified at least between the last few parties.And to address concerns from other reviews: I have never once had an issue finding a match.  The player count doesn't seem to hinder playing the game, and I also have friends that like to play as well, so best of both worlds.  My experience doesn't support those complaints, so YMMV.If it seems interesting, I'd say go for it.  It's not perfect, but it's certainly leaps and bounds better than some of the critics give it credit for.  And for the sale price and free DLC, it's extra worth it in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: For $20 at release, this game is amazingly solid. Keep in mind. For $20. This is a co op (or solo) heist action/stealth game. Sure. There's others that are similar, but this one brings it's own spin on it. First what this game does well...Solo mode. Multiple different ways to play solo! Different game modes, but the highlight is the roguelite campaign that's honestly decently engaging. For the gameplay. The story...yeesh...we'll get to that in a minute. But you'll play as...you guessed it, a crime boss. You're taking over Rockay City (stupid name, but whatever, move on) and you'll go about this by hiring crew, buying weapons, completing heists to fund your illegal activities. You'll be fighting for gang territory and evading heat from the police. It's a balancing act, but it's decently fun. There's random events to encounter, factions will react to you attacking them or even call for a truce, which you have the option to break. The heists and territory battles are relatively short and sweet. Nothing so intense you'll spend a lot of time on, but meaty enough to still feel like you're actually playing a game. The multiplayer is a little more of a traditional stealth/shoot'em up heist. It's mindless fun, you earn money, upgrade, customize, and that's kind of the loop. There's not a ton of customization for your guns, but it's still kinda fun to just unlock stuff. So the things I don't like. Sweet baby jeebus the writing for this is god awful. Like there's campy. And there's bad. Then there's this. The "humor" and believe me. "humor" is a very generous stretch is something that of a middle school child in the 90's wrote. I think it's trying to be campy. But some of the voice lines of this asinine script is truly headache inducing. If there was anything of a good idea of a storyline, it's completely washed out by the juvenile humor written by a robot that was told "make this funny, slightly edgy, and in the style of something the kids will like, but from the early 90's" and this is what it spat out. Very dated references. I...don't THINK the voice acting is bad? It might be. I can't tell if it's the writing or the voice acting. Considering I know these voice actors have other work that's great, I'm inclined to think it's the writing. Okay, Since I barfed out this paragraph about the writing. What else do I not like?....I guess if I were to be a bit picky, the random perks you get for promoting your crew kinda stinks. Maybe some weapon customization would be nice? I do like the little breadcrumbs of a reward that the grind could offer, but sometimes you just need that hook of seeing some upgrades that look really nice, and you're really motivated to play "just one more round" to unlock some cool stuff. This doesn't really have that. Overall, the $20 VALUE is great. I would gladly have paid $30 for some decent writing though.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss: Rockay City is more than just the anticipated Payday 3; it incorporates numerous quality-of-life (QOL) elements, offering a refreshing and dynamic gaming experience. This game brings a unique blend of strategic gameplay and action-packed heists, making it a standout in the genre.One of the key QOL improvements is the ability to carry a second bag, at the cost of reduced speed and the inability to use primary weapons. Additionally, you can command bots to neutralize guards or gather loot, adding a layer of strategic depth.The roguelike campaign is a highlight, featuring not just heists but also a strategic component where players must capture territory, avoid bankruptcy, and evade full-scale police investigations. This mode adds significant replayability and challenge, making each playthrough unique.Despite its simplicity, the story campaign complements the game well. It doesn’t burden players with complex moral dilemmas but instead enhances the gameplay with narrative-driven, planned heists. Notable missions include  each presenting intriguing scenarios, high difficulty, and substantial rewards.One of the most praised features is the removal of pagers, a popular mod in Payday 2. However, this doesn’t mean players can kill indiscriminately; murdering guards or breaking cameras raises the alert level, summoning the police at level three. Disabling cameras via a computer and tying up guards instead of killing them helps maintain a low profile. On missions against rival gangs, players can freely eliminate enemies without affecting the alert scale.Though the game has fewer locations, their procedural generation ensures that even familiar settings feel fresh and varied. This distinction sets Crime Boss: Rockay City apart from Payday, where repeated missions often felt monotonous due to unchanging environments. Here, the ever-changing layouts keep the experience exciting and unpredictable.The game's optimization is commendable, delivering stable FPS with high-quality graphics in single-player mode. However, multiplayer performance significantly drops, with FPS plummeting by six to seven times on my system, rendering the game unplayable even on minimal graphic settings. This is a significant drawback, especially since the multiplayer mode lacks the main campaign, preventing cooperative play in this engaging mode.Crime Boss: Rockay City offers a compelling blend of strategic and action elements, enriched by numerous QOL improvements and innovative features. While the single-player experience is robust and engaging, multiplayer optimization needs improvement. Nonetheless, its dynamic environments and varied gameplay ensure it stands out as a refreshing and enjoyable title in the heist game genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it, but barely... and that's a BIG "but".Edit: After a lot of needless frustration with having to kill the game multiple times per mission (read below) I'm changing this review to "Not recommended".It's an interesting concept with bite-size missions. The actors are simply legends, the music hits the nostalgia. But, apart from that, the game is really nothing special.It does, however, have some bad game mechanics. The perma-death of your characters in the single player campaign is questionable choice at best. The campaign is also over if your boss character dies. There are even level-up upgrades which gives you bonuses when re-starting the campaign. BUT... All of that goes down the drain considering the fact that you can easily open your Windows Task Manager and kill the game if you are in a tight spot and are about to lose a character or the boss. Killing the game will effectively restart your current mission.There is a reason why perma-death is offered in almost all other games that have it as optional - it's not because it's hard-core... it's because it's tedious, frustrating, boring and ultimately not fun - for all players except those few who explicitly want to play it.So, note to developers: If players need to kill the game in the Task Manager in order to go around a game mechanic - you've got yourself some bad game mechanics.This is supposed to be a stealth game. You have a lot of tools and game mechanics at your disposal to play it stealthy, and there are mission objectives to support that play style. However, the level design and enemy placement is not really though out very well. In many cases, you will find yourself in a situation where you simply can not accomplish stealth, simply because enemies are placed that way.I don't know what to say about graphics. Assets in your mission area are very detailed, character design is simply fantastic, but the whole environment, especially outside of the tiny mission area is simply - bad.There is a multiplayer mode, but I haven't touched it yet,... and probably will not touch it. I simply do not have enough time or friends to engage in it properly and I'm not really into teaming up with random players online. If you are into it, read other reviews which do cover multiplayer to find out more about it.Good idea, really bad implementation.

_childDocuments_.review: After logging around 12 hours and completing most of the Urban Legends campaign, along with trying out several other modes, here are my thoughts:Pros:  The game introduces a fresh twist to the heist genre, a welcome change since the days of "Payday 2." The dynamic maps, engaging storyline, intriguing voice acting, and high-octane gunfights bring a unique flavor to the gameplay.Cons:Unfortunately, the magic is frequently broken by numerous bugs. Let's start with the AI:The player-controlled bots are erratic at best. Sometimes, they behave like brain-dead guinea pigs; other times, they resemble trigger-happy chimpanzees, barely following instructions. When playing with friends online, they have the intelligence of a two-year-old, but in solo play there responsiveness brings them up to "Monkey with a Gun" complex which is "decent" but not great . The enemy AI is equally inconsistent, with difficulty levels not matching their labels—normal can feel like hard, hard can feel like normal, and extreme is a toss-up.Game Crashes: The frequent game crashes are incredibly frustrating. Halfway through a three-mission Urban Legends campaign, the game might freeze, leaving you stranded if you're playing online or completely freezing up if you're solo. This issue is severe enough to deter me from wanting to play again.Conclusion: While the game delivers a high-energy, explosive bank heist experience, the numerous bugs significantly hamper the enjoyment to the point of near unplayability. I am willing to push through the grind to unlock more gameplay and story elements, but this should be a choice driven by my love for the game, not marred by technical issues. Developers, please address these problems. I genuinely like this game and want to see it reach its full potential, but there's a lot that needs fixing.

_childDocuments_.review: This rating covers the state of the game currently along with the content, technical side and everything that's currently functional in the game. My review might miss some details in the game, but I'll note every one I can think of.To preface, I think the game is in a great state as is, has great multiplayer, singleplayer and I like a lot of how it works, but there are some weird things like a lack of a gunsmithing feature.Multiplayer, the multiplayer plays really well. The netcode itself isn't optimised, and as someone from South Africa it's going to be difficult to find games on 200 ping or less due to the ping being listed as a bar and not a number. The gameplay itself is very satisfying, reminiscent of payday 2, and for me the gunplay feels better. Headshots matter, but you won't run out of ammo if you don't hit them, I mostly played on hard and normal though. A good comparison would be: what if Ravenfield and Payday combined with a good campaign, better graphics, good humor and great gunplay. Note that during the campaign you can upgrade your team as well as the protagonist.Singleplayer, the Singleplayer is fun, you can choose "multiplayer" then play offline with bots essentially in small matches, or you can go on the campaign which is basically a very fast paced gang war style campaign. You get loot, recruit soldiers, take territory, defend it, and weaken enemies. There's also a roguelite aspect to it as well, i'm personally not a fan of roguelites(despite it literally stating that on the steam store page I know), but it's fun enough that I'm able to overlook it. The weapon balance isn't too leaned on the roguelite aspect so if you like a gun you can still use it, even if it isn't the best.Technical, as mentioned you can play multiplayer with yourself and bots, or with friends. Steam invites are a way you can use to get friends in, or with quickplay(which doesn't work that well), you can join game sessions using the session browser so it operates on session based servers. Weapon unlocks and skins are all RNG, there's no pay-to-win aspect or pay-to-get the best weapon or advantages in that sense(unless you don't buy the DLCs which are free right now, so this might become an issue in the near future)I find that I can play the game really smoothly on a 1080ti, but I have shadows turned down lower. Whether it's due to lack of optimisation or shadows just being really realistic, it might help if your game isn't running smoothly.There's a lack of a gunsmithing feature due to the roguelite elements, meaning that every gun and it's attachments are separate, I'm fine with it as is, but if the weapon pool gets bigger, there might be a need to have some sort of sorting or grouping feature.Appearance, You can pick the boss appearance you want, as well as the teammates you want, in the campaign the teammates are limited to a certain set of guns that can be exchanged between each other(so a weapon pool). The multiplayer aspect of this I forgot, but I'm pretty sure it's locked. The graphics are good, but not AAA so no realistic facial expressions or the like. It feels thematic and well made in the aspect of graphics. There are skins which are more like coloured versions of camo.Overall it feels like a game that has a lot of the technical inspiration drawn from earlier 2000s games(which I preferred over how badly modern games do it sometimes) where sometimes it feels like you have to jump through hoops to just get into a game, or that you're locked to online only like in most games nowadays. The music is literally from the 90s which I find enjoyable. The gameplay feels innovative, fun, and great even ignoring the early access state that it's in. I would recommend it, unless it gets worse.A list of features I think would make the game a bit more user friendly:Note: There are bugs which are covered in other reviews I have personally not encountered any so far. The only bug that I've seen was in multiplayer when my friend randomly got stuck and couldn't move.And stealth, normally I don't play stealth in games. I prefer to just go in shooting, hoping i'm hitting and trying to march through to victory. But in this game stealth feels enjoyable, you're still paranoid, but it's not like if you bump one pebble that a nuclear reactor goes off and it's just "well you should've watched where your boot was at that moment", it feels great.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Lots of potential. For it to be killed by live service monetization is ironic. Now they're bringing players back with the promise of all the DLCs for free. But be wary of a potential monetization effort by DLCs just like Payday. As long as they are priced correctly, I will buy.AI are pack mules for the money bags. That's about it. Enemy mobs seem to be fair. Extreme difficulty... is extreme. The rogue-lite campaign is fun.Multiplayer is fun as well. Support the game! Buy it! It's worth it (so far). A few bugs but definitely worth it for $20.A minor complaint: I am level 52. Each level grants you three magazines that can grant you skins for the guns or the bosses, AI mobs, and weapons. You can choose one magazine out of three. Not once have I gotten one silenced weapon or anything related to stealth. Other than the motion sensor. I would suggest giving the players weapons and utilities first before giving skins. I've been bombarded by skins that do not matter because I don't have the weapons to put it on!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 6.5/10. Needs more updates and fixes, but a good time waster for the price point. A game with potential that needs to be worked on.Crime Boss is a game I'm seriously mixed on. On one hand, it's very fun and for the price tag currently ($15.99 USD until 07/11/24) it's not a bad deal. On the other, there's a lot of flaws in this game that hinder the experience drastically and need polishing; like a Diamond that's stupid cloudy and jagged, but something can be made of it.My major concerns are the AI. The AI for friendly units need to be fixed or tweaked heavily, they constantly decide to run into the line of fire, ignore all semblance of danger and decide to eat 200 exploding propane tanks for breakfast, and get lost or stuck on random areas. Heists that are loud only, especially the "Big Heists", can easily fail because the AI decided to try to drive a car that's on fire and spray painted "DO NOT DRIVE, BOMB IN CAR". The friendly AI need either more damage resistance against explosives or just actually need to learn fire bad do not touch.My other concerns also come with gunplay, as guns are on a binary system here: Good or Utterly pointless. Most SMGs feel like peashooters due to bad feedback and even worse damage while shotguns are just stupidly broken, as even the most tanky enemies, like bosses during Territory attacks or Bulldozers fall over in 2-3 shots. Pistols also feel the same way, automatic pistols feel very poor due to harsh dropoff and weird recoil whereas revolvers consistently 1 or 2 taps at decent ranges. If Auto pistols or the SMGs get buffed and feel better, as well as the wonky balancing gets sorted out, I think gunplay would massively improve.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a  game, but I'm not entirely sure it's a good game either. Like many others leaving reviews like this, I only wish there was a way to leave a 'Mixed' recommendation instead of outright Yes or No. This game, as I've heard, is reportedly better than PAYDAY 3. I wouldn't exactly know because that game was borderline unplayable for me, with a somewhat spotty internet connection. That's a leg up for Rockay City - I can actually  it. The teammate AI is no doubt leagues more helpful than something like the OG PAYDAY 2, able to secure loot and down enemies in stealth and whatnot, but that's about as far as they go. AI likes to get directly into the line of fire a lot, and is generally only marginally helpful in a firefight. Stealth feels weirdly half baked, good in some ways (believe it or not I don't like the pager system in PAYDAY 2, but I know why it exists) and not so great in others (three strikes feel weird at times). The jobs themselves are hit or miss, either ludicrously easy if you have half a brain or just sort of braindead. Taking territory is an interesting thing, but it really just ends up being a money sink (why do all of my men disappear after a job. why does it cost tens of thousands of dollars to take a dozen men into a neighborhood?) with not too much reward, besides finishing the 'roguelike' campaign.I've only taken part in one 'big' heist, and so far I am not too fond of them. I went through four setup missions, dumped about a hundred thousand dollars into prep, only to get three strikes and FAIL the heist. No going loud, full stealth or you lose out on the job completely. Does it come back later? No idea. Is that a dumb way to handle a heist?  It feels counter-intuitive, but maybe I just didn't listen to a hint or some dialogue saying that I could outright fail. All in all, I'd give Rockay like...a six? Maybe? It's not horrible by any means, but it doesn't really function as a PAYDAY game as much as a PAYDAY inspired game. It doesn't feel like there's much focus on normal heists in the roguelike mode, and really my first experiences with the game aren't super positive. But it was cheap, and they generously bundle all the DLC into the single price, so that's nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much if PD3 and PD2 had a baby, but that baby ended up dropping out of high school.  The current sale price point with all the DLC is an amazing deal, but I just lost interest quickly.  Gunplay felt awful, and the AI is terrible.  Menus are clunky, and leveling up rewards you with a randomized reward, which is annoying.  Matchmaking doesn't seem to work at all, but the game does have a server browser.  The game has good ideas for its single player mode, but like I said before, the AI is just bad to make it an enjoyable experience.  Enemies and teammates just seem to move around aimlessly.  Game should have ditched the Hollywood stars and used that money to smooth the edges a bit.Game looks good visually, and the performance was ok.  Worked well on my ultrawide monitor at 1440p.Its a shame, because the game does have good ideas and a promising gameplay loop, but I just can't see myself playing this for very long, especially when you take into account the small playerbase.  I don't think this will be the go-to game for those who felt burned by PD3.

_childDocuments_.review: Bouy. Rockay City? What can you say about this game that isnt already scrawled on a tile floor in a public restroom? The game seemed like it was pitched to the numerous actors from days past as their digital time machine where hey could play themselves in their prime. Vanilla Ice could go back to be a respected member of "the culture", Micheal Madsen could go back to beating the bottle and tugging back on his girlfriends. Wait! Scatch that. Reverse it. Heck they even have chuck norris who has recorded over 8 minutes of dialogue. Lets be real the voice acting is shamefully and clearly where all the money went and long before anyone thought to write a script. I will say that Micheal Rooker is a consumite professional and will deliver his appaling lines with aplumb, even though he is an American Football themed criminal who you get to play weilding a Light machine gun whenever someone attacks your turf. Im getting a bit ahead of myself so Ill just say the plain truth about this game. The main gameplay loop is fine. Maybe even kinda addictive good. Like a live service game that keeps your attention until they feel like they have you and pull out inevitable money grab, but these guys knew they had a flop for a year on epic so no cash grab is in the works thankfully. As it stands this is simply a Paydayesque single player (unless you do the multiplayer thing) with a cringe worthy story that is lead by a man who clearly has been having a rough couple years because if those line deliveries were from a sober man I will eat my hat. Micheal Madsen is quite clearly drunk in nearly all his line reads and has been given no stage direction. Its all done in that verbatum style of cold reads that make it so so horribly unnatural you will want him to stop at some point. I give it a couple stars. I had fun and I am glad it seems to have been better recieved as the uniquely compelling dumpster fire it is. Slow down and look at the dumpster burn even though it is for sure making traffic worse for everyone else. I support buying this game simply so that the actors involved can continue to purchase the self medications that got them into this game in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good alternative to the much-hated Payday 3.The gunplay feels about on-par with Payday 2, which is serviceable- but very "early 2010s".Don't go into this expecting Rainbow Six Siege or Modern Warfare gunplay, it's fairly shallow and forgiving.It could definitely use some balancing for enemy spawn rates, and the more bullet-sponge-y enemies that break immersion a bit.Still, when it's put in the context of the rest of the game, I've been enjoying it a lot (as someone that's played an ungodly amount of Rainbow Six Siege).The writing is bad. Not good-bad, not entertaining-bad, just bad.There's a couple rules when it comes to good-bad entertainment:A bad comedy can't be good-bad. Jokes failing to land aren't funny.A self-aware movie/game that's TRYING to be good/bad will fail 90% of the time.There's a few moments here-or-there that might get a smile out of you- Chuck Norris riding a horse while carrying a Civil War cavalry sabre is one of the only moments that got a chuckle out of me, but that was about the peak of it.The casting feels very thrown-together.I can appreciate the intent of trying to create of sort of "Expendables: The Game" theme with people like Chuck Norris, Danny Trejo, and Danny Glover in the cast, but their performances are so phoned-in that it's more depressing than it is funny or entertaining. It feels like they paid each of them $5,000 to record some lines over a Discord call.Not to mention that the actual voice lines seem to be few and far-between.Also, it feels like they ran out of options when it came to casting...I love Michael Rooker, but he doesn't exactly fit the theme of "Campy 90s Action-Hero" game.Same goes for Michael Madsen, Kim Basinger, and Vanilla Ice... it feels like they were thrown into the game just because "They worked in entertainment in the 90s, and they're available".It'd be like randomly casting Kelsey Grammar to reprise his Dr. Frasier Crane role in this game, because the only stipulation seems to be "You existed in the 90s, yeah?"No hate to any of them, love them all, just a little wishy-washy on the theme of the game's casting.The overworld stuff is a lot of fun (seems to only be available in the single-player mode, be aware).Managing your gang, taking over territories (which results in a short gunfight between your gang and a rival gang), managing finances, keeping the "heat" low so that Chuck Norris doesn't find you and stomp you into the ground, it's a good time.Not particularly deep, but a good time for sure.Overall, for $20 (or the current $15.99 on sale) including all of the available DLC in the base price, it's been very worthwhile for me.Recommended highly for someone looking for a Payday alternative with a different vibe / offline gameplay- with some light multiplayer aspects on top.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple fun game whose name sounds like a fake mobile game, no real bs just straight up gameplay.The graphics are gorgeous and vibrant, the gameplay is simple and the guns are stupidly addictive to shoot. I'm very glad stealth is optional and the game doesn't punish you for going loud, because shooting in this game is half the fun. Every weapon feels and sounds heavy and powerful, with the LMGs in particular feeling incredibly overpowered and fun.The single player campaign is a roguelite, where you grow your criminal empire through missions and events of your choosing, where characters and their weapons, bought with your hard earned crime money, can be lost in a permadeath system. In theory it sounds bad, but in practice it's actually quite fun (and very forgiving, mind you, as characters can be rezzed indefinitely in a mission) once you realize the whole thing is meant to be replayed over and over, and the lack of permanence is its biggest feature.I know lots of negative reviews complain about the system but in my experience it's actually quite fun, with how chaotic and hectic the missions can get once you go loud, it truly makes you fight for every inch in the hardest difficulties, where you'll often question yourself if it's worth going back in for another bag or two of loot, or risk more characters and your haul trying to save another character from death. Adding to the system is the main character and boss, Travis, who gives you a 50% bonus on all the loot you get in a mission, with the drawback being that if he dies during a mission the whole run is over and you start from scratch.You'll win and lose many characters and money throughout the course of your criminal empire, and at the end of the session you'll be left feeling like no matter what, you did things your own way, even if you bit off more than you could chew then clawed out of a bad situation or died trying, losing the whole run.The multiplayer mode has a f-ton of gamemodes and absolutely 0 drawbacks for losing, so it's really fun to mess around with too, but in my opinion the singleplayer and it's permadeath system are the highlight of the game.

This is rather close to that.'member when payday 3... ok I didn't and still don't want to play it.But I drifted a bit there, game is rather fun for mindless shooting, has some good missions, has stealth, is not utterly ridiculous if you go guns blazing at lower levels but you will feel the heat, on harder difficulties you will of course get more of a challenge so this game will continue to grow in that regard.As for single player content, it's ok, acceptable I guess, do have some gripes with how the investigation advances, the goals and such, but it's rather well made, would love an endless mode, just fighting for territories back and forth without a "doom clock" on top of me all the time, yeah, lowering it or not just doesn't cut it, but that's my own taste, as I mentioned it's all rather well done and you do feel how your characters level up.Finally DLC, well I got this game with that DLC bundle and I can say it made quite the difference for my gameplay, some of the heavy hitters weapons pack are rather well made and well, they'll honor the nickname, that's pretty much it, if you're looking for a mix between Payday 1 + Payday 2 some good characters with decent (just decent) voice acting and acceptable story, this is definitely your game.PD: a really good thing is that bots (companion bots that is) aren't completely dumbed down as in the other games I mentioned before.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game about a year ago and plaed it a lot back then. It's a nice change of pace from Payday, its main competitor, in the fact that its enemies are fewer than in Payday, but more bulletspongey. I find the roguelike elements to be enjoyable, but quite repetitive. It's pretty trivial to win a good run once you find an optimized strategy that works for you, as opposed to other rogue likes - I think this game needs to either drop the randomness or fully lean into it.The reason for the negative review is that sometime since I last played the game and now, they have added images into the game that were generated using AI. I had hoped they would just be used in the Halloween map as placeholders for a seasonal event, which doesn't justify it in the least, but is at least reasonable, but once I hopped into Shuffle mode I noticed them everywhere. I would rather INGAME STUDIOS put up sketches and drafts of storyboard artists than them using generative AI. It not only feels untrue to the games 90's setting to use such technology, but completely goes against every acceptable stance on generative AI. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the 'Rockay' start, Crime Boss has definitely proven as the spiritual PAYDAY successor.  I played PAYDAY 3 and found it to be so bland and disappointing. Guards can be subdued which wont count against your 'suspicious action' (pager) limit.  The maps make sense logically and I liked how there was always a plan B for loud heists if you mess up.  As long as they release solid content and improve on what's here they will follow in the footsteps of the legendary PAYDAY 2.  This game does have a lot of stark difference from PAYDAY, like preset characters vs the 'Boss' characters, weapon rarities, and the Saints Row 3 like story.  Initially it was kind of annoying, but all the dumb lines and characters have grown on me.  I also like that this game has a single-player themed strategy mode that helps to add to the variety found in the game.  If you are a veteran PAYDAY player and are also disappointed with the state of PAYDAY 3 I'd recommend giving Crime Boss: Rockay City a shot.  *Last note I forgot to add in the body: This game does have some performance issues.  I have a 5800x3D, 3070ti, and great internet and I get ridiculous studders in the game if playing multiplayer.  Lowering settings helps but it seems to be present no matter what.  Hoping that some optimizations come out soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I have no clue how this game was a year ago when it released in EGS jail. I heard it was bad. It probably was. And Rockay is a stupid name. But the game I just got on Steam with all the DLC for $15? That game whips ass.Gameplay-wise it's another AA shooter, basically a smoother Payday 2 with regenerating health. Lockpicking, drilling, filling bags with loot, it's all there and it works just a bit smoother than P2, which you'd expect considering it came out 10 years later but it still bears mentioning given how badly Payday 3 blew it. You can actually give your bots orders so they can do objectives for you! Imagine!Multiplayer is what you'd expect, though the heists are generally less elaborate and more meant to be chained back to back. It's good, it's fine, it's mostly what you think it is. What impresses me is the single player. It's a roguelite, and for whatever reason it's a mix of Dope Wars and instanced FPS combat? I never knew I wanted that until now.Basically you have a map with a bunch of turf to take and ♥♥♥♥ to do. You can only do so much in a day and all of it costs resources. Turf battles are handled by your soldiers, one of whom you're always piloting, and their gear improves as you invest in them. Heists are for your team of named guys/gals and require more finesse, especially if you want to complete them in stealth to keep your heat down. It's not a wildly complicated setup, but there's a lot more going on there than you'd think. You'll be judging which heists to do based on what goods you'll steal, because those don't just convert to cash, you need to actually check their current trending value and sell when the time is right. Lots of heists require significant investments to even start but certain goods can often be used in lieu of cash, which is way more efficient if you can arrange it. You see the Dope Wars comparison? There's stuff here!Multi-step jobs are really nice, but what's impressed me so far are the mostly random character events that pop up like regular missions and very much aren't. I had a guy named Ranger who was a beast, my favorite squaddie by a mile. Eventually I see he gets a special mission, only it's for him alone because he was having a 'Nam flashback that I needed to handle before too many days passed. This put me in his shoes fighting in a rice paddy as he saved his unit from a sniper Rambo-style. Also his captain was Danny Trejo. What? What the ♥♥♥♥? This is awesome, why is no one talking about this???I'm not gonna say that Crime Boss will change your life or anything, and it's definitely got those AA rough edges (many of which are made manifest in the awful celeb performances), but if you want something genuinely different and you like heistin' I see no reason why you shouldn't at least try this thing. Especially now that it's so cheap.Rockay is still an incredibly stupid name though.

_childDocuments_.review: When Rockay first launched I had heard it was a disasterous low budget Payday rip off, and Epic exclusivity didn't help it. Having played it now I have to assume 505 have pulled off a No Mans Sky or something. Although this game has a multiplayer mode it plays far better IMO as a single player Roguelite take on the old Payday premise, heists are smaller and faster but with no trading hostages or doc bags to refresh downs the thrill is really kept up. There are still larger heists on par with Payday's Big Bank and they really lean into the cool heist asthetic but they are comperatively rare.The game has a lot of refreshing refines on core gameplay compared to Payday 2, gunsmithing is sadly gone and there are no huge RPG leveling systems but almost everything else is dramatically improved. Drills now encourage player to guard them by giving you the ability to speed them up, rather than random breaking and requiring lengthy interactions to repair, instead you can hold the drill to boost it for a time with a needle moving towards a green zone that will 3x the speed of the drill however the boost wears off after a few seconds so players will need to maintain their presence and if a player overshoots the green zone the drill will break and need to be restarted however this is far quicker than the old Payday 2 system. Bots are now far more useful and independent, with many missions they will dive in on the loot and bag it then run to the van on their own with little handholding from the player needed although they can be a little overly brave when doing so. You can also pick up fallen weapons from enemies now too!Player characters, with the exception of Troy Baker the boss, are mostly generic feeling but are meant to be disposable and function on a tier system. Common low tier characters will try their best with shovels and crowbars but can be upgraded with experience and reequiped with weapons from a shop. Some characters however are even given full on stories from a Vietnam war vet going through flashbacks to a cursed Jamican drug smuggler tracking down a voodoo witch. Stealth is also subtly reworked but for the best. You have a 3 strikes and your out system before stealth is broken and the cops are called. Eliminating guards or cameras will count as a strike, as well as trespassing in secure areas. However cameras can be disabled by finding a computer in a security room and simply shutting them off, and guards can be pacified by sneaking up on them and "intimidating" them through a sharp shoulder punch. These refinements feel a lot more rewarding and fair compared to trying to dodge guards while worrying about your 4 pager limit. Alternatively some missions have you infiltrating the territory of rival gangs which is a very different situation, gangsters do not warn you and shoot on sight but in return there are no off limit actions with them either and killing them with a silenced pistol or throwing knife is not penalized so long as the body is out of sight. This actually gives stealth gameplay two fun and different feelings to it.It's also worth mentioning the game is down right charming: inspired by 90s action movies and proud of it with many characters just being almost perfect copies of classic actors (in many cases voiced by them even); the game knows it's cheesy and is happy to have fun with it but never jumps the shark into being annoyingly goofy. The characters laugh with each other and shoot goofy one liners but it's played like friends having fun with each other; one particular scene featuring "Gloves" (Danny Glover) giggling to each other about Gloves wearing gloves was so goofy their laughter became infectious. Gloves as your heist planner and coordinator frequently chews up the scenery and it's clear Mr. Glover had a lot of fun with his role... unfortunately Chuck Norris, voicing the main antagonist Sherriff Norris either clearly did not take a video game role seriously at all, or regretted agreeing to the project; in either case every single line from Norris is bored and monotone, as if he just read through the script once not even trying to do more than say the right words, before stepping out of the recording booth and warning the devs his contract only required him to do one take. If he got paid a turkey sandwich with just tomato for this performance it was too much. Aside from him though the voice actors all do a great job with their performances; MIchael Rooker as Touchdown, the gang's enforcer is another stand out performance.Overall for 20 dollars I thought this was a great game and I'm happy to find myself coming back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna keep it short because I just wanna drop a positive review.It's an XCOM-esque roguelite heisting game. Basically, you take the role of a wannabe gang leader and attempt to take over a city, one turf at a time. Attacking rival gangs, robbing stores/banks to fund your army/team. There's actually a surprising amount of detail put into this thing. Everyone thought this was just a cash grab to capitalize on PAYDAY 2's success, but It really isn't. Crime Boss does a lot to distinguish itself with it's 80s/90s over-the-top cheesy VO and cutscenes, as well as the strategy portion of the game. While the actual act of heisting is pretty simple in it's mechanics, it does everything it sought to do well. Gunplay feels good. Stuffing a bag full of loot is satisfying as hell. There's enough variation in heists to keep things interesting. The random events and branching paths that can happen in the Roguelite mode are surprisingly expansive as well. Summary: PAYDAY 3 disappointed me tremendously. Crime Boss Rockay City Surprised me immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how to feel about it. I had more fun playing this game than i had playing the 2 hours of Payday 3 before i refunded it but i still found myself going back to Payday 2.It may become a great game eventually but right now for that price it's like a 5 out of 10.Here are my goods, bads and in-betweens:+ Control multiple characters in a heist+ Better allied AI pathfinding and intelligence than Payday (usually)+ More randomized heists than Payday+ Loose loot you pick up gets merged into a bag when you collect enough (more realistic than Paydays loose loot but more bags to carry)- Guns and characters get unlocked by leveling up (which is not too different to Paydays heist rewards) but guns have set sights and attachments. You have no way of customizing your loadout the way you would in...well... Payday.- There are no perks or skills you unlock by leveling up. Your entire playstyle is bound to the equipment you bring. Which you unlock randomly. This not only eliminates the need of planning before doing a heist but makes the gameplay feel more arcade-like. Select and equip your characters, do the heist, repeat. The Reward = some skins maybe.- gun sound is a a bit mushy and lacks punch-/+ The gameplay loop is not too different to a Payday heist but has a few key differences.Going in loud is not too different to Payday. You've waves of enemies you fend off until you can extract with your loot.Stealth gameplay however is where the differences are notable and (in my opinion) not for the better.You have guards patrolling the area but instead of taking them out and answering the radio to avoid triggering the alarm you sneak up to them push em down and cuff them. And there is no limit to how many of them you can cuff.You could clear an area of 20 guards and no alarm is going to trigger. So what does trigger an alarm? gun shots (no silencer)being spotted (obviously)killing or destroying a total of 3 guards/cameras (???????????)You can deactivate cameras by turning off the monitor. Why do i need to turn it off if no guard is still around to watch the monitor? In Payday you could use those cameras to your advantage but here you basically beeline to the camera, turn it off then clear the guards. I can get behind the idea that when 3 cameras get destroyed the operator may get a bit suspicious but when you shoot a guard then someone knows that something is wrong but when 20 guards are cuffed in an alleyway then that's okay?And it is way too easy to clear the guards. You can have a brick as equipment that has a few seconds cooldown. Throw brick > Guard walks to brick > cuff guard > move guard away > repeatCongratulations, you completed the heist.-/+ They have a rougelike campaign mode that i won't go into detail about. Not a big fan of roguelikes. But that's not the problem. The problem is the god awful voice acting... especially of the main character... which you are forced to play. There are 3 "different" campaigns and all of them are his campaign with different settings. Animations are so stiff and voice acting so generic that i'm not sure if this is some AI generated mess. From the writing to the voice acting to the animations. Just god awful. It's so bad i recommend to buy the game, experience that trash for yourself and refund it afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't really write actual reviews but the devs for this game clearly want to make it better despite the status it had when it came out.Also, I'm gonna try my best to avoid comparisons to Payday 3 unless it's a really good one. To also say I've played this game a bit on EGS (up to level 10) and I played PD3 on Xbox.What's Good:-Price: Even without the sale (and honestly the extra DLC) $20 is a good deal for a game with both a full on story mode and coop mode. Add on currently, as the time of writing, that it's $16 and all DLC is free for now and it's an absolute bargain.-RNG: When it comes to coop heist games like these, RNG is key. This is the one time I'll make a comparison to Payday 3. In PD3, RNG means very little, at most it's some items being in a different area, but for the most part every heist never really changes. In CB, whole level layouts can be completely different for the same heist. Whether it's the smaller jobs having completely different locations for the same "job", to the major heists having 2 to 3 different layouts along with different item/loot locations, different camera/security room locations, etc. It really varies up the gameplay to where you don't always exactly know where to go for everything without even looking.-Voice Acting: Is it *good* good? Not, mostly not at all. Some of the random team members have decent VA but for the most part it's Not Great. Is it so bad it's extremely funny and joke worthy? Yes, 100%. "New adventures await, buddy!" has become a saying in a discord I'm in. If you can sit back, laugh, and embrace the B list cheesy as all hell action movie level dialogue (which, from how the devs act, seems to be somewhat the point) you'll enjoy the cutscenes.-Guns/Gunplay: The gunplay itself is pretty good, nothing extremely noteworthy but it plays well and guns have a good feel to them. Some uh Strange designs for some guns but overall you have a decent selection that even includes melee weapons (unlike...yeah). Whats interesting is the fact that you can pick up guns during a level. You picked a team member that only has a shovel for a primary? Replace it with a dropped shotgun. Not to mention some levels have weapon caches on the map, not only giving you an extra option but also making the map feel a bit more alive.-Story Mode: The story mode is the definition of Good. Not amazing, just good. It's a roguelike where you try to capture every territory in Rockay City and, of course, get rich. It's got permanent upgrades that help on each run along with a different set up of characters and missions each time.-Heist Flow: Almost every heist has a very clear 3 stage progression in it's heist flow. Most noticeable are the new Cagnali DLC (which, btw, are 2 of the most insane and eventful heists I've played in a shooter like this). This type of flow just makes the maps actually feel like you are doing something.-Team AI: Not only will they smash and bag by themselves, put loot into the van, AND revive teammates, you can also coordinate with a ping system, telling them *exactly* what to do. Not to mention if playing solo you can even switch to a teammate and play as them.-Server Browser-Solo ModeCould Be Better:-Level Reward System: When you level up you are able to choose between 3 random choices as a reward. Rewards being appearances for your customizable character, team members, weapons, grenades/usables, and gun camos. The problems lie in that sometimes you can just have some bad luck and get some really bad choices or you can have the opposite problem where you have 2 good choices but can only pick one. While not a *bad* system it would be nice to have a set reward system or at the very least let us pick 2 options.-Leveling: Right now you can only level up once at a time. Meaning if you get 400 xp or 1600xp you are only gonna level up once. While I understand, so its not to just blow through the lower levels in insane time. It can feel a bit meh when you complete a big heist and only get a level. Maybe 2 levels would be better?Not Good:-Optimzation/Performance: Yeah, this is kinda the biggest problem with the game. While I can get it to run fine on a Deck, you will notice some studders and lags even on capable PCs. While not the absolute worst performance (it definitely runs better without Denuvo), I feel like it definitely needs some improvement.Overall, this is a great deal for a 7/10 game at just $20, let alone $16

_childDocuments_.review: Current state of the game has the potential to be really good. But it is still held back by serious bugs or poor enemy behaviour.-Dying while using your gadget in campaign turf wars, sometimes makes you unable to shoot or melee. Dying allows you to use melee again. Quit game & click campaign again, to auto-restart the turf mission(does NOT work once the result screen shows).-Multiplayer Results screens frequently get stuck on-screen when it SHOULD take you back to the lobby screen. You can however, still interact with the lobby functions, but you'll basically be clicking on memory.-. This is so bad & happens basically every day, it's almost on par with Helldivers 2 before they finally started fixing extremely common crashes.-Save. Data. Corruption: I Got to level 60+, beat the campaign 3 times, bought most of the campaign-boss assets. My whole computer Freeze-crashes when i try to start a multiplayer shuffle, so i hold my power button. Next time i start the game, i've fully reset. I don't even know if the freeze-crash was caused by the game, but this game is the only one where i have problems that severe. The gadget lockups, multiplayer result screen & pc freezing all happened so often with this game, i wasn't even blindsided by the data erasure, though i was still frustrated my 60 hrs of gameplay were wiped by something entirely the game's fault.-Alt+f4 during a mission asks if you want to surrender. (Why would you even do this when you could use the pause menu?)-The difference between heat ratings does not show the enemy equipment, armor strength or possible enemy types-No Pre-map planning or display of the Pre-mission map to show objectives.-Some objective tasks are vague or do not state that there is a possible penalty, such as the Vertigo Hidden Vault. Nasara tells you to find the Night manager's desk, he does not tell you an alarm will trip if you get the wrong one. First time players will struggle a lot with many missions that have no direction or warnings of dangers.-Police can use LETHAL GRENADES in civilian areas. I see them grenade my civ groups very regularly.-Civs are useless in loud, your AI teammates won't even try to ziptie them during loud.-Friendly AI cannot/Will not use their gadgets. not even the ones that don't do damage like the berserk or Mule booster. Your soldiers in turf war won't use them either.-Friendly AI Heisters will prioritize dropping off their bags higher than listening to your orders to stay with you, isolating them & getting them killed.-Friendly AI heisters cannot be told to ignore bags you don't want picked up, such as bag groups near the escape when you would rather they run to collect loot until the escape arrives, or only carry 1 bag so they can still use their primary.-Friendly AI heisters will aggressively subdue & tie down anyone even slightly suspicious, even if the act of tying them up is much more dangerous for a stealth detection domino effect.-Guns are SO inaccurate, you can't even hit an idle enemy in the head consistently 10 meters away from you because the accuracy is that poor. This is probably to compensate for the tightly packed maps, but this just causes frustration when my gun sight says it's on target, but the bullet fires off-target. Being detected from outside your vision is really hard to notice. You only get a small icon at the EDGE of your screen. & when you're playing online, you can hear the detection SFX for your teammates too, rather than ONLY yourself. There's no big centre HUD showing your highest detection either, so even if you're TRYING to keep an eye out for it, you're guaranteed to miss it at some point when playing online due to shared Detection SFX.-Shooting non-armored enemy parts has no extra effect aside from helmets protecting from headshot damage unless you shoot it off. But if your gun isn't strong enough, you still won't kill with 1 headshot to the exposed head.-Enemy Animation Smoothness: Horrible. 90d+ snap-turns are frustratingly common & massively affect your ability to hit the target.Pathetic, adding together all your AI Soldiers' kills is unlikely to surpass 5 Gear loadouts are randomized, sometimes making you spawn with shurikens instead of something like a grenade. Or an smg instead of a shotgun.(shotguns are really good) Bullet sponge central. A SINGLE one is ALMOST guaranteed to takedown ALL of your turf-war soldiers if you do nothing, even if there were no other enemy Turf Soldiers supporting them. I know they're captains & supposed to be tougher, but 2/3 captain types are straight up UNFAIR for your ai to takedown, those being the chainsaw or Mini-gunners. Both have really high HP, DMG & movement Speed.-Turf war captains may spawn at 10 soldiers remaining, if not, you can fully clear the area. If they do, you now have infinite enemy soldiers supporting up-to 3 captains. can have their chainsaw destroyed, but melee 1-shot your soldiers & sprint faster than you could with Swift-3. In Turf Wars, melee units are actually more dangerous than guns because they rush the target & are guaranteed to land the hit, & kill in 2 hits at most. whereas guns, have something like a 10% hit rate. A single Melee Soldier will take out 3 of your people easily if you don't kill it yourself. These ones shoot so many bullets they're guaranteed to kill every 2 seconds.Edit: The Backpack Sparks & they DO take more damage if shot there. For some reason, their miniguns don't have any speed penalty, they are literally SPRINTING AS FAST AS YOU, if you were to carry a pistol with swift-3.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a new PAYDAY.  =   =   -   - It's really fun, both in Coop & singleplayer Score mostly after spending about 60 hours in the playtest.  + gunplay & firefights are good & satysfing, IMO better gunplay than in PD3 + less "sponginess" on both sides: both cops, gangsters and you go down quick + difficulty seems properly balanced & there's in-mission escalation + enemy AI is pretty good + police models are good and realistic + bots carry bags, can do some objectives (and can be switched to or ordered around in SP) + some new mechanics, but mostly just the return of that "proper stanard" we're used to + as I said, standard: kicking, session browser, ping display, offline mode, actual cutscenes+ really good heist maps, most maps can be stealthed + stealth is decent + decent stealth-to-loud transition + might look goofy on screenshots, but it's purest old school PAYDAY in gameplay + graphics are decent, some bangers on the soundtrack + "Chains" from PAYDAY 2 is better Bain than Bain. Sorry Simon. + decent progression & enough of it to keep you playing + really good pricing, good price-to-content ratio, decent replayability  + has thrice as much content for half the price of PAYDAY "supposedly" 3 + if you're 30+: you're favourite actors are here and most of them do their job  - friendly AI can bug out and just get stuck (rarely, but it happens. _childDocuments_.review: Increasing Police Spawns and difficulty while barely (if at all) improving the Ally AI was a huge mistake. The majority of assaults quickly turn into repeated grenades and flashbangs at your feet almost nonstop, all the while sending 3-4 heavies at you  With VERY little downtime between waves now. Likewise, Robot police also arrive MUCH sooner too.Before: Hard and Extreme difficulty were annoying at times but i honestly found it fun despite the Ally AI often being complete dead weight during firefights. 1-2 heavies coming at you at once every once in awhile seemed about fair and pulling through and getting extra money was nice, ESPECIALLY in a super grindy game like this. There was also a lot of time to pick up Ally AI members to prevent them from dying completely (They don't defend themselves well so it Happens A LOT MORE than it should!!!)Now: 3-4 Heavies come at you at once, You have to CONSTANTLY run from grenades/flashbangs being tossed at you, police spawn in larger clusters MUCH FASTER, and there is almost NO DOWNTIME between assault waves. Oh, and the Dying timer goes by VERY fast now, have fun trying to pick up A downed henchman when they suddenly decide to stand and do nothing in the middle of 3 heavies and a squad of robo-police before they die.  Good luck trying to survive because theres a good chance the Ally AI will STILL stare and do nothing but let itself be shot. Even when they are shooting and trying to help it feels like they barely make an impact on the enemy count compared to when its just you firing on them and often just end up getting shredded and downed.I was hoping we would see some actual AI improvements but they seem to function about the same as before. PLEASE ACTUALLY buff the Ally AI. I don't even care if its just a temporary AI damage reduction/increase when they aren't being controlled, I'd just like a mission with 4 Elite henchman to ACTUALLY FEEL like i'm not the only one defending across the entire mission length.

_childDocuments_.review: In single player you play as a ‘crime boss’ attempting to take control of Rockay city after the former kingpin met an untimely end. You send soldiers out to get control of different regions (turf) in the city while competing with 4 other factions. If invading a turf occupied by another faction you select a number of troops to send in and take direct control of a soldier as you try to kill enough enemies before you run out of soldiers. These generally take less than 2 mins with a hard deadline of 10 mins.Each day 2-4 robbery opportunities are available to send a team of 1-4 people using your boss character and/or other specialists to steal cash or other goods to fund your expansion. These can also be fairly quick, though if you are going slow in stealth they can take 20-30 mins. After a day or 2 a big heist opportunity will become available that requires you to do multiple missions, buy equipment and setup, to take on a mission that will have a significant payout. The spoils from these can usually be pocketed for personal gain, or used to pay off a faction and take them out of the campaign.All the while the police will be investigating your crimes. If their investigations gets too far along before you gain control of all the turf, you will be forced to leave the city and will have to start the campaign over again. Since this is a roguelike game you will gain experience that helps unlock permanent upgrades that make future runs easier no matter if you win or lose.As long as your ok with roguelike staples like the inability to quicksave/quickload as a way to deal with mistakes made in a mission it works fairly well. Oh that guard spotted you and called the police, well time to go loud and get out with whichever loot you can. Wiz took a few too many bullets and died in the mission, well they won’t be available till your next campaign. Generally this works well, but there are occasions where the game just plain ♥♥♥♥♥ up and things like the distraction brick will be spotted by guards and called in as if they were staring at a zip tied hostage for no understandable reason. This sucks when it happens but after having played more than 20 campaigns I have only had this happen in 4 missions, and it did not stop me from completing the mission.The randomization of the missions works fairly well. There are 2-3 base layouts for most mission types with several changes to guard/civilian patrol patterns, camera setups, safe/loot locations, and security room locations. Even after 14 successfully completed campaigns I am still seeing new layout alterations and alternate patrol/camera configurations. And the roguelike campaign has random events that can occur during missions as you get further into a campaign that throw curveballs into otherwise solid plans.The multiplayer consists of picking a mission, or selecting 3-5 mission shuffle runs. Missions are generally fairly bite size and can be completed 5-10 mins with the largest heists maybe taking 20 mins or less with a team that knows the basics of what the mission is. If you are looking for a more bite sized version of payday, this does a fairly good job of it.The voice acting is a mixed bag at best. Most of the big name male actors for this phoned it in at best. Chuck Norris is absolutely awful, with the rest being anywhere from good for the lines they were given to drunk/stoned on set. Don’t know how much was down to poor directions given as they were recording or if they made all their request through Cameo with no directions, but generally most of the big name actors for this can’t have been worth the money spent for them unless they were impossibly cheap. So generally I have enjoyed most of what I have discussed above, other than the odd glitch making missions harder than they should have been (with a few times where it got me killed). The big pain point in my opinion is the way the game locks progression for gaining new guns, teamates, and equipment through a fairly slow XP grind that is shared between single player and multiplayer. Every time you get enough XP you will be given a choice of 3 items that pulls from several different unlock types. These can be purely cosmetic character skins exclusive to multiplayer (not usable in single player), weapon skins that are mainly for multiplayer (only indirectly used in single player with update 11), new guns available for single & multiplayer, New team hires for single & multiplayer, and new equipment like deployable turrets, grenades, or throwing knives.You start the game with no silenced weapon available until the you get lucky and one is offered as one of the 3 level-up unlocks, but given that there are less than 10 silenced guns in the game and there are over ~100-200 other things that the game can offer you each time your odds of being offed one are very small for many of the early level-ups. This means that if you are mainly playing single player, you are likely to have completed the campaign 2-3 times before you are ever able to unlock a single silenced gun. This can severely limit your options in several stealth missions until they become more available.Personally I would make it so the silenced Swiss (the weak starter pistol) was unlocked by default at the start of the game to give players an option, even if it’s horrible when things start to go loud. Instead you are left praying to the RNGesus every time you gain a progression level to not be given 3 options that consist only of player/weapon skins that are useless for giving gameplay options.

_childDocuments_.review: If you spoke to me a year ago, I would have wrote this off as cheesy, PD2-ripoff schlock that didn't have enough substance for the pricetag. Now, though, I have a lot further appreciation & interest into just what the hell In Game Studios were up to with this game.This isn't PAYDAY, rather a hybrid of GTA SA's gang takeovers, mixed with Payday-like FPS combat and roguelike stat & resource management. A gang simulator of sorts, all in a cheesy 90s B-movie wrapper, that's has more actual humor than the current state of Payday 3. You have a choice between a single player rougelike campaign, with substory mission "heists" that have more linear missions & cutscenes, and full peer-to-peer multiplayer of all mission and heist types with a game-wide career progression system. Loud and stealth gameplay are very mechanically simple coming from other heist games, but that's I think that actually works here with how often you'll be repeating missions, keeping tedium fairly low, with the turf war & crew resource management (kinda like XCOM I guess?)  breaking up the firefights. The point being it's serviceable enough to get the job done, but never overstays it's welcome, knowing how shallow it can be. Hell, it's enough of an innovation here that bots here can subdue guards & civs, loot, and bag transport all on command, or automatically on their own. I honestly enjoyed it.It's kind of a fascinating idea for a single player game, seeing all these mechanics in one place, even if's not trying to outdo Grand Theft Auto's or PAYDAY's legacies. It's seemingly just trying to be entertaining. Seeing Danny Trejo, Vanilla Ice, Michael Madsen, etc. all quipping the dumbest lines out of a bootleg Tarantino picture just puts the charm cherry on top for me, personally. To be clear, this game isn't trying to pretend it's better than what it is, and the devs seem to know this by now. They have fully embraced the memes, and seemingly just want more people to give it a try, thus the lower price and DLC giveaway. It's simply a fun time if your into silly co-op shooters, especially the few heisting games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Its all right first few hours.Its a heisting game mixed in with this rogue like campaign where you have a map and do thigns like taking over turfs, selecting missions and hiring folk, its not entirely explained well but you will quickly learn it all once you do a couple of heists.Although general gameplay is mixed, guns feel weak like there is almost no impact, to compare, and since almost everyone does, all 3 Payday games feel better with their guns. Things you shoot at also don't feel that great, this game has specials like your usual Payday or similar Horde shooter but i do not think they stick out that well, they feel more like normal cops except with stuff like a Shield or Taser, they just don't make me go 'Oh that is that special unit' they just blend in.AI partners are cool tho, you can give them orders and they seem very good at killing, plus they can stealth, but they have problems. They can on their own take loot, take down enemies and pick up guns but sometimes this makes them B Line out in the open and take lots of damage, potentinally killed. Sometimes they also get left behind and you are just wondering where they went, so bassicaly even if they have improvements over many other games you are still going to have to sit around to help them... constantly.Missions are varied, even when i visited same missions or in similar places they felt pretty good, the variation is on par with some of the best PD2 heists. Like a simple werehouse was used for a couple of different missions but in different ways and it was very good.Visually its also pretty good... except its a TAA mess and with FXAA its jagged, so all detail and nice models are vasted on whatever poison you pick, tho there are lot of options so you can probably get around it with something like Resolution scaling.Anyway, ill re do this 'first impression' after a 100 hours, but for 20 Euros this game is very good.

_childDocuments_.review: It calls itself an "action roguelike" but has zero understanding of what actually makes a roguelike good. It completely fails to provide any reason whatsoever for you to play through a new run. Your gun unlocks do not stay. Your team unlocks do not stay. What transfers is nothing but very minor stat increases such as:"gain 5% more xp""pay 5% less to attack a territory" "start with 10 more soldiers". This makes replays an absolute slogfest with nothing new or exciting. In literally any other roguelike you would start a run, play for 10-40 minutes finish it and get new things to try out next time. What is the point of replaying if your only reward is a minor stat increase? How does that provide any incentive for people to replay?This is without even mentioning the game breaking bugs that can completely screw you over and even end your run.The campaign itself is purely solo, so how about the multiplayer?It's lame and boring. It's nothing but random heists pulled from the campaign with zero sense of solid progression. Again, what's even the point of playing?It's barely better than PDAY 3, and that's a really low bar. I'd refund it if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple game, but it's a fun game too....Concerning Multiplayer;The heists are pretty varied, a bunch of bigger ones that will take you 10-15 minutes or so, and a bunch of smaller jobs and such that can be completed in 5 minutes or under. Then there are 2 systems to engagewith to make that content more interesting, one being a story-driven mode (term used extremely loosly) that sees you complete sets of 3 missions with cutscenes in between. And a shuffle mode that randomizes missions based on preferences. Both are pretty good, and overall it's a really fun experience to play this Coop with my spouse, alongside 2 (surprisingly capable) bots. Single player seems good to, haven't played it yet, but progression seems to largely carry over between modes, which is a nice touch by the devs.The progression is pretty neat, it's nothing groundbreaking, but it feels satisfying and there is plenty to unlock to keep you busy for a good few hours.PERFORMANCE:Since this seems to be hit or miss for folks, on a Ryzen 5800x and RTX3060 12gb this runs PERFECTLY for us, but only while using Vsync at 60fps, menus at 30fps at ultra settings. With DLSS at Quality we get smooth 60fps, no drops in sight, temps keeping under 70c. Make of it what you will, but for us, the game performs extremely well.OVERALLIt's a fun, adrenaline fueled ride full of dumb action, even dumber writing and a bunch of corny, badly construed characters. It's glorious, it's the 80s all over again, like a cocaine fueled rampage through neon and bloodsplatter.It's also 16 bucks on launch including all DLC, which is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I originally owned the game on EGS, where I played it for more than 60 hours. Since I tremendously dislike that launcher, I decided to get the game here instead and transfer my save, so don't be fooled by my total playtime here.That said, Crime Boss is a really good game in the heisting FPS genre and a strong competitor to Payday 3 (not that that's saying much anyway), but try seeing it more as "Payday 2 with some nice QoL changes". It's super easy to get into and has improved a lot since its original release.The roguelite mode rewards persistence, there are a lot of guns to choose from, and a decent amount of missions with surprising randomization that can drastically change the layout of even the simplest jewelry stores.The AI is very helpful as well, capable of looting and transporting said loot on their own, and you can give them orders by holding the middle mouse button. Being able to swap between your AI crewmates is a huge help and a great QoL feature in single-player.Multiplayer is almost plug-and-play levels of easy, and the connectivity issues present during its EGS days are mostly fixed, thankfully. Even in high-ping lobbies, the only issue I had was not being able to use grenades, but that's it.The voice acting and cutscenes can be silly at best or cringy at worst. If you have a soft spot for cheesy movies, I guess you can get past that.On top of all that, the game is quite cheap even without discounts, giving you good bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss is a very solidly put together game with an enjoyable and addicting gameplay loop. Looking at how the game originally launched a year ago and seeing where it’s at now is honestly nothing short of impressive. The game won’t blow your mind or anything, but for the price it’s going for? it’s honestly a steal.Whether you’re in it for the Roguelite campaign or the multiplayer heisting (which brilliantly – can still be enjoyed alone), there’s a lot of worthwhile stuff to sink your teeth into in this package, doubly so if you grab it in this limited time period when the DLCs are free.I gotta say, mad respect for the work on the bots in this game. They may not be human-level intelligent, but they're actually useful. I was honestly shocked to see they even go so far as to bag loot and even take it to the van all by themselves. When I boot up a game with bots these days I often expect them to be absolutely useless, but not in Crime Boss. Good stuff.Progression is simple but rewarding. You play the game, you get progress. No infuriating challenge-based progression in sight. The developers seemed to take community feedback seriously and constantly addressed it to make the game better than the solid foundation it had in its original launch.The writing and voice acting are simply hilarious and it’s clearly intentional, the whole thing feels like someone watched an 80\90s action movie while high on something strong and turned it into a game. I know it sounds horrible, but it’s actually entertainingly bad, and even if “so bad it’s good” isn’t your thing, you can still enjoy the game perfectly fine because the gameplay plays it 100% straight.I personally love the cheesy characters and dialogue. It’s so hilarious, it often feels like a fever dream.Good on IGS for not giving up on this. Their commitment to making Crime Boss a fun experience shows, and I’m excited to play it some more and equally curious what its future holds because the game is already a well-rounded experience that’s easy to recommend.Don’t hesitate to try this one! Preferably sooner rather than later.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game, feels like a direct upgrade to Payday's gameplay with more forgiving stealth (infinite zip ties and body bags my beloved). My only complaints based only my experience in the campaign:-AI isn't very reliable. They don't use equipment like grenades on their own, need constant baby sitting so they don't get overwhelmed, on rare occasions they get bugged and stand in the open getting mowed down. The later happens when they try to carry loot bags to a drop off point. -No breathing room between police attacks. In Payday, having hostages increases the time between assaults. Nothing like that in Crime Boss. Stealth as much as you can before going loud. -Enemy alertness in stealth is bugged. Not sure why, but some enemies are able to detect things that are not in view and out of range. Meter fills up but the alarm isn't raised. You need to distract by throwing a none explosive weapon (brick, throwing knife, etc.) near them and that'll reset their alert state.  I only survived the Hidden Vault mission due to one of my crew members health glitching and became immortal, I had to use him as a distraction after the other two got overwhelmed and downed repeatedly. Despite the flaws and speaking as a Payday veteran, I highly recommend the game for the price alone (especially for the Steam launch special, an absolute steal).

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, this is by far the WORST game I’ve ever played.In my opinion, it’s seriously bad.I was bored within 30 minutes because it’s just the same repetitive gameplay. The heists are identical, and the turf wars are nothing more than being dropped into the middle of a battle where you kill a set number of gang members to "win." There’s no real depth—just a bunch of NPCs shooting at each other.There’s barely any story, and if there is, it’s buried under poorly voice-acted cutscenes and must be further in the game, because the cut scenes so far are nothing like what they are showing in their videos to sell the game (like - they are little small little tiny things). The small in-game announcements before and after missions is just more annoying than helpful, and they feel completely disconnected from the player.Overall, this feels like a even worse Payday 2 knockoff but with some famous voices from actors slapped on it (and even then - they sound AI in places). The game plays like a series of repetitive mini-quests, which is nothing like the exciting game-play shown in their trailers.And if there is more of a story later in the game, it’s poorly presented and I couldn't be bothered to continue.
