_childDocuments_.review: This game spent a year in EGS and should have spent the time fixing flaws in the game that detract it, or otherwise does not value you time. All i can say is that the content is worth the price and it does provide a unique experience on the single player side albeit flawed due to bad AI goons that more often then not will ruin your entire run. They may burn your rogue-lite run anywhere from 0 to 10 hours wasted; note there are unlocks tied to this campaign completion.There is an overarching multiplayer progress where most unlocks are tied to RNG choices upon level. This is a terrible progression system all character skills and the authority to get the option to buy guns is through this system. I did not get a single skill card until level 40 and that already 30 hours into the game. I did not get a silenced weapon until 20 hours in the game. Much with these kinds of systems devs are trying to pad content and maintain player retention but at the same time not valuing player time. Your bots ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. I'm sorry i could equip these things with LMGs and it would not matter bots will just randomly decide  to stray off from you or away from cover and then die. IF you have a mission with a lot of bags they will constantly try to pick up the bags you placed in a strategic position. And when they do carry 2 bags at once this blocks off the use of the primary weapon which overall locks off firepower because they constantly pick up bags. Note that bots still have a limited number of downs so once they are gone they just die permanently on that run. I also do not appreciate the game locking away my goons when the game suddenly decides you need to play some kind of back story mission . Multiplayer, decent vary of missions and heists. The issues? Same nonsense as early pd2 days and pd3. You have issues finding games with people that want to play loud or you join a randomly lobby and they don't say anything and then they kick you for making it loud.  vice versa. Weird sync bugs like looping loot grabbing animations and view model locking caused by interrupting people's lock picking by opening the door from the other side; You know seemingly small bugs that you think would have been fixed after year? 3 difficulties; normal, medium and hard. Enemies don't seem to buff through difficulties from what i read and played. Player attributes get nerfed; like lower health and longer times between hp regen. Pick the difficulty you like and if you have some mates i think the game is decent fun. This is Payday at home.Voice acting is bad from 90% of the characters except for Nasara. His scripting seems a step up from the rest and he is voice by the voice actor of Chains from payday. The meme of so bad it's good only gets you so far.  Aside from Nasara and Maybe Gloves the rest of the caste seems to be just reading the scripting with no proper context given.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just terrible. I've tried my best to give it as good of a shot as I can, but it's just not worth your money.- Numerous game-breaking bugs are often an unavoidable consequence of core gameplay.- Abysmal movement. Everything shy of running forward halts or restrains your character's momentum in this game. Mantling is automatic along ledges, which also kills your momentum. Sliding is restrictive, bland, and clunky.- The netcode hurts my soul. Unless the host is your neighbor, you're going to feel the pain of teleporting everywhere and generally not certainly knowing where you're actually located relative to your surroundings.- The game performs terribly even on the lowest settings, and doesn't have the visuals to justify it. Framedrops are frequent, and you shouldn't expect to get more than 80FPS without a high-end rig.- Bots are stubborn, and prioritize grabbing/holding loot bags over their safety or your own. Bots would rather grab a bag than revive others, and will end up only using their secondary weapon because they can't hold a primary with two bags.- Automatic peeking during aiming and moving hurts the game. Your character will peek when you don't want to at all.- The health system isn't fun, and combined with the crouching peeking mechanics, makes it often impossible to find time to breathe or fight back when at a disadvantage.- The roguelite campaign is lengthy and repetitive. It's either too hard or too easy, and always for the wrong reasons.- Heist variety is lacking, even with all DLCs. With all DLCs, there are only 10 large-scale heists in the game. PAYDAY 3 launched with 8, and added 3 more free heists along with 4 DLC heists for a total of 15 large-scale heists. Most other heist variety comes from miscellaneous smaller-scale jobs that simply aren't comparably memorable or fun. The most they do is pad for time when the core content is severely lacking.And last but not least, revenue from this game goes to Bo Andersson. Don't buy this game, please.

_childDocuments_.review: Because the devs have shown actual dedication to fixing this game over the past year it's been out, Crime Boss honestly feels like the Payday 3 we were waiting for. Bots are smarter (for the most part), heists are way more interesting and there is a much wider variety to choose from.The campaign is really cool after you get the hang of it. It's a rogue-like crime simulator where you do jobs every day trying to take over the city from the rival gangs while also balancing your money and your "heat". As you do more jobs in one day your heat rises, thus making heists more difficult if you attempt them that day. Some heists are only available the day you see them on the map so it makes it very interesting trying to determine if the heat is worth the potential reward you get for doing the heist.Your crew members are expendable as well, meaning if they die on a heist they are GONE for the rest of the run. If you aren't careful you will very quickly find yourself soloing heists that are near impossible to complete and if the main character dies (Travis Baker) the run is OVER and you have to start over. There is so much replay value it's actually insane.Is it perfect? Hell no. But its genuinely a fun time and has some very interesting mechanics.Voice acting ranges from passable to godawful - looking at you, Chuck Norris. BUT I think it teeters on the "so bad it's good" in a way where it's kind of exciting to see which performance you are going to listen too next. Damion Poitier (VA for Chains in Payday) is the highlight, as expected.While there are still some glitches I've found, I wouldn't say there is anything game-breaking. I've only played for about 6 hours by now so your mileage may vary.Give it a try. Especially while it's on sale and you get all DLC for free, but honestly Crime Boss is worth the full price either way. I will update this review when I've put more time into it and if my opinion on anything has changed.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally beat this game's singleplayer after a few days and to say I was surprised would be an understatement. Is this music good? No, not really. Is the voice acting good? While I actually like a few of the characters' voices, not at all (Baker's lines are all so damn ridiculous and you can tell the VA isn't a VA). Is the gameplay good? It's super straightforward and simple, but also kinda fun if you aren't looking for too much depth. This game is "alright" in the best way possible. I would 100% not go into this expecting Payday 2 levels of heisting, but rather as just a heisting game doing its own thing (which it does pretty well I may add). I have my complaints about the AI (everyone seems to, which is understandable) such as the fact that it tends to sort of ignore gaurds and cameras when moving around in stealth, or the fact that when you retreat or push in combat they tend to stay hunkered down to inevitably get blasted by the police due to a lack of supporting fire. However, whether it was through sheer luck or just the way I was playing, I didn't run into *too* many issues with the AI in this regard. I like how they are actually somewhat proactive and in certain circumstances will actually *DO* things. On top of this, they are useful in stealth unlike in Payday 2 (not dunking on payday 2 in any way, simply just giving credit to the AI). The game also has a ton of variety and replayability, with tons of different variations to each mission and some random events here and there. Sure, its annoying when you're in stealth and some idiot npc lights a propane tank up with a cigarette, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it isn't cool. Speaking of stealth, I almost enjoy it more than in Payday. Failing a stealth attempt doesn't feel like the end of the world and due to a lack of a pager mechanic allows for some *interesting* playstyles. For example, in gangster missions, you don't gain any strikes for killing gangsters, unlike with killing security guards. So, if you have a silenced weapon, you can very much just waltz in and light them up (which makes you feel like a badass if you pull it off btw). It might be a bit *too* easy sometimes, but if you don't really mind the difficulty then you could have as much of a blast with it as I did. Personally, I love casing out the entire place and figuring out patrol patterns and locking down the security methodically, or just cheesing with the brick because it's honestly pretty funny. If you can tolerate the voice acting and the music, this is 100% a game I can recommend to anyone who is a fan of Payday but maybe just wants to move on from it. And if you're worried about not having friends, don't worry, I don't either (None who have this game at least.), but also the game has a very well done singleplayer mode. It is a permadeath game mode though so if you aren't into losing characters, then maybe it isn't for you. Personally though, I'd take the losses on the chin and move on, it is much more enjoyable if you do that rather than resetting the game over and over to get a "perfect run". And even when you lose, its not for none. By investing in assets, playing as Baker, or just really doing things in general, you contribute points to your boss level, which gives you permanent upgrades for your next campaign attempt. Also, don't expect a story. There isn't one. Not a deep one at least. I have no problem with this, but I can understand what it might be like going into this game expecting a fantastic story to make up for the bad VA's and music. Overall, I think this is, at worst, a mediocre game that isn't a bad pickup if its on sale. But if you're someone who sees these flaws as charm or character like I do, then you'll probably love it like I do. It is not a great game. But I love it, and I can not wait to see what they do in the future. I'm glad the devs didn't give up on this game when it flopped on release and I hope things only go up from here. If a friend has this game, go ahead and buy this. If not, probably still buy it just to give it a try. It might just be a game that grows on you. Or not. Now go do things and stuff or whatever.  Good game. Nothing mind-blowing. But it didn't need to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Payday meets Roguelite, but worse.They took everything that was fun from Payday, tried to remove all the dumb stuff and ended up being worse off.I will only sum up the deal breakers for me and refrain myself from describing the entire game:There are no pagers to answer during stealth, since this was a major gripe in PD2. Now you get a magical strike, whenever you kill a guard or civ. Stealth is as simple and barebone as in PD2, but there are virtually NO other stealth options or mechanics, besides the mighty brick. Which is the best item in the game, but also the only stealth item, which is also in a separat item slot that you have to bring with you. You can lure guards away to tie them down or outright kill them with it. No brick, no stealth. There is nothing else you can do to manipulate the AI. There are sometimes safes and vans to drill open. And again, they made the PD2 Drill session more fun, because you can increase the drill speed by 3 by interacting with it. But that's it. No skills, no mods, no nothing. Besides, drilling a safe will literally lure in EVERY.SINGLE.GUARD on the map to said location and then .... what? You go loud I guess. Or you kill/ cable-tie every mofo on the planet beforehand. At least cable ties are infinite and the NPCs don't spot "illegal lock picking" from a mile away or call the army, because you tossed a sports bag onto the streets. Except, when they do spot you hiding behind a barrel, that somehow doesn't hide your character. Sometimes guards spot you from behind, even though they aren't even turning their heads (You know, like in Payday 3) I though sprinting was the issue, but I could literally run everywhere without getting botherd, so who knows. Plus, you have these big open maps you can run around as you were playing an immersive sim, but there is NOTHING there. I never found additional safes, secrets or loot. Only more civs, that might as well be absent for the lack of impact or relevance they have for your current heist.Silenced pistols are as rare as a pink elefant and I never got any throwing knives or something similar. In addition, whenever you use a character for a mission, they have to recover making them unavailable for the rest of the day. But they also keep ALL their gear for themselves. Which means, you can't get the godlike brick back for any other character. And you can't buy a new one. I re-reolled the shop like 10 times and it never showed up. Why is this a thing? The roguelike-type shop doesn't add anything, anyway. There are no special effects or stats. They are always the same. Guns are basically unique gear (alla PD2) with different colored "rarity" that only costs you more to buy them. But no modding or buffing whatsoever. Mission descriptions are lackluster and offer no real important information of the mission ahead, even though you pay top dollars to "plan" them. You don't know if the mission is loud or stealth (no, I never once saw these icons everybody talks about in the forums), you don't get to know the general layout, no preplanning, no mission modifier, no assets. Nothing! If you guess wrong, than you run around with the wrong equipment, or the wrong character. For example: You would guess that a cash transporter heist is a loud heist? Which is true in this game, expect when it isn't. THEN you run around with hand grenades, pump guns and your slow as heck "brute" characters and you can't properly stealth the mission. Remember the mighty brick? Yeah, you can bring a brick OR a hand grenade, IF you ever get another one during your playthrough. The same is true the other around and much worse: Wanna stealth, nope it's a loud mission. Expecially, when you already have 4 wanted stars and the only brick was on a character who died last mission, because she took 7min to cross the road. So they buried them with it.And there is no restarting the heist, either. Which is odd, since it's a roguelike and reseting and randomizing the map is part of the genre. You have to quit the game and load back in to try the mission again. Oh, the game also permanently looks you in the current heist. So, if you have the above mentioned issues... I am really dissapointed by this game. I takes the great ideas from the Payday Series and put them in an 80s grind house charmed roguelike. I REALLY like everything about the game, besides it's polish, balancing issues and nonsensical gameplay elements that adds nothing to it.I'll wait for a major update before playing again and play Payday 3 in the meantime (which is improving on a weekly basis)What are your thoughts?

_childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss is the superior successor to the idea of Payday The Heist: a (cooperative) robbery shooter from an indie studio who unabashedly admits which movies they're trying to crib. Crime Boss notably improves upon Payday in a few ways:* Indie game pricing with no overpriced DLC or on-disk content moved to "DLC" as an attempt to pad sales.* A developer who cares about updating their release and knows how to have fun.* The mood and tone is vibrant and *fun*. Rockay is fun to fight through as a bright Miami resort city and the game is fueled with some delicious cheese. Treat the game more like Kill Bill or Lethal Weapon rather than The Godfather or Heat and you'll enjoy yourself.* The big heists actually feel grand, in scale with several missions/tasks of buildup and execution and they carry the refreshingly  simple premise of stealing anything not nailed down, as opposed to fighting ancient aliens or murky conspiracies. * There is an actual single player mode that is not only offline playable, but has a surprising amount of strategy akin to turn based strategy games.* Money is actually useful in this game, rather than Payday's money for nothing. You steal money to buy stuff, which then allows you to steal stuff faster/better with the stronger items you bought.* The developers don't care if you want to cheese the game (to an extent) and generally wont try to patch your fun out. If you wish to lure the guards one by one into a corner with the brick, knock yourself out.* The Crime Boss bots will help you with a lot of the busywork of Payday, like picking safe locks, ziptying lobbies of civilians, or moving bags of loot (not that this doesn't create its own problems).* Multiplayer has a simple server browser to get into/create the games you want, rather than trying to funnel you into crossplay/quickplay.Be warned, this game has some poor programming/has some design oversights and it does make the experience frustrating.* The allied bot AI is incredibly dumb despite being more useful. You can't command them to use their throwable, the allied bots like standing in the open, or the bots try to be helpful with picking up two bags but the decide to charge cops with just their sidearm. You can slightly mitigate this by swapping to a different bot, but please IGS, let me command bots akin to Mass Effect's squad system.* The game may just randomly break at times. During the playtest session, a hard crash on my computer randomly reset my entire save file, and one Gold Cup run randomly changed to the loud objectives of fending off the helicopter, despite the actual gameplay being in stealth.* Another example is when the stealth guards bafflingly turn into Robocop and can see behind their skulls, or can suddenly can find any guards/civilians you ziptied behind 2 walls, or can randomly see a broken laser underground despite the cops being aboveground.* There is no restart mission button in single player. I get this was a choice for the roguelite nature of the game, but the various AI bugs/lack of information can lead you to a situation you never were supposed to be in. You can work around this with Alt+F4/Task Manager to quit the game, but I'd rather the devs just put in a restart button by default so I don't need to deal with their programming breaking my runs.* Some of the single player tasks can quickly feel exhausting when there's no way to pay a resource cost to just skip them. If you have conquered most of Rockay except for 1 gang, you have to keep playing the Turf Defense instead of just paying $200,000 to automatically succeed. * The multiplayer mode progression feels awful due to the poor rewards scaling. You can rob entire trucks' worth of gold, empty grand vaults, or steal a yacht of coke from the cops and just get ... $200,000 for your effort. When most of the multiplayer unlocks cost hundreds of thousands of dollars, if not millions. (At least the payout for these in single player is in the millions and feels great.)If you can deal with some of the poor programming, Crime Boss is worth your money. So worth the money, that a friend gifted me the game (thanks hibestie) the moment it came out on Steam, before I had a chance to buy it myself.

Pretty straightforward.After having beaten the story on Extreme I could easily say it has been a while since I had this much fun playing a game. Your capability in these missions will determine if your action will be a contribution or the opposite. To enjoy this game, you will need to enjoy decision making, strategy and LEARNING as you play (super important). Going through tons of trial and error to figure out how to consistently get good outcomes from missions to better yourself is a part of the fun, becoming more capable through your internal knowledge rather than in-game buffs and bonuses. I can't just "equip a meta OP build" for my campagin, I actually need to get good but the difference between another roguelike game and Crime boss is, in other rogue-like games, where you'd learn enemy attack patterns, in here, you'll be learning how to cleanly complete missions, consistently. _childDocuments_.review: Crime Boss Freezing City!When it's not glitching out, it's like a mash-up of every cliché heist game you've ever seen. The missions are fun, the characters are funny, and the story is captivating. It's like Payday 2.5 after the let down of Payday 3.But oh, the absolute garbage that is the game itself.From the moment I launched the game, I was greeted with a level of stuttering that made me question if my PC was having a mid-life crisis. "Is this intentional?" I pondered as my screen froze.As I navigated my way through the missions it kept freezing. The detailed environments and character models are a feast for the eyes, making every heist feel immersive and lifelike.2.Hollywood Star Power: This game features a stellar cast of Hollywood actors, bringing an unmatched level of charisma and authenticity to the characters. Their performances elevate the narrative, making you feel like you're in an action-packed blockbuster.3.Voice Acting and Humor: The voice acting is top-notch, filled with memorable lines and witty banter that keep you entertained throughout. The humor is spot on, adding a delightful layer to the intense heist scenarios.4.Unique Story Mode - Roguelike Elements**: The story mode introduces an exciting roguelike twist. Each day is a challenge, and failure means starting from scratch. This adds a thrilling level of difficulty and replayability, as you strategize to make every move count.5.Diverse Missions: Unlike the repetitive bank robberies in Payday 3, Crime Boss offers a variety of missions. From attacking rival gangs to strengthen your position, to more complex heists, the gameplay is always fresh and exciting.6.Team Management: You can hire and manage your own team of criminals, adding a strategic layer to the game. Each teammate brings unique skills to the table, allowing you to plan heists more effectively.7.Upgrade Your Base: Customize and upgrade your office and vaults. This feature adds a personal touch to the game, giving you a tangible sense of progression and accomplishment as your criminal empire grows.In summary, Crime Boss: Rockay City not only looks better but offers a richer and more varied gameplay experience than Payday 3. From its star-studded cast to its challenging roguelike story mode, this game is a must-play for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the perfect heist game, but a great experience OverallWhile this game isn't flawless, it offers a fun experience. The developers clearly have a vision, and they've executed it well. It feels more like a worthy successor to Payday 2 rather than the soulless husk that Payday 3 is.The Positives:-Roguelike Campaign: Surprisingly enjoyable with some cool mechanics that add depth to the gameplay.-Stealth System: Instead of pagers you have 3 strikes. Killing guards, breaking cameras, or generally being careless with civilians will cost you a strike. but if you subdue guards and turn off the cameras in the security room it wont cost you a strike. Its easier than it is in payday as you can slowly controll the entire map instead of having to deal with random stuff in the bigger heists but I truly enjoy the stealth as it feels dynamic and fresh.-Functional Bots: The AI can loot, suppress, intimidate civilians and guards, and deliver bags for you unlike payday where they are decoration until the heist goes loud.-No circles to stand around, truly a visionary gaming experience.-Actual good armor system-Decent Gunplay: While not revolutionary, the gunplay is solid and does its job well.-Varied Heists: The game offers a decent selection of heists, keeping things fresh.-Map Randomization: A lot of randomization within the maps -Weight-Based Loot System: Every loot in this game is *loose lot* if you played payday, you dont just get a bag from a loot point. Instead each loot has its own weight and fills your bag. You can carry 2 bags at once but for the penalty of not being able to use your primary.-Fair Pricing: No microtransactions and a reasonable price point.-Dedicated devteam who actually wants to provide a cool experience unlike others who seemingly operate on a "your opinion, my choice" kind of way. *cough* mio *cough*The Negatives:-Voice Acting & Celebrity Focus: The voice acting can get annoying quickly, and the celebrity appearances, especially Chuck Norris, feel unconvincing.-Unnoticeable Perks: The perks don’t stand out and there is little customization-Random Progression: For each level up you get 3 random choices which can include a crewmember, a weapon, a weapon skin, a boss skin. Its not bad per se but i have yet to unlock a single silenced weapon after 3 campaigns.-No customization: Theres no customization for heisters and guns. Guns come with attachments from the shop and heisters are each their own characters.-Robot Faction: The inclusion of a robot faction feels out of place, even in this crazy setting.-Turf Wars in Campaign: Turf wars can be fun, but they get repetitive. An autocomplete option would have been appreciated.-AI Issues in Loud Play: The AI can be frustrating, often dropping bags to switch to their primary weapon, leaving them behind as cops swarm in. Additionally, the AI tends to path straight into danger and die if youre not babysitting them constantly.Summary:This game gets more right than wrong and provides a lot of fun for the price. For just 20€, it offers more content than Payday 3 likely will in three years, and without the need for additional purchases. If you’re into co-op or heist games, or if you’ve already sunk 1,000 hours into Payday 2, this game is a much better value. Payday 3 won’t come close in terms of fun for the foreseeable future, if it doesn’t get canned at one point.

Absolutely destroys any enjoyment whenever they turn up, because now you're dealing with nonsense cyberpunk instead of 90s b movie heist. Baffling decisions abound in this game. In some respects its more playable than Payday at present due to Payday 2 having FAR too much drudgery content, but I really hate the roguelite elements. If the campaign was coop that would possibly help, as part of the problem with stealth is your bots are utter imbeciles that will occasionally actively reveal you (in some areas/stages, the bots will beeline it to the drop-off with the loot and will not listen to orders not to do so, revealing themselves in the process).In sum, I guess it's worth the money and they might address the above issues eventually, but it's far from a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, I don't think it's possible to even look at the cover of this game and not know at least partially what you're getting into. Pretty much its entire cast is made up of actors (and Vanilla Ice, for some reason) you probably thought were either dead or retired, and frankly none of them sound like they were even trying. If you're the sort of person who will scoff at the cutscenes and go "Wow, I hope someone got fired for that blunder!", this is not the game for you. For everyone else, the voice acting can only be considered a net positive. You get Michael Madsen sounding like he's reading every line in the script for the first time, Danny Glover mumbling as if the studio called him in the middle of the night to record lines, Chuck Norris giving such a monotone delivery that you'd swear it was just AI if it weren't for the fact that AI would probably sound more like Chuck Norris, and more -- without even having to hook up your VHS player! It's beautiful and hilarious, and this was the entire reason I originally bought the game.What surprised me, though, is that beyond the inherent comedy of its premise, this is actually a pretty fun game after a year of consistent updates and overhauls. There's a full singleplayer campaign that's presented like a roguelite, with lots of unique story missions and a turf war element against various other gangs, and while I didn't really understand why it needed to be a roguelite at first it started to click over time in a way that makes it pretty interesting to play. You can hire a variety of crew members with unique voice lines that vary in hilarity, buy loads of different guns and equipment items, and unlock things that carry over into the multiplayer mode along the way. It is a little bit on the easy side, so if you're coming into this as a Payday veteran I'd recommend cranking it up to Hard from the start, and while the teammate AI is generally a step above Payday's bots (and you can order them around pretty consistently) they do have a few annoying quirks like routinely loading up with two bags just to drop one in what may or may not be a convenient spot when they swap to their primary weapon. But problems like that one have been few and far between in my experience, and if you think they might be a hindrance for a particular mission you do have the option of going in with a smaller crew or completely solo.In terms of the multiplayer, there's a surprising amount of content at its current sale price (which ends sometime in July 11th, to my knowledge), thanks to the addition of all the current DLC for free. You get at least 8 or 9 small jobs, 4 regular jobs, 10 proper heists, and 9 urban legends campaigns, which are like short mini-campaigns made up of a few different jobs. You can mix players and hired bots or just go in as a group of two or three if you want, and instead of being stuck with bots with default equipment you're able to choose who you hire from the same broad pool as the campaign, with a variety of weapons, skills, and personalities. And yes, you can unlock and play as the celebrity cast -- with the exception of Chuck Norris, as far as I can tell. I went into this game thinking that it would be funny if it were just total garbage, and hilarious if it were actually really good. But I think that it being not good enough to stand up to a juggernaut like Payday 2, but still pretty comfortably better than Payday 3 might be the funniest possible outcome that could have come from this. For $16 you get more content, smarter AI, all the QOL you didn't know you even needed, and a bunch of your dad's favorite actors treating you to the worst vocal performance you've ever heard in a video game, and to me, that's what it's all about. New adventures await, buddy!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what the legs on this is, but I would say its certainly an experience.  It's almost surreal seeing so many recognizable actors in the game and clearly were all reading their scripts on different days.  Like, the dialogue is borderline nonsense most of the time, but it's charmingly stupid to hear it coming from janky digital likenesses.  In the vein of bad B-action movie fare it has that going for it.  In the gameplay department you get a series of maps and various "heists" which are the manner by which you obtain money.  These maps are used well enough as a jewelry store during the day or night has different people around and, to some degree, affects how you approach the mission.  It's lightly randomized, and missions quickly begin to repeat but there is a bit more to it than the surface suggests.Where the game gets its momentum is from the roguelike aspect.  It doesn't really make sense, but it is a good enough motivator as its interesting how quickly a job can go sour.  If you forgot your heat was maxed and you slip up during a job, even a simple heist may quickly devolve into a nightmare scenario of tank cops.  This also makes Baker an interesting player character since his ability is extra loot, which you want, but if he dies its game over.  Hence you are appropriately incentivized to bolster your roster as well as decide who you should send or what order you should tackle missions.  Maybe keep Baker home even if that gas station robbery seems like an easy mark but you maxed your heat, or hell, maybe do that mission before you run an all out turf war.I played Payday a *looooooooong* time ago so my comparison point is fairly limited and I can say I get those vibes, but the purpose of effort here feels better.  Like, it has a nice flow between missions you spend time on and missions that are fairly snacky.  Again, I don't know if this offers up hundreds of hours of fun (a metric that's kind of goofy to begin with) but it did encourage me to keep playing.  Ultimately it's a pretty fast-paced first person shooter with some randomized elements to keep things fresh and on pace, with the draw of watching recognizable actors say slightly nonsensical lines as you try to take over the city.  Serviceable is the word of the day here as it's all functional in my experience.  As far as solo play goes I didn't run into any game breaking bugs though the lack of good team commands is a shocking omission.  You can work around it, but if you asked me to complain that's where I'd point.I can definitely say twenty bucks is a reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: (Game received for free ON STEAM - I have purchased and played it before on epic games' launcher)This game is sleeper hit. This game started as basically a meme, even before it came out originally on EGS it was that one weird game announced at a Game Awards show that looked like a weird GTA parody, where Michael Madsen showed up, said some words and left. But the devs took it to themselves to make this an actual fun experience, even if I'll admit I only really started playing the game myself on the previous update (Update 8 on Epic), at that point it was a much different and more interesting experience than it was at launch.You'll probably see it just about everywhere when people talk about Crime Boss that the voice acting is phoned in, badly done and even cringe, and yeah it kinda is when you really look into it, but when the game is so fun to play, it sort of wraps around into being really funny. All these big names ended up turning themselves into even bigger memes and the devs totally embrace it, celebrating things like MarioInATopHat's hilarious videos and making their own jokes like tiny Travis Baker with a high pitched voice walking around some guards (look it up on the dev's twitter, I'm not joking).They get to do that and have the community laugh *with* them because the game is genuinely good and fun to play, IGS took the opportunity to turn the potential this game had into real value and they've been absolutely nailing it! Sure, it's not a full on "No Man's Sky" situation but it's close! Of course, the game isn't perfect (yet), it has its issues like any other, but what's there so far is great.Guns feel nice to shoot; looting isn't just grab a bundle of some random thing and throw it around; you can actually try to mess around with different loot weights in one bag and optimise how many you take; there's build variety not only with your own "boss" character (in multiplayer), but also in the many crew members you can get through leveling up and purchasing them afterwards (the unlock method is reliant on RNG though which can be unfortunate when you want something specifically); the heists themselves can go from your usual robbing a bank, to going into a heavily guarded facility to steal a ton of gold bars, or even to  storming through a high-tech robot factory to blow it up and kill the owner.All in all, if you want a campy heisting game that takes itself seriously but not really, play this game, you won't regret it. New adventures await, buddy

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer: no. Long answer: also no. While Crime Boss shares many ideas and gameplay mechanics with Payday, it stands on its own merits. It features multiplayer with a surprising variety of game modes, and a roguelite campaign with challenge, strategy, and humorous writing (albeit cheesy).Loud gameplay feels distinctly different from Payday, focusing more on realism and Is less arcadey by nature (though I personally prefer PD2's loud style). On the other hand, the stealth mechanics are a clear improvement from PD2 (I've only played PD3 in beta and played PD The Heist very little, so I can't compare extensively with those two), allowing you to move zip-tied hostages and employing a 3-strike system that surpasses the pager system.The campaign alone justifies the game's $20 price tag (which, I might add, is a steal—pun intended hurhur). Crime Boss offers a more grounded experience than Payday 2; rather than fantastical heists like robbing the White House, it (The campaign) focuses on gang turf disputes, wars, and controlling territory.It also includes random events including but not limited to Most missions are diverse and incorporate enjoyable elements that are enhanced by these random events. Importantly, there's minimal insistence on stealth or loud-only missions, aside from certain campaign and multiplayer missions. This is refreshing change to PD2, where repeated failures due to random team members or bad setups often necessitate restarting  specific stealth missions.There are occasional issues with stealth sightlines and detection mechanics, but they're generally manageable and not as severe as they might initially seem.Unlocking weapons and equipment can be a bit tedious initially, but once you establish yourself, it becomes less of an issue. Compared to Payday, Crime Boss offers less weapon customization—weapons come pre-built with attachments based on rarity. This limits build variety slightly, though Payday 2's endgame build diversity often hinged on specific skills. Crime Boss doesn't achieve perfection in build variety, but it's far from bad.The music in Crime Boss varies between really good and forgettable, though it's unfair to directly compare it to PD2's iconic soundtrack.While Crime Boss doesn't yet match PD2's sheer variety of heists, it's a relatively new game with tremendous potential. In summary, Crime Boss: Rockay City is fun, affordable, and offers a unique take on the heist video game genre—a worthy investment of your time and money. As of this writing, all DLC is also included for free.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea how this flew under my radar, but damn am I glad I found it. This is scratching the itch that Payday left me with since Overkill can't get their ♥♥♥♥ together. Disregard the other reviews complaining about bugs; I've seen only one bug that affects gameplay (a guard in the bank sitting on a bench but clipping through the wall, impossible to subdue, have to kill). I have an occasional (maybe once every 30 minutes) frame stutter/pause but it hasn't screwed me over. More annoying than anything, but doesn't significantly impact the experience. The cast for the voices is crazy, though some of them phoned it in and their voice acting is atrocious (Norris in particular). In fairness to some of them, the script for some things isn't that great, but just remember what John Carmack once said about story in games ("Story in a game is like story in a p0rn movie. It's expected to be there, but its not that important"). The gameplay is what makes this game shine. The stealth mechanics in this are vastly superior to Payday's, and there's a significant variety of weapons for loud (and you can grab ammo for your weapons from downed enemies without any need for ammo bags). You'll visit familiar locations, but there's a good variety of them, some elements of the locations randomly vary each time you visit, and there's several set pieces that they assemble together randomly to keep things fresh. Your basic source of income in single player are the mini-heists that refresh every day, but there are also larger, more significant heists that take planning, have a story, have unique outcomes and story branches, and are worth a ton more dosh.Again, I've had a blast playing this. _childDocuments_.review: The game is a super mixed experience, one with many — and sometimes very much glaring flaws, but one that is ultimately fun enough for me to recommend. Perhaps that is helped by the low price point, lowering the entry bar, and the expectations that come with it.The presentation is so campy and unserious that it could be passed off as a B movie, but I find that endearing — since you can't take it seriously, it's only easier believe in the heisting fantasy and any in-world politics. The core gameplay loop has a lot of good ideas to it, both in multiplayer, and in the highly addictive roguelite mode:At the same time, however, there's a lot that bogs the experience down:I'd place it as a solid 6-7/10. Far from a perfect game, but one that I will still be playing for more dozens of hours, at least for its fun singleplayer campaign. _childDocuments_.review: A game I didn't expect to like but now I'm pretty sure I... love?Its odd. The big, hetero chest pounding machismo of hiring largely middle-aged "badass" actors from the 1980s and 1990s was why when I first saw the trailer for this game I wrote it off but after the abject failure of Payday 3 I decided that, hey, its got the right price point so even if it blows chunks it'll be worth it, right?And it is. Even if I don't like the roguelite singleplayer mode and with it was elsewise, the actors who are clearly not good voice actors (hi chuck norris, your line reading is so bad it makes me laugh) stand out in a cheesy 1980s mid-tier action movie kind of way rather than an issue of development. Likewise with the game: any scuff marks on this diamond are flatly because its a mid-tier game, not a AAA powerhouse release. The further we get from the 2010's the happier I am that mid-tier games are returning and the anachronistic, odd Crime Boss: Rockay City is the epitome of why we need them. The gameplay loop is fun and satisfying, feeling like an evolution of the heist game genre while not having eyes bigger than its stomach in terms of what they could accomplish with their budget, the gunplay is snappy and fantastic and the fact that it can be entirely singleplayer is phenomenal and really helpful for me and a game of this price point. Nobody can say what multiplayer games will live and breath forever, but ensuring that there's a healthy and robust singleplayer that more or less has the same features (and then some, tbh) was inspired on INGAME STUDIOS' part and I applaud them.The part of the game that really rocked me most noticeably was that it allows you to tell the bots what to do and even control them directly depending on what part of the heist your on. You're not pigeon holed into playing as Michael Madsen's titular crime boss, and thats good because a lot of situations will ask for different gadgets, guns, or perks. My first run was dominated by a southern belle in heels named Alleycat who straight-up was as fast as a motorcycle thanks to her perks and it was capital-F fun to just be allowed to exist and experiment in this gameplay loop.I'm also not a roguelite/rogue-like fan in general but the fact that almost immediately after the first run it feels more manageable is a nice change of pace. A lot of roguelites feel like you're just supposed to die, die, die and die until you have a good set-up but on my second run alone I was able to get more of the stories and characters than before and that was really nice! I didn't feel locked into a "forever game" where I'd have to sit and suffer for nine million runs to experience a fraction of the game bits and pieces at a time.My largest complaint is that in the single player mode you really can't experiment without consequences, and sometimes some heists are a little less intuitive to me than others. More than once I've ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up because I misread something or other, particularly in taking down the defenses of the more in-depth heists - this isn't just a problem with Crime Boss: Rockay City, though, I can firmly say that this is just a problem with a lot of heists. The man-on-the-radio exists to ameliorate this from becoming too present of an issue and for the most part this game doesn't do it too often but the few gaffes I've made have felt cheap or otherwise out of my control than a screw-up of my own making.There is also a specific job type where it glitches out and a gas tank starts to explode shortly after spawning in for no reason, immediately forcing the job to go loud. Pretty sure its not intended, and its on a smaller game map so its not TOO bad but when I bring a solo character to a map like that I'm expecting being able to actually utilize my awesome stealth abilities. Disappointing but not spirit breaking, I've not experienced many other downsides beyond a typo in one of the cutscenes, some UI faffery such as me trying to buy a crew member and then inexplicably buying the member next to them (might be an issue with mouse controls? Not sure.) This is probably one of my longer Steam reviews just because its bewitched me in the same way that other charming budget-friendly titles like Road 96 have. The clearly non-American spin on Americanism pipe fed by pop culture is truly a delightfully fun setting, and Crime Boss: Rockay City avoids the misogynistic and homophobic tendencies of similarly set settings like Grand Theft Auto. Its just genuinely a fun setting that is enjoying itself, not ripping down others.Overall this feels like a solid, AA, mid-tier heist shooter with a laughably juvenile 1980's story that sweats popcorn, spits bullets, and has Michael Madsen laconically slurring one-liners while better voice actors like Danny Trejo, Danny Glover, and Michael Rooker chew the scenery whenever they're allowed to.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is not Crime boss: Rockay City!Gotta say that the game has surprised me. From a barely coherent meme game that spilled onto epic, to a relatively fun heist game with pretty good replayability.The previous footage back when it first launched just gave me the idea that the game was a paycheck for old/inactive actors from the 80s. Although the voice acting is a bit stiff, it's not too bad considering it is all background noise for the gameplay that makes up for it.The good:-The gunplay is very satisfying and the guns feel just right for the most part.-The missions and heists are pretty replayable with things changing sort of like PD2's heists (objectives changing spawns, set-pieces varying and enemy type spawns changing).-Loot feels good. Filling bags with a meter instead of single items is something that I personally like.-AI can be very useful at times and work as individuals to a degree.-Enemies mimic that of the PD series with police/guards being squishy, swat being a fair challenge along with shields and specialists being a fair threat that can open up your defences and finally the Juggernauts and bots being real thorns in your side if you fail to go for their weak spots.-Leveling up to get rewards is something that I personally like. Getting a better tiered weapon, equipment, skins or a useful skill by chance always entertains me. Although it would be cool to get a random resource reward to pick from like money or XP too.-I like the stealth systems in place and the fact that the security cams are animated to move and change their viewing angle. Another animation I like, while on the subject, is the drill being animated to move forward towards the doors as it progresses.-The unique characters with special perks are a fun idea, especially of you wanna change up your loadout from your boss character.The meh:-Some of the level design is a real pain. For instance, in the dragon dogs heist, I can stealth all of the way into the vaults only to alert EVERY guard in the map and they then ALL single file path directly to the drill. It feels a little synthetic when that happens.-Some of the difficulty spike in the single player is a little disheartening, then again it IS a roguelite.-Quickmatch has it's moments where there isn't any way to connect to any other lobbies and just fails. I mainly play with a friend or by myself in a private lobby so not too much of an issue for me.The bad:-The AI can tank a whole heist thanks to their obsession with grabbing bags, dropping them and running off to get shot while trying to grab a random bag or dropping them and forcing you to backtrack all the way to try and secure it. In single player, you can somewhat control them by restraining their movement but in multiplayer, they just run rampant and screw up your plans of looting or storing bags until ready.As it stands, the game is very reasonably priced for the base content. Even more so as it is 20% off with all current DLC included until the 11th of July. There are also more expansions planned later on and the devs have shown that the game has promise for the future and that they are still working on it.-Edit 28/7/24-AI is now controllable, at least in invite only games, and they somewhat seem a bit more proficient? (That last part might be just my perception)-Edit 19/8/24-The latest update added some welcome additions but also new issues that I've experienced. The AI is generally worse now, making them unresponsive to commands in favour of finding where I leave loose bags and going to pick them up. This happens even when we are nowhere near them like on the upper floor of dragon dogs waiting for the chopper with the bags at the explosive wall to the sewers. They just rush over to them through gunfire and heavy enemies.The difficulty has also been tweaked to make things even more chaotic on extreme. This included random robots showing up and 3-4 juggernauts half way through, instantly killing the 2 bots and me and my friend. One thing that happened to my friend was that his cluster grenade was not throwable. This forced us to cower from the police around corners instead of being able to use equipment to create a stop gap and gain control of the fight again.Due to this and how frustrating it was, I have to change my review to a negative. The fun has been turned into anguish.Note: Just tried to do an armoured truck ambush solo and it was horrible. On extreme with bots, I notices that the bots refuse to fight back and just go down. The constant stream of police with no reprieve is unplayable, especially considering the hoards of specialist units that are not just more tanky but also destroy you in seconds. I did;nt even get to open the trucks let alone have any team members alive by the time that the saws were done.I don't think I'll be revisiting this until things are properly balanced or at the very least have the bots able to attack enemies that are more than 2 meters away. Not sure who asked for these changes but I don't think that they speak for the majority of players.

_childDocuments_.review: I've clocked ~250 hours into the game on Epic since its release last year, so let me share my two cents about it.- If you've played PAYDAY2 solo with bots back then, give this one a try.- If you like the idea of mixing heists with gang wars and roguelite FPS games, give this one a try.- If you want to shoot your way to the top of the Florida underworld with Michael Madsen and some hilariously bad celebrity voice acting, give this one a try.- However, if you're looking for a multiplayer alternative of PAYDAY3 which has no online-only requirements but plays exactly like PAYDAY3, then be wary, as the game does  feature the kind of online challenges and deep customization that you're probably looking for.Crime Boss is a single-player / co-op crime FPS, combining PAYDAY-like heisting with roguelite progression, turf wars and some scripted story missions, set in 1990s Florida. The game has dedicated single-player and co-op modes, and while progression is slightly different between the two, they both use the same heisting gameplay at their core.This portion reminds me of PAYDAY2, albeit missions can be selected from a menu (instead of a CrimeNET-like interface) in three flavors, with increasing difficulty and payout: single heists, a chain of 3-5 missions, and so-called Urban Legends mini-campaigns. All these are playable with bots and co-op.Completing missions nets you money and XP, their amount depending on the job's difficulty and your performance (i.e. how much loot you collected, whether you killed any civilians, and whether you completed the optional challenge of the job). When levelling up, you can select one of three random rewards (weapons, equipment like grenades or throwable knives, heisters, etc.), which you can buy with the money you earned.What might be disappointing for PAYDAY players is that the game has limited customization options as of now. Characters only have pre-set upgrade paths and a locked loadout, which means that you should hire characters with archetypes (tanks, stealthy rogues or damage dealers) that fit your playstyle or the stealth/loud job at hand. But you cannot customize weapons either: they come in colored rarities, with gray common weapons having the worst stats and no attachments, while gold legendary guns being absolute bangers.This is where Crime Boss really shines for me, as its campaign is a unique mix of story missions, PAYDAY-like heists, the grand heists of GTAV (including planning missions) and gang wars.Taking on the role of Travis Baker (voiced and portrayed by Michael Madsen), our goal is to take over the criminal underworld of Rockay City with our cohorts (played by 1990s household names like Danny Glover, Kim Basinger and Michael Rooker, along with Damion Poitier from PAYDAY2's cast), pitted against enemy gang bosses (played by Vanilla Ice and Danny Trejo), and the local police led by Chuck Norris (!).During the campaign, we pull off (increasingly difficult) robberies with Baker and our heisters to fund our crew, wage team deathmatch turf wars with gang members to take over city districts (snatching all of them being the main goal of the campaign), and occasionally complete random storylines with scripted story missions to get extra cash or unlock certain grand heists and unique characters to recruit.As the campaign is a roguelite:- It's strong on RNG, so our starting turfs and crew are randomized for each run, just like the available heists, story missions and grand heist plotlines available for each in-game "day" (the local equivalent of roguelike dungeons).- Time is of the essence, as taking too long to conquer the city eventually results in Sheriff Norris ambushing us, forcing Baker to flee (and triggering a non-standard game over for that run).- After each level up with Baker (and each run we finish one way or another), we can unlock permanent perks (more starting turfs and money, better payouts after heists, damage buffs, reduced investigation speed, etc.) that carry over to future runs, giving us the edge.Missions take place in small, randomized maps (while story missions are scripted and linear). Stealthing is much simpler than in PAYDAY: there's permanent enemy tagging on Normal difficulty, lethal and non-lethal takedown options (the latter not raising any suspicion), an unlimited number of zipties and bodybags, plenty of stealth items (throwable bricks to lure guards away, camera jammers, etc.), and cameras can almost always be disabled in security rooms. Silenced firearms are also a thing, but they can be heard by nearby enemies, so be wary when planning to take out larger groups. Stealthable heists typically turn loud after three suspicion strikes (e.g. guards see us trespassing three times), unless the cameras or guards see something serious (like dead folks) which instantly turns heists loud.Loud jobs are also fun, with cops attacking in waves, and special units (like snipers, bulldozers or tasers) appearing over time as we carry loot bags to the escape vehicle. However, with the increasing intensity of attack waves, we don't want to spend too much time on loud jobs, as we can get easily overwhelmed. Unlike PAYDAY, there are no random escape sequences after successful heists (but they might be a thing if we die during jobs, albeit rarely).Gunplay is neat: the pieces feel nice and include details like magazine check animations when pressing Reload with full magazines. Bots are also decent, being able to loot the spoils and pick up / carry / throw loot bags by themselves. In single-player mode, we can also command them with basic Follow and Hold commands, use a ping system to mark them the NPCs to kill/subdue or the loot to collect, and even take control of them.Crime Boss is pretty, with most heists taking place in industrial zones or the neon-filled downtown. Character models, guns and map props also look good, and the game runs decent enough on the recommended specs to be an enjoyable experience even on older hardware (although I experienced negligible performance improvements when tried DLSS with a friend's RTX 3080).Voice acting, however, is a mixed bag: it's decent when it comes to heisters, cops and other NPCs, but the celebrity cast's acting is laughably ridiculous (Chuck Norris' "performance" is probably the worst piece of VA I've ever heard in a videogame, and I'm playing them since 1995). The story and dialogue are also quite wonky, with the former lacking pacing (due to the time-sensitive roguelite mechanics), while the latter being full of typos and gibberish text, likely due to loan translation (the game's developed by a Czech studio and published by an Italian company).That said, the game's lack of technical polish is the most important issue it's been suffering from since its release, as Crime Boss still features occasional performance hiccups, long loading times plenty of annoying bugs (e.g. enemies detecting us in stealth through objects, or bots getting stuck in the map), and severe showstoppers as well (e.g. scripting glitches making story missions impossible to finish or freezes on the load screen). Some quality of life updates would also go a long way, such as having defeated gangs actually flee when they lose a turf war, or adding proper intro/outro cutscenes to all heists (and not just to the Dragon Dogs robbery).Finally, while it's more of a personal gripe than a real issue, the latest DLC (Cagnali's Order) kinda hurts the relatively grounded, 1990s crime thriller feel of the game, considering its cyberpunk aesthetics. Here's hoping the rest of the expansions will not stray too far away from the original 90s heist concept.Still, for all its flaws, for someone who played lots of PAYDAY2 solo back in the day, Crime Boss scratches a very particular itch of mine - and it scratches it well.

_childDocuments_.review: So lets start off with this, if you like the payday series but want something else with its own identity and flavor you will feel at home here. Buy it, play it for just under 2 hours and you can easily make your decision on a refund from there. Crime Boss: Rockay City gets my recommendation.For others just general thoughts-16 usd includes  the game and all content till now (update 9). (as of 6/18/2024) which if it had not included the DLC i would have passed. ( I think it would have been lacking to much content)The game is getting compared to the payday series because about 70% of the game is designed with a very similar game play and loop, the other 30% are changes made to the way weapons work, the way perks work, the roguelike element, additional territory missions, etc. ( oh and dont get me wrong the movement and other systems in this game while fewer then something like payday 2 are much better designed and crafted around the core game and there is a massive amount of work just gone into just that, I really feel it while playing)I have played 3+ hours solo (offline) and this is one of those games that is better with friends and geared toward multiplayer but the core of the game can be fully completed solo with bots. No games bots are as good as people but these are usable and do not get in the way. The main negative of the bots is i find them out in the open pretty often  and feel like they don't have any agency to get by cover and shoot from there and like sometimes i would rush to the van and they would be slowly stepping back while shooting at the slowest pace possible. ( as a dev i would probably make them sprint at all times in all directions while not in cover and that would at least prevent a lot of AI from having to be re-scripted as kinda a shortcut to fix that problem)At first i did not like that i could not mod weapons either unlike payday 2 but now playing this game I see why. In payday 2 if you had all the DLC  at least 1/2 the guns became redundant because you could mod them and make them very similar to another weapon. In this game more of them feel very distinct, so in a way while it was a design decision i feel like it was made this way to provide gaps for more DLC weapons to fill in the future with out every single gun feeling the same. Im still unhappy that i cannot have 250 bullets in the box on a m249 saw but... i get it. This game does also have a unique charm not to unlike what payday 2 had when it came out and the devs and community around the game seem pretty welcoming. It could just be games like this get a good vibe in communities cause its co-op pve focused game that necessitates some semblance of team work, L4dead, DRG, Helldivers 2,  but its a vibe that needs to be in more games as it makes you want to play more.I do kind feel like games of this nature should have their own sub genre once 10 or so of them start hitting the market something like (Heist) or (thief) because it is its own particular game loop. Like if i said this is a Action Roguelike first person shooter co-op game that really  does not explain how or what the game is. If I said "Heist, Roguelike, FPS" it sums up most of the game and you know what to expect.It is kinda nice seeing familiar actors too from other roles where they did not really get the appreciation that they deserve being more or less key characters here as well. the story comes off corny at times but I appreciate it, if the game took itself too seriously it would not work and it would be dull. If you read all this your probably interested enough to just buy it. Make no mistake as much as its being compared to Payday 2 or 3 it is its own game and its worth a shot. Kinda wish they had a one-two mission or timed demo but i think to get the full picture of what this game will offer you if your really unsure is to just watch someone play it. It was good enough that i bought one copy for me one for my brother. Some games go for 70usd and then on top of it have a whole lot of PAy to win stuff or skins or/and paid battle passes and they make me not want to even bother looking at those games. This game 16 usd (for now) and just DLC (real content) and weapons ( skin unlocks through regular progression) in the future, hard to argue with that.  The devs are actually putting in the work like the DRG devs do and personally Deep Rock Galactic  is my gold standard for the best coop supported game their is so i would think that pretty high praise for this game and team.Im done rambling.

_childDocuments_.review: Important note: this game is a shooter with heists, not a heisting shooter. Stealth and tact are really afterthoughts in this game.The missions are usually quite fast, most are best performed loud, and loot or XP does not get boosted by stealth or loud. If you are familiar with Payday 2 and are expecting that, this is not anything close. It is, however, better than Payday 3 in almost every way except the heists themselves. Overall, the campaign is fun and the characters can be quite funny. The maps are highly detailed and although the side missions are pretty repetitive, the big heists and unique locations are fairly well made.There are still quite a few bugs and glaring issues with this game, the biggest one being audio desync and overall poor audio quality. Most of the voice actors suck except for Danny Trejo, he put his heart and soul into this performance and he honestly makes the game so much better when he is around. Michael Rooker is also pretty good but I think he was given a pretty bad script.(CB:RC released for free on the Epic Games store so you already know this wont be an amazing game lol)

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice, I am impressed with the graphic. Beautiful story line, and most importantly the random scenarios. There are also many bugs and glitches that makes it a bad experience. So far I am 51 hours into the game, on extreme difficulty.Some times AI characters of your team get stuck in places and if you are to switch to them, then you can not switch back to your other character. Sometimes when pressing "F" key which is default key to hit and intimidate guards, it just wont work. regardless if you have or have not been detected.The mission descriptions lack enough info. some such as the bank robberies or armored truck robberies often surprise you with either a smooth and stealth mission or it just introduces you to a battle which in either case your team may not be prepared for.When commanding AI to Stay, sometimes they just move around, especially if there are loot or bags laying around. which in cases of the basement complex robbery could trigger lasers or in other cases it could alert cameras or guards. in other cases the AI just climbs up or down even when Stay command is given and places the AI character from your team in point blank for the NPC to shoot.You also don't get a chance to restart your mission and lose all progress, which keeps you on your toes. _childDocuments_.review: This game plays like the Payday games where you go and grab bags of loot and make it to your getaway vehicle. But there are different aspects to this game, including a rogue like element that makes this game very interesting and engaging. There's a turf war going on and it pits you against several gangs. You have to defend your turf and take other neighborhoods as well. Doing so will throw you into a map with the opposing gang members, no slideshow with a dice roll, you actually defend and conquer. You can upgrade your base and your recruits. Some recruits have interactive story segments which is awesome. You'll have to make business decisions that affect the outcome in some situations. You have your main character played by Michael Madsen. You can choose him for your missions or have him sit out and use other recruits. But if he dies, your progress starts over. It's real easy to get hooked on this game and it brings some great ideas that are not in other games today. It definitely deserves more recognition.

_childDocuments_.review: First let’s get the notable cast out of the wayMichael Madsen (Travis Baker the Candyman Boss)His handlers and planners consist of Michael Rooker (Touchdown)Kim Basinger (Casey)Danny Glover (Gloves)Damion Poitier (Nasara and Payday’s Chains)Rival gang bosses areDanny Trejo (Dragon)Vanilla Ice (Hielo)Law Enforcement isChuck Norris (Sheriff Norris)This will no doubt get me smited by Chuck Norris but his voice acting is absolutely horrendous, it’s so monotone and badly done that I was under the impression that it was done by A.I, everyone else listed imo done a really good job with their rolesGameplay wise this game will no doubt garner the comparisons with the Payday franchise but your not here to read about that game since your on this pageHere’s the rundownThis game is good for people who want to do short 5min heists or longer heists, you can extract from missions anytime even if you haven’t met the quota which will result in a failure but you will still keep what you have looted, this is handy but it doesn’t apply to all missions, this is for the short quick heists such as robbing a truck or a jewellery storeYou can holster your weapon at anytime provided you haven’t gotten to the point where the police are called or you have decided to “start heist” and you have unlimited throwables such as bricks, grenades or emp grenades but they have a recharge meter, you also have unlimited zip ties and you can have up to 3 hostages follow you at once and you can also zip tie security guards but you have to hit them first to get them to drop their weapon just don’t use the regular melee button otherwise you will kill them which will give you one strike to the 3 strike stealth system in placeYou have 3 strikes when it comes to stealth, things such as getting spotted in a restricted area, shooting a security camera and killing guards will affirm to the strike systemOnce the police are called to the scene the game has 5 levels of difficulty when it comes to the swat with it increasing evermore the longer you take to the point robot police will come into play to deal with youThe game has a few bugs such as intimidating a civilian can sometimes make them warp behind you or they don’t follow you correctly and decide to take a longer path around as well as your A.I bots getting stuckYou can carry up to 2 loot bags or 3 if your playing as Jupiter, carrying 1 loot bag allows you to still use your primary gun but the moment you carry 2 bags you can only use your secondary weaponThe A.I are a lot more useful whereas they can loot for you and even carry bags you throw either at them or on the ground and even transport them to the van on their own which is a great QoL featuresUnfortunately during the much longer heists such as robbing the bank vault and the kings gold bars I found myself at a loss of what I was doing, I couldn’t find the keycard to the elevator on the tellers desk for the lift in bank heist and and the bots were no help with that either, I had no idea where I was looking apart from Nasara saying it but I gave up in the end cause nothing helped to indicate where I should go after a prolonged search, same with the gold heist, I had no idea what I was doing when it came to opening the cages where the gold bars were kept and all I knew was that the drill was involved somehow.Playing in a public lobby will also give you an additional 10% rewardUnfortunately as you level up your account each level reward is RNG and you get to pick one of 3 choices that pop up ranging from weapon skins, characters and weapons.Sadly the weapons as of current are not modifiableThe campaign is a roguelite so if any of your gangsters die or are arrested they’re gone for good and if your using Travis Baker he’s a double edged sword, you can use him twice per day for a 50% bonus in loot but if he dies the run is overAttacking other terrorities: You hire gangsters to take over other territories so it’s more favourable the more you hire, if you die you switch to another gangster until either all your gangsters die or you kill the enemies.Defending your territories: You take control of Touchdown armed with a light machine gun and whatever amount of gangster your hire, it’s the same as attacking other territories but sometimes things like an attack helicopter that you need to takedown comes into playRegular Heists: These consist of you forming a team of 1-4 to rob places such as jewellery stores, banks etc etc each getting more difficult as the story progresses, the more members you have recruited the more you have to pay towards their cut when the heist is successful, if you think your about to be overrun sometimes it’s better to extract early to live to fight another dayThe campaign consists of day cycles and when you decide to mate a day as over it’ll also reduce the amount of heat the police have towards you and sometimes progress the storyAll in all a really great game that I’m having a fun with, don’t go into this game expecting it to be a poor Payday clone as that will just ruin your experience due to your expectations, instead go into it with a fresh mindset without the comparisons to give yourself a better outlook experience and determine the good and bad things from that perspective otherwise your just gonna have a bad time

_childDocuments_.review: Travis Baker discovered the method of creating renewable pocket bricks in 1992, allowing him to dominate the street gang fights without even using a firearm. The respect earned from his rival gangs allowed him to overtake the streets of Rockay city, brick by brick. He was eventually known as Travis Bricker, or Brickolini, even producing his own hit single, "All Bricked Up" in 1994. His reign would not last forever, as he unfortunately passed away from attempting to throw a brick straight up into the air to see how far it would go, only to be struck down by the very power he wielded so confidently. Rest in bricks.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it odd that a game so heavily hated on at-launch for failing to be a Payday successor is now looking to attract the audience that was scammed out of a decent Payday 3. In any case, it has certainly worked, just don't expect a good story, or any good gameplay... or a good Sheriff voice actor. "lEt'S gO." Anyone in the game would've been WAY better than Chuck Norris as a voice actor for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sheriff. Hell, I think the main character you play sounds like a more convincing Sheriff! But, I digress...It's not a good game by any metric, but it isn't a bad one. In comparison to Payday 3, it certainly does hold its merits over the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that the 3rd game was, and how the lead gameplay designer hardly played any of the previous games (got to like level 25 lmao). At its best, it is somewhat fun and it does add a few "unique" aspects, though don't expect it to be a 1:1 clone; it doesn't have armour systems, so no "risk-reward" plays, and it leans into specific characters having perks as opposed to a global perk system with characters acting as faces. It's TERRIBLE at its worst, boiling down to Payday 3's bathroom waiting simulator, since you're incentivised to not lose health without any reward for taking risks (faster health regen for killing enemies not present, etc.). It's... ♥♥♥♥. Even on the easiest difficulty (normal), the game is unwaveringly unfair if you're going loud, and sometimes you'll be forced into loud encounters because MEASDHJASGHD GAME DEISN ISYM PASSION.Even moreso, a lot of the stuff you might take for granted when you first play it NOW is likely to have been from recently-released updates, which begs the question: do you want to buy another cyberpunk, where you have to wait 3 years until the nothing game turns into a barebones minimalistic experience? Should we really have to wait for updates, and THEN pay for the game after a certain period of time with buggy, instant-release titles? Are your standards that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ low?3/10, Balance the game. Take notes from Payday 2, not Call of Duty. This style of game is how you end up with another Payday 3.

Rockay City. A thriving metropolis with excitement buzzing from the sandy bay to the towering skyscrapers. But beyond the glamour, there is a fierce turf war raging on... After the demise of the previous crime boss, there's an open vacancy for a new King of Rockay City - but it isn't just you who is fighting for the throne. Choose your crew based on their skills and expertise, and execute daring missions with the hopes of walking away with the cash, the turf and, ultimately, the crown.

Crime Boss: Rockay City is an organized crime game combining first-person shooter action and turf wars, playable solo or with friends. Take on the role of Travis Baker - a man with his sights set on becoming the new King of Rockay City, one crime at a time...

name: Journey to Foundation
detailed_description: Journey to Foundation is a story-driven sci-fi adventure set in Isaac Asimov’s Foundation universe, built from the ground up for VR. You are Agent Ward, a galactic spy with the Commission of Public Safety. What begins as a mission to investigate deserters in the Periphery quickly becomes a battle for control of all humanity. Throughout your journey, you’ll be faced with difficult choices. Decide whether to befriend or double-cross people, determine who lives and dies, and help different factions rise or fall in this branching story. Will you fight for a dying Empire, or will you join the Foundation to help rebuild what has been lost? CHOICE & CONSEQUENCE Make your decisions wisely - they can impact your journey and how others perceive you. UNIQUE MENTAL ABILITIES Use the power of Mentalics to influence or destroy your enemies and read their minds. TOOLS OF THE EMPIRE Disguise, blast, and hack your way through the galaxy with stealth, combat, and puzzles. KEY FEATURES Experience a gripping narrative adventure unlike anything else you can find in VR, with 6-8 hours of gameplay Interact with over 90 fully voiced characters brought to life by a top-tier voice cast including Jennifer Hale, François Chau, Jason Hightower, and more… Participate in the drama through an immersive conversation system where you make gestures, look for hidden dialogue choices, and interact with objects Accessibility options to make your journey comfortable: continuous movement, teleportation, snap turn, smooth turn, and vignetting Available with full voice acting and text in English, French, German, and Spanish
