short_description: A story-driven adventure among the stars, Journey to Foundation puts you at the center of your own sci-fi saga. Unleash your unique Mentalic abilities, gain information through diplomacy or coercion, and choose who to trust. Where will your journey lead you?

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is one of the better narrative-driven experiences in VR. I would best describe it as a TellTale Game brought to life in VR, which is mostly a good thing. On the positive, it absolutely accomplishes what it sets out to do: put you in the middle of this sci-fi drama where you have to make some difficult choices. On the bad side, some of the VR interactions & action sequences are a bit stiff and underwhelming.If you are not familiar with TellTale Games, then this is a choices matter story-focused game. There is also shooting, climbing, and puzzle solving involved, but all these are rather simple and not too challenging. Your character has special mental abilities (Mentalic) which allow you to sense the emotional state of your target or even manipulate their actions. For example, you can make a guard frightened and they'll walk away from their post, so you can sneak by or you can use the information of their emotional state to help you in your interrogations.You have a weapon (laser gun) that you can upgrade to be more like a shotgun, or a sniper, or an automatic weapon. The weapon can overheat and if does so, it'll auto-reload (cool off before you can shoot again). You can two-hand the weapon for extra stability, but I found that was not needed. You also have a multi-tool that you can use to either burn off screws or a hacking tool that'll open containers (after solving a cube color line connection puzzle). However, the key gameplay element is the choice-making. You'll choose from several dialogue choices by hand selecting them. Sometimes you can open up certain dialogue choices by taking certain actions, for example, by using your Mentalic ability. Sometimes you'll also have the option to take certain actions such as shooting the person you are interrogating or letting them live. While some of the choices are easy to make, you will definitely have to grapple with some very tough choices. It took me 6.5 hours to complete one playthrough. Game is running on the Unreal Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a mostly steady 90 fps. I did not experience any major issues or bugs. However, I did run into some issues, which I'm not sure how widespread they are. The biggest issue was this slightly lessened FOV (vignette-type effect) that was present even though I had turned off the vignette in the settings. It was very slight though. Also, some objects would go beneath surfaces (you could still pick them up though) and there was some clipping. Lastly, some animations were missing and there was just some jank overall.You do have full locomotion and teleportation available, along with smooth & snap turning (degree of turn / speed of turn). You can choose the camera to be head or hand directed. You can choose dominant hand. You can calibrate height and holster. You have both button crouching and magnet hands, so you can play comfortably seated. Voice languages are available in English, Spanish, French & German.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: This is close to a 1:1 Quest port. Even if devs added some realtime lighting and dynamic shadows, and some more high-res textures, polygon levels are horribly low. Compared to Red Matter 2, the so-called high-res textures in Journey to Foundation feel quite low-res, but I'm sure these are better than the Quest textures. The game has been designed for the ultra-low-end Adreno 650 phone gpu inside the Quest 2, and it shows all over this game. To enjoy this game, you have to look beyond the poor graphics, and I do like the story. There's so much conversation that this game feels more like some 3D book experience or a walking simulator. For that purpose this game does feel somewhat fresh (we do not have many such games in VR). Climbing and interactions are poor too, so whether or not you like this game comes down to how much you appreciate the story. For fans of Isaac Asimov, this game may be easy to recommend, for others it becomes more difficult to recommend.Like Quest games, there are no settings for graphics. The added lighting and shadows do take a toll. I get solid 80 fps using Index res 350% (about 32 million pixels per frame combining both eyes) with a RTX 3090. The game seems to force very blurry TAA for antialiasing, and you need to push SteamVR res as much as possible to reduce the blur. Sound volume is a bit too low with the Index, and there's no finger tracking, but everything else works fine with the Index.For the days when you're too tired to engage in VR games with tons of action, this sci-fi walking sim does have some advantages. Also, devs knowing they have no processing power with the Quest 2 have focused much on the story, puzzles and conversation - and there's some value to be found in this. If you want true high-end VR and great shooting/action, get Hubris instead. If you want a calm and relaxing game with tons of talk, this game can be recommended. - But I'm down to 5.5/10 - just barely making this game worth recommending -  then again, the nice dynamic PCVR shadows did help :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: A Narrative VR adventure/action game set in an obtuse grand sci-fi universe from the mind of legendary Isaac Asimov, recently popularized by the scope and scale of the Apple+ TV series?Talk about a niche product!For all the above reasons alone, The devs deserve a resounding thump on the back and an enthusiastic handshake with a fistful of dollars up front.The graphics may not be PCVR level top notch, but it's equitable to Star Wars Galaxy's Edge on the Quest 2, and honestly, perfectly serviceable. The Voice acting is 10/10. I'm just about an hour in, but I'm already digging everything they've shown so far.This is one of my favorite genres in VR, and one of my most memorable sci-fi franchises.The Initial generous 15% launch discount for the first 2 weeks was also a no-brainer.Get this game. Support devs like these and hope for more amazing content from them in the same or other storied franchises down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: Was really looking forward to a story rich game in VR, which are far too few in number. Unfortunately the graphics are indeed pretty terrible - which wouldn't be too bad if it had some kind of interesting artistic style, but it's just old-looking jank graphics. Also, there is no way to turn off what appears to be TAA anti-aliasing, so there may well be a lot more detail, but we just can't see it because TAA blurs it all out (Hubris was like this at launch, but the fixed it.) Probably a low-quality port from some form of 'non-pc-vr' is my guess. It is also somehow incompatible with VRPERFKIT, which is pretty unusual, meaning I'll have to try and use Reshade to get any sharpness at all. What a disappointment. When did devs decide it was OK to take all of these settings away from the end-user? I would have been more likely to have rated this a "yes" if it wasn't for the inability to properly manage the graphic options!

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game if your on index. The hand positioning is way higher than where your hand is, which I got used to, but I then got soft locked on the part where the game teaches you about keycards. every time I tried grabbing the card it always phased through the ground, making me reload from checkpoint, where it happens over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a one-dimensional VR game. Your first impression of every character is accurate, not because you are prescient, but because each character is inspired by an over-used trope. They will not deviate from their trope. This includes entities like The Empire, The Foundation, and a Pagan-like culture, the name of which I'm too bored to remember. The writing could have been generated by ChatGPT and the visuals are uncomfortably close to PS2-era. The game offers kinda-branching dialogue choices, but they shouldn't even bother. Whatever it is you think someone is going to say is an accurate prediction. Not too surprisingly, the lazy writing makes use of a power. Let's call it The Force, because the writers of this game abuse it in the same way Lucas Film uses the Force to make the plot go in directions it couldn't logically go otherwise. Sometimes the Force can be used to do this one thing, which would be a very useful thing to do in many situations, but it isn't used in those situations because then the game would end in Chapter 1. And then in the final moment of the game the power is used to do something completely out of left field.The development time must be 0.8 Star Citizen units long, because the game uses GUI elements that developers had rejected before the Occulus Rift became the Quest. You can toggle invincibility in combat by strafing left and right in a straight line, forever. Your firearm has no sights and the unadjustable angle of the grip makes a shotgun grip seem like a right angle. It seriously causes discomfort to my youthful wrists. No matter what your IRL height is, the game puts you at approximately 6.5 feet off the ground, and noticeably taller than all other NPCs (even though you play as a female.) This is jarring if, in real life, you are shorter than virtually everyone else, and your IRL feet float 18 inches from the virtual ground at all times. The game design is frustrating, and this extends especially into the puzzles which are both comically easy and impossible. They are of the "push this", "turn that" type of variety, usually to a single object, and as such they serve to waste time rather than challenge the player. But occasionally, the puzzles become unintentionally impossible. For example, there is this puzzle where you need to place the hand from a corpse onto a hand scanner. The corpse is adjacent to the scanner but, get this, the only part of the corpse that is a physics-based ragdoll versus a static mesh is the hand itself. If you are like me and your first inclination when seeing a corpse is bop it like a bobblehead, then you'll immediately determine that the corpse is a static mesh when your physical contact with its head has the same effect as if it were a wall. This rules out from your mind the entire branch of logic supposing the corpse, or a part of it, can be moved to solve a puzzle.  Other frustrating game design choices include a strange insistence that many things should inappropriately be accomplished by pushing a virtual button. Need to gather crew members to a certain place? Push a virtual button. Need to navigate the game menus? Push a virtual button (with a freakishly gigantic and unwieldy hands that doesn't even align well with your IRL hand). Want to quit the game? Push a very small virtual button, twice. Do it rapidly or else you need to do it again. The game is also fascinated by spreading stuck doors open. For no reason at all, the game randomly places partially closed elevator-type doors in your path that you must slowly, every so slowly, spread with your hands. I've spread first dates faster than doors in this game.  Now, you might think the slow door thing is to substitute loading times. No, we're not loading games from CDs anymore Grandpa. Or, to achieve a dramatic pause in the action? No. These occur during exploration segments of the game, or to more accurately characterize them, linear corridor walking simulations.  Or, to create suspense when danger is near? Nope. The spreading door fetish is puzzling, unlike the puzzles. If Journey to Foundation nails anything, then it would be truth in advertising. This game literally bends when you get to Foundation, immediately prior to actually seeing it. This is the only aspect of the game that defied my expectations, as it spent a good deal of words to impress upon the player how awesome Foundation is. The location, and the people who call it home, are rather important to the story. My expectation was for Foundation to be the setting for the climax. Instead, it's the backdrop for the afterwards. Rather than Journeying to Foundation, I suggest going anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: A lot better than I thought it would be as I dont normally like this genre of game - story focused with light puzzling and some action elements.   It's very disconcerting hearing the same voice actor (François Chau)  who played the arch villain Jules Pierre Mao in The Expanse.Environments are well designed with good atmophere.  It doesnt feel like its just quickly been ported from Quest as things are high poly with high rez textures.   VR hand/object interactions are also good and there are a lot of options to tweak comfort settings or reset height / belt position when switching between playing seated and standing.Only one bug so far with 1 enemy stuck in a wall, but it was easy to work around.Got this on discount and I feel like Ive got a bargain.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry, I would have liked to enjoy the game, but the realization and gameplay are just too bad. It's a kind of interactive movie, with a few dialogue choices and actions to perform from time to time. Except that the graphics/art direction are so bad for a movie. An artistic choice should have been made rather than using realistic but ultra-low-res textures, this totally breaks the immersion, particularly for large-scale scenes. Actions aren't really pleasant to perform (I ended up using the "skip" option as much as possible), and the dialogue choices are poor. It feels like playing a game from the very early days of VR. It could have been much better with at least a few spectacular scenes (in the SF context, there was plenty to do) or a faster pace, but I got too bored to continue. A good point, however, is the dubbing in several languages.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: Journey to Foundation excels where it's important: it's just a fun game to play. You want excellent VR interactivity? You want to have good blaster fights intermixed with using Jedi-like powers? You want a good story that you direct with the choices you make? Get this game immediately. I just finished my first run through, and now I'm going to go through it again picking different choices/paths to see how it affects the story flow and outcome.For those who loved the game Lonn, Journey to Foundation. And conversely, those who love JTF should get Lonn!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, a good VR game that didn't receive the marketing it deserved !It's always great to have an ambitious VR game, especially with narative on.Game isn't perfect, the art style would not please everyone, but the narrative is great and the VR gameplay is good.+ full french translation for dialogues is great.I'm sure a lot of PCVR users aren't aware the game came out on steam and don't know  its existence. Hope it'll change with this sale !
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about story and choices. Based on classic sci-fy literature of Aizek Asimov. It has relatively simple low-resolution textures and low LOD distance graphics (you will constantly see that some details just pop-up before your eyes). It is bad, because enviroment looks sometimes like in early 2000 3d games, but, on the other hand, it is very optimized and you can use a lot of supersampling. Nevetheless, graphics was pretty enough for me to make this game immersive. Characters are memorable, all of them are the part of a story, even the nameless wounded soldier that will told you door code telpathically. Journey to Foundation has not so many interactive objects, but you still have some VR features like climbing, opening doors and hatches, welding, interacting with consoles, quest items and hacking mini-game on some locks. Fights are mediocre and primitive - small arenas and simple copy-pasted bots with few moves. Health is restoring automatically. Just stay in cover and shoot. Weapon damage feels too low, that is why I prefere sniper rifle blaster variant, because it is able to one-shot enemy in head sometimes. Psionic mechanics are simple, but they are organically integrated into the plot and NPC interactions.I got this game on sale and it was actually worth it. It is rare example of story-driven game in VR. If you like sci-fy - try it yourself and make a decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great VR game. I have only spent a few hours in it so far, but I honestly think this is a worthy title. The graphics is simple, but it has its moments: ships passing by the windows, well-animated characters, and good mocap. The game is story-driven, which is the best kind of game for me, and yet there is some good action. Nothing new VR-wise, but overall satisfactory. Psychic powers are combined with good firearms; the enemies are not completely stupid like in Hubris (I wouldn’t mention it here if Hubris’s reviews weren’t closed). I would recommend this game to anyone who’s into good narrative-based games.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review: didnt finish yet. almost 3 hours in, the graphics are as what you would expect, they are and for the time being, will always be quest 2 graphics, if you're not to fond of it, you can skip it, if you don't mind and you're in for the story, go for it.the game has a really interesting story and great puzzles, the lip sync on the characters are great and the decision making in the story makes it more engaging.  It could be better, as there's several moments npcs just vanish into a wall after they're done talking to you. I honestly think that if they fix the minor bugs and upgrade the graphics quality, this could be a one of a kind game with a amazing experience.7/10EDIT: boy oh boy, i finally had the chance to finish this game and let me tell you, what a DISASTER, don't get me wrong, the story is VERY interesting, captivating even, the puzzles, AMAZING, the voice actors match their characters greatly, but oh my god... I don't know if it was due to budget issues but the game starts GREAT and slowly declines in quality, puzzles feel repetitive, the story gets slow, you don't feel any thrill on the CLIMAX, when i went through the climax i was super confused, it just... ends. No big moment, no background music, just ends, the game ends abruptly and all the characters feel lazy at the end, no spoilers for the story, if you want to know that see it for yourself, but even the characters stop MOVING, all the characters (not enemies) just slide through the ground, they don't walk, their heads don't have movement, the only thing that moves are arms (when ABSOLUTELY needed) and the lips.truly a game's potential WASTED.i unfortunately change my rating to a 2/10 i just can't get over the anticlimactic ending and the poor quality of the game throughout the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

_childDocuments_.review:
It's been almost two centuries since Hari Seldon predicted the fall of the Galactic Empire and forged a Foundation to mitigate the chaos and destruction that would come.

You are an agent with the Commission of Public Safety, a shadowy organization that maintains order in the Galactic Empire.

What begins as a mission to investigate deserters in the Periphery quickly becomes a battle for control of all humanity. With your superior officer in your ear, and the esteemed governor's daughter at your side, you must journey to Foundation.

The future is in your hands. In this immersive roleplaying adventure, you decide who will rise and what is lost to the fires of anarchy.

Disguise, hack, and blast your way through Asimov's groundbreaking sci-fi universe using the most advanced tools the Galactic Empire has to offer.

Where will your journey lead you?
_childDocuments_.name: Journey to Foundation

name: BAKERU
detailed_description: Disaster strikes Japan! Oracle Saitaro and his Festival Troops are using a bizarre festival to take over Japan. Bakeru travels to 47 Japanese prefectures to free Japan from the grip of evil spirits! Spectacular action set in fairy tale Japan! Bakeru takes place in 'Fairy Tale Japan,' a mix of modern Japan and old period dramas, which is divided into more than 50 stages. Battle on with Bakeru's drum! A secret treasure passed down by Tanuki Clan. It is said to be able to purify evil spirits. Fight through enemies and traps with simple controls! Transform into fairy tale heroes! By obtaining a Henge License, Bakeru can transform into whoever gave him the license. Transform into famous Japanese heroes like Kintaro and Momotaro to use their skills and abilities. Additional features have been added to the Steam release ・New Attack: Hurricane ・New Attack: Spinning Top ・New Attack: Hurricane + Spinning Top Combo ・Additional Enemy: Lantern Boss ■About the gameplay ・Play as Bakeru and use your 'Henge' powers of transformation to overcome stage obstacles and enemies. ・Features over 47 stages based on the prefectures of Japan, each with their own unique motifs. ・Includes variant stages where you transform into a vehicle and race off or take to the skies for air combat!

_childDocuments_.review: BAKERU gameplay is fast paced and very satisfying, controls are responsive and it's very fun to play. The combat system has actually a lot of depth, you have a parry system, perfect dodges, dashing, various combos and super moves. The transformations are also all fun and interesting and give you more freedom to fight your enemmies.Visuals are very colorful with a nice mix of modern and retro to them.It looks refreshing, the art style is nice and there's lot of details in the levels.The soundtrack is top quality as well as the voice acting.Overall it's a highly polished product and it's not surprising knowing that the developers at Good-Feel made few games for Nintendo.The PC port is great, the game runs flawlessly maxed with uncapped framerate.BAKERU is a must have if you're a fan of Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon, Super Mario Sunshine or old school action/platformers in general.I have not completed the game but so far I really love it.I am having an absolute blast playing this game, it's a ton of fun.There is a lot of content and collectibles to find here so the price tag is justified.Easy recommendation if you enjoy the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! Really fun to play & the creativity is solid.It's more like a Kirby game than Mario one, but has fairly basic  (but fun) combat that includes a parry system.This wasn't the format for Goeman - Legend of the Mystical Ninja (the game is touted as a spiritual successor to), but it uses a similar sort of setting & vibe.Definitely one of the best of it's genre around.Don't go in expecting Ratchet & Clank or Mario Odyssey... it doesn't have that level of budget, but has plenty of it's own charm & certainly scratches that itch. These sort of game are few & far between on PC... and this is absolutely one of the better ones.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna keep this review brief cause I've purchased and 100%'d the original Japanese release on Switch back in 2023: If you love action platformers that hearken back to the Gamecube|PS2 era of games, you owe it to yourself to play Bakeru. This localization is superb, the translation is very close to the former fan translation that used to be available for the original JP Switch release. Performance is amazing: supporting locked 30FPS, 60FPS, and Uncapped Framerate options as well as other graphical settings you can mess with.Some have said this game is a "Goemon Spiritual Successor" and while this game has some of Goemon's DNA in it (absolutely a byproduct of Good-Feel being Ex-Konami devs), Bakeru is very much it's own thing. Please approach and enjoy it as such!Please give support to this game's localization, it didn't do super well financially in Japan so it's a miracle it even arrived overseas!
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing this mainly as a heads up for anyone hoping for a spiritual sequel to the Mystical Ninja/Goemon games: this is not that. I was drawn in by the parallels to those classics, but they are pretty superficial - it lacks the story, sense of humor, and depth of game mechanics that gave those games their soul. It's a solid game, but has more in common with straightforward, maguffin-hunting 3D action platformers like Mario. So if that's what you're after, give it a look, but if you want more Goemon, keep looking.Also, I got almost 8 hours in and didn't even reach any of the advertised robot battles, so don't expect that to be a main focus unless it becomes one late in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: It is as if Super Mario and Takeshi's Castle had a baby and the offspring of which was Bakeru .Bakeru is a great platform game it's been a while since I've enjoyed one from being to end without stopping to play other games or do something else.I give this one 8.5/10 I do advise people to buy it even if the price is not that cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: You like Goemon, maybe you liked Princess Peach Showtime, or maybe you're a fan of Kirby games Then there is no question to answer, get this game, be addicted, and have a blastI literally couldn't put it down for a few days, and had a blast Totally worth the price of admission, with fund gameplay and music
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast so far! The controls and combat feel snappy and satisfying (after getting used to attacking with the bumpers), the levels are colorful and there's 8 collectibles/fun trivia to find in each level. If you like classic 3D platformers, you will love Bakeru!The game works amazingly well on Steam Deck OLED. Runs at 90fps most of the time, with some dips into the 70s. I assume you'll have a rock-solid experience if you lock it at 60, but so far the dips are few and far between, so I'll stick to 90. Also, this game just POPS on the OLED screen! It's so sharp, colorful and vibrant; a feast for the eyes!
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Yes. In all seriousness this is one of those games where if you're looking at it, you already had an interest in it and this is where I can proudly confirm that yes, it's good.You'll hear the words "spiritual successor to Goemon/Mystical Ninja made by Goemon/Mystical Ninja devs" here and there and yeah it's exactly that.And for those that don't know what that means, I can sum this game up as a very polished stylized action platformer that you might expect to play on the Gamecube or even N64. It won't necessarily knock your socks off but you'll have just a solid good time. 62 stages, collectables to get, and nice level variety. I give it an A grade.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games of the year for me. A trailer alone cannot do it justice. BAKERU is a spiritual successor to Konami's Ganbare Goemon series, and yet it feels like one of the very few 3D platformers of it's kind that understands what this means. This game ain't a subpar copypaste of Goemon's Great Adventure, rather it's a game that takes inspiration from the roots of it's developers while feeling entirely fresh and brand new.The level of attention and care packed into everything is something I don't see in most modern games of this size. For example vehicle levels are one of the most controversial aspects of a lot of 3D platformers, and yet they're a treat in BAKERU. The mecha levels admittedly feel a bit sluggish to play, but thankfully the boss levels that utilise the mech are built to accomodate it. There are very few points of no return, so it's a lot of fun to explore the stages at your own pace and pick up any collectables you missed at your leisure. The combat is very unique, as Bakeru's main weapon is a drum which makes the player use the drumsticks accordingly. Update: I have nominated this game for game of the year in the steam awards 2024!If you are on the fence about this game, I'd say it's well worth every dollar. It's one of those games where you don't feel the need to wait for a sale just to justify having it in your library.  BAKERU sets the golden standard of what modern spiritual successors of legacy franchises should be.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: One of the transformation give you yellow crocs and dual wielding fishing cane, I can only give 11/10.But to be serious, it's a nice little platformer with an original story. It can stand out as its own and not a nostalgia bait game for Mystical Ninja. Play with a controller, it is easier to control.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: A sinister festival is touring around Japan led by the evil Oracle Saitaro! Armed with his trusty Haradaiko drum and transformation magic abilities, Bakeru must restore peace to the land by roaring through over 60 fun-filled and detail-rich levels based on Japan's prefectures!BAKERU is a 3D action-platformer developed by Good Feel, who you may know from the games they co-developed with Nintendo. The game's quality and focus on fun are absolutely up-to-par with their previous releases. If you love platforming games, especially Konami's Ganbare Goemon series, don't miss this one!And don't worry, the PC port is fantastic, giving you plenty of graphical options without any jank or frame-pacing weirdness.FULL VIDEO REVIEW:

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun and charming classic style 3D carrying on the spirit of Mystical Ninja Goemon.Is it reinventing the wheel and wowing you every level? No you get a grip the gameplay pretty quickly and the variety that there is is rather spread out, and overall its on the easy side.But if you want something that is well polished and controls well, that scratches the collectathon or Goemon itch, and enjoy games with a very Japanese aesthetic to them I cant reccomend more highly!Sometimes you just want a solid classic video game and this delivers.Music is extremely good as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Mystical Ninja was one of my favorite games on the N64 and playing this game as its successor made me feel good. The nostalgia factor is absolutely there. The music is amazing too. Thing is, I wish it had more of the Mystical Ninja music feel to it and the open world feel. As an added bonus, Bakeru's voice actress is Junko, the voice of Naruto, which I am a fan of.Please pick this game up as the support for a sequel is needed.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a fun 3D platformer that has the vibes of games from an earlier time (like the late 90s and early 2000s), this is one you should consider. I never was aware of this game until they dropped the demo a few months ago and thought it was unique. As a Japanese game, it has been translated with subtitles but the voice dialogue is all in Japanese. I don’t mind it because the story is somewhat simple and there isn’t a lot  cutscenes. Just be aware that there is no English speaking, you have to deal with subtitles. I’m glad PC got this because it wasn’t even released on PlayStation which is surprising nowadays-usually games show up on all platforms. But this is only on Steam and the Nintendo Switch. It feels like a game that would fit that platform well because it is very kid friendly and bright, colorful and cute. The kid friendly aspect brings me to my biggest criticism. There is no difficulty setting in this game, it starts off very easy. It does get a little harder as you go but I didn’t feel challenged at all (after playing the first 8 stages). I wouldn’t expect anything super hard but I would consider games like Crash Bandicoot 4 or Mario Odyssey as being more challenging. I think it’s still worth the experience but there is no tricky platforming or combat sections that I have found yet.It runs great on the LCD model of the Steam Deck- mostly 60fps at the highest settings (there aren’t a lot though, just texture/draw distance/AA/resolution/V Sync). It does have some performance dips into the high 40s at worst  but most of the time it is just a flat 60fps.

_childDocuments_.review: Bakeru is an attempted throwback to action-platformers of the N64 to PS2 era, and it succeeds with flying colors. The game follows the tanuki Bakeru and his tiny friend Sun as they travel across Japan to stop the bad guys from mind controlling the entire country. Most every level in the game is based on one of Japan's many prefectures, with a few exceptions, leading to a game with about 60ish levels all of which are unique in some way or another, be it level theme, overall structure, or by being one of several "mini-game" type levels(such as time-trial racing or a shooter). Bakeru himself is very easy to control; he can run, jump and dodge but also has some more advanced moves the game lets you figure out for yourself such as the dodge-lunge(dodge, then press jump) which get put to good use towards the end of the game. His combat capabilities are well rounded too, with his assortment of light and heavy attacks and his ability to perfect dodge and parry incoming attacks as well as his Henge powers which give him access to several new fighting styles for a limited time. Each level is set up in a fairly linear fashion with a few side paths for collectables. The collectables are a highlight for me, being both fairly easy to get and intresting in concept. There's Souveniers which are nick-nacks relating to the level you picked it up on, trivia which are little tidbits of information usually relating to Japanese culture and people, and hidden tanuki friends who are used to upgrade your ship/mecha the Bunbuku.The graphics are a simple, colorful affair with almost every object and surface stylized to look like a traditional festival. The music is very upbeat with equal amounts of Japanese, western, and synthetic instruments used in its compositions(I particularly like the Okinawa level music). All of this when put together makes for an excellent game that feels like a spiritual successor to the Goemon games but with a fresh coat of paint. The game is fun for all 12 hours it takes to beat(20 to complete), and is well worth the asking price. $40 may seem steep for what some might see as just another indie platformer, but the variety, polish, and, most importantly soul the game has in spades elevate it far beyond being just another modern platformer. Highly recomended.

_childDocuments_.review: I never knew how to feel playing this game. On one hand it’s polished and technically competent, but on the other, it’s just so uninspired in actual gameplay and design. Its moments of inspiration and delight are few and far between; a fleeting moment where you wish you felt this way the entire game. I was always teetering on wanting to play it and being bored at the same time. The only compliments I can think to give the game is sometimes the music is nice and the Japanese theming of the levels are always beautiful and delightful to look at.If you decide to read on, there are gameplay spoilers in this review.You can’t ignore the little elephant in the room: this is a spiritual successor to Konami’s long dormant  franchise, perhaps slightly better known as  outside of Japan. It’s made by Good-Feel, who have been most notably working on products for Nintendo such as  (2010),  (2015), and  (2024). They’re a studio that is technically competent but have always put out bland games with appealing ideas but unappealing execution. Some original staff from Konami who worked on the Goémon series work there and on this title.As a big Goémon fan I was excited to play it, but it just isn’t there. The lead platform was the Nintendo Switch, so the game is graphically unimpressive and is saved by great art direction and design. The essence of Goémon is here in the whimsical and slapstick nature of Japanese mythology and culture, but doesn’t have the twisted edge that Goémon has with innuendo that gives that series its playful dissonance.The game has 65 levels and is stretched thin with barely any memorable content. The first third of the game is a chore because it’s so damn easy, empty, and uninteresting a toddler would yawn. I think they really overestimated how terrible they think gamers are. I can only make the educated guess that this title was designed to be aimed at extremely young players and they were unfortunately given the disdain that they were incapable of being challenged or had no attention spans.The game never reaches its full potential and doesn’t use any of its mechanics effectively. The entire game is uninteresting and flat, sometimes literally. Rarely will you do something engaging that pushes back. I really think half the game should have been axed and the different level elements merged together to provide a higher level of interplay and variety. Your main attack is you have two taiko sticks that you use with L and R bumpers, but the ambidextrous nature of this is never used in any creative way; a single button could have been used. Despite having the ability to jump, ground pound, parry projectiles, sidle, and use various special powers, the game doesn’t do anything to utilize them and even their very game feel is bland. Enemies are fodder and almost everything is just whacking it to death. The level design barely has any verticality or platforming challenges in most stages.There’s literally tens of thousands of ryo to collect to buy things and they only exist in units of one; it’s a grind even with a power-up that temporarily doubles your income. The only thing you buy with them is one time use power-ups, masks that do nothing, and robot upgrades.Each level is padded with five hidden facts, three souvenirs, and some have a hidden tanuki. They slow the game down to give replay value, and getting them doesn’t do anything, except collecting a couple tanuki allows you to unlock robot upgrades. You’d think looking for the hidden tanuki would be fun, but in practice it’s tedious searching for a well hidden object in big levels as you spend huge amounts of time scouring every corner. The yellow poop fact guy, whose name I can't remember, that is hidden in each level has almost the opposite effect being horrendously easy to find. The facts about Japan are genuinely interesting at first, but with 260 them, even they couldn’t keep from running out of steam, devolving into grasping at facts that have no semblance of relevance. The essence of a straightforward run and attack platformer like some of the classic Goémon games is sabotaged with these useless distractions and trinkets to become meandering and unfocused. At times the game made me swear it was funded by Japan’s National Tourism Organization with how on the nose it was with pointing out and praising the distinct locales of Japan and activities in that region.The map is awful. It starts out like a linear pathed game, like the classic Goémon games, and then psyches you out by allowing you to travel anywhere all over Japan in a flying vehicle. The camera never zooms out, you can’t see anything, know where to go, what levels you’ve been to, or what’s been collected in them. You have to go into menus to see what you’ve collected and to use a warp function, but it doesn’t help you quickly locate any level you want to go to. It is easily one of the worst parts of the game.The boss fights are a chore. They come in two flavors: rivals and kaiju. Both varieties are about blunt force and endurance rather than skill or strategy. Defeating rivals gets you one of four permanent transformative power-ups that require spiritual energy you use from defeating common enemies. They're more for show than anything else. You running out of energy to attempt balance makes them tedious to toggle on and off to prevent you from running out.The giant robot levels, which are analogous to Goémon Impact, should have been fun, but you move so damn slow it’s ludicrous. At one point I got stuck on one of the kaiju bosses and couldn’t figure out why the difficulty spiked. Turns out you can upgrade your robot and the game never even tells you! There’s no speed increase though and the battles are monotonous with no strategy, depth, or fun.There’s a couple auto-scroller levels, and the isometric camera absolutely ruins them by obscuring the view and providing unclear boundaries of which will kill you.The game also tries to give variety with racing and schumps stages, but besides being easy, they make you wonder what the point is. The racing isn’t a race. You don’t rank, you can’t lose, you can’t win anything, or if you can, it was next to impossible to know. All you do is get to the end before the extremely gracious time runs out. I mean, the controls and obstacles are fun, but there’s no reason you’d ever want to go back or any challenge to it where you need to improve your skills. Their only purpose is to break up the monotony of the rest of the game.Characters and story are, you guessed it, as interesting as rice gruel. The game left me feeling unsatisfied and I barely managed to get through it. It’s an AA game, but it just doesn’t have that spark of magic Goémon has. In terms of my personal subjective opinion of value, it has enough content that you  justify the price, but the quality of that content is so milquetoast I wouldn’t recommend paying more than $20 max. If you do decide to spend time with it, absolutely do not collect anything except enough tanuki to upgrade your robot.In terms of the PC version, it doesn’t seem to have an arbitrary framerate or resolution cap. It supports 21:9 ultra wide monitors. It looks fine and runs without any stuttering. The antialiasing is limited to FXAA or SMAA and is the biggest weak point with unpleasant aliasing and shimmering that can only be somewhat tamed with nVidia’s DSR feature. Its Nintendo Switch roots means almost anyone should be able to enjoy it on hardware from the last decade if not older.I wanted to like it, and I want Good-Feel to reap the benefits in its talent, but I just can’t be dishonest; I don’t think it’s worth playing unless you’re a rabid Goémon fan who is desperate to relive memories of a forgotten franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Bakeru is something unexpected yet long awaited. In its fullest spirit, it IS a new Legend of the Mystical Ninja / Ganbare Goemon game, right down to the notes in the music, the playfulness, the boss battles, and an atmosphere heavily infused in Japanese culture. The only thing missing is the iconic kabuki "YooooooOHHh!"It isn't a particularly difficult game. Once you learn the patterns, it's naturally gets easy. There are power ups you can buy if you need them. Overall, it's a fun and happy ride with a variety of set pieces. Stages are colorful, vibrant, and full of subtle details in visual and sound design. (Notice the motif of the lens flare when you look up at the sun.) The story is simple and lighthearted. As the hero, you venture across Japan purging the evil that has basically put all of its citizens into a perpetual festival frenzy; everybody won't stop partying, and you gotta find out why. Enemies come in different temperaments; some are aggressive, some mind their own business until you strike first. One fascinating thing noticed is that you can bump into enemies without getting hurt, unless they strike at you.Personally, it was a pleasant hit of nostalgia.  Looking forward to new adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: BAKERU is thoroughly... meh. 11 hours in I am struggling to continue and I know exactly why. The main reason is that this game is extremely repetitive, flat, boring. A series of design decisions make sure that this game kind of ... meh. You know.The main collectibles do nothing. In each level are *five little facts about japan (I am not joking) in form of a character*, *three souvenirs* that the region in Japan which the level takes place in, is "famous". Later you can find a hidden Tanuki that has transformed into some random asset, in some of the levels.I mean that as I wrote it, these collectibles do nothing. You can look at them or read them later, but they do not play into the actual gameplay. They do not provide upgrades or enable new gameplay. The Tanuki help upgrading your ship/transforming mecha. In 11 hours of gameplay I used said mecha ONCE. Now spotting the Tanuki that tranformed into a random Object in a level sounds fun at first but they collide with another problem that this game suffers from.Level design and pacing is just boring. The levels are all linear, which is not a Problem at all, but the spaces between the fun parts are often far to wide and long and constantly break the gameflow. The amount of walking while doing nothing is FAR to high. There is no reason that many of these levels are as expansive as they are. When the game puts in interesting elements they never are used in a fun way. At one point you can turn entire buildings. But its mostly used to make bridges. They use it once or twice so you can bash enemies with that. But there is no sort of urgency to that. You could also just let it be. They try to create Sonic level at one point but even that is completely without bite or energy. Like most of them are. The best levels so far were when the screen was after you and the player had to push forward. Because then they couldn't just stuff wide open levels full with random ♥♥♥♥ and you actually had some pressure and push to the gameplay. The collectibles make this even worse. Because souvenirs and factoids are boring and do nothing it becomes quite unrewarding collecting them. Especially when you have to go off the beaten path down whats basically a just as boring U turn before trekking back to the main path. Finding the Tanuki at first sounds charming until you realize that they used a different asset in every level. They do not tell you beforehand which one it is.  A bush with a tail is easy to spot. Not so with a sun chair in a holiday resort with dozends of other chairs that look mostly the same way. Or with a Umbrella on a beach FULL of umbrellas.Traversing most of the levels gameplay wise is just not fun.I am certain the developers thought that as well. I think this for several reasons. First off, to end a level you have to destroy some specific lanterns to unlock the endpoint of a level, a massive drum. First it were exactly three Lanterns. But in later levels, even the more linear levels, they give you more lanterns to bash then you need. And you can leave levels at any point and do not loose any collectibles or even money from doing so.The games visuals are.. okay. Highlight here are clearly the Character and enemy designs. But no matter the visuals if the game that is made from them is boring then they do not help.Now further on to gameplay. By hour eleven at least you will ahve gathered four special forms that baruka can transform into. The game does nothing with them.One makes you tiny and you can enter small spaces. Its barely used. Two are the same ability, destroying enemies from a distance. One is very fast and so its no problem that the game autoaims for you. The other characters shots are slow and the character is sliding around making it dangerous to use in most cases. Biggest problem here is though the autoaim, which likes to aim at random enemies in view direction of the character, even if the closest enemy is massive and directly in front of you. Useless. The fourth is basically a damage buff that you use whenever there is a horde of annoying enemies that you just want to delete. Combat could be good but for some reason they decided that you need to use two buttons for attacks. Your weapons is drum themed, so the two should triggers are effecting the left and right drim stick respectively. Problem is that it doesn't really work all that well. For starters the game doesn't really attack with the speed you can put in, making it worse that the combos, when you do it successfully, are slower then the standart bash. Additionally it happens frequently that the game doesn't evade/dash or black when you clearly did. I am not sure if some combos lock you in the animations or if the game simply can't keep up with the player. Either way its annoying. You can also charge either the right, the left or both stick, for respectively three different power attacks. They do not use eny energy or charges. So essentially this is how you will delete most enemy groups because it just works the best.This game feels at this point very flawed, very boring and kind of soulless. Which brings us to the Goemon Mystical Ninja comparisons. First we need to make a few things clear. When people bring this up I am thinking of Goemon Mystical Ninja on the N64, the first game.I bring this up because I genuinely think the second game was and is trash. For one it was far less ambitious, 2D, with terrible movement and finicky and inaccurate controls.Secondly I do not think that this game is worse then both of these games. That is just nonsense.But it also doesn't have what Goemon Mystical Ninja has. Incredible charm. A good atmosphere, charm and a certain bite. For example it didn't just throw you into level after level. You start in a small town (which frankly doesn't hold up), you soak in the atmosphere and talk to people about the ridiculous things that just hapened in the intro. It also introduces some really campy villains which are GREAT with a nonsense plan for world domination.11 hours I have gotten one really empty hub, your tea pot ship, and otherwise disconnected levels. Goemon Mystical Ninja also had interesting little and large fun sequences troughout its story driving the plot forward. In baruka I haven't had a conversation with a proper enemy ONCE. We do neither know why the enemies are doing what they are doing nor who the enemy actually is. I have yet to actually meet the big bad or have a conversation that isn't dissapointing. The former game had clichees and stereotypes but it actually did somethig with them that approached telling a story.Most importantly the old game painted a world that was removed enough that it felt new and interesting despite the clearly more modern sensibilities of its inhabitants and characters. The first sequence in Goemon Mystical Ninja is you and your friend fleeing from a shop because your partner thought it was s good idea to unveil his fat body to geta  discount on the shops wares. Baruka just flat out feels like a shallow marketing ploy for Japan then an actual story and world. And that in the worst way. Its extremely sanitized and just boring. It simply does not feel like the developers had a story to tell. The developers have just taken the most recogniceable symbols and elements of japanese culture or its different präfectures, cleaned them of any edges and then made some vaguely motivated levels around them.Its just soulless, there is no spirit behind it, no creative spark besides the main character designs.This is not a good game. It works (technically). But this game has run out of Steam after 11 hours.Not even a week ago I finished The Plucky Squire. That game was linear and done in 10 hours. But every minute was a joy, every five minutes was something new, refreshing and surprising. Not revolutionary but just really fun and energetic and when I was done I felt like I had gotten a complete, satisfying and fun package.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that doesn't do anything brand new, but everything it DOES do is polished to an absolute mirror shine.If you're unaware, Bakeru is a spiritual successor to the Goemon/Mystical Ninja series by the same team that used to work at Konami, and it wears that fact on its sleeve. The anachronistic take on feudal Japan, goofy enemies, and even mech battles: they're all here. However, it's also so much more than that and stands as a unique game in its own right.First off, the controls are fantastic. Insanely responsive and intuitive. Attacking is done with L1/R1, and while that may sound odd at first it works insanely well. Attacking with one button will get you a short combo, but alternating will let you extend your hits indefinitely. You can also hit both buttons at once for a strong attack, or hold them down and release for a charged shockwave. You also get single button charge attacks that will have you perform a dash attack and a spinning attack, which are unlocked automatically early on. Combat rewards quick reaction time: Dodging or blocking at the last moment will let you do follow-up attacks or bounce back projectiles, and your ability to utilize these will be tested more and more as the game goes along.The story itself is goofy and light-hearted. Early on you'll find and fight unique takes on heroes from Japanese folklore, and upon winning you'll receive the ability to use their powers with what the game calls "Henge." There isn't much spoken dialogue, but what is there is Japanese only. I'm someone who normally won't buy games if they don't have a dub track, but this wasn't a dealbreaker for me. The only annoying thing is that there's no subtitles for incidental dialogue such as during boss fights.TL;DR, this game is fantastic and I'd love to see it get a sequel. It also runs fantastic on Steam Deck, hitting consistent 60fps without sucking the battery dry and only the occasional hiccup in busy scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 hour impressions: good!Runs great on Steam Deck. The game was made to run on Switch so the performance is much higher here. When I played docked, 1080p with some momentary drops into the 50's when a lot of enemies are on screen. Otherwise a pretty smooth 60fps, which is a LOT better than the Switch.The game is pretty fun. It's an easy 3D platformer that plays a lot like Kirby and the Forgotten Land, so fairly straightforward and linear levels with a bit of breadth to wander around and look for secrets. There's a good variety to the levels and gameplay, and everything feels good to play. The polish is definitely present - this feels like a game developed by a partner who works with Nintendo often. Note: This is not a clone of Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon on the Nintendo 64. That's a game closer to Zelda. This is much more like Kirby or Mario.The game has a fun silliness to it. It's definitely got a dash of Mystical Ninja for sure, with the cheeky interpretation of ancient and modern Japan. The enemies look very goofy and the setups throughout the levels managed to get a chuckle out of me.Glad I picked this up. It's a lot of fun and I see myself playing through it once in a while. For sure one of the best 3D platformers on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game last week but it has lived rent free in my head ever since. Genuinely couldn't believe how fun this game was!Every level was packed with style and detail and the mechanics felt unique and intuitive. Even the gimmickier levels were enjoyable and never overstayed their welcome. It's really a game that just keeps on building on itself and has plenty of surprises in store for you. The taiko weapon is just brilliant and made every single encounter with an enemy feel fast and engaging with each hit providing satisfying feedback. Yes the game can be a bit easy especially if you use the items and Henge, but there's a decent amount of tech with both your combat and movement that you'll find a surprising amount of player expression in here. I know this game will lend itself quite nicely to speedruns! I'm already having a blast replaying levels to track down the collectibles or challenging the bosses again to get those No damage/No Henge achievements. I also love how most of the levels are based on the different prefectures in Japan and the souvenirs you collect are often inspired by things that prefecture is known for. I had a ton of fun trying to guess what souvenirs I would find in each level based on my own knowledge of some of these areas. The weird fun facts you get from Scoop were cute and presented in a hilarious manner so I recommend trying to find as many as you can. This whole game feels like a passion project and will go down as a modern day classic for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to be the first review of this game and give it a not recommend, but frankly there is no "there" here.While it appears to be like a spiritual successor to the "Legend of the Mystical Ninja" series, it is not.  Not even slightly.  World map reminds me a lot of "Goemon's Great Adventure" for the n64, but that's about as far as it goes.The game is a surface-level pastiche of every major Japanese video game series since the 1980's, interspersed with what seems to be either a tourism bureau travelogue of Japan or teach gen alpha kids about Japanese culture.The game feels like if Super Mario 3d World was on the playstation but had a Gamecube-era art style with a PS2 game's cramped and labyrinthine world design.  Controls feel like Kingdom Hearts mixed with a rhythm game.  There's some Klonoa and Ape Escape mixed in there too, but like I said this game is just a series of references loosely strung around a tourism advertisement.VERY awkward controls.  Left and right bumper to attack (which you have to alternate to attack quicker), a generous "perfect guard" reflect system like the Jedi series on the right trigger, a perfect dodge system like a number of Platinum games have on the X button (that you can hold to sprint), a limited jump on the A button (that you can press after a dodge to do a Mario long-jump), and the left trigger lets you switch between transformation forms that feel like various famous characters from games past.  It's really hard to pull of the button combos the game wants you to do and have it feel natural.  You can change the controls to your liking in the settings, but I'm not quite sure what a better layout than the original would be considering you HAVE to alternate left and right hand attacks.Each of the game's levels have 8 collectables.Three collectibles per stage are gacha capsules stuffed with foods popular in Japan or local produce.  You get a travelogue blurb about each.Five collectibles per stage involve you looking in out of the way areas for a "scholar" dressed like a pile of golden poop (no really) who is named "Scoop," and he gives you trivia about life in Japan.  Some of the trivia isn't even Japan specific, so that just feels low effort.The whole experience feels so unpolished, rushed, and low budget.  It's more of a tourism appetizer than a game.Nothing like Goemon.  The main character doesn't even look like Goemon outside of promo images.From the collectibles list it's short, only having slots for 12 levels.  Some people say there are 50 levels, but since you can beat each level in minutes it's still not all that long even with this "quantity over quality" approach.Game's story is explicitly under the impression you are a native Japanese child, but the collectibles seem geared towards getting Western adults to visit Japan (some of them are even a bit vulgar).Game's difficulty is tuned to be playable by VERY young children.I'm not sure who this is for, and to be honest I don't think the developers did either.---Edit to answer criticism this review is getting:I got my experiences from playing the actual game, seeing what it really is, then refunding.  The promo art is manipulative to make you think this is a "legend of the mystical ninja" sequel when it isn't even slightly, the main character doesn't even slightly look like goemon in game.I get you want to relive your childhood, I get you want some Hope in your lives, I get you think you can get it out of a corporate cash-in to boost tourism interest in Japan, but just no.  THIS ISN'T IT!If someone wants to pretend like a level select menu of an isometric view of japan, with cartoonish pop-up standees is either unique to goemon's great adventure or a substantive connection enough to declare this as "the return of goemon" then have at it.As for negative reviews being more common these days if every game available to day is pure slop then how is that on me for warning people?  I know you want to "feel something" and "belong" and so fall for marketing, and steam wants money, but these games I give bad reviews to are not only a drain on your funds but on your life too.It just isn't fun.  Even if there are 50 levels, the ones there just have no meat or enjoyment to them.  The bulk of the game is literally searching for a man dressed like poop to hear travelogue blurbs about Japan.I'm also not interested in partaking in blatant tourism bait or worse.  This game feels like it need to disclose some government funding with how obvious the messaging is.Awkward controls, exploitative game design ("hey, remember this game from your childhood that this plays nothing like!"), exploitative messaging.Just no.If I wanted hundreds of rewards and to have my review go viral, I would have lied and said the game is great not only to please the cognitive dissonance of the hype brigade but have steam boost my review so they could get their 30% cut off of sales.  I decided to tell The Truth instead.This is not worth the cost of money at $36, not worth the cost of time even if it was $10, and certainly not worth the cost of your Dignity and sanity just to defend it because you fell for marketing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and colorful game! Yes it's made by the people that did the older goemon/mystical ninja games(which i loved), and even thought it definitely share alot of the same spirit, it still feel like it's own thing. The stage are numerous, colorful and quite varried, the music is quite peppy, the collectibles are almost all optional but you'll still hunt them down because it's just fun to do, and the gameplay mix platforming and fighting real well. It's still mostly an easy game, but not TOO easy and the game is quite long without feeling bloated. It's simply really fun to play. It remind me alot of the PS2/Gamecube era in the way it's all designed and feel like, definitely a good thing.Definitely worth being given a chance, as long as you don't expect the hardest game ever, it will definitely give you a fun and happy time, and i hope it's not the last we see of that tanuki!
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was developed by Nintendo in a very good way. I grew up as a big fan of platforming mascot style games like Mario, and Sonic and this game reminds me of those. Good platformers seem to be few and far between nowadays and Bakeru has that Japanese quirkiness, happy music, and great gameplay mechanics the genre was known for. There are yellow turds that give you little trivia knowledge that you explore levels to search for! Not many games can say that. If you are a fan of old school platformers, this is a definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Bakeru is the best game I've played all year. There's so much content that it should really be full-price.Positives:+ The overall game design keeps throwing mechanic after mechanic at you, consistently subverting expectations. For example, you'll spend the first few hours on a linear world map until getting a ship, allowing you to choose between many levels at a time.+ Several levels are top-tier in terms of design, sometimes reaching Nintendo-quality.+ Optimization is CRAZY good. I've been able to maintain 60fps with default settings almost 100% of the time with a GTX 1050Ti & i5-7400.+ The music in particular just slaps.+ There's modulated difficulty. If you're struggling, you can choose to upgrade your health, buy items, use Henge abilities, etc. However, if you're looking for a challenging experience (like me), you can ignore everything. As a matter of fact, there are achievements for defeating bosses without using Henge at all.+ Combat feels good. Having two attack buttons to experiment with is a lot of fun.+ Love the unique scoop and tanuki collectibles.+ Bosses are varied and engaging.Critiques (both small and large):- There are many misleading invisible walls, meaning it can sometimes be difficult to determine what's a boundary or what's traversable. I get why this was done, but figuring out that fences are just barriers in disguise threw me off for awhile.- Enemy hit detection can be strange at times. For example, I've been hit by an enemy attack despite being behind them- Momotaro's Henge ability (shooters) could have been utilized better. There are very few situations in the game where you're forced to use long-ranged combat. Even then, I think Urashima's Henge ability (fishing rods) does a better job clearing out enemies from a distance.- The racing and dog fight levels, while a fun distraction at first, got repetitive for me. I think they should have been contained within normal levels.- I wish there was one last robot fight during Act III.- The default controller scheme doesn't let you dash and turn the camera at the same time. Therefore I recommend mapping dash / dodge to one of the triggers, and mapping Henge to L3 / R3. Thankfully, speed items (almost) eliminate the need to dash at all.- Your RB + LB charge attack has a height limit, meaning you can't stomp on enemies from a large cliff.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Really great action platformer. Reminds me of Sony PS2 3D action platformers and that is a really good thing. Super fun combat, really great art/graphics. It has the best collectibles I have ever seen in a game which are these fun facts that you collect throughout the stage. No bugs or technical issues. Just a great fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute treat for those who love the Ganbare Goemon franchise and wish deeply for more.To be more clear, it's aesthetic is delightfully on par with that of Goemon. It's gameplay however is something of an amalgam of Ape Escape and Mario Sunshine. it blends interesting platforming and serviceable combat together in incredibly beautiful stages, each hand tailored to a theme of each prefecture of Japan. The variety of the world types and enemies is a smidge lacking, mind. As well as the options Bakeru has for combat and platforming as a whole. It feels like a game that has played it a little safer than it needed too, and comes across on the much to easy side. Never mind the lack of use in exploration and platforming most of his 'Hinge' transformations give. It's very easy to complete the game without ever having used any Hinge besides Issun.Overall, the complaints I have spring entirely from a desire for more! Because the world and characters are all great. The style of each level is amazing. The trivia and souvenir, as well as the hidden Tanuki give levels a wonderful level of exploration and allows you to take in the sights, as it encourages you to look at everything the developers placed in each level. Hell, the movement tech thats here and zippy snappy nature of Bakeru makes this game unironically an excellent speedrunners game!! I look forward to trying to in the future!There is so much to explore and it makes me long for a sequel already, one with improved exploration, platforming and combat options. Genuinely a wonderful game that I feel everyone should play! And I'm gladder that it even exists in the West!Plz Good-Feel, next time, give the Hinge puzzle abilities! I literally never used Urashima Taro! It was a perfect excuse for a grappling hook!10/10 I needed a fishing rod grappling hook.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: An absurdly charming game. I already played through this on the switch when it initially came out, so seeing it run at a smooth frame rate with little to no dips is amazing. If you're into 3d platformers with a little bit of action, I'd encourage you to check this out. It's not reinventing the wheel or anything but it's still a good time. Though my biggest problem with this game is that there isn't much to do outside the main story. Even if you're a completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, if a bit overstuffed, 3D platformer. Love the music, the trivia you get as a reward for collectibles, and the use of Japanese geography in the aesthetics of the levels. Not a huge fan of the level design, which bounces between Nintendo quality and the Demon Ruins from DS1... just big open spaces with enemies scattered around. Wish the game were shorter and tighter, but I loved Goemon and I love this. It's just very comforting.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: We are blessed to have this appear out of nowhere. Originally a japanese-only, criminally underrated revival of Goemon, now localized and on Steam. This game feels like if the 3D Goemon games stayed in development and were then influenced by more modern platformers like Mario Odyssey and Kirby and the Forgotten Land. Every level has its own graphical distinction and gameplay elements, but you will spend a lot of time breaking open, collecting, and brawling things. Bakeru maintains the heart and wacky fun of its Konami-abandoned inspiration. There is a lot of national pride within this game, as it fully embraces the Japan setting.Playing this on my steam deck, I get what feels to be a smooth 60 fps even with high graphics. By comparison, I played the switch version that was 30 fps and flakey. A no-brainer for anyone wanting a showcase steam deck game. Or if you miss the dying art of 3D platformers. Sleeper hit I suspect.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Bakeru is an amazing successor to Konami's abandoned Goemon series. The levels are brimming with personality down to the placements of enemies, and the character designs are wonderful. The simple action gameplay is easy enough to understand and the punishment for death is light, but still provides enough of a challenge to keep players engaged. My only real concern is that this game, like Goemon, will fly under the radar for most gamers; it's absolutely worth buying, especially if you have even a passing interest in Japanese culture.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit of a throwback to the older days of 3d platformer/action games in a good way. If you loved Mario 64 and Ganbare Goemon, this game will definitely scratch that itch. Combat is a bit simple but the environments are lovely and the game is just a lot of fun. For a while there, I didn't think this game would be localized, but I'm so glad it finally was. It deserves a lot more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: A colorful and fun 3D action platformer inspired by Mystical Ninja Goemon games. This game is made by the people that made Kirby's Epic Yarn and Yoshi's Wooly World. The game design, level progression, item collecting is very similar to Super Mario 3D World.Your platforming actions are pretty simple: roll, dash, jump and ledge grab. Combat on the other hand has quite a bit of variety of actions. You have two attack buttons, each one makes Bakeru swing his arm based on which button you press. You can string them together to form a combo that also have decent lunging distance. You can also press both buttons to swing them both at the same time for double damage. You can also charge your attacks. Charging the left swing will give you a spinning attack that hits multiple times, the right swing will give you a huge lunging attack, and both will give you a huge aoe attack. You also have some defensive options: dodge roll and guard. Both of them also have perfect timings. Perfect dodge roll can be followed up with a lunge attack that will stagger. Perfect guard will stagger and can reflect projectiles.Bakeru also have access to transformations as you progress the game. These will change your offensive actions but they drain the transformation meter in the process.Each stage requires you to pop at least 3 huge lanterns to clear the stage. Luckily there are more than 3 lanterns so you don't have to worry too much about missing one in the stage. This game has a far bit of collectibles per stage: 5 trivia and 3 souvenirs. Some stages also have a tanuki to collect and they're a bit harder to spot due their attempt to blend in the stage by transforming into random objects.The stages are very colorful and have a lot of fun ideas within it. There are also a few racing stages and shoot them up stages but they're very few and very simple.The music is alright, there isn't that much but it fits the stages well.There are two types of bosses you fight in the game: a standard one where you control Bakeru, and a mech battle. The mech battles can take a bit to get used to.You can buy mask to wear and they are all very weird looking, fits the theme of the game.The game is overall on the easier side. There is no life count, you just lose money instead. To aid the player even further you have access to various items in the shop like attack up, speed up, revive when your hp hits 0, etc.This game is on the shorter side, about 15 hours for 100%. It feels really long though due to the amount of searching around during a level considering you have 8-9 collectibles per level.This is a very well made game. I very much enjoyed the game. This game is chill, comfy, and good time.
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: The game goes hand in hand with Okami for me, though they are different gameplays, they're similar in the inspirations they call upon within Japanese folklore and make it their own experience whilst always maintaining that wafuu sense of traditionalism into video gaming.Now take the above and add in a lot of 3D Mario inspired gameplay and you've got Bakeru!The game is labelled as Goemon's spiritual successor but I haven't played that one so can't really tell how similar it would be but can definitely see the same passion and energy there onto this.Bakeru is a level based game with lots of platforming and hack 'n slash boss fighting adventuring alongside the occasional racing.Each level has a set amount of secrets for you to find and if you miss any, you can always replay levels.In a way, the way in which the level design is done is more or less a feature of Japan as a whole in advertising the local specialties of each location set and there are no same sceneries throughout the whole adventure, making it an extremely fun experience of which places do not get tiring to go through.I got to a point within the game where you can find your souvenir collectables set out and thought I had played quite a lot of the game already but to my surprise when seeing all the blank spaces for the future souvenirs, there was a whole lot of empty space.This game is a lot longer than I thought it would be and that's nice 'cause it shows the developers really did put a lot into the game and there will be more things for me to see and enjoy too from what more things each level brings to the table but also makes this game worth the price, even if I got this on sale ahahah
_childDocuments_.name: BAKERU

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, looked forward to playing it each session I started it up. Got a little repetitive near the end, but the level design was good enough I didn't really mind. Good music, good level design, combat and enemy design felt good despite be relatively simple. The robot battles felt a little forgettable, mostly feeling like they exist for the sake of being similar to goemon with most be slow and pretty easy, but they're a small portion of the game and it was still nice to break up the normal gameplay along with the Browsby sections.
