_childDocuments_.review: I've played all AC titles (including the spinoff titles) and this is the first game that I have refunded throughout my 9+ years of Steam usage.Reasons:- Extremely clunky mechanics and traversal- Abhorrent voice acting so much so that I think the VAs are being underpaid- Feels like the game forces us to 'grow into' Basim by shoving what little excuse they had for a backstory. - Inorganic way to introduce the brotherhood, again it feels forced and lacks proper buildup. Anecdotally it's like being served a dessert before the main course; the excitement is there but somehow you can't help but feel something is missing. - I'm not even 2 hours into the game and Basim is already a full-fledged assassin. His training, his ideological shift, and his general process is not shown, which makes this very unrewarding and undeserved. - The game attempts to use 'easier cheat ways' to cater the buildup, such as subtle references to AC Odyssey and Origins. Unfortunately this does not work and just adds clutter- Overall mid story, both tedious and rushed, both at the wrong times.- Off-putting and clunky combat. Doesn't tick the 'old school' style they're gunning for, yet also doesn't hit the RPG-like style which many people were accustomed to. Hence the combat lacks depth and character- Partial ultrawide support. By this I mean that cutscenes are pre-rendered to be 16:9 and even dialogues (that are supposed to be rendered real-time) are confined to be 16:9Please for the love of God do not buy this game. This is coming from me who can tolerate the constant crashes and tedious repetitiveness of AC Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is like trying to make the best Lego construction by using playmobil. Utter compromised abomination. The main concept of Mirage is a "go back to roots" homage to the first Assassin's games, where the stealth and not the combat was the main focus of the game. However, they made it with ANVIL engine, an engine that is so animation based, that it all breaks apart in the first thirty minutes. Anvil is all about the animation and the spectacle, but lacks in precision. That could work with Odyssey and Valhalla where the combat was the main focus, but in Mirage where you want maximum precision in stealth and parkour it breaks badly. So you will have the clunky controls, falling through gaps, get stuck in the geometry, missing grabs, abruptly changing direction, missing the cover because the movement animation got you exposed and the lack of cover/corner mechanics. The battle (which the engine was made for) is bad, because it isn't the target of the game. So you have a game that could do battle well, but never does, and that does stealth badly but is all it wants to do. The story is mediocre, is too fast and too thin, mostly because it was supposed to be an expansion and not a full game. Once again, the lack of direction in narrative terms is obvious since, as many reviewer put it, the structure dictates the story and not the story that dictates the structure. The road to Hell is paved with good intentions. And this game has good intentions. But then Ubisoft being Ubisoft kicked in and produced this compromised abomination of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm disappointed in the game's playability one year after its release. The game has a lot of bugs that just make it extremely frustrating to play. These bugs would be priority 1 issues right after release, but here we are one year later, releasing on Steam with these issues.The bugs that are the most frustrating are the ones that you have a clear intention to do an action but the game decides to do something that ruins the entire situation. For example, when free running and climbing, you will often get sucked into a pole like you are magnetically attracted to it, you cannot climb it, if you try it will do the run up the pole then fall back down animation, you try to get around it but it sucks you back in... You will try to run up short walls, but if they have anything on them it will be an invalid action again stopping you dead in your tracks. You will even get turned around sometimes due to it sucking you into an action you had no intention of doing. Running near anything you can hide in will automatically suck you in even if you are in chase, in which case it auto ejects you out, but sometimes will get you stuck in a loop where you can't get away from it, and you just hop in and out while your enemies catch you.If that wasn't bad enough, half the time you go to assassinate someone, you have to worry about the game bugging out and making you attack with your sword instead. Coming out of a bush to assassinate the enemy has the prompt: you press it, they get too close, swing the sword, and now you are in combat and no longer stealthy. This happens so much it defeats the purpose of a stealth game. I am not talking about the game mechanic where you are detected, and an enemy intercepts your attempt. I am talking about you being in full stealth in a bush, and you get a guard to come over, and you go for the stealth kill and, uh oh, sword...These are the two most egregious bugs that make the game unplayable. I gave it a good try, but even nine hours in, so many of my plans have been ruined by these game-breaking bugs that it's more frustrating than anything to try and play.If you still aren't convinced, let's talk about the enemy AI. You can kill every guard in full view of everyone with throwing knives, and they don't even so much as try to find you. They get stuck in sitting-down and standing-up loops and trip over things in their path, which is funny the first time you see it, but then you realize it's going to happen a lot throughout the game. The enemy AI in this game is, for lack of a better word, just terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was first thought as a Valhalla DLC, and you notice that a bit over the game.Finally back to being an Assassin protagonist, this follows the origin story of Basim, a character first introduced in Valhalla. If you played Valhalla, you'll know why this matters.Visually the game does not bring anything different from Valhalla. Its pretty, but doesn't break any graphical ground.But the city is beautiful...it has a lot of life added to it, lots of little details. Just navigating around with Basim's parkour is almost therapeutical.Gameplay wise, you will see a lot of animations from Valhalla, but Basim is more agile, faster, having less armor also contributes to that. More parkour options, faster transversal navigation, makes you think of earlier AC games.The focus on Stealth is the big plus for me, personally. I've played all AC games with a stealth approach, even if the game forces or punishes you not to. One hit assassinations, the stealth animations and focus on all missions are very enticing and I loved this aspect of the game.I was hoping the game would have a more Unity/Syndicate like type of parkour and stealth (gameplay pinnacle of the franchise for me). Even though it wasn't, it was still a clear improvement from Odyssey and Valhalla.The only downside to it is the dumb AI. Even on Master Assassin and Permadeath, the AI is very easy to counter. I wish it presented a higher challenge.The game is noticeably smaller, which is at the same time a pro and a con.Pro because the story is more focused, there is less filler. You still have side content, but there's less filler activities for no reason to the overall arc, which made Odyssey and Valhalla feel like such a chore to finish...Con because it makes the game a lot smaller, taking less than 20 hours to finish it. At the same time, due to that, the original price tag was quite lower than usual for Ubisoft games, and adequate for the content.I've paid 70-80€ for 8 hours games...The story itself is not groundbreaking, but the focus on the Creed, overall conflict between Assassins and Templars, and Basim's background/transformation make it quite engaging and interesting. Considering the game is overall smaller, story focused and with less filler, makes for an overall better experience.Ubisoft is currently suffering from their own creative decisions from past years, but the internet is unable to distinguish a good game from a bad game, simply spreading hate towards anything that brings Ubisoft's name into it. That is quite obvious in most Negative reviews even here on this platform.The game is not groundbreaking, but it is quite good. I've played this game on Xbox, PS5 and now on PC, without a single regret. Even though I'm quite biased when it comes to Assassins Creed games (my personal favorite franchise), this particular entry does not deserve most of the hate it is being targeted with and for  people not influenced by trolls and haters, should give this game a go.I had high hopes for Mirage and even though it did not fully deliver on them, its still my favorite entry since Origins. Summing up all platforms, I probably have 60-70 hours on this game, and loved every minute of it.On sale, totally worth the 25€.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished Assassin's Creed Mirage on Ubisoft's launcher via a friend's account, and it was a big letdown. After Assassin's Creed Odyssey, which was their last great AAA game, Ubisoft's games have not been good. They keep putting out games with little to no effort, except for two amazing games such as Immortals Fenyx Rising and Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown. But most of their recent games, like Assassin's Creed Valhalla, Riders Republic, Ghost Recon, XDefiant, Skull and Bones, Far Cry 5 & 6, Motorfest, Avatar, and Star Wars Outlaws have all been really disappointing.Sadly, Mirage is another one of these games. It feels sloppy and rushed, with not much to offer. Here's why:The story in Mirage is simply terrible. The cutscenes look cheap, the facial animations are stiff, the dialogue is boring, and the whole story is not interesting at all. The characters don’t have any originality, and the plot is too simple. It feels like Ubisoft didn't even bother to make the story good. Everything about it is lazy and soulless.The action in Mirage is shockingly bad. There are literally only two types of enemies in the game. The combat is very basic and bland. Upgrades, like gear and skill trees, are shallow. Combat is extremely repetitive, and it wears out in the first hour. The parkour is decent. The movement feels okay, but the animations are way dated. It’s nowhere near as good as it was in Unity. In fact, since Unity, no Assassin's Creed game has had parkour that felt as even closely satisfying.I have to give credit to Ubisoft for their environmental design. They are god-tier at creating beautiful cities. I have always loved exploring the different cities in each Assassin's Creed game; that’s literally the main reason I enjoy the series and that's the only reason I will be replaying Mirage. I love looking at the amazing job Ubisoft pulls with their worlds.In Mirage, needless to say; the city is stunning. Graphically, Mirage is very good, and the art and visual design elevate the experience. But the open world still feels bland and lifeless, like in most of the series. NPCs just walk around, and there’s nothing interesting to interact with. There’s no exploration value; the world feels empty. It’s really just there to place parkour paths for you to use. The world doesn’t feel alive or immersive, even though it looks very pretty.The game design is the same thing Ubisoft has been doing since Far Cry 3. It’s full of repetitive tasks, side activities, and level design that they keep reusing. But unlike some older games, Mirage doesn’t do anything to make the repetitive design more enjoyable. The level design is okay, better than Valhalla, but still not that good. It works for stealth, but it doesn’t matter much because the AI is so dumb that there’s no real challenge.Assassin's Creed Mirage is another disappointing game in the series. It is a quick cash grab, made to get money from the old Assassin's Creed fans who don’t like the new RPG style. Ubisoft had to release this game instead of waiting and making something good. It’s clear they didn’t want to go five years without a new Assassin's Creed game, so they put out a low-effort title to keep the series going, which is a shame.To sum it up: The good parts of the game are the environmental design, which is still top-notch, the music, and the game length, which is about 15 hours. While this is short among the newer Assassin's Creed games, it feels just right after the long and torturous experience of 80 hours of Valhalla. I want to thank Ubisoft for at least bringing their games back to Steam on day one. That’s a good move, and I hope they keep doing it. But I also hope they start making more games like Immortals Fenyx Rising and Prince of Persia The Lost Crown. Those were really good and showed what Ubisoft can do when they try. I want their big AAA games to match the quality of those titles. Ubisoft still has time to bring their games back to what made them great, but they need to focus on quality, not just quantity.Follow My

_childDocuments_.review: Completed on Ubisoft Connect. I thoroughly enjoyed the exploration aspect of Assassin's Creed Mirage, particularly the world design. 9th-century Baghdad is a stunning and captivating setting. As always with the Assassin's Creed series, wandering through the world is an absolute pleasure. The integration of historical points is very interesting, and I found the codex to be a great companion in that regard, adding context and depth to the experience.On the gameplay side, there’s a focus on investigation when planning your assassinations. On the hardest difficulty, which I recommend, stealth is crucial, and avoiding direct combat becomes key. The sneaky approach makes you feel less like a powerful warrior and more like a cunning thief, which suits the game’s tone really well. As you unlock perks, Basim becomes noticeably more adept at handling difficult situations, though combat remains a risky endeavor. While some might call Mirage a return to the series’ roots, I see it more as a condensed version of Valhalla, but with a heavier emphasis on stealth and a more streamlined scope. This actually works to the game’s advantage, keeping things focused and tight.Performance-wise, the game ran smoothly on my end with no bugs that I can recall. The only issue I faced was some noticeable chromatic aberration at launch, but thankfully, that’s now something you can turn off and NG+ has been added.It’s always great to see Ubisoft bringing their games back to Steam. Mirage was a good experience, and I'm looking forward to future releases — especially if they launch on Steam at the same time as on other platforms./!\ Assassin's Creed Mirage is great on Steam Deck, maintaining a stable 45FPS on medium settings. However, there's a significant caveat here, since it requires Ubisoft Connect, you'll need a constant internet connection to play. Furthermore, whenever Ubisoft updates its launcher, it can temporarily break all Ubisoft games on Steam Deck until Proton gets patched. "GOLD" on ProtonDB.

_childDocuments_.review: Was iffy on getting this, it being a Ubisoft PC port, but happy to report it's excellent so far (a couple of missions into Baghdad). I've played every other game in the series, including the most recent trilogy, and this so far seems like the best possible result of all the experiments in gameplay mechanics that they've been bouncing around for years.From the moment I got the first quest that was essentially "Here's the guy you need, he's in This General Area, get to work!" I was sold. The investigation system and incentives for lower level street interaction (pickpocketing, etc.) are super interesting, and with my first playthrough on the hardest difficulty, combat so far is a pain, which it should be - getting war flashbacks to the parry timings from AC1.I haven't finished it yet, but I do know this game is short -  I got it at the 50% off rate for the Steam launch, and so far I think that's perfectly fair for the amount of content I expect to play, however as an AC oldhead I'd have honestly bought it outright if money allowed. Don't let the chuds scare you off of a good experience - watch some gameplay, see what you think, and grab Mirage if you liked the more methodical approach of the first game from back in the day!Edit: Forgot to mention - this game does run Denuvo, which normally would be a pretty serious problem, but by some miracle it runs better than even the older games in the series. My main rig died and I've yet to replace it, so I'm playing this on an FX-8320 and an RX580 at time of writing, and after some tweaking it runs smoothly around 45FPS. Throw in some scaling and I'm at a nearly locked 60, with imperceptible input lag, on hardware from 2011 - shoutout to the optimization team who apparently can do magic.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirage is... okay, I guess. It's certainly playable, but IMO it is by far the weakest entry in the series (barring Valhalla which I personally have not played nor have any interest in playing).AC Mirage does its job of scratching that Assassin's Creed itch. The gameplay works, and I think the soundtrack is great. If you want an entry point into the series, Mirage is not a bad starting point. But if you're an AC fan, I think Mirage appeals to neither fans of the old nor new eras.Where do I even begin? Mirage feels more like a checklist than a game that I would actually call fun. Missions are more or less the same; with the main differentiating factor being the confusing level design. I spent nearly an hour in one particular mission running around inside a prison looking for a way to get to the bottom floors, and ended up having to look up a YouTube video to find out where to go next. Turns out, the entrance to get to the bottom floors was stupidly in a hole in the wall located ABOVE me.And then there's the famous collect-athon bloat that we know well from other AC games, only the collectibles in this one don't even reward you with anything good. The actual good equipment in this game are locked behind paid DLCs, but that's Ubisoft for you.Something everyone keeps talking about is how Mirage is the return of AC to its stealth and parkour roots. And I would say... no? AC Mirage tries to combine elements of the Origins-Odyssey-Valhalla era with dated and clunky parkour mechanics not seen since AC1. The result being a game that manages to be worse than both Odyssey AND Syndicate. Basim runs around like he's wearing weighted shoes, and he frequently struggles to even go up tiny ledges. We also see the return of the "sticky walls" from the earlier AC games, where Basim gets stuck to walls and can neither climb nor drop down. Ubisoft fixed this in Unity, so what the hell happened?? It's also absolutely laughable that Basim cannot jump over ledges if they are just so slightly curved. A simple jump button would've really helped.Stealth is the same as it's always been since the first game. Stand in crowds or crouch in bushes, and you're completely invisible. And I mean completely invisible. You can yoink enemies into bushes while in full view of other soldiers, and you'd still be invisible to them. Enemy AI has also not improved and is as dumb as ever. I could literally dissolve an enemy with a throwing knife, and the guy standing right next to him would just go "SoMEonE tHrowinG sOmEthING?" and shortly go back to idling around like nothing happened. You can eliminate massive groups of enemies by doing this repeatedly.Assassinations are also so unsatisfying. Everything just feels off-sync, slow. and stiff. And the so-called "chain assassinations" that you unlock is literally just performing the same assassination animation twice. Assassinations in AC1 genuinely look and feel better, just look up video comparisons of it.Then we have sword combat which can be summed up as parrying until your target's parry bar is depleted, followed by an assassination. Basim is easily the worst swordsman when compared to the other protagonists in the series.I have never been this uninterested in an AC story. I thought Altair was pretty boring in the 1st game, but Basim here is utterly forgettable. It's a generic story of a street thief who gets "saved" and discovered by the Assassins, and goes on to investigate and kill the Templars. The guy has got very little personality, and it would've been so much better if Bayek from Origins returned instead. Not one of the characters in this game felt original or interesting in any way.To be clear, I don't think Mirage is a "bad" game. It does work, and newbies to the franchise might enjoy it. However, I cannot recommend this game because I don't think anyone would be missing out by skipping it. If you REALLY do want to play Mirage, then get it when it's at least -70% off, because there is absolutely nothing in this game that merits getting it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Assassin’s Creed Mirage feels like getting dropped into a history class taught by a parkour instructor. Imagine being at the peak of a minaret, gazing at the sprawling city of Baghdad, only to miss your jump and land directly in a pile of angry guards. Classic me.The game's setting? Gorgeous. It's like walking into a postcard of ancient Baghdad—if postcards had hidden blades and rooftop chases. Seriously, every time I climb a tower, I half expect someone to sell me magic carpets or falafel (though I’d settle for some decent fast travel).Basim, the protagonist, has mastered the art of stealth, which in my hands usually means "run at enemies with knives and hope for the best." The man has more tricks up his sleeve than a street magician—throwing knives, smoke bombs, even the ability to blend into crowds with the subtlety of someone who totally wasn’t just seen jumping off a 40-foot wall.Combat is like a graceful dance of death, but if you, like me, lack grace, it’s more like a clumsy tango of trying to block while screaming at the camera angles. The sound of enemies repeatedly shouting "there he is!" as I get caught for the tenth time is basically the background music of my life now.Stealth missions? Nail-biting. And by nail-biting, I mean that I inevitably mess up and get caught halfway through, leading to frantic rooftop sprints that make Baghdad look like the set of Mission: Impossible—if Tom Cruise had really, really bad luck.In conclusion, Assassin’s Creed Mirage is like finding yourself in the middle of an ancient thriller, but with a lot more yelling at guards who somehow see through my perfect hiding spots (a bush totally counts, right?). If you’ve ever wanted to parkour through history and make a lot of people very upset along the way, this is the game for you.Now if you'll excuse me, I have a tower to leap from… with style, obviously

_childDocuments_.review: Assassin's Creed Mirage is a game that resonates deeply with me, drawing me back to the roots of the series while seamlessly integrating essential elements from more recent RPG installments. This balance of classic gameplay and modern mechanics makes it a standout experience, particularly for long-time fans like myself who yearn for the essence of the earlier titles.From the moment I started playing, it was clear that Mirage was a love letter to the original Assassin's Creed experience. The game recaptures the sense of stealth, exploration, and freedom that characterized the early adventures of Altair and Ezio. However, it doesn’t shy away from incorporating the more refined systems of recent titles. The game effectively trims the excesses often found in open-world RPGs, allowing players to dive straight into the core narrative without the need to invest hundreds of hours. The main story is concise and impactful, ensuring that every mission feels purposeful and engaging.One of the game's greatest strengths lies in its structure. The pacing is excellent, allowing players to experience a compelling narrative without the usual grind that can sometimes plague the genre. I found myself engrossed in the story from start to finish, appreciating how the game respects my time while still delivering a rich and fulfilling journey. This focused approach makes it accessible for both newcomers and series veterans.At the heart of Assassin's Creed Mirage is Basim, the protagonist whose journey is both thrilling and emotionally resonant. The depth of his character development drew me in, and I quickly found myself forming a strong attachment to him. His struggles, ambitions, and moral dilemmas evoke a sense of empathy that mirrors the emotional connection I felt with Ezio in his own saga. The narrative explores themes of identity and belonging, making Basim's story not just about revenge or conflict, but about the search for self amid chaos.The game excels in its storytelling, with beautifully crafted cutscenes and dialogues that enrich Basim's character and his relationships with those around him. I often found myself reflecting on his choices and the consequences that followed, which only deepened my investment in his journey. In many ways, Basim feels like a modern-day Ezio, embodying the spirit of the Assassin's Creed legacy while carving out his own path.In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Mirage is a remarkable addition to the franchise. It honors the essence of what made the series great, while also incorporating the best elements from recent games. The tight, focused narrative and the emotional depth of Basim's story make this game not just a nostalgic trip, but a fresh and impactful experience. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone looking to relive the magic of the earlier Assassin's Creed games, while still enjoying the advancements of modern gaming. For me, it’s not just a game; it’s a journey that has left a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirage, the latest game in Ubisoft's iconic Assassin's Creed performance, takes players to 9th century Baghdad. This game is true to the series' roots and brings classic elements back to the forefront.Assassin's Creed Mirage tells the story of Basim, a young thief. While living an ordinary life, Basim meets assassins after a murder and decides to follow their path. The game focuses on the basics of the character, examining Basim's motivations and personal struggles in detail. The story offers a rich narrative by blending both historical events and elements.Mirage offers an open world design like in classic Assassin's Creed games. Missions are designed to offer players a stealth (stealth) focused experience. It prioritizes elements such as escaping from enemies, stealth killing and using the environment. The game has a more mission-oriented structure, with RPG details from previous installments of the series.The game draws attention with its detailed graphics that successfully reflect the historical texture of Baghdad. The city welcomes players with its rich architecture, crowded markets and fascinating atmosphere. The sound design is also quite successful; Arabic music and sparkles, the emergence of the player's game are more present.Mirage offers a smooth experience especially on new generation consoles. Loading processes are short and technical glitches are minimal. This offers players an uninterrupted adventure.Assassin's Creed Mirage offers a nostalgic experience for fans of the series, while offering an impressive story and gameplay to new players. Bringing back classic elements while also considering modern game dynamics makes the game both superior and traditional. In general, Mirage stands out as one of the most successful and exciting games in Assassin's Creed performance.

Even the first Assassin's Creed game offered a more engaging and fun combat experience with cooler animations. The parkour system, which should have been improved to provide a more fluid and dynamic experience, remains stagnant. Instead of the exhilarating parkour seen in Assassin's Creed Unity, that's what I expected to see in this game, the parkour mechanics are disappointingly similar to those in Valhalla, lacking speed and movement.The story feels cheap and uninspired again. I ask myself are there any consequences from the past what happend in other assassins creeds, I mean where is the sense of all of this. In Odyssey an Orgins you literally kill every member of this boring order of the ancients and there are still around at any time altough the assasssins are killing them over and over again. How cheap is this story that they are behind every empire and control everything and the people are oppressed because of them. Can't they think of a better story with a clever antagonism? And the dialogues are so dumb and boring, often feeling irrelevant and skippable. The only positive I can think of is the atmospheric setting and the soundtrack. There is no greater setting for an AC than the middle east with bagdad and alamut as the real authentic origin of the Ḥaššāšīn. But this seems to be a missed opportunity for me. It is not enough to just develop a game like the previous old ACs, it has to be more than this. For example the AI and world interaction are disappointingly shallow. NPCs and environmental elements serve merely as background, with minimal meaningful interaction or reaction to the player's actions. This lack of interactivity and dynamic AI detracts from the realism and immersion of the game world, making it feel static and lifeless.Of course, it was no different in the previous AC titles. But things have to move forward. Ubisoft has to take a step forward and try new, innovative gameplay. But what am I saying? It's Ubisoft, the most horrible studio in the gaming industry at the moment. And as much as I love the franchise and have played every part of it, I don't have the slightest hope for it. _childDocuments_.review: This was the game Ubisoft touted that the series would return to its roots. Is this true? Yeah but some of it has been modernized to recent AC games gameplay. One important thing. This game has no RPG mechanics. No level requirement for armor or weapons. No overpowered/high leveled zones or enemies. You can go anyway at the start and all enemies die easily. There is skill points and skills but the skill points are acquired through main missions, side missions, and exploration. There is no XP bar or level ups. You have no abilities. Like how previous games you could do some pretty stupid godly things with some of the abilities. You now have tools. Stuff like throwing knives, (These are your projectile weapons there is no bow) blowdarts, smoke bombs, lures, etc.The map size is actually good. Not too big or too small and because of this there isn't any bloat. Yes there are collectibles but the number of them has been cut down severely. I collected them all and did all the side content and I still beat the game at 35 hours. I appreciate this very much. Origins was fine. Odyssey was super bloated with a stupid big map. Valhalla was slightly less bloated but still suffered. Everything takes place in the city of Baghdad except for a small amount of missions taking place in the desert surrounding it. So parkour/freerunning really is prominent and the big focus as you traverse the city. Hiding places are pretty hefty. There is tons of places to hide in the city. They brought back the notoriety system from AC 2. Only three levels of notoriety but each level makes pedestrians more hostile to your presence and will call the guards when they see you. You can lower your notoriety by ripping off wanted posters or paying a token to a public holler to preach your innocence. This brings me to Tokens. There are three types of Tokens. Scholar Tokens, Power Favour Tokens, and Merchant Tokens. You can farm these easily by pickpocketing people. These tokens are used for groups. What I mean is, for example, you can use a Power Favour token to pay some mercenaries to cause trouble and give you easy way to sneak past guards. You can use a Merchant token to blend in with a crowd of people to walk past a guarded entrance. A Merchant token can be used to lower merchant prices (This counts for every merchant in the game so don't worry about having to use tokens on every merchant). You can also use Scholar & Merchant tokens during some main missions to bribe people into helping you in certain situations. The combat has been stripped down to barebones. You have a parry & dodge. That's it. You can use tools during combat. Most of the time you might as well parry enemies because it lets you instant kill them except the bigger enemies. One hit assassinations are back. I mentioned pickpocketing and there is a minigame every time you try to pickpocket someone but you're better off turning it off in the settings so you instant pickpocket with success each time. You're not missing much with the setting turned on.I'm extremely happy that no modern day sections or scenes are in the game. Everything takes place in the time period it is set in. I think we all stopped caring about the modern day stuff after Desmond's demise. I know they tried to bring it back with Layla in Origins but I just don't care anymore. Just let me play the time period only at this point. The story of this game is pretty basic, pretty simple and I'm fine with that. Especially after how much of a stupid mess Valhalla's story is as it just drags on.For achievement hunters it is an easy 100%. You'll easily get most of them by playing through the game naturally. I would recommend trying to get the achievement "Blade in the Crowd" ASAP. The achievement is bugged. There are ways to fix it but its stupid that it's bugged in the first place.I would recommend getting the game on sale. Just buy the regular version not the deluxe or master assassin version. The game doesn't have any story DLCs and the outfit packs are not worth it unless you really like how one looks. You can do without them.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished AC Mirage for the first time. Here are my thoughts as an AC fan of 12+ years.Since 2014, I’ve been waiting for a decent AC game with a cohesive storyline focused on assassins — not Vikings, Greek demigods with magical spears, or ancient Egyptian police. This game does tell a story about assassins, but unfortunately, I cannot call it a decent one. It’s disappointingly mediocre.The plot has little value. It adds almost nothing to the overarching storyline. There are no witty dialogues, interesting discussions, or charismatic characters — nothing! Mirage’s story feels like a very cheap piece of bubblegum: good at first, but tasteless and tedious for the remaining 20 hours.Another «Order of the Ancients» tree just kills me. No interesting villains with deep philosophy or strong character—just another bunch of no-name pricks with one or two lines before they die.Baghdad is gorgeous! Sultry, stunning, spectacular! It looks and feels alive thanks to Ubisoft’s artists, and finally, it feels like a big real city. Unfortunately, this is a one-time event. AC Shadows will likely go back to being as flat and uninspired as the last seven years of «cities» in AC Games.The level design of the city is decent, with plenty of parkour routes. But the gameplay mechanics can’t match the quality of the level design. The movement system is the best of the «mythic» games, but still lacking. The quality of animations is poor, too. Almost all of them are abrupt and look pathetic, nowhere near Unity’s standards.We asked them to boil down AC games: reduce the garbage content and focus on the core experience. Ubisoft did reduce the game’s size but didn’t improve the content quality. There are no interesting or unique gameplay situations.The stealth is pretty good! It’s far more interesting and intricate than the battle system. However, it lacks balance: your tools are overpowered. With all tools fully upgraded, Basim turns into a berserker with no chance of dying. You feel OPAF, but at least it’s better than dull, uninspired stealth.The OST is catchy and really fills the game with the right Arabian vibe.Honestly, I’m tired. This game is just OK. Mediocre. You won’t miss much if you skip it and play something else.I really miss the days when AC games were great, outstanding and unique. They were at the pinnacle of the industry, pushing boundaries and influencing game design standards. It’s sad that now we’re left with mediocre games lacking any real value.

_childDocuments_.review: It has more bugs than any Assassin's Creed (A.C.) game I've played, but I bought it on sale, so I can't complain. The plot is as nonsensical as the rest of the A.C. series, but the historical narrative and the graphics are colossal. I love wandering around the period recreations in these games, and this is no exception.
_childDocuments_.name: Assassin's Creed Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: Finally,Assassin's creed Mirage feels like a return to the roots of the series with its focus on stealth, parkour, and a tight, immersive city environment. It's a massive improvement over the bloated experiences of Valhalla and Odyssey. Gone are the endless grind and RPG mechanics; instead, you get a refined, story-driven game that reminds me of the classic AC titles. If you felt the series was losing its way with the past few entries, Mirage will bring back that old-school Assassin's Creed magic. A must-play for longtime fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Assassin's Creed Mirage

_childDocuments_.review: I would rather have a well-made Assassin's Creed Title from the RPG era than this half-cooked "Return to the Roots" title. What the long-term fans of this franchise want is a game that continues the long-term storytelling of the franchise with a game that doesn't feel taxing to complete. But what Mirage does is remove the lore building and give a bare-bones mediocre AC title. The back story of Basim needed to include more Isu lore rather than just a 5-minute cut-scene towards the end since that's what makes him unique from the other main characters we have been exploring. The greed and desperation of Ubisoft is very evident when you play through this. The big climactic twist was very cheap that many players including myself figured out way earlier in the game. I can't believe I am saying this, but this AC title needed to be longer to explore Basim's intentions and agenda properly.

_childDocuments_.review: Spent 25 hours in this game I will try to tell my feelings succinctly on this game. Spread on the minuses and pluses. Pros:- Good optimization, even considering that it costs Denuvo this is a record among AAA games.- Removed the annoying store. Now there are only skins for Uplay coins and treasure maps, which can be easily bought in the game by stealing 40-70 times from passersby without resorting to their personal finances.- Now there are no levels for bots and Basim himself. There is only a class of skill, which is almost in no way reflected in the battle. A pleasant bonus brought talismans of the level of the fighter, which increase depending on the progress of the fighter in the story. - Skins and guises have been separated. Now the player himself decides what he likes visually, and the characteristics do not fit, but still he can wear it safely. Weapons have also undergone changes and any weapon that you like can be worn in the characteristics of other weapons, you just need to go to the store and re-weaponize to what you like.- Skins from the premium edition do not bring too much imbalance to the game and you can play fine with the standard edition.- The atmosphere of the game is a 7/10. I really like the music, Arabic mysticism...aladdin... jinn...Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves. I love it and they managed to recreate it.- “Baghdad Stories” as additional quests complement the content of the game quite well and in general I'm glad they loaded the game with minimal tasks- Stealth levels are easy and the perk system is minimal, which brings us back to the genesis of the series.- Interesting contracts in the offices, but there are not many of them- Stopped giving experience points for kills, which sends us back to our old rootsCons:- The plot is mediocre at 5/10. In no way does it compare to the first installment, much less the Ezio trilogy. The ending is just not finished and not worthy in my personal opinion. Considering Baghdad played a big part in the origin story of the brotherhood, it's not clear to me why they didn't use almost anything from past installments of the legendary 10s series. Undoubtedly they made a step in the right direction, but there is still a lot of work to be done on the mistakes, let's wish them good luck in that :)- The graphics are average, it doesn't feel like a game released in 2023 against the background of other games :(- Throughout the game I encountered three bugs in quests and I encountered texture flickering more than 5 times when restarting the game. All of this was solved by another restart. Given that the game is a year old and these bugs have long been familiar to everyone - you could try to fix before the release in stim.- Removed the interactive guide. now you need to collect spheres and read the history of Baghdad if you are very interested. This had no effect on gameplay and was a nice addition, but for some reason they abandoned it.- No Russian localization- No RTX rays. Modern technology is only DLSS, DLAA. - The game itself is soapy and pale, and even at 4k resolution, I used filters “Sharpness at 100%” and “RTX Dinamic Vibrance” these filters transform the game to a normal look.- The developers didn't go overboard. The same synchronization points, the bird was not removed, weapons are very few in the game, including 1 blade. No other locations except Baghdad and Alamut, no winter and no interaction with wildlife (you can pet kitties). The whole plot resembles an investigation and you play as a homicide detective, all these branches of bosses and mini bosses they took from the Odyssey, nothing new in it.ConclusionsIf you're tired of the last three games in the series and the endless farming, silly leveling, insulting store - you should play. If you want to see/feel the same vibe from this game as the previous games with Altair, Ezio, Kenway, it's better not to buy it. My personal interest was in Iraq, the serenity of the game without levels, the pleasure of stealth on the story I did not count on and I do not advise you.

_childDocuments_.review: The default controller mapping is really bad. Like, change that immidiately before you even attempt to get used to it. There are some pretty good guides you can find on Youtube which you can base your settings off of. The story is for the most part one big nothingburger. While there definitely is some intrigue with the jinni and the investigating into the order can be interesting, there is one big problem. There's pretty much no emotion to any scene and no real stakes. Even the big traumatic event that sets off the story proper is just brushed aside and ever really talked about. Now here is where things start to look a little better. Now, while the stealth is great, you might think the combat look kinda meh. And you wouldn't neccessarily be wrong. However! Put the game on the hardest difficulty + permadeath and everything just gets a whole lot better. The threat of permadeath works really, really well for this game. It makes you want to stay in stealth at all costs. The combat, while still subpar, suddenly becomes a lot more tense. And you now actually have a reason to run away when in over your head, initiating an exciting chase!The option for permadeath have really elevated this game for me. And with it, it feels like this game is finally starting to lean into the vision sold to me in that first trailer for AC1. Something these games never really managed to hit, due to being too easy and death not mattering.Focus is lame, though. Not using that. As is the eagle. As for the parkour, it is definitely improved compared to the past few entries. However, everything is still very context based and hand-holdy. You can't really do manual ejects while climbing unless there's something really obvious for Basim to grab, for example. At least you can jump off stuff manually when you're standing on top of things. Ah, Baghdād. A beautiful city and the true main character of this game. With many distinct districts, a lot of detail and history, and rooftops that are fun traverse; this is what these games have been missing. While you can travel around the open area around the city, the city proper is where you will be spending the most of your time.  It feels really good getting back to this part of the world and time period again in AC. Get "" right away. Get rid of those really clunky Valhalla assassinations and replace them with something you could see an actual assassin use. Also, "" will make the hops feel a whole lot smoother. You can get these mods from Nexus.I am quite enjoying myself, actually. The missions are fun and the city is interesting to go through. But while I do think the game is good, it's not great. Fun in the moment, but not as good as it could have been overall. While I am really digging the ideas put forth into the game, the execution could be improved.Since I am enjoying it, I'll give it a thumbs up. Get it on a sale, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the Assassin's Creed franchise since AC2 and have played, completed and enjoyed the majority of the previous games. _childDocuments_.review: I regret buying this and playing it as long as I did. It's just kind of... soulless?The last Assassin's Creed I played was AC2, all the way back in 2014. 10 years later and this feels kind of exactly the same. Other than being in a different location, there was nothing interesting about this game showing me what the franchise had learned in literally a decade. And the location just wasn't particularly exciting either.HDR is crap. Literally the worst, most washed out HDR I've ever seen in a game which claims to have support.Combat is annoying, and there's like a permanent "guards will attack you on sight" meter which you *can* pay a guy to clear, but it seems to constantly just get triggered again whenever you do literally anything you're supposed to be doing as a damn thief-assassin - even assassinating guards from cover somehow.And one of the absolute entire reasons for this franchise to exist - parkour - is also frankly crap. Again, there was nothing new about the parkour here compared to what I played 10 years ago, but on top of that it is jank as HELL. The character is constantly vaulting onto things I'm not trying to, constantly refusing to let go of things I am spamming to let go of, and none of this automatic collision seemed to be turned off in tiny one-room indoor sections, so you are constantly autoclimbing and jumping all over the place when you're just trying to open a chest or, God forbid, trying to solving a moving boxes puzzle.The only redeeming part of the entire experience was the occasional history trivia you can pick up and learn about the medieval Arab empire, which was something I knew very little about so was genuinely super interesting... But that being the best part of the game kind of paints a picture of how ♥♥♥♥♥ everything else was.Just before 2 hours (i.e. the refund window) I thought to myself "it's not THAT exciting, but I'll stick it out, see where it goes" and in the next 4 hours it went absolutely bloody no where. I honestly feel hoodwinked. Lesson learned I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirage is the closest to a classic AC game from Origins onwards. The gameplay is legitimately stealth-focused with the reintroduction of both tools and instant assassinations; the world is a lot more compact with essentially no more than the city of Baghdad and its immediate surroundings; the RPG abilities are finally done away with. There is also an attempt to reintroduce social stealth and parkour, though both are somewhat limited and clunky. In terms of graphics and level design, the world is incredibly detailed and beautiful, and genuinely very interesting to explore and walk around in. Mission locations also provide you with multiple approaches, including environmental and non-lethal ones. The codex and historical facts are also implemented much better in comparison to Origins and Odyssey. All of this makes Mirage very good and worthwhile.However, it's painfully obvious that the game was originally intended as a DLC for AC Valhalla. I haven't played the previous game yet, which genuinely detracted from my understanding of the main character, his story, and particularly his ending. This is the only AC game in which I've experienced this, despite having played many of the earlier titles out of order. Beyond this, the game is relatively short, with quite little content outside of the main story.With all this in mind, I would recommend the game mostly because it is an actual attempt at returning to the original AC format, and it's mostly successful at it. Its relationship to Valhalla makes it more like Brotherhood or Revelations (as in, it's somewhere between a standalone game and an expansion) but that's not an inherently bad thing, and I'd say all three are great AC entries regardless. I got Mirage at 50% off and would say it was definitely worth £25. Don't waste your money on anything other than the base edition though.

_childDocuments_.review: So glad to have played this! Mirage feels in many ways like a realization of what the first Assassin's Creed, released 2007, was attempting to do. It's fun to think about there's a whole generation of gamers who've grown up with the longer titles (Origins, Odyssey, Valhalla). I would imagine if someone is used to those games, Mirage would be quite a shock, lol. In Mirage, you are not a god at combat. Instead, you must find ways to be stealthy and avoid direct combat. And the game gives a variety of tools. As a fan of the series, I'm glad to be in 2024 where Mirage exists as an option for more "classic" AC and I can still visit the three longer games. And yes, Ubisoft Connect remains gross, but don't let that stop you from playing a great AC game.

_childDocuments_.review: Shortage of the stuff below: I like the game and can recommend it to everyone, who is NOT expecting new mechanics/elements, but an overall nice Assassins Creed game. For Achievement-Hunters: You don't have to play in high difficulties or perma-death to get all of them. I also wouldn't recommend perma-death in case your character jumps off an area you don't want him to jump off, as this would perge your entire progress, including all the collectibles for achievements.I'm a great fan of Assassins Creed and therefore had to get Mirage, even though I, like many others, expected Shadows to be released this November. At least the delay offered enough time to finish Mirage before the release. Straight before getting to the actual suggestion of mine: If you expect a load of new mechanics and elements you don't know from earlier Assassins Creed parts, you might not like Mirage. As a more experienced player in AC games, it took me about 28 hours to finish the game and another 3-4 hours to gather all achievements after finishing the story.For me, the game felt like a remastered version of the Assassins Creed in Jerusalem, even though you play another character in here being located in the city of Bagdad. Graphics are awesome. Only issue I experienced sometimes were texture bugs (Floors flickering between focused and blurry) especially in the wilderness around Bagdad. Other than that, I love the day-night contrasts a lot.You play as Basim, who starts as a thief without any knowledge of killing. I like the character development in the story a lot.  I also like how Assassins are called "Hidden ones" here, underlining their way of operating in the game. Don't worry, you can still berserk around most of the time. I literally have nothing to say against the story. Talking about the game elements though: You fight against unknown members of an enemy-organisation (Called "The order"). So yeah, nothing new about the antagonists for an Assassins Creed game. You don't have Animus-elements outside of playing the Assassin like in some earlier parts.I do like the AI in this part. People react to you depending on your actions. If you successfully steal items from civilians, they will panic and call for guards. If they catch you trying it, you will recieve a wanted state and they will call for guards, targetting especially you. When wanted, people will also recognize your face on the roads, calling for guards. Guards itself can also recognize you when being wanted. You have an eagle to scout areas from the sky. This mechanic is known from Odyssey and Origins for example. Only partly unrealistic part here, simply existing to make your gameplay harder: Sharpshooters are trying to bow down the eagle once it enters closed areas with them on the roofs. You gotta kill them then to use the eagle vision again. But why?Enemies (Guards, Soldiers and Bandits) are nothing special. There are several types of enemies but once you get the hang of outplaying them, they don't pose a threat anymore. I hoped for a more challenging mechanic with bounty hunters, like in AC Odyssey for example. Overall, I didn't die a single time on higher difficulties. So don't expect to approach situations where you die in a lot. While your Assassin Master tells you that it's important to know how to handle lots of weapons, you sadly can only play with one possible combination throughout the whole game, being a sword and a dagger. I expected more options like in the other current AC parts.Overall though, I can absolutely recommend trying out this game while waiting for whatever AC Shadows is going to offer us. It feels partly refreshing finally having a newer Assassins Creed working like the older parts, without too many fantasy elements, but a more historical focus. Have fun trying!

_childDocuments_.review: I will start out by saying that I find this to be a MISERABLE game at every turn.I only bought this because it was the story of Basim, but the story isn't great, the voice acting is poor, the facial mechanics are poor.You're playing as a weak character where you can't fight very well when you get caught sneaking. The combat mechanics are terrible, with seemingly millisecond sensitive key presses that often don't register on time. I mean, wait for an enemy to come around the corner, press the Assassinate key when prompted, and it fails and draws in more enemies than you can fight. To me the combat feels like one big quick time event.In combat, the game often automatically starts climbing me up on things and I get slashed trying to get out of it.There are also map bugs. After an aggravating sneak to get in this compound to steal a package, I dropped it down over wall and then jumped down and fell outside of the map. I was confined by transparent walls with no way to get back out. _childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Assassin's Creed series, I was excited to dive into Assassin's Creed Mirage. While it’s noticeably shorter than previous entries like Origins and Valhalla, Mirage still packs an immersive and nostalgic punch, making it a joy to follow Basim on his journey. Set in a beautifully rendered world, the game captures the essence of classic Assassin’s Creed stealth, with an easy-to-grasp gameplay loop and accessible combat. The stealth mechanics truly shine here, rewarding careful planning over brute force — a treat for those who enjoy slipping past enemies unnoticed.The graphics, though not groundbreaking, are polished and atmospheric, adding a nice touch to the game’s historical ambiance. If you're a fan of the series, Mirage offers a streamlined experience that's both fun and full of the hidden mysteries we've come to expect from Assassin's Creed.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no Cassandra or Eivor to be found in this game.Initially this game feels somewhat disappointing. The movement feels clumsy, the animations are not very good even if the game technically flows quickly and legs seem to blend into buildings evety now and then.Clothes and buildings look detailed and fine, but faces are poorly done. Cutscenes are not in widescreen. Compared to the beauty of Odyssey or the coolness of Valhalla, Syndicate and Black Flag this game so far does not stand up very well in comparison. Even if Ubisoft waited almost a year before releasing it games from 2023 or 2024 should still deliver better quality than their 10 years old predecessors.After having played several hours and more of the chapters the feeling of unfinished and ugliness remains. You can walk through some people, you can ride through deers, and while the landscapes are incredibly beautiful the people in general are still at best very plain and boring or just outright ugly. There's no fan favorites like Cassandra or Eivor to be found in this game, at least not for me.In addition, while I believe the use of Arabic language as background talk between non-player characters may be done to increase realism, it also has a downside for me as a European who don't speak or understand any form of Arabic, in that I have no clue what the people are talking about. Is it directed to me, about me, about something not directly to me but which I might benefit from overhearing, or just the weather ? Seeing how much effort has gone into making the places themselves look realistic I feel I'm missing out on some parts by not understanding what's being spoken. Maybe it's nothing, but that's still the way it feels.But in short, good technical quality, nice music, ugly characters, same or very similar storyline as several previous games. Had the characters been better created I would have been much more positive to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending hours playing Assassin's Creed Mirage, my feelings are quite mixed. While there are a few highlights, most of the mechanics feel either recycled or poorly executed.  Let’s start with the grappling hook mechanic, which hasn’t evolved at all compared to previous installments. It’s disappointing to see such a lack of innovation when this element could have been more dynamic and engaging.  However, one thing I absolutely loved in the game is the cats. Yes, the cats are fantastic! They add a charming touch and bring the world to life in a small but delightful way.  Now, on to the Eagle Vision. It’s inconvenient that you can only use it while walking and not while running. This not only slows you down but also affects loot quality, which is a bizarre and frustrating limitation.  The pickpocketing system is overly simplistic. One button, and that's it. There’s no sense of challenge or risk, and it makes this aspect of the gameplay feel shallow.  When it comes to the PC adaptation, it’s downright terrible. The map control system is a nightmare – to zoom in, you have to scroll all the way to the bottom of the screen, and then scroll back up again to adjust the map. It’s unnecessarily complicated and detracts from the overall experience.  The inclusion of the Isu outfit is just laughable. It feels completely out of place and serves no purpose other than being a bizarre, unnecessary addition.  One of the most frustrating aspects is the enemy respawning. You can spend 15 minutes clearing a fortress, but if you step away for even a moment, the guards respawn almost instantly. It ruins any sense of progress and becomes incredibly tedious.  And let’s not forget the jump mechanics. It seems like the developers forgot about this basic feature, as your character often refuses to perform necessary maneuvers, leading to awkward and frustrating moments.  Now, let’s talk about the story. If it weren’t for the ending, I’d rate it a 2/10. It’s painfully primitive and feels like it was copied from previous games. The main characters and side characters are poorly written, and their dialogues are just awful. They evoke no emotions, and you never feel invested in their actions. The whole thing feels like a secondary product, with no real weight or depth.  In conclusion, Assassin's Creed Mirage had potential, but its execution leaves much to be desired. The world and the cats are the only things really worth praising. Everything else feels either underdeveloped or a rehash of old mechanics with no meaningful improvements.

I am one of those people who like Unity's parkour, story and overall gameplay. Sue me.Back to Mirage:+Parkour feels nice, not too over the top and is in very good sync with the world around you. You do not feel as if you're clenching your butthole just to hop over a fence.+Good visuals+Stealth plays out pretty nicely, as good as Unity I think.-Animations feel stiff. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale at $24.99 and am glad to have done soI am bias because I feel Orgins/Odyssey is the high water mark for the franchise.cons:-they changed the free run psychics too much, ie: character would get stuck trying to free run on ledges on either side of stairs instead of just walking up stairs, it's stupid-change in major game mechanics, attack/parry specific types of attach, hold for strong attack is too big a change and not intuitive-the story is very short, side quests are minimal, less than half of Odyssey/Origins-the story and narrative is not engaging; some of Origin's fetch quests is stupid like helping a grieving mother get their dead son's body but at least there's some historical context tied to it so you learn about ancient cultures, in Mirage, this is nonexistent -character development and voice acting is not very good; I get it, there's more context in Valhalla, which I didn't bother to play-massive miss on historical content, unlike Odyssey/Origins, ie there is lazy short text explaining significance of the Dome of Ass but that's it-map is way small compare to origins/odyssey, very large portion of the map is nothingness -no hunting/gathering-impossibly pathetic RPG elements, introduction of 'costume' where you put on an outfit for spec and another for looks but with zero customization (unlike in Cyberpunk) - what's the point? In Origins you can mix and match or use full set for extra advantage, nope, full set here only, and there's like 7 outfits, that's it, pathetic! -I didn't even bother with Valhalla because it had such bad reviews-graphics not advanced;  Islam is all about symbology and the mosaic/details are not high-res enough-no guided historical tour (really?)-extremely low re-playability, i'd just load the game to walk around, that's about it, unlike origins/odyssey because content quality & quantityKinda Pros:-amazing map/detail (but essentially lots of copy/paste if you look closely),-arabic voice for extra immersion-you can pet cats (finally)-supposedly easy to unlock 'full completion' (because it's so short a game, it's not really a plus but if you like medals, your's is in the mail)overall this felt like a lazy production for cash, zero heart or soul

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you really just like AC games and want to play it to have played it, this game is an annoying, frustrating piece of ♥♥♥♥. That being said... tl;dr The story is fine. The weapon and gear progression is fine. The characters are fine. The movement is not fine(I'd say the worst out of every AC). It's easier to just run around on the ground than it is to parkour.Movement, and free-running which I'd say is a core aspect of the game is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've never wanted to blow my own brains out so often in an AC game as I have with this one. Walk(just walk) around and hop up onto something but it won't hop off just by walking, then tapping A(xbox) makes you jump to another elevated surface, don't worry you can get back onto the ground after the 3rd attempt of leaping somewhere else or just rotating a couple times. Intentionally jump onto a ledge or railing and then be unable to move and just spin in place. Free-run onto a ledge with something on the other side(jar, weapon rack, bench, anything) and have a stroke and be unable to continue past it instead of just hopping over it and continuing on you need to backtrack or move to the side. Climb up a wall to an open window and instead of grabbing the window ledge(or going straight in which would be nice) Basim decides to entirely climb around and over it. Get on a ledge that an open window is on and try to shuffle to the side to be under the window, instead move to the entire opposite side of the window. Indoors with beams and bars to jump and swing on, a direct path they've made for you to travel above enemies to sneak past them only to swing on a bar and jump towards the bookshelf that is not only below the beam but also past it, directly into enemy view.  Run across a wooden beam and try to free-run jump across to another ledge etc. to just jump straight down into enemies. Get to a ledge and think "I'm going to jump down" to then jump diagonal and upwards. To hang from a ledge and try and drop down (B on xbox) to just jump across to an opposite ledge, repeating that on every ledge until it finally lets you drop down after the 18th attempt. To follow a free-run section identified by the white cloth to start it, get up on a roof, see the beam you can jump to to just ignore it and jump onto the ground. I've lost track of how many times I've tried to jump to a corner hook(the thing that swings) and just jumped straight down to the ground instead, or decided to land on the wall instead.Anything and everything with the movement in the game can and will go wrong. I've never had a clean, happy parkour traversal last more than 10~15(20 to be generous) seconds. Something goes wrong and bugs out or I've got to stop and look around for where I can go next if I don't want to just jump off a roof and lose some health.Valhalla had better movement and mechanics. I don't understand how they can make the same game(core mechanics) year after year and it gets worse every time.I wish I hit the breaking point of being fed-up with this ♥♥♥♥ sooner so I could get a refund and protect my mental health.

_childDocuments_.review: They said it over and over throughout the trailers and promotion of this game, and gadly, Assassin's Creed Mirage is truly a return to form, yes, it uses a lot of mechanics and graphics from AC Valhalla, and I believe I read somewhere this was planned as a DLC for that game, I'm glad it isn't, first, because Valhalla already has a lot of extra content, on top of the already long main story, and second, leaving this as a game on it's own didn't really hurt it. I see Mirage like Resident Evil 8 or Zelda TOTK, a direct sequel to the previous entry but also a spiritual sequel to a beloved game in the franchise, in Mirage's case, the very first Assassin's Creed.I've now played through every single game in the AC series, and I've loved every one of them, I'm not exactly a die hard fan so I didn't mind the switch to RPG-like, I very much welcomed it, since every once in a while you gotta try something new, else the series would get stale, but just as I received that change with open arms, I receive this "return to it's roots". The game is very much focused on stealth, combat isn't as fleshed out or has as much options as the previous 2, but you do have several new Assassination options and mechanics. The "investigate for an opportunity" before any main member of the order reminded me a lot of Unity, so that was pretty cool. Although you don't get other weapon choices other than a sword and your dagger, you do get a few Assassin tools, like throwing knives, traps, darts, etc. which are there to help you either keep your stealth or distract enemies to avoid combat, so you can approach the enemy in a variety of ways.The graphics are the same as Valhalla, I was hoping they upgraded a bit so we could notice but I guess we're gonna have to wait for AC Shadows to see any differences. The city does look beautiful.When they announced it was going to be a shorter game, I was hoping it would be more polished than usual and more linear, yet they still kept the open world elements from the last 3 like letting you choose which order member to go for, which I believe damages the story and pacing of the game, yes, it is short but the best parts are the beginning and the end, in-between is mostly fluff and I barely got invested on the characters apart from Roshan, Nehal and Basim. While the gameplay it's pretty good the game itself doesn't feel like an AAA game, has it's weird bugs and the voice acting feels a bit robotic. I just played God of War Ragnarök and it was such a shock coming from such great acting and writing... to this, it was difficult to get used to, I really hope AC Shadows feels more "complete".However, even with it's flaws, I do recommend this game, especially if you are an Assassin's Creed fan, after 3 games we finally get a true assassin, but beware, there isn't a single mention or sequence during modern times, for better or worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much of the game yet to have a thorough opinion, but what I've seen so far does feel much more akin to Assassin's Creed 1 and 2 than, say, Odessey or Valhalla. They've brought back a lot of the original mechanics of AC, like pick-pocketing, hiding in market crowds, the rooftop "booths", and tearing down wanted posters to reduce notoriety. Basim is an interesting protagonist so far. Don't expect anything too crazy out of the graphics and AC camels are about as well articulated as AC horses, but it seems like a good blend of some old and new tactics, themes, and mechanics. The prologue does feel a bit contrived -- like maybe we should've spent a bit more time there to really make the intent stick, but story is decently interesting so far. Only technical issue I've run into is that cutscenes don't always play like they should. The audio will continue playing, but sometimes the cutscene freezes on one scene, although you can tell it should still be moving. I've tried updating drivers and my computer and changing a few graphics settings (my hardware meets all recommended requirements for the game) and still am having that issue, so I'm hoping that's an early PC wrinkle that will get ironed out. I would recommend it if you like Assassin's Creed, but, as some others have said, buy it on sale.

It runs very well and no crashes. Stealth mechanics is back.Cons:No real ship sailing so far. That is one of the best things of Assassin's Creed Franchise.I wish there was a few more of different types of weapons.Yes, The Story. You don't play the single game for the story. For fifty dollars, I would not recommend the game, but we all know how that AC itch can get you sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth to buy if it's on Sale!!! Thankfully i have recently purchased it on the first week it's available on Steam.Points to consider when Buying:1. For Gamers who missed the "Assassin" playstyle bot some RPG Battle style like previous AC games. This is for me, probably the closest AC game to the AC 1 & 2 than other AC games. 2. New Feature called Assassin's Focus/ New Power? (I guess you could called it that). Some may like it, some may not. Me personally i really enjoyed it so much. If you don't like it JUST DON'T USE IT and IGNORE IT EXIST (simple as that).3. The Stealth mechanics is more enjoyable (when you are spotted only nearby enemies that will engage and not all of enemies will know your current location in an instant (unlike the previous games). Note: Some may find it too easy, making it boring or not enjoyable.4. The Location/Map/City is so Beautiful and Vibrant. Although some NPC has same weird AI sometimes (like walk to walls)5. The Game is very well optimized for Portable Consoles (Steamdeck/Legion Go/Rog Ally/MSI Claw). I often play it on legion go with High Settings you cloud get 90 Max FPS and and Average FPS of 50 with the Lowest FPS 30, also the Best part is it even runs on native (not using Amd FSR/DLSS/Xess).6. Combat is Easy (for me) it feels almost like AC1-AC2. The difference is you sometimes can't instant counter-kill enemies after successful parry. 7. Although the combat is easy, i would still prefer more attack animations/moveset like ACIV black flag or AC Unity. In game you only get 3 Basic Attacks and 1 Charged Attack moveset. After playing it for 12Hours+ i have got used to it and ignored the fact it has just limited moveset because i mainly played it using parry)8. The main story feels short to me. Around 2 Hours just for Basim to get the hidden blades aka become an official Assassin. The rest of the story feels rushed, wished that ubisoft spend more time in the story, so we could see more character developments. If you worry about the gameplay hours, you could always play the contracts mission or other open-world objectives it will take a lot of time. 9. Deluxe/Master Edition/DLCs are too expensive but if you have extra money, i'd say the Master Edition it worth to get the Skins and Weapons because it has unique perks that will help you play more easily especially it you are a newbie (the useful ones are Deluxe pack to get prince of persia weapons to heal when deafeating opponents and Fire Demon Pack to disintegrate after assassination)Overall i will give this game an solid 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Assassin’s Creed Mirage feels like stepping back in time to the classic era of the franchise, reminiscent of the simplicity and charm of AC 1, AC 2, and AC 3. The experience is refreshingly straightforward—focused on the core gameplay that made the series iconic.Side missions are present, but they don’t feel like a chore. The world is well-defined and engaging, making exploration enjoyable rather than overwhelming. While there are some graphical bugs and the occasional quirky Ubisoft bug, they don’t detract significantly from the overall experience.The game might not reach perfection, but it’s a solid title. I’d give it a 7.5/10. It’s not groundbreaking, but it delivers what it promises: a nostalgic return to the golden days of Assassin’s Creed, evoking memories of Ezio and the roots of the series. Definitely worth playing for long-time fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say something different about Mirage, spoken from an angle, which, I guess, must be understood first. Six points to get the perspective:1. I love Ubi games, always have (we're talking decades). Are they the best games there are? Not saying that. Just saying they do it for me. Big worlds, lots to do, state-of-the-art graphics. They are almost always fun . They give me something reasonable to do and for many hours, thus good value. Do you like Ubi games?2. I love stealth games. If you can stealth a game at all, I will. Slowly. Methodically. Aiming for flawless. And stealth games did not begin with AC 1. They began with the Thief series, which will always have a special place in my gamer heart. Do you like stealth games?3. Although I did have some fun with the early AC titles, they weren't perhaps my favs at the time. What were your thoughts, if any?4. I have welcomed the direction Ubi games and the AC series have taken during later years. Massive games that take me 100 hrs to complete. What is there to complain about? It's good value! Also, I am all for dropping all or most of the silly meta story of AC in favor of diving deep into various historical contexts. It's entertaining and educating at the same time. Therefore, Valhalla was great. Odyssey was nothing short of fantastic, at the time. Do you like lots of content, historical content?5. The way Mirage was announced and the way it was received at release put me off. I didn't want to pay the triple A premium for a game like . So I didn't. Didn't play it until recently, now available on Steam (and at a great discount). What were your early impressions?6. Mirage, sorry, I got it all wrong. (I think you might have too.)While I do hope AC Shadows will revert back to standard contemporary Ubi massive 100+ hrs, and with Mirage being quite a bit shorter (finished main quest at 45 hrs as a slow-stealthing non-completionist-but-see-most-of-it type of player), Mirage is still... wow... I would never have thought. Not with the introduction I got in media and social media at release.There is  put into Mirage from the dev team (dev army?) Yes, it is a bit clunky. Yes, it is this negative adjective, that negative adjective too. But synchronizing on the tip of a minaret, taking in the full 360 view of ancient Baghdad is absolutely breathtaking. This was the fantasy back in AC 1, what could not be achieved at the time. The city is massive! And it's like there isn't a single straight road in all of it. It's just this amorphous myriad of streets and little alleyways. Architecturally cohesive and credible, yet with so surprisingly little generics and predictability. Also far removed from Odysseys, although fun in a way, "we've got to put this famous monument in here and that famous monument next to it, not that they were originally in the same place but..." kind of design. No, if someone had told me they had found an ancient map of 9th century Baghdad and that the city in the game was closely modeled after it, I would have believed it. Mirage's Baghdad is  great. It's huge. It's credible to the historically ignorant (like me). It's fantastic. You gotta experience it.Also, I feel it's a bold game in a sense. I will explain. As disgusting as the historical viking culture was in many ways (I'm a Swede), and early England wasn't much better, AC Valhalla got good draft behind the Vikings TV series. It was exciting, relatable and appealing for all of us. When AC Shadows hit the shelves, every aspie gamer will buy it just because it's Japan. Because for some inconveivable reason Japan is much better and more interesting than any other place. And if that isn't enough, there is the remake of the Shogun TV series to back it all up. Well, historical Japan never really went out of style for the last 100+ years in the West, did it?Now, with Mirage, from a Western perspective, is there any less hip culture and geographical area to model right now than the arab world? Yet the dev team set out to do it and with such detail and devotion. They really tried. They tried to share their own discoveries with us. If you bother to actually read the encyclopedia that slowly builds through the game through your little discoveries and unlocks, you learn things about a rich ancient culture that Western school doesn't teach you very much about. The many thousands of man hours put into making this game... Just a couple of hours into playing the game, with it's somewhat slow start, I was having fun, I did, fun enough, but I also started to feel morally obliged to continue. Someone had put that many hard hours into making this, trying to show us a part of a common past that speaks to us to this day? Then you have to play it. How could I stomach not to?AC, please, never stop throwing us back into history! Ubi, never stop doing your thing!
