_childDocuments_.review: I was fortunate enough to play an advance copy of this game. I had been watching the development for a couple of years through whatever snapshots of progress were being shared online.For me, this game sits somewhere in between a life simulation, visual novel, and third person adventure. It pulls pieces from different genres to create a unique experience that is probably best enjoyed in a single session.The game will take around two hours to complete, and while there is a story to be told here, much of the real meat of the game is in the quiet time between the big story beats. The game compels the player to take time for reflection, time to take in the atmosphere, time to take a peek into another life. It's a quiet-loud-quiet-loud-quiet type flow.I really enjoyed my experience playing through Apartment Story, and it ran smoothly on my Steam Deck. I don't really have any nostalgia for PS1 style graphics, but I felt that the game utilized the look effectively, allowing for more complex ideas to be communicated through a simplified visual language.I think that discerning players looking for a story driven experience with rich atmosphere should give this one a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: There are aspects of this game that I really liked - the attention to detail in the apartment furnishing, the lighting, and the music were all great.Other than those things, this game really didn't hang together for me unfortunately. I like the idea of having Sims-style bars that you have to manage, but was disappointed with how little effect they had on the game. There are a couple of nice moments when narrative events impacted them but I found they didn't add much to the overall experience. In general the lack of reactivity present in the game makes me feel like there is a lot of wasted potential here. I appreciate that adding bespoke reactions based on the current game state is costly, but I think Apartment Story just serves as good example that games are not suited to the type of storytelling seen in linear media. There were multiple occasions where the seams of the narrative scripting were visible, with the game waiting for me to do the exact interactions it wanted in order to progress, and I don't think it dealt with any deviation from that well. It feels like this would have worked much better as a short film or written story.I'm quite tolerant of bugs and jank, especially in small indie titles, but I found there were enough of them to get in the way of my enjoyment. The lo-fi animations, while charming, did undermine the tone I feel the game was going for.Pacing wasn't great and there were long stretches of time where I felt like I was just waiting around for stuff to happen. If the waiting was intentional, it didn't work for me. The level design in the final scene was also confusing and kind of killed any impact the narrative may have had at that moment.Despite writing about the things I didn't like at length, I'm going to give a thumbs-up. I think it is really important that games keep trying to push the boundaries of what types of experiences they can give players and I think Apartment Story is an ambitious attempt at doing so. I'm looking forward to seeing more from the developers with the suggestion that the next thing they make is scoped a little bit more appropriately for their budget.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more an art piece than a game, but it works really well. Could be a solid proof of concept for a more ambitious game.I finished in just under 2 hours, and it was a complete story, as straightforward as it was.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I encountered bugs within the first few minutes. The very basics of picking things up and combining items to eat (which you need to do) are needlessly janky--the very first meal I made got bugged and stuck to the dinner table, I couldn't eat it. Oh well, I moved on but eventually got to a moment in the game where something was obviously supposed to occur...but it didn't. The game was running and I could move around, but time was no longer passing and my meters weren't going down. Basically I was two hours in and realized I wouldn't be able to progress and there's no way to back up or reset the moment or whatever. Not about to wade through the first two hours again.There's charm to this game for sure, but it's just too clunky and janky to recommend in it's state. It was cool that my avatar was able to watch porn and blast it while my friend waited right by my side. A true NPC buddy indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: A playable A24, minimalist, atompsheric flick - for good and for ill. It's more of a walking sim than its trailers imply. If you're fine with that you'll have a good time. If not, maybe wait for a sale and skip it.It genuinely makes the most of its limitations. It changes scenarios and oozes atmosphere. The Sims stat bars are extremely easy to manage, but they nonetheless invite you to ♥♥♥♥ around, take a break, reflect, and even create dread. Make food, smoke a joint, pee and shower in between the relationship drama. It's hard to explain how, but it works and immerses you into the setting.The bad part is that it's slow. REALLY slow. The game discourages skipping time by going to sleep, and doesn't have very many things to do even when you're at your best shape. This means a lot of the game's downtime is essentially filler, and it becomes extremely obvious when a scripted event happens instead of it being organic.The so-so part is the plot. It's well structured and explained, with good guys to cheer for and a bad guy to hate. Dialogues are short and sharp, and it's really cool how game mechanics are used for little character moments. That said, it's also very predictable, and ends on a bit of a "that's it?" note.P.S. There aren't multiple endings nor dialogue choices. All conflict is mandatory. Dying is a failure state. That's not good nor bad, and I realize it's a whole can of worms to accommodate for those choices. But it is just this little bit disappointing considering the infrastructure is already there for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: Apartment Story is a standout gem in the indie gaming scene, offering a fresh and unique experience compared to many smaller titles out there. The game transforms the everyday lives of apartment dwellers into a captivating narrative filled with meaningful choices and well-crafted characters. Each interaction feels significant, drawing you deeper into the story.The pacing is one of the game’s greatest strengths. It doesn't rush, allowing you to immerse yourself in the world and its characters at a natural, enjoyable pace. The narrative unfolds in a way that feels organic and rewarding, making you truly care about the people you meet and the choices you make.What sets Apartment Story apart is how it balances simplicity with depth. It doesn’t rely on flashy mechanics but instead uses thoughtful storytelling and character development to pull you in. The branching narrative and replayability give it a richness that’s rare in smaller games.Overall, *Apartment Story* is a refreshing and memorable experience—a must-play for fans of narrative-driven indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: The latest coffee-drinking, cigarette-smoking, beer-supping, dancing-in-the-living-room simulator from indie creators of The End of the World+, finding optimism in the claustrophobic apartment of a broke millennial. It feels like a small indie movie or single set play with it’s 3 characters and setting. The diegetic music nails the vibe, especially when you have a visitor. The dialogue feels human and contemporary. The art direction speaks for itself!This is unapologetically an artsy ‘’walking sim’’ style game, and some sections are about doing the fundamental chores that go along with being trapped in a Meat Prison inside an Apartment Prison, if you don't like that. If we get another similar game, I’d love to see more internal thoughts (Disco Elysium, 13 Sentinels) with voice acting and deeper characterisation.This game costs £6, and you should consider purchasing it. It is ridiculously ambitious - the flavor interactions are familiar from your Quantic Dream, Kojima Productions or a GTA - but conjured from blood, sweat and pixels rather than mocap studios. If you want to see more interesting games made in the UK, start here.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: This was brilliant. It's a nice little piece that's entirely based on vibes, until it's very very not. Since I heard about this, I was always curious how the whole sims-like life sim aspect plays into it, but it plays really well. There's some brilliant bits where actually looking at your stats while stuff is going on adds to Arthur's character. It's a very micro story about some crazy things, while keeping that almost low droning "life goes on, gotta get food, gotta take a shower, etc etc" kind of feeling. It's difficult to say more without spoiling things, and it's already a feature length experience as it is. I would say this though, if you're up for having well crafted downtime woven into your story telling, and down for something unexpected and different and potentially bizarre (at least in this medium), give this a go. This game isn't for everyone, but I am glad it's for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: Apartment Story offers a captivating atmosphere and a truly unique experience that immerses you in someone else’s life. Though the game is short, I actually appreciate that—it fits perfectly into my schedule since I don't often have time for longer games.The characters and environment feel authentic, and the art style is spot on. While the story can be a bit predictable at moments, the overall experience left me satisfied. If you're intrigued by what you've seen, I definitely recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone but I think some will REALLY vibe with it. This game deserves way more attention.There's a lot of jank here. The characters don't have a ton of depth. But this game made me feel anxious and powerless in a way that was pretty unique. And then a little frustrated by the end as my save file glitched and I wasn't able to finish the game. I ended up watching the final minutes on YouTube.As the story builds, I found the sims like, stat management elements helped build tension. Washing the dishes while you wait in paranoia for the consequences of what took place the previous day was quite interesting and made me feel surprisingly anxious. The characters weren't particularly intriguing and their conversations felt pretty short. There seemed to be so little connection between them that the ending conversation felt pretty botched, as did the drop of the ending screen considering how much style the game has overall.The game looks INCREDIBLE and definitely has the sauce. I would've loved to spend more time just hanging out in the apartment. It definitely passes the weird/chill/dreary atmosphere vibe check and for $7 and two hours of my life I found it to be a pretty interesting game and great way to spend my weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: A day in the life of Arthur:- Wake up.- Urinate for approximately 2 seconds.- Take a shower.- Prepare cereal on the chopping board (naked, because you forgot to put clothes on).- Write on the computer.- Look at explicit content on the computer.- Do…other stuff at the computer (tissues are there for a reason).- Smoke a joint with your roommate’s ex.- Discuss what to do with The Gun.Apartment Story is a short narrative-driven simulation game. Your character, Arthur, has recently lost his job, is drowning in debt, and struggling to find purpose in life. You must keep Arthur alive by making sure he eats, sleeps, goes to the bathroom, keeps his hygiene in check, and looks after his mental wellness using a sort of Sims-esque system of health bars. If these needs drag Arthur's Life bar down, it’s game over, so keeping them balanced is crucial (though not at all difficult).You control Arthur in 3rd person as he wanders around the apartment, using a targeting crosshair to highlight things you want him to interact with. Though all of the controls are a bit fiddly (picking multiple items up is particularly clumsy) and there’s a degree of jank to every element of the design, it somehow works with the low-poly aesthetics - plus the sheer volume of interactable “stuff” is impressive. The soundtrack is beautiful, composed of drifting electronic tracks from TRAAPS. There are several scenes of nudity and explicit content which feel somewhat gratuitous to me, but inoffensively so.At certain points, events will happen: the doorbell will ring, your phone will beep, or your electricity meter will cut out. What will you do? These choices feed the narrative, which is thrilling and completely believable. I swung between laughter and nail-biting tension as situations unfolded, desperate to make the “right” decisions. There are several ways your story can “end”, which makes for some replayability. All in all, I enjoyed this: it’s not perfect, but it is entertaining!(Notes: Works fine on Steamdeck. Multiple saves are not supported. Approx 2 hour run time. Well worth the asking price IMO.)
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: A moreish tone piece about soaking up the glittering mediocrity of a English flat — the sparkling rain on a window and the coloured light of electronics painting beauty onto the overcast and beige. Rupturing the quotidian is a sudden violence and passion that culminates into a genuinely suspenseful and effecting waiting game.There are quibbles with some awkward tangibles and the friction of some interactions chafe against the sheer elegance of its presentation from typography to UI but in less than a feature length film I found myself invested in the cleaning up of someone else's apartment, wanting more fictional television and knowing the depths of a character's psyche.Hell, it's worth it for the utterly charismatic materials and lighting alone.

Had to go grab a mouse to operate the gun lol. I was looking forward to this game for a long time so I'm happy to be able to play it :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's three in the afternoon, I'm stoned, I'm hungry but I don't feel like cooking or cleaning. I pick up a slice of pizza off the floor and eat it. But enough about my life, I have some thoughts on this game to share.Short experimental game that is surprisingly affecting for how short and simple it is. A relatively mundane setting and set of verbs makes the moments of tension and violence feel that much more shocking. The visuals really bring it to life, every detail of the apartment exudes personality and the lighting is gorgeous. The devs have said they plan on releasing more shortform games like this and I'm excited to see what else they come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: The Sims expansion you've always dreamed about! Taking the dramatic moments to the next level! LOL. ok ok I jest, but this is actually a fun little Sims-like game.You play as Arthur, someone who was laid off a few weeks ago and has been holed up in his apartment everyday doing nothing. The game lets you play three days of his life. You control Arthur like a character in Sims, he can cook, take shower, use toilet, making coffee, watching pxrn on the computer, eating dinner while watching tv after shooting somebody. That last part is not in Sims but it sure as heck is in this game! Like I said, taking the dramatic moments to the max. There are character dialogue cutscenes that unfolds each day to tell the story between Arthur and other characters in the game.The game can be completed in about 90 minutes to 120 minutes. My first run I encountered a bug where the gun disappeared after cooking/eating meal, which eventually caused me getting a bad ending since my gun was gone. Had to replay the whole game. I was thinking about leaving a negative review because of this, but this game was really fun up to that particular point. So I'd still give this game a positive, recommended review.2nd time playing the game since I knew what to do, the game could be completed with about 60 minutes. The trick of passing time faster is to tell Arthur watch pxrn on the computer all day, which makes him sleepy, and then he can go to bed, sleep, and the game time passes way faster that way.if you like this game, I recommend checking out "12 Minutes"Like I said, a wild little Sims-like, slice of life game. Recommended, 7.1/10
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game! Brought back so many memories of playing Remedy games as a child. It can be finished in one sitting but the depth to the characters, story and environment makes it something I will be replaying many times. Glad to be hearing the director/developer of this title wants to create many more of these short story experiences. I think that is what the world needs more of these days. Highly recommend adding this to your collection if you enjoy the type of melancholic titles that are comfy and can be enjoined on a rainy day whilst sipping a cup of coffee.
_childDocuments_.name: Apartment Story

_childDocuments_.review: I mean this in a positive way, this is a perfect game to chill out to. Yes, it's advertised as a thriller but there's a lot of down time where you can kinda just relax and interact with a lot of what's inside the titular apartment. The amount of stuff you can interact with is pretty wild considering how short the game is. How much enjoyment you get from the down time is dependent on how much you like SIMS-style character management but I dug it! I experienced a few glitches here and there (being unable to pick up an item again after I set it down somewhere, and being stuck for a little more than a while trying to turn off a light because there was an item in front of it). Nothing game breaking by any means, but worth mentioning. TLDR: I recommend it! A good, short game for a great price with an interesting story, replay-ability, chill soundtrack, and visuals I really dig.

name: Late Shift
detailed_description: DISCORD CHANNEL ABOUT THIS GAME Late Shift is a realistic horror serial killer escape simulator. _childDocuments_.review: Introduction: In the vast and ever-evolving landscape of video games, it’s often the simplest concepts that capture our attention and imagination. “Nut,” a clicker game available on Steam, epitomizes this notion. At first glance, it may seem like a trivial and absurd endeavor, but beneath its simplistic exterior lies a surprisingly engaging and community-driven experience.Gameplay: “Nut” is, at its core, a clicker game where the primary objective is to click on a nut. Each click increments a counter, and every few hours, players are rewarded with a digital nut image. These images, created by the community through the game’s official Discord server, add a layer of charm and uniqueness to the game. The simplicity of the gameplay is both its strength and its weakness. While it lacks the depth and complexity of more traditional games, it excels in providing a low-effort, high-reward experience that can be enjoyed in short bursts.Visuals and Sound: The visual presentation of “Nut” is minimalistic, with a dark yellow background and a prominently displayed nut. The lack of intricate graphics or detailed animations might be seen as a drawback, but it aligns perfectly with the game’s straightforward nature. The sound design is equally minimal, with subtle clicks accompanying each interaction. This understated approach ensures that the game remains unobtrusive, allowing players to engage with it passively while multitasking.Community and Social Interaction: One of the standout features of “Nut” is its vibrant and active community. The game’s official Discord server serves as a hub for players to share their nut images, discuss strategies, and participate in design submissions. This sense of community fosters a collaborative environment where players feel connected and invested in the game’s ongoing development. The community-driven aspect of “Nut” is a testament to the power of social interaction in enhancing the gaming experience.Monetization and Value: While “Nut” is free to play, it incorporates a unique monetization model where players can buy and sell digital nut images for real money. This feature has contributed to the game’s popularity, as players are drawn to the potential for financial gain. However, it’s important to approach this aspect with caution, as the value of these digital items is highly speculative and may not be sustainable in the long term.Conclusion: “Nut” may not be the most groundbreaking or innovative game on the market, but its unexpected rise to fame on Steam proves that simplicity can be a powerful tool in the gaming industry. The game’s minimalistic design, coupled with its engaging community and unique monetization model, creates an experience that is both entertaining and thought-provoking. Whether you’re a seasoned gamer looking for a lighthearted distraction or a newcomer seeking a low-effort entry point into the world of clicker games, “Nut” offers a delightfully absurd experience that is worth exploring.

name: Stranded Deep
detailed_description: TEST YOUR SURVIVAL SKILLS IN THIS OPEN WORLD ADVENTURE In the aftermath of a mysterious plane crash, you are stranded in the vast expanse of the Pacific Ocean. Alone, without any means to call for help, you must do what you can to survive. BUILD. CRAFT. SURVIVE. ESCAPE. Explore underwater and on land as you hunt for supplies to craft the tools, weapons, and shelter you’ll need to stay alive. Stay sharp: hunger, thirst, and exposure conspire against you as you brave treacherous elements and the dangerous creatures of the Pacific. Live long enough, Stay Alive! Health, Hunger, Thirst, and sunstroke. Manage and monitor these vitals through an interactive survival watch. Cure poisons, heal broken bones, and bandage bleeding to stay alive. Spears, Axes, Bows, Spearguns, and so much more can all be crafted through an interactive crafting menu or by the quick-craft selection wheel. Items in your inventory and on the ground around you can all be crafted into something useful. Harvesting, Craftsmanship, Cooking, Physical, and Hunting can all be levelled up for maximum efficiency or to unlock different crafting combinations. With dozens of tiers and building pieces to choose from; craft your very own home away from home. From a weak and flimsy palm frond shack to a solid clay brick house. Customise your own raft with sails, canopies, storage, anchors, boat motors, and more. If sailings not for you - fly in style by constructing a gyrocopter! Explore the procedurally generated world with no two islands the same. Dive for sunken shipwrecks, abandoned shelters from previous survivors, or search for rare sea creatures like whales. Build and manage your farm with water management and plant growth cycles. Hunt, Fish, Trap, and Skin animals for food or kill to insert your dominance over the pacific islands. If you’re looking for a challenge then take on one of the three bosses to obtain a wall trophy and a very important reward. Unlock Steam achievements! Compare statistics with your friends from the in-game leaderboards for whose the best survivor. Play online or split screen co-op modes! Customise your world through the map island editor. Play as Female or Male. Change your game difficulty. Play split-screen co-op, and so much more! Create your own custom island and add it to your survival world! Hand sculpt the terrain and manually place each individual tree, rock, and creature to create the adventure island you want! You can even share it with your friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep was released on January 23, 2015, in Early Access. It is now May 5, 2022, and this game is still in Early Access. The latest update from the developers was January 10, 2022.There are probably a number of reasons Stranded Deep is still in Early Access, 7 years later, but at least it has recently been updated. Hopefully they will continue to update this game in the near future, because it definitely needs fixes.If you enjoy survival games or have never played a survival game, I highly recommend this game. This is my favorite survival game out of several. I enjoyed The Forest, (looking forward to Sons of the Forest), I enjoy playing Green Hell, and so far I enjoy Night of the Dead, which is also an Early Access game. Stranded Deep is at the top for me because I love the ocean, swimming, aquatic life, and long walks on the beach........ :D*crickets* No? Ok. I'll just get my coat, but before I do that, let me explain this game a bit more. Think of the movie Cast Away, starring Tom Hanks and Helen Hunt. No iceskate and several islands to explore.While playing Stranded Deep, it is not as difficult as Green Hell, in my opinion. Stranded Deep does not require as much from the player, as Green Hell does. Originally Stranded Deep required the player to sleep, in the first days upon its release, if I'm not mistaken. The developers removed the Sleep requirement and left the following Vitals: Health, Hunger, Thirst and Sunlight (SPF). The player will build their Hunting, Cooking, Harvesting, Physical, and Craftsmanship skills, throughout the game.The player will be able to hunt on the different islands, as well as go swimming, and hunt aquatic life. There are flora and fauna on the islands and in the ocean, with Sharks being the main threat while swimming or traveling. Oh yes, you will be fighting off sharks! If you have a fear of the ocean, wide open bodies of water, or sharks, this game will test your fears. It is a good way to overcome them though. You just have to jump in and face the threats sometimes. As long as you are smart about how you do that, you can survive. After a while, it will be nothing for you to jump into the deep blue that is the ocean, and all you'll need to do is figure out how to not drown with the giant set of weights hanging between your legs.One of the many fun parts about this game is the player can build their home about as much as they like, as long as they keep up with their health and resources. I have been pretty creative with the homes I have built on the islands. The player can also fish with a fishing rod or go spear fishing, in every sense of the activity. They can build tools, weapons, and other items to help hunt, fight off aggressive animals, and even provide shelters. The player can even create gardens on islands, and grow their own food or plants like Aloe, which can help with protection from the sun. The player can build rafts too, and dare I say, maybe even a flying machine. ;)Another cool feature is the day and night cycle, and the storms that players can encounter while on islands, or even out on the ocean or while swimming. I just wish the day/night cycle could be manually adjusted, or at least make the daytime a bit longer. It always seemed like the nighttime in the game was longer.The best part about this game is that players can now game online together (2 player cooperative). Originally the game was singleplayer or shared co-op, where two players could play split screen co-op. Last fall, the developers added online cooperative capability. My friend and I played through the game on co-op, and were able to complete the game. There is an ending in singleplayer and cooperative. Both modes' endings are the same, however, there are downsides to this. First, upon completion of the game in co-op mode, only the host will receive the achievement(s)/trophies for completing the game, as well as for not using the compasses throughout the entire game. I was the host and my friend was the co-op partner. He could not initiate the game ending, but I could. After I initiated the ending sequence, I was the only one out of both of us who received the achievements for completion of the game, and for not using compasses. However, I accidentally held one in my hand during movement of supplies, and we both used the Gyrocopter which also has a compass on it. I am uncertain if the 'Magnets, how do they work?' achievement/trophy is working properly or not. So, be aware that if you are the co-op partner who joined a game with a host, you may not get either of those two achievements/trophies. Hopefully the developers at Beam Team Games, as well as the Beam Team Publisher, will fix the listed issues soon enough.The only real negative experience my friend and I encountered while playing co-op, was he would be disconnected quite often. I believe that the co-op partner is subject to client disconnection issues, regardless of where they are located, their PC or console, and internet connection. If you decide to watch any of my livestreams of our co-op adventures on Stranded Deep, you will see that he was disconnected more often than not. This was very irritating not only for him, but for me too, as this wasted a lot of time. Sometimes we would have to exit the game entirely and attempt joining again. DO NOT FORGET TO SAVE YOUR GAMES IF YOU ARE THE HOST. It is safe for both people to save their games, but the host especially needs to save the games. The disconnection issues were random. There did not appear to be any particular reason that would explain why he was disconnected. This issue is apparently quite common, as I have seen other people encounter it, while watching their gaming videos as well. So just be aware of the above issues. Singleplayer did not appear to have any online connection issues like that. Only while playing cooperative.Even with the irritating co-op partner connection issues, I still recommend this survival game before others. I am still playing it to this day, but we will probably wait until the developers create a fix for the connection issues, before we play co-op on Stranded Deep again.Also, if you like the music in the game, you can either purchase it through Steam, or get the soundtrack from Amazon Music. The music is fitting for the setting and I really enjoyed it. It has that sense of danger when sharks are around, but also adds a sense of happiness when fishing, swimming or building. It even has a sense of loneliness when it's dark outside, when you're alone, etc. but in a good way, as the music adds to the overall emotion of the game.Overall, Stranded Deep is amazing and the price of $15.00 U.S. is worth it for what you receive, along with its Early Access issues. It's still an Early Access game, so give the developers credit and the benefit of the doubt. I understand making video games is no easy task, but if they're still updating it like they did back in January, we just need to be patient with them. I will not spoil anything but the ending was interesting. I am curious to know what made the developers go the direction they went with this game, and whether or not a Stranded Deep 2 will be in the works. Obviously they still have a lot of work to do to resolve bugs and glitches with this game, but I am not opposed to a sequel. :)Buy this game and play it in singleplayer for a while, and then determine whether you enjoy it or not. I believe anyone would enjoy this game, if they give it a chance. I am glad I saw my friend had it on his wishlist, and that it was co-op. That is what made me purchase the game, even though at the time it was only shared/split screen co-op. This game is amazing and has a lot of potential to still be even better. Play it and record the issues you encounter, then report them to the developers. We can all work together to help make Stranded Deep even more awesome and adventurous. Lastly, don't forget your swimsuit. You're gonna need a bigger boat.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we are again with another Early Access Alpha release ( and review ) on Steam, lol!  This review will be rather long as most people want more of an analysis to base their purchasing decision on instead of just: "This game rocks! 10/10 would get stranded again!"  I've only played about 6hrs so far and as much as I would recommend this game I would also NOT recommend it.  Let me explain:  The controls, at least for me, are flawless and I haven't noticed any issues so far although it takes a bit to get the scheme down.  The graphics aren't groundbreaking but nontheless acceptable and the animations are smooth.  The crafting system if pretty intuitive and easy to use, instead of dragging and dropping like DayZ and going through an animation you have to manually move and manipulate the items OUTSIDE your inventory and the system is not too picky about whats on the ground as a small menu will pop up and show you what you can build with what you have in your pile and you can drop more craftable items in your pile to craft other stuff.  There isn't a lot going on at once onscreen since you are, ya know, stranded in the middle of the South Pacific with dozens of islands all around you in just about every direction.  Most islands are small with a few larger ones here and there but YOU WILL run out of resources on your little island getaway and will be forced to get out in your raft and explore the other islands and the sea for sunken ships and other very useful items.  There is a way to make a motor for your raft to GO A HELLEVA LOT FASTER than paddling along between islands at half the speed of smell but you will do metric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of paddling just to find all the gear and loot you need to have fun with the game and its system.  I mean, IT IS a game about being stranded and surviving but I hope for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they speed up the paddling, it gets REALLY boring paddling for ever to get to the next island, but what are ya gonna do, ya know?  Anyway, if the devs keep on it and keep improving upon the mechanics and the crafting system and add new elements and depth it will be a fantastic game, especially if they somehow eventually incorporate multiplayer into it.  So far I haven't found a map or anything in game that helps you navigate around the island or helps you get back to your HOME ISLAND, I suppose since every game is different that would be a tad difficult to put in.  However, if you find the blue compass for the love of GabeN don't lose it!  It is like the "Wilson" of Stranded Deep!  Happy Gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just pure fun, joy, relaxation, and intense moments. Here is a shining example of this. Started a new game, did the usual resource gathering, exploring the world, wreck diving. Found a bunch of useful stuff, and made a speargun and some ammo for it. Then I quickly put together a small wooden raft with a sail. Looking at my food supplies, crap we are super low on food, coconuts have all been picked and eaten... I need real food! Lets go shark hunting! I launch my brand new sailboat raft and equip my speargun and i sail around my island until I spot a tiger shark. This will be a perfect meal. I take aim and fire a few arrows into the shark. It gets super mad. It takes a run at me and nudges my boat. Silly shark, I think to myself... you can't get me im on a boat! Hit him with another arrow. He gets mad and hits my boat again. I'm laughing at the shark for hitting my boat instead of swimming away! Then all of a sudden, the shark slams my boat and flips me off of it!!!! I didn't even know that could happen! Now I am panicking! I am in deep water, my raft is upside down and this shark is hella mad at me! I start swimming for shore, but its further away than I thought. This can't be happening... The shark gets me. He does worse things to me than I ever did to him. I die. Game is amazing.

The majority of the "building" consists of zero creativity, you can pretty much only gather items to craft preset structures or items and place them on the ground.  Apparently you have a bit of creativity in how you can build a base later, but since it doesn't really serve any purpose as far as survival, it ends up being a pointless waste of time and resources anyway.  The game seems like it should appeal to me, and they even finally added co op which is great, but certain resources are so limited that it breaks down to just trying to find enough fiber to keep 2 people alive the whole time, which isn't fun.  I wanted to like the game but after playing it for a while I just found that I was extremely bored and didn't want to continue playing anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: STRANDED DEEP is a fairly decent game and has so much going for it. The maker(s) of this game could or should use real life as inspiration for the game. The beginning of the game is decent but the player has little to no things to do before the plane crashes. Maybe they could add a layer or two of emotion to the game. Give the player the ability to talk in the beginning with his family on his cell phone and after he hangs up thats when the airplane goes down. Maybe even show the flight attedant get sucked out of the plane. The player should have more options for your floatation device after hitting the water. With the right coding and programmimg from the right people with expertise, this game could be the ultimate survival game. The infinite lighter and flashlight don't exist but not in Stranded Deep. You could have an option to make time even slower in the game. Slowing it down by half or quarter. When you first land on your first island there should be random wreckage from your plane with random items to help you survive in the beginning. Gathering those itmes for later use. I.E. water bottles, medical stuff, and especially food (Airline food). There should also be a desperation mode. When your gauge reaches a certain level of being deprived you start to open up more options for foods and liquids. Because once the game updates and adds animals, bugs, and critters, etc... you should only be able to eat them when your level of desperation is high enough. Because if you think about it, why would a person go automatically to eating rats and roaches and bugs when they only got to a secluded island. When you have actual rations you could eat first. Now say its day 5 or 10 and you are low on rations. Your deprive mode bumps up a notch and your menu opens up options to drink shark blood or eat food raw. This bypassing the need to cook stuff when you are clearly unable to because you are too far from the island you had all your stuff on. Another idea( since there are thousands of randomly Generated  boat wrecks.) When not give the player the ability to scrap the boat wood and materials to remove and carry to the island and to use for building things. There are many things updates can do to improve the game but these are just a few.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like survival games but are getting bored of those bland generic survival horror titles? *cough cough* (I'm looking at you every zombie game in existence). WELL THEN, JUST BUY STRANDED DEEP. It's like Cast Away the movie but with 100% less Tom Hanks! This game is amazing, there are a few mechanics that are possibly too hard on the player and some too easy... let's begin with the easy:-Crabs. Essentially an unlimited, respawning food source. I'm not sure how they respawn but I usually leave a few behind from each cluster and a few days later harvest all the new ones. Food really is no issue with crabs. -Buckets? I've found a bucket on my first island every play through. It's infinite water essentially - I like how it works (except holding the bucket over a fire is essentially impossible because my character always holds the damn thing sideways) I think the spawning of them is perhaps too common though. -Land. This is a weird critique but due to the fact that with a bucket and a crab collony you can last forever - it gives no reason to leave the island. Having no threats on land made me a lot less willing to leave and actually face off against sharks. Now let's discuss some of the harder elements: -Storage. Why is there no mechanic to store my food neatly somewhere? I'd really like a table to place my possesions on in my house. In general I'm hoping the building mechanics are fleshed out a bit (of course for the game being in pre-alpha they have done a lot but this is just a suggestion for future). Whilst on the topic: windows and dissasembling placed structures. Too many times have I had to destroy something because it didn't snap to a corner properly. - Navigation. There's a generic 'island in the distance' model I've noticed. Thus you have no idea how far away each island is and at a distance there is no possible way to tell them apart. The compass can be looted but good luck without it. I don't mind the rafts being slow- but the issue of direction and distance needs to be addressed. -resource. The islands are tiny, and thus run out of resource very fast - this encourages you to leave the island. I like this mechanic but could we get a little diversity? maybe islands of significant different size? With this issue of Islands being light-years apart and navigation being as tricky as it is, it's really difficult to actually explore. (Big Islands Mod - Uploaded by I-o-IPositive7, fixes this issue - but makes the resources too plentiful - I would recommend an inbetween). -Storage - Again. How are you supposed to take resource back to your island if you only have 8 slots? if you're going to survive there for a while you're at least going to need 2-3 tools like a lighter, Machette, and Spear. You will also need a bucket and the paddle to move the raft. that's at least half your space gone on items too valuable to throw away. If you were building a house this is way too inefficient. Could we PLEASE get a way to store some items on the boat. That pretty much addresses all my main issues, I love this game thus far and see it as a game with incredible potential. NOTE: I UNDERSTAND THIS IS IN ALPHA STAGES - I WANTED TO MAKE SOME SUGGESTIONS AS TO WHAT COULD BE IMPLEMENTED IN FUTURE UPDATES. a it currently stands I love what I have to play with maybe 8/10 knowing that the game is yet to b completed. Would reccommend to friends.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS AN EARLY ACCESS REVIEW! IF THE GAME IS OFFICIALLY OUT, I WILL REPOST THIS REVIEW WITH A PROPER 'FINAL' VERDICT. I WILL ONLY TALK ABOUT THE GAMEPLAY ITSELF, NOT GLITCHES, BUGS OR ANYTHING OF THE SORT. THANK YOU AND READ ON!...I know what I have to do now. I gotta keep breathing. Because tomorrow the sun will rise. Who knows what the tide could bring?  That line from Castaway somewhat helps me explain my thoughts on Stranded Deep. A procedurally generated world filled with numerous islands seperated by miles of ocean, hungry sharks, and duct tape.Like Rust and The Forest, Stranded Deep is about survival. You start on a plane, learn the crafting mechanics, and then your plane crashes into the ocean, leaving you...well, stranded. You now spend your days and nights building shelter, fighting sharks, and finding parts to make an engine...that's about all you can do at this point, unfortunately...The game itself is visually impressive, being as realistic looking as possible, aside from one or two minor issues like the fact that you don't atually have a shadow...You have a wide variety of items to craft in the game to help you survive, giving you options to advance further than you thought you might be able to. The first time I built a raft and found out I could attach a motor to it, I spent hours simply looking for the parts to make it!The number of items in the game is impressive, and since this is an Early Access game, more will hopefully be added to better flesh out the experience. Same goes for the variety of wildlife you come across. And while games like Rust allow you to build massive skyscrapers with ease, I'm glad that in Stranded Deep it requires a lot more work given the difference in resource scarcity. I'm usually not a fan of having no resources, but for some reason I don't mind so much in this game.The game is fun to play, and while my only wish is they add a multiplayer feature, I feel it's moving well into the direction of a wonderful open world survival game.Hey, thanks for reading this review, and please let me know if you liked it! I like doing this sort of this, and want to do more! Also, check out some of my other reviews if you want some new games! Thanks again!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is immersive and thrilling, combining the tranquility of an island escape with the terror of the deep unknown. After approximately 10 hours of play I have experienced a lot of what the game has to offer such as the overwhelming sense of isolation, the desperation that pushes you to be resourceful and frugal with your supplies, and the great atmosphere created in the presence of wildlife such as sharks. On a more technical note, there are many bugs (which is to be expected of an alpha) which do cause minor frustration. Many have been rectified since the update (28/1/15) however mechanics such as climbing and jumping do become troublesome, especially when your character is trapped within a ship wreck. Furthermore the collisions on the fire effect should perhaps be dealt with as most objects place on a basic camp fire often gain a life of their own. Other than these minor detials, the most I can hope for is a slightly more detailed tutorial on lesser functions such as maintaining your health (without disrupting the overall tone of the game of course). I highly recommend this game even in its early stages, keep up the good work!

_childDocuments_.review: This game had potential to become a much more popular and successful game. In this game title you are stranded deep in an indie game with limited procedurely generated islands of very small size and variety. The elements of this game which stand out most are exploration, and resource management. This game has some meaningful references to the Thomas Jeffrey Hanks film "Cast Away" and  I feel there is even more room for pop movie references in this game i.e. a pirate ship with hungry Somalian pirates, a large Joe Versus The Volcano island with primitive soda drinking natives and a rescue ending which ends in "The Terminal" at an airport. These are good ideas for promoting this game, however there are some serious flaws in this game which could easily be repaired. I hope that the developers maintain their support, innovation, build good reputation, and create a following of gamers. Good support and follow through is what separates popular games like Minecraft from lesser titles such as Unturned and Castle Miner Z. Stranded Deep is decent in it's gestation period at $10-$15 USD. If they decide to create DLC's for this game I will be quite interested in purchasing those as well. If this game expands in variety and goes multiplayer Co-op, I will be both fantastically impressed and avidly promotional about this game in steam community and youtube. Make a great game guys! If you build it...they will come :)

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't spent as much time on this game as others and, having said this, I currently have a difficult time recommending this game. I thought that the trailer showed promise and I wanted a newer title in the survival genre, so I chose this over many other options. Having done so, I am greatly disappointed.The graphics are mediocre but functional from a technical standpoint, as are the gameplay mechanics, controls, etc. Unfortunately, functional isn't the only factor to consider. Each island looks nearly identical to the last; each tree is virtually the same; a shipwreck encountered early on is a near duplicate of every other one from that point on. In terms of gameplay, each action is repititious. Swim, then swim some more; row your raft for a half an hour, then explore a tiny island. While on the island, collect wood, coconuts, and other materials, then repeat the entire process.With no variety, bland environments (not just graphically, but interactively and intellectually), and little to do other than gather resources and avoid the sharks - which I'll admit, is a thrilling part of this title - this game is clearly a game in the works at best. A great start and concept that will need severe overhaulilng for veteran gamers to enjoy.TL;DR-------Repetive and boring, this game should be skipped over in favor for other, much better survival titles.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really hardcore, really fun and really compelling. It takes time to build your confidence and your supplies, but when you start to venture out and dive for loot you will start to really enjoy the process. With a minimalist interace and an intuitive crafting system, this game really immerses you in the experience of being a castaway. At first you will stay on the first island you find, but as your resources dwindle you will have to venture out onto the open sea in search of another island to plunder. With limited room in your backpack you will need to make hard decisions about what to take on each voayge, and more importantly, what to bring back to your home island. Without the ability to navigate at first, you will have to get creative so as to avoid becoming lost. I made sure that I chopped down a palm tree on each island I visted and pointed the trunk towards my home island. This saved my bacon a few times when shark attacks spun me around so many times I lost my bearings, and when fog completely obscured my view whilst at sea. When I found the compass on one lucky dive I began mapping my environs on paper and now have a detailed map of many islands and wrecks. I can't really describe how much fun this game is. There are no goals beyond staying alive through eating, drinking and maintaining your health. The slow trickle of items you salvage will add to your resilence and allow you to mount focused missions with specific tools. It's a sandbox experience that you control.

_childDocuments_.review: If you think you will enjoy the tropical scenery, the peaceful sounds of waves and campfires, and the mostly sunny and occasional rainy days that come along with the climate, you will enjoy the game.  Start off small with nothing but a raft and your tattered business attire, and keep your hydration and hunger and rest at an acceptable level to maintain your life. Beyond the scramble of the beginning days, you can build a rough home and base, sailing rafts, explore oil platforms, fish for small fish, rays, and sharks and smoke up your prizes, and enjoy being away from the hustle and bustle of the city. What's not to love? Every month or so (in real life time) you get a new addition to spice up the game. Hopefully they will add multiplayer or some rescue scenarios in the future, but the game is smooth and enjoyable for a pastime. Don't worry about the negative reviews. If you think you have an interest in the game, it may not be for everyone but if you are a patient and outdoor minded individual, go ahead and enjoy the experience. It will continue to grow and develop, so your investment isn't short lived.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance I thought this to be quite a serene setting; beautiful sea water stretching for miles around, warm sunshine beating down on a sandy island, complete isolation, and zero stress.Oh, how wrong was I.There are only so many resources on your starter island, which means sooner or later, you'll have to paddle out. Here I thought it was a quick island hop across some deep water. Little did I know that suddenly all sharks have become JAWS (which is a little ridiculous, but I'm willing to give in to a little fantasy here). So where a leisurely paddle across to island number 2, becomes a frantic race as the shark bumps your raft so you land in the water and it can eat you. If you are bumped off and find yourself in the water, be prepared for some wonderful bugs such as; not being able to get back in the raft, not being able to swim properly, and who can forget this classic: watching your raft literally fly away in the sky as its bumped a mere one time by the ever powerful JAWS shark.Early Access or not, it IS a good game and has a lot of potential. If you're looking for fast and great content updates however, it's not the game for you.The islands are too far apart.A lot of the physics needs changing.The sharks, if we're to keep them JAWS sharks, need to piss off after a few hours; I've never seen a shark wait three days and two nights circling a tiny spot of water waiting for me to leave. Without rest.It needs more variety; the only island dwelling wildlife are crabs. I also find it strange that only potatoes grow on this island, and disappointed I'm unable to make chips.All in all, I'd give it a rather too generous 7/10. Too many bugs, but has potential. Just need proper, meaty updates to actually happen. Maybe delay buying until then.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that could have been something special but will never reach it's potential due to it's developers.I'm going to recommend this game but be warned as it lacks in many QoL areas and has been out for 6 years now with no signs of any fixes.Below are examples.The game freezes multiple times when it gets to the "press enter" screen resulting in you having to restart the game until Poseidon decides you're worthy to play.The crafting menu is clunky - new players will struggle to navigate the multiple pages that are only accessible by clicking on text that doesn't always correlate to what is being shown.The inventory system is poor - You will inevitably end up crafting something you didn't want to (and waste resources) because you thought you had to click to begin crafting when for some reason releasing the c key (crafting menu) while hovering over an item causes you to begin crafting... That's right, releasing the c key to back out of the crafting menu will cause you to craft whatever item was highlighted anyway. Combat is primitive - Spears are great early game but unless your foe is sat on your lap you aren't going to be able to hit it without it hitting you first. Throwing them is the only viable option really.Damage / Balancing - Water and Food constantly deplete too quickly, while you can take about 15-20 hits from sharks before dying. Even if you manage to kill a shark, which is rather easy since they don't deal a lot of damage, you will get 3 large food from them which will last you maybe a day and half... a day and half food from an entire shark!!You will become familiar with the following:"The code you entered doesn't exist"Constant Disconnects - Happens to only the person joining, not hosting.Item Duplication - 1 Water Still turned into 4 and walked itself to the other side of the island.Inventory Wipes upon loading into save - DROP ALL ITEMS BEFORE YOU SAVE!Null Inventory - You end up with an item in your Inv that you can't use / don't really have then a message pops up asking you to contact the Developers because "It shouldn't happen".Honestly I don't know what's least likely...Your character escaping, orThe developers pulling their finger out.update... introduce bugs... patch... breaks something else... update...

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I can only speak to the single player experience, but I had a great time playing through the story. I loved the atmosphere and felt like the game delivered well on a real sense of aloneness and desolation. Occasionally I cursed myself when I'd get lost for days, capsized and sunburned, but ultimately I think it really added to the experience.Generally the graphics are decent, there are some ugly models (the bushes...) and a sometimes a bit more jankiness than I'd hope for (you ever see a tree shoot hundreds of feet into the air after you cut it down?), but I didn't run into anything gamebreaking.The ocean itself is truly gorgeous. The colors, textures, and sense of depth you get as the weather and light throughout the day change continually impressed me. I loved watching the sun go down accompanied by the sound of creaking ropes and the water lapping at my raft, all alone in the middle of nowhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of those games that I was most looking forward to when it first gleamed in front of the crosshairs of the average gamer. It had  immersion, you  as though you were stranded with nothing but a few survival tools and a cool yellowish dingy. You wanted to feel as though you were Tom Hanks, with your own personal Wilson, trying to beat the odds.Most of the recent reviews try to zone in on one thing, . , but they’re insignificant in expanding gameplay. Let me explain what I mean: When you put yourself in the limelight as these developers have done, through the medium of the early access, you become accountable to the end user. The downfall of Stranded Deep is, or will most likely be, that it cannot cope with the demand for growth; new updates that pull you in to keep playing, the survival aspect is not there to be able to fulfil this for the average player; there’s no tension.  Having returned after playing this game since it first came out, I can still say that the game looks even cooler. The islands are now saturated with more detail, they’re closer together, and they’re bigger.  Putting the glitches and bugs to one side, given that it was the experimental version, I found no new tools or weapons, or new building possibilities. No new gameplay mechanics or ideas. The shipwrecks are everywhere and there are no new food sources; except maybe a few fish.  Given that this was one of my most anticipated games, I feel the future for stranded deep is an uncomfortable one. The addition of a possible co-op mode will not constitute a revival of this game, because you find that you very rarely feel uncomfortable, and it’s this uncomfortableness that drives the gameplay. There’s no end in sight, the development may take years for any substantial gameplay to exist, and so unless you really want to support the developers, and I mean , then .

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is not a bad game. Its actually one of my favorite single player survival games (im not counting remote play together. that is not a substitute for online multiplayer and its laughable that the devs treat it like it is) The idea, setting, and gameplay are all good for the most part. The issue with stranded deep is the developer. Its been in early access for 6 years now with very long periods of silence from the devs and inconsistent updates. for a while i thought that Stranded Deep was dead, or at least i did until the devs stabbed their PC playerbase in the back. They ported the unfinished, unpolished game to consoles for a cash grab and then proceeded to create and release poorly planned, rushed, time exclusive content to consoles that does not make sense or fit the game so they could claim that the game had a half assed ending. They finally got around to releasing the content for their PC playerbase (who make up most of the sales of their game btw, we funded the company by buying this game) but its the fact that they treated their PC players as second class citizens. If this game was the developers priority it would have been out of early access a long time ago, they made more than enough money through PC sales alone (youre welcome Beam Team) and have had more than enough time to fund a team of extra devs and finish the game. If you want to buy the game because you just enjoy survival games then by all means purchase stranded deep, like i said its a fun game. But dont expect the game to go much farther than it already is, its been 6 years and the game is still relatively the same save for the previously mentioned "ending" and a couple of untimely bug fixes. If you dont want to support lazy ungrateful developers that treat their primary playerbase like garbage then dont bother wasting your hard earned money this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I came back to this game after YEARS of not playing it, but I saw that they had released it into 1.0. Which I thought would be a good thing, IT WAS NOT. The game was 100% better a couple years ago. Since then they've managed too break the enemy physics where I had a flying boar attacking me from the sky and the occasional giant crab hovering towards me menacingly, both problems occur at just the slightest of hills. plus when you kill a shark they either INSTANTLY re-spawn OR you can now have two sharks per Isle. Which completely negates the "grace period" you used to get after killing a shark that you could then use to explore local shipwrecks. The sharks are OVERLY aggressive now to the point that attempting to dive when one is around is impossible without getting hit, or just bitten and carried off. Unlike before where you could kind of sneak around them and still dive with relative safety. The worst part of all that is that, if i throw a spear at one of them, half the time it bounces off and then just vanishes through the ground and the same thing happens with my arrows which aren't cheap. I don't know what happened to the spears and arrows just sticking into an enemy but that needs to come back. There are limited resources and having to waste TONS on just defending myself is making the game FAR more grindy and risky than it already is. Lastly I just want to note, I put these 170 hours into it about two years ago and earlier. I've been playing since you could use palm trees as an areoplane, so i know that the game has had some rough physics. But having enemies that are essentially the terminator with fins or legs that can also fly, makes me just surprised the sharks aren't flying again like they used to too. Plus the items that just disappeared on me wasting time and precious materials, makes it so I can't recommend the game because every fight you have will be at a loss. Overall after coming back to the game for the first time in years, I ended up just turning it off out of frustration after only getting to my second island. I wouldn't recommend this game any more thanks to this release, I might come back in a year or two and try it again. But being roughed up as I have been and having this game essentially waste my night, I don't think I'd want too without the devs releasing a statement that they've cleared this jank up. The games hard enough, it didn't need flying boars and crabs, while your weapons vanish out of thin air too.

Case in point, getting stuck less than 10 minutes in under the side of the floating metal rig outside the first thing.  Can't blame me for wanting to leave the first island without going through everything first but then I cannot access the boat/raft from being stuck on the underside of it and no way to access the menu either.  So basically stuck.  Making it easier to communicate what I'm thinking in my head to the commands given to me and allowing me to easily pick up items, have easy access to read and understand the tools and hud around me, and always having access to a menu is definitely a worthwhile thing.  Can't say I recommend quite yet, it's unique and gives a great perspective on the genre but in the end has a few more things to work out.  Will check back in and see how progress is made, not giving up hope yet for this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels really unfinishedI won't even say the game is bad, it's just really annoying to play.The content and the concept are fine, but the execution is sub par.1. Terrible inventory management systemYou can only hold about 8 unique items (maximum stacks of 4 of an item), which seems alright, except the basic items you need to take with you at all times add up to over half of that space, leaving you only being able to hold a few extra items while you're out exploring to find new resources. Normally you would want to find somewhere to dump all of the extra things you come across to make room for more, but for some reason a large crate holds less than half as much as your "backpack" and your pockets do. I say backpack like that because your character doesn't even appear to have an actual backpack. This also leads you to having many of these boxes thrown around your campsite because of how few items they hold. Also you should keep in mind that you found these boxes, you didn't craft them because of how tedious it is to find enough items to craft the ingredients required to craft whatever it is you need.Also the user interface for your inventory in general just kind of sucks2. ZERO indication on what some controls areWant to figure out how to drop an item? You've got to guess. Want to figure out how to bind a tool to a hotbar slot? Figure it out yourself (yes, I ended up having to search the internet to figure that one out). In most games there's a small UI in some corner of your display that shows your options for what you can do with an item in hand, but this game has nothing. The input controls menu in the settings doesn't help either.3. Frequent crashesThe game just doesn't want to keep running for some reason. I'll be a mile away from home on my life raft collecting items about to head back, and the game just gives up and freezes. And before anyone reading this assumes that I'm using a poor-spec system, I'll list them off for you:CPU: AMD R7 3700x (clocked at 4.4 GHz, liquid cooled)MB: Asus Strix x570-eMemory: 32GB (4 x 8GB) DDR4 @ 3600MHzGPU: Asus Strix 3070 8G OCStorage: Samsung 980 Pro 1TBThe game runs smoothly, but it just randomly stops working. Kind of sucks because you can't just save your progress anywhere.4. Sense of direction, but no indication of how to get thereObviously, as you've been stranded on an island (or several of them), your goal is to get off of them. The thing is, though, the game kind of just leaves you hanging after you've finished the very basic and unhelpful tutorial. Eventually if you wander enough you'll come across the aircraft carrier, which has a plane on it. The plane is broken, though, and you know you need parts to repair it, but if you get easily bored of slowly paddling a life raft for miles between islands, good luck finding those parts. All I see is more little islands with a few shipwrecks around them, all holding the same basic materials.I've given the game several chances to impress me or at least have me coming back to it, but I can't seem to enjoy it at all. I usually REALLY enjoy playing open world survival crafting games. I am a huge fan of Valheim, I have played Rust casually over several years, and I just finished The Forest (and LOVED it), which is why I came to this game. It had been sitting in my Steam library for about three or four years and I was looking for more in this genre after completing The Forest. Definitely didn't find what I was looking for in this one.

What it doesn't tell you is that the paddle is attached to the raft and you have to look at it, pick it up, and then press and hold E to paddle and control the life boat. Okay, let's assume E is the button to pick stuff up since that's what I used to paddle.  Oh, it is! BUT The item you picked up will stay in your hand and there is no button to put it down.  E doesn't work.  Left and right mouse button doesn't work.  Weird.  Will it work if I pick something else up with E? Nope.  Those items will go into the backpack.  Then there are Items that are highlighted with a name but I can't pick those up either.  That's fine, maybe I need a tool but I still have a rock in my hand!  And this is all while the controls are clunky as all heck.  The sensitivity is awful.  They want $20 for that? _childDocuments_.review: I love all these new survival type games, and Stranded Deep ticks all of my boxes. Deeply relaxing and satifsying, until your raft disappears in deep water and there's a Great White nibbling your shins. I can of course say there are things that the game doesn't have yet which I would like to see, but it would not be a criticism of the game, just suggestions for it. We all need to remember what 'early access' and 'alpha' means. As an early access game, however, I don't think I have ever played one so beautiful and so smooth. Directions I personally would like the game to go in, in the future: -Keep adapting the sea life, I personally find it so relaxing and fun to dive into the water (specially when it's this lush) and explore the marine life. I would like to see slightly less sharks, maybe other marine life that could do damage, I don't know what would seem plausable in the location but jellyfish, swordfish, manta rays, maybe an octopus if you go into the depths, dolphins, whales... etc. You get the point. Not in abundance, as so to 'clutter' the place, just in few numbers.-More crafting, I would imagine this would be already in the pipe-line but still worth a mention. Ability to make a larger raft perhaps, by connecting them together as you would a building. I wouldnt mind having some sort of storage chest too, because on these games I suddenly become a horder and like to have it organised, doesn't have to be complicated, just whatever you could realistically make from bits of wood and lashings. -Slightly larger inventory, or a craftable/findable tool belt. Don't get me wrong, I think a small inventory is definitely the right way to go, but by the time I've got my tools together, I pick up a few sticks and I have to carry them over to my 'crafting pile' because I'm out of space. I think a toolbelt would be the way to go personally, just a few lashings and palm fronds maybe, a rudimentary holder. -Sea birds, and throwable spears for catching them. This would give the game a whole new feel I think, add that extra little dimension to it, hearing the... cawing... or whatever on earth that sound is, waiting until they land on a palm tree and spearing that bugger right through it's cawing face hole. Because we love nature, but we also love to kill nature and eat nature. -Air drops paid for by micro-transactions. Just kidding. Seriously.............. NOOOOOOO-!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! One of the best survival games I have ever played! I'm pretty sure it's my #1 atm! It definitely still needs work. Some of the bugs can be SUPER annoying, but some are harmless, sometimes helpful, or just outrageously funny! For example: One moment you could be dropping items and an item just freezes in the air, and its not even the item you were supposed to be dropping. I've lost a few tools this way. Then there is one where, if you get a specific island that has a ship wreck in the perfect spot, you can lure sharks in between the island and the boat and they will bug out and just spin in circles providing you with simple and easy food that can restore a ton of your food bar. Then you have the funny bugs, like a random boar floating above the ocean or running around on a ship wreck under water, also had a funny one where the shark started to swim inside the island. It actually scared the shiz out of me sitting there and a shark just attacks me from under the sand. I'm now terrified of sand sharks xD But all together this is a fantastic survival game and i would completely recommend it! Just a little rough around the edges, but the principal and idea behind the game is just awesome! i love the water and fish physics this game has, other than a few bugs, the physics are almost spot on to real life! Great game to play with a buddy! so glad they added multiplayer co-op! Even though it's only up to 2 players, it's definitely a fun late night game with a buddy! Worth the purchase for sure! Can't wait to see what's in store for this games Official Release! 1.0 Here we come!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is intriguing and a fun take on the survivalists experience. It has a really fun looting and crafting system with a skill tree and leveling aspect to it. These are traits to making a fun, lasting experience. I rate the game 2 / 5 stars, and not 5 due to the subsequent reasons.The only caveat which caused my friends and I to stop playing a couple hours in was the total lack of probably the most important resource: fiber. Everything seems to need fiber, and your small island has a very small amount. You need fiber to do practically everything, even going to a new island that to find more fiber. You can plant the fiber trees, but it's level locked and to unlock it you need to craft a multitude of items that all need fiber. The plant plot also needs a bunch of fiber. The main issue with all this is it doesn't respawn, and you'll find at best 8 fiber pieces on your island. It baffles me seeing the store page images showing all that progression because I know for us it was impossible to progress due to lacking basic resources every playthrough.

Dev peeps, This section is just for you oooor I guess for anyone who wants to read it, idc. The chance a dev even reads this is slim to none, but! here we go. Building in this game could be so much more fun with three little changes;   - Plantable, growable trees to replenish wood supplies.  - Relaxing the overzealous "cannot build here" thing because you're a pixel too close to something, sometimes it's something not even visible.  - Bringing walls and stairs down about a brick to prevent the huge gaps for buildings more than one level tall before a roof section. This doesn't seem like a big deal until you want to build a lighthouse!There is a 4th which would be pretty easy to implement I think, (and this one's more for weirdos like me) give the garden plots an option with a key press or when selecting to build them to auto-level instead of matching terrain. _childDocuments_.review: Basically your plane crashes into the ocean and you end up stranded in a life boat, You find other islands to some what explore to find new resources that help you survive. The problems with Stranded Deep isn't the concept of the game but the lack of depth and content along with many other features it lacks but desperately needs.  New players will find themselves fustrated as they try to figure out how to collect resources which will lead you to outdated Wiki pages and Youtube videos that promise to tell you how to do it but are 20 mins in length of some guy just playing the game. Once you figure out how to collect the resources it becomes another challenge to use the water stills ect that you made, For a developer it must be simple but for a new player it can be difficult to learn so you'll find yourself drinking coconut milk over water because trying to figure out that water still while dien of thirst just doesn't seem worth it. Moving on once you get out in the ocean you may find yourself having a bit of motion sickness as the first person perspective with a boucing around boat can be a bit nauseating and this is something you will have to do quite a bit if you want to explore the world or search for items in ship wrecks. I can say that the game can be a bit scary as you explore ship wrecks in dark water while sharks lurk around every coral reef and even during the day this can be intense as a bright sunny day with clear waters can turn to night as a thunder storm rolls in while your under water which seems like great whites love to prey on you in these most intensive moments. Beyond that Stranded Deep seems to seriously be lacking content because once you build a home/farm and get pass the need to travel with a nicely built base the game just drops off into " Well this is boring... Let's go play something else" For that I can't really recommend stranded deep as you don't have any story pushing you forward with no real end goal other then to end up bored and quiting, Even castaway had an ending, a story for struggle. I think this game would of been great if you had a time limit of say an F5 Hurricane that will kill you if you don't get rescue before it shows up and this could of really driven the game forward as you frantically trying to build up so you can make the long journey to the main land as you watch the dark clouds come ever so closer. I think this would of made Stranded Deep a true fight for survival in a race against the clock then a boring lack luster game that it currently is.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is a new take on the building/survival genre by placing you in the mdist of an island chain in the Pacific Ocean with only a knife, a watch, and your wits to survive. After spending a little time with the game, here are some initial thoughts...The game looks graphically gorgeous, and runs great on ultra on my desktop. The atmosphere and ambience is just right, with a sense of true isolation. Animals move around very realistically and water effects, lighting effects, and shadows look wonderful. Obviously,  lot of love was put into the visuals.From a gameplay standpoint, this game is early access and still in very, very alpha. There are numerous bugs, but none of them have interfered with my enjoyment of the sandbox. Some of them have required me to restart the application from desktop, so saving your progress is important. There are also instances where I would be paddling my raft, and the raft would jump 10 feet ahead of me, leaving me in the water. The game is very bare bones right now, so don't expect a super deep experience in its current state from a building and crafting perspective. Exploring wrecks is fun and exciting, with a constant sense of danger from doing so. Managing your hunger, thirst, and helath requires careful planning, and finds you stockpiling food and drink, and requires you to go explore when your island runs out of consumables in order to stay alive.All that being said, there's a ton of potential here, and the game is enjoyable in its current state. I'm hoping for a better control scheme for rafts, and possibly even creating a raft with a motor attached to the back, which would make island hopping a lot less of a chore and less nerve wracking, with sharks all around ready to tip your raft at a moments notice. Overall, this is a game worth the early access price, especially considering where it can go.
