_childDocuments_.review: MIXED REVIEW1. More good to say than bad. Overall the aesthetics and atmosphere of the game is virtually unparalleled in my opinion. The excitement of exploring, the way the shipwrecks and coves make your imagination ponder not only the games story, but if there's places like this on Earth that still lay untouched (unlikely - but nice thought).2. Upkeep is annoying. Having to refill fibre into water collectors takes enjoyment out of the game somewhat. I understand that this is a survival but it just feels unnecessary. 3. Getting poisoned at the start of the game is possibly the most irritating thing ever. Either make antidote relatively easy to come across or remove altogether - such a silly mechanic in the early game.... ESPECIALLY for new players (makes you just want to stop playing).4. BUGS/GLITCHES - my raft which I spent 7 hours working towards got stuck on some shipwreck and even in fly mode I couldn't budge it. Finally, after 20 minutes or so of faffing around, I got it loose but now it is unusable because I cant right click and move it????? HOW DOES THAT MAKE ANY SENSE? It made me extremely angry and I quit the game, when I revisit I will likely remake using the console but I would rather you just not put shallow level ships on every island which easily interfere with the raft. Make an invisible wall so you cant go near or something.Lastly, I like the game a lot, exploring and playing feels both therapeutic and exciting.... BUT,  it genuinely feels unplayable at times due to BS issues. Please fix.I rate positive because for £15.99 I would still have purchased and played this game.EDIT: Several months later I tried playing the game, 7 hours in and a bug where I died shortly after saving meaning that I am stuck in a death loop when entering the game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not a die hard fan of survival games, but this a good one. The Pacific feeling is great: travelling on your raft in the middle of the ocean, the underwater fauna and the beautiful environment are the biggest highlights of this game. After these years the game is still an eye candy. The crafting tree is somewhat realistic, the idea of boss fights and the endgame scenario is good (the execution is a little lacking). Building - while it definitely needs some updates after these years - never gets boring. However the vanilla game  gets kinda boring after 100+ hours, so I strongly advise everyone to install custom maps - search the internet for recommended maps and creators you can't go wrong - which is where the game really shines. There are tons of quality maps which are damn fun to explore, some of them even have interesting stories to tell. I hardly recommend to install  SKIROW's or Outlaw's maps if you are interested in such experience. Don't expect to pile of tons of resources (on raft or on a single island), it will cause performance issues even on high-end computers: annoying fps drops and increased save/load times. The main problem of this game - which is hard to digest for many seasoned players - is that the possibilities it could have evolved to are limitless, yet it's still in early access and not many game changing content is added nowadays. If you can deal with this, buy this game it's still worth every penny and cent.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/10The game, while showing some potential, is more than flawed. The combat is unresponsive and unfair, gameplay is barebones, lacks fun milestones or ways of significantly changing what you do(Throughout the game you gather the same resources, loot the same places and craft the same stuff, without real improvements or changes to the gameplay loop).Crafting, while present, is no fun. New structures do not advance your progress by any meaningful degree, you can't customize your raft and there is no incentive to progress to the "higher tiers" of buildings.The fact that you can't build any of the production stations on your vessel, yet the game requires constant island-hopping to gather new resources feels just wrong. The islands lack variation and seem to be always based on one of two blueprints you quickly learn to identify. The fact that you can tell what the resources, enemies and layout of every island is gonna be, before even setting a foot on shore kills any fun exploration might bring. The "story" adds 3 bosses but in combination with the unbelievably flawed combat system makes you dread every single encounter. And for every technical problem that the game has, the multiplayer makes it 10 times worse. It has everything: Absurd long loading times on high end systems, random disconnects, bugs, synchronization issues.The game needs work. At times you can see the potential: General Gameplay idea, Nice graphic effects, the water behavior, atmosphere during thunderstorms, yet all of that pales in comparison to the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: The first couple of hours are amazing, but after a short time you're all set up and there's really nothing else to do (that's when heavy dissappointment set in for me)...you can't explore new islands, yes there is a few of them, but they're all the same...on some there are boars and snakes, but that's it for diversity. You don't even need a raft, you can reach all islands easily with the starting boat. No incentive to build a house or anything, because there's no point to it. The idea and the feeling you get being stranded (survival) is fantastic. This could be a marvelous game, but imo there's not nearly enough content.What would make the game perfect (and will never actually be done):1) A HUGE random gen map with hundreds of islands (small, medium, and bigger ones with jungles and waterfalls)2) Biodiversity: More plants, more landanimals like monkeys, panthers, lizards, insects, spiders3) Higher diffculty: More distinct animals, but make em way harder to catch (panther will rip you apart), also random spawns, hard to reach other islands with basic rafts, storm-damage for structures, raft-damage when sharks attack, NO gyrocopter, and so on4) Random gen caves you can take over (if big enough, like in Cast Away)5) ENDGAME: a possible endgoal and strong driving force could be to reach main land someday, but that's should be difficult and take a lot of time and special ressources (HUGE map, NO gyrocopter). Also there should be a lot of preparation necessary to cross over to other islands, the journey should be treacherous (the further you go the more dangerous it becomes: shark attacks on rafts, whales, stormy weather, so it actually makes sense to upgrade your rafts and thus gather different materials)But unfortunately i know how it works in the game industry:There's 1000 games that are 10% finished after early access, if only some of the developers would take on partnerships with others to combine ressources and know-how, we would have games with rich content, that are actually finished when sold.I'm sorry to say this, because i know you guys have put in a lot of work, but as it looks now, Stranded Deep will be nothing more than a glamorous screensaver for my PC. As there is nothing to do than enjoy the beautiful view and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's all face it: this is a game created mostly to all people out there posting and twitting status like "Duck you all!! I wanna go to a desert island". Well that's the good news...this is your chance to feel what is like to be on a desert island. And it's awesome. Your dream is coming true: fresh sea wind on your face, the sun smiling at you, the relaxing sound of waves. No boss telling you what to do, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥ co-worker farting in an unventilated small room, no desks, no tasks, no agenda....it's just you and freedom. Plenty of coconuts to drink and eat, crabs everywhere, palms you can chop off and burn. You can even build your own shalter...a place to call "home". All is just like in your dream as the days go by, and then, suddently, a morning you will wake up realizing that you drank your last coconut yesterday night. All you have left is a stick of wood. A. Single. Stick. Ok, don't panic, there are other islands I can explore to get more to drink. Fullfilled with that hope, you dive, you start swimming for glory and survival. You fell powerfull and confident within few meters off the coast untill sharks show up. Looking at what they did at your leg you realize that they are just tasting your meat before you can become their meal. It's exactly in that moment when you ♥♥♥♥ your pants (thankfull you are alone so no one can see that) and you swim back to shore as fast as you can. Finally a thought break into your brain like a bright light: you are NOT free. You are trapped. Dehydration start to kick in and bleeding is not helping. Slowly you fall asleep praying that you will wake up in your small office with the air filled with that fart you are now missing so much!!Pros:-Devs are looking professional and hard worker (most important thing imo for an EA game)-Intense survival and thrill game (you need to use your resource carefully in order to survive longer, swim among sharks and fight em)-Stunning graphics-Few bugs (it's an EA and the most annoying of them are getting fixed tomorrow)-Endless biomes (no experience will be the same as another)-Craft system lovely made (no more UI or infinite stacking of mats in backpack)Cons:- Too many sharks- Weather and day/night/moon/sun is still laking of realism (I'm almost in my 20th day of survival and there is still a full moon every night), rain comes from a bright sky, few clouds, no wind and sea is always the same- Hunger going down faster then thirsty - Islands are often similar and way too smallThis is a EA and, as it's looking now, is totally worth the money.

The ToneI feel that the tone of the old and final version are drastically different from eachother. The final version is more light hearted and filled with hope (even the shark music was made more light hearted) and the colors and music reflect this. However, the old original version from 2015 was grittier and hopeless feeling. The occasional music that played (which was really one piano piece unlike the final version's bigger variety of soundtracks.) was depressing (and matched the hopeless feeling of being stranded in the middle of the sea where you would likely die in) and was the only real comfort you would get. The colors were sort of bright as well but in a more realistic sense. The shark music had some bits kept in the final version but was much more different and scarier and included a slow reverb and background beat that made it feel like somthing out of a horror movie/game. World generationWhile the final version had a big variety of structures and island types. The old version basically had the same feeling islands everytime as well as the ships. The only thing about the world generation that the old version does better is the fact that its infinite. What would improve the final version's world generation is if it you gave an option to turn on infinite islands. Although an upside to having limited islands is that your resources are actually limited which can make things harder later in the game and encouraging you to explore the islands more carefully rather than just loot real quick and find the next island.In other words i still recommend buying this. The old version and final versions have aspects that are a bit better than eachother and both worth playing. I would definitely go for the final version because theres alot more content and polish to it plus the mod support. Hope to see this game improve more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing my previous thumbs up to a very emphatic thumbs down due to recent changes to the game, and the developer's approach to our saves.  In a nutshell, they simply don't give a crap if we have the ability to keep playing.  The save I was working on I had 100 hours invested in, and it is completely lost now.  There is no option to roll back to a prior game version, and the new version trashed all of my resources, vehicles, farm plots, and outposts.  It is essentially a ruined game at this stage, and I have no desire to replay that many hours again to regain what was lost, especially when it could happen all over at any moment.  It was unavoidable, and we were given no warning at all.===============================================Original Review:While I did recommend the game for playing, that comes with some warnings about shortcomings the game (and it's developer) still have.If you play without downloading custom islands from the Workshop, you're in for a terrible experience - insanely small islands, none of which have any significant abundance of resources to use.  You'll find yourself bouncing around the open ocean in a rubber raft to try and reach others, which as we all know from Castaway is a hugely boneheaded idea.For that reason, DO download one of the larger island packs from the workshop and try to replace most of your vanilla islands.  It will make the game much more enjoyable and less of a continual stress-fest.  I recommend the following pack which I've used extensively in my games:Visuals in Stranded Deep are quite good, as is the progression of skills.  Crafting is interesting, though the backpack is never quite large enough - they really should have implemented different types of craftable backpacks to help the player more in that regard.Underwater environments are just interesting enough to keep the player engaged down there, but they are small and don't have a lot to do from a variety of gameplay perspective.Animals and fish still need fleshing out - there are still too few types to make hunting a fun experience.  Snakes, boars, crabs on land, and a few fish and shark types in the water is about all you can expect.Once you understand what the game can offer (and have replaced most islands in the Cartographer with downloaded workshop islands), you can get started on the meat-and-potatoes of what the game really offers:  raft construction and base construction.  Both are interesting and fun to do, though you'll find yourself spending a lot of time hunting down materials to advance both.Hopefully the development team realizes all the game's shortcomings and will work to add additional content and systems.  If they release in less than ~2 years (given the terribly slow state of progress it's had), they're selling it short.  At that point I'd change my review to thumbs down.  Their most recent focus has been porting to consoles, which comes as a deep disappointment to most PC gamers on Steam.  The game needs a lot more work, and yet it seems like the developer is going for a cash grab by taking PC Early Access funds and using them for cross-platform development.tldr;  Thumbs up and recommended only if using islands from the Workshop.  Game still needs a *lot* more content and development, but can be fun when you realize it's still in Early Access, and "you get what you get" from where it is currently.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone. After the 0.06 update, the engine has been completely changed, and the game as a whole has been diminished by it.When you started a new game of Stranded Deep previously, it went like this: You wake up on a private jet, flying over the Pacific, amidst some turbulence. You get up from your seat and go up toward the cockpit to make yourself a martini, combining fruit, mix, and finally, setting the top aflame for an added flair, before drinking it and returning to your seat. Shortly after this, the turbulence get worse, and the starboard bulkhead of the plane is ripped open violently, your safety belt the only thing keeping you from being sucked out, as the plane crashes into the black ocean. With water having filled the cabin,you have to swim free of the plane, and, upon getting onto the sole liferaft, an explosion in the engine knocks you cold. You wake up to see an island you've never seen before, drifting slowly in the liferaft. When you get to shore, the tiny island you're on seems isolated from all the other tiny islands you can see off in the distance, and the reality of the situaiton sinks in: This tiny island isn't enough, but it's all you've got. To quote Mark Watney, "I'm gonna have to science the ♥♥♥♥ out of this".First thing's first, is there food? Well, there are some crabs scuttling about, palm trees with coconuts, and- ooh! potato plant. It's not a whole lot, but it'll help you survive for the time being. If we're going to be having fish and crab, we need fire, and that means would. You gather up some rocks, and what sticks you can find. Unfortunately, you only have just enough rocks to make the fire pit, OR you can make tools, so coconuts will have to suffice til you can get a proper cooking fire. You make an axe, which will allow you to chop down some trees, and a hammer to help with building. A couple of yucca plants provide you with rope enough to get moving on at least a basic shelter as the sun sets on your first day, after chopping down a couple trees, breaking the trunks into logs, then breaking the logs down into useable sticks. You spot the telltale dorsal fin of a shark off the eastern shore, and know that tomorrow, you'll need to venture out on your raft to find out what lies on that island in the distance.Now it's like this: When you hit Start Game, you are taken to a 5x5 grid of tiles, each with a title, and an island on them, shot from overhead. Here, you'll pick which island you start on, complete with stats below the grid, so you can make an informed diecision. Once you pick your island, you appear in your raft, before a large island with a bunch of supplies on it. You don't see any other islands, but it doesn't really matter anyway, since this island has everything you need anyway. Your first day, you knock out a shelter, firpite with spit, and bed, using the crafting menu, along with an axe, hammer, spear, and a couple of fish traps that you place in the ocean. There are coconuts up in the trees, but they're so high up you'd break half the bones in your body trying to get to them. Better to focus on the multiple potato plants, and abundant fish life about, and leace the coconuts to themselves.Gathering... is frustrating. You attempt to hack down some palms, and are ready to run and grab fallen coconuts, when you realize your axe can't actually hit the trees, you check the next most likely tree, and it can't be chopped down either. You finally fina a sapling that allows you to chop it down, and it burst apart into two sticks. You decide to instead use driftwood, which has collected in piles of logs, so you use to axe break the logs appart into... logs, so that you can break the logs apart into sticks.The game has been SIGNIFICANTLY reduced in scope, and playability with the new engine, and the new system pretty much cuts out all real impetous for exploration, which should be one of the cornerstones of the game. Instead, it has veered sharply into the territory of standard sandbox fare, shedding it's unique feel for a much more mundane one. Not really worth the buy at this point, as there are complete games that does as much or more at this point than the plans for Stranded Deep.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful survival game in a stunning environmentEven though this game is in early alpha, it is surprisingly stable. The graphics are stunning and true eye candy to look at. The surroundings one finds himself/herself after an airplane crash are wonderful with so much to explore and discover. Surviving is quite a job in this game, since the resources on each single island are rather limited. Once you harvested all coco nuts you have to find more of them on other islands. And here the challenge begins. Even though there are many islands in the world of Stranded Deep, they are quite distant from one another. But the good thing is, on all islands you can find either resources (wood, stones, plant fibers, and food) and even wrecks. So surviving is possible if one is careful and watches his or her health. A substantial part of the game is finding stuff on islands. There are useful tools in wrecks near island shores. Gathering items is important. Find food, gather resources and craft a shelter up to almost a mansion. Since the islands are small and limited, a lot of exploring and gathering of resources is required. And here lays the challenge, because it is rather easy to get lost - even if you are lucky enough to find a compass. Navigating around in a huge ocean with only a raft, can get strenous, especially when you get cought in thick haze or a rainstorm. Your visibility diminishes to literally ZERO. Night falls at around 6 PM, after that it quickly is pitch black. One advice: keep track of the islands you already harvested, cause you might starve if you come back for food and all has been harvested by you already. Sure, there are still fish in the ocean, but fresh water is hard to come by. Another adversaries of ocean explorers are occasional tiger sharks which like to push and turn you around while you try to raft to another island. By this one can quickly lose orientation. And one has to be wary not to drop the paddle or fall off the raft, else you might be eaten by the sharks. If the developers continue to work on this game and implement more features and diversity, this game has great potential for success. It is a perfect game for PvE folks who are sick and tired of getting ganked everywhere. The thrill in this game comes from trying to survive in a portion of the world with very limited resources. People who love to explore and build will love this game. Over all a great game to play, So far I spent over 30 hours of real life time. And if you want to learn more about this game, check the great videos of "paulsoaresjr" on youtube.Pro's:- beautiful graphics- standing at the beach, listening to the waves and watch a sunset is very calming for a stressed out person- a gigantic world- lots of islands to explore- many things to craft and build- the thrill when you dive near a wreck and you hear the ominous music of incoming sharks- great game to practice compass skills Con's:- Time runs way too fast in game. One second ireal life equals 1 minute in game - so a full day/night cycle is 24 minutes   This should be definitely changed by the developers, since reaching other islands takes some time- some minor bugs (its still alpha) like disappearing items, items that fall through the floor of buildings and are gone- no sea birds- no wind, which makes Stranded Deep a rather quiet world- no thunderstorms or lightnings, even when it rains cats and dogs- ALL islands literally look alike from the distance, which gets you easily lost- rendering distance of islands and wrecks is too shortA very disturbing fact is, that when by example you pick an island that looks the closest of all, and you row towards it, it appears to move further and further away. All of a sudden, other islands appear way closer and in a jiffy you are entirely lost. As beautiful this game looks and feels, there are quite some surprising dangers in it :-)Over all I give this game a 8.5 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Being stranded is weird. At first it is pretty and fun but as soon as your little wonder watch (your only friend besides Wollie, Wilson's Australian cousin who doens't talk much), starts beeping and you figure out how to look at it, you see you are about to die of starvation, thirst and what I can only describe as general "being on an island - alone". Now what? I asked myself, and ate a crab, murdered with my handy pocket knife. I violently puked, again and again, because what is worse, starving or reverse eating a bunch of crabs? Then I figured out how to eat and drink coconuts. Survival is a cake walk, I thought, but soon my knife was about to break. Tools were now in dire need, but for the love of god how? With some crab magic (the internet) I learned how to arrange objects into different objects and soon found myself as the owner of sh*tty hand crafted tools. And that's when the small sand island started to become a fully loaded holiday resort. I build a bed, a house, a camp fire, ate and drank. Now survival was really easy. To bad I starved in a ship wreck because I couldn't get back out and eating you compass isn't an option. 10/10 Best hoarding simulator 2015

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is an older game, and if you've been with it for a while. You'll see just how much this game has changed over the time. It is graphically gorgeous with beautiful scenery and vibrant underwater wildlife. But the game isn't just for looks, it offers you a pretty standard survival game. But, it does offer some charm, it has recently launched a Co-op, so if you wanted, you can play with your friends! It has standard survival aspects, hunt, gather food and plants, get safe-to-drink water and treat wounds. Craft, build, and fight back dangerous creatures. However, one thing that I do find fun, is that there are many things you can find as you explore the various islands and open seas. You'll find easter eggs, like a volleyball for example, and you will find different buoys, these buoys are the spawn locations for different bosses. But I'll let you find them for yourself. Good luck, and stay alive!

_childDocuments_.review: Why is this one of the best open world survival games?You against nature without any additional violence, and yet this game is challenging, engaging and addictive. The game plays at a very slow pace, but with intense atmosphere of keeping yourself together to stay alive: water, fire, wood... soon you'll have to find ways to economize and to take risks to keep the water processor going. Resources are scars (except for food), challenges are constant... Great game with a minimalistic approach.While I'm at it, I like to summarize some points that, to my opponion need some attention:- Yuka grow too fast, Ficus could maybe regrow slowly after many days- Many clipping issues, but non game breaking (as to now)- Building a house need more advantages (ex. shelter, storage, ...)- Naming discovered islands would be cool- Hunger is too easy to satisfy- Herbs for curing? - New driftwood and other junk after a storm (to keep exploring same islands interesting)?- No roofs on houses?- Nice would be some mysteries to solve (skeleton wit note, bottle with map, abandonned cabin,...)- Fruit could satisfy thirst slightly- Impossible to recuperate items from build constructions??? (ex. bucket)- Streamline the construction interface! (now it's click heavy)- Scenery and items are plopping into image too late when nearing an island (rocks, trees,...)- Sickness and injuries should restrict some actions (now it does not matter if one is ill or not)- A peronal story to keep the player going forward, pushin the limits,...-...But I'm having a feast with this game. I hope that the developers will continue patching and expanding the game, because this game deserves to be a huge success.Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have anxiety? A fear of the deep, dark ocean? Hate water levels in games? If you answered yes to any of these, you're going to have a bad time.But, if you can face that, you're going to be addicted.At first you'll be so focused on base building and survival, you won't care that there's a story and way to actually escape and "win." But once you realize there's a story, well, you still won't care because by now you've built your own island paradise away from people and be honest, that is what we all really want.There are ways to toggle the ocean to be less intimidating if your fear of the deep, dark is too much. You can accomplish this by making the sharks passive (also an option for other animals). I'm not ashamed to admit that's how I play most of the time. Judge me if you want, but I won't be the one pulling shark teeth out of the rear of my dive suit. It only took one tiger shark knocking my raft over, spilling my hard earned supplies and biting my face before I noped out of that feature.If you're wondering about the difficulty, there is a fairly unforgiving learning curve, naturally. I mean, you're stranded on an island and this isn't Naked & Afraid. However that's quickly how you end up.Any island can be reset at your leisure during your game in the cartographer menu to respawn resources if you desire. You also have the ability to rebuild islands to force spawn resources of your choice and place them anywhere on your map (replacing current islands of course) to help you if you're running low on anything. Sure, this is the equivalent of a cheat or an easy mode but hey, its a single player game and you aren't hurting anyone. You do you, boo. Build that castaway castle of your dreams. Befriend the crabs, Ariel. Roast flounder over an open flame.Overall verdict: great time waster that you can jump in and out of at any moment.

Unfortunately I am still waiting and updates are rarely ever happening. They expanded the islands a bit, added 2 fruitplants, 2 animals to hunt, some rocks, a very few buildingitems and improved the graphics. The graphic is the best I can mention about this game because it is really nice. They also added an editor to create your own island but not all content is in there. I would not buy this game anymore, because you will have to wait months to have any bugs fixed or any new stuff. The problem is that the game gets superfast boring. It could get definitely a great game if you like survival games and if you come back in several years. I play a lot of early access games but this ones progress is the slowest I ever saw. The developers develop in the speed of a snail. I am waiting now two years for it and almost nothing happens. You should seriously consider to add someone to your team to get things faster done! You can not expect people to be patient forever. Unfortunately you may not mention any sligthest criticism on their forum in steam even if you stay polite because some fanboys will just offend you if you do and to me it also looks as if the developers don't read the proposals or complaints anyways and don't have a clue what's going on on their steam forum. I do believe that they improved the performance, graphics, changed the crafting and inventory menu and added a few items, but what's needed most would be a tutorial and the coop mode to give the game a better playable experience. Hopefully they get closer to do this and give the players finally a reason why they bought that game at all.I do believe the 15 Euros I did spend were a waste because I can still not really play that game for more than a very few hours because there is just nothing to do after exploring a bit and building a house. And I really tryed it pretty often every few months. I even did some map with their editor but the editor is also not really working very well and has a huge lack of content because you can not even terraform caves, you can only create hills and flat areas and you can not even change any textures. The point is you can forgive an alpha game a lot as long as it is playable at all for more than a few days because you still pay for it, you don't want to have a hang out on the beach simulator, noone needs that.The game looked so promissing in the beginning and thatfor some people still give it good reviews, but you rarely even see anyone playing it for more than a few hours before and it is definately a disappointing experience to have nothing to do after a few hours. _childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying I do not recommend this game if you bore easily, or don't understand that not all games deserve to be played for 5 hours straight.  This game is for those who appreciate exploration, crafting, and survival style games.  **Pros**Fairly large worldAggressive sharks and snakesBuilding systemBeautiful atmosphere**Cons**Slow update progress.  Devs focus on looks rather than functions and new content.The new Rotating inventory is annoying.  I prefer the old system.  This isnt a console game.The crafting is limited.  So is loot.  In reality, You would find an abundance of plastic bottles, string, scraps of random materials you could utilize in crafting.  It wouldn't be on every island, but polution is abundant and any documentary on island life shows you how much trash washes up on shore.  Wildlife seems boring.  They have worked on that by adding bats, snakes, boars, etc.  But the Sharks are extremely aggressive, take a while to master killing, and are just an annoyance once you've been playing for a while.  I also think more needs to be done with the rafting system.  A storage box on a raft would make loads more sense to me.  If i'm taking the time to travel to another island, I'm not going to go and bring back only what I can carry.  I would fix my raft up to hold more items to make it worth the trip.  This is something Flame in the Flood understood with their raft system. **With all of that out of the way, I have owned this game for quite some time.  I realize 40 hours seems low, but for this type of game, with the amount of content, I believe it to be average.  I love this game in short bursts.  I enjoy exploring the islands, killing sharks, and building a shelter.   I think the atmosphere is incredibly beautiful.  The sea forts are a unique change to the typical islands you see.  I do like the ideas the devs post about, but i wish updates felt more worth the wait.  The game has been out for a very long time in early access with very minimal changes, and very little content added.  Some of the content does not feel rewarding.  If i dive deep down to an unexplored wreckage, I would like to find more than 1 piece of cloth, or 1 roll of duct tape.  I realize not every site will be a gold mine, but scrap metal for building, broken storage containers that I can use in my shelter, plastic bottles, rope.  etc, things that don't corrode as quickly under water and would make sense to find would make it more worthwhile to explore and risk shark attacks.  The rafts need improving.  I have all this access to building large shelters, building a larger raft, but the bigger raft serves no purpose other than protecting me from tipping over when a shark is below.  It should serve a better purpose, haul more loot, provide shelter if a storm hits, etc.  These are all things I'm still holding out hope for, which is why i give it a thumbs up.  I do love the potential of this game, and the atmosphere.  I just hope the devs progress more, and maybe a little quicker.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep has a sudden and simple introduction and tutorial to the game and does a great job at encouraging exploration of their map. Even though the story of the game is quite lacking the survival aspect does a good job making up for it. The bosses were incredibly entertaining and really had me wanting more of those unique fights (even tho they really weren't too difficult). To add, Stranded Deep does a phenomenal job recreating solitude whilst having the ability to freely explore.Ive owned Stranded Deep since Jan. of 2015 so before i get to the nitpicking of the game, lemme say this: Its actually pretty awesome to see how much the game has changed, and being able to appreciate the direction its going. The biggest flaw of this game is its lack of content. Its nice to have the 3 bosses, a little helicopter, and a way to "end" the game, but its really missing a story to follow or things to uncover. A few more bosses or mini-bosses would help make the world feel less empty and less of just a survival loop. Overall 7/10 - Great game as a short playthrough. However, gets repetitive pretty quickly, no story, bugs (not game breaking), and not enough bosses/challenging enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: -There are many problems with this game but lets start with a positive, the setting, raft building and island hoping are a cool idea for a survival game. -Now for the bad, the execution, the core of this games design is almost never met since you spend most of your time just trying to get past all of the UI and gameplay chokeholds. -Now that first problem there UI, boy is it awful, the items in your inventory never display properly and are hard to select, the toolbelt is just another crafting road block to unlock hotkeys which is a feature that other games just have by default. Sometimes raw and cooked meat stack in the same place but you can't tell so you just end up eating the wrong food boy that was fun.- The notebook that has all of the crafting recipes is abysmal to navigate, I wish they had shamelessly copied The Forest or Green Hell in this regard. -Storage is another huge problem in this game, there isn't a good way to store things but there is a huge need to store things. This causes problems almost immediately and most times you just make piles of materials on the ground because your 3 measly slots in a crate were used up already-No Online Co-op, there is couch co-op which is a slap in the face for PC players. _childDocuments_.review: Hi,Please read this honest review before buying the game.My dad and I sit in the shed most weekends and week nights hiding from Mother Aunt Moredeborah watching Castaway.It is our best movie and all that Mum has sanctioned us to watch.We used to talk about how Moredeborah would follow us no matter where we went in the city and that the only way to get away from her was on a dessert island. Most times we would hug and cry after that conversation, most times. Then along comes this game. I remember I was hiding in the chicken coupe when Dad came scurrying in (he knew all my hiding place because he used them as well). I thought it was a routine fleeing of my Moredeborahs wrath. Not this time. He had urgent news to tell me and I could see how excited he was, as he had wetted his pant fronts and scraped his elbows. He gripped me, digging in his unkept nails, and he, pulling me in close said, "I have a way to escape Mother Aunt Moredeborah." I blinked back tears and choked out a whimpering "thank you father."That night we loaded up this game with a title that reflects our hearts sentiment. My father and I played for hours huddled under the blankets safe from the Mother Aunty. Without this game I think we wouldnt be here today.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this is still a very early alpha at the time I am writing this (Version 0.03) it is already my favorite game. The term "survival" has been stretched a lot these days, most people think of Zombies or other players shooting you on sight when they hear the term.However - "Stranded Deep" is different.  If you ever watched the movie "Cast away" you already get a feeling what it might be like to be alone on an uninhabited island and how hard it is to survive - but this time it's all up to you.The game is not even overly exciting, it's more of a trip into your inner self and after a while you understand why Tom Hanks was starting to talk to a volleyball in that movie. Now you experience loneliness, desperation and fighting for your life first hand. Incredible how happy one can be just to find an old machete in a sunken shipwreck deep down on the ground of the ocean. Or the joy you feel when you built your own primitive hut from sticks and palm leaves.No matter what kind of games you played so far - good chances that this one is unlike anything you ever played.At currently 15 bucks definitely my best buy ever.

A waving Stranded Deep logo appeared on my screen. As I sat out to start my new game I was crushed by how amazing it looked. It was 2015 and those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sun shafts and shaders still haunt me until this day.The game looked amazing and it felt amazing. Yes, , the intro, I know. The Forest came out sometime in 2014 and this intro was basically a one point copy. But everything after the intro. .You are flying to a unknown destination in your plane, private jet I guess, when you suddently crash. Stranded with only the emergency boat and your clothes, you arrive on a nearby island. A small, coconut rich island. From here on out, .✓ Incredible visuals since 2015✓ (Used to) Minimalistic design✓ Easy crafting system (Now bound with a skill system)✓ Fairly simple to get into and progress✓ Generated islands with different sizes and stuff✓ Sharks & other fish you can hunt & hunt you✓ Now with animals on the islands you can hunt✓ Old, rusty ruins of ships and other sunken buildings to explore✓ Swimming and diving mechanics are really nice✗ ✗ The new skill system breaks immersion for me✗ Sometimes necessary things (Like a hammer) are hard to find✗ Your items break ✗ I loved this game. I could always start it up and simply roam around my island with so much to do and so many more things to explore; every update. New gadgets, new animals, new weapons, more stuff to craft.I used to put coconuts or just scrap I didn't need at the place I left my island, swam a straight line to the next island, planted stones and looked for loot. That way I could always find my way back.In the last few updates the game has changed . That's not always a bad thing.The minimalistic swimming, diving and surviving game I once knew and loved has been replaced by a game that tries too hard to reach The Forest's state.Don't,  ruin this masterpiece. The menu has been massacred and the lovely tune of keyboard notes has vanished. Where did the minimalistic game from 2015 go? Don't get me wrong, the game is still incredible fun to play. But it's just not the same anymore. Back then I was able to play hours and hours, swim around islands, explore sunken ships and fight sharks. Now I have to skill up for ages before being able to build a base. That's not...no. That's not what we wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Once you learn the skills to survive for the long term, this game is very relaxing because the scenery is so realistic. It provokes a deep feeling of isolation combined with intense beauty.  A great time killer when you want to just veg out and relax.  The sharks are unrealistically aggressive, but that provides a palpable and exciting fear of exploring the deep waters.  There is little complexity to this game.  You just survive and survive... for months and month of game play that is basically the same, with the added fun of building a fantasy beach bungalo on each and every island you visit.  There is no end, at least not yet....

And other than the silly shadow of only the axe you are holding, and certain trees not planted on the ground (sometimes in the wreck), this game runs smoothly and is loads of fun. _childDocuments_.review: As it is currently in its early stages of development, Stranded Deep may not contain many features in terms of gameplay. However, what is currently present is very promising, and provides a great example of what could come.The current crafting system is pretty dynamic, but is limited by the lack of content currently in the game. Still, basic survival beats such as harvesting food from the environment, collecting materials to build tools, and some minor looting makes for a solid start. However, in my opinion, this isn't why I came to Stranded.What really makes this game interesting are the pockets of bubbling water across the game world that indicate a possible point of interest below the water. The catch is that the waters are infested with sharks. This, combined with the pitch-black depths that the character can dive to, really adds a layer of anxiety that I haven't gotten from any other game in a long time. Dark water terrifies me, and this game does a very good job at driving this fear home.To recap, this game may not have a ton of features, but those that it does are very polished, and provide a very unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another survival game—one that suffers from the same idiotic limitations every other survival game I've played suffers from: the inability to drink rain water by simply cupping your hands during a storm (instead having to scour the environment for coconuts or tarps or a handy nuclear fission device), the inability to survive a day without eating two pigs and a small cow, and the inability to skin an animal without gagging. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. This one adds the inability to eat more than two coconuts without vomiting (This is not a thing.) and more sharks in the archipelago than probably exist in the entire Atlantic Ocean.On the other hand, you don't have worms start erupting from your flesh if you eat without washing your hands. So that's nice. Overall, it's one of the better games I've played. The survival mechanics aren't too ridiculous and the environment is gorgeous. It really feels like you're on the ocean during a storm or diving in shipwrecks while sharks prowl around. I'd probably list it as my second favorite survival game under Green Hell.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with my opinion.For a Survival Game, this one is actually pretty good. When you read about what survivors in the Pacific Ocean had to go through to survive; this game puts you right into that feeling.You have to worry about food, sleep, and the elements; including the local hostile fauna. I do wish there was a bit more 'guidance' with how to procure certain things/items, or at least when to expect such things.I understand why the Dev's have made some things ambiguous, as to leave it up to us to figure it out, but it would have made my first 15 hours a lot easier on the PC Windows Gamepass version a lot easier.As for mechanics in Stranded Deep, there are some frustrating moments, when exploring a ship and the waves make it difficult. The water mechanics pass through the objects, walls-etc, without any effect on the water what-so-ever. It just rises and lowers, at a variable rate.I haven't found too many 'glitches' or 'bugs' that are majorly game breaking.MAIN BUG FOUND - Sometimes in Multiplayer, one player becomes desync'd and we have to 'SAVE-REHOST' to get them back sync'd up.If you have patience to learn the game and the patience for that one bug in MP, give it a go.Overall, after spending about 15/20 hours on a different platform and almost a day on here;I'd give this game a solid 6/7-10. It *could* be better but it's good enough to pick up and have some fun with.

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned this game since it was in alpha, enjoyed it for a few hours before realizing it all felt kind of empty.Since then, I redownload it every couple years to give it another try, seeing how popular it always is, and I'm always left disappointed and confused. I love survivalcrafts, but I guess this game just isn't my cup of tea. It feels janky, buggy, and, as always, empty. Row around for 15 minutes to get to an island, strip its resources, none of which are very varied or exciting, then row back to your own and deposit the resources. Repeat forever. Once in a while youll encounter a whale you can't interact with, or a shark without a point in interacting with (except to get its head as a trophy, but you can only collect so many before it stops being impressive). _childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is about as generic a survival game as you can get these days. The overall feel of play-style sways towards simplicity, relying on resource shortage and brutal forward planning in order to hold up the game play mechanic. The world doesn't really feel like it wants to open up to the player, instead opting for a feeling of helplessness and an inevitable grind towards success.Crafting is, at best, basic and, at its worst, frustrating. Creating a raft (your primary item of choice if you wish to survive) is simple, but also tricky to undertake because of physics collisions, weight distribution problems (placing a single vehicle tyre onto your raft can have the entire construction spinning out of control, or cause it to drown) and space restrictions. It's meant to be realistic, but the execution of it is glitchy and immersion-breaking, often adding frustration to your task. On top of that, there is very little you are allowed to add to the raft as a vehicle, ending up with your final creation being uninspiring and boring. Want to build a little sleep area that's enclosed, with maybe something to cook on - Nope! You can construct a shelf system for your crates, a sail, a rudder, a simple stone anchor and, if you're really feeling fancy, you can build an outboard engine. The latter of which requires a contrived, painfully slow process of farming potatoes (from limited resources) in order to distill them into fuel. It all feels a bit over-the-top., while also being incredibly underwhelming.Crafting on land is marginally more involved, with basic structures that you'd expect from a castaway survival situation. It's not terrible, but it's not particularly inspiring either. With resources being cruelly sparse, requiring plenty of island hopping to support any form of player home settlement, it soon becomes tiring to have to travel vast distances just to get some sticks or enough fiber for crafting  water production. Some might enjoy the challenge - indeed I did at first - but it soon becomes a grind, taking away the thrill of exploration and discovery and replacing it with necessity. Not really good for anything but die-hard survivalist wannabe's.As for the story - I honestly haven't come across anything so far that gives me a clue of what I am supposed to do to get home. It might be something added on final release, but as yet it's a big mystery to me. I see hints of what I can craft from the story (4 items) but there's no connection to them in any form so far in my 21 hours of this play-through (Day 32) that I am attempting in July of 2022. Hopefully that will change. People shouldn't have to look up spoiler guides and sift through forums just to find out what they should be doing. Short of that you will likely just float aimlessly around the game world until you bump into something, which could take little time for the bold explorer, or tens of hours for the cautious gamer.Now to the bugs; There's plenty! Physics causing catapulting of trees when cutting them down, physics glitches with your raft, instability issues and (for me) a flickering shadows problem that has existed for 7 years, with no progress made by the developers to fix it. I am not alone with this glitch. It's apparently quite common, especially the further you explore and on the larger islands. It's not the end of the World, but it breaks immersion considerably and is extremely uncomfortable on the eyes,Visually (aside from technical bugs), the game is very pretty to look at. The water elements are quite beautiful and there's plenty of wildlife to make it feel alive and atmospheric. Colour use is decent, giving a truly tropical feel to the environment. Indeed, graphically it is a great showcase of what modern game engine technology can produce. Especially when it's designed by a fairly small team.My gripes: 1)  It's not good to have a screen output that's uncomfortable to look at or that ruins all the hard work that's gone into creating this beautiful environment.2)  There's too much emphasis on forcing players to island-hop for resources. Encouraging the player to explore can still be achieved without brute force. The island sizes never offer enough space for a player to get comfortable in the game and create something special as a home. It feels like the developers are keen for the player to simply keep moving until the end of the, erm... story?!?3)  I want at least some direction when I play games. It doesn't need to hold my hand, but zero information just makes it aimless and uncertain. Not a good way to design a story. This needs significant work.4)  Making a player hop islands (taking up significant time, depending on distance) just to get a few logs to make planks, or resupply an island of wooden sticks for cooking and crafting, because there's nothing left to cut down on the island the player has decided to settle on, is contrived, boring and grindy. There's no need for this. Look at Green Hell or Subnautica for reference. There's an abundance of resources everywhere (for the most part) but it doesn't lock the player into position. Instead it makes preparation for exploration more enjoyable - heightening the excitement of discovering new places.5)  Staying alive is what this game is all about, but the grind added to make it fit into this genre is bordering on lazy design instead of thoughtful complexity. This is a tricky aspect that I also cover in my likes as well, but needs to be mentioned.6) My likes:1)  The world looks beautiful and the water is realistic feeling and immersive. The developers have done a great job with the overall visual and dynamic environment.2)  It sounds nice and there's plenty of atmosphere created around the player from the various audio elements.3)  A truly tropical vibe. A lovely water pallet and a vibrant and inviting overall feel for the world space.4)  With the exception of over-sized crabs, the overall look and feel of the wildlife is so good you'll likely want to spend time (especially under water) just drinking it in and experiencing the flora and fauna of a tropical dream holiday. It's not at all safe, but it's incredibly immersive. Enough that you don't really need a story if there was more space to explore on land and more emphasis on taking in the wonders of the tropics. Very nice indeed.5)  There's quite a selection of things to build, even if the game doesn't balance it well or give it purpose. It's not enough for impressive creativity, but it lends to the game enough to warrant a mention.6)  Staying alive is tough. You need to look where you are going and pay attention to your needs. it's what the game centers around and it, almost, works. I prefer thoughtful survival mechanics over brute force, lazy design. It's a bit of "love it and hate it" as far as this aspect goes.I'd give this game a somewhat generous 7/10, but must warn of glitches that can potentially ruin your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep starts off great, its early game is fun, immersive, with lots to do. Though once it hits mid to late game, it becomes very repetitive. It's ending is also one of the worst out there.The good:*Very fun at the start of the game*World is immersive at the start*Lots of fun things to do at the start*Sharks in this game specifically add a great horror element that I have never seen in another game that I have played*Shark AI for the Tiger Sharks and Great Whites is really good*Graphics are quite noiceThe bad:*Mid to late game is the same thing over and over, very repetitive. Collecting clay, dealing with creatures the same way, travelling long distances... the same way*Random World Generator causes too much meshing with wrecks, making many non accessible or causing the player to get stuck*Sharks, when moving fast, have more animations. Looks like they are moving in 15 fps, which breaks immersion*Shark AI for Goblin and Hammerhead Sharks is annoying, they are too rapid*There is no difference to building out of clay vs building out of sticks or planks, only visual differences, no reward for making stronger buildings*Hurricanes/storms are annoying, they pose no threat, lightning creates unpleasant flashes*Hard mode is annoying as it increase water consumption to insane levels*Nights are too long, day is too short, underwater visibility is too limited with a in game 5 hour window to be able to see well*No diving/swimming equipment, no fins, snorkel, goggles, armor, etc*Collecting clay is tedious and boring after awhile, mining pick the whole game*The games ending needs improvement*No fast travel, it needs it because travelling across the map is boring and takes a long time*Respawning snakes, crabs and large boars will knock your stuff around on the island, and you don't know when they have respawned, they often get you while you're in the middle of something.How the game could improve:*Add a map*Add more story elements, unique elements about each island, things to break up the grind*Add upgrades for equipment and buildings to improve their use*Add water tanks for collecting water, water filtration, water purification, gutters for collecting water, water tank storage for rafts*Make a polished world as the main world, and use Random World Generators for everything else. The main world could be polished, bug free, no meshing, add extra story elements, larger land masses, other deceased survivors and their stories*More upgrades for rafts, better rudders for turning, better engines for faster movement, better storage system, compass holder, etc*Essential storage for the raft that is visual and you can see how many you have without having to open every storage box. It could hold food, water, fuel, medical items, fuel etc*Add automated notes of what the player has done on an island*Add fast travel for islands you've discovered or add a marker the player can make and place so they can.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is absolutely terrible, there are no redeeming qualities what so ever. Many people may excuse it because it's in early access, but it has been in early access since 2015. If you play this game for any time at all you'll see that there tons and tons of bugs, unpolished edges, and broken systems, even in the first five minutes of gameplay. I have forced myself to play trough the bug infested maps, and game breaking glitches just to see if there is a reward that makes it all worth it.... and nothing! After toturing yourself for hours to get to the end you'll encounter no redeeming ending what so ever. There is nothing on the horizon, no goal to shoot for, absoulutely nothing. Its so bad that even the steam achievements are broken. At the beginning of developement the devs had a good idea, and if you look really closely you can still see the tatered ruins of a good game, but since 2015 it seems that the devs lost all care. I don't know if it is because of greed and money, or just lack of intrest; whatever it is, I doubt Stranded Deep will climb out of the grave it dug itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I finally bought this game yesterday after like 5 years of deliberation and it was... a roller coaster ride.I boot up the game with expectations high because I've always been a huge fan of castaway narratives. I see there was procedural map generation, exciting! I see a perma-death option, very exciting! I start a new game, learn enough about it to fully understand all the early mistakes I made.Start another new game, get poisoned early, run out of resources early, no antidote. I die on-route to a bigger island. Start another new game. This time I am fully ready. No poison for these feet. First island stripped of important resource, I set out for a bigger island to start building my new home. 4-5 hours later, I have a hut built, loads of resources and loot saved up, cooking setup, hunting, tanning some hides. Life was good, until I ran out of stones. There's no two-ways about it. I need to risk travel to another island to gather more. But it's almost my bedtime. I risk it. Gun it for the nearest island on my blow-up raft. Spend a good 30 minutes there gathering all I can, and set back in the same direction I came from. But something goes horribly wrong. In my tired, delirious state I lost sight of my home island, and went the wrong way. I arrive on this foreign shore scared, my heart sunk with the thought that I've gotten myself completely lost. What follows is a lot of paddling, I hopped between 4-5 islands trying desperately to find the small haven I'd built for myself, but couldn't find it. I messed up bad. This game is bad! Why so easy to get lost? Please noooo.  I think to myself "Maybe I'll just die and start a new playthrough tomorrow cause @#%* this.", at this point I just want to go to bed. But no, I can't. I paddle that crummy little raft away from the  as fast as I can, getting pelted repeatedly by  , on the brink of death. Somehow I get away, and make for the nearest island. At least I have a shot at starting a new life.You may not believe this, but I kid you not that the island I found myself on was the one on which I had so lovingly crafted my home. The elation I felt in this moment was so uplifting that I had a hard time getting to sleep after.I will never forget this moment. If this sounds fun to you, chances are you will like the game. But keep in mind that it can sometimes be a bit rough around the edges since it's made by a small team.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been over a year since its release into early access.  I played the original one then got bored pretty quickly.Its still FAR from being done... very little has changed and things have actually gotten worse.- I made a raft, but the raft was glitchy as hell and the propulsion system is utterly garbage... at least in the original they had a paddle. - You can't tell when food is cooked. So its a fun game of 'did I poison myself'- The animations for all the equipables is complete garbage.  Its been a straight forward punching animation with the tool in your hand.  Yeah... I'm punching fish with the forward end of a spear.- Theres no way to tell hunger or thirst... its a guess.- There is almost no need to explore since everything excluding mechanical and metal parts will consistently respawn on the tiny island you can start on.- Really? _childDocuments_.review: This game could have been great.I first found this game years ago, when it was still in early access. It seemed cool to me back then. But now? It's mediocre at best. The most used material is decently rare, causing you to constant go through motion sickness-inducing seas. Trying to control the raft is awful, and trying to move it onto land glitches out like crazy. The tutorial focuses more on the basics, and completely ignores anything more complex like SPF. I still don't know what SPF means, because the game never explains it as far as I could get up to. On top of that, being forced to go on a fetch quest just to save the game once is annoying. If you're a casual gamer, don't get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time it is not worth it to the budget gamer. The begining is fun, but you quickly establish yourself (<30 day in game approx 12-14 hrs) then nothing. With no story or goal it becomes clock watching. I then began searching more wrecks just for boxes and lanterns for decoration. As a result, I eventually run in to the boarder buoys. Currently at 50 days alive, only minor injuries sustained and treated. I have killed tiger sharks, gone deep diving. All that is left is to hunt a Great White and a Black fin, and find more lanterns.I should stated that I played The Forest a couple months before this one. The Forest set a really high bar for story, exploration, combat, and survival.Stranded Deep is a very pretty game runs well. Storms are epic. But once your past the first 15 in game days very little challenge. Has potential but so does a million other games that never come through. I wanted to give this a positive review and visually and mechanically I can, but it is not a sustainable play.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really did. But unfortunately between the bugs and the poorly thought out game play I just have no interest in it.For one, co-op mode is buggy. Several times we had to log out and log back in because he could see me but he was invisible to me. This was made even more inconvenient because the time it takes to sync back up to each other after logging back in is insane. As far as bugs go, solo or co-op, they're annoying to say the least. The raft will randomly flip you out and send you flying, or the raft itself will go flying 100's of feet away from you. Sometimes objects don't spawn until your right next to them. And the poorly thought out game play. There are many ways to desalinize water, but this game allows only one. You can build a gyro-copter, but you can't figure out any way to get fresh water other than a cloth and some dead leaves? The game mechanics themselves are rough and annoying. Jumping works, sometimes. Or sometimes not at all. And on top of all that, the visuals aren't that great either. The water is nice. Character animations are wonky. Just hard to get any immersion. After a few days I just couldn't see myself wanting to play this anymore. After playing games like Icarus, Dayz, Rust, Green Hell etc, this game feels buggy and outdated. And very limiting.

Only requests are bigger islands (maybe a square mile or so), and birds. That would be cool. I highly reccomend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I was inclined to write a negative review even though I think this game has better gameplay mechanics than Raft. It's really fun. It even has a cartographer feature where you can place custom island in your existing/new games. No other raft survivalgame offers that much. Combat is satisfying. The graphics are gorgeous. So is the music. And it's still early access so there's a world of possibilities to improve the game.But... Well, did I mention the game is really really fun? It surely is. Until it isn't. The game has many game breaking bugs right now. Crates that misteriously disappear when you drop them, even in single player mode. So carry a bed with you and save often. Coop is a desync and disconnect mess and takes a lot of time for the client to rejoin and sometimes the client can't for some reason. This game still can be the best lost-at-sea survival game out there if they manage to clear the game breaking bugs.I promise that I'll change my review to positive as soon as they patch the game. I just can't recommend it right now especially for coop mode because frustration is inevitable.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I did love this game. But unfortunatly, I felt like there was only so much that I could do with it after a while. Only 8 days into surviving, I built a great big awesome looking shelter. My food supply was potentiolly infinite and I was at a point where I was never hungry. I had ample resources, and explored SO MUCH of my world. But that was only with about 10 hours of gameplay. Now I feel like there is nothing left to do. There really isnt much else for me to explore, and even if there was, I feel like it would only be a repeat of what I had already seen. After I build my shelter, what exactly else was I suppossed to do? I wasn't surviving, I was thriving, and I wanted to keep playing, but with a very limited building feature, I feel like there really wasn't much I could do creativly outside of the map maker, which again, with it's limeted options, became repetitive really quickly. Again, let me say that I loved this game, and in the future, it can realy only get better, but at the stage it's at now, I really can't see myself playing it anymore.Even popular youtube channels only crank out about a dozen episodes a season on this game.This obviously is still being developed and there is going to be a lot more you can do in the game on the way so I will be recomending this to my friends. But don't be suprised if you find yourself with nothing more to do relativley quickly.Can't wait to see what else is in store in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is a game that doesn't have a narrow story. It's not a game with interesting characters. It's a game, with one objective, survive. Stranded Deep is a visually stunning game, with a great crafting system. Islands are free to explore, and if you can see it, you can go there. It's one of those games that has almost nothing wrong with it, but there is one issue. There is a short tutorial on how to craft items, but once you make land on an island, there's no crafting menu. You have to just throw down items and hope for the best. Thankfully, there are community guides to help along. Also, as a note to the developers, I love your game. Another great addition would be the integration of Steam Workshop. Community made islands, homes, and other such ideas. Keep up the good work.

It is well worth the 15 dollars, as it looks to be a promising future for Stranded Deep. Anybody who hasn't yet bought it should take the time to be a part of this.

Yes, it does have some bugs, and some manipulation is a bit awkward, but it is an excellent game I have enjoyed for nearly 100 hours so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this game has promise. It is the type of game that I have wanted for a long time; probably since I saw Cast Away was in theaters. Initially, the game gives you the sense that you've washed up on shore. You can experiment with items the way you would expect.However, this is an early access game, which suffers from a poor user interface. The game doesn't tell you how to do anything, besides the awkward tutorial in the open sequence on the plane.If you like the movie Cast Away and want to go through tedious and monotonous tasks like hacking away at tree trunks, this is the game for you. I like that I can craft and build, but the building seems seems very on rails. The structures you can make are built on foundations, which are very large and modular. It would be more fun if the buildings were more hackey.This game is in early access. I suggest to wait a few months for them to work out the bugs. For instance, if you jump into a washed up ship, you can't get out. You have to glitch your way through the ships. I'm sure this will be patched eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: Just as many pros as cons! I'm going to rate it high for now, but if the issues aren't fixed I'll rate appropriately!       So I really like this game! First off, I have a very real irrational fear of open water and sharks. Sure all people "fear" sharks, but I get the sweats, and shakes. I repeat over and over again that I can't move, and I quit and restart rather than get bitten/eaten. Don't get me wrong, it's ark, but no dinos. I know this is still a early access, but I'm just aching for more. So here are my pro's and con's.Pro: Hands down it's fun if you like sandbox survival games. The sharks seriously keep me paranoid. I always enjoy the building aspect, but I really like that there is also furniture. The water looks so freaking real! I get itchy and fearful just from how realistic the water is. I can spend endless hours creating my base, and exploring. Every time you start it's a new world. If you die, and go back to the save point, things may not happen the exact same way. It may not rain, and shark might not appear! Hands down I like the game and would recommend it to others. I "hear" that co-op is on it's way, that will be dope, however before I star that idea and get excited about them developing that; we need to address the con list, and there are many!Con: Wonky, the menu (craft) closes every single time you create something. I love that you can't hold 45 things at once, but it's also my greatest annoyance. As of yet there is not a chest to store items in, and what crates you do find can only hold 3 items. The smoke is like a puzzle, you sometimes have to walk back and fourth to get items on the shelf of the smoker. Unless you're holding sticks when you interact with the fire a second time, you'd never know you have to add more sticks to get it going again. It's locks up often. Save your game often (Must have a shelter to save). My computer is a Goliath, and this game is a snail by comparison. However you'd think this game was David, it locks up my system and I have to power down. It freezes up a lot. It takes 8 wacks to take down a tree, another 8 to seperate the trunk, and another 8 to make 4 sticks. If you have hit the tree 12 times, stop what you're doing and go to another tree, because your ax/knife is about to die if you keep going and the tree will yield no wood. Look up how to use the tanning rack, because you'll just stand there like a fool waiting for the leather to dry. It wont!Final thoughts: I don't want them to saturate the game with "easier" machanics, I like that you have to be active to survive and thrive. The sharks are terrifying, I've yet to go diving because I'm terrified. Co-op will be dope. I look forward to the bugs being fixed. Please input a chest into crafting!!!!!!!!!! I give it a B+ all around, but I've only got 24 hours in. It's worth the price, but you have to have patiences.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite buggy and glitches can be found here and there, but considering it's barely an alpha game, I believe this is an astonishing game and here's why.The graphics and visuals are incredible; the lighting from the sun and moon, the leaves fluttering in the breeze, the eerie depth of the sea... All these examples are just the beginning for what's in store for this game. The game is quite peaceful and the only dangers you encounter are sharks and staying healthy.There are some frustrating issues I wish could be fixed, like how difficult it takes to travel to other islands. Sharks can also knock you off your boat and sometimes your boat will randomly disappear in the middle of the water, leaving you literally 'Stranded Deep' in the middle of nowhere. Another annoying problem is the little amount of resources one can scavenge from a single island; at most there are a few sticks, some rocks and a few palm trees, which means you have to constantly travel for more resources. The sound and gameplay make up for all of this though, it's so relaxing and incredible to play. The company is still publishing updates here and there, so I believe the final beta release will be all worth it and absolutely incredible.I have high hopes for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, and it keeps getting better!  The terror I felt encountering sharks in the open water was like no other experience I've had in gaming!  It takes a good couple hours of playing to start getting the hang of things and realizing your mistakes, but once you get over those initial hurdles things make a bit more sense.  The tutorial is fairly basic which is nice because you don't necessarily want a tutorial holding your hand when you're in a survival game - part of the fun is discovering how things work.  The game is at once beautiful and forbidding.  The islands look like a place that you would really want to go to and spend time on... but not like this!  The first time I encountered a storm while on my raft I almost soiled myself - very realistic and loud and confusing.  The crafting is simple and the game spells out exactly what you need for each item.  The lack of space for carrying stuff can be frustrating, but that's part of the survival aspect of the game.  Highly recommended, but you have to play more than an hour before it starts hooking you, so give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the content is sparse, BUT its coherent and it works.It's a very well made game with great visuals that fuels the feel of the environment.You start by crashing with your plane and find yourself in the water with a life raft, a paddle, a pocket knife and a lighter.Next to you is a (very) small island with a few different resources like palmtrees, potato plants, yucca palms and rocks.From these things you can make foods, drink, camp fire, simple housing, rafts and a few tools like axes and hammers.In shipwrecks you can be lucky to find things like a compass, a bucket or other useful things that'll help you stay alive.Once you use up the resources on the island, you can paddle or swim to another very small island (of which there're plenty) and start more or less all over.As you do have limited carrying abilities, you may need to stash things on one island while exploring other islands, so you need to find a way to map the area to navigate between islands.For food you can also kill whatever creatures you may encounter in the ocean, but eating uncooked crab will make you sick and throw up, so be sure to build a camp fire and cook the meat before enjoying your feast. X-)So far its just about surviving in a very basic way that (needless to say) do become rather repetitive after a few hrs, but hey, its early access and its nice to see devs not being overambitious and pile in tons of contents that doesn't work.

_childDocuments_.review: It costs just as much as Valheim and Valheim is better in every single way. Even on special I don't think it's worth it for solo play.I primarily played this split-screen co-op (which Valheim does not have) and as I bought it on special I feel like I have my moneys worth as a group activity.However the more I have played, the more I want to play Valheim. To start, the biggest let down has been the building; if there is a collision (even with a rock formation) you can't build there. Building stairs has to be over a platform not from the edge. Placing structures is buggy as heck. Building a raft is cool but placing structures on it sucks (they can only snap to the middle of a raft platform).Farming heh, feels half finished; some things rot and spoil where others don't. Meat/cooked meat will spoil but if you leave it on the fire it wont. a bunch of the plants you can pick don't have a purpose.Cutting trees leaves stumps you can't get rid of, half the shubbery you can't even get rid of which made a fantastic looking community island, horrible.Base game islands are boring, community islands are mostly from older versions so have items with no use and floaty objects. Modding community is very small.Sailing is ok the waves are nice. Diving around your island to explore sunken ships cool, but 20 meters away from an island there is just a drop to a bottomless ocean, no ocean exploring.Animals will run around up in the air, clip through terrain. My character has shoes on, but stepping on a spiky starfish will poison me. Bumping a snake or lion-fish also poison.This is far from a complete game, videos/screenshots make it look much better than what it is. Graphics are meh especially for the FPS you get.If you are specifically looking for split-screen survival, buying on special is ok. Most of the cool mods appear to only work for player 1 tho.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of this game. I really think they nailed the idea of "survival" with how much you need to eat, freshwater you need to drink, how much to sleep, effects of the sun, and environmental dangers (poisoning from some ocean critters, broken bones from falls, shark bites). My problem is that at nearly 60 hours on my current game, I've used up every resource available to me that creates fresh water. An earlier version of the game had a water still that required you to gather ocean water, boil it, and collect the freshwater that left through evaporation. They replaced that with a solar still that runs on the leaves of palm trees, but they don't grow back or regenerate after you cut them down. They need to fix this and introduce some device you can make that is capable of consistently producing freshwater. You can set up traps for fish, hunt pigs on whatever islands have them, bird snares, farm fruit and never worry about going hungry. But you're screwed with water over time.The vehicles are cool (I wish they were a little faster) and the gyrocopter is a lot of fun. Sharks don't act like sharks but as an enemy they are great and a serious challenge. Solid 7/10, worth the money and a good time. Strongly recommend giving this a shot.
