_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and gorgeous.  The crafting system takes a lil while to get used to becuz you basiacally have to pile all your resources together on the ground to see what items you can craft fom them.  It's actually kinda neat compared to the basic crafting slots method other games use.  It does take a while to learn all the "recipes" if you will, but they're are easy to figure out if you use a lil common sense.  Then there are the beautiful sunrises and sunsets, as well as working at night by nothing more than the moonlight coming thru the trees.  Some days are foggy and others have crystal clear skys.  The ocean water is so clear and blue that you can spear fish from the shoreline, but beware of the occasional shark that swims into the shallows to investigate you. There is essentially no HUD, other than a small reticule, and if you want to monitor your health, hunger, and thirst, you have to look at your watch which also tells you the time of day and temperature.  The inventory is very small, only 8 slots, but things stay on the ground where you drop them.  This makes sense though because no one can carry 50 rocks and 100 sticks and so on.  It limits you to carrying the amount that any normal person could carry in real life.  Basically, this game is an outstanding survival game, located on a small island all your own, with limited resources, and enviromental dangers that you must avoid.  You get one life and if you die, you start all over on a new island.  This game is very fun and for an early access game, very functional.  There are still things to come such as an end-game where you actually get rescued.  Right now you can just explore, craft, and survive as long as possible, which is a challenge in and of itself as you'll find out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game for a long time. I've played this game for a long time. I've pretty much beaten the game as it stands right now and I feel conflicted. This game was beautiful and a load of potential. Sadly, it seems that the developers for some reason updated this game backward from whence it started, most likely due to formatting to console release. I remember when this game had a beautiful life under the water where you could find sunken ships anywhere even in the deepest parts of the water. I also remember when worlds used to be infinite and very fun to explore. Now the oceans lay barren and empty and the world a limited with an out of place yellow floating ball border with nothing but empty ocean after it. I know that the world is limited for reasons of bosses and island creations, but I still can't help but feel that something great was taken away from me. Something that could have grown into something beautiful.        I bought this game near the moment of this release, and I was really excited, I would even go on to play this game for hours on end. I remember when the community for this game was booming and everyone was excited to see what would come next. And for the most part, we were not disappointed. But there was one thing everyone was begging the developers to implement every sing update they posted. Multiplayer, the thing everyone wanted because no one wanted to survive alone. But as the days, months, and even years grew on, they never added it, but they added plenty of things that people never asked for. Eventually, the community started begging and pleading, but as time went on, so did people. The hype died down and the most abandoned hope. What went from people giving great ideas and sharing love with the game soon became people giving small comments of pity as they clung to what little hope they had left for the game. And while the developers watched their fan-base shrink, they decided to take action, but not to give the people what they want, but to instead bring out a console release. At which point I knew they had given up and decided to run for a cash grab before it was too late.        The game itself at first is very fun and exciting with plenty of things to look forward to. But after playing long enough you start to realize the grind and just how annoying it is to find the one thing that you need to start doing things that could be actually fun. Like building fun creations. But the building has changed for the worst as they implemented the leveling system that stopped you from building things if you were not high enough level. This leveling system has to be the worst feature I've ever seen in their evolution going backward. The sharks are fun to fight, but they don't even seem to tip over your raft while you sail to another island. Which in my opinion made the game before very challenging in scary. Now sailing to another island is just boring and feels like a waste of time. They also seemed to make the game more complicated as to get the fuel you need to get potatoes, farms, fuel machines, and Jerry Cans. Whereas before you just needed to find a Jerry can with limited fuel already in it. The progression in this game feels more like it's holding you back from experiencing the fun parts until you've experienced the rough buggy hard parts. It took days just to level up enough just so that I could create something that I've wanted through the entire game which I could also acquire in the previous updates just through perseverance and luck.        Overall this game is dying if not already dead, and though it may seem harsh to say and I may just sound like an old bitter man saying it, I feel that I have been betrayed too many times to have any hope for this game. Though it was fun and I enjoyed myself, I don't think that this game is worth it, it felt like a cash grab in the beginning, and it stayed a cash grab until what looks like the end. This game has betrayed and left it's fans alone for so long to play a game that can only provide so much fun. Is it really too much to ask for one thing? The one thing that everyone wants? I've said it more than once, everyone's said it, but I'll ask one more time...                              Beamteam, won't you please add online multiplayer so that I can just                                                                                        have fun with my friends and we can all know that you listen.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was out in Early Access since 2015 - I remember seeing a few youtube letsplayers trying it out, encountering myriads of fun little bugs: and I have been waiting for it to get finished and released ever since then. It promised a very nice environment, sort of vacation-like, which is appreciated during these hard times. But, unfortunately, little have changed since its initial release six years ago.There is little to do in this game after tutorial. Survival crafting games imply just that: need of survival, and lots of crafting, but neither are presented well in the game. It barely has any craft: the number of things that can be crafted and requirements for them are extremely low; survival does no present itself as a challenge; exploration is almost non-existent, as the whole content is entirely the same: once you have seen one island - you saw all of them, and once you've been to one ship- or plane-wreck, you've seen all of them. Hostiles are just three types of animals that pose barely any challenge at all, as well as the weather that sounds like something important (overheating and storms - sounds dangerous), but they barely do anything at all. It's not challenging enough to be a survival game, not varied enough for exploration, and not different enough to be crafting game.There is just three land creatures (plus a bigger, aggressive version for two of them), two air creatures, one type of water enemy (five visual variants, but they act the same), three world bosses, one type of harvestable tree and ten or so types of resources: you can imagine how little one can do with that. it's not like you have to have hundreds upon hundreds types of resources and enemies in your game, but when there is this little to work with, no game designer can create a game that is actually - you know - fun. It is more about quality that quantity for sure, but it's not like quantity doesn't matter at all, and it also dictates the quality of the gameplay. It is basically "go through tutorial and quit: the game", as tutorial covers almost the entirety of the game, and it's rinse and repeat since then.It all looks too raw for a project that released six years, and while it's vibrant, warm, and tropical - it is also very bare bones, repetitive, and quite frankly - boring. There's just nothing to do, unfortunately. I'd love to appreciate the game, but I have been playing it for three days, and can tell you with certainty: it exhausted itself in first two hours.

_childDocuments_.review: People, it's an early access game. Expect bugs and slow development (hence the disclaimer on EVERY Early Access Game). Be cautious with downloading user made maps that may not be compatible with the version you are running, it will cause weird bugs and random deaths. I love the "story" missions they have now, adds a good challenge to the game that it was lacking previously.The biggest downside of the game is the same as any barebones survival game, eventually you get to a point where you have all the supplies youll ever need, already built a huge mansion out of every material, and find yourself hunting for great whites and marlins just to feel challenged, at which point you start a new game from scratch and do it all over again. The replay factor of the game is based on your own personal creativity, try surviving without ever making the axe, or only drink from empty coconuts, or only use spears to hunt and fish. Challenge yourself and make it interesting. Try only travelling during the storms without a compass, that will definitely test your skills XD

_childDocuments_.review: This was surprisingly unfun. It's very similar to games like Raft and Ark that I have enjoyed a lot more, and it looks really good, but it does everything in a way that is just constantly irritating. I've never played a game with a more aggravating inventory system. It's difficult to switch between items and you frequently end up having to drop items from your inventory just to switch between objects already in your inventory. The crafting system is also incredibly annoying to use, more so than almost any crafting system I've dealt with. Even Fallout 4's crafting wasn't more annoying. The game constantly forces you to go through tedious and repetitive steps to do simple tasks, mostly involving popping in and out of the menus multiple times to perform simple things like cooking a fish. Steering the raft is one of the most unresponsive and frustrating things I've done in a video game. Having to constantly rebuild structures on new islands because they can't be moved or built on the raft is just a needless annoyance. All survival games have a degree of busywork involved in just staying alive, but the busywork in this game is more aggravating to figure out and more aggravating to repeat than in most.The underwater stuff does look great, but as far as the actual gameplay it's just a buggier, less fun version of other games I've already played, with nothing special to make it work putting up with.

_childDocuments_.review: After about an hour of sitting on an island wishing I hadn't accidentally used all of my rocks to craft tools, I finally resigned myself to my plan of paddling out to a distant island to see if I could gather up some more. I paddled for ages and was incredibly excited to see the new shore. It was a small island with a wrecked ship on both it's east and west sides. After gathering a sizable pile of rocks to take back to my sad little home island, I decided to pull out my knife and explore the shipwrecks.As I swam down into the tiny fishing trawler, I wondered how long I could hold my breath. Long enough to discover a hatchet stuffed away in a locker, and a fuel tank stored in the ship's console, and a spare lighter stored away in a toolbox. I excitedly tossed my treasure on the ground by my raft, eager to see what was located in the other ship.This ship was much larger, maybe a crabbing boat or something. It had at least two decks. I couldn't discover the hidden gems in this thing. Oooh! Is that another hatchet? Yes! Awesome! Whoa, a machete?! Sweet, I should probably go up for air. Alright, air is sufficient. Let's go back down. Wait...what is this music? There hasn't been any music before...this sounds...ominous. Please tell me there aren't sharks in this game...OH CRAP, THAT'S A SHARK. SWIM DAMN YOU, SWIM.After escaping what was certain death, I went back to my raft and settled on what to take back home with me. The rocks, the fuel tank, and my beautiful new machete. The rest, I left on the beach for easy access if I ever decided to grow a pair and finish exploring that boat.As I began paddling back to my island, I reflected on my performance while I experienced extreme fear after spotting the shark, quite happy with myself. I escaped the wrath of a frightening creature while stupidly swimming around in his home turf. I can outperform sharks, man. I'm awesome.It was at this moment of smug satisfaction that I heard the ominous music again and immediately reverted back to fear mode, and looked around my raft in a panic, trying to spot my tormentor. Suddenly my raft was violently pushed by something below me. I flipped out and started mashing buttons in an effort to pull out my new, prized machete treasure. In my panic, I managed to press Q instead, which resulted in my hurling the tiny plastic paddle I was using to transport myself home directly at the shark's head.Realizing I was now stranded in a raft with no way to paddle back home, being circled by a large sea creature with enough teeth to completely ruin my day, I quit the game and decided to sit in bed for awhile wrapped in a cozy, warm blanket.8/10 will most definitely play again.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Went back and watched Markiplier's video for this. A full eight years later, and the bug where trees float into the air when you chop them still exists. And this bug happens literally every single time you chop a tree. Should provide a lot of insight into the quality of the developer.This is not ready for release. I'm usually more forgiving with games, so I bought it despite the reviews. It seems like they just got tired of working on it and pulled the plug. Most games release 1.0 with a big capstone update, i.e. new content, completed story, etc. After 8 months of silence (from the last update), they release 1.0 with a very small handful of bugfixes. Thats it. They threw in the towel. Maybe with another two years of development, but if they stop here, then this is abandonware.So many things wrong in just an hour of playtime, so lets start at the beginning.-- Zero character customization outside of male or female. Everyone is a twin.-- Starting a multiplayer game takes several minutes to sync. Ive never seen a game take that long. How could that be considered acceptable?-- Poor/non-existent animations. Looking at my co op partner during the plane crash sequence and they are barely sitting in the chair. They are about a foot away from the back of the chair, and completely stiff. Dont allow the player to see things like that. Just hide it by putting the other players in different rows so they cant see each other. The first several times I climbed a tree there was no animation at all. You just slide up and down. Then suddenly they started working, so that was surprising. Rowing the raft is jarring, and you can see straight down your own neck.-- Notifications are shared apparently. I was told I was bleeding while at full health. Found out later that my co op partner was dying somehow, even though we just barely started and were still trying to build our first shelter.-- Terrible UI. Trying to move items from your backpack, that you apparently were just wearing during the plane crash for some reason, to another storage was just bizarre. Theres also no way to tell how much storage space a container has. You can also craft a toolbelt to unlock hotbar slots, but theres no way to put anything in those slots. If you have a full inventory with an item in your hand, you can drop the item and not be able to pick it back up due to a full inventory.-- Poor design choices. You can only cook one tiny piece of meat on a fire at a time. And why exactly does a rain collector consume palm fronds to create water? It doesnt actually collect rain, because that would require rain. It just consumes fronds to generate water.-- How exactly do you revive someone? My co op eventually died because he doesnt have a healthy fear of sharks, and his body just floats in the water, with no way to recover him and no respawn options.-- The last straw. The watch. The sun came up, and the alarm on the watch starts screaming and never stops. After five minutes of listening to that, I gave up.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I recommend this game, No I don't recommend this game as it is.So first off, this game is brilliant. It's been a long time since I played a survival craft game that I actually enjoyed. Stranded Deep is probably the stand out of the genre, with a proper end game from the start and everything working towards that point.Starting off as a scared survivor having to watch out for literally everything, as even accidentally standing on a poison coral could spell disaster in the early stages, and finally making your way to a fully sustainable, shark hunting killing machine, is super satisfying... Even more enjoyable considering they've added multiplayer!But that's about where the praise stops. THIS GAME IS BUGGY AS HELL. Now just to be clear, I've only played this game multiplayer - it might be a completely different story in single player (if that's your jam) but... It will crash without fail within half an hour..usually with a trail of strange things starting to happen. Sounds will stop playing, islands will disappear, LODs will remain as sprites...the inventory will stop working. And on the subject of inventory, it's possibly the worst system I've ever encountered. You have a very limited inventory space, about 8 items or something, but equipping a piled item will split the pile into 2 in your inv, often leaving you unable to carry things, or even change item, cause your previously free spots are now taken up by things you were already carrying. which makes crafting an excruciating experience.Exploring by yourself in a multiplayer game is not an option...get too far from your coop buddy, get kicked from the game and lose your boat. End of story, no exceptions. You can not do this.The land combat is lacklustre with one of 3 available spawns just walking towards you attacking until either you or it die. Coiled snakes and pigs flying into the sky when they can't reach you, and coming down later to walk towards you again... rinse and repeat on the next island. Now it might sound like I'm hating on this game, but I'm not. it's in early development, and it represents an incredibly enjoyable, extremely beautiful game in its current state, despite being plagued with game breaking bugs.So lets take a look at it.THE GOOD: * Stunning graphics - the water and storms are a sight to see. Oceans full of fish...just wow.* Diving ship wrecks for scrap - every second in the water is a terrifying risk vs reward of items or being killed by a shark.* Proper survival - hunting for food and shelter has never felt so important in a game.* Good progression - Each step you take opens up more options and your character evolves to become a true survivor.* Sailing through a storm and having your boat flip in shark infested water is incredible.* Coop multiplayer - is absolutely the best way to play this game (but also the source of the biggest problems.)* Having a clear goal from the get go - working your way towards escape from day one is a fantastic use of the genre.* Being able to craft from items you're standing near. (It's not only a good mechanic, it's necessary, given how terrible the inventory is.)THE BAD:*No Mapping...kinda - in a game about exploring, drawing the charts manually on a piece of paper, while fun at first...isn't fun for long... or just view the whole map from the main menu, which kinda sucks all the fun out of it.* Uninspired land based combat - with pigs and crabs that walk towards you attacking until one of you dies.* Online servers are shocking - a LAN or direct connection option are basically a necessity.* Separating from your coop partner will cause a crash.* Doing just about anything will cause a multiplayer game to drop out.* Very limited crafting options for the actual boats...which you spend 90% of the game out on.* The Gyrocopter - The gyro seems important at the start of the game, however, there's only parts to build one, which turns out to be almost completely useless in reality. if you lose it, its gone. and only one player can use it at a time.THE UNFORGIVABLE:* Less than 30 minute game time before some sort of crash.* Constant drop outs in multiplayer make exploring in this exploring game just about as painful as it can get.* One of the worst inventory management systems ever.So there you have it. Would I recommend this game? Absolutely...next year, when the devs have had some time to fix some of the many issues this game is riddled with.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is not perfect, I still reccomend buying it and playing the game.One of the hardest things for me while playing Stranded Deep is the fact I am terrified of deep water, AKA the ocean, which just so happens to be the setting of this game. To do good in the game, you must face your fear of what lies beneath the deep( if you are afraid of the ocean )and scavenge resources underwater.I will simply give a summary of all the aspects of the game and what I find good and bad about each. Lets' begin:GAMEPLAY: The gameplay is good, it's simple. Survive. You will start out with a lighter and a life raft, and will need to paddle to shore. The map is made up of several islands where you will collect resources like wood and stone to craft shelters and tools. Certain supplies can be found on land, like metals, tarps, and buckets. However, the real treasure is found in shipwrecks under the ocean. Sharks are a constant threat while diving down, so be careful of those little buggers as well.GRAPHICS: If you have a beast for a computer, and I mean a real beast, than you will absolutely enjoy the graphics of this game. However, if you have a crap computer like me, the graphics are so amazing you will need to turn them down to prevent your computer from exploding. Even on low graphics the game still looks incredible and can be appreciated.FEATURES: This game has many things to officer, including many gameplay mechanics and features such as:-A watch that will tell you the time, temperature, date, and your basic needs.-Several different ocean creatures( crabs, sharks, marlin, small fish ).-Intense opening scene.-Buckets.-Randomly generated map everytime you start a new game.And many more.To finish off this review, I just want to list some of the things I personally would like to be added to the game.-More land-based wildlife on the islands( lizards, insects, birds, etc. ).-An easier way to get water. It is not easy trying to keep that bucket upright trying to get it over the fire.-A co-op or multiplayer mode where you can play online or with friends to survive together!-Larger islands.-Two different modes: Story, where you must survive until rescued. Or an Endless mode, where you survive as long as possible.-More sea animals, like more whales( Sperm, Blue, etc. ), octopus/squid, and dolphins/orcas.So, to end off this review, this game is good. The reason I have little play time on the game is I don't play Steam all that too often anymore, but when I do, I enjoy playing Stranded Deep. I have had no bad experiences with the game so far, and I expect it to stay that way.PS. As with most early access games, this game includes a lot of glitches and bugs, so be warned!

_childDocuments_.review: We're coming up on the four year anniversary. The game was originally released with a goal to get out of Early Access by the end of 2015. That didn't happen. It didn't happen in 2016, either. In fact, the game is still Early Access with experimental builds, and no end in sight. Achievements have been disabled for this game from the start, as players were told they were NOT going to be re-enabled until the game was fully completed. I've been waiting over two years to play this game and enjoy it fully, and quite frankly, I'm done waiting. Their excuse of "increased interest in the game warranting expansion and addition" that would require delaying the finished product by THREE YEARS has yielded little more than fixing the ever growing list of bugs they create when "adding more experimental builds" and the sparse new content of sea items. Would not recommend buying this game anymore, especially not if you're hoping to conquer the achievements, which is something I waited 3 years for and won't see.Update: It's now been six years, still Early Access, still don't recommend, still OMEGALULing.

_childDocuments_.review: One of very, very few survival games along with The Forest to show some actual promise.However, right now the game is playable, and fun for a few hours, but there is no meat on the bones. Unless you know you will buy this in the future or you want to help out with the development process by testing, then there is no real reason to buy this game as it stands. The current lack of substance and features makes for a very pretty but rather dry experience with no real aim or goal. Surviving isn't really all that hard and the world around you lacks variety and real dangers.I will not recommend this game, but that doesn't mean it's bad - It means that you should just be aware that you won't be getting your moneys worth for a while. If you're okay with buying it now and waiting for updates, possibly helping Alpha/Beta test this product, then go right ahead! I personally couldn't quite contain my excitement and purchased this game shortly after watching Jim Sterling play it. This is one of those rare projects that Early Access was probably built around. If you miss the good old days of pre-release minecraft with new features being added in and the game growing around you, this could very well be the closest you'll get to experiencing that wonderful feeling again!

_childDocuments_.review: Day 2: Tomorrow I have to swim to that wreck I saw earlier. There will be something there I can salvage, surely? Got an axe yesterday. Had to use it to get back.  The sharks!! They scare me. Day 3 : Lucked out. The wreck revealed a torch. Flat batteries.  I got back to the island. I find a rock. A stick. A potato plant. I'm feeling vibrant.Day 4: It rained last night. I had nothing to catch the fresh water. Coconut milk again.Day 5: Axe is getting worn. I have plenty of wood. For now. Fire just went out. Must light another. Day 6: I despair at ever drinking fresh water ever again. Day 8: Went swiming today to get some fish. I FOUND A BUCKET!!! Rejoice. Need rain.Day 10: No rain. Tomorrow maybe.Day 12: Still no rain. Coconut milk and cooked crab. I want chocolate. And a burger. And fries. And... coffee..Day 13: Somehow I threw my knife away. I spent all day looking for it. How stupid!!!Day 16: Must. go. to. new. island. Nothing here. Can't last.Day 22: New home. Broken arm. Fell. Getting coconuts. Why did I jump?Day xx: Axe is broken. I don't know anymore. What should I do? Another island?Day xx+1: I'm dying. Broken arm, still.  No water. No food. No axe.Day 27: I woke in a daze. It's... raining. Raining!! I just might survive this. I look at my watch, it's 27th December. I didn't even remember Christmas. I sprinkled sand on a coconut and called it a pudding. It still tasted like.....coconut.. just... gritty. I laughed until I cried. I need a hat. Obviously.Day 28: Decided to live. Feel that it's better to die trying than to just...die. Swam to a new island. Met a whale on the way. It's song stirred me. I'm right. I.must.live.to be continued......

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sandbox game which brings out the boyscout in me. You can survive many ways, and you can die in an equal amount of ways. Sharks try to bump you off your raft if you're not paying attention, and if they don't succede in eating you, rest assured that you will eventually step on an urchin and require antibiotics. You will find items that can aid you, like a bucket for collecting rain water or boiling seawater, or flippers for faster diving and swimming. Lighters, flare guns, parts that can be combined into a working on-board engine, fuel cans, cans of baked beans, ponybottles with oxygen. And much much more. There are axes, hammers and machetes hidden inside sunken ships and planes, and what luxury cannot be provided from sunken treasures you have to juryrig out of jute rope, some sticks and rocks. No time to dilly-dally in this game. You might as well draw a map while you play, and start laying down arrows with rocks and lumber so that you don't get lost on the many isles.  One little bump on the raft, or a case of uexpected fog or rain can send you off in the wrong direction and you can starve to death trying to find your way back.But if you have contingencies in place and the right kind of gear with you, you are well on your way to becoming master of your destiny.Now, this game is Early Access, so there will be more features and graphic tweaks.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is a game which is difficult to recommend for a number of reasons, but ultimately over the time I spent with it I did have a lot of fun - your own experience will probably depend on how critically some of the flaws I'll point out below matter to you. There's also a bit of a balancing act when considering the game as it was almost entirely developed by just two people and in that respect is a very ambitious title, but on the other hand there are many issues which were tolerable when it was in early access but should not still be present now we essentially have the finished product. For context, my 125 hours of gameplay consists of several incomplete playthroughs where I got bored and didn't play for a few months at a time, and one complete playthrough which I eventually worked up the motivation for.Graphically the game looks nice on first glance with a suitably colourful tropical environment, decent water textures and some nice lighting effects. Up close however everything is quite low res, and worse still the game suffers from the worst object and texture pop-in I've seen in a long time, it reminds me of an old PS1 game where large objects on the horizon suddenly appear out of nowhere and textures remain in super low resolution even at quite close distances. For a game which involves a lot of long distance exploration in an open world this isn't great.The audio effects are perfectly fine overall. The music adds a bit of atmosphere and the sound effects are generally ok, although the very limited 'voice acting' (in quotations because it's really just the odd single word comment from your player character) gets repetitive quickly.The UI is functional although the crafting menu isn't the best, it would be nice if it remembered where you last had it open so you didn't need to scroll through every single time. Also, while the game makes it quite clear what items are needed to craft various recipes, it doesn't always give a great indication of what the resulting product is actually used for. I had played for a very long time for example before I discovered that a meat smoker isn't actually exactly the same as a campfire for cooking food.Gameplay wise, Stranded Deep suffers from the exact same issue that most survival games do - a rapidly diminishing difficulty in the survival aspect itself. The first few days in game definitely require a bit of careful thought with regard to gathering food and water and so on, but once you've crafted even just a basic encampment it becomes very unlikely you'll be in danger of dying of thirst or starvation or whatever. Another issue with the crafting is that a number of the objects you can make are actually pretty useless in the grand scheme of things. Now admittedly if you just treat the game like a sandbox and don't worry about the endgame (which is entirely optional to complete) being able to build houses and so on is quite fun, but there's hardly anything to furnish your creations with and from a survival point of view a massive house is really no more useful than the simple shelter you can build right from the start, other than perhaps providing a bit of storage space. Likewise you have things like toolbelts which you might imagine allow you to increase your inventory space but in reality just provide some quickslots for accessing items which isn't really worth bothering with.Regarding the game world, once the survival aspect has been dealt to, which as I mentioned above will happen pretty quickly, the emphasis switches to exploring the game world. This is fun to begin with as the different islands will have different loot and resources to find, but it very quickly becomes apparent that there is very little variety in the randomly generated islands. They essentially just fall into two categories - big islands with pine trees and wild pigs, and small islands with palm trees and crabs. Once you've visited three or four islands close to your starting island you will have pretty much seen everything the game world has to offer. It is worth mentioning that player created maps and islands are readily downloadable and this is probably the best way to play from an exploration point of view but it's a shame the default content seems so limited in scope.Finally, it's worth mentioning that the game world itself is still fairly glitchy - it's very common to see animals spawning in mid air, fish swimming through the air during storms, wild pigs running around underwater on the beach, and so on. None of these issues are game breaking for sure, but they do hurt immersion.So with all the problems I've pointed out above it might be difficult to see why I'm giving this a recommendation, but ultimately if you're looking for a survival game which is just you against the environment this is probably one of the more complete games available. Buy it when it's on sale and you probably won't regret it, but expect to constantly feel like you're playing a game which is still in pretty early access.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the premise of a castaway-esque survival game, and I was initially quite impressed with the expansive procedurally generated world, and excited to explore it. However, after a few hours of gameplay, the awe began to wear off, and the game's poor mechanics began to grow annoying. Sure, it's interesting to explore an abandoned vessel, but after spotting the very same wreck for the fifth time while hopping from island to island, you become keenly aware that you're playing a videogame with limited resources.I've found the mechanics and UI clunky and awkward. I ran after a boar with a spear for ages jabbing to no avail before discovering that spears must be thrown. To craft the same item multiple times I had to open the crafting menu and select my desired result for each repetition. In a boat half submerged, my character couldn't seem to decide weather he was standing or floating. It's the little things, and they add up fast.Overall, it's a neat concept that looks beautiful in screenshots, but during actual gameplay it's hard to find a reason to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is one of the unique survival games on Steam.You play as the role of a castaway stuck in the void of Pacific ocean.: Since every island has limited resources, you'll find yourself constantly wandering around the vast open ocean to find another island with yet another scarce resources.There are three ways in which you can travel from island to island: Swimming, paddling, and using a motor boat.Not to mention, sharks will occasionally draw an interest unto the player.You can do a lot of things on an island: Build simple structures, find/cook food, and sleep.In the vast deep sea, you can: loot shipwrecks, and hunt fish/shark for food.The crafting in this game is very unique compared to other games; You craft materials in front of you instead of the traditional craft-it-in-your-inventory/backpack.You need to watch out for three things: Your Health, Hunger, and Thirst.Everything that you do is a necessity for survival.: The graphics of this game is breathtaking. The water's effects are some of the best I've seen. Seeing water quality in other games is rarely done. In fact, they do not act like water at all. This game is an exception to that; moreover, this is an Indie game.The islands are filled with flora elements which makes up the beautiful island scenery.The water world is also perfect.You'll see tons of detailed biomes and aquatic fauna.The only disturbing thing to see in the game is when the player is poisoned and your flashlight/torch is opened. This gives me goosebumps whenever I see this.In conclusion, The graphics is superior in proportion to the file size of the game.: Throwing things around and cutting trees are the most realistic scenarios I can think of.There are many flaws in the Physics of the game: •Raft sinking in the presence of light objects, •You can climb a tree while chopping it down, •You can chop a tree while freely walking afar from it, •Swimming is faster than paddling, •You can use a tree as a raft, • and many more...: Most of the fish travels in schools.The three types of sharks has their own attitude towards the player.Great AI script.There are still a lot of bugs and glitches present in the game since it is still on Alpha stage.I would gladly share how to reproduce those bugs and glitches, Just message me.Stranded Deep is an extremely promising Early Access Game!Rating: Disclaimer: Everything is purely based on my opinion.Thanks for reading!~
_childDocuments_.name: Stranded Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Stranded Deep is pretty unique. I find it very chill and relaxing. I truely feel a sense of adventure traveling from island to island on my thin yellow life raft, oar in hand braving the elements. One such time I can remember being halfway to another island and suddenly getting caught in a huge storm. I paddled in what I hoped was the same direction for a few minutes but couldn't resist looking behind me to try and glimpse sight of my "home" island to get my bearings. After that point I was lost. The clouds were so thick I didn't know which way I was facing. Then as night came I was not only lost in the fog, I was also lost in the dark. I had mentaly maped out the nearest islands to my "home" but now was way off course. This was hillarious to me. It was like finding a brick of solid GOLD when I finally opened a chest with a COMPASS inside!  I eventually gave up on my mental map and grabed a piece of scratch paper and started maping my discoveries. I even started using real world triangulation to chart my discoveries with my new compass. I loved this. No minimap with red dots to tell me where to go. No yellow brick road to follow. You are just LOST, using your wits, this was great.Now with all that said, I will say this...At one point several months back (maybe a year ago?) there was an update that in my opinion drastically altered the game, and it really put me off at the time. The crafting menu's were foreign to my original experience, there were several glitches, and the world seemed much much smaller. I basically shelved the game after that for some time, with the intention of coming back to it later when the new changes had become more polished. I am happy to say, things have improved.If I could change/add one thing to this game It would be to add a Rip Curl (so I can hang 10 with a surfboard) the ocean graphics are great but sometimes the shoreline breaks immersion for me. (High and low tide would be cool too)I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a lot to this game that appeals to me: a survival simulator that prioritizes movement and has a host of crafting and exploration mechanics. However, this game is clunky, poorly designed, and not user friendly. The UI is difficult to use, and the programming is prone to bugs and glitches.More than that, this game is not yet fun. I tried to find a way to enjoy it, but the game offers neither reasonable challenge/difficulty nor a compelling story. The mechanics and controls are unrefined and do not complement one another, and the game is riddled with bugs. I thought it might be due to the game being in early access, but the game is more than five years in early access with monthly updates and has been released on consoles. The studio has had ample opportunity to address these issues, and it is clear they do not intend to make the game more user friendly.I decided to return the game after 65 minutes when, upon arriving at a new island after struggling to paddle the raft in anything other than a circle for five minutes, I was attacked by a boar, killed it, attempted to skin it as its head spun in wide circles and its war cries continued to ring out as though it was still attacking me, and then was killed by a crab with no indication that I had been at all injured to that point. I had no motivation to continue.Overall:Graphics: 5/10 - very early 2000sGameplay: 3/10Soundtrack: 5/10

name: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League
detailed_description: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League - Digital Deluxe Edition Jumping into the Digital Deluxe Edition unleashes even more mayhem with the Justice League Outfits for the Squad, 3 Notorious Weapons, 4 Weapon Dolls, 1 Battle Pass Token*, and 4 Color Swatches. *Battle Pass Token redeemable for Premium Battle Pass access (Seasons 1-4 battle passes, subject to availability). One Battle Pass available per season. WB Games may modify or discontinue online services with reasonable notice at any time. About the Game From Rocksteady Studios, the creators of the Batman: Arkham series, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a genre-defying third-person action shooter where the ultimate band of misfits must do the impossible to save the world: Kill the Justice League. Join the newly “recruited” members of Amanda Waller’s infamous Task Force X (aka the Suicide Squad), Harley Quinn, Deadshot, Captain Boomerang and King Shark, as they set out on an impossible mission to Kill the Justice League. Drop into an expansive and dynamic open-world Metropolis ravaged by Brainiac’s invasion and terrorized by the heroes who once protected it. Each Squad member brings their own traversal mechanics to help them navigate a sprawling and battle-torn Metropolis, combining free-roaming exploration and combat verticality for an unforgettable experience. Players are free to experiment with a variety of different play styles to unleash maximum damage on their enemies. Whether in single player or online with up to three of your friends, players can take on this suicide mission their own way. Post-launch, players can expect a continuously evolving Metropolis with free new playable villains, environments, weapons, in-game events, and more, all included with purchase of the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad: Kill The Justice League is not the gaming travesty everyone makes it out to be. Yes, there is flaws. Yes, it's insanely overpriced for what there is to do in the game right now. However, there is some good points to make following my almost 100% (at the time of writing this) playthrough of the game.The gameplay feels so amazing to play. The traversal makes navigating the city of Metropolis very fun, and somewhat engaging depending on the character you play (looking at you, Harley). The gear in this game has surprised me in many ways. I went in expecting it to just be standard +5% stat boosts, but the legendary items in this game can make or break a build, sometimes even surpassing the highest rarity in the game. To me, that is perfect. I want a reason to use every "high tier" rarity, no matter how build defining. I went into this game expecting hot garbage but was surprised with some honestly laugh out loud moments due to the performances of the voice actors, the animations team at Rocksteady (really good facial animations. You know the Captain Boomerang one) and the sometimes subtle storytelling through characters actions or reactions to things in the game. However.The story is very subpar. Expected better from Rocksteady, but at the same time, it's a live service looter shooter game. Stories in those games are either amazing, or half baked. No in-between. Between the funny moments it is your typical alien invasion story. This band of criminals is tasked to fight an entire alien invasion on their own, and by some amazing sheer deux ex machina bs, they do it. The entire storyline gets put on a cliffhanger for the live service elements, and frankly, that annoyed me. The ending cutscene is no means a good way to segue into the live service end game. The biggest complaint I've personally heard is how they "did Batman dirty". I disagree, as if you just simply watch the cutscenes, pay attention, and know of some easter eggs hidden in the game, there are hints that the Justice League you kill in game are not the real Justice League. To me, I am just simply letting Rocksteady cook with the storyline, see what happens. The game isn't finished right now, and as such I am eagerly awaiting future content drops.Overall, I enjoyed my time with Suicide Squad, despite some of its flaws and minor issues that Rocksteady and WB have already begun addressing. It feels great to shoot, traverse the city and just put your builds to the test. The future promised DLC coming in later seasons makes me hopeful for what Rocksteady is cooking. However, I cannot recommend anyone to spend the $70 USD/$100 USD for the game. Wait for a sale, find it cheaper through other means, and just play. Don't let the angry mob who wanted Batman to be the front focus of a CLEARLY advertised Suicide Squad game affect your opinion. Don't let the people who are angry at Sweet Baby Inc. change your opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Now where to begin...I'm not a big fan in general of "Propaganda & Politically charged aka 'Woke' Games in General" but here are my to cents on this one.So after playing this game for about 42 hours, I have actually not really seen much of the "Woke" content that all these people have been slobbering about. Okay, so some gender swaps here, race swaps there, and a gay flag here and there. But it is basically a parallel Earth or basically a different DC universe so who's to say these things can't be normal on this planet. The fact that Captain Boomerang literally makes a joke about "Floyd aren't you supposed to be white?" literally doesn't scream in my face "BLM" etc.etc.etc.This is coming from someone who even gave the new Saints Row Game a try and actually saw nothing "Hardcore Woke" or "Insert Full on Political Diversity, Inclusion, Etc. BS IN MY FACE 24/7" the entire playthrough.The SSKTJL can literally be broken down in these categories imo- -Story: 6/10 - A bit bland, but entertaining. The whole multiverse thing has been so played out in movies over the years...it's over-saturated. -Characters: 7/10 - I feel the character dynamic was okay, they didn't take it too seriously, the banter is what you would expect from a SS group and well it was aight.Now the nitty gritty- -Gameplay: 5/10 - At first it's fun, enemies are pretty interesting, boss fights are okay and somewhat challenging. COME ON!!! but the Squad Perks is nice I guess...Overall I give this game a 6/10 - I know a lot of people would disagree with me. _childDocuments_.review: Edit after playing a while longer in ()The tldr is: It's not a game for everyone.weapons have cool legendary effects. (edit but there are way too few to make it interesting) Characters feel uniqueThe same mission types are used way too much.The characters talk a lot and while i find them funny for some it might be too much.Ok in the game are 4 characters with unique movement options the jetpack for dead shoot,the drone for harley,the speed force glove for boomerang and king shark is just built diffrend and has charged jumps.So the positives: I love the movement.Esspecially harley with her drone can swing across the roofs and be super fun with her mps or pistols.I think the only one who feels a little less interesting is deadshoot due to it just being a jetpack.When you touch the ground with any character you can instantly do a slide that gives your next move extra momentum and refills your movement meter (harleys drone use resets ,deadshoots jetpack cools down etc)So you have a really nice movement buff for playing well.The melee feels HEAVY like when you hit a soldier they will become airborne and you can juggle them.(these are also more meh after playing for a while)The legendary weapon effects feel quite unique.I found a gun for harley that causes a certain enemy type to become frozen in the air with everyone around it with the draw back that this gun deals no damage to this kind of enemySo i see this enemy use this gun to get an advantage switch to my second one and just go ham on em. _childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game.  But it is definitely not for everyone.  Definitely not for the majority of video game consumers, I'd say.I would be fine giving this game either a thumbs up or down, but gave it a thumbs down just knowing that more people will likely read it and hope they read a more nuanced review of the game, rather than just click on clickbait videos and type "this game is trash" before even watching the video, which likely actually praised the game, despite the clickbait title and thumbnail.  (seriously...so many clickbait hate vids on this game still praise quite a lot about the game) Clickbait gonna clickbait, I get it.Preface: this review is based on the campaign w/ a slight touch on post-campaign endgame, playing solo.Pros- Excellent acting and directing.  Some of the gameplay set pieces are the best I've ever seen in video games.  Some of the cutscenes are great.  I'd like to explain more, but avoiding spoilers.  - The Flash segments in particular I thought were AMAZING.  Most people don't realize Flash is arguably the most powerful earth-based superhero out there, essentially controlling time and space itself.  I think Rocksteady did a great job making me feel the true power of the Flash through setpieces, cutscenes, and the boss fight (yes, despite obviously us beating him ).  Even him being  was a nice touch.  Plus The Flash himself was very well acted and well-written as his non-possessed self.  - Overall good writing.  A lot of lol moments.  Some characters were maybe a bit inconsistent with what I'd expect (Wonder Woman and Deadshot in particular), but whatever, they're serialized superhero characters.  Any writer can write them how they want.- The basics of combat are good and interesting.  Combat sequences themselves?  Ehh...   But the foundation is there for some great combat, if missions/encounters were tweaked a bit.- Characters aren't too distinguishable, gameplay-wise, but it is nice to at least have some differences in traversal, I guess.Cons- The most frustrating con that really makes me not forgive this game is the mouse&keyboard sensitivity bug.  It seems to not be too common, I've only seen a couple threads about it, but I have my mouse sensitivity at 100, even for ADS, and I still have to swing my mouse across my mousepad like 2.5 times just to do a 180 or look downwards while airborne.  IT'S ANNOYING.  Too many times, my hand/mouse is hanging off my mousepad.  - While combat design itself is fine, encounters are just too poorly designed to make combat itself fun.  There's just too much going on and not enough to really track or understand why something is happening to you.  I can go into so many details, but it'd take up the max character usage for Steam reviews and I don't wanna add it after editing.  But just some missions and encounters, you don't know exactly what you are doing or supposed to do, you don't know where you are getting hit from, you don't know why something isn't working, snipers teleport for some reason, you need to do specific attacks just to heal/shield regen in a lot of chaos, etc. - So I just talked about encounters, but how about missions themselves?  Some missions are just weird and nonsensical.  The ones with specific criteria (nades only do damage, crits only do damage, etc) just seem to be inconvenient for the sake of being inconvenient.  - Party AI is frustrating at times.  I wish I could assign them targets or have a "gambit"/instruction list.  Sometimes I want them to just go to that other building and kill those mofos across the street.  Instead they just follow me around and shoot at my targets or just traverse around seemingly not doing anything.  Sometimes I can't really tell in all the chaos.  They'll maybe shoot at something else if I'm just standing there doing nothing.  I get this game is designed for co-op, but party AI can use a big boost.- Characters being more distinguishable in gameplay would be nice.  Why can't Shark just do a full tank/melee build?  Why can't Boomerang have more abilities and mechanics built around his...boomerang?  I feel like Deadshot and Harley should have been the gun-focused characters with their own separate nuances, Harley maybe more of a hybrid or trickster character, while Shark and Boomerang should have been way more distinguishable.Neutral- While I love the cutscenes, there was way too many cuts to Squad members' faces for no real reason besides showing them confused, smiling, etc.  It sorta took away from some scenes.- Some defeats of bosses are very anti-climactic.  I won't say that's a bad thing.  I've learned that in storytelling, not everything has to be climactic.  As major things in real life happen that aren't really climactic either.  I know this was a criticism for a lot of people.  It was kind of weird, but I won't dock it.- I did not mind the "lack of enemy variety".  Encounters are so chaotic, I'm not sure that really matters.- Regarding Batman.  I know some people are saying if he and , it'd be a lot better and "respectful" to Bats and...Kevin Conroy for some reason?  Either way, I can't disagree that for an Arkham game,    That being said, I don't mind that it was  - I'm not sure about the live service elements, but they seem non-predatory and pretty easy to get upgrades.  Non-FOMO Battle Passes and no p2w mtx are nice.  I could definitely see the endgame being unfun just due to the missions/encounters.  - I forgot where I heard it, but someone said the campaign feels like a long tutorial for the endgame.  I could easily see that.  Various forced missions for crafting rewards are sprinkled in the game, instead of just wanting to go to straight to the "kill the JL" objective.Anyway, I felt the story was definitely worth the experience.  I think playing it and "feeling" some of the setpieces would translate better than just watching a video on YT.  I have no gripes with writing, treatment of Batman, etc.  But too many missions, encounters, and the annoyance of kb/m just made the actual GAMEPLAY unfun too often.  I would 100% recommend this game for diehard DC fans or diehard live service fans or fans of horde shooters even.  Anyone else?  Ehh...just be prepared for what you are getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: Dissapointingly hallow.As a DC fanboy, I’ve been hyped for this game since it was announced. I went into KTJL wanting to love it. But I came out feeling empty.To start, the way people felt about this game was solidified from day one, no one was happy with it. Despite the negative reception however, I held out hope. Back when the game hadn’t even released, and many elements of the story were leaked and people criticized the hell out of it, I was still optimistic about KTJL. The circumstances sorrounding the build up to release were unfortunate. First, it was, like I mentioned, the story leaking early. Meaning everyone knew that the justice league were actually going to die (and for some reason, despite the title of this game, were surprised) and did not like where rocksteady was taking the story. Then it was the death of Kevin Conroy which people used to bad mouth the game knowing this was his send off as Batman, a mean spirited argument if I've ever seen one. And last, the many articles that came out criticizing the game all being done in bad faith talking bad about every detail that leaked, like the hud being too crowded for example was a big one. Like I stated preciously, despite all of this, I was still hopeful that rocksteady would deliver a banger. And I was mistaken. I’ll talk about the combat first since I have a lot of things to say about the story. I’ll preface this section by saying I played through the main campaign as Captain Boomerang since I heard he had the best movement, though I imagine the rest of the characters vary little in combat diversity. The combat is actually fun. For being a looter shooter. It reminds me a bit of Doom Eternal, if DE had 1/4 of its arsenal removed. The movement is smooth and thrilling. You also have a variety of special moves in your arsenal. The big complain, aside from the something else I’ll mention earlier, is the gun variety. Seeing as there are only two guns you have at your disposal at any time, it makes the gameplay get a repetitive fast. It’s funny because the Arkham games which arguably have less variety in terms of what you can really do in combat, never got old throughout the four main games. And this leads into what I mentioned earlier, the gameplay gets old quick. This is in part because every mission, despite how it may be worded, is the exact same thing, shooting bad guys until you can do something or something happens. Also this game is laughably easy. Let’s go back to the Arkham games comparison. In those games  you weren’t always doing the same thing in each mission, you were also sneaking around, doing detective work and many other Batman-y things that complimented the combat. Nothing in this game compliments the combat at all, shooting is everything. To end this section, I’ll talk about the bosses. Aside from story things I’ll talk about later, the bosses are bad. I was playing on the hardest difficulty available to me and I never died once, aside from Superman’s fight but that’s because I was ignoring very obvious gameplay hints. The bosses just repeat the same few, and I do mean few, moves until you kill them. I don’t have more to say about them because there’s nothing to say. Now onto the very controversial story. I’ll quickly touch on the less important aspects of it and move onto the big issues. First, I really like the world building, especially in the context of this being the Arkham verse. Metropolis is great. I reiterate again, I was fine with the whole Killing the Justice League thing, as long as it was done right, and it was not (shocker). I'm not referring to the whole Boomer pissing on Flash or Lantern being in his underwear controversy as that's the kind of thing I expected from a Suicide Squad game. The problem is that the deaths of these characters are not treated with the gravitas they should be. There is no send off for any member of the League, aside from maybe Batman but I hesitate to call that a send off, and the second they die, it's not even brushed off, it's just not touched on in the slightest, like I get these are supposed to be bad guys but even then, I'd expect them to at least have SOMETHING to say. I couldn't even tell when I killed the bosses, they just die, again, there is no grandeur for anything. Then there's Brainiac. The fact that the final confrontation on the main campaign is fighting him as the flash (literally just reused the flash fight as the final boss) says a lot, seeing as he is barely a character. I don't have anything to say about him other than he was very disappointing. Sad seeing as he's the MAIN BAD GUY. Finally, the end was horrible. At the end of the story, they reveal that in order to kill Brainiac, we have to fight and kill 13 different versions of him throughout the multiverse, and once you kill the Brainiac in your Earth, Amanda stabs him in the head with something, the squad celebrate and then they're interrupted by Lex telling them they still have 12 more Brainiac's to kill and... cut to credits, no I'm not joking, the game ends and nothing significant happens because we have 12 other DLC's to promote. The only thing I can say I liked about the story was the banter between the squad, it got a few chuckles from me.Overall, from the combat, to the story, to the characters, this game is empty. There is nothing substantial here that makes it worth playing. It's really sad seeing not only how bad this game turned out, but also how rocksteady's reputation was damaged. Not to mention the hole DC keep digging themselves in by releasing flop after flop. I'll wait to see how they wrap up this game, if they even do it at all, but I've learned from my mistakes, so my hopes are not high in the slightest. As much as it pains me to say, this game is not worth playing, if you really want to play it, I'd wait for a heavy discount because $70 for this is daylight robbery.Final notes for DC (not like they'll read it): Please stop using the evil Superman trope, not only is it worn out, it's also the most boring thing you can do with this amazing character. Also stop making Superman villains Justice League villains (I'm looking at you Brainiac and Darkseid)

_childDocuments_.review: I initially thought Suicide Squad had a lot going for it with amazing gameplay and the fun of getting around the city. The animations are weird and frequently don't match the movement speed, leading to a choppy and disjointed experience. It’s some kind of weird looter shooter now, which I didn’t enjoy. Additionally, there are issues with frame tearing, and being locked into one character once a mission starts can be frustrating.It almost felt like they made just enough content to get past being refunded and then gave up. Overall, I can't recommend it. It might be worth trying if it's on sale, but it's definitely not the must-buy I hoped it would be. It might make more sense with more experience.I recommend it if you enjoy DC Comics and well-written stories. I recommend it if you like to loot and bashing mobs.I do not recommend it if you're looking for a solo game. I've already reached the limit of that possibility, the game becomes tedious in solo mode, and even a pre-boss phase during the campaign is simply unenjoyable when played solo.Lastly, I do not recommend it if you don't like filling gauges and grinding for endgame gear.The story promises to continue in the upcoming seasons, we'll see if it's on the same level as the vanilla game or if it's just a gimmick to introduce new characters.I hope to make it my go-to game between seasons with Diablo IV, Last Epoch, and PoE 2.IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER: I played the game on both PS5 and PC. While there's nothing to complain about in terms of technical aspects on both platforms (I even have a 3080 GPU on my PC), there's a significant visibility issue on consoles. Everything is way too small in my opinion in terms of the HUD and tooltips.

_childDocuments_.review: As a devoted Harley Quinn enthusiast, I'm thrilled to share my adoration for this game! Its engaging game-play and compelling story-line are a breath of fresh air, steering clear of unnecessary complexities that often bog down other titles. The voice acting and dialogue are exceptional, with Tara Strong delivering an outstanding performance as Harley, capturing her essence perfectly. The game also pays heartfelt tributes to Arleen Sorkin and Kevin Conroy, adding emotional depth and respect for the legacy of these iconic voices.The boss battles are a highlight, offering just the right balance of challenge and fun. What really stands out is the unique dynamics of each character. Their distinct movement and combat styles provide a refreshing and enjoyable way to navigate through the game. Additionally, for fans of customization, the range of outfit choices is nothing short of spectacular, enhancing the visual experience and allowing for personal expression within the game's universe.If you are expecting this to be a different game then move on , but if you want a new fun and refreshing game to play with fan service and good times nab it!

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League: A Chaotic Blast (Even When It Falters)Calling all anti-heroes! Brace yourselves for a wild ride with "Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League," the latest offering from Rocksteady Studios. Buckle up, because this game is equal parts explosive fun, quirky characters, and head-scratching decisions.Let's dive into the good, the bad, and the Harley Quinn-tastic:Story: Brace yourself for a decent, not groundbreaking, narrative. It's about the Suicide Squad taking on brainwashed Justice League members. It's enjoyable if you dig comic book shenanigans, but might leave you lukewarm if you crave Shakespearean depth.Characters: Rocksteady truly shines here! Each squad member - from the psychotic charm of Harley Quinn to the brute strength of King Shark - feels distinct and well-developed. Their interactions are hilarious and banter-filled, even if some lines teeter on the edge of cringe.Gameplay: Ah, the meat of the experience! Movement is a joy, with each character offering unique traversal styles. Swinging through the city as Harley is exhilarating, while stomping around as King Shark is a power trip. Gunplay is tight and responsive, a rare gem in today's gaming landscape.Side Quests: This area needs work. They're repetitive and uninspired, feeling more like chores than engaging activities. However, the live-service model promises future improvements, so there's hope!Fun Factor: Let's be honest, this game is pure, chaotic fun. Squad up with friends and the experience explodes. Even with random teammates, laughter and mayhem are guaranteed.Overall: "Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League" isn't perfect, but it's a solid adventure with loads of potential. If you crave a unique shooter experience with a quirky cast, dive in. Just remember, you're here for the fun, not the Pulitzer Prize-winning story.Bonus Tip: For an even wilder ride, crank up the difficulty! It'll test your teamwork and make every victory feel legendary.So, is it worth your time? Absolutely, if you embrace the craziness. Just remember, it's not for everyone. But hey, even Harley Quinn would tell you that's part of the charm, right?Yes.... This was written with AI (Google Bard specifically), but I gave it the important bullet points to hit on since it's going to write something way more cohesive than I can.

_childDocuments_.review: Warner brothers might be the worst game publisher currently, they are hell bent on becoming the next Konami, seemingly turning every game into a live service with reports of the next harry potter game being live service despite being the best selling game of 2023 and being purely single player. Mortal kombat 1 was massively gutted and rushed out the door with all the worst aspects of a live service game and now rocksteady have fallen from grace in the public eye by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ out a live service shooter set in the arkham universe that nobody asked for. However, I absolutely love this game and feel it's somewhat unfairly been shunned due to it's connections with the arkham universe and it's live service approach, but why do I like it so much? I might enjoy arpgs and looters but I hated gotham knights and the avengers game so why do I love this game which is supposedly worse than both of those games, sold less and has less players than both of those games put together? Well let's discuss.To understand my preferences let me take you back to 2012, we had another batman game drop which didn't feature batman at all and was more like call of duty, this game was called Gotham City Impostors and it was a novel idea for a shooter, one that opened me up to the idea of a shooter set within the DC universe and something that was unfortunately shut down and de-listed.That being said when I saw the reveal of SS I didn't hate it, I was reminded of sunset overdrive and outriders; two games I enjoyed quite a bit, all wrapped up in a DC skin. So why does this game get a pass but gotham knights suck? Well this is because SS was made by rocksteady which means we have a detailed open world with so many nods and easter eggs, characters that feel authentic to the source material (yes, even twink joker.) And gameplay that is so fantastic that I cannot get enough of it. Gotham knights doesn't feel fluid and traversal in that game is so poor that it made me really hate playing it whilst SS has a massive focus on distinctive traversal for each character. If you take the idea of teleporting, which both GK and SS have a character that travels by this method (boomer and Robin) you can see how they thought to make this fairly bland method of travel fun for boomer, judging distances and incorporating some of the flashes moves into it. Robin on the other hand will just pause the game as you select where you wanna go. Gameplay is fantastic but if you're expecting anything similar to the arkham games you will be disappointed, I didn't and I love looter shooters, if you enjoy any form of looter then this game will be an easy recommendation. As someone who's mostly only playing arpgs/looters I find this game has some of the best moment to moment gameplay. The story was pretty funny, and quite enjoyable. I think people are way too attached to the arkhamverse and need to remember that this game is not going to have a lasting impact, spoilers I guess but it's been leaked that the JL will come back and rightfully so, the idea of the SS killing the JL is silly and the fact they just shoot them with guns is even sillier but if you embrace that and remember this is a dumb idea for a story you'll have more fun with it, I get that retconning batman back into the JL is dumb, harley not having anything meaningful to say to joker is dumb and having two desdshots with no explanation is dumb (the imposter theory isn't canon nor confirmed by RS.) Just enjoy the dumb ride and you'll have more fun. Really my only complaint and it's a big one is that endgame is lacking big time, like don't get me wrong I get looters are based in repetitive content, I run monos in last epoch so I get doing the same levels over and over is par for the course for the genre. But damn son we need more variety in missions, we have like 3 varieties and it really hurts the game. I joined during season 1 but I've seen this was basically the same loop for pre-season 1, it needs to be addressed but somehow I think RS will drop most support for this game. All in all a very fun mashup of games that means we get an enjoyable gameplay loop with fun character wrapped up in a fun story. I found myself thinking of borderlands, sunset overdrive, tony hawk and ratchet and clank when playing this. Get this on sale but don't let the online hate put you off especially if you like looters.

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad is what they call a "safe" game. What does that mean? Well there is no innovation, no cool special features. You learn everything about the gameplay with in the first badly done tutorials. After that rinse and repeat for EVERYTHING.Imagine taking Fortnite and just picking 2 features and making an entire game about that. Doesn't work. Sure it's safe to make, very little bugs and they can spend a lot of time on cut scenes. But the gameplay itself is not engaging and I lost the will to play it. Out of all the staff that worked on this game, they knew it wasn't going to do well. It was too simple their designers lack any imagination, skill or experience. This seems to be the new trend with so called "game designers" in the industry now a days. Most game developers don't play games anymore and have even said they hate games. Well this is what you get when you have people with zero passion for your product working on it. Most people only like working on games so they can tell they're friends they work on games. But in realatity, work wise they barely do any work. They come in for 8 hours sure, and socialize for about 6. Then stay late so they can get a free meal and head home, with maybe have doing 2 to 4 hours of work that day. This is the industry normal over the last decade and it's showing in all the shutdown studios and cancelled games. If you don't like games, go work else were.Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League delivers an engaging experience with its captivating story, memorable characters, and exhilarating gameplay. However, the inclusion of Easy Anti Cheat (EAC) and the implementation of Game as a Service have left a sour taste in many players' mouths.Upon pre-ordering the game, there was no mention of EAC or Game as a Service, yet these features were later added without prior notice. This lack of transparency feels like a bait and switch tactic, alienating players who prefer to enjoy their games without intrusive anti-cheat software or ongoing service requirements.The recent debacle with the Steam Deck further exacerbated the issue, as the game became unplayable due to compatibility issues with EAC. While the developer's response acknowledged the problem, the lack of official support for Steam Deck/Linux raises questions about their commitment to diverse gaming platforms.Despite these missteps, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League shines in its storytelling, cutscenes, and character portrayal. Playing as Harley Quinn is a particular highlight, and the game delivers on the promises made in its marketing materials.However, it's disheartening to see developers prioritize features that cater to a minority of players while neglecting the preferences of the broader gaming community. The emphasis on online multiplayer and Game as a Service models often overlooks the fact that many players still cherish the single-player experience.In conclusion, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a safe game with no innovation marred by questionable business practices. While the gameplay itself is enjoyable for a very short time, the inclusion of EAC and Game as a Service detracts from the overall experience. Hopefully, developers will heed the feedback and prioritize player satisfaction over corporate agendas in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult game to review. Publications giving Kill The Justice League a 5/10 seem unfairly critical for what I think is a game with a very solid foundation and polished gameplay (server issues and bugs aside). 5/10 to me says the game is poor, bad, or overwhelmed with performance issues. While I do not think this game is bad, I can't recommend it.The story, for the most part, was intriguing and the voice work/character animations were top notch. While I enjoyed sections of the story and had fun with the boss fights, the live service aspect of the game ultimately made the story feel disjointed and unfulfilled. There were small snippets of Arkham lore that I enjoyed walking through and experiencing, but there could have been more.I found the gameplay to be very fun and held my interest for 30+ hours despite the repetitive missions. Repetition is incredibly subjective, as all games have some form of repetition, it all just depends on the quality of the gameplay loop. However, in this case, the same 3 or 4 mission types are presented throughout the entire run of the game and post game. And while more mission types are hinted at for upcoming seasons, you're asking your audience to really stretch their enjoyment as they patiently wait months for something fresh.The gameplay mixes elements of Crackdown, Sunset Overdrive, and Borderlands, and that sounds like a great mix for a cooperative shooter. While I'm not overly critical of the decision to give all the Suicide Squad members guns, I don't think the IP was the right choice for this type of game.Overall, I'm right on the fence of recommending, because I still think playing through the story is an enjoyable and fun experience, especially if you have friends to join you. The game has good bones, and after a few seasons worth of content could become a great game. Whether that happens or not is uncertain.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.  I think people are over-critical of it.  The game play is great, although somewhat repetitive during side content, but most games are the same.  The characters look and feel very different, even though the core combat mechanics are shared, they all have their own tendencies and quirks about their skill trees and movement systems, creating a sense of individuality, solving an issue that Gotham Knights had (not the same studio, but they are often compared).  The story admitted could be a little better, some of it feels off, but it's not bad, and is well made up for by the character interactions.  The Squad's dialogue with each other is amazing, although you'll likely hear some repetitive conversations during side content, but that's definitely not unique to this game.  I think the issue a lot of people have with this game is that they wanted an Arkham Batman game.  But this isn't and never was intended to be an Arkham Batman game.  It may take place in the same continuity, but since this game is based on the Squad, then it should absolutely very differently, and it does so in a wonderful manner.  And if you have any story issues or continuity errors, well, comics-based worlds are just like that.  Just because the past of this game is the Arkham trilogy doesn't mean this is the only future from that trilogy.  And they can all be just as canon or non-canon, because comic-multiverse science says that both or even a million branching paths can exist at the same time.  So give this game a fair shot, it deserves it.
