_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: Chaotic, messy, noisy, but overall much more fun than Avengers and Anthem despite having a lot less variety in the play experience itself. Juggle enemies, run and gun, grenade, apply statuses and use a few specials built into the experience to execute and do AOE. Mission loops involve clearing towers, escorts, wiping out enemies under special conditions, using vehicles to destroy enemies, traversal challenges, and keep the action mostly varied enough and more interesting than say Avengers and Anthem. However, Avengers had actual move sets despite constantly making players feel weak with massive bullet sponges and superficial difficulty. Anthem, too. Suicide Squad avoids this problem, and also makes it really easy to hot swap between characters and feel effective no matter the level. This being said, not sure what kind of longevity anyone could expect out of the End Game. Graphics: Optimization leaves something to be desired, atm. The game looks good considering how much it has going on. Story: Tons of NPC dialogue. Great quips. The story is messy but fun. For the genre its much better than most of its contemporaries at launch. Value: For a 10-25 hour experience on the hardest difficulty the game is okay. Pricing of the in game store is trash. For the genre? Hours to dollar is really weak, the game competes with Anthem and Avengers and nobody else.  I don't regret the game, and I think the people trying to ruin the experience for others are toxic garbage. I'd arbitrarily give the game a 7 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Opening sequence could use a brief overhaul but otherwise: Traversal and vertical gameplay is fun. Some of the best currently. Feels a bit repetitive sometimes but the gunplay and unique abilities along with the traversal click together to make fights interesting. The voice acting is top notch. Every character has their quips and one liners that go over really well. They also kept the par for the course on Amanda Waller and how manipulative and hateful she can be. Being able to modify your equipment and score some good perks that flow well in combat also surprised me. Seeing how things can come together when matched up with your “build” add a certain flavor to combat. The two boss battles I’ve done so far are memorable. They didn’t disappoint. It really felt like in some ways you were outmatched but counteracting them was a blast. My only real negatives are how empty the city feels at the beginning of the game. As you progress the map becomes more lively but for someone skeptical it could seem like the game is bare with no real point to it other than the mission itself. Secondly, just feeling like you’re in the same kind of fight until modifiers come into play and there are some annoying ones but it does change the game up some. Is it worth full price? At the moment no, I think 50$ would have been a great price point but considering you have some really talented voices shaping the cast and a beautiful city to traverse through - I’d say I understand that budget wise this wasn’t a small undertaking. Wait for a sale if you’re on the fence. Watch a video of gameplay if you’re curious. Overall it is enjoyable, but this is only my opinion. It’s a recommend for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it the greatest game ever made? No, but if you enjoy frenetic shooters with good movement mechanics and decent modern-Marvel-movie humour, you'll have a blast with this one. There are some genuinely laugh out loud moments scattered through SSKTJL, and the story has all the trappings of a modern multiverse-laden comic book movie. Good stuff, I hope Rocksteady get another swing at this world and the characters, I'd love to see their take on a Justice League game similar to the output by Sony and Insomniac with Marvel. They clearly have the skills to make movement and action that feels just as good, and write stories that are fun and engaging with a breadth of characters that never feel overcrowded or singular focused.

_childDocuments_.review: As a someone who has played all the Arkham Games on multiple platforms, multiple times I will say that this game is not the greatest, but it is something that if you are a fan of the previous games like me you will have a good time. Its really fun, humerous, charming, and great with friends even if its story and some gameplay elements are not the greatest. However, the people saying that this game "is just a quick cash grab", "disrespects Kevin Conroy (RIP)", and "ruins Arkham Batman and his verse", are completely wrong and are not true fans of the previous games. Sure, the game is not perfect but that does not mean that time and effort were not put into this game. I mean all DLC besides COSMETICS are FREE. Combine this with the fact that the developers have a long road map where they will add new missions, maps, and characters to play, and you have dedicated developers and not money hungry scammers. Also story wise, its fine. Sure, it has its fair share of questionable choices and is not better than the other Arkham Games but that doesn't make it bad on its own. In fact the addition of a lot of new characters, fun locations, and a meaningful way of telling all of it, and you will find that the story is not nearly as bad as people are making it out to be.Also this game can be played up with 4 friends who I can tell you first hand will have a great time.Bottom line, if you played the previous games, you will enjoy aspects of this one. Sure, this games has its flaws and its story is not the best, but it still is a fun time that you can revisit time and time again, maybe not for full price.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: *Pros:* 1.) The game has phenomenal character development with unforgettable quips and story moments. 2.) Moving about metropolis feels fluid. You experience acrobatic adrenaline exactly how they do in comics.3.) Gear drops have some interesting loot with the rarest of items themed to named characters. (Like Bizzarro's Undeath Ray!! "No harm will come to your friends.") 4.) Rocksteady included references that make you smile, some that make you cry and others agitated. (In the end, the goal of a cinematic story is to invoke an emotional response. In that they succeeded.)5.) Boss Fights feel as they should. Flash zips around. Green Lantern has military themed constructs. 6.) Than you Kevin Conroy for all the hard work and determination you put into the character over the years.(His performance was stellar. And there is a certain poetry if you take into account the Arkham games. It's only fitting that story comes full circle. Just as it would have in Zach Snyder's JL with Afflec and Leto.) 6.) End game opens and endless string of missions for you to play and earn those unique gear drops.7.) Full year of free content starting next month. *Cons:*1.) Gamer elitist think they are 12th level intellects because they were raised on cancel culture.2.) Enemy types changes as the game progresses, but they are fundamentally the same "Alien" designs.(While I understand the invasion was in progress it would have been nice to fight against street gangs too.)*Overall:*As an artist and longtime fan of the characters, I thoroughly enjoyed the story. All of the hate that people are generating for this title is uncalled for. Rather than moving on with their lives, they choose to bash the buttons labeled: "Hating this product gives me internet points". Truth is there is nothing wrong with the game. People are just jumping on the bandwagon because it isn't in the Arkham play style, and that's what everyone is comparing it to.  If you actually open your mind you would understand that this isn't a story about Batman, therefore he won't be the focus... *Surprised gasp*The end game is also being chewed apart for just being replayable missions, but if you think about it how is it any different than other successful multiplayer shooter games: Apex Legends, Fortnite or Rainbow Six?  It's not. In those game you group up with friends and you tackle the same missions over and over. Same thing, yet this one includes an actual story and it gets hypocritical hate... The problem isn't the game. The problem is the audience being over saturated with "#NotMyArkham".Once they move on to regurgitating hate somewhere else, this game will be more approachable. Cyberpunk 2077 felt the same childish disdain, but hardcore fans of the series stuck with it and got anime + DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'll try to be as thorough as possible to give everyone a real good idea about how to go about this game and see if its for you.Story:The story is a good bit more light hearted and plays quite different to Arkham, so if you are trying to extract an Arkham trilogy story experience from this game, it is sadly not for you. There is a pretty good eb and flow to the story which is nice. Yes there are dry moments but also some amazing sequences that left me in a pretty wow state. Overall, the character work and such were amazing with the members playing off each other. I think the main story felt a bit short right now. But given that the expectation is the story will keep expanding into each season, we'll see how this evolves. But unfortunate coming from Rocksteady who have been prided on their amazing story work in Arkham.Gameplay:As a person that loves fast chaotic gameplay, this was my cup of tea. Once you nail down the movement for the characters, they become quite fluid and have pretty unique playstyles that takes a bit to master, but fun to start getting used to this. I started with Harley as its the most Arkham like character but expanding in to Boomerang and King Shark was quite different and loved the experience so far. The chaos you either love or you hate. If you like borderlands or crackdown, I think you'll like it. But if you are die hard Arkham, probably not the experience you were hoping for. The modifiers add a pretty good change to normally just shooting enemys. As you move more into the later game, realize that movement and constantly being on the move is very important or else game over at the later stages. Get used to movement because it will be your only option once you get into the harder difficulties and endgame.Endgame:As I'm just entering Endgame, I've been enjoying it. The build crafting has a bunch of death with Notorious and Infamy sets (with Villan synergys to add an extra layer). I think it has quite a ton of depth to really build that dream character. And now for the difficult part. The missions. Like with most live service, the endgame loop gets a bit dry toward as you climb. Same style missions and then going into Elseworld and doing more or less the same. My hope as that the mission set expands as the season goes and brings challenges that really test the capabilites of my builds. I've always loved raids and I think it could work here given the character set, world, and mechanics. I have yet to reach the final horde mode, so we'll have to see what that provides as well.Features:I think they did a great job in terms of features. Social squad is great to pull characters that are pretty built up if you don't want to touch certain ones. Leaderboards, clans, and other social features are widely present which is awesome to see. Crafting, enchancing and other mechanics are built naturally into the story and really bring power to your builds which is awesome to see, which some of the bigger looter shooters are still working on. And plenty of loot to go around. I think I have more difficulty figuring out what to get rid of, especially since you don't have a gear score so everything is pretty viable even in endgame.Overall:I think its a good game, but pending because we have to see how seasons stack up overtime, like any live service. I think they did a pretty good for the initial release. I haven't had very many issues in terms of bugs/glitches. Very slight (got my character stuck in a turret and game crashed once) if anything. But very smooth. Pointing back to what I stated before, if you go into this game thinking you are getting an Arkham game (yes I know its in that universe), it is 100% NOT that type of game. But if you take it with an open mind and enjoy the game for what it is, it becomes quite enjoyable. But this really depends on what type of games you like. So I recommend it to the person who loves looter shooters/grindy games with a solid story. Because that's where the meat and potatoes is supposed to be.But off the initial release, there isn't much mission diversity which hence hurts the game's standing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to sum up this game in a concise manner, but I'll give it my best shot:Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a looter shooter, through and through. If you want pretty fun gunplay with little-to-no variation to get loot that makes your numbers go up so you can then go get more loot, then you'll love this game. If you want it for literally any other quality, you should wait for a hefty discount, or skip it entirely.As said, the gunplay is fun, the characters are all different enough to keep things interesting when you switch, and you'll never run out of stuff to shoot or loot to acquire. The story, on the other hand, is dreadful; it all looks fantastic, and the actors are all giving their A-Game, but it's hard to put lipstick on a pig of this caliber. After a few hours of playtime, you'll be able to predict the trajectory of every conversation and story cutscene, because they all follow the same basic structure: things look serious with some jokes sprinkled in, the Squad (or someone else) will step up to be badass, and then the badass moment will get deflated by another joke or slapstick mishap. Rinse and repeat for 15 hours.I think this game would be a solid recommendation at something like a $30 price point, but at $70 (or more, for the fancier edition) I really can't recommend it to anyone but the most loot-deprived Destiny addict.

_childDocuments_.review: Only issue I have with the game being a PC enthusiast Is that I can't enjoy the ray- tracing option that is only available on the pc version. The game if you really pay attention looks quite a bit better with it on however with its enabled just plummets performance no matter what hardware you have with stutters and uneven frame timing. Watch the digital foundry video as they can confirm this as well. The good thing though is that there is a easy fix simply turn this option off and your basically getting the PS 5 and x box serious x version of the game except with slightly better graphics with everything on max settings and true 4k resolution with DLSS quality option depending on your rig. With Ray-tracing off the game performance is like butter, high fps smooth combat I had no issues running game at max setting 4k. I have a rtx 3090 and 5900x cpu and at 4k I hover in the most chaotic sections any where from 65 to 100fps very smooth with a g-sync monitor capped at 120fps.As far as the game itself it is not like a game I have ever played before. Yes very different then the previous batman arkham games but it was obviously intentional. They tried something different and it works. I def recommend playing this game with friends, as it was def made for multiplayer. Not that you cant play the game 1 player it is still good enough to be a great experience but with people it is a much better experience going threw the whole campaign together. Two factors that matter when it comes to this title is game play and story. Both are incredibly awesome. The open world I think is great and looks awesome. The Graphics without ray tracing still hold up and although not the best looking game ever created still hold up as a next gen looking title. I hope one day the devs will give out a patch to perhaps make ray tracing an option in the future. Say what you want about the development cycle of this game and the many postponements but whatever the devs went through when making this game they made the right decisions. If this was supposed to be a micro transaction pay to win title I am glad they made the necessary changes before release to change that. Playing the game right now not finished I do not feel an need to visit the store. Everything as far as loot upgrades and skill tree materials for crafting are all achieved threw game play as far as I am concerned and you really feel your character being more bad ass throughout the game. You can also change character at any moment. My only negative about the actual game play mechanics would be that as you level a character up that you choose first to control that all those points you achieved with that character don't also transfer to another character if you do decide to switch. You will have to level up another characters talent tree from the beginning  by grinding experience all over again. Maybe I am wrong about this but it is how it seems to be in my play through. Why not just have the points stored from the character that you are currently grinding with universal to all characters. This can effect players that are playing one player or even 2 or 3 players if you decide that you want to try another character at any point of the story campaign or beyond. Also I am still not on agreement on any game being 70$ but especially for this one I think its a spectacular game but not worth 70$ that's crazy. Many people have an issue with that however since it is a live service game I dont see much of a problem especially once you add the difficulty of the different conditions to them. The story itself isnt as fleshed out as the other arkham games in I feel like it really took a back seat to the gameplay loop. As somebody who really enjoys story I was really hoping for more and was left disappointed and wanting more, especially with how they brought Batman back from retirement.I have had a few connection issues playing solo which is rather bad sometimes. Even with cross play disabled and making it so not even friends can join me I often get disconnected 2-3 times a session which pushes back progress and loses items. More recently however, with the update, I cant even play a mission with out it being unable to load the map and I have to quit and rejoin losing all progress.Lastly I had to contact customer support for a promotion WB Game were having where having with twitch drops. Considering this is a live service game I thought they would be a bit faster with what they were doing and a bit more helpful but I was left kind of shocked an soured with their customer support.All in all, I wouldnt really recommend this game, its overpriced, repetitive and at this point I cant see it living past the first season pass in March especially if they keep the price that high

However, the current state of the game falls short of expectations, making it difficult to recommend at this time.While the character designs are a standout, the experience is marred by a lot of bugs, performance issues, and optimization problems that hinder the overall gameplay. The repetitive nature of the missions adds to the frustration, and the campaign fails to deliver a compelling narrative.One of the game's major disappointments is its endgame content, which offers very little to engage players once the main story concludes. The lack of meaningful activities makes the endgame experience feel hollow and unrewarding.Despite its potential, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League struggles to overcome its technical shortcomings and falls short of providing a satisfying gaming experience. _childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly, this game came out blazing, the biggest issues as of 1 day after launch, are performance on old rigs (1060 runs it at 40-60 FPS always) minor bugs here and there that could ruin immersion, annoying voice lines that repeat too much here and there, and the skill trees aren't really customizable, just one big linear tree split into 3 segments.However, the PROS heavily outweigh the *very fixable* CONS.- Very Good story, with really funny bits sprinkled in.- Well meshed mix between combat and movement, both really fun- Interesting elemental mechanics that defy industry norms and provide important combat style changes, and several layers of combat depth- Heavily detailed world with tons of references to comics, previous games, and such. - Enemy variety is probably perfect for combat complexity, I just wish they weren't all purple aliensAfter having just finished the Main Story (hyped to try the endgame content), I believe this almost the best game we could've gotten about the Suicide Squad.So far it deserves a solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: TRY TO GO INTO THE GAME WITH AN OPEN MIND!I know this sounds like cope but hear me out. I’m a huge fan of the Arkham games and anything Batman. I’ve played all the main line games and I love them all. So I understand how a fan of rocksteady games or Batman could be apprehensive about suicide squad. Look I had the same kind of knee jerk reaction like all of you guys. I wanted to hate it but after playing a decent amount of time I can’t in good faith call it awful. One of the biggest points I have to drill is THIS IS NOT AN ARKHAM GAME. This is the suicide squad. It’s a new take of characters in the Arkham verse. So going in thinking of the other games is only going to set you up for failure. Gameplay is snappy and smooth. Shooting mechanics are satisfying and feel great. I enjoying upgrading my legendary gear through the multiple side quest and contracts you can interact with in the menu or map. Harley Quinn has been my main and I have been having an absolute blast playing as her. Seriously she’s awesome. Story is serviceable. I’m not a big fan of the joss Wheaton James Gunn comedy writing style that most super hero games adopt these days but that is just personal taste. Sometime the characters just constantly yap at the mouth and it can be quite annoying lol. I recommend giving it a try on sale or just playing for an hour or two and refunding if you don’t find it fun. Try letting go and just have fun with it I promise it’s not the worst thing ever like how some are painting it out to be.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought I'd hate this game. The truth is I've really enjoyed it.The gameplay is fun and I still find myself discovering new ways to fight which always makes a game feel fresh. The story is a lot better than I imagine it would be and there's lots of laughs. I think the main issue in this game is setting it in the Arkhamverse, had this just been a different universe people would love it, but building it on the back of Arkham meant people (including myself) went in with too much bias. It was a silly mistake, but it can't be undone and the negative press will likely kill the game. I hope not, as I can't wait to see what they do in future content and I want Rocksteady to be able to put as much into this game as they want, not what the market dictates.In short, if you can't stand the idea of a game that changes Arkham Batman's story, don't play it.But if you like Batman or DC in general, I'd recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Gets extremely repetitive after you beat the base game, as of right now the full game isnt even released yet (technically)Starts off pretty strong, chapter 1 to the game is a blast to play, you got plenty of story to go through, the game makes sense. It has fantastic combat, fantastic traversal, fantastic music. But then after you beat the base game, it all goes to crap. Basically, the base game is the prologue, you have a set task at hand which is demonstrated through a lengthy tutorial type of game play. Once you beat the end boss of the prologue you are now officially on episode 1. Episode 1 is 100% free roam, you have quite a few missions to do, but they are all basically the same, Kill this, defend that, escort those. You must do these in order to kill the 2nd braniac and unlock the joker, but not just once. You have to re-do all of this live service content until you reach a certain level which gives you the honor to finally take down the 2nd braniac.Once you do the stuff for episode 1, you are now onto episode 2 which is the exact same as episode 1! Do all of the random free roam content repeatedly until you have the required level for the game to allow you the honor of killing the 3rd braniac, which at the time currently (There are supposed to be 13 braniacs and you only have access to 3. So yeah... Fun! I had a blast with the prologue actually, but being forced to grind because the company doesnt want to actually make a story for the following chapters is not my cup o' tea.

_childDocuments_.review: I never review games and I felt inclined to throw my opinion into the void because there are a lot of interesting takes out there.   The game is held back by the live service genre that its trying to be but despite that, its VERY fun. Get it on sale. I've had a lot of fun with it so far and I definitely plan on sticking with this.Now for story-I love a good underdog story. As much as I love the story, I wish they did more to really get into the psyche and backstory of these characters. The only disrespect against them are in these character bios in my opinion. I understand many peoples frustrations and people have such high expectations.It all just worked for me. Now for gameplay- I remember Avengers selling you on each character feeling like their own game, well in this case, I feel like SSKTJL is much more deserving of that. Killing aliens is way more fun than killing the same robots over and over. Avengers feels like button mashing compared to this.To be fair, you are killing a lot of the same enemies, but I think the overall gameplay loop and the combat mechanics are satisfying enough where it didn't really matter to me. That doesn't change the fact more enemy variety would be appreciated. The world is very fun to explore. Its typical Rocksteady environmental storytelling. Final takeEvery live service game is gonna have a store with the expectation of milking so much money from you, and that's what holds this game back from its true potential. It is the worst part of this game. They really want to make money off this game, as it only gives you a sample size of cosmetic items for each character. In this particular case, this is definitely the worst offender of all the live service games I've played. Because of this, I'd recommend getting this game on sale.  However! All of that aside, this game is FUN. Do with that what you will. I dont think Rocksteady is dead. Not yet anyways.  They're held hostage by WB Games if anything. With the studios closing recently, 9 years to ship a game and to have the game fail critically like this? Oof.

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad Review EDIT APRIL 2ND 2024:Please don't buy this game, the season model is insanely grindy and it adds basically no story content. Save your money. Don't support this game till they acknowledge these issues, such a sad way to see rocksteady go down.TLDR;6.5 out of 10    (EDIT: 2 out of 10)GAME IS MIDThe gameplay is super funThe story is below average Not worth $70, get it on sale This game is “something”. I've played all the Arkham games, and I have enjoyed what Rocksteady has done with that world. This is a huge step away from what they've done before. After beating the story, if you enjoy DC IP and these suicide squad members you'll be entertained. The story has its moments but it is a little stale. It is a rocksteady story though that can't be missed. The humor was pretty good but at the expanse of characters, I wish we had more time with them. The gameplay is honestly the most fun I've had in a while with a game like this, it is super chaotic and fast-paced pace but it is so much fun. Traversal is super fun and just fast. All the characters are unique in traversal and abilities, but the gunplay on all of them is similar enough. This is 100% a live service game and you can't escape that aspect of the game. It's always online, weapon rarities, resources, contracts, dailys, and loadout crafting. If you just wanna play the story and play the next game in the “Arkham Series”, you can do your best to ignore this aspect of the game but it will always be there, offline play is set to be coming at a later date post-release. I can best describe this game as if Destiny, Borderlands, Sunset Overdrive, and Warframe had a baby and slapped an Arkham coat of paint on it. If you enjoy those games you will enjoy this game if you like DC. Overall I give this game a 6.5 out of 10. Not worth the full price, and would be more fun with friends. Pleasantly surprised with the gameplay and traversal but slightly disappointed with the story. Addressing the big giant bat in the room, Yes I am Upset with how they treated Arkham Batman but it's whatever. I'm just glad I got to hear Kevin Conroy reprise the role of one of my favorite Batman adaptations one last time after his passing.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I enjoyed playing this game for the most part, combat and traversal is fun, the characters are honestly enjoyable with good banter between them, the standout in my opinion is Boomerang as his traversal and his characterization is extremely well done.However there are too many things about this game I am not a fan of. Live service games are not my favorite, I am also not the biggest fan of looter shooters, being that this game is a looter shooter it is very very Stat heavy, there is so much to keep track of if you want to buff your characters loadout as much as possible. As an example, each weapon has its own damage stats just to start, most and especially late game weapon drops also have extra stat buffs that can vary between how you engage in combat to what type of enemy takes the most effect. There are also Charms and neck bomb mods that also have their own individual stats and stat buffs, and on top of that if you get infamy items there are also buffs that can add up for using multiple items of an infamy set. So on and so forth. If the explanation seems confusing or sounds obnoxious then you have an understanding of how it is in game. There are three separate skill trees per character which is fine, but it feels like you can't really see or feel the upgrades you sink into your character. This game also gets extremely repetitive, many missions and side missions end up being pretty much the exact same things over and over, the exception is boss fights but even the final boss before season 1 is just the flash bossfight over again. The game just gets boring. Lastly, I am a Batman fan, The way Batman is dispatched feels disrespectful to his character. I am glad that Kevin Conroy enjoyed playing an evil version of Batman, however i feel like his character should have been handled very differently. Canonically this is the same Batman we have played as in gaming for the last 15 years and having him snuffed out so blandly was just a bummer honestly. I'm not mad that he died, a Batman death can be a very impactful event, but it needed to be handled better.Thanks for coming to my TED talk

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League - A Disappointing Dive into ChaosRating: ★★☆☆☆Marketed as a high-stakes superhero extravaganza, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League eventually fails, leaving an unpleasant taste in the mouths of both gamers and die-hard DC fans. Any potential enjoyment is overshadowed by the combination of terrible gameplay, a dull story, and a dubious treatment of Batman's character journey. However, the thing that hurts the most is the knowledge that this is Kevin Conroy's last appearance as the recognizable voice of Batman, and it's a terribly misguided farewell.Let us begin with the fundamentals: the gaming. It's a depressing mess that falls short of being the exciting, action-packed experience that was promised. The praised squad dynamics feel more like an unneeded burden than a novel innovation, and the controls are awkward. The fighting isn't as smooth and sophisticated as one might expect from a game in this genre; it has repeated scenes that get old faster than you can say "Gotham City."The story, which is touted as the highlight, is a forgettable jumble of drab happenings. The narrative is shallow, and attempts at humor are frequently unsuccessful. Character arcs are flimsy attempts at evoking strong feelings in gamers who are immersed in DC mythology, and they fall flat. A cliched plot that undervalues the excellent source material ruins the possibility of an engrossing story.Perhaps the most grievous misstep in Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is the handling of Batman, voiced by the legendary Kevin Conroy. As the final chapter for Conroy's portrayal of the Dark Knight, one would expect a fitting send-off, a poignant moment to honor the years of dedication he brought to the character. Instead, the narrative takes a bizarre turn, betraying the essence of Batman and leaving Conroy's iconic voice attached to a character arc that feels like a slap in the face to fans.Without delving too deep into spoilers, Batman's role in the story is a departure from the character's core principles, and it's a narrative decision that does no justice to Kevin Conroy's incredible legacy. The mishandling of this farewell leaves a sour taste, tarnishing what should have been a momentous occasion for both the actor and the fans who have followed his remarkable journey as Batman.At the end of the day, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a depressing end to Kevin Conroy's Batman career as well as a disappointment for gamers. This game is a terrible disgrace to the memory of one of the most recognizable characters in gaming because of its unimpressive gameplay, dreary narration, and careless handling of a great voice actor's farewell performance.

_childDocuments_.review: SALE RECOMMENDATION: 20 DOLLARS MAXIMUM - 6-6.5/10DO NOT BUY THE DELUXE EDITION!!!!If you've ever gotten home and felt the need to grab a controller instead of a mouse, to just mind numbingly shoot at cannon fodder to satisfy your stress or adhd urges, this is it.It's an entertaining enough ride that doesn't require too much brainpower, and is even more fun to ♥♥♥♥ on with friends.- A decent game to play with close friends who you enjoy talking with for hours, while you do the menial labour required to reach the next story cutscene. STORY AND DIALOGUEThe story is surprizingly decent considering where it comes from, but that's when you let all your arkham and super hero knowledge sit on the sideline.  If you're a die hard arkham fan who keeps comic knowledge on hand, there may be a lot to pick apart. The banter was one of the highlights, i thought the evolving group dynamics were interesting and most nps give different dialogue responses(outside of main story) depending on your character, so at least there's thatGAMEPLAYBoy is this loaded. It's fun and fast paced but it is also,  extremely repetitive. The story missions are fairly unique, there's cool cutscenes, and it's a blast...for the first few hours. The game forces you to collect all your npc stores in the form of penguin, toyman, ivy, etc, and from there you play 1 of 3 missions, Hold the Point, or Rescue the Civilian, or Escort. That's it. the entire game. Every side quest is literally just this with different text. No unique interactions, surprise cameos, nothing. The guns feel like they don't do much, and from what I've played in 13hours, loot comes slow, doesn't add much feel to the gameplay, and once you have a legendary or mythic you can safely never check your loadout for the rest of the game pretty much. And XP is a griiiiiiind. Each character levels individually and doesn't level without playing them. The game struggles between telling you to play as everyone, and telling you to stick as one character. If you play as everyone you're probably not going to reach full builds for skills.The UI goes from fairly meh, to absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the late game as absolutely everything results in a 1000 visual effects going off. It's too much. The story builds up quite nicely, and then proceeds to speed run the ending as if to get you to the live service component as fast as possible. It's lazy writing that feels unfinished. They actually introduced some cool story elements and all of that is just ♥♥♥♥ on by a horrid final section of the game, and the worst final boss fight I have ever come across. When every fight feels like every other fight, you've got a stale game. THE ENDGAMEIt's not even a spoiler, the whole game points towards it. Once you kill braniac, which is a garbage boss fight. You're told there's 12 more Brainiacs across the multiverse. From there the long tedious farming begins and the game does nothing to help you how to understand it all. It's one of the worst endgames I've ever seen. _childDocuments_.review: I had overwhelmingly low expectations going in, and i was still somehow disappointed. I've never played the Arkham games, so i'm not biased by what came before, but this game was honestly broken on concept and had no shot at being good.gameplay wise:-the loot system is extremely boring and almost pointless. i'm getting showered in legendarily and uniques(hell the first weapon drop i got was a legendary) and my main character(boomerang) had a complete loadout of legendary or better before i even hit level 10.-the skill trees for each character are similar to the ones in borderlands, but they somehow ♥♥♥♥♥♥ them up since you have no agency over which skills you take. you get one skill per row per tree, and the game picks for you which tree you get a skill point for so you have to level up all 3 evenly. and even worse, most of the perks are extremely boring. you know in borderlands 2 how your perk loadout could completely change the way you play each character based on just one or two perks? yeah that's gone most of the perks i've seen so far are basic stat buffs. the only interesting one i've seen so far is a perk for captain boomerang that slows down time on an enemy when you melee them-the traversal mechanics are pretty dull. there's 4, one per character(a jetpack, a teleport, a grapple, and a super jump) and all four are too under baked to be even slightly interesting or fun to use. compare harley's grapple to the swinging in spider-man 2 and it really shows how under-used all of these mechanics are since they needed to make 4 instead of focusing on making 1 good one.-the difficulty is a joke. i beat green lantern and flash in one try on the hardest difficulty and acording to the game i was under equiped for both. neither fight was difficult, i just had to run around like a headless chicken for 10 minutes taking pot shots with the legendary sniper rifle the game shouldn't have given me yet.-the modifiers on missions are just flat out irritating rather than interesting. you want to only be able to kill enemies with a limited resource(grenades) that you can run out of and all your other weapons deal 0 damage? you want to only be able to deal damage with crits on enemies that have very unclear crit spots and all other damage heals them? no? too bad.-the game basically requires a controller since the mouse controls are so bad(good luck sniping)-the scopes are useless. i hit the button to scope in with a sniper rifle and it feels like the camera barely zoomed in at all, it just goes into first person instead of third person without actually changing the distence.writing wise: i hate it. i hate all of it. there are 4 characters in this game who come anywhere near close to likable, and they're king shark, boomerang(sometimes), flash(in the 3 cutscenes before he dies), and deadshot(because he hates everyone in this damn game as much as i do). the fact harley is a main character too doesn't do it any favors, because she is at her absolute most annoying that she's been in the past several years and not a single line out of her ear piercingly awful voice was funny. in fact none of the jokes in this game are funny, i laughed literally one time in 10 hours and it was when deadshot tried to snipe flash and then flash was looking over deadshots shoulder and said "did you get him?". that's it. that's the one funny joke in the whole game and i just spoiled it for you so if you want to play this game for the humor you don't have to anymore.and the overall plot is just a flat out bad idea to begin with, even if it were done well which it isn't, because where the hell do you go from here? this is a live service game so what the ♥♥♥♥ are you supposed to do now? the game's called "kill the justice league" so after you kill the 5(not even 7, 5) members of the league, what next? is a new league gonna form off screen and then get mind controlled by a different bad guy so we can kill them next and literally piss on their corpse again?if you like DC, don't play this game, because it couldn't be more clear that the writers of this game outright hate this property and only like harley quinn and wonder woman while wanting to disrespect every other aspect of this world that they possibly can.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played as long as I did to complete the story and to see what the "content" updates would have in store (Written as of Joker update), but I do not recommend this game at all. *Minor spoilers ahead*For the price the game is at ($90 CAN/$70 USD) the content and the updates are not painting a pretty picture for it being worth that price. If you REALLY want to play it, wait until it is maybe $10-$30. Even though the price of entry is steep, they also included micro-transactions like every modern videogame has now. Another strain on your wallet and I implore you not to buy anything from the store no matter if you paid full price like I have, or got the game for free. Be aware, some people who bought the deluxe edition have not received the justice league skins that came with the edition, as well some other players in general have not received the in-game currency that are used to purchase things in the store (As of writing this).The gameplay is nice but cannot save the entire experience you have in the game. The game is highly repetitive as you do the same type of objective and will always face the same enemies except for some small differences like big guy into fast big guy, or if they put a frustrating restriction on your objective such as shoot legs only, critical hits only, etc. As well, the game says it takes 11 hours if you only focus on the story missions, however, what they fail to mention is in those 11 hours, you only do about 4 hours of story specific missions, and the other 7 hours on missions that are meant for the endgame content but with the characters talking about the story. Also SPOILERS: Yes, you do kill the justice league.As of the first season with the Joker, the content you are given are the same missions you've been doing throughout the whole game. Before the game's release, there were rumours and leaks of a battlepass in this full priced game. The game did not launch with it, but the first season brought in that battlepass we were afraid of. The BP costs the usual 10 bucks that every damn BP costs in other games, but the content surrounding the game is not worth paying another $10 for some skins and coins. There is a droplet of story content added to the game, essentially telling you, again, to "keep fighting loser."Personally, I never liked this game's conception, but I went in to the game on release with both spite and wanting to be genuinely proven wrong as I love the Arkham games and wanted to believe in Rocksteady. However, I was surprised with how worse it was than I thought it would be.

_childDocuments_.review: In this specific moment, I cannot recommend it UNLESS you're a die hard superhero AND looter shooter fan, but even then for some people that may not be enough. Willing to update as the seasons come along.+ Presentation of the story is truly next level+ Graphics are fantastic, especially facial animations and quality+ Gameplay is initially exciting and dynamic, with an emphasis on verticality and traversal+ End game loot is interesting and changes the way you play- Mission variety is severely lacking, the activities are: protect two points, destroy purple points, collect resource and turn in, and follow a payload that stops periodically that you have to protect- Enemy variety is also on the light end, most of the baddies look like some variation of the purple, bio-mechanic alien with one "infused" type; there are also only 5 boss fights in the game- Characters play nearly identical with the exception of traversal; each character shoots 3 types of guns out of 6 total, throws grenades, has a melee, has a single target (Suicide Strike) and an AOE ability (Traversal Attack)- Talent trees are primarily stat buffs or boosts; some talents are even copied from each other's tree (example, Harley and Deadshot have a talent to increase melee dmg but increases melee cooldown by 2 secs)- Campaign is <10 hours if you commit to just the main story and you do the same repetitive activities listed above- Endgame is aforementioned repetitive activities with specific conditions that you've already played throughout the entire campaign- (Subjective) did not like the overall narrative and the way in which we kill the Justice League; many story instances were actually extremely disrespectful and not loyal to the source material

_childDocuments_.review: i was stuck on the loading screen for almost 20 minutes .... not exactly ideal.REVISITED:After some fixes and waiting almost the rest of the year, i decided to give this game one more shot to see if the hate it get's is deserved, or if it seems out of proportion. NOTICE- I WILL BE ADDING SPOILERS WITHIN THIS REVIEW FOR NEW PLAYERS WHO MAY BE INTERESTED IN THE GAME.GAMEPLAY: Now the first thing you need to understand here is that it is more of a manic shooter in thirst person than it is just your standard shooter, it tries to incorporate looter shooter aspects with risk/reward missions but mid way through the initial story you will already have most of the best items in the game, with little to no variety in between. Enemies can blend together with only the most mild of differences that can barely set them apart, though this is an unfortunate downside they still keep you engaged. Each character's traversal ability makes for unique combat which helps you with various play styles, though controlling specific characters can be tricky, especially during intense level missions. A very unfortunate factor is that the game include unique combat mechanics that are mission exclusives, vehicular combat, environment combat (in the ways of status debuffs) and what not are only used during for those sets of events instead of being majorly inclusive throughout the experience, but it does still makes those few moments in between fun during their use. Online play is optional, it is not required to play this game but having a friend or 3 to mess around for a chaotic shooting spree can be enjoyable so long as co-ordination is held, the enemies, while lacking in diversity, do become difficult when they gather on mass, so knowing who can help you is good, and preparing for solo's with 3 bots just means grinding prep work.STORY AND KEY MOMENTS OF THE GAME: CONCLUSION: Does this game deserve the hate it gets? To a marginal degree in some areas such as the lack of enemy diversity and handling of bosses, BUT in those area's it is something of tricky thing to handle with a limited budget, and despite being in development for almost 7+ years, it could not have been easy to include all the characters and functions they would have wanted to include. Is this game worth playing? Personally, i think so but not at the oversaturated prices they ask for. I grabbed this game while it was on sale, 14 and change after tax for the base copy, wouldn't recommend getting digital as it doesn't really offer anything substancial to enhance the gameplay experience outside of some costumes and a battle pass for more costumes, emotes ect.What are my final thoughts? Mmm ... Despite what complaints people may have, and regardless of flaws, this game shows an ambition that could have opened up a possible extension in all DC games, but either through poor decision making or financial issues, it fell just shy of the mark, if it had more time to properly develop its core goals and function, it may have been something to blow the industry away, but at the very least, it gave a solid attempt, but maybe they will get it right the next time, if there is a next time for Rock Steady Studio's.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I wish Steam allowed neutral reviews.In general I've been having fun playing it, but I feel hard pressed to recommend the game to most people right now at its $70-100 price tag and a potentially uncertain future.Positives:The story for the most part was interesting. It was interesting to see it tied into the ArkhamverseThe campaign missions were mostly goodThe gameplay loop is pretty fun, especially as you build up your skills and start experimenting with different buildsThe voice acting and cinematics were pretty goodNegatives:The side quests, random encounters (if you can call them that), and post-game content is very repetitive. It's always the same three-four types of missions with the same enemies.Because of that there isn't much of a reason to stick around after the campaign other than for grinding for equipment and completing all the Riddler challenges.The game isn't very well optimized. The game is playable and a lot better than some other broken releases we've seen, but performance isn't where I'd expect it, and often there are drops in FPS or short freezes when traversing. This was more of an issue with my laptop than my desktop, so your experience may varyYou would think that a live service game would actually have a decent amount of cosmetics in the store, but there isn't so farThere have been some bugs causing loading issues and progression issues. Some of which Rocksteady has fixed.The story, while interesting, feels like it ends at an intermission rather than a satisfying end. Presumably the story will be completed with future content, but with the low play rate it may be possible that a good ending is never provided. I hope I'm wrong though.There are things I enjoyed in Suicide Squad. I had a good time playing through the story and doing many of the side quest and the general combat loop can be a lot of fun and satisfying. Unfortunately with a lot of the non-story and end-game content being very repetitive, not great optimization, and uncertainty of the future of the game I would be hard-pressed to recommend it at full price. Maybe wait for a sale.I hope season 1 turns the game around and the future content doesn't get cancelled. I think there are some good things going for the game, but it should have been built out more, even if that meant delaying it for another year. Even as someone who likes the game, it's hard to have a lot of confidence in the game's future right now and recommend a $70 live-service game because of it. We don't know what will happen, so it makes no sense to recommend a game on what it may potentially become, only as it is. For most people I'd recommend waiting for a sale or season 1.Maybe things will turn around as time goes on. It probably depends how much Rocksteady is able to invest in the game moving forward. If things get better maybe I'll change my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Rocksteady... shame on you. What can I say about this game? I could talk about the repetitive nature of the looter shooter aspect. Horde mode, escort, defend objects A, B, and C. I could talk about the over inflated U.I. I could talk about how the ending of the game feels engineered to sell DLC and post game content. But what I really want to talk about is the story and characters. I grew up loving superheroes and I grew up loving the Arkham games. This game is... nothing short of disrespectful to those characters. The Squad exists only to tell cheap throw away jokes almost every 2 seconds and barely evolve as characters over the coarse of the game. Ultimately, for a supposed story driven game set in the universe involving some of my favorite childhood heroes, for me at least, this game is utterly disappointing and very disrespectful. The Justice League, us fans, and especially Batman deserved better than this after 9 years since Arkham Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Buy the game if you like DC. It's a looter shooter, so if you want Arkham-style games, look elsewhere. Great movement, hilarious characters, fun gameplay, story so far is great. Only a few hours in, and it's nowhere close to what reviewers actually think about it. Also, since it's live-service, it actually gets updates. Bugs will get fixed, unlike Star Wars Jedi: Survivor. yes, you have to be online, but they plan on adding offline support in a future update. 9/10 go on Eneba to get the game for $20 off. $70 is too much for any game, no matter how good it is.I bought a key for the deluxe edition $20 cheaper than it is. Played up to the section where you are able to choose your first mission to go on. I honestly don't understand the criticism. Jester award me all you want, the game is really fun. I've listened to Gameranx and MoistCr1tikal's reviews. I just feel like they're completely off. The humor is the typical DC humor. Deadshot is the only serious one, Harley being the jokester (and asking Wonder Woman to step on her at one point), King Shark being the dumb brute (and probably the most fun character to play/listen to), and Captain Boomerang is the one everyone makes fun of for being Australian and cowardly (but he somehow provides ACTUAL help in this game).The movement is EXTREMELY creative. Harley uses a Bat-Drone to grapple off of, King Shark just has brute force to launch himself, Captain Boomerang has a boomerang that teleports him forward, and Deadshot has a jetpack. The gameplay is extremely fun. You get boosts for higher difficulties. There are times when a character gets a Psycho Boost, and if you play as them, you get tons of xp, more health, etc... The enemies so far are pretty standard. Nothing special, just your stereotypical base level enemies. You can easily avoid them and just get to the story, or you can fight every single enemy in your way.Story so far is great. Introduces some more obscure DC characters, which I really like. There's a section that recaps the Arkham games so you don't need to spend more money to understand the rest of the lore. I've heard there's lots of post-game content. I don't know much about it. No opinion on it.I don't know if it's just me or my PC, but randomly, in combat, my audio will cut out. It's probably because I have to have everything on low, but hopefully add some better optimization for GTX 1650's lolOverall, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:I've returned now that we've been shown what the full game is gonna be like.  After being promised the free 'live service' year with story and characters, I had hope Rocksteady would pull something out the bag and show us what a live service can really be.You'd have to play hrs of repetitive missions to even play as the joker, or buy him for $10, really nice guys.  This is after months of people experiencing of a game breaking bug.  Negative review in protest essentially!End of game update:All of the boss fights are awesome, super themed, difficult, and reasonably complex, definitely Arkham level quality.  I find they fizzle out at the end though, with this most powerful superhero just kinda falling over and dying like a regular dude without speaking.The combat is super fun however doesn't quite have the staying power for me, and the enemy variety is there but nothing special.  The final mission shows the potential of the combat & mission structure, so there's real hope for the year 1 of content.  The current endgame however seems lackluster.The map and theme of the game is well done.  There's a few decent serious moments as well as some smart & awesome superhero based story beats like you'd expect from Rocksteady.  The humour definitely takes center stage while also playing it fairly safe.. it did still get some laughs out of me.So far the story beats are well thought out, and the lore and world are well realised, the Justice league are legit & the characters they chose for the suicide squad have turned out ok!  The combat requires some calm focus then you can start putting it together, after a few hours i'm starting to find it pretty fun, and the movement abilities are inventive.  Map is decent however potentially a little bit plain/unthemed will have to see, but layout wise it has incredible verticality, need to see it at night!  Graphics are decent & more modern overall.. however maybe less attention to detail in comparison to AK.  The game emanates respect for the Arkham series so far.

Thank God it isn't complete trash like that title. I will admit the endgame is a problem but lets talk our way there. So The gameplay loop is satisfying. I know a lot of people complain about the UI being all over the place but tbh it doesn't bother me too much considering you can turn most of it off & the gameplay is so crazy and chaotic the UI doesn't really phase me. I'm too busy trying to stay alive and kill everything with the amount of ♥♥♥♥ happening. As for the performance? I can get 60 fps on native 4k with mostly high settings I do have to turn 1-2 settings to medium. However the thermals are up there. So not a well optimized game but in this day and age unfortunately that's very common and at least I am able to actually hit target frames without the use of DLSS or dynamic resolution.As a long time arkham fan its crazy for me to admit it but the story is not bad at all. Nonetheless I felt some type of way being forced to put down my beloved heroes one by one because that was the only way to save the day. Bats himself wouldn't have had it any other way. I know people wanted a JL game but we can still get one. They can always do prequels that lead up to this moment and possibly flashpoint it later in order to restore the TL. It consists of literally grinding the same 5 missions over & over again for better loot (terrible rng btw) and to raise your mastery enough to get better rewards. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that like many people, I'm a huge fan of all the four Arkham games. While Suicide Squad: Kill the justice league is no where near the same level as one of those games, there is still quite a bit of fun to be had with plenty of good moments at least for me. While the story of the game is nothing special, it was still okay for me and the voice acting as always was spectacular with a great ensemble of cast members and I enjoyed the jokes even though they were cheesy. While I would've loved to see a proper justice league game in the Arkham-verse before the events that happened in this game (considering the story bits that have released so far - Season 1) I'm not mad or anything with Rocksteady for not doing it, as this is what they ended up making and surely every person that worked on this game poured that heart and soul into this.The combat is fast and mindlessly fun, it doesn't have the depth of the Arkham games but I guess it all comes down to the live-service aspect of it all. Graphics are good (Especially the character rendering and facial animations are very next gen), it starts off weak (The environments) when compared to the Arkham games especially Arkham knight as it's not as flashy and bold as that game was. It's more nuanced and I grew to appreciate it more as I continued playing, that said the performance could be a lot better on PC atleast. (The open-world Unreal Engine stutter fest is hard to escape these days, I really hope developers are able to fix this, I know that the folks who made Atomic heart and a few other games were able to, so I guess there is still hope).I mostly play single player experiences as that is what I enjoy most, and like many people I was initially put off by the whole live-service model as I typically don't enjoy that genre of games but I have to say that as a solo player, I still ended up having a good time. After 9 years or so since the release of Arkham Knight, I get that there could've been a much better game than this if Rocksteady had developed a single player narrative driven action game, but it's hard to escape the corporate overlords and them ruining the gaming industry slowly, I truly hope they learn sooner rather than later that this is not okay.But I'm happy that I bought this game finally and I enjoyed it thoroughly. I sincerely thank each of every person at Rocksteady for making this happen and wish them all the best of luck for whatever they do next. While this game is a commercial failure, I just hope that "at least this" is a lesson to Warner Bros. and countless other corporations that not everything has to be a live-service game. I really hope Rocksteady doesn't get axed over this and I urge the community to at least try the game and not simply bash on it.And lastly, Rest in peace to the legend Kevin Conroy, your legacy will live on forever in our hearts and a big thank you for giving us Batman. My deepest heartfelt condolences to Matthew White's family, who unfortunately lost his life because of all the pressure he was facing, it is really sad that we all are forgetting that all this backlash is being targeted at real people who're at the end of the day trying to do their best to make these wonderful games and they deserve better treatment. Not enough is being done from the community to stop this type of hate and it is high time that everyone realises that.

_childDocuments_.review: What a waste of missed potential. That's honestly the best I could say about it in summary. Is it terrible? No, it's not the worst game ever, nowhere close. It's just... mediocre at pretty much every avenue. It doesn't feel like it fits in the Arkham universe at all even though they're forcing it into that universe. The characters have very little of actual interest outside of them being characters we already like from other media. Some jokes land (not enough to full on laugh but some made me chuckle), but the writing overall just feels very first Suicide Squad movie instead of The Suicide Squad movie quality, if that makes sense.Graphics are nice but even there there's major issues: Tone-wise it clashes with the established universe, but worse: performance is actual ass. I have a 4090 and this game can't hold 60FPS, no matter the quality settings. DLSS does absolutely zero (in fact, it somehow makes performance worse). You'd think by now they would've addressed the most pressing performance issues, but sadly not.The AI for the enemies is braindead. There's like only 3 or 4 enemy types that you fight all the way through outside of the boss fights. The boss fights at first seem pretty far apart but then suddenly you just kill off Justice League member after JL member. And even they aren't really interesting. All they do is taunt. There's only one moment that actually had some depth which was when Diana (Wonder Woman) calls out for Barry and he briefly becomes himself again to talk to her. The Suicide Squad in this just makes no sense overall. Superman, Batman, The Flash, Green Lantern, even Wonder Woman, all these can't stand against Brainiac but somehow these 4 people with no powers and just some gadgetry can not only fight and kill Brainiac, but also kill Superman, Batman, The Flash and Green Lantern. Never did it actually feel like what they were doing made sense, it wasn't written well. It was always just "oh we found this new macguffin that will stop the powers of this hero"Boss fights were very uncreative except for the one against Batman. All of them were just bulletsponges with shields. Exceptionally dull.The combat is pretty fun for a while but with the performance being as it is (constantly fighting to hit 60, often falling below 40) it's hard to enjoy. I played the entire game as Harley Quinn and got an OP pistol pretty early on which I finished the entire game with, so I wouldn't say this game was a challenge, except for actually understanding all the different damage numbers/affliction numbers. If seeing numbers goes up makes you feel things, you might like this game but to me it's just another game in literal 30+ years of games doing this thing where they have new weapons with higher stats except those weapons look exactly the same as weapons you already had. Weapons drop so often as well that there's barely any reason to ever craft or mod (I touched those things once)Overall, just genuinely a mid-ass game with maybe 1 or 2 highlights. I'd give it a 6/10 on a scale though think scales don't really tell the whole story so the context is definitely important.Rocksteady fell hard with this game imo. Arkham Knight isn't perfect but it's miles better than this game sadly. Which sucks because I genuinely like Harley Quinn and was excited for a game with her.

The game is dark at times yes, You're playing as Villains, it's to be expected. I haven't made it to the Batman boss fight yet, but so far I believe they've written Batman really, really well. He's a force of nature, especially for just a Rich guy in body armour. The Crafting is wonderful, making it not too RNG to create the build you want. The enemies are varied, have a great variety & at the point of the game I'm at, don't feel like Cannon Fodder. All in all, I'm really enjoying this & I'm looking forward to keep playing it, hitting endgame & playing the new Seasons (Which all content besides some cosmetics for the new characters, are completely free with NO FOMO)

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say it's truly unfortunate how many people have decided it's in vogue to trash talk this game. The specific details they go to when doing so suggests they enjoy playing it just as much as they enjoy the gripes.As of this writing, Suicide Squad is still in an early state. Endgame content isn't especially deep yet, and there are still obvious bugs throughout the game. But it's playable. In fact, my sub-minimum specs laptop plays the game at a solid 25-30 FPS. Bug fixes come regularly.The primary appeal of the game in my mind is the IP. The DC universe in which it is set and the characters have a sense of familiarity that makes the gameplay more appealing that it would if we didn't already have some idea where we were. Character dialogue and cinematics really help sell the game.From a gameplay perspective, the types of enemies and missions can be repetitive. That's where the story helps drive the experience. If you're just in it for the grind and the loot, you may not enjoy it so much. What sets Suicide Squad apart from others in its genre besides the setting is character traversal, which to my surprise I found myself using more and more skillfully as I progressed. The biggest drawback to learning the game is that a great many gameplay mechanics aren't clearly explained in-game. Since the game is still pretty new, there isn't a good resource to point to for explaining the nitty gritty details yet. Fortunately you can get by without them fine for the most part.This is clearly no Batman Arkham game, despite building on the franchise's legacy. I wouldn't call it the masterpiece those games were ether. But heck, it's still a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I played single player games for 5 years and mostly prefers single player game. Look into my steam profile and see how many single player games there is. Here is my spoiler free 2-cents takes on this game:*I got in on day 1 of PC early access and did not get kick out of server nor encountered any bug. Frame rate is super smooth, 70 to 90 fps 4K resolution, did not need to do any setting adjustment. I'm on RTX 3080Ti, i7 12700k. 1) Story, facial and voice acting. -As of writing this on 10hrs playtime, I had not completed the story. I did not rush thru the main story back to back; did some sides mission/riddles puzzle to unlock new features/lore and loot in the MASSIVE beautiful open world. -voice acting is super high class feeling in which u can feel the emotions of the dialogues. It's not mono tones. -facial animation is the best and top notch! During close up cinematic cut scenes, every main character and NPC u can see the micro expressions on their face. -lots of funny moments actions, not just dialogues. The comedy part of this game is even better than guardian of the galaxy (which I completed). Because the 4 members of SS will make hell break loose in a funny way inside the game. -story I would not say it's rich (witcher 3 rich) because that's the gene of live service game where story is not the focus. However, it's quite immersive as every part there is surprise and u would not have expected this would happen. Glad that in this game it was being interpreted exactly in the movies where suicide squad is not a totally evil teams, they do have a good side but don't want to show it out. 2) Combat (the main fun!) -combat is very fluid smooth transition from Melee to range to explosive to changing weapon to dodge to transversal to special moves there is literally zero down time. -the shots fired from different types of weapon u can feel the hit impact, it feels life-liked bullet impact. I played a major chuck of hours on competitive FPS and would say that SSKTJL have somewhat similar feel on the firing of different types weapons (SMG VS heavy rifle LMG etc.). -screen can be chaotic most of the times during mission but this is also the difficult part because u can die anytime from stray bullets (if u stay on same position for too long) -the chaotic part of combat is immersive because they want u to be airborne most of the time to make use of the unique transversal method that I had not seen before over my 5 years of gaming. -characters have few sets of powerful animated special attack that change then tides of battle.3) RPG system-the loot is diversify and skill tree makes a major difference in ur power. It's a min-max-er dream come true! -different character uses different sets of weapons. And different sets of weapons have different augmentation with different playstyle. So there is no excuse to say all characters only "shoot guns". I had not get to end game yet because I'm still enjoying the story main mission which comes from someone who loves single-player story driven game. However playing co-op turn the fun up to another high level. Last but not least, it's understandable that people have otherwise opinions. But if this game were to made by other dev that did not made any batman game before, people will sure have more positive experience. So just because it's not the game expected from a dev and start nitpicking every aspect of gameplay; which is proven good by other players too (gameplay wise).

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting this is sitting pretty at 86% positive rating despite 99% of content creators hating on the game and Rocksteady! Makes you wonder about the motivations of some of these 'reviewers' and what the effect it has on the gaming industry.Anyway, on to the game - the moment to moment gameplay is really fun if you like games like Sunset Overdrive/Agents of Mayhem/Saints Row (the good one). The cut scenes and characters are all top notch. So for the gameplay alone I can't rate it any lower than 7/10. However, the class diversity initially looks limited - essentially each class playing very similar apart from how they traverse the game world. Unfortunately the combat seems basically the same regardless of your character choice. (Hopefully this improves further on in). The missions fall down to the basics of 1) go to point A/B and kill lots of enemies for a few minutes, 2) go to point A/B and defend the zone for a few minutes, 3) or the much loved escort missions ;-) It's a shame really, such a lack of mission diversity. Also, at first, the gameplay feels at odds with the live service aspect, like the game doesn't know what it wants to be - initial impressions it all feels somewhat disjointed. It's too early for me to comment on the live service end game element, but due to the repetitive mission structure and lack of mission/class diversity I can't really score it beyond a 7/10. Nevertheless, the gun-play is really good fun and definitely not the dumpster fire some YouTuber's are alluding too. Unfortunately it's also by no means amazing and could have been better.Just wish they followed the route of Guardians of the Galaxy and didn't go down the Live Service route. Please learn from the mistakes of Marvel Avengers.Update:Completed the campaign in 32 hours with most side missions done and just a bit of multiplayer, so not a bad length really. Above issues still apply - limited class diversity and disappointing missions that are essentially 'world events' rather than actual curated missions. Despite that, did I have fun in those 32 hours hours? Absolutely!Pre-season end game just looks like redoing existing content on harder difficulties to get better weapons and loot, which doesn't really appeal to me. So will now focus on multiplayer and maxing out each characters level, until season 1 is released.Update.Multiplayer servers haven't worked for around 3 weeks. This is predominantly a co-op shooter, and it doesn't work. So just can't recommend in its current situation.Update before season 1 drops - Multiplayer is finally working again!!! Here's hoping they don't make a mess of season 1.Season 1:No new map, just a re-skin of the existing one. No new enemies or content, just skins. Yes, we get Joker, but what's the point if all you're doing is grinding the same old same old. All in all a lazy update. Lots of guns, just little else other then grind...grind...grind on the same activities.

However as someone who's a big Task Force X fan, Kill the Justice League, story and characterization wise, to me personally, is some of the best Squad content we've gotten in years. (and trust me when I say I will speak up if I think characters have been wronged-- but I digress).Gameplay wise I'm not a huge action shooter player, but am having a lot of fun with this, and not dying  often so make of that what you will.My biggest complaint would be the lack of an offline mode for single player but supposedly that's to come and hopefully I don't look back on this comment as something that aged horribly.

_childDocuments_.review: Got 200 hours on this game on ps5 and bought it here. it runs like ass so I'm here to not recommend this on pc but on ps5 or series x. anyways, the game's much better than people say, the loot is genuinely incredible and the central hook is how it leverages the dc villains for themed loot based on their superpower or gimmick like firefly's grenade lighting up the battlefield or parasite's melee weapon being used to consume a status effect on a weapon to drastically increase melee damage like by 1000% or something crazy like that. The endgame is repetitive, yes, but it's no different to greater rifts in diablo 3 or the pit in diablo 4. It's a hyper push infinite grind that you can theoretically do forever as you further minmax your gear. That won't appeal to everyone and perhaps that was a misstep for a live service game looking for broad appeal. The story's bad and there's not much to say there. It was in a ton of rewrites and eventually needed to conform to the live service format and where it ended up was just better than Arkham Origins ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story in my opinion. I suspect that just like Arkham Knight and Origins, the same people who ♥♥♥♥ on this game and hated it when it came out and continue to now will take the game up years in the future from now after support has almost certainly ended for it to pretend they loved it all along and it was done dirty. I see you, y'all are the scum of the media community. You did it with Knight and Origins, you did it with Amazing Spider-Man 2 after No Way Home came out to pretend you always loved Andrew Garfield's Peter Parker and his movies (they're both ♥♥♥♥ by the way). Lastly, gameplay-wise, this game carves out a very interesting niche as I can honestly say I've never played any game like it. It's pretty rad and I recommend you give it a shot through to endgame because that's where the loot game really kicks in and you can see how well the gameplay is complimented by the loot and the different notorious items and infamy sets. You might actually like it more than you thought.As a looter shooter for me: 9/10 cause I love DC and I love looter shooters and this scratches both of those itches exceptionally wellAs a follow-up to the Arkham games: 6/10 cause the story just isn't good. _childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game and definitely enjoyable if you have a friend to play through the game. Writing is fine, and the story beats are fairly predictable, but still not terrible at all. Gameplay is where the recommendation gets murky, as this game does not play anything at all like the Arkham games before it. Melee combat with a twist of gadgets is just not there, this game is mostly a third person shooter with some melee mechanics. It's not a bad system at all, but if you just completed any of the Batman Arkham games, it will take some time to get comfortable with the mechanics. As for characters, they all have their individual specialties and perks, and although I enjoy playing as Captain Boomerang, many others will likely hate his traversal and play style as much as I hate playing as Harley for the same reasons.Overall, the game is not bad at all, maybe not worth it for the pricetag and battlepass nonsense, but as far as a good romp to play through with a friend, you could definitely do a lot worse. At its worst moments, the challenges of side missions can become frustrating, and some of the boss battles seem nonsensical, but at its peak, you're just flying around skyscrapers shooting aliens in the face while the cast juggles passable jokes between one another.
