_childDocuments_.review: I got Suicide Squad the last time it was 80% off and although I've had SOME fun, I wouldn't really say it was worth it even at a budget price.The core combat is definitely the best part, which is the bulk of the gameplay. Movement is generally very good and with a bit of practice you can zip, slide and fly around while shooting all at once. Once you settle on the character you enjoy most and get them leveled up it can be pretty addicting just charging from fight to fight. I like that even reloading has a dynamic element of getting faster reloads for timing them right. The endgame has some endless levels where the enemies slowly ramp up their stats as your increase your body count that can be a fun challenge.Despite the "squad" focus, I feel like the game works fine for single-player. I've only played with others a couple of times and it didn't feel that much different than with bots other than human players seem to take longer to revive you vs. bots who are programmed to just come and pick you up once you're down. Maybe if I was part of well oiled full team instead of just having fun with a random single player I'd notice a bigger difference but I don't feel like I'm missing much playing on my own.But the further you get away from the main combat, the worse things get. The attempts to introduce variation to make things less repetitive actually make fighting less fun. Collect dropped bits to toss at a weakpoint, guard a certain spot until a timer finishes, use the game's one and only vehicle to kill enemies, it all just feels like hoop jumping. You're not allowed to just enjoy slaughtering enemies during these parts, you gotta make time for these cliched objectives that unlike the combat, have no real novelty or thought put into them.The level up system is very basic. Each character has their own unique skill trees, but on said trees you're only allowed to spend one point per each tier. You must then spend another point in the next tree, and the next before cycling back to the first one. It's a lot of excess to make the skill system look more complicated when it's very linear. Even more linear than the Arkham games which didn't have a complicated skill system either. Some tiers don't even have a choice, just one skill you MUST pick.The equipment system though offers a lot more freedom. There's a lot of potential to make some busted builds and I've managed to cobble together some pretty satisfying ones myself, but it felt like it took a lot more work than it should have. Poor UI and weird design choices drag out what should be otherwise simple. You've got the standard colored tier levels for rarity but then you got pink "nefarious" gear which has unique bonuses and red "infamy" gear that have bonuses that get stronger for using more pieces from its specific set.It took me a while to realize that each infamy set has three COMPLETELY different sets of bonuses based on the numbered tier AND what villain it belongs to. There's no in-game database listing all the gear effects you see, you just got to look at EVERY item individually to see what they do. The game throws weapons and mods at you for everything you do so eventually you'll hit your cap meaning you'll have to constantly store or break things down to make room for more. If you don't, every bit of new loot gets stored in their own individual emails you must click on to claim to add ANOTHER clunky system onto the already bad inventory management.And beyond those issues is this is still a very buggy and poorly optimized game, even six months past launch. I've been running the game on the lowest settings and still getting crashes fairly often. There's no easy way to quit missions and sometimes closing the game bugs out my weird online ID in a way that seemingly locks me out of the server for several hours. Sometimes you just can't get logged INTO the server at all and you MUST be logged on at all times, even when you're by yourself because this is an ALWAYS ONLINE game. It's also a "live-service" game, but they've botched that so bad that the only way you'd notice if there's a costume you REALLY want that costs extra. They're still pushing out updates for these "seasonal" content additions, which suggests the dev team is being mandated to prioritize new content over fixes and improvements. And the in-game UI for the "episodes" at the time of writing this shows we're not even half-way through this weird multiverse adventure. Assuming things continue at the rate they are and they just don't pull the plug in the future, it'll be probably 9 months before they're done with the add-ons, which means it'll be that long before FIXES and OPTIMIZATION can be the priority.They are doing bug fixes with the updates, but the notes for the last update clarify a previous fix wasn't retroactive and so they just UNLOCKED a bunch of in-game audiologs for the first three episodes cause they couldn't figure out an actual fix. And the unlock requirements for the audiologs for the most current two episodes have bugged out on me so I'm stuck waiting for a future fix to presumably just unlock them for me cause glitchy Riddler content (yes, he's back again...) is impossible to count for some reason.I don't got a lot to say about the story because it's a mess lots of other people have already covered from different angles. The short version is you got numerous conflicting scripts and concepts all hastily cut and pasted together to form a schizophrenic trainwreck. Someone clearly really liked the Justice League. There's a lot of weight put into the scenes of them being used and mind-controlled by Brainiac... then someone else was asked to write bad jokes for the Squad to be annoying DURING these scenes, if even that. A long fight between Wonder Woman and Superman has the Squad standing around doing NOTHING for like three minutes, probably because they weren't even intended to be in that scene.Although there's a LOT to take issue with, I'd say the biggest problem with the story is the Squad are just unfunny and awful. Harley and Boomerang are both just brash, dumb, losers with no redeeming qualities. Deadshot really isn't any better. He has a daughter he'll barely mention and a facade of being a "professional" that drops all the time to show he's as petty an stupid as the others.King Shark, shockingly, is the only bright spot. He was effectively raised in prison and is very well educated but has little outside experience, which is mildly amusing. He's also the only who notes the cruel irony in having to kill heroes who actually SAVED the Squad just earlier in the game. The story would still be a mess, but if they populated the squad with more semi-likeable people who can occasionally be funny, that would have gone a long way to salvaging this mess.You CAN unlock additional characters and as of writing this there's three new ones and presumably at least one more on the way. But this is part of the "episodes" set after the main plot, so none of these new people can interact with the main plot. There is a new plot in the episodes of rescuing the Justice League, whom apparently weren't completely dead or something?As of writing this, both Flash and Green Lantern have been "saved" and they remaining "roadmap" makes it clear we'll save Batman, Wonder Woman and Superman in the coming seasons. But these seasons have VERY few cutscenes and clearly only a fraction of the budget the main game got, so this part of the "story" feels like an afterthought at best. You cram both Flash and GL into a cyro tube after getting them back so they don't have to write anything for them in the future.TL:DR - Just keep waiting. Maybe check in on the game mid-2025 when hopefully they'll be done with these "seasons" and can start fixing things.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so, bit of an odd review because yes I'm giving it the thumbs up but it's highly dependant. If you buy the game expecting it to be in the same style then yes you're not going to have a good time....it's different.This very much feels like a game that's meant to be played with other people (I'm not that kinda player myself I much prefer single player games) and it might very well be more enjoyable with others. The skill trees  And to some degree feels rather pointless.The basic story premise is ok, but I think it could have been made far better. The way the suicide squad is handled I think is nice, and the characters themselves are fun. The amount of cut scenes or interaction, to me anyway, feels like you're involved in the story and in that sense it's well done.The game play itself is fun, however some of the missions I find irritating in the sense that you can only kill mobs for that mission with say critical damage only, anything else does zero damage. It can make some of the fights a bit frustrating. Some of these fights I've found harder than killing the Flash or Green Lantern which again is disappointing.Is it worth the money? I think I paid about 20 pounds too much, I'd say a good price for it would be 40....maybe 35.So TLDR all in all would I recommend getting it? If you go into it expecting Arkham gameplay then no, if you go into it with an open mind for a different kind of experience with those games then sure. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR - I don't think it's a bad game, just a very polarizing game. You will either love it or hate it. Watch the videos, the game isn't trying to hide what it is. It is exactly what you see in the videos.  This game has possibly the worst first 2 hours of a game I've ever played. It is either boring you with very long repetitive cinematics where your characters keep forgetting about the bombs in their heads or it is non-stop teaching you new mechanics without giving you time to master the ones it showed you previously. I have almost exactly 2 hours of playtime, and I did one real mission. I haven't even really played the game yet and I have to decide if I want to refund it or not. The gameplay seems schizophrenic. Non-stop jumping, dodging, and combos. Jump up, shoot people, fall down. Swing over, shoot people in mid air, drop down, combo people, jump up again. This is the gameplay loop. Also, shoot the purple glowing spot. The beginning of the game feels like the end of most other games, where you have lots of movement options and different enemy types. And you learned how to use them over time, but in this case you do them all from the start. Just watch the videos on the store page, watch much the characters jump around and shoot, or do a 180 and shoot, or fall from the sky while shooting. That is the game.Yet at the same time, the world and scale of the game is interesting. The character models are impressive. There are moments where something special is happening. This looks exactly like a game I should enjoy. But the one mission I did play was on rooftops, and I kept falling off because I wasn't used to doing the combat and movement at the same time. And I realized, it will be more of this, and it will get more complicated. I like King Shark / Harley, they are fun. Deadshot is seemingly devoid of a personality. But every time I have to listen to either Captain Boomerang or Amanda Waller, I want to stop playing. This game acts like these characters are familiar to us, that we've seen them before, and we all love their jokes and personalities. And maybe some people do, but I'm guessing for most of us we barely know anything about them. So we have no connection to them. I'm sure they grow on us over time, but at the beginning it's terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main story/side objectives and here are my thoughts.Gameplay: In my opinion the combat is very rewarding. You can feel yourself getting better and better as you play. The unique character traversals flow together seamlessly with combat. Whether you're zipping around enemies as Captain Boomberang and blasting them with a shotgun or raining fire from above as King Shark from an enhanced leap. You'll feel the power in the characters with all their abilities as well as their weapons. Leveling: Each character talent tree is split/mixed in with 3 main play styles. They allow for a variety of different ways to play the character. The talent tree seem to mostly focus on melee, weapon/crit damage, and survival. Weapons and loot that you collect works well with the talent tree too. I found myself swapping my talents around often to try new things after finding loot that had good synergy. The best part about the talent tree is you can respec without it costing anything or being a hassle. Story: The story had its ups and downs. Each character was full of personality and enjoyable to watch/interact with. There was a lot of humor and jokes throughout the whole game as well, which I personally liked. Story to boss fights were what fell short. At some point things felt anticlimactic and underwhelming after building so much hype. Story could have been longer too. Sometimes felt like things were happening way too fast.Multiplayer: Playing with friends is extremely fun in this game. The competition mechanic in this game is engaging and addictive. Most missions show who preformed the best and in doing so gives them control over which mission to select next. You can also make/join a clan and have your friends characters join you as bots as you play. There can be multiples of the same character in a session but you will miss out on dialog in the game so I don't recommend it. Story progress is shared though if you want to do an entire play through from start to finish with friends. Endgame and Future outlook: I haven't delved into the endgame as much as of right now but it's fairly straight forward. You complete various missions that populate the map to increase your mastery and world tier. This will allow you to do harder content and get better loot as you play. Most missions that populate are similar to ones you've completed during the story so it can get repetitive. There are new modifiers and difficulty tiers that add new elements to how you play. A decent amount of unique loot becomes available to grind for in the endgame as well. The coming seasons look promising in terms of adding more content and characters so I guess we'll see.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is excellent and full of humor that keeps me gigglin'. I can see what some people mean by repetitiveness in the gameplay missions, but the combat is so exciting, variable, and engaging that I personally don't really mind. The whole experience is only enhanced if you're a huge DC Comics nerd, or just a superhero nerd in general. Captain Boomerang's traversal and combat gives me hope that we're inching closer and closer to an open world game where you play as The Flash🤞Not sure what IGN's beef is with the game but they really seem to love hating on it 💀

_childDocuments_.review: Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League is a new genre-bending action-adventure shooter that can be played solo or with up to four players in online co-op. Based on iconic DC characters and developed by Rocksteady Studios, creators of the Batman: Arkham series, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League combines the studio’s signature character-driven story gameplay with third-person shooter action. Featuring an original narrative set in the DC universe, Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League takes place in a richly detailed open-world Metropolis. The story follows Suicide Squad members Harley Quinn, Deadshot, Captain Boomerang and King Shark who must take on an impossible mission to save Earth and kill the world’s greatest DC Super Heroes, The Justice League. Restrained with lethal explosives implanted in their heads, all four DC Super-Villains have no choice but to band together and carry out this untenable assignment as part of Amanda Waller’s infamous Task Force X. Fans can tailor their experience, whether playing on their own as a single player, switching between characters at will, or teaming up with friends in multiplayer co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: Controlling a mysterious figure that has inherited the legacy of the evil, long-dead Overlord, the player emerges, near death, from the ruins of the old Overlord's Dark Tower. Only the player's actions determine if they will rise to become the new all-powerful Overlord; it's all down to how much of a bad ass they want to be in order to succeed...evil or really evil! Played out with plenty of black humour and dark irony, the game immerses players in twisted parodies of classic fantasy scenarios and characters. Overlord's key innovation is the introduction of an array of impish creatures – the Minions. They believe you are the old Overlord reborn and will use their unique skills to fetch, fight and die for you. Throughout the game players actively control a horde of these gremlin-like critters and they follow your every instruction no matter how despotic or, for the Minions, life threatening it is. [Codemasters]

name: Crash Drive 3
detailed_description: Are you ready for THE car stunting playground? Experience ridiculous fun in this cross-platform multiplayer, free-roaming game! Drive monster trucks, tanks and more amazing vehicles across a huge open world. Level up, play events, earn cash, unlock new cars and discover secrets.... Crash Drive is back! Destroy a gigantic beach ball, catch robbers as a cop or steal the king's crown, these are just a few examples of the 10 fun game events this game has to offer. Participate in these random competitive events, beat your opponents to earn the most cash and buy awesome new cars or customisations. By using nitro boosts you increase the car’s nitro capacity, by driving at top speed you increase its top speed... catch the drift? ‘Maxing’ all stats for a car increases your player level allowing you to buy new cars or customisations. Collect over 50+ vehicles and customise your car with funky antennas, boosts and unique number plates with your in-game name on it. Reach the maximum player level to prestige and show who is the real Crash Drive 3 boss! Solid golden car anyone? To the moon and back! Drive around freely and explore the boundless and varied open world at your leisure. Fly a rocket to the moon, storm the king’s castle in the forest, go to the saloon in the wild west canyons or experience ice drifting fun in the arctic snow. Done with icy cold? How about a relaxing ferry trip to the tropics? Each area is unique and filled with secret areas, collectibles and special easter eggs... Think you’ll ever be done exploring this world? Blast or crash opponents from the sky arena to score points and dominate the battle arenas. Win in order to buy new tanks each with a unique play style. You will have a blast in the exciting tank battles mode! No matter which platform your friends play on, you can always play together thanks to cross platform multiplayer support. Or if you want to do some stunting offline, switch seamlessly to a fully single player experience anytime you like!

_childDocuments_.review: I've had to change my review from positive to negative to positive. Here's why. AN IN DEPTH REVIEW So you can make an informed purchase! haha!Firstly, straight up this game, from the moment you load it up, it's just a good time. Always a good time!The few(8) negative reviews on here suck, so I'll try to address those first and the actual issues here. This is my first Crash Drive title. 1. You don't need a roll button since the game does roll you over back, but a rest button could be handy. 2. I have played for over 12 hours and have not come across a single hacker, so Don't know what that fella is on about. You can exploit the game somewhat but it's still not "hacking". Yes there's driving into exploding barrels sending you miles into the air to get massive stunt chains, it's fun. But most the other exploits have been patched. 3. There are enough game modes, but since you have autojoin on you can wear yourself out buy playing them one after another, you're definetly engaged however. I feel the issue is not the number of gamemodes but rather how crown and cops n robbers are usually finished in less than 30 seconds without even trying, this can apply to 2 more gamemodes but. It's way too short. Needs to be extended and designed so those two at least go for 5-10 minutes in length each. There's no fun to be had in a cops game mode if it's so quick. Either implement lives that scale with the number of players or redesign it completely and add more to be more engaging for longer. Even a Road rage takedown style mode would be better than cops n robbers at this point: Smash into as many players as you can in 5 minutes. Whoever gets the most tags on unique players wins! Throw in a recharging defense weapon to all cars so you have to be sneaky to tag them. That would be fun. Bugs: Sometimes paying to max a car does not increase your level as it should. Happened when I was almost done maxing a car and only had $3000 left for it to be maxed so I paid and it didn't count....it does not count towards unlocking a car. Happened to me twice! What the hell! This is potentially game breaking!There's this really annoying bug where if you teleport to garage after winning an event but the timer isn't over, your score is reset and you lose everything!Issues: Needs a second camera that's more modern. Feel like we need more control over the camera, ability to adjust or turn off horizon tilt as seriously makes it look and play jank on anything other than a mobile device. To add to this we need some more PC esq features like adjustments for brightness, gamma and ability to use your PC audio mp3 etc files in game. FOV slider is optional but would be nice. Additionally allow analogue axis for steering. The Pros: I plugged in my PS4 controller and it was instantly playable and just works. Nice. Don't know if it's because of software I have installed to make it happen but cool.Multiplayer is seamless and done well. Netcode's ace. Love that you can on the fly change regional servers and no loading times in between! Especially useful when a mode you loathe rn comes up and bam into a more fun region!After I unlocked the trash truck, about 16 hrs in, MAN the game is way more fun again!! It was fun before, but ho le cow this truck is badass! Also really highlights the beauty of the map Forest, this map really comes alive with this truck, fully maxed. You are flying!Ok This reminds me, the army-schoolbus(and probs schoolbus) in this game has terrible engine audio so I want the City Bus from Burnout 3 to replace it entirely and give it the fun stats of the trash truck but with more airtime and less boost!The game is like burnout paradise in more ways than one! Especially how you can spend endless amounts of time just having fun in a multiplayer map, maybe playing the objectives and feel totally content just goofing off The driving mechanics itself fits perfectly to the environments, quite polished for how simple and arcady it is. Basically rocket league feel. It is fun and doesn't hinder the gameplay modes at all, but rather it enhances it so it's well integrated and thought out. Jumps on maps and challenges are well thought out, there's many and varied. Virtually no wait time as you're auto joining game modes whilst free roaming. Tutorial is non-invasive and implemented perfectly.Minus the lack of polish on car models, This game would be like racing/car combat game on crack to newcomers to the genre. Playing on multiplayer is a must!I appreciate few things in this game that I don't typically find in a game like this(and being a mobile port and all). But that could also be because I primarily bought this as a spiritual successor to Burnout Paradise' multiplayer. The way you stunt around the free roam map doing challenges with others in particular is close in feel. So that's good news to me. Other than that game seems decently optimised and so far things are good, hopefully they add more game modes because even with the content on offer I still feel like the RRP Price is asking way too much! Thankfully I got this on a bundle sale off fanatical, and will try to enjoy it mainly for it Feeling like a Spiritual successor to Burnout Paradise multiplayer, minus all the awesome damage effects that you only find in a burnout game! Maybe the developer could add some more varied challenges too!. Happy it has massive cross platform as it will keep the game alive! Will post more issues as they come up. But fun if you don't mind some mobile graphics and lack of brightness/gamma adjustment and missing horizon lock(which will be jarring for some I imagine). Worth it on sale. so far for a mobile game port it's 7/10, wait for sale.Cons:  Tropical and the tank battles seem useless. Tank battles are basically RNG fest, there's no room for what little strategy is possible without adequate cover. It's  an open platform which you fall off or get killed. THat's it. Even a kid could make a 20sec game mode in GTAV and it'll do tank battles better. I'd like to see swampy maps or just better design here, needs actual props on the ground for cover. This is my least favourite thing up against bots.Although the car upgrade system is sweet, what issue I have with it is since you can't change car colors or rims, the cars don't feel like your own much. So to compensate the game makes you unlock new cars rather quickly, as long as you keep playing. this I feel is poor. Need some decals or something more to make your car feel like yours when bought. Another con here is the balancing of some cars. The limo has poor flipping ability in air, there's little compensation for it. It needs to earn coins at a higher (1.1x) rate since it's also a long vehicle, requires more skill overall. Otherwise there's no incentive to play with vehicles that are "sub-par", which can turn the fun down a lot I imagine in higher ranks. I do think the game is way overpriced at $30+ because primarily it needs more TLC and polish for the price it's asking as a PC or proper PS4/8th gen title. It doesn't feel bare bones but compared to PC exclusives it certainly lacks some staples of the industry. Comment freely if you require clarification. I see myself, in these trying times getting about a hundred hours out of it if I don't encounter some more annoying issues/ommisions. Multiplayer is seamless. Overall glad the game exists but it does need even more to do and more game mechanisms to avoid getting stale to a hardcore fan of the racing/ car combat genre! Tropical map is straight up a disappointment, it is already stale. Happy gaming!Arctic is by far my fav level for maxing. Forest is such a cool level. Haven't had much time with Canyons, I am still enjoying the first map damn near 20 hours in! As you get vastly better at the game, suddenly everything in the map seems like it's perfectly placed to learn new stunts and fly off them onto other things! Neato!! Excluding the 2 bugs, is good bug free gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: Crash Drive 3 is a nice, casual stunt racing game with non-stop solo and multiplayer competitions, lots of different cars, 4 mid-sized maps to freely roam in, and collectibles to hunt down.Gameplay is pretty simple. You are dropped on the first map in the starter car and are free to roam. You can explore the map, perform stunts on many different ramps (or use some ramps to reach secret areas), hunt down money crates that occasionally drop from the sky, search for well-hidden collectibles, or try to unlock the next map. Each map also contains 10 rings that you can fly through, and passing each ring at least once is one of the many challenges that the game has in store for you.Up to 9 other players may populate the same map. After 30 seconds at most. an event will start in which you can compete against these players (though you're also free to ignore them, the events are purely optional). The event is randomly chosen from a diverse set: "Race" is a checkpoint race, in "Stunt" you're trying to score as many stunt points as possible (mid-air maneuvers and good landings award extra points), in "Tag" you're trying to touch as many objects as possible while stunting, in "Collect" you're competing for coins that rain from the sky, in "Beachball" you're trying to do the most damage to a giant ball, in "Find the Ring" you're trying to fly through one randomly selected ring as soon as possible, in "Cops and Robbers" you try to collect gold bars (as a robber) or hit the robbers (as a cop), in "King of the Crown" you're trying to steal the crown by hitting the player that has it (and then evade the other players for 60 seconds), and in "King of the Hill" you're trying to push other players out of a circular area that spawns randomly. All events are easy to understand. None of these events take longer than 4 minutes, many are shorter, and the pause between two events is only 30 seconds, so there's always something going on. This creates easy, uncomplicated drop-in, drop-out gameplay.There aren't any lobbies, so you never need to wait for a game to start. However, if you want to play with specific people, they can join you on the same map instance. If no one else is around, the events change into solo mode, where your task is to reach a certain target, e.g. score 16,000 stunt points within a time limit during a "Stunt" event. The difficulty of these solo tasks will adapt to your skill: If you succeed, then the next target in this event will be higher - but if you fail, then the next target will be lower. The solo tasks can also be played in an offline mode. In addition to the 9 events, there's also a "Tank Combat" mode with special vehicles on a fifth map.I had great fun with these events, and found this game a great way to relax. Even if you just have 10 minutes to kill, you can quickly do 2 events and have some arcade-y stunt racing fun. Even if you lose, it's fun to perform weird stunts - there is no damage model, you'll always flip back on your wheels even if you land on your roof, and your "boost" even lets you fly for short times.Depending on your performance in the events, you'll earn money, which you can then use to buy new cars or improve the ones you already own. However, you can also earn money by hunting down randomly spawning crates, and your cars also improve automatically when you drive them. There are 47 different cars in the game, and each one handles a bit differently - so there is meta progression that keeps players engaged as they keep unlocking new cars. There are also a few cosmetics that you can adorn your car with.Graphics are fairly low-fi, but I didn't mind - for a game like this, smooth performance even on weak hardware is more important than fancy graphics. Sound effects are servicable. The music consists of very upbeat rock instrumentals - a bit generic, but I always enjoy listening to it, it puts me in the perfect mood for this game. I do like rock and metal music in general though, your mileage may vary if you don't. There is no voice acting.I also liked the level design. While the maps aren't overly large, each map has some special touches. For example, the "Forest" map has a medieval castle in its center, and there are catapults which can throw your car across the map.Regarding usability options, the game lets you rebind keys for movement and all actions, which is great. Graphics settings are a bit sparse, but you can turn off motion blur and enable vsync and anti-aliasing. Three separate sound volume sliders let you fine-tune music and effects. Screen shakes can be switched off. Unfortunately there are no options for players with certain disabilities. Colorblind filters would have been useful since some parts of the game use color-coded information in red and green. Players who are hard of hearing may have difficulties in events that require you to evade other players that may approach from any direction - but there's a "look behind" key that may help.Taking everything into account, I recommend Crash Drive 3 to all players who think that casual stunt driving sounds like fun. It's a game that knows exactly what it wants to be, and that's designed to fit its fairly unique niche very well.

_childDocuments_.review: Because I enjoy Crash Drive 2, I volunteered to help test this game (unpaid, but I got a free copy) and have played every day for over a year. Not  because I'm dedicated (actually I'm rather lazy), but because it's fun.Like CD2, you can easily play for just a few minutes at a time, as each event or tank battle is only a few minutes, so ideal to fit in to the spare moments in a day. The vehicle physics is certainly not realistic, but rather sort of cartoony. You can drive up vertical walls, spin mid-air and many other impossible but entertaining things. It is particularly crazy on the moon.It is as competitive as you want to suit your mood. You can just wander around exploring and doing your own stunts or you can join in the events, which are often rather silly. In my opinion, it is more like kids messing about in a school playground than an olympics (I mean this in a good way!).Could it be improved? A couple of things from CD2 are missing: changing your tank colours (although there are other customisations) and some of the comic book style special effects, both of which I rather liked.However, the graphics and gameplay are vastly improved. It looks great played on a big TV. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game released in 2021 and quite dead says the steam charts. Well they are very wrong. This game is very much alive due to seamless multi platform support and there is always people playing from console meanwhile PC players numbers are plain inaccurate. Perhaps the short sessions play havoc? Anyways there is good reason why console players come: The design here is just friendly all around. Games like this they last long because it is designed to last. Core game play loop is just do what you want and mess around and make money. Or don't. Want to take part in activities with others? go ahead. Or skip if you dont feel like it. No harm done. Want to find secrets and do challenges? Go ahead. No harm done to anyone if you do your own thing. Want to play tank battles? it's got it's own arenas and rules and again: No harm to other game types. Smack talkers? Cheaters? Yes. I have seen one trying to grief events and sending some pre-defined messages like 'Look at me!' while flying around in a car.  Cheaters are few and no wonder: They have no agency in this game. They can zip around with their cheat engines and it matters not at all. What do i care if some cheater decided to cheat on events that change every few minutes? It is what cheaters do but their imprint on game play is non-existent. They can't do squat.  But you can change maps, do other things like stunt, hunt for green circles and collectibles, make money e.g. just plain ignore them and enjoy the game. Rare are the multiplayer games out there where the design is so solid cheaters dont get reactions and no satisfaction and instead they need to really work for it so no wonder there are very few of them even if the devs dont enforce anything. I was astonished there is no reporting function to the game. But playing some more i don't really know if it would make any difference. Excellent game for quick sessions from 5-30 minutes. Or longer if you feel like it. You get money on each session for doing your thing and you use it to unlocked new cars and cosmetics. 9/10 of it's kind really. I can't think of any better one. Previous game was decent but this one is even better. I think the best part is how solidly 'friendly' they have made the design e.g. no matter how you choose the play the game it is always right.

_childDocuments_.review: I probably wouldn't have looked twice at this game if not for the fact that I had gotten two copies of Crash Drive 2 for less than $2 and had a surprising amount of fun with it. Crash Drive 3 is "more of the same" of Crash Drive 2, but improved in virtually every way. It's easy to jump in and out with friends or random players, and there's no obligation or strong push to join in on any of the events that are taking place constantly. It's very much a go-at-your-own-pace experience, with few exceptions.The first big exception is that unlocking more vehicles requires you to fully "level up" a certain number of previous vehicles. They level up naturally as you drive them, but if you were really looking forward to driving the police car, and it requires you to level up 15 more cars before you unlock it, then it can feel like a real grind trying to max out one car after the other before the payoff comes. And that just unlocks the car. You still need to purchase it before you can drive it.And that brings me to the second big exception: Cars get more and more expensive to purchase. I've never really had a problem having enough money in the game for the things I need/want, because I don't spend it on anything until the moment I want to buy it. But I introduced a very young family member to the game and he doesn't really understand the concept of money yet. He gets really excited checking his garage every few events to see if anything new has been unlocked, and if he sees that the "buy" button is enabled, he clicks it. This means that he doesn't realize that the reason he can't afford the firetruck he's been dying to drive since the moment he got the game is because he's constantly spending all his money on accessories like license plates or exhaust/trail particle effects. He also doesn't understand that going into his garage to change vehicles in the middle of an event makes him lose all his progress in the event, meaning he doesn't score very high or win very often which means he earns less money than someone a few years older might.Other than those two roadblocks, we've had a great time playing, exploring, driving around crashing, and participating in events. Whether you've got only 5 minutes or a few hours to spare, you can easily fill your time with Crash Drive 3.Oh, and there's also a PVP tank battle mode in the game, but I don't really care for that kind of competitive gameplay, so I generally don't do the tank battles. That said, it seems perfectly serviceable most of the time.I'm inclined to say just wait and get it steeply discounted, like I did. But I've put almost 20 hours into the game by now and expect I may double that by the time I'm done playing it, so from that perspective, the full asking price seems reasonable to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Crash Drive 3 offers a modest single-player mode that can be completed in around 3-4 hours, but this is mostly training; a non-competitive way to learn the lay of the land so you won’t embarrass yourself when you finally launch the primary PLAY mode of the game.  Here, you are thrown into one of the game’s five unique world environments with up to 11 other gamers.  A logo next to their name tells what system they are playing on or you can toggle off cross-play support if you wish, but I saw no reason to do this.  Even on launch day the game was running great with no lag and smooth player drop-in/out between events.Much of the content is shared between the offline and online modes, but there are numerous events that you can only experience in the multiplayer mode like King of the Hill, Cops & Robbers, Steal the Crown, etc.  Player XP and cash are shared between modes and the winnings in multiplayer are often far greater than the $2,500 you make winning a solo event.  The pacing of the game is unique in that you have this small window between events that counts down offering you brief moments to explore and collect hidden secrets or smash cash crates.  There is very little downtime so you are always engaged in these randomly changing events.The Tropics level is home to a special garage featuring all sorts of tanks that you can use to play thrilling Tank Battles on narrow platforms and arenas suspended above the landscape.  This activity is crazy-addictive, bringing back ancient memories of Atari 2600 Combat and Battlezone from the arcade.  The tank combat has its own progression system that will unlock other tanks that offer their own unique style of play.Full review at

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun open world racing game more interested in arcade goofiness and over the top stunts than being any kind of realistic driving simulation. _childDocuments_.review: A Great fun driving game  where you have to collect things, race, battle, do stunts etc in a bunch of different environments.The Graphics are kept pretty functional and a bit cartoonish but there's no need for more, this isn't a realistic driving game.The music is nice although can get a little repetitive after a long session.The gameplay is great fun playing against random opponents on the internet, I do worry if the online crowd disappeared the game might not hold up too well in single player but as it is there are usually plenty of people around helped by the fact you are playing with players from the Xbox, Playstation and Switch as well as the PC.There are plenty of cars to drive but it can take quite a while to gain the money to unlock them. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot more fun that I thought it would be and perfect if you're just looking to waste a little time. It's essentially a series of minigames that you can play either alone or in multiplayer on several differently themed tracks (a desert, a forest, the arctic). I would definitely recommend skipping the offline mode as it's a lot better as a multiplayer game.The only strike against the game is that the controls are a little stiff on the keyboard and it's a lot less fluid than other games of its type. Though this can cause some minor annoyance from time to time, it won't take away too much from the fun.Recommended for anybody that just wants to tear around in a variety of cars for a bit and see what kind of stunts they can pull off.

name: Ghost Song
detailed_description: On the desolate moon of Lorian, a long-dormant Deadsuit awakens from slumber—armed and combat-ready, memory clear of purpose. But something new is stirring… Strike out beneath the surface in search of answers in Ghost Song, an atmospheric 2D adventure of self-discovery, ancient mysteries, and cosmic terror. Explore winding caverns lit only by bioluminescent flora, battle strange and powerful creatures, and acquire new abilities to help you unearth this alien world’s long-buried secrets. Descend deep into the darkness—only then will you learn (or is it remember?) the truth. FEATURES Discover what lies below Explore the twisting alien tunnels and long-abandoned labs of an expansive, beautifully illustrated Metroidvania-inspired 2D world filled with secret chambers and a haunting history. Power up and progress Acquire potent weapons and game-changing new abilities in the depths, unlocking access to new strata of the moon and optional hidden areas. Face challenging foes Combat the fungal aliens and metal husks of Lorian with responsiveness and precision. Level up your power, and customize your suit and blaster with an arsenal of modules. Blast and smash Master the distinctive rhythm of Deadsuit’s core combat. Pummel enemies with your rapid-fire blaster, building up barrel heat that empowers your melee attacks. You are not alone You’re not the only entity trapped in this unfamiliar place. Encounter a cast of voiced characters and discover their own tales of survival, courage, abandonment, and redemption.

_childDocuments_.review: I could tell you about how much I love this game, but instead I'm going to tell you what I know about it's journey.Matt White was a simple gamer, just like us. He liked Super Metroid, he liked Dark Souls, he even liked fighting games. It had been years since Nintendo had touched the Metroid franchise. So, he thought to himself, why don't I make one?It was 2012. Matt had already been toying around with Flash sidescrollers. Having fun dipping his toes into making stuff, just for fun. Matt was also an excellent artist already; he drew comic book art, in a style similar to those old 80s sci-fi anime's. He didn't really know anything about programming, but after conversations with a mutual, they agreed to partner up and try to make something special. Try and make a Metroid-like that was somber, yet lively, and hauntingly beautiful.So a Kickstarter was made. Matt didn't really know anything about making games. Few people outside of the industry really talked about it back then. They did some math, guessed about how long it would take them, and a goal was set - mere $15,000. A measly amount compared to even most indie games of today. It seemed like enough back then. And the Kickstarter was a rousing success, funding waaay above goal. Not quite enough to reach the oft-joked about Wii U stretch, but a windfall nonetheless. The money was divided evenly between the two bright-eyed and idea-filled partners. This was it. It was time to hunker down and get started.But then the programmer's work started to slow. He would miss calls, skip out on meetings. He stopped returning messages. Slowly, he himself became a ghost of the project. He had taken the money, but wasn't producing the work. There was so much to do! But only Matt remained. And only Matt would continue the project.Stencyl is a good engine to work with visually, especially if you are new to making games. Although shaken by the silent departure of his once-partner, he soldiered on; dutifully creating all the artwork, pulling from sound libraries and implementing his ideas into the game engine. It was rough going, for a single man. But it was going. And that was all that mattered, with the weight of the fully funded Kickstarter behind him, and the growing coverage of his dark, yet vibrant take on the (for the time) neglected genre.However, Stencyl just couldn't keep up with Matt. Fixing bugs was a struggle for this new developer. And the more content and artwork and ideas he shoveled into the engine, the longer and longer it would take to compile, sometimes up to 45 minutes for each change! Instead of smoothly moving forward, working on the game was becoming frustrating. This couldn't go on. A change had to be made.So Matt makes the tough decision to switch engines, communicating this to all the Kickstarter backers. It is an understandable, if regrettable choice. The game was already at least halfway done! But it was also necessary. The engine was pushed as far as it could go, and Matt, burning the candle at both ends to make his dream a reality, had no choice but to start over.The next years are spent learning to code. Unity has plugins to work visually, like Stencyl. But so much MORE could be done by directly coding it. Ideas exploded forth. The animations could now be expanded upon. Even more options for including melee and different weapons were now a possibility. Matt hadn't stopped playing other games during these years, and they all helped to shape and grow this new vision of Ghost Song.A vision I hope you will enjoy in its completion as much as I have.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a super enthusiastic recommendation. I do think people should buy this, if solely to support a guy who went through what he did to make it. It's beautiful, if nothing else, but it feels squarely like a freshman effort in the gameplay deptartment. The story arc feels...disjointed and the gameplay feels like it's missing elements that were intended but cut. This is my overall impression actually. In an effort to finally release this game, which must have been a sisyphean burden hanging over his head, tons of ideas and features got cut. It's a shame, but totally understandable as well. I feel like this would have benefited from a team effort, not just in dividing up the duties, but in working on overall design as a group. I really hope we get more from the creator, and that he isn't burned out.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Ghost Song. And I have 25/42 achievements on Steam, so I did a fair bit of exploring. There is a lot I want to say about this game and that already implies that I will get into spoiler territory for the game. What exists of the game currently would still need a couple of months to rebalance, tweak and polish the entire experience. But even that won’t make the game good or exceptional. There is a functional game here or rather assets of one that need a proper redesign from scratch in order to be good.With that out of the way:. It suffers from the common western trope of - just putting a lot of things together that might not even be cohesive.For example - why does the sprint mechanic exist? It serves no purpose in combat or in platforming. It feels like they slowed the player character down just to add the sprint ability and pad out the game since it also consumes stamina. If the base speed of the protagonist was that of the sprint mechanic OR if the sprinting did not consume any stamina, the game feel would remain unchanged. In fact, either of those would be a QoL upgrade.And this is a microcosm of the entire game. It feels bloated for the sake of dragging playtime.You have to get ship parts from 5 extremities of the map which is the main quest and the game basically forces you to make your way back to the hub area from the extremities of the map. Since you can’t carry two ship parts at the same time and can’t fast travel while carrying the ship parts (game logic), it feels padded. It doesn’t feel thought out honestly.In one case, there were two ship parts that were very close to each other, but I had to go through 60% of the route at least 4 times because of the design.Since we are talking about the map, another problem is the empty rooms. There are wayyyyyyy too many rooms that exist for no reason. For example, while fighting the first quest boss (the spear lady in my case), you have 2-3 completely empty rooms between the last save room and the boss. It almost feels like I have to go through antire walking segment to get to her. And this is the case with a lot of bosses where the save room is placed between 3 rooms of either emptiness or fodder enemies and the boss.And I am NOT saying that empty rooms are bad. A lot of games do this to build atmosphere, but with Ghost Song doing it for every boss, it becomes a pattern and hence loses impactful. Even outside of the bosses, there are many empty rooms or rooms that are too big for no reason.Compounding upon this, players will notice that the game hasn’t been cartographed properly. 90% of the rooms on the map don’t show details within the rooms, but for some reason, there are some parts of the map that show roughly how the platforms are placed. Makes me feel like they released the game before it was completelyu finished.When I say polish, I am talking about the minor things like I did above with the map.There was this one point in the game where a platform was visibly too high to reach with a single jump. My initial visual response was that I could not reach it. But due to instinct, I tried anyway before realizing there was a platform below it that was hidden behind the environment asset which I could use to climb on top. This is present right at the start of the game and is a thankfully a one-off thing, but there are many little things like these that could have really been avoided with more time in development.Keep in mind, I do not have issues with the animations. They look fine for a puppet animated game, but they don’t feel impactful because there isn’t enough of a feeling of acceleration or deceleration (if that makes sense).The entire game feels like it's on one note. There are no highs and no lows. There is no sense of pacing - building tension, middle, and then climax. This extends to the story, combat, boss designs, and everything else.You could find important items just laying around that are just there in the environment with no indication beforehand.With the story, I never had a sense of escalation either. I just had to go to these places, find the parts and would find side characters muttering about in the environment. There was no change in the world. It doesn’t help that the music for the most part is flat or just ambient. There are a couple of cool tracks, but I can’t think of one that’s stuck in my head or that made me go "WHOAAA!"Also, the story simply ends with a…. “Huh that’s it moment?”. Maybe I did not get an alternate ending (?), but from what I have read, the endings don’t have that much of a difference.I don’t really see it having any redeeming points if I am being honest. A lot of the things besides the art feel average or not thought out.The praise this game is getting is unjustified and there are way too many good games released this year for them to be ignored. There are many MVs in 2022 that deserve more praise if Ghost Song is getting an 88 on metacritic.Are all far better designed games.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I noticed this game is sitting at Recent "Mixed" reviews. Not sure why, because I really enjoyed it. Yes, it has a few frustrating aspects, but those are outnumbered by the amount of good features this game provides:1. THE GOODa) Music is calming, surreal and really fitting for the theme.b) Beautiful character and environmental artwork.c) Combat is fluid and fun with a lot of unique modification combos and weapons to choose from.d) Boss fights are unique and well done. Challenging enough but not overly difficult, either. Well balanced.e) Story is written well with interesting dialogue. Get to know each member of the crew.f) Game isn't cluttered with pointless side quests. All storylines are interesting.g) Lighting and shading is beautifully done.2. THE NOT SO GOODI'm not a fan of the aimless wandering to figure out where to go next. While this is common in many metroidvania games, Ghost Song lacks fast travel locations. It has them... but they're very minimal, so there's lot of tedious back and forth.While the story is good... sometimes dialogue drags on for awhile with pointless conversation. "..." is overused quite a bit.The ending was... OK. I believe there's more than one, but I wasn't a fan of how short and abrupt the ending I got was. I wish games/developers put more time into their endings. Give us a bit more story. Cut scenes. I don't want to spoil anything... but the ending wasn't great.3. OVERALLNot a fan of Steam's Thumbs Up/Down review system, so I'd give this game 3.5 out of 5 stars.I feel the "Not So Good" is just picky stuff, though. Overall... I highly recommend this game. I really enjoyed it and could see myself playing again. Ignore the recent "Mixed" reviews and focus on the Overall "Very Positive." There's a New Game+ feature, as well. That's a positive!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish Steam had a rating in between thumbs up and thumbs down because while I don't think Ghost Song is an outright bad game I personally found it to be really lacking compared to the games that inspired it as well as other modern Metroidvania titles.It's a competently made Metroidvania with good atmosphere, solid exploration and upgrades, and a novel heat-based combat mechanic. But the game doesn't really have much else going for it outside of that. The boss battles, while typically a highlight in many of these types of games, are all uniformly mediocre. And the story, while lonely and dreary, didn't really invoke the same kind of wonder as its contemporaries or even actual Metroid games. The map is also kinda small and lacking any truly memorable areas and while I'm glad it didn't overstay its welcome, there's no real sense of tension or build-up all throughout, just find one ship part and move on to the next one rinse and repeat. By the end of the game I was left wanting so much more than what I got.For $20 you could certainly do a whole lot worse, but considering that the indie space is absolutely PACKED with extremely high quality titles of a similar style to this, that alone makes Ghost Song an even harder sell imo. I'd say the game is worth checking out if you're a fanatic for this genre like I am. But for everyone else I'd say wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings, my beautiful bastards,It is I, your ever-dapper raconteur of digital escapades, here to regale you with my musings on "Ghost Song." Let's drift into the eerie, bioluminescent abyss of this sci-fi Metroidvania.First, let us toast to what "Ghost Song" accomplishes with aplomb: the atmosphere. Stepping into its world is like wandering through a half-remembered dream on a desolate moon. The vibrant alien landscape pulses with bio-mechanical life, blending organic and metallic horrors in a visual concerto that’s as unsettling as it is captivating. The music? An otherworldly composition that thrums in harmony with the world’s eerie beauty, echoing through the desolate corridors of your journey. Truly, the game’s ambiance is a haunting masterpiece.However, my dear bastards, the enchantment wavers when we delve deeper into the narrative abyss. The story, like a ghost at dawn, dissipates under scrutiny. You, as the enigmatic Deadsuit, awaken on this forsaken moon with scant guidance. Lore is scattered like spectral breadcrumbs, tantalizing yet frustratingly elusive. Tracking down these narrative nuggets feels like chasing phantoms through a fog—intriguing yet maddeningly incoherent. The plot threads dangle like loose wires, leaving us yearning for a resolution that never quite arrives.And then, there's the denouement—a dissonant crescendo that crashes upon the shores of expectation with all the grace of a drunken banshee. The conclusion offers more questions than answers, a disappointing finale to an otherwise promising journey.Turning to the gameplay, one cannot overlook the melee combat, which clangs and clatters like rusted gears grinding against each other. Deadsuit’s movements are as stiff as an android’s joints in cryosleep, robbing the visceral thrill from encounters that should pulse with adrenaline. It's a damn shame, really, for a game so rich in aesthetic splendor to stumble so conspicuously in the realm of mechanics.Moreover, the sense of direction in "Ghost Song" can be as nebulous as the lore itself. The game teases objectives and leaves you to chart your path, often leading to frustrating dead ends and tedious backtracking. It’s an experience that occasionally feels like trying to navigate a maze with a map drawn by a drunken cartographer.That said, I must tip my hat to the developers for their stellar work on the atmosphere and music. The world they've crafted is hauntingly beautiful and thoroughly immersive, making my time with "Ghost Song" an experience I won't soon forget. Despite its flaws, the journey through this eerie, bio-mechanical landscape was one I ultimately enjoyed.Let me distill my critique into succinct bullet points for those of you who prefer brevity...In conclusion, "Ghost Song" beckons with a siren's call of atmospheric allure, yet flounders in its narrative execution and gameplay mechanics. It is a haunting experience, both in its aesthetic prowess and missed opportunities. Approach for the atmosphere, my beautiful bastards, but beware the nebulous depths of its storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to leave a negative review, because this game is obviously a labor of love and has some great atmosphere, but it really does not feel finished.  There are glaring design oversights and a general lack of polish.  Doors show up on the map which are not there, main bosses for some areas can be skipped _accidentally_, and balance between different builds is basically non-existent.  The combat is actually pretty well done, but the few enemy varieties are very uninteresting to fight, so it falls flat.The story is incomplete and difficult to get invested in, which is too bad because the voice acting is actually pretty good, and it feels like the central idea is fairly compelling.  There are scenes, though, which are supposed to have some kind of emotional impact but fall completely flat because there simply wasn't enough work done to justify them.Positives+ Good voice acting+ Great soundtrack+ CombatNegatives- Lack of balance between builds/weapons- Boring boss and enemy design- General lack of polish throughout the game- Empty areas (beyond what's necessary for atmosphere)- Rushed and incomplete story

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful metroidvanias I've experienced.Ghost Song hits on that melancholic - bittersweet tone that Hollow Knight often had with its atmosphere, only here the feeling stems from the loneliness and emotional baggage of the few you meet along your journey. The game is filled with charecters that I had connected with by the end of my runtime. The npcs arent so deep that you haven't seen these types of struggles before, but something about they way they speak here just feels so genuine.Questioning what you are and what makes you - you. Considerations of your failures. The protagonist constantly unsure of what form they even take beneath their suit, or whether its even a suit at all. None of these things are that new... and I've seen them before... but the delivery of every line and written text just has a certain genuine quality to it that gave me a feeling of connection to the crew - and the few other lonely people you meet along the way.Its the atmosphere and sense of quiet sincerity in each of the characters voices that makes it feel real. In the end Ghost Song made me feel something, which is more than I can say for most games that I play nowadays. Its a solid metroidvania. It has incredible, somber music. And reminded me of a quiet, nostalgic feeling that I don't often get to have. Hopefully you enjoy Ghost Song as much as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I  like this game, and hope to  like it moorewith some patches, but as it is I just find it a bit frustrating.- hit boxes need tightening for some bosses.- there should be a degree of bounceback/hitstun on attacks and contact, as it is it's very easy for enemies to simply walk into your melee attack and damage you/damage you with  contact then match your movements and get you again (the red skulls in the junkpit are a prominent example of this). which imo feels awkward.- some enemy ai favours tracking your characters movement way too closely which makes evasion feel overly difficult. Yes git gud, but this feels like the bad kind of attack tracking. A core part of what makes metroidvanias fun is exploiting enemy movement and some enemies in this are just deeply frustrating.- I feel like while restricting fast travel to statues is fine, levelling should be available at save points, running back to statues to level is onerous. Relatedly the souls games and other titles with "drop currency on death but retrieve from corpse" systems usually have homeward bone equivalents OR drop the souls outside of boss arenas/other one way traps.- being able to drop the difficulty midway should be implemented. I'm fine with not being able to raise it again, I get that cheevos and all, but having to restart cause you get hours in and find some of the difficulty effects obnoxious is kind of galling and the kind of thing to get people putting a game down.This all said, I really like the general gameplay, the exploration, aesthetic, VA and the combat when it doesnt hit the above issues.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a bad habit in Metroidvanias and similar genres to confuse difficulty with "difficulty." The former can make beating a game feel like a real accomplishment; the latter is tedium. This game feels, to me, full of a lot more of the I-Wanna-Be-The-Guy-esque "just reset a bunch until you do it perfectly" gameplay than any genuine difficulty. The enemies are absolute tanks, and the level-up system lifted from Dark Souls doesn't change your character's effectiveness in a meaningful way. I still recommend Ghost Song, however, if you have more of a tolerance for this type of game than I do. The world is cool, the suit and gun upgrades are interesting, and the melee combat variety with swappable equipment is a nice touch. Despite the game's design not being to my liking, I feel it is well-executed generally and might warrant a full playthrough on easy when the memory of the headache that was attempt one fades.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I wasn't into Ghost Song at first. The murky, gnarled artstyle and zero premises turned me down, let alone the rather weak state of our protagonist. You don't even have an objective until you explore a certain amount of areas. However, the game wins me over gradually. It does the exploration part of metroidvania really well. Secrets and NPCs spread across the alien landscapes. I even grow accustomed to the artstyle, and in the end fall in love with it.This is hands-down the major reason that keeps me interested throughout the game. Strictly speaking, it isn't something crazy new or creative. Features like breakable walls with subtle clues and ability-gating obstacles are well-tuned. Yet, Ghost Song manages to integrate a lot of things to season the established formula, adding more surprises on your journey. Bizarre, distinct design of each area jumps between alien-beautiful and eerily disturbing. It will make you frown but you will want to see more. Backtracking may be tedious, but the dev has put effort into making it less tiresome to go through. And there's NPC. NPCs are mostly stranded human survivors and Android crash-landing on this strange moon. You will encounter some of them in various areas wandering. Whether it's random or scripted, I am really surprised to find them and delightful to hear their stories .→Voice actors have done a great job in this game.→Combat needs some time to get used to but ultimately it is interesting.→: The dev recognizes the tediousness of backtracking, and designs some interesting twists and encounters to alleviate that feeling. There's one encounter which I still hold dear even after I finish the game: I killed a roaming boss, she was rooted after defeat. She said some quips and I left, thinking that was her last words. The next time I backtrack through this location, I was surprised to find out she wasn't dead and she greeted me leisurely, then proceed to talk about her way of living and other stuff. Moments like this really makes me fall in love with this game.→: Still, unfortunately, backtracking in Ghost Song is infamously long and tedious. May be it's because the safe points are rather scarce, or the option to teleport only ties to the Big Bots, and they are often hidden places which are limited or hard to reach.Ghost Song's story is so obscure to the point that it is irrelevant. There's only one over-arching story -you meet some survivors and you want to help them rebuild the spaceship-, and you only know it after roughly 30 minute into the game. No item description like the souls-series. The other thing that remotely relates to the story is NPC's diaogue, except the majority of dialogues often goes to personal struggle, or specific scene from the past. Individual areas, besides stylish backgrounds, might not even have NPC to tell you something at all.中文小簡評→一款幾乎沒啥故事的類銀河系惡魔城，儘管如此我還是很喜歡。→這類型遊戲的特色都有齊全，而本作著重探索。→畫風有種異域美，介於詭譎跟魔幻之間。→可以在很多地方看得出製作人的用心，特別是回頭探索的部分，可能會遇到遊蕩的NPC，隨機出現的Boss等。→角色配音十分到位，我很喜歡聽他們分享故事。→戰鬥有趣，但需要時間適應。→雖然在回頭探索上下了多功夫，依舊難逃無聊及煩躁感，其因歸咎於存檔點太少太分散，而能傳送的點都放在一些難以抵達的位置。→跟主線故事相關的事物幾乎為零，只有幾位NPC的對話會扯到一點點關係。

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty and has nice atmosphere going for it, but unfortunately that's all it has going for it. The story is mediocre and the most interesting parts of it are just background lore details that never get explored, and the most interesting encounters are just discarded with no follow up development. The combat system has a good foundation with the heat system encouraging swapping between melee and ranged attacks, but it's let down by bad enemy design that focuses overwhelmingly on flailing around and dealing contact damage that makes staying at range the better option against bosses, and the heat system is trivialised by an ice weapon you get, which is also stronger than melee weapons without any of the risk. Also, the final boss is so pathetically easy it just left a bad taste in my mouth, which was compounded by the ending.The gimmick of being locked out of fast travel when picking up a part and needing to take it back to the ship (the main hub area) is initially interesting, but enemies are so easy to avoid and the world map lacking connections outside of the most central area means you don't really need to make any consideration of what path to take, you just go back the way you came and deal with a few extra enemies on the way.There are also some shops around the game with ridiculously bloated prices; if you wanted to buy everything without moving into NG+ you would be spending literal hours trying to scrounge up the money for it. And one of the most expensive shop items is also needed to access a hidden area of major story relevance.I had high hopes for Ghost Song but in the end it turned out to be a thoroughly disappointing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to rate this positively but it does too good a job of holding itself back. Parts of it are legitimately great - the art is fantastic, the voice acting is solid, I find myself invested in the characters and the survival of the crew, but... god it's just a slog to actually PLAY.  Traversal is slow and a little janky; the dodge ability goes whichever way you were facing when you left the ground during a jump, sprinting is nowhere near fast enough for a game that requires as much backtracking as a Metroidvania does, and having bosses slowly grind down your HP bar, forcing you to backtrack to a repair station every few attempts, which are often quite far away, is just... you struggle to understand from a game design perspective what was going on there.On top of that, I thought we had moved past enemies damaging you on contact even if you dodge their actual attacks.  I want to see more, I just don't want to play more to get to it, which is kind of a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great metroidvania. Exploration is satisfying with many different biomes housing unique mobs and hazards. More importantly, environments feel real, wildlife will react to your presence in different, believable ways. It's immersive and while the actual level layouts are nothing new, they're never frustrating either.Combat is even better: you're given a lot of freedom in how you attack enemies. Your ranged weapons have infinite ammo but overheat after too much use, which weakens them temporarily but also buffs your melee attack's damage. You can game this system in different ways depending on how you prefer to play, which is great.Story is the part of Ghost Song i enjoyed the least. Your objective for most of the game is rather uninteresting and while there are lots of characters to meet and do side quests for, all of their stories feel rather isolated from the rest of the narrative. There are many intriguing mysteries, but a regular playthrough will not yield the answers to the game's most interesting questions. Some will see this as unsatisfying, others will see it as an extra layer of replay value, both of which are valid.Finally, the soundtrack is wonderful and always fits the action. While not the most memorable OST, it's a pleasant listen even outside of the game.Easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: From the gameplay standpoint it's a well crafted metroidvania made in concord with the classic tenets of the genre. The intricate network of locations that we will traverse through is decently designed and implementation of the souls-like level up mechanics makes its exploration not only rewarding but tense as well. The wildlife that will obstruct our journey can be quite a nuisance. Here with help comes a thought-out combat system where once our only ranged weapon has overheated we can use it as a melee to inflict more damage. This quite innovative tactic  is especially helpful as the foes not only can be tough, but also tend to quickly shorten the distance between us.However no matter how interesting the gameplay is, this is one of those games that you play mainly for the vibes. From the very first moments, the game captivates us with the haunting eerie atmosphere of the alien desolate world which is further induced by the amazing shoegaze soundtrack and gloomy art-style. And this is the main reason you should check this title out.

_childDocuments_.review: Which was going to be a Dark Souls inspired metroidvania. Back when that was a novel concept. And it was a powerful one, sending masses of people to a discord, backing on the kickstarter and preordering it on Humble.Having been part of some of the earliest demos, I can tell it it's been worth the wait. Supposedly a "shorter" metroidvania, the five hours I've sunk in so far to acquire a few weapons and upgrades don't  short, seeing as I only just got to the double jump ten minutes ago. aren't just in their designated locations - neatly marked with beams of light sometimes in the middle of an area you've already explored - but some roam. Some are only introduced after key points in the story. They're not terribly difficult as far as metroidvania bosses go, with easy patterns and distinct telegraphing movesets. But they pack a punch and they play into the mechanics for your Deadsuit nicely.The  is beautiful, from the first haunting notes played in the main screen to the atmo heard around the caverns. Sound design on enemies is sometimes a little confusing - is this a boss enemy waiting for my approach or just a flying mob - but nevertheless distinct and crisp.The voice acting is gorgeous, far better than to be expected of endeavours that usually take this long. Characters are distinct. Have weight to them. The Deadsuit itself is endearing and sad when rarely piping up. It doesn't just set the tone, it clamps it down completely. I find myself exhausting every dialogue willingly just to hear the moments of talk between two strangers. A superb performance with very clear recordings.The terrain is 2d, but there are subtle depth tricks and 3d elements implemented with far greater care and attention to detail than Castlevania ever pulled off. Little perspective changes as you walk across masses of scrap metal, some alien flora that briefly obscures you as you walk under its boughs. The design is striking and well coloured, making even drab monochrome areas look distinct and full of detail despite sticking very clearly to its palette.All in all I cannot recommend this game enough. It's unforgiving but not cruel, and once you get used to the interesting combat mechanic of swapping between ranged and melee it becomes a very neat dance with characters, only  by new mechanics every time you acquire a new module to enhance your abilities.Perhaps we've gotten used to mediocrity in these types of games. Perhaps Matt was just driven by perfectionism and refused to live by "good enough".This game is a love letter to the type of games it was inspired from, and stands far better on its own because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a struggle, as it feels like there were a lot of good ideas - that never really became a coherent whole.The strongest part of this game is the first few hours. You wake up, no memory, no direction - just eeriness and plenty of opportunities to explore. It's atmospheric and feels like you are discovering a vast world.After the first few hours, you'll meet a spaceship crew who then all jostle each other to fill the air with quite meaningless dialogue, and handily mark on your map everywhere you'll need to go to finish the game. That's quite a contrast to the first few hours.There's a lot of upgrades to find which require different energy amounts, a la Hollow Knight, but then they undercut it by having your energy amount linked to how long you are prepared to grind levels. Boss difficulty is all over the place, while having a system that makes Bosses harder the more you lose to them, unless you backtrack back to one of the few repair points.And perhaps the cardinal sin of Metroidvanias - in a game that leans on backtracking even more than most in this genre, you can't make movement itself feel like such slog.If the score for this was not Binary, I'd give it a 6/10.
