_childDocuments_.review: Barring one glaring issue, this became one of my favorite Metroidvanias (coming from someone that's been playing these titles since the original NES Metroid and Castlevania). The visuals and sound are enthralling and it was unusual to have a Metroidvania with a decent narrative - both through evolving NPC relationships and environmental storytelling. Just about everything was thoroughly intriguing and I couldn't wait to find out more. As far as action goes, a variety of movement abilities, melee, and ranged weapons kept the minute-to-minute play interesting.Buuuut, the game just ends. No anticipated climax. Only one resolution. Little explanation. Cheap artwork and no meaningful dialog. Not even a hint of a pre/sequel to fill things in. It's like the devs ran out of time or threw up their hands while shouting, "Bored now!" and left the Friday afternoon janitor to draw and write the closing scenes while everyone else went to Vegas. And I say that after nearly 100%-ing the game, using no guides, and getting the "good" ending. I spent 20 hours on a single playthrough, loving nearly every minute of it, and this was the disappointing return. Does that change my recommendation? Absolutely not - but know you'll have fill in a ton of loose story threads on your own.Another thing to note is that unlike me, you may get sick of backtracking. The game has limited fast travel and the primary loop involves fetching parts from the ends of the map and manually returning them to base (usually with new enemies on the way). That's not terrible, but NPC's and minibosses spawn and move around with each part returned. This means to 100% the game in terms of items and story, you're going to have to re-explore the  map six or so times. I personally felt that the carrot-on-the-stick was enticing enough for this activity, but you may not and I wouldn't blame you for it.+Beautiful artwork, decent animation+A lot of nice touches all over the place (I love that water cools your gun)+A number of unique or rare mechanics+Voice acting pretty good+Very relaxing music. Absolutely love it. Available on YT, Bandcamp and Amazon.+Great sound design, attacks and explosions "feel" weighty+Controls are generally responsive+Encourages a mix of ranged and melee combat, tailorable to your preferences+Bosses have multiple phases, often show damage and telegraph pretty fairly+Fascinating lore+A number of genuinely creepy enemies and areas+Many NPC's - friend and foe - have personality+Most secrets have subtle audio or visual clues+Ability cooldowns also have audio and visual clues+Can disable controller vibration+Normal and casual (less death penalty) difficulties+Multiple save slots+New Game++RPG elements and mostly open world, so you can work around tough fights+You can also simply run away from or past many bosses~Some blood, no gore or swearing, very minor statue nudity~Not a lot of documentation of the game available online~Devs seem to have abandoned game?~Unusual number of "empty" hallways with not much of anything to see or do~Save point frequency inconsistent at the start~Could use another one or two fast travel points~A number of enemies require awkward crouching to hit~Screen transitions could be a bit smoother~Mouse cursor occasionally appears on screen~A few enemies can get stuck in walls~A number of permanently missable items and conversations if you're not thorough~Game doesn't hold your hand and expects you to find hidden mechanics and lore~One UI element I never figured out the purpose for~No end-game item/ability for finding secrets you missed?~No completion %'s listed anywhere before or after credits?~You have to re-explore the entire map each phase if you want 100%~I appreciate the purpose of the Curious Gizmo, but I wish the intent was at least hinted at in the description. Wasted a ton of time re-exploring the entire map, hoping to find its use - only to look on the forums later and see that I didn't need it due to earlier exploration.-Unskippable splash screens-One softlock attempting to access  forcing an Alt+F4-Ogre being able to instantly turn around and change his massive hurtbox is cheap-Map markers have a number of bugs that devs haven't fixed for more than a year-So much lore is left unresolved, and not in a good kind of way-The final minutes of the game are an enormous, effortless letdown, even with pre-hinted "good" ending revelationPlayed on:Win11, i7-14700K, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SExplorer difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: is a Metroidvania with Souls-like elements. The story follows a newly-awakened Deadsuit who took upon herself to assist the surviving crew of a crashed spaceship. There are no story-related choices (the main character auto-replies in dialogues), though some of the mandatory objectives can be achieved in different order. The story and the dialogues are written well, and the characters are likeable, so the protagonist’s lines are fitting and going along with the objectives comes easy.The combat is functional - the main default weapon is a gun with rather limited range, while the damage decreases the farther the target is. There are other ranged weapons with different attack types and abilities, as well as melee weapons. Also a combat drone. It should be noted that there is contact damage and it hits as hard as a normal attack from the respective foe, which usually makes ranged combat preferable. The main character has few attributes which can be upgraded at the infrequent fast travel points, while the save points are much more plentiful. Additionally, there are modules, which provide quality changes to the protagonist’s abilities, such as healing while attacking in melee, double jumping, or being able to see foes’ health bars. The bosses are diverse, challenging, and have some background story. Most of them have several stages or additional mechanics. A few are the same as the regular enemies, but larger. The main aspect of a Metroidvania is exploration, and the world is interesting and engaging to explore. There are a lot of optional paths and secrets, while the traversal is comfortable. There are very fast travel points, but the map is not too large. Additionally, the locations change slightly as the story progresses, most notably, during the return-to-camp sequences, while new abilities allow to access previously unreachable areas. The visual design is stunningly beautiful and easy to read at the same time. The music is pleasant and does not block foes’ attack cues nor distracts from the game. The dialogues are partially voiced, with the VA being of good quality. The controls are reasonably comfortable and rebindable. No significant bugs have been encountered during the playthough, only a couple visual ones. The only technical flaw I can see is auto-saving in the same slot, which is typical for Souls-likes and can be circumvented by copying the save files with Windows Explorer manually. Overall, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful atmospheric game with intriguing story lore. I genuinely enjoyed the dialogue (but you can skip past it and not have the extra engagement). Good fun. Combat was challenging and I found myself dying and retrying over and over for some of the bosses (some of which I came back to slightly later). You pick up different modules and different weapons, and based on your level you can choose how many and which ones to equip, and then you can toggle through the equipped weapons during a fight. This enables you to adapt to different enemies, but will also challenge you to approach familiar enemies with different loadouts and adapt accordingly. I don't play metroidvania normally. I bought this game because I played the Swapper and Ghost Song promised me the same vibes. I did find it frustrating having to go back through previously explored areas once I had new abilities unlocked - but most of that frustration may have been because you cannot sprint or dash in the early game. During late game play it was easy to move through the map.I really value how you can play the game your way and your style, because the skill development isn't linear, but cumulative (and you must choose what you have active at any given time).I absolutely wanted more from the game. I approached the final boss fight really hoping it would unlock some new chapter instead of finish the game. I didn't want to begin a New Game + BUT after writing this review I think I will afterall. There's more modules and weapons to find and play around with and the difficulty has already shown itself to be adaptive. Plus there are some resolutions for some characters which I did not find in my first play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, but wanted to write on for Ghost Song.I've been following this game since 2016, and I feel like it was worth the wait for sure. The game is absolutely beautiful. The music fits in perfectly to where I always enjoyed it, but it always felt so smooth to be that I barely noticed when it was coming and going. Very seamless, very appropriate, very good. The art is wonderful as well. Each area and scene has so many layers to it that give the world so much more depth, immersion, and distinction. I really loved the combat system, seeing what all sorts of combinations I could use between the melee weapons and various alt blasters. I really enjoyed the gun heat mechanic that forced you to be more strategic in combat and not just rely on a blaster from far away. Finally, I really enjoyed all of the characters and their stories. I loved the writing and the development of the overall story and the stories of the characters. It was really fun to piece it all together.There are certainly some things that couldn't have been done different, but I know the dev team is listening and changing what they can, and its also their first game. I discovered after beating the game that it was easy to miss a number of character interactions, some that are necessary for the full ending and deeper lore. That said, this isn't too unique with most Soulsborne type games, but I think there could have been a bit more guidance. I didn't feel like the game was a huge challenge, but it was so fun to explore, and I'm already excited about my NG+ playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game more but i just can't. I can see the love and effort poured into this game but my main issue is that the design choices and poor QoL options make me feel like playing the game is a chore.-----------------------Minor Spoilers ahead-----------------------Like really? The game could have made use of its save points to be fast travel points as well but decided to use another landmark that are only 6 spread quite far apart in the world. Most of my game time was spent running around places i've already been and although the scenery and environment look pretty it gets dull moving back and forth the same rooms over and over again and it makes searching and exploring for collectibles a bore. Speaking about moving back and forth the same rooms. The game  your ability to fast travel at some points of the game and expects you to do a watered down fetch quest  throughout the whole game. This not only artificially extends the play time of the game but also makes me dread the fetch quest sequences whenever I defeat a major boss.The story was good but in the end felt abrupt and incomplete. The story is probably the least of the issues i have with the game. Rather, its the controller options and bugs left in the game that are more major.The game recommends you to use a controller to play the game but forces you to used a fixed layout that you are unable to change. I didn't have much issues conforming to the layout but i feel in a metroidvania where combat and exploration is key, controller input customization is A MUST HAVE. Other than this there are a few bugs left in the game that can disrupt your game play. For me i have experienced the character dashing in the opposite direction after a wall jump for example. Others have reported being locked out of a side quest because of some boundary being present after dying. Granted the developer has been pushing out updates to fix these issues but its far to say the game is complete in any sense.The combat is decent but the only customization available are the special weapons and your equippable weapon. There is a "class" feature but its not expanded upon and is only used to show your specialization in a certain stat, there are no combat or gameplay benefits for changing your "class". At the start the blaster feels like it can be expanded upon but there was no functionality to upgrade or use a different blaster in the whole game other than those special weapons.Movement is alright apart from the opposite dash bug that i experienced a few times. The sprint button feels redundant in the game.Overall, a decent but unpolished Metroidvania marred by its design choices and lack of controller customization. Story ended abruptly and felt it can be expanded more via more endings rather than just a slight variation of it.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: A tough choice between thumbs up and thumbs down. The biggest problem with Ghost Song is that the game's story gets in the way of actually playing the game: the game is littered with missable NPC encounters which change what happens thereafter, and you most of the time are given no hints where to look for them and when. It also occurred to me way too late in the game that character development might even be a subject of relevance at all, and that every time you return a ship part you pass a threshold for completing missable content. I also wonder if the game would fare better if it just did away with the minimap altogether, since it has a lot of shortcomings and issues which can lead you to assume you already checked certain areas when you didn't. It makes some of the exploration feel like clueless wandering, which is really unfortunate. Once I realized this and just accepted my fate of having to check every single room in the game a second time, paradoxically, I suddenly got far more enjoyment out of the game. I would also have liked to see more combat in general. As is tradition with soulslike games, you respawn enemies by visiting some sort of save or checkpoint. There aren't really many opportunities to do this strategically to farm about for a slight level advantage. Only one spot comes to mind and it felt more like an exploit than part of the game. Ultimately what leads me to give this a thumbs up are the lore and the dialogs. There isn't too much to go by, but just enough to spark your imagination as to what is even going on in the game's world. Also thumbs up for being able to tone down the cutthroat game mechanics when starting a new game. Definitely give it a chance when it's on sale, but curb your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: A graphically pleasing souls-like action side scroller with a splash of metroidvania. I wasn't blown away by the game, but it's good enough. The graphics and environments are really nice. Everything seems squishy and alive. So many gross sounds. The atmosphere and mood of the game is really good. Feels very nostalgic. The old decaying robots all over the place made me so curious as to what happened here. And the bodies that appear human which are posed add some creepiness and mystery. I read a bit of the lore after completeing the game, and it's interesting. Unfortunately a lot of it is buried and hidden in interactions that you may not stumble across, kinda like Dark Souls. While these encounters are not crystal clear and seem random, I actually kind of liked it. I fought and lost to a boss once (a sliver of hp left, very frustrating) and it wasn't there when I got back. Other times, areas I've walked by a dozen times had a random high health or boss enemy. Or new enemy types would start to appear. Or an NPC would just be there for some reason. Makes the world feel alive.The combat is decent. Challenging in the beginning, but once I adapted and found what worked for me, it's pretty simple. Though some bosses have really large health pools. Leveling is good. I really like the idea of a slowly growing pool of points I can use to select from many different mods for customization. It allowed me to deselect mods I really like in favor of better ones, knowing that I just needed to keep pushing and I'd be able to equip it again soon.Some gripes:1. Final boss and ending were lackluster. It was a nice reveal, but just felt very unsatisfying.2. Screen transitions are bad, there is no continuity and each environment is basically a fresh load. Doesn't feel smooth or natural. When you go up, a platform is placed below you that you stand on that disappears after a short time, which seems sloppy.3. They really needed to increase the amount of fast travel points. Or at least some way to fast travel back to your most recent fast travel point. Collecting secrets and items at the end becomes a slog.For me, the game had no replayability, it just wasn't that good. About 16 hours for 61% achievements. Do I think that's worth the price tag. Probably. Would I wait for a sale to get this game, definitely. But is it still worth picking up? If you like souls-likes and side scrolling metroidvania-lights, then yes.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to give the game a score 7/10 would be that score but I'd still advise finding out more about the experience others would have had, also you want to ensure that they're actual Metroidvania fans and not some clown who saw a gun or two in a trailer and assumed this is a run n gun game or something. But I really want to emphasize: GIVE THIS DEVELOPER A CHANCE & SUPPORT  if they were to build on what I've seen here and they pay attention to the players with another shot at this their next Project won't be really good, it'll be GREAT!With that said, I pretty much only completed this game because I started it and I always try to finish what I start, I absolutely LOVE Metroidvanias so that alone would be enough for someone like me to complete Ghost Song. I enjoyed it and I DO think the world building, story, characters etc. will scratch that itch for casual Metroidvanias but it's not for reasons you may expect. It can get boring at times backtracking and the fast travel system...yeah, not the best, but what we have here in Ghost Song is better than most.Your heart will race at times because of tougher challenges as you mosey along but not because the stakes are naturally high (Think Super Metroid or Axiom Verge). Whether the stakes are high or not will be based on  your personal decision to care about the characters you meet along the way and I MUST add here though that even though persons CAN be pretty chatty, they actually DO feel  real and relatable. I cared about the freedom of some persons I wanted to hear what certain synthetics had to sayI was personally blown away by the fact that an A.I. had so much personality I wanted to get a missing part or two to help it alongI DID find it interesting that other species casually exist and it's no big deal to anyone I did find a few environments very eerie, lonely and isolatingAnd I DO wish I could find out more about the universe in Ghost Song...so I just call it a side story in the world of Mind Seize and make that my head canon, problem solved.Buy it

_childDocuments_.review: I feel... weird, about this game. Like, it's good - quite good - and it's clear a lot of love and care went into this, but I come away from it feeling... unsatisfied.The positives are pretty obvious - this is one of the most beautiful and atmospheric games of the year, full stop. The visuals successfully create an alien, claustrophobic environment that's still... kind of serene and chill all the same, and the minimal but effective soundtrack and sound design do a lot to sell that atmosphere, it's an absolute delight of a world to explore.The combat mechanics are their core are great, too - the balance between guns and melee that encourages you to use both, the additional of powerful weapons limited by recharging ammo to encourage experimentation, a range of movement upgrades that all tend to be helpful in combat, an instant health recharge that works more like a regen so as to not be too overpowered, a whole set of tweaks you can equip to change your power or gamefeel, on that level there's a lot to love....but the game reeeeally stretches itself way too thin. There's simply. Not enough game to get sufficient use out of all of the tools provided, especially when certain tools end up feeling like game breakers (I literally do not know why you'd use any other melee weapon besides the painwheel!) and the game's already fairly short 8 hour runtime is padded out by a drought of fast travel points and most egregiously, the run halfway across the map to deliver each ship part that doesn't really... add anything when you're likely going to get funneled into the same return routes each time.The plot also has intrigue to it but, again, doesn't have room to build... there are ideas, there is lore, but when the main quest boils down to "collect ship parts to fix a ship" and you end up learning very little about, you know, the player character even by the very end of the game, it's hard to get too attached to the world or the characters.And parts of the world just feel... underdeveloped. What's up with that top left area full of dragonfly-type enemies that has literally nothing in it? Why is the final area comprised of two long hallways broken up by... what feels like a midgame boss slapped right before an abrupt ending cutscene? I also don't like how easy it is to get locked out of a few specific characters' storylines just because you didn't happen to find them in between delivering ship parts, which inevitably leads to quest lines left hanging that you wanted to see the end of. There's also aspects of the gameplay that... don't feel so good.Game devs.I'm begging you.Stop. Including. Run. Buttons. They're annoying, they're unnecessary, they lead to RSIs, they almost always come attached with a stamina bar that limits the game for the sake of limitation and just slows down the pacing of the game in general. The repair mechanic also feels... punitive, not as egregious as Rain World's karma system but it achieves a similar effect in that it basically forces a run back to one of the few repair points if you incur too much damage. It gets tedious..There's also some bosses who just feel... too big (the ogre) or too agile (Henriette) to reasonably be fought - the latter looooves to just run away and both your ranged and melee attacks have a fairly short range on the whole so that fight turns into an annoying game of cat and mouse... and she's fought twice. Not helped is that many bosses have long stretches of running, with often... not... much standing between you and them, just... running, to get back to the fight. I don't know why saves can't just be placed before bosses. Eh.There's also an abundance of hidden, breakable walls, but I actually think they're generally telegraphed pretty well... I just wish you ended up having some kind of tool to detect them or help with cleanup to any extent that doesn't amount to looking up a map online. The economy's also screwed - despite going out of my way to explore as much as possible, despite equipping both the nanogel increasing module and the nanogel magnet module fairly early on, I still ended up having to grind for about an hour to reach the amount needed to buy everything available and upgrade my suit to level 30. None of this was needed to /beat/ the game, sure, but it just feels unbalanced - I ended up never upgrading my suit again after about the three hour mark when more expensive shop items become available just to be able to afford shop items.I think in the end I feel like there was potential here, but also too much ambition, and the game world simply doesn't sprawl enough to capitalize on either. Tack on a few spots locking polish or balance and the end result is a game that's beautiful in the moment, with one of the more striking metroidvania worlds in quite some time, but one that struggles to leave a lasting impact, and that feels very unfortunate. I still definitely recommend it, even at full price, but I was hoping to get a bit more out of this than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game, definitely a surprise whose quality caught me unaware! Even though it lacks polish in some mechanical aspects, the art direction, soundtrack and especially the story are really well done. It captures better than most that poignant feeling many of the soulslikes try to emulate from the original Dark Souls, and does it in a grounded and heartfelt manner. The characters are all well written and believable and the mixture of mysterious big epic and day-to-day events is balanced, creating a very genuine style of storytelling. The exploration is satisfying, the combat is serviceable but has its particular challenge. From what I've read other reviews some people dislike the gun/heating mechanics but I found it a clever twist in the old soulslike formula that separates it from most other games of the genre. And once you start getting better gun modules and melee weapons it becomes much more interesting to combine and find ways of dealing with certain enemies or areas.All in all, an easy recommendation for any action/exploration or soulslike fans! Hopefully there will be a sequel somewhere down the line in which it strengths are reinforced and the fumbles adjusted to create an even better gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel sort of bad to give this a no, but I can't in good conscience say yes. TLDR: Story and art look lovely, but general weird decisions about the controls and enemies make it unsatisfying to play.The art of this game is lovely, and the story seems to be shaping up to be very interesting. However, there are some decisions that were made in the development that I really feel were just wrong. The game is very difficult, which is fine in and of itself, and it's difficulty comes from two things prominently. 1 is that everything is pretty chunky health-wise. Fine, that just requires that the player be very meticulous and cautious. Not sure that's BEST decision for all the time, but whatever, it's okay.2 however, is that the player's movement is pretty clunky, which I would argue is a problem here and I kind of want to air it out here, because I feel like people will defend it and I want them to know they're wrong. Feel free to scroll past now, if you don't want to bother with my annoyance with this point.On that second point, clunky movement is not always a downside, but it ends up being one here because the game is already meant to be highly difficult, in terms of enemy health. You must balance being able to do damage with staying out of reach. And you definitely have to stay out of reach, because the damage you take from brushing up against any enemy whatsoever, implies that they're all wearing contact nerve poison cologne or something. Which considering your base move speed is extremely slow, and any action that you take (such as using your melee weapon on an enemy that got pretty close) you have to just sit there for a solid second, aka: long enough to guarantee they get you with that cologne from before. Commonly, this may also result in you getting hit a SECOND time because your suit bugs out or something from the smell.Not too long into the game however, you'll get the ability to sprint and a dash with invincibility frames. Unfortunately these aren't super helpful. It takes a moment to ramp up your sprint, so it isn't meant to be a way to get away from things (weirdly). The dash is good, but then the weird decisions come back again to make it inconsistent. Many of the bosses have wide enough hurt boxes, that require you to dash through them at specific heights. This would be fine if they didn't also sometimes have a yell thing (which they don't telegraph) that interrupts your dash, commonly while you're inside them. This will result in you being hit TWICE for sure, because the initial hit will get you, then you will not be able to dash out again before a second hit happens because you got hit so you have to pause there for a second. Lastly, for some reason the dash does not supersede other commands. This is a particular gripe for me, because I would sometimes accidentally push the analog stick slightly diagonally down, which made me crouch and unable to dash. Considering I'd never actually found a reason to crouch, I genuinely don't understand why it's even an option. And if you've read this whole thing (wow you must be bored) and are thinking: just use the keyboard then you dunce; the game says right on the title screen that the game is intended (wonky button controls and all) to be played on a controller. So somehow, I feel like my screw-ups with the analog sticks are actually intended. So yes, some of it was me, but there were still decisions made about the game controls and environment design that I just disagree with inherently.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for a few months since seeing it in upcoming and I'm frankly disappointed with out quickly it showed itself to be poorly done. It's pretty and there's not much more to appreciate about it than that.It suffers tremendously from clunky, stiff, poor quality combat, which should be a death sentence for anything trying to be a Metroidvania. The "shoot gun to make gun worse and melee better" system feels like a B-grade attempt to be different for the sake of it and it falls really, really flat. Melee feels god awful and it's only made worse from being forced to do it. The animations feel slow even when they're short, do not flow well either into each other or anything else, have insufferably small hitboxes, and often have absurd recovery times. This applies to most other animations as well, like jumping and dashing. Mobility is unforgiveably poor, with the dash being a stand out in how useless it is during combat thanks to the nonsensical cooldown on invulnerability that isn't visually communicated and leads to getting bodied by enemies more often than actually evading anything. The jump is likewise nearly unusuable thanks to its atrocious horizontal distance and excessive height. This also makes the platforming very poor.Some other bads:- Some enemies have inexplicably large health pools and take way too long to kill, for no apparent reason.- Leveling up does not appear to make any noticeable difference. Kill speed feels the same no matter how much you pump weapons, your death speed feels the same no matter how much you pump health.- Every game nowadays wants to be a Souls-like and 90% of them don't understand how to do it well, including this one, and it's really tiring seeing the same tropes (stamina bar, lose upgrade points on death, tedious/punishing confused with difficult) get copy pasted all over the place.Reading other reviews, this game has apparently been in development for 8-10 years and I don't know what that time was spent on because it sure wasn't the gameplay.Speaking of other reviews, a word of caution to readers - I've (now) gathered that this game has hit cult following status because something something Kickstarter underdog one person developer, and from my experience actually playing the game that appears to be the only reason it's getting as much praise as it is here. The game is ultimately not as good as many of these reviews make it out to be. Thankfully, it showed me it was poor quality fast enough that I didn't miss that two hour window.Pay attention to your play time and have your finger on the refund button if you decide to get suckered by the hype.

_childDocuments_.review: Good metroidvania, loved exploring the map. Atmosphere was awesome, plot was great, well worth the price.There are a lot of guns available, but I felt like I really only used about 2. I like that there are a variety of melee weapons, but I have  hard time using most of them since they are slow and this is a game where you suffer contact damage, so if your spacing is off even just a little you'll run into the enemy and take damage. _childDocuments_.review: Great game that won't take too long to beat. my playtime shows about 10 hours which I think is the ideal length for games of this style. I really like the music and art. Movement was great once you get double jump. the MC's default jump is a bit too vertical for some of the earlier platforming but there's not enough of those to be a solid complaint. I liked the module system though i beat the game with probably fewer than half of them acquired even though it looked like I filled out the map. For the most part the game's combat was not too challenging but i prefer that in this type of game personally. I did not really like how spongy some common enemies were. i dumped most of my points into power up my gun but i would still cross even early on rooms with enemies that took way too many hits to kill. the portrait art for the human faces look pretty bad and i don't feel like they fit in with the rest of the art of the game. The map was mostly fine but sometimes the exit from one room didn't line up with the entrance to the next and i once got stuck because a door i passed by earlier wasn't represented on the map at all. A reddit post from someone in the exact same situation got me back on track though. The story and character interactions were neat but the people talked for waaaay too long and they took the dark souls approach of having to speak to someone 4 or more times times to exhaust thier dialog. what they had to say was interesting but it could have been cut back substantially without harming the game. _childDocuments_.review: Remember how the catchphrase for Dark Souls is 'Prepare to die"? Well, the catchphrase for Ghost Song could be "Prepare to wait." Wait for you main weapon to cool off, wait for your subweapon energy to refill, wait for your dash/run stamina to refill, wait for the NPCs to slowly speak...All enemies are damage sponges, especially bosses. Coupled with the "waiting" issue, most bosses take over 10 minutes to defeat.Only 3.5 traversal upgrades. The half upgrade is a weapon that is alos used to break special walls but there are only like 3 or 4 of those walls. Technically, you could argue that there are two more but one of them is only available at endgame, the other is "need-a-guide-to-find" hidden and both are optional.Only 7 "level up + fast travel + restore your max health" devices in the whole game which, coupled with the Souls-like death system (you drop your money/exp and need to get it back + your max health is reduced), makes it very frustrating. Also, they are weirdly placed (some are very close to each other and there are huge areas without them).This "weird placement" thing is also true for the save points and most bosses don't have a nearby save point.Many mandatory pathways are hidden behing fake walls/floors/ceilings.The main plot point of the game is that you need to find 5 devices and bring them back to a specific place. Emphasis on "bring them back". One at a time. Without fast travel.Most sidequests are missable because bringing back a device acts as a point of no return. If you don't find and speak to everyone until you exhaust their lines between each device, you're screwed. Also, there are no in-game clues about them.The game doesn't pause when you open the map or the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: If i had to sum up why you need to play this game in one word it would be 'atmosphere' or 'mood'. This whole game, despite some flaws has a truly unique vibe that i haven't seen anywhere else. It feels lonely and depressing like some other games but most of all it feels alien. From the environments & soundtrack to the writing and story, everything feels strangely ouf of place. But somehow it works, it feels like that's just how things are in this universe. Not everything should adhere to our habbits & standards, and that's what makes it so cool. The game sucks you into it's world, which despite being alien felt very immersive. This experience is unique and worth a playthrough because of it, but there's also some game to be had. There's a ton of strong points but also some negatives which i hope to sum up here.Okay so since the game is a metroidvania level design and movement are the two most important aspects (imo), here ghost song is adequete. With a big interconnected map featuring tons of shortcuts & side routes to explore, many of which you'll have to backtrack through as you search where to go next. This is because this is one of those metroidvania's that doesn't hold your hand and isn't afraid to let you get lost from time to time. This fits in with the theme of being stranded on an alien moon however because the fast travel points are poorly distributed some areas will start feeling like a chore to thrudge through after a while. Add to this the fact that the 5 objects you have to gather in the far corners of the map don't allow you to fast travel until disposed at the central hub and you've got a very backtracking heavy experience. This wouldn't be much of an issue if your movement wasn't so slow/restricted, especially at the start. There's also too many long connecting corridors with nothing to do except for walking to warrant such a slow walking speed. The platforming is also a bit iffy at times due to a lack of ledge grapling, which is kind of a standard in metroidvania. All in all level design and platforming is mostly solid but it has it's pain points, many of which could be alleviated with more fast traveling points.There's also some combat to be had but i found this to be pretty mediocre. There's some weapon and build variety with stats and charms but this is poorly balanced because ranged is vastly superior to melee combat. You can also safespot/cheese many enemies with your range advantage. Combat isn't really satisfying because the balance isn't quite there, with many enemies simply having too much health rather than being challenging. This also applies to boss fights which were pretty dissapointing in my opinion. There's some enemy variety but not enough to spice up the combat. Luckily combat isn't a focus in this game as most of the time you'll be exploring/wandering which can be very relaxing thanks to the brilliant soundtrack & visuals.The soundtrack is an absolute masterpiece featuring moody synth that gives it a floaty feel, spacey distorted guitar strokes found in indie rock and some chilling piano to add some emotion to it. The soundtrack feels warm but lonely and fits this game like a glove. It's one of those OST's you'll listen to long after you've beaten the game, and worth a nomination for game awards as far as i'm concerned. The soundtrack complements the gorgeous visuals as well, which are hand drawn. And while yes, there's a lot of repition in the environments (goop everywhere!) it's an alien planet after all, filled with massive ecosystems where (THE GOOP) thrives, hence why there's so much of it. Despite this there's still many landmarks to orient yourself which are often also worth a screenshot. The visuals and audio work in tandem to set the aforementioned mood.I want to give some story thoughts as well but to be honest it's pretty vague and mysterious, so i didn't get all too much of it until the end. I think being left in the dark is part of the experience and intrigue so it's best left for you to discover. This you can do by talking to all the characters you meet, which will give you a grasp of what's happened. I have to mention that this happens through a mix of text and voice acting which is a very odd design choice (or perhaps budget restriction?). Characters can go from text to voice in the middle of the conversation which feels very strange. I'd have prefered voice only as the voice acting is pretty great. The writing is STRANGE but like i mentioned this helps give the game that alien feel.Lastly performance was great and i did not encounter any bugs so it's safe to say that this is a well made and finished product, which isn't a given these days. In the end the game won't be for everyone but if you love unique atmosphere and figuring out things on your own whilst wandering a vast and gorgeous 2d world then this is for you. Game gets an easy thumbs up from me, as it's a well made and unique experience that's worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice game, not without it's smaller shortcomings but none of them were big enough to make the game unenjoyable. The thing that probably blows my mind is that it was made mostly by a single guy, because I feel like I'm judging it by quite high standards for a single-dev game. If i had to say my biggest gripe would be the writing, especially regarding to the worldbuilding. There's amazing, unique areas, but not enough is said about them, which, considering their short-ness, can make them feel shallow, sometimes. This isn't a big deal, but it sucked a little bit. On the other hand, the atmosphere is nothing short of incredible, the variety of areas reminding me of the first time i played hollow knight, and ALMOST makes up for the shallower world storytelling.As far as the writing went, even though I said I didn't like the worldbuilding, the place where the writing shined the most was the character designs. All of the npcs had great dialogue and I thoroughly enjoyed coming back to them to get new dialogue.All in all, the game does something right which I seek in all metroidvanias, but that I struggle to describe well. Joy of exploration? Curiosity? Telling a story? It's a feeling that arises from multiple combined factors: story, atmosphere and everything. It's hard to describe, but it does it well, and that's probably the biggest reason why I have to recommend the game and compliment the dev for accomplishing something that many games don't.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game after 10 hrs and I absolutely loved it. I wasn't really expecting anything in particular as I haven't followed the development and just happened to see that it was releasing on Steam. I enjoy metroidvanias, but don't actually play them too often. Ghost Song was so surprisingly engaging for me so I'll try to list the reasons:1. The environments/art style was gorgeous - everything in the game looked so good. The foreground always was nice and detailed, but the backgrounds often had many different layers that really gave incredible depth to the game. I really enjoyed just traversing through the game because it was so pleasant to look at.2. Very Unique Melancholy vibe with the perfect soundtrack - I really enjoyed how mysterious and lonely and melancholy the game felt. It didn't seem as much dark and dreary, but more somber and reflective. I thought the soundtrack throughout the whole game fit so well with the journey. I would love coming back to areas just to hear that familiar song start playing. 3. Great sound design - all the sounds used throughout the game from running to weapons to ambient noises were top notch. There were so many great little details like your blaster over heating or the little mechanical whirring with leg movements. The ambient sounds were very well done and made the areas so much more immersive.4. Compelling plot - I don't want to spoil anything for people who haven't played yet so I won't use any details, but I really enjoyed the mystery and the plot of the story. I feel like I often find myself playing through games based on the tasks I need to do and the story is just something to justify the tasks. As much as I enjoyed the game play of Ghost Song I found myself motivated to progress to find out more about story and lore of the game which isn't often the case for me. The game has a lot of optional dialogue and I always wanted to read through all of it.5 Solid game play/mechanics - I thought Ghost Song felt very fluid and fun to play. It's fairly challenging as you can't pick up any kind of health from enemies, but the enemies in general aren't too fast and aggressive so if don't rush into combat you'll probably be alright. I only died to normal mobs a handful of times when I'd get stuck in a room with more enemies than I thought and get overrun. i-frames after taking damage don't last too long and you can end up taking a lot of damage quickly if you're in a cluster of enemies. Overall I really enjoyed the movement and combat.     I think Ghost Song is a work of art as much as it is a game. The art and music and mystery were something special that I'm glad I got to experience. Thank you to all who worked to make this game, I thoroughly enjoyed it and know I'll continue to come back to it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a weird metroidvania. If super metroid is an action game first and exploration game 2nd then this is primarily exploration and secondarily action game. There is higher emphasis on sights, environment and background art than tight controls and maneuverability.. which certainly has its own perks but also its cons aswell. First things first. Areas look great and distinct. Enemies have sufficient variance. Areas live up to their themes and game just oozes the exploration vibe. Those are certainly this games strong points...But on the other hand while areas you explore are certainly very cool, pretty even, this comes at a cost where your character feels powerless and controls feel unnecessarily clumsy, inaccurate and unresponsive in combat. To put negatives politely, horizontal movement feels sluggish even after you obtain ability to run faster, add-ons you use to improve yourself lack oompf, most of the new weapons and upgrades are quite disappointing and leveling is a bit.. underwhelming. There are good tools but you have to find them.. and then you have to find and stack enough upgrades make those tools feel at least passably decent. This creates perpetual feeling that you aren't especially powerful and even the weakest enemies which felt annoying or spongy at start will still feel equally annoying towards the end. This certainly makes the game feel more of an exploration game where everything is at least a minor threat instead of this being a god run where you instantly laywaste everything at your path.Its okayish metroidvania and does deserve a recommend. It doesn't quite live up to its potential on the combat side though.Story on the other hand is.. remarkably weird. I don't say yay or nay to it but if there was a message in this game then it was utterly lost to me. Too many characters have cryptic mumbo jumbo in their lines and while the overarching weirdness is strangely interesting at times, it doesn't make any effort in decrypting itself to you. This game left me with somewhat of a hollow taste since there is no way to track things which you have found out, no aid to piece and parse interconnected things together and often too little information to deduce anything. Its like a slideshow of interesting pictures which tell you a story but in the end it makes it too vague to feel satisfied in the end. I am confident I missed several hints and clues but even Elden Ring devs had more mercy with the story than this.. and that game had me doing weird poses in front of statues for christs sake.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is an interesting combination of "what was the dev thinking?" and "wow, the dev really thought this out!".The combat is a lot of fun.  Your primary weapon will overheat, and both your rate of fire and your damage per shot will drop.  However, this powers up your melee attack.  So in addition to having to observe the bosses carefully for openings, you also have to balance which attack method you'll be using.  There are also a great deal of sub weapons that you can use, as well as Hollow-Knight-esque charms that alter stats (some will let your main gun build heat quicker, some more slowly, for example).  So you can tailor your loadout to your preferred playstyle and experiment to see what works best for any given enemy or boss.The ability gates are well used, and the map is interactive enough to let you mark where you couldn't progress so that you can double back once you have new abilities.  The game is also pretty obvious about where those ability gates are.  None of the Metroidian bombing randomly and hoping you magically unlock something to get you out of a room you seem trapped in.The story is, in my opinion, rather beautiful.  So as not to spoil anything, I won't touch on my thoughts on the story as a whole, but I will comment on how the story is told."What is the deadsuit?  How did it get here?  Why did it activate now?" All these questions are answered in the game.  Rest assured.  However, it took me several playthroughs to find these answers and I don't think it should have.You have to hunt for the story.  And not in a fun way.  Functionally, if you'd like to experience the full story behind the game, you will either need to use a map that details where and when you need to meet up with certain characters (a good one would be , or you will need to re-explore the map after every single quest item is delivered in order to run into the characters who will advance the story.  Some of this I understand, as a good metroidvania game will have multiple paths to any given objective it isn't really possible for the dev to know what path a player will take to the next objective, or even what the next objective will be.  However, the game already uses map icons to lead you to the main quest items.  It seems odd to not have map icons leading you to story beats.  A character in the main hub could ask you to meet them in a certain area, or tell you that they'll be in a certain area so that you can look for them actively, instead of having to be lucky enough to stumble across them in some out of the way area.  Or even your passive sensors (or something to that effect) could pick up a strange reading.  Or, heck, you could even hear something echo down a corridor and go look for what that sound was.There are some quibbles about the speed with which it takes you to traverse the map, but once you have a few movement upgrades under your belt that largely goes quickly enough.  Also, the fast travel seems unnecessarily sparse, and the need to walk every main quest item back to the main hub is kind of odd.  But by and large, those are relatively minor gripes.Keep in mind, the dev (from what they've posted on reddit) was initially programming the game around a different engine, which had to be scrapped and started over from scratch.  So that the game was completed, and is genuinely this fun to play is a miracle in my opinion. If you like the MV genre, this game is worth a go.  It has Hollow Knight's fingerprints all over it, but not in a bad way.  I would recommend using a map like the one I linked above if you're more of a story-driven gamer, and if you're heavy into exploration, then be ready to explore the map a *lot* if you want to catch the story while you're at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is an alright game that's fun to play, and at times is gorgeous to look at. It could've been great, but (ironically) never finds its own unique identity.There's a major elephant in the room that has to be discussed: Hollow Knight. Ghost Song isn't just inspired by HK, it directly lifts many features from it. The design of HK seeps into every crack of Ghost Song: the charm slots, the unlockable movement tech, the npc 'quests', the healing system, the Soulsian 'lose all your money when you die' system, etc etc. HK lifted some of it from Dark Souls, and I'd argue not all of it worked for HK, but unfortunately Ghost Song never evolves past HK or puts a unique spin on the design. In a world where HK didn't exist, Ghost Song might've been a bit more exciting, but it's hard not to feel like Ghost Song is a somewhat shallow clone of Hollow Knight with Samus' arm cannon instead of a sword.At its core, Ghost Song is a game about exploration. I'd imagine anyone reading this already knows the formula, but for those that don't: you explore a series of caves looking for new movement tech, which lets you explore new caves to get new movement tech, etc. New movement ends up being the usual fare: a dash option, and better jumpy jump. That's it! Nothing wrong with that, and each upgrade is genuinely fun to use. However, this style of progression has always felt arbitrary to me; the new movement tech makes the game significantly more fun. Why is it held back? Extra jumps and dashes make navigating whilst maintaining momentum feel great. These being gated for so long mean the player's getting to play a worse version of the game until they unlock them. I don't think Ghost Song's world has enough going on to force this Metroid-esque gating. It only takes a couple of upgrades to fully explore the whole map, and the order of exploration didn't have any narrative or mechanical connection. A game like Metroid Dread has a sprawling labyrinth, with movement and weapon upgrades opening up alternative and faster routes for progression. The ability to break through certain obstacles, survive environmental hazards, get new movement tech, etc all open up Dread's world. Ghost Song's just got a couple of high ledges, and a few doors which can only be broken by missiles. Once you get past those ledges and doors, you're not really required to use your new mobility to navigate.For the actual explorey stuff, there's nothing particularly new going on here, though most of the zones are a visual delight to behold. At times Ghost Song feels like it was designed by a team of artists, who forgot to add gameplay or narrative purposes to the world. I don't expect every room to have greater meaning, but so much of this world is unexplained. Why are there giant disembodied heads sitting in the background? Why do trees instantly grow through people that die? What's up with the random cicada hive? Too much of the world exists because it looks cool, but has no purpose beyond that. The store page says "Journey beneath the surface on an atmospheric 2D adventure of self-discovery, ancient mysteries, and cosmic terror. Explore winding caverns and acquire new abilities to unearth this alien world’s long-buried secrets." That sounds cool! I want to do that! Having finished the game (with all the narrative achievements), there's no secrets to unearth. Certainly no ancient mysteries, nor cosmic terror. There's a bizarre revelation about your main character, and a bizarre side plot going on off-planet, but these only occur in the literal final minutes of the game.There's not a huge variety of enemies within the game, but I think there's enough. The bulk of combat involves flying skeletal robot heads, gloopy glop blobs, zombie-like humanoids, and a weird bug infestation. There's a few mini-bosses sprinkled through the game, but these are almost all humanoids with guns, each with one or two unique attacks. Sometimes they punch instead of having guns. From memory, there's only 2 or 3 minibosses that aren't generic humanoids. If you've seen the Dark Souls 2 boss critique, it's the same story here. Individually these are all fine, but after a while they start to feel too similar. I can't think of a single boss that was more interesting than any boss in Hollow Knight, Metroid Dread, or even Super Metroid.A notable problem the game has is the resource economy. You get nano-gel (money) from uninspired methods: kill enemies, find clusters to break open, or find items that give you instant boosts when consumed. Money is used to level up, or to buy upgrades from shops. The balance of this currency unfortunately feels confused. There's achievements for collecting all the items in the game, but there's simply not enough currency available to purchase everything without excessive grinding. Levelling up has an exponentially increasing cost (100 for first level up, 2500ish for your 30th level up), and levelling up too much makes it near-impossible to afford upgrades. On top of this, the shops populate with new items as you advance the main story. Several new items get added to shops at a point where there's only one room, and only one mandatory fight left in the game. All of this means the player either saves up money hoping for new cool toys in the shop later, sticks to early game upgrades, or grinds enemies that drop a pathetically low amount of money. An example of this: one item in the shop increases your luck from 6 to 7, and costs 8000 to purchase. This has no noticeable affect on gameplay, and saving up to buy it means you'll probably miss out on 4 weapon modules. I really don't know why stuff like this exists, and I'd argue the game would have been better cutting the shops entirely. It's mind-bogglingly frustrating too, because there's an in-universe conversation about the currency being useless to the shops. It doesn't do anything, and the shops have no need of the items they sell. One of the shopkeepers even offers to let you take his entire stock for free, and the main character bizarrely says no simply because the shopkeeper enjoys bartering. Moments like this are infuriating.As for the plot and characters in this game: there's not much to say. The story exists entirely within 2-3 1 minute conversations near the end of the game, and none of the characters have any development. Whilst not terribly interesting, this is a flaw of the entire genre at the moment. I don't think Ghost Song is any worse than the competition in this regard, though it would've been nice for the player character to be more involved with the plot than they actually are. The actual story/reason people are on the planet feels like a season 2 retcon added in post-production, and the game might've been a bit more coherent if it was just entirely cut. This is not a game to play for the story.Overall, there's fun to be had. Movement feels great, art is nice, shooty bang bangs is competent enough. There's unfortunately just better games trying to do the same thing. I don't think I'll ever proactively suggest someone play Ghost Song, but if you asked me to play it? Sure, give it a go. Maybe wait for a balance patch or a sale. Definitely play Hollow Knight and Metroid Dread first.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It tries too many things, and ends up feeling spread too thin. Combine that with some horrible design decisions it ends up feeling like a chore.I pre-ordered this game in 2015. Was it worth the 7 years? NoIt has the makings of a good Metroidvania, but for every good idea it attempts, it fumbles that idea, if in a minor way.1) It has a charm system like Hollow Knight. Most of the charms are either mildly useful, or completely worthless.2) It has areas locked behind obstacles that require upgrades to get passed. These are few and far between, and are often short hallways with a small consumable at the end.3) there is a lot of weapon variety. Most of the blaster weapons feel the same, some of the melee weapons are an active hindrance (the heavy punch is so slow, with such a small hitbox that you are better off just using something else).4) There is a level up system, similar to Dark Souls. Even after leveling up considerably there seems to be very little actual effect. Even the common enemies hit hard, and have a ton of health. I believe the intent here was to encourage the player to shoot an enemy, then using your buffed melee to gain the kill. Most of the time this actually translates to shooting, and then walking away, repeat, repeat, repeat.5) It has voiced dialogue. But only sometimes? Most NPCs will have a fully voiced first line of dialogue, and then it is text only for the rest of the conversation. Unless you get to a point where there is a randomly voiced line three text boxes in... only to go right back to text only. At best it is strange, and at worst very jarring, which ruins the pacing of the conversation.As I was exploring the map I discovered a tight jump that would get me to a secret area. It required a sprint and a double jump, and if timed correctly was no problem. I still missed it a few times while learning the controls. In order to attempt this jump again I thought I could just jump back up and try again, but no. In order to attempt again I had to go the long way around, to the far side of the map, looping back to just above where I started. Or, I could quit to the main menu and restart, landing me at the last bonfire I sat at, which was considerably closer.If quitting the game is more convenient than playing the game, this is a problem, and ended up being my breaking point.

_childDocuments_.review: There's good ideas in here, but it kind of lacks in execution. Gameplay:All the good stuff from metroidvanias with a little bit of dark souls flare in there in terms of difficulty and progression.  But There's too many systems that work against you, they alleviate a bit as you progress and get stronger but having to manage, stamina heat, and energy felt like a chore,  Where some times during fights all you could do was run around and wait for it to recover.  Some of the animations are long and feel clunky so melee weapons are usually vastly inferior to ranged.  Also everything is way too expensive, and the game encourages grinding for some upgrades which feels antithetical to metroidvanias.Story: It has good ideas but it was all a little try hard for me in terms of being too deep, and especially the characters constant use of overly complicated metaphors got a little old at some point.   Felt like an indie folk band in game form.  Graphics: It was pretty, no complaintsOverall: It had promise but kinda failed to deliver by the end, wish it would have been a bit more put together in terms of pacing and story delivery.  Also the ending was a bit of a whimper compared to the rest of the game and left me kinda dissappointed.  It's not a bad, but I wouldn't go crazy over it either.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of charm in-bedded in the art, music, and presentation but that's where it stops. The gameplay is the most frustrating thing I've experienced in gaming in recent memory, and yes, I play Modern Warfare 2 (2022). Hollow Knight is one of my favorite games of all time and I've longed search for other metroidvanias to help fill the hole until  Silksong finds its way into our lives. Unfortunately, this isn't it. The gameplay is so frustrating. It feels like the game intentionally screws with you such as if you die in a boss room, your "essence" does not spawn outside of the room but inside - in the middle of the boss fight. The game encourages you to upgrade your character but you can't do it when you hit a difficult boss because you have to fight the boss to continue no matter how low level you are. There are times where you have to trek all the way back to an area without fast travel only to meet new enemies and you're given no health stims or any sort of help that you normally have and the enemies respawn so as you continue to die, theres a gameplay mechanic that dwindles your health every time you die unless you "repair" but you can't do it if you're treking and lose all of your progress when you die. I love new experiences but tacking stuff into the game to make it harder doesn't leave any sort of satisfaction.I recommend letting this game go by until either it fades into memory or the developer decides to fix some of the aggravating things about the game. I hope for the latter.

Kinda mysterious, with quest lines that you have no idea how to actually complete unless you get lucky, and good voice acting. I'm a sucker for that kind of stuff.I'm reviewing this well after I've played it, so you'll need to look to other reviews for specifics about combat and other aspects I've probably forgotten. _childDocuments_.review: This is undoubtedly my favorite game in the genre right now, possibly ever but I'll let the honeymoon period wear off.FYI- Steam is my second purchase of this game, I've already completed the game on Switch.  Doing my second playthrough here. I'm a lifelong Metroid and Castlevania fan and this game seems to scratch both itches at the same time.  It has the RPG elements of recent souls-like Metroidvanias/Castlevania, multiple melee and ranged weapons to find and try out, collectibles and secrets everywhere and the tone, atmosphere of Metroid.The soundtrack is INCREDIBLE, they absolutely nailed it here.  If you're a big music fan you will appreciate the melodic swelling, reverb and delay used to set the tone here.  Fans of artist like Explosions in the Sky will love how this team translated the isolation, discovery and confusion your character is experiencing into music.Complaints about combat seem to be from people wanting to play this as either a metroid game or a souls-like and not a combo of the two.  Your blaster is not meant to carry you, using the overheat mechanic in combination with your special blaster and melee weapon, most enemies will shred in seconds, there are no true bullet sponge enemies just people confused about how to approach these encounters. This took me a bit to get used to and there are some melee weapons that are just "better" overall but experimenting with them all was really enjoyable and I'd like to see some adjustments to make some melee weapons more practicable. This was a 10/10 game for me after a year of many disappointing Metroidvania games this one stands out as the best.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review than negative. This game has good sides and not so good. I may still update the review later.It's a scifi-style metroidvania with some philosophical discussion and human relations. First off, the graphics. For me the quality varies. Sometimes it feels atmospheric, even scary, and overall the quality is good. But often it's a bit too bright and cartoonish. A post-apocalyptic game like this would benefit from darker theme. I feel it's a bit lost opportunity. Some people complain the game is short, but I guess that's pretty common. Axiom Verge was also short. Still, there should be about 10 hours of gameplay. Not much replayability, although you can try creating a character with different stats. Every time you level up, you choose a stat to increase. It doesn't seem to make that much difference which one you choose. Also, some stats increase just by leveling up. Some players also compare this to Dark Souls. Yes, in the default difficulty level, you lose most of the experience points when you die, and also some suit quality, which will need to be repaired (nothing permanent). I played on explorer, to avoid that hassle. Apparently there is also some enemy scaling on default difficulty level.Good:+ Voice acting+ No crashesBad:- Art is too cartoony and colorful (personal opinion)- Overall a bit bland- Not much replay value

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna lie, I got frustrated with boss fights more than once, but overall I loved my time with the game. _childDocuments_.review: This was a genuinely good game. I loved the gameplay, atmosphere, music, and story. I have been waiting for maybe 5 years (came across rumors of it when looking to scratch a Metroid itch) on this game to come out and it did not disappoint. The game is basically Metroid Dread meets Dark Souls II in terms of gameplay and atmosphere, it is challenging but not so hard or punishing that your average player could pick it up and play it fine. I finished the game, 100%ing it in about 18 hours. There is also a NG+ to keep going and continuing where you left off (only minus some items needed for progression).My only criticisms:- The Beam weapons probably need their own point system for being able to use them, having skill points shared between skills and beam weapons makes it difficult to choose what to use, most will find the abilities more useful. I cleared the whole game using only the base beam, missiles, and a melee weapon. I suggest this because what makes games like this fun is the ability to use unique abilities and that includes beam weapons. I am sure they had some good utility and everything but I barely got to try them out. They let you switch out skills somewhat easily but I just never thought it worth my time. - I would have liked to see more I guess like major bosses. There are some sort of small bosses throughout the game and a pretty okay final boss, but seeing some actual bosses that force you to use the game mechanics to their max would have been nice (with an ability to get out of beating them). Most bosses in the game do give you something for your time, I just remember facing the boss blocking the first ship part and expecting to get some cool spear or charge attack and got really nothing. I think this game has something going for it, I hope to see a DLC for it maybe picking up where the game left off and I hope to see more games from the devs of this game!

_childDocuments_.review: a really beautiful game!!the gameplay is fun & satisfying, but nothing too special — if you've played a lot of metroidvanias, i think you'll find nothing new in the mechanics, but nothing really poorly done, either.where the game REALLY shines is in the story and writing! this game's dialogue is quite literary; it frequently made me stop for a few moments to think about an implied aspect of a character or of the world, or mull over a very evocative and well-constructed passage, in much the same way that a great book does! the characters are all thoroughly fascinating and well-realised, and hearing more from them serves as a strong motivator to progress the game and explore its corners looking for more dialogue. the voice acting is also quite good for a small indie game like this! it's not fully voice-acted, but the start and end of each conversation is. it's enough for you to get a feel for each character's voice, and read the remainder of their dialogue with that voice in mind!for the writing alone, this is a very positive recommendation from me!! add the phenomenal atmosphere and soundtrack on top of that, and this may well be one of my favourite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: there are metroidvanias out there that are simply just better than this one. don't play unless you're REALLY trying to scratch that itch.another metroidvania review, this time i didn't even bother trying to finish this one because it's just a miserable experience from the get go. cutting to the chase:what's good:- has both the metroid and castlevania elements i guess- cool artstyle, but...no seriously, can't even think of anything else positive to say. why's it bad:- cool artstyle, but it's used in some really unappealing looking designs. imagine an artist with a great style but they were told to draw 'ugly'. hard to explain, it's pretty but not.- music MIA? am i supposed to vibe to just white noise? by the time some resemblance of music kicks in i've already resorted to just pulling up spotify.- on the topic of music, some of the sfx designs in this game are just so disgusting sounding. i get designing 'yucky' sfxs but these are just irredeemably bad.- sound mixing is all over the place, it's that meme where you have to turn up dialogues but turn down the sfx during movies. especially dolly. please fix dolly's voices and sfxs.- doesn't actually respect your settings. i turned down all volumes ingame thinking that could buy me some peace, only to have my delusions broken by hearing more of that bubbling sfx in the next area, why? luckily volume mixer was there to save the day.- minor gripe, but this game unironically could've benefitted from being voiceless if they are just gonna be implemented lazily like this. the mc makes zero noises other than when she talks, no grunts no nothing. didn't think this was going to bother me, but it sure does for me in this game.- exploration is a meme whenever you either dash too far, or too little for some platforms, causing you to have to do a 'hol up' manuveur. wouldn't normally be a problem (other metroidvanias have this too, i know) but it's glaring when you do it ALL game.- somehow, they managed to make each biome look the same, just with different colors. i understand that logically i could just check the map to know where i am, but would be nice to visually tell where i am in terms of biomes.- the metroid-like armgun idea is cool but turns out to be the downfall of this game for me. it got frustrating very quick to try to aim with my controller. they won't even let me fully commit to full shooty because my armgun would heat up and shoot slower, which is the cue to go melee except... melee sucks? even with weapons they just feel like a waste of gcd. them forcing me to switch it up between ranged and melee actually makes the game way more clunky than it has any rights to be. also they punish you going full ranged by making you do diminished damage outside a certain range in order to 'encourage' you to melee... yeah it sucks.- i am assuming all named enemies are bosses (even though some of them are more like elites, while others real 'bosses'). these are all just sponge fights with no real mechanics. - there are two types of bonfires, the ones with a robot statue, and the random flowers you find on the road. however, when you walk over the random flowers you have to WAIT for them to bloom before you can interact with them. you'd be zooming through an area just to not notice one because they take their sweet time to bloom. not to mention the fact that the resting animation is just too slow.i am not sure what even is this game trying to be? it's just a crockpot of games i know and love and it does NONE of them justice. so like... what exactly is the vision here? it's that meme of "all indie games are HK copycat metroidvanias" except it's 100% true for this game. hard avoid. you'd probably have a better time playing hollow knight with the gun mod.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is OK 👍[RELEASE DAY REVIEW]As you can see, the game was released today and I already have ~4 hours non stop! The game is amazing. But I usually start with cons before pros, so here it goes:[CONS]- Movement can be a bit clunky sometimes.- Extremely slow start (But gets very rewarding once you get upgrades and new weapons)- You can be damaged on enemy contact. I hate this mechanic so much.- No balance between weapons and you'll find yourself using just a couple of them.- Some animations are rather slow. (e.g. Accessing inventory system to change a weapon or upgrade, you have to shut-down your suit, change whatever you want to change, then turn on your suit, this gets a bit tedious half way through the game)- Not much enemy variety. (But they are weirdly interesting)- The game fails to tell you what to exactly do, which results in you endlessly roaming some rooms to find some characters or objectives.- Lack of hints.- The game has some poor design choices where you can SKIP some missions/secrets and cannot redo them at all unless you replay the game. (In the process, you cannot get some achievements)- The game has some rather bad achievement designs. (Finish the game in under XXX hours)- You can dash & sprint but they cost Stamina, but sprinting feels useless compared to dashing.[PROS]- Fairly big map.- A good accessible inventory system. (same for the map/items/consumables etc...)- Auto-loot; Loot will fly to you automatically, and you can get items that make it even faster to reach you.- Interesting story line.- Game isn't stale: Find hidden places, get more weapons, get suit upgrades etc...- Well done voice-lines. You and the people you meet have voice-lines and not some gibberish like other games usually have.- Attacks, dash, wall-leaping & jumps feel very fluid! Extremely satisfying to navigate through the game.- Game has a very captivating art-style (Effects, colors, sounds, music, enemies, biomes)- Challenging (Game is really not easy at the beginning but you start catching up with upgrades!)So far I haven't had any crash, bug etc... and it has been a great smooth experience! I'm already LVL 20 in-game and will keep playing till I finish it! What a fantastic Day-1 release.I recommend this game as it has a very enjoyable experience! (Also controller support is perfect)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun is smallish metroidvania. The real draw is the atmosphere. There is also the mystery, both about yourself and the world you are in. The world and the culture feel alien, it was a puzzle to understand what was going on, and what had gone on. And it was also fun to run into a character and talk with them to learn more as I wandered to caves of this world. I had fun piecing it all together.The downside is the level design. The map is not fun to navigate once you have mapped it out and travel points are sparse. The grind to get cash is also not fun either. The game could have used a fair bit more polish in these areas.That said, the game-play is tight and quite enjoyable. The variety in weapons and little tools were great to experiment with. And the boss fights were changeling and varied, but I never felt like I could not beet them if I didn't do just a little better next time. The music is good at conveying the feel of the world along with the art design. But, you may want to turn the volume down a notch for specific enemy cries.Even if it is a bit of a rough game in some places, it is very charming and overall a good time. If you are a fan of metroidvanias and artistic melancholic moodiness. I recommend this game. If you're unsure, get it on a sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: While I wouldn't say I'm the biggest fan of of this genre of game I have played many like it and this one is by far one of the weakest. For one the level design doesn't flow very well leading to confusion in places where that shouldn't be the case. The check point and fast travel systems are a mess with you needing to go through so many hoops just to get back to where you need to be. Not only that but you cant even fats travel when you are carrying the ships parts making the game feel like its padding out its run time. The bosses aren't much better with most of them being bullet sponges with dull move sets. This last part is just my own nit pick but the game has me locked in what is basically and endless death loop with no way for me to get out of it and this is when I lost all interest in finishing this game, don't buy this there are way better options out there for you.
