_childDocuments_.review: Serviceable. That's the operative word here.It's a metroid. You've got a lot of laser modifications and suit upgrades to choose from with a Hollow Knight-esque charm point system limit. The limit's raised by your suit level. It's a sound system. Only, the systems that these 'badges' support (combat and movement, the only two systems that matter in a metroidvania) are lackluster. The gameplay loop here is not strong on the fun factor. There are other metroid games with much more compelling movement and combat than this one for cheaper prices.If the gameplay isn't too much fun, you'd hope the other parts are. The developer inserts good prose into the NPC dialogue, but the story doesn't compel. Music is either absent (leaving only discordant festering bug noises to hear as you traverse screens) or somber acoustic guitar (kinda boring). No qualms with the graphical style, but the main issue is that there isn't a lot of variety visually - the same colors, familiar aesthetics everywhere. The appeal here is that it's a serviceable metroid and we don't get those too often. But look, there are way better ones to play than this. _childDocuments_.review: I don't really have many positive things to say about this game, and sadly, despite having donated to the Kickstarter, I don't think I even care enough to finish it at this point. Fair to admit that this review is based on me playing as much as I think I ever will, but certainly not all of it.It won't take a new player long to realise the intent of this game is basically Dark Souls meets Hollow Knight, and frankly, it's pretty shameless in stealing from the former series. You lose your in game currency when you die, but it can be retrieved by visiting the same spot when you respawn. Being killed depletes your maximum health until you "repair". There are weird characters with pretentious dialogue sat around being philosophical. The problem is not only that it's really unoriginal, but it invites comparison, and this game just doesn't execute anything as well as the games it's stealing from.The first thing which compares badly for me is the interactions with other characters. The dialogue is OK at best, but the voice acting isn't great. Dark Souls went to great lengths to hire talented voice actors who's performances gave significant weight and credibility to their generally quite hokey dialogue, but here it sounds like it was performed by the developer's friends and family. This is a problem, because frankly they don't have the chops to sell their lines, and consequently it makes both the script and the performances fall flat.The presentation isn't really to my liking either. I'm not a big fan of the "hand drawn" look at the best of times, but here everything just feels so samey. Enemies mostly look the same, even bosses. Most of the areas are pretty much just big piles of egg shaped things in different colours. Most of the female characters' profile pic artwork looks like the same person. This is definitely a matter of taste, of course, but even accounting for that, there are real issues. Dark Souls expertly blends the exquisite and the horrific to create a world that is both beautiful and ugly at the same time. Everything here is just ugly, horrible, unsettling... it's not a nice or particularly interesting place to explore.That's an issue for another reason, as there is a huge amount of backtracking through rooms and hallways that are either irritating to navigate or depressingly boring. Never before have I felt so often that a game was wasting my time. The slow run speed just makes everything feel like a chore, and the tiny platforms (and the fact that your character seems to happily be standing still on an edge one second, only to slip over it the next) make most of the vertical traversal feel tedious too.The combat is for the most part the saving grace of the game, and is fairly well executed and satisfying, until it gets into a really difficult fight, then it kind of falls apart. Most of the weapons are pretty much useless though so I found myself using the same stuff for most of what I played. Finding new weapons was usually exciting until I tried them and immediately unequipped them. Enemies and bosses are quite punishing in the Dark Souls tradition, but some are just poorly balanced. The big yellow thing was just offensive really and really exposed the drawbacks to the dash in particular.I wish I had more positive things to say about this game, but it feels like despite the horribly unoriginal game features, the developer tried to be really ambitious, but didn't have the skills or experience to deliver on their vision. I'd be willing to give them another chance, but next time, perhaps getting a few things really right would be better than getting everything wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: IMO, Best Metroidvania since Hollow Knight itself. Great controls, incredible atmosphere and exploration. Didn't even have my eye on this one! An absolute buy if you love Metroidvanias, and a probable buy for most everyone else. Enemy design is excellent (graphics and art are super-cool all around)- 'lil bit of Lovecraft to some of them, and unique ways of being dangerous that you'll learn to handle with your various tools and weapons. The combination of melee weapons and blaster/firearm attachments is inspired, and very fun. You can try to play it safe and shoot from afar with the accurate Cloudburst Rifle, or get up close with blasters, rockets, and spears, taking advantage of the melee damage bonus granted by heating up your firearms.The RPG mechanics are very strong too- suit and weapon modules governed by power (along the lines of your pins from HK), and ever-increasing levels of customization open up as you continue to level your three main governing attributes according to your style. Definitely interesting.Great difficulty level too. It's punishing if you aren't careful, but you can always come back with better weapons and leveled up. Haven't had any seriously frustrating deaths, but it's enough that you do need to watch yourself. Standard souls 'lose your exp where you die with it, go fetch' death penalty system.The voice acting and sound also deserve a shout-out- like HK, a lot of the story is understated, but the characters you'll meet are quite compelling, even to me, and that is not why I buy games.Haven't encountered any bugs. Platforming can be a little tricky, but it isn't because of poor controls. You'll learn it! Also, tricky platforming has not been frequent, at least so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Over eight years ago, I backed the Kickstarter for this game, and I can say I'm happy with the final product.  This is a solid Metroidvania with gorgeous artwork, a haunting story, and fun combat -- but it does have a few issues, largely due to taking a little  much influence from Dark Souls.One particular thing that makes this stand out from the crowd is that your character, the Deadsuit, is not silent or an emotionless protagonist.  She talks, has a personality, and has interesting interactions with other characters.  There's a surprising amount of dialogue, and there are a lot of good character interactions between bits of lore that you'll have to piece together to figure out the full story.One of the most interesting aspects of gameplay is the balance between ranged and melee attacks; shooting your gun causes it to eventually overheat, which decreases its damage and firing rate, but your gun being hot causes your melee attacks to deal more damage until it's cooled down.  This leads to an interesting balance of firing several shots, then closing in to take a few swings before backing away again.  There are also a wide variety of equippable modules that change your gun and melee capabilities so you can focus on one or the other, but it's always important to have a degree of balance between them.And it's a good thing combat is fun, because otherwise the game might be a little too frustrating to deal with.  It's fashionable to call any game that is difficult and has a dodge ability a "Soulslike," but this game draws much more inspiration from the Souls games than most.  Death is quite punishing; you lose all of your nanogel (a resource used to level up and buy equipment)  your maximum HP is reduced.  To restore your HP, you have to make your way to a fast travel point -- of which there are relatively few in the game, and many save points are nowhere close to one -- and recover a bit of money to pay for it.  Save points also tend to be far from boss rooms, so simply retrying a fight where you died can require retreading a fair amount of terrain.  After you've acquired a good number of modules and figured out some good combinations, the game's not too hard, but this can be fairly frustrating early in the game if it takes you several attempts to beat a boss.  There are a handful of other typical Soulslike annoyances, too, such as the game not pausing when you have the map open, which has lead to me taking unnecessary damage from offscreen enemies that I didn't realize were attacking me.Perhaps the worst thing about the game is a cardinal sin for Metroidvanias: missables.  There are a handful of side quests you have to progress by talking to NPCs repeatedly at the right points during the plot, and if you don't, you can permanently miss getting certain achievements and modules.  I don't want to call that , but one of the best aspects of Metroidvanias for me is the final end-game sweep when you go over the map again and collect 100% of everything, and it's possible you won't be able to do that here if you didn't talk to somebody at the right time.Despite my complaints, though, I had fun with it, and it's a remarkably polished effort for a game that came from a very small team who had no idea what they were getting into when they started.  I don't want to spoil anything, but it has a lot of cool, creepy moments that had me on the edge of my seat, and I'll admit I teared up just a bit at the end when I finally pieced together the whole story.  It's definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls crossed with Metroid. I liked it overall but it does a lot of little things that annoy me — characters have to be spoken to multiple times to complete their conversations, there are too few fast travel points, and not only is there a corpse run mechanic but you suffer max HP damage every time you die, encouraging death spirals. (I’ve said this before but to reiterate, corpse run mechanics are bad for exploration-focused games. You should be allowed to give up and explore somewhere else if you find yourself against a brick wall.) I also disliked that the protagonist was characterized as pacifistic yet you’re always railroaded into combat.I did like the heat mechanic, though. Your blaster overheats if you use it continuously, sharply inhibiting its damage and rate of fire; however, the heat makes your melee weapons much stronger, creating a synergistic gameplay style where you trade off between ranged and melee. It’s a nice way to mix up both Metroid and Dark Souls style combat by forcing you to vary your tactics instead of doing the same thing all the time.There is a surprisingly involved story, but it seems I missed some of it by not talking to characters at the right times, which was annoying. It generally feels like a teaser for a larger story rather than something self-contained, as it keeps bringing up worldbuilding details that are never explained or elaborated on. Like, is Saymund objectively right about ghosts and gornah, or is he crazy? I also found the ending very unsatisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of wasted potential. It's not BAD, though. It does everything right. There's just something missing.This is essentially a Metroidvania, but with quite a bit less emphasis on finding new tools and power-ups than those games usually are. The map feels more sparse than other games in this genre, but the environments are well made and detailed. Enemies and bosses are respectable and well designed, too, so the combat is refreshingly nice. Your character opens up enough options throughout the game to allow some basic character builds, as well (primarily Melee focus vs Gun focus). Music choice is good, the atmosphere is superb, and the sound design is basically perfect. New Game+, too!Meanwhile, traversal is...Well, traversal is awkward. Throughout the game, you will notice that you move much faster vertically than you do horizontally. The character's regular run is noticeably too slow, and if you find the sprint item, the sprint is ALSO too slow. There's also an animation-lock on the sprint, so certain actions that only happen while you're sprinting become unusable until you're "fully" sprinting. Strange movement like this isn't necessarily weird in, I'll go ahead and say it, the older 2D Metroid games, but this game manages to feel worse than those because it doesn't make up for the awkwardness with snappiness and responsiveness. It feels just as sluggish as it looks.Meanwhile, the story. Without spoiling anything, it has some legitimately interesting lore that freely steps in and out of the realm of spirituality. It's also obviously copying Dark Souls. Important details are hidden while lore pieces are hinted at piece by piece. The problem is that lore in general only enters the story a handful of times and usually without context (not-from-this-game example: "Hey, I heard you like oranges. Delicious and super juicy, right? So when god made the world, he set up a council of seven sisters who boil the blood of the ancients." "...I see.").The visible events of the game are very straightforward, which pushes you towards wanting to know the backstory. What you can see of the lore is written very well, yet it constantly comes up only as an aside, almost as if the writer didn't ever want it to be mentioned.TL;DROverall, this is an easy pick-up. On the gameplay side, movement doesn't feel very good, and the overall pace of the game is somewhat slow, but it does everything else right. It just feels like someone wrote a story much longer than this, and then someone else (HOPEFULLY it was someone *else*) came along with some scissors and went "nope" on 70% of the script.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is a beautifully atmospheric game. From the haunting music, to the vibrant and alien levels, and through to its fantastic story.I’ve just spent about 10 hours with this game and one of the most wonderful things about it that I can say is, it left me with a sense of mourning. I knew that the story was coming to an end, I knew I was going to learn the secrets of Little Blue and this dying moon of Lorian, and I mourned what would be its end. I feel that is an incredibly hard thing to do with a game, but the games themes itself of mourning loved ones, and learning to carry on, largely mirrored my own feelings for the game and its characters.Ghost Song, in short, is a wonderful game. I can easily recommend it to Metroidvania fans, especially those that enjoy a bit of souls-like mixed in, but I can also easily recommend it to those that enjoy a game that has such a huge amount of beauty and love put into its entirety.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, but I have some criticisms. The "Dark Souls" leveling system does not meaningfully contribute anything of value to the game, in fact that system in general is a pretty artificial reward system on its own anyway, but it's extra pointless here! The controls can be a bit funky at times, I also personally wish the stamina wouldn't affect running while traversing the world. Better yet, it would be nice if on top of no stamina use during exploration there was a toggle, it's annoying to have to hold a trigger to move the character at even a reasonable speed. While Ghostsong seems a bit more polished this far after release, there's hard to pin down roughness across the board. Like when the sound effects cut abruptly when entering/exiting a room but the music remains consistent. Also, I'm pretty tired of the lose your money upon death mechanic. Admittedly there is an argument to be made that losing the money encourages players to return to retrieve the money and forge onward, I'd already want to return if I was enjoying the game. So for me, instead of encouraging exploration, it's just an annoying little hassle, not the end of the world, just tiresome and uninteresting. Dying and being sent back to redo rightfully tough encounters is a good enough punishment on its own! All in all, despite my complaints, I ultimately pushed through for the finely crafted thought provoking world. Ghostsong is dreary and depressing, ancient alien landscapes wither away in the background, corpses litter the terrain, most fauna is threatening, the world is starved and dangerous. There remains wonder in these desecrated caverns, little pockets of light and life are hidden in the deepest corners. I couldn't help but push on, experiencing the terror and beauty with the eagerness of a child. It's engaging to hear characters lament the state of the world, how it used to be, one can only imagine the series of events that formed this world. There's this release of tension when you're out of danger and around safe npcs that's so wonderful, I always take the time to hear their stories and struggle to survive. I don't want to say much more, but Ghostsong is absolutely a world worth exploring. Anyway, GAMEPLAY, the emphasis on both ranged and melee is neat, the enemy designs are cool, the traditional upgrades are fun but the weapon upgrades are particularly fascinating... It's pretty fun, but I definitely was pulled in most by the arresting world.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:-The atmosphere of the game is interesting: an isolated moon , with alien creatures roaming around and a sense of mistery.-Similar  to metroid(although worse)-Your aim is not limited to 8 directions, you can lock your aim and aim at whatever angle you like.-The difficulty level is fair: it's not easy but you feel that if you lose it's because you made a mistake(I played on the original difficulty setting)-You can progress any way you like, you don't need to complete the quests in order.-Lots of dialogue options from the npcs.-The control is  tight: jumping, shooting and running feels satisfying.-Combat has some interesting ideas: your cannon can overheat and when it does your projectiles will be less powerful...but your melee weapons will get a  damage boost. Also, you can attack with long range weapons, basic shots and melee weapons , so you can try different combinations.-Customizable options for the character(Imagine a charm-like system)The bad:-The character portrait of the npcs(when you talk to them) is not too detailed.-The game uses several ways to artificially extend its length. For instance, once you get a certain item and you have to bring it to your home base, you can't fast travel.-There should be more fast travel points.-Some parts are unclear on how to progress, you may get stuck even if you have all the abilities you need.-The scenery can become repetitive(Yes , I get that it's an undergroud cavern system but it feels monotonous and bland after a while)-The story starts out very strong but you end up with more questions that answers by the time you reach the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game what feels like ten years ago now, by chance, and tucked it away in my memory to check on later.  When it released on steam and got only mostly positive reviews I looked into some of the development history and grew concerned that Ghost Song might actually not be what I'd hoped it would - what I felt like the art had the promise of representing.  I've played a lot of games and I'm not easy to please at this point, so it would be a sadly familiar story for a promising "indie" (or AAA) game to suffer a turbulent development and wind up releasing as less than I'd hoped.Fortunately, I think the result is quite respectable.  I think the most unique things the game has to offer are its sci-fi setting tinged with spiritualism, and the melancholy-yet-cozy soundtrack and atmosphere.  Metroids Zero Mission, Fusion, and Prime were some of my favorite childhood games, and even though Ghost Song has a fair amount of character interaction in it, still I feel the echo of Metroid's exploration-in-solitude.  I liked the character writing, too, and of course the art is gorgeous.  I also enjoyed how object retrieval increased the stakes of traversal and made me re-conceptualize my map routing - a fresh take, for me, on what it means to backtrack in a 'vania.Pros first.  The basics are all accounted for: surprisingly tight and streamlined metroidvania, not exactly complex but nor simple.  Combat and platforming feel somewhat slower-paced than some others of the modern era, but I still found them fast and complex enough to be satisfying, and minimal "bloat" exacerbating the inherent repetition and backtracking in metroidvanias.  The "normal" difficulty was hard enough for me to die a few times and need to learn some patterns to beat certain bosses, which feels like about the right tuning for me, and there's an easier difficulty for those who might otherwise get frustrated.  I appreciate that upgrade-hunting is not overly focused on randomly shooting walls, though there is a little bit of that.Cons, now.  Honestly, nothing felt particularly frustrating.  Some enemies, even a couple that look identical or near-identical to others, are jarringly more formidable than others nearby.  This doesn't happen often, but I did find it noteworthy and after a couple of such experiences I did find myself playing slower in new areas with familiar enemies.  Some interactions, items, and achievements are gated behind timing-specific interactions with little or no indication - which means if you want to see everything, you will have to guidefollow or blindly sweep the whole map multiple times.  I'm a thorough player and I don't mind some backtracking, so with some liberal use of map-pins I got to see *almost* everything in my first run with minimal guidefollowing (only at "last call"), but it still bothers me a bit that I played even a little more thoroughly than I thought was reasonable and still ended up missing some things because I didn't canvas thoroughly enough *at the right times*.  It's really not that big of a deal, but.. for Old Moon:  It was good - I had fun, I vibed, I was challenged by some of the combat, and I saw and thought about some things I hadn't before.  And it wasn't too long or too short for the story it was trying to tell.  Thanks, Old Moon, you did not disappoint - and I look forward to seeing your name again sometime, if you're still interested in making things after Ghost Song's development struggles.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is an interesting game. It's very much carried by the atmosphere of the world it's set in and the art style. I can recommend this to Metroidvania fans, but maybe not your average gamer. I'm taking a break from it right now because traversing the map can feel like a chore - sometimes you'll go between screens and there will be no enemies to engage with. Fast travel is few and far between. Bosses range from trivial to insane difficulty spike with no rhyme or reason. BUT - It's very, very intriguing. The world they've created is up there with Grime. My jaw has dropped several times at some of the set pieces. I just wish that extracting the narrative was more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite Metroidvanias. The melancholic atmosphere is top shelf, expertly capturing the moody isolation of OG Metroid but with some Dark Souls flavor. Enjoyed every minute I had with the game. Happy to see some new content dropped since I last played. Any reason to hop back into the Deadsuit :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I am still working on the game. But first playing it on my switch, the controls were really confusing and after some time of walking around I gave up. But I gave it another try on PC and I'm glad I did. I really love some of the areas and it's art style, really beautiful, really concerning... Sometimes even scary! Even on PC it took me some time to handle, and I die every once in a bit upon encountering bosses by total accident or just when I stumble into a new area and don't know what to expect. Fear of the Unknown is amazing in a game like this right?Play the game, recommend it to friends, if you already have it, keep playing, keep supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song just oozes with melancholic atmosphere and a sense of exploration. You are stranded on a moon infested by some sort of plant infestation without any memories. Your only purpose is to help a stranded crew that crashed due to a magnetic field which pulls every spaceship onto the surface. While the premise is not that intriguing at first, it develops into a greatly written tale of sacrifice and humanity that just gives you enough lore bits and clues to comprehend your place in it, while it can sometimes turn into a guessing game of where you can obtain that knowledge because some vital NPCs move places or turn up out of the blue in different spots on the map you already marked as explored, my sense of wonder still kept the better of me, and I'm sure it was purposely designed that way. It's not as grand or entangled as Hollow Knight or the modern FromSoftware games which obviously deeply influenced the game, but rather focused on a certain theme, and I found that rather refreshing.It plays like a typical modern metroidvania with more focus on ranged combat than melee. You have many different modules, some more helpful than others, and several weapons. My favorite was definitely the precise laser gun mixed with a satisfying magnum of sorts. The biggest gripe I have, though, were the boss fights, which were very unspectacular and rather easy. Most of them had three moves at most and a rather large health pool, which turned them into a test of patience rather than skill.The soundtrack, though, was something else; I absolutely loved it. It's practically a more simplistic "Tomorrow's Harvest" album from Boards of Canada with a more melancholic touch. The song that was playing in Stoffbloom will definitely live rent-free in my head for the next weeks. Also, it absolutely helped to alleviate the already lonely and post-apocalyptic atmosphere to the next level.If I were to make a list with games like Hollow Knight, this one would definitely be among the top three. It comes very close to some aspects of it, and I think with a few more fine-tuning in the gameplay and some more budget to alleviate some of its presentation, the next game of this studio can reach new heights.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game's story and world. Once you unlock mobility options its very fun to traverse and explore the map. The characters endearing and well written. Many of them I loved withing a handful of lines. I do have issues that really make the game unfun at times though. Replaying the game is a chore due to the shear mass of dialog you need to get through adding a lot of tedium to new game plus. Getting it in the game causes you character to slow down, leading to times when you will get effectively stuck in large enemies without being able to escape before you die. Add that on top of the punishment for dying being your maximum health is lowered. Add that on top of needing currency to fix your health leading to grinding nanogel forcing you to waste time going to and fro the big bots and then to whatever you were trying to do. ADD THAT to the robots being very sparse and some bosses being far away from one leading to you having to go from your save space to a robot to then grind nanogel to then go back your last save point to then go to the boss again and you get a recipe for utter agony. I really do recommend this game but of my goodness it could be so much better without the punishment for death and or more frequent robot locations. If you decide to pick it up I do think you'll enjoy a good 85% of the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun game but shorter than i expected. Theres also some problems at the end of the game where it doesnt tell you where to go so youll probably need to look that up. Its worth a playthrough though as its beautiful in some places and the weapon and module variety is fun. I found most everything but not all maybe 5 were missing but im not a completionist and just wanted to take a tour of the scenery in game and enjoy the story. It has interesting characters but a lot remains unexplained. Which is fine sometimes its better that way.  If youre looking for a new metroidvania and havent tried this one give it a shot youll more than likely enjoy it. I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania, very atmospheric, the sound design is top notch, the visuals are great, we really feel like we’re lost on an unknown planet.I really liked the dialogues with the npc, they all do small talk and it’s really melancholic, making it touching and well, believable.The upgrades are interesting, the challenge is nice, there are a lot of things to unlock and you can customize the weapon with the modules.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Top quality Metroid clone for PC, beautiful and atmospheric. The mechanical design is inspired by the 80s - 90s scifi anime which is much appreciated. Plays as expected, you have the freedom to explore and take on many of the bosses in any order. My usual complaint about metroidvanias is not having enough teleport points, it's ok to make the player run around at the beginning, but after hours of backtracking it would be nice to have more shortcuts. 90 fps on Steam Deck OLED.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game 5 stars. I beat it before the update and played it a second time to encounter new content. The music is melancholic, the voice acting is great, the art style is one of a kind, and the immersion is like a drug hit straight to the veins. If you want to play a game that captures the metroidvania nostalgia don't hesitate to buy this game. Don't even wait for it to go on sale. It's worth the $20 bucks. Just play this game and enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever played a game that established a melancholy atmosphere while driving the concept of positive nihilism quite like this. The story and characters are really compelling, and there's something really special here that is worth your time if the themes resonate with you. The gameplay is a little janky, but it's a perfectly serviceable Metroidvania and borrows familiar mechanics from other games of the genre.This is definitely not for everyone, though. You'll need to be patient as the story is drip-fed and many points are implied (Similar to a Souls title). Some game mechanics are not explicitly explained and left for you to discover through experimenting, and you'll find yourself wanting just a few more fast travel points than are available. The combat may be frustrating until you explore other places and find other upgrades or grind, but the game is non-linear so you would need to arrive on that conclusion on your own. I think you'll know within the first hour or two if this game vibes with you or not.Overall though, if you're a fan of Metroidvanias and the world captures you, the unpolished elements won't bother as much and you'll really enjoy what's being offered here as it's obvious a lot of heart and soul went into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that nobody's talking about this absolute gem is infuriating! It's got it all: excellent combat, incredible atmosphere, and don't get me started on the soundtrack. Been waiting 10 years for this game to come out and it definitely paid off. This, ladies and gentlemen, is Metroidvania done right!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dripping with atmosphere, and I find myself lost in its world every time I play it, enhanced tenfold by the fantastic soundtrack. The whole thing feels extremely grounded despite the setting reaching pretty far into sci-fi fantasy. I feel like what most people might have issues with is the general gameplay. Objectively I find it slow and methodical, with mistakes being punished severely sometimes by the player's limited movement. I believe this enhances the experience and immersion, but I definitely see how it could be a deal breaker to some.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is very much a mixed bag, representing some of the best traits of the modern Metroidvania genre, while also stepping firmly into some of its worst potholes. On the good end, its NPC dialogue is absolutely fantastic. These interactions are very Souls-like in their often meandering or indirect nature, as well as their progression (accompanied by NPC movement) to match your progress through the game. In addition to scattered hints as to what's "really" going on in the game's narrative, it's loaded with intriguing character writing and lovely sci-fi concepts that make me want to spend more time with these people, and learn more about the world beyond this strange planet on which we're all stranded.This character dialogue is delivered with the help of extensive and compelling voice work, which I give top marks. The music is also fantastic; familiar and enveloping but never intrusive. The in-game sound effects are more variable; there's a LOT of high-pitched shrieking or other grating noises, and I can't say I was ever really grabbed by a particular weapon or enemy sound effect.You'll spend most of the game engaged in combat and traversal, both of which are serviceable. Combat includes some really fun weapons, upgrades, and ideas - such as building up excess heat by firing ranged attacks, which heats and therefore boosts your melee weapon, encouraging you to switch out. It's mainly let down by how fragile the player is, how limp your attacks often feel, and how punishing death is, all of which discourage experimentation and taking risks; I picked the missile launcher as a generic secondary weapon and basically never looked back.The other anchor around the neck of the combat system are the modules. These are points-based upgrades which you swap in and out as you see fit. The problem is that boring but useful modules are in abundance, which crowds out more situational but interesting combos; your extremely limited points mean every module feels expensive, especially when basic game functions like "automatically pick up currency" or "see enemy health bars" are also gated behind modules that you ALSO have to pay for. Plus, actually swapping out modules involves a tedious shutting down process for no obvious reason.Traversal suffers from the occasional janky-feeling platforms and walls, but it's mainly let down by how slowly and non-deliberately you acquire movement upgrades that make it faster and more casual. I made it most of the way through the game without stumbling on the double-jump, for example, and could well have missed it entirely. The sprint is anaemic, the dash is very limited, and other tools like faster movement or triple jumps are gated behind more of the aforementioned pricey power modules.The game's visual design is also a little hit-and-miss. You'll find great visual moments - characters, boss animations, or "dioramas" that really pop against the background. The details in that background can also be really neat, but mostly only when the game is dealing with "real" looking fungal forests and alien mountainscapes, places that feel like they might actually exist, instead of bare industrial junk pits or pulsating goo nests. The individual areas in the game, however, lack much in the way of striking atmosphere or identity. I've barely finished it and I couldn't tell you much about any one particular zone, compared to the memorable lairs and regions of other Metroidvanias and Soulslikes.On the inarguably, almost cripplingly bad end of things sits Ghost Song's fast travel and corpse runs. There are a bare handful of fast travel points (which are also level up points and repair points) across the game. They are distinct from save/heal points, which don't let you fast travel or level. This makes getting anywhere very slow and tedious, especially when scouring the game world for NPCs to talk to. Shortcuts are relatively limited, movement is pretty slow, and the low number of fast travel points means they're not even placed anywhere consistently useful, since they need to be equidistant from many different areas. There is also no in-game "teleport to last save point" function, despite being able to effectively do so by just... quitting and reloading.It also makes the now-staple "corpse runs" particularly bad, because you're typically being returned to a spot far away from your corpse, with a long and slow journey back to it. Worse, each death inflicts a permanent reduction in max health, which you remove by paying currency at a level up point... except you lose all your currency when you die, so even if you revive near a level up point, you'll still need to go collect more currency or just proceed with your debuff. And once you HAVE recollected your lost currency, and beaten whatever killed you, you'll have to manually backtrack to one of a very few level up points in the entire game in order to actually spend your goods.I cannot possibly overstate how badly Ghost Song is served by its paucity of fast travel. It's a decision that exacerbates so many other sub-par qualities that would other be entirely ignorable. It's bad to the degree that if I wasn't deeply invested in sunk costs, it probably would have killed my playthrough, regardless of how much I was enjoying the atmosphere and tone.In summation, give Ghost Song a try if you love the genre, focus on story, and are extremely patient, but don't go in expecting a butter-smooth gameplay experience that's consistently enjoyable in itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game.The core gameplay loop is alright, though painfully derivative of Hollow Knight. Where this game fails is how it blunders literally every other possible aspect, demonstrating a total lack of respect for your time. Scarce fast travel and huge maps mean you're traveling at least eight nodes to get to anywhere of note, and the abominable Dark Souls mechanics shoehorned into the game ensure that you're going to feel that travel every time you die during a boss, and especially when you're fighting the boss that just killed you but with less health than when you lost the first time. NPCs will have unskippable voice lines, which aren't poorly voiced but are slow and unskippable, and you can't be sure if an NPC will have something useful for you or not if you talk to them. Getting a ship part involves disabling fast travel so you can hike your way back to the base camp, which does absolutely nothing for gameplay other than add a few more enemies on the way back.To add to all the tedium, about half your special weapon options are utter garbage. The shotgun in particular stands out - you need to buy it, and it has worse DPS than your regular shots at all ranges. There is not a single use case for it, but you had to buy it instead of literally anything more useful.If you've played Hollow Knight, you've already experienced all the good this game has to offer. If you haven't, go play Hollow Knight instead of spending money on this game. The gameplay here isn't worth the disrespect for your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I played this right after Lone Fungus. But I didn't get to complete Lone Fungus because it tries too hard to emulate Hollow Knight but changes it up in a bad way and is really only completable by players who have mastered complex control input combos to reach and unlock most of the map, instead of through the standard abilities.That's what I love about Ghost Song. It doesn't copy other games and does it's own thing. It is more open-ended, allowing you to explore several routes picking up new abilities and power-ups along the way. And there is dialog - spoken dialog as well as text, and the story, writing and performances are mostly very good. Even though I was generally happy with the slower pace, I found some dialog a bit long and uninteresting, not really adding much to the story.I usually don't like boss fights in games because they are too fast paced but I enjoyed the bosses here. Not to say they are easy - they're not. But they are somehow more interesting, well balanced and not too challenging. Most are well balanced. There is one that shows up in different nearby locations which seems to be determined by RNG, but it can be a pain to go back and forth between them and wait around a while to see if they show up. Another only appears if you're carrying certain items, but that's not made clear in the game at all. Luckily there is a great map linked in Guides to help.What did I not like? I was hoping mid way there would be a pick-up that would automate taking health boosters when low because you can only take one at a time and have to wait until the health bar has absorbed it before taking another, which is easy to miss in boss fights. It would be awesome (too easy?) if you could pop 2 or 3 of those things at a time. It would also have been good to get the option at some point to fast travel from anywhere.Overall, although it has some tedious travel and repetitive gameplay, Ghost Song has plenty of great things that makes it different to other games and mostly enjoyable to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game almost immediately became one of my favorites right from the beginning. Everything from the art, to the soundtrack and voice acting, to the overall atmosphere is captivating. The gameplay is challenging without being frustrating and can be made more difficult if you're up for the challenge. 10/10 can't recommend enough
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: wow, this game is really catching me off guard in a good way. My first impressions were I wouldn't like it, not generally a fan of aiming ranged weapons - more a fan of just going in melee, but then I came back to it and am really having fun. The amount of different items you find, the secrets, the Metroidvania qualities, the unique dialogue and atmosphere, all keeping me hooked. Yes - I would recommend this to any Metroidvania fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is crafted with time and passion by basically a one-man team. it's an atmospheric metroid-like game, so for all the fans of the genre out there, this one is definitely to try! it's not in the rank of a hollowknight alright, but I think I enjoyed this one more than the last metroid dread. Really chilling OST in the likes of a 'dungeons of the endless', the visuals are highly detailed and thorough, characters are quite interesting, the exploration is not that deep, but it's still refreshing to discover new zones, some of them are really beautiful. To sum up I'd say that this game reminds me of "Stray": it's not the sum of its elements that defined the experience you make of it, it's an overall feeling you get which makes it unique and memorable.-> tl;dr pretty fun game
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until all the content was out for this game and wow, I’m so glad I did. Ghost Song truly is a masterpiece. The art style, the story, the combat, the exploration, the secrets, everything was better than I thought it was going to be. I’m a huge metroidvania gamer and this easily has become a favorite of mine now. I highly recommend buying this game! I regret not purchasing it at full price because it definitely deserves it. Can’t wait for the developers new game that’s being worked on!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: A slow, melacholy, and more "methodical" take on the Metroid formula with a good amount of Souls-y influence and not too terribly much taken from the Castlevania side. Personally, that's exactly the mix I'm looking what I'm looking for:The combat felt a little limiting and stiff at first, but I came to really enjoy it over the course of my playtime. I can't say it'll be the same for everyone and some of the more limiting design decisions may rub some players the wrong way, but by the end I had enjoyed my time with the game thoroughly and am looking forward to whatever may come next.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost song is an amazing game, it is the closest to Metroid of any game that I have personally found on Steam; many games tend to favor the Castlevania side of 'Metroidvania' (not a bad thing, just not what I prefer).There is a lot of exploration but the world is fascinating, mysterious, and gorgeous. The NPCs add a lot to the game, which is something that I didn't quite expect. I really enjoyed running into different characters throughout the world and hearing their thoughts/stories.The combat is awesome, I love that the blaster heats up your equipment which increases your melee damage. There's so many different projectile types, modifiers, and melee weapons that it's likely you won't play the game the same as others. Enemies may seem tough at first but you level up pretty quickly and they go down much faster. There's a lot of bosses, many that are optional and they are pretty tough, I didn't lose too often to them though; if you have experience with other tough metroidvanias you'll be totally fine, if not, there's an easier mode which I'm sure makes it a breeze (didn't try it).The music is phenomenal, this is one of my favorite parts of the game. The soundtrack is free on YouTube as well so you can listen to it anytime.There is a New Game+ mode and I've cracked into it a little, but I saw a post from the dev saying there's a content update coming, so I'm going to wait for that before I start another playthrough. From what I've seen it does change things up a little bit, but not enough experience to comment on definitvely.I didn't want to write too much, but this is easily one of my top games on steam now. If you like Metroid then this game is for you. It's certainly a little creepier than Metroid, but I really like that about it. I'm glad the developer was able to create this and I look very forward to his/her future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad little Metriodvania.  Beautiful art work and soundtrack make for a very somber atmosphere throughout.  Controls are reasonably tight, and way laid out.  There's a bit of a mystery story that kind of keeps you guessing.  A bit on the short side (completed in 15 hrs), but I did miss some pickups, and some areas.  If you're hoping for another Super Metroid, or SOtN, this isn't quite that scale, but better than many games in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a bit clunky at places, Ghost Song is a really good metroidvania that is very heartfelt and had a bold ending that I found really moving. I immediately fell in love with the game because of the beauty of the environments, the great voice acting by the main character and her awkward walk cycle. Where it falls down a bit, is having too many npcs and having them talk way too much. I think if they had half the npcs and dialogue, they would have felt more significant. Nevertheless, I was sucked in despite myself to the main story which was beautiful. There's a strong sense of melancholy to the world and the game kind of expresses the feelings of grief and letting go.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost song is a solid enough metroidvania which plays like a cumbersome Metroid due to some soulslike touches.The atmosphere, environments, sound is good here.The metroidvania elements: abilities, collectibles, branching paths, map etc are all competant.  I would have liked something better to mark or help with finding secrets at the end of the game (Partly as a result, i chose not to pursue post-game map cleanup)Bosses are fine, nothing that stood out as memorable.  I was able to cheese a couple of them.Aiming to shoot is done by holding down the L trigger and firing with a button.  While you can get quite quick with this setup, it isn't as fast and smooth as using right analogue to aim and firing with a shoulder button.  Their choice does fit the games slower pacing, but i'd have preferred the latter.The game contains some soulslike elements, some are cumbersome, others were fine:Corpse runs (you drop your souls when you die like in dark souls.  This one wasn't an issue for me).There is a stamina bar, and this means your dash frequently goes on cooldown.  I just found this annoying when travelling across the map.Some items that you collect force you to go into the inventory screen to use them to acquire their benefit.  e.g. items that increase a stat by 1 or jars of souls like the boss souls from dark souls games.  This is redundant.  Why not just award that benefit when i run over the item?What else..  Breakable secret walls. There are a number of these that you can tell can be broken by the gaps on the map, however many of them can only be broken from one side, and there is no visual indicator of this, so although you know you're trying to break the right place and travelled all this way to go and do it, nope.  Not allowed.  That annoyed me somewhat.The game uses a weapon overheat system.  Once it gets hot from repeated firing, your melee attack does much more damage (and gun damage is reduced).  I don't love or hate this system.  It was fine.All in all this is a fine metroidvania that felt a tad cumbersome. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Game is glitchy and makes me wish I hadn't bought it. Controls are flaky and not always responsive, Changing directions and dashing takes time, and you cannot stop slow move animations to change course in the event of trouble. So using a slow melee move means the boss just whips up on you as your character finishes the heavy sword animation and being whipped up on slows your movements so it only gets worse. Some bosses just like to glitch out and not return (old singer).  Directions/Guidance aren't really given in the game so you're stuck indefinitely adventuring until you find the single power (double jump) up you need to traverse the other 50% of the map. The points (nanogel) needed to level up doesn't appear to get better the further you go in the game, it seems pretty static as the cost to level up just to increases. Normally you get harder enemies that give more EXP or something related to that and monsters scale with level difficulty or zone difficulty. This game's method doesn't seem to scale well.I can't say I recommend this game, which is a bummer. I really like the artwork and the concept, but the gameplay just doesn't feel polished. It feels klunky and half baked :(  If you bought this game and now feel pressured to finished. I'd recommend a walkthrough guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: If Hollow Knight is more like Dark Souls than Metroid, Ghost Song is the other end of that. Your main weapon is an arm cannon that is pretty rustic and overheats a lot, but can be used to bludgeon enemies pretty effectively. Blue, the robot you play as, is also more chatty than the usual mute protag, which helps her feel unique. You level up at these statues in order to improve your firepower, HP, or stamina, usually collecting permanent upgrades along the way if you notice any hidden walls or take on a challenging room.It's kinda easy to nag at the game for it's lack of originality, bcus most mechanics are ripped wholesale straight from Metroid, Souls, or Hollow Knight, without much to make it different. It also has the usual Metroidvania trappings where if you're not comfortable backtracking and searching every nook and cranny, it'll get boring fast. Despite that, I'd still recommend it to anyone that likes 2D Metroid games and / or Soulslike stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, with interesting lore, a lot of sentimental vibes, great moody soundtrack and a cast of surprisingly (for a metroidvania) nicely written characters, with whom you build deep relationships. Also, the graphics are stylish, very detailed and pretty. Has minor flaws, like the needless soulslike mechanics (which you can rid yourself of by choosing a special difficulty option (unfortunately only at the start of the game). Really deserves a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It really leans hard into the Metroid side of metroidvania (which is absolutely rad), but the world and story of Ghost Song is where this experience really shines. It's really hard for me to get into metroidvanias sometimes, but I have been completely entranced by the visuals, the world building and ahhhhh the music. Deadsuit is an extremely interesting character and despite not really having much to say, every time they do speak it made me really happy. This game shocked me with it's environmental storytelling and I won't spoil the way it kinda plays with your expectations on what kind of stuff a game like this can do.When Deadsuit talked to the big bot i cried.If you like the vibe of Metroid I honestly couldn't recommend this game more. It takes what I love about that series and makes it more intertwined with a narrative and it just keeps getting more interesting as I go further. I will updated this review when I finish if the story ends up disappointing but I somehow doubt it will.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song carries a beautiful melancholy in how it presents characters, the world and the protagonist. This melancholy is both aching and soothing, and done with great care. I would've loved it if the combat received the same attention for detail. Fighting is still fun, but some of the difficulty spikes resulted in frustration that for me didn't fit the calming wonders the game offers. I played the game on the intended difficulty, and I can imagine that the story difficulty would've better fitted my play through. Nonetheless, the dialogues were touching and made up for it. I was actually curious about the NPCs and cared for their dreams, survival and ambitions.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song combines the Metroid formula with an emphasis on medium-to-close range combat in a really fun way, and that's before factoring in the great character writing. The combat system's focus on swapping between ranged and melee attacks and rewarding you for timing each does a great job of encouraging experimentation and aggression, and also has enough build variety to pretty easily focus in on one of the two if that's your preference. The world building is also one step removed from something like Dark Souls's vagueness without being completely transparent, but still has enough data to make get a coherent timeline of events and motivations. Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed the game. I liked the visuals, art style, moodiness, and the soundtrack. The story was a little vague, which I didn't mind; it reminded me of the way Dark Souls tells its story along with the NPC encounters and storylines. I felt the combat could have been better - it was too easy in some ways and slightly frustrating in others. There was a lot of backtracking toward the end of the campaign. For a one-person project and their first game, it's still quite the achievement. Buy it, but wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pleasant, atmospheric metroidvania. It's not revolutionizing the genre, but it's an enjoyable experience. Overall, I found it a fair challenge. Mostly pretty easy, although quite punishing if things go wrong. You have very few invincibility frames after getting hit, and you don't have a whole lot of HP, so if things go wrong you can be dead fast. However, I rarely felt it was anyone else's fault when I did die - I screwed up or got careless. I rarely needed more than 2 attempts to beat any boss, so I never had issues with runbacks to bosses or anything like that.Pros:1) There is a mechanic (introduced during the tutorial, so not really a spoiler) where your blaster (think Samus from Metroid) heats up as you use it, which in turn makes your melee attacks do more damage as they are overheated. Several items in the game allow you to balance the blaster vs. melee damage by powering them up separately, and changing how quickly or slowly the blaster overheats. This aspect of the combat was a very cool idea. Even with the blaster, you do more damage the closer you are to your target. So there's a risk-reward balance on keeping your distance.2) The visuals in the game a really nice. It has a really clear vibe, from the art style to the music, which is sometimes warm and pleasant, and other times downright creepy. I thought this was well done.3) Openness of exploration. I don't like that, at some point, you get very clear markers on the map to serve as targets for your exploration. I prefer to just be a bit lost. Super Metroid never gave any clues, and it's an absolute classic. HOWEVER - there is nothing in the game that forces you to do them in any particular order. I played the game 3 times (first blind one, then a speedrun, then a deathless run, to get all achievements). The first time I did things very much out of order, got the power ups in a strange order, and it made my playthrough very different. Sometimes harder than it was supposed to be, other times much easier than it was supposed to be. I really appreciate a game that lets you choose your own path.4) I'm not normally into voice acting in games, but I actually thought they did a great job with it in this game. The actors were very believable and natural sounding. I was surprised.Cons:1) Although the balancing of blaster and melee attacks was a cool idea, overall the combat wasn't terribly engaging. Most of the time I could just keep my distance and largely avoid boss damage. The fights didn't have the dance-like flow that you get in fights from Hollow Knight. This is a tough comparison, as I consider HK one of the greatest games ever, so that's a high bar. But the movement in the game is very smooth, but not really tight and precise. I felt this negatively impacted the combat experience a bit.2) In the early game, movement is quite slow. If you know where you're going, you can get several speed and mobility / jumping upgrades very quickly, but you can also easily miss them for a long time. With the base movement, your speed is slow enough and the map is big enough that it can get a little bit tedious to explore the map. I like getting lost a bit in a metroidvania game, but with how slow the movement is it could get a bit frustrating at times to retrace your steps and look for another route. I've seen some people say you need more fast travel points, but personally I would much rather just have a little faster movement speed. Fast travel doesn't really involve exploring. I like to wander the map and see what I can find, I just want that wandering to take a little less time, especially since there are some corridors without much to do. An occasional empty corridor to make the points on the map line up isn't a big deal if you can move through it quickly, but is a bit more irritating when you move so slowly.3) Balance. When upgrading, you have 3 choices: gun power, melee power, and kind of an all around stats boost. However, as mentioned above, you can largely avoid damage if you're careful, and when you take damage it often comes very fast. As a result, I found most of my stats (ie HP) no very relevant. I felt like just going all in on either melee or blaster damage was an obvious choice, and allowed you to dish out lots of damage fast. This "glass cannon" build seemed so much stronger than a balanced build. I'm not sure how to balance this better, but it just felt a bit lopsided to me.4) One last thing about pacing. The dialogue was nice, and the characters seemed genuine and pleasant, built some nice narratives throughout. However, most voice-acted dialogue can't be skipped. The voice actors did a great job, but especially on subsequent playthroughs (like the speedrun and the deathless run) it was a bit frustrating. It would be nice if there was some kind of "hold this button to skip" thing. It's minor, and only really was an issue after my 1st time through, but worth noting.Conclusion:Despite having some flaws, I very much enjoyed this game. Obviously, I played it 3 times, so it did something right. It's a good fit if you like the Metroidvania genre (more so the Metroid than the Vania), and if you like the mix of somber and hopeful atmosphere. It won't blow you away with platforming or combat, but both are done well enough to be a good experience, and the game as a whole delivered what I wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is better than the gameplay, but I still recommend.   It's like watching a clumsy toddler discover the world around them, but with a arm canon.  Pros would be story and characters, a map that lets you place various markers, and decent combat with switching from ranged to melee, and having a badge system that helps to customize it.  Cons are with say combat, you get different weapons you can find and use with only one needed for progression you get about as soon as you start the game.  But even with all the options, they don't feel great.  There's a few that spawn friendlies to do damage, but outside of one that worked on a few bosses pretty well, the progression weapon just works better with whatever melee weapon feels good to you.  Just good, fast damage.  There is also a moral system in place, no idea how it works, but after knowing the characters, a rerun with all the same crap side weapons you get just is not in the cards for me to explore.tl;dr, Nice story with interesting characters and good voice acting, combat has a decent core with mostly crap sides.  If you can catch it on sale, pick it up

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively low-key Metroidvania with some Dark Souls influence- stop me if you've heard this before. Besides the stamina meter, punishing but generally fair combat, and die -> lose your cash -> go pick it back up loop, Ghost Song really evokes the feeling of the latter type of game with its v i b e. Lorian V is rife with decay and a suffocating feeling of hopelessness evoked through its beautiful art and soundtrack and brought to life by the supporting cast. Their individual quest lines unfold in a very similar manner to the Soulsborne games, and it's quite possible to miss their conclusions if you don't hunt them down. The game does a pretty good job of telegraphing when they move (if not necessarily where), so it's not too tedious if you want to go out of your way to complete their stories. I personally found them interesting and enjoyed pondering the philosophical quandaries they each posed.In terms of gameplay, movement can feel somewhat limiting at first, confined to your regular run speed and a single jump. There are only a small handful of movement upgrades throughout the game, but they are hugely impactful to exploration, and navigating the world feels smooth and clean before long. Combat offers an interesting balance of long range and melee combat. After firing your arm cannon for a bit, it starts to overheat, massively slowing your rate of fire. The heat powers up your melee weapon, however, allowing you to do huge damage at close range. It strikes a really cool balancing act that stays fresh by providing a plethora of weapons to find that allows for a ton of experimentation.The game is not without its faults, though. For one, the pacing is a little off; much of the game is centered on finding five ship parts, and the first one takes much longer to get to than any subsequent parts. Bosses, while generally well designed, tend to be bullet sponges. It's less of an issue in the late game when you've got access to a bunch of powerful weapons, but it makes some early fights a bit tedious. There are also some aspects of the story and the universe that I wish had been fleshed out a little more. I understand that not everything needs to be presented with huge amounts of detail, but some things felt just a little too under-explored or under-explained (you can't tell me that  and just move on like it's nothing!).Overall, this gets an enthusiastic recommendation for hardcore Metroidvania enthusiasts and a  more reserved recommendation for casual fans. It can't hang with the greats of the genre, but it's nonetheless thoroughly enjoyable and should not be overlooked.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to play this after seeing mixed review on it. Turned out to be a great metroidvania. Loved how the story really doesn't spoonfeed you anything, allowing you to form your own ideas about the story without going too far into theory crafting. Combat is challenging, but fair. Would say it's on the easier side of things as far as this genre goes. Exploration can be repetitive, but that's more to do with this having some roots in a soulslike.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever played a game that was both amazing and a massive disappointment. I've been waiting on this game since the kickstarter days in 2013 and now after finally playing it I don't think I've ever been this torn over a video game beforePros:- Atmosphere was great. It could have been better though (Explained in the cons section)- Gameplay was really fun. Loved the addition of secondary/melee weapons- Soundtrack was GODLIKE- Absolutely loved the story and lore. Felt like I was playing Dark Souls for the first time with all the weird cryptic stuff and NPC's. The cosmic horror aspect was *chef's kissCons:- The old art style and atmosphere before the reboot looked a million times better than the final game. I know there were a lot of hiccups with the old engine which caused the change but I feel something really unique was lost in the process. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adored the old 80's sci- fi anime aesthetic it had going on and the game just looked so much darker and creepier. I honestly have never seen something so hauntingly beautiful than that old build. Now it just looks too bright and Hollow Knight-y- The Dizzy/pet mechanic is completely absent from the final game- The NPC's seemed to have a lot more going on with them in the old build. Many NPC's that used to be in the game are absent in the final version- The game is way too short and feels somewhat unfinished. Areas like Six- finger woods and Junkpit feel like complete, fleshed out areas while Roteshotter and the underwater section felt empty and lasted for like three minutesAll in all, I really do like the game a lot and I'd love to play more but seeing what the game could have been makes it a bittersweet feeling

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly absolutely loved this game, sure it definitely has its rough edges, but, the world, the characters, the mood, they were just excellent. The gameplay definitely takes a bit of getting used to and can come across a bit clunky I think, but, I think that's more to do with its style, it's actually quite smooth and works great once you get the hand of it even on the more difficult bosses, and there are some pretty difficult bosses.I will say though, that the style of game that it is won't be for everyone, it has a lot of backtracking with limited fast travel options, and it is often very unclear where you should go or what you need to do, with some mandatory upgrades hidden in areas that seem like they would hold optional secrets, and some progression items not standing out well in your inventory. It is a game about being lost and wandering, in theme, story, characters, and gameplay, and along with that it can have some pretty difficult boss encounters that are their own kind of mystery to try and figure out how to beat. The whole game has that wandering mystery element to it and I'd say as far as the main progression none of it is so obtuse that it feels cheap, but, it could certainly be frustrating if you're not coming into the game ready to just wander and explore and be lost.The above are certainly somewhat criticisms of the game as much as it ultimately worked for me, I do think it would have helped if the mandatory progression items and abilities and where they need to be used were laid in a clearer way, both in the world and in your inventory, or at least having more elements in the world that would help guide the player on the path. The bosses are a bit of a more complex issue and I'm not sure there's really a "fix" as it were, to have these difficult boss experiences while also being adaptable to the various playstyles present in the game.Still, this game was just about perfect for me where I'm at right now, hit all the right beats and themes and I'll be quite excited to see what comes next from these developers. Easy recommendation, even if you should definitely be aware of the kind of game you are getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: First time writing an review for any game, so I'm sorry for missing some good critical points. First of all, the game has this unique atmosphere along an ost tracks that matches the tone. Loneliness and exploring tone is what the game is setting off, it hit the mark for it, really pulling me in of what's going on in the background, listen to one of the track while heading off in the map making you feel you are alone but yet there is something make you feel calm.  The art style was clearly thought out to fit with the tone of the atmosphere and musics, the colors seem vibrant for the tone this game is putting out. Even with the bright colors, it also seem dull to match the planet, giving this idea of the world is vast and bright but with through your eyes, its dark and lonely. Next, the overall gameplay. Now the combat system isn't going to break any news or will be the highlight of the game, its simple, rather that can be good or bad for certain people, for me, it could've been better. There isn't crazy fighting animation or crazy weapons, its just a gun from your arm, with different type of bullets. It can overheat do more damage with the negative of slowing down, there is special weapon, same arm, with different kind of bullets. It's simple like I said. The enemies are unique but get old fast, unless you meet the bosses with their nice design but weak fighting system. While the design getting boring real quick, their sounds don't get boring. Each enemy make this unique sound which I wonder on how they do it. It brings the little horror vibe out of it, since you hear it before you see them. While the enemies are great to look at and their sounds they make are unique, they do get boring rather faster than I thought. Yet, it didn't made me stop playing the game, it could be the curious side of me and me wondering how this story will go.Overall, The story and the planet what made me keep playing, wondering what is happening with the MC, why are there bodies around the planet. Why are there enemies on here and how they got here. The music makes you stay attached with the colors and the lovely voice acting from the characters. This game got my approving of unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, this game has some of the best ambient music I've heard in a while, and the dialogue is very enjoyable to listen to/read. Couple those things with the interesting alien world and exploration, as well as challenging gameplay, and you have an incredibly engaging experience. There's a new game + so there's more incentive to replay it, which is always a welcome feature.There are a few quriks and cons to the game however. The very first of which you'll experience is that the game isn't as well optimized for keyboard/mouse as opposed to a controller. Also, there's a lot of backtracking and running around in places you've already been because fast travel points are few and far between. Overall, I had a lot of fun playing it despite the numerous frustrations. You should definitely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with a great soundtrack to make you feel immersed in this atmospheric and enigmatic moon. Controls aren't all entirely flushed out with not being able to use movement actions while in crouch, precision aiming being a little jank, but overall controls are smooth. The story is quite decent but it does require you to explore and find the NPC's through out different parts of the map at different times in the game which may lead to missing parts of the lore in your first playthrough. The voice acting is very well done as well so +A on that. Some of the enemies are well balanced while others are extremely annoying to fight due to the precision aiming not being accurate which is probably my biggest gripe. In the first half of the game there's a lot of exploration and backtracking but in the second half of the game everything becomes quite linear both in where you're able to go and in the map layout. It's not a perfect game but overall I think Ghost Songs beautiful world and atmosphere coupled with it's immersive music is more than worth experiencing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm CAUTIOUSLY recommending this if you enjoy the genre, because I don't think it's horrible. I think it's pretty decent, with some major quality of life gripes that frankly might cause me personally to stop playing.Ghost Song seems to excel in atmosphere, and its melancholic approach to both world building, music and sound design seems to work well enough. On the other hand, I honestly don't care about the story itself, and characters you come across are hit or miss. I often find myself skipping through dialogue with the more generic human characters — not to mention many of their portrait photos look strikingly similar on the more humanoid ones, which honestly just seems lazy and doesn't help endear me to them. Mechanically, this game works rather well. All of the hallmarks are there. You have dashes and double jumps and precision aiming, and all sorts of interesting armaments and power abilities...I have no complaints in this department.What makes me "cautiously" recommend this title is the sub par approach to fast traveling and saving. As with many MetroidVania titles, the game features a "bonfire" saving system, with additional areas that act as fast travel hubs — just like Blasphemous. Unlike Blasphemous, these hubs and save points are too few and far between, often requiring you to spend a minute or two just to get back to a boss, rather than place a spawn right outside said encounter. This adds unneeded pad to an otherwise solid experience and makes it harder to learn how to actually fight the bosses through repetition.Progression is tied to locating multiple ship parts scattered throughout the game world, which naturally have major boss fights associated with them. The craziest part of this is that once you acquire one of these ship parts, the game literally tells you "fast traveling is not allowed," while you are holding the part, meaning you have to run alllllllllll the way back to the ship you are trying to repair. I've already done this once, and when coupled with the other progression and quality of life hurdles, I don't think I have it in me to do this five more times.Someone suggested on a forum somewhere that the save points should also be fast travel points. I think this at the very least would help, but the developer also needs more of them, particularly near boss encounters.So, anyway, play it if it looks cool. But, just know if you're new to the genre it might waste your time. There are better titles out there like Blasphemous...
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is a metroidvania that leans more on the Metroid side. You play as a suit of space armor that may or may not be human, blasting aliens with an arm cannon that can augmented with several different weapons. Its Metroid to a T and isn't a afraid of the comparisons. That being said, its a solid game overall. Shooting is punchy and killing enemies is satisfying, game looks and feels great, and my entire playthrough was on my Deck with 0 drops or hiccups in performance. Its not a very difficult game though, don't expect Hollow Knight levels of encounters here. The main drive is the story and characters, but i feel like i need a gigabrain to understand the dialogue between characters.Everyone talks in metaphors and riddles, im not going to spoil what i feel like the game's about, but i also feel like its up for debate and personal ideas on what is being said between the lines. The game has a very surreal vibe throughout the my 9 hour playthrough. Music is more about setting the tone rather than getting you amped up for a boss fight, and the bosses are more like giant sponges of regular enemies you've already faced. As mentioned, the combat is never really difficult, and my first death was around the 5 hour mark to rushing through an area and not stopping to heal up.Ghost Song is a solid game from start to finish, and has a general tone i haven't seen before in a metroidvania. Don't expect breakneck pacing with insane boss battles, i'd honestly recommend this after a long day, just to deflate and relax. $20 is a great price, and i don't see myself going back to 100% this, so a one and done is more of what i think most people will get out of the game.
