_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: it's fine.  One of the top ten metroidvanias of 2022, but not one that is going to be held up against the likes of Hollow Knight or Symphony of the Night.It's fascinating to see the different takes on this in the reviews.  Some people say the exploration is bad, but the combat is great.  But others say the exact opposite - that the combat sucks and the exploration is what makes the game good.In my opinion, the world is mostly fun to explore, and the combat is just average.  I found the movement to be a bit tedious.  In particular, there are some "quests" that make you trek through the same areas multiple times, and the lack of fast travel during those times made it feel like a pointless way to pad the game length (even if the reasons behind not being able to fast travel make sense in terms of the way the world works).  As many people have noted, the dash and sprint mechanics are both a bit pathetic, so you never quite feel like you're a complete master of the physical world.  There's no movement that feels particularly satisfying to pull off.Some of the bosses feel like a bit of a slog.  Many of them change up their attacks halfway through the fight - so it's nice that there's a bit of variety there.  But as with the movement, none of the fights felt all that satisfying.There might be story - i try to make it a point to avoid reading any dialog.  But i don't think there's any new ground being broken.  I thought maybe there might be some intrigue or backstabbing or twist, but i didn't notice (again, i barely acknowledge any story at all, so maybe it's deeper than i'm giving it credit for).  Also, as of this review i'm only halfway through the NG+, and i have not yet gotten all achievements, so perhaps there's more just around the corner that might surprise me.Art is nice - very metroidy.First play through for me was 8.5 hours, and i will likely eventually finish NG+.  So perhaps i'll get 16 - 20 hours out of it?Overall, an enjoyable and competently made game that will probably entertain you for 10 hours if you're a metroidvania fan.  Buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: If you have been following Ghost Song (GS) throughout its long production, I probably do not need to tell you this is a labor of love. It has been a long time coming and the effort put into this game shows... for the most part. While not without flaws,  a variety of weapons and tools, and a world worth exploring with steps worth retracing.A lot of attention to detail has been put into this game; from branches twitching in the wind, to the "overheat" system, to passive enemies that only turn hostile when you attack them, to the effects of standing too close to an exploding enemy and wearing their hemolymph/blood/phloem fluid/Kool-Aid/whatever (and the impact it has on your suit and weapons).GS does not really have a story when compared to other platform action game franchises like Metroid, Ori, or Castlevania. Similar to games like Hollow Knight and Sundered, however, the vague story behind GS is mostly revealed in play and with some character interactions.All you really know is that you awaken on a planet and begin to wander. You act and sound quite human, but appear and function quite machine-like. A cyborg? AI? Android? Conscience transfer? You eventually discover the surface littered with wreckage from spacecraft. Eventually you discover the how but the "why" is one of the biggest mysteries behind GS. In your adventures, you make friends, enemies, and discover strange alien environments. To traverse barriers and explore new realms you must discover new passages, tools, and weapons.Pretty standard for a platform action game. I strongly suggest you use a controller. Took a little getting used to but not bad.Gameplay is enjoyable especially as you get used to enemy patterns and weaknesses. Some enemies are very tough but there are areas cleverly put into the game to avoid them and destroy them from a safe spot. It is rare I complete the same game twice. I completed this game 3 times.Mixed bag. Some areas have wonderful music and sound design. Others not so much. Enemy SFX are excellent in every instance but one - the cyclops jelly-bean rabbits. That was a bit... eh?There are a few issues with volume, where some enemies or characters are very loud while others are quiet. The voice acting is well done even if the dialogue does not reveal too much about the story, but the mystery is part of the charm. Overall, I would say the enemy and character SFX are excellent.This game offers absolutely wonderful parallax scrolling, an interesting art style, and strong animation. Some of the late-game areas, and some of those enemies, look a bit rushed but by the time you get there you will not have to look at it long. Again, the cyclops jelly-bean rabbits seem out of place in this game. Character and enemy models are very nice and interesting, and they seem appropriate for the tone the game is trying to create. With a couple exceptions, one does not know what is native to Lorian V and what is invasive. As it should be on your first visit to an alien world.This game is somewhat short but has moderate replay value. This game was in production a long time but I think it was worth the wait. It has some flaws but the care that went into it makes up for it all. This game is definitely deserving of a sequel and I hope to see a longer, deeper installment in the future (or some good DLC).Try this game if you:1) like platform action titles which evoke a sense of nostalgia for the 16bit days2) enjoy supporting indie projects especially if when effort and care are put into them3) moody, atmospheric games with good art direction and a sense of mystery4) want a platform action game that does not require you to have the timing/reflexes of a fighting game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Short, Deep, Fun and sometimes Challenging. If you are a Metroid/Castlevania veteran like I am, you can figure the bosses out and get a strategy going. There are mysteries in this game that will hopefully be revealed in the upcoming updates. The developers have been fairly communicative with the forums and discussions, which is a plus. The graphics are solid, the soundtrack will make you feel like you are slipping into a slow depression (This is not a negative thing. Some of us like the full range of human emotion). It fits with the theme of the game and the things you discover along the way. I've played through on the New Game + and the game is engaging enough to make me want to get all the achievements and write a review.  You get a variety of weapons and the enemies are various. The bosses are a pain the first round, but after some trial and error, you can get the right method to getting them down. There are also harder named enemies that you may not fight multiple times. They will move or stop spawning if you lose to them too many times, so as to not trap you behind a difficulty wall that cannot be passed by certain gaming journalists. Wouldn't want another Cuphead Debacle.  Other than that 8/10, Can't wait for the updates, want to see if the developers get brave and move us off the  world we start on and if this will become a smoother Hollow Knight franchise. (I liked the game play of this a little more than I liked Hollow Knight)

_childDocuments_.review: (This review should be pretty much spoiler-free, anything mentioned in regards to progression I tagged as spoiler regardless)So, Ghost Song.Metroidvanias are probably my favorite genre, not just due to their play style, but also because of their explorational freedom. Something that I'm still missing in a lot of more recent games, where, even with worlds themselves growing in size, they increasingly feel more like a guided list of tasks or quests ("go there, do this") instead. (Linear stories are fine, but with those I always get the feeling that there's something missing,  I must've overlooked at some point.)But this title? Especially at the beginning, it gave me back that nostalgic feeling of exploration, running around somewhat aimlessly to figure out what I'm doing and how to progress, while at the same time being challenging enough to make me advance cautiously at times. Of course exploration's not the only thing, there's characters to talk to, lore to figure out, with beautiful graphics and a great soundtrack playing in the background. It's just, it is an aspect I was missing in games that had those in them as well. The combat system seemed a bit sluggish at times (especially considering it's ranged weapon-based, which makes evading finnicky in some fights); in metroidvania terms, this game definitely is more on the Metroid side of "punch through things with force" rather than the Castlevania side of "learn proper evasion". Contact damage is a thing again as well, something I don't particularly like - but at the very least every area is spacious enough so you can somewhat keep your distance and focus on ranged attacks.I wouldn't call it frustratingly difficult or a huge challenge, you have a lot of options for increasing your fighting power if an area proves a bit too much for now. The game is a bit on the shorter side, so it won't even take a lot of time until you're doing fine pretty much anywhere on the map.As per usual, Ghost Song isn't entirely free of faults either. I don't recall seeing any bugs beside two, but one of them was a bit annoying in terms of exploratory sense (which is one of the main aspects I look for in this game category): map markers. I was happy to see those were a thing, but: they don't stay the same. Whenever I reloaded or restarted the game (so, after death or in-between sessions), the marker categories would randomly change, making it impossible to use one category for a specific thing (difficult enemy, different kinds of ability-requiring obstacle, possible or actual point of interest; typical metroidvania things) - which in the end made me just use a single marker category for everything and re-visit them every now and then to check whether they'd become relevant. Definitely not a deal breaker, as periodically traveling around the map seems like a good idea anyways to find out whether I'd missed anything, but having to walk those long-ish distances can slow down actual progress a lot.The other "bug" I came across is mainly the map sections not being properly aligned, so some room transitions don't look like they're connected on there - and your own position is displayed a bit inaccurate as well sometimes. Which is fine if you notice it and keep it in mind, but can also lead to confused searches for room exits that don't exist at all.Nonetheless, both of those issues are very minor, they didn't really get in my way at least.TL;DR / Conclusion: Very charming, almost bug-free [well, this ain't Hallownest] metroidvania that felt more "bare-bones" with less explanations about things. Timewise on the shorter side (depending on how much you intend to do in terms of completion), but in my opinion worth its price.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited 9 years for this game, expecting it to never surface, and I am pleasantly surprised by the results of it.  I'm 5 hours in and enjoyed the entire experience thus far.  As someone who grew up enjoying Mega Man games, Metroid, Castlevania SOTN, etc, and has grown to enjoy SoulsBorne games in more recent years, this one has an overall fair, but somewhat high, difficulty for a Metroidvania (MV).  Thus far, I do not feel overpowered nor have bosses become trivial but remain challenging (but we'll see if that changes).  The weapon variety I'm liking so far and most feel at least somewhat diverse from one another, and I've found use for each at some point or another.  The atmosphere is strong for me, and I'm interested in learning more about the world and the character.  The lore isn't overwhelming, but not nothing either (or at least, so far).  Enemies are unique and have a lot of variety and ways of defeating them.One important note for more casual players: The "normal" difficulty, however, is sure to turn some people off to game.  Unlike Metroid or most others in the series, "Statues" that work as both Leveling locations and Teleporters are both very, VERY few and far between (I've found 2 in the last 5 hours).  Save points are fair bit more frequent, and heal you completely, but won't let you level up (I would argue you should have been able to level up at save points).  Upgrade materials (aka "souls") drop upon death (like SoulsBorne games) and if you die, you have one life to pick them up or lose them completely, which means the game becomes harder essentially as you'll surely be packing 3-6+ levels worth of souls (early on).  This makes for a VERY punishing system if you struggle to clear bosses and areas.  Hardcore vets may find it somewhat average in difficultly (from another review I read).For me, it's been refreshing to not have a boss die in a few hits.  The long traversal through levels and the longer trek back, are weighty as you have a lot to lose and no easy way to get out.  While I haven't lost any (significant) number of "souls", I have certainly dropped 6+ levels worth of souls that I had to carefully get back too.  But most bosses I've beaten in 1-2 attempts.All in all, I easily recommend the game, with the caveat of making sure players who don't want to be punished or are less versed in platformers/MVs go the Explorer route.  It may not please all Hardcore Veterans, but to me it stands tall in the genre and is sneaking it's way to to top of my favorites list.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game 5 years ago on the recommendation of a gaming magazine that doesn't exist anymore, I missed out on the kickstarter bonuses but managed to get in early anyway, and eagerly awaited the product. You will get lost, you will have problems with some bosses, and you will die a fair bit, but it's all in good fun.  The NPCS are somehow like Darksouls 1, and open up secret items, levels, and other stuff you really want, and just like Darksouls the ending isn't always pleasant. The only issue I've had with my hours of playtime so far is that some of the NPC dialogue goes on a bit too long, there's some jank to upward transitional platforming, and power scaling doesn't really work as well as I'd like. Overall it's an enjoyable experience.  This  is indie Metroid as Bloodstained was indie Castlevania.UPDATE: I beat the game, didn't complete everything, but on a strict dollar to hour ratio it's solid. Only issues to note- enemy types aren't varied enough and I find myself wishing things weren't so hp bloated- environments are cool but I really wish he went in more with the destroyed civilization he alludes to- NPC dialogue is interesting but needed to be cut down to half- bosses are mostly fun but go on a bit long only bad one is the guy with the skull club- mechanics of the game are there but needed a bit more polish, enemy patterns can be a bit basic or obtuse at times- Story is pretty understandable, but missing on some events means you lose huge chunks of context so it seems unintelligible - travel speed and fast travel in general needed to be better implemented, I don't mind the return runs with parts but this could've easily shaved an hour or two off of playtime. - there's a lot of weapon variety but a lot of them are kinda useless given the hp bloat and weapon limitations, dev should've looked closer at SOTN/Bloodstained and Metroid for better balance in shots and melee. Still a very solid 7.5 game, a must play if you like atmospheric metroid like games, if it had come out sooner it would've been regarded as a classic.

The combat is pretty simple, yet clever in how using ranged weapons builds up heat that powers up your melee attacks for a little bit. Enemy designs are great, both in their look and their function.The universe seemed like a really interesting place, but the dialog wasn't quite doing it for me. It was just a bit too theatrical for my tastes. A bit too rehearsed-sounding to feel natural.Beyond that, I guess I just wish for more of the good stuff. Bosses in particular. I liked the ones in there, but it felt like by the end they couldn't keep up with the given movement options, or that the movement options didn't come into play. _childDocuments_.review: I waited eight years, and it was worth it, but I want to see some more work done on it before I'm satisfied.I didn't come in expecting a AA experience, to say nothing of AAA. I came in expecting the work of an extremely small team that had to restart development and deal with real life.I wouldn't say I was disappointed overall; the nature of your character is a solid mystery with a reveal that you actually have to earn separately from just accomplishing the signposted tasks. The music and sound feel professionally produced, there's more animation than I expected, and the overall gameplay mechanics are both distinct and fun.The core of the issue is the game's pacing. I played on the intended standard difficulty under the promise of getting some kind of extra reward, and it was almost never easy. On one hand, a big challenge of search-action/Metroidvania titles is empowering the player without making them so strong as to remove any challenge, and this game averts that. The blaster's heat system is distinct from other titles in the genre and, while I love the way it plays with subweapons and badges/equipment, I also love how it enforces a mindfulness in combat that highly-punishing damage gives me more artificially.On the other hand, the difficulty expects you to die once or twice to many bosses, and the sense of accomplishment never undoes how it feels when that slows the game down. Grinding quickly becomes an absurd prospect with experience requirements inflating rapidly, and stations for leveling up being spread out too far. Most games in the genre have a traversal move that's impractical for combat but great for distance, and I think the only way to improve the pace without dismantling the game's systems would be adding something similar.So like, yes there's a BIG low to this game, but it's only so impactful because of how well the rest of the game tends to operate. Aside from nitpicking the outdatedly-slow dialogue system and what appears to be an unfinished NPC questline that wasn't fully removed, the game's a delight. I'm poor as balls and not sure $20 fits now, but with some tweaks it'd definitely be worth a replay and earn its value. I recommend if you're really into these titles, Metroid, and/or are willing to wait for some updates.

_childDocuments_.review: The introduction is approachable, mysterious and easily funnels you towards a point when you have gotten some essential abilities and the game opens up. The graphics look great (especially on my OLED screen) with some striking use of bright colors, darkness and faux 3d parallax effects. Is it not quite as spectacular as Ori and the Will of the Wisps, but I am really impressed that they delivered this kind of quality in an indie game. The feeling of movement and animations are better than in most metroidvania games, and it has been a joy to discover new traversal abilities. The game is more focused on exploration than bosses, but there have been some interesting mini-boss battles which make great use of your movement abilities. The game has some fun ideas about combat dynamics, such as your main gun heating up and slowing down the firing rate, but enhancing your melee abilities while it is hot. When you level up you unlock suit battery power which you can distribute on different suit subsystems (found in the world) which significantly alter combat, and amount to a fun progression of combat gameplay. The game is really good!

_childDocuments_.review: This is really a unique take on the metroidvania genre: visually stunning, with the atmosphere to the world, the characters, the lore, the enemies and the music, there is a gentle sadness, almost melancholy, emanating from this game, which I personally enjoyed very much.The fighting mechanics, weapons and modules are varied, you have several bosses that are all interesting to fight, and I really like how you will often make surprise encounters with NPC you've seen previously during backtracking, which makes the world feel alive.I really would have liked something a bit longer and bigger, and as usual with games shrouded with mystery like this one, I would have liked a little more information about the lore to have a better idea of what happened to this tragic moon. _childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting to buy this game the moment I saw its Kick Starter project, and I've waited 5 years for it. Was it worth the wait? It's quite complicated for me to say, but I'll list some of the goods and a few not so good points regarding this game. After all. I was looking a good Metroidvania after finishing Salt and Sanctuary. So, here we go:-The Good:-- Absolutely stunning artwork, although this game runs on Unity engine!- Very atmospheric and immersive (not sure if it was the correct word, but to me, this game was.)- Beautiful background (I think it was handrawn, but I may be wrong)- The lighting in certain areas were... legit captivating (the area where you see huge butterflies).- Amazing background sound effects (The Roslck Drift areas sounded terrible and terrifying in a good way)- The sound design (again!) was awesome... Listen to the drizzle of your barrel overheating)- Easy to play if you're veteran of Metroidvania.- Character control is tight, and great!- Price is quite OK, not too cheap or expensive.The Not-so-Good:-- Too short! I extended my gameplay just to see if I can get past Level 40.... and finally finished the game at Level 44 (I could just complete the game at 9 hour, but drag it to be finished at 20++ hours of gameplay).- One enemy can get on your nerves if there're too many of them; you'll figure out as you explore certain area.- The bosses were pretty easy for me; except for Elsom the Ogre (his huge flail caught me by suprise, and it was a clever way to prevent cheesing the boss by Phase Dashing through him).- As some may have complained; the normal jog and running/sprinting speed was too slow. (Maybe to make players to take it easy, I presume?)- The story could have been...better? I think the concept of a talking and thinking killer machine (the Deadsuit) may have been inspired by Masamune Shirow's Ghost in the Shell and other works like it, and I liked it, but... maybe a little bit of a tweak might improve the overall story... just maybe.So, this is, in my opinion, was a good game; not great, but good IF you enjoy taking your time OR loved atmospheric Metroidvania. To me, this is a slow-pace Metroidvania, and some may find it off-putting due to its short gameplay time and other 'quirks' If you don;t care about the 'quirks' and the not-so-good parts of this game... and enjoy stunning + impressive handrawn background + sound effects + great character control, buy this game. IF you're looking for a fast-paced, slashing/shooting, rage-quit inducing Metroidvania, you may need to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game! The story and atmosphere sold it for me. I was sincerely invested in the outcomes of the player character and NPCs. On the original (hard) mode, the combat was challenging and the modules and weapons were fun to mix and match to find a solution to some tough boss fights. And, the sound design is amazing. I can still hear Old Singer wailing off screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is a solid metroidvania sidescroller steeped in bittersweet vibes. This has been on my radar for nearly a decade and it's finally here! I bought it at full price and I have no regrets.While the gameplay is really fluid and polished, it doesn't really do anything that other titles in this genre haven't already done. That's fine though—the main reason to play this is for the excellent sci-fi plot, which deals heavily with themes of existentialism and yet is told with enough simplicity and charm that it manages to avoid coming across as too pretentious.I can also say Ghost Song has a great soundtrack, top notch voice acting, and a beautiful unique art style.A full playthrough—that is with the player trying to do everything that can be done in a single run—should take around 15 hours, and possibly up to 20 if some additional grinding is done to level up. A casual playthrough could take substantially less time (perhaps 8 hours or less). New Game+ is also available.The lead developer worked on this project for a very long time. If you're at all interested, give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: A nice metroidvania, although due to the way you are asked to explore the world a lot of the movement upgrades and modules either come very early or near the end of the game, which messes the pacing up a bit.Although that does mean you can explore most of the game from the start provided you find the necessary upgrades.tl;dr: A good time to wander around in.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is not the best Metroidvania I've ever played, but it might be the most artistic. The game is obviously a labor of love; a notion that is only reinforced by the saga of its turbulent development cycle. I usually recommend games based on how enjoyable they are, and less on how moving they are, or by how much I think the dev deserves your money. This is an exception. The gameplay is rough around the edges, and frequently not as fun as I'd like, but I still have no qualms about recommending it to anyone that appreciates a good adventure with a poetic and emotional story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda like Metroid meets Hollow Knight with some NPC questline mechanics borrowed from From Software (albeit not quite as obtuse). Apart from a few bosses, maybe a bit on the easier side on Metroidvanias. It has the right feel of "oh, there's a place I can't get to yet" and "I wonder what's in there" that makes you want to explore. Upgrade system is pretty much Hollow Knight, but it works and fun to try out different combinations, although there aren't as many useful ones as I'd like and I tended to use the same set-up most of the time. On the minus side sometimes backtracking to an encounter can feel like a chore.All in all I definitely recommend it, it's a very strong game in the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game.  My only complaints are 1: that the leveling system needs a lot of work.  I leveled up fairly quickly at the start of the game, and by the end, even with a xp-boost item I was only getting 1/10th of a level from a boss fight (and I never felt over-leveled or anything).  2: the map makers your given are fairly worthless.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game has somewhat special meaning to me, it was the first game I ever wishlisted on steam. Back then, when it was in the early stages of development I was already certain I would have something special here once it got released. It took way longer than expected, in between I lost hope I would ever see it finished. Finally, the wait was fully worth it.This game has issues, it is by no means perfect in any way. I'm sure some of these issues can yet be patched out. As far as metroidvanias go it is rather short and not too difficult, for better or for worse. Some of the stats and build options feel rather redundant but I don't want to get into too much detail.I mostly played this game for its atmosphere. The visuals are beautiful, the story is mysterious and captivating and if you pay attention you have something truly emotional and touching at your hand that is only amplified by the wonderful music and voice acting and how it is written in general. I love this game and I teared up a bit there at the ending.I recommend this game, give some love to the developers who worked so hard on realizing their vision for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Issues with the blatant padding and rather slow movement speed sort of compounding said padding issue aside, as well as it's relatively short length, I quite enjoyed Ghost Song as a nice atmospheric experience due to it's great sound design and Music, like for example in the infested areas. it's almost sickening how disgusting and churning the areas feel simply because of that.I was also oddly rather invested in the main character The Deadsuit or "Blue", she gave off a childlike innocence despite her rather monotone delivery (Don't worry, it's not Metroid Other M levels of monotone) while also seeming to be withdrawn and wanted to avoid conversation, she opened up later on though which I quite liked, the other NPC's you meet were rather interesting, with some of the more eccentric characters having some cryptic philosophical esc leanings/ramblings like that relatively obscure game about souls that are dark or something like that.Sadly though it really appeared the later areas were rather rushed, or maybe they just ran out of time, as they were fairly short, and the aforementioned padding with having to take every main Ship part (there are 5 in total) all the way back to base camp while disabling your fast travel for no other reason than padding game length, they did script some robot skull enemies to activate and cause you trouble on the way back, but that's all they really did.Overall though I would say it was a rather solid Metroid like experience, not the best I've ever played but I still enjoyed my playthrough of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD: The Music, art style, voice acting and world building.THE BAD: The short length, lack of enemy variety, and insufficient quest tracking.THE BOTTOM LINE: Ghost Song is a beautiful game depicted in a gorgeous hand-drawn art style reminiscent of Hollow Knight. The game wears its Metroid influence proudly on its sleeve, yet introduces its own mechanical twists in its mix-and-match perk and weapon heat systems to keep things fresh. As mentioned above, Ghost Song's main strength beyond its looks are its earnest story and well written and performed characters. While I wish it was longer and I didn't have to backtrack quite so often to not miss out on any side-quest story beats, I give the game a strong recommendation to anyone who is a fan of the Metroidvania (emphasis on Metroid) genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: I waited this game for years. Watching the development since 2014 and bought as pre-order in 2016. No regret. The game is wonderful and matt white is a pretty great guy. I lost my access to my order in humble bundle, but he personally generated a new steam key for me!If you like metroidvania, atmospheric games like The Swapper, and games which makes you fear to die in the game, this game is for you.The soundtrack is awesome too.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song is a game I had been looking forward to for years and now that it's finally here it was still worth the wait.It really delivers on the atmosphere with an eerie soundtrack and environments with secrets to discover. It can get quite challenging especially early on in the game when you haven't leveled up enough or found enough upgrades and modules, but some of these bosses are optional too so if you're really getting stuck on them then just avoid them or come back later when you're ready.Mixing up different modules to change your focus on your gun or melee or maybe somewhere in between allows the player the freedom to approach the game how they want.The story is quite mysterious in itself and leaves some things unanswered or up to interpretation but its different quests are often full of charm and emotion which made the journey even more engrossing.Definitely recommend this game. I might give NG+ a try soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for the excellent vibes, atmosphere, and aesthetic. Also really enjoy the melancholy in the story.Gameplay wise, yeah its a metroidvania, pretty standard progression with standard abilities. Combat is not bad, and I really enjoyed playing around with the heat and melee mechanics. Essentially ended up using a build that heats up quick to get my sword flaming red and cut through everything. A few annoying things like not being able to quickly progress dialogue options, map icons not lining up, having to power down the suit to fit upgrades, but my time with the game was definitely enjoyable. Very glad I played it, and no problems recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks gorgeous with both vibrant and haunting environments to explore. The only negative aspect to the game, at least to me, was a lackluster ending that I felt was abrupt. There should have been more to it. Otherwise, everything else about the game was awesome making this title a gem in the metroidvainia genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  If shoegazer was a video game style, rather than a music style, this would be it.  The artwork is beautiful and the soundtrack is matches the artwork perfectly.  The vibe is very much in line with the same kind of curiosity and sadness that games like Hollow Knight and Ender Lillies exude.  The gameplay is great as well.  The appearance of the enemies, the timing of the upgrades and weapons, everything is so well thought out.  There is such a glut of crappy 2D metroidvanias that imitate what the very best of these type of games have to offer, without really understanding what makes these games work.  That is not this.  I would put this in my top 10 because though it may not be the greatest at any one thing, this game is literally a near perfect package, taking it in as a whole experience.  This game is right behind Cult of the Lamb as my favorite game of 2022.  You can tell the developer was trying to create art, not just a game, and I always appreciate feeling a developers love for what they are doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: A somber, slow-paced sidescroller. Has a lot in common with Dark Souls, and a few bits of Hollow Knight as well. Improves on Hollow Knight in several ways, such as the ranged attack improving the flow of combat a bit, and a dodge move being unlocked quite early. Combat is a very interesting mix of your basic attack which overheats, your special attacks which require an energy meter to fuel them, and melee attacks which are boosted by your gun being overheated. Surprisingly few memorable bosses, but many boss fights are optional or skippable in some way. The game's story is scattered all over the place, if you're familiar with the Dark Souls system of randomly encountering NPCs and missing half of them in your first playthrough you'll know what to expect.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Memorable games are always greater than the sum of their parts. Kudos to the devs in this regard, as I will be remembering this game for a long time to come. Atmosphere creeps and oozes out of every aspect of the visual and sound design, and this alone makes it a praiseworthy Metroid-styled game. I found the dialogue and unexpected voice acting surprisingly palatable, serving well its small cast of pleasant characters. This emphasis on polishing atmosphere and character-driven narrative create a rare sense of joy and incentive for the player to slow down and appreciate the quiet and still moments.If you are a fan of challenging metroidvania gameplay, it's a mixed bag. At first glance, this game looks and feels just a little sluggish and cumbersome. However, I would say that altogether, the mechanics are beautifully implemented for the platforming and map design in-place, and have a decent ceiling for optimization that keeps even simple traversal engaging. Personally, there is a little too much emphasis in the design on restrictive mechanics (e.g. stamina management while sprinting) over refining mechanics (e.g. movement techniques and animation cancelling) for me to want to play and replay this game for the joy of the optimization. As a side-note to this, I was disappointed that the keyboard input support was token at best - the game was clearly only designed to be enjoyed with a controller.Everything said, Ghost Song is fun and polished in wonderful ways, highly recommended! I hope the creators continue making cool things.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it finally came. I never minded the wait, in the end it made getting the game all the more sweet.So you like Metroidvania games with the emphasis in the Metroid part? I thought this game was that. It's not really. It feels a lot like Super Metroid in the beginning. It feels alien, desolate and lonely. For a while that was all I needed. Then it became something else, something less Metroid, something more human and emotional.At the end this isn't a Metroid clone. It does it's own thing and does it well.It also borrows a lot of it's storytelling and character vibes from Dark Souls. It's not a bad thing. Strange things are going on on this moon, I dare you to find out what.This game has a lot going for it. The atmosphere, the characters, the sound design and music, the combat, the storytelling through environment (as well as written dialog with some great voice acting). It's not long, but it's not short either. It felt long enough without becoming tedious.This was an experience. I'm not sure I'll play it again. Maybe some day.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

All Metroidvania fans need to play this. _childDocuments_.review: Very rarely anymore do I pick up a new game on a whim and actually finish it. I saw the beautiful artwork in the trailers/screenshots, and noticed it was in the metroidvania genre so I decided to give it a shot. I'll put it to you simply, I enjoyed the experience a lot. I won't say it's my favorite game of all time, but this personally did a lot more for me than games like Ender Lilies, Dead Cells, and Blasphemous (although I do want to revisit that last one soon). Games with strong artistic-representation and intriguing character development, at times, are much more satisfying for me than any gameplay could offer. And in my opinion, that gameplay is here. Yes this is a game, and it should be reviewed fairly like one; But regardless of where it falls short in it's gameplay compared to other metroidvanias, it still left a strong impression. It stands on its own, and should be treated as its own experience. A somewhat intense, but at times, soothing experience. I know I'm hardly mentioning actual gameplay elementsthemselves, but just know that pretty much everything you'd expect to be in a metroidvania is here (with some minor Souls-like elements). People have given bad reviews for this game being on the shorter side, and for the boss fights being either too easy or too tanky. I'm here to say that passive charms (yes, akin to hollow knights charms) are fun to discover and use in combination with one another to buff damage to make those tankier encounters go a bit smoother. This is the type of game that takes a bit of exploring to get everything out of it, but its no Axiom Verge when it comes to getting stuck. You can mark your map whenever you hit dead ends, and even discover breakable walls to secret passageways. Don't worry, the game is made a certain way that rewards backtracking and exploration for those with a keen-eye. Even just exploring old areas for the sake of boredom may net you another chance to talk to an npc you haven't seen in the last few play sessions. These characters are integral to the pacing of the story, lore, and world. The voice-acting is fairly top-notch. It helps to make sure you talk to someone multiple times in a row until their dialogue is exhausted. If you're like me and enjoy speaking of important but lesser spoken subjects like mindfulness, mentality, and identity, you've come to the right place. I honestly couldn't recommend a better experience metroidvania-wise in 2022. Enjoy it while you can, and if you do, there's even a New-Game+ mode for those left wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game that i couldn't put down over the weekend i got it. It has a similar vibe as hollowknight and a similar feeling to the OG metroid games. The story kept me fully engaged and the art style is stunning enough to keep me interested even when i was just roaming around the map. While some of the boss fights feel strange and item placement for a few key ones seems very missable, I think it plays into the story fairly well. If you like metroidvania games, this shouldnt be in your cart, it should be in your library already.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Game was pretty fun to play for the first couple of hours. Something that was mad annoying was the fast travel system in between robots. I have only come across maybe 4 or 5 by the time I'm writing this review and you have to run all the way back to a certain robot if you aren't already there to get any fast traveling done. That, combined with a pretty big map became a major problem fast. Another aspect of the game i found strange was the boss titles, I guess the minor titles didn't strike me as boss fights because they looked like standard enemies but as I progressed through the game it was easier to tell who was a boss and who wasn't. Some fun parts of the game were all the cool modules you could get for your suit and blaster which added more variety to game play, and getting to know all the NPCs stories whether they are robot or human was a nice touch. The last thing I can say about the game from what I have played through so far at least, is that the room designs before some bosses are very poor in regards to not having any save point or fast travel robot before the boss itself. For one of the major bosses the nearest save point is almost on the other side of the map and I had to go from that point all the way to the boss over and over again, just to finally beat the boss and realize that the next robot/save point can only be accessed by killing it beforehand. Seems the devs dropped the ball on common sense there. Seriously. The nail in the coffin for me was reaching a new area for the first time and there was a cool new boss totally fair and all that but this particular boss jumps out of arena view every so often forcing you to leave the room and come back. Normally this wouldn't be an issue because the boss HP bar isn't affected and the fight usually continues on like normal the second you get back in there. However, it seems that when you get the boss down to 15% or lower it refuses to fight anymore and retreats permanently no matter what I do. I don't know if it's supposed to be a bug but I fought it right after the most recent bug patch so I'm assuming it's just a troll boss then because it is literally unkillable for me. Decent game for a bit? Sure. Worth 20 of your hard earned dollars? Definitely not. I only got about half way into the main game but I don't think I'll be picking it back up anytime soon until major bugs are patched.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those moments where I wish there was a middle option between Yes and No. I'd recommend the game, but only on a discount.  There are good moments in the game, like the Art-style, the voice acting. I also generally enjoyed the 'feel' of your character, Deadsuit. The way you have to shut down to switch out weapons and your Implants feels nice, the movement is also a bit on the slower side, though I can imagine some people might have issues with that. Please remove the sprint function though, the 'speed' you gain from it is laughable and just doesn't really do much, in combat it's useless too. I like the   of the Gun, how it overheats and such, but that kind of leads into the problem that your Main Weapon feels pretty weak, the damage isn't great, it overheats rather quickly unless you run with certain Implants that improve those two aspects. It doesn't really give you the impression that you're getting stronger over the course of the game, because the leveling system attached to this game might as well  not really exist. Any points you put into having more HP, do more gun damage or have more Stamina / Ammo bar feel so insignificant that you wonder if it really does anything.   Mostly I was neutral on the combat, but there have been frequent points where I just felt frustrated because things like the i-frames of your dash were inconsistent or the enemies / bosses hitboxes are.  The Story has some good threads in the background, like   but it kind of fails to really expand on that much. You're just told to collect 5 parts to repair a ship and to shut down a Field that prevents you from leaving, with the NPC's having some minor stories of their own (That are entirely missable) that you can help them with. It really boils down to being a Fetch quest with a backstory that is far more interesting than the chunk you actually engage with, hell, the game doesn't even bother to tell you  you can't fast travel with ship parts, it just says you can't and you have to accept it. The game also stops pretending that the parts have any meaning. You get the names of individual parts told twice at the beginning, and after that they're just generic ship mcguffin 1-5. No dialogue to explain what these parts are supposed to do or why they are needed to fix the ship. I know this is a incredibly minor thing to complain about, but it's an example of a lack of polish the story has that you interact with. It feels like there was barely any time spent on giving the player a reason / some agency on why they explore this junkheap of a planet. This game has many issues, and you're not going to find something as extremely polished like Hollow Knight here, but that doesn't mean that this game is some unplayable mess. It had it's good moments and I'd recommend it, but only if you can grab it with a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first impressions recommendation. I've been really enjoying this game. It is a standard Metroidvania so far but what sets it apart is the setting and tone. If you let the game pull you in, the atmosphere is hauntingly good. Lonely ambient music, weird, truly alien monsters, strange terrain contrasted by the non hostile npc here and there. Voice acting is good and gives each character a distinct personality. Mechanically the game is sound. Plays like a Metroid game, if maybe not as fluid. Upgrades and new weapons are sprinkled through just enough to give you a new toy to check out, but not so much to overwhelm you. I may come back later to add more as the game progresses, but it's an easy recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly haven't really played many metroidvania style games and nor are they typically my thing but this game has been a lot of fun. _childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Ghost Song has been a long time coming, especially as an original backer from 2013. The wait was well worth it, what an excellent experience. The story is simple, but the characters surrounding the story is what makes the atmosphere and tone all come together. The controls work great, they're responsive and smooth. No clunkiness here. The music is sparse, but loaded with emotional post-rock tunes that can truly soothe the mind and relax the soul. I would find myself sitting in areas with the game paused just so I can enjoy a track.The Deadsuit is an excellent protagonist, she's mysterious but also kind of timid and funny. On top of that, she's very customizable. Similar to a Souls game, you absorb energy that you gain from defeating enemies on the planet called Nanogel. With the gel you can upgrade 1 of 3 stats, and each stat offers a unique playstyle. With a high Vigor (governs HP & physical strength) you can be more of a melee monster and equip a sword and go ham on monsters. This was my favorite way to play. I also tried the Gunner style, which is a sustained damage playstyle that focus' on DS' arm cannon. Lastly is Resolve, which governs your Energy that allows you to use your special weapons. You can go full on Mega Man with a high Resolve and equip all sorts of different weapons and be super versatile.On top of all that you have modules, which give the DS different buffs, some passive and some active. There's a lot of customization to be had, and I found myself having fun coming up with different ways to play the game. I was surprised when I ended up playing a pure melee/lifesteal bruiser idiot over what my original plan of being a super fighting robot Resolve build.Another very positive factor for me is that the game isn't absurdly difficult. Too many Metroidvania's have been coming out lately that have Soulslike difficulty, and I'm glad this isn't one of them. When you die, you do have to grab your stuff like in a Soulslike, but it's not a big deal because the game isn't terribly difficult. This is more about the joy of exploration and feeling the vibes on this virtually lifeless planet. My one complaint, if I need to add one, is the map. I don't like how when you enter a room it completely shows the room on the map. The gradual map clear is not only more visually satisfying, it's also less confusing. I'd have to use markers constantly to mark rooms that weren't fully explored because if I left it up to my map, it would be a fully explored room.All in all, it was worth the wait, definitely going to be replaying this a lot in the days to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: So far only played an hour or so, but I'm loving the atmosphere and play style. From the locations, character, progression through the levels, and even the baddies, it is clearly influenced by Super Metroid. You even start the game on the surface of an alien world, outside your ship, and it's raining. This is the closest thing to Super Metroid I've played since...well Super Metroid and I'm enjoying every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Not nearly through right now but I like this game and think I've seen enough to give this a thumbs-up. At first I found it pretty hard, so I switched to explorer difficulty, which doesn't make the fights/enemies any easier but goes easier on the penalties for dying. Basically this helps you level up faster and makes dying less frustrating. The thing is, after a while I got the hang of it. After leveling up a lot and finding useful stuff to upgrade the game opened up for me.I like the various secret areas that one can find and that often give you something satisfying. All in all the game feels great. It's an intimate experience with some deep thoughts. The people's stories are interesting and I'd like to know who the "deadsuit" (the protagonist) actually is and if they all manage to escape the planet.To get a proper feeling of this game you should definitely play until you reach the stranded ship and its crew, which serves as a hub. Up to that point I felt rather lost and didn't yet see what the game's about. I like the exploration, the characters and their stories, the combat (I play with a controller and heavily remapped the buttons) and the calm blend of action and contemplation. _childDocuments_.review: So What is Ghost Song?Released on Steam (and other platforms) on Nov 3rd, 2022. Ghost Song is the first release by Developer Old Moon, and Published by Humble Games. Announced on Steam Greenlight way back in 2015. Ghost Song has been in development for a very long time, running mostly on a successful Kickstarter.It featured at least one complete reboot of the project. So what we are getting is the product of that reboot and restart. Despite that, this is a stellar example of the genre. Ghost Song is an Indie developed 2D Metroidvania which features intricately designed areas, plenty of mysteries to uncover and a crisp, refined combat system. Ghost Song takes place on a desolate moon, but features numerous biomes with their own inhabitants and quite stellar themes. Having the Art, Design, and Systems largely handled by a single person is, and still remains, quite impressive. For the asking price of $19.99. I got 20 hours worth of enjoyment out of it. Which means I got what I invested in, for sure. I have not, as of this writing found everything. I spent an additional hour after beating the game, exploring more of this world. As there are some lingering questions the game leaves you with. Beyond the stellar art direction, music, and game-play mechanics there are things that will inevitably detract from the experience for some. This is an Indie developed game and there are some things that definitely show that aspect of it's development. I.E. There are some UI elements that aren't as refined as others, particularly noticeable with the Secondary (Melee) Weapon art. This is also the case with the map art, as there are connectors between zones that don't quite match up. So you could spend some time trying to get into an "obvious secret" and find out that there is nothing actually there. Some people would complain about the lack of voiced dialogue throughout, and for that, I don't have a problem with reading small bits of text. For the dialogue that is spoken, I am impressed with the voices throughout. The Deadsuit's voice actress in particular is impressive. She covers a subtle range of interest and confusion with the events as they transpire. She seems thoughtful and considerate with her choice of words. For such a quiet protagonist, I got pretty invested in her goals and with the other characters you meet along this journey. I am not the biggest fan of the "Talk to a Character Multiple times to Get All the Dialogue" gimmick that seems to be a Dark Souls inspired fad, but I didn't mind it. There's only so much additional dialogue attached to them, and my genuine interest in the world made me largely ignore something that would normally make me roll my eyes. Gameplay wise, the combat is crisp and smooth. I've largely encountered nothing in the general running and gunning that I wouldn't find any issue with. There is one thing that eventually stopped my initial play session (of around 9 hours) and that was contact damage. The Contact Damage in Ghost Song is some of the highest I've seen in recent memory.I'm not sure if it was a product of my Statistics or Equipment, but I was taking close to 10-15% of my health in contact damage from a single encounter. In at least one notable case, I got completely destroyed by a boss in seconds due to contact damage alone.It was enough to stop my play session, but wasn't enough to stop me from inevitably booting the game back up and continuing with my efforts. Combat is somewhat unique in Ghost Song. Your primary "arm cannon" deals a short ranged buster shot that builds up heat. That heat is then transferred to your Secondary (Melee) Weapon.You can also equip different Modules that allows you to have an additional ranged attack of various sorts. Most modules need to be found from defeating various denizens throughout the world. Other modules exist to modify how you go about encounters or exploration and are your usual standard fare. It creates this synergy of exploring for new encounters, using your primary to build up your melee, then releasing your built up heat for melee and peppering targets with your weapon modules for additional effects as needed.I beat the game on Original Difficulty and didn't find it too challenging. If you're a fan of Indie Games, a fan of Metroidvanias, or just interested in the premise. I'd suggest picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece.Story and characters are engaging on a level almost unparalleled in gaming. Gorgeous scenery and haunting music tie together the feeling of the game beautifully.Don't get me wrong though, this IS a Metoridvania with a huge emphasis on combat. The mechanics have a wide variety of options for all play types and allow experimentation on loadouts between ranged and melee. Controls are fairly smooth and make sense, without overloading the controller with too many options.Two difficulty levels allow this to be exactly the type of game you want it to be, and the ability to grind means you'll always have an option to power up and come back to an area if you're getting too roughed up.I can't recommend this enough for any fans of Metroidvanias or just amazing sci-fi story telling in general.

_childDocuments_.review: there are by now a lot of (good) 2D Metroidvania/RPG/Soulslikes and tbh.i'm pretty done with the genre by now, but Ghost Song was on my radar ever since i saw the first "trailer"i completely forgot about the game and i don't realy know why it took so long.but when i saw it pop up on my list i just went for it.and what to say? this is now probably my favorite 2D action-rpg game.yes, i prefer it even to S&S and co. or some of the other more famous ones.this is probably one of the prettiest 2D games i played in a long while. it's the art-design, the colors, the effects, lighting and especialy the animations. it's not just pretty, this is a piece of art. the art-style is very destinct and beeing backrounds (screenshot don't do the grafics justice) or models...it's amazing.then there's the voice over and the sound-design. there are a couple of mixing issues (loudness mainly), but apart from that the voice-over pulls you right in (trying to avoid spoilers), while the music complements the somewhat melancholic feel many a scene ooze. the main character's voice-actor does a fantastic job and so does the other "cast". but the most important part about these games (or every game?) is the gameplay. initialy i realy didn't feel it. takes a while to get used to the rythm between Metroid-esque shooting and melee, you also unlock many abilities along the path as is typical in the genre. the moment i got the dash it just clicked. mixing melee and guns gets pretty natural along the way and hitboxes are spot on. the soulslike aspect comes from the "leveling" system: enemies drop currency, you can spend said currency to upgrade your suit. it's basicaly 3 stats to begin with. it's not a full on hardcore rpg. but levels do show and it plays into some other aspects aswell. if you die you respawn while at your place of death a pretty tree(?)thingy blooms, which you can collect. there's also multiple extra weapons both for your melee and special attacks for your gun.but you can also find modifications for your suit, passive and active effects to slot which play into the stat-system. you got a finite number of energy which you can reserve for equiping specific moduls (think Nier Automatas programm system).the game feels amazing, it's very motivating and just very well done.what stands out is the love and attention for every detail. if you want to change your active modules you don't just go into a menu, you first gotto power down your suit (probably also for balance reasons); when you die you leave a tree-root-structure which also plays into the themes of the game, the gun mechanic works on the longer you fire the slower but more impactfull and the more heatup your gun your melee attacks do damage which is all also both visible (gun getting more heated, steaming, etc.) and audible. i could go on and on...the dev(s?) realy put alot into this game and it pays of.probably my game of the year and a very special metroidvania that needs more exposure.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good, bite-sized Metroidvania experience. I did not 100% it but it took me ~9 hours to finish, getting roughly 70% of all the items.Even though it borrows from Souls-like games with its leveling up system and losing max health on death, until you pay to repair it, it was never frustrating and the world was fun to explore.The map leaves a bit to be desired as its not clear if you've explored somewhere fully or not, but the world is small enough that you can double check if you're not sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: A Charming, challenging and Intriguing Game.If you like the original 2d Metroids, Axiom Verge or Hollow Knight I strongly suggest picking up this game. Controls are sharp, any boss can be fought without taking damage, and if you die, its pretty much your fault.I played the game on Original difficulty and never found the game to be unfair. Gameplay progression-wise is fairly clear, you should find the first objective organically.  I did wander for one of the later objectives, but when i found it, realised it was not hidden at all, i just had missed the entrance.Story is interesting, left a little to the imagination, there is no great conclusion or "big picture" behind the story. I did wonder what this "world" was like at times and did get somewhat attached to characters. But its not the main focus of the game. The actual Progression, Abilities, passives and weapon system is very fleshed out, and I did feel like trying out the different weapons and build. Very reminiscent of Hollow Knight charm system but with a souls-like levelling and weapons choices. Art style is amazing, if you like Myazaki's Nausicaä, you will be right at home. There are elements of horror/surrealism. but for the most part, what stood out was a sense of mystery and wonder. For a one man dev team, this Blow My Mind. I did encounter 1-2 audio bugs, but nothing game altering or immersion breaking. Overall would recommend.Great Job Matt!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Just beaten the game at 10 hours after trying to explore each nook and cranny. It's short enough to play on a weekend and it's quite the experience. The environments, enemy design, sound design, soundtrack, and effects are well made that it contributes to an immersive experience.The combat is interesting and it has a Metroid X Dark Souls vibe to it. Though I think being able to dash while the stamina bar is still charging is a bit overpowered but at least the i-frames has a cool down so I guess it balances out. The sprint move is somewhat pointless as dashing multiple times is just the faster way to travel. Sometimes after a save the icons that I placed on the map will change symbols. Some would complain for how short the game is but I think it is worth the price of entry as it is top notch in quality. It's better to have a well made game than to add padding just to add more "content". I'm hoping that there will be DLC in the future that'll add more areas/items/enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Mid play-thru review (2/4 ship parts):Pros:+Engaging hand drawn environments, exploration/backtracking doesn't feel like a chore at all. The art is obviously a labor of love; I remember first hearing about this game 5 (?) years ago and hoping it would actually come out. So far it has been worth the wait.+Main combat loop is satisfying, upgrades/weapons are fun to experiment with. Switching between ranged and melee makes it feel different than Metroid or something like hollow knight.+Challenging, but nothing has felt unfair so far.+platforming and movement is satisfying and rarely frustrating.+Resource management is well balanced and has prevented me from being able to cheese enemies. +Leveling system complements and encourages exploration, although I would like to have more than 3 stat options.cons:-No directional melee attacks for most of the weapons I've found so far, it feels strange given that you can free aim in any direction. I should be able to thrust upward or downward with the spear or sword.-Creature/ambient sound design reminds me a little bit too much of hollow knight.-The penalty for death is largely pointless, if it's going to lower your max health it should be a more significant amount OR the cost to repair should be significantly increased. Maybe this is in the sweet spot for everyone else, but I wouldn't mind a bit more risk and tension when exploring the map.-Missiles should be more situational or should be obtained closer to the halfway point in the game, I've found myself using them more often than other weapon modules due to the range.I'm looking forward to completing it and I will update this review when I do.

_childDocuments_.review: You wake up as some person inside of what's called a deadsuit.  Your character is a weirdo and if you knew them in real life you would probably despise them.  Anyway you make your way to a group of humans and offer to help them repair their ship.  Something has gone wrong on this planet and people are being infected by something and death is all around.The art is wonderfully done.   The interior of the ship looks nice and the depths of the planet look quite haunting.  You will often stumble upon a man or woman who made their final stand against the unholy denizens of this planet, caught in some pose of despair upon their knees.  I appreciate every moment of these scenes as it really helps add to the atmosphere of this game.  Something is most definitely wrong with this place and we need to get out of here quickly.  The map and UI is very functional and there are plenty of upgrades to keep you busy.  A variety of melee weapons that you can equip as well as a suit which has multiple modules that you can equip so long as you don't exceed your suits maximum power output.  This can be upgraded though so with time your suit is capable of taking on a much heavier workload and thus make you far more powerful.  Overall it's a souls like bonfire upgrade system which is tried and true, I won't complain about it.The sound is actually really exceptional in this game but I had to turn it off for one stupid reason.  The dash ability makes this horrendous screeching sound when you dash twice in a row (something you often will do) and I couldn't tolerate it for more than a few minutes.  I might just be too impatient but it's almost inexcusable given how excellent everything else is in this game.The UI is well done and you can quickly see where you are and where you need to go.  It's standard stuff I don't need to spend much time here.My final statement is about the minibosses.  I think this is where the game shines.  Every so often you will encounter a powerful hunter or enemy on the map in random areas who are really difficult to beat.  They will usually speak to you and in the process reveal a bit about the world we inhabit.  I enjoy this part of the game immensely.Anyway, try this game so far it puts these other sidescrolling souls like metroidvanias to shame.  I have a few gripes with it but overall I am enjoying the challenge immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game, binged it for 2 days straight. The environment, music, story, level designs, combat was all great. The only thing i wish it had ( which heck, might be in the game i just didnt find it, is a way to find the secret walls)Still 10/10, would recommend playing it blind, it is very fun to explore and find new things in the gameThanks for making it!

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my honest review, considering I've waited for this game's release for over 9 years:So to summarize:- art: 9/10, characters, enemies, environments, and effects are just mesmerizing,- UI: 3/10, the map is badly done, icons and texts are barely visible on small screens, I tried to play the game on SteamDeck, was forced to connect my gaming device to my TV just to not harm my vision,- Level design: 3.5/10, it does seem like the game's polishing is rushed, you also can tell that the developer had in mind some features, but they decided to skip those for the game's final release. My main complaint about level design is that it should've been done properly, it's either QA/testers have failed to properly test the project, or the developer didn't have time to fix all the issues.- voice acting: 6/10, though, unfortunately, voice acting cuts short, and 95% of the dialog is only text,- Sound effects 8/10,- Music: 8/10,- Dialogs: 7/10,- Narrative: 5.5/10the issues in more detail (may contain spoilers):- level design issue: you can shoot through the walls if you stay too close to the wall, also some enemies (i.e. with spears) can attack you even though the wall should've blocked the attacks,- level design issue: some obstacles in the air are not placed in a good way, so you might get stuck in some areas where you simply could've jumped from obstacle A to obstacle B, this does apply only when you start playing and your character doesn't have various abilities.- bug: if you try to visit the shop at the end of the game when you've collected all ship's core items, the shopkeeper will not be present, however, you still can purchase items, and the shopkeeper still will be talking with you.- bug: you can't click on the menu button (i.e. you want to exit the game) in-mid dialogs,- level design issue: game's difficulty is unbalanced, the beginning of the game is much more difficult than the rest of the game, basically it gets much easier when you progress the game, while there should be a balance. The punishing and the reward system is not correctly done as well. Sometimes you get special items from the corners of the world, sometimes you need to kill X amount of random enemies for the drop,- level design issue: there are some temporary boost items in the shop, I personally think the amount you can buy is very little, and the prices are exaggerated,- bug: I tried to revisit one of the bosses (a tiny goblin-like creature sitting on a skull), but unfortunately I couldn't fight with that boss due to the game wasn't triggering the fight's event and it let me just grab the reward,- level design issue: you can tell that game's leveling logic, i.e. collecting guns, abilities, and suit upgrades is poorly done, just as an example, do you really need to have 2 types of guns - green and red alien shooting, what purpose does it serve? ----------------------------- Would I recommend this game to my friends?No, unfortunately, I personally think that the game needed at least 2 months of testing/polishing.- Is the game worth $20?No, in its current state it's worth $10, after proper testing/polishing maybe $15,Considering that game have good art choice, music, and some interesting dialogs and characters, and considering that the game might be polished later, I won't rate this game "negatively" and will recommend trying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful layered 2D graphics and an engrossing atmosphere. Ghost Song may not be as action packed as some similar games, but I kind of prefer it that way. The world is creepy and mysterious, but also charming in a way that makes me want to avoid just blasting away and killing everything I see. As someone who enjoys immersive exploration, I'm definitely feeling satisfied just unraveling this game's many secrets. At $20 It feels like there is plenty of interesting content to keep you engaged for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful! Think run'n'gun/exploration like Metroid plus stat/equipment upgrades like Dark Souls all set in a beautifully detailed (yet creepy) alien atmosphere. If you like Metroid-like games, this is a definite grab! The artwork is wonderful! The music is fantastic and creepy! The sound effects were a bit too loud, but there is an easy fix for that! The sparse voice acting is perfect (and really creepy at times)! The controls are responsive and great! The story starts out intriguing enough to make me ask the questions: Who am I?  Why am I here? What is this place? and makes me want to explore every nook and cranny to find the answers.I haven't had any crashes or bugs crop up either (so far) on my modest and rapidly going out of date computer rig.Please note that a game controller is highly recommended. I'm using a PS3 controller and have had zero problems or complaints. Hopefully mouse and keyboard controls are refined at a later point, but if not, it is still a fantastic experience with a controller.Negatives?  I do feel like a few of the 2nd weapon modules are not useful and unnecessary so far,  but maybe that will change later in the game.  But the sheer amount and variety of them is high enough that I don't feel like it really detracts from the game.  Those modules that aren't useful, I just ignore.Overall a fantastic experience so far, hopefully it will continue to till the end!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this so far - excellent atmosphere (visuals/audio), interesting gameplay, and an intriguing world. I was worried from watching footage that controls might be pretty stiff but the controls feel quite good.Overall, so far would definitely recommend, particularly to those who like metroidvanias!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghost Song

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 6(7)/10A gorgeous metroidvania-meets-souls game with an incredible art style and a solid combat system that incentivizes varying your attacks for more damage, using heat from your shots to burn enemies with your melee attacks. The music is very subdued but fits the world excellently and sets the tone of the game well. As for the the negatives there is a lot of backtracking and running through sparsely populated rooms, as save points are few and far between, shortcuts even fewer, and fast travel stations fewer still. The main questline of the game gathers ship parts from the far reaches of the map, disabling fast travel while carrying a piece and not allowing you to carry multiple pieces at a time, which would not be so much of an issue not given the very few movement options and few overworld movement upgrades which do not give much reason to rediscover old areas because nothing new has changed or unlocked, paired with a very limited stamina system makes overall exploration not as fun as it could be.As a huge fan of Metroid games, Axiom Verge, and Hollow Knight, I can recommend it, but it doesnt shine as bright as many other games in the genre and would not recommend for people more iffy on the genre. It has the potential after being shined up and some of the more obnoxious gameplay elements possibly being changed to be a powerhouse of the genre with the art direction and bones that it has at its disposal.

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me say that I have kept track of this game since it was in it's very early stages of development and have supported it as much as I could and even played the Demo and hoped it would get a full release and my wish came true. This game is literally homage to 80's & early 90's Bounty Hunter/Cyberpunk Anime (Iria: Zeiram the Animation). The environments and graphics are just absolutely beautiful and a  treat to look at while exploring. The main character you play as "Deadsuit" is about as mysterious as you would expect but it goes great with the atmosphere that surrounds you and truly makes you curious enough to go places you wouldn't think twice about going. Deadsuit uses a Gunarm similar how Mega Man and Samus Aran fire their weapons and can jump and dash at will. The controls can't get anymore simple than this unless you don't have a controller. If you're playing this with a Keyboard then I highly suggest getting a controller as it was meant to be played. The game overall is definitely "Metroidvania" and will bring back that feeling that gamers fell in love with in the first place. Do yourself a favor and get this game, You won't regret it especially if you love 2-D action adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game for what feels like a decade, awesome responsive controls, awesome gameplay, quite challenging difficulty (relatively), great atmosphere, the soundtrack is very relaxing, the environments are wonderful, the bonus unexpected VA is a really nice touch, and the art is gorgeous! Still making my way to finish the game (just started today), and can't complain about anything thus far. If you're a metroidvania/sidesrcoller fan, this is a must have, definitely worth the mullah.

name: Armillo
detailed_description: Rock and roll your way through a colourful world in Armillo, a sci-fi-style rolling platformer. In a once-peaceful galaxy, invading Darkbot forces are cruelly capturing small, blue critters. Flying from planet to planet, help Armillo rescue them and take back his home: a series of spherical 3D worlds featuring all manner of obstacles and enemies. Your main weapon against the Darkbots is Armillo’s roll, which lets you navigate paths, dodging or wrecking anything in your way. Jump and boost your roll to destroy tougher enemies, or collect power-ups to gain special abilities. Along the way, solve cheeky puzzles and grab orbs, which you can spend on bolstering Armillo’s powers for improved Darkbot routing. And that’s something you’ll need, as you battle multi-stage bosses in their own worlds. Within every level, track down a hidden Parallel World, where you’ll be challenged to speed run through a 2D zone. You’ll need lightning reflexes and your best, old-school platforming skills in these special stages – especially as you’re pushed to beat each stage against the clock! With snappy action, vibrant graphics and puzzles to stretch your mind, Armillo is rolling to defeat the Darkbots in this riveting 3D platformer,

_childDocuments_.review: This is one very fun game experience!  And, I must say, of the hundreds and hundreds of games I've played in my time, it's one of the more noticeably unique experiences I've had. Well done! Fans of marble rolling games will undoubtedly find a lot to love here, as will fans of character-based platformers.  This could easily have been an exceptional title for a console, though I do appreciate that we PC gamers got it. I'm reminded somewhat of some of the real classic console platformers from the glory days of the genre in its 3D heyday, such as the legendary Rare library of titles as well as Crash and even Sonic; though they all play much differently from Armillo as well as from each other, it could slot right in along them and be comfortable and appreciated. Every level offers a number of new mechanics to learn and have fun with, and the bonus 'dark moon' levels between the main levels as well as the unlockable further bonus levels offer even more variation. The feel of rolling a balled-up space Armadillo through the increasingly intricate, twisty tracks and traps and tricks and enemy face-offs never (at least for me) starts to get old.  This game has been a wonderful surprise, coming as it did out of nowhere AND being currently free. I can't recommend it more. With so many titles available these days, it can be tempting to play a new title until it gets 'old' or something new and shiny comes along and then move along regardless of how much game there may still be left unseen and unplayed, but Armillo is an experience I want to stick with until there's no more left. Fantastic!
