_childDocuments_.review: Before anything, lemme tell you a small story, reader of this reviewThe game when released, to boost it's popularity, was released for free to be turned paid later. think one of the many Free2Keep deals out there, but placed right at the beginning of the game's lifebut turns out, they could not change it back. Thus it is free to this day. Why I am telling you this? You will seeFor now the game.At first as you boot it up you might notice that the UI welcoming you is... well nothing special to put it simply. but don't let that fool youThe game itself and it's gameplay is a mix between classic sonic, super mario galaxy and all that with pinball like physics. Somewhatit's hard to compare to anything specificbut what I can tell ya is that it works. the game is fun to play. The controls themselves are very basic, yet responsive, and most of the changes and challenges come in variety of things you find in different levels, such as powerups or stage hazards/mechanics. And there are secret levels that play in side scrolling 2D mode to mix things up too.The game is just nice to playVisuals are simplistic, about what you would expect from an Unity game, but made well. There is nothing you will find out of place as you playMusic, also, nothing spectacular, but does it's job very well to sell you whatever situation you are in right now, and thus fits everything well in the game tooSame goes for general sound design. It's just made right and it fells right as you playAgain, the only con I could bring up is the UI at places being a bit meh. In game as you play the HUD is good, but menus such as the pause menu or the file select screen look... ehbut that doesn't take away anything form the game itselfso go ahead and download it and try it outAnd if you do, here's the reason why I told you the story earlier:if you do play it and like it, consider helping the devs out. if you click on their name to see all their products, you will notice a "DLC" for this game is present here simply named "Support the Developers"it says up front that all it does is support the devs, and changes absolutely nothing in game. And you can't even see it anywhere on the page of the game itself, only to be found if you do what I saidand it's cheap too, being merely... I'm guessing 3.5$, as it was around 15zł for me (and to lazy to check rn). So go ahead. Give the devs a tip for the job well done if you think they deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a mixture of Sonic + 3D platformer + 3d Maze + Pinball + mini game puzzles like Soukoban and Memory game. And they seems to mix incredibly well together. Great job!The secret stages of the game goes into 2D platforming and it feels a lot like Sonic with those skills but the game play is pretty original and fun though. There's even a secret planet in 8-bit design to explore! :3The story is very simple but it's done in a very balanced and great story telling style. Making it very enjoyable.Beautiful Graphic, Nicely planned stages with quite the difficulty (seems like less than 10% players able to reach the ending), hidden secrets to explore, great music, even though the story is simple but it's done in a great story telling style, truly a masterpiece!The ending hint of a sequel, will surely look forward to it!

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterclass in game design. From its incredibly crafted worlds, to its deep lore, and engaging gameplay. You can really tell the amount of love and passion the developers have poured into this masterpiece. Armillo is ahead of it's time, and in the future, many games will surely follow in its footsteps. While the game may be free, these developers work very hard to give us the content we want. So if you have the means, please consider purchasing the Support the Developers DLC package for this game. It does not grant any actual content in the game, it is a way we can show the devs that we love what they make, and quite frankly, they deserve it. I've still barely scratched the surface of what Armillo has to offer, but I can't wait to engross myself in the endless content the devs had made for this game.Armillo has not only changed the way I look at games, it has changed the way I look at life.Thank you, Fuzzy Wuzzy Games Inc.You have shown me true art, and moved me to tear with this game.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I may be a bit biased, but when I first played this game on the Wii U 6 years ago, I was actually quite impressed with how varied and fun the level design was. It has a really nice gamefeel with the rolling, and the music, while not and OST, still fit its level very well and provided some amazing stuff to listen to while playing. My only real problem with the game is that the 2D levels have some weird floatiness to them, but they are still pretty fun. Regardless, I highly recommend you pick this game up, even after it is no longer free, as these devs do deserve your support. I think a sequel is very much deserved, and could fix the few issues that this game has.

_childDocuments_.review: This game from what I've played feels very fresh but at the same time has that classic vibe to it. The presentation is basic but not in a bad way, it reminds me of the old Playstation and Nokia ngage platformer style games and I am very happy to see that. The level design is pretty good and feels unlike anything I've played before. That's not to say that it doesn't bring in elements from other games like sonic and pinball but the way it's presented feels, as I mentioned before, fresh!Now, someone said that it has a lot of dialogue but from my experience it seems just fine and dialogue for the most part is well written and manages to set a tone similar to classic platformers, which I like. I do understand that it might not be for everyone. I wish the dev team all the success that they deserve and hope this game becomes more well known!

_childDocuments_.review: A WiiU Nintendo eShop game from 2015-now a free Steam game. 	Armillo is surprisingly decent for what it is. It has decent length to it; unlockables; 'hidden' levels. A plot with some twists. And the central game mechanic is an interesting blend of monkey ball with some speedier segments and light platforming. People call it a mix of Sonic with Mario Galaxy and Monkey Ball. Which is slightly misleading, but I get where it comes from. The dashing and speedier segments give it the Sonic comparison. It being in Space gets it the Mario Galaxy one.	It's still a game that is slightly rough. Setting up your controls is weird. The dialogue feels a bit rushed at points. The 2D levels are especially awkward to control. 	But despite all of that, it is surprisingly competent. The music is shockingly decent to good. Game itself looks good. Each level has a unique gimmick or new game mechanic. On the surface it looks like a budget game. Even in-game its not exactly a triple A production. But the developers really put in some effort in the areas that matter.	I'd pin this at the 10 dollar range if they were to put a price on it. If they can clean it up a bit, I'd definitely buy a sequel.	I'm not calling this a must-play, but if you do you'll be pretty shocked at how good it actually is.

_childDocuments_.review: silly cute rolling game. controls could be improved/touched up a bit, and there should be more visual feedback when taking damage. This game has a ton of heart. I recommend setting the startup parameter to match your resolution, as the game does not support >1080p by default. In steam, set the following as a launch parameter: -screen-height 1440 -screen-width 2560 (replace the numbers with your screen's resolution). Once I changed that, the visuals were actually quite nice for what the game's going for, there is a lot of funny and solid, if silly voice acting. There is a progression system and a reason to save your buddies, and the interface is actually quick and intuitive. Anything that could be confusing is thoroughly explained. I love this game more than I would have ever expected, hats off.

_childDocuments_.review: Armillo is essentially two games, one is an incredibly well-made top-down platformer, while the other is a barely functioning, frustrating side-scroller. Luckily, the majority of the side-scrolling content can be skipped.The good news is, the top-down levels have variety with just the right amount of challenge.Pros:✅Impressive soundtrack✅Charming worlds & characters✅Rewarding upgrade system ✅Free✅Shovel Knight Cameo (This is the most important part)Cons:❌The Side-scrolling levels are like if a college student was given a week to code a game from scratch, bad controls & even worse level-design. ❌I ran into a glitch where an item in the shop was purchased but it wasn't activated. Re-buying it fixed the issue. (This happened to be the most important item in the game which adds 30 seconds to side-scroller levels, I only discovered it was glitched after completing all but one level with a gold medal, I'm scarred for life)❌There's a giant eerie human face that haunts the background of certain levels (This is not a real con, its just spooky)

_childDocuments_.review: A fun cartoon 2D and 3D puzzle platformer which feels like it would have been a lot better with the original motion controls.  As it is, there’s something lacking.  It’s mostly light in challenge and isn’t particularly memorable or engaging, but the characters are cute, although the voice acting feels out of place, and the graphics are ok, if a bit basic and sometimes too dark.  Unfortunately, the awful jump/boost mechanic really brings this otherwise enjoyable and entertaining game down, especially in the 2D sections with it consistently not working or barely making an impact.  This makes the game far more frustrating than it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game quite unlike anything I've played before. The main levels play a lot like a top-down Sonic the Hedgehog (but they're actually good) with some Super Mario Galaxy sprinkled in, while the bonus levels are hard-as-nails 2D platforming. The game does have something of a learning curve, though, and don't expect any handholding. You're given the option of starting files in easy (three base hp) or normal (two base hp) mode; I'd recommend easy mode just on principle because of just how tough the game gets in its later (and bonus) levels.If you like cute, tough platformers, snap this one up right away! It's free, so you have no excuse!

_childDocuments_.review: More of an encouragement blue thumb. is a chill, casual platformer. The game clearly feels like an indie game, with a quite simple gameplay and a very predictable level design, unfortunately not taking advantage of the spherical maps to bring anything special. The first 30 minutes are plain boring, but the game gets more interesting beyond that. There is always a bit of challenge for completionists, like unlocking and beating all 2D levels, but other than that the game hardly lasts longer than 5 hours.Well, not complaining there, the game is for free which is an excellent initiative. Simply don't expect anything out of ordinary, simply a nice little casual entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great! Pros:- Very unique. I fell in love with it right away.- Pretty tight controls. The blast jump isn't perfect in the 2D levels, but you get used to it.- Lots of surprises! The game is full of unlockables, secrets, and new gimmicks on stages.- Difficulty curve is perfect. I never felt bored or unchallenged.Cons:- The graphics are great, but some areas were too dark so I wasn't always sure about where I was going or where the boundaries were.- It would be nice if we knew how many orbs there were on each stage. _childDocuments_.review: Armillo is a great 3D platformer and controlling the character feels good when travelling across the "planets". I do like the look of this game as well, but I disliked one thing about this game.The 2D levels made me feel that I was fighting against the controls rather than the levels themselves. You can only double jump in these 2D levels, but the response time for the second jump felt awkward. I did overall enjoy completing the game 100%, so with this in mind, I would encourage people to check out this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The endearing modest-frills 90's style graphics and menus are part of a very creative and playable platformer/roller. Each level seems to offer a new style of challenge and the difficulty curve is very nicely handled - helped along with timely upgrades and fairly spaced out checkpoints. At numerous points Armillo's level design had me thinking of Sonic and Mario [Galaxy] - fine comparisons for any action game.My only criticism is that I found some of the shading to be very dark and this hindered visibility somewhat. This is a very minor point, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Armillo

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, when I opened this game for the first time, I got goosebumps upon hearing the music and seeing the map of planets. There is a very nostalgic feel to the game, it reminds me of Xbox/PS2 era games. The game itself is fantastic, especially for a free one (at time of review). I have just finished the first world, and each level has been a good challenge, fun without being punishing. The mix of platforming and puzzles works seamlessly too. Also, Armillo is a very cute character, which is a win in my books. Do yourself a favour and get this game. You won't regret it.I may update this review when I have finished the game.(It would be really cool to see the soundtrack online too!)

_childDocuments_.review:
Rolling Platforming Game. Sci-fi parallel Universe theme. Massive amount of gameplay elements.

Armillo is a unique, fun rolling platforming game with a sci-fi parallel universe theme. It features a massive amount of gameplay elements. For one, there is the regular 3D world, followed by a bonus stage on the moon. Then there is the evil parallel universe, and special 2D speed-run inspired worlds. Lots of unexpected deadly twists, and surprises await! The star of the game features a space armadillo named Armillo. He's not your usual armadillo as he's capable of blasting off to space in order to travel from planet to planet. He's joined by his little blue critter friends and his brother. What's supposed to be a peaceful galaxy becomes ruined by the invasion of the robotic Darkbots. Where are they from? Why are they here? But one thing is for sure, they certainly are not the friendly type.

name: Black Mesa
detailed_description: Join Our Community About the Game Relive Half-Life Black Mesa is the fan-made reimagining of Valve Software’s Half-Life . Black Mesa: Definitive Edition Update 1.5 brings together all the improvements to graphics and gameplay across 15 years of development to create the final version of Black Mesa. There has never been a better time to pick up the crowbar and play! Single Player Campaign You are Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist at the Black Mesa Research Facility. When a routine experiment goes horribly wrong, you must fight your way through an interdimensional alien invasion, and a bloodthirsty military clean-up crew in order to save the science team... and the world! Features A completely reimagined and refined single player campaign, including all new and expanded Xen levels 19 chapters of fighting through top-secret labs, running atop harsh desert landscapes, sneaking into abandoned railways, and leaping across dimensions Mind-Blowing graphics and effects, never before seen on the Source Engine Face off against an army of classic enemies, updated with new features and engaging AI Wield an arsenal of military hardware, scientific prototypes, and the iconic crowbar through incredibly detailed environments The all-new soundtrack and voice acting create a more immersive experience than ever before 50 Fun and challenging achievements Multiplayer Frag your friends across 10 iconic maps from the Half-Life universe, including: Bounce Gasworks Stalkyard Undertow Crossfire Workshop Create your own mods, models, and maps with the Black Mesa Source SDK, then share it with the community on the Steam Workshop. Steamworks Collect the full set of trading cards, backgrounds, emoticons, and achievements! Featuring Steam Cloud, Steam Workshop, closed captions in multiple languages and full controller support.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever made ascended to even a better masterpiece. You can feel all the true love and effort Crowbar Collective have put to make this a never-forget experience. From the deepest dark corridors of Black Mesa to the alien misterious enviroments of Xen you will go through a thousand marvelous gaming experiences, some of them ones of the best I have ever had thanks to the combination of momentum and soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: There are a ton of detailed reviews on this already and I don't really have much more to add for them, other than to say this is without question, the definitive way to play Half-Life 1. Xen is still way too long (but that's in keeping with the original and they wanted to adhere to that vision) but the quality of life improvements they made to that section of the game make it far more enjoyable than it was originally. They've also managed to take what is basically a 16 year old engine at this point and make it so some really gorgeous things, particularly with exterior environments and lighting.This took 15 years to come out but given the size of the team and that it started as a mod, I can certainly see why. This team is very talented and absolutely deserves support. Very much enjoyed this.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: The experience of playing this game is abseloutely wonderfull. One of the best story games i've ever played. I have not played the origional HL1, but i feel like the experience i had playing this game is the same that people would have had when HL1 was first realeased. Truly a game worth buying and playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa's level designs are equal parts faithful and refreshing. They pick Half-Life's highs and subdue it's lows.Would be the perfect re-master if the combat wasn't so different. Enemies like the HECU Grunts seem much more aggressive than in Half-Life, and some of the weapons like the crossbow function a little differently.I wouldn't recommend Balck Mesa as a replacement for Half-Life 1, but rather an addition. Black Mesa is best experienced having played the original as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking "this is just a re-make of half-life" then re-think yourself cause it's amazing what Crowbar Collective made here... Every single piece of this game was lovely, buy it just to thank the developers for the huge work behind this masterpiece.Sound: 9/10 (Wonderful music placed meticulously where needed)Gameplay: 8/10 (A revisited version of the original, basic mechanics are the same tho)Graphics: 7/10 ()Optimization: 6/10 (A bit heavy for what it brings on the table)Just a note here,  felt a bit unpolished but in the end it was one of my best gaming experiences so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Many players of Black Mesa will have of course played Half-Life and I am no exception. Black Mesa does a very good job of sticking to the source material in many places, although I feel that Xen stretched it very close to being just a brand new alien world. But given the circumstances of the original Half-Life's Xen, a reimagining was in order (As well as Xen still being in beta at the time of this review.)The soundtrack by Joel Nielsen is absolutely incredible. It shines no matter what track it is, from Surface Tension to Questionable Ethics, all the way to Transcendent (The first track in Xen).The weapons feel really close to their Half-Life counterparts minus some balancing changes. The voice acting goes from just above average to incredible, some of the actors really fill their role perfectly, while others seem to be giving it a pretty good go. I understand that this is merely a fan project, but some lines could certainly be redone.All in all, I personally recommend anyone who hasn't already to play the original Half-Life before trying Black Mesa out. While it is an incredible piece of work, understanding the source material helps a lot as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original Half-Life, I was excited to play this remake. From the very start Black Mesa captures the distinctive Half-Life gaming experience. It is easy to see that a lot of care and attention has been put into making Black Mesa not only an accurate remake, but an impressively upgraded game in terms of graphics, sound and stability.At the time of writing this, the end alien levels have yet to be made, but even so, it is still a fun and worthwhile endeavour. It goes without saying that if you are a fan of the original, then Black Mesa is a game you really should have in your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't get away with the original, too dated. This was perfect. Brought the first Half-Life game up to the standards of the second, if not better in some cases. If you want to visit the first Half-Life story, absolutely play this game. If anything it's made me crave a third game even more. The crowbar collectives effort should be applauded.

_childDocuments_.review: "Gordon Freeman, in the flesh – or, rather, in the hazard suit. I took the liberty of relieving you of your weapons. Most of them were government property. As for the suit, I think you've earned it. The borderworld, Xen, is in our control, for the time being … thanks to you. Quite a nasty piece of work you managed over there, I am impressed. That's why I'm here, Mr. Freeman. I have recommended your services to my … employers, and they have authorised me to offer you a job. They agree with me that you have limitless potential. You've proved yourself a decisive man so I don't expect you'll have any trouble deciding what to do. If you're interested, just step into the portal and I will take that as a yes. Otherwise, well … I can offer you a battle you have no chance of winning; rather an anticlimax after what you've just survived. Time to choose …Wisely done Mr. Freeman! I will see you up ahead."

_childDocuments_.review: They screwed up the details, but what is left is a beautiful reimagining of the original Half-Life game mostly true to its part. Half-Life 1 was a master piece and in Black Mesa this continues. If you want the original experience buy Half-Life 1, but if you want Half-Life brought to a modern age this is a must buy especially since the weaker part is remade from scratch making it fresh even for hardened fans. On a Rail has been cut down, but if you like me rather have the original experience look for On a Rail uncut on the workshop before you play a campaign and it will be given back to you.

The puzzles, the platforming, the combat, all accompanied by gorgious graphics and a very atmospheric, melancoly soundtrack, help to really capture the feeling of being a lone theoretical physicist off to undo the horrors of an experiment gone wrong.Edit: After playing through Xen, I can't help but praise the game more! Truly an outstanding acheivement that I had the honour to play through! Thank all you creators for the outstanding job you did!

The remake of the classic Half Life 1 is much better than the original game (especially the Xen part) and is what Half Life : Source should have been. _childDocuments_.review: Nothing can really reproduce the feeling I had the first time I played Half-Life, because I can never experience it in the same context. It was the first shooter I played - really, one of the first ever made - that departed from the linear, repetitive structures (both narrative and gameplay) of its predecessors. Games like Wolfenstein 3D or Doom were fantastic in their own right, but no one had yet quite imagined a first-person shooter could be as imaginative or immersive in its worldbuilding and storytelling as a role-playing game, or have a level design that felt open and connected even as it funneled you into each new chapter.So as groundbreaking as Half-Life was - both as a new kind of game and as the then-height of 3D graphics, it was also a centerpiece of an important part of my childhood, among those years that decide a large part of who you are as a person. Had I not played Half-Life back then, would I even play video games now? I remember being filled with a hunger that first time I destroyed the Nihilanth, only to be whisked away aboard a transdimensional tram car, to hear the G-Man's cryptic offer - the kind of hunger you felt when you finished one of your favorite books or movies for the first time and somehow subconsciously knew you were going to be searching for more of the same even as you return to it dozens of times.So when I tell people about "that game" I know the hype and probably reverence in my voice is suggesting an experience they may never find in it, and I try to downplay it and keep my focus on the gameplay and the story, and make excuses for the graphics and the context that time as sadly surpassed. Because Half-Life, great as it is, can never be what it was. But Black Mesa comes as close as possible to that memory - it genuinely *feels* like Half-Life, even where changes were made for graphical, physical or aesthetic reasons. In other words, It's what everyone thought or wished they were getting back in 2004 when Valve released Half-Life: SourceUPDATE 1/1/2020: tl;dr I had a lot of fun but boss battles (especially Gonarch) need some re-workI have since finished playing the new Xen chapters, and I have to say I am quite impressed. The original Xen was one of the weaker parts of Half-Life - still good, but not nearly as memorable as Office Complex or On A Rail or Surface Tension. In Xen, Crowbar Collective have truly made the game their own, while still providing that essential Half-Life feel. It starts off a lush and immersive alien world, with some unique puzzles and some enjoyable combat. The later chapters, especially Interloper, show the alien society in more detail, with friendly Vortigaunt slaves that won't attack (And even sometimes help) without a Controller around, and the Grunt factory feels so much more like a factory than its predecessor.As you get closer you can actually see the final portal looming in the distance, and the closer you get the more the enemy attacks force you to stay on your toes, punishing you as much for hesitating as for making the wrong choice.The final battle with Nihilanth was really enjoyable - even though it didn't have the jump pads and portals of the original, it had the pacing and patterns that make a boss battle a fun challenge - though I did have my fair share of complaints.First, there were several points throughout Xen where I was ready to move on to the next part, but couldn't, because there were just a few too many puzzles. Rather, the puzzles could be repetitive at times. I would clear one area by solving a puzzle, only to encounter almost the same puzzle - and since I now knew how to solve it, it just felt like extra steps. Also, the level design on Interloper, specifically the factory areas, felt a little... empty. Not that it wasn't a massive improvement on the original, but coming from the dense and vibrant environments of Xen and Gonarch's Lair, it's hard not to make a comparison and find it lacking.Also, the boss battles: They are hard. And not just Nintendo hard or Dark Souls hard. The key to good, challenging gameplay that rewards the player is to make sure that anytime the player dies they can figure out exactly why, and learn not to do that in the future. Don't hold the player's hand, necessarily - they still need to figure out how everything goes together, but (especially in boss battles) attacks should be patterned/telegraphed or otherwise either predictable, or survivable, and weak points should be identifiable. Random chance can factor into the fight, but not to such an extent that it will entirely make or break an attempt by the player.Nintendo knows this, and FromSoftware knows this, and that is why in the same instance as their games are known to be extremely difficult, they have been totally and repeatedly mastered by people who took the time to learn all the mechanics. Crowbar Collective are obviously mostly dedicated gamers, and they definitely have an idea what a good boss battle should be, but they just barely missed the mark with Gonarch and (to a lesser degree) Nihilanth.The issue with Gonarch is simpler, but with a greater impact. The first fight is alright, as the terrain provides enough cover that she can be kited around between attacks and going to the healing pool which she can only reach with one of her two ranged attacks. I beat the first fight in Hard mode having only died two or three times. The second fight, however, is an enclosed space with a single column in the center for cover, no heals except for what arrives in two supply pods, and damaging spike hazards spread out across the walls. Gonarch's attacks are random, not very well telegraphed, and in some cases purely unavoidable. Because on hard mode she requires damn near all the rocket ammo in the supply bins to be beaten, she will always at some point start her chase attack (different from the charge, which is telegraphed and if you dodge she will hit a wall and stun herself) and often times will get stuck in the same mode until you die. You cannot outrun her except with boost jumps, you will almost always run out of boost before she stops chasing, and you cannot dodge or kite because there is no cover and she can turn on a dime. You may survive getting hit once or twice by this attack, but you will get flung into the wall, and if you hit one of the spiky parts you'll take even more damage and get slowed coming out as she's attacking you again.On top of this, the pieces of debris that fall from overhead at the start of the fight, which the Gonarch flings at the player with one of her attacks - are just a little too tall to jump over reliably, and they often get in the way of a boost jump and stop you in your tracks. If you don't see them and/or do not boost at the absolute apex of your jump, you'll just stop, not far from where you started, most likely still in the path of whatever attack you were trying to dodge.There is simply nothing about the Gonarch fight which can be learned to make the battle more winnable - you simply need to both get really lucky with the attacks she chooses on top of never once making a mistake, and after hours (an entire night of playing) of losing the fight, I changed the difficulty to Normal - something I have only ever done rarely in 25 years of gaming, and not at all recently - and won the fight on my first try.I've seen discussions where people say that those unable to beat the Gonarch need to simply "get good" or "put more time into it" and I am convinced that, though they won't admit it, they're bragging about nothing more than the sheer luck or time they were able to throw at the fight.The Nihilanth fight was much easier - still hard, but its mechanics were mostly learnable. I do wish I did not die to nothing, go flying in the air seemingly randomly, or spend hours shooting missiles on the final stage when all I had to do was hit it with the Gluon.tl;dr Great game, Xen rocks, fix Gonarch

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa may hands down be the best way to introduce someone to Half-Life series.Reimagined Half-Life 1 on the source engine doesn't just try to redo what has already been made but also bring it to a more modern standard which is a lot more approachable for new players. They've removed what were arguably the worst aspects of Half-Life 1 and fine tuned what it got right. Players are less likely to get lost in these levels or get stuck solving puzzles which in the past made simple sections frustrating to complete.Black Mesa bridges the gap between the events of Half-Life 1 and 2 in a way that a new player can understand while also working perfectly as a standalone experience if you're not interested in other Half-Life games.Everyone should play this at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a lot I could say that hasn't already been said, Its Half-Life 1 reimagined in more modern standards, and it's done with a lot of love and respect for the original material. One thing I would like to say that I don't see being talked about enough is how amazing the soundtrack is, this fan-made game has one of the best OST's I've ever listened to in any game, period. The highlights have to go for Blast Pit 3, Forget About Freeman and all of the songs on Xen, loved the guitars and piano across the whole thing, Joel Nielsen did a superb job here

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing remake of the original Half-Life game. The soundtrack, voice acting, combat, characters/enemy's and places in the game is amazing, beautiful and doesn't remove those awesome feelings you get as you did in Half-Life, its smooth and feels great to walk/run around and shoot. The enemy's in this game is not easy to kill (it depends on what difficulty level you are on) and that will give you a challenge through out the campain. Everything fits perfect in the remake and doesn't disappoint at all. If you have ever played Half-Life and likes it or love it then i recommend this 100% to you. The multiplayer is also lots of fun and feels like those classic deathmatch you love or loved. The Developers have been working so much on this game for around 10 years and its worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Well I just "finished" Black Mesa, the graphically improved version of the original Half-Life, and I have to say I was very impressed! Not only is the game Graphically enhanced but the voice lines are all redone and it really is a new game consisting mostly of new textures with a few pulled from HL2, there's also a variety of new npc models made exclusively for Black Mesa. They even included unique models specifically for Dr. Kliener and Eli Vance as their models for HL2 were originally based off the 2 or 3 models for scientists in the original.Although, you might be wondering why I put "finished" in air quotes and that's because the game isn't actually 100% completed yet, they have everything done up until you go into the portal to get to the Borderworld of Xen. Once you go into the portal you get a message saying the assignment has been postponed as they're gathering more research. Essentially what they're saying is that it's not done yet but once it's finished it will be added to the game free of charge!However even without Xen the game is a fantastic deal! It really helps bring the original Half-Life into the modern age of gaming whilst staying true to the story and game play of the original! As a result I can whole heartedly recommend Black Mesa to anyone who would like to revisit the original Half-Life or to anyone who has never played Half-Life but would like to try it out and find out the origin of the series!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely at least as good as the original, but more modern - somewhat better graphics, and a physics system (which is not nearly as relevant as in Half-Life 2, but they did go somewhat overboard in that, hehe.)As of 26/05/2018, the last 1/8th or the game is not finished, and there are a few things that may be polished up in the future - the only significant thing being the fact that the Vortigaunts sometimes can't attack effectively because their attack is blocked by guard rails (which does little to block bullets, making these encounters sometimes too easy). And while it's obviously a "recreation" of Half-Life 1, they have put a ton of effort into improving some of the levels... Much, if not most, of the game is so reminiscent of the original that you might not notice the differences, while some areas are significantly visually different, and a few are different in gameplay terms - mostly, in my view, for the better. Black Mesa does include quite a few characters with unique audio that I don't remember from Half-Life 1, and a few of the jokes are slightly raunchy, so I think they're original to Black Mesa. The quality of the voice-over is impeccable. Overall, I highly recommend playing this game, either as a replacement for Half-Life, or for the memories, or just because it's a pretty good game. Judged by a modern standard, or the post-Half-Life 2 episodes, a soulless, mindless game critic could sneer at many aspects of the game, but we're not soulless, mindless players. We actually liked Half-Life 1, and Black Mesa is definitely living up to its namesake.I hope Valve throws some assets at these guys to get them to make Half-Life 3. ;) Valve is running out of excuses!!

Health/suit recharges and ammo should have probably been more scarce throughout the game and that's about it, if you're thinking of buying this game, think no more and start playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a rare thing when I choose to actually play the campaign of a first-person shooter three times within the space of a couple of months because I couldn't stop thinking about it. I thought it was just nostalgia and yeah, that contributed in the first play through but I went through the second and third times simply because I enjoyed the game. It's just so damned good! It keeps all the vital elements of the original game; the puzzles, the action, the set pieces, the story and its ever expanding stakes and expands on them - it's big and bold. And while it's can't be said to be original since it's a remake of Half-Life- this isn't a simple remake, this is probably the most imaginative remake (a re-imagining?),  I've ever played.The original was criticised for the Xen levels since compared to the rest of the game they felt rushed, bland and less detailed but I'm happy to report that on the subsequent play-through's I  looked forward to getting there. Your introduction to "Xen" is glorious, and gives you the sense that this is place where the xeno's thrive in the wild, and where scientists came, set up camp, observed and gathered specimens way before things went south... In the original game "Interloper", the penultimate level before the battle with the main antagonist was remarkable in one regard: It was a long boring slog in unimaginative arenas which served no way to drive the story. In Black Mesa, yes, it's still long, but it reinforces the idea that the thing that you are in is this massive bio-engineered factory used to build more bio-weapons and that its a place of research and science. The puzzles are stream lined the battles are tough but its well paced and I enjoyed the verticality.Crowbar Collective and all the developers who contributed to this masterpiece deserve all the success and credit they get and AAA developers really need to take a look at this and ask themselves whether they do the industry and the FPS genre, easily the most accessible game genre, justice when they ship their 8-level, 6 hour (If you're lucky) lack-lustre campaigns. The original half-life came out in 1998, with the sequel two years later. I would defy you to suggest that FPS's have moved on since then because as far as I can tell the only thing that's been added is quick-time event and unimaginative stories.  It's genuinely the best FPS I've played since probably Doom 2016 and easily the best remake I've played this year. It's simply  that good.This is a classic FPS in the best possible style, a monument to one of the biggest games in history and stands testament to what FPS's can be. It's more than worthy of your cash at a mere £15.Glorious!

_childDocuments_.review: I got Black Mesa sometime way back around 2012, with the original mod build. Then, when it went to a full-fledged game, I bought it instantly to support the developers because I love Half-Life, and I'd wanted to see something like this happen for so long. I played the game here and there for a year or two but never more than 30 minutes at a time because I really, REALLY wanted to wait for Xen.Then it came: Xen. Crowbar Collective have made the game whole. It's time to finally play it.As of writing, I'm only 3 to 4 hours in, but it's such a great game so far. It gives you Half-Life in a newer, shinier wrapper and for you to open up and enjoy.Half-Life, and the sequel episodes, are my favorite game franchise of all time. From the time I first played it in 1998, I was hooked on it. If you're as big a Half-Life fan as I am, pick up your crowbar and get this game.They're waiting for you, Gordon, in the test chamber...

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life 1 is a classic but very flawed game now when you consider the advancements in technology. Many of the puzzles feel strange and archaic and I found myself relying heavily on online guides, but this fan made remake seems to eliminate any issues. Just by exploring the environment and trial and error, I've been able to understand the solve the puzzles here and the newer graphics look downright beautiful. Xen isn't out and probably won't be out for quite a while, but what is here is very satisfying and great. If you want to play Half Life but can't get over the graphics or have some issues with either combat or the puzzle solving, try this version.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this to be done for nearly 15 years. That's a pretty long time, and usually with projects like that, you end up with the Duke Forever effect. Too much time, too much change, leading to a bad product. Half-life is one of my favourite games of all time, so I waited with anticipation, waiting to see if we got another DNF.Not this time. Crowbar Collective have collectively NAILED this entire project. The earth-side parts of the mod have been released for a while. They are great - pared down in some areas that needed it, trimming the excess fat. Other areas expanded and re-shaped to better show the Black Mesa Research Facility at its finest.Xen, however, is not entirely like that. The entire chapter has been taken apart, and then the best parts of that have been moulded into a huge new chapter, far bigger than the original Half-Life chapter, far more than some meagre jumping puzzles and oddly shaped rooms. It's complex, winding, introducing new mechanics not seen in Half-Life at all, and the beautifully crafted levels give a real sense of scale and credibility to the entire Xen dimension. This is a masterpiece, and I would not have been upset to have paid a full £30-40 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful rewritten story of Half-Life!!! I remember having spent hours and hours on Half-life, driven by the story! But all together bring us to a wonderful story, a marvellous adventure! :DMy surprise was mostly when I discovered the new part of the Half-Life world, Xen! Xen, is really a success! It is rare when I feel some deep emotions in game. Xen was so beautiful and dangerous at the same time that it succeed to trigger a deep emotion of wonder in me!I rarely put some comments and appreciations on games! But this one deserves a big positive one and a big "bravo"!!Well, there still are some little bugs like being stuck in automatic doors when you stay on it when it is closing up; or some sudden crash during heavy graphic moments. But in my global experience, those bugs were minor compared to the enjoyable moments into the game.Maybe the crowbar team will fix all of them one day! ;)Good job guys!! And what a wonderful creative set! Keep going on! ;) :D

_childDocuments_.review: Having been introduced into the Half-Life franchise by HL:Alyx, I decided to finally experience the rest of the franchise. I wanted to get a complete understanding of the games' origins, I decided to play both the original HL and its remake.With both under my belt, I can safely say that Black Mesa is, in my opinion, the definitive way to play HL1. That's not to say that the original is bad. Far from it. It's very easy to see why people still love it and its importance to gaming history,However, having experienced it with more recent eyes, I can say that it hasn't aged well. BM takes what makes the original good, throws in a few spices, and cleans up it's rough edges. The two are somewhat different experiences, so I still encourage a playthrough of both games, but if you MUST choose between one version of the game to play, this one is easily the best way to experience one of gaming's giants. Great remake and the team should be proud.Post game edit: This game was, simply put, a masterpiece. This and HL: Alyx have cemented me as a fan.

_childDocuments_.review: So good. Sooooo good. Even without Xen this game is 10/10. Plays just like the original Half-Life with a few things changed for convenience. Vortigaunts are no longer instant hits when they can see you as they lock into the direction they shoot, grenades handle like proper physics objects instead of weird lumps, the crowbar still swings insanely fast, so many good changes.Ladders are still awkward to use, marines and snarks have pretty ridiculous damage outputs, there are still a handful of instakill annoyances, and a few sections are missing for some reason (like the area with the marine on the missile launcher in On a Rail or the Tentacle and helicopter bit in Surface Tension). Even with the exclusion of a few parts, it never feels like something is missing. Everything else is amazing. Graphics, gameplay, story, 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a remake of the original Half Life with new mechanics but still retaining that nostalgia feel; and with Xen in public beta i can fully review Black Mesa with very little criticism. It should be obvious to any and all gamers; but for those who don't know the story. You are Gordon Freeman a scientist running late to a big science experiment obviously with premises involving science experiments you know that it's going to go wrong and sure it enough it does. The Cascade Event crippled the entire facility and cutting off members of Black Mesa staff as they are hunted down and killed by not only aliens from the border world of Xen but a military cleanup crew. Armed with your wits a basic loadout and the infamous crowbar you must resolve this disaster before it's too late! If you know the original Half Life game then you would know it involves platforming and puzzle solving while gunning down hostiles. The game incorporates stamina and more alternate fire options. The game also has multiplayer as well...While the game still retains the nostalgia feel. They added and changed a few things like for instance female scientists, a Eli Vance model and other things that should be obvious once you come across them. The audio for this game is simply amazing! While giving the gun sounds a new look; i think to be completely honest the soundtrack is the best thing ever. The composer did a brilliant job and sure enough i bet you will have a few Black Mesa OST in your playlist. The visual overhaul (obviously) is breathtaking. Truly breathtaking especially when you get to Xen. You will feel a sense of nostalgia but have a sense dread and eeriness and not to mention that science fictional edge. I think we can all recall how disappointing Xen when we first traverse it back in 1998. Just random boring assets thrown together and a lack of a "science outpost" because heck you would think a base would be there to some extent right? And not to mention survey equipment, etc. Well prayers are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ answered with the public beta test of Xen and Gonarch's lair with obviously more to come. The world of Xen truly feels alien and look a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ research outpost with zombies in HEV suits! I can't described just how breathaking, beautiful the world of Xen is. And with more to come before the finale i can't wait for what they have in store next! Just be aware this is in public testing so don't fret if the levels are buggy and glitchy. They are working hard on it. Glitchy and stuttering, with random crashes every now and then.For a remake of a classic game that VALVE REFUSES TO DO THEMSELVES! LET ALONE FINISH THE TITULAR SERIES! The remake still retains the nostalgia feel and a new breath of fresh air that fans will enjoy it's not only worth the asking price but at anytime a sale comes up!

_childDocuments_.review: This is . There are many aspects that remain faithful to its inspiration, but there's also plenty both in a balancing and narrative sense that are different. Make sure you go into this with the right expectations. - - - -1) : Excellent visual direction. The style is recognizable-yet-distinct, and attentive to detail without getting bogged down or becoming overly busy. 2) : Soundscape and music were on point. Immersive during moments of intrigue, and exciting during moments of intensity.3) : The pacing and level design is (mostly) good. Marked improvements on platforming, consistently full of places to explore and things to discover. 4) : Black Mesa's weapons sandbox is about what you'd expect from a Half-Life title: simple in a way that lends itself well to thought and creativity. 5) : The A.I is fairly par for the course, capable but prone to janky decision-making. Still more than sufficient for keeping combat moving, and for making each encounter interesting. 1) : Being a work of passion from an extremely small team, the game has a few glitches. Most of them are more a mild inconvenience, but during my playthrough I did encounter a gamebreaking issue that forced me to reload a save. I'd hardly consider this a noteworthy obstacle to play, but it is noticeable and you will most likely encounter odd behavior every now and again. 2) : While this point squarely belongs in the 'pros' section, there is a point towards the end of the campaign where the game really peters out, resorting to repetitive ideas that grow stale very quickly. This section can, as a result, feel drawn-out in a bad, not to mention obvious way. Lastly, there are more subjective aspects. How's the game's replayability? Good, I'd say. It's a Half-Life inspired title, so you be the judge. How does Black Mesa stand up to the original Half-Life? While the former does invite comparisons, I prefer to look at both games as different creative works. As above, you be the judge. Overall, I'd recommend this game without a wink of regret. Black Mesa is a worthwhile experience and a refreshing take on a style of game that has largely (and criminally, imho) fallen out of popularity. (Also, the Xen redesign was incredible. Such a fantastic use of an idea that was always brimming with potential.)

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is phenomenal, with a few quirks and very few legitimate complaints. As a fan of the original Half-Life (warts and all), I have to say I felt right at home in this excellent remake.The visuals are nothing short of stunning, the HL2 engine is pushed to its absolute limits and everything looks crisp, detailed and in general you can tell there has been a LOT of love poured into the visual aspect of things. Especially Xen. Xen is so incredibly oozing with style it's... I can't really put it into words you just have to see it for yourself.In terms of sound, I'm also impressed. The sound design in general is also top-notch, great weapon sounds (especially the Gluon Gun, wow), pumping action tracks, cool ambient music.The story is largely left intact (save for the two marines that capture Freeman, that was a bit of a strange departure), so I won't waste words on it. Moving on.The gameplay carries over very well. The aliens behave more or less identically to the original. The marines are relentless, even more so than in HL1, and some areas are the cheap kind of difficult as a result, but overall, I enjoyed the action-packed middle section of the game, it felt a lot more natural than in the original. That said, I could've sworn the MP5 had 50 rounds, that the pistol wasn't so strong, that the shotgun had a faster rate of fire and so on - so in the weapons department, some things feel different, but not in a way that I'd say they feel "off" or "worse. You just have to get used to it.The maps (save for Interloper, more on that shortly) are just amazing as well. I can't get over how well they managed to expand upon the ideas in the original with a tweak here and there to make the whole thing even more palpable, tangible and flowing super-smoothly. Black Mesa in Anomalous Materials feels a lot more teeming with life, the survival horror is soup-thick thanks to the excellent lighting and layout of the first third of the game, Surface Tension and Forget About Freeman are awesomely brought to life, On a Rail is shorter (yay), Lambda Core and Xen are amazing too, just nothing but good things to say, again.Any negatives, then...? Well... not really, no. I didn't have any performance drops, bugs, I had the odd ragdoll spaz-out but that happened in HL2 as well, nature of the beast etc. The weapon and story departures aren't significant enough to make up a worse experience. The only thing that really ticked me off was Interloper. That map was tedious to begin with and for some arcane reason, they decided to stretch it out even more. The whole organic factory shtick grows old really, really fast and all the puzzles are just a variation on the same thing over and over again, just... annoying, is the word I'm looking for. The initial vista, the Vortigaunts and the crystals powering the Gluon Gun were nifty and all but other than that, it's just utterly forgettable platforming with some hasty combat sections.All in all, if you haven't played Half-Life one and graphics are what is putting you off, well, no more excuses for you! If you played and loved the original, you'll love this as well (and hate Interloper even more). Win-win. Limitlessss potential!

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is an unbelievable game that I've followed since its very humble beginnings as a Half-Life 2 mod. The developers over at Crowbar Collective are some of the hardest workers I have ever heard of, not even mentioning the perfectionist attitude they bring to the scene. I waited so long to give this game a review because frankly, I had to see Xen for myself. I had to  that this was a worthy remaster of the original Half-Life game.I was wrong. It was not a worthy remaster. It was To call Black Mesa a simple "remaster" of Half-Life is a crime. Every aspect of Half-Life, whether it's the movement, the graphics, the , or the combat, is taken into careful consideration by the developers. They take these aspects and rework them in a way that translates beautifully to a game that holds up to modern titles. Black Mesa is one of few titles where you can wholeheartedly say that the developers behind the scenes are extremely passionate about their work, and that they come from a long history of making and playing games like Half-Life.From the surface , Black Mesa may appear to be simply remaking what Half-Life was by copying the level design and reimplementing it into an updated engine with better graphics, but the devs take creative liberties that feel exactly like Valve itself came back to redevelop Half-Life. Veterans of the Half-Life franchise will find themselves in a world that is all too familiar, yet still new and enjoyable to play, giving them a wonderfully nostalgic feeling that persists throughout the game.Weird, clunky level design that was occasionally seen in levels from the original game are taken and rebuilt from the ground up in Black Mesa, providing a very consistent gameplay experience that is new and fresh, yet still distinctly Half-Life. We'll get to Xen in a second.Gameplay mechanics seen in Half-Life 2 are placed into the original Half-Life world, allowing the player to sprint. There is no zoom feature as seen in HL2, but rest assured that your favorite Half-Life weapons still have their zoom features. Another small note, flashlights don't have a limited battery. I thought this was a bit of a weird change that some players may find too easy, but the levels are typically well-lit and the use of a flashlight is typically unnecessary; it's more of a convenience than anything. The long-jump ability seen in HL has been reworked to provide the player with a limited 3 jumps that they may use in succession before they have to wait for it to quickly recharge. After playing through the long-jump levels completely, I can safely say that running out of jumps before having to wait for them to recharge is NEVER a problem.The music of Black Mesa is simply enthralling. Joel Nielsen is kind of a genius when it comes to taking the original industrial music of Half-Life and making it into something beautiful, yet still true to Half-Life, featuring bits of hard-hitting rock, some almost orchestral pieces, and then a complete turn-around when the player reaches Xen (I'm getting there!)To be honest, combat hasn't changed very much from Half-Life to Black Mesa. Thank God. Any changes made were simply to streamline combat and make it just a bit better looking, and you will likely find yourself using weapons you didn't use as much before (namely, the Gluon in Xen)Now onto Xen. I could write another review entirely for this section of the game, but I'll try to keep it brief and informative.If Half-Life's Xen was the strangest left turn in level design history, then Black Mesa's Xen is the greatest left turn in level design history. Everything there is to hate about Half-Life's Xen levels is rebuilt completely in Black Mesa, taking familiar features such as the factory in Interloper (my favorite of the Xen levels), and providing a completely new environment for the player to explore. The puzzles are simple, yet complex enough for the player to feel smart when they complete them. I won't spoil any of it because frankly, Xen is something you need to experience for yourself. It's a genius set of levels and I've never been more satisfied with waiting this long for it to be released. Whether you've played the original Half-Life or not, please pick up this game. It was worth the wait.

There are other examples as well, but  because of this I don't feel there was as much tactics in combat compared to the original, it felt like it was a case of simply kill the enemies as quickly as you can.  It's also a bit disappointing that xen has never been completed, the payed retail version of black mesa has been out for about a year now and there's still no word on it. _childDocuments_.review: What to say? The first half of the game is updated, improved version of the old classic that we know and love. Until we get to Xen. The first time Gordon teleports in, it is absolutely gorgeous. Xen is now half of the game, and is worth the asking price on it's own - it is completely re-designed, re-scored and refreshed. I found myself spending a good few minutes standing there, looking up at the environment each time after emerging from a cave system, with the score swelling around me taking in everything. It really is excellent. Joel Nielsen has done a superb job on the soundtrack - it is very hard to believe that this is a fan made game in every aspect - and is a credit to everyone who worked on it for so long.There are a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - getting stuck on scenery occasionally, some of the sections felt a little bit too long and in one later battle with the Alien Controllers my 970 struggled with all the particles, dropping to 10fps (at 1440p) but a game restart cured that after finishing the section. I'm nitpicking, however. Don't let it put you off, the experience is worth it. Completed in February 2020.Everything leads up to the Nihilanth fight, an exposition which is tremendous. A climactic battle in it's truest sense, with the amount of destruction that rains upon you as it gets closer to the end being truly awe inspiring. No hyperbole. _childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa: Source or Black Mesa is a Half Life 2 Modification by very enthusiastic Half Life gamers. This modification is less of a modification and more of a total conversion overhaul. This game is a complete rehaul of the original Half Life with almost identical levels & gameplay, what makes this game so special that it's not like any of the other "Half Life" remakes or Half Life: Source? Read on and find out!Black Mesa re-tells us an already very familiar story and amps up the anty by 10, with the solid plot line from the original Half Life with the glory of the Source Engine 2013 technology.You are Gordon Freeman, a scientist hired to perform experiements in an underground research lab below Mexico desert. One day on your job you're tasked to insert a rare specimen from the planet "Xen" into a reactor machine which causes a resonance cascade that destroys the research facility, but the worst is yet to come. As you battle your way out of Black Mesa research facility through these strange alien creatures & a corrupt military task force hired to keep the Black Mesa incident a secret and stop anybody that is attempting to escape from the facility a strange man in a blue suit stalks Gordons every move, who is this strange man & why is he here? It's up to you to unravel the mystery of this strange man.The gameplay is the same familiar gameplay you would expect from any Source Engine game, it works identical to that of Half Life 2, it's got solid gameplay, a beautifully & lovingly crafted modification that everyone expected "Half Life: Source" to be but were let down, this is what we wanted from Valve but in the end we got it from a very tallented modding team.With a complete overhaul of Half Life you can expect things to be compaired to the original & with this total conversion you should expect to see a few significant changes to the original game, some new places to explore, some alternate paths to take and some new faces to encounter, although not identical to the original game it's very cannon to the original & nothing that is in the game feels out of place.The gameplay is solid, the guns feel like the original game & most importantly the game has 100% it's own content, nothing is stock Half Life 2 assets, even the enemies are recreated with rather noteable modifications, they even went as far as to add their own voice actors to the game rather than using the voices from Half Life 2, however in the Steam release you will hear that a few of the characters are using the original voice actors from Half Life 1 & 2, this is nice to have the noteable voices back in a game that is trying to be the Half Life game it does so well to replicate.Yes i certainly recommend this game, if you're still on the fence about paying for a modification then you can try the free version of this available here: If you  own the original Half Life you  own this! If you own the original Half Life you still  own this!If after playing the free version you still don't feel like buying the game then there's nothing i can say to make you change your mind. However i will say that the money you spend here is going towards making these modders into an indie developer company which you should do as you can see they've really poured their heart and soul into this game which could easily be improved further.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, oh my god this game. Make no mistake, Black Mesa is more than just a Half Life remake; it took the first chapter of Gordon Freeman and ran with it, and in doing so created one of the most incredible gaming experiences of the 21st Century. The levels from Black Mesa Inbound through to Lambda Core are broadly similar to the original Half-Life, but they've been improved upon in tasteful ways to make the gameplay flow smoother than ever before. Nothing extraneous, everything with a purpose.And then the long awaited Xen creates a climactic finish to Black Mesa that even Valve would be proud to put their name to. The finale that Half-Life deserves. A much longer and fleshed out Xen, a terrifying and stressful battle against the Gonarch, and Interloper; far longer and more ambitious than any level that's gone before that will leave you feeling elated and exhausted. All before the climactic face off against the Nihilanth.And every level, with it's fanatical attention to detail, magnificent art design, superb scripted scenes, are all accented by Joel Nielsen's masterful soundtrack that is arguably the best ever put into a game. To this day. Black Mesa is the finest piece of work ever created in the Source engine; I would without hesitation put it above both Portals, Left 4 Deads, and even Half Life 2. And after all the Garry's Mod content, the Source Filmmakers, and extensive library of mods for all the games, Black Mesa is the perfect send off for one of the most endearing, versatile and historically important game engines of all time. This game is perfection.

_childDocuments_.review: Real good faithful remaking of Half-Life. For those going into this their first time, keep in mind, this is a game that had been around for 20 years now. Despite the years, the gameplay still holds up today as a solid FPS. It set the grounds for FPS to come back in 1998 and despite the age of the game, this remake brings you back to the glorious claustrophobic tunnels, vents, and awful looking behind the scenes of the Black Mesa facility following the accident. While I never actually beat the original Half-Life back in it's younger days, I did get pretty far and for whatever reason never kept going. This remake was so well done, it kept me going all the way until the sudden ending which as far as I'm concerned doesn't take away. Yes, you heard, it's not complete, but despite this, you will get a solid 11+ hours of gameplay out of this. It feels long...   The biggest take away if I had to nitpick is that from what I can remember of the original, the AI of the marines was superb. They had crazy tactics and always got around on you. The AI in Black Mesa is overall pretty weak on the marines and everything else. In fact there are times where you will find the creatures not even moving and you can easily pick them off. Glitchy here and there but not terrible. Actually amazing when you think about it that the original AI still stands out above this, but obviously Black Mesa was done with a lot of heart and I can't knock against that. I'd say 95% of the time it remains faithful. If you are new to the Half-Life franchise and never played one or even missed the original and went right to the second, now you have a good reason to give the first part a go with this solid remake. Everything is in tact and with extra details scattered around, it definitely brings life to what otherwise would look like an empty facility if you played the 1998 version.   Looking forward to them finishing up "Xen". In the meantime, I feel satisfied with what they gave for the money I spent.UPDATE - Xen has released. In fact the game has finally been completed. I said, forget skipping right to Xen, I want to replay from the beginning! I feel like they've added so much more lighting effects and polish to the existing world than when I initially fired it up in 2018. It feels super polished now and the right way to experience this masterpiece.So um, yeah, reached Xen, mind blown. Pick this up if you never played Half Life 1 and want to see what 1998 played like. Even if you played and beat HL1, still pick it up. This is like my 5th playthrough... Top 3 ATG FPS ever made. Might be numero uno for me.
