_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, good intent, poor execution. That's Black Mesa in a nutshell.Black Mesa is, unfortunately, NOT a worthy reimagining of the source material. Even when viewed as an "alternate" take, it cannot stand. And since the majority of reviews I'm seeing here would suggest that Black Mesa is essentially Half-Life: Remastered, I feel there's a strong need for someone to step up and say "Whoa, Nelly. Let's back up, here." Because this is certainly not the case. Let me explain why (I'll try to be brief).First, I hate to knock these guys' work. This all began as a fan project - a labor of love, if you will, of an unusual quality. And I mean that. There's some seriously great work in here. There are some admirable sound-alike voice actors (though this itself is an issue, which I hope to have space to touch on ahead), the maps are fantastically well-designed and evocative of the original game without being straight copy-pastes, and some aspects of the game have been remixed just enough for things to feel fresh.What really lets it down is the just horrible lack of nuance. Everything is in-your-face and over-the-top, *especially* the awkward, flailing attempts at nu-Valvian "humor." There's a scene early in the game where three scientists prattle in metaphor about Half-Life inspiring them to want to make games, how their vision is similar but different, they can bring things up to snuff with the power of modern technology, etc. etc. - and it's positively dreadful. Just straight-up face-wrenching cringe material. Honestly, they could have even done this the correct way. There's room for it in the game, surely. They just lacked the skills to get that statement in the game without completely shattering the mood and sounding terrible. But it doesn't end with this. Every other line of dialogue is some smarmy reference to the original game that makes the whole thing feel hokey.Black Mesa is *constantly* trying to be funny, and constantly sabotaging its own mood in the process. It's a real shame, because the excellent environmental design tends to do a fantastic job building up ambience - only to have some dumb sign, poster, or quip from a character bring the whole house of cards down on a whim. Yes, it's that much of an issue. It's not nearly rare enough to ignore. While a little bit of levity can serve even in an otherwise straight-laced experience, a lot can be ruining. Especially of that humor is particularly juvenile - which is the case here.But that's not all. It's not just the humor. The overall design is compromised by a general lack of restraint. Eli and Kleiner are shoehorned into the game, and very, very awkwardly at that. They don't fit in at all, and their appearance is just one more drop of cringe-fuel - just a name drop for the sake of having one, as though they wanted to get the characters in there, but they had no idea where to do it. Music cues are placed in tremendously galling places, such as the return trip to the rocket test chamber. It's awful. In the original, you had the by-then familiar sound of the monsters hammering on the walkways, and your own silent determination to finish one last step and do what you have to do to win. In Black Mesa, you have godawfully generic electronic music hammering in your ears just screaming "yes, yes, you're about to do the THING!" and completely ruining the moment. Does that sound nit-picky? It ISN'T. The first game was *defined* by everything having been done for a reason. Everything was handcrafted to provide a mood, and every music cue was very, very decisive and meaningful. There was no room for "bum-chicka bum-chicka bum-chicka" just for the sake of it.And then there's the sound-alike voice actors. They're fine. In fact, in a lot of ways, they emulate the original *two* voice actors (scientists and security guards) pretty much perfectly. But *why* emulate them at all? Why make the entire voice cast one scientist voice and one security guard voice? Surely, with where we are with technology today (I mention this only because the developers did, with their characters' cheeky treatise on their design philosophy near the beginning of the game), they could have gotten away with using bit lines from multiple contributors? Why does every security guard and every scientist have to sound the same, especially when the scientists all sound like silly cartoon chariactures (that voice actor was definitely trying too hard at times)?The dedication to sound-aliking the characters also comes off as hokey and pointless, even if the actors themselves did a good job. And the idle chatter? Every other line is a silly, goofy "joke" that just torpedoes that mood. "Do I look cool when I hold my gun like this?" Right, right. I know that the original game had humor in their dialogue. The difference is that it wasn't juvenile. Big, big difference.Compounding the issues are actual technical shortcomings. The Source engine is surprisingly inept at the task of recreating Half-Life, strange as it is to say. I'm talking about the fundamental feel. Gordon doesn't so much as walk as he floats through the air. Guns feel more like airsoft props than firearms. Jumping is unreliable and feels physically wrong.Worst of all, fights against enemy AI feel like matches against multiplayer bots - and I don't mean that as a compliment. I mean, the most generic, mindless multiplayer bots. Human soldiers shuffle back and forth while hip-firing rifles with near perfect accuracy at any distance. This particular flaw is familiar to anyone who's played through Half-Life 2. The AI is pretty much the same flawed AI of the Combine troops. And there are TONS of human opponents. To make up for their lack of intelligence, the devs placed HECU Marines in massive numbers. The result of this is maddening death by hitscan out in the open with next to no cover in maps like Surface Tension. Fighting the soldiers - a highlight of the original game - is without joy or thrills here. Just disappointment.EDIT: The game is now 1.0. It's still terrible. Due to the awful, floaty controls, Gordon is a damage-sinking tank. Enemies are bullet sponges. The gunplay is utterly joyless in that familiar, disappointing Half-Life 2 sort of way. Childish humor permeates the entire experience, and the entire game feels themeless, toneless. There's no sense of place or being. You just W+LMB, float down corridors, clicking things until they ragdoll. God, it's so terrible.I highly doubt that the majority of those giving this thing positive reviews actually played the original Half-Life.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Remember HL: Source? God, it looks even lamer now. But the port was much needed for this gem to happen, of course, so here's its redemption arc. The devs call Black Mesa a re-imagining, but I'll be bold and call it a full-blown replacement. Seriously, if you'd recommend the original over this to a newcomer, you must be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hipster. Crowbar Collective managed to enhance my favorite Half-Life in every possible way while staying true to its core - I certainly felt the familiarity, but also appreciated the novelty. This is still a hard sci-fi story about the mesmerizing unknown and cyclopic machinery. The difference is that now it keeps pace with the times by looking, sounding, and playing even better than before.I liked all of the level, monster, and weapon re-designs. They didn't go overboard, every little thing that you know and love is instantly recognizable, yet enhanced in some way. The weapons feel more punchy, even the MP5 got better. Still sounds a bit like dangling a keychain than anything, but with an added kilo of keys. The new grenades physics was the only thing I didn't like - it makes them too unpredictable, and you can't throw them as far as in the original, which diminishes their usefulness. Whatever, they aren't essential. To end the paragraph on a positive note, the new gibs are really nice and juicy.The new lighting made the game much more creepy than I remembered. Manually applied with taste, it added a ton of volume to the levels that themselves underwent many changes. Some of the changes were subtle, some quite drastic, all of them equally harmonious - nothing seems like it doesn't belong. I played the original for the last time decades ago (but many-many times) and it was often really hard for me to tell the new stuff apart from the rest. There's no touch of amateurishness, a distinction in quality  that would tell me exactly where Valve's work ends and Crowbar's begins. Except maybe for sticky collisions and minor performance issues by the end.Crowbar Collective are very inspired people, it is evident in their designs. Residue Processing reminded me of Silent Hill with its terrific rust textures, Questionable Ethics have that retro-futuristic Alien vibe. Xen labs reek of System Shock and its jungle made me look around for a Predator in the trees. Gonarch's lair and otherworldly underwater caves are purely Lovecraftian, and Interloper's factories are so Abe's Oddysee that it hurts. I don't claim to have guessed everything (or anything) correctly - just wanted to point at how good the designs are, whether they derived from pop-culture or came from raw talent.Colossal wind tunnels, toxic waterfalls, deepest shafts, claustrophobic underwater segments, atmospheric unearthly locations, impressive set pieces, overall multi-layered level design - everything I value in Half-Life was there. Yet every part carried a nuance, a slight shift, a surprise. Then I got to Xen in which the innovations weren't subtle at all. I can't say that I hated the old Xen, but this one completely blew me away with its epic bossfights and alien technology type puzzles. Without exaggeration, both are the best in the genre. Visually Xen definitely is the most compelling alien world that I've ever seen and traveled through. Utterly fantastic, a true magnum opus. It needs to be seen (and played) to be believed.Letting their fans enhance their property like this and then allow them to sell it on Steam makes Valve ultra-democratic. Like everyone else, I have my qualms with it, but in this case, I can't help but applaud. They deserved it. Just look, for example, at Nintendo and their unending battle with emulators. Hell, these control freaks would forbid streaming if they could. Fans remastered their games, virtually ported them to PC, despite all the inconveniences of reverse-engineering. And what does Nintendo do? It fights them, tries to sue them, in best-case scenarios just ignores them, and refuses to use their expertise!Then they open their fat purse to go and make crappy, outdated remasters by themselves instead. Nintendo isn't the only one with the attitude, of course, but I had to limit myself to one example, this review is already too long (it's not because I'm some hater, I swear). The point is that we should all value Valve for not being such boomers. And praise Crowbar Collective for being as amazing as they are. All they needed to do was not to ♥♥♥♥ it up, yet they followed their ambition, which led them far beyond this simple goal, and their bravery paid off big time. The team really did a number on some of the outdated moments, and I think that they managed not to lose anything aside from the jank.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man. Black Mesa isn't just updated visuals on a newer engine, far from it.The re-imagining of the events of HL1 while still keeping what made the original great goes above and beyond what I was expecting before trying it. The extended versions of certain chapters are exactly what the game needed to extract even more juice from the setting and story. The Xen chapters are almost like a second game, a fantastic journey in a completely revamped and gorgeous alien setting.Some clipping and collision bugs that are natural to the Source engine and a somewhat lengthy chapter (Interloper) that felt like a marathon are the only flaws I can come up with but insignificant compared to what the game makes you feel while playing it.This is now, for me, the  story of the events that lead to the Seven Hour War (sorry HL1, you didn't quite age like a fine wine but you still deserve your place in history and a replay once in a while).

_childDocuments_.review: Do you recommend this game? Yes. Yes. Yes.This remake does not only polish the amazing, great and original experience that was Half-Life, but ACTUALLY improves it much more, this isn't just a remake and a remaster, but also a rework and an update to the original experience, one that the developers surely knew how to develop over time, and as in of now, the game is totally complete and basically enhaces the Half-Life experience, while most people recommend playing Half-Life and then Half-Life 2 (which I also suggest if you don't mind Half-Life's old graphics, I personally do not mind them.), you could also just play Black Mesa and play Half-Life 2 right away if you liked, it's better than starting Half-Life 2 fresh without anything prior to that. This game is a gem, and it definitely deserves the level of attention it has received and hell, perhaps even more. THIS is what an actual remake and remaster should be like.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game. For nostalgia's sake, and for modernizing an old goody, its existence is appreciated. The soundtrack alone elevates the game, in terms of tone and sophistication, far above where the game deserves to be (I listen to the soundtrack fairly often; it's just that good). For the actual modernization, though, I feel like the developers didn't go far enough and some of the game just left me marveling at how stuck in the past it is in terms of playability/control and experience.The story is the same as it was, which is fine, though some of it is made more visible, such as the actual invasion. That's nice. More depth is always appreciated, especially if it isn't contradicting canon.The visual design is so much better than it was in the original HL, and really brings this game closer to HL2. The Xen environments are sometimes outright fantastic in terms of visual design. It's really a shame I can't finish the Xen chapters. Which leads me to:Bugs. I can't finish this game without console/cheat tactics because "Interloper" has a massive bug that crashes the game at some point, and the saved games in that chapter crash the game as well. Since it's a GRUELING, LONG, and SLOW chapter, there's no way I'm going to restart it in the hopes that the bug doesn't get triggered the second time around.The developers have shown no interest in correcting the bug since players are so defensive of this game and of the developers, and everyone seems to just offer the suggestion of "try again" or "load the next chapter to continue playing". I'm not interested in either.If you want more info about this specific bug, see the discussion area for the game.Ultimately, the time I spent on this game was a mixture of enjoyment and rage, and I cannot advise someone to buy it, only to risk a similar experience. I am uninstalling it at this point to free up room for newer games, since the developers aren't interested in fixing their own mistakes. I do not bow and scrape or walk on eggshells for developers who sell their product. This ceased to be about purely the love of Half-Life. It's a product, and I paid them for it. In the end, I cannot finish it, because they have a game-breaking bug in it that they wont fix.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is good and worth the money.As a remake it does a great job of taking all of the major beats from the original Half Life and giving it a source engine facelift. Its not a one to one conversion, but you can easily see a room in the remake and identify what area its supposed to represent from the original.Graphically it looks great, not just in the sense that they did a good job of modernizing the old gold source models, but also in general quality, if you didn't already know you'd probably wouldn't guess that this was originally a fan project that was going to be released for free.Gameplay wise it's a mostly faithful recreation, the changes they've made for encounters are universally positive, either by adding novelty, making the memorable highlights of the original more distinct in ways they couldn't back in the 90s, and making improvements where the original tripped up. There's some movement tweaks, if you crouch after running you do a little action movie slide, and the long jump module is greatly improved, allowing you to use it while moving in any direction.The biggest changes have been made in the Xen chapters of the game. In the original Half Life they were rushed, clearly half baked and unfinished. In Black Mesa they've gutted everything and rebuilt from scratch, and the game is much, MUCH better for it. You have the flavor of the original Xen at some parts of it, but it's mostly brand new content, to the point where some of it is unrecognizable, to the games significant benefit. What was a few short chapters of mostly low gravity platforming and a couple of boss arenas before has now been expanded upon to the point where its like a quarter of the game, and has brand new puzzles, encounters, and enemies. The last areas before the final boss feel appropriately climactic, the encounters are hard, and the music is great.Personally, will this replace the original Half Life for me? That's a hell of a question, I couldn't tell you for sure. Something I can answer is: If you're someone who likes Half Life, or wants to get into the series but the first game seems too old and clunky to get into (You'd be wrong, by the way), would this be a good game for you? The answer is YES.I'd give Black Mesa 9 snarks out of 10, the Xen improvements are worth the price of admission, check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Remakes usually make the terribly stupid mistake of taking the original game and remaining rigidly faithful to it out of fear of alienating the original fans, rather than refining it and remaking it to bring its essence to a new era. Black Mesa doesn't make that mistake. It takes the original Half-Life, a dated landmark in shooters and interactive narratives, strips out the annoying fiddly bits, and refines what remains into a tightly designed shooter that transitions between survival horror and full out action shooter without ever changing control schemes. It isn't the best feeling shooter on the market, but it is the most exciting shooter, where resource management never overwhelms action, while still remaining critical to the pacing. I can't imagine how someone can like shooters and not like this game. It's a full, complete, and fantastic remake that's worth double its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa, a game that started as a fan project, and now as a wholeheartedly and criminally underrated full experience game capturing the inmersion from the original Half-Life into an intense gunplay and crowbar bashing style, the chapters feels alive and deadly, and last but not least, Xen. Yes, Xen feels enormously amazing to traverse… that’s it, I have no words AAAAAAAAAABuy it… and if you do itWisely done Mr. Player! I’ll see you up ahead
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: If a studio is remaking a game and it doesn't go to the lengths Black Mesa went to do justice to the original Half-Life, that studio is making a money-grab. This is the quintessential remake against which all other remakes should and ought to be compared. It's damn near perfect. The only complaint I have is the same I had with the original game: Xen. Where the Xen levels in the original Half-Life were sloppy and unpolished (Valve did confess to rushing them through development), the Xen levels in Black Mesa draaag on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on and on. The mechanics and level design for Xen are improvements by every measure. However, Crowbar Collective over-corrected by making the Xen levels so long they end up outstaying their welcome. Make no mistake, Xen is great fun to play through, but it gets exhausting.I only recommend you buy and play through the original Half-Life first if you want to fully appreciate the masterpiece Crowbar Collective so lovingly put together for us to enjoy. Black Mesa is a testament to the skill and passion of the team at Crowbar Collective, and an incomparable tribute to what is arguably the greatest, most significant game ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: One word, Excelent; this game is the remastering of the Original half life, it deserves to be the best remasterized copy, Good weapon and environment quality, I never thought to see this game remasterized one more time with this kind of quality with some cons like the fast Xen development, they did care of the other envionments except this. Simply excelent
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful recreation - for the most part. I'm a big fan of the inclusion of multiple routes into a lot of areas. It is well thought out and appreciated. Black Mesa modernises most of the chapters without overstepping it's creative license and tells the age old story well. Right up until Xen.Remember Xen? The thing that made this game take ages to come out?I can see why Xen took years to finish now though. It's heavily drawn out, especially Gonarch's section. This is now a very long chain of set pieces before the actual fight. Perhaps I'm misremembering after all these years on how long it took in the original but I don't think so. It spoils the game's pacing and by the time you get to the fight you really can't be bothered with it.Aside from some , the rest of the Xen additions are wholly unnecessary and felt quite boring to "puzzle" through once the initial 'wow' of the scenery in the first few levels wore off. Especially when you think how little of Xen's stuff makes it into HL2!I'm also not a fan of the new closing scene. In the original, it clearly shows HECU/Marines have tried to invade Xen (whether before or after Chapter 1's scenes). Why's that missing for such a transparent faced, reality bending tram over and over showing nothing?The HL1 carnage highlights the trail of destruction Gordon, a scientist, and everyone else has left behind. It is perfectly timed with the "I am impressed" part of the G-Man's speech. It's supposed to be making Gordon finally take stock of what he's done and evaluate his actions versus his tendencies and morals as your stereotypical science nerd. Is he shocked and disgusted and says no? Or does he believe what he did was necessary for a greater purpose and accept?In Black Mesa it's now a very underwhelming scene for such a critical moment in the Half Life franchise. Like people trying to mimic the words without understanding the language. It makes it even more frustrating that Xen has had so much time spent on it when this scene feels like it hasn't.Sorry to say that Xen was not at all worth the wait, guys. I appreciate your efforts but they could have gone elsewhere than Alien Casual Puzzle Simulator. Like on the ending!Last point, the AI cheats HARD on locating you. Somehow you've done worse than the original here and made the Marines & Slaves omniscient. A single person skulking around a noisy industrial builiding or warzone while people have their backs to you? Forget it. Positioning in HL1 before attacking was key to winning fights but that's gone in BM.TL;DR - Good up until Xen, and worth a pickup on sale. Workshop already has a co-op mod being developed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I played half life 1 multiplayer with my friends in gmod, and that began to peak my interest. My friend recommended this game to me afterwards. I think it is well worth it's price. I gotta say, this game captured my imagination. The levels are detailed and stunning, especially the surface levels and Xen. The game play is engaging, and I have yet to tire of it. Buy this, buy this now.

_childDocuments_.review: ===Pre-Release Review===It's hard to believe that 5 years ago this was a mod up to the Xen chapter. Now with the near release the game should be in its final stages and ready for release. Sadly it is showing its age. Mechanically it will be that old school FPS you know and love but also with visuals to match.If you played the original half life and want an updated version then Black Mesa is it. It does a remarkable job of bringing the original game up to a nearly modern standard while retaining the shooting mechanics of the late 90s. That said its not all sunshine and roses. 5 years ago the visuals was remarkable. Fast forward and its age is showing. This is the problem with a long development cycle. The pre-Xen chapters looks outdated. Even with the highest settings that the engine can muster textures looks like it is stuck in the early 2010s. The game also retains its DX9 roots so none of the extra features from DX11 or DX12 makes the cut.I am going down hard on this game even though I recommend it. It is a swan song for Half-life. If you ever loved the game you must play it. If you never played Half-life but want to know what it was like this is a good recreation with a modest visual upgrade. However do not expect it to look like any 2020 Battlefield or Call of Duty.===Post Release Review===Pretty much everything that I stated above still holds true. Xen is an amazing re-imagining however just as with the original game Xen is also the worst part of the game. You are treated to a beautiful introduction that starts to tapper off. The once serene landscape gets replaced by dull shades of brown as you progress. Credit for sticking close to the source but it really does show how the design went down hill. This game is still recommended however as an easy replacement to the 22 year old original.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a high quality recreation of an iconic classic. It's just different enough in small places to keep a veteran player on the edge, it's faithfully remade everywhere else to keep the pace, feel, and story as fun as the original.From what started as 'just a mod project' almost ten years ago, BM became this work-of-art retelling that has everyone eager for Xen havoc. If you don't have it get it, you'll want to play from start to finish and come back again to see an alien world like never before.

_childDocuments_.review: A great remake of the FPS that made all the other singleplayer FPS campaigns we see today, Counter-Strike and Team Fortress. Fantastic game that you should buy to support the hard-working developers. With the 1.5 Definitive Edition that the hard-working developers released in the end of 2020, the game is better than ever.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something touching about seeing this game finally finished after so many years of work. I remember playing the early access version, then the version without Xen, and finally finishing it once development was complete.It's an absolutely incredible piece of work. To see fans come together around a common passion and make a work of this quality is simply breathtaking. For me, this is quite simply the best remaster I've ever seen. I'm not going to write a review to explain how legendary Half Life is, but simply to talk about what Black Mesa brings to the table.Black Mesa does much more than bring Half Life up to date; it captures its essence and extends the experience, adding elements without ever distorting the original.Everything it adds is tasteful, the new sequences fit in perfectly with the most mythical moments of the original, and the new soundtrack enhances the experience.I can't end my review without mentioning the work done on Xen. This part of the game, which was the weakest in the original, has become a masterpiece. Apart from the penultimate chapter, "Interloper", which I found too long and repetitive. There are so many striking new sequences. The arrival on Xen, the discovery of the place, the battle against the Gonarch... So many memorable new moments. Much more than a game, Black Mesa is a model of what people can be capable of through passion and without the means of big companies.Thank you for everything Crowbar Collective.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Macaroni this is good.Black Mesa is a remake of the original half life which has been in development for over a decade. Now, finally it is released in its full form and this is absolutely a must play.Not only is the base game lovingly recreated, remastered and rebuilt in certain areas to take advantage of the source engine and iron out some kinks with the original levels but the Xen levels have been COMPLETELY redesigned to become in my opinion the absolute highlight of the game.The Xen levels have been in development for years and now having finished Black Mesa from start to finish I can say it was absolutely 100% worth the wait. The Xen levels are amazingly good and you really feel like you're exploring an alien planet from beyond, helped a ton by the drop dead gorgeous visuals and aesthetic design along with the incredible musical score by Joel Nielsen.The music in this game deserves a special mention because it isn't something that plays all the time, rather it kicks in at certain moments during the game and is used to build up certain scenes. In the base on earth portion of the game the tracks are a mixture between Melodic Piano tracks and more heavy slow rock style tracks and the two genres often cross over.On Xen the music becomes a lot more euphoric with some amazing vocals done by Joel's wife, Kala Nielsen, being one of the highlights of the soundtrack. A lot of the time in the Xen levels you'll reach a moment where you stumble into a new area and you're met with an amazingly beautiful sight coupled with the music beginning to kick in and you just can't help but stop and gawk at what you're seeing. It's truly incredible what Crowbar Collective have managed to pull off in the Source Engine here.Really my only complaints are that I hit a few bugs and glitches here and there, most of them were minor, like the autosave kicking in at the wrong place causing it to autosave while I was falling to my death (thankfully you can quicksave on the fly and quicksaving does not overwrite your previous quicksave so if you happen to quicksave mid fall you can roll back to the quicksave before that) but I did hit one glitch where an NPC got stuck in the Surface Tension chapter and I was forced to NoClip my way through a door in order to trigger the next NPC event to get him unstuck (this is a known issue apparently).It's a bit awkward but thankfully these glitches are very few and far between. You may not run into any of them at all.With all that being said, Black Mesa is an incredible experience and an incredible way to experience Half Life, either for the first time or for the fifteenth time. So what are you waiting for? Because they're waiting for you Gordon, in the test chamber...
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Half-Life 1 HD remake. Because it wasn't under the constraints of time, the levels are a lot more indepth than some of the ones in the original Half-Life 1 game. This game was put onto Steam on May 5th 2015 and they expect to have it complete around the summer of 2017. The developers have put so much time into making sure that everything works properly and feels incredible. Even the unfinished product left me giddy with how challenging and fun it was. This is well worth the money if you enjoy the Half-Life serries.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original Half-Life in the late 90s/early 00s. In fact that particular game resonated with me more than any other FPS at the time - for some reason, I loved the unique atmosphere and (perhaps ironically, considering the sci-fi scenario) the reality of it. I really believed Black Mesa could exist. This remake brings back those feelings and to me, it achieves exactly what it was trying to do: upgrade HL1 technically by 20 years while at the same time retaining the game's wonderful setting, atmosphere and moral dilemmas ("Unquestionable Ethics"). The only very minor thing I would criticize is the weapon sounds - the shotgun blast in HL1 had a deep low end to it, it felt like it can shake buildings. I can't say the same of the shooting sounds here, however please keep in mind that in the big scheme of things, this is REALLY minor. I've had a wonderful experience with this game and it reinforced why I love the original as well. THIS IS HOW YOU DO REMAKES.EDIT: I have finished the full game now and need to say this: Xen and Interloper BLEW MY MIND. The complete reimagination of these worlds, the visuals, creative puzzles and new set pieces were just mindblowing. I was expecting something cool but not such an expanded beautiful experience... I absolutely loved this game. The original will live forever but I'd say Black Mesa is the most immersive HL1 experience you can have today.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite me liking Half Life to an extent, I firmly believe Black Mesa improves upon on the many foundations of the original game and is a very well done and executed reimagining of Half Life. From the chapters to AI behavior, puzzles, combat sections, soundtrack, community mods/maps and especially Xen, it's all well done. Interloper still sucks in both versions though. That said, it's up to you to play either the original or the reimagining.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a love letter to Half Life, a glimpse of how far the FPS genre (and video games in general) have come since HL1, as well as being one of the finest games I have ever played. Being an authorised fan remake of the original Half Life, the game shares a lot in common with said game, but also adds in brand new assets, levels, and brings the game into the modern age. Pros:- The Black Mesa Research Facility looks better than ever. While maintaining roughly the same layout as it did back in the '90's, the modern incarnation benefits from modern graphics technology, more detailed environments, as well as the physics of the modern Source Engine. - A host of improvements to gameplay make Black Mesa a highly enjoyable experience. While core mechanics still focus on blended puzzle and gunplay segments; Black Mesa both reuses and improves segments from the original game, while also adding new and original content to existing segments. - Brilliant audio and FX design. 'nuff said. - XenCons:- There's a few minor bugs, but these can potentially be attributed to the age of the Source Engine, and I didn't encounter any that were game-breaking. Most bugs are related to physics or AI for certain opponents. - Some of the new additions to levels feel a little too formulaic and underwhelming. I haven't played the original Half Life in years, so I can't figure out whether all of the bits I thought were rather poorly done were necessarily new, but a few of them I definitely don't recall being in the original. Regardless, none were overtly bad, or deserving of mention, so YMMV. Overall, Black Mesa is one of the best games I have ever played. If you love video games, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Black Mesa Incident. Those four words are either understood entirely, or they're completely unfamiliar. There is no middle ground. Gamer's do not simply forget where the legendary Half-Life franchise began. As someone who played the original game on the PlayStation 2, this was a bittersweet trip down memory lane that made me feel like a senior citizen who is driving the newest model of their first car from 50 years prior. It's the same car, you get the same rush and comfort that you did in your 20's, but it's become so much more. More powerful, more attractive, headlights bright enough to shine through a man's soul and a touch-screen display capable of things you've only imagined. That's Black Mesa. The same ride, but it's cranked up to 11.I do this thing where I pick 5 specific categories for each game that I review, since not all games can be judged by the same metric. The categories for  are:  Yes, Xen actually gets it's  review category. We'll talk about why shortly. Come along, Free Man.This is the most important category, because the entire objective of Black Mesa is to recreate the incident in it's entirety. And oh. My. Sh*t. Did they ever. Black Mesa does an outstanding job at retaining  of it's source material, while expanding tremendously on each and every aspect. This game is such a rollercoaster of different atmospheres that I would need a much longer review page to cover them all. The game starts off gently, then quickly turns hectic with a heavy focus on survival horror. As you play and grow accustomed to your situation, Black Mesa changes it up time and time again. Eventually you'll slowly shift towards pure action and some major a** kicking. Then you've got stealth sections, mysterious experiment labs, an all-out war between man and alien, then.. you'll find yourself quite literally between dimensions. It's wild. The way the development team carefully expanded familiar areas, and created new ones that mesh together so wonderfully is a f*cking delight to play through. It's about a 15 hour campaign, and you won't be disappointed.You read that right, I just gave a Source-engine game from 2013 a 9.25 / 10 for graphics. It's not just about the comparison between this remake, and the original from 1998. The changes are quite obvious there. No, this is about the atmosphere that was created within Black Mesa. I can't even begin to tell you about the absolute beauty of Xen, it genuinely made my jaw drop. Now the game has obviously been completely remade from the ground up. Pretty much every model and texture is original to this game, but the way the team managed to invoke so many emotions through environmental story telling is fantastic. There's so many moments of overwhelmingly creepy areas that are filled with dread, to beautifully scenic views that give you brief moments of relief. Not to mention that the Black Mesa Research Complex truly looks like what you would hope a secret government facility would look like. The shadows and new lighting add more than I can express. However, this is still a Source game. Even if you have a high-end PC, you'll still have framerate drops. Especially during the above ground combat. If it weren't for that, this darn well may have been a 10 / 10.I really love what they did with sound design. Sounds are so, so important to the atmosphere of anything that intends to immerse you. The sounds of explosions, alarms going off, distant gunfire and unrecognizable roars all piled into a collapsing facility would be enough to invoke PTSD, in a good way. The voice acting & music in particular is where Black Mesa excels. The actors that they got for the guards and scientists sound so close to their original counter-parts that I actually thought it was the original actors. That's awesome. The music will blow you away too. It's incredibly well-made and stays true to the familiar tunes of the entire Half-Life series. There are a couple issues though. For one, the music plays very rarely and occasionally misses the mark when it should be featured . You'll also hear some familiar physics sounds from Half-Life 2, and oddly enough - marine screams from Doom 3. I remember sounds well.The meat and potatoes of any game, playing the d*mn thing! Black Mesa's gameplay is about as Source as it's gets, and that's not bad at all. Source games are known for diverse gameplay in puzzles, combat, and physics. Black Mesa has no shortage of any of those, and an abundance of vent-crawling. The weapons actually pack a punch, the puzzles are plentiful and actually make you question the solution, and the physics are as goofy as always. Truth be told, there's not much I can say here that most players aren't already familiar with. I will mention one aspect that I appreciated, they kept the military dangerous as f*ck. These guys have some of the most accurate shots I've seen in a game, and they utilize  quick movements to make themselves harder to hit. It was both frustrating, and refreshing to have actual challenges in NPC combat.I know how strange it must seem to find a review category based entirely on a few levels within the game, but Xen is much more than that. Do you remember the original Xen in Half-Life? Didn't take too long to beat, pretty empty and nothing too crazy. Well, the team behind Black Mesa said "f*ck that" and created something I never expected. Xen took them forever to finish, which I was a bit critical about since I was waiting for the full release before I played and reviewed the game. I'm happy to say it was worth the wait. Xen is without question, the most diverse and gorgeous alien world that I have ever played through in a video game. It's amazing. So many parts of the world are bioluminescent, which gives everything this otherworldly bluish glow. Xen has it's own version of alien swamps, forests, caves, and even deserts. Not to mention the dangerous new lifeforms that reside there, and the horrifying . Xen is a masterpiece in it's own right, and you get there just after you think you've seen everything that Black Mesa has to offer.There you have it, Black Mesa is an outstanding achievement in fan-made games, and the definitive way to experience where Half-Life began. To think that this entire game is fan-made, it's a hard thing to comprehend after playing through it. In my opinion, this game is worth every penny in that asking price. Hell, it's probably worth more.From a lifelong Half-Life fan, thank you Crowbar Collective. So.. about Half-Life 2..

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is an FPS developed by Crowbar Collective, and the Definitive Edition was released in 2020.This is the Source Engine Remake of the cult first Half-Life published in 1998.The least we can say is that the talented developers have masterfully revisited Valve's masterpiece.The great scenario of the game originally written by Marc Laidlaw remains unchanged.The player embodies Gordon Freeman, a brilliant scientist recently graduated from M.I.T., working at the Black Mesa Research Center in New Mexico.During an experiment aimed at analyzing a crystal of unknown origin,an immense catastrophe of unprecedented scale occurred: a resonance cascade.Dimensional portals open here and there from which unfriendly aliens emerge.The army was called in to help stop the invasion, but seems determined to cover up the whole affair.You must do everything to try to get out of there, help your colleagues in difficulty, and destroy what is at the origin of this disaster...Black Mesa lives by Half-Life's motto of "Run, Think, Shoot, Live."The game retains the charm of yesteryear, oscillating between combat, reflection, and platform making it original.Unlike the sadly unloved Half-Life Source, Black Mesa is not a simple port of the first Half-Life to the Source Engine.Although the maps, enemies and plot are similar, the developers have taken some liberties, refreshing the original work.The very essence of the game is respected, and even embellished in many areas.The pace of the combat is much more frantic, the shootouts are dynamic to say the least.Some complex sequences have been simplified, while others have been largely redesigned.The game has a much more elaborate and spectacular staging than its glorious ancestor, and sometimes offers great moments of bravery.We are amazed at every moment, since the effect of nostalgia is enhanced by all the new things.Half-Life has never been more beautiful and immersive than in Black Mesa.The game pushes the limits of the ancient but still very effective Source Engine.The graphics are sublime, the lighting and reflections magnificent, the particle effects striking… The weapons become covered in blood when you pulverize an enemy in close combat, the game can be very gory, almost giving the impression of playing a modern version of Brutal Half-Life.The game accentuates its connection with the other illustrious Half-Life games, by borrowing various elements from them, including gameplay mechanics.It's possible to pick up various objects to clear your path, to burn Zombies using flares, to look for a valve to place on its support in order to use it, to reconnect a cable to a socket, to launch a flammable barrel on the tongue of the Barnacles so that it explodes once it reaches their mouth... The sprint system and the flashligt are similar to Half-Life 2, except that they no longer drain the battery of the H.E.V. Suit.The NPCs are much more numerous and detailed than in the past.First of all, scientists have a plethora of models, including female ones for the first time.Female scientists should have appeared in Half-Life 1, but only a few leftovers remain in the Half-Life Alpha and Half-Life Source files.The models of security guards are also much more diverse and better armed.Indeed, if they are often equipped with their famous pistol, some have revolvers and even shotguns! From time to time you can even lead a small squad of "Barneys" and Scientists.These valuable allies often interact with each other and have new lines of dialogue, in addition to those already well known.Some recognizable characters and elements now appear in Black Mesa.Gordon meets the likeable Issac Kleiner and Eli Vance early in the game.Vortigaunts communicate the same way as in Half-Life 2. Galanga!Don't forget Dr. Magnusson’s famous "microwave casserole"…The enemies are essentially the same as in Half-Life, but with models that resemble some of those in Half-Life 2, including their animations.In addition to the already well-known Xen creatures (including the iconic Headcrabs, the intelligent Vortigaunts, the fierce Bullsquids and many others), Black Mesa introduces :the Zombie Torso previously seen in Half-Life 2,the Zombie Security Guards and H.E.C.U. coming straight from Opposing Force and Blue Shift,two new variants of Houndeyes, the first one is explosive and kamikaze, while the second is a larger and beefier,and a sort of underwater Barnacle, undoubtedly drawing inspiration from the unfinished Sand Barnacle from Half-Life 2 Beta.The Military H.E.C.U. and Black Ops are as tough as ever, and can give you a hard time.They communicate constantly, attack in groups and are not there to make up the numbers.Female Assassins are extremely agile and flawlessly precise, and have the same Long-Fall Boots as the protagonist of Portal 1 and 2, Chell ! Additionally, there may be enemies where there were none in the original game.Black Mesa is much larger than before, and teeming with life and little details that will delight even the biggest fans.The weapons are exactly the same as in Half-Life, but are not necessarily picked up in the same place.Some have a few difference differences in their gameplay, such as:The 357 Magnum has an Iron Sight, similar to Half-Life 1 in multiplayer.The crossbow has a real scope at the scope, making it more practical and more realistic.However, all those guns seem much more powerful and impactful, giving a more dynamic combat feeling than in the past.The last part of the game, taking place in the "Border World" Xen, has been completely remade.The artistic direction is totally original and splendid, it's a perpetual visual feast.It almost feels like we're on the planet Pandora from the Avatar, one of James Cameron's masterpieces of the Seventh Art.This alien universe is adorned with its most beautiful shimmering colors, mixing caves worthy of HL2: Episode Two, lush jungles, and settings similar to the abyss. The firmament is covered with clouds of sparkling stars and a multitude of celestial objects.This ecosystem made up of several biomes is teeming with life and details of the highest quality.The flora is colorful, accentuating the exoticism of this distant land.The local fauna is variegated, and while Boids fly peacefully in the skies, other species are much more harmful.The aliens that we slay throughout the game are there have new variants.The Vortigaunts are much more surprising beings than we might think at first glance...Some areas are very industrialized and mechanical, while others are tribal and primitive, like in the Oddworld games.Xen contains traces of human activities, there are some installations and devices of all kinds.The original soundtrack by Joel Nielsen is simply masterful. It magnificently accentuates the feeling of strangeness and drama of the events suffered by Gordon Freeman with quite calm and mysterious sounds. During the fights, the music is very rock or orchestral and emphasizes the epic feeling of this atypical and mythical sci-fi shooter.On Xen, the music is as unique as it's breathtaking, composed of captivating sounds and exquisite lyrical female vocalizations.Black Mesa respects the authenticity of Half-Life by providing it with the necessary new features and accessibility.Newcomers will love the intriguing storyline, the masterfully orchestrated staging, and its anthology sequences.While veterans of the Half-Life franchise who have completed the first game countless times will appreciate the improved graphics, realistic physics, dynamic combat, subtle references to other episodes, and all the elements brought by this remake. The original work from 1998 is in no way stripped of its charm and is brilliantly modernized, with a delicious touch of fan service added.This is a must-have game.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is the fan made re imagining of what Half-Life 1 would look like in the modern day age of gaming. Since 2005 the game has been in development, however it is finally finished with a definitive version! The voice acting is spot-on perfect, the writing for the characters is clever and insightful to the story. Joel Nielsen, the composer of the musical score, did an amazing job. Many of these music tracks capture the atmosphere of whatever situation Gordon may be facing, whether it be an ambient or an action sequence. The soundtrack has gone through some small changes over development.The fact that it has workshop support is a bonus for us. Games that have Steam workshop allows for replay value, with amazing community content. I think the gameplay regarding the weapons and the enemies is for the most part balanced and has a fair gradual difficulty. Some complaints I might have are that the soldiers seem to be dead accurate. The Gonarch fight in Xen is a much improved version of the original Goldsrc HL1 fight because it gradually paces properly. Xen also manages to balance the gameplay of combat and puzzles. My favorite aspect of Xen would be the art style as well as it exploring the story and lore of Half-Life in greater detail just as it does in the earthbound levels. I love the artstyle/artpass in Xen because I'm fascinated by the cosmos and seeing this is comforting and relaxing to me, but I digress. The only complaint I have about Xen would be that sometimes I feel I died a cheap death by the alien controllers, however the devs balanced the fights. As for Nihilanth and Endgame, you play for yourself and watch your jaw drop, because that pushes the engine to the absolute .I am so amazed that Crowbar Collective was able to pull off a title like this, given that this is their first game! I highly recommend this if you're a fan of the Half-Life franchise. I bet Valve is secretly proud of them. I am excited to see what Crowbar Collective's next project will be, I am sure I will enjoy it. I think they won me over no matter what they choose to do next!

_childDocuments_.review: is how remakes are done: This game took Half-Life's story and gameplay principles and took the to our time, mainly from a graphical standpoint. The game closely follows HL's story closely and mainly uses its basic level structure, it may, on some occasions catch you off-guard by reinterpreting an area in a completely new way (like Xen probably if it ever comes out). Gameplay-wise, I did not see any problems and there only exists one flaw where the game will crash if you hurt its feelings by using the wrong graphics settings.Black Mesa's gunplay is pretty fun, no weapons feel too weak or too strong; other than that, there's not much to say except that it follows old FPS traditions instead of having a 2-weapon-limit.The game lets you interact with the NPCs which either help you fight or give you access to some secret or crucial areas (and while I do know that they are basically just numbers in my RAM, I always want to rescue all of them).TLDR: This might just be the best way Half-Life could be remade and if you liked HL1, play it; if you didn't ever play HL1, play that first and then appreciate how far we've come in PC graphics (and voice acting, Michael Hillard is just so great).Edit:Xen is an improvement over the old Half-Life's, however it feels very long (I think it was another 4 hours) and sometimes very annoying. Still, while being kind of an anti-climax (and some might just want to skip it) it is still worth playing through.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a remake of the original Half-Life game by Crowbar Collective (with the blessing of Valve). You experience the events of the Black Mesa incident with updated graphics and some minor addition in the later chapters. Most of the game is faithfully recreated apart from the final 4 chapters were they added some more content and tweaked a few things.Pros- Much improved graphics.- Stayed very true to the original, story is exactly the same.Cons- While graphics are much better than the original they are not quite 2020 graphics as the game was in development for a long time. More like 2012 graphics which is still great. Just don't go in expecting Ray Tracing etc.- Game felt easier than the original and one or two early levels were shortened a bit.Overall this is excellent and a great game in its own right. Play this if you are a fan of Half-Life and want to see the Black Mesa incident again with better graphics or if you think the original is too dated and you want better visuals.While they added more things in the final 4 chapters you could tell which part of the game was from the original and which were made for the remake. The extra bits while good didn't feel like they meshed with the rest of the game.Played and streamed the whole thing a couple of years ago and here is my video Review at the time :

_childDocuments_.review: It's a staggering achievement.As I rode the tram into the Black mesa Complex, I felt the old magic, the same way I did when I was a much younger, more innocent man, playing Half life 1 on a computer that likely couldn't interface with the internet today.The scale of the game is unequaled in an FPS. Black Mesa Complex is huge, and Xen, ever bigger.  It's not for show either, the player maintains a sense of moving through the world.Now however, the visuals resemble those of the games successor Half Life 2,  which arguably ranks among the greatest first person shooters of all time, and has aged like a fine wine thanks to the love and dedication of it's community.  The image was widescreen 1080p, textures are updated...  but it was HALF LIFE, and I felt like I had left Kansas once again.Crowbar Collective have made a faithful update toHalf Life 1 that inspires the same sense of awe and wonder that I felt the first time I stepped into Gordon's HEV suit.They haven't made it a full "AAA" style update with pointless graphic features, Mo-Cap and animated every little thing. The interactivity is as high as Valve ever made it, imo, no one was better.  However, the game loses NOTHING without all the bells and whistles of a modern production.  If anything Black Mesa feels even more immersive without those distractions, and runs wonderfully, likely even on lower tier systems.The overall effect highlights the absolute genius of Valve during their heyday, a development team who did nearly EVERYTHING right, and deserves all the good fortune, accolades and wealth that they've garnered in successive years. Simultaneously, the brilliance and devotion of Crowbar Collective, who made it their mission to faithfully update one of the most immersive, beloved gaming experiences of all time for modern audiences, is on full display.Side note, Black Mesa is a Master Class in how modern developer's should treat classic properties, they have not "reimagined" the experience, subjected it to the whims of modern politics or taken excessive creative liberties. Crowbar Collective's love and devotion for the original title shines through on everything they've done, and I am grateful.To people who have never played HL1, do yourself a favor, and play this, and while you are doing so, marvel at how many things you have seen in other games found their origin here, and in many cases, failed to live up to Valve's Timeless creation.Then play Half Life 2, and you will understand why  legions of devoted fans are still so perplexed and frustrated  that Valve Never released half Life 3 and finished Gordons story.  (No matter how brilliant it is, ALYX does NOT count).  You will understand why even to this day, 15 years after HL2, there are still those who dare to hope.Don't miss this.  Worth it at twice the price.(apparently, they have added at ton of additional content, MP and custom maps.  I am not sure, but it can only make the game BETTER)20 out of 10, go grab your crowbars.Addendum:Perhaps the only subpar section of the original game, underwhelming after what was an outstanding Adventure, it felt like Valve rushed through Xen.The same clever puzzles were there, interaction and combat wise, it was a worthy ending to the title.Visually however, Xen was a disappointment in half life.NOT ANYMORE.After I passed through the Lambda portal, I knew I was in for a treat, hell, the visuals from the portal itself are jaw-dropping...  and perhaps i was misremembering, but the level itself is MASSIVE, alternating between puzzles, combat, platforming and running for your life.Crowbar Collective has improved on every aspect of Black Mesa's Final chapter.The entirety of the realm feels alien, yet believable.  Weird and wonderful, everywhere you look you are greeted with pure visual spectacle, surreal, deadly eye candy.The Flora and Fauna are believable, with the exception of the entirely gravity defying nature of the landscape, but I suppose that's part of Xen's phantasmagoric allure.  Despite this, it still comes across as a believable biome, the various monsters that had tormented you on your journey through the Black Mesa complex are shown in reasonable context, intrinsic parts of the environment, both in locomotive capability, and camouflage.  The creatures appearances and offensive capabilities are explained, without a single word, by their unnatural habit.The environmental puzzles that allowed Gordon Freeman to Weave his way through the Black Mesa complex also exist in Xen, I have to commend the developers on the fact that none of it felt obvious, the pathways you would need to take to get where you were going are intrinsic parts of the environment, they look like they belong there, not that they merely exist to facilitate Gordon's Passage.The sound design is fantastic, blending the odd noises of the creatures with further environmental sounds, creating the impression of an alien rainforest, brimming with life, and very much seeking to take yours.Xen's natural properties explain why Black Mesa was so interested in researching the place, both for it's levitating materials, as well as elements of a natural origin which were capable of generating tremendous electrical (and otherwise) energy.I recommend moving cautiously through the area, visually identifying Environmental hazards, and how to use them on your enemies. Even on medium difficulty, ammo is scarce.There are a few surprises, and I'm going to leave it at that.Like every other part of the game, the completion of a puzzle leaves you with a tremendous feeling of satisfaction....  it's an added bonus, that the entire time you are more than happy to stop and take in the scenery.No one has done first person puzzle-platforming better.The Gonarch is the Gold standard for boss fights. Nihilanth is also fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Its an amazing game and personally a Remake done right. My only Qualm though is Xen itself now on its looks or what it does its beautiful and that's not the problem. But my problem with it is Xen is a REALLY performance taxing section I feel some more optimizations should have been made because even being reasonably above recommended specs you WILL drop frames regardless of graphic setting unless you have a High to Very High end PC.I dont have the right to say its huge size causes it to overstay its welcome because im not a long time fan but that is a nitpick of mine. But I will say Xen needs to be broken up or optimized more for performance and if unable should raise its minimum and recommended specs accordingly on the store page because if you fall onto the recommended specs 20 to 30 fps is the norm on the Xen section with some sections in it going as low as 10fps. I am very tolerable to that but I am saying this right now to play the game at 60fps across you'll need to high ball the recommended specs in the games current state.As for the two achievements PhD in Pacifism and Laser Immunization its very hard if you try to do that in 1 run but remember you can save and reload at any time if you made a mistake. So I recommend saving much more often to get those two because there very arduous and difficult otherwise as saving and reloading does not invalidate achievements so long as the failure was done before the save.Sure its save scuffing but its how with quite a lot of trial and error was able to get those 2 achievements that will save you a lot of headache if your a completionist.Also if your wondering about performance to quell any about my rigs inability these are my specs and I will compare them to the recommended. And tell you if the Recommended is Greater then [>] or Less then [<] my system to quell any, my computer is to weak comments. I was Playing the game on Medium to Medium-High settings.OS: Windows® 7 (32/64-bit) or Greater<Windows® 10 (64-Bit)Processor: 3.2 Quad Core Processor or Greater<AMD FX-6300 Six-Core Processor 3.5GhzMemory: 8 GB RAM<20 GB DDR3                         Graphics: 4 GB Dedicated Video Card or Greater<Radeon RX 5500 XT 8 GB Dedicated.On Medium to Medium-High Settings I get 60FPS most of the game 30 to 60fps on the outside sections and anything between 10 to 30FPS in Xen. And just to eliminate outside factors id still get these frames regardless of Discord Streaming or other applications outside of the game being up or closed. Despite punching twice as hard as recommended in some of the requirements when recommended means at least to me you should be fully able to play at 60FPS reliably on High and almost all the time on anything lower then that.So what does that mean? Well it means that Xen and the Outside sections are not considered in this performance analysis and thus this analysis is only based on the inside sections which do encompass most of the game and you will get 60FPS flat in those sections with Recommended. But if you do Recommended or lower Frame loss in those later sections is inevitable so for 60 FPS flat as I said prior you WILL need to High ball the recommended for that kind of frame rate across the game.Hence why the game is still recommended because about 70 to 90% of it is still very much playable but because of this obscene performance demand in these places when recommended SHOULD account for that on Medium at the very least. I have to drop it to a 7.75/10 because of some of the later more intensive scenes and of course Xen one of the most anticipated sections in the game is sometimes rendered completely unplayable because of that.Also and I know this next part is off topic but it highlights an innate flaw with the specs of a game in Steam it will tell you what is required but that doesn't always apply to ALL of the game. Most of the game can be easy to run but select sections can be completely contrasting to its expected specs causing this situation where a person buys and plays a game expecting it to run fine on there rig only to run into that large section that renders it next to unplayable.Its even worse here because Xen is at the tail end of the game so you play through most of Black Mesa and now cant beat it because Xen is a performance hog of a section outside of expected specs and cant refund it since your now past the 2 hour refund mark not saying you should if you play through most of a game but for instance if someone less genuine was to do that it would be a nasty rug pull scheme. Thankfully that is not the case here its an amazing and genuine dev team that hopefully will fix that, and I managed to get through it and beat it but still, that's pretty bad.

_childDocuments_.review: - Yes, particularly if you've NEVER played Half-Life and don't have any games on backlog...still, yes, even if that doesn't apply to you. - Ok, weirdo. Imagine you're a doctor who works at Area 51's sister facility and you're getting ready to experience the most insane day ever.  - NO. This is what Valve meant to make the first time they made Half-Life. The game has evolved on nearly every level, not just textures, and you would think it was developed much closer to today than it was. Unfortunately, I've only played Half-Life on Xbox 360's Orange Box, so I had to buy the original Half-Life again to compare (it's been a while). I only booted it up and compared the first chapter of both and that's all I needed to do to see what Black Mesa actually was. Black Mesa is so good that I won't be able to forget Half-Life again. In just the first chapter there are complete chunks of Black Mesa that didn't exist on the original. The chunks are so expertly inserted that when you experience it backwards, it kinda feels like Half-Life could be the mobile version of Black Mesa.Black Mesa is actually a masterpiece like people say, but isn't perfect. I'm overly critical in Cons because it's so good I want to be more constructive for the sake of wasting my time giving my opinion. - The environmental story telling is so strong here it could be used as the benchmark for identifying future masterpieces. - Real love and time was put into crafting believable details every step of the way; even the marker written on white boards is legible and contains interesting info. - No inventory screens and minimal HUD makes the experience immersive af.- The game isn't short, and can afford you a few really nice, long, unforgettable sessions of time. - The atmosphere and level design is done in such a way that keeps things feeling as fresh as they can and makes you want to keep playing. - The story itself is so interesting that I'm almost convinced this all really happened and they only developed this game as a cover up to hide the truth in plain sight...- The gunplay is not what you come here for, especially if you're a seasoned FPS player. Hit boxes and recoil can feel so sketchy at times, even when you know they probably aren't. - Everything/everyone is a bullet sponge unless you're using a few of the more obviously powerful weapons. Honestly, it's just the Glock, MP5, the Hive Hand, and the suicide bug grenades. Such trash. - Multiplayer is included, but for me, is unplayable. Maybe I always join a bad server, but there are never more than 2 for me to pick from with a total of 25 people playing. You lag and teleport constantly, but it's clear you would be having fun if it would just act right and more people played.  - Some boss encounters are very unbalanced, where vehicles are able to withstand much more damage than is acceptable.  With that said, I was compelled  to write this before actaully  finishing the game, so I hope the last boss is good.-  Platforming sections of the game can be ridiculous at times. If you press 'S' while moving forward in mid-air, you literally stop moving, which led to some bad deaths for me. Later in the game, if you double jump into a surface, you'll reflect off of it like a beam of light, which might also make you die. -  No menus or objectives means getting lost will likely be an issue for you at least once, no matter how much attention you pay to details or how good you are at navigating in general. The game feels much more old school in the sense that it doesn't hold your hand. Some people complain about it, but I think it makes you a better gamer. I broke down and googled ONE thing, but I had a regert because when you figure it out on your own, it's rewarding. I wonder if a lot of gamers today even really know what I mean...- The default difficulty is "Normal", which would be the equivalent of "Easy". It's pretty much Story Mode, because you won't die. The "Black Mesa" setting feels much better, but it seems to only prevent YOU from being a bullet sponge, enemies still eat bullets.All in all: Good times, Worth It.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game! One of the best and immersive game I have ever played and is probably one of the greatest remake of all time. I have played some of the original Half-Life to compare it to this game. In my opinion, Black Mesa is pretty much that but improved in many aspects (Especially Xen), even though it's build upon the concept of Half-Life, it feels different. The visuals are impressive and its surpisingly well optimized for having that many graphical details, the combat is fun and challanging and so are the pussles and the soundtrack is absolutely BAD ASS. Had a blast throughout the whole game. But there are some small issues (which are quite rare) with the game, some areas the AI behaves weirdly and does not attack and places where thing are acting weird and some areas in Xen has large framedrops, but they are minor and the game is very polished otherwise, hope some of these issues are gathered out once the game is fully complete This game should be like todays game, not holding your hand throughout the whole game like most games today, showing big arrows guiding you where to exactly go and task bars showing exact details of what to do like distance of the objective, flashing pickable objects and AI designed to give the player advantage. This game is designed to let you figure it out by yourself by looking around your environmet and the enemy AI is designed to actually challange you and give no advantage what so ever, it gives you a very rewarding feeling when progressing levels and it makes you feel smart and good at the game, and lets not forget... The beauty of Enviromental Storytelling. No cinematic cutscene crap that games nowadays just fills it with. This is not a movie for god sake, its a video game, we want to play and interact, not watch! Yeah you hear that Hideo Kojima, your latest title was more of a movie than a video game, atleast you made it entertaining for the people watching Let's Plays. Developers should play this game and most of the older games (Like Half-Life, Quake) and start to realize that games back then had a way better concept for single player games. But it's all about the money, and majority of the money comes from the casuals, and they don't like challanges.Amazing remake. Pretty much the Enhanced Half-Life9.5/10Would play through the whole game again in Hard Mode.Edit 1: Added another opinion

_childDocuments_.review: It's so nice seeing Half Life in updated resolution and graphics, the presentation is really well done. And, frankly, that's about all I really expected from this, soo.... Good job.There ARE, however, a couple things that are much WORSE than the original:-LADDERS! I don't know HOW they managed it, because the ladders in HL were EPICLY bad, but they somehow made them EVEN WORSE. They are SUPER sticky, dismounting is a pain, and shoots you off in some random direction ~70% of the time. Just horrible-Turned soldiers into a bit of an ass - ache: they are SUPER twitchy, the hit registration against them is a little dodgy, while THEY, on the other hand, have terminator aim.-They messed around with almost ALL of the puzzles. Some they cleaned up and improved, a bunch they made WAY worse, and some they just took out entirely. Pretty crappy.-Xen. What was basically the most teeth pulling, overlong, and not worthwhile section of the original, they decided to: Make it about SIX TIMES LONGER, add about 200% MORE platforming puzzles, put in what is basically a turret section that takes WAY too long, and completely removed ALL portal elements from the Nihilanth fight.Overall? I'd say it's worth it for a veteran Half Life player, just seeing everything with a fresh coat on. To a newcomer? I'd honestly recommend just going and playing the original. Sure, it's not as shiny, but it performs better mechanically and it has much better pacing. This very much FEELS like it was made by "fans"... Which can be good, AND bad.

Every weapon is useful, nothing feels underpowered or useless, exploration is rewarded, so is attention to detail, and ammo is scarce enough to stop you from going ham on everything but common enough that you don't have to worry too much about wasting ammo which pushes the player to use the most appropriate weapon for the situation without being too punishing.You don't need to be told all this, you likely already know what you're in for. Buy it and enjoy, it's hard to not have fun with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is it folks, this is what a master piece looks like. I played Half-Life way back in the day and am a huge fan of the series, so I would have been delighted by a quality remaster. This game is not a remaster, its not a graphics update, its not a fresh mod on an old game. Black Mesa is such a radical improvement on the classic Half-Life that it was like experiencing the adventure for the first time all over again. With master class voice acting, superior level design, intriguing puzzles, toe tapping soundtrack and frantic combat, the Black Mesa team have made a unique and engaging game that I would recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Black Mesa because I had never played the original Half-Life and wanted to experience it but with better graphics.  I am okay at FPS games, and I played the game at its default difficulty of normal.I thoroughly enjoyed my time overall with this game.  I had only one crash late in the game, and don't recall any bugs or glitches while I played.  From the beginning up to Xen, I really got immersed in feeling like I was making my way through a gigantic complex.  There are times that feel claustrophobic, and others that feel epic and genuinely brought a smile to my face.  There are times where you are working your way down corridors, and there are huge battles in open arenas.  I enjoyed that there were times that were low key, where you were doing some platforming or exploring or puzzling, so that it wasn't constant action.  The game "breathes", and I prefer that style immensely.Xen onward was a mixed bag.  I loved the first couple areas of Xen.  It looks fantastic, and you are given plenty of opportunities to enjoy the alien flora and fauna.  From the first big boss fight onward, my excitement started to wane--but it wasn't terrible by any means.  The difficulty definitely jumps up.  You start having combat that is a bit different than before in that you really need to continuously move quickly.  Previous to this, I felt I could duck in and out of cover.  You start having long chase scenes where you have to puzzle out your path while instant death is constantly on your heels, which can lead to what feels like trial-and-error with little actual strategy or skill involvement.  Epic feeling once you know where you are going, but annoying until that point.  Levels start to feel long and repetitive, and felt more like gaming challenges than immersive experiences.  Some are fine with that, but for me the level and encounter designs felt lesser than what came before.  Final boss battle is intense and will give you a challenge but feels very epic and I enjoyed it.If you like FPS games, it's a good one.  Just be ready for a difficulty jump at the end, and remember that when in doubt, run like hell.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't even a remake anymore, this is taking Half Life to the next level. The visuals are stunning, especially in the new Xen levels. The levels have all been faithfully redone, and in many places, even made better. This is overall, all around, just better than the original. If you liked the original, play this version. If you have been on the fence about playing the original Half Life because it was an older looking game, play this. Honestly, everyone who worked on this game, you all deserve a medal. Half Life was my favorite game growing up, and to see it like this, it is just, so amazing. Play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I ignore Early Access titles, and normally I wait until I've finished the game before reviewing it, but oh.my.god. this game is amazing. Screenshots on the Steam page don't do it justice, the team behind this remake has made Black Mesa feel alive like never before, particularly the attention to detail in the level design (watching the game world slowly infected/taken over by Xen life is great). I'm just completely blown away by the level of quality in this title, I can emphatically say that Crowbar Collective has done the original title justice. If you love the original Half-Life, this will hook you start to finish. If you've never played Half-Life 1, but want to know what you're missing, and are perhaps put off by the 1998 graphics, this is the way to play the original campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Very little community mods of any game have come as far as Black Mesa, you can't even really consider this a mod anymore but a .After 15+ years of development, it shows in its quality and refined reimaginings of Half-Life's events.The Graphics are stunning and truly push Source beyond its limits.The new Xen chapters are a great improvement over the original.The improved AI of many of the enemies bring lots of fun to combat, especially against Alien Grunts.I can't wait for whatever CC plans to do after Black Mesa, hopefully it doesn't take 15+ years though.There's too much praise i can give this game, utterly an incredible piece of work, "I am impresssssssed".
