_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original Half-Life so this won't be a comparison review. The graphics are modern compared to some of the screen shots I've seen of the original game. I'd say they look like a game that came out in the 2010's. Some of the later areas in Xen look gorgeous but suffer some frame-rate issues and lag even on a 1080ti but I did have all the graphics cranked up. It's a re-imagining of one of the grand-daddies of First Person Shooters. Fundamentally, you shoot things, find new weapons, solve puzzles, and do some light platforming. There are some intense firefights with some decent AI that hides behind cover, and tries to flank you. The couple boss fights were well developed and had a good amount of difficulty. The voice overs for the NPC scientists and guards are fine, nothing great but they sound like they were done by the same voice actor. The music that plays during some of the more intense moments and in the Xen chapters are excellent. Something I'd actually want to hear outside of the game. I particularly liked the otherworldly tranquil feel of the Xen music.I decided to get this game because I saw it on sale and wanted to immerse myself into the Half-Life universe prior to starting up the new Alyx game in VR. The game has a lot more play time than I expected for an FPS single player experience. Even though this is a remake of a classic, I can see how the original disrupted and changed the industry. Crowbar Collective did a superb job modernizing Half-Life for today's audience!2 thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: A game where a lot of love was put in its development. On the most part, this game feels much better than the original, due to the improved engine and newly added mechanics, as well as Xen being expanded quite heavily.We probably won't be seeing Half Life 3 in this decade due to Valve's secrecy and Steam being too productive for them, but this game will definitely fill the void for all Half Life hungry fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played Black Mesa as a mod for HL2 and while I liked it, there were many things keeping from having much fun. But I'm glad to say that most problems I had with the mod are not present in this game and I had a lot of fun playing it.To start off, the atmosphere in this game is perfect. The original Half Life didn't really impress me in that sense, I mostly just played for the gameplay itself. Black Mesa took the setting and nailed it on the head, it easily blew Half Life 2 and its episodes out of the water for me. I often took time to just soak in the environment around me, even more than I did in Portal 2 and its amazing set pieces. From the rusted under layers of the facility to the cliffside Mesa, it impressed me.In terms of actual gameplay, the game is far more balanced and less cheap than it was as a mod. Enemies feel like they take the right amount of damage for the difficulty. Weapons feel balanced and are often fun to use and the layout of the maps compliments the battles. Though fun to use, some weapons feel underpowered, specifically the shotgun and partially the pistol. The shotgun feels like it does to little damage for its spread, even at close range a single shot isn’t always enough to kill an enemy soldier or vortigaunt. The pistol isn’t viable in combat compared to the machine gun which does the same amount of damage per shot and has pretty good accuracy. In the original Half Life the accuracy was allot worse meaning that at longer ranges, the pistol was viable over the machine gun, but due to the accuracy being good on the machine gun, the pistol is underutilized even in a situation with only one or two enemies. Another thing that bugs me (as it did in HL2) is that the max ammo for the revolver is only 12, oftentimes I would come across 2 boxes of ammo for the revolver and never be able to pick up both. This is also a common problem with the 9mm bullets as there is always way more than you could ever hope to hold, and I run out of ammo to quickly while in combat often and I would strongly recommend raising the ammo capacity to around 240.The only enemy I feel is unbalanced is the bullsquid, I feel it has too much health for its high bullet resistance, especially because of how early in the game you first encounter it. It never took as long to kill in Half Life.The Music is top notch, while I still greatly enjoy the HL soundtrack, the music is very well made and compliments the atmosphere of the situation it plays in, surpassing the original soundtrack in that way.I had a few game bugs pop up as well.2 game crashes, once while transitioning a map, and once while saving. I also had a graphical glitch in the tunnel right before the gargantua fight in surface tension were textures were stretching across the screen, a simple game reset fixed this. Other than that, there was minor stuttering when I would launch the game and load a save, but that always smoothed out within a few mins of playtime.Overall I would highly recommend this game, it exceeded all expectations I had. The problems I mentioned are so small and can easily be fixed manually if one wished by opening the skills configuration file and changing the values, though I wouldnt recomend this however unless you have played through the game before.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a Half-Life game, but after hearing almost everything there is to say about it over the course of years, it was something I've always been interested in trying. Then Black Mesa came along and it seemed like the perfect way to dip my feet in. Does it live up to all the hype? Kind of.Context is key here. This game was one of the first narrative based shooters, and it gets its story across without breaking up gameplay with cut scenes. The gunplay feels fluid, every environment feels different enough, and the story has a nice escalation to it. However, I don't think it's going to leave as much of an impression as it did upon release when playing it for the first time in 2020.The NPCs you interact with tend to have similar personalities, and even when escorting one down a few hallways, they always end up staying behind amidst disaster instead of trying to escape with you. Certain sections also feel a little bloated, especially when traversing through the alien world (although it is the most interesting part of the game). A smaller enemy variety also starts to wear itself out by the end of the game too, with the exception to the final couple bosses.This remake can feel like more of a time capsule of its ingenuity than something currently revolutionary, and that's not a bad thing. The extra polish makes it more palatable to newcomers, and in an age of deliberate grind and microtransactions, it's good to keep in mind what made games fun and engaging in the first place.7/10 you can also pretend you're a Ghostbuster, so that's neat

_childDocuments_.review: The Pros of Black Mesa.+ Outstanding Level Design+ Tight Shooting Gameplay+ Great Weapon Variety as it was in the original+ Good AI+ Great use of the Source Engine+ Does what all remakes does right, getting rid of the bad and improving on the good+ Much Improved Voice Acting+ Puzzles are put to smart use+ Great Customization in the options menu+ Xen is a beautiful sight and a stronger level+ Great Final Boss+ Mod Support, use the Nostalgia Music Mod for true Half-Life 1 musical experience+ Mature storyline+ Smart use of Enemy variety+ Ending+ Maintains the themes of the Half-Life seriesThe Cons of Black Mesa.- Bugs as expected from the Source Engine- Certain jumping sequence in Interloper can softlock your progress, forcing a hard reset unless your smart enough to save the game- Multiplayer doesn't bring much original bone to the game- Doesn't innovate the Half-Life formula all that much- Forgettable Soundtrack that is no where near as thematic and atmospheric as the original- Can be brutally hard in the later levels, its not much of a flaw but be ready for a challenge- Some Action Scripted Sequence feels pointless in narrative structure- Framerate can dip from places, it'll depend on your end of the experience- Will be hard for other Remakes (Besides Resident Evil 1 & 2 Remake) to top thisFinal Score for: Black Mesa.Story: 8/10Design: 9/10Gameplay: 8/10Presentation: 8/10Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The playable character is physicist Gordon Freeman, who becomes part of a failed experiment in the Black Mesa Research Facilities laboratories, somewhere in the deserts of New Mexico. This catastrophic event will trigger a series of events that you will explore throughout the game.The gameplay consists of going through corridor passages, overcoming puzzles and a story that is always told without the use of any cutscenes. The game tells everything through dialogues both with companions who will accompany you and through random characters scattered around the map.Puzzles are a big part of the game and some are very challenging. Not knowing what to do, however, never means you're playing the game wrong or that you're not paying attention. It means that the developers of the game wanted you to get lost in the game and so you have to explore the environment and figure out what is wanted of you.Don't wait for any indicator in the game to guide you to the destination. You have to figure everything out yourself. Although it's a more or less linear game, there are many tricky areas and I honestly don't think there's anyone among us who hasn't stopped at some point in Half-Life to think about where you're supposed to go or what's expected of you . However, after sometimes less, sometimes more time spent researching, you will realize that the level design of this game is absolutely brilliant and once you understand what is wanted of you, everything starts to make sense. The levels are varied, the tasks are not repeated with a few exceptions, and the balance of action and logical sequences is perfect.Black Mesa is clearly the best way to experience the first Half-Life.

If you're into FPS campaigns, then you're in for a treat with Black Mesa.I have already played and finished the original Half Life, but now with Black Mesa I could finally understand how big of an impact this game had back in the day, and I can't wait to play HL2 because of this.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is pretty great. It could be better but it seems like Crowbar Collective is working on some fixes so they are forgiven for now. Anyway, here is my pros and cons for this wonderful homage to the original  from 1998 (as an aside, Happy 21st birthday HL1!).Pros : • Great sound effects (firearms, alien weapons, etc)• Great particle effects (gunsmoke, dust/particles in light beams, etc)• Voice acting great (the actors used sound very much like the original)• Animations (really nice when compared to orignal)• Music/OST (the composition sounds amazingly like the original)Cons:• Glitches (mostly buffer crashes or bad rendering)• Rendering (the surface scattering on many of the objects in the game, especially xen could use work)• Bullet-spongy enemies (Developers did discuss making enemies weaker)• Annoying save zones/gates (saves you in the middle of being mortally wounded)These were my main topics, but I'm confidant that once its out of beta, it will be a polished and highly criticized game. Good work Crowbar Collective thus far! I can't wait to see what's next!P.S.I am using the Black Mesa [public-beta] for future reference, so I do have a few more bugs than those who are not using the same version as me.7/18/22This game has come along way since my last review. Crowbar Collective has since added in offical workshop support, resulting in numerous mods, some of which have become essential to my playthroughs. They fixed nearly every bug, resulting in a very stable game with only minor bugs that are usually related to the rendering of the game as that is processed by the CPU. I would certainly say this has become of the best games of the last decade and I can't wait to see what else CC develops. It would be interesting to see if they get permission to remake other Half-Life games into high quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa was originally a Source Engine mod which was released to the public back in 2012, but was announced a number of years previously.Considering that Black Mesa was made by a group of modders, the game has significantly overshadowed other Source Engine mods in terms of quality.Black Mesa can be compared to many AAA 8th Generation titles which are released currently. High graphical fidelity as well as gameplay that is similar to many shooter titles today.Is Black Mesa good? Yes, in fact I'd say that it's better than the original Half Life. There are a number of elements of Half Life which no longer hold up, most of which have been removed, reworked or reimagined entirely to fit in much better in the game. The attention to detail will make you remember the original Half Life in a more favourable way. I have only one complaint, that Residue Processing is still as horrible with its platforming as ever, that's it. Surface Tension is however much better in execution. Tanks are mobile, appear 3 times and have a much more challenging AI. Infantry Fighting Vehicles also debut, but appear once. Snipers are better and are modified versions of the Combine snipers of HL2.As far as I can tell, gameplay is enhanced and that elements from HL2 gameplay is adapted while staying true to the original HL gameplay.Xen is missing from the game at time of writing this review. Apparently the plan is to totally overhaul the Xen levels in order to make them more playable and provide a superior player experience.The game up until that point is very much polished. There is very little to fault the game with. Perhaps a lack of voice actors (I suspect something like 6 were used). The player is also sometimes prone to getting stuck in invisible objects (time to brush up on console commands and noclip) but now I'm nitpicking.I recommend Black Mesa for all those who played the original Half Life and want to relive the game with modern graphics and modern gameplay. I also recommend Black Mesa to those who have never played Half Life. It permits players to experience the original game with the original plot line, but experience it in a modern way in line with many other games released today.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of the past is made into one of the best remakes of all time.Now this is how you do remakes! You take the original, fix its flaws and build upon it to make a modern game out of it. A good remake should become the ultimate way to enjoy the game. If people look at your remake and say "Well, a lot of it had been done better in the original", you have failed. If people say "Well, this feels like an entirely different game from the original", you have failed. Yes, I'm looking at you, Capcom! Instead of reinventing the wheel, you just fix and expand. And Black Mesa is a briliant example of it.It's really mind blowing when you think that this game was made not by a giant studio with tons of budget and divisions of people, but merely by people who just really enjoyed the original and who, for most part, have been driven purely by enthusiasm.This is a full-blown indie-AAA title. It's not a "Half-Life 1 with models from Half-Life 2". Will lightnings, effects and everything, it's much better than Half Life 2. And most importantly, it's much better than Half Life 1. I will go as far as to say, you can play this game instead of Half Life 1, and you will get everything HL1 has to offer and more.It should be a $60 game. Anything less is a steal and you better get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, they really fixed this one up. I played it a couple times back when it was a free mod and while there was plenty of potential there was just so much "off" about it. The soldiers were way too OP, the weapons handled like crap and it was too hard. Not in a challenging way, but in a cheap way. It was garbage.However, lately I had been on a Half-Life binge and figured I'd give the mod another go, so I forked over the new $20 price tag.I don't know if it was Valve's intervention or community input but good lord did they turn this game around. Not only does it finally meet the original Half-Life's standards, it goes above and beyond them. The remodeled Black Mesa looks fantastic. Everything else has been upgraded as well: weapon models, characters, enemies, there are even some new nooks and crannies to be discovered. It feels just like it should: a fresh new take on an iconic classic.First and foremost: Pathfinding. Since all entities are based on the Source engine, NPC's no longer get stuck on boxes or corners; they go AROUND. You almost never have to look over your shoulder to make sure they've got your back. Likewise, not only are the new marines more fun to fight, they have combine AI which means no run-stop-fire-run-stop fire; these guys run AND shoot. They actually look and sound like real human beings too, in fact I found them incredibly sympathetic and even started to feel sorry for them as their mission began to fall apart one platoon at a time. The new military PA system is incredibly threatening, as are the new turrents. And don't get me started on the Alien Grunts, who resemble some sort of angry Nazi Super Soldier.All of the weaponry is a pleasure to use. Most of the set-pieces from the original have been redesigned to pay homage to the original game while adding little twists to keep the player on their toes, giving you a sensation of both nostalgia and apprehension that is hard to capture. In the level Office Complex, setting zombies on fire using flares causes the sprinkles to go off and alarms to activate. The military base at the end of Surface Tension is now elevated and riddled with sewer pipes, forcing you to engage with marines vertically instead of horizontally. During the famous cliff descent, bombers fly overhead and obliterate distant targets on the horizon. Late in the game you come upon a tank moving down an alley firing sideways toward overwhelming hordes of Xen fauna. Do you intervene, or wait to engage the victor?There are the usual Source quirks. The game skips from time to time, especially when using the flashlight. I found grenades extremely difficult to aim; they would often fly off to the right of my crosshair, bouncing off the rims of doors and other openings and landing back at my feet. You can dodge the Vortigaunt thunderbolt now, which seems like kind of a cop-out; in the original, staying out of sight before their "charge" sequence finished required on-the-fly tactical maneuvering. Now, their most unique and memorable trait has been nerfed. I only encountered a few glitches; some corpses float in the air, and the same with some objects during outdoor sections. Some marines seemed too slow on the uptake later in the game, and I was infuriated at monsters would automatically rush me and me alone during three-way firefights.These are small issues compared to the bigger picture, which is impressive. This game is clearly a labor of love nearly a decade in the making, and will only get better when Xen is (hopefully) released later this year.

_childDocuments_.review: It's impossible to overstate how much of a game changer the original Half Life was at the time. The opening 15 minutes consisted of a monorail ride through the expansive Black Mesa research facility and small talk with the coworkers. By this point, before anything of any significance had happened, I was all in. FPS games had been around for nearly 10 years, but none had introduced storytelling beyond 'shoot the bad guys' and maaaaybe 'find the blue key.' But Half Life introduced an actual plot and story line: at a top secret research facility in New Mexico, an experiment goes awry and opens a rift with another world and you, playing scientist Gordon Freeman, are one of the few survivors. You need to try to escape the facility while avoiding a government containment and clean up team.But alas, Half Life got old and it *felt* old. The story was still stellar, but the graphics were stuck in the late 1990s. That's where Black Mesa was born. Black Mesa isn't really a reboot or a remake, it is more like a digitally remastered Blu-ray release of an old movie: sharper picture, better audio, maybe some deleted scenes, but by and large the same story nearly scene-for-scene.The graphics in Black Mesa aren't GREAT, but they're certainly several steps above the original and they're enough to make the game feel modern enough. I got those same tingles on that opening monorail ride and had a wide smile on my face when re-encountering familiar chapters I'd played 21 years before. And the 'Zen' maps, depicting an other worldly planet that Freeman encounters later in the game are oftentimes downright gorgeous!That said, Zen is also the only knock on the game for me. I'll admit, I wasn't a big fan of the Zen chapters in the original Half Life. I liked the familiarity of the earth-bound Black Mesa research facility and jumping to another astral plane with different gravity, toxins and creatures just felt like too much of a hard turn for me. I emphasize the 'FOR ME' there, as I realize it's subjective. While the Zen levels in Black Mesa are truly beautiful, it feels like they're also significantly longer than they were in the original game. I'm going off of memory here but it felt like Half Life, the research facility chapters made up about 70% of total time spent in the game while Zen chapters made up the remaining 30%, while in Black Mesa I spent about 10 hours each in the research facility and the Zen chapters. For someone not all that keen on Zen to begin with, more Zen did not make Black Mesa a better experience. Finishing the 'Interloper' chapter in the Black Mesa remake was more of a laborious chore than an exciting adventure. It was a very lovely laborious chore though.All in all, Black Mesa is a nice way to enjoy the original 1998 Half Life experience through the eyes of a 2012-ish computer engine, and if you've not played the original Half Life then Black Mesa is definitely a game worth acquiring.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is an incredible and faithful remake of the seminal Half-Life.  It's not just a lick of paint to spruce things up (I'm looking at you, Half-Life: Source), but a total overhaul, while still remaining true to the spirit of the original.  The one exception is Xen; notoriously a low point at the end of an otherwise incredible game, the final chapters have been reimagined and fleshed out in a way that makes them enjoyable to play and compelling to experience, while adding meaningful context for other aspects of the Half-Life canon.It's hard for me to objectively review Black Mesa on its own merits as an FPS in 2020, rather than simply viewing it through the lens of the original Half-Life, but it certainly  enjoyable to me.  It's clear this was a passion project for the team, who were largely volunteers until fairly well along into the remake's rather protracted development.That said, I would like to highlight the absolute sadistic nature of the game's most difficult achievements.  While I love that there aren't any multiplayer achievements (or any that necessitate excessive grind) that would exclude a single-player-only gamer like myself from racking up another complete set of cheevos, the fact that there are three separate achievements that require carrying an object through, respectively: two entire levels, half the game, and nearly the entire game is downright cruel and unusual punishment.  This is only exacerbated when ladders and teleporters can be an exercise in frustration.But I .  That said, if you've done the longest and shortest ones already, I say there's no shame in activating buddha mode for the last one, for the sake of your sanity.  Oh, and when you enter Questionable Ethics, bring both the  to the lobby and leave them there.  That way, you can save after you make your way through the facility and can start your next run without having to make your way all the way around again.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa:Was it worth to wait?Is it worth to buy and to play?Yes and yes.This game takes the Half-Life franchise and the source engine into a complete new level of gameplay, high-quality design, conceptual interpretation and technology. It's the end of an era.All Xen chapters are fully available and offer that kind gameplay and atmosphere Half-Life 1 was originally supposed to contain and even more. The brilliant redesign and extension of the environmental setting and the implementation of completely new gameplay elements and scenarios makes the borderworld finally become alive.The only negatives I can say about this game are:-Currently bad performance and critical issues for various users-Some critical issues that might cause crashes (Most of them are already beeing addressed and will be fixed to the final release)-Multiplayer issues in the current state of development-Some other minor bugs and issues throughout the gameJudging by the great job the developers have already done over the past 7 years since the first mod release I suppose that these issues will be fixed before leaving Early Access so in general I can say that Black Mesa is just a masterpiece of a game of the Half-Life series and the entire Sci-Fi FPS genre. It's not only a great remake for all Half-Life fans it's also a great game for experiencing a thrilling adventure as well as for a very first contact with the FPS genre and the Half-Life universe from the beginning.Black Mesa definitely proves what can be achieved by people who love their community, think of thair work on a game as a passion and love to give back to the community instead of only beeing interested in making money.I'm agree that both Black Mesa and the team of Crowbar Collective have... limitlesssss... potentialll!

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a stunning remake of the classic 1998 first-person shooter game, Half-Life. Developed by Crowbar Collective, the game aims to capture the essence of the original game while updating it with modern graphics, improved gameplay mechanics, and other enhancements.One of the standout features of Black Mesa is its faithful recreation of the original Half-Life experience. The game follows the same story as the original, with players taking on the role of scientist Gordon Freeman as he battles his way through the Black Mesa research facility, fighting off alien invaders and navigating the complex's many dangerous and mysterious areas.But where Black Mesa truly shines is in its updated graphics and gameplay mechanics. The game features stunning high-definition visuals that breathe new life into the game's iconic locations and enemies, making the experience feel fresh and exciting even for players who have played the original countless times. The game also features new and improved mechanics, such as updated physics, improved enemy AI, and new weapons and items that give players even more ways to take on the game's many challenges.For fans of the original Half-Life, Black Mesa is an absolute must-play. The game's attention to detail and commitment to capturing the spirit of the original make it a truly unique experience that feels both familiar and new. It's a game that will bring back fond memories of playing the original Half-Life as a child, while also providing an updated and enhanced experience that is sure to captivate a new generation of players.Overall, Black Mesa is an outstanding game that is well worth checking out for fans of the original Half-Life, as well as anyone who loves first-person shooter games with compelling stories and challenging gameplay. It's a true labor of love that captures the essence of the original while elevating it to new heights, making it one of the best remakes of a classic game ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: The tedium of one of the Interloper chapter, where the game is running on fumes.The somewhat ludicrous alien storyline.The loading screen hiccups.The choices matter moment... that ultimately doesn't matter.The somewhat crude pathfinding.That's literally all I can negatively say about this game. When HL originally came out, I ran Windows 3.1, and begged my parents for a graphics card. I'm old enough to remember people lauding this game... and I'm very happy to now understand why. It's a remarkable piece of game design, of level design, of puzzle design. It stands the test of time exceptionally well, and I would've loved to play it when it came out (despite my aversion to monsters/aliens/fantasy).I thought I'd be playing this for the historical value (with eye candy added), but it turns out I had a genuinely good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Single Player:Story spoiler:It's Half-Life 1 how do you not know the story? Seriously? Fine. The story takes place at the Black Mesa Research Facility in New Mexico. You play as a theoretical physicist named "Gordon Freeman". You are heading off to your normal day of work and to nobody's surprise everything goes to hell. You are then sent throughout the Black Mesa Research Facility against both the U.S. Military and aliens alike, starting your adventure in the Sector C research labs, making your way through the offices of Black Mesa, the railway transits, hell that is known as the surface, and then the lambda complex. (To be Continued: Xen.) The game is basically one long "Get from Point A to Point B" with a bunch of puzzles, confusing level design (To new players), and some small boss battles along the way. But with the twist of the design forcing you to plot how you will play the game through, make you conserve your ammunition, and at some points question your mental sanity and wonder how the hell you're supposed to get through that room with 3 health and no armour left at all.Level Design:Can you really count "Level Design" since it's a remake? Damn straight you can. A lot of small and large changes were made to the game's levels. Even adding some new areas to the game. Some of the more noticeable changes are the scenery during the introductory tram ride, sector C laboratories, and the surface areas. It's just enough of a difference to keep the game going without making it feel like you're playing something that isn't Half-Life 1.Downside in the level design: The "Vent maze" and the "Tram maze" were cut from the Steam version of the game as the developers said they don't feel they were made to their standards. A user has re-uploaded them from the mod version to work compatibly with the game on the Steam Workshop.(On a Rail Link) (We've got Hostiles Link)Cutscenes:The game has been given a much more dramatic feel with more voice actors, facial generation, and quite a few added little cutscenes and dialogue. For example in Half-Life 1: "What the hell are you still doing here? Get topside I hear troops are coming to rescue us." Almost every guard or hiding scientist has their little story to share when you find them. All the existing cutscenes in the game have been overhauled amazingly well, one of my favourite being the "Tentacle Scene" in the rocket firing chamber. which has seen some rather nice improvement in visuals and sounds from the mod version. Also the new voices for the HECU soldiers in the Steam version are a ton better than the original mod version's in my opinion.Gameplay:The game itself plays relatively similar to Half-Life 1 with added physics, but controls and moves as if it were Half-Life 2. You have the option in the "Black Mesa" section of the options menu to make your character always run, more like Half-Life 1 was. Holding sprint in either mode will make the player run significantly faster and play an animation on all weapons other than the crossbow and the satchel charge. The weapons all function the same. Satchels explode on command, grenades have their same insane movement influence in gravity.Soundtrack:Joel Nielson did an amazing job. Damn near perfect. (My personal favourite song being the first On a Rail segment) The soundtrack seems to fit amazing with the ambiance and progression of the game and it's story. The combat music is some of the better sides (Questionable Ethics #1 being an exceptional example) and fits very well into the Half-Life feel of the game. I truly imagine this mod would not have made it as far without his works added to the game.Other:The visuals, sound, and AI for the game have been extremely improved upon. (AKA HECU and scientists no longer run into grenades.) The visuals to the game are extreme. Quality you'd expect from an actual game studio. Albeit limited due to the source engine. The sound design is superb, meant for modern systems with surround sound providing an extremely immersive experience.A few smaller new features were added to Black Mesa, such as an auto-crouch jump (This can be turned off from the "Black Mesa" section of the options menu). Which I can only feel was added solely because of DSP.Multiplayer:Note: The multiplayer is incomplete as of the current time this review was written and has some changes planned to be made. I will keep this section bound to core elements only.Gameplay:The game in multiplayer plays near parallel to Half-Life: Deathmatch's. And yes, crossbow bolts explode again. The multiplayer maps are being remade and modified to Black Mesa's play style and completely overhauled in visuals. It feels essentially like Half-Life Deathmatch but with an HD remake overlayed over it, but with changes in all the right places.Levels: (?)The multiplayer maps have to be downloaded from the Steam Workshop. If I have to guess this is so the developers can easily update a map without having to release an update for the entire game. As of the current time there are the following maps available from play officially from the BMS team: "dm_rocketfire, dm_tension, dm_office, dm_rail, dm_shipping, dm_boom, and dm_power". Adding up to seven maps currently.A list of the good, and the bad:Good:- Complete Overhaul. Not much more needs to be said there.- Balanced and fun to play multiplayer which will have more features in future updates- Just holy hell that soundtrack.- Plenty of little Easter eggs, inside jokes, and references to find everywhere.- More improvements than the free mod versionBad:- The AI can still show it's typical for the source engine at times (Several times I've walked up to HECU Soldiers and they did not do anything but stare at me with their gun practically in my throat.)- Being on Source, you can expect both good physics, but at the same time physics that will break at a moments notice and likely injure or damage the player.- Just holy hell, the human assassins will swarm the player and just spray away with their guns, making it extremely difficult to kill them without explosives or wild gunfire before dying. (You have about 5-10 seconds on the medium difficulty before they kill you.)My "Overall" rating would be ultimately a  9.4 out of 10.The game itself is very balanced in both singleplayer and multiplayer aspects, the game plays and runs fluently. I've got no real complains outside the human assassin's tendency to swarm the player.

_childDocuments_.review: Run. Think. SOURCE.Black Mesa is a complete reimagining of Valve's original Half Life, the game that rocked the world with it's unbroken first person narrative and the most realistic interact with the world... at the time. Black Mesa sets out to do what Half Life: Source wishes it could do, conserve the original Half Life into the Source Engine and after 15 years of development, we finally have a chance to pick up that crowbar once again and experience the resident cascade that changed the gaming industry once again. Gameplay is exactly like how a Half Life game should be, shooting, environment puzzles, and one immersive story and Black Mesa recreates these features with a fresh coat of paint. Firstly all of Gordon's weapons return and look and sound better than ever and generally have the same features with a few new alternative fire modes or details. Level design is largely the same as with being a reimagine some areas have been extend or completely reworked, such as new side rooms, On A Rail being shortened, and of course the entirely revamped Xen which is one of the biggest highlights of Black Mesa. A once loathed section of the game now turned into a living breathing environment that now has less clunky platforming and is wayyyy longer. Having played the original game first really helped me enjoy all the remade rooms and features of the original while the new Xen chapters gave me something fresh and new to enjoy.For a Source Engine game finished in 2020 the visual style of Black Mesa is down right incredible, taking 16 year old technology and crafting some of the most gorgeous scenery that I've seen in the engine really only INFRA could rival with such beautiful visuals. But then Xen comes along and completely raises Black Mesa to the top, gone are the bland polygonal island and in come islands that feel populated with life, like you're the one invading their habitat. I'm so glad I got a new computer so I could run the game at Ultra and see all of these amazing environments.As a neat little bonus, Black Mesa features it's own Multiplayer deathmatch mode and more importantly Steam Workshop integration so you can download the important things like the original Houndeyes sound because for some reason they couldn't use the originals. But regardless this feature makes the game's self life infinitely longer with the advent of new user created maps and campaigns being made. Heck maybe someone will recreate those 2 little expansion packs?Overall, Black Mesa is a completes everything it set out to do, remake the original Half Life in the source engine with a new coat of paint, brand new features, and a less annoying Xen. While I still would recommend playing the original first to appreciate how the original innovated games (And It's still a pretty decent play) I would totally go for playing Black Mesa once you have a general idea of the layout of the Campaign. Now with Black Mesa and Half Life Alyx being released last year and gaining great praise, I wonder what else the Half Life series could bring us?

Apart from the occasional CTD, I haven't noticed any bugs or glitches either. If Valve were to make this game, I doubt they would do a better job than these guys. Heartily recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Source MMod on a megaton of steroids. For a remake, it's very faithful to the original, and adds a fresh coat of paint to the late 90s hit. Xen, in particular, was reimagined masterfully, transformed into a beautiful but equally deadly universe. Bunnyhopping is still very powerful thanks to the sliding mechanic, and gib explosions are even more satisfying.However, some achievements are cookie cutter fetch quests and/or feel like a complete waste of time, because more than one gnome per Half-Life game is insanity.Also, the Long Jump Module has been made less fun to use. Instead of using duck jump, it is now a double jump, which conflicts with bunnyhopping, and has a slow charge/depletion system. Luckily,  can be easily modified to remove this limit.Furthermore, picking Source was one of the biggest issues for me. While the engine was born with Half-Life 2, this remake doesn't constrain itself enough to compensate for poor multi-threading of the engine, so it often hogs an entire thread, which makes the game stutter even on high-end setups. No amount of tweaking video settings makes a dent, the CPU is inevitably going to be the bottleneck in many scenarios.In the end, despite its shortcomings, I consider this to be a fantastic remake. I honestly can't say whether I prefer this remake or the original, but other than the music, pretty much everything's there regardless of which game you pick.

_childDocuments_.review: What Crowbar Collective has done here is an incredible achievement. They have made a remake that surpasses the original in every way while remaining true to its spirit.Xen has been shockingly-well-upgraded with perhaps 8 hours of varied and intense gameplay. There was never a dull moment. The new mechanics are uniformly terrific. The graphics are beyond gorgeous. It all felt so fresh it might as well have been a new game. There are so many innovative ideas here, some physics-based, some conceptual - It feels not only like an evolution of Half-life, but an evolution of Half-life 2 as well.Black Mesa is very difficult - I strongly recommend playing normal difficulty until you're well-acquainted with the game. Some players might even need easy mode. You will die a lot. But the experience is well worth it. This is the definitive version of the original Half-Life, and a remarkable game in its own right.

This version is a masterpiece in it own right, and isn't even completed just yet. If you're already a fan of Half Life, play this game. If you're somehow oblivious enough (and in a strangely enviably way, lucky enough) to have never experienced Half Life, play this game. Don't wait for a sale, these devs deserve the support.

_childDocuments_.review: "Rise and shine Mr.Freeman, rise, and .. shine"Alright so here it goes. This is the way every gamer wants his favorite game to be remastered. I first played Black Mesa on non-steam version which was the only available one . I enjoyed it so much and wasn't complaining about anything. Half Life was always my favorite game of all time , and I grew up playing it . Much love for this game <3Now for the review. This game is amazing. The graphics looks better than most of the games that are coming out today (since this was an old game but now it's released on steam) . It's still in the beta phase but don't let that fool you. This game is just like Alpha , but it doesn't have the full story (as far as I can remember it misses Xen and other parts after it) . Pretty much the game itself is not the same. Some locations are completely changed , and I mean really changed. Weapons (like the crowbar in the beginning) you don't find it after the laser room  , the location is changed ( don't want to spoil anyone) . And many other places are done even better than in the original Half Life . Animations are cool , crowbar hits are amazing and that's why I use it most of the time . Graphics are ... AMAZING !!!. The game looks like it's next gen and yet it has proven that . The only bad part is that the game story is not full. It misses Xen like I mentioned before . That is the only thing I hate about it but they will release it soon. Online is always good to play while waiting for Xen , but not many servers to choose from. A few servers with constant players , but still the online is playable and I didn't experienced any problems.So yeah. This game is amazing. It's like you put Half Life 2 with far better graphics and animations with Half Life 1 story.10 out of f u c k i n g 10 !!!!!Worth every penny . _childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is the definitive way to experience Half Life.Just to preface this I wouldn't recommend playing Black Mesa before Half-Life 2, just to get better acquainted with the Source engine and properly recognising some characters is also a nice detail. Also, while I do think that Black Mesa is a better game than Half-Life, I do still think there's a lot of value in playing Half-Life first just to appreciate how much has been overhauled and changed while still staying recognisable.With all that said, this remake is phenomenal. It is an upgrade to Half-Life in almost everything.The presentation is the obvious thing to highlight. Its visually stunning the entire way through from the opening Tram Ride to Xen. The updated visuals however serve more of a purpose than just to be jaw droppingly gorgeous, but it enhances the environmental storytelling in ways that the original couldn't with the far more detailed world. It’s a vivid reimagining of Half-Life, while still maintaining the original’s tone and atmosphere. The sound design is also incredible with all the weapons being very satisfying to fire and couple with a soundtrack that’s just AWESOME!The gameplay has seen a bit of an overhaul too, the gun play is still very solid, enemy encounters are a lot more dynamic and the overall level design I’d argue is much better paced than the original, cutting down on some of the more tedious sections and focusing more on its set pieces and the original’s highlights. Finally, there’s also of course the completely reimagined Xen, which is just an incredible spectacle to play all the way through.All in all, Black Mesa stands out on its own as a brand-new experience while still being faithful to the original game. It is one of the best remakes of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the 15 year wait! A fantastic remake of the original Half-Life in the Source Engine.Xen is a masterpiece and visually makes up for the rather lack-lusture parts of the Black Mesa Facility.The level design is top-notch and has continued to receive updates since release.There are some interesting new puzzles and variations on old puzzles.Parts of the game that were cut down are supported via the workshop - for example "On a Rail" that saw considerable cuts in the vanilla release has an entry and is supported by the devs with updates.My greatest criticism of Black Mesa is that, despite the wait and many continuing updates, some parts of the game have not seen much attention from their Half-Life original parts; which considering how much of the rest of the game has been updated seems a little odd.Nonetheless 9/10 would kill the end boss again! (If only to see Xen one more time)

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to relive the origins of the Half-Life universe in a brand new way or set foot into it for the first time, this is absolutely the way to do it.What started as a fan effort over a decade ago has turned into a game better than many titles from big-budget AAA studios. Black Mesa really feels like a completely modern evolution of what Half-Life was. Xen, in particular, is *completely* different in an astonishingly good way. What was my least favorite part of Half-Life is my favorite part of Black Mesa. The detailed environments, lighting and visual effects, great soundtrack, and all new gameplay/storytelling really turn Xen into the exploration of an alien world that I had always wished it was. Even with all the changes - everything fits. Nothing felt out of place to me. It felt like this is what Half-Life really would have been had it been made today.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is not only a true love letter to one of the biggest games ever made, but also a prime example of how the gaming industry should be. It is a perfect recreation of the original Half Life. Everything from that game is in here, many times in improved ways.Gameplay: While feeling modern, it retains the same fast paced style that defined Half Life and the old school shooter from the 90's that you rarely see today. The remake of Xen is impressive, expanding and improving in every way its original conceptGraphics: I honestly can't believe Source is a 20 years old engine. There are a couple of times in the Xen levels in which there are FPS drops but if that's all you'll have to pay for a game to look this good on an engine this old, then I'd say it is a really small price. Black Mesa is certainly not the best looking game ever but there are plenty of times in which it doesn't just look "good", but actually beautifulSound: As immersive as it should be in a game like this. Also, the soundtrack by Joel Nielsen is one of the coolest aspects of the game. It is memorable, atmospheric and catchy on its own whlie still retaining the style of the soundtracks for the Valve made HL games.However, probably the most important thing about Black Mesa is what it represents. The gaming industry isn't what it was anymore with big companies, triple A games, cosmetics, microtransactions, professional competitive scenes, etc been the rule. You can clearly see how Black Mesa was made by HL fans for HL fans, keeping everything that made the original one great while also improving in aspects that weren't necessary to get people's love, yet they did anyway, like an MP mode, necessary tweaks to some levels, a soundtrack that feels as one made by Valve, etc...

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a brief history of the main Half-Life games and their Metacritic scores:Half-Life 1 (1998): 96/100Half-Life 2 (2004): 96/100Half-Life Alyx (2020): 93/100Does Black Mesa, the remake of Half-Life 1, live up to these standards?PROS:(1) The game is an immersive, intellectual experience, filled with puzzles, a great narrative, and lots of sci-fi.(2) The physics of the game (Source Engine) is still top-notch and has been used in other successful Valve titles (Counter-strike, Portal).CONS:(1) Although the game is a remake of a 1998 title, I think the graphics could have been better for a 2020 release. The lack of stunning graphics affects the immersion.(2) If you get stuck in a puzzle, you can spend a lot of time trying to solve it - maybe a bit too much. I think there were too many brain teasers in the second to the last level.RATING:8/10 - Although this game is not as spectacular as the other Half-Life titles, I think it is still worth playing. I got the game on sale for 4 euros and it was a good bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, well worth every dollar. The detailing is amazing, not to mention the faces on the npcs. I love how there's a little intro thing for every weapon, and the designers even added some extra scenes that weren't in the original game. Every time I walk into a room, I think, "Ahh.. I remember this part." Or, "I don't remember this! This is cool!" Or something like that.  It really makes the world of Half-Life come alive for me. The animations are amazing, especially the running and walking. They really ramped up the Marines, making them less stupid and more human. Even the vortigonts look amazing, just like Half-Life 2. If you were afraid of the headcrab zombies in the other games, I was too, and the moment I played this my fear vanished. The noises they make are a lot easier to bear. All in all, this game is amazing! I think that Crowbar Collective could be trusted to make a pretty decent Half-Life 3. I whole-heartedly recommend that you buy this game, if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life is a game that means so much to me, as a fan of the game since I was just a kid. To this very day it's one of my all time favourites. It was also one of my dads favourite games and I can still remember when he first showed it to me and I became obsessed with this world. Then Half life 2 came out and it was only a matter of time before I stumbled upon this mod called Black Mesa. I was so excited for a remake, I told my dad about it and we both began eagerly anticipating it. Of course, little did I know how long of a journey it would be before I was able to play even the initial release. I finished school, then I finished college and even finished University before I got my hands on the early access. I must have visited that website over a hundred thousand times for information and updates...But was it worth all that waiting? This re-imagination of the original is outstanding. The level design has been fantastically reworked to make so much more sense with the addition of many cleverly designed puzzles. The attention to detail is astonishing and had me smiling from ear to ear as I would frequently relive the moments I had experienced as a child. So many moments were just so brilliantly worked in... And Xen! What a beautiful recreation - it's so much more than I could have ever imagined it would be! When you first enter the border world my jaw dropped and I couldn't stop looking at the mesmerising scenes. Honestly, I'm still in awe. The Crowbar Collective Team have knocked this one out of the ball park and I can't thank you enough for the work you have all put into this game over the many many years. Unfortunately my dad passed away from cancer a few years before the release, but I know he would have loved it as much I did. He was able to play the initial release back in 2012/13 and thoroughly enjoyed it. I wish he could have seen Xen though - He'd have absolutely loved it.I look forward to seeing whatever is next from the team.

Xen level was so stunning i took my time to gaze around the world. The physics is still pretty much the same as the OG Half-Life. Bhopping arround still fun imo. Though i hate it sometimes you get stuck because you hit a rock while being chased by a damn alien giant. 10/10 Devs nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with Half Life starting with the mod "Absolute Redemption" when I was 9. My cousins installed it on my grandparents computer, and the rest is history. I didn't play the actual game until I was 14, and once I did, it changed my life. I remember being so shocked how it took me that long to finally play the campaign of the original game. Anyway, this remake has given me the same feelings I had when first playing the original campaign. Things were unpredictable, sometimes a bit too drawn out and repetitive, but quite beautiful at the same time. Extremely smooth. The fact that they made this game using an engine that was released in 2004 is amazing and speaks for itself. Once you get to Xen, you understand why it took them 8 years to finish the game. If you want a classic 90s FPS experience completely redone, Black Mesa is for you. Half Life 3 Confirmed.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been a while since i wrote a review for a game, but after this game I wanted to leave my thoughts.My god, Black Mesa.I did not know about this game until a week ago, after i played through Half Life 1 with one of my best friends who is a huge Half-Life Fan. To be honest I didn't expect much of it, since it was a fan-game, but my expectations got blown away within a couple hours of playing.This game looks beautiful, the sounds are sensational and it feels very well polished.The soundtrack ranges from dark ambience to epic action music that makes you feel like you are the only person who can save this planet. Which you are, ironically. The gunplay feels really fun and rewarding. Let me talk about Xen. The last third of the game takes place in the so called borderworld Xen, which was created entirely from scratch by the Crowbar Collection. In the original Half Life 1, Xen was a not finished mess. The textures were awful, the gameplay wasn't that much fun for me. Black Mesa's Xen is perfect. It is perfect. Floating islands surrounded by a colorful nebular void. Thousands of plants, flowers, minerals that bloom in gorgeous colors. An ecosystem that has never been created so well before.I finished the game multiple times and got all achievements within one week. It didn't tire me for one second. Not even when I played through the whole game a second and third time after finishing it, just to bring the pizza and the purple hat to the end (If you know you know).Play this game, if you want to get into Half-Life. Even if you don't. It is worth your time.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life and it's sequel are my favorite first person shooters. The franchise offers a unique experience to the genre that has yet to be surpassed. I have replayed them hundreds of times!Black Mesa offers an incredible re-imagining of Half-Life. Both in terms of it's gorgeous visuals and spectacular audio. The people who were responsible for it's detailed  environments, sound design and character development are a top notch level of talent! The Crowbar Collective has offered a stellar tribute to one of the greatest games of all  time. I wouldn't change anything about what the game offers in terms of its presentation.What I would change is the most important part of any fps, the combat. The developers have decided against an exact replication of the original game. There certainly is nothing wrong with that choice. In fact I am overjoyed they decided to optimize some of Half-Life's more tedious and unnecessarily long chapters. While this has worked to improve the games pacing, it has hurt a crucial area of it's mechanics.Black Mesa's redesign of the weapons makes fighting enemies far more aggravating. This is partially due to the larger number of enemies that have been included into the new ambush sections. Dealing with these new threats is particularly difficult because the reduced amounts of ammo that can be carried. Also, the damage in certain weapons (Specifically anything using explosives) has been reduced substantially compaired with the arsenal in Half-Life. Let me use the submachine-gun as a perfect example.The SMG from Half-Life One:Ammo: 50 round clip - 250 reserve - 10 grenades. Fairly accurate with a fair amount of recoil that was automatically compensated by Freeman.As anyone knows the amount of ammo and number of guns was reduced significantly from half life one to its sequel. However whatever Valve took away they added something to replace it.The SMG from Half-Life Two:Ammo: 45 round clip - 225 reserve - 3 grenades. Very accurate and faster firing speed with a small amount of recoil that was automatically compensated by Freeman.While we lost a small amount of bullets and large number of grenades, we gained a far more accurate SMG with a higher rate of fire.This is what the SMG looks like in Black Mesa:Ammo: 30 round clip - 150 reserve - 3 grenades. Accurate in small bursts with a fair amount of recoil that is NOT compensated by Freeman. Grenades damage and area of effect was also reduced.By these numbers the new SMG should be pin point accurate, no recoil at all and should fire even faster. The alternative being that the grenades should be at least 2 times more powerful than either of the Half-Life's.While I could certainly go over the issues I have for each of the weapons, I won't.Instead I will offer a quick list of changes that, in my opinion, would make for a better tribute.1: Pistol - Half-Life 2 - Semi-Auto is love, Semi-Auto is life.2: Magnum - Half-Life 2 - Suit Zoom + Accuracy = Head shot.3: SMG - See Above... :-)4: Shotgun - Half- Life 1 - Needs interruptible reload animation.5: Crossbow - Remove the arch, faster reload, 25 ammo.6: RPG - Please fix the laser guidance. Rockets bounce off enemies.7: Explosives - Half-Life 1 level of devastation!8: Exotic Energy Weapons - No issues.9: Xen Weapons - All good.10: Sprinting - Half-Life 1 - Let me sprint in ALL directions.This is one of the times I wish the recommendation system had a mixed option.I LOVE what has been done with the games graphics, sound and characters.Not a big fan of the combat...

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer: I've never played the original Half-Life, but I'm familiar with the story.Black Mesa in one word - grandiose.Story, though not original, is still phenomenal by today's standards.Graphical execution is top notch. In quite a few places I've lingered in order to appreciate the scenery, especially in Xen.Music is amazing. So much so, that the soundtrack has become a frequent flyer around the house.Level design is marvelous. Size of the maps are very big, sometimes a bit too much. But I wouldn't want them smaller because this fits with the story of an ordinary theoretical physicist's in an extraordinary situation.The only cons I have with this game has nothing to do with the gameplay, but with some achievements.The F***ING hat. And then the F***ING pizza. With sprinkled Source engine physics voodoo on top. There's a special place in hell for people who decide to inflict so much frustration on other people. And this special place is reserved for Half-Life 2: Episode Two's Gnome achievement guys. CC, you've decided to put TWO of those in the same game. Not a short game, by any stretch of the imagination. Hell's new, 10th circle, will be exclusively for you.Maybe it's just me, though.Bottom line. Black Mesa is THE way for anyone to enjoy original Half-Life's story. _childDocuments_.review: It is the '98 Half-Life, but rebuilded with great detail and slightly modified. This is the chance to experience one of the best games of all time in a fresh new look. In the original HL, I never liked Xen too much. The technology wasn't ready yet. I hope Black Mesa excels here. This recreation exceeded my expectations!Update: While the chapters in the Black Mesa research facility are very close to the original HL, Xen is a reinvention rather than a remake. The pace of the game changes from a sightseeing tour to an old school Doom- or Quake-like FPS and back. The balancing throughout Xen is improved and the game mechanics promise exciting battels. One can argue that the one or other sequence could have been shorter and that the first encounter with Gonarch (played on hard) is not just a hell of a fight but feels like being on another extra skill level. On the other hand, Xen is beautiful, dragging the player in an alien world that feels somehow real. With incredibly updated graphics Xen is reborn to be a fantastic experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, the best remake Half-Life 1 could get, and it's not even a Valve game, it's only licensed by Valve but Crowbar Collective are responsible for this masterpiece. I'm sure that ANY fan of Half-Life, and games that run on Source in general will find this game enjoyable. The base game is great enough on its own, but my oh my, check out the great Workshop this game has, from cool weapon reskins, to comical meme sound packs such as the Sr. Pelo Gluon gun, there's a mod that will surely enhance the already great game.And let me tell you you, the wait for Xen was completely worth it, I got the game in 2017 and waited 2020 for them drop it and it was worth the long wait 100%. Xen is actually a playable, fleshed out area instead of the rushed mess it was in HL1 back in '98. Everywhere in Xen is visually stunning, I'm shocked the Source engine can look THIS good quite frankly, every area has a unique visual style, from the flora covered caves to the basalt-crystally areas, every new section presents it's own unique aesthetic.The Nihilanth is like... and actual boss now. With multiple phases (the last one tanking frames but looks awesome non-the-less).Joel Nielsen went nuts on the OST, gotta be one my favourites ever. It's too damn good, every track is perfect, from the music in the facility evoking hopelessness and destruction, to the xen ost being awe-inspiring and mysterious10/10, one of my favourite games ever, and a remaster of the first installment of my favourite game franchises ever, this remaster runs on all cylinders

_childDocuments_.review: A game that, by all rights, should be great, and in many ways, it is, but due to typical indie dev arrogance, a habit of huddling around their 'chosen ones' on discord, not being receptive to even the most basic of gameplay 101 reasoning, even when it's fed to them in a way that big, real, actual development studios would pay money for, and changing things 'because muh feels,' it's taken quite a beating, and been tarnished to the point where key moments, like the early game, are completely ruined unless you use a workshop mod to restore it to before the indie devs, in their typical indie dev arrogance, used their feels to change things for the sake of change. Or to please some of the chosen ones on discord. We have yet to find out the true reasoning, and likely never will, because indie devs, no matter what outfits and colors they wear, remain indie devs, once again much to my personal dismay.Ignoring the damage done to the gameplay experience, you'll find a UI so broken that, as of this writing, you must actually, for real, use the legacy UI if you are to access things like (and this is not a full list): multiplayer, multiplayer character creation, changing crosshair style, accessing the limited controller support, rebinding certain keys, toggling on and off so called legacy features, forcing joystick usage...Attached to this game is also, and I say this with no hyperbole, the worst community you will ever find, anywhere, for any reason. It's a cult fixated on a collective persecution complex, and every single so called veteran is a private profile guy, who's been allowed to insult and mock everybody not part of the cult for years. Only now that the game's finally released are actions being taken against them, and like the cult they are, they respond to it by attacking 'the enemy,' which are paying customers who committed the sin of not spending 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year watching this game's development for the past 14+ years. They will be in this steam review, and in your steam reviews, oblivious to the fact that their behavior only proves the point. Stay far, far away from anyone who claims to be a BM veteran, all associated discords, and the steam forum itself until it gets a proper cleanup.If we are to ignore all that, launch with the 'legacy' UI, use a simple workshop mod that erases the developers' feels based early game changes by restoring weapon progression the game was balanced for since 2012, and pretend the cult doesn't exist, we'll find an amazingly scored and paced game. Some call it a remake, or a remaster, of half-life, but it's actually a retake. Black Mesa is half-life as envisioned by the developers, not as played, and what they've been dreaming and thinking of when they hear the word 'half-life' for a decade and a half. Their ideal half-life, so to speak, that's been in their heads for as long as it's taken Valve themselves to make a worthwhile title. While the game sticks to the beats of half-life, and seems superficially similar, it's a completely different beast in every way. Everything is bigger, bolder, more involved, and there's an actual story here, which there wasn't in half-life, contrary to popular belief. Beats, events, and characters from half-life 2. the expansion packs, and so on, all make appearances or get mentions, as well. It's an incredibly ambitious title, that manages to be longer on its own than all the actual half-life games combined. It's also several orders of magnitude more difficult, even on the easiest setting.Half-life itself has often been derided for how easy it is, especially at the time of release 20+ years ago, but Black Mesa takes more of a Quake 2 approach to difficulty. Oh, you died? Well, then try again until you get it. Due to being a source engine game, it also incorporates the normally silly physics for actual gameplay purposes, particularly in the second act's Xen chapters. Gone is the simple 'jump a bit longer'-module, in favor of an actual long jump module, that can be used in conjunction with source physics to skii, slide, skip parts of levels, and so on. Other more contemporary features are also key parts of the game, like quick throwing grenades, sprinting, short combat slides that depend on your momentum, which ties into the sprint function, longer dry reloads for ballistic weapons, ironsights on the revolver, AI opponents that don't actually mess around, and so on. All of this is set to one of the most amazing soundtracks you'll find this side of the deus ex or guilty gear series, and backlit by graphics I wasn't aware the source engine was capable of. The gameplay is fast, furious, and unapologetic, with the occasional pauses to explore alien wilderness, find out what horrors befell those who came before you, or catch radio chatter from soldiers who are bleeding out, while paramedics try desperately to keep them conscious and talking. It's an extremely atmospheric title, with a lot more in common with Quake 1 and 2 at times than half-life, but it works so beautifully. Just like how the best parts of half-life were revisioned, so were the bad parts. Xen, once a 30 minute garbage heap of frustration and cut corners, is an expanded second half of the game, now truly alien and otherworldy, where human ammunition and supplies, as you'd expect in an alien world far, far away, are scarce to the point where you must make do with local means and improvisation. The formerly pathetic joke boss fights are now actual boss fights, showcasing that giant headcrabs that have a rather large sac, so to speak, maybe shouldn't be taken so lightly. Maybe, just maybe, they only grew that big because they ate the rest of the competition, which includes mister Freeman himself, if you're not careful.Despite all the good, the bad critically outweighs the good as it stands, and the devs hiding out on discord for over 3 weeks, while the game rises to top seller and earns a popular title tag, with critical bugs and errors that they themselves have shown zero interest in fixing, instead relying on forum users to help other forum users troubleshoot things that only the devs are actually truly privy to...well. Until they actually start behaving like developers, or the game magically gets some kind of workshop mod that fixes all the technical problems, I can't in good faith recommend this game, regardless of how much fun I personally have had with it. Even I'm not immune to the problems, and I know for a fact the average reader will have a terrible time with the game in its current state.Hopefully, they don't take 14 years to address the 1.0 disaster. If things changes, and I sincerely hope they do, I'll change my rating and write a more in-depth review, but until that time, it is what it is.Edit may 12 2020: the devs just put on the biggest clownshoes since hawken, fractured space, and MWO. You will wish you were dealing with PGI when you look at their forum, or try to get help with the game. Avoid Black Mesa at all costs. It's not worth it, and according to the devs, they have zero interest in fixing the very real issues 'until sometime later 2020, at the earliest.' Just another indie trash fire, overhyped, bloated, and full of arrogance. They have gone so far as to hide and censor away very real criticism for the bad UI and lack of controller support.As far as I'm concerned, there's nothing for you here, unless you bought in already.Edit: 12:01: spelling errors.Edit: I regrey nothing, and if you disagree with anything, you're wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a 2020 first-person shooter game developed and published by Crowbar Collective. It is a third-party remake of Half-Life (1998) made in the Source game engine. Originally published as a free mod in September 2012, Black Mesa was approved for commercial release by Valve, the developers of Half-Life. You are Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist at the Black Mesa Research Facility. When a routine experiment goes horribly wrong, you must fight your way through an interdimensional alien invasion, and a bloodthirsty military clean-up crew in order to save the science team... and the world!

_childDocuments_.review: Before the pros and cons,you need to know that I'm the kind of gamer that pays attention to graphics and animation quality.I simply can't ignore them because this is the 21st century for God's sake.I'm also not a fan of old games.I only play them again for nostalgia.Black Mesa,on the other hand,surprises me.The nostalgic feeling and the modern feel of the game is very balanced for me and I admit that I like this game even though this is based on an old game.This game is the old Half Life modded with way much better graphics.Don't expect some epic gameplay like Crysis's or CoD's or Battlefield's.They're trying to keep the classics feel alive.Pros :+ Great graphics,but not epic (remember,it's a mod)+ Classic half life gameplay.The nostalgic feeling is the only reason why I bought this game.+ Steam workshop available with cool mods from the community+ Haven't tried the multiplayer,but I saw a lot of people is having fun with it+ Puzzle combined with horror and shooting action.Just like the old half life+ If you played the old half life,you'll be very satisfied with this game.The improvements are drastic and amazing.+ Challenging gameplay (single player)Cons :- The graphics when you're inside the building is great.But,when I was playing the level on the surface,I realized that I shouldn't expected much graphical improvement from a mod of an old game.- Almost zero soundtrack.I understand they're trying to keep the classics feel but the thrilling part of the game is a failure due to lack of creepy soundtrack.There's no 'feel' along the gameplay without proper soundtrack.- Boring single player story.Not enough plot twists to 'wow' me.The story is really monotone. I understand it's Half Life, the multiple award winning game etc etc but that won't stop me from criticizing it- Crude animationsOverall,this is a meh game. The pros and the cons is balanced for me and I got bored to play this game after a couple of hours. I meant no offense for the half life fans. I know that they're trying to revive an old game by combining it with the 21st century gaming technology but I do think they need to do more to attract more people than just half life fans and 20 year old guys trying to replay their childhood memories.Of course,not all of the current players are either of them and I don't know they are successful statistically or not. I would still recommend this game even if you are not a half life fan. It's still worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: While Valve's Half-Life: Source was merely intended to show how easy it was to port GoldSrc games to their new engine, the Crowbar Collective have gone above and beyond to provide a proper, full fledged, remake.Originally developed as free mod, Black Mesa was approved by Valve for a commercial release. You may be able to find the mod version online, but note that it does not include the final chapters of the campaign or the multiplayer, and it runs on an older version of the Source engine. This standalone version includes the full game, and has numerous bug fixes and improvements over the mod version. It also has a chapter select menu with all the chapters available to choose from at the start, a great quality of life feature.I found the performance on Linux to be acceptable with OpenGL. Though it's possible to utilize Vulkan with DXVK. On Linux, simply force Proton. On Windows, DXVK can be manually installed, and may yield better performance than Direct3D.More info here:

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal achievement, AAA game, and work of art. You can see every day of the 14 years worth of blood and sweat that was put into this. There are some great puzzles here and it does start to feel like a big build-up, but then becomes a bit repetitive and frustrating about 2/3 through. _childDocuments_.review: My conclusive review on Black Mesa, the (almost) complete remake of the original Half Life:Pros:- Completely new textures- New environments (although similar to Half Life's, obviously)- Completely new voice clips and lines for characters to say that are surprisingly close to the originals, but much higher in quality.- New music- Movement is less slippy- Option to go back to the original movement system if preferred- Guns are more refined and less weird to use- Greatly improved visuals and physics courtesy of the Source engine- Stays quite faithful to the source material while adding new and interesting areas and challenges.Cons (Keep in mind, most of these things are very minor anyways so they don't detract from the game much and will probably be ironed out in the full release):- (Medium Importance) enemy A.I. doesn't have the complexity that the A.I. from the original game did, most notable in the Marines, who would flank and try to flush you out of hiding spots with grenades in the original game, and Vortigaunts, who are more cowardly in the original game and will run away if damaged. For a demonstration in the absurd complexity of Half Life's A.I., see this playlist: - (Low Importance, probably will be fixed) There's a couple of little mild immersion-breaking bugs such as the auto run feature not auto-running after a loading screen until pressing the key to go slow once, and then in the chapter "On a Rail," when going up a slant in the beginning of the level it will slide you to the back of the train for seemingly no reason instead of just keeping you at the front of the train.- (Medium Importance) In most areas, the level design feels flush and polished in terms of both looks and gameplay. In certain areas though, it feels ever so slightly as if it was designed more to look pretty and to cater to more advanced players that already know what they're doing rather than serve an actual purpose or be friendly to newer players and therefore isn't as fun as the rest of the game.- No Xen yet :(Welp, that was it I guess, My Final Verdict:Very Highly Recommended for anyone who likes Half Life and even people who just like FPS games in general, just don't come in expecting Valve's level of polish to every single thing like I did, Crowbar Collective did a very good job with this though :).
