_childDocuments_.review: forever changed the way I play and appreciate first-person shooters. While it wasn’t the first FPS to feature a (good) story, I was impressed by how you get to experience the entire narrative from first-person perspective, by its scripted events, and by its deliberate pacing.  was intense, cinematic, suspenseful, complex, and fun. It raised the (crow)bar of excellence very high.Nowadays, some developers remaster or remake their hit titles for modern gaming systems. Valve did port  to run on the Source Engine in 2004, but the resulting product --  -- was generally considered inadequate. Consequently, a group of dissatisfied fans, branding themselves as Crowbar Collective, decided to volunteer their time to remaster  properly. It was in this way that the  project began. started out as a fan-made mod of  for . Released in 2012 after 7 years of development, it’s still available to download for free at the time of this review. However, the mod only goes up to the end of the “Lambda Core” chapter. The developers spent an additional 8 years converting the mod into a standalone game powered by the Source 2013 engine, adding more details to many of the levels, and re-imagining and completing the Xen levels. The final product of that Herculean effort is . is a notable achievement. The developers essentially remade  so that the story and aesthetics align with those of the sequels. Because of that, the game’s narrative is more cohesive with the  lore. This includes formally introducing players to Dr. Kleiner and Dr. Vance at the Black Mesa Research Facility, and showing the Vortigaunts being enslaved on Xen. I believe these changes will not only satisfy many long-time fans, but also ease unfamiliar players into the  game series.My memory of  isn’t as exact as those of players who play it on a regular basis, or who have played it recently. What I remember most about  is the general thrill from playing it, and being in awe of a few prominent set pieces (e.g., stepping out of a drain pipe onto the cliff of a mesa as a fighter jet zooms by). What  successfully accomplished is letting veteran players experience similar excitement, suspense and tension when playing it, as if they are playing  for the first time.The original graphics of  haven’t aged well. Even the level designs, which were ahead of the curve back in 1998, are rudimentary by today’s standards. To remake  properly, the developers couldn’t simply insert models with higher polygon counts, slap on new, high-definition textures, and call it a day. The challenge of remaking a game like  is that it needs to feel contemporary, but also deliver the spirit of the original. I was very happy to see that despite the new visual presentation,  is similarly paced and subversive as .The developers interpreted the original material, remixed level designs to make them feel more modern and less rigid, and spruced everything up with advanced lighting and water effects. They did such a good job with the visuals and elaborating on the levels that I was convinced that  had always looked and played this good. It took me watching playthroughs of the original game to snap myself back into realizing how rudimentary  looks in comparison, and how much work the developers had put in into making .Yet, the developers did show restraint on the interpretation and remixing. They couldn’t and didn’t rearrange the layout of Black Mesa Research Facility too radically, and didn’t add new elements that are too disparate from the original concepts. Some levels are likely easier to contemporize (e.g., “On a Rail”, “Surface Tension”), and some harder (e.g., “We’ve Got Hostiles”, “Lambda Core”). What we end up getting in  is some unevenness throughout the many levels, which may be an unforeseen consequence of modernizing a classic game while staying faithful to the source material.Let’s address the elephant (or Gargantua if you will) in the room: how are those re-imagined Xen levels? For those unfamiliar with , the original Xen levels were not very good to say the least. Even my co-worker who enthusiastically recommended  to me back in the day advised me stop playing upon arriving at Xen. I didn’t listen, and got to experience first-hand how mechanically and tonally different those last levels were. I believe that many people still hold  in high regard only because the first 85 to 90% of the game was so good.Crowbar Collective did a really great job re-imagining Xen. They expanded the scope of each level visually and structurally. In fact, the new designs bare very little resemblance to what Valve delivered back in 1998. Instead of sticking with the original pukey yellowish-brown shades, the developers assigned each level its own colour scheme. There’s tranquil, mysterious purple in “Xen”, followed by earthy orange and brown in “Gonarch’s Lair”, and finished off with dangerous red and alien green in “Interloper”.Significant changes were also made to the terrain and flora, with “Xen” partly inspired by the forests of Pandora from the movie, , “Gonarch’s Lair” featuring an elaborate underground labyrinth reminiscent of Shelob’s lair in , and “Interloper” having an industrial look that reminded me of . The expanded variety of colours and environment is a much welcome change.In spite of the creativity and effort, some purists will not like how these newly designed levels greatly deviate from the original. I didn’t mind it, but my biggest complaint about the new levels is that they’re just too long, so much so that I found they overstayed their welcome. Plus, these levels are much more challenging than what the first 70% of  presented. Ironically, Xen in this game feels very much like an afterthought as in .In the end, Xen is Xen. Despite Crowbar Collective’s best efforts, these last few levels just don’t fit well with the first part of . The transition from Black Mesa Research Facility to the alien world is still as jarring as before. Xen feels like it belongs to a different type of game, like ones that star alien-killing space marines, who make their enemies tremble with fear. You can’t fault the developers too much though, because a remake of  just isn’t complete without these divisive levels.I love , and I will enthusiastically recommend this game to anyone interested in the  game series. Coincidentally much like the co-worker who recommended  to me, I love this game up to the end of the “Lambda Core” chapter only, for I’m rather apathetic about the Xen levels. Yet, I recognize that no matter how you slice it, Xen -- in its original or remastered form -- will be divisive among  enthusiasts. So who knows, you may actually enjoy them more than I did! No matter what, the creativity and hard work that Crowbar Collective had put in into modernizing , and redesigning Xen from scratch are praiseworthy. And for that, they deserve not only our thanks, but also our financial support.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that defined FPS shooters as we know them today, but remade to fit modern standards.Spoiler-Free reviewBlack Mesa is a great remake, not always as faithful to the original, but for people who desire Half-Life after finishing them all, this is what you need.Black Mesa is actually comparable to Half-Life 2, due to sharing the same engine, physics engine, things like that. With some few differences. Physics puzzles are lessend due to them not being a focus in Half-Life 1, and the game focuses a lot more on action compared to the previous titles. You are Gordon Freeman, a scientist working at Black Mesa. An important test is scheduled today. But you're late! In your haste you go to the test chamber immediately after putting on your radiation suit named the "HEV". However, the test goes horribly wrong. Perhaps you should've stayed home today. In other words, this story is the exact same as the original Half-Life, with only extremely minor changes to fit the world/gameplay.I am not sure if I should compare this to the previous Half-Life's, or see it as a standalone. Compared to the previous Half-Life's, this game delivers mostly. Not always, but it's got that Half-Life vibe on it. As this is Crowbar Collective's first game, it is quite spectacular.Black Mesa still runs on the Source Engine, and while that keeps the gameplay very faithful, the graphics can only go so far. For Source Engine standards, Black Mesa is beautiful. For modern standards in 2020, it's average. However, this is not meant to be an AAA game, and as such, I believe it's looks really good if you were to call it "Indie". Performance wise however, is a different story. Some parts of the game truly push the Source Engine, and as such, the framerate can't keep up. While 90% of the time it stays above 60, in heavy scenes it can drop to the 40-30s. In the Xen chapter there was even a point where my framerate was at 7 FPS for a short period. For reference my CPU is a i5 3470, and my GPU an GTX 1060.Black Mesa sounds absolutely great. It is a massive update compared to the original Half-Life which uses compressed sounds from the 90s. Use headphones, your ears will thank you.Black Mesa is a great game. Should I call it a Half-Life game though? I am unsure. It's faithfulness is up to debate. Some parts are added to pad out the gameplay, or improve where the original failed, yet I feel like I would've enjoyed this game more if it was even more faithful. I especially felt this at the Xen chapters, where the levels were so much longer than the original game, and so different that it felt like a different game all together. But on the positive side, yeah. This game is wonderful. However, please, play the original Half-Life before this. That's all.This game gets a solid 7.5, the performance issues prevent it from being an 8 or higher. For any future players: Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone knows of the Black Mesa Incident... the origin of one of gaming's iconic heroes, Dr. Gordon Freeman, and the start of the Half Life series. Black Mesa is a labor of love by the Crowbar Collective, made of both long time fans and new faces to the HL community, remaking the start of Gordon's epic adventure and fight to save Earth from invaders from Xen and other parts of the multiverse unknown. As for what to expect from this game? A wild thrill ride tearing apart xenos, black ops troops, and a number of devious puzzles that not only lives up to the standard set by Valve with Half Life 1, it exceeds it. Pulse-pounding firefights, mind bending puzzles, iconic moments, and witty dialog from friend and foe alike, all topped off with an epic Final Boss you can't help but sling a one-liner at when you crush them under your power-assisted, high-impact reactive armor clad, orange, boot. A bit of gaming history for the younger gamers wondering "what's a headcrab?", "Who is the G-man?", and "what's with the crowbar jokes?"... _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that this isn't an exact copy of the original Half Life by a long shot, as is impliments lots of new mechanics and changes some events, but this isn't bad to any degree, and actually helps as a result. Black Mesa is a beautiful game, both gameplay and visuals-wise. It's not too much to look at, and it isn't too little, while leaving HL1's feel to the game in there. The combat is also nice, and the guns feel good to use and their animations are fluid and sound nice as well (My personal favourite weapon is the MP-5 or the Tau cannon or whatever it is). The sounds in-game are nice as well, with the characters sounding fresh and good, the ambient sounds seem very real as well, like outside the facility with the wind and the helicopters in the distance, even in Xen, it's very nice to listen to. The level designs are also very nice and follow their HL1 counterparts well, with a fair amount of them just being complete re-skins and re-models of the levels (which I'm not slamming on, I love that aspect). The enemies and NPC's are nice to look at as well, the HECU Soldiers are detailed and fit their whole purpose well, and even the scientists are fun to be around. The animations for some of the NPC's are kind of weird, like the Alien Grunts, which seem very reminiscent of HL1's movement animations for them.The soundtrack done by the amazing Joel Nielsen is just LUDICROUS! Especially the early Xen levels' music is just jaw-dropping to listen to. I wish I could have it all on cassette to listen to!Overall, it's a solid 100/10 from me, definitely worth the $20.

_childDocuments_.review: I think for many of us the reason the original Half-Life dug its place deep in our hearts is that it did something that no game had done before. It told a story with no interruptions, without taking you out of character. Yes, the second point I list is a completely separate project that simply runs on the same platform. For anyone out there that enjoyed the original Blue Shift - you can play the first 3 chapters redone as a mod for Black Mesa (or maybe by the time you're reading this even more chapters are out). Saying this is a mod doesn't do it any justice. HECU Collective's Blue Shift is an absolute triumph. It's better than Black Mesa itself. A key reason is being able to experience the same "calm before the storm" from the eyes of Barney. Their work shines brightly in NPC interactions and environment design in chapters such as "Questionable Ethics" and "Interloper". Many say "Interloper" is unnecessarily long. I concur - the chapter fleshes out the lore of the Vortigaunts - something that the original game failed miserably. It also introduces surprisingly creative gameplay mechanics.Yes, the original was too long and too messy. Yes, we needed this fix. If you want to play this chapter true to the original you can download it from the Steam Workshop as a mod. It's very well made.Many hardcore Valve fans believe having the original game end on Xen is a giant mistake. And rightfully so. Crowbar Collective managed to make Xen the world Valve envisioned 20 years ago but was never able to realize. Xen is so good it could have been released as a separate game but it would have outshined the earth-bound chapters.The game would have been unplayable without it. It's disabled by default - you have to toggle it in the options.It's  A M A Z I N G.The team tried to stay true to most of the key points in the original levels. That, combined with the fidelity of the source engine is a recipe for disaster. This is no longer a shooter - it's a puzzle game - you spend 80% of the time trying to figure out how to escape the room. These are pointless and just slow down progression. The only interesting and creative plug puzzles are on Xen (portal to Gonarch's Lair). Arm yourself with a bit of patience - grenade volleys are broken; rocket homing is broken; glitchy shotgun and crossbow reload animations; completely butchered tau cannon. I played the game on "Black Mesa" difficulty which should have been somewhere in the middle between normal and hard. The variables were broken to the point where gameplay can be completely unrewarding and unfair. The entire weapon arsenal has no stopping power whatsoever. Even the tau cannon can barely kill a marine at full charge. What a joke. Don't bother and play this on "normal" so that you get a little bit of fun out of the combat.Ammo capacity is cut down to probably 1/3 of the original limits. You can't have any gun preferences - the game forces you to use all of them. You have to scout every location for every crate if you want to have a semi-steady supply of ammo for your preferred guns. So when you're not doing escape room puzzles you're busy with a scavenger hunt.The game offers multiple choke points that feel like a scenario a 12-year-old would produce in GMod: First, the game intentionally starves you from certain ammo types e.g. shotgun shells and MP5 bullets. Then it puts you in a tight room. Then it spawns an absurd number of enemies e.g. 12 headcrabs. A challenge with no thought put into it quickly becomes a chore, the opposite of fun.As absurd as it may sound - the original Half-Life has significantly better enemy AI. Or at least significantly better-fitting for the game environment. The original marines communicate with each other, they regroup, they use cover, they feel real. In Black Mesa you're fighting reskinned Combine guards with no tweaks to the self-esteem they display in Half-Life 2. At times combat felt so much like Half-Life 2, I was surprised to find out my dead enemies had dropped MP5s instead of Pulse Rifles. The original Half-Life was a fast-paced, fun shooter that rewarded skill and bold moves. Black Mesa is the opposite. You have to play by the rules - hide behind cover, use interactive environmental elements, blow up barrels, let opposing forces fight each other, etc. If you try to play in the style of the original game you quickly get punished.I've played the original game multiple times. It took me 13 hrs to complete the Black Mesa campaign without any hints. That's probably 3-4 hours longer than it should have been. And this has nothing to do with the extended Xen. Xen is great. The redone original levels are the ones that suck.It's fairly obvious when this project was at its darkest hour, based on the mind-numbing level-design of "Surface Tension" and "Forget about Freeman". My advice to the players that don't have an endless supply of patience is to entirely skip these chapters.Come on Joel, for real? Rock guitar blasting so loud I can't hear MY OWN shotgun fire let alone hear any of the 8 marines shooting at me... This doesn't fit in the Half-Life universe at all.

_childDocuments_.review: has some frustrating ups and downs, but for fans of the original , it is a must-play love-letter-turned-experiment that demonstrates everything great and everything awful about the original title.But I'm getting ahead of myself. Pitched as far back as 2005,  began life as a faithful remake of the original Valve classic, recreating classic moments shot-for-shot in an updated engine. Over ten years later, the game is, at the time I write this review, technically unfinished; it is still in Early Access, awaiting the release of the completely reimagined Xen chapter. However, much of the rest of the game is in-tact, and there's a lot to be said about what it keeps and what it changes from the original game.The writing, perhaps, is the strongest update, even moreso than the graphical and engine improvements. Characters from the acclaimed  are introduced early in the game, creating a sense of continuity with later  titles. Scientists and security guards have more dialogue, and the game on the whole has a greater feeling of being alive; while the original game was a hallmark of detail for the time, the remake takes real strides to make the people of the game world feel like more than cardboard cutouts. Pacing for other scenes have changed too; those expecting to pick up the crowbar shortly after the Resonance Cascade will be surprised to see how long it takes before its apperance at a far more dramatic moment. (As a final sidebar, I feel as well that the updated score deserves some much due credit, as Joel Nielson's work is really something else.)Equally interesting are what the developers at Crowbar Collective opted not to change. The random difficulty spikes in the game really break the flow of play, with the lobby sequence and that damned dam being particularly egregious examples. It seems peculiar that these moments were not redesigned to better direct intentional play; I can only conclude that this decision was made to preserve the difficulty of the original game.Yet therein is the problem.  seeks to update and retell the story of , yet it is ultimately trapped in its precursor's shadow. A paradox,  is a game that looks ahead to what new technology can do to improve games, while itself being trapped by design philosophies of yesteryear. Even the sentiment that the game is an updated retelling is something of a paradox, as it's been in development for . While the act of recreating and preserving the experience of the original game is perhaps a noble end, it does leave one wondering: if Crowbar Collective set out to adapt the game, why not pave over the mistakes of the original in this re-telling?At the end of the day,  is a hard game to get behind, but the dogged determination with which it recreates  is still impressive. As a project which began life as a fan project but has grown into a full retail release, it's hard not to find something oddly motivational in the experience. As a shooter,  feels about seven years too late, but it nevertheless remains a good shooter. It's not an experience for everyone, but for those seeking to experience  with the capability of modern hardware or for those looking for a sharper, cleaner version of the original, it remains a title worth playing. I may not love , but if nothing else, I admire its tenacity, and for that, I do recommend picking up a copy.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the easiest recommendations from me. I'm not a hardcore fan of the Half-Life series but I recognise its importance for gaming as a whole and the cultural impact it made more than 20 years ago. The original HL was definitely a revolutionary game for its time but I doubt I'd play it today. I'm too spoiled by the modern graphics and gameplay gimmicks that it lacks. You just can't immerse yourself in that blurry, gnarly low poly world with very few details compared to the modern games. No high res textures can fix it, unfortunately.Enter Black Mesa. A small team of really hardcore fans remade HL1 from scratch and made it a modern, vibrant game that still is THAT Half-Life with the same (and even improved) atmosphere, story, friends and enemies. Despite it was in the making for 14 years, the visuals still look good. Yes, it's not a fresh pop-a-mole shooter from Activision or something that would put your GPU to its virtual knees, but everything looks good enough to not distract you from the gameplay process. Until Xen. Because if the main part brought back memories from playing HL1 back in 2000s, Xen doesn't. That's why it plays and feels like a sequel to the Earth part, it's so unlike anything you played before it, and absolutely not like the boring floating islands in HL1. The graphic there is totally up to the today standards (at least it's the best the old Source engine can do, the FPS overall is like 4 times lower than in the Earth levels), it's alive, it breathes, it tells a story that connects Black Mesa with Half-Life 2.If you played HL1 before you'll still have a lot of fun revisiting the familiar locations. They're not copypasted of course and only the most iconic rooms are recreated close to the originals. Everything else is new. In Xen you'll meet only two well known bosses (but the battles with them are completely different) and that part is so long it could easily be a standalone game.Another important part of the game is music. At times it discords with the scene and suddenly brings unexpected emotions and understanding of what's really happening right now. I won't spoil it but you'll see and feel it I hope. Xen's music organically enhances the intense parts and creates a unique atmosphere that's drastically different from the boring and hostile feeling of HL1's Xen. Here you're like a guest that came not to destroy but to understand this world (and destroy. A bit).It's really an AAA game for a very low price considering the amount and quality of the content. It doesn't matter that a small team made it, you can't tell if you don't know it. The game is solid, it keeps the good tempo, the difficulty of fights and puzzles is polished, you're never bored. I'd say even HL2, the official Valve game, pales in comparison with Black Mesa. Go play it and you won't be disappointed.Played the game through on Debian Linux, i7-7700k, 32 Gb RAM, NVIDIA GeForce 1070. There are some broken shaders or textures in the Linux build (black polygons in some areas) and a severe FPS drop in the portal tower (lambda generator) area. FPS drops to 5-10 and since this puzzle requires a good reaction this renders it unplayable. Fortunately, you can play on Proton (force it in the game properties) but you'll need to put -oldgameui to the launch parameters or else you'll have no main menu for some reason. Then DXVK (D9VK) kicks in and you'll have a great performance and hopefully no graphical glitches anywhere. Or you can wait until this is fixed in the native Linux build.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a fan remake of the original Half Life that released in 1998. In 2004 Valve released a "remaster" of the game called Half Life Source, which has mixed reception from the players due to being essentially an extremely buggy Half Life campaign + multiplayer with no redeeming qualities other than maybe slightly improved lightning. Enter Crowbar Collective. They decided to take matters into their own hands and start working on their own version of a remaster.The first versions of this game appeared in around 2012 as a free Source Mod for anyone to download. After that, they started working on other aspects of the game such as lightning, AI, Xen levels and more details. In May 2015 they released it to Steam as an Early Access game while working on the other bugs and taking another 3 years to finish Xen. 5 years later they finally finished the game and released version 1.0 on 2020. So, what is so good about this game?- Stunning graphics especially on Xen- Xen is 10 times better and (almost) the entire section is amazing- Nihilanth boss battle is freakin AWESOME- Dialogue is much more clearer now and you understand more on what to do- Soundtrack is GODLIKE- Difficulty is more balanced compared to the original- Gunplay is very smooth and feels great- Perfect price for a remake- Performance drops every now and then (played on a GTX 1650 TI, so performance might depend on your own PC)- Interloper is a bit too long- Multiplayer is nothing special and is deadDespite the cons, this game is an essential to anyone that is a fan of FPS puzzle games and especially a big fan of Valve games. My recommendation is for you to play the OG Half Life first, then if you want a more balanced game with better graphics, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played this game I was skeptical it could recapture the old feeling of playing the original Half Life as a kid. That it wouldn't capture me in the game like the original did all those years ago, but the more I played, the more I kept getting immersed into the game. I tried to keep as many scientists and guards alive as possible, killing every alien and zombie I could find while scrounging ammo from every nook and cranny I could find. The setting and design of Black Mesa is really well done, those old cement walls and goofy corridors in Half Life 1 are made to look more like an actual research facility, giving depth to a place that wasn't in the original. It's a fun style of world building and story telling that really immerses you in the facility of Black Mesa and makes exploring a much more enjoyable experience.  The gameplay holds up as a Half Life game, fast paced combat paired with quick thinking during the tighter and more enemy packed combat scenarios like Questionable Ethics and Xen. The AI can be wonky at times but not enough to hinder the experience as it happened rarely. The music in this game is fantastic, it feels close to Half Life's style but not indirectly copying, including cinematic or very orchestral soundtracks to display a mood in a certain chapter, going so far as to spin the rockets burning the tentacle monster from slaying a monster to putting down an animal. However there had been sometimes where the game's soundtrack would drown out the rest of the audio, leaving me to try and listen to scientists over the music.   Something that impressed me in the game was how it went about humanizing and making the player empathize with the enemies, throughout the game you can listen to radio comms and scripted scenes showing the soldiers being decimated by the invading alien forces. The voice acting in a radio comm where a soldier tells a medic he's losing a lot of blood and lost his IFAK was one of the outliers, the medic calmly telling him to heal himself while gunfire goes off as the soldier chokes up blood and doesn't know what to do. Later on in Xen you encounter Vortigaunts who aren't hostile, one is being beaten by a Grunt and once you promptly kill it, they all begin to cower. This is something I really enjoy in this remake as in the original Half Life it was hard to really understand the Vortigaunts weren't evil at first, later on in the original they'd attack you like any other enemy and in the remake it shows the controllers taking over the minds of the enslaved Vortigaunts.   Lastly the final chapter of the game that was recently added after years of development, Xen. The levels were eye catching, gorgeous scenes of alien foliage and scenery that really makes me forget i'm playing a source game. They add these little Black Mesa work stations here and there that really tell you that the scientists really set up shop before any of the invasion happened. I do believe some of the parts did go on for a bit too long but not long enough to ruin the experience as in the original Xen was long and felt like it went on forever. The Gonarch fight really did justice to the creature, giving it a surprise appearance and then a whole chapter dedicated to puzzles and fleeing from the monster to one big boss fight at the end with an amazing boss theme. The Interloper chapter felt a little reminiscent of a Xen version of Residue Processing, lots of conveyor belts like the original but now there's jump puzzles and small battles that lead up to a long elevator battle with infinite gluon gun crystals that really make the entire chapter so much better. The Nihilanth boss fight was done a lot of justice, in the original he'd throw teleporters at you as you shot bullets and mobs, in the remake he spawns in these broken sections of Black Mesa from different corners of the facility with ammo and health. He has three phases that have shield generators, a bubble shield, and a final one on one. He rains down energy like artillery, laser beams, brings up the ground itself into spiky mountains, the Nihilanth gets a whole set of these powers that make you feel like you're fighting a final boss. The only thing that's really disappointing it he fact G-man isn't voiced by his original voice actor and as much as the guard voice actor tries, it's just not the same as the original but I give him props for almost being able to replicate his speech patterns. TL;DRCombat is fun and fast paced save for some sections where you can die pretty quickly if not paying attention and some wonky ai at partsMusic is absolutely fantastic and a big part of what makes this game so goodSetting makes the research facility feel realistic and encounters with Gordon's coworkers and enemies can really immerse you into the game's dark and sometimes hopeless setting. Xen is an absolute masterpiece visually and runs a little long sometimes doesn't feel like a slog to replay and gives respect to the two final bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is greater than the sum of its parts and a cool update to Half-Life. I won't hide the fact I went into it expecting constant reminders I was playing a game made by a mod group, but it's more than that. Firstly, the soundtrack changed the way I experienced certain moments. Joel Nielsen's Resonance turned the failed experiment at Black Mesa into something resembling a horror movie, which was unexpected. Then there are the weapons, with the combat shotgun being one of the coolest I've used since the original Doom. Map updates were more than welcome and it was almost relieving to see some of the less fun parts of the original had either been removed entirely or streamlined into a more modern approach.It's still Half-Life, fortunately. Even the jumping puzzles remain, as archaic as they are. They're a blunt reminder that the 1998 version came out when games were actual games, and not so-called cinematic masterpieces. I think the Black Mesa developers tried their best to minimise jumping puzzles but a few remain, like the oh so amazing conveyor belt sequences. Joy. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly an amazing game. There's even an achievement for not killing any of them, which made me happy!I'm not a master writer of reviews or anything, but this one definitely deserves something for just how good of a game it really is.Good job, guys.

The two boss fights (Gonarch and Nihilanth) are at least 10 times better, with several stages, and strategies to deal with.Memorable moment: Having to outrun a pack of Gargantuans and looking at them across a giant void after escaping.Worst moment: The long elevator ride against hordes of Controllers. Almos made me ragequit. The most annoying game in the whole game, in waves, in an inescapable elevator level. Bad call on that one.

_childDocuments_.review: Crowbar Collective did an excellent job remastering the original Half-life. Black Mesa redelivers the entire experience with more than fresh coat of paint (they tore the whole house down and rebuilt it from the ground up) and reaffirms Half-Life's place amongst the greatest games of all time for newcomers and veterans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't satisfied with this remake when I played it a few years ago and left a negative review. Something felt off about the gunplay, the way enemies behaved (the tentacles in Blast Pit, and the soldiers) and the way the game felt more like the inferior Half Life 2, rather than the original game.I'm playing it again now and most of these issues seem like they were fixed. Fighting soldiers feels a lot more fun, the tentacle boss reacts properly to my actions and the game just feels more like Half Life.A few things I still think need to be addressed:- The ichtyosaur needs to have its scary roaring sound, it's the scariest enemy in the game and its roar is what made it so memorable. I want to hear that sound whenever I fall into a pool of water because it scares the crap out of me. The sound it currently makes isn't startling enough.- The hivehand's projectiles really shouldn't work under water. In fact, it probably shouldn't work at all against certain enemies. It makes it too easy and tempting to just pick off enemies from a distance while they're defenseless.- Xen looks beautiful but initially doesn't feel very threatening. There's a lot of puzzling, but the meat of the game should be fighting enemies.- The intro sequence is a bit over the top, this is still just a big cutscene no matter how impressive you make it. Cutscenes are bad.The real problem with the original Xen was that at that point in the game, you have a big arsenal of weapons for use against strong enemies, but when you get to Xen you suddenly stop fighting soldiers and female ninjas. Houndeyes, barnacles, zombies and even bullsquid are no match for you at this point. Grunts and Controllers are the logical choices for enemies at this stage, but the initial bits in Xen don't include them. Ichtyosaurs are another good option and you did include them in the mod, but as I said they're too easily picked off by the hivehand. Basically, Xen should be more difficult and less of a platformer-puzzler.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is so good and professional, it's impossible to tell that this is actually not an AAA-title with big publisher but a fan-made game that baked 14 years in the oven. There are tons of changes. Good changes. Essential changes. It's not even on par with Half-Life. It's tad betted. It's Half-Life as you remembered it. Minus the ugly models, jank, poor Xen chapters and abysmal movement systems from 1998.Black Mesa is fun, beautiful and engaging FPS game with great pacing and surprisingly competent visuals. It's a good FPS game even without the Half-Life legacy. Long one too. Took me 20 hours with Xen on Normal.Honestly, if you love good FPS games or good games in general, you should definitely pick Black Mesa up. Even if you're not into the Half-Life craze, it's a crime to miss such focused and honest single-player shooter w/o service bullcrap, fp2 BR mode or mtx.Support the devs! And welcome to the Black Mesa Research Facility.

_childDocuments_.review: This faithful reworking of the original Half Life offers a lot more than one would first suspect. This isn't just a graphical overhaul. Gameplay, level design/aesthetics, sound design, music, etc, it is all reworked and most of that is for the better. The changes to much of the level designs also help the maps feel far more modern and give the Black Mesa Complex much more life. However, this game does far more than recreate the old Half Life game we love. It fixes the entire ending of the game. I personally liked the old Xen levels, exploring alien worlds is always exciting. However, it was obvious that Xen did not get the attention or time it needed to fit in to the rest of the award-winning game that was beloved for years. Crowbar Collective sought to take the time to do it right, and I believe they went above and beyond what was required of them to finish the entire story. Xen is absolutely astonishing. Visually breathtaking, audibly thriving with life, the team managed to take what was essentially a few large platform levels and build a living, believable alien world. In addition, the Xen levels are far lengthier, taking nearly as long to complete as the Black Mesa Complex levels. And I could not be happier, mostly. There are a couple negatives I have with Black Mesa, the only big one being the manufacturing level in Xen is a massive slog to get through, with repetitive puzzles and incredibly long fight sequences that play out the exact same way, there's little room for diverse gameplay, unlike the rest of the game. This level was arguably the worst one in the original game, but at least its stay was short. Here, it will take you quite awhile to work your way through. Another issue I have is with the way Gordon moves. It's often quite hard to control where exactly he lands as being launched through the air can be disrupted by touching anything at all that will drastically alter your direction. Landing is also an issue as you will slide around very easily. It's not floaty, but it does feel like Gordon is trying to walk on ice. It is also frustrating at times when you get stuck in certain map or prop geometry. It makes the game seem unpolished when this happens as there is very little you can do to stop it. However, it's not impossible to get unstuck and is more of an annoyance than a hindrance. Aside from some very minor nitpicks, there's not really anything else of note to hold against this game. It was incredible to play through, and because it was so masterfully recreated to suit modern times, it does not make me feel nostalgia when playing it, but rather excitement for a "new" game. Which is what I had many years ago playing the original for the first time. And I look forward to playing through Black Mesa many more times over the following years.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa feels like a game that should have been released by Valve years ago. I still cannot believe this was made by bunch of fans. They improved the original in many ways without compromising the original vision. My only complaint is the last few chapters starting with Xen. It seems the Crowbar Collective team really wanted to make these last couple of chapters their own and diverge from the design of the original. As a result, what should have been a climax turned into a chore as these chapters are too long and have so many repetitive objectives and puzzles. Although I admire all the hard work they put into these chapters, it seriously hurt the pacing.Half-Life 1 still has better game design than most games today so it makes me mad that Valve has stopped making video games. Black Mesa is a reminder of the good old days. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa pays a wonderful tribute to the original game, but with a modern twist. It's Half-Life, but as we remembered it as kids. First part of Xen really blew my mind with incredible visuals. Gonarch is really overpowered on Hard, hopefully he will be fixed soon.Interloper is the longest and the most boring chapter in the game, I have no idea what the developers were thinking. It needs to be shorter and have more engaging moments with enemies. I love the boosted Gluon Gun and the epic elevator ride before the grand finale.Nihilanth boss fight is on a completely new level compared to the original.Overall, it's a solid 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best re-made games I've played.I tried the original Half-Life up until the railways level like more than 10 years ago but I haven't finished the original due to extreme motion sickness I was having from the graphics and old CRT monitor I had at the time. This remake of the game helped me a lot to enjoy what Half-Life has to offer. The story is a 10/10 for me, I enjoyed playing through the entire game, solving puzzles and meeting some random NPCs. Graphics, sounds, and level designs were also great, the only downside for me was (minor spoiler alert), . There were some minor bugs and level glitches here and there which could be fixed by reloading a save game most of the time. I was also getting some random FPS drops on certain levels but nothing game breaking.I had a really fun time playing this game and it brought back a lot of memories from the original.Would definitely recommend others to play this. I'd give it a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is unapologetically Half-Life. Every aspect of this game feels like it was designed to be as faithful to the original as possible while reimagining the parts that could be improved to make the game feel more tight and satisfying. And god, the Xen remaster... nothing could have prepared me for how fun Xen was to run through.If you liked Half-Life, you will like this. If you haven't tried it but enjoy other Source Engine games and/or want to experience one of the most iconic games of all time, *try this.* This is the best way to experience Half-Life in this decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a game unlike no other. While I'm rather new to half life franchise as a whole, having only finished playing the games about 1-2 months ago, Black Mesa I would say is one of the best half life games I've played. While it's not official Valve half life, it still does an excellent job at doing what Valve does right, immersive and engaging storytelling. The graphics are amazing, and Xen truly is a breathtaking experience. The gameplay is fantastic, and each of the weapons feel unique and different from one another. Each level is carefully designed, and no puzzle is either too hard nor too easy. If you're a fan of the Half-life franchise, and you're looking at playing a modern remake of the original, this is your huckleberry.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Very good in some regards but it feels like they missed the reason HL1 was so good. One example real quick is a wood shop early in the game. The room contains literally two machines, a drill and a rotary saw, and some wooden beams and the rest of the room's barren. It just feels very lifeless compared to the original. Watch some videos on all the dumb little nuances put into the original like simulating alien's sense of smell. The gore's cool, the gameplay's solid but it just feels like an average Unity shooter in terms of what it brings to the table whereas the original just kicked the door down and brought forth a new era of gaming. I guess it's cool to see how much we take this stuff for granted nowadays when back then it was insane that npcs had microwaves and got mad when you overcooked their food.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome!I got the game a while back, and played through what they had then, not knowing it was in early access, and enjoyed it and was looking forward to its completion when I found out it was still in beta. So when the launch version was released, I started it up again. I was blown away at the improvements they had made, the game was good before, now it was fantastic. Then I got to Xen...My jaw dropped. _childDocuments_.review: Wow! This is my first time playing through the whole of  and it is quite the towering achievement, even as old as it is. Crowbar Collective deserve some of this merit as their work has updated the game to be more in line with modern sensibilities of game design, such as with more forgiving checkpoints, and also added a layer of polish that preserves the character of the game for future generations.I was quite surprised at how quickly the game rattles along and very rarely feels boring or confusing. The levels are so cleverly designed that you would be forgiven for repeatedly feeling like you've broken the game  or gone the wrong way, only for your curiosity to be rewarded with progress or a juicy secret.It becomes more apparent as you progress through the game how much of an influence  was on the Valve-developed original. From the linear-non-linear map layout to the bizarre arsenal you can bring to bear, it's amazing that a game that harks back to 25-year old game design principles still feels so fresh. Even Freeman's famous silence is a knowing reference to the Duke's motor mouth - itself a throwback to cinema of the 80s.I will say that I found the game to start to drag around the  - it was a little deflating. Another issue I had was that I sometimes found myself in the middle of a firefight and I needed to change weapon to something that wasn't to hand, which can be quite laborious at the best of times - this never felt like it added anything to the combat; it felt dated. If it sounds like I'm nitpicking though, it's probably because I am, a little bit.It has been quite refreshing to play a game that doesn't ask me to spend a hundred hours scouring for side quests; losing my patience with loot boxes, or suffering the myriad modern game mechanics designed to keep me playing and paying ad nauseam. I would quite like it if this became a thing again: for a game to be about telling a story, rather than just tapping my wallet.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a long journey; It all started in 2008, when it was called Black Mesa: Source. Black Mesa: Source was basically a fan made recreation of the 1998 classic game made by VAVLe called "Hλlf-Life". The mod team shared it's first trailer in 2008. But after delays and pushback to date, Black Mesa: Source was released in 2012 on ModDB. The mod initially set Black Mesa Source as a free modification. Skipping to 2015, that's when it really kicked off as VALVe (the creator's of Hλlf-Life) has given the approval of the game being green lit via it's service "Steam greenlight", which as of now has been defunct. Black Mesa Source was renamed to "Black Mesa" and became an Early Access Game, being sold on the Steam Store for $20 USD. It was an amazing thing for the developers, but one thing was still missing from the remake, Xen. Xen is the last levels in Hλlf-Life where you travel to the unknown borderworld, known as Xen. The reason why Xen wasn't added in the early days (as in 2008 - 2015) because the dev team wanted to recreate the Xen levels as in Hλlf-Life, the level design was really poor, it got Gabe Newell, CEO of VALVe to say the he didn't like the design of what Xen looked like in the 1998 Hλlf-Life. The Dev of BMS wanted to make sure that the mod wouldn't have poor level design of Xen. Black Mesa would receive basic small updates, not constant, but little content that could add stuff in the game, like the Crossfire update, which as the name suggests, adds 1 new map to Multiplayer mode, Crossfire (a Hλlf-Life classic map) That was one to name a few.Years and years have passed from 2015 to 2018, that's when the Black Mesa community and fans were given it's first look at Xen with a Trailer showcasing, the beauty nature in Nov 19, 2018. Into the year of 2019 on June 26, the dev team released 3 chapters of Xen to the public in a Beta test stress for Xen levels, see how different player computers were to one and another, this test was implemented for number of reasons, the most common was to see game performance, bug fixes. In December 6, that when all the Xen levels was released. Into the new year, new decade of 2020;After the huge full beta announcement, we would have thought of something that the team would do, but, in February 24, 2020 an article on Steam news for the game was published titled "Fear Not The Long Road" by Adam Engels. The article was him describing his years on how he started and what he encountered in the years. However, what was really intriguing was on before the last line "Black Mesa 1.0 will launch Thursday March 5th on Steam." This confirms that Black Mesa will now exit Early Access Game, which has been in for the past 5 years, and after from reading that, I think to myself going back to the Source era of Black Mesa, we have to appreciate the devs at Crowbar Collective. As a fan of Half Life and this mod, it makes me tear up to the point of now, realizing how far it was from completion, and now how close it's now to completion. I want to say, from the bottom of my heart, thank you @Crowbar Collective. The team that worked on the game, whether it was code, sound, visuals. You all have to give yourselves a pat on the back and a thank you from the community. What a journey it was and still going to be a journey after the March 2020 release.Feel free to correct any thing that I may have forgotten or mixed up.Article news -

_childDocuments_.review: I put off playing Black Mesa for a long time, but recently I decided to satisfy my craving for some nostalgia and finally beat Black Mesa. I deeply regret this decision.The Good:The early game is really, really strong and strikes an awesome balance between faithfully recreating the original and polishing some of the rough edges.Some of the enemy and weapon changes really help provide new challenges and new tools to old veteran players, such as the improved soldier AI and the ability to aim down sights with the revolver.The art direction is absolutely gorgeous, especially as you get to Xen.They cut out a pretty massive chunk of On A Rail, which was a brilliant decision on their part. I also think they cut down Surface Tension a little as well, but it may have just been better pacing. Solid improvements on both partsThe Bad:The enemies are absolute damage sponges and it's not unusual to have to spend and entire SMG magazine to kill a single human grunt. The weapons have really, really odd random spread that you have no control over, so accurately placing shots is a near impossibility with the SMG and the shotgun seems to be biased to the lower half of the crosshair around 60% of the time.Sometimes, the damage feels random as well.A lot of the new environment detail makes the maps less readable, since a lot of the interactive switches and doors you need to go through are marked with green lights. This also happens to be the art team's favorite color light to put next to decorative switches that don't do anything.Interloper. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. INTERLOPER. I HOPE YOU LIKE SPENDING A SOLID TWO HOURS RIDING CONVEYOR BELTS, DOING SOURCE ENGINE PLATFORMING, FINDING WEIRD RED BLOB THINGS TO BREAK TO TURN OFF FORCE FIELDS AND FIGHTING WAVES OF ALIEN CONTROLLERS WITH A GLUON GUN WITH INFINITE AMMO ONLY TO SPEND MORE TIME RIDING CONVEYOR BELTS TO FIND MORE RED THINGS TO SMASH TO TURN OFF FORCE FIELDS THIS IS YOUR LIFE NOW READ THIS BIT OVER AND OVER AND OVER FOR THE NEXT TWO HOURS THEY MADE XEN WORSE HOW DID THEY MAKE XEN WORSE HOW DO YOU DO THAT?!?!?!?In summary, Black Mesa starts strong and has a pretty solid middle, but manages to absolutely donk it up at the end making it a very faithful reproduction of the original. Needless to say, I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, i am a big fan of the Half-Life series and i must say that if there is any con on it,they are the graphics. Yes, i know that it came out in 1998 and it's pretty decent for the time. I honestly find the graphics not a major point in games like these that have a high replayability value, but there will always be a "IF" there were good grahpics, this game could be even more enjoyable...So now, let's move on to Black Mesa itself. They use Source Engine and best graphics. Logically. But apart that, what is there to note? From the original gameplay i could find a lot of diferences between the original game and this fan-made remake:->Some puzzles have different ways to be solved;->Some areas are accessed in a diferent way (took me a few minutes in the lab to realize that the door i normally would pass through in HL1 is closed and i had to go a way around through a freezer);->Some areas have some different music themes for (for example) when you are fighting, in the middle of a puzzle or in a new area. I don't know about this change, i think it's a bold move since in some cases it increases the thrill and "mood" and others simply is a bit...uncessessary.->Some new events were created, not much, small stuff.->Some details in HL1 that weren't explained "properly" (and by that i mean not getting our attention for being extremely little details) are actually more...clear so to say. Like the cooking pot in the microwave that you make explode. Now seriously doe, i never heard of Eli Vance until the second game. There is one thing to add down about Black Mesa: the game ends (for now at least) on the portal to XEN. The developers said that there was a problem with the organic textures and Source engine. They are also expanding XEN. Again, a bold move since a lot of the players didn't really liked that area. There are taking their time and honestly, i can't blame them. They are making a remake of one of the best FPS/Horror/Sci-fi games of all time. Valve's Serie have a powerfull name in the industry.So as a final review: ->Is it worth it?Yes, but keep in mind it's a growing game. If you are afraid of it, consider either purchasing it on sales or downloading the Black Mesa's mod from the official team website (keep in mind XEN won't be included, so if you want future releases, buy the game).

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life was one of the core games of my childhood, representing a huge milestone in FPS creativity, storytelling, and interaction. Before this were games like Quake and FPSs had the stereotype of not really having in-depth story. I did recently replay the old game and while it's great, it does show it's age. Black Mesa is an unbelievably great remake that is absolutely true to the original game. The updated graphics are just right so that the game still looks like the original with all its charm and style. At first I thought, yes this is a great remake, it's fun and makes the old Half-Life accessable to a new younger generation. But then I made it to Xen and HOLY CRAP you guys went the extra mile and then some. In the original Half-Life, I hardly remember the Xen levels to be honest, yeah they were unique but never stuck in my mind. Black Mesa's Xen is truly an alien world full of new puzzles and challenges. Half-Life was really all about creating intense emotion purely from the setting with hardly any words being spoken, and the Xen levels put me in awe. Some might say that Xen is too long, especially compared to the rest of the game, maybe too many puzzles repeating themselves, and kinda weird or even dull gunplay, but whatever, I still loved it. If you've never played Half-Life before, do yourself a favor, pick up a crowbar and play Black Mesa.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant reimagining of a timeless classic. If you've never played the half life series before but are turned off by the dated-ness this is a great way to get the same experience with a more modern feeling. It stays true to the original but it's also not a carbon copy.For those of you who are familiar, this is not just a fresh coat of paint or some HD textures. It's the entire game redesigned and remastered. The levels and puzzles will be familiar, but the entire thing feels different; it's a totally new experience and  absolutely worth playing.Now for the thing on everyone's mind: is it worth $20? As a standalone product, absolutely. It delivers enough content with the quality to justify that price tag.The point of contention here is that the game was released earlier as a free mod. I haven't played much of the mod, but the money and valve's support here seems to have been used to take the mod a bit beyond what it could achieve as a mod alone - full use of the latest source engine, a multiplayer mode with steam workshop integration for maps, graphics and sound improved even further, gameplay stability improved greatly (I haven't encountered a single bug or glitch on my playthrough). Certainly, this is an improved experience from the mod and not just the same thing with a price tag slapped on. I'm given to understand the devs have kept the mod release (now legacy version) available for free so it's up to you to decide whether $20 is a worthy asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a lot of video game remakes exist nowadays. The video game industry is saturated with lazy remasters as in remasters that only bump up the frame rate, add some sharpened textures, etc. But Black Mesa is one of those faithful few remakes that exists. It's the entire first Half Life game remade from the ground up with pure attention to detail and modern gameplay.Although I never played the original Half Life, I can easily say that Black Mesa does an incredible job of creating the feeling of isolation and dependency to survive an enormous government facility whilst hunted down by aliens from a different world and Government agents who are sent in as a kill squad in order to cover up the incident that occurred on the unfortunate day of May 16, 2000.You take the role of Gordon Freeman. A graduate of MIT who landed himself a job at the Black Mesa research facility located in the state of New Mexico.  Gordon works under a "classified" administrative sponsor. On the day of the Black Mesa incident, he is late to work and during the tram ride, you get to witness just how big the facility is, unknowingly knowing that this isn't even a quarter of it. He gets into his iconic orange HEV suit and begins his work for the day. Today he has to insert a specimen into the Anti-Mass device. Unknowingly this causes a catastrophe which forces Earth and the border world Xen to collide with each other bringing the Xen creatures to Earth. Gordon wakes up and gets to exploring the facility hoping for a way out.● Beautiful graphics ● Solid gunplay and gameplay● Compelling story● Very long levels ● Lots of weapons ● Great optimization ● Lots of unique enemies to fight ● Steam Achievements● Steam trading cards● Excellent price ● Xen ● Workshop support ● New soundtrack● Gore system ● Broken Marine AI ● No objective reminder ● Subtitles Whether you're a Half Life fan or a newcomer, Black Mesa is THE game to play if you want to get into the franchise or revisit the first game. Black Mesa is not just a new coat of paint but a complete rework from the ground up. The stellar price for the amount of content and replayability you get is just way too grand to pass up. If I had to list my top 5 game remakes I would without a doubt put Black Mesa on that list. Crowbar Collective have outdone themselves and did something that the majority of today's Triple-A developers can't do: deliver a game made with passion and love. The only thing that is holding me back from giving Black Mesa that sweet 10/10 is the Marine AI. I'm sorry but If I have to go into the files of the game to make the enemy AI more bearable then you failed at making the enemy AI good.

_childDocuments_.review: After 15 years, this project is finally complete, however i have owned this version since it released in May 2015 and the old mod version since before it, never regretted it. Black Mesa has become more than a remake, its a re -imagining if not more than that at this point. Ever since purchasing this i was waiting for this to leave EA to do this review.BM is an excellent re- imagining of the classic game Half Life from 1998 in the Source engine. If you have played Half Life before you can use that knowledge for the earthbound levels as a reference. The earthbound levels are great, aside from the improvements the Source engine normally has, as well as the extensive modifications CC have done to it to make it look truly beautiful, the level design is great, combat is great, as well as the fact they have improved the AI since the mod and even first steam versions, as well as maps. The game also has multiplayer which works now ans is very good. But many of us were waiting for Xen, and i can assure it wont disappoint. It takes advantage of the modifications CC have made to  the engine. Valve have stated they regret the original because so much was cut, but CC have massively expanded it. In it you will find human made labs, new extremely detailed  environments, new NPCs/variants, really new everything, but still faithful to the the original game. Overall this is a excellent game. CC really out done themselves. Highly recommended. 9.8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than the original. I was expecting a simpre retexture with the Source Engine, but they redid some parts of levels and completely made evreything look better. I've played all the Half Life games at least 3 times. But Black Mesa turns Half Life 1 into a spectacular brand new game. I'll go over the pros and cons and give a summary at the end.PROS:-Made the guns look like real guns-Made New models for evreything-Made a Zombie Guard-Added new voicelines and character interactions-Made new animations for all the guns, including sprinting, reloading, fireing, and made a animation for when you pick up the gun for the first time-Made objectives clearer-Made Female and Black Scientists so they're all not the same 3 models-Hired some diffrent voice actors for scientists and gurads so they don't all sound the same-Looks great-More Interactions with guards and scientists-Got rid of a ton of stupid bugs in HL1-Made it modeble via Steam Workshop-Added new tons of new sounds-The Achievements are actually cool, and you don't get them just by playing the gameCONS:-Diffucult, but not much more than HL1-Sometimes NPC's bug out -The music is a little worse than HL1 but still excellant-Hazord Suit still talks for 5 minutes when you put it on-Xen levels aren't realeased yet but I don't really care about thoseSUMMARY:It was tons better than I expected, I spent my first 20 minutes maxing out all the dialougue. Excellant game, 20 US dollars is a deal if you play it multiple times. But if you see it on sale definately a great grab. You might not be able to notice some of the changes if you've never played the original Half Life, but it's still a great time. It took me 13 hours to beat the game on my first playthrough. I plan to play this game for years. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well, as a youngster, half life was the first video game i played at a young age, so there was always a special place for the series in my heart. half life 1 was perfect in my opinion. as time passed, and half life 2 episode 2 is now way behind me, the series just got old. with so many new games coming out, i almost completely forgot about the game that started my love for science fiction, horror, and crowbars. i happened to stumble upon black mesa a few years back. i bought it as soon as i saw what the plans were, and how much work was put into it. i wasnt disappointed at all. it takes the now outdated (in only a few aspects) of the original half life and gives it a new polished look and feel. areas are different but still recognizable, ai is smarter and more challenging, and weapons have a new look and feel but keep the same old feeling of the original game we all love. it isnt just a graphics overhaul like i thought it would be, it is a more current retelling of the original game (if that makes sense) i thank the team making this game because it brought me back to my childhood, but in a way that felt like a new experience as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent fan-made remake of the original Half-Life game. I thoroughly enjoyed the first part where Freeman has to escape the facility; It kept true to the original story and maps while also adding some additional rooms and spaces to explore. The introduction, just after the Resonance Cascade event, is even more atmospheric and spookier than the original - adding in the half-zombies was a great touch. The soundtrack is also marvellous; Internal Conflict by Joel Nielsen goes too hard.However, this game is not without its flaws. It did crash on me a couple of times, but most often during the Nihilinth boss fight. Unfortunately, I did spend a good chunk of time relaunching my game and reloading uncorrupted saves before the crash trying to figure out how to defeat the boss. It took me far too long to realise that the rocket launcher was doing negative damage to its brain (makes sense) so once I swapped to the tau cannon I easily overcome it and was able to finish the game. Getting thrown out of bounds may have also added salt to the wound...The Xen level is absolutely gorgeous (so beautiful in fact there are entire guides on how to farm it for screenshots). Visually extremely stunning and rich in fauna and flora I actually preferred this over the original. The alien levels do drop off a bit in quality as they go on. The Interloper chapter was particularly tedious and repetitive, some parts poorly construed and thrown together. Perhaps the developers were also running out of steam towards the end.This game is well-worth a play-through but is by no means a replacement to the original which I believe remains the GOAT.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best remake I have ever played. It took a very, very long time to develop but it is worth it.If you liked the good ol' Half Life, you will love this. _childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life 1 is a piece of gaming history. In its time ground breaking, an overall great game and even now still greatly enjoyable. It is still a flawed game, infamously with the short and jarring Xen levels.Black Mesa seeks to take everything that made Half Life great and keep it, and make everything that wasn't so great and improve it. Crowbar Collective recently finished and released the Xen levels in beta, which made me replay the entire game (on hard, for extra adrenaline). The levels on earth are easily recognisable from the original game, iconic scenes like the tentacles in the silo and the trash compactor are indistinguishable from the original aside from better graphics.Xen however, is a far cry from its original, and in an amazing way. No more rushing through three platforms, a short boss fight and a small factory to get to the end boss. The Xen level is an expansive look into the "outskirts" of the Xen planetoids, with a look into the human expedition and what they left behind. The Gonarch's Lair reminded me a lot of the Antlion Guardian battle in Episode 2, with a huge level of constant encounters and running away from the beast. Interloper shows you the gigantic complex used to launch the invasion, from the lowest levels where oppressed vortigaunts live amongst sewage, to the highest peaks where arrays of Grunt containers are transported to teleports.The Nilathant battle is magnificent as well, though slightly too easy in my opinion due to the abundance of ammo and health strewn around.All in all, Black Mesa is a love letter to one of the most important games in gaming history, and a very well executed one at that.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm finishing this review now that I've completed the full game. The scope of Xen is a step above anything that's come before and has made BM something truly special.In short: Excellence in single-player form. Black Mesa does everything right when it comes to remaking HL1: whether it's the masterful atmosphere, the moving score or the puzzles and the enjoyable gunplay, you'll be sure to enjoy it. And you'll enjoy the Xen chapters even more. While I've fully watched the original Half-Life, Blue Shift & Opposing Force I've never played them, so this review will be more oriented to those who also have not.Like the original, Black Mesa is a very linear game where each chapter is focused on progressing the overarching plot through particular goals. In practice, this means advancing through the facility while solving puzzles, aiding allies and killing foes. Enemies come in a number of unique forms and can be a real challenge in the harder battles (God forbid if you run max difficulty and realistic damage mods like I do), with each type demanding different approaches to fighting. In general, both the puzzles and battles strike a perfect balance of difficulty and frequency and the weapon options are varied and offer many playstyles. When you get to Xen you unlock the Long Jump module which is not only a pleasure to use but offers crazy movement shooter potential.You'll be met with a lot of supporting characters who can aid you in combat and give hints: interacting with most is optional, but the real Gordon Freeman in you will be doing everything to save your colleagues. Gordon himself is, of course, mute, but there are hundreds of different dialogue lines in the game -- more or less every character you meet once the story is properly in motion has unique lines. With scant exceptions every character type (i.e. scientist, guard, marine) shares a single voice actor and base model, but the VAs do such an excellent job it isn't really an issue. The staged scenes are great and very much add to the experience.Throughout all of this you'll be faced with the daunting atmosphere surrounding the Black Mesa Research Facility thanks to the musical score and the map building. It's some of the best atmospheric design I've experienced! What really shoulders the burden of those grim and melancholic themes (as well as some action packed moments) is Joel Nielsen's score. Not only has he updated certain pieces as the game's development ran along, but he composed a dozen fantastic new tracks for full release. It's hard to imagine the game being so good without them: they're a crucial part of the experience, as are his less discussed ambient tracks.Equally, a masterful use of textures, lighting and ambience are common to all the chapters, with each area of the facility having unique textures, assets and layouts. I'm a tremendous fan of the abandoned industrial areas in particular -- I consider the On A Rail Uncut mod practically canon. The BMRF's map designs become more 'logical' as the game progresses (compare the well planned Lambda Complex to the haphazard Anomalous Materials Labs), but I don't consider this a weakness of the early chapters: they're just as atmospheric at times and their designs pay extensive homage to HL1. I don't think we could have it any other way.Xen is the ultimate fulfillment of all of these points, barring characters -- you don't come across any BMRF or marine personnel, though you know the former are supporting your every move from across the dimensions... but I'll leave that for your entertainment. It looks beautiful, the music is powerful, the boss battles are crazy good, the exploration is fun...Black Mesa still has multiplayer but last time I checked there were under ten people online. It might be the case that certain groups organise BM matches at certain times -- there are certainly other games I've played like that. BM multiplayer was very fun, but you'll definitely still get your money's worth with only singleplayer. I heartily recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have a chance to play original half-life, but I knew that the story is great and one day I decided to buy Black Mesa as it was a more modern approach to telling the same story. While playing the game I couldn't help but noticed lots of tiny details that make experience much better. It was clear to me because of the that developer put lots and lots hours of care, love and hard work. It was much more obvious when, after completing the game, I looked into some compression videos and found out for example how was redesign xen, all the boss fights, lots of single objects and details they had to add to make every single room more believable, more realistic and more live. I respect the original game but after so much time you should agree that there was not much to go off. Sound design is also great, lots of music turns out I was listening to remixes before knew about the game. Huge rework and redraw of all weapon, characters and locations, while trying to preserve the same feeling and same map as was before. For me as a guy who didn't play half-life games (just half-life 2 a little, and huge fan of portal played all games and mods) it was so fresh going around  without objective task, minimap, compass or arrow to next task. You always had to figure out yourself, but the clues is always there either it be a green light near the next door or path you should open or go, or red something blocking the way. Overall level design in my opinion was great and I caught myself on an that idea especially in the beginning to middle of the game. (except few minor moments but more on that later)Crowbar collective did a tremendous work, especially for such a cheap price and this game imo was a great force to invest me into the half-life story.The game is not all shine and rainbow, but hat's just a few minor hiccups that killed my love to the game a little bit, still game so good I can forget it easily. As I said game does not always clearly indicate what you have to do.Firstly there was door in the coolant tank 02 in Lambda core, where you have to find this little door bellow in the corner, I even get there but didn't saw that door was open neither consider it. Second there was an explosive room while making portal in Xen with clever puzzle which I almost figured out but I neither saw nor consider that door in use too and was stuck not understanding why the force field didn't work.Huge bummer for me was sometime corrupted saves in the beginning of the game, sometimes I just could load and have to use previous save instead of the last one. I didin't care much about it until it climaxed in the explosive room where for some reason every other save become unloadable before and after puzzle, so I have to load the exact level map through developer console. I skipped the part where you stabilize portal and jump into it (not the part fixing all three lasers), so it was not huge miss but it killed immersion for awhile.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn its good. This game delivers, what the original Half-Life wants to be. _childDocuments_.review: Strong recommendation, for both those who played the original and to those who are new to "traditoinal" linear FPS games. Black Mesa has everything which made the orignal great, and improves, adds and tweaks enough things that its worth a second run-through for old timers and to be accessible to a modern player.In particular for veterans of the orignal i would say its worth coming back to play the Xen levels. Just like in the original it changes up the game loop completely, but IMO this time in a much better way. Most of the Xen content in Black Mesa is completely new, it feels as if by taking as much time as they have to create it Crowbar Collective were able to portray Xen the way Valve would have wanted to but didnt have the time or technology to pull off back in the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: A remake of Half-life that honors the original game's story and quality. It improves nearly every aspect of the original game. Levels, maps, and bosses are greatly enhanced. The soundtrack is unexpectedly amazing and fitting. The NPCs also feel more alive and are given more character compared to HL1. The game also has this nice little reward mechanic in the form of dialogue or equipment when you optionally save the NPCs. Even the human enemy NPCs are given more character with the way they are built as a threat but humanized along the way.There are so many intense moments in the game and the buildup for each is spot on. I also liked the fact that they cut down and improved the more annoying parts from the original game such as the rail chapter. They massively improved the Xen chapters from the original game in terms of gameplay, length, and map design. Some people might disagree with me and say that the Xen chapters are dull, and honestly I can see why as it did feel tedious, but I liked the concept of being in this uncomfortable alien world trying to get to the center of it all.The only thing that I find off of this game is that there are some times that the game will have you run around the same area trying to find the right way to progress. I have to admit, the level puzzles feel repetitive, slow, and kinda dry especially considering just how many puzzles are in the game. This was also an issue from the original game and I really wished they've done something fresh to improve on it. However, it does feel satisfying to see yourself progress throughout the game when you finally get into the action. Overall, it's an excellent buy for both who played the original half-life and for those who haven't played it yet. Half-life is one of my favorite video games of all time, and Crowbar Collective really hit the nail in polishing and refining it with Black Mesa.

_childDocuments_.review: For the longest time one of my gaming shortcomings was that I've never played Half Life.
