_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa has been a shockingly fun game. The pacing is as good as anything else out there. I'd attribute this to its story progression and level design. I still have a lot of questions about how the world works, but I suppose that's just how knowing things works. Much of the time, you don't understand anything. Is it linear?. It is a game that makes you feel powerful, and yet it is made clear, that you have no control whatsoever. The ending reinforced that. Those themes are powerful because they are reflected in my own life. I have power and yet I lack control. I know things, but there's so much I don't understand. In that sense, the story was excellent.The gameplay was enticing. I would not describe the game as exceptionally difficult. It fulfilled a power fantasy in a setting where the odds still feel stacked against you. That's rare tbh. You have to figure things out to progress. I wish more games did that. Main things it could improve on are the feel of shooting and moving. They could've finessed the movement systems a bit more for the remake, but honestly that's nitpicking, especially considering the game originally released in 1998. Final review 9/10. Very memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: What all remakes should aspire to be.  Lovingly crafted by dedicated fans over many years.  This utilizes Half-Life 2-era's Source Engine and pushes it to the limit.  I remember playing Half Life as an adolescent and thinking it was a great game.  As time passed I appreciated the legacy the game had and it's way of showing you the story rather than narrating it to you.  Black Mesa captures all that and modernizes the graphics to the extent of the engine's limitations and even expands on the original game.  Some levels like Surface Tension and Xen went from being relatively short affairs to substantial journeys (the Xen chapters in particular received a healthy expansion). The Gonarch boss from the original went from being an arena boss fight into becoming an entire level unto itself as Gordon is relentlessly stalked by the creature.  The music that pops up here and there does a ton to help accentuate the mood - Joel Nielsen did excellent work with the music that hits at the right narrative moments and gets the blood flowing.  While the devs have expressed interest in making original games, they'd certainly be on the shortlist to make an updated Half Life: Opposing Force or a Half Life 2 remaster.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Although I had played Half-Life 2 and it's episodes a long while ago, I actually never got around to playing the first Half-Life. I'm not sure why, maybe I felt the story was easy enough to understand from what I heard about it. Also, since I mostly started playing video games during the late 2000's to early 2010's, It's sometimes hard for me to go back to much much older titles since I get too distracted by how dated they may feel.Black Mesa had caught my interest for quite some time, but I wanted to wait until it was completely finished before getting it (it was on Early Access with the final chapters missing for the longest time). I gotta say, it's crazy to see a game company not only authorize a fan remake but allow it to be sold on their storefront as well! Nintendo would NEVER do what Valve did.I bought it recently and played through the whole thing. Yep, it is most definitely an amazing video game! I made the decision to play the game with keyboard and mouse instead of my controller like the good old days when I played Team Fortress 2 with friends. It took some adjusting just because it's been a while since I played that way, but it feels so natural.One worry I had was that I wouldn't get to feel for the story since there weren't any big name characters like in HL2, but the depressing and dense atmosphere more than made up for it. Where as HL2 feels more optimistic with Gordon interacting with a team of resistance fighters, Black Mesa feels bleak and hopeless. You're just one guy trying to survive the hell that you unintentionally created. The few characters you do come across don't stay around for long, so you always feel somewhat lonely.It wasn't until I played Black Mesa that I realized that I forgot how fun the combat and puzzles were in the HL games. I always feel like a genius whenever I figure something out or find a secret area. The new enemies (or I guess old enemies lol) were really cool too. There were so many crazy aliens that I never had the chance to fight in Half-Life 2 like the Bullsquids and the Gonarch.If you're planning on starting the series, this definitely a great place to start!

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is flawed, but it's still a perfect remake of the original Half-Life. It echoes the highs and lows of the original game without copying them slavishly. The pacing isn't always great, there are sequences that arguably overstay their welcome, but this game feels like my memories of Half-Life. It is a labour of love and IMO is up there with the original. If the people who worked on this were to be involved with any post-Alyx continuation of the franchise, I would be quite optimistic.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: A truly wonderful recreation of the 1998 classic. Between the great soundscape and soundtrack, the high quality models and wonderful lighting, and gameplay that shows it's roots, Black Mesa has a fantastic feel to it.The audio in this game really makes me feel like I'm there. I can't call to mind any other game that uses 3D sound to quite the same degree as Black Mesa. The soundtrack is something else too. I would imagine it's hard to recapture the eerie feel or desperate rush of adrenaline the original game's soundtrack produced, but I believe the guys at crowbar collective nailed it.I appreciate Black Mesa's loyalty to the gameplay style of Half Life and other classic shooters (running at 70 mph with health and armor that can survive 100 bullets, firing at enemies that can survive just as many) instead of the more realistic approach more modern games are taking.I cannot wait for the full release!

_childDocuments_.review: This review might be a bias because I am a colossal fan of Half-Life series. Black Mesa is a complete reimagining of the original Half-Life game from 1998. Keeping the original charm but with major upgrades in visuals, dialogue and mapping. The difference from legacy version is future single player content, steam trading cards, Steam workshop intergration and multiplayer. You can get this game for free on the site (SIngleplayer only, old engine) but after ten years I think they deserve some money for the work they have done. (have downloaded legacy version years ago and played twice before purchasing this version.) It is early access and Xen, Gonarch’s Layer, Interloper and Nihilath are not included in the single player. Some minor bugs can be observed such as allies getting stuck in between open doors. Overall though it’s a fantastic fan remake worth checking out if you are new or a veteran of the series.The reason I would not recommend this game right now is the minor bugs that ruin the experience, such as enemies shooting through solid surfaces or your rockets hitting invisible walls killing you (vs tank blocking your path). When this game is complete (out of early access) I will replay and adjust my recommendation as needed.As promised I have replayed it from the beginning with version 1.0 and they have greatly improved the overall package. Environment changes are an interesting inclusion. Xen re imagining is great piece from the team and well put together. With version 1.0 I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. It's not Half-Life, it misses the point of Half-Life more often than not, but it's a competent shooter with some clever puzzles. A lot of work has gone into it and it shows. There are things added to the original (the game particularly shines in alternate paths to well-known maps), but then there are subtractions that baffle me. It's by no means the "definitive way" to play Half-Life, but it's good fun. Mostly.Enemy placement and numbers don't always work in the game's favor. There's no need for so many headcrabs and houndeyes in certain areas, they're just a nuisance. Enemies rush a lot more than in the original, which changes the core of the combat. Assassins are downright stupid and can easily be picked off, because in their efforts to rush, they end up clustering in small spaces. Also, Black Mesa might have the most unreliable shotgun I've played in a game. (EDIT: Disregard the previous statement, I have since played Doom 3)Additionally, Crowbar Collective worked really hard on Xen and I don't want to be a douche, but I found it pretty damn terrible. It's not every day I miss the original Xen. Half of it is good, but after Gonarch's Lair, it's a pointless slog. Also, word to the wise; in a game with unreliable physics, you don't want narrow ledges and frantic enemy chases. F7 may as well be bound to the right mouse button from some point on, as Gordon gets launched to oblivion because he hit a pebble on his way to a platform. Honestly, in three play-throughs, I only went through it one and a half times, I couldn't tolerate it any more than that. Lastly, the game looks and sounds great, but optimization is questionable. Because we're talking Source Engine, most modern systems won't deal with any massive problems at 1080p, but in certain areas there are massive dips in framerate. When you go from an average of 230fps to dropping below 60, something's wrong. There's also the occasional bug (nothing game breaking, fortunately) and the collision is atrocious; I've had bullets bounce off of empty air and I got stuck in the geometry way too many times for comfort. The game still gets a pass, because I think it's entertaining for the most part. Just do yourselves a favor and enable Always Run in the options.

_childDocuments_.review: To younger players this game may seem mediocre, but for me Half Life was my very first PC game and it sparked a life long interest in Science and science fiction. _childDocuments_.review: I have my controversial opinions about the Half Life games. The world it builds is amazing, and the story has always been great, but I have problems with almost every installment of the franchise just because of the gameplay.I disliked a  about the original Half Life game. I left a lengthy negative review on it, where I listed everything I liked and disliked about the game. I will not touch on everything here, but I am going to bring up what I think was fixed.- The level design is basically completely fixed in this game. The original was miserable to navigate and boring to look at. It was from the 90s, so it is understandable why their environments were less than subpar, but that doesn't change how miserable it is to play today. In the original I got lost at least 20 times, in this remake I got lost like maybe 4 times. They have completely fixed or removed the struggle areas that made the original so difficult to sit through. I feel like the removal of some of the game also really helped improve the experience, as I felt like the original dragged on for way too long. Xen in this game is also phenomenal. Comparing Xen in this game to Xen in the original is like comparing any other food in the world with food from England. Xen is the most miserable part of the original game, and in this game, it is honestly the best part. It was gorgeous and I thought it was a great length.- The sound effects in this are actually pleasant. The sound effects in the original almost made my ears bleed. The best example I can give for just how much better it is in this game is the voice lines of the military. In the original, I had a very difficult time really understanding what they were even saying. It was like I was exclusively hearing them through a dollar store walkie talkie even though they were right in front of me. This is completely fixed in this game, and I actually empathized a little bit with the military. It truly felt like I was killing actual people who were just doing what they were ordered to rather than killing random guys in suits. I heard them swear, I heard their emotions during battles, it is genuinely crazy how much better that alone made the experience. This doesn't just affect the military, but they were definitely the ones that benefited the most from not having old crunched audio.- I experienced significantly less glitches. It wasn't a perfect experience, especially when I was achievement hunting(hate the pizza box), but it was much smoother overall.- Black Mesa did a great job with integrating the style of tutorial that was in Half LIfe 2. The original Half LIfe never explains anything.- I was bugged by the amount of boards in the original, it was a nitpick. I truly don't know if the amount of boards was reduced, or if I just got so used to stupid boards that I stopped paying mind to them.That was everything that I wanted to mention as it directly counteracts things I listed as negatives for the original. But I also feel like mentioning just a few more things without attachment to my previous review.- This is thanks to the new sounds and better environments, but I actually got sucked into the story significantly more. I cannot describe in words just how many more emotions I felt throughout this game, even though it is just a remake. I felt actual horror and disgust in the first section, as the NPC improvements made them feel like real people. They weren't goofy, bitcrushed scientists dying comedic deaths, they were actual scientists stuck in a situation they would almost definitely perish from. I really took in just how horrific the situation would actually be to live through here. It felt much more powerful. As mentioned before, I actually empathize with the military. I think the choice they made about the members of the facility was stupid, but they do not seem like a purely evil force in this game. They are just trying to contain what they know could cause more harm, and many of the men you actually face were just ordered to do what they are doing, unaware of what they were getting themselves into. There are some military members that I was happy to kill, but that was based off of what they said(yet again, voice acting caused more emotions in general). Xen is the main benefactor of this rework. Xen feels charmingly alien-like this time and not annoyingly alien-like. The scenery is breathtaking and not just, floating rocks. The creatures feel so natural to the environment instead of just feeling like a strange crowd on a bunch of rocks. The part that 100% benefited the most was the portrayal of the Vortigaunts. It is so so much easier to understand that they are slaves. I was left confused in the original, but in this one it is blatantly obvious. You also get to see a lot more on their living conditions. I watched a Vortigaunt cry over one of his friends that was killed. Xen is just a powerful area to experience in this remake.- For a dislike, I will be frank, the achievements are ass. Beware other achievement hunters, you will have to drag  items through a majority of the game all the way to the end to 100% this game. I liked most of the achievements, they felt very creative, but there are the difficult few that really annoyed me.Thank you Crowbar Collective, for remaking a game that I wanted to enjoy so badly, but couldn't in its dated state. Black Mesa is how I got to feel what thousands of people got to feel before me with the original, with the masterfully crafted story given to us by Valve.

_childDocuments_.review: The definitive version of a timeless classic. Black Mesa breathes life into the parts of Half-Life which were originally lacking, while staying true to the look, feel, and fun of the original. I can't recommend it more.If you've never played Half-Life before, this is the version to buy. While this is technically a fan remake of the original, it doesn't feel like it in the slightest. If I had been told this was an original release from Valve, i would believe it. The devotion to recreating iconic moments in the game and updating them with modern graphics and design sensibilities is truly a wonder to behold, but it really shines in what it's changed. The jewel in it's crown is the total restructuring of the final act, Xen, which has been expanded and refined into a much better form. The original Xen was clunky, overly confusing, and extremely short. The new Xen makes up a third of the game's total length, with dozens of new areas amounting to three new chapters in the game's story. It also adds characterization and color to the alien world, making it feel like a place where people live and work rather than a strange video game level. My favorite location is the Vortigaunt Village. The final boss has been improved greatly as well, with new phases, attacks, and an entirely new combat strategy. It's also quite grandiose, compared to the wet fart that it was in the original.Complaints are few, and most of them can be laid at the feet of perhaps being a little too devoted to accuracy in some areas. For example, were the loading zones really necessary to recreate? Surely a little pre-loading wouldn't have gone amiss.So, like I said, this is the ultimate version of an already fantastic game. If you haven't played Half-Life before, or want to revisit it, play this version before all others.

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps it's because the original Half Life maps are still familiar to me, that even though the graphics are renewed with more details that for gameplay purposes they didn't age well. I get that the authors have to make them as faithful to the original as possible, but in light of new innovations made in Half Life 2 and other newer games, it just made it feel that the first half of the game in Black Mesa wasn't a very enjoyable experience.But the worst offender in the experience to me was the HECU grunt enemies. What's supposed to be one of the main enemies are just bad. Erratic movements by them felt very awful to deal with.What's worse for me is also the HECU's inhumanity regarding the things around them: they never talk about why they were ordered to kill every scientists, and even enjoy doing so. I get that this too is also keeping it faithful to the original Half Life, but that self-imposed limitation is what prevented it from being better e.g. exploring the potential layers of the grunts.Edit: it was pointed out there is one conversation regarding that, but I missed it.I guess we'll just have to have to wait for their rendition of Opposing Force for that. We'll see, if it's even gonna be made.With all that said, the game becomes much, much better once the creators broke free of those limitations of needing to follow too much of the original Half Life, and Xen is the proof of it. And oh boy the game is worth it merely just for Xen alone.New mechanics, new creatures or enemies, amazing soundtracks and graphics...Soundtrack wise... I didn't really like the ones in the Black Mesa facilities. I still much prefer the original's. But again, everything at Xen's is just so much better.Credits should also be given to the map designs that helped players navigate the map. I notice that paths where the players are supposed to go were given different colors or lighting from lamps, giving subtle hints. I appreciate small details like this which tells me that the devs put a lot of thoughts into making the game.Definitely try it just for the Xen's experience alone, and witness what a community of fans can do when they create something with heart.I also notice there are a few other reviews who gave a bad recommendation, being stopped during in Black Mesa and never to experience Xen. I implore you to get through it until Xen, or at least skip it with the chapter selection.

Xen is the obvious show-stopper in terms of environments with it's cosmic colorful pallet and beautiful space sky-boxes which look stunning.BM also delivers a high-quality iteration of HL's OST, with a noticeable bump in fidelity. _childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a game that I have been following ever since I got into Half-Life. I would check up on it whenever it released a trailer or a gameplay video, I played the original 2012 mod, and yes, I purchased it the day it got put into Steam Early Access. Looking back, I couldn't have imagined how long it would be until this thing reached its proper conclusion. That said, having just now finished the public beta with all the Xen chapters, I am very pleased to say that it was worth the wait. No memes, just the hard truth. Now, before I touch on the Xen chapters, it's only sensible that I touch on the chapters featured in the original mod and the early access build, that being the chapters taking place in Black Mesa. Crowbar Collective did an excellent job reinterpreting the setpieces of the original Half-Life, whilst still remaining faithful to the general layouts of each area. Some places haven't changed much since the original mod if my memory serves me well, but in spite of that, they hold up very well in spite of being at least eight years old. Now, if you're someone who has played the original Half-Life to death and aren't sure if it's worth laying down $20 for what appears to be simply a prettied-up version of the game, worry not. This game is in many ways a beast of its own entirely, especially with the Xen chapters taken into account which I'll be getting to shortly. For starters, the combat feels quite different from both Half-Life and Half-Life 2. This is by no means a bad thing, but if you go into this game with the lessons regarding combat you learned in those games (like I did), expect plenty of booboos. The enemies are ruthless and they pack a punch even on normal difficulty, so you'll have to act smart in order to get the upper-hand in situations. On top of that, many puzzles are totally revamped in order to take full advantage of the Source engine. They take heavy inspiration to the type of physics-based puzzles, found in Half-Life 2, but in spite of this they manage to find their own identity with each having an interesting solution. It is an experience quite unlike any Half-Life game, but still manages to feel like a proper Half-Life experience overall nonetheless. Now for what really spurred me to write this review. As some of you may know, Xen is now fully playable via the public beta in order to help squash bugs and polish up some spots. Having waited so long, I decided I would take my chances and try it now, and boy was I in for a treat. To put in plainly, Black Mesa's Xen chapters blew my expectations right out of the water. Crowbar Collective took the original Xen chapters, which were a bit underwhelming in the original, and cranked them all up to a hundred, effectively making Xen the highlight of the entire game rather than a tedious and clumsy rushjob. I cannot understate how breathtaking it all is. Each chapter is beautiful, engaging, and quite lengthy to boot! While I could get through Xen in the original in as little as an hour, Xen in Black Mesa is about the length of a Half-Life expansion or episode. Playing through it all finally put things into perspective; it made perfect sense why the Xen chapters took so long, and why the team was so secretive for the longest time. Overall, Black Mesa is the Half-Life experience I have been desperately craving, and I can't wait to pick this up again once Xen goes out of beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just the fact that I'm turning 20 next month and I'm just looking back at the years I spent goofing off in high school, but all of a sudden 2012 really does seem like it was just yesterday. I remember waiting ferverously at my laptop, staring down the timer that was ticking down to the release of the Initial mod edition of Black Mesa. I remember eating the sandwich I brought home from Sonic as I watched the gorgeous new and improved tram sequence, thinking back to the first time I ever played half life back in 2009. For the uninitiated, Half-Life is a legendary first person shooter developed by the industry novice Valve that took many of the cliches the burgeoning FPS genre and smashed them over it's knee, mostly with it's coherent, uninterupted narrative and realistic level design. Alot of the technique that went into Half-Life was later mimicked by many other studios and developers trying to grasp what made the new king of the FPS genre so great... It was also the first FPS game I had ever played as a young kid, I remember begging my mom to let me play it even though it was rated M.Black Mesa, however, was born out of a desire to improve upon the lackluster Half-Life Source, which was released by Valve shortly after the release of Half-Life 2. People were understandably underwhelmed by what was essentially a port of the game with no real updates to the gameplay other than some wonky looking lighting and ragdoll physics. Forunately for the rest of modder-dom, a group of developers got to work to bring the world of Black Mesa up to the graphical standards of Half-Life 2.Initially released in 2012 without the Xen levels, Black Mesa source really did bring the game into the modern era, accomplished by but not limited to, updating and adding character and weapon models, fleshing out animations and textures, giving us clearer voice work, improving and expanding the maps from Half-Life to make them even more believable than they already were, and also adding in it's own custom soundtrack. You can certainly tell from just watching the initial Tram sequence that the developers treated this as a passion project for the longest time.Graphics nonwithstanding, there were a few changes to the pacing of the game which do change up the pacing and balance from the initial half-life. For instance, you get the crowbar slightly later than you normally would, and you'll pick up a revolver in the room with the guard behind the gate where you'd normally find a shotgun. Even though this mostly works to the game's favor, it does have some questionable decisions. The sequence you play through before you get the crowbar consists of you scooping up flares and throwing them at zombies while you wait for your security guard buddy to very slowly kill them for you. You can tell it was made to show off the capabilites of the source engine, but it's a very annoying sequence to actually play through. Even though these experiences aren't frequent enough to make the mod a chore to play, they certainly do feel a degree less intuitive than the original half-life. Overall though, the current release of the mod really does make the combat feel more visceral and more satisfying, with the gunshots being suitably menacing and the overall feel of shooting does make the combat sequences of the game all the better. They absolutely nailed the firefights you'll get into with the marines and black ops, as well as the aliens still being fun to fight.That being said, I feel like the sound design is mixed in some places. The voice acting for the Guards and Scientists is cleaner and crisper than it was in the original, but I feel like the original Half life has more memorable quotes that still comes ahead over Black Mesa. The sound design for the Aliens and Zombies is for the most part great (especially for the vortigaunts!!!), but I feel like specifically the houndeyes feel much less menacing than the original counterparts. The HECU in the game sounds quite frankly horrible, you can kind of tell that they were taking a page from Opposing Force's friendly grunts, but the enemies having almost friendly sounding voices doesnt hold a candle to the menacing voice chatter of the HECU from the original games.  On the topic of the sound-track, Black Mesa has it's own OST. The ambience and mood is on point, and when the soundtrack wants to make Gordon's experiences feel all the more primal, it can with tracks like the one that plays during We've Got Hostiles. Joel Nielsen is a very competent composer, but there's mods for people like myself who prefer the original OST.The last topic that needs to be addressed is the game, despite having been in development for over a decade, is still unfinished. The Xen chapters have been being worked on for a very long time. Some people will say you should shy away from purchasing until it's finished, and while I think their anger is understandable, I don't think the absence of the weakest part of the game is too terribly detrimental. Normally, I'd end my review with a footnote explaining my views on the game I'm reviewing, but I feel like Black Mesa is a unique case, as it does very much improve upon the original in many ways, while also falling short of the original in others. I feel like before buying Black Mesa, you should consider whether or not to try the base game first.  If you've never played Half-Life 1, and have no interest in it's vast ammount of mods or expansions, I'd say pick up Black Mesa in a heart beat. If you've played Half-Life 1 but want one of the biggest nostalgia trips of your life, I'd pick BM up on sale. If you want a game with tons more content, I'd pick up Half-Life 1 and it's expansions as Half life 1 has some of the most legendary mods known to gaming. Overall though, Black Mesa is worthy of being compared to the original, and it's certainly worth your time if you do decide to pick it up.

Would definitely like to see this update treatment done for Half Life 2. It would be great if Valve could continue with more sequels for the series.

_childDocuments_.review: In light of the newest public beta, I am retracting my previous review, as the state of the game on Linux has improved dramatically. Of course the game itself is top notch. Respect to the developers for addressing platform issues.---Do NOT purchase if you're a Linux user. The native version is a cruel joke using the woefully outdated ToGL rendering the game unplayable due to severe graphical artifacts including dynamic lighting bugs that result in pitch black levels. When using Proton, the game springs a memory leak leading to an unavoidable crash within an hour of play (usually less). This happens even if you leave the game idling on the main menu - leave for 45 minutes and observe memory usage had gone up by over 1.5GB. This would not be an issue if it were a 64-bit application, but it's not. Linux support should not be advertised as the game is patently unplayable in its current state, unless you're willing to play in 30 minute instalments between crashes. Developers don't give a solitary ♥♥♥♥ about this platform.

_childDocuments_.review: Great product I enjoyed very much, graphics look amazing for using the Source Engine (10 years old) and the game play feels pretty good in my opinion. I think they've stayed pretty true to the original Half-Life while making worthwhile updates to the look and feel of the areas. I have only played the original Half-Life about two times but this felt like a pretty new and good experience to me. I definitely think it's worth playing for all the extra details.This being paid is not a problem what so ever as they have a free build on their website that they will keep updated along with this version. One of the reasons it is paid is so the developers get a Source Engine license which gains them access to parts of the engine they've never had and can add quite a number of features that simply can't be present in the free version as that version of the engine is more locked down. Be nice guys, 8+ years of work is worth 20$/€...

_childDocuments_.review: I think they created one of the best examples on how to make a good remake.When it comes to design, I have absolutely nothing to say against their work. I love the fact that they managed to re-create the same location's geometry but in a modern and realistic way. Walking down the corridors of Black Mesa really feels like walking on the Aperture's rival facility. If an original game had some weird locations that server no purpose, this fan-made remake manages to show us how it would actually look like in real life. Every single location has more meaning and depth to it. Memorable locations and interactions way more fun to explore, because most of these locations were expanded and filled with the activities that weren't there in the original game. And yes, Xen. Xen is nothing like an original Xen. They managed make push the limits of an old game engine to its maximum showing a quite impressive scenery in 2020. The first part of interloper was really fun and beautiful. Design 10/10Gameplay was unchanged, though some of the weaponry feel way more powerful and alive, obviously. Sometimes it got me feeling a little bit bored with the same types of enemies around the corner. Developers had no intentions of creating new enemies, which is absolutely ok. Maybe for a person who never played original HL lack of variety in gameplay and types of enemies could get really boring. Boss battles are way more fun to play. Gonarch is now an hour long actually fun and dynamic boss-battle. The Hihilanth is not as hard and fun as Gonarch, but it still feels fun fighting it. Gameplay 8/10I hoped they'd invited the G-Man impersonator for his role though.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and a modern alternative for people who haven't played the original Half-Life. BUT!Xen and Interloper are the most tedious and annoying levels I've ever seen in video games and they made the whole endgame one big miserable experience. I can understand that authors wanted to make those levels longer to show the lore in more depth than the original did but it could've been done with just 15-30 minutes of additional gameplay, not with 4 hours of endless jumping and connecting cables. Thumbs up for the rest of the game and dedication to create it, but the end ... that should not be there
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: I blew up a guy, then I found his eyeball on the ground. Fantastic!As of now, they're working on the 6 last maps for the beta release. I've run it through all the way to the portal to Xen, and I've had a blast! Literally as well, I've been blowing up people and freaks left and right. The attention to detail here is great, and as a fan of the original games I must say this one certainly nailed it as an HD-remake! And now I can finally understand everything those marines say as well, 'cause the sounds and several voices have been improved a lot. And the lighting - So friggin' amazing! Black Mesa is like a whole new world compared to the original game now. And let's not forget about the music, which is fantastic.Now I'm eagerly awaiting the release of the last 6 maps, which is coming very soon!Long story short: I love this, they've done the original game great justice and made an awesome recreation!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. Especially Xen part.Music and atmosphere are awesome.One major disadvantage are bugs and glitches.Sometimes Gordon do not run properly forward. But rather sideways.Sometimes he just get stuck in textures and can't move.Also, sometimes Gordon interacted with platforms like he was pushed away from it. Thus, platforming was pain, too. That is not hardness but just buggy controls.Buggy controls were the most annoying thing of all.Game also crashed few times.There was also bug with railcar. On sloped rails gordon moved to back of railcar.Final boss in pre-final phase was quite weird, too.He just got me and that's it. Seems like I won by some exhaustive search. Not by any skills. That's not satisfactory.In general I'd recommend it if you are a fan of HL.

_childDocuments_.review: you already know I'm obsessed with itback with another relistening of MY GOD ONE OF THE BEST PIECES OF VIDEOGAME OST I EVER HEARDLiterally can't get over how the title "Ascension" is the most fitting title I have ever seen for a track that opens many amount of interpretations BEYOND the literal context of the section where it plays.You can make a lot of figurative interpretations that fits the grandiose/epic scale of this track for being the moment of where Gordon Freeman ascends to some sort of status that no one thought would be possible. This is why personally in my mind, this even surpasses some tracks of some other videogame osts I like such as Halo, and Ace Combat. Wait was I sup-, OH RIGHT, uh.... The game itself As someone who got drawn into Half-Life extremely late, I am just simply impressed. For a fan remake, it's undoubtedly a masterpiece. With me having the all of the Half-Life 1 levels and sections memorized in my brain, it was fun going through the campaign and seeing how those sections are adapted to modern visual fidelity. From my judgment, I'll say it stayed faithful to the original material.At least from the Earthbound sectionsWhen I reached Xen, I wasn't expecting it to literally be pretty much reimagined on a big scale. Different level design, beautiful environments, and it is even longer, I was not expecting to be like 2-3 hours longer in time for me to get through compared to the OG Xen levels. The entirety of Xen and Gonarch's Lair I find really enjoyable. Interloper was at its peak at the starting sections and the ending section, but the middle section is where I can agree on how much of a slogfest feeling it is. The repetitiveness of the plug puzzles really got me.The final boss, while it still can be beaten in a few minutes, the visuals on top of the bullet hell nature feeling I get from it of really sells me on the amount of times I repeated in my mind that Xen is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane.To sum it up, I love this game, so much that I just had to do two more playthroughs to gather the achievements.Screw that pizza box for somehow getting me killed several times.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably one of the best remakes ever and its certainly the best fan remake! I love the new/remastered music this game brought to the classic Half life experience, all the new voice acting etcXen! After playing in Xen I can see why it took them a few years to release the Xen chapters, they did the rare thing of taking their time rather than just publish now and fix later. I'd buy it again at full price and its more than worth it and if you see it in sale, theres no question on getting it!
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Altho its a fan remake Black Mesa does everything that original Half Life did but better imo. Sure there are some changes that people will debate but graphics, atmosphere, sound (shout out to that one guy who did voices for all male scientists, that was cheesy AF but in a good way) and everything else was brought up to modern standards. Combat feels like HL2 (its Source duh) and if that's good or not... I dont know tbh, I personally always liked it and the team made a good decision to keep this feel in tact. Buy this game, support devs, I cant wait for final release of Xen!--EDIT--Xen was fantastic, stunning, maybe a bit unstable when I played it. Factory section is kinda annoying, but its really better Xen than original one. I CAN ACTUALLY BELIEVE ALIENS ARE ABLE TO LIVE THERE! Felt like an explorer, adventurer.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: The Half-Life experience multiplied by three, and it feels like too much. I'm not used to Half-Life games having this much action, intense music, puzzles, or extended boss fights. It was an exciting and interesting way to replay an old game and I'm glad I played it, even though I don't love it as much as the other Half-Life games.This is not a direct upgrade from the original Half-Life and you should pick the version that suits your play-style. If you want something slow, steady, and simple, go with the original. If you want something fast paced, action packed, and more complex, go with this.8/10, great game, but not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Entire essays could be written about the massive achievement Black Mesa is, and how it improves over the source material even in parts once thought could not be improved upon, all while also making sure to proudly wear its own identity along the way.Black Mesa is much more than a full remake of Half-Life - is a new way of experiencing that same fascination gamers might have felt back in '98 (I was born in '94, so obviously I can't tell by my own experience) but backed by 20 years of insight on what worked, what did not, and how it could be made to retroactively fit better with the overarching bigger-than-life universe that is Half-Life's.If you need one word to wrap up all of this blabber, it well could be:Black Mesa is a .
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game that go above and beyond what a remake/remaster usually is. Not only does it beautify the already genius Half Life 1 with its incredible level design, gameplay variety and near perfect rythm but then it adds a whole new game on top of it. Because a whole new game is what Xen feels like, it's multiple hours long and nearly indistinguishable from Valve's own work, if I had been told that it was an addon made by Valve I would have believed it. The new areas are gorgeous and interesting, enemies and bosses have been reworked and made better (that Gonarch level is just perfect) and it has the best OST pieces of the entire game.It's honestly incredible what the Crowbar Collective has achieved here and it really feels like a love letter to the original game in all the best ways possible. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Black Mesa

_childDocuments_.review: Black Mesa is a re-envisioning of Valve Software's seminal game Half-Life. You will re-visit the inaugural role of Gordon Freeman and his memorable journey through the Black Mesa Research Facility. Expect detailed environments to explore, a huge cast of characters and experimental weaponry. All-new music, voice acting, choreography and added dialogue give way to a more expansive and immersive experience than ever before. [Valve]

name: MythForce
detailed_description: Inspired by beloved Saturday morning cartoons, MythForce unites swords & sorcery with gripping 1st-person combat in a new roguelike adventure. Brave the dungeon alone or join forces with friends to take on an ever-changing Castle of Evil! Become a cartoon hero in a Saturday morning cartoon fantasy world. Scratch that nostalgic itch with wholesome fun that's easy to pick up and play (but tough to master). In true roguelike fashion, each time you’re defeated, you’ll have to start over at the beginning — but every playthrough makes you a little stronger. Level up as you explore the dungeon, uncovering magical artifacts and upgrades to make you say “I HAVE THE POWER!” Wield legendary weapons and powerful magic to smite hordes of enemies in an immersive fantasy dungeon-crawl through a colorful cartoon castle. Fresh adventures await with each new attempt to storm the keep! Explore a replayable dungeon with treasure, traps, and terrors lurking around every corner. Brave the dungeon alone or join forces in co-op mode for up to 4 players. Choose your team wisely — each hero brings unique skills to the fight! Meet the Heroes of MythForce : Victoria the valiant Knight joins forces with Rico the charming Rogue, Maggie the wise Mage, and Hawkins the deadly Hunter. Together, they form the legendary team known as… MythForce! These courageous champions are all that stand between Eldryth and the tyranny of the vampire lord, Deadalus. Will our heroes prevail against the many malevolent minions, tricks, and traps in his ever-changing dungeon?

short_description: HARDER, BETTER, FASTER, STORY UPDATE NOW LIVE! Patch 1.0.5 introduces a new combat encounter system, new enemies types, faster gameplay, radical new cutscenes & much more! Stay tuned for 1.0.6!

_childDocuments_.review: Man is this game not getting enough love, and it's a shame. Admittedly, when this initially launched I didn't like it. Combat was slow and clunky while there didn't seem to be much incentive to continue playing. I ended up refunding as a result. Fast forward to April 2024, a massive patch was released. You can view the patch notes (Update 1.0.5.0 Patch NotesThe Harder, Better, Faster, Story Update) to see all that was covered, but the mention of story content and speed fixes was enough to draw me back in. I picked this up with a friend, and we're not too far into the game just yet, but it's miles better than it was at launch. Unfortunately, this didn't launch in the state it's currently in, and reviews prior to April 4 2024 are still bubbling to the top, doing this a disservice. Had the game launched in the current state, it'd likely have received much more positive feedback and attention. The developers deserve a HUGE shout out for turning this back around. The animation style and gameplay are great if you enjoy cooperative rogue-likes. Characters play differently and offer multiple weapon sets to choose from. Abilities, Perks, and Equipment are all upgradable, giving the sense of progression as well as variety in how each player builds their characters up. This is like playing the cartoons I grew up on, and that's been wonderful. Co-Op is online and supports up to 3 players.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of the prevalent negative feedback regarding game mechanics, bugs, and clunky controls, I approached MythForce with unwavering optimism. I'm pleased to report that it exceeded my expectations.Regarding Bugs:I did encounter occasional setbacks, such as getting stuck on the floor with skeletons descending upon me from elevated positions. There were instances when my primary attack button didn't respond unless I initiated special powers to "unstick" my attacks.While all games have their share of bugs, issues tend to be resolved over time. Admittedly, investing in a game with known bugs isn't an ideal gameplay experience. However, I haven't encountered any game-breaking bugs so far—fingers crossed for continued smooth gameplay.XP Leveling:The game's approach to XP leveling might deter some players since in-level XP doesn't persist. Although you progress through stages and episodes, your level doesn't carry over when revisiting earlier episodes. Yet, the game doesn't solely rely on in-level levels or XP. Strength is gained by collecting glyphs, gems, and gold, creating a prolonged and challenging grind.You advance through Armory/Sun Disc Tiers, acquiring weapons and enhancing stats with gems. The learning curve may initially suggest a straightforward Hack/Slash style, but it requires subtle strategy, especially when playing solo on higher difficulties. Environmental utilization and precise timing become crucial.Nostalgia:The game boasts beautiful graphics, fluid animations, and seamlessly integrated mechanics. Co-op mode adds a humorous touch to the experience, delivering on the promised Saturday Morning Cartoon vibe. Similar to classic 80s/90s games, restarting from the beginning upon death can be frustrating, but understanding the mechanics improves with progression.Replayability and Final Thoughts:Every playthrough or replay offers a unique experience as each stage is randomly generated. The increasing difficulty requires extensive grinding to prove your worth. In my first day of play, I dedicated a solid 10 hours to the game. Despite its initial toughness, the grind proves immensely fulfilling, with each hour spent feeling worthwhile. The absence of a paywall for cosmetics is a definite positive. Whether you team up with friends for added fun or embark on a solo grind to showcase your prowess, MythForce offers a compelling and rewarding gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: MythForce

_childDocuments_.review: I like this 80s cartoon Joel Haver fever game, but it's got issues. Issues that ultimately prevent me from recommending the game as of its current state.Multiplayer suffers a bulk of the issues. The game is peer-to-peer, but this game’s P2P is unstable all the time. I play other P2P games with my friends and those games are nowhere near this game’s instability. Perk/Smith shrines bug out for non-host players, mobs stutter about making range attacks difficult to lead and land, you’re never sure how close a mob actually is before it's too late to evade, the lobby can just suddenly break down and you can only invite half of your group back for whatever reason. The roguelike aspect of the game is a bit too grindy. After every run you get these glyphs that can be used to upgrade your town’s facilities. Armory (makes your starter gear stronger), constellation (allows you to slot gems and increase your base stats), emporium (allows you to find higher tier versions of trinkets), and conclave (allows you the ability to acquire a higher tier version of perks.) The amount of glyphs you get on the available difficulty is chump change after that first upgrade. My point being; expect to only get tier 2 of glass cannon for the longest eternity from biome 1 to 3 and still waiting in ng+. Melee combat feels uncomfortable, weak, and risky . Range is just the best of all worlds, even with the latency issue. When trying to switch to your off-hand or vice versa the game will eat the input, and it does this often. There are not enough variant tile sets per biome. You could easily see the same long center staircase leading into a big rectangle room four times in the same 40 minute run. The mob variety basically comes to an end at biome 2 of 3. The bosses of each biome are set, meaning there is only one. Dollar tree He-man monster, Hextar the necromage, and Deadaless the vampire BBEG. That is it. I enjoy parts of the game but I just cannot recommend it in its current state. I might play a little more with my friends if they wish to dive back into this lumpy pool. I know some of you won't understand and would want to reply with “Well if you thought it was d**s*** why are you still playing, huh? HAHA GOTTEM!” I never said it was any type of poop, and the point of a review is; to help others make a better buying decision, to share my experiences, and to let the developer/publisher know how I as a paying customer of their product feel.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is honestly close to good, but there are numerous issues, some would be easy to address, others would require some time from devs. Nothing that is truly requiring a full rework from the ground up, but tiny things that gnaw away at the enjoyment of the game. Off the top of my head:Perk/Enchant balance is all over the place. Perks vary from incredibly helpful to completely useless or detrimental to a surprising degree. Defensive perks are incredibly weak compared to the damage that enemies do, and offensive perks scale so quickly that they outpace enemy health hilariously fast.Hit reg: The only things that hit you in this game are because of their absurdly misrepresented hitboxes, and Caster mobs that teleport on top of you and throw a huge AoE suddenly. This wouldn't be so frustrating if these attacks didn't empty 60% of your health bar in one hit, but as I mentioned earlier, building defensively in this game is simply too weak compared to enemy damage.Missions: Why is the method for unlocking the next difficulty of a mission to beat it on the lower difficulty, instead of beating the previous level on the given difficulty? Why do perks/enchants scale so high in level when the chapters end so quickly that you have no time to level them up? Why are perks/enchants not weighted towards helping upgrade ones you already have instead of offering every perk at equal %?Voicelines: Love the voice acting, hate hearing a character point out the exit door 3 times in 5 seconds. The game is riddled with tiny design choices that just make you wonder why? The game is like... 90% playable, but that last 10% really detracts from how much fun this game COULD be if it was really cared about. You can tell there is a lot of love that went into this game, but it feels like when it came time to clean it up and ship it out, someone else came in and said there wasn't time to do any of that.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually kinda enjoyable for the dozen or so hours (the playtime info is incorrect due to a bug I'll mention below) I have played WHEN it actually worked, but I can't recommend it due to many nasty bugs and the overall unpolished state it is currently in.Note that I mainly played solo, co-op gameplay is more fun but it's hard to complete a co-op session due to constant network disconnects.: Nice art-style, great cheesy 80's cartoon feel, and the combat is mostly fun, especially if you get to play co-op with friends.: While the characters and objects have nice cartoon-ish look, the level map structures have some cheaper 3D-ish look, so the whole thing doesn't really have much cartoon feel during the gameplay itself (I think maybe it will feel more cartoon if there can be a third person perspective mode? since the characters look clearly more cartoon-ish). Actually the levels feel unpolished in general, there are invisible map barriers where arrows just stuck in mid-air, steps leading to straight stone walls (not collapsed stones), and minor glitches where rooms are filled with some kind of dirt pile but you can "clip through" and open chests sitting "inside" the dirt pile. Also your character can "clip through" the level transition barrier "halfway" and shoot enemies with ranged attack without entering the level.Also it's hard to call the levels procedural generated, as there are maybe half a dozen or so level maps for each chapter with mostly the same loot/object and enemy placements, so each level is randomly chosen as one of those available maps with very limited randomization of shrines and entry/exit points. Considering each run has more than 15 levels, it's inevitable to encounter quite some level map repetition in a run.And the random skills/perks and items you can picked up in a run can feel quite unbalanced at times, a lot are clearly useless while a few are extremely powerful. The traps and stuff are also more annoying than fun most of the time. Overall level design and skill/perk/item systems feel unpolished.: somehow the game requires Epic Games client to play, which in itself is nothing unbearable for me (but it may drive off some others), however I believe this Epic Games client may be tied to some of the worse bugs the game currently has. First, at times the game status keeps showing "running" after exiting, that's why I have 50+ hours playtime shown here, sometimes I played for an hour and exited, and the game time just kept adding for hours as it's still "running" for steam, and I cannot start another game session without a system restart as it's never really exited. I found out that force killing some background Epic Games processes in Windows Task Manager can end the "running" status, but not sure if it would have some side-effects for new game sessions or not.The network connection is extremely unstable, not sure if it has something to do with the Epic Games client or not, but it keeps disconnecting and going "play offline" at times. Also it seems it will keep switching between "offline" and "online" mode automatically, which leads to another bug: when you are picking a perk/skill and getting a "network disconnected" message, it means you have automatically picked the "dismiss" option, AND it will automatically pick the "dismiss" option for the ENTIRE RUN afterwards. That means once you get a "network disconnected" while picking a skill/perk, you cannot get any new skills/perks/ability upgrades from shrines or shops, and when you try to buy a skill/perk/ability upgrade from a shop, you spend the gold but get nothing! I think maybe it'd be better to have a "permanent" offline mode option where there would be no more "network disconnected" popup, currently even when you chose to "play offline" it will keep switching online/offline in the background somehow, with the untimely popups ruining the run.And there are complete control freeze at times, which is happening a lot since I'm in chapter 2, so much so that I have not been able to finish episode 5 due to this nasty bug, as some levels into the run all controls would be suddenly lost at some random point, the character would stand still with animations still playing, but no keyboard or controller input would work, so the game still plays on with the character standing still, and there's no way to proceed or even exit the game except a force kill. : this is about parts/designs of the game that's neither good nor bad, but just feel strange. first the character level progression is completely fixed, meaning you will be at a certain fixed character level at a certain map in a certain episode. So you will start episode 1 at level 1, episode 2 at level 4, episode 3 at level 7, and then back to level 1 at episode 4 (as you are entering a new chapter). It's okay for a roguelite game, but still strange.And the game shares the same resource (gold) for shopping items in the run and upgrading the character outside the run, so you spend less in a run, you get more points to upgrade for future runs. This is kinda strange as it makes less incentive to spend gold in a run (at least before maxing out character upgrades), thus leading to a potentially less varied and less fun game run. Other roguelite games I have played mostly have different resources for in-run purchases and out-run upgrades, so you don't have your hands tied when purchasing items/upgrades during a run.Lastly the constellation system, not sure if it's because I'm still not grasping the whole system or not, but since it's "constellation" where there are "lines" connecting the "slots", I kinda expected when you place certain same-type or different-type gems in "connected" slots, there would be some extra effects, but so far it seems there no such effects? Which makes the whole "constellation" thing feel strange as it just functions the same as separate gem slots with a bundle of lines not having any meaning?, I think this is a nice and fun game, and I'd recommend it despite its unpolished state and some weirdness in its designs, but right now given the nasty bugs (which may or may not be related to the required Epic Games services running in the background), I cannot recommend this game until the devs can get all those game-stopper bugs fixed up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love randomized dungeons and rogue-likes, and while I don't recommend Mythforce, I did have some fun with my time with it. The game reveals it's shallow nature very early on, but if there was more content and randomization, this could be a game I'd recommend.Let me tell you about a game called MYTHFORCE(!!!):(A) There's hardly any randomization to the "randomly generated dungeons" (which are really just repeating rooms in a random set) -In any particular dungeon you encounter the same 3 or 4 rooms which loop repeatedly. About 9 stages are broken into 3 areas. There are 3 stages in each of these areas that are essentially exactly the same, with just 3 or 4 rooms repeating.(B) Disappointingly few options regarding the Rogue-like aspects of the game. By the time you've played a couple of hours you will have found almost every perk/ability/and aspect available. Some are essential to a painless run, and therefore you quite quickly find your "cookie cutter" build. There's no variation and loot drops are unrewarding.(C) Combat is dull and simple, each character has a light/heavy attack, a block, and 3 abilities. The abilities never change, not even when you change gear. I could have a bow and a 2 handed sword, but my abilities are still shield bash, shield throw, and a atk power+ roar. Very shallow.(D) And lastly, this game is REALLY cheesy, and not in a good way. It tries to emulate an 80's cartoon, but it's more a mockery with none of the charm. You'll find yourself wanting to skip every cutscene and line of dialogue.Now, just say it aloud in your head, "Mythforce!"

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastically well designed game, especially with the latest patches. Most reviews complaining about this game are of the older version - do not regard. Character and playstyle customization is fantastic, with weapon loadout swaps akin to Vermintide 2. Every character can use some form of melee and ranged, with most also being able to wield magic so your team isn't locked to a playstyle per character.There's only more content to be added and from the updates it's clear the devs are listening. _childDocuments_.review: My interest was piqued just like everyone else's: the look and feel, and the promise of being able to play in a world just like the Dungeons and Dragons TV cartoon I loved as a kid.Unfortunately, this game turned out to be mostly look and feel covering up a mediocre, ho-hum game. It's not terrible by any means, but after during run #2 I wondered, "is this it? Is it just a glorified corridor hack n slash where I fight various skeletons over and over?" The skeletons hit you with swords from way, way farther away than their swords appear to swing, changing weapons in game is clunky, the action is repetitive even 15 minutes into the game.By run #3 is wanted to quit even when I was doing ok. I felt, if I got to keep my level progress to run #4 then I'd keep the game. Nope, you have to start all the way over at level 1 each time. I have uninstalled the game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those "I wish there was a neutral option" reviews.As a roguelike, this fails hard. - There's no between-character progression other than stages and overworld levels. If you don't like your character after farming for 10 hours, guess you have to farm another 10 hours for gems.- There's no between-stage progression. You start fresh every time, which makes sense because (next)- Balance is ALL OVER THE PLACE, as many others have mentioned.- It's nearly impossible to solo on harder difficulties, especially with curses like "if you get hit, lose 10 max hp". Like, WHAT?- The overarching progression is... not fun? 1. You give items a higher drop chance. 2. You slot gems, which you have to ceaselessly farm (here you have to choose between damage and defenses). 3. You level max perk totals, but you can't delevel them so you can't actually make a consistent build. 4. You upgrade weapons, for incrementally doubling damage.- If you decide you like a weapon and don't want to use/upgrade the other one, well then you're definitely going to get a bunch of weapon upgrades for the one you're not using! Hah!- Gold is shared within the map and is tied to overworld progress. If you decide you actually want to use the shop, you lose out on progression. As a multiplayer game, it succeeds somewhat. Though, there are caveats. - You can give build-specific items to your friends. But, if any ability upgrades drop, it's first come first serve. Chances are you won't even *see* them. - If one member is bugged, the run is over. "You must gather your party before venturing forth!"- Quickplay is fun sometimes, awful at other times. It commonly places you in matches that are nearly over. Most of the time, you don't get any perks. You don't get any starting items. Sometimes it'll place you in a match where the host is AFK, and you CAN NOT join any other games (it'll just keep sending you to that one). Additionally, you'll be placed in a game that is NOT the difficulty you selected.There are a lot of bugs and QOL problems.- Hitting skeletons with a bow is damn near impossible to the point that playing the archer is inadvisable.- There are holes you can fall down and never come back from. You're not dead, but the run is over for everyone in the party.- Some abilities are 'slippery' in that you might miss if you're slightly off of the hitbox even if your weapon actually hits them.- General bugs. Sometimes you might use your Mythforce ability and not be able to attack. Other times, there are floating wall textures.- Enemies will occasionally spawn right on top of you.- Enemies will get locked behind the black spawning walls (tldr: bad level design) where they can hit you but you can't hit them.As a massive fan of their BG2 port, I'm kind of disappointed by Beamdog's take on roguelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: More of a neutral review, but given the full price, it isn't worth that.The theme and art style are executed very well - but that's about it..I beat the first 2 levels, so I'm not sure if I explored all the systems or not fully but there's not much making me want to yet..The combat feels unresponsive, you'll hit things and there's almost no feedback (until toward the end of a run when you're decked out, but..)Levels are over just as you feel you're getting somewhere, I almost feel like they should go for something more like gunfire reborn.And then there just doesn't feel like there's much of anything.. Rooms in a level repeat a lot, you'll see the same few upgrades and items and each character's 4 abilities are very basic and can't be customised/upgraded much at all.I'd understand if this was early access, but it isn't.I'm aware the dev's did update the combat once already (I shudder to think how bad it was before) so I'll keep an eye out for further updates but doubt I'll touch this again until then.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the style and graphics! Everything else is... well to put it nicely, it needs more time.First problem, epic service dependency, I do not want to launch a game via one platform, only for it to open another platform and launch it from there, what's next in the future? A nest of platforms just to run a video game?Second, after finally able to get in the game from the long initialization of epic service, after starting a quickplay game the tutorial were just dumped to me explaining everything at once in the form of GUI highlights, in silence, that tells me that this game does not have a proper tutorial, which means, its not finished.Third, after I dismissed all of the tutorial slides, I was immediately teamed up with another player and immediately skeletons just appeared and started attacking us, we killed them and more appear, we killed them and more appear, we killed them and... nothing happened? We were wondering around until we found what seem to be a way forward, then skeletons appeared and we killed them, skeletons appeared and you would not guess what happens next! Rinse and repeat for pretty much the whole game.Only momentary excitement I felt was during the 1 and only mini-boss fight in that mission against the mushroom mage, and even then the tactic between me and the other player was to just gang up on it and spam attack until it's dead. Afterwards, rinse and repeat.Finally we made it to the last room, there was a dialogue with the antagonist, OK cool let's do this, we thought, nope the guy ran away and leaves his minions to deal with us which we just need to keep killing them for.. 2 minutes straight I think? Which then we opened up the big chest at the end and.. we don't know we just get stuff from it, pulled the lever and the level just ended.This game just feels unfinished, at certain times I can tell that it has the potential to be fun and engaging especially seeing the potential to mix and match certain perks and upgrades, maybe later on it's more fun going against tougher and smarter enemies that just doesn't waddle to you slowly and swings their weapon at you slowly and gets staggered on every strike. I'll follow the development of the game, still hopeful that this game could become a good game later on, just not at this moment.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I was expecting a Saturday morning cartoon type of game and this is exactly what I got.Imagine the aesthetics and graphics of cartoon shows like Masters of the Universe and Thundercats, mixed with the beautiful animations of Dragon's Lair with actual first person gameplay.There is a story, accompanied with beautiful cutscenes and voice-overs, which is exactly what you would expect if you grew up watching these shows.The gameplay loop is quite addictive and the soundtrack never gets old. The first person movement is quite realistic and fun, at least when you play a melee character and swing a greatsword up, down, left and right obliterating everything.One minor complaint is that there should be better audio feedback when you block or parry with your shield or sword.It needs more crunchy metal clashing sound effects.It's like playing a game while living in the Stranger Things universe.For Steamdeck players: Set the FPS to 30 in the game's options menu, otherwise the video cutscenes will not be synchronized with the audio.Please add more playable characters.I believe Dirk the Daring should join Mythforce.This game is a love letter to everyone who grew up watching Saturday morning cartoons in the 80s and 90s.You can easily have at least 20 hours of fun, even if you just play solo. Totally recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: (Revised after patch 1.0.3.0.) Still 2/10 - Do not buy. Still no matchmaking: Online is still unplayable if you're not host, and clicking 'Quick Play' still puts you in a random quest. An "improvement" to Multiplayer added the ability to chose a difficultly when clicking Quick Play, so now you can chose a random Easy, Normal or Hard game and suffer 900 ping, or chose Mythical I, II, III, and find no games at all. Upgrades are still MASSIVELY overpriced: 5 weapons, 23 Perks, 30 Trinkets and 18 Constellation slots all with 4 tiers to upgrade, plus 1 million gold worth of skins and voice lines, etc. To obtain 1 million Gold, it takes hours and hours of grinding, and maxing your Constellation by converting Rare Shards would cost over 50M Gold. Do the math.After 40+ hours of grinding I am barely half way to "maxing" 1 of the 4 character's. Yet you can see everything the game has to offer and complete the whole story in just a few. All costs need to be reduced by 75% - 80%. All difficulties should unlock after completing the story on any difficulty. Shards and Gold should be shared between characters.The game NEEDS a lobby where we can search for games that are available, see Ping, Quest, difficulty and characters in game.I genuinely tried to like this game, but I still cannot.

_childDocuments_.review: MYTH FORCE! MYTH FORCE!The action is snappy, and quick with fun layers of build variety as you get perks. Each Hero feels unique while maintaining a thread. Get this on a sale. While a really fun and good game, 30$ isn't that much. It still isn't worth the price. I got it on sale for 15$ and do not regret it. I have two criticisms to give.1 - not enough, we need more episodes, one reason the game isn't worth 30$.2 - it wants to be a rogue lite/like, and wants to be a looter, but doesn't do either well. Do I even need to explain this?Now, as I went through the reviews here on steam, I assumed that a bunch if kids tried this game and failed.If we go through main complaints:1. Uses Epic Games - well...no. It only uses Epic Online Services (EOS), not the launcher. You can hate Epic Games Launcher for whatever reason, but I see no issue with using EOS. 2. ThE pRoGrEsS iS nOt sAveD afTeR eAcH rUn - do you even know what a roguelite is? You do some runs by using everything you can get during the run just to get to the finishing line. _childDocuments_.review: As someone have said already: I wanted to like this game, but I just can't.The core idea behind the game is good - a co-op adventure, made to feel like it's just an another episode of the 80's cartoon show. Visuals are great and it does indeed look like an 80's cartoon. NGL - that distinct look was exactly the thing that sold this game to me.Unfortunately, behind a cute picture hides a "not so cute" gameplay. At the 2 hour mark I already knew that the game wasn't good and I was deliberating if I should refund it or not. In the end I've decided to give it a bit more time and explore it more thoroughly and 42 hours later I think that I should have refunded it back than after all. Now I will explain the game's problems, so that you can avoid my mistake.1. Playerbase and connectivity issues. This game was designed as a co-op game first and foremost. But unless you have a few friends from the same town willing to play the game together with you - you better forget about the "co-op" part alltogether. First - the playerbase is low and you will be quite lucky if the game matches you with someone else at all. Second - even if it does, there are no dedicated servers, the game is hosted on a player's PC and the netcode is terribad. Every, EVERY SINGLE ♥♥♥♥ TIME that I was connected to someone else, or someone else was connected to me - the ping suddenly decided that using Mars as a reroute point is an excellent idea. And I'm not talking about a 0,3 second delay that is enough to drive crazy most modern gamers. The games goes a full on unresponsive mode with teleporting mobs, 5-10 second delays, invulnerability issues and so on and so forth. Every single ♥♥♥♥♥ time. It's literally unplayable. After trying for about 20 times at different time with different people - I've just gave up on the "co-op" idea and simply played solo. And just one more thing - there is no host browser window. You can't choose your region or a game's map that you want to play. Thre is only a "join a game" button and the will of the RNGesus.2. Basic gameplay. Many players complain that the game is too slow and easy. And indeed beating the maps on the Normal/Hard difficulty is not too hard at all. Mobs are slow, they don't hit too hard and are generally easy to beat. The real game starts at the Mythic 1-2-3 levels. But the thing is - most players will never even see them. There are 9 maps in total and every 3rd one has a major (episode) boss and the steam stats say that the first boss was beaten by 31% of players, second by 13% and the last one only by 8%. Is it because they are progressively harder? Not at all - it is because players loose interest in the game that fast, thinking that there is no point in playing it if it's this slow and easy. But the thing is that going from hard to mythic bumps the difficulty by A LOT. Monsters suddenly 2-shot you, they become stronger and their number increases, you need to pray for the good DPS perks and in general be constantly on alert. This is an entirely different game. Personally I think that the Mythic difficulty should have been unlocked right from the start, instead of requiring beating the hard difficulty first - just to show that the game could be a lot more brutal before ppl decide that it's too easy and lose interest in it.3. Maps and animations. This is a "roguelite" type of a game where levels "change" each run. The thing is - there are simply not enough assets to make levels feel any different. Every single run feels absolutely the same. It gets dull very, VERY quickly. Also the game lacks "funny distractions" like some silly critters running around, moving mechanisms, mysterious spirits floating around, etc, etc. For a good roguelite this is a must to take off players eyes away from the repeating assets. If you constantly bump into the same walls, stairs and 2 coffin models all the time - you get tired of it quick. Another issue that breaks the immersion - poor animations. Some of them are ok, skills are mostly well done, but others... For example there are plenty of chests in game. They literally have 2 frames on em - "closed chest" and "open chest" there is no "opening" animation it just unlocks instantly in 1 frame. When you attack jars with melee weapon, weapon just stops for a second and then jumps to the next frame. It doesn't feel smooth at all. Some people might defend this by saying "it's mimicing an 80's animation style with abrupt cuts" but this is no 80's animation it's 2020's game and to enjoy it players want smooth animations that flow well.4. Perks, progression, grind.  Every single one defencive perk (aside from vampirism or health restoration) is utterly useless. Especially if you play solo. If you stack up all the defencive perks they will barely reduce the incoming damage, but with inadequate offencive capabilities mobs will steamroll you easy AF. On the other hand if you manage to stack only the best damage-related perks you can critshot even a mythic-level boss with a few good hits and oneshot most other mobs. This is a poor balancing. Next is the progression issue - whatever character you pick up in the beginning - you better stick with it,  because the only thing that transfers between characters - it's the castle (shops) upgrades. But gold and constellation crystals - are separate. And you will need A TON of gold to max up even a single weapon. And without a maxed weapon good luck trying to beat mythic-lvls (not entirely impossible, but way harder than it should be). Most people will drop the game waaaay before they get even a single weapon to the max lvl. Default gold drop amount should definitely be increased by at least x1,5-2 and both gold and crystals should be an account-based asset, not a character-locked.5. Hitboxes. They are one more issue that makes me enraged. I've lost count how many time did my character got hit and died by a monster swinging a sword like 5 meter away from me. Seriously, lizardmen swings at empty air not even close to your character and boom - you take damage from it. Fkk this. Also this works the other way around too, especially with arrows - many times when you shoot right at the enemy - the arrow just go through it without inflicting any damage. Especially if it's a sceleton.6. This may be my personal issue - but WTF are those lightning acolytes, devs? The most brutal, unforgiving and cheating enemy of all. They AOE hit waay out of the hit zone (there is no such issue with fire or cold acolytes, only lightning), their direct lightning strikes are instant, unavoidable and hit harder than any other enemy or attack in the whole game. On mythic 2-3 it gets so bad, that i really afraid of them more than any boss, and instantly dump all CD's on 'em if i see one. Don't tell me this BS is by design >_>So all in all - decent idea, that i would love to support, but poor execution with disfunctional co-op, poor balance, excessive grind, boring level layout, technical hiccups and many other things that may not be critical on their own, but together they snowball into one unpleasant mass - all this make this game an expirience, that i would recommend to avoid.PS: I think that there is a chance to save this game, but I don't think that the devs are brave enough to take the required drastic measures to actually do that. The game needs to be closed for approx 1,5-2 years and in that time a total rebalance of the gameplay and progression should be done, levels impruved and made fancier, dedicated region-based servers for co-op implemented, etc. But it's a lot of work, that require time and money and with the amount of interest (or to be precise with the complete lack of it) that gamers gave the Mythforce... I think that this game is on a straight path to mists of oblivion atm, so no one will actually try to resque it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from fast paced games such as Roboquest or Gunfire Reborn, then you need to manage your expectations with this one.First of all, this game is clearly meant to be enjoyed with atleast 1 other person when playing.
