You will run into situations, depending on which character you have chosen, where you will need to revise how you play and how you use the different mechanics of the game to tackle this obstacle.Outside of a few bugs and (for some reason) near invulnerable enemies, this game is a treat for the eyes and mind with the right group of friends. _childDocuments_.review: Overall: gorgeous visual style with a game that needs to be thoroughly reworked. I bought it once and returned it, but promised friends I would try it with them. At first glance, the visuals promise a colorful, exciting cartoon adventure but the experience is boring and bland.Stamina: the game would be better if the stamina mechanic were completely removed. All these comments are true at launch, and after their 20% stamina buff. The game forces you to play at a slower pace, making action a tedious wait. I've never been so bored in a battle. The only real way to play is nursing your stamina and kiting enemies if you are a melee hero. If you run out of stamina you can't run, fight, block, etc. so if you aren't watching your stamina then prepare for a self-induced stun-lock of exhaustion. At higher difficulties, exhaustion is a death sentence. The way stamina is treated would be bad enough as is, but if one weighs the stamina economy against the damage you can do, Prepare to need 3-4 critical headshots with the archer to take down a generic grunt, multiply that by the a couple enemies each wave and a couple waves per room and you realize you just spent 30 minutes waiting to kill an enemy. If you saw combat from the trailer, you might think that combat was exciting - I don't believe they would have sold a single copy if they left a complete engagement in the video instead of a quick clash.Characters: the heroes are distinct, their skills all kind of overlap in use just because there's so little dynamism to combat. The melee characters are much higher risk, ranged characters are clearly the safer choice,Dungeons: repetitive, simplistic tiles with little functional variation. You'll clear a mob of enemies only to have another wave drop in on you. Sometimes enemies get stuck at entrances and you have to hunt them down.Sound: I would return the game over how poorly the sound is implemented. Enemy footsteps get quiet the further away they are, but at a rate that means I don't think the game plays the sound cue if they're out of melee range. The music is samey and repetitive (you can easily hear were the loops are). Spatial sound like Dolby Atmos really struggles to make the sound mean anything. This game is the audio equivalent of a grey smear of noise. Features: I returned this game once already because it doesn't have ultrawide support and even had limited 16:9 support.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable little title. Kind of a roguelike L4D mixed with Doom combat arenas. I didn't play it at all until the 1.0.5 update, which apparently has made combat much faster. I've found the combat to be mostly fun and engaging and am a bit surprised this hasn't been a bigger hit. I still think there are some further improvements they could implement, though.There's meta progression in that you bring gold back from missions (Or spend it during the mission for gear/upgrades) which can then be used to level up weapons, perks, and items that you find during missions. The upgrades can be pretty significant power boosts, so there is a feeling of progression. Upgrading a weapon, for instance, essentially doubles attack power.Upgrades during missions range from perks (faster move speed, more physical/mage damage, vampirism, etc.) to weapon upgrades (adding elements to weapons, increase charge attack damage, parry bonuses). Some of the upgrades don't seem to make a whole lot of sense and seem very niche. For example, a %increase to charge attack damage for every 1 meter moved while the attack is charged. It's not super practical to run around with your weapon charged up, though I suppose you could cheese bosses with it by walking in circles before you enter the arena. There are 4 classes that all play distinctly and each have their own unique abilities. Two abilities and an ultimate with a fairly long (50 second) cooldown. I found 3 of them to be pretty fun to play, with the Paladin having the most fun kit. The thief/assassin or whatever he's supposed to be feels kinda terrible though. He's the only character without a dedicated movement ability. Everyone else has what's basically a get out of jail free card. He just has "Pocket Sand" which only blinds enemies right in front of him.The art style is definitely the most eye catching thing about the game, and it's great. Love the 80s Saturday morning cartoon vibe.The cutscenes and voice acting are downright awful, though. I've started skipping them. In the cutscenes, the characters have no ambient movement. They just are there static/motionless, but they still blink. It's major uncanny valley territory.The voice acting is the worst I've heard in a very long time. Maybe ever. I don't know if they were trying to go for a cheesy thing or not, but if they were they failed and it's just bad. There's no emotion in any lines. Everything is delivered flatly. Characters also only have a couple lines for each ability or environment interaction, which results in a lot of repetition of already cringe dialog.Other than that, I think the game's pretty solid and fun to play.The only thing I've noticed is I put the game on easy to see how it played and ended up realizing it's way more fun to be able to mow down enemies in a couple hits. As-is, on normal and above a lot of enemies feel like bullet sponges. I've beaten a mission on the Mythic 1 difficult, I think it's called, and I didn't find it as enjoyable as the lower difficulties. It didn't actually feel much harder. It just took longer. For reference, the difficulties are Easy/Normal/Hard/M1/M2. The highest difficulties give extra resources for upgrades, but take longer so I'm not entirely sure if that's a more efficient use of time until you significantly upgrade your character.If the game reduced enemy HP to the levels of the enemies on "Easy" and doubled, or maybe even tripled, enemy density while increasing their damage, it'd be tons more fun running around the arena and whittling down enemy numbers.Overall though, if you're looking for a co-op PvE FPS with character progression, this is a pretty fun title with great visual style. Just be prepared for some terrible voice acting and cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody reads these reviews anyway, so I'll just leave here that I like the game.Haha, okay, seriously.  I like the game.  I'm gonna tell you about the game, and then I'm gonna talk about a couple things I see people don't like.  It's my opinion, leave a clown or something or just scream in the comments, I'm cool either way.What it is is a first-person melee game.  That's like a first person shooting game, except the ranges are really low.  Like, y'know, melee.  Short range hack-and-slash.  It's a whole lot less of "put reticule on bad guy and click" and a whole lot more "get close enough to do that reticule thing."There's a couple characters that do more ranged stuff.  Couldn't tell you much, I've been playing the swashbuckler-guy exclusively.  My wife's been using the paladork lady, because being a big meatwall with a shield is her jam.  It's cool.We've been streaming it on alternate accounts, so I've got more time on this game than you think.The playstyle is more methodical, rewarding good positioning and being aware of the enemies.  And flailing away with attacks can get punished, so you need to keep your attacks measured and even.  Getting hit in the back does a lot more damage, and with no radar you really need to keep looking around.  There's a brief "you are about to get hit from this direction" symbol, which is your only clue you're going to get walloped.  The game will end you quickly if you're inattentive or impatient.  I rather like this.It's got "roguelike" elements, where progressive playthroughs let you unlock benefits which permanently upgrade your character.  If you enjoy a bit of snark, you can replace skill with persistence.What it looks like is cel-shaded.  It's trying to be "Saturday-morning cartoons" and I can believe it, except Saturday-morning cartoons never had a framerate this smooth, or for that matter, looked this nice.  When I was a child and watching cartoons, they were flat-out rubbish.  I watched them anyway.Another thing that makes it suitably Saturday-morning cartoon is the plot, and the voice-acting.  It's one thing to be a mediocre voice talent doing a cartoon (writes the guy who is a mediocre, *at best*, voice talent) but it's another to ape that style convincingly.  It's very, very difficult to be a believably so-so actor on purpose.  Which means they're great.There's also a plot, revealed in tiny dribs and drabs, about some guy named "Deadalus" (this name is brilliant, seriously) who has an army of undead and other things that... I'm not sure, villainy no doubt.  But a plucky band of heroes will foil their plan every Saturday morning, I'm sure.Okay, finally, coop.  Right?  If you've read my reviews, you know I love this stuff.  Parties came together smoothly, gameplay was had.  Excellent.A couple sticking points:  The game kind of throws you right in there with just a couple static screens of tutorial to explain the works.  Truth be told, it doesn't really need it, except maybe to explain what the super-powerup-MythForce attack does.  You stab (or shoot) bad guys.  You try to avoid getting hit.Arrows kind of come from out of nowhere, and exposure to spellcasters doesn't come 'til mostly through the first dungeon sequence.  The solution for all of the above is to keep moving, pretty much, but my first encounter was unpleasant to say the least.Areas in the first mission have been a bit samey.  There's perhaps six or eight rooms, though they'll arrange them so you come in from different doors.  But you soon realize where the hidden loot is.  So a little variety mightn't go amiss.Some people have moaned about "EOS", confusing "Epic Online Services" with the Epic Game Store (which is abbreviated EGS but come on, people).  It's an Unreal Engine Game.  It's going to have EOS.  It doesn't make you buy games from their store, it installs itself once, and it lets you play with people pretty smoothly.  I'm no fan of their game store at all, and have snubbed it so hard the only game I bought there I bought again on Steam, but let's get our facts together here, eh?Anyway, a game that rewards patience and positioning, runs great, and is a bit cheesy?  It's my kind of game.  MythForce is a great coop adventure.  I don't know how many legs it has, but I expect the missus and I may go through the whole campaign at least once, and I'll probably try to headlock a few friends into getting copies so we can run a full team.  It'll be a good number of streaming episodes, if anything.  It's got my swashbuckling thumb up.

_childDocuments_.review: Though the game hasn't yet reached its full potential, and is rather short for $30, many problems it suffered from have been improved upon as of the Harder, Better, Faster, Story Update. The melee combat feels a lot more fluid, and gets better as you upgrade your weapons and perks. Each character has 5 sets of weapons they can choose from, and can hold two sets at a time. The differences in weaponry aren't particularly notable across each of the characters, however, and are often just one main weapon, with a varying secondary weapon of either a dagger or a shield. This isn't enough to warrant purchasing and upgrading an entire new set of weapons, and I think more of a distinction should be made between the weapon sets, such as giving the characters a larger variety of weapons altogether to give them more distinct play-styles. Victoria, for example, is unique in that she is the only character who can use a great-sword, which is a much-needed change of pace when the rest of the weapons are either maces or swords.In contrast to melee, ranged weapons tend to be lacking, with poorer hit registration and, in the case of the spell books, poor damage too. Damage-over-time effects rarely make much of an impact, and some, like bleeding, poison, and fire, feel exactly the same but with a different coat of paint. I tend to ignore them altogether, and focus solely on melee.The story cutscenes give much-needed life to the game that otherwise wasn't there originally, especially during the final boss fight. Before the update, Deadalus would simply keel over instead of the cutscene that now plays, which was very anti-climactic. In addition, after completing each level, a short cutscene of Deadalus taunting the player character plays, with dialogue changing depending on which member of Mythforce you're playing as. I enjoy it, as it sprinkles a little bit of flavor when playing through each level.There is grounds to improve on the cutscenes, though, and the story in general. Most of the cutscenes have dry deliveries from the voice actors, and voicelines repeat throughout several cutscenes (The amount of times Rico says that quote about dropping in to see his old gang and stab them are enough to drive me mad).Often, at the start of each level, one or two characters are shown discussing mundane things while the others inspect stuff in the background. While they would be nice on their own, these are rarely worth the time to watch, as the content the characters discuss are rehashes of things that have been better explained by the in-game dialogue. With what limited cutscenes the game has, with the 9 levels in the game, they feel like wasted potential.The cutscenes tend to shine more from Hexstar's chapter and onwards, when each of the 4 characters have more of a speaking presence, as well as highlighting their personal history with each of the major bosses (Maggie and Hexstar used to be part of the Lyceum and have a personal rivalry, while Rico used to work under Deadalus).More could be done to flesh out the team of Mythforce, and their greater world, through these cutscenes, so as to not rely on gathering everything through the lore entries that drop. Most of the information you actually gather about Mythforce's team dynamics is through Victoria's 'Field Report' lore entries, instead of naturally while playing through the game.Additionally, despite their importance, none of the figures of the Citadel make an appearance at all, and Sylvia just has a non-speaking cameo during the opening. While this *is* slightly understandable, as the characters are on a journey to Deadalus' castle and don't necessarily have time to mingle, I feel like at least acknowledging the presence of these characters would help give more life to the story currently present.Personally, I'd suggest waiting to get this game on a sale. While it's improved from its original state, it still has a ways away to go, and I hope the developers will take the time to get it there.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR the game is bad, and you should go play Robotquest, Ravenswatch, or hell even Gunfire Reborn if you are looking for a new roguelike to play. I don't normally write reviews, but this game made me so disappointed that i had to. I returned this game after only an hour and that was with me playing the game with a friend.Let me start off by saying this game, even without the bugs, would not be good. The only "saving grace" this game has is it's theme. Beyond that though it falls flat in almost every regard in terms of a roguelike. I tried REALLY hard to like this game but I couldn't.Combat: A horrible mess.The combat and movement is extremely clunky, slow, and due to what i assume are bugs? There was many times where I'd attack an enemy and the attack would just do nothing. Literally had arrows passing through enemies and hitting the enemies behind them. Melee attacks whiffing at point blank range, etc.Additionally, the enemy AI in this game is terrible. They will walk into walls, and sometimes just straight stand there looking at you and do nothing. Had one enemy once that just start spinning in place.Enemy variation was also lacking. Granted i played for only an hour before returning it? I only saw two enemy types the entire time i played. Which essentially were just dudes who walked at you or threw stuff at you.When the Enemies do act proper things can get rather frustrating. There are certain enemies that will knock you down if they hit you. The problem with this is, the time that it takes to stand back up? It has already hit you with another attack that knocks you back down.Level Design: Repetitive. The level design in this game is extremely repetitive even for a roguelike. In an hour of playtime I saw the same exact level designs repeated multiple times. Even in separate chapters. Perks and Leveling: No meaningful choices.The perks in this game are so uninspiring and bland. For an example your standard perk options are something along the lines of: "Deal 20 more damage" "Your weapon now does Ice damage" "Heal for 1hp when defeating an enemy" Not once did I run into any perks that I thought were engaging or build defining like other games in this genre. Nor did i find any perks that seemed to synergize that well. When I did find something that was remotely interesting it was so underwhelming that simply attacking normally was more efficient. Characters: Lacking. This is one area that I thought was going to be this games saving grace but I was wrong. I thought this game was going to be filled to the brim with character quips, and interactions that would be funny. But they were sadly silent for the most part. To me this is the biggest pain point for me in this game as it was the thing that sort of drew me in.

_childDocuments_.review: Mythforce once again reminds me that Steam really should have a "mixed feelings" option for recommendation, as this game is in what I'd class a weird position, however in it's current standing, I feel I have to lean towards negative. (For Context: As of review time, I have beaten 4 levels, and shall update one I finish the rest.)Mythforce has the look and graphically works well within the idea of it being a TV show from the 80's or so, character design wise look like they'd easily fit in, and the games opening cinematic has a lovely nostalgic feel to it, with a tune I find somewhat addictive, honestly this was originally the thing that got me interested in the game.Character wise we have 4 to pick from, Tank, Mage, Ranger, Rogue. Each bring their own abilities with them and feel different enough to warrant experimenting with. The characters have some personality, but personally, I feel a bit more could of been done with them, maybe make them a bit cheesier, give it that proper old school feel with how they speak, also some more lines would of been good, as I constantly hear the same lines within 30 seconds (Note: Apparently the characters "bark" less now according to the 1st hotfix, however I didn't notice that much of a difference on my end, still seemed too often).Loading into the game, you're hit with a wall of text as your "tutorial", having a small level to help introduce players into the game and explaining how things work would of been a better choice, but either way, you'll get the info you need to get going.Being a Rogue-like similar to Gunfire Reborn, as you progress you'll gain perks to level your hero, normally having 3 options for you to pick from, they will reset per run and you can set up your character in weird and wonderful ways.The Combat is basic in nature and sadly, currently, feels somewhat clunky, movement and attacking just feels a bit off, like it needs a bit more speed to it, enemies so far haven't had much variation and can feel very sponge-like taking damage, I've not felt challenged particularly, but on the odd time enemies have cornered me or some such, it just feels more tedious than fun to deal with them, I've had the odd enemy glitch into the floor or shoot to the sky as well, as I've progressed into following levels, I was seeing more of the same enemies already, just with bigger health bars and higher damage, I'd of expected *some* variation in the first few levels at least, but I could be being overly picky on that front.So far, the constellation system for upgrading yourself personally seems slightly pointless, I understand it will take multiple runs to upgrade it properly, but so far, it just feels like it will be a tedious task, knowing that I have to grind out crystals to upgrade, regardless, you'll get options to boost defence, damage, reduce cool-downs and such, you also have a store to buy weapons, outfits, emotes and voice lines, some of that stuff is overpriced in my opinion, but i suppose they need to try and encourage replayability.As no friends have purchased the game yet, my only experience of online has been me joining on a random game, and having someone random join me, and so far, it's very much been a bad experience, despite my internet being decent, having constant lag or ping issues made it irritating, also seemingly only having quick play and no option to look for rooms or specific missions to join feels silly in a game that seems to push the co-op as a major selling point.The first big boss was a fine fight, nothing to write home about, I loved how the game used the main theme in a remix, giving it a nice feel, but after beating it, I didn't feel fulfilled, I just felt like it was time to stop playing for a bit, as it was just an OK experience.Overall currently, that's the problem for me with this game, it's just...OK, and lately, the gaming community has been constantly served great or amazing games,  feeling OK or just passable isn't enough now, this game needs work if it wants to stand out, it needs love from its dev team and it needs to start putting the right foot forward, this game COULD be great, it could be like the great cartoons that you love to come back to and view again and again, but for now, it's just a re-run at 6am on a random channel when most people are asleep, sure, some might catch it, but one it hits 7, the real good shows start.I truly hope that as I progress in the game, my feelings will change and I can change this review to positive, however I doubt that, not until more work has been put into the game, I'd advise waiting for a sale as it stands for now. (Edit #2 : as of the First hot-fix patch, Achievements have now been fixed & the stamina system has been improved a little bit, but not enough done yet overall to change this review positive)

_childDocuments_.review: Was hesitant about playing mythforce and only jumped in recently at patch 1.0.2.2.Recently revisited (1.0.5.2) as quite a few patches happened that improved the game a lot in a good way.So far the different classes feel nice, quite well balanced and each is fun to handle in their own right.Have tried out multiplayer and it was fun to work together, but solo mode is also very viable.Each run takes about 30 minutes which feels nice enough length wise, not too long, not too short.The melee combat feels nice now after a patch and works well, one switches a lot between melee and ranged to take down foes more easily.The energy management feels nice at this moment as well, the added extra energy makes it quite usable and is forgiving if one messes up at the start. (yes you can not keep blasting or swinging but need to use the terrain as well in a tactical manner to not run out of energy)The game is quite forgiving, nice 80's cartoon vibe, a lot of upgrades can be found everywhere.For the grinding part, this is a roguelite and I can see that it will take many runs to get things at higher tier like the weapons, trinkets, cards one finds as well as the constellation (stat boost for the characters).Got pretty far with upgrades but for an ultimate build the grind will be quite extensive especially for the constellation, everything else seems manageable, but perhaps a shared coin and gem stash for the chars would help out so one can use a favorite char to boost a less favorite one.As I am planning to play this game off and on in short bursts and the characters even without upgrades are well playable at least for the first levels and the few upgrades I bought started spawning in the world I felt a bit of progression. _childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you have a fantastic concept, great art style, and killer soundtrack? Well, add in a slew of half baked systems and a plethora of bugs and you get Mythforce. This game really deserved some more time in the oven and its a shame it doesn't seem to have reached its potential nearly a year after release. Releasing originally as an Epic exclusive also killed all momentum this game would have possibly had on PC if you ask me. Despite this, I won't completely write off the game and if you can find it on sale or in a bundle (like myself) then you can still get 10-20 hours of enjoyment if you can handle the issues the game has.Let's start with the good. If it wasn't obvious, Mythforce is inspired by 80s saturday morning cartoons and I would say it does a very good job in capturing this. The characters, story, and voice acting are intentionally cheesy in a way that is charming. The great soundtrack ranges from power metal to synthwave and the tracks that accompany the boss fights set the tone superbly. The general gameplay loop is fun, especially with other players, and if you get blessed with particularly good perks on a run you really feel like a god.  I mainly played the archer hero, Hawkins, whose play style rewards hit and run tactics as well as precision headshots. Hawkins, along with the other 3 heroes, have their own unique play style though you are able to unlock other weapon types for each hero potentially transforming their play style radically.Mythforce has 9 levels split across 3 themes with their own boss. These themes being forest ruins, crypts, and an opulent vampire castle. I think have a another 3 levels, theme, and boss would have nicely rounded out the current offerings. Additionally, some greater variance between the sets of levels would have been better. Both the crypts and castle share the same traps and for the most part, enemies. On the other hand, the forest levels feel more unique but are capstoned by the most disappointing boss fight of the game. The 2nd and 3rd boss fights on the other hand are quite the spectacle and feel like they were taken from an MMORPG raid. Enemy pathfinding is chaotic, ESPECIALLY when playing with multiple people. It's very noticeable when playing Hawkins since you are generally aiming to land headshots. Enemies will jerk around unnaturally as they can't seem to decide which player to move to and attack. Add in the fact that enemies will constantly get knocked to the floor or slapped around by attacks, thus moving their hitbox, and you'll soon learn landing shots with your bow isn't worth the effort when playing co-op.During my time with the game, I also encountered a lot of latency related issues when playing with others. Lag being the obvious one, but also hits not registering despite good latency. I also encountered one freeze and maybe half a dozen crashes during my time with the game. I never had any performance issues, but given that I'm playing on a high end system built earlier this year, I wouldn't expect any. Luckily most of these crashes seem to happen when transitioning from end level screen to the main menu so no progress is ever lost.These are the more noteworthy issues I encountered while playing Mythforce. I think this game had a lot of potential, but so much of it is squandered by lackluster design. I definitely had fun with the game despite my disappointment and if none of these issues scare you away, then you probably will too. If there is ever a Mythforce 2, I hope Beamdog can take this fantastic premise and create the game that it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten to watch this game develop through beta and early access, and it's become a solid game that's a blast to play.  The art style is a fantastic callback to cartoons of the 80s, and there are a lot of small details that show the amount of care and dedication the team has put into the game.The combat doesn't feel slow or clunky at all, contrary to what some reviews are claiming.  Rather, the feel is much more deliberate and tactical than other horde games, allowing you to time your strikes and pick your shots.  If the frenetic, twitch based gameplay of similar games has turned you off to the genre, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 15/12/23The game today received a combat update and it plays SO much more fluidly :) I'm so pleased that this game is getting better, i'd love to see it expanded on. Kudos to Beamdog, the game has improved by a large margin in only a few months. THEY'RE ACTUALLY DOING IT GUYS!-- -- --Edit 10/12/23:The issue noted below with hit registration with magical attacks seems to have been largely resolved! Please disregard that below as it seems fixed :)-- -- -- Mythforce is a great little title, with a hopefully bright future ahead of it.It's a co-op roguelike with a cracking art style. I often see 'melee focused' mentioned when talking about this, but I think that depends on what character you play as, as of the four currently in the game  two are melee, and two are ranged focused.You journey through 3 sets of  levels in each biome, of which there are 3 with a selection of secrets smattered through, and a boss/horde/special encounter at the end. It starts slow as the first sort of half of the game is very easy, but once the enemies start displaying some slightly different behavior the game becomes A LOT of fun, especially with a friend or two in tow.Progression is drawn out nicely, without being too long to feel unrewarding, and the weapons feel decent. There are some hit registration issues however currently particularly with the mage character, which has been identified as a netcode issue and is expected to be rectified shortly. This issue does not seem to exist when soloing, or if whoever plays mage is hosting the session though.

_childDocuments_.review: One feels transported back to the cartoons of the 80s.Choose a hero and team up in cooperative mode to beat up the villains and their countless henchmen. Nice!The dungeons/castles, etc. of each chapter are randomly generated, similar to Diablo. They do repeat, yes. Some more different rooms would be nice but its ok.You can do it, Beamdog! ;)   At the end of each chapter, there's a boss waiting, along with a cutscene in the style of 80s cartoons that advances the story.I partially disagree with some of the reviews here.The game isn't launched through the Epic Launcher, and there are no missing save options.(after all, it's a roguelike)At the end of each run, you can permanently enhance your character to progress further in the story.Regarding the claim of always having the same skills, that's not entirely accurate either.As you progress through the game, you'll come across items that significantly modify your skills. For example, you can turn a static turret into a permanent companion or transform a stationary shield into a frost sphere which follows your steps.Each ability can be modified in three additional ways, which complement each other. As a result, you end up with completely different abilities than you had at the beginning of the run.If you're up for a cooperative roguelike experience, this is the right place for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a positive, but this is a mixed review, but TLDR: Buy if on sale.Good: Art style; intro song; roguelike/lite for replay-ability (only good if you like/understand this game type. some people dislike this game type)Bad: Combat could be more interesting; AI is simple; maps are repetitive, town UI is pretty horrible and took me a second to realize I could interact with the buildings.Mixed Feedback:There is "build" variety in the gem/constellation system, and some control over your roguelite runs with affinity system to influence gear and upgrades. Armory system lets you change up primary/secondary weapon and level up damage for your selected build type, but this all feels mostly generic and could use some extra style to make each build stand out change how the character is played completely (something like a speed build, or a tank build, or a ranged build, utility build, etc.)The game is fun and engaging enough, but lacking something to make it really hook the players. Would be great for couch co-op or in an actual arcade. It is missing an "excitement" feel to it though. There were no times when I was running with a group where it felt like we had to strategize or felt amazing for beating a boss or hard encounter. We just ran around and hit things till they died. More development may help this game really stand out, and I feel a lot of love for the 80s in this with the art style and it is fairly polished for what it is, but it needs time to grow, which I hope it will.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun melee oriented FPS, but also has ranged combat with magic.  This game improves on Vermintide's combat by having less m1 spam.  You can perform different attacks with different effects, and energy costs.For example a sprint attack knocks enemies over, where you can execute them.  Any hit on a grounded foe does critical damage.  This reminds me of Dark Messiah, where you could use the same strategy.  Power attacks can knock enemies out of their attack animations, and light attacks are quick and easy to get away with.  There is also a perfect parry/block/dodge system, where timing these actions gets greater results.  A perfect parry grants a free riposte.  A perfect block knocks giant foes to their knees.  A perfect dodge avoids all damage, even if you were hit.The game has a stamina system like a Souls-like.  This makes combat deliberate, and you must have a plan before attacking.  You can also customize your character to have almost unlimited stamina, if this is something you don't want to deal with.The game features full character stat customization, allowing you to stack health, armor, damage, attack speed, stamina, or cooldowns.  Mages can be tanky, if they choose.  You also can equip a lot of weapons on different characters.  The hunter and rogue can use magic, if they choose.Finally, the game features 5 unique abilities to each character.  All characters share overdrive, then each character gets a jump ability, a utility ability, a combat ability, and an ultimate ability.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is fantastic with a great soundtrack and interesting character abilities. I didn't finish the game because I got tired of falling through the floor and losing an entire run to it. The fourth time was enough that I just didn't care to finish the game. There is "exploration" in the levels, but probably the biggest gripe I have is that while most games would add an optional area with an optional miniboss that had loot, this is instead a set of empty hallways with chests that is just a time sink to open. Put a guard or something in the area and it would really bump up the interest in the area. I wanted to like everything in it, and I had fun when it worked, but the fact that there are game breaking bugs like falling through the floor once every 2 hours is... not great.

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a toughie. The premise is quite fun. Co-op shenanigans in a world reminiscent of late 80s to early 90s cartoon shows.It's I *guess* supposed to be a roguelike, but the gameplay doesn't quite make that clear to the player from the start. The level design is incredibly samey and gets super tedious after even just a few levels. The same exact rooms get repeated numerous times even within the same level, which is just plain bad design.  The tilesets need way more variety to make exploration and encounter design more inviting.Combat is okay. Nothing to write home about, really. You can do some ranged stuff and some melee stuff. There's special skills that operate on cooldowns that you can utilize in combat to gain buffs, debuff your enemies or just straight up deal damage. The ultimates feel super weak. You don't get that sense of becoming unstoppable for a brief moment. Finetuning the balancing here would make the game *feel* more like the cartoons it is trying to bring to the forefront of your mind.Since I have no friends, I did play the game solo. That most likely impacted my gameplay experience. Albeit additional people would not make the samey level design any better or the ultimates more rewarding.It's a 'mild recommend' from me. There's plenty of potential here and the devs seem dedicated to bringing more to MythForce over time. I hope they stick to it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love 80s era cartoons like He-Man and She-Ra, Mythforce will be right up your alley. Mythforce combines that 80s goodness with a competent first-person battler. Mechanically, it does not do anything radically new, but as a whole package, it's great!There's a decent selection of characters, each with their own unique special abilities and the combat is quite snappy without being overly frantic. The game is divided into 9 levels with you having to survive through each of them at a stretch. On each run you get to choose power-ups and artefacts to help you through the respective dungeon, but once that level comes to an end, the items vanish and you must start anew. This hybrid between a roguelite and an episodic story was fascinating, and even I who generally do not like the "rogue" genre, had a good time.The game as it stands has a definitive ending, but there definitely was an indication that they wanted to do more levels (and more story) as a DLC or a season 2 or something. I am not sure if such plans are still on the cards, but regardless, I had a jolly good time, and highly recommend this to anyone who found what I said intriguing.

_childDocuments_.review: Received as a gift.Took 7.4 hours to beat the campaign once in 3 player coop, that includes 2 game overs from bad runs due to bad RNG with perks+enchantments.I'd say it's a 7/10 right now, definitely better than it was when they first released the demo but definitely could still use some work.  Not a lot of variety in rooms and you see the same ones repeated in all dungeon types (there are 3 episodes per dungeon type and 9 episodes total, so 3 dungeon types total).Would be nice if you could choose not to have an off weapon, getting perks for the weapon you don't use, even on reroll (you get 4 rerolls per level) is a real bummer.  My 2 coop partners were both the sorceress, both were doing pure spellcasting and they would routinely get 3 perks for melee only, then spend one of their rerolls and get 3 melee perks again.  Seriously needs to be fixed.Has a FoV slider, I maxed it out, at the start of each level you have to attack once for it to apply your FoV if it isn't default.  If there is headbob I didn't notice, I am really sensitive to both headbob and FoV so if there was headbob it wasn't enough to make me feel nauseous.There were sync issues at times (like one player would hit an enemy and the enemy wouldn't take damage).Allies can block projectiles, ie. a sorc casts a spell it hits their ally it doesn't go through them to the enemy.There are higher difficulties to play on and achievements for grinding through them. _childDocuments_.review: Updated review after playing for much longer. At first i really wasn't sure i liked this game but over the week since launch i have found that i can't stop playing it, so i'm updating my review to reflect that:The more i play this game the more it clicks and the more i fall in love.Right at the start anyone that grew up in the 80s will fall in love with the whole presentation. The developers and the art team behind this game absolutely knocked the presentation out of the park. The sounds, the music, the characters make me feel like a kid watching He-Man again. The visuals of the game, the way the environments are lit and rendered are absolutely stunning as well. You can stop moving at any point during game-play and you have a screenshot right our of a Saturday morning cartoon. Its impressive.On top of that the game runs butter smooth across all settings on both my PC and on my Steam Deck. The Deck can run the game at an impressive 60fps without a sweat if you drop to low settings and because of the art style the game looks just fine. Or if you want to turn on that gorgeous global illumination you can set that to mid and keep everything else at low and you get a very solid 40fps. Both are more than playable.  The game controls wonderfully on the deck as well. I actually think its my favourite place to play.At first the game didn't hook me in the way i was somehow expecting. I couldn't put my finger on it and i thought i didn't enjoy it. However i have found myself playing this every evening or picking up the steam deck to do an episode run whenever i get a moment.Each run takes around 20 minutes and each time i finish i now want to do just one more. It's great. Now that the game has clicked for me an i'm into it's rhythm i totally love it.I think the best games are the ones that do take a bit of time to warm up to. Those are usually the ones that stick with me the most. I've got a disgustingly large Steam library and so i tend to float away to other games quite easily. This one has kept me coming back and is becoming one of my favourite pick up and play titles.The developers seem to be listening across steam and their discord. It is clear they are taking everyone's complaints about the game into consideration.This feels like the sort of game that will continue to grow and get better over time.I'm really glad i gave this title the time it truly deserves and i can't wait to continue to play and also see how it grows and develops.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good times!I was initially leery of grabbing it due to mixed reviews, but I quickly picked up on the fact that if you sort by "hours played" anything over 1 hour was "overwhelmingly positive". Folks either bounce off the 80s cartoon vibe and don't get it, or they stay and really enjoy it for what it is. I happened to be one of the latter.The premise is straightforward—you can play solo or as a part of a colorful fantasy team of warriors (very Masters of the Universe) that defend the land of Eldryth. The game this reminds me most of is something like Vermintide, but instead of static maps it has procedurally generated dungeons assembled from a rooms themed by chapter with usually a midpoint miniboss and a final bigger encounter. Every 3 "episodes" (aka levels) or so you fight one of the Big Bosses who usually give you some cheesy dialogue about how you'll never defeat them and backstory (like who they are rivals with etc).It is a roguelite (something like Hades) where the runs take between 20 mins for earlier episodes, and maybe 40-50 minutes for the later ones. This means you have to restart your build each episode (level) and have some ways to boost your starting stuff or what's accessible to build from between each outing.Network connectivity was straightforward (it uses peer-to-peer and I had no lag with my friends even though some of us are hundreds of miles away). They really nailed the graphics and I love the voice acting. The cartoons they have for each chapter are fantastic, and I love the music.At first the game felt a bit simplistic, but that's mostly playing on normal. The AI seems rudimentary, and there isn't a ton of nuance obvious. But every time you beat a level you can play one difficulty higher. And mythic is no joke. You're quickly learning to watch for those incoming attack prompts, keep an eye on archers to dodge as they fire, and those rudimentary AIs become a whole lot more threatening when you can't drop them in 2-3 easy swings and you have to kite one and use cover to regenerate enough stamina to get a charge and big hit in on the archer sniping you. Suddenly whether your power attack will knock something down, or where you're hitting with that attack (back, head, body) becomes a bit more important.So I'd say it's great for some casual players who want to soak up some vibes and dialogue, and spend 20-30 hours with friends just goofing off and having a good time, but you can definitely crank it up and challenge yourself a bit. There's even some advanced progression and  some resource grind for folks that want to get absolutely everything. The first group will enjoy those hand-painted backgrounds in the crypt levels, and finding secret passages, and hidden treasure, and the second will appreciate the difference in split second management of heavy vs light attacks, perfect blocks, and your friend who can land those headshots for crits over your shoulder.If I have one complaint it's that I would love more episodes and characters. But for a small indie studio, and a $30 game, this is about right. If they have DLC planned, they have me and my crew's money for sure.All in all, I greatly recommend the game. I'm a big fan of those old timey cartoons and I love the vibes they put into this, so me and my friends are sort of dead center of their target audience. Give it a go. If the reviews are any indication, you should know within the first hour or so if it's for you. ^_~ Hope to see you in Eldryth!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have to update based on some of the recent changes and fixes in the game as it has dramatically changed my opinion on if I would recommend this or not. The major issues I felt were hindering the game's immersion have all been resolved and the game feels fantastic. This includes everything to do with super ultrawide- and yes, it's completely supported now!For using higher video settings, this game chugs along for its post processing. I'm running on a 3090, and it was still unable to get up to 60fps. You can run it at Medium settings. Looks pretty good there too since its art lends to lower settings pretty well. <- This is still somewhat of an issue, and the advice here is still pretty accurate, but now it's still pretty good on high settings comparing to before. The perks and skills do in fact feel augmentative in nature. I feel like as a beginner, it still does feel like there's missing context to some of the perks and enchantments during the selection of those skills that might not be clear that say, you're going to get either damage to all weapons or just the one, but this was because there wasn't any clear enough indicators of what the differences between the two. After a few games its extremely clear, but yeah, it's still somewhat relevant for new players. Enchantments change the weapons and how they function. Perks are all around changes to the way your character works. Keep a close eye on the top text. It's crystal clear if you're paying attention lol. The gameplay has changed from its initial feeling to it definitely feeling faster. I originally complained about how it felt slow, and didn't know why in the past, and now it feels completely liberating to be dashing around like a crazy person. Kudos to energy being infinite when not in combat (this was always a thing, but I never mentioned how it really did make transitions to new rooms feel faster). Anything outside of movement to me is subjective. I found more use out of the skills the more I played it. In the kingdom you get the ability to customize the traits of your characters. Just look around a bit. It's pretty well balanced and in a good way. Addendum: I will admit, the grind is real with this; people are right and you will need to play a lot to upgrade other characters from the start again. But, that's just by choice. It's play to win, not pay to win. :)The audio was always something I really enjoyed, and this hasn't changed at all. Yes, there were bugs, but now I haven't seen any issues with it. Albeit yes hearing the hunter say "THE HUNT IS OVER" very often kinda just feels funny to me instead of it being annoying or breaking immersion. To each their own of course. The art is absolutely gorgeous. The skills and how pretty they looked was really nice.Overall, comparing to before- if you were waiting for things to be better like I was, I give a wholeheartedly appreciated green light for this now. Be sure to have a few friends on deck though. The single-player experience is still fun, but I can still see this being 100x more fun with friends etc. The most important thing I feel right now is that if you really felt let down, this team has really done everything they can to bring it back. And its worth playing. Art/audio/gameplay/story/accessibility.. Definitely is miles ahead of where they were before. And I'm so excited to see the changes this game has going forward. Great job guys.

_childDocuments_.review: Mythforce: Fun, if a little flawed.I've very much enjoyed this game, especially with friends. The perks feel impactful, the meta-progression feels VERY impactful, and the general tome of the game is very fun. The soundtrack is excellent, and a lot of the visuals are both clear and visually pleasing.What I mean by this is that it resembles (obviously) the aesthetics of an 80's cartoon. The way they outlined interactive objects, enemies, and allies makes them look like figures on a backdrop. This help you distinguish very quickly and easily between what's important and what is not.There ARE a few drawbacks: 1. Bugs. Not anything gamebreaking so far (16ish hours in), just a few minor bugs. Inability to access some shrines and such (fixed by switching weapons or using an ability), fell through the floor once (my movement ability returned me to the map). So, nothing GIANT, but enough to notice, and be annoyed by.2. Lack of labeling of the hub areas building. I've played with several friends, and it seems counter-intuitive that we can click on the buildings in the background city (at first). 3. Why is my party option automatically set to public? I don't want strangers joining my game. Without some kind of ingame chat, it feels highly impersonal and awkward. 'Friends only would be a much better option in my opinion.Those three items comprise my main complaints. None of them are deal-breakers, and they all seem like things that can be relatively easy fixes (I understand how complicated fixing bugs can get, but this is already in a better state than, say, the average Bethesda game). Also, they've already dropped a hot fix patch to fix some of the bugs, and that's a good sign.Overall, I highly recommend this game, especially with friends. Plenty of value here for the price!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to enjoy here, and a lot of potential in the game for more enjoyment going forward. The aesthetic is fantastic and hits an amazing point of nostalgia, but it definitely covers up some slower, somewhat repetitive gameplay especially once you get to the higher difficulty tiers. Even at Mythic I, I spent as much time just running from enemies while my stamina slowly recovered, turned, landed a hit, then went back to scurrying because the enemy HP outscales your ability to damage it so quickly when you start out a level. That drawback being said, I still enjoy the game and plan to put more time into it. I feel like I am chasing a dragon for a good build though, and there are no dragons - currently the levels feel too short to put together a truly overpowered build and putting together a truly overpowered build is one of the hallmarks of the roguelike/lite genre. So far, each time I finish a floor, I walk through the exit feeling like my build is just barely about to start coming together, without the change to really use that build before I start the next floor and I start out at zero again.A mode where you can chain floors together so you can put together more of a build would be a fantastic add (though given the pre-release was 3 floors chained and they removed that, I feel that isn't the direction they are going). Still, for a good bit of Saturday Morning Nostalgia with some friends, you could definitely do worse.Edit: Coming back after I have finished all achievements, including Deadalus on Mythic 3, I can say they are still improving this game. There is still a lot of fun to have here, and having put this much time into it, I think I can safely say it is worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm seeing a lot of bad reviews with really low play times. (less than an hour)Several of those reviews point out that you lose all progress between missions. That's simply not true. This is a roguelite. There's both in-mission progression that only lasts through the current mission, and there's permanent progression that carries over between missions.The in-level progression consists of a variety of pickups/buffs that improve your weapons, skills, and grant special passive effects. The pickups have 4 tiers of quality, but you will need to improve your permanent progression in order to get the higher tier upgrades. As stated, the permanent progression increases your chances of finding higher tier upgrades during a mission. Additionally, you can improve your damage, your resistances, your speed, etc. You can also unlock cosmetic stuff in the permanent progression system like new outfits, emotes, and voice lines for the characters.There are currently 9 missions, but each mission has several levels of difficulty. (some of which need to be unlocked) The missions are procedurally generated. It seems that the first 3 missions are a bit lacking in variety, but the other 6 seem to be way better. This might change on harder difficulties. (I haven't made enough progression to do those yet)Though it seems somewhat weird, the characters can mix things up by equipping a small variety of weapon sets. (rogues can equip spell books, mages can equip melee weapons) However, you can only take two sets with you per mission. You can also upgrade these weapon sets with permanent progression.Though there are complaints that the devs didn't listen to anything during EA, they did make a few significant changes that were especially helpful. I think that they really dropped the ball on tutorials, but if you've played similar games (Gunfire Reborn, RoboQuest) it shouldn't take you long to pick up.There's also complaints of a lack of content. There are only 9 levels and 4 heroes at the moment, but it sounds like the devs plan to continue adding to the game over time.No one that I've played with has had any performance complaints. No crashes. No in-game glitches that have interrupted play. There is a weird visual glitch for some folks that looks like there's a dirt overlay on the screen. A workaround is to set your graphics settings to the LOW profile, (this disables the overlay) then drag the quality sliders where you want them. (devs have stated that they are working on a fix for this as of this review)I recommend the game, but I'm a bit hesitant at the $30 price tag. I'd absolutely buy it again at $30, but I feel that some folks might not feel that there's enough content to be worth it at that price. The Humble Bundle Store currently has a deal for 50% off of a 4 pack, which comes out to $15 a person. At that price, I 100% recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me clarify- This is not a thumbs down, game bad thing, this is a "Steam needs a Middle option for reviews" thing. Because I'm not mad at it, and it's not really bad, my negative review is STRICTLY because I think the price is too high for what they're peddling.This game is "ok", but it's not really a $30+ game at ALL.This is my biggest gripe. This would be a really great option in the $19-$24.99 bracket, you know, where I expect Indie games that aren't quite up to AAA quality to sit. GET IT ON SALE, GET IT ON SALE, GET IT ON SALE. Wait for a sale, it will be worth it on sale. It's real arrogant of these guys to throw it up on EGS for a year, and then bring it to Steam STILL f*cking unfinished, and missing basic coop game options, like voice chat, or a text box, for example. BTW, this game has neither and wants you to use a sh*tty radial menu during combat. This is another example of "just ok".  Actual great games will generally let you talk to other players because they don't have a cucumber in charge of that department.These guys made a coop game where you can't talk to the people you randomly meet, that's not "good". I don't CARE about it, but it's not a "good" design. It's basic af, and only "ok" It's got a great art style and it has some cool features, and IS fun, BUT--it makes you install EOS, which heavily depends on you, because some people are like f*ck epic, and some people aren't, but the ones who ARE, will refund instantly if a game has it. -Sound design is weird and while it exists, it's like a bunch of times i kept thinking, "man, this sound design sure sucks, i can't tell where creatures are at, and there's like a ton of sliders for audio but you really don't need that many, you just need to do a good job at the default settings, which they did not. -hitting barrels and pots gives you money! this is generally cool, but in this game, it's really underwhelming. -there's an overall lack of visual and audio WOW factor. The art design is great, but it's like they're just counting on that to make everything cool, and it doesn't really do it for ME? For example, there's no like special auras around dropped items, or stuff they want to direct your attention to, it just kind of exists in the world, where other games will be give that thing an outline, or make it sparkle a little bit to draw the eye? This does not do that. -They went with a sort of hybrid system of like overwatch skills, and what feels like half-a-vermintide for melee. It's ALMOST really good, but as it is, it's decent and passable. Overall, for me, this sits at around a 6.5 out of 10. There's a ton of room for improvement, and it's even more pathetic when you learn that this game has been out on EGS in early access for about a year now, and it STILL has a bunch of stuff that needs work. I'm going to give some time before fully making my decision. I wish that these reviews had a middle option, but right now i can't thumbs this sh*t up, the price is too high and it's really not much more than, just, "ok"

_childDocuments_.review: I played several hours of the demo, enjoyed the experience at the time and thought it had lots of potential, but upon returning months later for the full game, and only minutes after getting back in to it, much of what I once enjoyed now feels tired, and many of the things I hoped were placeholders are still there, making the full experience fall flat.I really would've loved if this had more varied maps with proper enemy placement and a moody soundtrack instead of feeling like an endless survival mode in copy/pasted prefabs sections. I don't know how to describe it, but it feels like the enemies don't occupy the same space as the location.The roguelite mechanic is easily the worst aspect for me, especially in the form of drawing cards between rounds. Stopping the game entirely to have me make a choice in a hallway between random perks and debuffs instead of designing and balancing the gameplay from the start is just frustrating.It just doesn't feel like it's ready for release, and tests my patience with every step which is a shame because the premise, art style and presentation of this game are everything that I should love. There are some minor multiplayer replication issues (e.g. Victoria's split arrows do not replicate correctly on client side), but all in all the experience was top notch stable and fluent: No crash and no connection loss in any coop run. I mention this, because I read some other player's reviews about "bad servers" of this game, which just makes no sense: It appears to be a peer-to peer-hosting system using EOS, so there should be no connection problems unless the players themself have a bad internet connection. I recommend to play coop on hard to unlock the next difficulties.

Not to mention they laid off 26 of their staff on Sept 19th, a week after this game "released".This game's entire marketing gimmick is that its reminicent of 80s cartoons. But it also plays like its for someone who's not much of a gamer, someone in their 40s or 50s. The game is just.... slow. The overwatch-styled hud will mislead you, its not ANYWHERE near as fast paced or responsive. The game is full of shambling enemies that are effectively walking health sponges. Moving around doesn't feel fluid and dynamic. The powerups are roguelike and kind of interesting but you're really just stuck with your 3 abilities and they arent all that interesting truth be told. The whole game is really just... good on paper poor in play. Almost as if the people making the game are good at... pen and paper games... and not dynamic action games....I played as Maggie the wizard, the only of the four characters marked at 3/3 difficulty. It was not hard, despite somehow at the very start I lit myself on fire and spent the rest of the 20 minutes at 30% hp. No, it was mundane and boring. You start with a fire book as your weapon, and the standard attack is a fire puff. When I say puff, I really mean it, you have to be right on top of someone for it to even hit them. Okay sure, I'll just use the strong attack, charging up a fireball to lob at people. That worked well, outside of the fact that doing this spends your "energy" aka mana aka stamina so the entire time I played, for 20 minutes, was me just slowly charging and lobbing a few fireballs and then needing to wait to restore my energy and lobbing more. The enemies whether skeletal or mushroom in nature, wordlessly appear and shamble forth. Of my three abilities, one was a teleport, a shield, and a summoned bird that acted as a peashooter turret. So basically the next twenty minutes was nothing but slowly lobbing fireballs at walking sponges. It just tells me that there's some clear issues in the game loop and weapon/skill design. When your core game loop feels like you're kind of just existing and swimming through molasses, you have to go back and tune it up.There are some other things that bothered me. I did die once, because a mushroom-person spawned behind me, wordlessly and without sound. Normally in a game there would be SOUND to help you there. Thankfully I was playing with a random who picked me back up. There's no indication on how long this takes for the person on the receiving end, which is kind of basic game design guys. The "tutorial" is just a bunch of popups on your screen with endless "dont show this tutorial again" checkboxes to check. All of which pops up when you first enter a game, so hopefully you share my experience in trying to matchmake and finally land a game only to be standing there for a minute reading and then disconnect from the host. Character selection is also a bit weird, its a neat concept to have all the characters sitting there, but the way they look up at you is super uncanny valley. The loading screen is the mythforce logo with the guy saying "MYTH FORCEEEE!", I am unsure if that plays every time but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I can see that getting annoying.Again, its like the people who made this game are an era behind. It feels like they are too used to pen and paper rules, that they designed all of this in a box and translated that to a game while never sitting down to make it feel fluid and dynamic. It feels like they know how dnd works and how to make a custom campaign and character backstories, but then looked to modern games like overwatch to try to design their game around without understanding anything about gameplay. This is your dad's video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, this is the best of the "Rogue-lite" games my friend and I have played over the last few months! Without a doubt.The campaign is more "on rails" than is Roboquest, but the gameplay itself is the most fun we've had with this game style.You play as one of several "heroes," each one of which has particular built-in perks. Nothing new there. But the various perks are quite intriguing, and, each "hero" has its own in-game dialog that runs and interacts with the other "heroes'" in-game dialog. The net effect is that the game just doesn't take itself seriously, which adds to the fun. 19-hours in, and the running dialog is still entertaining rather than monotonous.For example, the "Victoria" character hits a trip wire and gets herself all corroded. The "Maggie" character, in a deliciously snarky tone, says, "Victoria, did you not even SEE the trap?" And it goes on and on. Back and forth. So far it hasn't gotten old. It probably will, but then it's just background noise.The "lite" part of "Rogue-lite" in this game is a very detailed, intuitive, and fun-to-grind tech tree. There is a "constellation" of four-colors of gems that you acquire throughout each run. You can spend "shields" (another in-game drop) to expand the constellation, opening new drop-points for your gems to enhance weapon-power, crit-damage, lucky-shot, various defenses, power-cool-down reductions, and so on. Cleverly, you can get 10 of a particular gem color and then stack them into a single higher-power gem, so you replace a single gem with a stack. And you can combine stacks (in exponential) fashion three more times (if you have time in your life to gain the many hundreds of gems needed and the millions of in-game dollars). It's an intriguing approach that is satisfying to build out.Of course, you can also level your weapons, which (unlike most such games) this game lets you keep! So, find your preferred weapon combo (you can have a primary and secondary), and then grind to level them.You can also level "trinkets" for both power and drop-frequency, and you can level perks for power and frequency that are granted at drop-stations between each part of an "episode."In short, there's LOTS to motivate you to mine for in-game drops and perpetually level your character, weapons, and chances. It's by far the best of the "tech" approaches I've seen in a "Rogue-lite" game.The story line is about as meh as all of these games. It's a "story" to motivate your pass through a particular run, nothing more. It also motivates some of the running in-game dialog between the characters. Again, meh, but the in-game dialog has enough high-points to be worth having in the game.The weapons are fun to play and feel right. Again, this is something that many games can't seem to manage to get right, but this one does.The balancing and difficult scale "correctly" IMO. "Easy" mode is indeed manageable for even your initial low-level, low-tech characters. "Normal" is a for-real challenge, even with a half-leveled character. We haven't even tried harder difficulty-levels yet, because "normal" is plenty enough of a challenge for where we are in the grind path. So, there's a LOT of replayability here.Co-op works well, with a simple Steam invite. I will say that a couple of times the servers have seemed to have trouble getting us connected, but that's been rare. It IS something you should be aware of, though, because the MOMENT that it becomes more money that it's worth for them to keep the servers up, this game is insta-dead! Remember Loadout, which was great until the moment when it was insta-dead. You are definitely taking a risk with this sort of multiplayer/co-op support. But you'll almost certainly get your money's worth by the time the insta-death happens.This game gets it all right IMO. It's our go-to game at the moment, and that's saying something, given our limited game-time opportunities.

_childDocuments_.review: Notes:- Gameplay consists of procedurally generated room-to-room runs of approx. 30 mins with an upgrade perk after each one.- Combat is fun and distills much of the feel of Tiny Tina's Wonderlands into a tidy roguelike.- There's plenty to upgrade, and plenty to customize about your kit, with different weapon types and favored items.- Stat upgrades are handled by a 'constellation' system where you can slot different types of improvements into different slots. i.e., a combat slot could be fit with a gem to increase physical attack, defense, attack speed, or combat cooldown, while a utility slot could be fit for crit damage, health, total energy, or ult cooldown.- The graphics are kitschy and nostalgic, especially if you grew up watching cartoons from the late 80s.Let's address the feedback on the Steam page first of all. Most of that comes from before the most recent patch that corrected a lot of problems, but it's still a new game with very few reviews, so each individual review will swing the stats wildly. It's not going to win any awards, but it's a fun romp well worth the half-priced (maybe not full priced) admission. I've played with some randos, which went well, but I'll bet it's a blast with friends. It currently supports crossplay between Steam and Epic, though it is available for all consoles. There's definitely room for the game to grow. It feels a bit like a final-stage early access title, but the devs are taking tons of feedback and working to improve it more than it already has.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a full release, the game feels the same (or even a bit worse) as it was during the demo - decent base, but needs some work to get it to be fun. Core mechanics are in place, but content is very lackluster. The need to grind for metaprogression to get decent raw stats and unlock higher tier upgrades made me not want to continue after beating the first major boss. I started 4th level and seen that my character is back to lvl 1 and takes around 10 attacks to kill 1 basic skeleton even after dropping the difficulty to normal, so either I am missing raw stats or it's just normal that enemies become damage sponges, neither of which is fun. Maybe (big maybe) if all metaprogression was shared between characters it would be less painful to grind it out, but in the current state I can't make myself continue to at least finish the whole game on single difficulty. Luckily I received the game for free, because otherwise I'd be rather disappointed even at half a price for the experience compared to other similar games. I only played single player, so multi player experience might be slightly different.- Visuals are nice- Access to both melee and ranged combat with every class- Too repetitive due to lack of room layouts, interesting upgrades (you'll see almost the same perks, weapon upgrades, and items every run), and very little weapon changes- Items are quite rare to find outside of 2 shop rooms per run, and they give such small bonuses at low tier (in demo you could get any tier immediately and felt like they were dropped more frequently. Even then items felt only OK-ish, mostly few generic buffs that aren't too noticeable). Most chests and pots in the rooms just drop gold to be used in those shops that each contain 6 items in total- Higher tier upgrades (perks, weapon upgrades, gems, and items) are locked behind metaprogression which takes many runs to upgrade everything- Most metaprogression upgrades are not shared between characters, so you have to grind them with each character- Difficulty is severely gated behind metaprogression upgrades (I went into 3rd level on hard with "new" character and I did 11 critical damage to the first boss which had 6k HP despite having perk that makes me deal 75% more damage. It took me probably 10 minutes to kill it with the help of environmental fire trap because I had no raw stat upgrades from metaprogression; the run got much more tolerable few rooms after when I got some stat boosts)- Some ability upgrades have buffs only for allies which is disappointing for single player experience

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of negative reviews that point towards the game being slow; I can see if as a solo player in the first level. This game shines with Co-op, it speeds up and the challenge level increases with modifiers that definitely allow you to customize your characters differently every run. It can be a grind and could benefit from a little optimization for sure (looking at you, not shared gold across characters), but we're definitely having fun in this romp through 80's nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the aesthetic and haven't experienced game breaking bugs post-patch (I played during the open beta and skipped out on it after hearing about the bugs post-release). _childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I have 7 hours in this game, and have made it through half the current levels solo normal mode. Thats not to say i haven't tried out harder difficulty. While there are some glitches in the game (Rapid heavy attack abuse, primary weapon fire getting stuck sometimes, targeting with the rush attack) the game-play is interesting. My only complaint is that most of the character ability for the mage just kinda suck. slow fall is useless and is easily outmatched by every other midair ability, the teleport is nice but the cool-down is a bit much, the turret is ok but useless if it ends up missing all the time, and the sheild is underwhelming for an ultimate. Fortunately its not my top character to play. There are some cool things you can do in this game though (Such as using the rouges double jump and a dash attack to mover super quick almost anywhere) and this game is for sure going places.

_childDocuments_.review: I played very little, but I can tell it's one of those "With a party it's better" games. It feels very good, it also needs some polish. The edge detection and the toon shader are really really really good, props to whoever worked on that side.-I would like to see more particle effects, when enemies spawn, when you pick up something and some interactions feel a little tame as well. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: If you want a deepish rpg/roguelike experience go play Barony instead, this is more of a FPS.Honestly, for what it is it's an okay game, but you can't go into it and expecting a dungeon crawling experience like Barony (which is a great roguelike game which I highly recommend).What this is however is more like a FPS which you're supposed to enjoy with friends. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I played a little bit solo just to test it out and had enough fun that I recommended it to my friends. After a 5 hour play session, we all wanted to come back for more. Cons:The lobby/permanent upgrade menus could use a little bit more guidance, it was not completely obvious that the buildings in the background of the lobby were upgrade shops and I think they could use some signage so you don't have to click through them trying to remember what is where.The difficulty jumps up in chunks, you will obliterate enemies in one room and then potentially get slaughtered like cattle in the next.Needs a more room variation per tile set. There are multiple areas in the game with their own aesthetic but within each area it feels like you see the same 6 rooms infinitely.Pros:This is a fantastic co-op experience! Lobbies were easy to set up and manage, we had little to no connection problems.The characters and abilities all feel unique, satisfying and good in their roles.The in game dialogue between the characters is fun and adds a lot of flavor to the game.Do yourself a favor, pick Maggie's ice tome, hold down the attack button, profit.You don't have to pick a different character than your friends which means no one is locked out of a character they want to play but I suggest trying a team of all 4 characters because some of the ability combinations are wild.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game but it just isn't fun or engaging enough to continue playing. Right off the bat I have encountered some bugs that prevented me from attacking. It happens when shooting a bow. I managed to unfreeze my character by spamming abilities and eventually I could use normal attacks.As far as I know with my little time with the game, there is no customisation or perma loot / equipment. Characters are pre-defined which is fine I guess but it would have been better to make your own hero.I haven't seen any inventory aside from character screen and any loot that drops is replaced by a new one. This for me is a deal breaker. A dungeon crawler with no cool loot aside from minor upgrades ( like boots that give 5% more movement speed ).... now I get it it's also a roguelike but this could have been done better. Many games in the genre offer some sort of reward that players can either carry over to the next run or unlock better perma equipment and the starting area. Another minor gripe is the fact that any loot does not show on your character. Moral of the story is : The game is not for me. It may get better but I don't want to go over my refund window so it is what it is.Worst of all : Epic Online Services. Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: Far from perfect but a pretty fun game that manages to be both chill and chaotic at the same time. For negatives: the enemy/player balance feels off like it doesn't scale to the player count, bleeding out and dying is too fast and boring for fewer than 3 players and meta progression is relied on too heavily for loot to start becoming interesting.The game does look great though and when loot gets interesting, it really adds a cool risk/reward element to the game. There's enough content and challenge at the moment to make me want to keep playing. It feels like a game that'll shine if you can get a full group on voice good chat and music playing.We need dinosaurs, voice lines for standard enemies and multiple paths so I'm hoping there's plans for a lot more development. The game really does feel like it was made for 4 players so if you can, I would wait for a sale and try to convince friends to grab the game or split a 4 pack on sale from Humble. You can join or have random people drop into your games but you then run the risk of encountering loot goblins.Good game that just needs friends and some quality of life stuff work!
