_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game up to about the last tier of equipment and about two thirds the campaign, and I can say I mostly love this game. Probably closest in genre to games like Vermintide, but here you play a 80s comic character attempting to tackle the vampire lord Deadalus over nine levels of progressively harder room-by-room dungeon crawling.The graphics, the voice acting, and even the cartoon intro for the game are perfectly evocative of the era the developers lovingly draw from, while still maintaining a surprisingly deep combat system, with cooldowns, stamina management, ultimate abilities, and a soft rogue-like game loop that will have you revisiting some of the same levels for more gold, more upgrade gems, and more unlock glyphs.Which leads to the only real complaints one might have of the game - that you could easily want more episodes to play. Right now the path to a "full build" requires millions of gold and possibly hundreds of gems. While progression early on feels very good, the late game gets a little bit grindy. Hopefully the company is planning more episodes to come.For $30, I felt like I got exactly what I wanted - a love letter to my childhood coupled with a game I could sink a hundred hours into. As a bonus, the company seems particularly checked-in with responding to the game's playerbase and is rolling out patches quickly as bugs are discovered. If you're in the mood for a hack and slash game with rogue-like elements, and the idea of a villain cheesily hamming it up from a balcony before letting his minions take care of you fills you with delight, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is promising but it's lacking in content. For now what I'd like to see are longer more challanging missions. Maybe some kind of holdout mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the premise and art style. If you grew up in the 80s, Mythforce conjures up Dungeons and Dragons, He-Man, and Dragon's Lair (technically a cartoon video game, but still). Comparisons to Gunfire Reborn are superficial at best. The physics and combat in Gunfire are far more polished and responsive. If you are expecting gameplay akin to Gunfire or Borderlands, you will be disappointed. If you are expecting it not to install Epic's Game Store launcher, you will be VERY disappointed (note to devs: you need to patch that out, ASAP). This game does not feel finished, but the potential here is huge. I hope the studio does the right thing and incrementally works at bringing this game into its own. It's poised, just on the strength of the art style, of being at the top of the rogue-like looter-shooter pyramid. In the future, if Mythforce wants to become legendary, it will channel a far-future setting (think Jack Vance's Dying Earth or M. John Harrison's Viriconium stories) and marry it to visuals that will evoke Thundarr the Barbarian without calling down the wrath of IP lawyers.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Brewdog has taken feedback seriously and fixed a lot of issues I had with the game at launch. Big respect :) MythForce looks stunning and perfectly encapsulates the look and feel of 80s action cartoons. Unfortunately, its repetitive gameplay loop, frustrating stamina mechanic, and unrewarding progression system spoil what could've been an exceptional game.There's a treasure chest of potential here and I think Beamdog has the talent to eventually make the game shine, but MythForce doesn't quite feel like a full release yet. I desperately want to love MyhForce, and I'm hopeful that future updates will remedy its flaws

detailed_description: Marvel's Midnight Suns Legendary Edition DARKNESS FALLS. RISE UP! Customize the look of the Midnight Suns team and extend your adventure with the Marvel’s Midnight Suns Legendary Edition! The Legendary Edition includes: - Marvel’s Midnight Suns base game - Marvel's Midnight Suns Season Pass, which includes 23 premium skins available at launch and four post-launch DLC packs The four playable post-launch DLC heroes included in the Season Pass are: - Deadpool - Venom - Morbius - Storm Season Pass Premium Skins available at launch: - Captain America (Future Soldier) - Captain America (Captain of the Guard) - Captain Marvel (Mar-Vell) - Captain Marvel (Medieval Marvel) - Magik (Phoenix Five) - Magik (New Mutants) - Nico Minoru (Sister Grimm) - Nico Minoru (Shadow Witch) - Wolverine (X-Force) - Wolverine (Logan) - Blade (Demon Hunter) - Blade (Blade 1602) - Iron Man (Iron Knight) - Iron Man (Bleeding Edge) - Ghost Rider (Spirit of Vengeance) - Ghost Rider (Death Knight) - Doctor Strange (Strange Future Supreme) - Scarlet Witch (Boss Witch) - Scarlet Witch (Fallen Scarlet Witch) - Spider-Man (Symbiote Suit) - Spider-Man (Demon Spider) - Hulk (Fallen Hulk) - Hulk (Maestro) With the inclusion of the Season Pass, the Legendary Edition lets you keep the pressure on Lilith and expand your roster of Marvel heroes. This extra dose of vengeance includes four post-launch DLC packs, each introducing a new fully playable hero, new missions, new enemies, and more. The Season Pass also includes 23 Premium Skins at launch so you can customize the look of the Midnight Suns team. Note: Premium skins must be used with the equivalent in-game character. Characters may require unlocking through gameplay. Post-launch Season Pass content and the premium skins will be automatically delivered in-game upon release. DLC release timing for post-launch DLC will be revealed at a future date. Terms apply. Marvel's Midnight Suns Digital+ Edition DARKNESS FALLS. RISE UP! Customize the look of your Midnight Sun team with the Marvel’s Midnight Suns Digital+ Edition! The Digital+ Edition includes: -Marvel’s Midnight Suns base game -11 Premium Skins Premium Skins include: -Captain America (Future Soldier) -Captain Marvel (Mar-Vell) -Magik (Phoenix Five) -Nico Minoru (Sister Grimm) -Wolverine (X-Force) -Blade (Demon Hunter) -Captain America (Captain of the Guard) -Iron Man (Iron Knight) -Nico Minoru (Shadow Witch) -Ghost Rider (Spirit of Vengeance) -Magik (New Mutants) Note: Premium skins must be used with the equivalent in-game character. Characters may require unlocking through gameplay. Premium skins will be automatically delivered in-game by 1 December 2022. Terms apply UNLEASH THE DARKER SIDE OF MARVEL When the demonic Lilith and her fearsome horde unite with the evil armies of Hydra, it’s time to unleash Marvel’s dark side. As The Hunter, your mission is to lead an unlikely team of seasoned Super Heroes and dangerous supernatural warriors to victory. Can legends such as Doctor Strange, Iron Man, and Blade put aside their differences in the face of a growing apocalyptic threat? If you’re going to save the world, you'll have to forge alliances and lead the team into battle as the legendary Midnight Suns. With an array of upgradeable characters and skills allowing you to build your own unique version of The Hunter, you will choose how to send Lilith’s army back to the underworld. About the Game Marvel’s Midnight Suns is the ultimate crossover event combining the rich story, character relationships, customization and progression of an RPG with the tactical strategy and combat mechanics of a revolutionary new card-based tactics game. Set in the darker side of the Marvel Universe, you will forge unbreakable bonds with legendary Marvel Super Heroes and dangerous supernatural warriors in the fight against the world’s greatest threat yet…the demonic forces of Lilith and the elder god Chthon. Your Marvel Adventure You are the Hunter, the first fully-customizable original hero in the Marvel Universe. Personalize your appearance, choose your reactions to situations, and build friendships with Marvel legends spanning The Avengers, X-Men, Runaways, and more. Decide who to take with you on missions, which missions to embark on, and a host of other options to make this a unique experience. Fight and Think like a Super Hero From the creators of the critically-acclaimed tactical XCOM series comes an engaging and deeply customizable card-based battle system that rewards clever thinking with Super Hero flair. Deploy a squad of Super Heroes on tactical turn-based missions to thwart the forces of evil. Use your environment, move around the battlefield lining up the perfect shot or combo, and then launch devastating hero abilities to gain the advantage in each epic encounter. The combat leverages the best elements from tactical games and card-based combat in a truly unique and thrilling experience. Live Among the Legends Spend time exploring what Super Heroes do in their off hours. Explore The Abbey—your very own mystical secret base—to discover powerful hidden items and secrets to aid you in the conflict against Lilith and her minions. Befriend and get to really know some of your favorite Marvel heroes as you interact with them in ways beyond the comics or the films.

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK.  Not bad, but not great.First, I didn't play all the way through.  There is a fairly catastrophic bug in the T.H.R.E.A.T. Room, after the second upgrade.  The room is important for leveling up lesser-used heroes, but the bug - which prevents cards from being refunded - makes the room utterly worthless.I suppose that I could just go back to an old save, or spend my valuable time serving as an unpaid play tester, but honestly the game is simply not engaging enough to make the effort.So I guess I'll just call this an expensive waste of time, and move on with my life.So, to summarize:  The game is OK, but extremely repetitive.  Some obvious and game-breaking bugs detract from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after finishing the game. TLDR: Not a terrible game, but a disapointing one, so i'm leaving this as not recommended. Casual, if long, game for casual fans of marvel/superheroes, rather than tactical games.First impressions were mostly correct, with only minor changes. Game is split pretty much 50/50 between narrative portions of "walk and talk" and gameplay combat missions. The narrative portions suffer from mediocre to godawful dialogue and butchering some characters. There's way too much angst and fake drama in everything, the writers treat everyone like quirky teenagers in a soap opera, doing little more than talking aobut their feelings 24/7 while the world is ending. Not entirelly terrible, some characters are good, but major issues here. 6/10. Story narrative is mostly fine. Nothing special but cant complain.Combat gameplay is kinda fun, but in a super simplistic way. Its extremely easy, even pushing the difficulty as far as the game allows, its pretty basic, there's really not that much options or tactics variation. Heros mostly fall into basic categories of "multitarget damage/single target damage/support", with individual gimmicks doing very little to add options or variety. Difficulty also only makes the enemies spongier, the fights longer and more tedious, but not really more difficult. Enemy types are also pretty low for such a long game. You'll be fighting the same 5 hydra goons for 20-30h, though in lategame its a bit better.Some other random things:Visuals are good, especially on the in combat abilities.Game has a ton of cosmetic unlocks, but 99% of them are recolors of the same 2 shirts for most characters. Game is long, took me 60h, and with more sidemissions and other extra content could go to 100h. That's not a good thing imo, the pacing doesnt support that kind of lentgh, many gameplay aspects become really tedious by the end.A month after release technical issues are still there. Framrate sometimes drops 3-4x for no apperant reason. Extrely frequant crashes on going to bed/ending the day. ---Original first impressions:So far:The writting is atrocious, the dialogue is like a edgy "helo fellow kids" fanfic.The main character is unbelievaly boring, and with some of the worst voice acting in any game in years. Voice acting in general very sub par.Combat is a glorified puzzle game with minimal pretend-depth, that belongs on a mobile game. But with great attack animations. No mod support (the absolute best feature of xcom2) to sell the awful looking costumes in the mtx store.But if you're here, you probably dont care about most of that anyway, so here's the important part:Game stutters like crazy and crashes a ton. May be a decent 7/10 eventually, but stay away until they patch it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is a lovely mix of Slay the Spire and XCOM, with less probability to make someone with a 98% hit chance miss. There are so many good things to talk about with this game -- there's amazing writing, there's solid mechanics, and the graphics are literally insane, As someone who loves Marvel and strategy games, this is a major win for me across every angle. Where things kind of fall apart for me are 2-fold. (1) Optimization is abysmal. I'm using a 3080ti, but RTX Ray Tracing will give me 3 frames a second, no lie. The game stutters if you try to use it at any capacity. The fact that some people (not all) are also reporting crashing is wild. (2) There's zero need to try to make your Tony Stark Robert Downy Jr. Why are you? You aren't making Spiderman or Dr. Strange like their counterparts, so it just seems really off-putting to me.If you go in expecting XCOM, you will have a bad day. If you go in expecting something new, with solid mechanics and a TON of play time that doesn't get stale (15 hours so far), I recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. I love Marvel. I love Xcom. I hate Card games. I love Persona. I love this game. Despite not being a big fan of card games or deck building, and being very suspicious of the whole random cards per turn thing, I quickly fell in love with this game. There are flaws, some of which I hope will be fixed in patches, others that are disappointing but not gameplay relevant. - Gameplay: fun and easy to understand. Exciting battles, fast paced, and so far challenging on Normal difficulty. - Story: your typical marvel comics story. Good villains, good teammates. Decent but not earth shattering. - Dialogue: I love it, I laugh a lot at it in a positive way. It reminds me of comic book writing. This is a bunch of super heroes having fun and making fun of each other. - Graphics: hit and miss. Some characters are decent, others are quite poor. Main character for example has a much nicer model than Iron Man who really does look like an average Sims character. In game abilities and animations are great though and you really feel the impact of your powers.- Voice acting: good overall. I would say that those that I dislike the most are characters that are very present in the MCU. When you compare this Iron Man to Robert Downey Jr, it is a negative. On the other hand, Blade and Nico are quite good IMO- Sound effects: satisfying, good.- DLC/Microtransactions: you can get in game currency for some of them. You can ignore the rest. Not even slightly annoying in my mind. Plenty of in game stuff to unlock through gameplay. This is not pay to win. Comments about the game being SJW or woke: sorry, I do not see it at all. This is just normal every day Marvel comics stuff since the 1960s.

_childDocuments_.review: Firaxis has made a part bioware esque/X-com tactical game with card mechanics. It is great. It features a score of Marvel superheroes and you (Hunter - a hero you create yourself). They all live in an Abbey wich surroundings you can explore and pick flowers.A big part of the game is making friends with the very talkative other heroes (all of whom seems to have a rather lot of issues) so they all can level up to help you in the other big part of the game - battling all kind of supervillains and their henchmen.Your hero also have their own issues with his/her mom, wich also is the  big antagonist of the story.It really is a great game - I am right about now playing my second run with all dlc. To bad not a lot of other ppl will ever play it. So, will we ever see a follow-up? Nope! Will we then get some X-com 3 at least? Does not seem that way - and that is a pity because this and X-com 1/2 are about some of most fun I had in the last 10+ years.

_childDocuments_.review: I have such mixed feelings about this game, but I have to ultimately NOT recommend.The combat mechanics are AWESOME with environmental attacks and knockback effects, but there are too many other things wrong with this game.The 2K Launcher is totally dysfunctional and needs to be disabled to get the game to run properly. The camera is janky and sometimes jerks around. There are bugs that will never be resolved by the developers who already moved on. The RPG elements are bland and copy-pasted from games that are more than a decade old. The writing and dialogue ranges from moderately okay to the most awful cringe ever. Some dramatic story moments that could be good are immediately ruined by unbelievably stupid attempts at humor in a stereotypically millennial-esque can't-take-anything-seriously sort of way.Don't spend money on this, especially not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very story driven. If you're expecting a trip down MCU memory lane, you will be disappointed. If you're open to (or are already well-versed) in the comics, you'll enjoy this a lot. The story drives you and there's not a lot of obnoxious grinding. I find the characters to be very engaging and brings me a lot of nostalgia from the animated Marvel series I used to watch as a kid. I'm not a huge fan of turn-based combat and the card thing took some getting used to, but it doesn't take away from the experience. Highly recommended for Marvel fans.

_childDocuments_.review: My second favorite game of 2022, just behind Elden Ring. I loved almost everything about this and I'm not even a Marvel fan. _childDocuments_.review: Marvel Midnight Suns is truly underrated. It's a complete game with full content and no micro transactions. The pacing between the main story, the card battles, exploring the Abbey and relationship building through npc dialogue is enjoyable. This game is pretty solid and unique and deserves a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely and mind-blowingly fun for Marvel fans.Addressing common negative reviews:For the comments referencing the 'cheesy' dialogue - I believe these players may be . The personalities, dialogue, and voice acting all perfectly portray these characters as they are in the comics. Firaxis did an amazing job at doing some of my favorites the justice they deserve. For the comments referencing how skins shouldn't cost real money- these are , so the people that have them already had to pay, you guessed it, real money for the higher game editions. It's  if you only want one or two. I don't think enough people that leave a bad review for this reason understand/know that these skins are part of premium, higher editions of the game.Some personal notes: I do think the female voice actress for Hunter is a bit... stiff. It's obvious she's not bad, but the direction isn't my favorite. Thankfully, her combat dialogue and model are awesome enough for me to overlook it. I'll be doing a Matt Mercer male Hunter run next. Great animations, engaging gameplay both in the Abbey and on the combat field. It's as difficult as you want it to be and as customizable as you want it to be, giving you a lot of freedom to make some crazy team combos. I for one really love to gather everyone up in one spot with Magik and let them taste Ghost Rider's sexy Charger or feel the power of the gd sun with Cpt. Marvel's line-beam-of-doom.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the more I like it. I wasn't really into the super hero genre, and wasn't even familiar with a bunch of these Marvel heroes before playing this game. After playing this game, I'm motivated to go get the Marvel Champions card game (I know it's not the same thing). The socializing aspect of this game between missions (chatting up your allies and getting favor with them) felt like a bit too much at first, but once into the routine, it's a lot less and much more tolerable. You have incentive to do it because the rewards of increased favor include stat increases and new/better combat abilities. The whole game feels a lot like an old school BioWare game like Knights of the Old Republic and Jade Empire, except with card-based combat and some light deck building.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put in ~40 hours of playing the game since launch day and I am really liking it.Edit: After 350+ hours and completing the game, liking it even more.The tactical combat is great and there is enough variety to not get bored with it. The UI is well thought out and you can save games/load games for when things don't work out like you thought they would.  This happens sometimes because interactions can get complicated and there is no "grid" on the play field so you might not get that AOE just like you thought..The RPG in between is a lot of fun as well. I tend to be one of those people who tries to do all or most of the "side quests" but that isn't required of you.  The decisions you make impact things down the road in the story, though I'm not to the end yet.I've gotten a lot of fun out of it and I expect I will get a lot more before things are done.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up for its firaxis xcom pedigree and - as expected - the gameplay really delivers. A pretty unique tactical, turn-based, pinball, beat-em-up all built on top of a pleasantly robust deckbuilder. As a Marvel skeptic I really wasn't expecting to be interested in the "dating sim" aspect of the game but Midnight Suns actually delivers a surprisingly likeable and well written cast of characters that make the weird little platonic dates you go on - and the narrative built on top of it - surprisingly compelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic strategy game. Fun for Marvel fans and normies alike-- the cast of characters in Midnight Suns are likable, varied, and unique. Highly recommended for strategy fans both expert and casual, this game is pretty easy to pick up but hard to master to its fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: After a solid 128+ hours into this neat Firaxis title with main campaign finished, I can thumbs-up Marvel's Midnight Suns (not to be confused with Midnight Sons), but not by a lot. This is not your daddy's XCOM or your sister's Chimera Squad. This here is TCG strategy action with snippets of XCOM elements that kind of make you wish you were playing XCOM2 instead. The actual length of story is not long if you ignore the extra stuff. By "extra", I mean the extensive mind-numbingly long and sometimes awkwardly delivered dialogue in your magical home base called The Abbey. That is where you spend the bulk of this title (better get used to it).When you're not slinging RNG cards at bad guys in the shiny little flat faux-3D playpens the game throws you into, Midnight Suns becomes a character-driven relationship simulator game similar to XCOM: Chimera Squad, but with more fleshed out friendship mechanics and somewhat better writing (albeit with some very cringe moments...I'm looking at you, Nico). I'll let other better reviews talk about the boring technicals and interesting, yet sometimes enormously frustrating gameplay and just focus on the cast:Hunter = generic awkward fish out-of-water heroic avatar for the audience with major mommy issues (found the female to be a little more compelling than the male (Matt Mercer still did a good job tho), also Dark Hunter dialogue adds a bit more spice to the Abbey chit-chat)Blade = grumpy discount Wesley Snipes, also... "YOUR MOTHER!" (best combat line in the game)Captain America = surrogate dad, a walking love letter to classic wholesome golden age comic book mentality that is virtually extinct nowCaptain Marvel = better than Brie Larson (and that's not saying much)Doctor Strange = perfect foil for Tony Stark (their banter is some of the best writing in the game), not as charismatic as MCU Strange, but truer to the old comic book versionGhost Rider = he's alright, not as badass as the MCU version in Agents of Shield, but likableHulk = SMASH (also, Bruce Banner is a ♥♥♥♥)Iron Man = discount RDJ (but in a good way), perfect Dr. Spooky foilMagik = grumpy Russian stereotype, but weirdly likeable and her snarky lines are way more entertaining than...Nico Minoru = insufferable young millennial with annoying combat cards that have long AF repetitive animations (worst character in the game by far)Scarlet Witch = Wanda is decent, but in truth she is quite simply............WASTED POTENTIAL (I think Firaxis dropped the ball with her both in story and gameplay, but still better than MCU Wanda)Spider-Man = very fun and likable as Spidey should be, his friendship with Robbie should make Marvel consider doing live-action or animated crossovers with Spider-Man and Ghost RiderWolverine = iconic chill Canadian war veteran badass uncle-type, too tall (devs clearly preferred Jackman's height), also Steve Blum's voice is back (again...yay...)No thoughts on Deadpool since I won't try DLC content until the full season is released. When all the new stuff is complete, I'll try a New Game+ since I badly need a break from this (the replayabililty is not very strong due to the length and repetitiveness, and also the things NG+ takes away from you such as your cards and first 25 levels not counting the bonus champion levels).Closing thoughts:One thing I greatly appreciated (besides the awkward pauses between lines) was the dialogue tree system. This is not your usual Nice/Naughty/Neutral system like Mass Effect or Dragon Age. It's more like Alpha Protocol (bet you haven't heard that name in a long ass time) where nice or professional responses aren't always the best approach. The writers mixed things up by making each character react differently depending on the topic being discussed. For instance, Magik generally likes dark lines, but I found that often the neutral, and very rarely light choices actually went over well with her.Midnight Suns is worth a shot if you're a big Marvel fan (especially the pre-2010 comics), or just dig that old Sid Meier turn-based thinking-man's game with a little Magic the Gathering flair thrown in. Would NOT advise purchasing at full price, however. Get this one on sale, and for goodness sake, try to play more than two hours before passing judgment on it.Godspeed, Hunters.

_childDocuments_.review: So played for a while (after reading the reviews) and, I have to say, as i often do these days; "I dont know what people are crying about!" - with regards to the game itself, the microtransactions are another thing, we'll get to that.So, long story short: No, this is not a "dating sim", not even sure where that came from! Yes, you can raise/ lower affinity with your team but not sure what that has to do with dating, (there's a lot more to dating, kids!). Possibly because the friendship meter is represented by a heart? i dunno.Also, yes there is a lot of non-combat stuff to do, much of it is actually optional but definitely encouraged. (the abbey grounds are immense!)Not sure what people's issue is with the dialogue, they all seem pretty canonical in terms of their personality. Childish? no. I'd say sometimes puerile but then, I'm 40 and these are broody, mostly teenagers with the odd man-child thrown into a big brother house. I actually enjoy strange and stark bickering, i think they got it spot on with their personalities (particularly stark). And always good to see Cpn. Marvel, my fav character in the mix!All that aside, the game has grabbed me in a surprising way, (i don't play card games at all, usually avoid them tbh!)The battles can be truly cinematic and there is a lot more strategy possible than I initially expected, once you get the hang of the card system and the teams basics. I even don't mind the hunter, seems a decent bit of lore goes with him/ her and there is some customisation possible, though not as much as they'd have you believe, you'll need to dip into the store for that! Yes, that's right! This completely offline, single player TBS with light RPG elements has premium currency! Now if you're like me and aren't really that into cosmetics (the standard cosmetic options are pretty standout actually!) this ain't such a problem, never have and never will suffer from FOMO, but i just don't like the precedent. At least it's just cosmetics to be fair, but some people will go nuts paying a AAA price and not getting everything in the box.Either way, i reckon you could do a lot worse than this, it's a solid title that really scratches my superhero itch, it's immersive character interactions and strategic battles will keep you entertained for many hours and I for one am loving every one so far! 8.5/10 (would be 9 if they'd included Star girl! I mean, she's magical right?)

_childDocuments_.review: In summary, Marvel's Midnight Suns falls short of expectations, delivering a mediocre experience across its narrative, visuals, and gameplay mechanics. While it may not be essential for those who aren't die-hard Marvel enthusiasts, there are still some aspects worth exploring.The gameplay revolves around collecting cards, with each superhero possessing 10 types, except for the main character who boasts 30. Each mission also presents a different objective. Initially engaging, the gameplay loses its allure over time, becoming repetitive. Moreover, the balance of cards leaves much to be desired, with some being overpowered while others feel underwhelming.Where the game truly shines is in its character interactions, both in terms of quantity and quality. The superheroes come alive with banter and humor reminiscent of their comic book counterparts, though some interactions may feel forced.For Marvel fan, this game is a must-have. However, even for non-fans, especially those fond of turn-based tactics, it's worth giving it a shot.🔘 MS-DOS graphic🔘 Ugly, but still bearable🔘 Fine, nothing too fancy🔵 Pretty good🔘 Next gen graphic or art🔘 What is the story?🔵 Written by 5 years old child🔘 Something that'll hook you up with the game🔘 You can remember the story after you finished the game for a while🔘 You cannot get it out of your head🔘 You want to delete it after a few minutes🔘 It's not for everyone🔘 Could be bored after a while🔵 Can keep you entertained for hours straight🔘 It's already morning?🔘 Just mute it🔘 Few of them are good🔵 Not the best, but it's good🔘 You get immersed in the game🔘 Sometimes you will need to stop playing the game to hear it.

_childDocuments_.review: First time leaving a review since I really got hooked on the game. And after reading some of the bad ones and positive, I think I reached a some consensus that people ought to check their system requirements, I am running on a GTX 1660 SUPER, hardly anything impressive and experience no lag or game-breaking bugs. Pros: - Absolutely addictive gameplay. Most of my hours were achieved over the weekend. The card system gets so much better once you get the upgrades going and start to build a solid team composition. The card system actually works amazing, and as a big XCOM fan, I think it is only an improvement as you no longer have to suffer the 95 % hit chance miss. No save-scum needed. - Variety of Heroes. No one feels like they play the same and contribute with a certain talent to the team. The replay-ability is amazing due to this. For instance I ran majorly with Hunter, Captain Marvel and Magik for my campaign, and then I switched it up with different heroes and it felt like a new game altogether. Cons: - Weak story & voice acting. - Friendship grind feels like a chore - Backstory dump on every friendship activity Conclusion: The combat system alone is one of the better I've seen in a while, there are a lot of problems with the game, but that is mostly down to the storytelling and Hunter's voice actor who feels more robotic than anything in their responses. At this point I would probably have preferred a mute protagonist. I have a stark feeling that this will be a much better game next year with more DLCs and story content added. Right now, story is as predictable as it gets. The heavy lore dump is a treat for Marvel Comic fans, but I can see how newer players won't get much excitement out of it and end up skipping most of the conversations. I can say that this is one of the rare games where the combat is the most exciting with it all, enemy types are unique and plenty new ones they didn't show in trailers.

_childDocuments_.review: PERFORMANCE FIX BELOW:First I would like to say that this game is amazing, if I did not have to manually find a solution for the performance issues it would be a home run. That being said I have found some workarounds that essentially completely fixed the performance issues many people are experiencing. I have tested this on both my laptop which runs a GTX1070 and my PC which runs an RTX3080 and it improved both by a large margin. I recommend making all three of these adjustments:1. In the NVIDIA control panel set your VSINC to "on" instead of "let the app decide"2. In the NVIDIA control panel set your max frame rate to the refresh rate of your monitor. My laptop has a refresh rate of 120 so I set it to 120. Simple. 3. Disable the 2k launcher, this is a known issue with the 2k launcher. (Plenty of videos on youtube showing how to do this. Basically it just changes the file path to launch the game directly instead of through the launcherAfter implementing all three of these solutions I can play the game stutter free even on the much less powerful laptop. Hope this helps others because I really enjoy this game and it was a total bummer when it was running so poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: An absolutely outstanding deckbuilder / turn based tactics game with a lot of really hit-or-miss character interactions bolted on (that you can either ignore or click through quickly).(EDIT: I also have completely ignored the DLC. No idea if it is good value for money. And the 'premium currency' stuff bolted on by 2k is just silly. Ignore it.)The turn based combat part of the game is absolutely outstanding. I thought I wouldn't like the randomness of the card draw but it is a lot of fun, making you think up new strategies on the fly and not just relying on the same 'optimal' strategy every turn. In the 46 hours I've played so far, I think I've only been screwed by the RNG just not giving me usable cards once. (And I could have built the decks better.)One thing I like about Midnight Suns compared to XCOM is that it is a move at your own pace game and much less punishing. Don't get me wrong, that sort of feel is essential to XCOM, but here it makes the game feel more like a superhero movie and less 'stressful'. I don't have to be constantly thinking about how a risk might set me back hours in the campaign, possibly even wrecking the campaign.Unfortunately, the rest of the game varies between acceptable and not-so-good. The inability to save multiple decks per character is a bummer and something I really wish Firaxis would have added. The card pool available for characters also feels too small. For example, having different types of quick attacks available to each character so you can tailor their strategy would have been nice. You can do some of that with card mods, but it isn't the same.Hero balance is also a bit of a mess. Just about every guide to the game notes how Captain Marvel is just underpowered. Blade is also let down by how events are resolved; his unique thing is applying bleed modifiers to enemies. Unfortunately, Bleed damage applied *after* the enemy acts. The limited healing options means the overall strategy is not taking damage, but Blade's whole thing is accepting weaker cards/increased setup to in effect give the enemy more opportunities to attack you. The way the game is setup and self-balances means you aren't screwed by using weaker heroes, but then you have a mission where you bring out top-tier heroes and you are like "Oh, yeah, why am I using the other ones again?"The Abbey interactions is where the game really starts to struggle. The Bioware style of conversations and hanging out with characters is very hit or miss. Some are great, like just about anything with Ghost Rider; while some are just boring, like Magik. The quality is all over the place and it is obvious Firaxis was unsure how to approach the thing so they just threw everything at the wall. I'd say the character interactions are most similar in quality to Bioware around Dragon Age Origins or the original Mass Effect.Abbey exploration on the other hand is a combination of tedious exploration and fetch quests. The story is fine. I'm not a huge Marvel person, so I have no idea why people care about the Scarlet Witch so much and hearing her constantly brought up did get grating. The pacing of the plot also feels a bit off. I have no problems with the visuals. I'm running the game at medium on a 7 year old computer that was good when I made it. I have some massive but brief framerate drops when there is loading going on in the background, but nothing more than slightly irritating. The environment design is extremely boring, but thankfully the animations - particularly the superhero attack animations - are great and haven't yet gotten old.Soundtrack is surprisingly forgettable given how good the XCOM soundtrack was. Sound effects are also nice and meaty in combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Strong recommend solely for the core combat gameplay, which is a blast. It's like they took XCOM and replaced the repetitive percentage-based combat variance with splashy deckbuilding variance, sprinkling in fun explosive effects for good measure. This is what genre crossover innovation looks like. You could remove all the Marvel stuff from the game and it would still be fun.The "dating sim" stuff I find pretty tedious. Personally I find all the Marvel stuff played out and tedious at this point, but it's there if it floats your boat. Hanging out with Marvel and friends provides gameplay benefits so it may be worth a bit of effort, but I emphasize only a _bit_ of effort because it's easy to skip all the cutscenes and conversations by mashing the right mouse button.My only complaint is that it stutters once in a while, but I imagine this will be fixed in an upcoming patch.

_childDocuments_.review: - Really awkward camera in battles. - You are rarely given new cards, making the deck combat system less interesting- When you finally do get a card, 70% of the time you can't add it to the deck, because the system is very limited. You can't have too many of the same card or the same type. But most of the cards are garbage. And you can't replace them, just because the cards you do have spares for can't be added. - Very annoying open world. Nothing interesting, but the game wants you to look for garbage loot there. - The game also wants you to look for useless loot multiple times. At some point you unlock an ability that reveals something at specific hidden places, so you gotta go over the whole large boring map again just to find those places. Of course, there isn't any way to mark those places on the map when you find them the first time, so you just forget the exact spot in the samey forest where the small symbol is drawn on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rock.- A bunch of chests scattered around the map. Locked. Taunting you, because you'll never have enough keys to open them. When you do open something though, there's garbage there. This game feels like a mobile game that wants to manipulate you into buying bundles... But it's a single player game. - Very few different cards, meaning there isn't really much creativity or deck building at all. _childDocuments_.review: Weird and clunky animations outside of combat, pretty boring story. Not a whole lot of strategy to this game. The card ability system is interesting but combat overall is not nearly as tactical/challenging/rewarding as Xcom 2. Unit positions and movement are effectively irrelevant. Your dude at the back doesn't have to worry about burning through movement to attack their dude at the back and vice versa, whereas in Xcom 2 movements cost action points and you can't do everything you want.Oh and on that note, no hit probability. Everything hits, no RNG other than random card draws. So combat entirely relies on who you hit first, an attack which you know will hit, no matter where your people are on the map, and the attacks you're allowed to make are randomized. Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of this game. I really like the most of the characters chosen, and I think all are written to match their comic counterparts while also giving (at least most of them) a compelling individual narrative and story throughout the main campaign. The light social aspects of this game may not appeal to everyone, but if you're a Marvel fan you'll definitely find things to enjoy here. While the card based combat didn't sound initially appealing to me, I really came to love the way it worked and creating decks and improving them for each character as the game went on. It added a lot of strategy and nuance to what could have been a more generic action game. The enemy and encounter types add a decent bit of variety, but if you try to grind out maximum friendship and experience with all characters it will probably start to feel a little stale. This game is definitely worth playing all the way through and I really hope we get another game like this from Firaxis in the future, even if it's not a direct sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost; it's a fresh fun single player game with much loved marvel assets made by the people who make Xcom, that also has some quite boring and repetitive parts, along with some unfortunate development decisions. THE CARDS: Going into this game I was well aware that it used deck cards. The deck cards are different attacks, buffs, special moves, draws etc. Each of your party members have 8 cards equipable at a time. You acquire new and duplicate cards throughout intel missions, caches, friendships, leveling up etc. You can upgrade your cards using duplicate cards and essence(a common resource).. I had no issue with using cards in battle. With it being turn based you get 3 card plays and 1 character movement per turn(unless otherwise stated). I liked that you could eventually through Yard upgrades get access to modding your upgraded cards especially with the 'quick' mod allowing the return of a card play when you kill an enemy with that said quick modded card. Thought the cards would get tiring but they fortunately didn't, it kept the game engaging rather than always using a light or heavy attack like a bad button masher. THE ABBEY:Where you end up spending A LOT of the gameplay time in. The Abbey is a plot of land pulled out of spacetime into it's own little pocket. It's maybe ~15 acres. You live here, with all the other playable characters, a dog, a cat, a ghost, and the Caretaker.. You also train daily with the other members, upgrade cards/stations, explore the land, uncover mysteries, gather ingredients, build friendships, design your room, craft, send out intel missions, start standard missions etc. Each day you will be able to do one standard mission from the mission table. Before the mission, DURING THE DAY, you can utilize the abbey grounds doing all previously mentioned things. After the mission you are sent back at the abbey at nighttime where you can only do a few things around the abbey before sleeping and starting the next day: you can still explore, craft, even sometimes hang out with the other characters but not much else so make sure you do everything you need to before starting your 1 daily mission. The missions:you get to choose 3 characters for each daily mission, with one specific character(depending on mission) being required leaving you with 2 other spots to fill. You also get a choice to include specialty consumable items(doesn't use a card play) that you acquire throughout various situations including crafting. Missions are going to be; kill everyone, kill a specific enemy, destroy 1 to 2 specific items, secure 1 to 2 specific items, secure 1 to 2 specific items while killing everyone or a specific enemy, or lastly destroy/disable 1 to 2 vehicles while killing everyone or a specific enemy.. It's a pretty easy chess game after your first few missions you start noticing right away where you need to get your characters in specific spots, and when they should be there to utilize cards, moves, terrain pieces etc most effectively. Never had a character die, doubt many people did either.. Overall I liked this game quite a bit. Put a few hundred hours into it beating it, then played newgame+ just to finish up the 2 still needed achievements to 100% it(which didn't happen). The missions were pretty engaging and while themselves not the greatest challenge I found myself setting my own challenges of how fast and few turns I could finish each mission in. Doesn't benefit you anything other than getting 3 stars which gives you a whopping extra 20 gloss. The abbey however got to be pretty tedious.. They try to break the monotony with all the exploring and mysteries but it doesn't help all that much especially after about day ~25 in game. The stuttering and crashes pretty much got fleshed out the first month with updates while launch commands lets you bypass the 3rd party launcher all together. My biggest complaint and why I can't recommend this game full stop is the DLC.. 2 months into launch DLC achievements started being added to base game owners for individual DLC when it gets close to release. This is unnecessary and predatory. Aside from that, the DLC's seem to be absolutely not worth the asking price either. Deadpool released right as I beat the game right before I could get the last remaining achievement. They want $15 for his DLC which adds literally 2 hours(3 missions). I don't agree with these DLC's at all. Advertised at launch and added that fast just screams that they should have been included as part of the base game and not kept out for a quick cash grab a couple months later. For the four characters they're drip adding you are expected to pay an entire second games price.. TLDR; If you just want the base game and don't care about finishing the steam achievements or getting the worthless DLC, BUY MIDNIGHT SUNS WHEN IT GOES ON SALE. It's worth $39.99

_childDocuments_.review: "Marvel’s Midnight Suns” stands out as a strategic gem that may not cater to all gamers but certainly shines for those who appreciate depth. The game boasts a rich array of mechanics, allowing players to craft unique decks for their heroes that align with personal playstyles—be it defensive, offensive, or specialized roles like healer or tank. The strategic layer extends to environmental attacks and difficulty-based challenges, ensuring a dynamic gameplay experience.Initially, the game may seem monotonous, but as you delve deeper, it unfolds new adversaries, formidable bosses, and intricate layers that captivate your attention. After a month of play, I’ve completed just the first of three chapters, indicating a substantial content offering. As my skills improved, I found myself breezing through missions, thoroughly enjoying the immersive experience. Visually, the game is a marvel, especially when played on maximum settings.However, there are aspects that might deter some players, and I’d like to share these from my perspective:1) Excessive Dialogue: Post-mission, the protagonist, The Hunter, engages in extensive conversations with other heroes at the Abbey, the game’s headquarters. These dialogues influence the light and dark balance points, affecting friendship levels. While integral to the narrative, the sheer volume of dialogue can become tedious, even for a self-proclaimed nerd and Marvel enthusiast like myself.2) Mandatory Day and Night Cycles: The game enforces night-time activities at the Abbey following each mission. While these free-roam tasks add variety, they quickly lose their charm after several repetitions. The routine of sleeping, researching, and engaging in activities before embarking on the next mission feels unnecessarily drawn out, detracting from the game’s pacing.Despite these critiques, my overall experience with “Marvel’s Midnight Suns” has been positive. The game’s strategic depth and stunning visuals have provided me with many enjoyable hours. I rate it a solid 7 out of 10, acknowledging that while it has room for improvement, it remains a commendable addition to any gamer’s collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Few important bits at the top (no spoilers)-I had no bug/crash problems-I played for free during a weekend event, but won't be buying it-I've played the modern xcom games, the combat is very different-I have a moderate amount of marvel comic knowledge7.5/10 overall~~~~~~~~~~~~~~::Some positive notes::This game is pretty good and will take many dozens of hours to complete. There are a moderate collection of heroes that you get as you play the main story. Each hero has various moves that have the correct aesthetic for that hero.  Most levels are puzzle like, knocking the enemies around in the most efficient way possible, ultimately trying to create combos and chain reactions. Some of the combos are reeaaally fun.The characters were pretty accurate, with a few deviations for creativity.There are many many nods to marvel comics and movies, some I felt were a little forced and some were delightful.The base (open world) is really big, lots of nooks and crannies, filled with hidden things to find, and things you'll have to come back for later (metroidvania like)Your character runs really fast, and there is also fast travel while at the base There are so many consumables in this game. They are meant as situational "get out of jail free" cards. I mostly ignored them.There are also many collections in this game, some were pretty cool, like the stylized marvel tarot cards, others were interesting journal entries by the main characters.There is an in depth favor/affection rating throughout the game, and a light/dark side system. I never maxed these out, but they were interesting enough that I cared about getting them. It's not as obvious as other games, ultimately it was a good part of the game, although unnecessary (you can ignore it, though you will miss some good perks) ::Some negative things::Things got a little repetitiveYou can't turn off animations...They are animated really beautifully in some cases, but I feel like it really pads the playtime. You can skip some dialogue lines, but during a cut scene, you can only skip the entire video or none.Some heroes have more impact than others. Unfortunately for every mission the game forces you to use one specific hero, sometimes a specific whole premade team.Sometimes you are left with just fighting the boss. Slapping each other until they die (boring).Periodically the game suggests you increase the difficulty. Every time the game suggested this, I did increase it (a little easy).The card collection/TCG aspect of the game was lacking. Perhaps in the first 12 levels there is not much customization, or perhaps I saw all there was. I was not able to look through a champs available deck and trim excess/build a new style.You have to play with heroes even if you don't like their moves or their personalities. (Tony Star, Dr. Strange, Spiderman)There are too many currencies: dozens of plants, Several different essences, credits, intel, keys, gifts, artifacts, gloss and possibly a few I missed. There are ~5 "essences" that are used to upgrade cards. This seemed arbitrary and could have just been 1 resource (card dust, etc)Everything out of combat is somewhat like daily quests/time management sim. You start your morning, pet your dog (+affection), check research (base upgrades), open boxes to get new cards (coils), then open more boxes (pyramids), check your spec ops mission (away missions), open more boxes (intel for spec ops), collecting any glowing orbs that appeared overnight, buy the new gift shop item, upgrade any new cards, daily training (affection+xp) then run around and talk to each person who has a new conversation (shown on the map, easier than it sounds). After everything is done, you take a mission, either general or story, complete it, then the after dark events happen, such as: hangouts, club meetings, old god challenges, more exploration, and conversations, then sleep, repeat.The DLC, as far as I can tell, are parts that were purposefully left out of the game to make more money later.tldr~~~~~~~~~Overall I thought it was fun, but I was left really wanting to play Xcom or playing Marvel Ultimate Alliance instead.If I had more time, I would continue to play all the way through, but I was not hooked enough to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, but I can't see any reason to re-play it. _childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns has managed to achieve the dubious feat of being a bad game that somehow salvages a shred of enjoyment through its combat system. While the fights are undeniably fun, the rest of the game is a mess of poor decisions, infuriating design choices, and an overall lack of understanding of what makes a game compelling.Let's not beat around the bush – the narrative is an absolute dumpster fire. The plot feels like a half-hearted attempt to shoehorn a player-created character into the Marvel universe, resulting in a cringe-worthy protagonist that nobody asked for. The story lacks depth, coherence, and any sense of urgency or stakes. It's a haphazard mishmash of generic demon-hunting tropes with Marvel crap thrown in.The character interactions are cringe-worthy at best, with dialogue that seems like it was written by a child. The attempts at humour fall flat, and the forced camaraderie among the heroes feels like a desperate attempt to replicate the success of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.Now, let's talk about the graphics and animations – a disappointment on every level. The environments are bland, uninspired, and lack the vibrant energy that should be inherent in any Comic game. Character models are a mixed bag, with some looking passable while others appear like poorly rendered knock-offs. The facial animations are downright atrocious, with characters displaying the emotional range of cardboard cutouts.In conclusion, Marvel's Midnight Suns is a hot mess that somehow manages to salvage a modicum of enjoyment through its combat system. But don't be fooled – the frustration, disappointment, and sheer incompetence displayed in every other aspect of the game make it a hard pass for anyone expecting a worthwhile gaming experience. Save your money for something that respects your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is a mix of turn-based tactics and deck building with a hefty dose of RPG relationship-building.The game is quite long if you want to do everything and it has the same affliction as an XCOM game. The one that keeps telling you that you can afford to do just one more thing before you go to bed.I had a good time with the combat, with each hero having their own playstyle and role. I regret, however, that there are no unique animations for specific hero combinations when they do their team-up attacks; you just see one hero attack, then the other from the other side, never appearing in the same shot.Running around the abbey and hanging out with heroes while they relax between missions reminds me of Xavier's Mansion in X-Men Legends. _childDocuments_.review: Disregarding the performance issues since those have been whined about to death in other reviews...What this game is, in a nutshell, is a tiny indie card game with millions of dollars of budget thrown at it. The actual gameplay is the same kind of thing you'd get in a £5 roguelite card game. The rest is endless cutscenes, minigames, exploration mechanics, multiple crafting systems, research systems, and so on and so on. There's even a friendship mechanic similar to old JRPGs. So far I've played for a little over 5 hours and have spent less than an hour of that playing the actual card game.I want to be clear that no individual part of this game is bad. The voice acting is middling, the card game is serviceable (if very simple, probably to appeal to Marvel fans rather than card game fans), the graphics are pretty, music is solid, and each of the minigames and sub-mechanics are solidly implemented, even if none of it is particularly innovative or interesting. The trouble is, this is basically another 'Spore'. It's a bunch of minigames taped together to try to disguise the fact that there is no actual core gameplay experience worth talking about. Nothing is fleshed out enough to be considered a central gameplay mechanic. What this absolutely IS NOT is anything even vaguely like XCOM, despite what a lot of the press suggested. This is about as far from XCOM as you can get.I'm recommending on the basis of every individual piece being fine, but it's extremely tentative. If you're looking for any kind of in-depth gameplay, or value for money, or you're not really a Marvel fan... avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent superhero battle game.  It works best if you liked games like Three Houses or Persona 5 where half the game is the combat and half is the social simulator aspect, but the Abbey is still largely skippable if it doesn't interest you as much.Combat revolves around attacks, support, and heroic cards.  Attack and support cards build heroism while heroic cards or environmental attacks spend it, so balancing what you've got available keeps you in a good place.  The game won't allow you to make decks that are _too_ unbalanced, so you're encouraged to experiment.  Heroic cards are basically just 'better' attack or support cards, and both types of cards have a lot of different things they can do even if attack cards largely deal damage and support cards largely don't.Each hero has a distinct flavor and personality and basically all of them are interesting, there's a lot of options with deckbuilding but also the decks are small at 8 cards per hero so it's not going to overwhelm anyone who doesn't like decks, and the storyline is interesting.  The writing style is very comic-book, many quips at the start although it gets more and more serious as things go more and more south in the world.  If the jokey nature of the beginning missions is offputting to you it doesn't stay like that.  However, I personally felt that everything exuded the comic book feel I was expecting and all the voice actors do a great job in their roles.Combat is largely flexible to be as hard as you want it to be, the harder you make things the more you're going to have to synergize and build decks that work with each other since your heroes will go down in 4-5 hits.  I found Heroic 1 a nice balance of fun without things being trivial, but you could push it to Heroic 2 or 3 probably if you're looking for a decent 'hard' mode.  While there are some potential quibbles about not having enough plays to set up good combos except if you get lucky, the nature of the game forces you to switch up your team constantly which gives things a lot of variety.With the DLCs purchased, I enjoyed their missions but it did remove some desire to try to 100% all the friendship stuff since there's more heroes to deal with.   Thankfully, all that stuff is optional.  The game dragged perhaps a few hours longer than its content could manage, but not so much that it felt dreary.  It was about the time I got the 'hey it's the final mission so finish up what you want' that I was ready to be done, so that's about perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Great game, addicting if you love strategy and Marvel. Characters are accurate and the gameplay is especially fun if you turn up the difficulty every time it gets to easy.Cons: Denuvo, overpriced DLC (with too little content, 3 missions is very short for $20 each), crashes a lot even on DX11, the dialogue is like Fallout 4 both in the sense that your choices don't mean what you think they'll mean and they have little to no impact on the story at all.It's a shame this game underperformed, but at the same time it seems like most of that is because of the publisher. The game came with Denuvo without reporting it until the last minute on Steam, it had stuttering issues because of the 2K Launcher, it was poorly optimized, was marketed as XCOM with Marvel heroes but turned out to be a card battler (still great but that should've been more clear), and it didn't help that it almost seemed like this was going to be a replacement for XCOM 3.

_childDocuments_.review: One review called this "the best superhero game to date" (or something along those lines). I thought that was a bit of an exaggeration, but after playing it for 100 hours (and counting), I'm much more inclined to agree. I AM pretty sure it's the best superhero game belonging to a pre-existing franchise. It's a more fun, more entertaining, but less tactical XCOM 2. The writing is phenomenal, and it boggles the mind how much of it I'm missing--you'll likely NEVER exhaust all the various dialogues you can have with each of the heroes. Not having grown up with the comics, the version in my mind of these characters tends to be the MCU one, and I really appreciate both when they hewed close to those, and when they differed. I actually prefer Midnight Suns' version of Captain America, Blade, and Storm, and I may have a new favorite Peter Parker (but you're probably safe, Andrew Garfield.) I'm getting close to wrapping up the story, but the game lets you follow very much at your own pace--I could, I suspect, do side missions for the rest of time. There's been enough variety that, even though mission objectives repeat, they haven't (yet) felt repetitive. In short (ha!), 100 hours that have not felt AT ALL like 100 hours. Play it and see for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, bought the Legendary as a Pre-order. I have had ZERO issues so far. None. Not one. I don't know what the issues are but it's clearly hardware or your settings or your internet connections. I am running my game on Epic at 4k from a very high end SSD drive with a 3080 Ti video card. Flawless performance since install. Even with Steam and the 2k Launcher both running in the background. Don't blame the game.Now, hopefully there will be much more tech savvy posts/patches to resolve your particular issues but this game is beautiful, engaging, easy to learn and impossible to master. Graphics are stunning, fully voiced characters with dialogues that had me laughing-smiling-cheering-tearing up since the first two minutes. Puzzles, mysteries, collections, exploration, special side quests for idle heroes, three separate crafting systems *so far*, and even two pets! And you want customization? ..this is your Nirvana. Your clothes, your companions, your eyes, your weapons, your face adornments, your room, hell even your bed sheets and drapes are all fully customizable with hundreds of combinations. Hundreds.It's the best game I've bought or played this year. Period. Full stop. Worth every penny regardless of what edition is right for you.*Addendum after 40 hrs played and the 25G patch applied one week post release: THIS IS THE GAME OF THE YEAR if  you love RPGs, Marvel Heroes and/or Turn-based combat. Bar none!*

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended when on sale for half off or better only.This is a very good and very simple 'puzzle combat' tactical game.... under layers of mobile and AAA-chasing dreck. The actual missions are quick and enjoyable, and the story is a fun and slightly lighter take on the Midnight Sons/Suns comic runs. The new hero/heroine fits right in in the spooky side of the Marvel universe, depending on how willing you are to retcon the villain Lilith.Sadly it's got frustrating time gating, tedious materials collection, and a rather pointless open world aspect that all feel like remnants of some other game. I'm probably glad it's not that game -- the open world portion has chests that drop randomized cosmetics and power-ups that were likely designed to have lootbox cash shop keys rather than the in-game key system we actually got -- but it's still mostly worse for their inclusion given the fairly simple lightweight nature of the underlying tactical game. The net feel is of a mobile game trying to parrot triple-A trends at the minimum possible depth.A tighter focus probably could have released this as an uncritically delightful double-A title for less development cost and at half the initial price... which is about where I'd recommend buying it.Given the open-world and collection elements a part of me wishes they'd made this as an attempt at an iso-hack-and-slash, a solo revival of Marvel Heroes. All that tedious real-time travel would make a lot more sense in that kind of game, and there's definitely a contingent of us who miss the brawler superhero genre. If you're listening, 2K/Firaxis and license-holders.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game enough. I could go on for hours about the loving and fun treatment that each included member of the Marvel family gets, their sincere inclusions and contributions to the story, the enjoyable simplicity and yet complexity of the combat, the beauty of the visuals, the quality of the voice acting, and more.I could talk about the enjoyment to be derived from solving the mysteries of the Abbey when not off fighting Hydra and demons. I could discuss the satisfying friendships you can develop with every playable character, or how stat bonuses and other side-quest rewards are neatly tied into that system. But I'll keep it brief.PROS:- Nuanced and interesting combat system, easy to learn, hard to master- Nearly a dozen difficulty levels, from 'mind-numbingly easy' to 'punishingly impossible', and everything in between. Tailor your own experience!- YOUR OWN PET DOG (SHE IS A HELLHOUND :D) - and YES, you can pet the dog, praise and play with the dog, as well as take her exploring (she will alert you to hidden things nearby!) You can even pet the black cat that roams the Abbey- Main character is fully customizable, morality system is interesting but not overblown or obnoxious. I've only used the female one, but I really enjoy her voice acting.- Upgrades, research, item crafting, artifact hunting, 'side missions' you can send lesser-used heroes on for rewards (including cameos from the Thunderbolts, Defenders, Agents of SHIELD, and more) - there is literally so much in this game, all of it completely optional, but all of it generally well-implemented and adding to the experience- The humor is generally very on-point, I laughed more in the first 10 hours of this game than I have at the last 10 years' worth of Marvel movies, even when those movies were TRYING to be funny.- Tons of optional cosmetics, from room upgrades, to outfit changes, for both your character and the other heroes. This includes both in-battle and 'relaxing' outfit choices, and palette changes, all of which is purchasable using in-game, easily-earned 'gloss' resources.- Tons of antagonists, villains and supervillains throughout the story, unexpected twists and turns, but no forced time-pressure- New Game+ option that lets you bring over all unlocked heroes and use them from the start of the story, especially good for those few you only unlock near the end of the game- And more!CONS:- Gathering 'reagents' (crafting resources) by hand, around the Abbey, night after night, gets very tedious by 100+ hours in. All crafting recipes need to be found, and they are EXPENSIVE!- Cosmetic options for 'in-battle' costumes are strangely limited, and every character has one 'paid' or otherwise locked outfit. Otherwise you're stuck with palette-swapping their original outfit, several of the palette swaps just look bad. (Though plenty of them look good!)- Every hero has an 'ultimate Midnight Suns' outfit you unlock when you reach level 5 friendship with them and do their challenge mission, but several of these outfits have glowing flames in really, REALLY dumb-looking spots (whose idea was it to put a single flame in the center of Captain America's shield, or give Captain Marvel a single flame atop a metal mohawk?) - you can 'turn off' capes for your character's outfits, but you can't 'turn off' these frankly awkward flames.- While the game has nearly a dozen systems I find fun, almost none of them 'interact' with each other (witch's cauldron, item crafting bench, character side-missions, etc) - which can make them overwhelming to a casual player, and you get basically thrown at all of them so you'll know they are there.- Cosmetics purchased with in-game (non-money) currency don't carry over to New Game+. Neither do crafting components/reagents, or character bonus stats.- Not all characters are equally-usable, some are SEVERELY gimped or outright useless on higher difficulty levels due to enemy HP creep. This can also apply to post-game high-level missions.- The ability 'customization' or 'mods' system is RNG-based, which can also become very tedious very fast. However, playing on higher difficulties basically requires using this system for each character, which means spam-rerolling 'mods' for EACH INDIVIDUAL CARD at steadily-mounting, ludicrous costs in resources.- Research tree just kind of 'ends'... it doesn't much feel like the last research options available are endgame-level 'tech'.- You MUST come in with a tolerance for 'imperfect' characters - characters who are set in their ways, or full of themselves, or that just plain make mistakes and act out. Marvel heroes are flawed, and they are faithfully-depicted as such here. If you can't stand characters who may not like each other or who make realistic mistakes, you won't be able to stomach the story.- Still some bugs and glitches, especially after the DLC patch. Plus, some sidequests can be bugged ('Hang out with X character after a mission', but you don't get any hang-out options with ANYONE for a week in-game, that sort of thing.)- Some minor other gripes.Tl;dr: Do you love Marvel? Have you been disappointed with the quality of Marvel moves in the last 5+ years? Do you really wish you could just immerse yourself in the world and go on an ADVENTURE with a bunch of Marvel heroes? Then play this game, and do it. This game is a love-letter to Marvel fans, and, in my opinion, amazingly captures the bombastic action of superhero team-ups in tactical XCOM-style combat.It is a game with oceans of heart and soul, and I haven't finished with it after 100+ hours. It is worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin? The Good: The combat is so much fun and amazing. It feels good and it looks good and it satisfies that itch we xcom lovers have, but in a new different way. Its refreshing to see something different combat-wise and have it not feel so drool. I feel challenged when I enter a combat scenario and I have to spend some time thinking and plotting out my moves based on the cards I was dealt. The graphics look AAA tier and the animation is candy to my eyes as my laptop overheats. The music is also another plus in this game, it fits the game well. The Bad: Unfortunately there's a lot. Not enough to make me refund the game, but enough to question the direction this game MIGHT be heading and wither to justify the cost for the game. Like others have said.... The dialogue, my god the dialogue. It would be different if they had better things to say... but my god what a slog to get through. I skip it every chance I can get. The Marvel dad jokes are getting to me as well. its hard for me to stay immersed and take the characters seriously with all the impudent comments they make. "The homeowners association isn't going to like this" -D.r Strange in reference to his 19th century wizard house. The ultimate reason i'm giving this game a thumbs down and I will do this for every game that does this.... Yes, the monetization... In a single-player none the less. Who am I going to show off my cosmetics too, My cat? My girlfriend? Both would leave me if I ever bought any cosmetics in this game. Lastly, thank god they didn't make it to where you had to buy this... they have (Loot Box like feature in this). Thank you to which ever developer stood up and said no to this. because you know the suits at marvel wanted to have loot boxes in this game. If you are reading this review and you love gaming no matter what generation you grew up in. Have some self respect and put your foot down to this kinda of monetization. We all deserve better.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a game we did not wanted but very much needed. This games deserves better than Mostly Positive for sure. It is the best and most fresh game I personally played in the last 2 years. I give it a solid 8/10. People who are expecting yet another Rogue-Like card builder or a x-com clone should stay away from this game because even though it looks similiar on surface , deep down in game design there are massive differences. And , this is NOT a RPG, you cannot "create your own hero" and choose powers from a set of 100s. You have some leeway with the gender and appearance but the character's story and his/her powers is mostly rigid. Which is the right choice to tell a good story.Many of the negative reviews I read make me face palm, as they barely scratched the surface with 5 to 10 hours or rushed the game to the point they are literally not engaging with 80 % of the game. Besides many complaints are about overpriced DLC ( which you absolutely do not need to buy ) or about technical glitches of which I encountered a total of zero in 100 hours. I rarely defend any game in steam but here the hate is absolutely not warranted and the fault is here with the customer not the game. Most of them are probably from salty misinformed day-1 purchases.--- Combat ---It has tactical combat which plays akin to x-com series, on top, it utilizes a deck Building system for the abilities of your heroes. What is different in Midnight Suns though is it does not share the urgency and danger of a x-com campaign. You do not permanently lose your heroes. Which makes it a very different - and better in my opinion - experience. That is why I do not think people who want another hardcore x-com experience will like this game. Similiarly card system is not there for you to make a vastly different build. But rather it enables you to change your heroes skills slightly to better suit your composition and spice up the combat by familiar card-battle mechanics. For an example you cannot make Blade to be a Support character as much as you try, his main focus is DPS. This is why I also think that people who want a solid TGC or a Rogue-Like akin to Slay the Spire should tamper their expectations. ---Exploration---Missions are separated into story missions and side missions which you can do in your own pace. That is crucial for the game does not force you to do something in X days , so you can take your time to level your heroes with side missions, build up and explore the abbey (your base) , and connect with the residents.The abbey and its surroundings is masterfully crafted and has it's own meta exploration mystery, in which you try to unravel the past and the backstory. You progress through this via a metrovid-style skill blocked progression system which assures you do not burn through all the exploration in 1 night. Even after 100 hours I am still not finished with exploration. And I was very thorough. The collectible Books and Lore is actually relevant to the main story which deepens your understanding too why is all this happening. ---Social System---The social system in place -which does not deserve the hate it recieves-  enables you to build up friendship with the resident heroes and unlock better skills and synergies with them. There is tons of well voiced dialogue in this game. After 100 hours I am yet to hear a dialogue repeat itself. Is it sometimes cheesy and emo? Well yes, but this comes with the Comic territory. That is the quality you can expect. People who are complaining that the dialogue is bad probably never read a marvel comic in their lives and are here to complain because they watched an Angry Joe review. (who actually liked the game).Yes the social system is not Persona, but it is better than your average banter system they slap into each game nowadays. It actually reminds me of Bioware games of old. ---Story---Story is actually good for a Marvel IP. I would consider it at the same level as the story of any avenger movie. At the end of the day it is a comic story and is not made to compete with Elden Ring or a David Lynch script. But it has enough action, cheese and ups and downs to be better than anything MCU is producing in Phase 4. Yet again, I cannot comprehend how people can hate the story of this game , it is as solid as any DC Arkham game. ---Technical---Graphics are very good , and game never dips below 60 frames (borderless v-sync) with my 3080. It definitely feels polished and never ever crashed in 100 hours. I encountered 0 bugs, be it in the UI or in Animations, which are top-notch. Effects are spectacular. Soundtrack is well done and integrates itself into the game well enough. I cannot confirm any anti-cheat software reducing my Framerate in any way. Again the complains here should not be taken seriously. Just don't try to play the game with a potato.---Cosmetics---Game also has tons of cosmetic options which are unlocked via chests scattered around the Abbey and its surroundings, via social interactions or directly available to purchase with the in-game currency. I saw a premium currency in the inventory but never seen a shop for it, and did not ever had the need to buy anything because I am yet to unlock all cosmetics I saw. Even If I would like to spend some cash , which I never do, I would not now where. The game does not promote its in-game store to the point is is only available in the main menu. Once you are in the game you cannot even access the marketplace! I am not saying that MTX is good but Midnight Suns keeps it to meaningless cosmetics an hides it away. ---Conclusion---I did not have any expectations for the midnight suns and was positively impressed by it. I am playing nothing else than this game since I picked it up and I immediately fell in love with it to a degree that I am looking to do a second run with a female Character. After 100 hours I was literally feeling dread because I thought the game will end soon but instead of a end-game cutscene I just progressed into the act 2. I sincerely believe that the game deserves better. This has the potential to be a very good franchise.
