_childDocuments_.review: Word on the street is that Midnight Suns is a critical success but a financial flop... so what gives?This game is a fried ice-cream banana sandwich. You like all the ingredients... but they aren't exactly what you expect.Truly a not so hidden gem and worth picking up. Somewhere between XCom, Slay the Spire and Fire Emblem 3 Houses with a cast of Marvel Characters brought to life by all star voice over work.     *Yes, Critters --> the male main character is voiced by Mercer and the best member of the Midnight Suns (Magik) is done by a Russian Laura.*But you said XCom, Slay the Spire and Fire Emblem 3 Houses? Those are three things that probably don't blend I mean, yeah, it's an acquired taste... but the gameplay loop does get there.You have a lot (and a mean a lot) of slice of life interactions with the characters that reminds me of various jRpgs and aRpgs. You build friendship (???) with the marvel heroes through these interactions and this can effect combat?? Some of it does fall flat... but other stories really shine. I didn't know I needed to attend a book club with Blade, Captain Marvel and Captain America until... well... I attended the book club. Or how Tony Stark is a complete oversensitive dolt who can't help but offend the younger heroes of the Midnight Suns... and don't get me started on Magik's story. If anybody lays a hand on my little sister there will be limbo to pay.Each hero has a deck of cards that you upgrade and build on as the game progresses. The card battling element is truly enthralling. They did an excellent job making each hero feel and play differently. They each have at least one unique mechanic. Niko has random Roulette, Ironman loves ironman cards, Blade makes things bleed... They are not incredibly well balanced but you can clear the game with any of them.Right, the xCom influence can be felt in how you gear up your squad and mix and match your squad. When going on missions you'll pick 3 heroes and play all three of their decks shuffled together. This pushes you to find combos between the heroes. For example; Wolverine enjoys multihits and Doctor Strange can buff base attack so they combo. Or Niko reduces the cost of expensive cards so you can combine her with a hero chock full of expensive finishers.All in all I had a blast on both my first playthrough (pre-dlc) and my return to the game (after I bought all of the DLC). If you do pick it up; don't do too many sidemissions. The game lets you continue to run sidemissions as much as you want. Yes yes, sometimes you need to take some time off from the story but if you over level too much it drains the fun out of it. Finish the game with at most 2 sidemissions between each story mission and you'll thank me later. New Game + or barelling on after finishing is a better outlet for your desire to upgrade every card and get every ability.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the more fun Marvel games I've played in quite a while, it brought back a bit of the fondness I had with X-Men Legends and Ultimate Alliance.It is not without it's faults, but it offered something new in terms of a Marvel property, and fun gameplay taking a novel mix of tactical turn-based combat, deck building and role-playing character interactions that impact gameplay; which you could consider a pseudo amalgamation of X-Com, Slay the Spire and Persona.Sadly, it didn't sell well enough and was abandoned very quickly a year into release, despite this it is still worth playing, but there are a few things to be noted and areas of lost potential.The PC port has issues, from the launcher to the two most notably being a potential game-breaking bug in a later mission making the mission unwinnable due to changes brought about by the DLC, that will not get fixed. While there is a work around with in-game items or by playing on a lower difficulty, there is no warning for this issue. Additionally, for those who want to 100% the game, one of the later game outfits is bugged out, and has a very high chance of just not appearing when unlocked, with no other way to obtain it without mods.These bugs will not be fixed as the game was abandoned post DLC, which brings another issue forward, the lost potential.The endgame credits and DLC all build to a future event, DLC story expansion or new game. Which sadly will never appear, with Dr Doom, Dracula and Mephisto playing a role in the build up and potential story, it is a very unfortunate loss.On a personal level, my main complaint comes from the character roster. Simply, too many characters don't fit and are obviously there as marketing elements. A fantasy/horror game that relies on the Avengers over Marvel's untapped horror characters is unfortunate.I understand they help to entice potential customers, especially as characters included are now well known via the MCU, alongside long standing fan favourites like Wolverine and Spider-Man, are at the forefront. They just feel out of place.An argument can be made for Hulk and Venom with their ties to the One-Below-All and the King In Black, but the others are an even greater stretch from Captain America's werewolf period and history with Dracula, Spider-Man with the Spider Totems, and maybe Deadpool and his history with Death (although Deadpool as a character is very oversaturated, much like Wolverine).This could have been resolved with other DLC characters, but losing slots to Captain America, Captain Marvel, Wolverine, Spider-Man, Deadpool, Iron Man, and Hulk was a bit boring.We got a nice bundle of magic and horror characters as playable with Storm, Magik, Blade, Ghost Rider (Robbie Reyes), Scarlet Witch, Dr Strange, Morbius, and Nico; alongside cameos, Easter eggs and references to others like Man-Thing, and Johnny Blaze's Ghost Rider.But it would have been great to see others join the lineup, give lesser know but fun magic and horror characters the chance to be seen and know, build their fan bases and open them to a new audience; with interesting styles of gameplay and designs, we could have seen Agatha Harkness, Kushala, Man-Thing, Juggernaut, Daimon Hellstrom, Jericho Drumm, Wiccan, the Ancient One, Shaman, Wong, Rintrah, Clea, Elsa Bloodstone, Werewolf by Night, Captain Britain, Pixie, N'Kantu, Simon Garth, Shiklah, Sleepwalker, and Manphibian, etc.Even additional antagonists like Baron Mordo, Enchantress, Morgan le Fey, Doctor Doom, Dormammu, Selene, Nightmare, D'Spayre, Malekith, Loki, Kulan Garth, Moridun, the Black Tide, Morlun, the Hand, Robert Hellsgaard, and the Hood, etc.Despite all this, it is still a solid game worth playing, but go in with the right expectations. If you don't like tactical turn-based combat and deck building, or the universe of Marvel Comics, then this isn't for you.It regularly goes on sale, making the complete edition affordable, and worth picking up.It is very much a fun game very few people played sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I love Marvel and turn based tactics games. So, it's a great combination for me, in theory. In practice... Well, let's make a short list of pros and cons:Pros:- Each and every hero feels unique and has their own, very lore-friendly set of moves and attacks- Card based tactical battles are pure fun- Card crafting, upgrades, etc. is very easy to comprehend and upgrades actually do make a difference- A lot to do in-between the battles - clubs, training, hang outs, story cut scenes...- Interactions between most (but not all) characters- Cringe - yep, it can be a pro too if you're into it ;)Cons:- I haven't counted but the game crashed on me at least 30-40 times in the first 30 hours of play. Perhaps it's a mixture of AMD CPU and nVidia GPU but it shouldn't have happened anyway... It's just tiring, really.- Very few kinds of missions- Very little variety in enemies and special "bosses"- It's less XCom and more XCom Chimera Squad- Performance (or lack thereof) - my PC may not be the most powerful out there but it's not a weakling, and Midnight Sun's performance is just all over the place. Fortunately most if not all FPS drops happen outside of combat.- Cringe - sometimes it is what it is...OK, so what could be done to make it better? Apart from performance and crashes, which are obvious culprits to redo, I'd start with adding variety to missions and enemies. Seeing the same four or five hydra agents with an occasional "boss" enemy is not enough. Why not add some more Marvel villains, the lore is huge and it wouldn't be tough to find some extras (if not the more well known characters) to add as opponents. Missions and mission maps could be expanded too. Switching from current arena-style maps to more XCom-like multi-screen locations with various new objectives would be a God-send for Midnight Suns. There's a lot to fix and change and hopefully, Firaxis will get to it.My final score is...For a Marvel and turn-based lover: 8/10For a Marvel or turn-based lover: 7/10For everyone else: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: An underrated gem, and one of the most fun experiences I’ve had in a long time. mix of social sim and tactical card based combat. _childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this game a lot. The story is actually decent. The voice acting is mostly good. Some cringe. I personally can't stand the Hunter's female voice. But overall, 8.5/10The gameplay is 10/10 for me, and I knew it would be. I love XCOM games and I love deckbuilders. This game is a wet dream.Performance: 8/10. For me it has been smooth as butter, but with some minor bugs. Example: After playing awhile I randomly get a graphical bug around my cursor in menus. A restart fixes it, but it's annoying. I play on max settings, with no tweaks, and the only frame drop I experience is after an Intel Mission, when the game generates a comic-book style cover art for the hero who completed it, the game stutters for a split second. Other than that, my performance has been great; But I have a fairly new PC that I built in 2021, with a 3070ti. It shouldn't be expected that everyone has brand new PCs for this game, so they need to work on their optimization, from what I've been reading about other players' experiences. Currently unacceptable IMO, if people can't enjoy the game. Skins: 8/10. I bought Legendary, and the skins are... okay. I have a favorite for each hero, and unlocking new color palettes is cool and all, but I hope more skins are coming. I'm coming from Marvel Heroes, where I had like 10+ skins per hero, (and every skin for my mains), and I just miss that. I'm totally the kind of person who will drop tons of cash on skins if given the chance. And for the low cost of skins in this game, that come with color palettes to further customize? YES PLEASE. More. Just make sure they are iconic and high quality. So far so good.The Grind: So far, I've found the resource system and grinding to fluctuate quite a bit. At the start, I had a lot of credits, but I was essence starved. Once I unlocked some Forge upgrades, and the Cauldron, my essence problem was solved, but training and upgrades depleted my credits. Now I'm constantly credit-poor, and hoping to get credit missions each day, so I can upgrade my stations. I'm sure once I do that, I'll have more uses for essences and I'll be running through that stockpile too... So yeah, this game can feel a bit grindy, but it's not too bad. If I run out of a resouce, it's usually 1-2 missions before I can afford it. It's not like long-term goal setting, where I feel like I'll never unlock something. It just takes a bit of budgeting and planning. My first play-through, I was reckless in my spending. I'll definitely do better on the next. Mods: I don't know if they'll ever support mods officially, but they're coming, and I can't wait. I don't think Hero mods are doable in the near future, they'd take a ton of work... but QoL and Skins and balance mods definitely seem doable. NSFW mods are already in the works LOL. Rule34. Personally, I just want a mod that turns Captain Marvel into Cyclops lol. Cyclops is my favorite X-Men, and Photon Beam is my favorite card in this game so far. I think it would be an awesome reskin lol. Overall, I highly recommend this game IF your PC can handle its current unoptimized state. Once they sort out the bugs and performance issues, It'll be a solid recommend to everyone. Having a blast so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam was letting people try this game out for free for a weekend (you would have to pay for it after that).  My experience with Marvel games of the past, such as the Ultimate Alliance series was positive.  I also though X-Com was a cool concept, so this seemed to be a marriage between to two with a card game like element thrown in.  Well, it only took me a few hours of play to decide that this was something I needed to own and play all the way through.  It's a good game.  As of February 2023, I haven't encountered any bugs in 38 hours of play.  The dialog can feel a little off at times, but it still has a certain charm to it.  It has a lot of dialog though, and lines that are in context with the current situation. The tactical game play is really well animated and easy to pick up.  The exploration game play is a nice change of pace in between missions, but can be tricky at times. I admit to using Google in some cases.TLDR: Shockingly good game. Animations look great. _childDocuments_.review: There's no middle point and I guess I more dislike the bad things about this game than like the good things so that's why the thumbs down. Let's start by saying that this is not a categorically bad game. On a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the best game ever and 1 being the ET the Extraterrestrial, it would probably score a 5.5, maybe 6 on a good day. The good: Visually polished, reasonable gameplay, interesting storyThe bad: Let's start by the obvious: 2K Launcher. I had to find a way to bypass it to avoid the game crashing to desktop on launch 25% of the times. Why 2K need a launcher and why they use one so clunky and unweildy is beyond me. Having multiple launcher bloat is becoming a bane on gaming. The game is visually polished but unless you have a high-performance GPU and tons of memory, you'll end up playing it on minimal settings.  While the story is great, the hours sunk into chasing resources and grinding for them takes away a lot of the fun once you've explored the grounds. The gameplay gets repetitive after a while. The system is unstable and crashes all too often. If you're going to get it, get it discounted. Don't pay full price - it's not worth it even on a good day

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way first:CONS: Graphics: The game's graphics appear very dated. It says Unreal Engine, but Arkham Knight looked better in 2015. This isn't to speak poorly of the design. All the Legendary armors and a lot of the premium skins looked great design wise. But graphically speaking, it's not great. Think Dragon Age (which oddly isn't the only aspect that reminds me of that game).PROS: Everything else. I have loved just about everything about this game. It's taken me completely by surprise, because I was on the fence about even buying it. The combat is incredibly fun, deck-building can be incredibly entertaining, and exploring the abbey and solving it's mysteries had me hooked really quickly.The abbey and it's exploration along with friendship building and gift giving reminded me a lot of the at-camp party-building dynamics of Dragon Age. But even though the combat is isometric, it is turn-based card play versus semi-real-time game play.This would honestly be my GOTY were it not for how incredibly dated the graphics appear. It would have increased my enjoyment of the game quite a lot if this had the graphical fidelity of any other AAA Marvel game released in the last 2-3 years, while keeping the core gameplay elements currently present.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this game out on the free weekend expecting disappointment but was pleasantly surprised with my first few hours. The combat is based around teams of 3 heroes where actions are preformed with cards you draw each turn. Different heroes have different roles like support dps tank ect and use your resources differently. I really enjoyed making a new strategy each turn depending on what cards were drawn and the heroes I had to help. Seems like a simple to pick up hard to master kind of game which is fine by me. There was definitely a lot of story/plot focus from what I played. Probably 70% of my play time was cut scenes or interacting with other heroes in the games hub area. I don't know if this is just the game trying to set up the plot early on or if the whole game plays out like this, but even though it was a crazy amount of dialogue I never once wanted to skip a scene. It was well written and kept my attention. If you're not a marvel fan I don't think you'll like this game but the combat was addicting either way. I'll probably pick up the full game at some point but definitely on sale. I'd like to get the DLC characters too but no way am I paying $99.99 for this. I'd pay maybe $25 for base game and $35-$40 for legendary edition.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Waited to pick this up on sale and I'm glad I did. It's fun, but oh my god so many cutscenes and the whole concept of friendship and hangouts was such a bad idea. This is coming from a guy that loved XCOM 2 because cutscenes were minimal and gameplay was focused on strategy and tactics. The battles are fun and I do everything I can to get into those as quickly as possible by skipping all dialogue. Does the typical Marvel fan love all this friendship stuff?? It makes me feel physically ill when I listen to it...I'm upset because I know the potential of Firaxis and they could've taken the best parts of XCOM 2 and combined it with Marvel. This game is definitely easier than XCOM 2 so if that was a barrier to entry for you before that will not be an issue here.I think this game also went a little overboard with the loot and all that crap, everything you picked up in XCOM felt meaningful, this game can feel like an ARPG with how much loot it dishes out.Could've been so much better, but worth it for the fun card battles if the game is steeply discounted.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line: This game is not a "play real quick after work" type of game; more like a weekend killer. I'd say I recommend this game, but just barely. The combat is amazing. I love the deck building aspects and building different decks to work with other decks. The turn based missions are a big reason I keep playing the game. Unfortunately this represents about 20% of the game.Everything else in the game is mind blowingly slow paced. There is so much dialogue that I'd say about 75 - 80% could be cut and you wouldn't miss out on any details. Now you can skip pretty much everything but knowing when it's going to be new or even relevant information is hard to gauge sometimes. They do keep the hangout sessions brief but eventually they start to repeat and its just another thing that drags on and on and on. The whole "relationship" system feels extremely out of place and doesn't really do much for the game at all. You will need to use it however because its a way to unlock combos and additional costumes. The daytime nighttime cycle also doesn't make any sense. There's basically no point to the night time except it provides an additionally opportunity for more dialogue, and to run around and look for essence. This game just piles on stuff to do in order to increase the amount of time you're playing it. Frustrating to no end, I can not understand why it focuses more on relationships than it does combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little disappointed when the darker tones I was expecting don't seem to be there, but the game is fun and contains somethings I've been wanting from video games for a long time. It allows you to create an avatar and allows you to play with your favorite charactersYou can customize just about everything and everyone. There are genuine laughs to be had. The combat system encourages experimentation. Overall its a fun ride, but if you want a darker toned experience this really isn't for you. I've spent the last few (in game) days planning a birthday party.

I also love the open world Mortal Kombat Krypt-esque style of exploration. I hope they continue to release content for this game even past the season pass dlcs, I am not ready to put it down. Honestly, I can't recommend this game enough. More people need to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this purchase expecting to mostly hate it, but my opinion of it now couldn't be higher! The Cinema-tics in this game throughout despite some smoother instead of more detailed approach are just fantastically fun to watch and humor everywhere possible, but not too thick. The game on a highest end system doesn't stutter that often except between the Sword and the Table area. There was I think just 1 flower I couldn't pick through - game error / Collision error. The combat is way more fun than it looks on the videos. The game lasts literally forever so far with plenty left at 60.2 Hrs atm played. Brings life back into the Marvel World and its Universes with interesting viewpoints from amazing characters. Happy to say I was wrong about this game and Extremely glad I gave it a chance!! --Here's my challenge to YOU... try not to binge play this game and watch the funniest and most tedious speed runs ever if anyone has the Avocados for the task!!!-- Small edit - Found some more of those same errors with plants and meshing/non-loot. There was also some dialogue that was prompted before the pre-dialogue that didn't make sense for one of the characters responses to something until after the pre-dialogue played. I believe I am close to done with game with mostly everything obtained without scoping out the achievements for whats left to get and I cant wait for more content for this game!!!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:I don't remember when was the last time a game annoyed me this much. Plenty of either questionable design elements or ones that are a perfect example of what is wrong with modern game design. It feels like they tried to add in too many things and didn't put in the work to make any part really good. Like they hoped the Marvel sticker will sell it anyway.What I liked:- Kicking people off buildings never gets old.- The story doesn't disappoint, it gives what a Marvel story should.What was not great:- OMG the handholding. I specifically turned off tutorials before starting, and I still had to go through an introduction where you can't progress the story until you "Sleep", "Upgrade a card", "Buy a skin".- Awkward camera use. This is both a card battler, but you also have to position your heroes to use environmental objects, like edges and barrels. Yet there is no normal bird view to see the battlefield properly and it really feels poorly done.- The whole third person running around a castle collecting paintings and such just doesn't fit well into a turn based card battler. Again, could have been good, but it would need more work.

_childDocuments_.review: There were several concerns I had before purchasing this AAA game. Based on game description and community engagement leading up to release, it had been on my wishlist for months (if not year(s)?). I enjoy tactical turn based combat (xcom, div2), card games (slay the spire, monster train) and enjoy the Marvel/comic IP. I figured it'd be a home run, but having learned my lesson on previous launch day purchases decided to wait and read reviews first. So here are my concerns and reactions:1. In game currency, DLC, battle chest, money grab, P2W angle. The reviews heavily indicated the ridiculous in-game currency required for purchasing in-game components. Ultimately, yes, this is a thing. In my 40h so far (progressed story about 6ish? core/story missions), I've only encountered specific items that ultimately cost real money (via in game currency). These components are the "super cool" variant outfits worn in combat. All other 'ingame currencies' that purchase items (gloss, essence, etc) are acquired by completing missions and exploring the grounds. I believe you can purchase some of these in game currencies with real money; but the 'super cool' suits are definitely locked behind a paywall. As far as I can tell, they have absolutely no bearing on gameplay or cinematics. 90% of variant/custom suits/clothing can be acquired with in-game grinding. I personally don't mind this model, I feel reassured content and support will continue for a game I enjoy with these purchases. I haven't spent any money outside purchase price (and don't intend to) and don't feel as if I'm at a disadvantage or turned off. If this model bothers you, then you will likely be bothered when you come across it in game.2. Cringey dialogue. This comes up in reviews quite a bit, and I had already formed my personal concern long before release during the dev showcases. They genuinely got very giddy at very cringey dialogue I had thought was borderline satire; but they would comment "that is so cool!" and I realized nobody was in on the joke with me. So, yes, there is cringey dialogue and probably a lot of it- but I actually lost track. The immersion in this game is so powerful that I didn't realize until recently I hadn't minded sitting back and watching the character interactions and conversations. I cannot recall any portions I'd laughed at or rolled my eyes. I think there is a difference between watching as an audience and participating as a player. I let myself get lost in the world and enjoy the silly banter. I get that may not be for everyone.3. Immersion/side quests. At least one review downvoted the game to sheer non-main-game-gameplay (/words...). That reviewer is absolutely correct in their assesment. Depending on the type of player you are, there is a lot of time devoted to building relationships, exploring abbey grounds, reading lore and engaging in drawn out conversations with some "drama". From my understanding, you are able to experience everything the game has to offer by skipping almost all of these items. However, there are handicaps that come with that as your relationships and recipes discovered on abbey grounds (amongst others) do impact combat. I wouldn't call it significant, but it's certainly greater than nothing. I have not found this distracting, in fact, I'm often enjoying the respite from combat and look forward to uncovering another clue to the Salem witches. I've probably spent 3/4 of my playtime on non-main-game-gameplay (it's gonna be a real word now), and have thoroughly enjoyed that time. As someone who gets impatient at wasting time and just watching a movie vs playing a game, I can suggest if you're on the fence, you're probably going to enjoy the ride. This should be a non issue for almost of all us; but there is a lot of non-main-game-gameplay. A lot.4. RNG. This just comes with the territory. Conclusively, they've done a good job and it's balanced well enough (base decks, acquiring cards, drawing cards, enemy actions, etc). All attacks always hit so that eliminates my xcom rage quit tendencies. They also do a good job reminding players of effects, persistance implications, and potentially bad moves (this enemy cannot be knockbacked), as well as other areas. There is still RNG and I've restarted more than one mission due to a misunderstanding of my actions. I personally think the 'difficulty' slider is excellent. You gradually unlock increased difficulty (with even greater increased rewards). You can slide up and down at your convenience. I'm probably more of a casual than hardcore gamer myself and find myself maxing the slider on 'easy' missions and pulling it down for 'hard' missions.Bottom line, I really can't find anything significant to complain about. I'm sure I could nit-pick some items, but the game flows so smoothly it's swept under the carpet quickly. This is a GREAT game and unless one of the above reasons is strong enough of a detractor to turn you off; buy this game with full confidence. This one's a winner, thanks Firaxis Games!

_childDocuments_.review: Half thumbs up atm (so I guess a 'nice job fist bump'?).  Wait until the next video driver update.  I updated everything & NVidia still wasn't showing it as an option in GeForce experience to optimize.  I have a ticket in to them (this happened with Fifa 23 as well).My card is above the median, and about 20%th percentiles under the recommended card, which should be well in performance range for Med-High settings (I'm ultra on every other game), and the video froze on high settings during a loading screen transition about 20 min in (music still playing, full black screen).Overall its feeling like their 1st dev meeting went like this: Question: "Which gamestyle should we use?  Cards, 4x, adventure...?"  Answer: "Yes."Quick ratings:Gameplay            A-Music                   BDialogue/Story     B+Art                        B-Graphics               C-Replay                  D+Bugs                     C+Expectations        B-Gameplay is a tough one.  Some weird camera stuff to get used to and they set the default mouse sensitivity on 'duper extra spinney' for some reason, so that's annoying to have to tweak.  This is NOT Xcom or anything close to it.  It's WAY more of a comic adventure story/dating mobile game than it is Xcom.  It's 4x light for sure.  There's plenty of strategy, there's plenty of base building, but there is a decent amount of grind and storyline in between all of that.  The story is good enough to hold it all together, and I don't mind the 'friendship' stuff because I like comics, and that's what glue's it all together in this game.  It's not the game I was hoping for, but it's a good game and is keeping me interested.  I'm sure I'll get at least 100-200 hours out of it.Dialogue is decent/good/chuckly.  I'd recommend being a Marvel fan for full effect, but there's plenty in there for everyone.Music is good, nothing to write home about but it sets the tone.Graphics feels a bit "kiddie" even with the High settings.  I'd expect a bit more, I dunno, dank? with this storyline instead of the shinie faux vampire Anime sort of vibe they've got going with the game art?  Bugs are there, just minor stuff like a single crash while I was saving the game.  It's mostly just related to the graphics issues.  But shouldn't be given the AAA title & extra like 9 months they had to launch the game.Edit2: I changed the replayability rating from a B to a D+ b/c there's no way I could go through that story line again.  It is full on heavy teenage angst + midlife crisis.  The entire thing is about listening to EVERY character tell you how worthless they are IN EVERY TRANSITION OF THE GAME.  So you are a full on therapist, and omg does it get old doing that over a dozen Heroes plus, multiple x multiple times.  There is close to zero replayibility b/c of how tied into game advancement/combat all of that hero counseling is.  I don't think I could ever play this again like I have with Xcom.  It's fairly clear that Disney had an iron grip on this thing and tried to make it a game that appeals to everyone, and as we look back on it it's not going to age well.  I'm thinking that thumbs down will be permanent at this point.  I'll grind through it b/c I love comics and strategy, but it's starting to feel like work to get to the parts of the game that I enjoy.Additionally, even after an update to the game they have not aligned their graphics with Nvidia.  Nvidia says my card should be on the highest settings, and the game says I should be on med/low settings.  The game is correct, b/c even after the update I'm getting the same stuttering graphics issues I was before.  I've gone through everything on my PC with a fine toothed comb to try and maximize performance and I don't think it's me.  My rig should be able to handle medium settings based on the provided game specs, Nvidia agrees, and for some reason it can't.Edit1: So I've got a 6gb 1060, just under the recommended 1070, and 16gb of RAM and it's still lagging a bit in some transitions as well as taking awhile to load new areas.  I used the in game optimization button (which did drop it down to med. settings), and restarted everything first.  So not much more I can do aside from drop to low settings I guess?  The game just needs some optimization I think b/c I play FIFA 23 fine, which has very similar/recommended range of vid cards and less general RAM issues as well.  I've got another 16gb RAM I've been too lazy to try and pop in (b/c I haven't needed it, just bought it on sale 6 mo. ago), so I can try that, but it seems to be pretty clearly a VRAM slowdown so dunno if that'll do much.  Maybe area transitions.  3-4yo rig, so dunno how much higher I can go with the Vid., and of course we just passed Cyber monday.  Dumb of me not to check I guess.  Userbenchmark says I'm at about 57%th percentile for gaming 3D performance.  1070's are running about $200-250 rn, so if you don't have a new rig or recently upgraded, you will see some occasional lag in this game even on med settings.  I'm 50 hrs into the game, so it's playable and predictable where you'll see performance issues, but they're mildly annoying and more than infrequent (I'd honestly recommend low settings for EVERYONE that doesn't have a 1070 or higher based on what I've seen, but I just can't do it personally).I'm enjoying the game, and it has some replayability, which is saying something b/c my standards are high for that.  But it will remain a thumbs down though until they fix the optimization issues.  I'm gonna keep ranting here b/c I just have never had a graphics issue with any game up to this point, not even close to this.  It feels like they've jumped a full 1-2 years ahead in graphics requirements in the span of 2mo. since the last AAA title release.  Don't give me a recommended range of cards, put mine in the average to above average range and then make me put it on low settings.  I just don't see a reason my card shouldn't be able to handle the graphics when there is definitely nothing special about them that I can see.  I've played games with better graphics than this, they're just HEAVILY shaded I think, which is 100% an optimizable thing.  I've got 3 relatives that do that sort of work, it feels lazy to me.  Cool stuff, not bad, but if I can max out heavily modded Skyrim and see individual leaves on trees I should be able to handle a "whoosh" fire blast from Cpt. Marvel on medium settings in this game.  That and we're getting to the point where the human eye really can't see the difference in a lot of these quick moving things, the still art is MUCH more important than the moving art.  I mean ffs my dude's feet are below the ground on the training steps sometimes and he does a full on Fat Joe 'Lean Back' when he stops (even my wife noticed just glancing at the game).  Who cares about the million pixilated whoosh magic when you've got stuff like that and getting hung up on scenery running around the grounds to pull you out of the immersion.  It feels like bad/rushed design decisions/PM goal issues from the graphics folks.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has 3 aspects:1) Narrative story. RPG style with decision selections that raise/lower your friendship with each character or the main character's Light/Dark rating. Friendship and Light levels grant bonuses in the combat phase of the game. If you're a Marvel fan the writing is decent and stays mostly true to canon. 2) Combat. Turn-based. Limited actions per turn to play cards from each character's deck. Each character has a customizable deck of 8 cards that are all shuffled together at beginning of combat to make a 24 card deck. Combat has interesting elements such as environmental effects, combos, status effects. Puzzles with enough complexity to be interesting and enough variety to not seem too competitive. There's a main story line and side stories if you got the DLC. There's always multiple side missions with varied rewards so you can stretch out the game's main quest as long as you'd like.3) Exploration. Running around the home base area looking for hidden things to gather collections, unlock RNG chests, etc. This aspect appealed the least to me. I followed an online guide because I don't enjoy running around looking for random hidden stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely don't understand the positive reception of Midnight Suns. This is a mobile game, through and through. The "strategic" combat, the card system, all the upgrade currency crap. Everything about this game feels adopted from a mobile game. It wouldn't feel out of place to have an energy system that only allows you to do so many missions before you have to wait for a timer or pay for continued access. The combat doesn't feel any degree of tactical or strategic. Bounce enemies off each other. Do an ultimate to clear the board. Rinse, repeat. Bland, generic, uninspired. Gone of the days of actually customizing your squad. Get ready for cosmetic packs. There is some weird hub system where you go around talking to everybody between missions. Feels like annoying busy work. I don't understand why this is in the game and seems to take up so much of your time. Uh oh, Ghostrider has a dilemma and needs my help to figure out what to eat for lunch. Good thing I was there. The story. I don't even really want to talk about it. Its not great. Its not even a campy comic book feeling type of story. Just a boring bleh outlined by popular characters and call backs. I really don't have anything positive to say about this game. I can't imagine I'll ever play it again. I wanted to get a refund but I played too much time. Why? Because the tutorial feels like it lasts for hours. I kept thinking that after this were going to see where the game opens up and gives you some agency. Nope, that was just the game all along. It treats you like a moron, I guess because that's the only people that they figured would buy this product. I guess I'm the sucker. Maybe if I open one more mystery box of cards it will all come together!? Yeah, right. Don't waste your time with this crap. Do anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could leave a starred review because there is a lot to like, even love, about this game.  But ultimately all the good things about this game don't outweigh just how exhausting Marvel's Midnight Suns can be.  The game feels like it was built around microtransactions that were pulled at the last minute.  I would only recommend playing this game if you can install mods.Pros:● Genuinely interesting strategy and deck building game systems● The characters are well written and feel true to their comic book counterparts and there's a nice Bioware-style conversation system to get to know them● An arch, but interesting, story.  The game's story feels like it would be a well-received months-long comic storylineCons:● Extremely limited resources that feels like the game is begging you to shell out a couple bucks to get some extra power or friendship or triple your gameplay time grinding these resources and secondary progress (can be "fixed" with mods)● It doesn't NEED it, but the fact that they incorporate a Bioware-style companion system, I'm genuinely surprised there are no romances.● The characters look awful.  Everyone looks too smooth and vaguely plastic.  Like action figures come to life and I mean that as an insult.  It also doesn't match the more realistic textures given to the scenery.● Wolverine is one of the tallest characters.   ● Wolverine, 5'3" 1.6 m, WOLVERINE, is taller than Captain America.● There were a ton of weird visual glitches.  Enemies sometimes wouldn't leave the battlefield after they were defeated, just ghosts hovering around their companions, unable to be interacted with.  Characters would wear their bathing suits in random cutscenes.Final score: 3/5.  If you're a big Marvel fan or really into the idea of a card-building strategy game, you'll have fun with this if you install mods.  But for everyone else, it's better to give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great fun when you get into it, I usually despise Card battle games like this but somehow this one time I actually enjoyed myself. However while I say this is a good game it still has its own issues that hold it back. To make things quicker here are my bullet points.Good:- Story is engaging and interesting- Most characters are well developed & try to reference their past in from other media (comics, movies etc).- Abilities are really cool and flashy- Customisable character and choices (finally a superhero game where I can make my own, with restrictions)- Relationship system to get closer to characters and learn more about them- Mostly good voice acting.- Mostly cool suits- Graphics for the most part look great!Bad:- Only 4 character models for everything/one, 2 slim or buff bodies for every character. The buff body for males is possibly the worst I have seen in a game, having ridiculous looking bubble arms that clip into themselves. What have they done to wolverine!?- NPC models are god awful when they are shown, nearly every female npc has the middle part that gives them a massive forehead- Skin tight clothes, a t-shirt and trousers do not cling to you like your body is about to burst from it unless you bought the wrong size. Storm has an issue with wearing a jacket that leave a hole in her chest that you can see through too. Just overall weird looking casual clothes, like they are painted on.- Not enough character customisation and not enough GOOD options. The voluminous hair looks terrible, in fact hair overall looks off for some reason. Skin tones are not properly shown in creator as when you get in game they can actually look darker than they appeared, for example choosing a white looking skin tone in creator you find in game they are actually very tanned.- Ending is very abrupt. For the finaly you'd expect to do a lot more and it take more fights leading up to it. Instead of a warm up to the final battle you just sorta get put in it. And then when your done it just ends, no closure or real ending jsut a cliffhanger. It's still GOOD but too short for a more fuller feeling ending.- Final boss is a JPEG with animated tentacles around it- No side quests, which were really needed to add more to do. You only have general missions outside of story ones and they are all the same with no context beyond "Kill this thing/turn off this bomb/open this chest/stop that car/save those people because I said so".- Nico. I actually like her as a character in the game but god does she cause unnecessary drama at the start, complains about non-issues but is treated as though everything she is complaining about is 100% true and she is valid. Like come on.- Dark and Light is very un-utlised as a game mechanic. It's literally just for cosmetics and skills. Why not make it a part of the story, the more dark you are the more you act cruel or single-minded in cutscenes or story moments. The more light you are the kind and more compassionate you are, to a fault. The Power alignment is even more under-used and jsut a throwaway mention at times, why not jsut call it Balance.- Very low chance of a sequel, even though they sequel baited. Which is very aggravating and disappointing.So yeah this game is mixed overall but even so I still really enjoyed my time with it, all it needed was either more time in development or just more thought put into it. There are more good and bad points I could make, like DLC characters not being that well integrated into the main story, but you get the gist hopefully. I still recommend this game, I was so put off by the card system before playing that when I actually got it and tried it I was surprised by how good it actually turned out to be. It's just a shame we may never get a sequel because it didn't do well enough and the team that did it have mostly all left :/tldr; Game is good with a mix of positive and negatives but if you give it a chance it may surprise you.Overall rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, but it was marketed very oddly. I think this, and its delayed release date, hurt its sales when it first came out.The game consists of turn-based combat with a unique card play system.People hear "card play" and immediately think "cheap mobile game." This caused a bit of sticker shock when this game was released for around $50.In actuality, while the card mechanic is central to the combat experience, it's not a major component of the game as a whole. The game includes resource farming, crafting, varied character interactions, and exploration components as well (it should be noted though that the entire game is single-player only).Had this game released closer to a $30 price point, and with better marketing that downplayed the card mechanics and instead talked up the other aspects, then I think it surely would have been a solid hit.As it is, I strongly recommend picking this game up when it's on sale. It really is a lot of fun. EDIT after finishing the base game (about 84 hours of gameplay):The game got a little grindy between story missions (it was literally the exact same 7 or so battles again and again), and I was thoroughly sick of the conversations with characters and "hangouts" by the 2nd act, but it was still a lot of fun. I'm heartbroken that there won't be a sequel to this game. It ended on such a bittersweet note. Having finished the game, I do think it's WAY overpriced given the amount of content. It really shouldn't be more than $30 list. Still, it's an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a light tactical card game featuring Marvel heroes, a light friendship simulator, and light exploration game. Players will take the role of 'The Hunter', an original character to the Marvel Universe, as they try to save the world from demons. Along the road, they'll recruit a number of Marvel heroes as they rebuild a team known as 'The Midnight Suns'.This game is a bit of a mixed bag for me. I do enjoy a lot of the genre's it's pulling from, but I feel like the overall experience is mixed because it tries to do too much. Throughout the game, you get to fight enemies, make friends with the Marvel heroes, or explore the abbey, each experience featuring a different gameplay style. Each of the systems do work, and rewards for participating in one benefits the other gameplay aspects, however each gameplay style on their own feels like a simplified version of their respective genre. For the Tactical side, I enjoy the card system, but I found the positioning aspect of heroes a bit strange, as the attacks would automatically choose where I landed. A bigger problem was that I was able to attack any enemy from any point of the arena. This made the combat feel "flattened" in a way as I had characters zipping throughout the battlefield to dispatch enemies quickly. Aside from that, this is definitely the highlight of the game for myself, as I enjoyed trying to beat the levels in as few turns as possible. On the friendship side, I felt like the writing in place both expected the player to know these characters to an extent (there are easter eggs thrown throughout the dialogue); but the reward was mostly learning more about their backstory and their point of view. The writing is a bit variable in quality (might be a bit corny for some) but it gets the job done. Finally, exploring the abbey will give you mysteries to solve, ingredients to collect for crafting, and cosmetic prizes (earned through opening the treasure chests scattered throughout the map). The map opens up a bit more as you explore and earn abilities to open more pathways. This portion of the game was fine, but the Abbey feels mostly empty the further out you go, as characters would mostly cluster around one spot.Ultimately, Marvel's Midnight Suns is a game that tries to do many things, and is okay at most of it. In the end, if you're looking for a lighter tactical game and are a fan of Marvel, I do recommend this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the biggest mixed bag I've ever played.  While I love it to death, I know it's going to be a hard sell for a lot of people.  Let me explain the pro's and con's as to why that is;PROs: - Fantastic TTB combat, I would describe it as an eclectic mix between Xcom, Into the Breach, and Slay the Spire.Draft cards and build a deck for wide cast of super-hero favorites, complete missions using tactics and strategy, and use the environment to manipulate enemy positions to line them up and knock them into each other.CONs:- Probably some of the worst writing I've ever seen in a video game in my life.  The plot is serviceable but paper-thin in lots of spots.  The dialogue is atrocious; there are conversations where characters deliver lines back and forth to each other that don't feel like human conversation.  Some of the characters have... dubious motives and actions that doesn't feel like something the character would do or say (Example as a very minor spoiler:  .  There are lots of scenarios and conversations that feel straight from a cringey slice-of-life high school anime, except with adult super heroes.  And there is A LOT of dialogue, I mean on the level of something like Fire Emblem: Three Houses.- Speaking of Fire Emblem: Three Houses, this game includes an overworld/hub where you have to explore and find crafting materials.  It's tedious and awful, and while you could probably ignore them, they allow you to craft powerful consumable cards that can make-or-break certain missions.TLDR; the gameplay is amazing, that plot is serviceable, and the writing for the dialogue ranges from cringe to outright incomprehensible.  6-7/10, play it if you like Xcom and Marvel but don't expect too much from the dialogue and story.

_childDocuments_.review: repetitive gameplay, way too much dialogue, way too little actual action. Progression is locked behind hundreds and hundreds of dialogues between the different characters, that are all written like they're a quirky teenager. The game was billed as an action packed game, which "borrows" from slay the spire, but realistically, every combat is the same. You get your cards in the same order, you solve the fights in the same way. In Slay the Spire, everything is randomized, and it takes some level of skill and thought to do the fights. In this poorly balanced mess, you have one path to solve each fight.The open world stuff is clunky and poorly paced. The combat, which you will probably want to be doing, is also clunky and poorly paced, and repetitive. Want to watch your favorite super hero do a cool attack? Who wouldn't. Want to watch that same super hero do that attack 500 times with very little variation in the animation? Want to listen to them give the same one liners over and over? Realistically this is a pretty bad game. The reason that this game exists is to get children and people with poor impulse control to spend money on skins, which is kinda scummy.

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, I am unable to give a thumbs up for this game. There are severe stuttering issues, even on the lowest settings. I have an Nvidia 1660, about 3 years out of date, but I can run Witcher 3 (Pre newest update) on high settings without issue. This game's graphics aren't to that level, but it stutters, the load times are long, the game freezes on the inventory menu, the MAIN menu stutters.It's very poorly optimized for PC.The gameplay loop is fun, combining the card game aspect and XCOM turned out to be better than I thought it would be, so if they can iron out the stuttering issue, I'll revise.Edit: there are a couple of fixes that are floating around, one of them is pretty universal. The problem is the 2K launcher. Google how to bypass that. The second fix has worked for me, might work for you. In the main menu, switch to DirectX11. Those two things have lessened the stuttering, but not eliminated it.Switched to recommend as the gameplay loop is fun, and the stuttering issue appears to have been resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review:Gameplay - It's got a great storyline. I'm only 36 hours in and I feel like the story just keeps going. The fact that I can go at my own pace and disregard the main "Story Missions" to work on leveling up my heroes is nice. One big downfall is the voice acting not quite hitting the tone I want it to compared to the Marvel Movie actors. Tony Stark, for example, has a voice actor I'm not really into. It's too.... whiney. The world is small to explore, but it's got alot of secret puzzles to solve. I give the gameplay 8/10Difficulty - It's pretty easy. I think i lost against Venom once but managed to figure out his tactics the second time around. Although I play on normal mode atm. The secrets and world map can get confusing as the puzzles don't really give any good hints. You just gotta figure it all out on your own. Card building takes some time to figure out as well, but after you get the hang of it, it's just a matter of resource management. Obtaining resources is a lengthy process though. Alot of running around and collecting daily, or taking on random missions to obtain the resources. It's pretty safe to say the difficulty imo is a 7/10. With 10 being super hard.Note: This game is almost unplayable until you disable the launcher for the game and adjust the settings to pretty much minimum. Loading times are still insane and huge attack moves can freeze the game for a few seconds. This game isn't optimized for crap. The dev's need to focus all their attention on optimization before launching more content. But I do see it being a solid running game in the future. :)Overall, with everything this game has to offer, I would give it a 7.5/10. With potential to be a solid 9.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: If you like just chilling with Marvel superheroes and then figuring out how to optimally use the cards you've drawn to have those heroes kick the heck out of Nazis and demons, then you'll like this game. It has a great gameplay loop, and the characterisations and interactions with the heroes are great, with a nice range of heroes in all senses of the word. I would like to see more interaction between the heroes thou, as there's only really the club interactions outside of Stark and Strange's banter at the forge (which is among the best bits in the game), although I do understand that that was probably a production limitation since making dedicated interaction stories between each hero would have been much more work.It does suffer from some lack in diversity for the missions, with the fact that every mission takes place in pretty much the same arena with no interior walls that only change aesthetically, and there are only ever 4 objectives (defeat all enemies, protect device, destroy device, or secure object) probably being the major reason for that. The fact that the final fight is just 4 waves of juiced up normal enemies (with so many "evil effects" on them you might have to turn down your graphic settings to keep things running at a decent rate) was pretty disappointing. It could have been so much better, especially since you were going in with all the heroes.Speaking of, if there was one major change I would make to the game (besides an actual final boss), it would be being able to do multiple missions in the same day with different heroes. Like there's already a few story missions where you have different teams for different parts of it, so I would have liked it if you could send out like 2 squads at the start (since you start with 8 heroes you should be able to do 2 squads of 3). It would help with the resource balance, the level up problem with some heroes just getting so left behind they had to implement an auto-level system, as well as just having to do the basics (gamma coils, daily training, etc) so often. I'm hoping they're making a sequel that addresses this issues, or that they open it up to mods that can add that kind of stuff.Since my complaints basically boil down to "I wish there was more of it", I do recommend it to anyone who is interested.

_childDocuments_.review: This game WILL be very good when the optimisation is fixed at the time of writing for many people including myself it runs like an arthritic slug climbing Mount Everest.The game shows that i have played 2.7 hours but i can honestly say the majority of the time it is just loading in between cut scenes.The combat seems fine as is the voice acting(the current stuttering will be fixed).My current computer specs are above minimum but even people who have top of the line equipment are making the same comments about loading times,i repeat it is poorly optimised and i can see why the initial release date was kicked back.I do recommend this game but with a caveat of the problems need to be fixed (Firaxis say they are working on it urgently).If you buy the game but only have minimum specs i would say you will have a nightmare playing it until the issues with optimisation are eliminated

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played X-Com, stay with X-Com.If you've not heard of X-Com, play X-Com instead.No spoilers and i've played the entire game at this point...The battles (missions) in Midnight Suns are very cool and a lot of fun. The card-play mechanic works surprisingly well, the action is fast-paced, and you truly feel like Cyclops commanding a load of superheroes in the field. You face some cool villains and each hero is completely unique in combat with thematic abilities, so having to decide which individuals to take on which missions makes for a nice challenge. Making a comic book cover for each mission is a fun touch, akin to how easily you can get lost in Gwent in Witcher III and wake up Sunday wondering where your weekend went.However, the non-battle stuff that takes up 2/3 of the game is dull, and does not impact the game at all. It's more 1st person than X-Com, and all you do is talk to other Superheroes and do childish stuff like planning surprise parties and mediating secret crushes. If you're picturing a school playground right now, that's spot on. That's exactly what it's like. This friendship-driven element has nice morals, but makes for dull game play.There is no real base-building that affects the game play. You can buy aesthetic things and discover new areas, but it has absolutely no impact on the game. It's also very unclear you can do this, and i didn't realise until the end of the game! So there's some proof pudding that it's all pointless. There's also a hell of a lot of resources, but you forget about them very quickly. There's no Age of Empires-style mechanic for acquiring them and having to think carefully about where you spend them: you just find them or you don't. And, as mentioned, the things they buy influence the game so little you stop caring.A slight annoyance is how all the heroes level up automatically very fast. You can work so hard to get one hero up a couple of levels, but when you hit a milestone, they all bump up to that level anyway. This is very unsatisfying and makes you forget that levels are even a thing.Glad i got it on sale.Now stop reading this and go play X-Com!

_childDocuments_.review: A nice surprise, gives me a Marvel fix at a time where the MCU has left me disappointed. If you like Firaxis' other games like XCOM, you'll enjoy the gameplay here. However, most of the time is spent following the narrative and taking part in the RPG style relationship system and hangouts with heroes. If you like that sort of thing, you'll really enjoy this. The writing is far from a masterpiece, but it has a charm and comic book feel and the characters all feel unique and true to their source. The story is serviceable and plenty long, you won't complete this in just a few hours. The season pass is worth it, with the DLC all being part of an interconnected side story away from the main plot. This means you don't need the DLC to experience the full story, but it provides some additional fun interactions and missions.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is sort of story-first, action-second? And the action is kind of a turn-based tactics thing that involves deck-building and careful use of available resources under complex conditions. The theme that unites these two aspects of the game, I think, is leadership.  But, be ready to spend some time building relationships, managing social crises, etc., in addition to the turn-based fighting.The characters (Midnight Suns, working with a few Avengers and a smattering of X-Men) are much closer to their traditional comic book versions than the film versions. The voice-acting is well done once you understand that, and also that the player character, "Hunter," is...simple? I mean this in the nicest way. At first the voice work seemed wooden, and then I was like...no wait, this character is kind of reserved and inhuman because (well, reasons. no spoilers.) The story is character driven and great.I love it. It's a great example of itself, and a great tribute to the comics. If you like these kinds of games, you will love it, too. If you were expecting a game focused mainly on fighting, without too much concern for managing relationships and decks, it may take some getting used to.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who likes XCOM and comic book characters, this game was a good fit. The gameplay in battles is fun and is a good difficulty. The attack animations and character details are well done and I never got tired of looking at them even after 60 hours. The story is good is well, nothing award-winning but entertaining enough that keeps you motivated to push on.I will say that while the voice-acting is good (a lot of the characters reprise their roles from other Marvel shows and games), the actual dialog is very cheesy and painfully PG. There is some funny dialog here and there, but I found that after 20 hours I had to begin skipping the casual dialog with the characters (something I never do in games) because it was just so tedious and melodramatic. A lot of times it felt like the characters were high-school teens with the silly drama they were coming up with, instead of seasoned adults. It is essentially required to gain powerful bonuses as well, but I just wish the actually dialog was more entertaining such as something in similar conversation RPGs like Mass Effect or Fallout. If you love the Marvel movies and shows however, you will likely like the dialog but just wasn't for me.The DLC is hit or miss, I would really only recommend them if you like the characters they provide as they don't offer much to the main game and story. I found the DLC missions to be a bit harder but much more annoying, but they are very short, just 3 missions per DLC.Overall, if you like XCOM, Marvel, Card Collecting, and Dialog heavy games, then I would recommend this game, primarily if it is on-sale. However if you don't like Marvel style dialog or hate anything card-related, then I would advise against the game.

Started over immediately, skipped all the cutscenes, backed up my saves manually and got cloud sync working as well.Still, between the compatibility issues, general unoptimized code on Windows (cf. massive frame drops around the Abbey, sleeping causing game breaking freezes, wonky animations during battles), and releasing a DLC before fixing outstanding bugs, I wouldn't recommend buying the game until the next Steam sale and/or after more patches come out.

_childDocuments_.review: For those thinking this game is going to be Xcom with a marvel skin be warned, the only similarity between the two is the movement and turn based combat, beyond this the two diverge heavily. _childDocuments_.review: Writing: decent. Especially if you're gen ex. Lots of the pop culture references in the first 4 hours were references  to 80s movies like Ghost Busters or Gremlins. Tony Stark made me laugh out loud a few times, and I like how the main character is kind of socially awkward because she comes from a different time. Graphics: very good. It's pretty. Ray Tracing doesn't seem to make a big difference and impacts performance even on a beefy rig, so I'd say don't use it.Animation: Combat animations are great, but facial animations are kind of plastic and there's no emotion on the characters faces. It is my pet peeve in a game with cinematic style cut-scenes like this. It's kind of like dragon age inquisition or mass effect in terms of facial animations. Voice Acting: All in all I would say very good. Stark is good, but takes some getting used to after all the years of RDJ. You spend a lot of time talking to team members at your base, building your relationships to get better bonuses - so its a good thing that the writing and VA are good - that could have ruined the game for me.Gameplay: much more tactical than I was expecting from a card battler. It's not really that much like XCOM. The vast majority of movement comes built into the attack cards, there's no cover, no ammo/reloading, no load-outs for each character - just some "gear" which any character can access with only 3 slots. But I am having a lot of fun with it. You can set up a lot of cool synergies and pull off interesting combos. There are a lot of interactable elements in the environments as well. Performance: I have run into zero issue (other than ray tracing). Lots of people are complaining  about stutters though, so YMMV. If you don't have a $5000 PC you might need to turn down the graphics some. All in all, I really like this game. I think it is getting unfairly review bombed because some people don't want to turn down their settings, and microtransactions. The Microtrans don't bother me, since they're just for some premium cosmetic changes. You can still earn a lot of customizations through in-game means, and the game is the important part, not some fancy costume you have to pay a few bucks for.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, with fun card-based tactical RPG combat and a lot of great character writing.  It is, unfortunately, frontloaded with a LOT of talking- but once you get past the tutorialized stuff and the introductions, the gameplay follows a really satisfying and fun loop.  Building individual character 'decks' out and then seeing how they play off of one another in combat is really interesting, and with a roster as strong as this game has (a great mix of prominent and semi-obscure characters) there's a ton of interesting combinations to find.There's a lot of love put into this game and it's characters, and a lot of fantastic design put into the gameplay.  If you like Marvel stuff you're going to really enjoy this, especially if you love seeing superheroes in a casual setting getting to know one another.  It honestly offers an experience that's completely different from any other Marvel game, focused on the characters and who they are instead of just showing off cool superpower moments.

_childDocuments_.review: I held off on getting this due to fear of it being a dumbed-down XCOM. In a way that is true, but now I am sorry I did not pick it up sooner. Combat is turn based and will remind XCOM fans of its combat. There are no & chance shots here so any strategy you use will actually work. I found this made the game much less frustrating to play than XCOM, though the tactics are less deep. I was greatly surprised by the graphics of this game - they are amazing. The textures and lighting look realkly good in 4K. The only complaint I have is that a few of the animations are stiff. This is more noticeable during 3rd person section of the game. Instead of an overview of the base, this time you control a character in 3rd person to explore around and have conversations. I found that this led to an increased sense of feeling part of the world. For someone who is tired of Marvel movies, this game is a major step in the right direction. Mature themes and jokes that are more than silly puns really add to the game.The customization and story have outpaced XCOM 2 for me so far and I would recommend anyone on the fence to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for a bit over 100 hours now (on PC). Gameplay is great, graphics is great. minimal issues with bugs. My 8 year old gaming PC runs Midnight Suns at medium performance. This is good enough for me since this is not a life action shooter where reaction time matters. It's a round based battle card game for heavens sake. So up to here I would recommend the game to others.BUT: I have a big issue with the storyline. Almost every second main story fight, I win the fight and then the storyline continues as if I have lost. Greatly illustrated by the cut-scene. This really sucks! If the storyline requires me to lose a fight, the cut-scene should show another super-villian charging to the rescue for the bad guys. That would be way more plausible than showing a boss-villian that I just have beaten up badly twice, wiping the floor with my heroes.I can't recommend the game the way it currently is. It's a solid 2 out of 5 stars for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Firaxis always makes great strategy games. So the core gameplay is fun and intelligent. 2 main reasons why I don't recommend it. Aside from having a great gaming PC with countless performance issues for no reason, (1) the game's sort of campus navigation system, running around a mansion just to get to story cutscenes and such is unfun and a waste of time. In fact, i got stuck in a spot amongst this world with no explanation on what to do... Only choice I'm left with is to reload a save from a whole match ago just for what? To get stuck again? No, thank you.(2) And after probably 20 matches, I STILL haven't unlocked simple options such as character customization or even picking my own characters for a mission. I can see corporate forcing these lame decisions on Firaxis because their other games offer much more freedom such as XCOM and Civ. I am a game designer and this game just felt out of place in various ways, I can see why it failed.Sadly I got the year pass, wish I could get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, it's fun. Playing this makes me imagine the developers coming up with ideas for this game and whoever was in charge just said yes to every one of them. There's XCOM elements but not quite, there's an RPG 3rd person exploratory story slice complete with jedi power wheel abilities and light/dark system, there's card game dynamics in the combat and a 'passing of each day' system like in XCOM, complete with a bedroom you can upgrade and adorn. The spaghetti they were throwing at the wall was very sticky that day and everything made it into the pot. All that said, its a very fun game and it runs fairly easily on my low to mid grade laptop. Also, there's a full metric ton of actual comic book references and lore drops to the great Marvel universe. Sometimes there is too much cut-scene dialogue, story shoveling but you can skip it easily and its not necessary, as the NPCs tell you frequently. The characters don't seem overly concerned with what's going on in the story, so you shouldn't either. It's a very satisfying Marvel game. Not a good turn based combat game like I was expecting at all. This is NOT Marvel XCOM. But maybe one fine day...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not done with the game just yet but I'm pretty close. This was another game I bought on a whim because it seemed like a random fun game to play for a few hours, but I ended up really digging it more than I thought I would.The actual core gameplay is a lot of fun, I love doing the missions. The relationship stuff is fine, there are a lot of different card crafting/modifying things and ways to add abilities. Every hero has their own style that sets them apart from each other pretty well. I don't really care for the crafting stuff personally, but there is a lot of it here for those that do. Running around the Abbey (the Fire Emblem Monastery-like hub) gets old after a while and I just want to play the missions but you kinda have to do all the extra stuff to get new cards and abilities. The gameplay in battle is fun enough though that I'm still coming back despite being kinda tired of the down time in between.Been playing on the Steam Deck a lot and it can be a lil stuttery here and there but plays great otherwise, a nice handheld game for sure. Playing the game on normal and it's challenging enough to make me think but not overbearing, minus a few missions I ran into trouble with. I just finished a boss level that took me like 2+ hours of restarts to finish but that was the worst one so far.Overall I like the game a lot, there's a chance I may not end up finishing it if I end up burned out before the end but I've put in a lot of time that I still feel confident in recommending it. I don't think you even need to be a big Marvel fan, I like and follow some of the stuff but I'm nowhere near like a huge fan or anything. Def a fun game!EDIT: Okay I did end up beating it, totally worth it. Those last couple battles were pretty crazy, I'm glad I stuck it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Firaxis doing a turnbased tactical game in the Marvel universe? Is this Xcom with supersuits?No it is not. It is:- 20% Combat.This part is like a weird mobile-like collectible cardgame. Quite fun though, but it is not Xcom. On a good note, this system is getting better and more fun the more you play. Expect lots of hours into the game before the system is getting really fun though.- 30% Social interactions.Just like in Bioware games. Talk to people, listen to their whining, chose replies, build relations and chose to be good or bad. Has ups and downs depending on the conversion, but it is generally quite entertaining if you like the Marve lore.- 50% Daily tedious must-to-do chores.Pet the dog, read some books, open yesterdays lootboxes, upgrade stuff, train and twice a day you take a runaround the abbey and look for glowing orbs. If it has rained, horray, you get to run around a quite big outdoor map and look for exciting mushrooms and flowers. The pinnacle of the superhero experience.I knew there would be hit and misses with the game, but not how much time I'd spend on the different gameplay features, and I feel there's quite an unbalance here. Too much tedious collecting and management, not enough action.

_childDocuments_.review: I felt the need to write a review of this game after completely disregarding it last year. If you love Marvel, if you love the relationship building and slice of life elements of games like Persona 5, if you like turn based combat with strategy, flashy animations, building decks: This is the game for you. I have loved every moment, although it can be slow at first, and the graphics can be iffy, this game is such a unique blend of mechanics that I love in other games that has led me to reaching act 2 at the 70 hour mark. So many aspects of it are just purely addicting. I originally bought the game just for Spider-Man and thought I wouldn't care to play the other characters, but THEY ARE ALL SO MUCH FUN. Playing around with Magik's portals, Ghost Rider's ability to make enemies implode, and then your own hero having a super blend of unique powers that even split off into dark and light is awesome. Sure sometimes I do get tired from getting resources and trying to modify cards but in a weird way, its so satisfying after working to get what I want, and it really does not take long. Enjoy the conversations with the heroes, enjoy the exploration of the Abbey and its grounds, attending the clubs and seeing which heroes join is also fun and hilarious.. like interesting Wolverine, nice job joining book club, but not reading the books LMAO. Look this is easily one of my favorite games of all time and I'm going for 100%. I haven't even unlocked Hulk and Scarlet Witch yet, and the fact that the Midnight Suns variant costumes you unlock after maxing relationship level and completing that heroes individual challenge mission is AWESOME. _childDocuments_.review: I initially dismissed this game, due to day one technical problems, what felt like fan-fiction writing, a generic story and the fact that it was not X-com 3.   The battles were great, but everything else felt sub-par.  I'll get it on sale down the line, I told myself.  But something was nagging me and so the next morning I brought it again, and boy am I glad I did as this game is actually amazing.  It just doesn't leave a good first impression, but once you accept the game for what it is, you will find that it is actually great fun, beautiful to look at, huge, and challenging.  Its actually a lot like x-com too: you have your fun but challenging tactical battles and a base that you upgrade and grow alongside the battles.  There is so much to do and all of it is fun.  since i am not a huge superhero guy, I skip through most of the dialogue, but everything you do adds to the meta game of making a kick ass team (literally), so that you can go back out there to kick some more ass.  The battles are glorious, on brand and actually quite challenging.  There is a constant feeling of marvel (pun intended) as you explore more of the Abbey ground and discover yet another cool system.  The story is actually not bad, as such stories go, and you get used to the constant quips.  You can skip through anything that annoys you and customize your experience - in my case the battles and opening up the Abbey.  Also, most of the problems I had with bugs and stuttering on day one seem already fixed, unlike another recent cluster♥♥♥♥ release (cough Calisto Protocol cough).  I can't put this game down now, and I am a 53 year old man who stopped reading comics decades ago.
