_childDocuments_.review: Honestly was not expecting much, I'm a huge XCOM fan but with this being a big IP game with an OC and all the horrible Marvel games in recent years I was ready to give this a miss and just enjoy the nerd rage response from others on YouTube.I can't recommend it enough after playing through it non-stop: The story is really weirdly high quality, the positivity of the main cast balances nicely with the darkness of the backstory around the abbey and the main villain, all of it is especially fleshed out and nuanced; the combat is addictive, I hate card games normally but it's usage here is probably one of the best I've ever seen with how they represent the characters' abilities and modify each other and the battlefield; I at least like all the main cast and love the majority, they decided to focus on the animated and comic book incarnations of the characters which I feel works very well; the main character fits surprisingly well with the rest of the cast, and the dual morality system works quite well with providing new abilities, new dialogue and story changes based on your alignment.My biggest gripe with the game is perhaps the menus, it's kind of annoying to have to run between four different stations in the base before every mission; you have to manage ops missions from one console which can give items to the other 3, then there's the Forge to open the Coils (lootboxes essentially) and purchase additional abilities, then run to the training yard to further upgrade abilities, get daily modifiers and heal injured units, then pop into the card menu accessible anywhere to equip and swap abilities. Sometimes you have to sprint between stations multiple times to get everything sorted out. Then finally run to the mission table to start a mission. I can understand why it's been made this way I suppose, but I kinda wish I could either fast travel between each station or just have it all accessible from the character menu, since it can get tedious to flit between the same 3-4 areas every in game day. Only a minor gripe though, the rest of the game is top notch and absolutely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: To cut through all the bs reviews, here's an easy way to determine if this game is for you.Do you love all things Marvel or just super heroes in general?Do you like tactical/RPG games?Do you like A LOT of depth to your characters and their stories?If you answered yes to at least 2 of these you will enjoy this game, plain and simple, and I would recommend this game to anyone who did.This game has a lot of love for the Marvel franchise as a whole, and it is clearly on display with how much thought went into developing each character, giving them all FULLY voiced dialogue throughout the entire game which is staggering when you actually see just how much dialogue is in this game. Some characters you will learn to love and some you will learn to hate. Combat is definitely a highlight as well, being able to launch enemies into barrels that explode killing multiple enemies at once never gets old.All that said, this game does have some cons:Story is weak at times, plot holes are plain to see with weak justification.The arguing between characters definitely gets old, and is pretty unrealistic at times given what's at stakeIt's probably just my computer, but this game lags constantly, ruining epic moments all the time

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, over 40 hours in now with all DLC characters unlocked and on the team, so I think I have a fairly good handle on this game. PROSMarvel roster: a great, if really odd mix, of characters. Some are the 'big name' individuals the Marvel cinematic universe made so popular (Tony, Steve, Strange). Others are lesser known (Nico, Magik, Robbie Reyes). Either way, it's a wide mix of individuals who you don't usually see get to work together so that, in and of itself, is fairly interesting.Card Buidling: Honestly thought I would hate this aspect, but it's one of the things I enjoy the most. Being able to create a deck (aka build) for each character is a lot of fun, especially when you start synergizing it with the rest of the three man team. There's a lot of room for flexibility and while each character semi falls into the 'holy trinity' of RPGs (healer, tank, dps) there is far more crossover than usual.Animations: Fantastic in combat. Spells and abilities look great and characters have great style when executing them. Legendary abilities are especially fantastic and give off the same vibe you get when pulling a summon out in FF VII. A different spin on mission types: look, at the end of the day the mission style is very much that tried and true formula brought from the Xcom franchise. Protect this, extract with this, kill all enemies. But there are some nice variations here, most notably with things like the Nest Mother and environmental combos. It's not going to make the genre do a complete 180, but it's nice to see something beyond the 'shoot this barrel to go boom' simplicity.Music: great music selection that meshes well with the things going on onscreen. I think we all knew that was going to be a strong point the minute we saw the first trailer.MEHVoice Acting: Can be both good and bad. Gave this a meh rating because I don't think it primarily the voice actors issue here. There are some that are a little flat, but most put on a solid performance. It's just a shame the writing is so bad (more to follow on that). Costumes and Customization: They aren't horrendous here, but it's really restrictive for an RPG style romp, imo. Granted, you don't want to have established characters breaking the lore by wearing wild stuff, but I would have appreciated more customization of the OCs outfits and more than 2-3 choices for each of the established heroes. Plus, this is a superhero game. If you're going to be jumping into the arena of custom characters in superhero genre, you need to have something robust when it comes to character creation. Abbey: I love the Abbey in general as it feels less stuffy than the Sanctum and less over the top than Stark Tower. I also like the tie in to Salem, the witch hunts, and overbearing religion. It's kind of cool, but I do wish it went a little further in depth than just the journal pages you find lying around or the exploration parts. BADThe Writing: while the main story isn't horrendous, it's your normal super hero/save the world affair, there is far to much time spent on building 'relationships' with all the characters. That in and of itself isn't a bad thing in an RPG. Mass Effect and Dragon age are exactly that and it's hard to find games that resonate so strongly with players when it comes to character relationship compared to those two. Here, the writing is just really bad. There are high points. Some interactions were a lot of fun. Being able to sit down and watch Blade, Steve Rogers, and Carol Danvers discuss the finer points of the "Art of War' was kind of cool. Talking philosophy and the cycle of life and death with Dr Strange was unique. Even theory crafting with Eddie Brock on what it would be like to fight a T-Rex was kind of funny. But the majority (I'd say at least 80% of the interactions) are hack writing. Most of them devolve into the established character telling the OC they've 'never connected with someone until they met them' or 'you're such a great friend'.. Never mind that all the Marvel characters have been on multiple teams, hundreds of times in the past, or that the OC is the stiffest and most unlikable of the bunch  (so the simple concept that EVERYONE connects with them is highly laughable). Most of the interactions will be like that. Eye rolling, sub par writing with dumb comments thrown in (Captain Marvel just couldn't help herself and had to talk about 'shattering the glass ceiling' even while laying outside and staring at the stars). It's frustrating because it could have been so much better and this game could have been another Dragon Age level title. But writers are hacks these days it seems, in almost all mediums.The OC: I hate this person. Look, the story behind them and what they're supposed to do is solid. But damn if they aren't written like a complete ♥♥♥♥. Yeah, they have a moment of funny dialogue or something which hits a high point, but they're so stiff in this odd attempt to pull the 'fish out of water' trope. Since you're essentially playing this character, it drags everything down.Open World (Abbey): my god, I'm not sure who decided this was a good idea. The Abbey serves as the 'base setting' for your squad, very similar to the hovercraft in XCOM. Only issue is, they tied this weird open world mechanic into it where you have to run around to collect materials for upgrades and investigate the Abbey grounds. I can see what they were going for, and it may have even worked, if it wasn't so shallow and half ass executed. Instead, it feels like a tacked on feature, that didn't have enough time dedicated to it to develop properly. So instead of adding intrigue and suspense, it's simply tedious and atrocious. They should have left it out and streamlined the game a bit more. As it is now, you'll spend some of the early hours exploring the hell out of it, forget about it for 10 missions, then get sent back out to explore the same areas you already have. It's kind of annoying and god help you if you love to burn through items in combat. You're going to need those mats since each item is 'one use only' and I don't envy anyone who has to farm for them.CONCLUSIONOverall, I'll give this a recommend, especially when it's on sale. I've been fairly apathetic towards the Marvel IP for years (since WandVision turned out to be a dud) because of the way Disney has run it into the ground. But this game helped remind me why I grew up loving these characters so much. While there is definitely some points I would suggest Firaxis leaves out or improves (drop the open world mat farming and hire some decent writers instead of the randos simply sitting in a starbucks) the card building style and combat was a breath of fresh air. It had just enough randomization to keep combat interesting, tempered with allowing the player just enough control so it doesn't feel cheap or ridiculous. I had, and am having a good time with the title, even with it's glaring flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this was a very fun tactical turn-based strategy game. I haven't purchased or played the DLC, just the main game. I'm sure that the DLCs add some extra variety to the game but honestly even what was present in the base game still felt pretty good.It definitely wasn't perfect, but what we got was something that deserves a sequel. In the same way that, IMO, XCOM 2 improved well upon the formula of XCOM 1, I believe a MS2 could be a better version of this.If you're a Marvel fan, I think this is even more of a joy. There's lots of references to enjoy within the game in various forms, from name drops of different characters, collectibles of vintage comic books, to character cosmetics that reference different versions of the available roster, there's a treasure trove of "oh cool!" moments to be had for fans. It's clear that the people who made this game either were Marvel fans or at the very least made sure to do their homework to deliver an authentic Marvel video game experience.There are some things they could have done better for sure, I think some character balance was off and some of the RPG elements felt rough, but at the end of the day what I played was a polished experience that by all accounts should have done way better commercially than it did.Now for some scores:It's kind of campy but that fits in well with a super hero storyline. You've got an apocalypse looming on the horizon and you, The Hunter, are prophesied to play a key role in it. You're accompanied by two main hero groups: The Avengers, the veteran apocalypse-averting crew we all know, and the Midnight Suns, a group of (mostly) young blood who've been united as a team specifically to help fight off the forces of Lilith. You'll meet up with some extra characters too, especially with the DLC, but beyond that you maintain a core group of just a dozen or so characters that you'll take on missions and become friends with. Honestly, I really enjoyed the story but it's got the typical amount of required hand-wavey-ness that most super hero stories require you to undergo in order for it to fit together, so it certainly isn't a masterpiece.It is, at the same time, less and more tactical than other games in the same genre. You forgo the typical battle map with cover, flanking, and Overwatching-All-The-Time and replace it with environmental hazards and a card battle system. With only (typically) 3 card plays per turn though, sometimes your favorite characters can end up just sitting there looking pretty if you just don't draw their cards, which feels bad. Also unless you have certain characters in your party, the environmental hazards can sometimes just be too difficult to incorporate into your battle strategy. But with the way it is built, it works well, and that's valuable in it's own right.Pretty basic sound design, but I give props to the voice acting. The characters all sounded perfect to me. I don't know if these people have played these characters in other media, but they knocked it out of the ballpark here. In some ways they did really well and in others it could use more work. During cutscenes, there's a weird out-of-focus issue when it is focused on a character's face where the character is blurry but the background is in focus. Also the world details were pretty sparse. The battlemaps you play on are very barebones. The cutscenes seem to be pre-rendered, so if you're playing on highest graphics the cutscenes are actually downgraded. All in all it could be improved upon but it doesn't look bad.I didn't play this game on release, so I'm sure there were stability patches that made my experience much smoother than it would have been for people on release, but I can't change that so all I can say is that it ran pretty great more or less. There was some issues, like if I moved a lot of characters around at once it could get really confused as to what to do. The final mission also started really wigging out on me for a bit (a save and reload fixed it). But I can't say I can complain too much here.I definitely recommend it if you're a fan of tactical turn based games or superhero games. There's multiple difficulty settings as well to make it fit your desired challenge, and the only thing that affects is how much "gloss" you get as a reward per mission (a resource used to buy some home base outfits and combat outfit colors for your roster of characters, aka cosmetics). There are some outfits for the characters that require either the season pass or premium currency to acquire which I'm not a huge fan of, but by the end of the game I had everyone decked out in their Midnight Suns outfits so the premium cosmetics are very avoidable IMO. I haven't bought any of the DLC as previously mentioned, mostly because the given price point seems high IMO. I can't comment on it other than that. The base game though is definitely worth it, especially if it's on any kind of sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly good.  I think this game suffered from bad marketing or something, because I wrote it off for awhile as a Marvel cash grab which was going to be a knockoff of XCOM.  I couldn't have been more wrong!  Fortunately I grabbed this on sale on a whim and I'm glad I did.  The combat has fairly little in common with XCOM other than being 3D and tactical, and I'm really enjoying how it works with the deckbuilding system.  The story is deep and engaging, there's a lot to explore at the home base area, along with base building, crafting, a friendship system, and more.  The graphics are pretty good and it's fun to try out all the different heroes.  The playable characters are a nice mix of the biggest names, although there's a few fun niche choices as well.This is way, way better than I was expecting it to be.  Pick up the Legendary edition on sale and try it out, Midnight Suns is an underrated gem which needs more love, so that we can get more DLC or a sequel someday.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it, if you enjoy Marvel and like the idea of interacting with heroes with your own character, then its absolutely worth it. I played the highest difficulty that was available to me (Higher ones gradually unlock) so some balancing of power will be different if you just play it on the story mode. This game also scratches that strategy itch, but its not xcom (though without the % hit RNG, one may say its better). I've gotten all but 1 achievement that requires a new game+, so ive experienced most if not all of what this game has to offer.I'll give some good and bad next.The BAD:-In its current state, even with fixes, the game chugs, has a fair amount of soft bugs, with a couple hard bugs. Some dialogue is cringey/cheesey but its limited to a couple of specific characters and you dont have to use them. -The game on higher difficulties has a lot of collection/grind. You need certain resources that spawn at your home base to craft and upgrade cards, bloating the experience.-More of annoyance but you cant turn off tutorial windows once you start the game, the setting is only available once the save file is created.-Some characters are unbalanced/weak and are close to unuseable on higher difficulties.-You can't create more than one deck, despite the amount of cards you have only having synergy with specific allies. -Some of the later dialogue is confusing and doesnt flow if you've done any of the extras you can do in the main hub of the game. These are few, but will leave you saying 'Wait that was addressed before'The GOOD:-Custom character (somewhat limited on variety) but in some ways it felt like when i first played KOTOR back in the day, being able to interact with characters and universe in a different way and honestly the biggest selling point.-The Voice acting is on point. A lot of familiar voice actors from the shows makes me feel more connected with the story.-When the game isnt lagging or chugging, the visuals are beautiful and the animations are a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The long and short of it, this is a real fun strategy game with some flaws that can make or break your experience.Positives!- Fun combat system- Collecting cards and building the set for each character is engaging.- The characters are well realized and acted, and don't rely on their MCU characterization! Getting to know them is a great time!- Combining fan-favourites with less well-known characters is worked into the story of the team.- Choosing dialogue to befriend characters feels engaging because they won't always like the same type of response every time. - Befriending heroes is rewarding in both gameplay and story!- Combat animation feel punchy and exciting!- Villain fights are an interesting challenge.- Using environment in combat to damage, stun and move enemies around never gets old.- The main hub is fun to explore!- I'm a fan of getting an original character to play as, and The Hunter works well as an audience stand-in.Meh.- Very basic story, some good and even great character moments, but nothing out of the ordinary for the main story.- Limited set of cards. I would've loved to see a greater variety of cards available for each character.- Arenas are reused a lot, and it would be nice to have greater variety there as well.- Visual customization is very basic, and it feels annoying to have to pay with an ingame currency for things I've unlocked to use them.- Visual style, graphics and animation in general is pretty bland. The character designs are solid, but outside of the superhero suits and the fights it all feels pretty stale.- Spamming gifts to make people like us in 2022. There must be better ways to build relationships in games!Negatives...- Messy bugs like enemies sinking into the floor making them hard to target, heads whipping around in cutscenes.- Stutters a lot even with the 2K Launcher disabled, even though it helps. Had to set the final fight to my lowest graphical setting to be able to play at all after a while.- Dialogue and subtitles don't match up at many points.- Dialogue often don't match up with earlier choices. My character got surprised by the same info several times. - Dialogue choices often felt misleading, and often didn't cover what felt like obvious responses to certain situations.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a brilliant game.The game brings to life the characters we've all seen on the big screen to the characters who have barely seen the limelight.With the game's focus more on strategy, deck building and limited resources, the game plays more of an XCOM-like than a true hero beat-em-up which feels refreshing compared to other superhero games that have been released.The combat does get sidelined by dialogue and relationships which to me was amazing.The best part of a game where you get to basically insert an OC is to just be able to hang out with all your favourite superheroes from genius, billionaire Tony Stark to angsty, emo Illyana Rasputin and learn more about their personalities and stories that you don't really get to see in movies and tv shows.If you are here to buy this game just to see your favourite heroes fight then you're in the wrong place.The beauty of Marvel has never been the never ending action scenes but the stories, relationships and melodramatic drama in between which this game properly brings to light.TLDR; This games a masterpiece for the true Marvel fan

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is a bit of a mixed bag.Pros:* The turn-based, card-based combat system is great. It has tons of interesting mechanics, interactions, and dynamics. It is a bit puzzle like (in an Into The Breach sort of way), such that it can be very satisfying when you figure out the perfect set of plays to turn around a bad situation.* The whole game is very polished. Other than one crash-to-desktop the only bug I experienced was a missing line of audio from a dialog.But also... Cons:* For a strategy game, there is a lot of non-strategy part of the game. Way too much. I'd estimate that over 80% of my ~70 hours were spent listening to dialogs, farming components, and playing a weird hero-fanfic-friendship simulator game.* The grind is real. You'll spend literally hours of the game running laps around the building each day, looking for little glowing resources that are 100% critical to upgrading cards to keep your deck relevant. As you progress through the game, you'll need even more resources to reroll random card mods till you get something decent.* For a deck building game, they sure make it a massive pain to build decks! To break down unneeded cards you have to run to one end of the abbey, to upgrade cards you need to run to another area. You need to go deep into a character menu to unequip cards that you'll want to upgrade. But you'll need to fill in the deck while you have those cards out, then manually dig through the deck and your card stockpile to place them back in. Why not allow upgrading of cards equipped in your deck? Why not just have one tool for deck management, upgrading, modding, and disassembling??* Nothing you do matters to the story. Sure there is only one ending, but that is fine. But every time I beat down an enemy boss, the cutscene is as if none of that happened. Beat down a boss... cut to a scene of your group cowering in fear of him. Beat down a different boss... cut to a scene of your group getting beat up, watching idly while he monologues, triggers his doomsday trap, and leaves. The conclusion to almost every boss battle was extremely unsatisfying.Overall, the core aspect of the game (the deck building turn-based strategy) is very good, but the only way I'll be doing another runthrough is with mods. Namely mods that dramatically decrease the grind, in particular by bumping up resource collection, friendship gains, and removing bad card mods when you reroll them.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Combat! Lots of fun. (Recommend buuuut only on a really good Sale.)Terrible story. I mean, you have to try super hard to make a story about Marvel Heroes so vanilla and uninteresting. It's not possible that it happened on accident. The "Every Choice Matters" slogan from the trailer is a lie, bold faced. Nothing you do matters. It is very very linear. What you say may affect what some one thinks of you, but it won't drop you below the current 'Friendship Level' you have with that character. So, in short, you can't make them hate you, not really, I tried. It's also not like you can change the outcome of the story or even any of the situations. Nothing you say or do will have any affect on the outcome of any quest what so ever. I have over a hundred hours in this game, because (aside from a really fun and addictive card system) I like to see the different directions an rpg can go, this one doesn't go anywhere. The majority of the games story (for what it is) is trying to make you hate the classic characters and drag you into constant nit pick sessions between the characters. I mean, these Super Powered Crybabies all act like it's junior high all over again. Trying to find clicks and see who can be the most dramatic at any given moment. Everyone has their feelings out on their sleeves. It's interesting at first but half way threw Chapter 2, I just wanted everyone to shut up. Especially Nico, Dear Lord she never stops!Fun Combat with an Interesting Strategy Card System, Absolute Gold! 8/10Graphics, Beautiful. 7.5/10Music, Fantastic. 6/10 (-1 point, because as awesome as it is, it is mind-numbingly repetitive)Voice Acting, Very Well Done. 7/10Story.... Ehhh 2/10 (+1 point for good voice acting)Honestly, it just seemed like an excuse to make a Marvel game with no real direction as to what kind of Marvel game. Its not thought out. As I said, most of it is meant to make you hate the 'Old Guard' and if you grew up reading Midnight Sons, Nightstalkers, Darkhold, etc, don't expect to see much that will bring back the joy or sense of wonder those titles held. The Midnight Sun's in this game universe are all younger heroes (even Blade claims to be in his 20's but as a half vampire he's not really sure. _childDocuments_.review: Midnight Suns is an odd game and I really struggle with recommending it at full price. I think a half price it's a definitely worth it, but I think most strategy vets will get bored of the combat very quickly. After beating the game, I reflected on my experience and wondered why it lacked the magic feel of X-Com 1 and 2. Heck I think I enjoyed Chroma Squad more as well. I'll list what I find to be pros and cons:  Pros: -Great animation overall -Marvel characters are well voice acted and sound like you think the characters should -Marvel characters act like you would expect if you watched the movies -Combat is fun at first -The story is a comic book story for those that like that -Some have reported lots of bugs and performance issues, but I have had few. I had a couple crashes on only 1 mission and the final mission had a severe frame rate drop for the whole mission. My brother has a 3080 and I have a 2080ti and we both had this issue on the final mission. Overall though, the game is snappy and responsive. I think a few abilities may not work correctly, but I am sure that will be ironed out and didn't affect my ability to complete any missions. -controller support is great -some may like the difficulty curve on normal is much easier than X-Com -there are some fun customization options for your main character (nothing special) -all characters are viable (but some are definitely better than others) Cons: -The combat is designed in small arenas and your characters can't perma-die. so, you lose all of the tension from fog of war and easy fights. I realize this isn't X-Com, but what they fill those holes with is...nothing. There's no added depth to compensate for the streamlining of combat. In fact, the game strongly incentivizes you to take out the enemy as quickly as possible. You get to a point where you can win a map in 1 turn before the enemy can even move. The other big part of combat is using the objects conveniently placed in the arena for extra damage (think explosive barrels) that don't require cards to use. Once you figure out how to maximize your turns, the game becomes trivial very quickly. Slay the spire this is not. As you play the game more, it just feels like it's missing something, as the game never ramps to anything cool, new abilities are just different versions of what you already have. The exception is legendary cards, which you can only use one of per deck. The legendary abilities are so laughably broken and so easily cheated out, that it takes away any cleverness you may have felt. They're more or less a win button. -There isn't very much depth to the combat, there isn't very many abilities (cards) per character, and most characters abilities overlap with each other quite a bit. There are 12 card abilities per character and you can play 8, so don't expect to be making some insane strategy or expect to have some cool unique build. You get to add modifiers to your cards at random, so expect to grind A LOT for currency if you want to try and make a perfect deck.  -There is a big lack of enemy variety. This one really shocked me because X-Com always kept introducing you to new enemies to keep you on your toes, but don't expect this here. Even the last mission you're fighting the same trash enemies you've fought a million times. It disappointed me. Of what enemies are here, X-Com 2 vets will notice Hydra enemies are ripped right out of X-Com 2. There are also some demon enemies that are very similar to their X-Com 2 counterparts. This lowers the difficulty bar further when you know exactly what to expect. -There is just too much dialog and most of it isn't interesting. You keep listening because there are Easter eggs and bits here and there that are great, but they get fewer as the game drifts more toward established characters. Firaxis really tried to make the characters their comic book counterparts and I think the Avengers roster really hurt the game's story. I would've preferred more new characters or characters that gave more creative freedom. Nico and Magik were my favorite characters and I didn't expect that going in. The other big issue is that characters are dealing with the issues they've already dealt with in the comics, so most of the character's problems you're not going to care about if you already know about that. Firaxis goes back to well several times for the same character and it's just incredibly boring. "Yes Robbie, we know you think we only value you and not Sparky (his demon power)" you'll think to yourself when dealing with Ghostrider. Most characters have the same recurring problem and there is A LOT of dialog. It definitely would have helped the game (maybe not sales) to pare down the character roster to improve individual stories. -The game is made in the x-com 2 engine and the visuals look dated. Since the game is zoomed in more the lack of detail is more noticeable. I think a cell shaded or comic book aesthetic would've really made the game pop, but that's just me. It's about PlayStation 3 level, with better texture smoothing. -There is a lot of filler. It feels like half the game was cut out and what is there was stretched. You are forced to do a generic mission after each main mission. You may decide that it's not needed because you're doing so well, but sorry, you have no choice. It's baked in. -Too much progression is locked behind friendship levels. I was only able to get 2 people to max friendship level by the end of the game, which you will want to do to earn their legendary card. There are also powerful passive abilities and upgrades lock behind friendship. Also, I was never able to figure out why I could or could not hang out with a hero after a mission. Sometimes you can, sometimes you can't. Doesn't matter if it's a story mission or not, it just seems to be random. It's just a poorly implemented system. Friendship hangout scenes are some of the worst in the game imo, with some of the worst dialog. It's just boring. -There is some very light puzzles and rewards for exploring the Abbey grounds which is mostly optional, but a big chunk of content. You learn about the Salem Witch Trials through many characters diary entries. This simply did not interest me. There weren't really any fun or interesting surprises, just a way to get the games many currencies. There are far too many currencies for no apparent reason, since they can all be gotten in the same channels. Anyway, I think the Abbey exploration kind of sucks, but it is a nice change of pace. Like a lot of this game, it feels designed to take up time rather than be fun. Was this game supposed to be a live service, but changed at some point? I wonder... -Some heroes, like Ghostrider, are straight up broken. Some characters, like your dog, are so bad you're better off leaving them dead so you only get cards for your main character. The frustrating thing is that for story reasons the game loves to decide who you get to bring to a mission for you. This is annoying because characters level slowly and they don't get experience by simply being in the mission. It seems that experience is given on a per card played basis. So, the rich tend to get richer. There is a grind mission you can do, but it is painfully slow, the same every time, very easy, and done on a single character basis. With 11-12 characters and 4 more coming in the season pass, this is a time sink, and a bad one at that. -There is a base building aspect, but unlike X-Com, there is no time restraint, so you will be able to get everything. Without any sacrifices to make, it makes this a superficial and pointless system. -There is a light vs. dark dialog choice system and I hate it. I usually love this type of thing, but I want to pick my responses based on role playing, not to go full dark/light so I can unlock things. character limit :(

_childDocuments_.review: Free weekend review: I actually really enjoy this game, but I gotta be honest that it's definitely not for everyone, which is why I'm not recommending this game. The gameplay seems so niche, like a weird mix between XCOM Chimera Squad and Slay the Spire with more than a bit of Persona 5 social links added into the mix. If that sounds like something you'd like then I'd say give it a go, but wait for a sale because even though I like it I wouldn't pay full price for it. There's just too many things that are "off" for it to be worth 60 euro. I'll try to get into some of it.The combat is interesting, but kind of outstays its welcome by adding a wave or two too many enemies into every battle. I feel like they could have added a more interesting way of balancing out combat than to just add 2 or 3 weak enemies every turn.The "good stuff" in this game is the heroes interacting with one another and most of this happens back at the abbey that serves as your base. While most of the dialogue and friendship boosting seems like it'd work better for an X-Men game taking place at the X Mansion it's still fun here, even if it seems like it's not really in style with many of the characters. The writing is well done though, which means that the characters themselves will often point out that normally they'd probably not go painting in the woods with you.The voice acting is.... Decent, I guess. There's some characters that maybe could have used a better actor or a couple more takes for their lines at the very least. Just as an example I started the game out with the Male Hunter as my main character, but decided I'd rather start over with the Female Hunter since the male version was just Matt Mercer speaking with his normal voice and that broke immersion a bit for me when I know that it's him I guess.After playing a good chunk of the game as female though I wish I had stuck with Mercer, since the directing they gave the female voice actor must have been "Can you sound bored and confused at the same time?"She honestly sounds like she could do just fine if they let her go with a more natural voice, which is a shame.Now for the thing I hate the most in the game: Currencies! There's like at least a dozen different currencies you have to keep track of and the game does a poor job of explaining how you earn some of it (Knowledge for example), what it'll do and how much you have, while other currencies can be found in your inventory with a tooltip for where to earn it and spend it. Mix this with a Mortal Kombat Krypt-like island that you are meant to go and explore now and then and you'll likely be very confused about what you are meant to be gathering for the game and what you are just gathering for the sake of a lore dump. I'll admit that they do have some good lore in here, but the way it is presented could definitely have been handled better.Now to wrap back around, there's enough of this that I can tolerate and enjoy, so this is a great game for me. Others however, might find it very niche and intimidating to get started on, especially if they only know marvel from the MCU.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a discount. Still probably not worth it. I didn't play too much, but there were a number of things that made it undesirable to start off right out the gate.1. The game is a memory hog. 8gb of active memory being pommeled at almost all times and causing lag even during simple attack cinema scenarios in combat. This spikes hard when the cinematics are playing. Put that into perspective: COD, FF15, and other graphically intense games run quite smoothly on my laptop. This game however, with it's mediocre graphics absolutely beats my machine up.2. The cinematics are uninspired and the dialogue is equally so.  The story concept is good, but it's poorly executed and clunky.3. The tutorial is actually pretty good. 4. After sitting around watching dialogue for too long, you finally go on your first mission, but there is a lot of 'running around' in environments that make it feel like you should actually be playing an entirely different kind of game. Like... an MMO. But then,  when you actually PLAY the game, it's a turn based strategy game. IF the mission and character interactions were less MMO / RPG and more Strategy / Tactical it would feel a LOT smoother, and waste a lot less time. At the onset it feels like the Running around in mostly empty zones just to interact with THIS object, or THAT NPC... is there to simply waste time in the form of stretching out gameplay hours and so on. I think I understand that they were trying to make it feel more immersive... but they REALLY missed the mark on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with the good, the game overall is actually fantastic in most aspects. The humor is great whether you're familiar with these characters or not. The characters themselves are also well written, they all feel like the characters they're supposed to be and not just caricatures of them. The amount of characters in the game is also great, as long as it isn't too obscure you're probably going to find some of your favorite characters here. The gameplay itself is also well done and all the characters are fittingly thematic to how they are treated inside with the card-game mechanics. And the bad, but it's more due to preference than anything actually bad. It's done by the XCOM devs, which are fantastic at what they do, but have a tendency to make games very difficult where every individual fight is equally difficult and taxing on you. This is great for most people, but me personally I don't like games like XCOM or Divinity: Original Sin where every fight is supposed to be extremely deadly. I don't like how it doesn't let me make character build choices simply because it's cool and fun rather than because of how effective it is. Especially in this Marvel game, I would want to use all my favorite characters in a team together rather than have to take characters I don't like for mechanical reasons. This isn't helped by the fact that I'm just not very good at strategy and tactics game, but again that's not the game's fault, it's just a miss-match in tastes. I would personally enjoy a difficulty option lower than Normal that would let me play the game in a more chill form that I'd enjoy, but I also recognize that I'm not necessarily the game's target audience in the first place. TLDR: It's a fantastic game that you're probably going to enjoy, but the game can be pretty difficult. Every fight is going to be tough and if you don't like XCOM you probably won't like this.

Pour your water mixture into your flour and mix by hand until you get a rough dough, then transfer to a work surface and knead until it starts to pull away from the work surface and is relatively smooth.Place your dough in a greased bowl, then cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 - 2 hours at room temperature or until double in size.Punch down your dough and dive into 300g pieces. Form those pieces into balls and place them in a floured proofing pizza box, cover with a lid, and proof at room temperature for 3 - 4 hours. _childDocuments_.review: This game is quite addicting! I have personally never been able to enjoy turn-based combat, it just never clicked for me. Midnight Suns' combat is very accessible and the attack animations look amazing, plus you can use the environment by slamming enemies into objects for extra damage. There is a LOT of extra exploring, talking with teammates, leveling up abilities, crafting. etc. and I LOVE every bit of it. I am the kind of player who talks to every single crew mate in Mass Effect between missions, so this side of the gameplay suits me well. I can understand how some players may be put off by it, but for me it's perfect.There is a lot to learn, but I feel the game gives you new things at a good pace. It has a fantastic "day" mechanic where you sleep to start the next day, then each day you can explore, visit your craft stations, and run a mission when you feel like it. After a mission, it's usually evening and other social activities may trigger, then that's about it until the next day. What I like about this system is that, unlike something like AC: Valhalla, you never feel overwhelmed by the amount of stuff to do. There's only so much you CAN do, until you yourself decide to sleep and advance the clock. The RPG elements are fun, working on the card decks for each hero is fun, it's just an excellent package. You can choose the combat costumes and the off-duty costumes for your character and for each hero, and you unlock a ton of them during gameplay. There is even a light/dark mechanic for the player character, that changes the abilities available to you. I am very glad I decided to try this game, I'm looking forward to playing for many more hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a detrimentally excessive amount of talking. Not only is there a truly colossal amount of it, but it is almost entirely the most generic and mundane low effort writing imaginable. I like lore. I like worldbuilding. I like narratively driven video games. For me to have this complaint is unusual, but here we are.The rush of completing a difficult encounter is without exception tempered by a sigh of exasperation when I am transported back into the hub social area and am inevitably forced to faff around with mountains of witless dialogue. Midnight Suns doesnt just have a relationship management minigame, relationship management  a big chunk of the core gameplay. All of it is tied to combat efficacy, so you can't really just skip it; it is essentially mandatory.I wouldn't have an issue if only this element of the game was interesting or engaging, but it wore my patience down to the point where I just gave up.

_childDocuments_.review: Not at all a Marvel fan? No problem. My love of Marvel is skin deep and ends at Spiderman (Batman on the DC side). Even Avengers doesn't do it for me, though Blade was and will always be badass and was a main draw for me to get the game. All the same I found myself super engrossed in the interactions between the new player MC and the other heroes, not to mention learning about heroes I had literally never heard of. By the end my favorite in the game was actually Magik, a character I didn't know existed. This game actually makes me regret not being born about 4 years earlier to have hit the comic book craze. It also makes me regret not supporting it a lot sooner as a Firaxis and tactical game fan. I usually hate card games, but once more, this game is making me rethink my stance on that. Maybe I don't hate card games, maybe I just hate bad ones. Midnight Sun is worth your money and hopefully we can get a resurgence and see the Midnight Suns appear in other media and hopefully lead to another game. Even if not this one, I would adore getting the chance to be with the characters as they were imagined and brought to life in this game.Marvel fans, if you bought suicide squad or avengers and you didn't buy this game, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame on you. Shame on me for not trusting Firaxis. Shame on the gaming community for letting down a genuinely good game during one of the bigger slumps since the early nineties games industry crash. Even the length of this review, almost certainly my longest positive review should say something. Hell the game even gets small things right that I've only seen in a few places. Such as head items not deleting hair. My female hunter's hair would actually gather at the edges of her hood, or be noticeably pressed down by a headband, and that's the custom character's one of many hairstyles against one of many accessories. The people that made this game, made it with love, and its sad that they didn't get the love they deserved in return. TLDR buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start I need to admit that I may be a little bit biased because I love turn based tactical games and in particular X-Com series by Firaxis. Naturally I had big expectations of this game given the franchise that they were using. I was also sceptical about the card system, but it turned out to be one of the best components of the game, so, without further ado here’s my grumpy opinion.The game probably has the worst of cliché storylines and the dullest of protagonists dialogue wise, however given that it is Marvel universe expecting something more is naïve. But everything that the game does wrong with cringe dialogues and superficial story it makes up in core gameplay. Card system is really well thought through and the protagonist is OP as hell, however you can win even without having him on your team of 3. The card system is really well thought through and allows you to mode each hero to your liking creating a super soldier. Each hero has a deck of 8 cards comprised of offensive, defensive and super abilities. There are of course rules to how you build you deck that you should consider because some cards generate ‘hero points’ and some cards require ‘hero points to be played’ so thoughtful balancing and upgrading of the deck would be key to your success and ability to chain attacks and use environmental attacks (all these require hero points, unless you play a special card).The graphics and moves look crisp and mixing the heroes on missions gives you almost infinite possibilities and variation of graphics to keep you entertained. score 8/10 – game play is great, marvel universe depicted is near perfect, but it needs a button to ‘skip all dialogue’ and quasi RPG base exploration.For more grumpy reviews follow my curator page at

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended but know well in advance what you get into.You will like this if you like a good card-based tactical combat, if you like building and optimising decks to combo things together, and you don't mind too much a bit of "card pack randomness".Combat is fun, especially if you're a board gamer as this feels like a good tabletop sim. Every character has a different playstyle - reflected heavily by their set of cards - and there are many chances to create some cool and powerful combos. The game forces you to use most of the charachters across all missions, so you need to invest and know their abilities to make sure you know how to use each character abilities at best.The abbey in between missions it's the boring part of the game. It feels like a "mobile" game with all the social/friendship sim stuff; can get cringy at times; it's sadly a bit needed, but you don't need to max out all levels to succeed (but helps); and some of the currencies you get are luckily only for cosmetics.The good part of the Abbey, is actually exploring the grounds, solving the mysteries and putting together the lore.The story overall can drag a bit, but there are a cool few nice battles that squeeze your brain to pull them off if you use a certain group of characters.

_childDocuments_.review: To make it clear, this game isn't inherently bad, but it does have many problems. Some are minor, while others are not. I was tempted to write a negative review because of the serious problems that this game has, but at the same time, I don't hate it. To make it short.+ The list of characters includes less popular characters. Blade, Nico, Magik etc. It's not just Avengers or X-Men again.+ The plot of the game is fresh. + Still modern Turn-Based combat (XCOM), but with superheroes. Each hero is different. Some of them have unique mechanics. No more random recruits. + Different outfits.+ No Overwatch. Many XCOM clones used (and probably still use) this mechanic. It makes the combat boring and repetitive. I can't imagine how a PvP match in a game with overwatch would look like.+ No Chance to Hit/less RNG. I had enough of this mechanic back in XCOM 2. I remember when my character with a shotgun was in front of the enemy and with a 90+ chance to hit, he still missed the shot. In MS, you always hit the target.- Annoying enemy types. It's how XCOM and now MS work. The more you advance through the story, the more enemy types you will encounter. Some can multiply and clone any unit, others will make bonds with other units, so they can't be killed separately. I honestly had enough of these games. It's like every Turn-based game is using this formula.- Some outfit choices are poor. Fallen, Medieval etc. There are much more interesting options in the comics.- Item/Plant gathering mechanic is filler. This is not a MMO. Not even a classic RPG.- Some of the dialogues are cringe, silly or woke. Also, Deadpool used the same joke that Iron Man used in Marvel's Avengers. " For Me? You Shouldn't Have." Do I need to explain to you why it was MS who stole the joke?- Speaking of woke. As you may or may not know, the Marvel has gone woke since the 2010s. Why 2010s? I will tell you, my curious friend. Around that time, the Disney company has bought Marvel. 2010s became an era of "cashgrab" movies. With each movie it was worse and worse. More dumb humor, more woke stuff. So we have come to the point where a lot of people are tired of this crap. It's not limited to movies. Comics have also taken this direction. Race change, gender change.Ms. Marvel (Carol) took the mantle of Captain Marvel, who is originally a man. They had to change the damn character and make her look like a lesbian feminist. She will tell you how poor Thor is sad that he is number 3 of the strongest character, after Captain Marvel and Hulk.Ghost Rider (Johnny Blaze) (white male) was replaced by a new character - Robbie Reyes (Latino). Not that I have anything against Latinos or Robbie, but I'm pretty sure that Johnny had enough popularity.At least they didn't include female versions of Hawkeye and Thor. We do have old lesbian witches...- This game is a technical mess. FPS drops in some battles (I had this in final battle), long loading times before the Abbey (even with SSD), texture (neck) bug, character animation (battle) bugs, broken music (will stop playing) bug. The biggest problem is the Abbey performance. FPS drops are huge. Developers released a few patches, but that didn't solve the problem."Take-Two CEO Srauss Zelnick admits the tactical role-playing game Marvel's Midnight Suns developed by Firaxis has been a commercial failure.""December release window could take some blame, as it pit the game in direct competition with other anticipated titles like The Callisto Protocol and High on Life. Though, The Callisto Protocol underwhelmed both critics and audiences alike and is also considered a commercial flop for its publisher Krafton."By now, you should know that games released in December were mediocre or worse. Few were also commercial failures. Weak excuse, in my opinion. Also, Jake Solomon announced his departure from Firaxis.This genre is not very popular. Add to that MS card-based combat system, filler content, and poor optimization, and you can see why this game failed. Few people like turn-based games. Especially card games.Who was the target audience for Midnight Suns? According to statistics from one website, Marvel fans are predominantly white. With the number of males being a bit higher than females. Latinos were around 9%. Others are even less.Around 40%  of the "fans" were Millennials, quarter Boomers, quarter of X people and around 7% were Zoomers.If we bring statistics related to "gamers", then the number of female players will drop significantly.Now I will ask again - Who was the target audience? I'm not trying to be an elitist, but the facts don't care about our feelings. Dialogues and some character choices made me think that this game targeted "rainbow" Zoomers. Some TBS fans may find this game less tactical or simply hate superhero stuff.Some "older" (not children) players won't find dialogues/characters interesting.Many Marvel fans won't like new/replaced characters.I'm not saying you should ignore this game, but if you plan on playing it, then be prepared for bugs/performance issues. I also think the price is too high for what we get.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros * Lots of Marvel characters and lore * Makes you want to play Xcom instead* All characters have tons of costumes you can customize * Lots of iconic characters you can get in your team* Easy to mod and have bunch of mods that fix terrible game design choices.Cons * Writing is bad.* Horrendous card combat system.* All fights have annoying timers or "reinforcements incoming" after each turn. It's not fun, it's frustrating.* There are only few types of fights on repeat and you will know what to expect each time. * Most costumes and visual items look terrible.* The best characters are locked behind paywall in a premium priced game.* Voice acting and directing is just wrong. It's jarring how bad many of the characters sound. Not a great casting neither.* It becomes somewhat playable only with mods.* Game showers you in dozen different currencies, unlock mechanics and lootboxes (luckily only acquired by gameplay) right at the start. It makes it feel like lacklustre live service wannabe, that was changed later in development. But the "log in tomorrow for more free premium currency" feel is still all over the gameplay. What if Xcom was badly designed card combat game with mostly talking instead of fighting or building base. If you just want to hang out with random Marvel characters and spend infinite hours clicking through dialogues, you might like this. If you want good tactical combat and game mechanics, this might be one of the worst games in the genre. Writing is bad. It's "hello fellow kids" and Josh Whedon`ism overload. Most of the jokes don`t land. The main conflict once again is just another world ending "giant laser in the sky" type of bs that you cannot relate to. Game has increadibly annoying superhero social media app, where your companions will often bother you. Entire gameplay loop mostly is walking back and forth around your home base and repeat the same exact tasks every day. Wake up, do mandatory conversations, do several daily tasks around base, complete one mission, then go to bed. And repeat that endlessly. It's about 70% talking to Marvel characters in annoying dialogues, and the rest remaining 30% is tactical gameplay, which is not very good neither. Combat is bad. All your characters have cards as moves that you randomly pick in each turn. But you can use only up to 3 per turn. Sometimes 4 with some boosts. If you are unlucky, you can get stuck for several turns, where you cannot make a move and will lose fights, because all your randomly picked cards in hand needs to be charged by other, weaker attack cards. No basic attack outside cards. And you can only have up to 3 team members in a fight. And when building character`s deck, you can only have certain amount of different card types. There are way to many restrictions for combat to be fun. Most of them luckily can be fixed with mods, but the game is balanced around those restrictions. Combat is big step back from Xcom. Better go play that.

_childDocuments_.review: I was intending to leave a negative review until around the 20 hour mark, in the end I really enjoyed the game, but would say it has two main faults.Firstly, the mechanics are very complicated. There's a tonne of things to learn and numerous varied in-game currencies to earn to drive each of them. The time to proficiency is long, and running through all your daily tasks can feel like a bit of a chore by the end.Secondly, the pacing in the open-world Abbey portion of the game is wrong, as it allows you too much freedom at the start. You can get through around half of the exploration and questing within a few in-game days, which has two negative impacts:1.  It ruins the balance between the exploration and card battle aspects of the game. The card battling is by far the stronger portion, but you can spend so much time on the exploration in the early game, that it makes the card part feel like an after-thought.2. You do eventually hit a gate in the exploration part, and then have to wait several story missions to progress (without any indication of WHEN you'll be able to progress) and no longer have anything to do at nights.There is a tonne of content here, built around a really strong card game as the base. I would recommend the game, but caution you to pace yourself with the Abbey exploration, otherwise you may not find the first part of the game very enjoyable.Last thoughts - Magik is best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.  It's no real strategy game, you buy a marvel movie with some interactive elements and minigames.2. The dialogues are rather funny, I laughed twice (which is a lot for me) and had 1 cringe moment (in 4.5h ). The story is interesting.3. I enjoyed the combat minigame very much, but it never was a challenge to win.Verdict:Whenever the designers had to make a decision between 'more like a marvel movie' or 'more like a strategy game' , they went for the movie. I would still have bought it, but the nail in the coffin is the absolutly desastrously stupid decision to lock the veteran and expert difficulty modes!!I don't care if I play with robots, super heroes , dwarves or whatever , only the game itself must be fun AND CHALLENGING ! So, if the designers already force me to rather watch a movie than playing a game, why the hell I'm not allowed to make this rare combats more challenging ?!?Under absolutly no circumstances I can imagine to play this 'game' again from the start after finishing, to be able to play the next higher difficulty mode!!!I had 5 or 6 combats ranging from 2 min to 8 or 9 min. All in all I spent maybe 30-45 min actually 'playing'!I guess I spent almost 20-30 min walking around the abbey, and that makes around 3.5h watching a movie.Remember that I said the story is interesting? _childDocuments_.review: For the x-th time, why isn't there a Neutral/Meh option for the reviews?The visuals are gorgeous, the terrain and costume textures are beautiful, so much that at times they made me feel like I could almost touch certain elements. The same for skill / attack abilities. (Mostly)So why Negative instead of Positive when I would prefer Neutral? - Talking. Too much pointless talking. I get that game designers wanted to develop the personality of each member of our crew, but it ended up either shallow, or thinned out due to "likability" system, with scarce handful of interesting motives available later. It's not tragic, we get a chance to learn some backstory for this particular iteration of Iron-Man, Logan, Wanda and so on, but again due to the likability system, it feels like each story ends up being a poor drama, where the main character is the savior, without whom the other superhero would crumble due to sadness. <Sob> Add to it an incredibly poor facial expressions, or even their lack outside of the main story and it makes it hard to get invested.- Pacing and battle systems. The main story isn't bad, it's Marvel focused on the Arcane, in some ways the "Abbey" gives me Harry Potter vibes... But the title should be focused on battle more. There is such a potential in the battle system, it's satisfying, the number of heroes to choose from and their skills give us a lot of options and possibilities to set up powerful combos and to decimate the enemies, especially with the ability to use the environment, or even enemies themselves as a damage source. If I could move from one battle to another, it would be great, but we are locked in an unbreakable loop of: Choose battle mission, be done in 3-10 minutes, back to the Abbey for the Night phase, sleep, wake up in the Abbey for the Day phase, now you may choose another mission. It may not look like much by reading it, but doing it for 50 or 100 times...- (By the way: certain passive character skills are locked behind likability system, so you better talk and talk and talk...)- RNG and associated systems - each completed mission rewards us with a loot-box containing cards (active skills) of the heroes who participated in the mission. Later on you can craft those cards, but in order to get access to the specific card, you need to receive it at least once from the loot box. Best of luck!- Cosmetics. Lots and lots of cosmetics ranging from entire new costumes for all the playable heroes, through their recolors, ending with options to casually dress up the crew while they're chilling in the Abbey. Some people will love it, some like me will consider it useless, even more when it comes to the main character. I was greatly surprised why the initial character creator would offer such a small number of options... Surprise! Ten times of that is available later on through unlocks. But! But, but! You don't simply unlock the modification. You unlock the option to unlock it, for which you still have to pay with the in-game currency.The game certainly has potential, but the developers needlessly thinned everything out. Wait until it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: When I became aware Marvel Midnight Suns was coming out, I added it to my wishlist immediately. For a little background, I love turn-based games, X-com type games, super heroes, and games with heavy talking (Pathfinder and other RPGs game of its ilk).I am an older player with a full time job and lots of kids. Have been a gamer for years. I provide that info just so you get the gist of my perspective.With that said, this game is amazing. There are shortcomings for sure. The character animation is stiff when moving around in RPG mode (moving about the abbey). The facial animation can be a bit odd at times too.While I noticed this in comparison with some 4A games, it was manageable to me in the sense that I could still connect with the characters. That and some minor QoL items (the mouse cursor staying on screen during cutscenes) were really the only things I would say detract some.On the plus side:1. The game is LONG. I think this is a good thing (with all of my caveats above). I am 48 hours in and I feel like I am still early or in the middle of the game. I could quibble about some of the dialogue being unnecessary. But, the amount of building, exploring, missions, etc... is amazing when you compare to a lot of games that take less than 15 hours to complete, feel less satisfying, and cost just as much. I would put this in the category of a great value.2. The game is technically excellent. Again, I am acknowledging the animation items mentioned earlier. But, I have a 10700K processor, 32gb of RAM, M2 storage, and an RTX 2080 Super graphics card. I can run the game with mostly Epic settings (some shadow settings are on high) and get between 60-90 FPS depending on the scene. Considering the amount of content and variety in the actual components (settings, cut scenes, dialogue, actual missions, etc...) that is a very good achievement in my mind. There are still some optimizations I think they could make (occasional stutters) but overall I think it is great. It crashed once prior to their recent patch.3. This is subjective, but I love the variety in the incorporated game styles. There is base building, resource management, deck building, turn-based battles, RPG elements, and much more. It scratches a gaming itch in many categories for me.If you thrive on action all the time and do not like games with heavy dialogue then you will likely not like this. I am not 100% sure that even if you loved Marvel you would overcome it if you did not like the dialogue and the mission downtime. But, if you are a gamer like me as described then you will love it and should get it. I would rate it 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game of the year.  While Elden Ring will always be #1, it was difficult and had a lot of moments that would make me rage, only to go back to it like a toxic ex gf.But on a serious note, Midnight Suns fulfills all of my Marvel Gaming desires, the gameplay is easy to learn and hard to master, the card system is really just a move set that allows you to juggle between the 3 characters you choose to do missions with(In side missions, you can replace Hunter and go with 3 Marvel heroes if you so choose to.)  I had so many worries with this game, and how the mainstream reviews were complaining that areas like the main hub world, The Abbey, were uninspired and boring. _childDocuments_.review: The game has several flaws to its core design. Such as how it actually gets easier when you have fewer heroes "alive" due to your hand not being watered down by three different "decks". (Since you can only draw cards for "active" heroes.)The abbey outside free-roam section is also completely disconnected from the main game-play loop. You can literally ignore the entire thing and miss basically nothing. Which is good, because the free roam section sucks. You have no mini-map. This makes it very easy to turned around/lost. The map you bring up is also heavily lacking in details on what things are located where. So it's barely of any use either.Balance is also heavily off, with both Hunter and Iron Man standing head and shoulders faaaarrr above any of the other heroes. Some cards are also badly designed/utterly useless. Which is a problem, because you only get EXP/cards for the heroes you use. So the less you use someone, the worse they become.Speaking of cards, the card upgrade system is also a slog once you arrive at the "mod" mechanic. Mods are randomly generated, and trying to re-roll them gets expensive *very* quickly. So you actually have to keep juggling multiple copies of the same card(s) as you attempt to RNG a "good" mod for them.There's also an enemy with a very poor design in the late game. Its gimmick is that it will duplicate itself every time it survives being hit. Ideally, you build up your "hero" meter, and hit it with a super powerful attack. The problem? If you *don't* attack it...it will duplicate itself anyways! And then the duplicate will start duplicating other enemies as well! On lower difficulties this isn't too huge a deal, but the highest difficulty sets all enemies to 225% HP. So not only is it much harder to kill in a single blow, but it has a lot more time, and damage, to start stealing your HP to heal itself back up.It's not a bad game, but it's one that you can stand to wait for a sale on.Just don't but the season pass. That thing is overpriced to a sickening degree.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it short. I think this is a game made by marvel fans. Everyone is not a background character and you can go as deep into their lore as you like, bond with them to learn more. They all feel like they should. All playing like they should and act like they should. If you like anyone in this roster, you are going to be surprised how much writing they put into them. You will learn something about everyone here and outside just lore dump, you get to see them all interact with each other like real people and not like a super hero movie. Its a dorm full of all these hero's with their masks off and you can see everyone get on each other's nerves and make friends with each other. Its very charming how much of a real person they make everyone seem. Its also optional too if you dont want to waste your time on the writing and just want the gameplay and main story.The gameplay is pretty solid. Its turn based "everyone on your team acts" and then your opponent does the same. The actions you can do on your turn is based on the cards you draw. Oh by the way, its a card game too. Everyone feels powerful and their animations are beautiful. Its a wet dream for a nerd to see their hero's fight together like this.For a marvel fan, its a must if you like to interact with these hero's like never before in a marvel medium. If you just want the cool looking combat, I recommend.If you are not a marvel fan but interested in getting into it, I recommend it. Like I mentioned previously, you get to learn the lore of everyone and their personalities. Its charming and the gameplay is fun to watch.If you are not a marvel fan and not interested in learning about marvel. Its an above average game. writing is competent and sometimes even compelling. Combat is very unique and will give you a fun experience. Wait for a sale to give it a try....or not.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's fun if you like turn based card games but it's a lot easier to immerse yourself into the game if you're already a big fan of the franchise and these characters.The core game play becomes very fun and tactical the further into the game you get; at first it might be hard to fully grasp every mechanic and the most efficient ways to play. That sounds like a given, "the more you play, the more you understand" but I feel like a lot of people could easily give up on this game within the first few hours as it might not be what they expected or feels kinda slow. The game straight up runs like ass. After all the optimisation possible like disabling the 2K launcher or installing on SSD there's not a lot you can do to get the game to play on anything smoothly above 60fps unless you are willing to sacrifice high or epic quality graphics which I wouldn't recommend as the graphics themselves are already well below the quality of a standard game with this price tag.The story and characterisation is very good. I enjoyed playing through the campaign, everyone has a personality and a role besides a few outliers. I feel like having DLC does enhance you're experience as the characters you obtain via DLC fit right into the story at whatever point you obtain them making content that wasn't originally in the game work very fluidly. Also all the designs in this game are amazing, Fallen Hulk and Fallen Venom are some of the best designed iterations I've seen of these characters.There's a lot going on in this game and for the most part it's really captivating. With several things happening at once whilst still making each plot affect the other, it all plays very nicely and it really gets you invested in the main character. Hunter themselves isn't the most interesting character unfortunately in my opinion, despite how much lore you are given with them. You get the option to go down and light and dark path with Hunter and ultimately i don't think it affects the game play whatsoever.I finished the game at around 44 Hours whilst doing DLC and side quests in that time and I enjoyed the majority of the game very much. I will say post game seems to be very bad, bit of a spoiler but all the events of the game seem to be retconned or just didn't happen, the only explanation of this is that Hunter woke up in a time before the events of the Finale and that's it. It really ruins any immersion you had in the game and the characters seem a lot more bland as everything that happened... didn't? Post game aside, it's a great game for Marvel fans and I could see people who have never heard of these characters finding some interest in it too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for me. And that's OK. I'm sure the people who it is for are having a blast with it! I didn't read anything or watch anything about this game at all before going in. My brother absolutely LOVES it. Additionally, I was a HUGE fan of Ultimate Alliance and someone who is off the Christmas Card list now had mentioned it gave them very strong UA vibes (it does NOT at all, btw) so I bit on the digital+ sale. And while it's not a complete waste for me, I was definitely underwhelmed. The story elements are cheesy, but entertaining. The graphics, while a huge complaint for some folks, I think fit it very well. The voice acting ranges from competent to outstanding. What ruins it for me (and what will save it for the right person) is the combat mechanics. It feels very mobile-game. I do not like card/deck builders at all - again, not knowing what I was in for - but I gave it a go anyway. And I just absolutely hated the combat. You have a limited set of mixed offensive, defensive, and buff/skill cards which get drawn randomly, coupled with some very limited move/sacrifice/point based options in any battle. It honestly feels more like Ooblets than any other game I've ever played. Though Ooblets is mercifully much shorter in the battles department and has round limits. The battles in Midnight Suns drag on and on and you're clicking the same handful of cards over and over. I would have much rather had a set of skills with burnable 'mana' or even a non-card based opportunity system. But if you love card mechanics, this is probably very light weight and might even be TOO simple. I'm just one of those people who doesn't understand the need to shoehorn cards into systems. Looking at YOU, Back 4 Blood. The game also requests a lot of lore knowledge to *fully* take in. It's not required, but it certainly expands the experience if you're aware of some of the non-film Marvel storylines. That's one of the parts I loved, but could see it turning off a casual Marvel fan. Also, Tony Stark pulling a constant Shaggy Rogers re: g-g-g-g-GHOSTS got a little thick a little quick. Overall though, I can't recommend it for people like me, who aren't looking for card clickers. And I definitely don't love the mobile feel to everything, including monetization mechanics. Also, googling how to bypass the 2K launcher is ESSENTIAL if you don't want really awful stuttering. The game is jam packed with the horsemen of the PCocalypse. Denuvo being the biggest offender, but extra launchers absolutely not helping matters.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan. The tactics side doesn't feel as deep as something like XCOM, but it's still really fun, and at max difficulty I quite frequently find myself just barely making it through a mission, with every choice both before and during the fight feeling appropriately important.However, I consider the real selling-point here being the social aspect. Think something like Fire Emblem, where over time you'll get to know a cast of interesting characters, and hopefully, if the writing clicks with you, start to care about their stories. Despite this being a licensed Marvel game, my favourite characters were ones I had absolutely no connection to, such as Magik and Nico. I had never heard about them before, but as a result of this game, I'm looking forward to checking out their comics. Bear in mind that if you're not interested at all in that part of the game, you're likely going to be disappointed by Midnight Suns. While it seems to be technically possible to avoid most of the conversations, the average playthrough will be nearly equal parts conversation and tactics combat. If one or the other isn't your cup of tea, the experience will be frustrating.That being said, my only real criticisms are related to stuttering and the dlc pricing. The stuttering seems to be completely caused by the 2K launcher, and it is easily bypassed through Steam launch options. A quick search for "midnight suns stuttering fix" should give you all the information required to fix it, but that players have to do that in the first place is inexcusable. Regarding the dlc, they seem to be ridiculously overpriced. At the time of writing only two have been released, being Deadpool and Venom. I've only had the opportunity to try Deadpool's so far, and while the missions were overall enjoyable, and Deadpool himself is a lot of fun to play, it definitely isn't worth a fourth of the overall game price. During the current sale that ends March 2nd, Legendary Edition (which includes the season pass) costs 59.99€. For that price I would recommend going for it, but at the normal price of 99.99€ you're getting robbed.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a triumph, seamlessly blending compelling storytelling with a sincere focus on character narratives and the power of friendship. As a Marvel and gaming enthusiast, I found the experience deeply immersive.The narrative delves into the intricacies of each superhero's life, transcending typical tropes and enriching the overall gameplay. Midnight Suns stands out for its commitment to exploring personal connections and friendships, creating a more emotionally resonant story.Gameplay is a well-crafted mix of strategy and action, requiring thoughtful planning in tactical combat. Each character's unique abilities add depth to battles, while the polished graphics and authentic comic book aesthetics enhance the visual experience.Respecting the source material, Midnight Suns honors the legacies of its characters rather than relying solely on their popularity. Anticipation for a sequel is high, as the foundation laid in this installment promises an evolution of the narrative and new challenges for beloved superheroes.
