_childDocuments_.review: 1. Many people mention the side activities taking too much time. It's a little frontloaded, but once you get a popup saying "Exploring the Abbey is optional", they mean it. You can do all the side activities at your own pace. There's enough stuff to be stretched out nearly over the entire campaign if you're just doing a little bit between missions. Let me put it like this: the bonuses from the roleplaying & exploration will make the game easier, which means you can bump up the difficulty, which means you'll spend longer in combat.2. You'll probably find the writing less awkward with a female protagonist. You see the "default" hunter in the artwork and promo material for this game, and it seems to be the perspective given the most consideration in the writing. Matthew Mercer gives a great performance as the male Hunter, but I think most comic book guys are going to feel weird being asked to get all up in their feelings with Blade if they created a self-insert.3. This is NOT a dating sim. The friendship mechanics might give people that impression, but you cannot ♥♥♥♥ Tony Stark OR his porno stache. You need to become friends with characters to unlock their passives, but you can get friendship slowly just from missions if the combat is all you care about.4. The Abbey mystery sidequest is 100% worth doing. On top of getting a new armor and passive for completing it, you will also have a much greater understanding of the story. I don't recommend doing the final mission before you at least finish this questline. If you get stuck, read Wanda's open book in the library for a new hint each day.5. Play with whatever characters you want. This isn't XCOM and you can't "fail" a campaign. Every hero will be at most 3 levels below your avatar. (Almost) every character has a story mission you  take them on, so I do recommend taking a character on a general mission at least once to learn their unique mechanics. But any character you don't like, you can safely bench for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: This game won't be for everyone, let that be known right now. The combat, which is a tactical card-based system, is very much similar in certain ways to the XCOM series (which makes sense because it's the same developers). And the story is long-as of right now I'm just now getting to Chapter 3 after over 88 hours. To me, all that is a plus. The game takes a while, which means you are with your favorite characters longer. The characters and their unique abilities all feel genuine, and honestly it's some of the best writing in a game that I've seen in a long time, give or take a few awkward moments. They really managed to capture the comic side of Marvel with a little hint of the MCU mixed in.There are plenty of things that may be considered problematic elements. The game tends to suffer from occasional stuttering and camera glitches. A couple characters have some graphical issues (at least for me, running an NVidia 980 Ti, one character in particular has a graphical bug on his neck that is VERY prominent). Pacing wise the game does get bogged down at times before speeding back up, and it can cause a little feeling of whiplash when that happens. The microtransactions aren't in any way necessary, either. All in all, the game is a must have for long-form RPG players, Marvel fans looking for an Ultimate Alliance-style story, and/or fans of games with unique tactical elements. If you can get the Legendary Edition on sale, even better. The characters that come in the season pass are well worth it, as are their storylines. I got the Legendary Edition on the summer sale and I don't regret it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought there would be a game that would outdo XCOM 2 for challenging turn-based combat, but here we are. I'm over forty hours in so far and I'm still sitting in chapter two. It's a big game with lots to do in it.It does suffer from the release problems of choppy performance here and there, with a sprinkling of crashing to desktop. It could also use a better autosave system as if you're not in combat then it is quite possible to lose 30 or forty minutes of play time to a crash. _childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is surprisingly fun, but I unfortunately cannot recommend it in good faith. It constantly crashes, is riddled with bugs, and stutters a ton, all while being a full priced AAA game with microtransactions. To be fair, if I did not look at the Steam page, I would not know it had microtransactions as they are very not in your face, but it still has them. The crashes are annoying and only made worse by an auto save system that saves very infrequently. The first crash made me lose 40 minutes of progress and since then I’ve been manually saving quite frequently to avoid losing much time again. The bugs are numerous and include things like small graphical issues, cards not doing what they say they’ll do, settings constantly resetting, camera randomly jerking around, seeing two of the same hero on your screen at once, not being able to interact with things you are supposed to be able to interact with, and not being able to move the camera on the battlefield. The game is also missing a ton of basic features, like an FOV slider and the ability to get a good top down view of the battlefield. The game’s tutorial told me about a tactical view, but it does not seem to work.Now that that is all out of the way, frustrations aside, I do enjoy my time in this game. The game is split into 2 parts. The first part is a surprisingly fun turn based combat system. I'm usually not the biggest fan of card games or turn based combat, but I do enjoy the combat in this game. It’s simple enough that I can just play without worrying about learning any complex systems, and its filled with satisfying sounds and animations. The second part of the game has you babysitting a bunch of adult children who all really want to be your friend and share all their problems with you. This is also surprisingly fun, mostly because I can laugh at it, but also because parts of the story are genuinely interesting. Besides, I don't think anyone buys Marvel products expecting great writing. During this second part of the game, you can also explore the hub map, but you cannot jump and there are many invisible walls, which just discourage exploration.Marvel's Midnight Suns is a fun game, but if it’s going to be charging AAA prices, it needs a lot more polish. Still, I got a cheap copy in a bundle, so I will continue to play it, even if I do not recommend spending your money on a product that is this poorly made.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy turn-based tactical combat or deckbuilders, there's a good chance you will enjoy this. I know that hardcore xcom or deckbuilding enthusiasts have criticized this game as a diluted version of both, but I think the combo works quite well.Things I liked:1. The voice acting and character development was great. It really gives you an immersive experience in the MCU and explores some of the lesser-known characters.2. The interactions between the different groups of allies was pretty well done.3. The combat was fun and satisfying. I really liked that you can tune the difficulty setting until you find a level that is just hard enough for you.4. Good mix of progression elements and strategy.5. A few different types of gameplay keeps the play experience varied.Things I didn't care for:1. The crafting system's shared resources heavily discourages you from using your limited supplies on consumables until very late in the game. This makes much of the research tree feel irrelevant.2. Some of the abilities and mechanics are very poorly tuned. Summon Charlie is a disappointing capstone for Light Hunters, and some of the ally Legendary abilities are way less useful than others. 3. Lack of variety in Legendary abilities. I spent a few hours grinding out friendship exp to unlock them all, and was disappointed that almost all of them are basically the same, with a few of them having crippling disadvantages for no great reason.4. The final battle forces you to use random team compositions that are very different than your usual teams. This actually caused me to fail the fight and have to turn down the difficulty setting, which was really anti-climactic. You spend the whole game building interesting team combos, and then you don't get to use any of them for the last fight.Despite my complaints, this is still one of the few games I've actually finished in the past year. It was definitely worth the energy and I enjoyed it a lot.In total, it took me 69 in-game "days" to complete (nice) and about 80 hours of gameplay. I liked the episodic nature of it, which suited my adult time availability fairly well. I could play 1 or 2 days and feel like I accomplished something.

_childDocuments_.review: I can accept the military grade cringe super-hero dialog, or the mobile game production quality, but I am constantly snoozing at the glacier-speed pace of the game. Despite being developed by Faraxis (Civs and XCOM) there are zero options for 'action camera' or 'battle speed' during battles (aka the actual game play)Every move/card you play will take 7 seconds while the camera zooms in your character, charges the attack or maybe runs around a bit, bad guy is womped while dipping in and out of bullet time and then your camera is thrown into 3rd person where ever your hero ended up requiring you to adjust zoom and pan to where you were just previously looking. I actually want to play this game and I was hyped for this being on humble bundle but this doesn't even feel like a video game but more of a infants sensory activity peppered between the lowest quality Marvel film.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly good. Sadly it is once again ruined by greed.Very challenging game that never feels unfair. Has a huge cast of different heroes which each bring their own unique play style and card decks to experiment with. The game offers many mechanics that allow you to develope your team and improve. You can feel the dedicated work and the creativity that went into this game. Very talented people working at firaxis.I would give this game a perfect score if it weren't for the greed that apparently has to ruin every good game lately. The paid skins in a full price title are absolutely criminal though. You pay 60€ at release and the game still has content locked behind a paywall. Greed in it's purest form. Therefore even though the game is a masterpiece and I will play this for many hours I just cannot recommend. It is too scummy.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked:- You can choose and customize the character you want to play with, choosing the gender, race and appearance of your character.What I didn't like:- The customization of your character is somewhere on the border of decency. Far too little. When will game creators learn that a success factor in modern games is the detailed customization of your character? And when I say this, I'm not only referring to the character's face, but also to his body. Look at the last Saints Row series, if you pretend you don't understand what I mean.- Lots of talk and little action. Excess of filmed scenes and a lot of unnecessary chatter. It can be seen that the game is made by millennials, much more prone to socializing and unnecessary whining, than action. I mean, I like action games with cutscenes mixed with fighting. The Mass Effect series, Assassin's Creed Odyssey or Saint Row, are games that show how action should be mixed with filmed scenes. But this one... it's way too boring.- The fighting section is much too simplistic and repetitive and in the end, after 10-20 fights it becomes much too boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Great combination of a deckbuilder, with some strong Dragon Age vibes in the side conversations (if that's your thing) and XCOM style mechanics but with some incredibly bad issues in the PC port tied to performance.  I'll just chime in on what other reviews have said and say keep away from the ray traced options (for some reason they aren't pre-cached so you'll get stutters every first-special-effect on every load and it will drive you bonkers), and disable the 2K launcher.  With those options disabled plays perfectly on my 3080 in 5120x1440 with the exception of *terribly* zoomed in pre-rendered cut scenes (guys, the black bars are fine, I don't like having every character's head cut off!), and some weird FPS drops in the manor/mansion.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very different from what's popular, and I think that's a good thing. It also had a surprisingly rich story and characters and tons of content. Definitely not something for everyone, but i encourage you to give it a try. Had some performance issues but can be mitigated by updating graphics settings. I would love to see a sequel!Edit: end of the year awards and still sad this game got panned on release. Still hope to see more of it
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and use of the characters. Each character felt unique with roles that they could play. Every fight felt like the best of X-COM tactics but without the "99% chance to hit point-blank shotgun but whiffs" frustrations and the stress of perma death. Overall, it felt like a more casual X-COM but in a fantastic way, and the campaign is a lot longer than I would have thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple yet fun tactical rpg .Combat: you play cards with different skills and attacks and then watch the animations play out. Can use environment attacks (knocking enemies into walls, each other, your own characters, dropping things on them, explosives, etc) as well. As you proceed through the game, more heroes will join, you will collect stronger cards and be able to upgrade copies or add modifiers after you unlock the ability. Your characters stats will increase with level ups and through gaining friendship levels with the other heroes. All of the skills and abilities are fitting and make sense for each hero and are varied enough to make for interesting strategies and complimentary combinations.Exploration: this part of the game was a pleasant surprise. Your home base area is expansive and has many sub areas to explore and unlock (though I can see this part actually being tedious on subsequent playthroughs). There are even a few simple puzzles. You will be given access to more areas as the story progresses. I just wish there was a mini map. You will be pausing to reorient yourself frequently.Story and characters: story is fairly simple and is typical comic book fare. Save world from big bad. I'm impressed with the amount of dialogue for each character. I am not totally familiar with all of the characters, but of the ones I do know, it feels like they are true to their comic book personalities. Can feel like you are running a daycare sometimes with a lot of childish bickering between the heroes, but makes sense in the context of the story and with characters who have egos like these. Main character is original self insert avatar for this game and the way the other heroes act towards him/her (you can choose and customize appearance) can be a bit tiresome. Once you start gaining friendship levels with your crew they start laying on the compliments and praise pretty thick, comes off as kind of too much. Like characters thanking you for being their friend and talking about how you are the coolest and best and strongest, and how they could only do or be x because of you. World revolves around you kind of nonsense. Really makes you appreciate the ones who bust your chops. You can also do activities with one of your crew after a mission to hang out and increase stats and friendship and unlock cosmetics. Can train with them once a day for the same rewards. No romance though. BFF is the max level. Oh and I think the devs intended for the avatar character to be a woman like in all the marketing, because some of the animations look a bit silly for a man, like walking/jogging in some cases.This game is very grind heavy for cards, resources, stats, and cosmetics. At certain points I wondered if this was originally going to be a live service or mobile game. I am playing with a significant number of mods from the nexus to speed up progression significantly. That colors my review, keep this in mind. If I wasn't using the mods, I would probably be frustrated with how long it was taking to unlock things. The most significant rewards (for me) are costumes, accessories, and palette swaps and once you find them, you also have to spend in game currency (which you earn at an unreasonably slow pace) to unlock them. I get why they did it this way to keep engagement, but it would have been nice if you just had to unlock a customizer that lets you choose custom colors for each part instead of palette swaps. Costumes are all pretty good looking for the most part, nothing looks ridiculous or ugly (apart from some of the MC masks/accessories). You get each hero's final costume after reaching max level of friendship (which takes a long time) and solving a puzzle combat scenario. Again, if I wasn't using mods, I would likely be upset at how slowly you earn resources. In order to get more cards for a specific hero, you have to bring them on missions. You can only bring 3 characters per mission and there is a roster of around 15, which do become playable at a decent pace. This means that some of your characters will inevitably fall  behind. Even if their level kept pace, they would have lower stats because doing missions with heroes earns you friendship points and those unlock stat increases for those heroes. And even if those kept pace as well, you would still be lacking in attack and skill cards because you only get them if you use that hero. And even then, the cards you receive for the heroes used are random, you get to pick from 4 randomly generated cards. They should have just had an in game store where all cards for your current playable roster were available for purchase instead of this bizarre gacha. There is also a weird dark/light dialogue and card mechanic that seems to only serve the purpose of unlocking 2 costumes for the avatar, a dark and a light costume. Both are underwhelming (imo) and you need way too many points in each to unlock the costume. Seems like they intended for you to unlock everything over multiple playthroughs, but who has that kind of time? My only other complaints aside from the grind are performance issues, I'm getting a lot of hiccups and texture popping for a 4080 card and high end processors. Game has its own 2K launcher which I also find annoying. There is a costume for Blade you can only get by linking a 2K games account, which I won't. Avatar dialogue choices don't actually tell you what the character will say, just gives you a general idea that doesn't always match what they say, so if you like to rp you can't really be sure about your choice (there's a mod that fixes this). Overall, I am really enjoying my time with this (heavily modded) game. If you like Marvel and tactical rpgs, I'd give it a shot when it is on sale. 80 hours in and it is still fresh and fun for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Only played an hour so far, but the card combat seems fantastic. Anyone who has read the comic books will enjoy the interactions with the other heroes. Whoever is expecting a carbon copy of XCOM gameplay with Dostoevsky-level dialog is insane. This game has tried something newer and a bit out of the box for a card battler/RPG and it's fresh air... And let's face it, if it were an XCOM clone we would have the same people complaining that it's low-effort sequel with no innovation.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly the best marvel game out right now for me. The strategy behind everything makes it so satisfying to win and you can adjust the difficulty  to make your game either really easy or nearly impossible to beat. Truly recommend this for any marvel fan or just any fan of a good RPGThe combat is where this game shines.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: The tactical aspect has potential and the plot and characters represent a good use of the Marvel IP. But trying to mash-up a random draw, card-based system with tactical gameplay is just awful. It would be like creating a turn-based fps. The two systems contradict each other and drag down an otherwise promising game.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly, it's a really good game. Even if they obviously reused things from XCOM games, its mechanics are different enough from XCOM that it feels like its own game. The story is good, the graphics are good, the different activities are pleasant enough and the difficulty is actually better tuned than XCOM imo. They managed to make the licence work well too. Unfortunately for this game, marketing didn't inspire trust (at least for me) on release but now that you can grab a bundle with all the DLCS on sale at a reasonable price, it's actually really worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: You will have read this is a game of two halves and this is pretty much on the money.  The easy bit: the combat and main game is excellent. It combines a whole host of other influences and make a unique and very enjoyable experience. The animations are superb and the use of the surrounding environment gives a whole new take on the strategy mechanic. There’s some great boss style battles to be had as well. And then the social sim; so at first I found this difficult to get on with. The writing is often questionable and the animation of Hunter running about the Abbey, well, looks a bit odd. That said, as the game progressed I became more invested in this and actually ended up quite enjoying it. There’s some decent lore to be found and some good puzzle based exploration. Collectables and improving friendships help offer bonuses to characters in combat and once you get your head around how the system works, you can reap the rewards. It’s not going to be to everyone’s taste but overall I’ve really enjoyed Midnight Suns and I can’t remember playing a game that feels so unique for a long time. It seems to feature in nearly every Steam sale so it’s well worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥ this.I know I know, how dare I give the game I played 70 something hours negative review but I feel it deserves it considering I wasn't able to force myself to finish it. I keep giving it chance after chance, mostly because I thought card system had potential but the game is just such a chore to play it's infuriating.Let me list some of my impressions in no particular order:- Story is juvenile and idiotic even by marvel standards and most of the characters are alternating between trying to be "bad-ass" and funny and honestly I can't say which of the two made me cringe more. Couple of exceptions here and there but boy am I glad I don't have to hear Tony ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Stark again.- Abbey busywork is just padding trying to hide obvious lack of proper gameplay and it's brutal time waste without any redeeming qualities. I hated it.- Environments are super low effort, with the exception of the Abbey itself. It almost feels as if the game was intended to have similar overall structure to XCOM (base to upgrade, research etc) but then some genius executive had a brilliant idea and we ended up with this crap.- Did I mention the story sucks?- Difficulty system is interesting in theory, In practice game teases you with possibility to increase game difficulty at specific intervals without any regard to how well equipped your team is. Without stronger cards the hydra goons are going to wipe the floor with your heroes (which is oh so stupid when you stop and think about it)- The card system itself really does have potential but it is completely broken.  As far as I can tell, there is no discard pile, so the mechanics of discarding cards to draw ones you want doesn't really work the way you would expect it to. In addition, early cards are mostly crap while later ones are broken, so balance is completely out of wack.- And for crap cherry on top, the UI is one of the worst I have ever seen in turn-based tactical game. You can expect to make moves you didn't want to do because you have to fidget with camera for targeting and camera keeps resetting. No damage indicators whatsoever outside environmental damage you can expect, so you have no way of knowing how much damage can certain enemies dish out without actually being hit.I wish I didn't get it at full price, but honestly it would hurt even at a discount. May this review help you avoid my mistake.Peace.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Long Story Short- Wait on this one.... At time of writing a little over 4 hours in. Still unlocking more and more new unnecessary or as of yet really explained features. The Story feels OK and the combat is interesting and fun, but there is so much bloat thrown in. Cosmetics, Decorating a House, Relationships, Light/Dark system, some sort of currency shop (multiple currencies needed from what I see) Can not pause during the MANY cut-scenes.There is No Steam Cloud Save, so forget playing on PC and Steam Deck or Other PC without having separate games. Graphics are OK but definitely not AAA high end, and some of the cut-scenes suffer from some artifact and what looks like dated recording compared to the game or other cut-scenes. I will continue just for the main story because I am interested, but otherwise NOT worth release price. This seems like a $15.00 MAX game.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Great!  I'm not much of a deck-builder, nor the biggest fan of XCOM 2, but this game is fantastic.  Deck building is a fun kind of RPG mechanic for me, and the graphics/animations really add some flare to the turn-based combat.  Team management at The Abbey can be a slog at times, when I really just want to go on another mission, but it's alright.  There's some side-objective motivation to use all the characters, which can also be a little intrusive, but for the most part, you get to play as a lot of fun characters.  100% would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: If you like XCOM, it's not a 1:1 reskin, so be aware that you're playing a deckbuilder RPG that uses the XCOM engine and devs. I think there's still a lot of similarity in the feel of the game due to cycling characters and making decisions, but this is not Marvel XCOM, it's more like Marvel Slay the Spire.Edit: After finishing the game, I have to say it was really good, particularly for a genre filled with mediocrity. XCOM and XCOM2 are unimpeachable, but honestly, Midnight Suns is a solid secondary experience to those titles, ESPECIALLY if you like Marvel. The relationship building was a little corny, but at least they put some time into it and sunk some lore in there. I hope it gets a sequel, and will definitely play it. I hope it has more customization and a solid mod community.The best part about this game, aside from its addicting tactical gameplay, is that I remember the Midnight Suns comic run from my childhood, and how obscure it seemed compared to Xmen or Spider-Man. I thought it was pretty cool to see some of Marvel's darker heroes in the spotlight.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game and enjoy it. I don't know why though. It's cheesy (in a bad way), repetitive (also in a bad way) voice acting is not great, story is not great (get's the job done), book clubs and car clubs??? huh???? This game should not be fun but it is. I think that the rpg aspect is the best part. There is crafting (not really useful unless you craft abilities), exploration is fun and rewarding for the first half of the game. The graphics are solid but the models look strange in some animations and every male character has the same body. I enjoyed growing my character and finding team comps but this became shallow as you find the best team early on and then never use anyone else. I used other teams on + game and had fun messing around with DLC and awkward team comps. I want for people to play and support this game so we may get another (BETTER) version in the future. However, I cannot recomend this game on pc in it's current state due to the crashing!!!! I have never played a game with so many crashes! I have a beefy rig and can max settings on many AAA titles with descent framerates but this game is a stuttering, crashing mess! I had very little issue with most of the core game. Usually crashes occur when setting up missions or starting missions. Both DLC's have been a train wreck! I can't even play the Venom DLC because it crashes every five minutes. In Closing; This is an average game that punches way above it's weight. If they manage to fix the crashing issue I would definitely recommend it. Until then Just play Xcom 2 with mods and name your team after marvel characters...UPDATE:After uninstalling and reinstalling the game has not crashed in about 3 hours of gameplay. This happened before with Deadpool DLC. Not a great solution for those of us with less than 50mbps download.UPDATE: as with last 2 DLC's I had to completely re install game to play!FINAL UPDATE:New DLC, same crash issues!
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!Yes the talking is a bit much at the start, some of the voice acting is subpar (looking at you Hunter). The combat is a puzzle that I enjoy solving and its visually great and sounds great so its very enjoyable to see enemies fall to the amazing moves the team pulls off.The characters seem to meld well in combat allowing you to grab whoever you want and still be able to win if you plan the battle properly.Storywise its good, nothing incredible but enjoyable. The characters respond mostly as they should, and there is enough twists and turns so far that i'm finding myself loving the cutscenes. The Abbey part of the game which is kind of close to a Life Sim and exploring isn't what I was expecting, and admittedly can be a bit tedious but it allows you to do it at your own pace. So you if just do a bit here and there you'll enjoy the snippets of interactions and interesting environments enough to want to keep going with the change of gameplay. I have Darktide, God of War, Horizon Forbidden west.. but i'm here playing this and don't want to stop! I'm no way near the end of the game yet so maybe that'll change.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played through this game, I would overall say its not worth the playthrough. I was told it has elements of xcom, but other than research and a bit of unit positioning, I found the combat to be extremely dry after the first half of the game. You are always on a small square map (limited map differences) doing the same resource management constantly, which became tedious, especially when you need to do a general mission ot unlock story missions.Unless you REALLY just want more random Marvel lore/storylines, there are definitely better turn-based  strategy games out there to fill your time. I love the characters, so it was fun to see the uncommon interactions between characters, but im very glad i bought the game during a steam sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off with this - somehow, this game has rekindled in me an urge to play and has made me feel enjoyment while doing so.It is difficult to pinpoint exactly what specifically is there in that formula that it offers, but it does its job marvelously (pun intended). For those, who are on the fence, I'd say give it a whirl, if you don't like it - refund it, you will definitely get a feel of what this game is about within an hour.Gameplay is as simple as you make it, really - first and foremost, it's a card game, second, it's a little bit of an exploration game as well, this part is optional, but it's still interesting to see the little stories/ get additional cosmetic items. Visually it's definitely not a revolutionary eye candy, but it doesn't look bad either, the aesthetics are just right, I believe.I'm not a huge Marvel fan so I went into this without a lot of expectations, perhaps this is what made me really enjoy it, but that's beside the point.Story is quite simple too, has a few twists and turns, nothing really mindblowing, but that's how it usually is with comics, probably. I was pleasantly surprised, that when I felt like the story is coming to an end, the game spewed out a way to extend it in a very fluid way. There's quite a bit of "friendship is power" talk too, so it might be too big of a pill to swallow for some, but then again, it's not too invasive, I think.Perhaps it's the simplicity of it all, most of the actions/options what you can do feel natural and this is where the magic's at. I, for one, 57 hours in am still going for the optional missions and am almost avoiding story missions only to prolong my stay with the game.There are a few faults with the game that I can point out - I've had one mission which I was unable to complete due to mission-specific cards not appearing, but I'm glad it was not a story mission, so a reload of the game and selecting another mission helped. And the other thing that is something I am still frustrated about is that if there's a mission you cannot complete for one reason or another - there's no way of going back to mission select screen to attempt another one, that might be easier. So the only way of doing that is to reload the game prior to the selection of a mission. This, however is barely an inconvenience, because the game autosaves before every mission select, so there's that. Pathfinding sometimes screws up and either takes a bit to figure out the way to the target too, but that doesn't really take too much away from the overall enjoyment.Bottom line - this is the first game I have written a review for, so in my head, it means something and I suggest giving it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem in my opinion. Tactical battles are simply great with many layers of how to combine characters together and how to adjust their "decks". At the start it seems really simple, but the more you play - the more depth and the layers of tactics are added to the game and feel great!  Almost every character written really well and I did not expect that from this game - even though the overall story is nothing special, but the dialogues between character are written really well. The more you increase the friendship with the character - the more you learn about them, so you start to feel of them as real characters with deep personalities.Exploring the Abbey in the free time as also really enjoyable and let's learn more interesting stuff about not only grounds around your main hub, but also hidden story of this place and characters around you!Honestly, I can't recommend this game enough. Well made, Firaxis, well made.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept. Good jokes. Strong characters I enjoy being around. Excellent gameplay loop. Could it be excellent? Absolutely! Is it? No, it's buggy as ♥♥♥♥. On one hand, there's a lot of clipping and sometimes dialogue lines will play over each other. There's an occasional bug where dead enemies are still standing up- they can't be targeted and the game recognizes that they're dead, they don't do anything or actually exist, but they look like they're alive. On the other hand, I have to undervolt my GPU to avoid the game randomly shutting down my entire computer. Even with that, junction temps reach 105 C in the pause menu- higher than actual gameplay. This thing is undercooked. It BADLY needs some patches. Unfortunately, the devs abandoned it after it tanked on release. Very unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: A good strategy game if you're looking for something lighter without being overly easy. Decent narrative that does a good job of feeling like a comic book storyline. DLC is take it or leave it, would only recommend if you are interested in at least two of the characters and if you are then it's probably best to just get the season pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just completed The Marvel Midnight Suns, I'm thrilled to share my enthusiastic review! This game beautifully blends the iconic Marvel universe with the strategic brilliance reminiscent of XCOM 2. The graphics are visually stunning, and the characters come to life in a way that Marvel fans will truly appreciate.The gameplay strikes a perfect balance between action-packed superhero battles and tactical decision-making, reminiscent of the XCOM series. The diverse roster of Marvel characters, each with unique abilities, adds a layer of strategy that kept me engaged throughout.What sets Midnight Suns apart is its gripping storyline and character development. The narrative unfolds with cinematic flair, and the interactions between characters are both entertaining and emotionally resonant. It's a Marvel fan's dream come true.As a fan of XCOM 2, I found the strategic elements familiar and enjoyable, yet Midnight Suns brings its own unique flavor to the table. It's a must-play for fans of both franchises, offering a fresh take on tactical RPGs within the Marvel universe. Thoroughly enjoyed every heroic moment!

_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: Memory leaks. Crashes. Random bugs. Yep, plenty of them. Grindy and repetative? At times, for sure. But still, somehow manages to be one of the best Marvel games around, featuring the most fun card-based combat systems I've ever toyed around with. Not only that, but Midnight Suns tells a heartfelt, well-written story that brings out the best of it's vibrant roster. Those of you familiar with these heroes from comic book pages will be pleasently surprised, as some of them are way better written than anything the House of M has done recently, but I digress.So, here's the gist of it: if you don't try hard and just enjoy the ride, without attempting to complete everything on your first run, this game is an absolute blast. Sure, you will hit a few bumps along the road, but the sights will be worth it. The core loop is almost addicting, while managing to offer plenty of lore for you to sink your teeth into. Not only that, but some of the plot elements are real heavy hitters, highlighting the human side of our favorite legends. Also, there's a dog and you can pet it and yes, it's a mechanic. There's no hiding the truth: even though this game offers tens of hours of content, it still feels unfinished at times. It's obvious that the scope of the project was planned to be way bigger than the existing product, with a sequel after-credits teaser to boot. Sadly, the outlook of that happening isn't that good as of today. But I hope I'm wrong. I hope that we do get that sequel some day. Because I'm 100% convinced that Moon Knight was planned to be a part of this game and there isn't a single force in the universe, capable of convincing me otherwise. But I'll have to wait out until we get a sequel in order to see my fav hero enjoy the fun stuff, donning gold. So, TL;DR, here we go: Midnight Suns is the best Marvel game since Ultimate Alliance 3 and one of the best tactical games of its year. And that's not "nuff said", but I emplore you to find out why yourself. Yes, it isn't perfect. But it deserves your attention and love. Mark my words: this will be a cult-classic a decade from now.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game may have some bugs here and there it's definitely one of the best marvel/superhero games I've ever played.THE COMBAT:While players might be discouraged by the card-play turn-based mechanics of the combat, it's definitely worth a shot. There is a learning curve to understanding the mechanics of how each character works and what team synergy works best. However, it is so satisfying when you are able to mow down multiple enemies  in one turn. The game does a great job of capturing the strength and abilities of each of it's superheroesTHE ABBEY/COMMON AREA:People who are not be a fan of marvel characters might not enjoy these segments of the game. But trust me, if you like/love these characters, these moments are amazing. Never in my life did I think I needed Captain America to ask me about his relationship problems with Blade. Kicking it with Captain Marvel or Spider-man is also a treat.THE HUNTER:While i still wished it was only marvel characters only, the Hunter is still a pretty interesting addition and the way they are used throughout the story really proved their existence in this game. Building this character and making your own deck with powers you select makes this character really worthwhile.THE NEGATIVES:There are still a lot of bugs in this game. Sometimes they are game breaking, sometimes they are not. It seems that the developers are trying their hardest to fix them which is always a good sign. Some parts of the story or dialogue might seem like they break the pacing of the gameOVERALL:Amazing video game, hopefully they make another one. If you enjoyed XCOM or strategy games this is definitely something i would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen. This game is AMAZING. There's so much story, so much to do, so much to explore, that I'm about 20 hours in and I've only done a handful of the story missions. Lilith is an interesting villain, and I'm not familiar with much of the Cthon lore, so learning through this game has been very fun.Speaking of fun! Like with the media surrounding Guardians of the Galaxy, I love being introduced to characters I knew only a little about. Especieally when they're this well done. I knew a little about Ilyana, but all i knew about Robbie and Nico were their hero names (and that Robbie has a SOV kinda sorta). Now I love them all, I feel attached to them the same way I do the Guardians and I'm excited to see their stories unfold! More Blade is always a good thing, I've been a fan since the films and this Eric is infinitely approachable and a powerhouse on the battlefield. I love him slowly opening up to your Hunter and the others, I can't believe how real these friendships feel. They're so well-written, and I'm actually drawn more to the Suns than the familiar Avengers (with the exception of Carol). Combat is a blast, especially once you've gotten the hang of each character's unique playstyle. My favorites to have on a team with my Hunter are Robbie and Carol, but Magik's portal usage comes incredibly in handy and each team member plays in such a way that you can't go wrong with any of them! I love upgrading abilities and using the environment to help thin the numbers of enemies, combat never gets boring or feels slow. Sometimes it feels overwhelming, but as you level up abilities and upgrade your training area you get little actions that make the action economy feel more expansive. I'm addicted to this game, and I'm so, so glad I was able to get it. I'm looking forward to more DLC characters to expand my friendships and more zones of the abbey to explore! 10/10, this is the most fun I've had with a single player game since GOTG!

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of this game. The combat's really fun and the story elements are great. If you like X-COM, Marvel and keen on a game with some chunky narrative, this ones for you. There's an old school BioWare-esque style that flows through the story-telling.  It's not always perfect and there are areas the story is shallow (the relationship with your team elements can sometimes feel a bit gamified), but it's a genuinely fun romp, with some great moments and characters, as well as a pretty decent narrative overall.. I honestly feel this game is criminally under-rated. It really deserves a sequel. It's nice to play a game that does take a few risks, it doesn't always land, but I love how unique it feels, the ideas and story are a real nice change from a lot of modern games, reminds me of how games used to be 5 or 10 years ago, when there was somewhat of a soul to game creation and story crafting, which is often lacking in 'most' (not all) triple A game studios.Would love to see the developers return to this series.

_childDocuments_.review: Still so far so good.Midnight Sun's isn't perfect by any means. If you aren't a fan of Marvel, half of this game just isn't for you. Puzzles, easter eggs, chests, lore, and endless exploration of the "Abbey Grounds". The abbey section of the game reminds me a lot of the Krypt from Mortal Combat. It's not enough to make me not recommend the game but microtransaction in a full price game are dog water. Some of the skins genuinely improve the experience, like the "Bleeding Edge" Iron Man suit... So F whoever made that greedy decision! But, to be fair the Midnight Suns gold and black outfits are awesome and I think you get those through gameplay. If the 4 DLCs from the season pass end up being light in content it won't be worth the price and I'll be pretty angry! I will poop in your oatmeal Firaxis! Just kidding.... or am I? On a brighter note the combat is great! I really enjoy the card system even though it RNGs you to death sometimes. The voice acting ranges character to character from mid to excellent. My least favorite character is Magick, I just don't like her. My favorite character is probably Nico so far. In Conclusion (TLDR):I'm really enjoying my time with Midnight Suns. I enjoy walking around "The Abbey" looking for secrets and gathering supplies. Combat has always been one of Firaxis' strengths and this game is no different. As a Marvel fan I love the game minus a few things like microtransactions. I recommend the game to Marvel fans but if you aren't a fan I don't think you will get much out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel RPG Meets XCOM.Thoroughly enjoyable game the superhero genre compliments the turn based strategy genre surprisingly well. All the characters play really well, like really well, i don't often mentally stop to give props on the nuts and bolts of a games, but props to the devs on the character design here are well deserved. The gameplay loop is fun but some may get annoyed at how this seems to be a game of two halves RPG and turn based strategy where every combat is followed by at least a little team building or cycle of things to do between missions, sure alot of it can be skipped but at least initially you aren't gonna want to. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a welcome departure from all the happy-go-lucky Marvel games we've seen so far; Midnight Suns is darker and grittier, while still maintaining that Marvel humor. Its gameplay loop is simple: Slice of life central hub > mission > slice of life central hub > mission. The closest game I'd compare Midnight Suns to is Fire Emblem: Three Houses. If you just want pure strategy, strategy, strategy or action, action, action, probably give this one a pass.There are tons of classic Marvel plot holes but the characters pretty regularly acknowledge them ("Yeah, actually we've probably all died at least once at some point or another"). The story isn't anything to write home about, but it's good enough to keep you motivated to see the heroes through to the end.My only gripe with this game is its optimization. Poor performance, crashes and visual bugs galore. Things like characters facing the wrong way during dialogue are pretty easily ignored after a few hours of playing, but that's no excuse. Performance-wise, some areas are worse than others, and astonishingly the worst performance I get is on the initial menu screen. If you start up the game and it's choppy, see if clicking New Game and playing works out for you. I can deal with dropped frames on the main menu. Crash-wise, I can't isolate the issue, but with auto-saves and the wherewithal to save frequently, I haven't experienced any colossal loss of progress. I've also encountered a handful of soft-locks, mostly in the training yard.Finally, I just want to add for anyone just buying the game OR experiencing performance problems to first disable the 2K launcher or bypass it by launching the game directly from its executable. For some reason the game hates it with a passion and can slow to a crawl while it's active.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a full review or anything. Pros:- Lots of voice acting- Good graphics and excellent performance- Really cool tactical combat and turn-based card mechanics. Cool animations.- Doesn't appear to be woke or anything. Even Captain Marvel is portrayed a lot better than in the modern comics/movies. I just wish she had her long hair like the older books.- The abbey grounds remind me of exploring those old church retreat houses as a kid.- Mass Effect like conversations with your team- You can tell the devs cared about the source materialCons:- Must play at 1080p for the fonts to be readable. They are too small at higher resolutions. They are unreadable at 4k. UI Scaling doesn't let you go high enough to compensate.- Maybe a little too much talking in between missions. This one is subjective.If you are a fan of marvel AND turn-based combat, I think you will really like this game. It's not a "must play" or anything, but it is a quality product. My biggest problem with the game is definitely the UI Scaling though. Developers, please don't do this again. The minimum font size at 4k should be 54px, and probably much larger than that honestly in most cases. You shouldn't have to strain to read text in your games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dragon Age Inquisition and are a fan of Marvel, this game is for you. I bought this game 3 days ago and I have since non-stop grinded the story and the friendships. WARNING: Mild spoilers ahead!THINGS I LOVE ABOUT THE GAME- What sets it apart from other titles?1) Your character - the Hunter - is essentially a fish out of water when it comes to friends and learning about the 21st century, and I love the little things you can notice throughout your daily and nightly conversations with the Midnight Suns/X-Men/Avengers Heroes as the Hunter gains knowledge of the world they woke up in. There are also 3 clubs to take part in (my personal favorite is EMO KIDS)2) The game is SUPER customizable - every character has multiple outfits to wear into battle and to wear around the Abbey, and all are easily obtainable through chests on the grounds and leveling your friendships.Although Gloss can be hard to come by at times, if you get into the rhythm of doing a couple of general missions to get Coil, Artifacts, and other goodies to significantly buff the stats of your heroes before going against the Blood Gates and higher-leveled fights, you'll be able to rack up Gloss to buy outfits, accessories, and you'll even be able to replace the paintings in the Abbey with paintings you find, or pictures you create.3) The day/night cycle is actually something that I really enjoyed in this game. Even though there's an apocalypse on the horizon, when you wake up in game, it gives you a sense of direction and control in your RPG life. You're given daily tasks in the morning, and in the common-areas there are blips to collect. You can hangout at Havens with character you want to enhance the friendships of, and when all that is done, you go on a mission. When you come back, you join a hangout, go to a club, explore the grounds for more hidden secrets to Hunter's past, or you can simply go to sleep.4) Characters and friendships in this game work very similar to Dragon Age Inquisition as I have noticed. Each character is their own person- they have their own belief system, their own moral compass, and how they expect you to respond to improve your friendship. Same thing goes for Havens, Hangouts, and Gifts too - they'll either like it, love it, or hate it.Overall, this game is fantastic in my honest opinion. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a very nice surprise. It is one of the best games I have ever played. The story is top-notch, which is good, because much of the game has the feel of an interactive novel. There is a lot of emphasis on your character's relationship with the game's many heroes, but because these are Marvel characters that you have at least heard about already, the interactions and dialogues are all very interesting. The story's pacing is very well done, and you are welcome to move through the story at light-speed or at a snail's pace, depending on how many missions you want to run between story missions.The combat in missions is really a card-game, and the challenge is working out how to use the abilities/cards of the heroes you take with you most efficiently. The deck-building is managed between missions, and players who are into the meta of the cards can devote a lot of attention here. If you want to be more casual about it, you can just keep the skill level on the low side. The system is very well done... almost surprisingly so. Between missions and character dialogues, your character has another story that you can progress at your own pace that explains some of the back-story of the game's primary protagonist. This is more a game of exploration and a series of solo missions. It was a nice addition to what is already a very big game.The final mission was brilliant, and the game's ending was good. That's hard to pull off in RPG's with such an epic feel. There are few games that I consider to be masterpieces like the Witcher 3 or XCOM 2. This one qualifies. It was ambitious, but actually pulled it off.
_childDocuments_.name: Marvel's Midnight Suns

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been an addiction of mine since getting it on sale. Holy crap, so fun, the card system i thought was gonna be awful coming from XCom but it blew me away with how they managed to work it. I loved the character customisation, the story, but the MAIN thing i loved was what a few others hated, the hanging out outside of the missions with all the heroes. It added such a cool layer to the game that made me want to constantly levelling up friendships to help everyone get max stats etc.100% worth your time, really want to see an expansion or a full fledged sequel ASAP!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was my first exposure to turn- based card battlers. I didn't really know what to expect, but I thought "it's a Marvel game so there's gotta be some cool elements to it". I wasn't wrong.  This game has kept me captivated from the start. The gameplay and character development/ customizations are enjoyable, moreso than I thought they'd be. I enjoy the strategy involved in each battle and with several difficulty options to choose from, you'll likely find something that works for you too. There are many collectibles and side missions to keep you busy. The story line is typical of what you'd expect from a comic book series, but with way more emphasis on witchcraft, demonic possession and the occult (parents, it's a central theme of the game...you've been warned). An interesting, Sims-like focus is placed on developing friendships with your teammates. Fully upgrading a hero's abilities is dependent on the relationship the Hunter builds with them both in combat and around the Abbey. I will warn you, this game has crashed several times on my laptop, but not on my Steam Deck. I'm not sure why b/c the laptop meets all recommended specs and I use the same internet for both devices. The laptop loads via 2K while the Deck seems to load directly through steam. Maybe that's it?  Anyway, the point is the game is fun but over priced and the Season pass is DISGUSTINGLY overpriced. Definitely buy on steep discount. Overall I'm really enjoying the base game. User reviews and price have kept me away from the season pass for now. You can enjoy the game with or without the season pass, but you can't get all the achievements without it... weasel move, 2k. Base game 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Revised Review (post-patch)TLDR: I enjoyed the game, but it has flaws.Caveat: I am a big fan of Superheroes, Turn-Based and Firaxis.The Good- The writing for the story-line is very good.  Drama, twists-and-turns, humour and heart.- There is a lot of character dialogue.  Most of it is quite good.- The card mechanics for each hero is fairly unique and flavorful.- The combat and challenge missions were interesting tactical challenges.- Charlie is totes adorbs.The Bad- The game is not entirely stable.  I have experienced multiple crashes, freezes and graphical glitches.  Before the patch, the save game system was also unstable.  Future patches may rectify these problems.- Hunter should have been named Gatherer considering how many plants and mushrooms were picked during the game.  Yes, your character, a super hero, needs to run around gathering reagents like this is some sort of fantasy MMORPG.- Do you like searching your house for loose pocket change?  Then you will love the orb gathering mini-game.- At the time of this writing, the number of options for deck construction are very limited.  Hunter has *some* limited options.  All of the other heroes have next to none.- Linked in to the limited deck options is the absence of replay value.  Once you have experienced the story and fiddled with the available cards, there really isn't anything else to try.Final verdict: It is worth playing once just for the story and dialog.  If the price tag is too steep for a single play-through, wait for it to go on sale.  Or wait longer for the YouTube story compilation videos.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the $50 season pass, but man this game was great. The last time I grinded out a game like this was when XCOM 2 released. No, you won't have to worry about 99% chance of hitting and missing (for the most part). The combat is well developed and there are MANY levels (on higher difficulties) that require more than just using whatever card/heroes you want and still winning. The mechanics are smooth and well developed. There is an endless amount of replayability and everything is well animated. Although I experienced some stuttering issues, it didn't affect my gameplay at all. There is a lot of depth into this game and the Abbey environment that you explore is a humongous upgrade compared to XCOM 2's menu UI of research, upgrades, etc. I liked the pace and many of the challenges. There are a lot of surprises, references, and a lot of dialogue that I can appreciate because of how much time went into creating the depth of the characters and the environment. As a big Marvel fan, I can further appreciate the interactions they threw in between all of the other characters as well. Albeit parts of the story were kind of lacking, it's something that is easily looked past.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with some caveats.The battles are a great combination of Slay the Spire and Into the Breach (which is, I guess, very similar to Fights in Tight Spaces).The characters are well written and the relationships you can develop are engaging.And then there's the upgrade system, which is finicky beyond belief. Different currencies to upgrade attacks, hero cards, skills, more currencies to buy upgrades you've unlocked, another currency that you have to spend to send your heroes on missions (rendering them unplayable for the next battle), and some of those currencies can also be used to craft cards and items for use in battle, but crafting potions is a different set of resources entirely. It feels like a game built to encourage micro-transactions, except the only micro-transactions in the game are cosmetic, as far as I can tell.The way you end up farming resources for upgrades and crafting is by sacrificing cards you're not using, but this just discourages experimentation with different deck builds.But, all the problems with the game's resource economy aside, a really fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Marvel's Midnight Suns is a game that seamlessly blends the rich tapestry of Marvel's universe with engaging gameplay mechanics, creating an experience that is both exhilarating and emotionally resonant. From the moment players step into the shoes of the Hunter, a customizable protagonist grappling with inner demons, they're drawn into a world teetering on the brink of destruction.One of the most striking aspects of Midnight Suns is its diverse roster of characters, drawn from across Marvel's extensive lore. From iconic heroes like Doctor Strange and Wolverine to lesser-known figures like Nico Minoru and Ghost Rider, each member of the Midnight Suns brings their own unique abilities and personality to the table. The game masterfully weaves these characters into its narrative, exploring their relationships and inner struggles in a way that feels authentic and compelling.But Midnight Suns is more than just a collection of beloved characters; it's a game about grappling with darkness and finding the light within. As the Hunter, players face off against the malevolent forces of Lilith, the Mother of Demons, in a series of intense tactical battles. These encounters require careful planning and strategic thinking, as players utilize their team's abilities to overcome increasingly difficult challenges.The game's card-based combat system adds a layer of strategic depth that sets it apart from traditional action RPGs. Each character in the party is represented by a deck of cards, featuring a variety of abilities and tactics. Balancing offense, defense, and support becomes crucial as players navigate through battles, inviting them to experiment with different strategies to overcome encounters.Beyond its gameplay mechanics, Midnight Suns delves into themes of power, identity, and societal responsibility. Through its diverse cast of characters, the game explores issues such as discrimination, privilege, and the struggle for equality. Whether it's Blade confronting his dual nature as a vampire hunter and a vampire himself, or Magik grappling with her traumatic past, each hero's journey reflects real-world struggles in a way that feels both relevant and impactful.However, Midnight Suns isn't content to merely entertain; it also challenges players to reflect on their own beliefs and biases. By presenting complex moral dilemmas and exploring the consequences of actions, the game encourages introspection and empathy, inviting players to consider the ethical implications of their choices both in-game and in the world around them.Of course, Midnight Suns is not without its flaws. Some may find the learning curve for the card-based combat system to be steep, while others may be disappointed by the lack of certain fan-favorite characters in the roster. Additionally, the game's narrative pacing can occasionally feel uneven, with certain story beats feeling rushed or underdeveloped.Nevertheless, these minor criticisms pale in comparison to the game's strengths. Midnight Suns is a triumph of storytelling, gameplay, and social commentary, offering a deeply immersive experience that will leave a lasting impact on players long after the credits roll. As I immersed myself in the world of Midnight Suns, I felt a profound emotional connection to the characters and their struggles. Their triumphs felt like my own, and their defeats weighed heavy on my heart. It's this emotional resonance, this ability to make players care deeply about the fate of these fictional heroes, that sets Midnight Suns apart from other games in the genre. It's an experience that transcends mere entertainment, leaving a lasting impression that lingers long after the game is over. So whether you're a seasoned Marvel fan or simply someone looking for a thought-provoking and engaging gaming experience, Midnight Suns is an adventure not to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I am especially enjoying this game; it has pulled me away from most of the others I'm in the middle of because I find it so addictive.  It's a little rough around the edges, most notably that you currently cannot pause cutscenes.  With the game missions being turn based, it's that one flaw away from being a game you can easily step away from to answer the door, take a bio break, or actually interact with your family.That minor annoyance aside, I'm having so much FUN with it.  The writing is good enough to find your favorite characters familiar.  The combat system gives you reasons to think and plan and chain actions together.  The difficulty can slide if you find yourself struggling or winning too easily.I enjoy the pacing of having a breather to explore and socialize between missions.  The relationship system is nuanced enough to have you thinking about the personality of the person you're talking to before making choices, and over time the conversations you have affect your own balance.  The "heroic" answer is not always the one you need.The graphics are smooth and immersive.  The area available to explore is somewhat limited compared to massive open world games, but there's lots of secrets to find.  Also I like how you have lots of options for changing your look and also that of the other characters you work with.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge RPG tactics fan and let me just say, I am really enjoying this game! Reviewing a game for what it is versus what it isn't can be a tricky thing for some player to reconcile with. Is this a X-COM game system? No. Is that a bad thing. No, in my experience, it is not. The card battle system is a cool spin how to execute actions. The smaller "map" areas keep the battle momentum fast and punching "POW!" Seriously, I appreciate how they have combined gameplay systems that fit into the superhero motif - I mean would a cover system really make sense for these god-like characters? As a huge Dragon Age and Mass Effect fan, I enjoy their blend of RPG and tactics. And this is definitely subjective, but I am really enjoying the story. I don't think the writing is bad at at all. And learning about the magic side of the Marvel universe is bringing a smile to my face. Cash shop don't really bother me if it's all cosmetic. It's when it's ptw that I give a side-eye. They are trying something new here and I think this is a good start to a new tactics(RPG) franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: That was a pretty good time.It's an intense game - resources-wise. I literally had to get a new computer to run it and cut the load time between levels down to 5-10 seconds. On the OLD one it was more like 10 minutes. And that's not hyperbole. Anyway, that's my problem, not yours, but just a heads-up.But aside from that, such fun. Normally when I have a game that lets me screw around for as long as I'd like, then this is what happens:1) Complete as many story missions as are necessary to open things up.2) Stay where I'm at, repeat things, overlevel to a ridiculous degree.3) Start to get kinda sick of the core gameplay loop, but I'm still mostly having fun.4) Reach a point where I need to unlock something else, do another story mission or two.5) Now that more is open, return to step 2 until the whole process has gone from "kinda sick of it" to "JUST END, ALREADY!"6) Dash through story missions until I finish it.With this one, though, I never actually got sick of it. The nature of the gameplay itself almost always kept things fresh for me. Combine different mission maps with different sets of enemies, different challenges, the different characters you can pick for your team, the different abilities you can equip, and ON TOP OF ALL THAT the game randomizes which abilities you get and in which order*. Every level's unique no matter how you slice it, and that's a recipe for a game that stays engaging longer. As you can see from 109 hours playtime before I even got here.*Randomized, yes, but your whole "deck" is determined when you enter the mission. So restarting the mission does NOT change the deck you're using - not just the cards you start with, but all the ones after that, too.Really, aside from the fact that it's long, there's not much negative here. The animation is good - gestures and facial expressions carry about as well as IRL, the voice acting is really impressive, the music is suitably epic, the dialogue is sharp. The gameplay itself is fun, battles are actually entertaining. Honestly, I could've probably gone on playing for another 100 hours if there was more story to it (and probably will when the DLC drops).The only negatives are just a little weirdness for the most part, clearly unintentional stuff, very minor. There's the typical dialogue cutscene where characters suddenly forget where they're looking and their heads start turning all around while talking normally that seems to happen at least once in almost every game that allows for it these days. There's a conversation near the end where it looks like the subtitles and the dialogue in the choices wasn't actually proofread. Also your teammates will often ask you for 'a favor' to give you a chance to do something that'll give you a little friendship cred with them, but if you refuse it (I was doing a light playthrough and got asked to increase my dark points and I was like 'nope!') they'll JUST KEEP ASKING. I had to refuse that 'favor' almost every single day."Oh, go talk to Blade? Well, OK, but if he asks me to raise my dark rating again, I'm gonna stake him in his sleep."In a review I read, they counted the mostly-empty hub map ("The Abbey") as a negative with having to go exploring and whatnot - but really, if you don't  to, it's not a must. And if you run, then by the time you've unlocked all the areas and fast travel, it's really not that much of a hardship anyway, if you even opt to - which again, you can just  if it's a problem.I think the main thing that I have against it is that I think I'm just getting to the point where certain story tropes just annoy me more than anything else, and the whole "this entire plot is driven COMPLETELY by miscommunication, and if you just replaced ANY instance of "oh, this person told you THAT was my motivation? Ho ho ho, oh, child, they're keeping you in the dark. Well, K, bai!" *POOF* with "oh, they said that's why I'm doing this? OK, no, have a seat, you should probably understand what's actually going on here, JUST SIT RIGHT BACK, AND YOU'LL HEAR A TALE!" then the story would've been over in Act I" thing is getting pretty old for me, personally.I mean, I get why it's a thing, but maybe it doesn't need to be like 98% of all stories ever? That'd be a cool change of pace.But still, it was suitably epic with how it all panned out, so it's hard to be  about it, but it's worth mentioning.Anyway, definitely recommended, but if your PC might not be up to snuff, be ready to refund. I probably don't need to tell you that, but I just did anyway. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like X-COM, this game will be up your ally and a new learning curve that literally lets you enjoy "grinding" for improvement. What I truly love about this game is how it tells a great story with you constantly progressing through it in your own way, making your own choices, and truly giving a sense of forging your own destiny within the story.Game play feels like a board game, but has that strategic fun of X-COM, only no huddling for cover and you're at the mercy of the cards. Taking time to read up on how to use the heros and make good combos is key. Along with the constant upgrading, you can almost practically play the way you want with each character.I will add one quick negative and that is if you're using the minimum you might run into graphics issues occasionally. Nothing major, just occasional cosmetic bugs.Overall, this is a game that will keep you wanting to keep progressing.

_childDocuments_.review: The comic book story is very well developed and the graphics are quit exceptional ... along with the strategic challenges of including drawn card play to make each encounter unique and engaging is very fulfilling. Truly a unique accomplishment by the developers.  Outstanding job ... well done.

The character personalities are interesting and there is enough customization with cards and decks (the basic items of combat) to make the game enjoyable for most.But the game played terribly on release. Some people blame the 2K Launcher (and there are posts on how to bypass it), but the bottom line is that you will get MUCH smoother gameplay on consoles (at least at the time of this writing). That is unbelievably disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this between my Steam Deck and Desktop to 100%.Gameplay loops between Setup and Combat.  A lot more to the setup side of things than Firaxis usually did with X-Com, similar to Persona 5 or Fire Emblem Three Houses.Combat plays great, kinda hard to describe.  Genre wise it's a Deckbuilder Tactics Game, sorta like a weird hybrid of Slay The Spire and X-Com.  Mechanically unique and interesting. The vibe of the game is not unlike that found in JRPGS, especially with the way the story and progression is handled.  Setup involves third person exploration, training and improving your relationships with the cast.Difficulty feels great.  Harder difficulties were offered as you get further into the game.  Coming from other card games at a top level (Slay the Spire, Runeterra, Hearthstone, Marvel Snap), I felt the challenge was always appropriate, taking the harder difficulty whenevered offered.  For a single player card game, its actually really refreshing.I'd rate it as highly as Persona 5 Royal, weighing more on the combat, but taking a hit in its story.The story isn't terrible, it has a lot of cool moments for sure.  If you enjoy Marvel films, you'll be fine here.I personally did not experience any crashes, having played this game rather late in its lifetime.++ Fully Voiced! OG Actors too! (insomniac Spider-Man, Nico shares the same actor as the show)++ Enormous and Diverse Cast++ Combat gameplay is fantastic and unique.+ Scaling difficulty balance+ Great Steam Deck Game (combat had solid performance.  Controller Controls are good)+ Blade= Comic Book Writing- Combat voice lines get old unfortunately (crazy amount everywhere else)- Slow animations- Card Balance could be better (mostly fine, reinforcement could be better though)-- Exploration can be a slog. (optional thankfully, unless 100%)-- Setup is awful to deal with post game.--- Denuvo100% is time consuming rather than difficult.I had to do a full playthrough and a half to achieve it.I'd only recommend getting the Legendary Edition of this game on discount over any other version of the game.Price kinda gets rough buying the DLC later otherwise.Had a better time listening to heavy metal and rock on my second playthrough, matching the music of the marketing.When it comes to conversation choices, I'd recommend ignoring the light / dark alignment and just choosing the text that makes the most sense.  Unless you're going for the full light or dark achievements.Light Spoilers BelowDLC Campaign Missions have a focus on Blade + DLC Characters.  The OC will take a backseat for Blade at times, so build appropriately.I regret grinding prior to the final mission, the games difficulty only scales further after beating the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rate 2/5 Everything outside of the combat is boring and annoying, and you are out of combat for around 10-15 mins after each mission.Don't know why they tried to add the whole friendship level and constant talking to the other characters to try to make the "story" better, but I just want to get to the action and stay there.  Not be brought back to the base after every mission to run around and talk to people and watch lame cutscenes that have nothing to do with the main story missions.  Everything could have been added into 1 or 2 menus, but they decided to try to make the game more interactive and they just made it tedious.If you can get over that very large hump, the actual gameplay and animations are great.  However, every time I return to base, I just want to turn the game off.  Let me just pick the next mission, holy damn.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game. The card style combat was never stale, the voice dialogue and lore were impeccable, and the exploration was more than I expected. This game is definitely one of my favorites. I was hesitant at first because it has turn based combat, but after playing it, I realized it was the only way it would have made sense. I feel like the only flaw with this game was its marketing. It completely slid under my radar until a friend recommended it. I really wish that it was marketed properly because it deserves a lot more praise than it has received.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 part boring visual novel with bland writing1 part mindless but fun exploration and (very) simple puzzle solving1 part fun and engaging tactical battles1/2 part poor performance for a game that doesn't look that good1/2 part shameless cosmetic in-game purchases in a single player gameFront load the boring visual novel into a 5-hour tutorial phase. Then, burn the mixture by adding in shameless cosmetic purchases that the player can buy with real money and weirdly bad performance. _childDocuments_.review: I am not really a fan of Xcom-like games but this game is just awesome. It is a mix of RPG and turn based action game with strong focus on relationships and exploring. It perfectly avoids what XCOM makes boring for me - combat after combat after combat.This game is like 40% combat (with approx. 11-15 characters who have decent uprgadeable roster of cards), 40% story (including hours of chatting with your teammates which in the end boost their combat performance) and 20% exploring small area around your base.Roster of heroes is interesting, there are hundreds of different builds, combinations and archetypes. If you like uprgading stuff, interesting characters and tactical combat, this game may be just for you.Oh and i reccommend buying Legendary Edition - side stories of all 4 DLCs may take only 6 hours, but you can enjoy all 4 new character in "base game" for more than that. They offer unique features and they are not just reskins.Overall, 9/10 for me, BUT, if you expect all combat and no story/talking/social stuff, you may be disappointed.
