_childDocuments_.review: What a good game.  Something that I figured was just another adventure game that quickly spiraled into something that has a very unique identity in the metroidvania genre.  A game where your choices matter not just for an outcome for a quest, but for the large overall narrative in the game.  Quests that are done when "Good" have significantly different outcomes than "Bad" and the game's last quest changes drastically as well.  The final, ultimate quests, are so well done that I have to recommend folks play the game multiple times.  Classic is a great challenge, and casual every other time is absolutely worth the eventual speedrunning you get done.Edit: Just finished the Alcedor/Cervul mode and this is such a good ng+ mode.  More enemies, different trap placement in some areas, some of the platforming can be a bit *too* easy, but Cervul's kit makes you feel like Sonic in this game.  Good game, good extra mode and good ng+ styled gameplay.I will say that I have a few complaints. The charge move having an odd tail and lack of air control in a precision platformer is a decision.  I would say that if it had no tail that was uncontrollable and included a fall, and you could regain control after a bit longer of a dash period without a fall, it would fit precision platforming better.  By this point I'm able to pull it off in one or two tries, but, it still feels a bit odd in an otherwise great set of platforming challenges.  Kastka Castle is a bit tough for the precision the game asks out of other situations (a bit of wiggle on the up-charge would help), and Stormheim Castle is capable of overwhelming you when already asking for precision.  While those challenges are something I am used to, I have to make sure I warn others as the spikes may turn off others.  Casual mode will make those castles not a big deal, but Classic players may pull out some hairs.Great game, with some great twists and changes that make it really worth finding the endings.  Also gave me a huge want for something like it now that I'm nearly done.Edit 2:  Just finished the ribbon/platinum.  Great game.  Wholly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I sadly didn't have any money to back this when this was on Kickstarter. i did keep track of this game via a few indie game Youtube channels and also did the time to do some research on this title's development and Berzerk Studio as a whole. And I am VERY glad I found out about this, just by pure luck many years ago(Abridged/Brief Development and Developer History)i'll briefly touch up on Berzerk and then I'll give a review. I'll keep this history lesson as brief and informative as I canBerzerk Studio has been around for 10 years give or take. From what I gathered, they're designs for a lot of their games and the directions they took were one of 3 ways1-Bizzare and Chaotic- A lot of their games had absurd concepts  or settings that made very little sense when put into real world context, but they made for very addictive and fun time wasters 2-Gory/Edgy-Given their name is Berzerk Studio this should be a dead giveaway, but a lot of their games do NOT hold back on the brutality, gore or violence. Thankfully, its done to either enhance a game's vision or to give it some "morbid sprinkles" if you will on their cakes of games3-Familiar, but not a rip off-This is one of Berzerk's big ideologies with game design. A lot of their games will undoubtedly remind you of some of the greats of old from the NES/SNES and Arcade era, but Berzerk always would add enough zany and over the top bits to give their own unique take on thingsHow I missed these guys during the flash era I don't know, but here's hoping this can be my way to fix thatThe last thing I will mention is that Infernax is technically a game that got "boosted" via Kickstarter and crowdfundingEssentially Berzerk went through hell and high water to get a publisher, but they all insisted on censoring the gore and violence for a publisher. Eventually the team of 3 had enough and they decided to publish on their own. (at least until The Arcade Crew came around) Infernax's first build's playable versions of the game came around in 2015. But, thanks to their Kickstarter going well, they made an additional  3000 USD (4K CAD since they're Canadian) to enhance the game and add more features and polish to it.And you know what Berzerk, ya'll did a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WONDERFUL JOB here. Its a bit awkward in how it's structured, but it's VERY unique. And I'll explain why while dividing the review into chunks(Actual Review)At it's heart, Infernax feels like a mixture of an ARPG, Castlevania, Zelda II, and Dante's Inferno put all together.I won't go into spoiler territory, but the basic gist of it is you are the Duke of Upel known as Alcedor (name change is via file names just like Zelda, which is a great bonus, some names can even get you secrets and Easter Eggs)(Basic Story and Branching Paths/Choices matter)Alcedor returns to his home of Upel, but to his dismay, the entire land is overrun with dark occult magic and evil demons and monsters are everywhere in sight. Everything from specters to zombies to demons to ghouls to lizard people. They are all lead by the evil demon Paimon and it's up to you to destroy him and save the land and your people from this evil curse and a grim cultOr... is it???If it's not a dead giveaway just by my wording alone, what was surprising to me and quite unique is that this game actually encourages replayability with multiple endings. I'm aware some Metroidvania's have multiple endings, hell even Symphony of the Night has a few given it created the genre, but it's not often that these multiple endings are BIG enough/conrete enough to warrant replaying. There are exceptions however, and Infernax is one of them. Because you can choose to be good or bad, and your actions DO matter and impact the game world around you.Do you want to be the hero and rescue and help as many people as you can while banishing evil like you were supposed to initially? Go right ahead. But if you would rather explore the what if scenario's of what would happen if you instead joined Paimon's forces and helped him conquer the land you swore to protect, you can choose to betray your people and your cause. However good or bad you want to be, it's up to you, but it will lead to one of four endings. Plus there's also cheat's you can get for beating each ending and after completing certain secret/hidden objectives as well.Bear in mind there's a total of 4 endingsGoodUltimate/Pure GoodEvilUltimate/Pure EvilA branching story like this encourages replayability and will stack up quite a bit of play time, this in turn makes up for the game's otherwise short length (About 8-10 hours per playthrough)This is all while along the way, you will be making Dante's Inferno style choices for possessed people around the many different villages you encounter. Your choices matter as to what abilities/spells you unlock as you decide people's fates as well as which of the two factions will approach you and what kind of side quests and ending you'll getIt's either kill or rescue/exorcise. The choice is yoursThis obviously is very reminiscent of Dante's Inferno with the similar Punish/Absolve options you'd get and the abilities you'd get from them. It takes a bit from Infamous however as I said these do affect the ending in the long runGameplay wise, this is essentially a mix of Castlevania and Zelda 2 The Adventure of Link,You gather potions, talk to people, and visit towns and shops to accquire spells, weapons, armor and potion bottles.But the usage of save shrines (holy statues that are save points) as well as the style of platforming, the way your character moves, and the ways you attack would make everyone in the Belmont clan smile and get all giddy. Everything from a Thunderstorm/Firestorm spell that is similar to Grand Cross to a shield spell that reduces damage and heals you a tad to a full heal to even being able to change from day to night at will (thats needed for some quests and puzzles)All of this topped into a gore filled package against disgusting monsters and slain villagers you need to rescue and avenge, and what we have is a VERY well crafted love letter to the genre greats of the late 8 and early 16 bit era, all in very nicely M rated packagingNext up is my villian playthrough and then I'll try to get both ultimate endings.But I REALLY hope we get more games like this (Modern Retro Castlevania/Metroidvania likes) and here's a toast of a green Elixer to Berzerk doing a GREAT job and to hopefully Infernax becoming a series!Bonus point because the soundtrack is quite a banger as well (:

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one thing I don't miss, it's NES games with janky hitboxes, limited controls, and instant death pits. Thankfully, Infernax limits how much it's a thorn in your side (mostly).The platforming in this game is relatively simple. Your first run of the game is limited largely to a standard strike with your longer-than-wide weapon and a shield that blocks many projectiles if you aren't attacking, which does seem to balance itself well between attacking and platforming. There are upgrades along the way that can change how you platform or approach battles. For the most part, the platforming feels pretty solid. Enemy hitboxes and player hurtboxes are incredibly forgiving, allowing you to have some very interesting close calls with parkour in a barn full of zombies. The downside to this is an enemy's hurtbox and hitbox are the same. So those narrow escapes are offset by needing to strike a zombie's groin in order to deal a killing blow. Normally not a big issue, but the game starts to introduce instant-death pits as you progress...You can acquire lives or potions. Lives are used upon death which resets your position to when you entered the room and replenish after a game over. Potions heal your health (or mana/magic points/pewpew pool) but have to be bought to replenish. Early on in the dungeons, it leads to weighing how much you may want to use a potion to heal yourself or if you want to save it for the next room, as they can be helpful for harder enemies. However, once the game starts to add more NES pits with more and more ways to put you in them, the priorities get weird. It should be noted I was playing on a higher difficulty with my first runs and the lower difficulty option (casual? I forget) doesn't outright kill you when you fall into a pit. But if I had the ability to choose, I would prefer if pits scaled in damage with enemies on most difficulty settings (Dead Cells has ruined this for me in most games now).I started to feel more of a push to not use my potions in dungeons and save them for bosses, which makes sense in theory. But along with that, holes and platforming scale in difficulty more quickly than bosses or enemies themselves, so my priority started to lean heavy on everything being allocated to pit resources, Either by strategically taking damage so I don't waste excess health in a pit or focusing on lives before potions. The biggest downside this has is it makes bosses and enemies feel underwhelming. Unless they're also planning to put you into a pit, all that face-tanking practice makes their patterns super easy. I think my favorite late game boss was the bad ending boss as it was one of the few bosses that made me retry more than a few times on my earlier runs. The only other boss I can think of that I died to almost as much was largely due to being (semi-spoilers) . This is largely a subjective thing and maybe I'm that bad at platforming. Or just so good at strategic face-tanking.However, what is probably my favorite part of the game is the replay value, which tends to be my favorite thing in most games. There's various endings, triggered by a multitude of ways to play this game. This includes dialogue choices, a lot of various characters which play very differently, and even particular player actions. Some of these I would never even think to ever try, but at least the achievements helped give me some ideas. The gore is a bit much for my liking, partially cuz I'm a weenie but also cuz sometimes I can't see what's killing me, especially when it's red demon blood spraying to and fro. The aesthetic is still tolerable and enjoyable enough. And the game doesn't take itself serious enough for me to feel tonal whiplash between getting pranked with pits, a kill screen with way too much fire, eating wall chicken, or paintball mode (or too much gore mode too I guess). I think my biggest gripe with the replay value is my favorite character to play is stuck as 2nd player, which means I had to do the co-op singleplayer mode. Not to be confused with the singleplayer or 2-player co-op mode, which also adds replay value.Most my gripes with this game are subjective but maybe an easy fix with a few more accessibility toggles. But still enjoyed it for what it is and I don't think it needs any backseat dev'ing at this point. And it's even a game to play with friends?! Now that's a mode I miss from the NES and SNES days...

_childDocuments_.review: I like challenging retro platformers a lot, and I tend to replay ones I've fallen for frequently. Infernax hits me right where I live. Like "Hollow Knight", it wears its retro Metroidvania influences on its sleeves. Unlike "Hollow Knight", Infernax isn't a 60 hour marathon to the end, but instead packs a retro game length paired with its difficulty. Like "Shovel Knight", Infernax augments its short main compaign by packing the game full of reasons to return to it. Unlike "Shovel Knight", these 'other things' aren't extra campaigns and modes, but new ways to replay this one, with several endings to find, and new playable characters to uncover. In this tale of three indie knights, Infernax stands above the rest, when it comes to crafting a game you'll be unable to put down until you've squeezed every last bit of nectar from it. Frankly, it's a masterpiece, and any fan of retro platformers and metroidvanias owes it to themselves to play this game. And replay it, several times.

_childDocuments_.review: FINAL VERDICTEPIC Castlevania-style side-scroller with a killer pixel aesthetic, superb soundscape and story that is truly worthy of multiple play-throughs (and co-op multiplayer sessions if you can find some DEDICATED friends, it's a LONG game for co-op). Push through the platforming leading up to Combbelton Necropolis and you will be rewarded.OVERALL 9/10A playable work of art that is fun to play and reaches heights few come close to achieving. I highly recommend it! (for reasons I will state in other sections ;p.) Sadly it is over all too soon as the game is very short (but you can play through as other characters [all but one suck though ;p]).GRAPHICS 9/10The game is clearly inspired by the Castlevania series (Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest imho) and transposes it to a more medieval setting with medieval knights in full armour using standard medieval arms: maces (the protagonist and your avatar), halberds, swords, and so on. I really liked the art design, it honours the 80's-90's Nintendo (SNES) pixel aesthetic while taking it to heights never reached before (I don't think you'll see a man's head being caved in by a mace in a real SNES game OoO).SOUND/MUSIC 9/10The soundscape was a treat to the ears and made the action viscerally real; you can feel the impacts and blade slices. I might even buy the soundtrack! (It's really catchy!)CONTROLS 9/10I used a controller and had no issues whatsoever. During the Contra playthrough (Maxime Gunn) I had issues with the rocket dash (holy charge) but other than that I had no problems (other than issues with stun locking discussed further in "GAMEPLAY").PLOT 8/10A very well written story that works for all 3 branches (good, evil, evil to redemption). I felt that killing (or even sparing) the suffering man at the start should be viewed more as a neutral act (you weren't doing him any favours when you "spared" his life). The story reached epic proportions without jumping the shark or feeling corny (the evil playthrough where you have to storm Darsov city was one of the most epic experiences I have had in gaming. It was refreshing for once to see a story where bad guys aren't misunderstood, they're just bad guys. The writing really makes you feel the game's sense of morality and I approve.GAMEPLAY 9/10The levels are profoundly really well designed and stood up to multiple playthroughs. Each has their own unique aesthetic that keeps your interest from waning.An issue that didn't affect me (since I used a guide ;p) was that on your first playthrough it is impossible to determine the effect of your actions and there are no take backs. For example, if you decide to let the talking skeleton go because he might not be a bad guy then you have no option to run up and deal with him after he joins his larger, well-armed friend.I found it irritating that I couldn't warp out of dungeons to restock my provisions (potions, etc.) but it made the game harder in a way that fits the Castlevania aesthetic it was going for (I suppose >_>).The stun locking was mildly irritating at times (Stormheim Castle especially) but not rage quit inducing.I felt that there should have been a save point before Combbelton Necropolis. That jumping section almost made me quit; I speedran through it after I had some experience but it is somewhat daunting for first time players and video walkthroughs were no help. Thankfully the accessibility options got me through it.While I appreciate the addition of multiple characters to lengthen gameplay and keeps things fresh all but 1 of the characters suck (Maxime Gunn, who is brokenly overpowered [Machine Gun Man in the year medieval!]). The Stranger's shotgun should have an ever so slightly longer reach as well as dealing more damage AND shooting it while standing in place SHOULDN'T push you back (eg. you can dig your heels in). The pushing while jumping is interesting though imo and has potential. Not being able to use potions is a little much though imo. Every other character I played (eg. the wizard) were brokenly UNDERpowered  making them impossible run throughs (for me at least, I'm not THAT dedicated ;p).

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone that grew up on NES greats like Zelda II, Castlevania II, and so on, this game is for you. The towns look like Zelda II towns. The houses, doors, and interiors look like Zelda II, nearly down to the pixel. The dungeons will remind you of a harmony between Zelda II and Castlevania II, complete with wall chickens. The overworld has some nearly familiar sights with the giant rock wall you knelt next to with a crystal in hand to be swept away to a different area. The day/night cycle will take you back to when green zombie days infested previously less difficult areas. Night rewards the farmer as well, with more XP and gold. This was a great game and a great love letter to a historical era of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Castlevania fan. It has been one of my favorite series since the moment I played the first one on NES way back around 35 years ago or so now. I've gone out of my way to collect every game in the series including Rondo on PCE, and Nocture in the Moonlight. So seeing Infernax, my first thoughts were that it was going to mimic SotN, with 8 bit  a bad way.I was very wrong.My favorite Castlevania has always been Castlevania II: Simon's Quest. That game was so ahead of its time...and Infernax nails it dead on. I have never had so much fun with a Castlevania clone as I had with this. If you are like me and you loved Simon' Quest...this is a no brainer. Get it.But lets go even further....because something big was added to the game that changes everything:2 player co-op was added.Now I haven't yet tried it, but my buddy is ready to do so.....so right now I can't report on that. But co-op isn't the big thing I was referring to....Remember the Konami code? Try it on the main screen....and you will get the most amazing hidden game mode I have seen in any game. The game will change to the style of yet another great NES masterpiece: Contra. And it plays so darn fun in a Castlevania themed world. its fun to pave the way in the main quest, and then go over it with guns blazing right after on a Contra style save.I thought the $20 price point was going to be too high.....its not. This is defiantly a gaming gem to purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think anyone would be surprised to learn that Infernax is a good game. A damn good game even. The blood, the gore, the deep love for the old-school Castlevania games. It's all there, but wearing a modern, pixelated, blood-soaked jacket.Infernax caught my eye after watching a few “no damage boss fights” videos of it, and I immediately fell in love with the design and the gameplay. I adore the Metroidvania's, but this... this is what Castlevania 2 for the NES should've been when it was first released. And I have a niggling in the back of my mind that the developers thought the same. So, Infernax was, presumably, born. A love-letter to Castlevania as it was back in the old days.Being an old-school wannabe, Infernax is filled to the brim with similar mechanics but modernized.  The game offers two difficulty settings. Casual and classic. Casual includes everything the game has to offer but allows a bit more leeway with health, damage, save-points and environmental hazards. And on death you're spawned at the start of the screen you died on. Whereas classic mode foregoes the silk gloves and tests your 80's gaming skills to the max. That means no in-between save points in dungeons, instant death pits and when you die it's back to your last save point. This allows players of all skill level to enjoy the game however they want.Next, the pixel art. By God is it glorious. It's gory, bloody, visceral and truly a work of genuine art. Event regular enemies die in the most satisfying ways and bosses explode in a fireworks display of viscera and blood that covers your player sprite in spades. The soundtrack is likewise amazing. There weren't any tracks besides maybe the “evil path” overworld soundtrack that stood out but it did a good job of adding to the grim atmosphere.Infernax's gameplay is a mixture of action and puzzle-platforming, and balances the two quite nicely so neither overstay their welcome. Some of the later platforming sections got a bit old, but mainly because I hate moving platforms. The boss fights were all rather unique and managed to challenge me up until the end.To add to the combat, the game offers spells and different abilities you can use to kill enemies. Each dungeon houses one special ability, most of them metroidvania-like abilities like a super jump or a dash. Other abilities and spells are found throughout the world by completing quests and finding the appropriate trigger points to buy these spells/abilities.Speaking of quests, now's a good time to mention that this game has a pseudo-moral system. By completing certain quests your character will gain good or bad karma which plays into the way the story unfolds. And not just in the way of a mediocre good or bad ending. There's even endings for beating the game as mostly good, mostly bad, a redemption ending and many others. This adds to the re-playability I've not seen in any other game,Last, but not least, the game has recently added a co-op mode. You can now choose to play on your own as just yourself, play with a buddy or play alone and be able to swap between characters. The second character is a somewhat different play-style with his throwing axes and includes his own special abilities that you can upgrade to your liking.In short, Infernax is a bloody good game and shows what Castlevania 2 could've been and more. While it has its problems (story being a little lacklustre, the game is fun and doesn't overstay its welcome. And has a ton of re-playability with all the endings and secrets to find as well.

_childDocuments_.review: this game walks a pretty thin tightrope between pretty standard modern hard-but-fair design and bordering-on-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NES hard. there's castlevania knockback and you WILL get knocked into instant-death pits, lose all your lives and set yourself back twenty minutes of progress. but also it hooked me and i'm on my fourth playthrough right now, highly recommendGAMEPLAY:your main character is essentially an old-school D&D cleric, with a mace and shield. it plays like a pretty standard NES platformer; you can jump, swing your mace, or crouch. your character is two tiles tall, one when crouching, and most enemies and projectiles will attack at either your top half or bottom half, so there's a lot of crouching to duck under projectiles or attack shorter enemies. you have a shield which blocks projectiles and is always active - when standing it covers your top half, and you can crouch to protect your bottom half. it's inactive when attacking, though, so mastering using your shield is mostly about patience and not panicking - if you're standing still and standing/crouching right, you're pretty well-protected by the shield. you can also learn and cast spells, but your mana is pretty limited and only comes back at checkpoints so you'll mostly be relying on your regular moveset. the game has a leveling system taken straight from zelda 2; you get XP from killing enemies and can spend it to increase your health, damage or magic - but the more you level one of these attributes, the more expensive it is to level further, while ones you haven't leveled as much stay cheaper. so as a result you generally end up levelling all three, and don't really get much customization other than which one is ahead by a level or two.rather than being a linear platformer, the game's world is designed more like a metroidvania, with you opening up new paths as you explore. it is still pretty linear, and you'll mostly be following a set progression path, but it's still satisfying to explore with lots of side paths and optional quests. it also has really satisfying progression where you get a noticeable upgrade or new ability 1 to 3 times per hour. the game's not too long, most of my playthroughs clock in at 5 or 6 hours, so it's able to keep up a pretty steady pace of becoming stronger in a way that feels very earned.the pixel art is pretty standard. it sometimes feels a little inconsistent, where most of the art looks like an NES game, but a few bits like spell icons have visibly too many colors (to the point it looks more like a SNES game) and the gore covering your character doesn't really match the rest of the character's artstyle. the game's overall vibe is somewhere between an NES castlevania game, and those old newgrounds flash games with excessive gore for shock value. that said this game has the best and most customizable CRT filter i've ever seen - even just having all the CRT settings on low smooths over a lot of imperfections really pleasantly. it really helps the visuals look better and more cohesive than it otherwise would.there are some things i dislike. some parts of progression can be pretty cryptic (especially the bit where you have to cast a specific, missable spell to summon one of the game's mandatory five dungeons), and there are moments of frustration that i don't think are outright unfair, but definitely feel unfair in the moment after you've lost your last life to an enemy ledge-camping a hard jump and knocking you into a pit. it's not nearly as cruel as a lot of actual NES games, but it's definitely closer than most games are nowdays.a co-op mode is also included, and it's fantastic. it would've been simple to just give player 2 a copy of the first character, but the player-2 character - the main character's squire - has his own moveset and progression designed to complement the player-1 character and have them cover each other's weaknesses. definitely recommend casual difficulty if you're going co-op, though, since the amount of extra stuff on screen makes things more than chaotic enough to make up for the difficulty dropoverall i still recommend the game if you can put up with the abrasive NES-era qualities. for as punishing as the game is, it makes really good use of its difficulty in a way that feels really rewarding to overcome, more so than a lot of genuinely harder games. there's an easy mode where the difficulty feels just right, without really diminishing the feeling of accomplishment.

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is a great love letter to Castlevania 2 and just an okay MV.  And while it is stylistically impressive, It comes served with a side of jank and is on the shorter side. If you enjoyed Infernax, I recommend: Alwa's Legacy, Cathedral and Astalon: Tears of the Earth for similar music/pixel art (But better games imo).  If you liked the punishing nature of an NES feeling metroidvania, I recommend Mortal Manor (it has god awful music though).  Castlevania 2 is a game which most people wanted to like but found irritating.  Infernax improves a lot of the issues that plagued that game and feels much better to play.  You will experience some cheap deaths, questionable controls (some of the abilities you get later on have weird key combinations to execute).  Sometimes you can overshoot a jump using these abilities which you cannot cancel out of, and to expect us to commit to memory the exact distance of the forward dash for instance feels unreasonable and any resulting deaths do feel cheap.  Some transitions feel a 'little' slow to skip through (skipping through text, saving the game).There are some long runs from save points (no save points inside dungeons, forcing you to either complete it all or exit it whenever you make some progress to save your game).The music/sound, style, graphics, animations - They are all great, they nailed it!  Small things like the death animations are just hilariously good.Without some of the cheapness, some better controls/handling for the abilities, this would have been a solid B.  I'd like to see this sort of game done like that, plus a significantly larger world, with more powers and things, and additional customisation trinkets like some MV's, then perhaps we could get something really special.Worth the experience if you spent time on the early Castlevania games.===================== =====================  Aeterna Noctis | Astalon: Tears of the Earth | Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom | Hollow Knight | Cathedral |  Doomblade | Afterimage | Elderand | Ori and the Will of the Wisps | Environmental Station Alpha | Ender Lilies: Quietus of the Knights | Depths of Sanity | Alwa’s Legacy | Steamworld Dig 2 | Islets | Blasphemous | Haak | Outbuddies DX | Mortal Manor | Escape From Tethys | Treasure Adventure Game | Chasm | Haiku, the Robot | Monster Sanctuary | Rabi-Ribi | Elliot Quest |  Momodora: Reverie under the Moonlight | Lone Fungus | Aggelos | Iconoclasts | Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night | Death’s Gambit: Afterlife | After Death | Catmaze | Omega Strike | Plague of Yamorn |  | Wuppo | Sheepo | Ato |  Castle In The Darkness | Alwa’s Awakening | Pharaoh Rebirth | Yoku’s Island Express | Guacamelee! 2 | Shantae and the Pirate’s Curse | Shantae: Half-Genie Hero | Axiom Verge | Strider | Minoria | Souldiers | Bone Appetit | The Witch & the 66 Mushrooms | Destroy Space Aliens | La-Mulana | Guacamelee! | 8Doors | Gato Roboto | Super Panda Adventures |  Rain World | Dandara | Blaster Master Zero | Sundered | Salt & Sanctuary | Valdis Story | Insanely Twisted Shadow Planet | Apotheon | Nyaruru Fishy Fight | Aquaria | Lootbox Lyfe | Rex Rocket | Bad Pad | B.I.O.T.A. | Shadow Complex | Chronicles of Teddy | Grime | Phoenotopia: Awakening | Timespinner | Dust: An Elysian Tale | Fearmonium | ====================

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of classic styled games such as Shovel Knight, I thoroughly enjoyed the "metroidvania love letter to the NES" experience that is Infernax.  The sprite work is lovingly detailed and dark, the gameplay loop is tight, the choice aspect makes repeat playthroughs varied and unique, the music is banging (my personal favorite is the default night theme), there's lots of secrets and alternate characters you can discover, it gets not very frequent but major updates (like they just added coop with brand new cutscenes and dialogue) , and many endings to find.However, I have a few nitpicks. For one, if you 100% everything in a run, then it will take you about 3 hours, which is pretty short in my opinion. However, the game is intended to be played multiple times to get all the endings, so keeping each run short is kind of a blessing. Second, there is little sprite details that bug me. The alternate character- The Stranger - has a shotgun, which gets better shells when you upgrade your weapon. However, his reload animation keeps the same red shells no matter the upgrade. Splash screens and specific cutscenes as alternate characters are unchanged from the main character, so you'll be playing as the stranger, but then all of a sudden you're Alcedor in the splash screen. Dialogue for alternate characters that aren't even closely related to Alcedor are unchanged from the medieval lord, so- once again as an example- you'll be playing the stranger: a time traveler from the future thats a reference to almost every classic 80's action or horror movie- and yet people will still see him as their lord. Though Im pretty sure its too much to ask for completely rewritten dialogue, new splash screens, and completely revamped cutscenes, it would still be a nice touch.tl;dr: Its a great Metroidvania that's a love letter to nearly every major NES game that's meant to be played over and over to find all the secrets and endings.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun retro style Castlevania clone.  It's a good game and really scratches that nostalgia itch but it has a few quirks.The game is difficult, but annoyingly gets significantly easier as the game progresses instead of the inverse, which seems like a really odd challenge scaling model.  The first dungeon is by far the most difficult one you will encounter, as by the time you get to the second dungeon you will have far more abilities to be able to handle the various threats that stand in your way.My only other gripe is that some of the abilities that are required for tight platforming sections are needlessly obtuse to pull off.  Not giving away spoilers but one ability you will be using for a lot of platforming sections requires a button input followed by 3 button inputs.  This becomes incredibly frustration when trying to preform these actions in super right window platforming.  There are options in the accessibility settings that can change this, but even the solution they take to this is needlessly obtuse on a modern 12 button controller.  (It's more akin to smash brothers than it is to a platformer).All in all though its a lot of fun.  Upgrade system is satisfying, and there are plenty of exploring and secrets to find.  I wouldn't hesitate to try this out if you're a fan of metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid throwback action platformer. It's only a metroidvania in the shallowest of definitions, though it does ironically have a lot of pre-SotN Castlevania influences. I'd say Zelda 2 runs just as strongly in Infernax's blood, but not really Faxanadu like other reviews might suggest.A bit over 15 hours and I was able to complete 3.5 playthroughs across the 2-ish morality paths to get 100% achievements. Most of the game is the right amount of challenge on Classic mode with Casual being a bit too easy - except for the third dungeon. F*** that dungeon, it's the bad kind of old-school platforming. Thankfully there's no punishment for activating any of Infernax's various cheats you discover; unfortunately, you won't have access to any of those until exactly after you beat the third dungeon once. At least it makes replays less frustrating.Bosses are definitely the highlight, with excellently horrific designs that really makes the generic common enemies look even less impressive in hindsight, which is a shame.I don't think there's anything that Infernax really does above-and-beyond similar games, but it provides a solid enough overall experience that fans of the NES-era will have a good time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic throwback to the old school hard games of yesteryear (or should I say NESteryear) and the Evil Dead movies, if you are a fan of Zelda 2 or classic Castlevania, you'll take to this game like a fish to water. Filled with multiple endings and several bonus characters, the game has EXCELLENT replayability. This game gets two thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Gory good stuff.  Casual mode is a major plus, I wish more of these retro-hard games had one.  Look, I grew up with the games Infernax is aping.  If I wanted to slowly saw my own ♥♥♥♥ off with an NES controller, I'd go play Castlevania II.  I don't think it's even that much easier, it just cuts down on some of the major annoyances, eg. cheap deaths from getting knocked off ledges.Anyway, lovely pixel art and fun creature designs - at least the bosses, the regular enemies are mostly your bog-standard skeletons and zombies for most of the game.Gameplay is about what you'd expect.  None of the quests were so obtuse that I had to look up the next steps, so that's a nice improvement over Infernax's main inspiration, Simon's Quest.I'd say playtime clocks in at 8-12 hours.  Probably closer to 8 for most people who aren't faffing about like me.  You could replay it and do all the opposite moral choices.  I'm given to understand that a big questline late in the game is completely different should you be good or evil.  It's a pretty tight game so I might actually do that at some point.Silver star!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent homage to some of the NES era greats! It blends the best aspects of Castlevania II, Legend of Zelda II, and a few others. It also includes a slew of features that allow you to adjust difficulty as you see fit, though you'd better believe I was hellbent on finishing the game in Classic mode my first time through. Looking forward to subsequent playthroughs, as this game has multiple endings and characters to unlock. Also an excellent game to play on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, surprisingly easy and fun, except Stormheim Castle (water castle) and Kadjanto Stronghold (poison castle) that are designed so you instantly die in the water or poison, respectively. The game also has a bunch of secret codes and characters for you to replay the main story with, pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: The Metroidvania that I needed! I really like the option on this game and it's been fun so far. No issues, plays on my rig great, and no issues streaming it either.UPDATE: I ran into an issue where progression is halted at  a certain point in the game. It's a shame that no one ever play tests these games when they are released. Just like the Iconoclasts and a few others that are not able to be completed in any form, this game has gone the same way.This game should be avoided!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Very similar to Zelda II and Phoenotopia, though a lot shorter. It has a pretty rewarding gameplay loop, though the stat boosts can be maxed out fairly quickly if you find the right place to grind, The instant deaths from water/lava are the only bad game design choice and the only real source of difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight of a game! The music, art, and world are all pretty great. The difficulty with Classic restarts is just about right (though there might just be a special place in Hell for the maniacal dev that set-up some of the platforming in Kastka Palace).More than most games, this feels like a labor of love and a bombastic display of skill and artistry on the part of the devs. Highly, highly recommended if you grew up with Castlevania 2/Adventures of Link or if you're a young whippersnapper that likes retro titles.PS: If you're gonna do an Ultimate Evil run, I had a blast with Wizard mode.PPS: If you end up liking this or just like pixel-art retro platformers with great music, go play Cyber Shadow!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like a mix of Legend of Zelda 2 and the old Castlevanias. Pretty darn good I'm not usually a big fan of platformers and I found this pretty challenging at some points but it was fun enough that I really just wanted to keep slogging through the tough parts. Lots of replayability with alternates to the main character (input during name select on file creation) and the two moral paths play very differently in how you use certain spells. I guess my only thing is that bosses get to be way too easy if you just stack all the buff spells and whale on them. So most of the challenge of the game is environmental. There's really 3-4 a few challenging platforming sections that really cause certain sections of the game to drag on but that might also be me being bad or trying to rush those sections. I would say pick up the game on sale. Maybe not worth the full 20 bucks I liked it well enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my first steam review, but I love this game. My first playthrough I thought - that was a cool, very tough NES style metroidvania game. But on subsequent playthroughs you learn to really love the game, appreciate all the care the developers put into the secret characters, alternate storylines, and hidden areas. And if you get stuck there’s plenty of accessibility options and old-school cheat code systems you can use to help. Highly recommend, and excellent on steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Game is cool until you get to the water castle. From there the difficulty turns from "fair and challenging" to "dodge the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or get insta-killed". It's like they looked at all the negative ♥♥♥♥ from every Castlevania and "Metroid-vania" game and put them all into the water temple, which is a crapshoot to even discover (use your lightning spell at the end of the pier; how the hell was I supposed to know that?). The game became incredibly frustrating to play when I got to this point, soI stopped playing and I'm not sure if I'll start it back up again. I know there are simple cheats I can activate on the main menu, but that would sap all the fun and challenge out of the game too.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play classic mode unless you hate yourself or you're trying to speedrun samsara. There are no rewards for beating it whatsoever, all you get is a worthless achieve.I've replayed this game a sh*tton of times and had an immense amount of fun playing it ever since I switched to casual mode. Easily my favorite game of last year. Sorry powerwash sim, if Infernax hadn't come out in the same year you'd be goty for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game.  Plays very similiar to Castlevania II: Simon's Quest and Zelda II: The Adventure of Link.  Music is catchy, multiple playable character classes (with name codes) for great replay value.  Game is a little on the short side, just 5 castle areas with a possible couple more levels depending on playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to all the old Nintendo 8-bit classics. This is both a good and bad thing at times, but overall it's positive. I thoroughly enjoyed this game. It's a lot of fun and despite the different difficulties there really isn't much difference. The only threat in this game is the one-hit kill terrain and pixel perfect jumps at the end of it. Despite that, I 100%'d it because it was fun. The morality system is neat and not too complex. I liked seeing the changes in world. The memes and call backs to old video tropes was funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A fun lil' call back to Castlevania types of games, II in particular. There's a bunch of other elements here and there, as well as the various kinds of secrets and types of characters you can play as which makes playing it anew different in how you will execute things such as the Contra like mode. Overall a recommended play, especially on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been so amazing! Working on the last two achievements to finish this game and it was worth all of the time put in! I enjoyed the different characters, the story, and the ability to cheat if you want! (Gotta kind of work to get that though!) Overall, an amazing game that I'd like to see more games made like! _childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you remember the good old Castlevania games, this leans heavily on the same concept.You could even say, it's a re-imagining of Castlevania.The controls are solid, the story is engaging, albeit the directions and quests are not always clear. Unless you know how to progress already, chances are you'll search around for 30-40 minutes just to finish one quest.The game also features a day/night cycle where at night different, stronger monsters spawn, however to mitigate the increase in difficulty, you upgrade your gear to keep the overall difficulty quite linear.Long story short; I'd recommend it, if you like playing good old platformer RPGs. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game exceeded my expectations as a classic Castlevania clone. This game manages to get the look and feel of the classic Castelvania game and combine it with many elements of Symphony Of The Night. That one line right there should get players excited for this game for any true Castlevania fan!!! Smooth controls that are tight, allow you to traverse the world feeling good about NOT dying so easily from stupid cliff falls or pixel damages. Level up, upgrades, side quests are all present in this game. Choice of direction allow different story branches.  All-in-all this game is one badass game and should NOT be missed by anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best indie games I've played in a long time. It's wonderfully designed, with everything Castlevania fans want and *so* much more. The gameplay mechanics are simple, but well-balanced and responsive. The level design is outstanding, with new challenges and secrets around every corner. It doesn't hurt that the graphics are vibrant and detailed too. On top of all that, Infernax boasts an impressive amount of customization options, in both its story and gameplay. Spells galore, sidequests aplenty, and an engaging morality system that determines how your endgame plays out. Add in a rockin' chiptune soundtrack, reminiscent of Castlevania 2 itself (this game's spiritual predecessor), and you have a recipe for success. It's not too difficult either, on a casual playthrough, at least. Infernax has a nice blend of challenging enemy and obstacle design, while also telegraphing clear patterns on how to overcome them. I loved my playthrough so much that I put in every extra bit of effort to get the Ultimate Good ending first, so that I can come back time and time again for more. And come back I did! I've so far completed an Ultimate Evil playthrough, gotten the Future Ending, and 100% completed the Demonology. All I have left is to get the "Path of the Wretch" ending, and I'll be set! Infernax was worth every second.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and short little adventure with a morality system in a nice throwback to pre-SotN Castlevania. Nothing groundbreaking but still an enjoyable 8-or-so hours of bashing demons and facing the true danger in this game: pits.Special mention to the "cheat codes" that help a bunch when you've already completed the game but just want to go achievement hunting. While some may consider the length lackluster, I feel like the replayability of the different endings more than makes up for it as it strikes a great balance of not being completely tedious to replay, and probably short enough to beat in one sitting for the more dedicated.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game similar to Castlevania in style and gameplay. It also has features of Zelda2. I would say quality-wise this is a near perfect game. It has great music and amazing 8-16bit-ish graphics. The gameplay is solid and fun and has nice spells and skills. Everything feels satisfying. The atmosphere and story is well done. There is even this Simon's Quest feature of day and night shift - but done right. The game also has quests of good and evil nature and the character can be seen as a hero to normal people or villains depending on how you play. I felt like the game is a bit heavy on gore and occult signs though. Obviously the developers were Satanic Freemasons - not sure how I feel about that but they make great games. When you play the evil way you can join an evil hidden cult that conspires and murders people who expose their secrets. Can't get any more Masonic I'd say ;-) Anyway, great game. If you're anything into these kinda games you should totally get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good.  Basically a mashup of Zelda 2 + NES Castlevanias, but not as hard as any of those.Seems like the game is harder if you do a good playthrough because it unlocks an ultimate dungeon.  I only had one gameover on classic mode and it was in the final dungeon, that was when I learned it doesn't save your progress and you lose XP + gold like a Soulslike, it just puts you at the last save with all progress made since then lost.  So I broke the ultimate dungeon into a few dives, leaving to restock and save after getting a key or two.  You can grind in this to make things easier, but the ultimate dungeon seems tuned to you being max level with all upgrades, so I think if you get an advantage for the last dungeon, it isn't much of one.EDIT: Played it again a year later since the coop update, this time did an ultimate evil playthrough.  Lots of fun, took 5 hours and did everything (first playthrough in singleplayer took 8.5).
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax – now this really is something special.  I went into this fully expecting it to be another indie metroidvania, but instead I got the spiritual successor to Simon’s Quest that I never new I wanted, all wrapped up in stupidly delicious pixel gore and a love off all things 80s and Metal.  It really is a crime that this game seems to have flown under the radar.On the surface, this is a rock solid 2D platformer with strong RPG elements, and it presents you with a lot of choices that have a tangible effect on the game, such as what spells and skills you have access to.  The graphics are sickly good, the chiptune soundtrack is pumping, and controls are responsive and satisfying.  There’s also a bit of metroidvania to the exploration, as different parts of the map become accessible as you can new traversal skills You could probably blitz through the game on your first try between 6-10 hours (8.7 for me) depending on how skilled you are, and the bosses, while fun to fight, aren’t that hard.But the real genius of Infernax is that there’s so much mystery and secrets bubbling away under the surface, that I barely even saw 50% of the game on my playthrough.  I left plenty of side quests unfinished, and I never even fully upgraded my gear, and even an optional dungeon that I never got through.  Throw into the mix that there are multiple playable characters and multiple endings as well, I feel like I’ve barely scratched the surface with Infernax, and given how much I enjoyed my first play through, I couldn’t be happier.I’m gonna take a break and play something else for a while, but I will be back to smash more zombies with my pixel mace very, very soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! This game rocks! It's got old-school feel and smooth gameplay. Well designed. Doesn't overstay its welcome. I may have had to look up a few tips when I was stuck but that was my only real disappointment. So much fun in a tight, retro package. I've played it through 3 or 4 different times!Love it!Get it if you enjoy retro style games and a good metroidvania.I'm going to update my review so I can get a steam achievement! Woohoo!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: While Infernax’s gameplay and design rely too heavily on its antiquated inspirations, the experience is elevated by its unique presentation and ideas. ProsFor me, the moral system was the most interesting idea and it’s implemented well. I completed three playthroughs and was surprised that the third act of each route offered completely different enemies and story arches. The pixelated gore and unsettling still frames during the choice sections are in abundance and works to define Infernax’s overall presentation. ConsAt times, the controls can be horribly frustrating. For example, your character’s jump. The height is not dictated by the force which you press the button, rather a default height that will cause you to unintentionally hit flying enemies and traps.The primary weapon used throughout the entire game has an unusually short range and requires Ninja Gaiden-like precision. Additionally, the upgrade system too basic and doesn’t add anything to the overall core gameplay. While I appreciate multiple endings, perhaps there could have been a shortcut or skip once you complete the game once in order to experience everything. Requiring four, full dedicated playthroughs is too much, even if the game is only four-five hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game! I always liked the open world metroidvania feel of "Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest" for the NES but felt that game was missing certain elements that would have made it great. 'Infernax' has all the best elements of 'CV2' and adds additional ones that the game was missing. I always like when games (like the PlayStation 2 game "Lord of the Rings: Two Towers") has other good guys fighting along side of you to make it feel like the whole land is gripped in war, not just the hero. 'Infernax' has this element and it made the game feel more epic. Having towns in a game show you the people you are fighting for which makes the world you are in seem more real. This combined with the open world game-play makes the world of 'Infernax' fun to traverse.Games are also more fun when you are given more reasons to replay it. With the "good guy / bad guy" paths that you can take (as well as the multiple characters you can play as), 'Infernax' gives you so much to look forward to.Great Job, 'Infernax' Team! Hope to see more games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Hits that itch Castlevania and Oldskool fans have been dying to scratch, before dragging you into a world of its own. Don't be intimidated by its bluster of being super hard, kids these days are just fat and weak. Take your lumps, rise to the challenge, save the world or burn it down. Killer soundtrack is a plus!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute must buy if you are a fan of NES era Castlevania (specifically Simon's Quest) and Zelda 2. This game is a love letter to those games with nods to other NES era video games. Infernax does such a good job at what it sets out to accomplish, you will find that your knowledge of the games it is recreating can help you find secrets and easter eggs. Multiple playthroughs are encouraged by having multiple endings and different ways to play the game. My only issue is I find it to be incredibly easy, even on "Classic" mode. The only thing I would say is semi challenging is some platforming parts, but the bosses and enemies go down easily. If you are seeking a challenge, I'd probably play a different game. If you want a fun, quick romp through a game with neat callbacks and easter eggs, absolutely give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: The morality system where your choices really do matter is a great mechanic. It has replay value baked in due to that. The core gameplay is fun and has a healthy amount of challenge. The 8-bit art style is great, especially with the themes in this game. Infernax is a love letter to NES Castlevania and maybe Faxanadu that's good all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game.  The way your choices affect the character's appearance, abilities, music, the world's appearance, the fate of npcs added a lot of replay value.  I normally put games for a time before subsequent runs but with this I picked it right back up for a 2nd pass after finishing my first goodboy run, I binged straight through a new evil guy run and my jaw was on the floor for most of it.  Incredible package, and I loved the references to 80s pop culture.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who loves metroidvanias and still appreciates the retro graphics of the early Castlevania games, will feel right at home in the World of Infernax. For anyone on the fence, like I was for a few months, buy the dam game. The game is extremely challenging at points but never too much to where I wanted to permanently put the game down. The game has so many great things going for it: it hits that sweet spot of tough and fun on top of having; excellent writing; fantastic ability progression; just enough secrets to keep things spicy; and not being so long that I get sick of it. I LOVED THIS GAME. Buy it. Enjoy it. No need to thank me.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and fun metroidvania, very reminiscent of Nintendo 64 Castlevania titles. Catchy 64 bit music, makes for a short and sweet adventure (you can probably finish it in a weekend). Gameplay-wise, you get a similar challenge from platforming and fights. Hitboxes are unfortunately not razor sharp, which occasionally creates a bit of awkwardness. I have also on occasion encountered some bugs where you get trapped in certain screens and can't progress, but this seems to resolve when you reload the game.It is no Hollow Knight or Shovel Knight, but definitely worth playing if you are into metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is a fun game if, like me, you're into retro-styled metroidvanias. It's not the very best but it's a fun time while it lasts. The difficulty isn't that bad. I found most challenge coming from the platforming in dungeons rather than the bosses. Initially the platforming isn't that bad but some of the mid and later stages require you to use a couple of power-ups you get and it can sometimes feel a bit clunky. Add to this a few occasions where enemies are placed in very awkward places and it can sometimes become annoying. I can understand why they did it though.  As for bosses, I found that you can cheese pretty much all of them by taking a hit and just thrashing them during your invincibility frames. More often than not their health will go down quicker than yours, especially if upgraded.The graphics are 'retro' with some nice art in cut scenes and the the writing is pretty good. Overall I'd certainly recommend it if you're looking for a short metroidvania to tide you over.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Takes aspects from multiple game series (Castlevania 2, Metroid, and one more that shall remain a secret!) and refines them to make a game that will challenge you and make you keep coming back for more!Multiple endings! RPG morality system that affects the world and how the world reacts to you!  And bonus secret dungeons that are entirely optional!The soundtrack holds its own against some of the greatest hits any retro style game has come out with!I cannot recommend this game more and for its full price of $20, it's definitely a steal that easily is worth every penny!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: NES style action with a leveling system and RPG elements reminiscent of Zelda 2 and Castlevania 2. Great fun so far, got 2 of what I think are about 4 total endings. Lots of characters and paths to choose for a lot of replayability. Very good visuals and music, lots of interesting monster design and phenomenal gore effects. Loved the metal homages in the achievement names! Also, money and XP accumulation felt very natural. I got everything I needed just by fighting enemies while exploring and clearing areas. Near the end of the game I chose to grind the last bit, but only because I was close to maxing out and didn't mind just finishing the rest before continuing - it did not feel necessary to do so.Though I compare it to two famously frustrating games, there's a lot more quality of life here. NPCs don't give away puzzle solutions, but aren't needlessly cryptic either. Solving things feels like an accomplishment without pushing me to my absolute limits, and the knowledge I gained on my first playthrough made me feel adequately prepared to start finding things for the other endings.I absolutely recommend it, but with a couple of warnings for things that may put people off:- Some of the platforming sections are...overly frustrating. There are only a couple that come to mind, but they require use of some unlockable movement abilities in a very strange way that did not feel good to complete.- Bosses are mostly easy. They're still *very* fun to fight, even if they're not the biggest challenge, which I find more important. This is definitely a little more upsetting due to the aforementioned platforming issues, since the boss fight can be a bit underwhelming after finally clearing an annoying section and having the fight be your payoff.- Certain events are not telegraphed well. I don't mean information given by the game - that's still fine! I mean certain things like clearing a quest, and having the results trigger another event somewhere on the map that you won't know about until you stumble there yourself. There were things I could have easily missed if I didn't just happen to be in the area, and I find that frustrating. It's not the fastest game on the planet, which is no problem when you know where you need to go next, but re-exploring the entire map just to see if anything new popped up is not something that feels good here.- No New Game+ mode that I've found, making it a bit of a slog if you just want to see other endings or mess with a new character without having to complete everything at starting stats. I know there are supposedly cheats you can use; I don't know if this locks you out of achievements or not.Regardless of these gripes, it's clear a lot of love went into this game and I haven't been able to put it down! The world itself really grabbed me as well - the absolute chaos during the events and quests were a blast to experience and kept me looking forward what was coming next. Absolutely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: OK, what you should know before buying this game1. It is pretty hard, but it is FAIR.If you are one millimeter on the platform, you'll not fall, if you have even a slightest chance to hit the enemy, you will hit.First run till good ending took me about 13 hours, and 4 and 3 hours is only for the two difficult castles, but this is very satisfying when you actually make it.2. From the first try you will 90% not get an ultimate ending. Or you can use the guide, of course, but it will spoil some fun.3. Bosses are easy. If you have enough skills to beat the level, boss fight will feel like a walk in a park, every single one of them. 4. Music and secrets just awesome, when i guessed the way to spawn one of the castles or cure the man in a basement, it was great! 5. If you are into retro-platformers, you are risking to become addicted ti this game. Like me. Cause now i am going to play it all over from the start to get ultimate ending!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I only give a positive analysis because there are accessibility options and casual mode, which were necessary for me in order to clear Stormheim Dungeon onwards. The platforming mechanics are VERY clunky with plenty of instadeaths and there are too few save points. If the controls were more polished, then maybe the challenge would be worth. Everything else is good, though!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: It's got all the bells and whistles of a proper side-scrolling ARPG, plus references and nods to a ton of old-school franchises, which I won't spoil here. It's a lot of fun, in a challenging, old-school kind of way. Please check this out when you have the cash and time for some basic metroidvania backtracking!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Great throwback to the days of yore with the NES.  Heavily influenced by games like Castlevania II: Simon's Quest, Contra, and Zelda II: Adventure of Link.  The story is pretty standard but it's good enough to keep you going.  With the addition of a morality system, multiple endings and hidden unlockables, there's plenty of replay-ability to give you good value.Highly recommended for anyone that likes a good challenging platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: It is like you combined Castlevania 2, Metroid, and Megaman. It has the tight controls of Megaman, along with the great soundtrack. It has the exploration of Metroid, and it has the gothic feel of Castlevania. Then it takes it up a notch being more of an adult game. Great play! 10/10 would buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Would very much recommend, a top notch quality game, and after successfully 100%ing all the achievements, I can say it is very challenging and rewarding the all it's endings. If you're a fan of old style games and want a game that will kick your ass but is super rewarding when you turn the tides, play Infernax
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game! Excellent art and music, gameplay was pretty good. I got burnt out before checking out all the possible endings, but I feel I got a satisfying experience out of the endings I did get. It was a bit hard to tell the "morally good" option of a couple of the choices, but if you do a "do whatever I want" unguided first playthrough then you'll have fun either way.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the classic castlevania games then you will LOVE Infernax.It is fantastic!Great homage to classic NES action games with a bunch of elements that add a surprising amount of replayability.I truly cannot stess enough just how good this game is.Don't let the price tag put you off it is more than worth it, you absolutely should buy it RIGHT NOW.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games I 100%'d, and even weeks later I'm still constantly thinking about it. Somehow the RPG elements of this Castlevania-like game really shine through, and your choices matter A LOT which makes the game a whole hell of a lot of fun. The choices have lasting gameplay and story consequences that can evolve into more choices later on too. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: It's Castlevania II, without all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.And I mean that with all the love for Castlevania II, but this is a smooth running, responsive metroidvania game.  You can control yourself in mid air, there's still the fun day/night cycle, the bosses are creative and fun.  The RPG elements are right where they should be for this: basic and in the background.Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 - They clearly understood the assignment.They made what I would consider the perfect game.If you love Castlevania II Simon's Quest and wanted an updated version of it - This is your game. This game literally checked all my boxes, I would personally like to find the developers and pay for hookers and champagne for the lot of them.It has copious amounts of well done 2D gore.The environments are amazing.The game play is nearly perfectThe game is challenging and will have you angry - but you learn how to move forward by trial and error.The boss battles are super neat.Did I mention it has lots of gore???Your character is an absolute BAD ASS.The game has an excellent sense of humor and many Easter eggs pointing back to the source material - Looking at you kneeling by the cliff for 10 seconds. Appears to have multiple endings and new game plus with a bonus feature I won't give away as it was a nice surprise. This is literally in my top 3 favorite games and i'm nearly 40. This is a masterpiece of its genre.Seriously, Devs thanks for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never actually played either Zelda 2 or the pre-Symphony of the Night Castlevanias, but I've seen enough of them to know the kind of gameplay Infernax is referencing. The best way I can describe it is a platform-heavy metroidvania with RPG elements and various ways the story can play out based on your choices. I HAVE however played a much earler game from developer Berzerk Studio: A humble flash game called Homerun in Berzerk Land, back in my Kongregate days.In Infernax, the player takes the role of a war-weary crusader knight named Alcedor, who has returned to his home and fiefdom in the Duchy of Upel, only to find it in the throes of a demonic curse. Beginning with little more then a suit of rusty mail and a stud-less mace, through the lands of Upel and a series of five major dungeons, Alcedor must battle cultists, undead, demons and more in an attempt to cleanse his lands, along the way acquiring new gear and spells, performing quests for the citizenry and being presented with a series of moral decisions that steer the player towards one of a surprising number of endings. Slain enemies award XP and gold. XP can be spent at the Souls-esque save shrines to permanently increase your damage, health or mana, and gold can be spent at various vendors for new equipment, spells and other items. The game uses a unique version of a lives system wherein you can purchase additional maximum lives from some vendors, and they are restored any time you touch a save shrine. Losing a life merely kicks you to the last screen transition you crossed, while losing them all kicks you back the last time you saved, with all progress since lost- including things like major equipment acquisitions and boss fights, so watch yourself. There is an optional "Casual" difficulty that lets you keep some of your XP and gold gains, but that won't help you with the platforming.Which brings me to my biggest complaint about the game. Some of the platforming sections in Infernax are rather more obnoxious then I would like, especially in the fourth dungeon, Kastka Palace, and one extremely annoying acid room in the fifth, Kadjanto Stronghold. Mercifully, it's always possible to leave a dungeon and save outside, say, after collecting a key or upgrade, and save yourself some time and effort if you run out of lives later on. As my playtime would attest, it's doable, and not as frustrating as say, the Plague of Shadows DLC for Shovel Knight, and certainly not like the bonus dungeons in Guacamelee or some ridiculous romhack kaizo game.It's worth exploring as much of Infernax's map as you can, though I could say that about most given metroidvanias. There are a handful of bonus dungeons and out-of-the-way NPCs with additional gear you wouldn't obtain otherwise. This is also necessary to obtain some of the more involved endings. Infernax is a fun 2D action game and certainly more respectful of the player's time then its spiritual forebears, or even other recent retro-platformers. It's technically on the shorter side but feels content-dense regardless- there is no wasted space on the map and you're always doing something towards a specific end. I enjoyed its dark atmosphere, audio design and boss fights. However, the annoying jumps may preclude me from further playthroughs, at least for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is a solid and unique retro offering for the fans of Castlevania-style games. It can be described as a cousin of Simon's Quest if it was actually a good game.In a nutshell:Pros:- Solid gameplay- Surprisingly deep story and choices- Perfect game length- Many endings- Useful difficulty choices- Satisfyingly gory pixel art- Great boss fights- Amazing OSTCons:- Classic difficulty can be way too challenging, especially in dungeons. The game is plenty challenging in Casual mode, make yourself a favor and switch to Casual if you find the game frustrating. - The game makes a fairly bad job at explaining that the choices you make have a deep impact. I recommend you first play the game blindly, but consider doing many runs to get to the different endings. They're worth it.- Fighting monsters can get daunting, but nothing worst that classic 8-bit Castlevania offerings.Awesome game, I'm on my third playthrough and never thought I'd get THIS enamored with Infernax. Can only recommend. Great job Berzerk !
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done retro game that has its roots from castlevania. Amazing gameplay and setting. Only problem is I want even more content with how much I enjoyed it! Its replayability is very particular as the core gameplay is the same but with new characters and different endings. Would wholly recommend this game at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably not going to say anything that others have not.  This game is what the games I grew up with should have been.  Of course, it is made for an adult audience with all of the gore and occasional nudity.  It's full of humor, especially in the form of Easter eggs and inside jokes for the target audience.The team that made this game knew exactly what they were doing and did it well.The only real negative for me was the instant death platforming.  While the game itself isn't truly hard, especially in casual mode, it does have some moments involving spear launchers knocking you into pits of instant death that might result in a gray hair or two.All in all though, it is worth the buy.  It also includes a set of alternate characters which give it some real replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for a splatterfest as you are asked to save the retched people of a land you abandoned for the Crusades. Upon returning home you find that everyone you encounter is asking you to make decisions with minimal context and maximum consequences. However, if you are up for the platforming challenge that only Mario Maker mixed with a Souls game can bring then jump right on into Infernax a pseudo Castlevania 2 clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting to enjoy this game as much as I did.  At the time of writing this, I have clocked in nearly 39 hours.  I've beaten it 7-8 times in the span of days and gotten all achievements.  A lot of developers who try to do a retro-themed, "difficult" game usually just add nonsensical design choices meant more for twitchy, precision platforming.  Infernax can be tough... but seldom ever is it unfair.Imagine Zelda II, but darker, more responsive and even more fun.  Imagine Simon's Quest without the obtuse puzzles, no visual restraint, and the ability to control yourself mid-air.  There's just a lot to like about this game, and, honestly, I can't recommend it enough to someone who wants a solid, action-adventure type with RPG elements, exploration, and multiple ways to play.I only have two complaints.  1st: The game has a morality system that can be tough to figure out, and you have to be all the way good or all the way evil to get the best weapon for your playthrough.  Not entirely a deal breaker, but can be a bit rough when you want to see all the content.  Though that does make the "Free Will Sacrifice" achievement a little tricky.  (Tip: start "good" quests before turning evil so you don't get locked out)  2nd: to hell with the Kastka Palace with its teleporting mages and a myriad of ways to fall down a pit.  Great music though.Also, the soundtrack's pretty stellar.  All right, that's enough praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax does what Simon's Quest wishes it did. Solid platforming and combat with a “mostly” fair difficulty. This game is great in every department. Sound, music, gameplay and control. It also has a karma system which admittedly isn't too deep, however it is better than most because it changes the world around you. You can help a farmer's barn then actually see it get repaired or push out cultists to have access to a new spell. Things like that help in feeling your decisions have an impact on the world around you. I won’t spoil the quest lines but I would highly recommend picking a path and sticking with it. The non ultimate endings are very underwhelming. Thankfully the game is quite short with probably a 3-5 hour play time, plus with the inclusion of cheats allow for a make your own way to play. You also can play 5 different types of characters depending on your name or cheat which won’t drastically change the game play but is welcomed when you want to play it again.The only criticisms I have is I wish you could actually make multiple saves on the same playthrough and not one master save. The game could have had more overworld secrets. There are a few, but more would of added to exploring areas. Another dungeon would be great. And lastly, would've been helpful to get a slight nudge to the player to assist when things are unclear. One of the last dungeons has a very unclear way of using the double jump that I thought I was doing it wrong.All in all, a stellar game worth your time if you like 2D adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Classically styled metroidvania with modern controls and gameplay. What's not to like?The pixel art (especially the 'high-res' cutscene artwork) is masterful. Enemies require unique strategies to dispatch effectively. Tons of spells, abilities and equipment to find, and multiple endings.If you like Metroid, Castlevania, Shovel Knight, etc., then this game is for you.5/5. A masterpiece in retro gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A modern day mix of games of old makes for a pixel art bloody good time. Infernax hits on all of the nostalgia strings while managing to incorporate modern elements to make this game feel like it belongs in this era. Good length and multiple endings gives this game some good longevity to give you enough blood for your buck. Check out my full review here:
