_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania 2 but godlike. Infernax is a beautiful little game where you go around breaking magic seals in castles in order to take down the big bad demon evil at the end. The absolute designs of devil's and being able to thwack skeletons and mob monsters in the open world is a classic exploration style joy. Shhhh don't forget your game wizard codes to for later playthroughs as they make the game even more fun and no I won't spoil the funny antics that come from unlocking things like chainsaw mode. Lastly just remember Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, B, A on the title screen. If you know you know.Absolute treat of a game that I'll be coming back to from time to time to grind out the remaining endings so do yourselves a favor and play Infernax!!!!!!!10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: There are a LOT of interesting gameplay mechanics, and when you've uncovered the various characters and means of playing the game, it's entertaining to say the least. This game has had a lot of love, almost fell away from the eyes of most people ever since the loss of access to Flash games. Sure, there were some workarounds, but this game fell that much deeper behind the veil of legend. And now, here it is!Easy to get into, easy to accidentally into self-destruction, but it's still its own challenge for each playthrough. Normally I don't do evil runs (and I haven't as of yet), but I can be convinced to see every aspect of the game, and all of the means of seeing the 'grey area' ending arcs. The extra lives can be useful, but if you can keep from dropping yourself into pits of spikes/acid/lava/water/youalreadyknow/etc., you can complete it real damn well!I will spoil one single thing in this game, by means of a hint. *Facing towards a cliff looming over a dead cropfield, one may crouch down and observe it, in order to soar into the skies with no fear of falling.* Those of you that know the reference (lookin' at you, Arcade Crew 'n Berzerkers), I think you'll enjoy the end-result.It -can- be distracting or confusing with going in various directions, and not knowing where to go. There was -one- point in the game that I didn't quite know where to go, in order to get further into the game, until I started the basic gaming-troubleshooting, and it pays to LISTEN TO THE NPCs, as the hints aren't exactly telling, but they do help you figure things out, unless you're one of those smert gamers that'll catch on quicker than I do.Absolutely, get this game, absolutely play it as much as you can. Classic mode is the way to go, but sometimes you can do casual, if you wanna throw in some extra challenge for yourself. Also, go do an ultimate casual run with no extra lives, and comment if you manage to do it! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Game is amazing. A real callback to when I was a kid. It's like a mix of castlevania and faxanadu. There's a morality system that generates several different endings, fun easter eggs and references to old classic games, and even a built-in cheat mode so you can skip grinding for money and exp or even go full invincible without tanking your achievements. I saw a friend playing it and I wanted in. I would suggest getting as many endings legitimately as you can stand before you start messing with the cheats and extra characters. Pay attention to the books you get after each ending and they will give you information and cheat codes without having to look them up immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the late 80's to early 90's, when I was in elementary school, video games were naturally the talk of the playground (or the Simpsons if it was Monday morning), and we always bragged about which video games we beat, which video games we loved, and which video games were cool. Among my favorites were Castlevania III and the Legend of Zelda, I could never get enough of either game. Does that mean I despised Castlevania II or Zelda II: The Adventure of Link? Absolutely not, some of my fondest memories are of me screaming at my television screen when the inevitable game over screen popped up, and my father yelling "TURN THE NINTENDO OFF!" at the top of his lungs. I didn't turn off the Nintendo then, and boy am I glad I didn't because lo and behold, here is Infernax, that offers the best call-back to my childhood possible. It also invokes elements of Contra, though to be honest, I may have spoiled too much.Multiple enemies? Check. Two different difficulties? Check. Awesome weapons like a mace, sword, axe, gun, chainsaw? Check. Cheat Codes that remind me of the Game Genie? Check. A wonderful soundtrack that you'll invariably want to buy? Checkmate.If you enjoy cheap shots and getting knocked into bottomless pits and raging at the heavens, this is absolutely the game for you. It's not exceedingly difficult in my opinion, but you'll want to think twice before jumping once in certain portions of the game, lest you have a Deep One knock you off a wheel unexpectedly. The game is rich in exploration, gore, amazing tunes, spells, and much much more. Buy this game, you won't regret it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty awesome throwback you can toss on one monitor while watching stuff on the other monitor. For a single-character playthrough, it'll take 10-12 hours to complete with all items not using any cheats. If you want some pretty cool character unlocks or abilities, go ahead and look up the cheat codes online. Don't feel guilty, either. If you owned an NES or SNES, you'd be reading Nintendo Power for the latest guides, and you'd be rocking a Game Genie to smash that fourth wall.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little platformer metroidvania. One of the highlights of the games I have played recently. Let's open it up a bit.Graphically, it's basically a pixelart game the closely resembles Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest the most. It's nice and colorful and the character design is nicely morbid and bodyhorrorish.The story is simple but it has some branching paths that really surprises you along the way. It's an engaging way to get more playability to the game. There are also secret characters to unlock that vastly differ from the gameplay you were used to so that's fresh also. The sounds and music are awesome. Meaty tunes and nice EXPLOSIONS. Just awesome. This game would be NES hard if the controls weren't so tight. The controlling of the character is easy and responsive. There are few places that are super hard platforming but you'll manage in the end with practice. People were complaining about the map and there is lots of backtracking but if you played the game a bit further I think there would be something to make the backtracking trivial...perhaps. :) I have no huge complains about the game. It's a bit of a short side but high replay value keeps it engaging. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. 5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you like castlevania 2, zelda 2, with some shove a knife up your @$$ music(shovel knight). You'll love this game.It's a really fun metroidvania game that plays like those retro games with decent gameplay, loving care, nice quests, and fun references.It is brutal but in the typical nintendo hard kind of way, and us old retro guys. we liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 8-bit and castlevania then you can't go wrong with this game.It's addicting, fun, has some fun references to older games and it's beautiful to look at.It also has multiple endings for replayability and it's really worth checking out,especially if you're into retro games.I honestly liked it more than shovel knight
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every minute of it.its simple but detailed at the same time, the bosses are great and look amazing.the abilities and upgrades are a pleasure to play with.the Easter eggs are cute and funny.the story is badass.the soundtrack is ROCKIN!Its quite challanging as well so that kept me interested No doubt.The Cheats are really fun too! (Try the Konama Code on the title screen *wink*  *wink*)
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Lite spoilers in this game (just in what content is included but nothing game breaking)This game is solid. Not too long and designed to be played multiple times. (3~4). I beat the game as a Good/ult good knight, evil wiz, non-aligned warrior, repentant knight, and Konami mode for the future run.I would recommend this:1. First playthrough: Knight, Evil/ult evil (mace isn't great as a weapon)2. Warrior: Good/ult good3. Wizard for short playthroughs4. Konami for the future ending and for lols.I found the wizard extremely unrewarding to play. It's the hardest class to survive with and does poor damage. The allure of range attack is lost when it does low damage and requires mana. It was more effective to use Thunder than to spam basic attack. I didn't get to max attack b/c I chose to max mana... it just doesn't work. I spent most of a boss fight waiting for mana to regen before unlocking mana potions which will drain much needed gold from you. I think the wizard needs a higher mana regen rate as you either level up mana or when you get a better weapon. It just sucks... period. Konami dude just washes any reason why the mage exists.I wish profile graphics for non-default player characters were included in all of the story scenes and reactions. Seeing the normal or evil knight when you aren't plaything that sucks. Plus, the other characters don't even get a reaction. Just a static photo much like the npcs. That was a missed opportunity. The cutscene graphic changes would have been nice, but I'm just talking about having a good and evil face change that you get playing the default.Gold gain is frighteningly slow if you don't do quests. For certain runs, it makes sense to wait on doing quests until you understand when to do them or what to do. The extra life is a god send while potions are cool, early game they aren't as valuable as a whole other life.  Lives get replenished at save shrines while pots have to be acquired elsewhere. Speaking of early game, there are areas in the 2 and 3 dungeons that if you aren't playing perfectly are very difficult to try and backtrack to the outside shrine. As the wiz and warrior, I had a few death loops where I was just trying to get a key or key item and get back to the shrine so I wouldn't have to do it all over again or 1-life the entire dungeon (which I couldn't do until much later). There would be the cheap floating eye or axe thrower or something else located strategically by a pit that no matter how well I battled, I would inevitably die there. I get that it's nostagic, but some characters don't have a solid ranged option to deal with that and you have to hope your timing is flawless.The bosses are easy (most people are saying this). The boss that you have to attack the tongue, that was needlessly drown out... I think the most interesting bits were the ult good/evil raids. I wanted more of that. The Ult Evil raid was the most challenging aspect of the game. The ult good version really needs a bump in difficulty, especially given what the cult can do.I'm satisfied with my purchase. This peeled me away from Elden Ring. I've recommended it to my friends. Definitely a good amount of time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A whole lot of fun. One of those rare games that sucked me in to the point I felt I needed to get all the achievements just to see the story beats; don't regret the time spent for a second. Even after seeing everything, the combat is tightly built enough that doing further runs has been possible, just playing around, sequence breaking, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax plays like an old school metroidvania style game.  When I say old school I mean things like experiencing knock back when getting hit, dying when falling in water/lava, etc..  I've completed my first play through on classic mode and really enjoyed it.  Since beating it I've looked online and there are multiple endings and more things for me to unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Got recommend this game by Lythero and extremely glad they did! Usually I am not interested in these sort of brutal old school platformers, but the charm of this one really hooked me, especially after completing the game for the first time, leaving me with only very minor gripes with the game. This is also the first game I have ever played that actually made me want to 100% complete the game! After my first completion I wanted to learn more about the story and after 50 hours I managed to achieve that. I enjoyed it so much I am now working on the 100% speedrun for the game haha :DThank you devs for all the little attention to details in the game, as well as your show of interest in the speedrun community for the game. Has been a great experience overall so far and I highly recommend <3
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game answers the question of "What if Zelda2/Cvania2 had been refined?" and then slams a demons face against the corner of a table exploding in blood. Infernax wears it's inspiration like a badge of honor and adds in a morality system, multi endings, multiple playable characters and great sprite work to be a contender for best indie game. Very challenging with lots of quick (sometimes unfair) deaths and very speed-runner friendly set ups to rooms that will drive you to get all the endings. I cannot stress any more that this is a must play game of 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: A *really* good metroidvania in general even if you don't like the retro themes, but if you do theres a handful of easter eggs and references to Simon's Quest and other games in the genre from that era, the art is fantastic and the controls are smooth. My only real complaint is that some enemies should not have contact damage (flying enemies that just shoot stuff) and other enemies can spam a ranged attack so fast you cant really do anything about it without leaving agro range and hope the reset changed their pattern
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this nostlagic trip back to Simons Quest, but done good. The Easter Eggs and secrets really add a lot to the game and it was a really pleasant experience.But fair warning, it has some tough platforming sections and really hard Boss fights, especially if you take alternate routes.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every detail of this game. It's like a blend between Castlevania and Zelda 2. The story is fine, the gameplay feels pretty good, the progression and game balance are just perfect for this game and the art is beautiful. You can tell when something is made with love and passion, and this game is one of those.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game buuuuut there were problems. If you want to see all the bosses in this game will take at least 2 full runs, if not 3. The game has multiple choices where if you don't choose right every. single. time. you lock your save file from being able to see the true ending.I hate this so much, and it ruined wanting to play again. That said I enjoyed what time I did spend on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Notes: It may not look like it from the trailers, but the last three dungeons require a good bit of parkour. It is certainly possible, just know that ahead of time. As for the combat difficulty, every boss is very fair and can often be beaten first try if you take your time. There are spells to use as well but you don't get a ton of mana, so you won't be spamming spells. I mostly used spells for utility and healing instead of offense.Also, the game is only 7-10 hours long, but there are multiple endings that give a unique narrative so the game is very much replayable. There are a lot of "Choose A or B, but if you choose A you can't get B until another playthrough" decisionsThings I liked:The music, map design, the villages/npcs are charming, progression (enemies don't get OP super fast), bosses, and the branching narrative paths for each endingThings I disliked: When you hit water/lava/acid, you immediately die. Life lost, go back to the start of the room. This can be infuriating in some cases because if an enemy or projectile hits you while midair, you go into free fall. This makes some parkour sections feel very tedious.As for bugs? Didn't encounter any
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Play Infernax. Just do it. They took the graphics and sound of an NES Castlevania, made it a Metroidvania, and combined it with the leveling of LOZ II. Quests, sidequests and the option for good or bad playthroughs don't hurt either. It's the best parts of Castlevania and LOZ II combined in the best ways, with some modern flavor added in as well. Good combat, fulfilling progression, multiple endings and good music. And  all of the achievements are named after heavy metal songs. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun mix between Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2. Overall worth your time if you enjoy casually brutal games and Castlevania gameplay. The gameplay is reasonably fun but be warned that you will be going through the same rooms many times with little changing.The difficulty is both a nice challenge and an unfortunate aspect of the game. As you progress through dungeons you may find yourself wanting to exit the dungeon and save just to keep the key or ability you spent time and health getting so an unfortunate death doesn't make you replay that section yet another time. Ultimately there are an unfortunate number of instant deaths in this game that just eat at your progress.This game is still worth your time if you aren't terribly put off by the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, combines tight action platforming in a light metroidvania with a simple but rewarding combat system tying it all together. Although short, Infernax really makes the most of it's tight (yet still engaging) environment, gritty 8 bit graphics, and simple but dynamic story to create an incredibly rich and immersive experience. Can play a good guy or a bad guy, and watch the world flourish, or recoil in accordance to your actions and decisions. This game really makes me wonder at the possibilities if other games from the 80s and 90s had the level of freedom and immersion this does. Truly a masterpiece, I really want to continue to explore the world of infernax, slaying demons, time traveling, and uncovering all the incredibly well thought out design of this game. PLEASE, make a DLC, this is fast becoming my favorite game, and would love to see it expanded on! Cannot recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Yet anoher neo-retro metroidvania, this time with a big dose of Simon's Quest, a whiff of Zelda 2 and, as an additional twist, real choices to be made, impacting your environment to varying degree and leading you to one of the four possible endings.Add-in some inventive boss design, acidic humor and built-in cheats to enrich subsequent playthroughs, and you've got a winner, well worth of the ~8 hours you'll need to see it to the end the first time around.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Great little Castlevania 2 / Zelda 2 / Faxandu hommage with good controls and enjoyable gameplay. Nice soundtrack! Also, the game doesn't overstay its welcome, something I always like! But you can get some more playtime out of it by playing the multiple paths/endings (if you want to). I'd say the casula mode is doable even for people who don't usually enjoy "NES-hard" games. I enjoyed this game very much. 8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely worth the premium over other Simon's Quest-likes. Trust me, I've tried several other, cheaper ones, including one or two that aren't much cheaper, and they're all far from great at best. This one, though, has great dialogue, great graphics, great music, and some of the best gameplay in this type of game though some attacks can be finicky.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.  This game is basically a love letter to the old school Castlevania (More the Metroidvania type) games but with some modern conveniences.  It's hard but not "Nintendo Hard".  There are so many easter eggs and details put into the game you can tell the developers really love this style of game and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny.   Wife and I loved the Castlevania references such as "wall chicken"  I laughed out loud for a good minute with that one.The only complaints I really had: Enemies with ranged attacks will spam them continously  "Axe throwers" as example.Teleport mobs can go outside the room your in and still shoot in..  The platforming in the almost end dungeons ramps up, but the LAST true dungeon gets ruthless between platforming and enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Slight spoilersIt's a really, really solid game! The game play is very satisfying plays like Castlevania and Zelda II in many ways. The only slight gripe I have is with getting the ""true ending"" but even then it just depends on if you are OK with replaying the game multiple times or not. If so I would easily recommend the game as the reward is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Great game in the vein of Castlevania II, Zelda II, and Faxanadu.  This game is a love letter to those classic games.  A lot of tricky platforming with falls to your death.  Combat gets fairly easy by the end, platforming is more likely to kill you further in.  A lot of people complain about the up-jump attack being janky, I had no issues with it, playing on keyboard.  I rarely failed to pull it off, I was more likely to die from failing a jump in some other way than not having that attack go off.  If all else fails, there are cheats you can use to make certain things easier.  Or some just for fun, like over-the-top gore mode.  Certain things about the game may not be to everyones tastes, but this game nails what it set out to be.  It is exactly what I expected it to be and I loved every minute of it.

Sad its so small :(:( I want more lore !:DReplay value (hell ya!) I cant say how many times I said .. ah man if only I would ove chosen differently.Will definitely play around the world once more for sure!Thx for making this awesome gem Berzerk Studio and hope you will make many more entry! :D:D:DCheers!

_childDocuments_.review: I cautiously recommend this game. First impressions are great as you're introduced to this brutal world with choices that have meaningful outcomes and they mostly due, dialogue reacts to you different based on choices you make, and your actions have consequences, something not common for this genre. For me where it falls flat is subsequent playthroughs as the game ask you to beat it multiple times to get all the endings, and honestly, after 1 and a half playthroughs im kinda burnt out on it. Especially since there's no new game + to speak off where you can mostly breeze through enemies to rush through the game, there are cheats invincibility and infinite jumping, but it doesn't change the fact that you have to grind EXP and go through all the dungeons to get each power up and defeat each of the 5 bosses AGAIN to get an ending. For the first playthrough the game is great, every playthrough after that, idk, pace yourself ig.

_childDocuments_.review: Music 10/10.Difficulty starts out decent at 6/10 but you quickly become overpowered and the difficulty goes to 2/10.Combat is very simplistic, you swing your mace left or right, block with your shield, jump, duck and cast a spell every 3 minutes or so. :PThe RP element is a bit light for my taste, but it does increase replayability.Fairly small map, tiny dungeons, inconsistent hitboxes and a fairly linear progression.Overall i still enjoyed this game alot more than i expected :DTotal 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: What a little gem of a game!  A great revisit to what was great about games like Castlevania 2 and Faxanadu without all the frustrating issues and poor play control. The game has several endings, and you'll want to unlock them to find them all.  If you like a challenge, still play on casual mode.  Casual mode just includes more save points.  Trust me, there is nothing fun about redoing progress.  You'll still have a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: Infernax is an outstanding game that pays great homage to the games of yesteryear, such as Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link. _childDocuments_.review: Good retro platformer action, I appreciate all the small touches that pay tribute to Zelda 2 and Simon's Quest. _childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Zelda 2-esque style game with the same leveling system. Open world like simon's quest with eventua fast travel. Multiple endings, good vs evil playthrough, secret ending etc. Music is good, controls are responsive, monster variety is okay, dungeons are similar to Zelda 2. Saving can be obnoxious as it forces you to backtrack heavily if you want to save progress during dungeon. One shot pit are meh but it's very nes/snes era like so be aware. I recommend to people who like old platformers, with no checkpoints, progress loss and the whole package. It is a nostalgia trip.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Castlevania 2: Simon's Quest and Splatterhouse had a baby, but that baby completely overshadowed its parents and went on to become a successful entrepreneur. Brutal classic era platformer with great visuals and music and tight gameplay. Absolutely worth the price, but PREPARE TO DIE A LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: Great so far. Difficult at some points, but feels fair. If you want more save points, the game also allows for casual difficulty (not my cup of tea though).Is it worth the price tag? As early as now I'd say yes. You get more than your money's worth of enjoyment if you're the same type of player as me.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid level design and platforming. Enjoyable exploration and progression.  The art is very good as well.  Difficulty of platforming and normal enemies is moderately high.  Expect to game over numerous times.  Bosses are actually quite easy.  I never died to one until the very final boss (Who killed me in two hits). Has several routes determined by the choices you make through the game. I got a mediocre "good" ending by not choosing absolutely every obvious "good" choice, which seems like it just has less content than going pure good or pure evil.  So there's replayability there, but I recommend just focusing on one side or the other per run.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Finished my ultimate good run.  Really like this game, highly reccomend it if youre looking for an old retro style castlevania 2 like game.  There is enough differences to make me want to play my ultimate evil tomorrow night!  EDIT:  Took me just over 17 hours to 100%, and I think a few extra hours are on there because you can miss one particular trophy on your ultimate good run, which made me do another whole run.  I love the game wizard codes, and the fact that they dont stop you from getting achievements,  I was able to tackle most of the game on classic mode, once I decided I wanted the achievements I just turned on a couple codes and ran through it hella fast.  I suppose if I had one gripe about it, it would be that I thought it was going to be a bit harder.  I even made it far more difficult for myself, as I wanted to keep my "lives" so anytime I died I would do a save reload to keep my life.  Until I found out the save statues just replenish them anyways.  Music and gameplay are awesome, graphics are the style I like, almost a good 20 hours from an indie game is pretty solid, could have been harder. 9/10 would play the sequel, and will follow this developer for more gems like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Review is based on a first-time blind playthrough. It's very fun and designed well. I missed stuff, blindly did (and failed probably) some side quests and it ran me about 6 hours, but it was a good 6 hours. The side quests aren't generic and give interesting rewards, and I can tell there's a ton of variety that any one playthrough can have. I definitely plan on doing multiple playthroughs and getting all the achievements. If you watch trailers or something and think you might be interested in this game I recommend it for sure. Have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple yet challenging. As other reviews have said already, it has a castlevania'esc feel to it. Kill and acquire experience to strengthen your character and collect gold along the way to buy further support items. Its pretty straight forward but very well put together for a smooth feel, I especially appreciated the various cutscenes and good or evil event choices. Pixels like old nintendo and music that compliments for that good nostalgia play. This game is definitely worth a playthrough or two!
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, yes, yes.  LOVE this game.  I've been watching and waiting for this game to drop for some time now, and I'm happy to say I'm not disappointed in the least.  It has the NES look, feel and difficulty that I was really hoping it would have.  Basically, you take Castlevania 2 and Zelda 2, squash them together and you get Infernax.  Day/night cycle and vibe of CV2, leveling/RPG and combat mechanics of Z2, exploration aspect of both and other misc parts of those games thrown in for good measure.  Movement and combat feel very good and the difficulty is at a good level (not easy, but also not unfair)The decisions you have to make are really quite interesting.  It's not the typical "be good and all the good stuff will happen".  There are serious and sometimes negative consequences (increase in difficulty or missing out on something) for choosing the good path (like real life).  I won't say anything beyond that, but I really like the mechanic, even though it hurts sometimes.I only have a little time on Steam so far, but I've played quite a bit more already on Xbox via Game Pass.  Love it so much I had to support the devs and actually buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: Imagen if Castlevania 2: Simons Quest and Legend of Zelda 2: Links Adventure were combined and made using modern day design principles. A challenging, straight forward 2d action platformer that wear its influences on it sleeves while adding new features to the mix. Highly recommended to support a one man dev team making his fun dream game.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not leaving a negative review because the game has a lot going on for it , but I felt like the most important aspect - combat - was rather underwhelming. I'm used to classic Castlevanias and other retro games, and no matter how simple the core gameplay is, they compensate for it with creative enemy attack patterns and challenging AI behavior. Infernax didn't give me the feel of being challenged when walking through the levels or even fighting bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Infernax

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game initially from a Twitter post and then I saw one of my favorite Twitch streamers Retro Island Gaming (Macaw45 later in the day too) was playing this when I woke up. The game looked cool, and the controls seemed tight, and the mechanics appeared sound. I bought it and I’m having a blast. I have nothing really to pick apart about this game at all except maybe a harder mode. I’m not a stickler for difficulty, in fact I like accessibility in games BUT I want an extra challenge to this game. Maybe a mode where you can’t take any hits, one hit death. Something to really test your reactions. But besides that, this game is just solid through and through.

name: Borderlands 3
detailed_description: Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box This title is included in Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box! Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition is the quintessential Borderlands 3 experience, featuring the base game plus all 6 content add-ons and the full collection of bonus cosmetic packs! Borderlands 3 Super Deluxe Edition Continue your Borderlands 3 adventure with the Season Pass! This content is included with purchase of the Borderlands 3 Super Deluxe Edition, Borderlands 3 Ultimate Edition, and Borderlands 3 Collector's Edition. The Season Pass includes: Moxxi’s Heist of the Handsome Jackpot campaign add-on. Guns, Love, and Tentacles campaign add-on. Bounty of Blood campaign add-on. Psycho Krieg and the Fantastic Fustercluck campaign add-on. All 4 Multiverse Final Form Cosmetic Packs. A Butt Stallion weapon skin, weapon trinket and grenade mod. About the Game The original shooter-looter returns, packing bazillions of guns and an all-new mayhem-fueled adventure! Blast through new worlds and enemies as one of four brand new Vault Hunters – the ultimate treasure-seeking badasses of the Borderlands, each with deep skill trees, abilities, and customization. Play solo or join with friends to take on insane enemies, score loads of loot and save your home from the most ruthless cult leaders in the galaxy. A MAYHEM-FUELED THRILL RIDE Stop the fanatical Calypso Twins from uniting the bandit clans and claiming the galaxy’s ultimate power. Only you, a thrill-seeking Vault Hunter, have the arsenal and allies to take them down. YOUR VAULT HUNTER, YOUR PLAYSTYLE Become one of four extraordinary Vault Hunters, each with unique abilities, playstyles, deep skill trees, and tons of personalization options. All Vault Hunters are capable of awesome mayhem alone, but together they are unstoppable. LOCK, LOAD, AND LOOT With bazillions of guns and gadgets, every fight is an opportunity to score new gear. Firearms with self-propelling bullet shields? Check. Rifles that spawn fire-spewing volcanoes? Obviously. Guns that grow legs and chase down enemies while hurling verbal insults? Yeah, got that too. NEW BORDERLANDS Discover new worlds beyond Pandora, each featuring unique environments to explore and enemies to destroy. Tear through hostile deserts, battle your way across war-torn cityscapes, navigate deadly bayous, and more! QUICK & SEAMLESS CO-OP ACTION Play with anyone at any time with online co-op, regardless of your level or mission progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3: A Phenomenal Evolution in the Realm of Loony, Loot-Fueled ActionBorderlands 3 is nothing short of a gaming marvel, a triumphant return to Pandora that stands as a shining example of the pinnacle of cooperative loot-shooting action. Developed by Gearbox Software, this third installment in the beloved Borderlands series not only honors its roots but elevates them to new heights with a staggering array of enhancements, innovations, and sheer exuberant fun. If you thought the franchise had already peaked, prepare to be amazed—Borderlands 3 redefines the very essence of what makes a loot-shooter extraordinary.From the very start, Borderlands 3 immerses you in a world that is as visually stunning as it is richly detailed. The game’s art style remains true to the series’ distinctive cel-shaded aesthetic, but it has been refined and expanded to create an even more vibrant and dynamic experience. The diverse environments you’ll explore—from the bustling, futuristic cityscapes of Neon Arterial to the lush, perilous jungles of Eden-6—are beautifully rendered, each brimming with character, life, and a sense of boundless adventure. The level of detail in these environments is nothing short of remarkable, making every moment of exploration a visual feast.The narrative in Borderlands 3 is a tour de force of storytelling, blending the series’ signature humor with an engaging, action-packed plot. The game introduces players to the Calypso Twins, Tyreen and Typhon, who bring a new level of charisma and menace as they seek to harness the power of the mysterious Vaults for their own nefarious purposes. The narrative is not only driven by thrilling set pieces and intense confrontations but also enriched by moments of genuine emotion and character development. The interplay between the charismatic characters, including the returning heroes and new faces like the lovable but troubled Vault Hunters, creates a story that is both epic in scope and deeply personal.Speaking of Vault Hunters, the new roster in Borderlands 3 is an absolute triumph. The four new characters—Moze, Amara, Zane, and FL4K—each bring their unique abilities, playstyles, and personalities to the table, offering players an unprecedented level of choice and customization. Whether you prefer Moze’s explosive mech-based combat, Amara’s mystic siren powers, Zane’s versatile gadgets, or FL4K’s beastly companions, there is a Vault Hunter for every playstyle. The depth of the skill trees and the myriad of customization options allow for a highly personalized experience, ensuring that every player can tailor their character to fit their preferred strategy and playstyle.The gameplay mechanics in Borderlands 3 are a masterclass in refinement and innovation. The shooting mechanics are as satisfying and fluid as ever, with a vast arsenal of weapons that are both diverse and delightfully over-the-top. The game introduces a host of new weapon types, each with their own unique effects and attributes, adding an extra layer of excitement and strategy to combat. The loot system is more rewarding and varied than ever before, with an astonishing array of guns, grenades, and gear that cater to different playstyles and tactics. The thrill of discovering a rare weapon or a perfect piece of equipment is a key highlight of the game, driving players to explore every nook and cranny of Pandora.One of the standout features of Borderlands 3 is its expansive open world. The game’s maps are larger, more detailed, and more varied than ever before, offering players a rich tapestry of environments to explore. Each region is filled with hidden secrets, challenging enemies, and dynamic quests that keep the gameplay fresh and engaging. The game’s quest design strikes a perfect balance between narrative-driven missions and optional side quests, providing a wealth of content that encourages players to dive deep into the world of Pandora.Cooperative play is where Borderlands 3 truly shines. The game’s co-op mode allows up to four players to team up and tackle the campaign together, adding a new layer of strategy and fun. The seamless integration of cooperative play means that friends can easily join forces, share loot, and strategize together to overcome tougher challenges. The cooperative experience is enhanced by the game’s robust matchmaking system and the ability to seamlessly drop in and out of sessions, making it easy to enjoy the game with friends regardless of their schedule.Sound design and music in Borderlands 3 are equally impressive. The soundtrack features an eclectic mix of tracks that perfectly capture the game’s frenetic energy and diverse settings. The voice acting is exceptional, with performances that bring the characters to life and enhance the game’s humor and emotional depth. The sound effects—from the explosive impacts of gunfire to the satisfying crunch of critical hits—add to the immersive experience, making every moment of combat feel intense and impactful.The attention to detail in Borderlands 3 is nothing short of extraordinary. The game’s environmental storytelling, from the derelict remnants of past civilizations to the vibrant, bustling cities, creates a world that feels both expansive and intricately connected. The character interactions, dialogue, and lore are rich and engaging, adding depth to the narrative and making the world of Pandora feel alive and vibrant.In summary, Borderlands 3 is a monumental achievement in the realm of first-person shooters and cooperative gaming. It’s a game that excels in every aspect, from its breathtaking visuals and captivating narrative to its innovative gameplay and extensive replayability. Gearbox Software has created a world that is both expansive and intimately engaging, filled with humor, excitement, and endless possibilities. Borderlands 3 is not just a game; it’s an experience that captures the very essence of what makes gaming so thrilling and rewarding.For anyone seeking a game that offers a perfect blend of action, humor, and adventure, Borderlands 3 is an absolute must-play. It stands as a testament to the creativity and passion of its developers and a shining example of the heights that video games can achieve. Whether you’re a longtime fan of the series or new to the world of Pandora, Borderlands 3 promises an unforgettable journey that will leave you eagerly anticipating your next adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER ALERT! Enjoyable and addictive looter shooter. If you are familiar with the borderlands franchise and can appreciate the humor, this is just more of the same!Story / writingThe story more or less continues after the ending of borderlands 2. You are, yet again a vault hunter and stumble upon a 'baddy'. The twins are super annoying and I think the developers tried to achieve this (perfectly hitting their mark). I couldn't wait to just annihilate these irritating brats. The overall progression of the story was thorough and well connected at first, but after a while it all blended down to 'go there and fetch this'. Small plot-twists aside, I couldn't look away from this glaring problem. For a (possible?) next installment, I would either try the flush the story out a bit more, or change the progression altogether. 6.5/10GameplayIT'S BORDERLANDS, WHAT DO YOU WANT? Run, Shoot, Loot. Repeat for 70 hours.Ok but seriously. Jumping in, it felt exactly the same as Borderlands 2 and the pre-sequel, which isn't to say it was bad, because that formula was already more or less on point. Small additions, such as the selectable firing modes add a little bit extra compared to the older installments, but for the rest everything felt the same. Driving was still sh** and quests were varying (in context, not in actions) and amusing. 7.5/10Graphics / styling artBorderlands. New edition. Either you like it, either you don't. I like it. 8/10Sound designNothing much to say. The sounds during metaplay are nothing fancy, but they get the job done. During significant story-progressing quests however, the choice of music and vibe is absolutely spot-on It think the contrast between these two deserves 2 different scores: Standard 5/10 & milestone quests 8/10The lootI am a bit dissapointed in the variety and more importantly lack of mutations of loot. Yes there are a ton of different weapons, but everything eventually boils down to the same selection of weapon classes and classes within these classes. When receiving legendary loot there could be the one or 2 odd ones, but I want weapons that are out of place, crazy, unpractical, overpowered and underpowered at the same time, ... I remember in Borderlands 2 a legendary gun that was really good, kept it for a long time. But everytime you fired it, it kept screeming at the top of it's lungs. Loved it!. Another one started cursing everytime you hit an enemy... This isn't to say the loot is not satisfying, but I found myself doing the same routine over and over again for 70+ hours: Find a good epic/legendary, kill every f***ing living thing, loot and sell absolutely everything. Repeat step one and there you go. A bit lackluster... 6/10AftermathNot really a tangible thing to score a game on, but a very important characteristic for me. After finishing (having done most of the sidequests beforehand), I did not feel empty or sad that the story had ended. I did not really feel the desire to continue playing or start everything over again (which is the thing with borderlands, having game+ mode in its 'mayhem' modes). I just concluded that I enjoyed it, watched the end credits and reminisced of my fun time with the whole franchise. A bit dissapointing, because I like to get emotionally attached to games, but yeah, wasn't really able to. Only the final cutscene, where you-know-who goes to you-know-where and every character you encountered is watching, that got to me. +1 for that. Still, won't come back anytime soon I think. 6.5/10Overall scoreThis is still an enjoyable game, you can start this franchise here if neccessary (Although I recommend starting with BL1). Don't expect the best or most emotional story, but more a stable, well constructed looter-shooter with good and specific humour, that doens't take itself too seriously. Picking this up when anything under €25 is a good buy. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start this review with something I said partway through the Eden-6 planet, "I wanna hang out with the gay couple" to me Hammerlock and Wainwright were characters that I cared about completely and I feel that way about almost every character on Eden-6 but I will get into characters later.To me Borderlands 3 when it was announced was something to be hopeful for a new Borderlands game 5 years after Pre-Sequel I guess you could say put the game on hiatus although after playing 3 I regret how harsh I used to be on P-S.Pros: Gameplay as always is excellent a Borderlands game would utterly fail if the killing dudes with bigger, better and more outrageous guns wasn't satisfying or fun to do but as always BL is able to pull this off. Exploration is fun to do just block out what you are doing and just explore the world around you to your hearts content and the world is of course bigger than ever with multiple planets to discover new things to shoot and new things to shoot them with.Hammerlock, Wainwright and Clay are the best characters you will meet in this game their dialogue is nothing short of amazing and personally I was surprised that these 3 characters are the most well written and fun to interact with, with Wainwright and Hammerlock being cute together and Clay being a people person.Cons: The story for this game is awful not once did I care what my objective was nor did I care about our cast of "characters" the only exception to this was doing pretty much anything on Eden-6 except for the Balex quest.Characters: Lilith to me always just seemed somewhat bored and tired to me throughout the story she no longer seemed like the badass she was in BL2 who was capable of standing on her own now she is basically "Leader of Crimson Raiders and barely participates or does anything cool" which you can attribute to the fact that she loses her powers but even then she still seems pathetic which I feel is a bit of a disservice to her as someone who had always held their own and at least to me was the best character to play as in 1The Calypso twins were not intimidating and were mainly just irritating but not in a good way and I feel like their goals were kind of confusing like they left to open the great vault and then were like "lmao lets be gods instead who cares about character goals" maybe it was on a tape but I just didn't care enough to find it.Ava is a character who didn't deserve to get anything she should have been written in as a joke character rather than a main one, she is written to be a stupid teen who barely understands how the world works and yet in the end she gains everything I would even argue she is the reason that Maya dies to Troy, yet she apparently with the dumb advice from Maya on "running towards the fire" is enough to spur Lilith back into action even though by the end of commander Lilith & the fight for sanctuary she proves herself to be a leader worthy of leading the crimson raiders yet she needs to be lectured by some random character who she probably has only known of at the very least a day, I understand Lilith would have been devastated by Maya's death but she wouldn't listen to Ava, and even though Ava hasn't proved herself at all she is shoehorned in and becomes the leader of the Crimson Raiders, not you the player character, not Tannis (who is also magically a siren even though all lore prior to BL3 was done so that you must be born a siren you don't just become one), and she also sidelines her friends for Ava a character who hadn't even done anything to prove herself as leader material, if Ava had been written better maybe I would have liked her but she was written so poorly. Playable characters: I will only talk about the one character I played as since his abilities were the most interesting and I cannot care to replay the game to play as the others and thus enters Zane Flynt. His abilities are to summon a Digi-Clone of himself which acts in a similar way to the Holo-Jack ability in Pre-Sequel drawing enemy fire as well as firing at enemies, but Zane also gets an added ability to be able to switch places with his clone which can cause fun scenarios in which you just keep switching and shooting a boss to avoid a majority of damage. Zane also has the ability to place down a shield that he can either wear upon himself or leave on the ground for his teammates, and a drone which attacks enemies. His play style with the digi-clone reminds me somewhat of Timothy from Pre-Sequel which is what initially drew me to him, if you enjoy the idea of switching places with a clone and using a shield for either yourself or to help the team then I would say pick Zane however his dialogue can get really boring when in fights, I have heard him mention his middle name being Ferocity so many times that it got grating to the point I was thinking of turning off voices and only leaving subtitles on, other than that he was alright he wasn't as memorable as the other playable character for me but he was pretty decent.The only time you should really purchase this game is when it is on sale and even then you should really have some friends to play with you so you can just make fun of pretty much everything in this game otherwise you will pretty much find this game to be an uninteresting mess of failed ideas, as my friend said to me when I got the game "When we play together just never think of this game as a Borderlands game"  I feel like that statement sadly rings all too true for this game and if this is what we have for the future of non DLC Borderlands then the franchise might be better off ending.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 8 10 4 8You would think that for being a looter-shooter Borderlands 3 would lack in terms of story or character development but it is the complete opposite, Gearbox shows once again how much they focus on world building and creating memorable characters.We don't have Handsome Jack as the main villain anymore, nevertheless, Gearbox has an ace up their sleeve (or should I say... two aces). I'm talking about the Calypso twins, two real scoundrels that make their appearance through most of the campaign. As usual, there is one of them who carries the voice of command and in this ocassion it is one Tyreen Calypso. Her brother (Troy Calypso) is a sacrifice in order for her to shine, she even refers to him as the parasite, she posesses great spark and wits which makes her a great villain.More than the campaign itself, the most interesting part is what we do during the journey, the exploration feels way better with the addition of collectibles and it's a nice touch to put some secondary missions near the main ones so we can increase our experience points and score some sweet loot while not having to leave our main goal behind.The game is really long, when you think you're reaching the end they show you that you're not even close to it and that's a good thing if you know how to keep the player entertained, and Borderlands 3 does just that, some of the objectives in missions can be stupid but that's the whole point, this game doesn't take itself seriously most of the times and the person who benefits from this the most is the player.I'll be honest, everything related to the story, how charismatic the characters can be is something that gives the franchise a lot of personality but it is not the most important part. As you might think, the most relevant part is the shooting and as a looter-shooter that is where most of the work should be put into.This franchise hasn't been exactly "nailing" the handling of weapons, aiming, recoil, etc. Borderlands 3 learned from the past and improved every single little aspect about it, making this a solid shooter that holds up to the rest.They have also improved our character's overall agility, adding slide and climbing mechanics makes the combat feel more fluid and makes you be constantly on the move when fighting almost without you realizing it, everything feels smooth and fun.Another addition is also the secondary fire mode that some weapons have and that you will learn about in the beginning of the game, this can turn the 4 weapons that we usually have into 8, a rifle could be used as a shotgun, a pistol could fire rockets as well as regular bullets, etc.Of course not everything is great, during our constant fights we will see very noticeable mistakes in the AI, some of them not even noticing you while being right next to them, this is compensated with huge amounts of enemies on the screen but I think that for a title this big this should be fixed.In the beginning of our adventure we will pick between Amara, Fl4k, Zane and Moze, each with their roles, Siren, Beastmaster, Operative and Gunner, respectively. Like always every role is different from one another but even more so in this title.Just like in previous releases the level cap is 50 (57 after DLC and it might be increased even more after the rest of them come out) with every level gained we get a skill point that we can spend on new abilities or in increasing the power of a skill we already have.Each character offers a decent amount of specializations and we can always respec our abilities and switch class mods to change playstyle if we ever feel like it. The game also contains cosmetic items that are all earned in-game by collecting eridium and trading it with Crazy Earl, some of the cosmetics can also be dropped by random enemies or bosses.Like I mentioned above, there's a huge variety of weapons in this game, to highlight some of the differences with Borderlands 2, not all Tediore weapons explode when thrown, some can turn into turrets and chase down enemies, there's a brand new type of weapon that consists of an overheating system instead of reloading, every weapon also has an overall score so we can see if it's really worth replacing one weapon for another.Borderlands 3 also introduces a new element, Radiation, and gets rid of slag damage from its predecessor. Radiation damage has a DOT effect and it also damages enemies around an irradiated target, this allows us to chain kills and overall feel more enjoyable than slag.We also have a "faction" system, there's many different manufacturers of weapons and the more we use a certain brand the more we can increase this loyalty with them, this allows us to get rare improved weapons from our favorite manufacturer.Once we're done with the campaign we can start with New Game+ and the new difficulty settings called Mayhem Mode, as you can imagine this mode offers a greater challenge with enemies having a greater amount of health and dealing more damage, with this comes a set of legendary weapons that can only drop when playing in this mode.Borderlands 3 has an infinite amount of good things. From the amazing shooting mechanics to the great homage to the old fans with many familiar faces from previous games making an appearance. We can only imagine what Gearbox could have done in all this time if they focused a little bit more in innovating or in making a more memorable endgame, nevertheless, Borderlands 3 is still a must-have.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say this game is as good as it's predecessors, buuuuutttt.... well, not so much. As far as game play goes, it's still quite close to Borderlands 2 and the Pre-sequel. I have very little issue there. Where it falls flat is in the humor, story and acting departments. The jokes are seemingly non-existent, or flatly juvenile without any trace of cleverness. ( Sorry, but all the torgue guns being named some euphemism for a ♥♥♥♥ isn't up to par. ). The storyline is pretty thin, even by shoot 'em up standards and the characters feel like hollow shells of themselves, particularly if you got into the character development that happened in some of the DLC from Borderlands 2. So, what's the cause of this would you say? Probably the fact that Borderlands 3 is set across an entire galaxy instead of a single planet, but still within a 60 hour game. In all total honesty, I think Gearbox and 2k screwed up on this one. They could have kept the cash cow going for at least one more game without us getting tired of the same planet-wide stakes if they'd delivered the same comedy, decent (again, for a shoot 'em up) plot and characters you genuinely find yourself enjoying (If you haven't played the Tiny Tina DLC for BL2, you missed what GOOD juvenile comedy looks like.) The fact is, there's a lot here for potential but they just tried to cram too much into too small of a plotline and run-time, and well... that's how you get mediocre results. Long story short, for a series that refreshed the shoot 'em up genre to remind us that it is possible to have an enjoyable plot while you explode bandits, and had such noteworthy story-telling episodes as "Tales From the Borderlands", this one fell flat on it's face and didn't begin to live up to it's elders. Unless you're really only into turning psychos into meat bicycles, then you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game expecting it to follow in the BL2 format to some extent, but it did change quite a lot (for better and for worse).The good: Aside for how it looks, the new character mechanics are a really good expansion on the pre-existing leveling system. Getting you character's habilities on the very first level just makes more sense. The guns and gun system have been improved and expanded. The story, although I've played for just shy of 2 hours, is quite interesting, loved the development of Sir Hammerlockm, Timmothy, and Krieg.The bad: This game has been severely dumbed down. Just from the get-go you are prompted to select either easy or normal, which is a first for the series. I know that most of the lines have been presented in a sarcastic way in most of the games, but this is just cartoon levels of sarcasm that gets annoying really fast. And the worst detail of them all, if you take more than 10 seconds to do any puzzle, you'll get reminded of your objective some 5 times, and then the NPC that gives you the mission will just outright give you the answer to the puzzle. It really just treats you as if you worked for IGN and had a fresh 1950s lobotomy.Just thinking of who are the main antagonists gives you a headache. _childDocuments_.review: It's very good in some ways, very bad in others.The gunplay is super solid. More guns with more gimmicks, more often than ever before. You're gonna be spoiled for choice by the time you reach the ends of the main quest, and even then, you'll have barely scratched the surface. Ice is back and Slag is nowhere to be seen, and there's a new kind of status, Radiation, which makes enemies attack anyone in sight, friend or foe. Weapons feel strong and responsive without having to put all your skill points into gun skills, and with some thought, any enemy can fall before even the weakest of weapons. Enemy AI is till a ♥♥♥♥♥, though, and the loot in some of the harder areas is insultingly poor. Who knew a lauded Vault could be so barren?The characters are... not as hot. There are no standouts. Everyone is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or just absolutely insufferable, and I could hardly stand them. With the death of Handsome Jack came the death of the only likeable character in the franchise aside from Krieg, and there was no way the twin villians in this game could even hope to hold a candle to Jack. The Vault Hunters in 3 are bland and basic, the ones from 2 either have their entire characters assassinated or are simply nowhere to be found, and the ones from Pre-Sequel are treated with the same respect as a wet turd. The Sanctuary lot are still terrible, and it gets worse as time passes. Lillith is a plot contrivance, weak when needed to be and strong when needed to be. Tannis makes me sick to my stomach, constantly questioning how such a poorly written character could hold such importance. Ava... is an insult. A straight up kick in the balls. Whoever wrote her should be fired.This game isn't as bad as the tech test that is Borderlands 1, and is utterly outclassed by the brilliant Borderlands 2. The gunplay being so satisfying almost makes me want to place it above the Pre-Sequel, but I don't think I can justify it. Everything else attached to the gunplay drags this game down to it's death.

_childDocuments_.review: The positives and negatives of Borderlands 3 are quite complex. Compared to Borderlands 2, the gameplay is far tighter, and it feels like a modern AAA FPS, while Borderlands 2 felt more like an RPG with FPS elements. I would consider both to be pretty games, with Borderlands 2 still holding up today due to being so heavily stylized. (Though the performance of Borderlands 3 leaves a lot to be desired. With an i9-9900k and a GTX 1070ti, I frequently get frame drops into the 40-50fps range with a lot going on, and a capped 120fps when just walking around) Writing-wise, most characters in 3 are just insufferable, while 2 had a plethora of whimsical characters who didn't overstay their welcome, as well as a remarkable villain. Both games are written with jokes and pop culture references heavily intertwined, and while 2 wasn't perfect keeping things from falling flat, and not all of the ones in 3 were complete misses, the jokes and references in 3 far more often fell flat or were a little too on the nose compared to 2.The gear variety is far greater in 3, but this leads to a quality vs quantity issue. While there are hundreds of Legendary tier items, only a dozen or two are viable at endgame, high level content. Lots of this gear is neat and fun, but just isn't really usable. Additionally, at the high endgame ("Mayhem") levels, gear drops with an additional buff ("Annointments") and frequently this is what actually determines if a top-tier gun is even usable in high Mayhem levels. It artificially adds another layer of RNG to an already mind numbingly grinding game, and it is very frustrating farming a weapon and getting it to drop dozens of times, but none have the Annointment buff you want and are useless otherwise. These buffs can be as much as +200% weapon damage, and like the weapons themselves, only a handful out of the variety of them are even viable,Borderlands 3 is a fun game if you can ignore the writing, but endgame wise, it just doesn't deliver. I wouldn't say it's not worth picking up at a steep sale to play for a couple dozen hours, but it certainly does not have the longevity attached that 2 did, even with 2k and Gearbox cramming a games-as-a-service model down with it, with temporary events, regular level cap changes rendering your gear obsolete, and now a *second* season pass.

We were given Diamond keys right? Basically being able to open  up a room of legendary items and choose from them. Sounds cool right? Well.. _childDocuments_.review: I don't play any Borderlands game for the story, so this one's cast of cringeworthy characters in a wonky narrative didn't trouble me. This game is excellent where it counts: the gameplay. It's straight up FUN, and is a good time either solo or with a group of friends. The gunplay and overall mechanics (such as movement and helpful QOL changes) have been improved even more from the already great Borderlands 2 experience. Even the vehicular control is a bit less clunky this time, allowing for the brief driving bits to be enjoyable enough. The weapon designs look better than ever, and feature plenty of wacky ideas put to good use.Yes the story is relatively weak, so if you care about that I suggest you skip this entry and wait for Borderlands 4 (or just play the DLCs). But I wouldn't say the story is terrible, moreso just not great. The new characters are a mixed bag: the Calypso twins and Ava are the worst offenders, all three being annoying at best. But most of the other NPCs are just fine and they did a good job adding in many returning faces from previous games in ways that make sense. BALEX is my personal favorite of the new characters, he's a riot. That trademark Borderlands sense of humor is on full display here, and many of the side missions are actually fun and change things around permanently, in minor yet noticeable ways. Your choices do matter.Some people have complained that Legendary drops are too common in this game, and that makes them less meaningful or impactful. At first I agreed. But ultimately I think it's a positive change, as it allows you to have fun trying out various builds without too much grind. There are many hours of enjoyment to be had with this game, and don't miss the worthwhile DLCs.

Honestly that kind of innovation in games was around a decade ago, how is it not here? It would have made the ending almost satisfying if I could see and proclaim that I was the one who won the day. _childDocuments_.review: Soooo...over the course of playing this from start to finish I've ended up being saddled with one burning question searing into my brain - WHY AM I STILL PLAYING THIS PIECE OF ♥♥♥♥?!The story starts out entertaining, but quickly becomes both annoying and insulting; the antagonists are tedious, lacking any of the wit or charisma that Handsome Jack had. To use wrestling terms, they don't have heel heat, they just have "go away heat" (in other words, it's not fun to boo them, you just want them off the screen); It tries to replicate the shock of what happened in 2 with Roland's death, which ultimately falls flat both because we've barely got to know the character from an NPC to player perspective, and because it's just setting a bad precedent for expectations; None of the plot twists are interesting or unexpected, you can see them coming a mile off. Claptrap and Tiny Tina BOTH take up more prominent roles, a concept which just baffles as they are like red hot pokers in my ears every time they open their mouths; it does a horribly obnoxious fake-out ending, made all the worse by the fact your character isn't present in the cutscene; to expand on that you're not present in any of the cutscenes, which is especially insulting when it comes to the post-final bossfight cutscene! One of the characters has essentially been setup to fail in a lot of fans' eyes because those fans will only ever associate them with being the cause of the aforementioned character death. And the storymode's ending isn't simply insulting, but outright offensive to anyone who ever had any investment in the series and characters, especially as it ultimately denies the player the ability to be the one to save the world.And then there's the technical side of things, some are actual observed problems, others are just personal gripes: We STILL can't abandon or reset quests, which is especially irritating if you happen to misinterpret the sentence "talk to me before you go" as "you can talk to these people in whatever order you want, but the quest won't be available before you've spoken to me", silly me *eyeroll*; inventory is still a mess, I don't know if this is because it's optimised for console or what, but that's not an excuse, get your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ alignments sorted; getting quick travel to work is a chore as even when you're clicking on the right spot, it won't initiate until you click on the correct side-menu; one manufacturer of weapons is, in my opinion, almost completely useless with the exception of the SMG's, and I don't know if that's an intentional bad joke on the part of the devs, or if they're just badly designed, but either way Maliwan weapons are mostly only useful for pocket money; Eridium has been relegated to only being used for buying cosmetic upgrades, making the farming of it next to pointless, whilst in Borderlands 2, it was needed to get those all important inventory and weapon clip upgrades. But now those are all paid for with standard cash, meaning that you're desperately having to penny-pinch to make it possible to expand inventory to a size worth a ♥♥♥♥; Reload times are absolutely horrendous with some weapons, with some of them taking so long that I was sometimes thinking "Shall I just get myself killed, it'll probably be faster?"; Cutscene text can end up constantly appearing on-screen for hours after the cutscene happened. This can also happen if you go out of bounds and die, with the alert continuing to flash after you revive. In both cases fixed by quitting to menu and starting again, but THIS SHOULDN'T NEED TO BE DONE.And then there's the fact that Gearbox/2K are gouging for so much DLC it's unreal. Here's a great idea - how about you make a decent game first, then I might consider getting the DLC (In case anyone is wondering, what DLC I do have I won in a giveaway)I'm likely forgetting a whole host of things that annoy me about this game, but overall I just hate this and the only reason I completed it was because I'd already gotten as far as I had.I would say the game is in desperate need of patching, but no amount of patching can rescue it from the utterly garbage story. And of course, it's not like that patching will happen anyway now that Borderlands 4 has been announced, which will undoubtedly perpetuate all of the technical and logistical problems mentioned above, because why fix what has been broken since 2009?

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a very long BL2 expansion.  Which could be good or bad, depending on the individual. For me, it made this game slightly above average. While I did enjoy the game, nothing felt new or inspired. The story is mediocre at best. BL2's ending opened a lot of potential, which this game did not deliver on. I really thought it would lead to a BL MMO, but it did not. That I could get behind. BL1 and 2 were much more interesting and engaging games.There are almost too many zones to explore, so there is no shortage of content. Each zone is also massive and there is quite a bit to do in each one. There is a shortage of fast travel in many of the zones, so going back to complete zones feels cumbersome and boring. There is also a shortage of vending machines, which makes selling the massive amount of loot acquired a slog.The map is terrible, zooms in and out too slowly, and is often buggy to interact with. There are many glitches and bugs while platforming, in menus, or in the map. Some are a minor inconvenience, while others will crash the game. The most frequent game crashing occurred when interacting with a vending machine. This is disappointing, given that this is a AAA game with a ton of content.All of that said, the game is still worth playing. DLC from season one pass is good, I can't speak to season two. I waited for a 50% off sale and grabbed it with the season pass. Worth it. But not a game worthy of getting when it launched. I hope the next title actually progresses the franchise.This game has quite a few references to other games, music, and pop-culture, which I thought was neat. The sound effects are also extremely well done. The voice actors are really good, as they always have been in BL games. Mr. Torgue is so good lol. Some music is really nice, but some of it is really bland, boring, repetitive, or too ambient, though some of the more ambient music is pretty nice, particularly in The Handsome Jackpot xpac.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend. I unfortunately never played any of the previous Borderlands games, but I had an absolute blast playing through this. If you want to know what a good looter-shooter is, this is it. The RPG aspect is very real as there's easily millions of different ways to play the game, different skills you can use, unique weapons from bosses, and much more. And with the correct builds, you can be ridiculously overpowered, but that doesn't ruin the game like it sometimes can, it makes it even more fun, being able to zoom around the map at 100mph while doing damage the faster you go (my personal favorite). With an NVIDIA GTX 1080 Ti, playing in 1440p with medium settings, I would sometimes drop to ~60fps when there was a lot going on. This is totally still playable, I just strongly prefer having 120fps+.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 I was a huge fan of the first borderlands game, really fun looter shooter that was funny and engaging. BL2 was decent as well but my god what a nosedive BL3 has taken. First bad taste in my mouth was that I had to wait out a year of exclusivity nonsense before I could play it, and I finally got my hands on it for half price when it launched on Steam. Even paying half price I'm massively disappointed. First the good - The combat is decent, it plays well and the environments are up to par with what I expect from Borderlands. The climbing mechanic is a good addition. That's it. Onto the bad - The dialogue and characters are completely insufferable, everyone tries so hard to be funny that it just makes me cringe listening to them. My co-op partner turned off voice volume completely because it was so horrendous. The menus are so unnecessarily convoluted, some of the UI elements don't even unlock until you've beaten the game so why are they there? Tracking multiple quests is beyond tedious, as you can only check the location of an objective one at a time and then have to back out of the map to select a new one to plan a route, it's such a huge ballache. I can't set the game to any higher than medium (even though my PC should be able to run it at ultra) because the game crashes if I change any graphical option. The awfully unfunny dialogue made me instantly not give a ♥♥♥♥ about any of the characters or the narrative, so I uninstalled it after a few hours. Wouldn't recommend this to anyone, pick up BL1 for a fiver instead. Score - DNF

_childDocuments_.review: I came back to this game with a beasty new PC... Ryzen 9 7900x3d, GeForce RTX 4070Ti, 2TB SSD (main drive), 64GB RAM.BL3 crashes a LOT. Even worse, I usually have a Twitch stream running in the background, and it'll take down Twitch with it. It'll also screw up Discord so I have to restart it. One crash made Chrome hang entirely. It'll also cause various other bugs.This ONLY happens with BL3; plenty of other games, from Terraria to Elden Ring and Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, run just fine. Great even. But BL3 ALONE causes a TON of problems.I've adjusted various settings like lowering performance and switching between DX11 and DX12, verified game files, and even uninstalled and reinstalled the game, with no improvement.I STRONGLY advise people to avoid this game entirely unless they resolve its issues.I solved a lot of my stutter issues by putting -notexturestreaming in BL3's Steam Launch Options... but it doubled load times. BL3 has graphical optimization issues. Bad. I'm looking for a way to turn Volumetric Fog OFF to see if that helps as an alternative.I'll be honest; I paid $50 for BL3 with Season Pass (Super Deluxe)... and I wish I hadn't. They threw out a lot of what they learned from previous games, and the end result feels rushed. As soon as you beat the game, you can immediately go to Mayhem level 10, buy some M10 Anointed gear in Sanc, and go farm tons of exp, Guardian Ranks, and M10 Anointed loot and Legendaries.You can also go from level 1 to level 60 (the cap) without much difficulty in the very first playthrough. I did. So I beat the game and immediately got access to level 60 M10 Anointed gearIn short, once you beat the game, you'll get VERY overpowered VERY fast. It gets boring, even on multiple characters. There's not a lot of replayability.The story is also flimsy, and a letdown. They do a lot to demystify Sirens. A key plot twist partway through feels forced, in light of previous games (), and they spend most of the game making an oddly likeable character .They've also broken muling; all characters share the same bank vault. It can get BIG, but, in this case, "BIG" means "MESSY"; there's not enough sorting options to reasonably store gear for several characters in there. If you want to experiment with different builds, this can get out-of-hand. However, your only other option is to run a new character to Sanc, buy as much backpack space as they can afford, and have them hold gear in their backpack.Original Review:I thought I bought Borderlands 3. I apparently bought a graphical stuttering emulator with desynching sound. It's making my aim game miserable and even killing me via missed jumps. I've been trying to troubleshoot it ever since I got BL3, but absolutely nothing has worked... it runs BETTER than it used to, but not WELL. And this on an Acer Nitro 5, model AN515-51. Even with everything turned way down or off, the stuttering continues.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend but with reservations.  The game still has a lot of what made the other games fun, but this game is not a worthy followup to those games.Pros:- It's still a fun slaughter fest.- It still has that Borderlands humor.- D.va... err, The gunner is fun to play.Cons:- The story could have been a lot better and more fun. There are some fun elements to the story, but it doesn't move along fast enough. The writing was clunky, too. And they slowed the game down by making you do stuff that was fun initially but eventually became a grind. Does every vault key need to be assembled from fragments?!I liked that they brought back characters from other games, but they underutilized them. - The voice acting is okay, but the game design makes the characters repeat themselves a lot.- There are things in the game that seem designed to slow you down, not make the game faster. For instance, the teleport system is crap. Driving is more a grind than fun. Respawn of trash mobs is too fast, so you have to fight your way through junk you've already been through. - Boss fights are inconsistent. Some are super easy, some are boring, one seemed super hard. But the big problem is I haven't left a single one feeling like it was crazy fun.- What's with the DLC cash grab? If you buy the base game, there are several - yes, several - DLCs that will cost you more money. It's annoying.- Maybe it's just me, but I didn't think the siren's powers were as fun as they were in the previous games.- Not much has been updated. Weapons are still pretty much the same, etc. Powers feel mostly the same. They take you to different planets but it still feels like Pandora.If you liked the other games, you'll probably like this one, too, but it's not a great game and there's so much more they could have done with the game to make it really superb.
