_childDocuments_.review: Feels solid. The sliding, climbing & vaulting mechanics are a welcome addition. The movement feels very well paced, and serves the game very well. It truly shows the generational leap between Borderlands 2 & Borderlands 3. This is being supported by a set of phenomenal animations & audio design, that makes for some extremely satisfying gunplay, with bombastic weapon sounds & crisp reload clicks & slams. Furthermore, the new ragdoll physics and destructive environment are a nice touch that certainly makes the game feel fresh, and will keep the game fresh for years to come. Most of the soundtrack is fantastic. Zone music is sometimes outclassed by it's predecessors, but the sound mixing of boss fights & the change in tone each stage is phenomenal and makes you wish for the boss fights to last forever. Gun sounds are an absolute joy to listen to. The timeless cartoony art style feels refreshed, crisp and unique. I'm genuinely surprised it could even be improved on from Borderlands 2. The game is a joy to look at. Replayability being the word in the looter shooter genre, Borderlands delivers a balanced, satisfying end game that doesn't require 40 hours of grinding for a specific single piece of equipment, or glitch-saving for a quest reward roll. On the other hand, the end-game bosses and raids are rather forgettable.That being said, those are the only things that make me feel any joy playing the game. And after so many hours of trying to love the game for what it is, the cons massively outweigh the pros. ..Seriously? You've got 4 writers working on the game, all novices, and task them with following up on one of the strongest villains in the industry, tying loose ends from The Pre-Sequel & Expanding upon what happened in Tales from the Borderlands? Randy couldn't think this through while pocketing millions of $? This is not a matter of promise, or fan expectations, this is a matter of expanding on a successful franchise. What they did with the story in this game is abhorrent. Dumbing down characters, killing off fan-favourites, introducing new, unlikable characters, practically non-existing villains.. Really? I'm not one to get riled up over fictional characters. I quite frankly don't care. But I'm wildly surprised even Gearbox doesn't care from a business standpoint on delivering a solid experience. If writing a videogame story is considered art, then this is the absolute bottom of the barrel kindergarden trash you'd stop reading after the first paragraph. Disgusting. Fire these people. We've all seen DLC's & a season pass coming. It's been in all the games before. The main difference was the quality of the product received. Whilst Borderlands 1 & 2 DLCs would offer us 20+ hours of entertainment, I've breezed through each Borderlands 3 DLC in less than 4 hours. Irrelevant, forgettable experiences with no reason to return to them. Shameless. Gearbox should have kept their bar, match or beat what they offered in the past. With the addition of Season Pass 2, with even less content, and a 30$ price tag, adding in such basic features as daily objectives, the first standalone raid boss or a gameplay mode, the practices are even more vile. As a consumer, you should never let anyone get away with this. That was the final nail in the coffin for this game. With the series taking off to multiple planets, i must say, this is a very underwhelming part of the game. Half the maps feel like tech demos. Wide like an ocean, shallow as a puddle. Many zones are empty, bland, forgettable. Each planet has about half a dozen or less zones, excluding Pandora.  While i really tried to love the game, it fails to deliver a satisfying feeling upon it's completion, and the novelty of the introduced systems wears off after the first maxxed character. The game turns into a boring chore you wish you could skip through due to terrible writing, poor quest design & the idea of going through this mess of a story all over again, which is a fatal mistake for a looter shooter, where replayability means everything. 2K is killing off the series with predatory monetisation & Gearbox writers are clueless as to what to do with the story. Borderlands 3 just came and went.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, B1 was a revelation in all its areas. B2 was an impossible surprise that made it even better, it had a hard mode after you've beaten the game. It was cool to see if you can survive in a deadlier-then-ever Pandora environment. After that, the prequel didn't try to fool us, it presented itself honorably as "just" a well made fill-in, and because of that it was more then ok. Borderlands 3 is the largest of the series, and some may say that it's washed down. I don't think so - for the most part the first run-through is a very good gaming experience filled with......pun jokes, politicaly not correct scenarios, weird enemies, things to discover down the unbeaten path, heck I even liked the psychological story - I don't know why everybody whines about that. The story makes sense in all its parts and is well put! Graphics is short of amazing, music and sounds are outdoing themselves again. The atmosphere, the sense of exploration of derelict space stations, wild jungle bushes or just same ol' same ol' corners of dusty-rusty Pandora. Quests can be pretty funny, ingenious, really. This is where GB have always shined. Shooting feels alright, everything has the right "kick". The sheer amount of different weapons and different effects, all cool (maybe little too much of elementals and not enough good "standard" weapons, but whatever). So, that's the good part. Now for some critique.1) Skill trees and playable characters feel somewhat bland. I loved Roland, Brick, Lilith, Mordecai, Axton... The way they delved into the combat while being able to adjust to new strategies as well. The new playable characters in B3 are sometimes too haughty, shallow to some degree, and their builds force you to choose only few, similar late-game builds and equipment (same mistake initially seen in Diablo 3). Save, perhaps, for the robotic beastmaster. That one in the very least has sorta the right amout of grit, his remarks are fitting, and I feel he can actually use any sort of weapon to a good outcome.2) Mayhems - i.e. late game difficulty and replaying settings. I know it's the modern standard to have 1-10 difficulties in mmo's each 2x as difficult then the latter, ...it just doesn't seem to work here. At least for me. Subconscioussly, it drives you to play under the most difficult mode Mayhem 10/11. But I daresay for most of the normal people, fun ends somewhere at Mayhem 2-5. Why? Because only the selected few have the mental capacity to understand the zillions of mechanics together, and have the time to farm so much they can acquire the neccessary gear for these. For the majority of the rest, even the mobs can be bullet-sponges, the bad-ass versions of them are obnoxiously fortituidous, and it may take aeons to kill the bosses. (ok the last one may be actually good). All killable, survivable, yes, but kinda devoid of the FPS fun.I mean, what's the point of having a best Sniper legendary when it takes 3-6 headshots to kill a simple mob enemy? What's the point to a largest assault gun magazine there is if you need to spend half of it to kill just two mobs? Etc......I wish to throw a grenade; three enemies in screams being electrocuted, run in close while dispatching two more by my hard hiting double SMGs, hide around the corner and when the last one comes, switch to shotgun and shoot his head off with one well placed snap shot, splattering his brains everywhere. Phew. Intense. Fun. Deadly enemies, shields down, half the health, but I did it. Now wait for the shields to regen and go again. THIS is what Borderlands was about! Sadly, totally not what Mayhem is about for the most part. Yes, you can say you don't have to play the Mayhems, and stick with the "vanilla". But then again, everybody wants to push themselves, everybody is doing it, you will feel empty not trying if it's ♥♥♥♥ there.... This destroyed the feeling of replaying the game for me :(So, look, I recommend the latest Borderlands by all means. You'll get dozens of hours of pure shooting fun and weird scenarios, as you are used to in the first (..two) replays. It's just that unkindly bloated approach to the late-game replayability that stales the palate of the whole picture. %  Gameplay (subjective, non-rating)	☐ 	You'd Need Depression Pills☐	Don't Get Me Wrong, But…☐ 	Probably Better Than Watching Netflix☑	Late For Work Again…☐ 	Please Put This On Piedestal Of It's Genre ❤ Atmosphere	☐ 	Is Probably an Eupheism☐ 	You May Have Emotions☐ 	You Will Have Emotions☑	The Fog Of Baskerville Salutes☐ 	I Watched C-Beams Glitter In The Dark Near The TannhäuserGate ☯ Story 	☐	None To Speak Of☐	Look, We All Have Some Tales..☑	You'd Tell Your Friend☐	Gandalf's ALIVE!?☐	You Don't Want It To End Ever ☼ Graphics 	☐	Danger Of Loosing The Eyesight☐	Who Needs Graphics☐	Worth To Stop And Look At The Sceneries☑	Fantastic☐	Miracles Happen ♬ Music	☐ 	Turn It Off Please☐ 	I Forgot It Had Some☐ 	This Is Actually Nice ☑	Invigorates Your Headphones☐ 	Orpheus Cries ☠ Difficulty 	☐	Press a Button☑	You'll Learn It Soon ☑	Prepare Well, Young Padawan☐ 	So You Wanna Be a Jedi Master?☐ 	You Must Beat Darth Vader  ۞ Gaming time	☐	I Should've Bought a Movie Instead☐ 	Somewhat Long (10-20hours)☐ 	Now This Is Something (40-80 hours)☐ 	I Like To Live In My Games (100-200 hours)☑	You May Never Have a Girlfriend (200 - infinity) ＄Hardware Requirements 	☐	Wooden Abacus Is Enough☐ 	Just Have a PC☐ 	Just Upgrade Regularly☑	You Will Need To Buy a New RIG☐	Quantum Computing Here I Come § Bugs 	☐	A Broken Anthill☐	An Anthill☑	Well, What Did You Expect From a New Game?☐	You Can Do Without a Repelent☐ 	Sterille Environment

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to recommend BL3, I simply cannot. Does it have some good elements? Yes. The gunplay is very good- the best in the series, I would argue-, there are some good characters like BALEX and Wainwright Jakobs, and some good maps like Eden-6, but by and large the game is plagued by HORRIBLE new characters with cringe-worthy dialogue, long, linear mediocre maps with predictable and boring quests, and even the gunplay is damaged by massive amounts of welfare loot and easier starter difficulties that limit the value of tactics and damage types. If I weren't such a completionist, I would have stopped around 11 hours in, instead of finishing the base game at over 55 hours, but I was determined to make sure the game wasn't just wretched in the beginning and made the effort to find all of the secrets, complete all sidequests, and finish the base storyline. At the end, I was left feeling glad that it was over. I have no intentions of replaying at a higher difficulty, (higher difficulties are unlocked by beating the game), as I did numerous times with BL2. There simply is no incentive, given how common legendaries are, how horrible the writing is for the main story, and how its new characters like the "Twin Gods", Ava, and Lorelei are actually painful to listen to... and you have to listen to them a lot. What's worse is that many of these new characters are, at times, forced on you at the expense of classic characters who are treated like idiots, and cutscenes that leave your amazingly powerful character out as you watch the predictable plot play out between oblivious protagonists and seemingly omniscient antagonists that aren't even remotely likable. And yes, the humor is mostly terrible in a kind of way that might be expected by a writer that is a poorly socialized 12-year-old that resorts to loud and obnoxious behavior to get attention, and finds the word "turd" utterly hilarious. I lost count of the amount of times that word was repeated, but it was likely in the dozens if not scores. The exception to most of these complaints comes from the planet Eden-6 which altogether seems designed at a much higher quality, as well as the dialogue and characters, but that's maybe 1/8th of the game.On a final note, the game seems poorly optimized as, even well exceeding the recommended system req.s, I encountered symptoms of memory leaks and some weapons seemed to lag out the game simply by switching to them, while I could fill the screen with explosions and action, otherwise, without a problem. Still, even at low specs and DX11, the game had performance issues at times, not to mention progression loss in the "Borderlands Science" minigame.So if you want a good looter shooter, BL2 is still the gold standard IMHO. If you want good gunplay, then there are numerous other titles to consider.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it was a fun game to play through once- but they really kinda messed up with this Borderlands game. They were too ambitious I think, tried to make this something it didn't need to be. The story was rather predictable past a certain point, seemed like they brought some characters back for no reason besides to just end them! It was a disaster. The new world system was awesome, except for the fact that those maps were huge and most of the side-quests in this game were just boring "hey travel ALL the way across this place to do a silly fetch quest, then go back!" and you may be saying, 'well that's just how Borderlands is!' But no, this was pretty unbearable. In Pre-Sequel, I've 100%ed the side quests on at least seven different playthroughs, and Borderlands 2 I think I'm at four 100%s? I don't even think I did half of them in Borderlands 3 here. The new worlds were suuuuper pretty and they did a great job with them, but I don't really think Borderlands was meant to be this whole massive open-world adventure. The ending to this story was veeeeery underwhelming, honestly seems like it was kinda rushed- I managed to finish off the FINAL BOSS in about ten shots of a shotgun, the only thing that stopped me was the artificial time-gating of the boss with invuln phases after losing a certain amount of health. If you want to play this game for the story, I highly recommend doing so! But please wait till the game is on sale, it's not worth $60. I've heard that the DLC is a good time, but the main game kinda left a sour taste in my mouth so I don't think I'll try them myself anytime soon. I'm hoping that if they plan on releasing a Borderlands 4, they fix some of these issues- but I worry that they'll take it even further away from what Borderlands originally was. The antagonists in this game were absolutely DREADFUL. Hiiiighly unlikable. The whole Twitch-streaming bad guys thing probably sounded good on paper, but it was executed terribly. Literally every cutscene with them in it I was half tempted to skip, at least in 2/pre-sequel Jack was kinda funny. There were actually very few likable characters in this game, but that's up to personal opinion of course, so I can't speak for anyone. Was a fun way to kill some time, but I don't think I'll end up putting any more into it!

_childDocuments_.review: I was beyond excited for this game when it was first announced, as bl2 is one of my all time favorite games, however I cannot in good consciousness recommend this game. Let's start with the good, what little there is.1) Gameplay. The gameplay is the best in the series, and one of the most fun shooters I've ever played, as long as you turn the dialogue off. Or if you don't count the bossfights which are all so underwhelming I can't remember a single one from the entire game. The guns all feel & look great & the variety in character skill trees has never been so worthwhile.2) Soundtrack. The soundtrack is surprisingly good, I often find myself just taking a second to actually Enjoy the music while i'm shooting & looting. Hell even the weird radio songs in a few areas are fun! However the end credits song feels... out of place & in poor taste considering what happens right before it. 3) Visuals. Guns, characters, enemies, & Pandora itself has never looked as good as they do in this game. Picking a vault hunter was harder than usual since each of them has a fun design. I didn't just automatically gravitate towards one character in particular like I did with the previous games. Unfortunately good gameplay, designs, & music won't save this game from piss poor writing. The writing in this game is so bad it's almost insulting. Old character's feel like parodies of their previous selves, two of which in particular are reduced to one Very Minor personality trait. Some of them make decisions that make them look like the dumbest people in the universe, all in order to progress the nonsensical & barely there plot. New npc's are forgettable & uninteresting with hardly any depth or personality to them, despite the voice actor's & character designer's best efforts. Only 2 new npc's felt like valuable additions to this series with the other 2 possible one's having high potential that's wasted on this mess of a "story", if you can call it that. The vault hunters each have no real bearing on the story whatsoever, with them phasing out of existence whenever the plot needs to progress & a cutscene needs to happen. Despite the fact all 4 of them are canonically there. I will say that the dlc's are each Slightly better written than the main game but.... not enough to make me care. I still sat through the entire game relatively bored with a blank expression throughout the whole game. The only dlc where I Wasn't mostly disinterested was the second one, but that's pretty much only because of it's pseudo-horror setting & the fact it was about 2 of of my favorite characters from this series. The rest of the dlc had the same effect as the main story but with less groaning due to how awful the writing was. In conclusion, If you don't care about the story or characters & just want a fun mindless shooter you can play with friends or zone out to while listening to a podcast or something, yeah this game's pretty decent as long as you turn the dialogue off & skip every cutscene. Don't pay more than $15 for it though. If you want a good game or care about these characters? Yeah don't buy this game. Although, I'm guessing if you do care about that, then you probably already bought it & was just as disappointed as the rest of us.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say it's better than BL2 overall, mostly due to an excellent gameplay experience though the story is subpar compared to BL2's story.  Below is a spoiler free review from a (very) casual gamer perspectiveGameplay------------+ Clearly improved from BL2, even though there are one or two bugs it's still a great experience and feels very smooth with marked improvements from its predecessor.  + I liked how weapon manufacturers clearly have their distinct gun style and this in turn will create a player preference towards some brands over others.  This also has a bit of a drawback in that some companies are vastly superior to others.  From my own experience, I found DAHL and Torgue weapons to be great for my gunner while Tediore and Atlas were lackluster (for the most part).  + Enemy AI is improved and it's nice to see some enemies sliding and seeking cover.  It's not perfect but it's good enough for a casual gamer like me.  + Vehicle combat is much more fun and I really love the range of upgrades and mods you can do to your vehicles.  I hope this gets expanded on in the future because this was one of my favorite parts about the game.Cons--------- Story was good but I think the main problem was that the devs wanted both comedy and serious drama all together but at times the two didn't fit together.  Some character arcs didn't get expanded on as much as their should while others had way too much spotlight on them.  I found that the main characters in the story were rather annoying while side characters were a lot of fun and interesting.  For me, the side characters made the game much more appealing and engaging than the main storyline ones did.  It was a mistake to sideline so many great characters from previous installments to make space for new upcomers.  Most infuriating for the majority is probably Ava.  IMO she's not a terrible character but terribly written into the story.  She gets no real development but reaps a lot of rewards that would normally come from a developed character.  Had she reacted to events in the story differently and maybe took a more minor role I think she'd be a great fit.  As such, I think it was "too much, too soon" and she ended up ruining a lot of the story itself.  I'm a bit saddened that some my personal favorites (Ellie, Mr Torgue, Brick) didn't have larger roles.  I liked some of the tapes that explained characters like Krieg but wished there was a throwback to all the characters.  I would like to have known what became of Axton, Gaige, and Salvador.  I suspect this will come later in a DLC which would be fine with me.  I did like the inclusion of characters from Tales from the BL even though I never played the game.  It was a good move to encompass all previous games in some sense rather than ignoring previous events. The antagonists were alright, Handsome Jack is a hard character to trump in terms of a character people love to hate.  In that respect, I don't think the twins matched Jack on that level.  My main issue with the twins is that too much was made to make them hateable, to the point where it felt forced rather than a natural tendency to dislike them.  I also couldn't wrap my head around how they could use their powers so well, far far beyond what other sirens could do without any explanation. The exploration factor was really well done.  I loved travelling to different planets and the challenges section on each map really made it more fun to look around and explore hidden nooks in each area.  I hope this gets expanded on more in sequels and DLCs.Overall -- great game, a lot of fun and a good third sequel but the story needs work.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game breaks my heart. Borderlands 2 is one of my favorite games of all time and to have it followed up with a game that feels a hollow shell of a borderlands game is just an absolute shame. The bones of a really good borderlands game are here but the story and humor (The very things that made the borderlands games so special) were completely unbearable for me. The best way I can put it is that this is a masterclass in how NOT to do Ironic humor. Near enough every joke is absolutely groan worthy and typically goes on to the point that the, proverbial, dead horse they've beaten into soft serve has gotten sick of it as well. The story feels like it doesn't take itself seriously, the characters are practically all bland or annoying (or both), with most of the new characters being forgettable at best. The gear progression is totally busted with guns dropping so often that it ruins the magic of finding loot and you'll constantly be overloaded with mid guns. The combat feels way easier as well, with enemies having way less health and guns seeming to punch WAY above their weight class. I had a level twelve vladof AR shredding a level nineteen boss several times faster than the higher leveled guns I had. All of this is before you factor in the alt fire modes, so on top of being over saturated with guns they all have alt-fire modes to take into consideration. It's just overwhelming and it makes looting and comparing more of a chore than it needs to be.It pains me that all this is the case because, as I initially said, the bones of a really great borderlands game are here: The gunplay is great, I like the alt-fire idea, there are some cool ideas and environments, this game really COULD have been amazing. If nothing I said bothers you then maybe you'll like this game but I can't recommend it in good conscience. Play Borderlands 1 or 2 instead, even the pre-sequel would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: I DO NOT RECOMMEND.  If you are thinking about buying this game, maybe don't.  I wish I hadn't.Borderlands (1) was a solid shooter with amazing co-op.  Borderlands 2 was an even more solid shooter with better story and some solid feels; I especially loved Assault on Dragon Keep.  The Pre-Sequel was fun; I liked the narrative, even if I didn't like anything else as much as previous games, but that's fine.  No one does it right every time.The character roster offers a recycled mishmash from the first two games' special powers.  Maybe they used up all of their good ideas, maybe their creative staff quit, but I was expecting something at least on par with Borderlands 2, and this one fell way, way short.Story is... mediocre at best.  I KNOW there are/were good writers that have contributed to the Borderlands series.  Where Did They Go?  The plot relies heavily upon the weakest element of Borderlands 2 (the constant taunting by Handsome Jack).  In addition to the intermittent taunting by the antagonists, which is less witty than Handsome Jack's (who I loved to hate), these two are just . . . not.  I feel like it wouldn't have been hard to do better.  Add to that some arbitrary cutscenes, seemingly for the only purpose of trying to blindly lash out in hope of triggering more feels.  They were trite, stressed my suspension of disbelief, and eventually I just turned off the dialog and waited them out so I could get back to the game itself.The combat engine is closer to the Pre-Sequel (which I liked less than the system in B2), but if you liked the Pre-Sequel, it's like that. I was looking so forward to playing 'Borderlands 2 but Better', and what I ended up with was a boring mishmash with a few extra features.TL;DR:  Lame.  1/10.  Would not buy again. _childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler-free Review)When the game was released on Steam, I hesitated for a while, for two reasons:1) Gearbox Software is a morally bankrupt company. This is known. 2) A lot of reviews have been surprisingly negative.But I wanted to form my own opinion, so I did:The gameplay is fantastic. They added crouch-sliding and climbing, which makes movement and combat a lot more smooth and dynamic (Also: No more invisible walls).  The gunplay was cranked more than a  few notches. Every gun fells as it should, meaty, heavy. You can nearly feel the impact every bullet, grenade or elemental laser has. The aiming is 100% precise, just mind the recoil.Apart from that, it's the action-rich gameplay you can expect from a true Borderlands game. It's one of those games that you can play for hours just for the sake of playing it, because there is no drag or frustration, just pure, fun gameplay. And all the while you're rewarded with tons and tons of loot - of which it feels like the variety has also increased a lot compared to the previous games.A lot of people, even those that love the gameplay, have a lot of negative things to say about the story. And after completing it, I have to completely disagree. Don't expect a Bioshock Infinite level of complexity of depth, but if you do that going into a Borderlands game - honestly, that's on you. The story reveals a lot of the mysteries of the world that has been established in the previous games. You can expect the classic Borderlands humor, and it never gets stale. There is a bit of drama, a few plot twists, etc. They keep the story interesting.Every side quest is interesting. Even though they are often of the nature "Kill X" or "Collect Y", the story and dialogue around them make them worth playing. No quests ever feels like a chore. And then there are those gems that completely derail from classic quest design, like a Bandit gameshow, where a contestant get's shocked to death if he gets to many questions wrong.In the trailer, it says that one game journalist called it "A love letter to fans of the series". And it is. No matter how many or which previous Borderlands games you have played, you will find tons of throwbacks, references and familiar faces.The game introduces a few new characters, one of them is Ava. There are some people that find Ava annoying, but I could not really understand that. She is a bit clumsy, but that makes me wanna protect her more.The main villains obviously cannot compete with Handsome Jack. But even though I wished for that, I did not really expect it. The theme is annoying twitch streamers ("Can we copystrike the Vault Hunters?"), but their obnoxiousness cranked up to the max. They do horrible, psychopathic things, livestream them and then end every stream with their tagline "Like, follow, and obey." You are not supposed to feel any bit of sympathy for them, you are supposed to want to see them dead. Plain and simple. Some people may not like these kinds of one-dimensional villains, but then again, I don't play Borderlands to get confronted with difficult moral choices or deep philosophical questions.And with that I mean not just the graphics. Several times, when out of combat, I found myself not moving for a minute or so, just staring at the horizon or the sky - because the game just looks SO BEAUTIFUL. The environments offer a variety of settings, a Midwestern-style village mixed with a jungle, a Cyberpunk-city, good ol' Pandora with its Mad Max/Fallout like environments, etc. The enemy design also excels, especially when it comes to bosses (of which there are many). The bosses themselves, their attacks, the arenas they're in. They're all so unique and so badass.All the classes you can pick are fun and unique. No class plays the same. Hell, not even the same class with different skill trees plays the same. The skill trees are really defining, nearly every skill feels extremely useful. Every Tree even comes with it's own action skill, sometimes even more than one per tree. Every tree also has modifications for the action sill that sometimes turn it into something completely new. The fact that you unlock your action skill at Level 2 is also fantastic, you get to experience the defining factors of your class right aways. You can also respec relatively cheaply, so there is a lot of room for experimenting with different builds.The new loot and level systems are just great! With the instanced loot, there are no discussions about who gets what loot, and for me, that makes the whole experience just more fun. Some people liked the previous system, with collective loot you have to fight over, and if you do, don't worry, it can be enabled optionally.The same goes for leveling. With the "cooperation" mode, the enemies, their health, damage and loot are scaled to the individual players. So even a Level 1 and a high level player could play together and both can do their part and both get useful loot and receive a good amount of XP. This, again, can be switched off optionally, with the "coopetition" mode, in which the enemies and loot are scaled to the host of the session. Whatever floats your boat, you can have it.I cannot say a lot about this at the moment, cause I am not that deep into the Endgame now. But I love the Guardian System, which allows for a constant progression even after you hit the level cap. The Mayhem system allows you to crank up the difficulty level to whatever degree you want, keeping the game challenging and giving you something to actually gear up for. Then there's tons of free content in the form of events that Gearbox puts out, so there's is always something new to do.The one thing, THE ONE THING, the Pre-Sequel did better, was the way the player characters and NPCs interacted with each other. The NPCs would react differently to every character, and vice verse. Just one example: Jack flirts with Nisha, has respect for Wilhelm and despises Fragtrap. And there's unique voicelines for all of those. And this theme continues throughout every single conversation in the Pre-Sequel. Sadly, this was discarded for Borderlands 3. We are back to the nearly-mute characters of Borderlands 2, with no unique responses from the NPCs at all.Balancing of equipment is terrible. You can discard 90% of the legendaries, even if they are fun, because there are 2-3 weapons that kill every boss within seconds and one-shot every non-boss, outperforming every other weapon by far. That, at least for me, takes a bit of fun out of the game. Sure, one could just not use this weapons, but then again, they shouldn't have been put into the game in the first place, or at least balanced better so that the other legendary weapons can at least compete. It's always a bad thing when avoiding an element of a game increases the fun.Including the release on another platform, the game has been out for more than half a year. And what do we get:- Glitches that break quests, forcing you to quit the game and repeat the map- Permanent disconnects- Sub-par performance even on high-end setups (experiences may vary, but that just shows the lack of optimization on the side of the game)That's really sad to see and could have probably been fixed by now, if not for the DLC.In conclusion, even though there are a few flaws to this game, they pale in the face of all the good things this games has.Borderlands 3 is definitely worth the full price. I don't know about the Season Pass, as I haven't played any of the DLC yet - but I guess time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good.The level of variety in environments is far better than the Pre-Sequel, the variety in weapons is greater due to alternate firing modes and new buffs, and in general the combat feels faster and fresher.There are two areas though that are less than stellar:1) The story is mediocre in my opinion. I don't want to get into it, because there are some nice surprises admittedly that I don't want to ruin. But the story is just, well, muddled. 2) The balancing is really, really poor. Some weapons seem to be just an automatic 'use this the rest of the game and you win'. The hardest levels to get through, honestly, were the 10-15 range. By the time I got to level 16, I had a super-powerful rocket launcher that I am still using at level 23 and beyond. And the action skills have gone from afterthought to probably too powerful. I use the rocket launcher until I can get back into the Iron Bear, and after the action skill ends go back to rocket launcher (or a lesser weapon if just an enemy or two remain) and rinse, repeat. The balance is such that I'm really only ever upgrading shields, grenades, and class mods at this point.So B3 is probably my favorite since BL2, and I think might surpass it in many ways. But the weapon loot, which is a main draw to the game, is wonky because I find myself sticking with one or two weapons far longer than in previous games. The balancing is pretty off, and while it can toyed with and improved, I have to admit it's pretty strange using just the same weapon most of the game so far. Again, ever since maybe level 14-15, I've used the same one-two weapons almost exclusively... no need to change out for elemental damage. Excellent game, glad it's on Steam now, but it needs better balancing currently.

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't recommend the game to people any more, which is a shame because there are little nuggets of good sprinkled throughout the game. Yes, long established characters are underutilized and most of the new characters don't have any time to get fleshed out in any meaningful way (Wainwright and Clay being the few exceptions here). They focused too much on being bigger and not being better. Gameplay is the arguably the best in the series, and the fine tuning of the guns and manufacturers is delightful. The DLCs were mostly well executed, with the standouts being Handsome Jackpot balancing both fan service and a solid heist story, and Bounty of Blood's excellent blend of sci-fi and western narratives with gorgeous locations and character design.Unfortunately, the highs don't make up enough of the lows. The Calypsos could have, *should* have been interesting, but they were more annoying The direction of the game seems questionable at this point, with Season Pass 2 being presented as more content, but having vastly different ideas as to what content means. Sure, adding things to the game which wasn't previously there is technically content, but the whole approach just feels cynical. There's an attitude of, "it's got Borderlands on it, of course you'll buy it" is fairly obvious, and everything after is going to be met with scrutiny or indifference.tl;dr - God, these pretzels suck.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played this game on release, it felt mid.  Slow introduction, enemy variety so diverse that it felt difficult to develop a battle plan, far too much dialog, a low skill ceiling (even for BL).Now, years later, and the devs have done an amazing job of spicing up the game.  Option to start your character at level 13, bypassing the tutorial.  Incredibly well made DLC with great weapon variety, amazing soundtracks, quality locale.  A fourth skill tree. Three seasonal events which you can toggle on at any time to add spice to the world.  Mayhem mode and Annoited weapons to raise the skill ceiling significantly.  All these changes have given BL3 room to breath, and the result is that it's better aspect have started to shine though.BL3 is a fantastic looter shooter to play with your friends.  The difficulty scaling perfectly handles a level 50 joining a level 6's quest. The main story has double the content you expect, and the DLCs easily double that again.  You can easily sink 100 hours into this with friends, which is something you won't find elsewhere on the market.  Long running narrative coop games are a rare thing, so treasure this one.While it is by no means perfect, BL3 is easily one of the best coop FPS out there.  Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: SpoilersThe game was enjoyable, but still not nearly as good as 2. The graphics improvements were great, but there were several other aspects of the game that were lacking. I am writing this review after completing the main storyline as the Beastmaster, so I cannot comment on any of the DLC content.Gameplay was good with the usual logically configured controls for keyboard and mouse, I only had to change my crouch/slam key to X. The slam mechanics carried over from the presequel were not really useful in much of the game, as compared to the presequel. The new climbing mechanic was interesting and added some depth to the geography.The storyline was for the most part interesting, but pretty linear. There is not a plethora of side quests to do, as the prior games, and they all just take place in the area you are currently working on. There are very few times the game sends to back to a place you have been to complete a new quest or side quest. It just kind of plows through the zones. And with the addition of the space travel, it really seems disjointed, unlike 2 and the PS that really felt like you were exploring a planet.The part that really fell short was the antagonists. Tyreen and Troy. After the great writing and performance of Handsome Jack, we are left with these 2 idiots. Not scary or sinister, just annoying. You just want to kill them so you don't have to suffer through any more of their stupid cutscenes. They come across as super childish version of a Dragonball Z villain or something similar. And the final battles with each of them are not memorable at all. Nothing compared to the Guardian fights in prior games. And Lilith's death (?) at the end was lame. I will not comment further on that.Other minor issues I had: The new Torgue battle ground got me excited, as those were some of my favorite parts of BL2. But, they condensed the entire 5 stage battle, with multiple rounds in each stage, into one quest. So, if you fail on round 5, you have to start all over again, as opposed to BL2 where each stage was a new quest. I gave up after one shot because I'm not going to waste that much time trying to get through it. It's loooong, and failing means you start over. Poor design and a bad idea to change how it functioned previously.Next issue is the cartel mobs. How frickin' annoying can you get? I mean, I get the storyline here a little, but they really don't play into much except possibly spawning a boss that may drop a legendary gun. But when elite badass ratch are spawning 2 more elite badass ratch, it is getting ridiculous. And why are ratch even in the cartel? Poor design or foolish story writing there.Next is the broken catch a ride loadout system. So, it is really cool that they added all of the modifications and upgrades to the vehicles. But the loadout system is completely broken and will only save one loadout sometimes. So I don't get to use the neat new mods because I am not going to go through every mod available to build my preferred vehicle every time I need to spawn one. So i just quickload and take whatever is saved. Big disappointment there, and makes collecting all the upgrades kinda useless.Finally, there is a sound glitch that many are complaining about on forums, and I have it occasionally as well, but if I reboot the game it is usually fine. So not a huge deal, just annoying.After all that, why am I recommending the game? Because the mechanics are great, the weapons are fun, and an FPS with a skill tree just makes my day. As a stand alone game, it is awesome. And if I hadn't put over 1000 hours of gameplay into BL2, I may have loved BL3. When you compare the two, 3 just doesn't really do the series justice story and writing-wise. But, I am excited to play through the DLC and work on all of the other classes.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)If you're a fan of high-octane action, irreverent humor, and a galaxy brimming with chaos, then Borderlands 3 is an absolute must-play! Gearbox Software has once again outdone themselves, delivering a gaming experience that's as explosive as it is hilarious.From the moment you step foot onto the vibrant and diverse planets of the Borderlands universe, you're thrust into a whirlwind of epic gunfights, larger-than-life bosses, and a treasure trove of loot that would make any vault hunter weak at the knees. The game's graphics are nothing short of stunning, with each environment meticulously crafted to create a visually captivating world that's teeming with personality.But it's not just the visuals that shine; the gameplay mechanics are refined to perfection. The gunplay is tight and satisfying, with an arsenal of wacky and creatively designed weapons that'll leave you grinning from ear to ear. Whether you're unleashing fiery explosions, summoning creatures to aid you in battle, or simply making foes dance uncontrollably, the variety of weapons ensures that no two encounters ever feel the same.What truly sets Borderlands 3 apart, however, is its writing and humor. The game's script is a masterclass in comedic timing, delivering punchline after punchline that'll have you laughing out loud. The returning cast of characters, from the iconic Claptrap to the enigmatic Tyreen Calypso, bring their A-game, while new faces add even more depth and charm to the series. The story is engaging and takes unexpected twists that will keep you hooked until the very end.And let's not forget the co-op experience, which is where Borderlands 3 truly shines. Grab your friends and dive into the chaos together, sharing the thrill of exploring new worlds, battling hordes of enemies, and collecting enough loot to make a Scrooge McDuck vault jealous. The seamless drop-in, drop-out co-op ensures that the fun never stops, and the camaraderie and teamwork required to take down the game's toughest challenges are incredibly rewarding.In summary, Borderlands 3 is a spectacular journey that combines heart-pounding action, side-splitting humor, and an addictive loot loop to create a gaming experience that's nothing short of legendary. Gearbox Software has once again proven their mastery in crafting an unforgettable game that will keep you coming back for more. So grab your favorite weapon, team up with some buddies, and get ready to embark on an intergalactic adventure that's as wild as it is wonderful!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that across console and PC, I have thousands of hours across the Borderlands over the last 10 years.It pains me to not recommend this game but I just can't. It is the worst in the entire franchise in so many aspects that I can't say it is worth the money, at least not as of writing this review.-The main story is by FAR the worst the series has ever seen. The Calypso twins are unlikable villains for all the wrong reasons. You never are given a reason to hate them that stems from an emotional connection to the characters that we've all loved since Borderlands 1, TPS, 2, and Tales. They are introduced as these annoying, arrogant Twitch thots that make you want to slam your head against your keyboard every time one of them talks. They are no more than a means to an end, and that is the worst thing your MAIN VILLAINS can be. There is no endearing hatred like with Jack, there is no mystique surrounding them like Steele and Atlas in BL1, and I would venture to say that even Zarpedon and Dahl were better antagonists in TPS than these sad excuses. -Humor is practically absent in this game. I don't even think my nonexistent 12 year old cousin would laugh at 99% of the dialogue in this game, story or side quests. Speaking of side quests, what a fall from grace this game is. Out of the 91 total side quests in the base game, there are maybe a handful of actually interesting side quests that held my attention for longer than 30 seconds. The rest are just unfunny, uninteresting, or not fun, usually a combination of the 3. They dropped the ball hard here as well.-Without trying to spoil too much, what happened with the characters? Ava is perhaps the most annoying thing in the game and I genuinely wish she was the villain because I might have cared enough when it came time to kill her. Unfortunately that's not the case and you can't kill her, so I'll just have to imagine it every time she speaks or does anything. They killed off other characters for basically no reason, other characters from past games don't return for... reasons? And on top of all of that your character does not exist in cutscenes, even if you were literally standing right next to someone when the cutscene starts. At least half of the "big" things that happen in cutscenes in this game could have been prevented by your character if they didn't get teleported to the shadow realm.+I will say that the gameplay is top notch in this game and really the only redeeming factor. It is really fun when you strip away the dialogue and story. Guns feel great, movement is the best it's been in the series, and I like things like the 3D map and Guardian rank. I will also say that if you drop this same gameplay into LITERALLY any other game in the series, that game would be objectively far better than Borderlands 3. Even the TPS would be more fun than BL3, which I think it is anyway, but that is beside the point.+The DLC is good at least. So far we have had DLC1 and DLC2 released and I loved the Casino setting with... you guessed it, Jack back. The game instantly became engaging as soon as an actual good villain was reintroduced, go figure. And with DLC2, the Lovecraftian horror style fit surprisingly well with Borderlands. Maybe they will continue to put out good content in the future, and drop the price to make the game worth it.Overall this is a game that feels nice to play on the surface, but has villains, side quests, and a story so terrible that it ruins almost every good change this game made. I do not recommend playing this game, especially if you care about story in games or are not already a Borderlands fan.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've thought about this for a while, whether to recommend it or not. I eventually came to the conclusion, that it's a good game, but it's not what I had hoped for in a Borderlands 3. I want Gearbox to know that, while I appreciate the work that went into this, it's not the right direction. Sacrificing storytelling and character building to chase the latest trends is not what I would call good game design. The main story is weak. There's no other way to say it. The baddies are bland, annoying and I hate them for all the wrong reasons. Characters that were built up over the last two games are killed off in what feels like a whim and for no effect other than to build a character that's not terribly likable to begin with. Some don't even show up at all which is a bit unfair towards them. The gameplay is great, and it improved a lot from the predecessor. Guns feel even better, look amazing and are more varied than before. Although the new Atlas guns strike me as very niche weapons, the thought that went into specialising the weapons manufacturers is admirable. Sliding and climbing are a thing now too so navigating while on foot is a whole lot easier and less frustrating. Loot feels balanced enough, although legendaries drop almost hilariously easy. Perhaps that's by design but I feel that it devalues them somewhat. Then again, most of the leg's are gimmick weapons at most and not practical in combat. Graphics have been turned up a notch as well, with textures looking crisp as they can and weapons shining as they should where there is metal, less so where there is plastic. It just looks real, no two ways about it. Reloading animations have been given some love too. What I'm not a big fan of is how there seem to be all of maybe 30 quests in the whole game, spread over 5 planets. It feels like alot of wasted space and opportunity. Where BL2 had lots of memorable and funny/quirky quests in all different areas, the ones in 3 seem a bit few and far between. I don't think we needed repeatable quests either, it just gives you the illusion of something to do. All in all, I do think my purchase was worth it at 50% off, and I will definitely play more of it. But I implore Gearbox, please think about what made BL2 great and learn from this. We don't need annoying wannabe streamers as antagonists if all they do is wallow in how much better they are and have no significant character arcs or motivations.

_childDocuments_.review: Nov 2020: For those who got no time:No character development, no interesting arcs, not a single good dialogue, no immersion, missing characters, rewritten characters, ignored/ cancelled past events, laughable animations & cutscenes, bad art direction, loot-system is beyond f*cked, terrible forced humor, boring leveldesign, utterly atrocious and hollow villains, worst story of all time in any media ever, not even a rewarding ending- exactly the opposite. Almost everything in this game exists purely as an annoyance to the player.A huge middle finger to all the fans. More details below:I was a huge BL fan. And since I heard a lot of negative feedback before I started playing, I tried to look at BL3 as neutral as I could. It still managed to disappointed me to the point, where I dropped the franchise.- Yes, the gameplay is a bit better than it's predecessor. Ledge-grab & sliding are a nice addition. Though, sliding is completely useless - not a single map requires you to do it. - Graphics obviously. Though I really, really miss the thick outlines from the cell shading. They were charming and unique.- The guns got more oompf and have overall more interesting designs, better sound, animations & weapon skins. - The Soundtrack does mostly a good job at mixing things up while also keeping the Borderlands vibe.- Bandits are more varied, though they lost humor.- Voiceacting is.. okay at best. But most of the time it's very obvious, they're reading of a script, which just breaks the immersion.- UI is too cluttered. Too many colours. It's clunky, slow and bad at handling a lot of items. I also miss being able to see yourself in the inventory, where you could turn around your char. - Old characters are either completely rewritten or missing entirely from the game.- Great characters are being tossed aside after 2 missions, while new shallow, annoying and utterly dumb written ones get all the highlight.- The sound mixing in this game is just bad. Got a 5.1 system but had to set it to stereo, since I could not hear anything as soon as I looked away from talking NPC's.- Players voice is so overpowering loud in contrast to everything else, it's so annoying. Sound options don't help at all.- Gearbox thought it was a good idea to let the player talk.. ALL THE TIME. And since each character has only 10 lines to say, every 15 seconds you hear a really ret*rded, cringy clichee line, that only cheesy kids cartoon villains would say. It's so bad with Amara. I want to slap her each time she says: "I cAn FeEl tHe pOwEr!!" or "mAkiNg hEaDliNes!". No one would ever say that. And her jump sound is so overexaggerated, she's as annoyng as the "villains" themselfes. But more to that later.- Leveldesign is extremely underwhelming. So many copy-pasted assets everywhere. Nekrotafeyo was the only place where it felt like, it was truly a different world.- Eden 6 is the biggest area in the whole game and it's just a big swamp.. with more... swamp. It's design is extremely bland and boring. Just awful. BL3 goes interstellar and they make swamp worlds.. wow.- The Vaults are so disappointing.. again! This is the 5th entry and they still f*cked the vaults up so hard. They are all  They just didn't care. Very questionable..- Loot-system is broken beyond measurement. Legendaries drop as often as blues in BL2 UVHM. There is not a single point in picking up anything below Legendary, since the game gives you 20+ in less than 2 hours. I got 9 Legendaries from one mission, which renders them completely unimpressive. Because of this, I don't even look at purples anymore. In just a few hours of playtime, my entire inventory was full of gold gear. I can't for the love of everything make sense of this. Why have over a billion guns when only maybe 100 are actually interesting? Marketing, I guess. And the saddest part is, that most legendaries are complete trash too. - The Vault Hunters are so uninspired, boring and annoying characters, it's so sad. They constantly yell and scream full-ret*rd-mode. I'd rather have quiet characters again, than having these constantly sh*t talking gremlins, that give you cringe goosebumps every few seconds.- All the animations in this game are not motion captured, which means they are just garbage. Even an untrained eye can spot how stiff and clunky they are. A triple A 2019 game with that budget should have mo-cap. - The cutscenes look like someone from Deviantart made an amateur fanvideo. They are so unbelievably bad, It's the only time the game made me laugh. From awkward camera angles to extremely bad amateur animations. The pacing is so off, they weren't even trying. So, so unbelievably awful. And what the flying f*ck happened with their faces? Everyone is so ugly now. Art direction? Hello?! Where are you at?- And to the final act of this clownshow: The "story". I actually still can't find proper words for this ungodly monstrosity they call a "story". It's easily the single worst piece of awful BS that I've ever encountered so far. Not even in videogames, but movies and series as well. The fact that not a single soul at Gearbox was like: "uhm guys, this actually sucks f*cking gigantic balls.", is just depressing. The Calypsos had great potential. But then they started talking. God, those awful voices they got. I want to vomit all over the place each time they open their badly animated, ugly mouths. They're just huge pathetic twitch vag*nas, with absolute zero backround story, no real motivation. The game wants you to believe there is but boy there isn't. The "twists" are so last minute made up, it's just a big insult to all the fans. That moment when Troy finally seemed to evolve from a leech to something greater, the game decides to throw it all away and act like it never happend. It's so blatantly obvious, that they had no idea what TF they were doing with this continuation. Then the whole siren "plot".. just really, really st*pid. So the writers decide to take ALL the established siren rules and throw'em out of the window. Why? fanfiction, that's why. And then they continue to make up new ones, that contradict with everything we know. It's the most merciless form of lazy writing I've seen so far. Truly atrocious. Can you believe someone got paid for this? Heck, my dead grandma could write a better sequel than these buffoons.BL3 ripped bigger plotholes into the franchise than the eridium scar of pandora. It's like they really, really wanted to f*ck it up. Garfield-effect had better writing than this dumpsterfire.- Nothing in this game gets taken seriously. A few of your beloved characters die? NPC's make fun of it with unfunny jokes and everyone instantly forgets about it. Are you excited what the guardian at the end of TPS meant? Too bad, that script got cancelled. Never happened. Wanna know what happened at the end of Tales of Borderlands? Too bad, writers are actually too lazy to care and ignore it all.And let's just not even start with Ava. The single worst, r*tarded ugly f*ck of a character I've seen in anything ever. And the god forsaken credit song at the end- I wanted to shoot myself. Truly, f*cking awful.Borderlands 3 made me feel I'm watching a 40 hour long trash movie. Sadly not even a good one.I'm not nearly as angry as I make this sound like but I really had point it all out. I honestly don't care about the pros. The cons overweigh BL3. BL2 is such a better experience in almost every way. Hopefully they hire a competent writer for BL4. f*ck me.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I rather enjoy the game, but:Bad story and characters:It seems like at the start of development apparently only a rough outline of the story was "finished", hence there are numerous plot holes. The powers of Sirens are no longer firmly established as in the second part of the series. The (new) characters are badly written and not comprehensible in their actions. From this basis unclear, avoidable and dull events emerge which are worked off in cutscenes to get the rough development points of the unfinished story done. Thereby previous and important characters of the preceding parts remain, with two exceptions, completely in the background and are almost interchangeable. And this with the promise to focus more on the story in the third part. On the contrary the whole lore of Borderlands has been greatly elaborated which I really liked even though the narrative is a lot of bs. But a few moments in main and side quests are still very well written.Great gameplay:The weapons are creative, feel good and fit into the typical abstract gunplay of the Borderlands series. There are different vehicles with changeable components that are very easy to drive. The bright spots of the game are moments like finding a new vehicle part or a nice weapon while moving through a very nice and colourful world. Enemies are pretty fun and only get to be bullet-sponges in late-game Mayhem modes.Too much profit orientation of the publisher:In the end it's just like Red Dead Redemption 2, because 2K-Games has released three different versions of the game, which also differ from the content of the game. Even by pre-ordering the game you got bonuses in the game. Moreover, even today there are still some bugs and errors. Instead of letting Gearbox finish it, 2K has most likely put pressure on them again and with a promising marketing campaign and deliberately pushed the fans/players to buy the product while it was still unfinished. _childDocuments_.review: (please note that, whie it says i have <10 hours in the game, ive played far more on PS4. i only got it on pc recently)BL3 is a really weird case of a game. its simultaneously the best and worst in the series at the same time for very different reasons. first off, barring a few minor nitpicks, this is the best gameplay in the series no question. the guns typically all feel amazing to use and the extra movement options in sliding, mantling, and ground pounding add a small bit of extra depth that doesnt go unappreciated. while ive only had extended experiences with moze and especially (my boy) zane, and not really any with amara, all of the vault hunters here are interesting as well. nothing feels like a retread of anything in the past games, the closest really only being zane's digi clone being an axton turret on crack. the added depth to the action skills across the board is a total breath of fresh air as well, each class having 3 (4 with designer's cut) action skills (or in the case of moze 6+2(?) mods for the one skill) with a handful of modifiers each. the one part about the gameplay i dont love is the enemies. the variety is nice enough, though i do wish there wasnt such a *massive* abundance of COV units. though in some cases i prefer them cause then theres the maliwan soldiers which can sometimes be an absolute pain to fight, especially the heavies. apart from that, the gunplay feels incredible, especially with the manufacturer revamps. dahl guns now switch between firing modes like a traditional fps as opposed to only when ADS, jakobs weapons are much more varied overall with different types of guns (lever action rifles my beloved), tediore just gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥ wild with whatever happens when you throw spent guns, atlas makes a return from BL1 with an interesting lock on mechanic (though, imo, they arent my favorite to use), maliwan now focuses on always having 2 elements instead of just 1, torgue has sticky rockets on top of the traditional gyrojets, vladof is typically 2 guns in 1 with its swap system, and hyperion guns can spawn with shields that deploy on ADS. it really is the final form of borderlands' gameplay and apart from D&D-ifying it for tiny tina's wonderlands, idk how theyd really go further than this in a sequelbut now for the ugly, opposite side of this same coin: the story. (btw, spoilers, im not gonna bother tagging, but also you are not missing much) now, im not the kinda person to disect much about why things dont work in games narratively, but theres plenty of videos online that could do that leagues better, but i'll say what i can. first off, these villains are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ atrocious especially following the absolute legend of handsome jack. they did troy absolutely dirty and he would've been a far better villain than tyreen. hell, they had plenty of room to actually build him up as a twist villain to overthrow tyreen. there were practically hints of that from any point after promethea. but instead, we had one of the most obnoxious characters ive experienced in ages as our BBEG. but tyreen is far, far from the worst character in this game. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥... ava. now, in the directors cut dlc, there was a cut scene where it actually gave ava some level of depth and reasoning for her actions after maya's death. but of course that was scrapped and we're left with one of the most blatant mary sues ive seen in ages. and thats not me trying to imitate some star wars sequel loathing neckbeard, no, she's actually a mary sure unlike rey who just happens to be too good at things. she's given no flaws, no weaknesses, nothing. again, im not qualified to give a deep analysis on her cause idk how to do something like that, but believe me when i say she's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible. as for maya, she has bay far one of the most unearned character deaths ive seen in a while. moving on to the new characters, theyre enjoyable but forgettable at best and obnoxious at worst (ava being a far outlier to the latter side). the exceptions to this id say are wainwright jakobs (who is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ treat and the best newcomer in this game) pain and terror (which would've been much better arena commentators than torgue again) and the vault hunters themselves. apart from amara (who isnt bad just kinda flat and bland) all of the new vault hunters are easily the best new characters here, especially zane and fl4k.  the returning cast is also pretty hit or miss. ive already mentioned how dirty they did maya, but othr than that, all of the returning hunters were treated fine enough. sure, axton and salvador were relegated to announcers for the faux battle royale mode in the designer's cut dlc, but theyre entertaining enough there that it's not that bad i guess. zero's good enough, he has a role in the story but not a big one. pretty short and sweet overall, not much to hate or love. arelia is brought back from the pre-sequel in a fine enough way as a boss for winny/hammerlock's section of the story. not much but she didnt really need it. vaughn and rhys are brought back from tales and apart from rhys' recasting, both are pretty entertaining in their own right. neither have a massive presence in the story, with rhys only being prominent during the atlas v maliwan arc and vaughn being a side character for the intro on pandora, but they're still enjoyable gaige is in a similar boat to zero, only she was relegated to DLC 2. and krieg is actually pretty well explored as a character in his own dlc. which actually brings me to the dlcs themselves. while none of them really hit the highs of BL2, they're still leaps and bounds more enjoyable than the base game's plot. hell the only one id consider weak is bounty of blood and thats really only just forgettable. handsome jackpot is also where we see the return of jack's doppelganger, timothy. unlike most of the other returning PCs, timothy is actually a key part of the handsome jackpot dlc. i wont spoil it as much since thats actually good (even if the new characters there are wildly forgettable apart from digby vermouth) but he's certainly enjoyable. as for the other, general aspects of the writing, its fine if not as good as 2 in places. some of the side missions can be pretty charming and funny, the unique weapons are full of fun references, its just more of the same just not quite as up to par. if you loved bl2's writing youll... really like 3'sto summarize this absolute bloody rant of a "review": BL3 is a great game if you're already a fan of borderlands. i would not at all recommend this as someone's first exposure to the franchise. if you're new, start with 2, maybe give pre sequel a shot, and *then* play 3.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: If you liked the *combat* of BL1/BL2 and didn't care at all about the story, writing, characters, world, or anything else, then you might like this one. If you are interested in anything other than combat for combat's sake, give this one a pass.I'll illustrate my annoyance with one particular pair of scenes from about three-quarters through the game. As part of the previous planet, you picked up the mentor-figure (Maya) and a tagalong kid (Ava). On the current planet, in the vault you open, the kid (despite everyone telling her to stay put) sneaks in (somehow, despite all the monsters). Because of this, Maya hangs back to watch her while you go into the vault. When you come out, cutscene-incompetence engages and you, Maya, and the kid all stand around gormlessly while the villains drain the vault guardian's power. The kid stupidly yells about how Maya is going to beat them up, causing a distraction which allows one of the villains to drain the power/life from Maya. Despite the obvious fear this should cause in the kid, she continues taunting them until the villain force-pushes her across the room and they flee.Back on the ship, everyone is having a sad remembrance of the fallen mentor (at least I think it was sad; I was just bored). The kid gets angry at the messiah-figure (Lilith), yelling that Lilith was at fault for Maya's death because Lilith allowed her to go on that mission. Not a single person corrects the kid, or consoles Lilith. Everyone acts as if the kid has just spouted the truth. *facepalm*After that cutscene, I did some digging and discovered the cause of this stupidity: BL3 has 4 writers. Only one of them has any writing experience prior to this (another bad game) and only one has any significant experience... in visual effects. Was Gearbox so strapped for cash that they literally couldn't hire a single writer with any skill? Did they care so little about anything in this game that they thought hiring 4 no-names was a good idea? There are so many starving writers out there with the right chops for worldbuilding, but apparently Gearbox hates anything that isn't guns. Rather fitting, that.Gameplay's fun, I guess, but I lost interest near the end because I hated the dialog so much that I ended up turning off voices and music and listened to a podcast in the background. Oh, and there's tons of jank everywhere. Reproducible jank that would have been easy to catch. But, again, Gearbox doesn't care.

_childDocuments_.review: The key to enjoying this game is A) not taking the base-game story too seriously and B) recognizing the base-game story is not that great. Not the worst thing ever, but also very much a downgrade from BL2's writing. I like that BL3 is now a space-faring, galaxy treading adventure due to the amount of different environments you can AND WILL come across in this game. Lots of planets, lots of main and side quests, and plenty of awesome characters to meet for the first time or see again.The gunplay and loot system is the best it's ever been. LOTS of weapons and alternate modes for them, and a lot of freedom to create many different loadouts with each character available. My one and only pick in this game will always be FL4K for the amount of cool stuff you can do with him. I mainly switch between his Spiderant and the Ion Loader robot, but there are way more possibilities and combinations that I have yet to discover. The game is made a little more forgiving in that it's easier to get through in the single player mode, but tough enough that you'll still experience challenge when fighting the game's wide variety of enemies and bosses.The DLC for this game was what made it a much better experience for me. It kinda sucks that the DLC expansions hit a higher mark than the base game, but they retroactively improve the game as a whole, so I'm fine with it. I got the Ultimate Edition of BL3 for $28 bucks, and that's a generous price for the amount of content included.

I have finished each game in the franchise multiple times, and make it a point to use each playable character all the way through to the end. I have thousands of hours of gameplay under my belt. While I understand what 2K did with their platform exclusivity when Borderlands 3 was released, I prefer to have all my games in the one place (Steam), so I waited until it was available here. I started playing it the day it was released on this platform.I have to admit, the initial thoughts I had were quite negative. The first few hours of gameplay left much to be desired. The story was poorly constructed, the missions were mediocre and the constant (and I mean CONSTANT) badgering you get to complete the missions was incredibly off-putting. This is a "Loot & Shoot" title which is supposed to reward exploration, but having characters constantly tell you what you need to do got very stale very quick. The writing and dialogue was hardly exciting. There were no comedic elements (Torgue), endearing characters (Scooter) or well written villains (Handsome Jack) to be seen. Just annoying characters which seemed to meander on like they had no real purpose. I decided to press on and give the game a chance.I'm glad I did. As the game continues, it also matures. I found the new "slide" mechanic useful finally, as well as mantling. Much more could have been done earlier on to establish the benefits of both. Looking back, I think I forgot both were a thing early on. Nevertheless, as the game matures, everything starts coming together. The voice cameos were a massive surprise (which I won't spoil here). I would never have thought I'd hear those voices in a game, but they were quite refreshing and entertaining. As the story progresses, it becomes more nuanced, but not with too much sophistication. There are elements of lore building I see which could expand the game for the future, and they don't seem to be tacked-on to fill out the game. Sure some characters are maligned for good reason (and you'll know which ones when you play), but others play to their strengths.I have finished the game once at this point with one character, and should finish it in the next week or so with the other 3. The playable characters balance quite well. With the right combination of weapons, artefacts, shields, and mods, there are times where the game is throw-your-headphones challenging, and some which make you feel like an unstoppable god. The unlocking of certain features took a little too long for my liking, constantly wondering "what is that empty slot I can't fill?". However, once you unlock all the abilities of your character, you can really have fun.Overall, I would say that this game has just met my expectations. I encourage everyone to play it because there is value and fun in doing so. Is it the best Borderlands game? I think 2 is slightly better in every aspect, but not by a large enough margin to hate on 3. I see what they were trying to do with the 4th in the quadrilogy, but the execution of 2K's idea was lacking. Assessing the game shows its flaws, PLAYING the game shows its strengths. I would recommend this game to any Borderlands fan, or anyone who likes a good FPS. Push past the first few hours and you WILL have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a game I’ve been meaning to play for a while now but had to wait a bit to enjoy it on Steam as I refused to buy it in the Epic Games store. I figured to wait until a deluxe edition came out with all the DLC, bugs fixed, etc. before jumping in. I’m glad I waited since it was well worth it for the most part as I loved the original and its sequel and this one wasn’t so bad. It’s nowhere near as good as the original two but it’s a decent experience.All the usual Borderlands style of things is here from the great graphics, amazing weapons, and the beyond satisfying gunplay. It’s a lot of fun to get all sorts of unique and different types of weapons and plow through enemies. Even the boss encounters were awesome as it’s a tried-and-true formula that has defined this franchise for over 15 years now.It was great to see the return of many beloved characters in the series from Lilith, Ellie, Tiny Tina, Moxxi, and many others. Besides that, the graphics, soundtrack, and overall loot are all fantastic. I had some incredible weapons while playing which made it even more fun to go through the entire game. Now, the biggest issue I have with this game is its main story in the campaign and all the boring side quests.The entire story from the campaign is the WORST I’ve ever seen in a Borderlands video game. It’s so terrible, cringe, immature, and flat-out dumb that it took me away from the overall gaming experience. I knew going into this game I wasn’t expecting an amazing or super serious story but this just sucked. The main villains are trash and the entire story is a weird, hot mess.It wasn’t as funny or as good as Borderlands 2 and yeah, I get that this wouldn’t have Handsome Jack who is a legend in his own right but common now, the main villains could have been a lot better. It feels as if it was written by a bunch of teenagers who looked up #Borderlands on Twitter and used the most immature tweets they could find to write a story around them. The main story gets boring from the halfway point on as I just wanted to finish it already, collect my Steam Achievements, and be done with this hoping the DLC is better.There’s just way too many fart jokes, characters in underwear, pictures of butts, and a high degree of immaturity and not of the funny kind. Besides that, this game also has a good amount of bugs and issues while playing. Loot will disappear into the ground and it froze a few times. It also crashed numerous times while playing out of nowhere and luckily, everything was saved so I didn’t lose my gear, character, or progress. If that happened, I would have given this a negative review, uninstalled it, and never played it again but thankfully, that wasn’t the case.I will say though, after completing that abysmal main campaign, the four unique DLCs were a lot of fun to play. I enjoyed “Moxxi's Heist of the Handsome Jackpot” the most since we got to see the return of Handsome Jack. “Guns, Love and Tentacles: The Marriage of Wainwright & Hammerlock” was awesome since it was Lovecraftian-themed and I love horror so that resonated well with me. Both “Bounty of Blood” and “Psycho Krieg and the Fantastic Fustercluck” were fantastic and again, the graphics, new DLC weapons, and bosses were all a ton of fun. The storylines here were a lot better.I didn’t waste any time trying out the mini-game of “Borderlands Science” as it didn’t interest me at all and the same with 2K Games trying to tap into the battle royale scene with their “Arms Race” mode. I tried it and it’s okay but when it comes to the co-op and multiplayer aspect of Borderlands 3, you’ll find some people playing but not a ton so expect queue times.Crossplay and cross-platform are possible in Borderlands 3 so if you use its matchmaking you should be fine during optimal days and times depending on where you live. I was able to get into matches pretty quickly for the campaign but nobody was playing the other modes so keep that in mind.I give Borderlands 3 a 3/5 for being a decent experience and still being one of the best looter shooters ever made. I am hoping 2K Games learns from their mistakes here since if this had a great story as the original and sequel did, this would be a perfect game. Unfortunately, the storyline is terrible and the bugs, glitches, and crashes were a shame. Aside from that, the DLC balances things out, the graphics are great, and the multiplayer works well during primetime. Here’s to hoping Borderlands 4 brings this incredible franchise back to its roots since this one was very close to being a dud and a negative review.
