_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've played in like forever, and here's why:In one instance, during the side mission called "Healers and Dealers", Ace Baron, the questgiver, asks you, the vaulthunter (VH) to acquire some medical supplies that has been stolen or just needs to be collected by NPCs in the area. While this task may seem easy enough, there are some twists that makes the task harder to complete. But do not fret however, Ace will be commentating your performance during the mission, as well as help you during possible hardships.One medical supply you have to bring Ace is located in the middle of the map, high up in a container. Although this sounds fairly easy to overcome, the way up may be a setback to some players. Personally, I had a very rough time getting up there. It took me about 4 hours and around 70 to 100 tries to catch the ladder mid-air. While the task in itself is not very hard, the way to the task is harder than you would expect.Now, when you arrive at the spot where the medical supplies are supposedly located at, Ace talks about the resident who is located in said container. In one instance of the dialogue, Ace Baron says the following:"That punk-ass is a black market dealer. I'll bet dollars to deez-nuts he stole those supplies. Dude's a pushover..."When I first encountered this dialogue, I instantly dropped doen on the floor, dead of laughter. To think that Gearbox would include such a based and red-pilled pop-culture reference in their latest installment of the Borderlands series absolutely blows my mind. The line "deez-nuts" still cracks me up everytime. Even while just typing this very review, I had a hissyfit of chuckles.So all in all, I would consider Borderlands 3 as Game of the Year (GOTY) material.TL;DR: Deez nuts. Ha. Gotem!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 55.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiralling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Title: "Borderlands 3: A Loot-Filled Adventure That Delivers."Review:As a massive looter shooter fan and a longtime follower of the Borderlands series, I eagerly dove into Borderlands 3 with high expectations – and I'm thrilled to say that it exceeded them all. Gearbox Software has truly outdone themselves with this latest installment, delivering an exhilarating gameplay experience that kept me hooked from start to finish.From the moment I stepped foot on the vibrant, cel-shaded world of Pandora, I knew I was in for an unforgettable ride. Borderlands 3 is packed to the brim with the trademark humor, charm, and over-the-top action that fans of the series have come to know and love. From the quirky characters to the absurdly hilarious dialogue, every moment of the game is infused with the unique personality that sets Borderlands apart from other shooters.But what truly sets Borderlands 3 apart is its addictive looting and shooting mechanics. As someone who thrives on the thrill of finding epic loot and mowing down hordes of enemies, I was in loot heaven from the moment I started playing. The game boasts an insane amount of guns – each with its own unique stats, abilities, and effects – ensuring that no two playthroughs are ever the same. Whether I was unleashing fiery explosions with a rocket launcher or raining down bullets with a rapid-fire assault rifle, the sheer variety of weapons kept me constantly engaged and eager to see what I'd find next.And let's not forget about the co-op multiplayer, which is where Borderlands truly shines. Whether teaming up with friends or diving into the chaos of online matchmaking, the cooperative gameplay adds an extra layer of excitement and camaraderie to the experience. Nothing beats the thrill of tackling tough bosses or raiding enemy strongholds with a group of fellow Vault Hunters by your side.In conclusion, Borderlands 3 is a must-play for any fan of looter shooters or the Borderlands series. With its addictive gameplay, hilarious humor, and endless supply of loot, it's a game that will keep you entertained for hours on end. Gear up, grab your friends, and get ready for the loot-filled adventure of a lifetime. Pandora awaits!

_childDocuments_.review: I know I'm just repeating what every other reviewer has said about this game, but I mean it when I say that the game is incredibly fun to play, but the main story and writing is absolutely awful. If you play Borderlands for the gameplay, Borderlands 3 is a great investment. It's very polished and very very fun to play once you get the hang of it. If you've played the other entries in the series and don't mind seeing your favorite characters steamrolled into cardboard shells of their former selves, then by all means buy the game. But only when it's on sale. It is absolutely not worth the full price.Some executive decisions were made during the process of creating this game that sucked the signature writing style right out of it. If you got attached to the characters in Borderlands 2 and The Pre-Sequel, then you will be sorely disappointed by this game. Lilith is an emotionless punching bag whose lost all of her fire, and Ava is the immature screaming child wailing on that punching bag. Maya brought some light and fun back into the game, only to be literally turned into ash because of the aforementioned immature screaming child. _childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD- The gameplay loop. It's the one thing that offsets the many flaws. If you liked the gameplay of BL1/BL2, you'll like BL3.- Various planets with varied enemies, color schemes, and levels of civilization. This makes for a nice change of pace (and visuals), even if the locations don't exactly come together into one big, epic narrative.- City locations for all of us you enjoyed Opportunity, Old Haven, and Sanctuary.- Writing is closer to BL1 than to the abysmal, trying-too-hard bro "humor" of BL2. Almost none of that poor man's Joker, Handsome Jack; little of Claptrap, and Tina and Claptrap toned down.- More verticality. This makes for more interesting levels (and the return of the jumping puzzle, a la Robolution). It can also be a bit much at times, making the levels a bit busy, target acquisition chaotic, and traversal tedious (you can see your destination, but have to go the long way around because of elevation), but I think on balance, it's just about a plus.- 3 free "creature slaughterdome" clones.- Typhoid deLeon logs. Sure, they're silly, but they're the only exposition since BL1's Tannis' logs where I was looking forward to finding the next one. I guess the voice actor makes them.THE BAD- Even six months in, this feels like an unfinished product. Some keys are rebindable, some aren't. NPCs still do random callouts while you're playing an audiolog, cutting it off (but at least now, it can be replayed from the menu -- you may still miss quest exposition though). Netcode unaccountably seems flakier than in BL2.- Go to Lilith for more exposition.- How does she never learn our names?- Amara's meh callouts. Also, wings > arms. On the plus side, switching between 3 action skills is neat.- For all the new skills in the siren tree, you can no longer build something like "Nurse Maya", with instant across-the-battlefield revives, targeted remote healing with your gun, and so on.- No Doctor Zed.- No Mister Torgue. (Except some boring, generic, and repetitive lines in the wave defense.)- Tannis kinda ruined.- Many new characters are bland ("People sure need their coffee, amiright?", "Jack Light" Katagawa etc.). But since I prefer bland writing to terrible writing, I feel bad even putting that in this section. I just wish we'd gotten Katagawa or TPS-Jack the first time around, rather than having to suffer through BL2 Jack, perhaps the worst game villain in history, first.- When BL2 killed one of the BL1 player characters, I thought it bad judgment, but at least it wasn't "my" character. BL3 has now written out 3 out of the 4 characters I've played in the previous games. Meh. In one case, they didn't just die to protect a universally hated character, it was also implied that despite a lifetime of practice at "their thing", they didn't really understand their action skill, and one of the antagonists exceeds their power level by orders of magnitude almost immediately. Way to spit on the graves. Not cool. Ellie better show up as a playable siren in the next game to make up for it.VERDICTI've kinda enjoyed playing the game with my mate, flawed as it (once again) was. But part of me's like, "I hope this BL3 thing blows over in time so I can get a group to re-run Digistruct."Get at half-price or better if you're a hardcore BL fan and aware of the flaws.ADDENDUMI gotta keep it real. I really wanted to like the game, but it's now two years later, and I haven't even started the DLC. As I said before, I think this game killed the franchise for me. Like, stop giving fan favorite characters ♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths just be edgelords, yo.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 is a game that’s incredibly easy to nitpick and incredibly easy to make fun of. However, Borderlands 3 is also incredibly engaging with its gameplay loop of shooting and looting. First, let me give you the generic spiel about how this game’s writing just sucks because it’s absolutely true. Every time I hear an attempt at a joke (which I’m not given a break from unless I’m fighting) it feels like I’m getting an elbow nudge into the ribs while the writers are winking at me and telling me how funny they are. Having to sit through dialogue where the joke has run its course or the joke is part of the story progression is just irritating. Don’t get me wrong, there can be some funny things in the game, but they’re derived from playing the game rather than having to sit through someone’s haphazardly organized pile of jokes to tell during comedy night at their favorite bar. There’s no point in complaining about the competency of the Borderlands 3 writing though. Not much has changed since Borderlands 2 in that department and you’re pretty much treated as some savior because you’re THE Vault Hunter and you’re just THAAAT BADASS. If you’re going to bring up how Borderlands 2 has the better story, just don’t bother. Borderlands 2 is more competently written than 3, but it’s hard for me to judge since I don’t really give much attention to either story. They're both pretty bad imo. Story and writing aside, what we have here is a very very competent and enjoyable looter shooter with some really gorgeous visuals and some really entertaining gameplay. Coming from a very depressing and lonely experience of playing BL2 solo, there were a lot of core improvements made to modernize and improve gameplay. Borderlands 2’s shooting had always felt a bit lackluster to me, and the philosophy of necessitating cover during the earlier parts of the game never really felt right either. For the variety of weaponry at play when it comes to Borderlands 3, I feel like most of the guns were done just right. Manufacturer identity through each gun has been tweaked in such a way as to give each of them a very defining characteristic. While guns will still fall towards certain archetypes, like SMG, Shotgun, or Sniper Rifle, each Manufacturer offers something valuable to the player by offering perks. Jakobs allows a shot to ricochet on a Critical. Hyperion has shields on ADS. Maliwan is all about Energy weaponry. There’s enough to fill a niche for all sorts of fun experimentation and that really helps with encouraging players to further engage in the gameplay loop to find what best suits them. Movement has also been refined to be up to par with modern shooters. Mantling, Ground Pounds and slides are only 3 small additions, but do much to improve the feel of movement. If your FPS game doesn’t have anything to transform your player’s movement in some way in 2020, what are you doing anyways? It makes movement a much more active and fluid choice. Okay yeah sure, grenade jumping was removed but overall when it comes to fluidity in combat it’s much better.When it comes to content, I haven’t really gotten through to finishing the game yet as I’ve been going through the DLC on my own pace. The DLC however is most definitely a buy on sale sort of thing and I wouldn’t recommend buying it for its base asking price because it doesn’t really feel like it adds much of anything new other than diversity in visuals. What I will say though is that I really haven’t found myself getting tired of the same grind as I was with Borderlands 2 as opposed to 3 when it came to the main campaign. I think that speaks to just how much better the gameplay feels. I know there’s going to be nostalgia-heads saying that 2 is better than 3 in terms of content, and they’re absolutely true. However this takes away from the merits of 3 for just having better gunplay that leads to better encounters overall. To me that matters a lot because that plays into the content you’re paying for as a whole. I didn’t buy the DLC for 2, but again I didn’t enjoy 2 as much as I did Borderlands 3. This game goes on sale now for 50% off. It even had a free trial event. If you want to buy it, definitely pay for it when it’s on sale. That’s all I have to say.

_childDocuments_.review: A quality sequel to an amazing series. I've played BL1 a little, BL2 extensively, and I think they've improved the game in satisfying ways without pay-gating core content. The gun-play is as fun as ever and new customization options keep different playthroughs fresh and interesting. The story, however, feels a bit too ambitious. Plots are disjointed and feel a little forced at times. The game plays more like a series of related DLC than a single cohesive story. Perhaps more appropriately, a single story, cut and distributed among distinct DLCs, each of which could have constituted its own game in the series with more development. I thoroughly enjoyed most of it, but also believe they could have done themselves a favor by focusing plot elements down a bit and expanding upon main story pieces.However, where this entry stumbles on story-telling it excels in world-building. Gearbox really took advantage of the opportunity offered by an interplanetary story-line, introducing new environments, enemies, and characters along the way that really kept gameplay captivating and adventurous. They did such a fantastic job developing worlds and lore for these planets that it's a shame that they're mere footnotes in service of an almost-entirely unrelated story. Perhaps we will see development of these later.

I guess, but I feel Borderlands 2 has much better combat and weapon balance (not to mention a well thought out story). BL3 still looks (graphically) pretty darn good though. I'd prefer to give it a mixed vote honestly.That said, I two issues I have with this game (BL3), and one of which with the BL series itself: Like other entries in this series, weapon balance between weapon types is not great, but for BL3, it's even worse. Pistols are balanced for normal gameplay. Except a lv 4 common pistols deal TWICE the damage of lv 8 Legendary SMGs. And that's not because of any sidegraded parts or anything, which means it's . And since SMGs only have a somewhat faster firing speed, (average pistol fire rate is 4-6 shots per second, for SMG's it's fire 5-8), somewhat worse accuracy, and twice the magazine size, they simply don't compare. So you're taking two and half as many bullets and seconds to kill something with less hit reliability for just twice the magazine? No, that's a waste of gun and a weapon type, as well the time gearbox employees spent making it, and the money spent on the employees making it. In BL2, SMGs weren't quite as bad, but still a poor choice due to damage per shot being a bit too low to be worth while and the firerate not being much higher, and along with the quite noticeable horizontal recoil didn't make it easy to lands hits with the rapid pace of shots when ADS'ing, especially due to with the poor hipfire of guns that the BL series has. Rifles (not snipers) were quite viable, due to being a balanced of fire rate and damage, making them on average somewhat better. Guns that fired more slowly had more damage to compensate, and pistols did a bit more damage than rifles in comparison to thus making them overall somewhat better (or worse) in terms of dps as long as you could hit your shots and didn't mind the slower fire rate or having a semi-automatic trigger. But the game was clearly balanced for rifles with well balanced stats. At least SMGs in BL2 had a class mod for Maya which gave smgs much more respectable damage in exchange for a small accuracy penalty, but this still made them a niche weapon at best.Except BL3 gave rifles the SMG treatment, making them effectively making them just a "reskin", making another weapon type obsolete, instead of just SMG's being total garbage. BL3 has also reduced the firerate of shotguns quite a bit, with firerates being about 1.5 shots per second, rather than the average firerate of 3 that BL2 had. And they didn't give them a damage bonus to compensate for the loss of fire rate ether, so they are a poor weapon overall. The only significant change is that shotguns can ragdoll targets, which means they're now crowd control tools, not the raw damage dealers they used to and should be. My second issue is that there's no weapon transmog. Yes, it kind of seems petty of paper, but hear me out. With the advent of very high quality graphics in games (I mean BL3 looks amazing to me on medium settings), and the fact that the design of some guns simply look way better than others, yet perform poorly in comparison to a gun that is nearly identical in same (ie Brand C's type R pistol compared to Brand C's type R- pistol), and vice versa, means that unfortunately, I can't use that really nice, yet weird looking shotgun (it has a bulge-y barrel that would NOT be considered for good weapon design IRL) unless I want to lose out on a large increase in damage of different shotgun that has a much more realistic design that is identical in terms of rarity and type, but just doesn't look anywhere near as satisfying or awesome. This is mainly due to how different gun parts in the game have different stats, and unfortunately, it seems the more "conventional" and "realistic" looking guns tend to end up with much better stats. With transmog, I could keep the awesome look of one type pistol for the game while I fill Pandora's denizens with lead while having the functionality from a much worse looking pistol that has better stats. And no, modders for the BL series don't have any mods out for such, and I don't think they'd be able to be able to do such ether, as I haven't seen any rekins of of guns. That said, I have seen some  reskins of Maya and a few other BL2 characters you can play with in game with the use of TexMod.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 to me is a celebration of everything the series stands for—excessive loot, outrageous humor, and relentless action. I feel that although it plays it safe by sticking closely to the franchise's established formula, which is both its greatest strength and its most notable weakness, fans of the series will find much to love. I hope that newcomers won’t be overwhelmed by the sheer volume of content and the series' distinct style, which us fans look forward to. That said, it delivers a high-octane, loot-shooting experience that's best enjoyed the way you want to play it – either solo or with friends. Despite some occasional technical issues (which weren’t much at all), its engaging gun-play, diverse character abilities, and vibrant world make it a worthy successor in the Borderlands saga.My Personal Rating: 8 out of 10

It feels poorly optimized even still.  I have stuttering, frame drops, and huge amounts of freezing routinely.  Just now the game crashed prior to even getting to the main menu. _childDocuments_.review: Edit after almost 100 Hours from a player who played every Borderlands game out there with every DLC:In short: Brilliant Borderlands game, with very high replay value. Everything in this game actually made right and proper. The DLCs are spot on and the Mayhem Mode brings new challenge to the table so even seasonable players who will keep replaying this game over and over again will not get bored from walking around like an unstoppable god and actually have challenge while replaying the game. Read the rest of the review for  more details!Lets get it out of the way right away yes the main anthagonists are boring and not fun. With that said Borderlands 3 is an amazing game and as somebody who played every other borderlands game and dlc I can say this game absolutely stands to the standarts. Matter of fact after I replayed the game lots of times I begin to understand why the main anthagonists behave like they do...You even begin to understand annoying Ava...-The story is still fun and will take you on a wild ride. The locations are like the best most fun locations from previous borderlands games seperated into different planets.-The gameplay and gunplay incredibly good. Guns finally look and ressemble realistic guns and they are fun to shoot! Weapons are tactical, effective have cool special effects. Guns were big turndown for me in BL2, somewhat better in TPS and here in BL3 again lots of nice guns like in BL1.-A lot of actions and shooting, especially dont go for the easy difficulty. Begin the game with normal difficulty it is challenging and fun. It begins slowly than towards levels 15-20 there is so much going on on the screen, so much non stop action! But you already trained for it and ready for it, you just automatically react to situation and act! It so much worth it.-Love the new characters! Especially Moze <3 !!! Sexy and deadly, and the idea that she has a mech that she summons! Whaaaaat ?!?!?!? Sick!-Very good soundtrack matching the atmosphere. -Graphics! The game does look stunning. It still has this Borderlands theme, but more graphical and shiny now.-Bosses, finally lots of Bosses that can be challenging and that fun to keep farming and beating them.-Mayhem Mode! This is the best for me. I hated replaying previous Borderlands game where I just run around and slaughter everyone even on Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode. mayhem mode is like an insanity/veteran difficulty that will bring the challenge back in the game. You kill enemies quickly but don't fool yourself you slow down for a moment and they will annihilate you.-Totally reworked badass rank system, where you actually get to improve your character and you will have to do it for the Mayhem levels. -The DLCs this is where this game just keeps nailing...Handsome Jackpot:  is like a return to Borderlands 2 world with all Hyperion Loaders trying to kill you again and the casino heist is mad fun. lots of atmosphere and fun! Guns, love and tentacles: Might not be my personal favorite, but the Ctulhu atmosphere is not bad :)As I said before: A pretty good and solid Borderlands game, if you close your eyes on the stupidity of main Villians and just focus on the action and the fighting its just as good if not better than previous Borderlands game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but it could be better. Since I never play in Coop mode, I never have some of the playability issues some have reported. Initially I had some problems with the game locking up and a variety of odd visual issues. I solved those by locking the max frame rate to 60fps. I immediately noticed the visuals were much sharper and the other visual issues went away. The one problem I have is that after playing B3 I have to reboot my computer to get my internet connection back. Apparently this has something to do with the anti-cheat software they use. However, after locking the frame rate to 60fps, I didn't have that problem. As far as gameplay goes, I prefer the way the fast travel network works in previous iterations of Borderlands. It doesn't make sense for the Sanctuary Fast Travel station to not allow outbound travel. It also doesn't make sense for the various fast travel stations to not allow the player to move to areas they have previously visited. This kills the open world feel of the game. Another odd gameplay issue is that missions don't tell you where you need to go. If you are in Sanctuary, the map always points you to the Fast Travel station, but the only travel destination is Sanctuary. That blows.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun experience if you enjoyed the previous titles. Pretty much delivers what you expect from any Borderlands title; guns, explosions and references to pretty much anything that has been slightly popular. Borderlands 3 does deliver more-so however in it's improved mobility adding a nice feeling slide to the game and the ability to grapple up onto things rather than just jump endlessly at a something until you do as in previous titles. These combined make the whole combat experience feel a lot more fluid and more in like with something like Doom if you want to be up in their faces. Something that the series really needed to make those close combat builds more interesting imo.The setting does feel rather interesting and gives a good look into the wider universe of Borderlands. The story however is pretty average.Overall, I wouldn't pay full price for this game, but it's a great pickup whilst on sale if you enjoyed the previous titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Borderlands 3 on launch on Epic and then again on Steam for half off on the Steam launch. I have about four times the play hours as I do on Epic than I do on Steam with this game, have played all the characters extensively, all builds, and have ran all content extensivley. The late game is currently a complete waste of your time. Gearbox ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game up royally with their Mayhem 2.0 system. The new system increases enemy health by 12500% (not a joke, that's a literal number of hp in the game) on mayhem 10, the highest setting. And with the new farming system that increases the weapon damage with each mayhem level, the difference between a mayhem 1 drop and a mayhem 10 drop is only about 120%. The only weapons that make mayhem 10 viable are some new event weapons. Borderlands 3 has two aspects of it; farming and end-game. Farming for the right gear from story bosses is where you'll spend the vast majority of your time. And it can be satisfying, but once you get it, there's nothing to do with it. Essentially, even before mayhem 2.0, Borderlands 3 is about farming gear so you can farm gear a tiny bit faster. It's a great time-waster, the story is atrocious, but the combat and gunplay, mayhem mode (which is unlocked once you beat the campaign), is good up until around mayhem level 5 or 6. The ability to reroll your different mayhem modifiers makes it so you can make them inconsequencial, which most of them are up to around level 5 or 6. There is no end game and with the direction Gearbox is taking the game, there never will be. It's all about farming gear. And mayhem mode 2.0 ruined everything that made farming bearable.

_childDocuments_.review: I dislike that the ratings system is a binary yes/no determination.  I have mixed feelings about this game, and don't feel that either recommending or not recommending a game like this does it full justice.  In Facebook terms:  "It's complicated."There are several pros and several cons that I feel will make justifying my rating rather difficult without venturing into spoiler territory, so I will just do my best to outline some of the features I liked and disliked without going into too much detail.The game, visually, is stunning.  I'm not running on a toaster, but neither am I running on a top of the line gaming rig, and the visuals of the game are quite amazing, but I suspect they could be even higher quality.  Still retaining the cel-shaded (I *guess* this counts as cel-shading) art style of the first two games, BL3 has refined that style to a much cleaner format that doesn't have as quite a hand-drawn feel as BL2.  This is an improvement artistically, but overall, the art direction is somewhat lacking beyond that.  Yes, you do go to several other worlds throughout the game, but I felt that they weren't really so much distinct planets as they were just expansions of the similar environments that we saw in BL2.  In other words, it felt to me like all the designers did was take the images from BL1 and 2 (and some from Pre-Sequel....*shudder*), polish them up, and then build expansive maps on them, while simply labeling them as separate planets, rather than the expansions that I felt they were.  I don't expect a full open-world experience, but there just didn't feel like enough of a difference between the maps of BL2 and 3 to justify calling them different planets.  The maps themselves, well, I felt that they were too damn big.  I haven't done a side-by-side comparison between the maps of BL2 and 3, but I feel that someone on the design team was a bit too fond of the ridiculously large maps of the Pre-Sequel.  I don't know:  maybe the maps in Borderlands 2 were the same size, but it felt like you could traverse them on foot a lot faster than the maps in BL3.  Granted, the Catch-A-Ride vehicle system makes traveling by foot somewhat of a stupid choice, but I'm of the opinion  that if you make a map interesting enough, you don't need to pad it out simply by making it enormous.  The story also gets some mixed feelings from me.  I've played through the entirety of the main story line once, and find that I'm not particularly compelled to play it through a second time.  I played BL2's main story line through several times with each character (even the DLC characters), and while the  initial surprise of some of the story's twists was gone, I still felt that the story was enjoyable.   This time around, I'm kind of hitting "meh" status, and I don't really have an urge to see what the other three character's abilities and skills are (I played through as the Gunner the first time).  I do feel that I will eventually get through the storyline with the other three characters, but the desire to do so feels like I could easily put it off, and am not losing out if I never do so.As for some of the twists in this particular story, I had moments of "Oh, come on!  What crap!" more often than I did moments of "Oooo!  Neat!"  Again, I don't want to get into spoilers either here or in the comments (not that I expect anyone to have read this far in my review, much less comment on a game that's over a year old - I know how you gamers have short attention spans), so I won't divulge any details, save to say that I was rolling my eyes in exasperation more often than I was grinning with enjoyment.  There was one particular trolling episode that I did enjoy in the later paths of the story, but much of the structure of the plot I just kind of shrugged my shoulders and went "meh".  My biggest issue with the story is the climactic battle: all you end up doing is shooting the final boss down.  Granted, this *is* a shooting game, but COME ON!  You can make a final battle in a shooting game more involved than this one was.  A *supreme* anticlimax.  The celebrity cameos had me going "huh, wonder what the point of  person being in the game is".The new elemental effect (radiation) was an interesting touch, but seemed a little too similar to the Ignite proc that I felt it was a little too close.  Having the slag elemental effect return would have been a nice touch, and having the cryo elemental effect make an appearance was also cool (pun not intended).The loot, while of a greater variety than BL2, made me question just why it was so easy to get Legendary weapons.  Maybe RNGesus was being kind to me during this first play-through, but by the end of the game,  was legendary quality.  This cheapened their importance, I thought.  The point of things being rare is that they are a unique item with an importance that is associated with their rarity.  Making a butt-load of new legendary weapons may be nice in theory, but it tends to lessen the impact of getting one when every new boss seems to drop them like dandruff.Making the eridium store mostly cosmetics and weapons that I could easily come across seemed like a step backwards, though I  appreciate the fact that buying bank and backpack space is simply a matter of purchasing them, rather than scrounging eridium.  The multi-function feature was also a nice addition, but felt like it could have benefited from a bit more fleshing out.  Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game at full price (to be honest, I don't think any of the big AAA company games are worth the price they charge, especially ones run by Randy-Bo-Bandy Pitchford), but if you get it at a discount during the holidays, or midweek madness, or something, then it'r probably worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: The reasoning behind this DLC review is to say that it definitely hit home during this pandemic. The DLC is a show case of meta-gaming and real life issues to be solved for peoples of all differently walks of life. Beyond the endless violence, its a tale of mental struggles and bettering ones self each and every day. _childDocuments_.review: SPOILER WARNINGI have 666 hours in Borderlands 3 at the time of writing this review. I have completed multiple solo playthroughs on normal and true vault hunter mode. I have played through the game co-op with friends during their first playthroughs as well. My experience of borderlands 3 felt like a beta test. If I helped beta test this game for you, then you’re welcome. I do believe that this is my karma for making jokes about the people on the epic game store doing so for me. They did fix most of my gripes with the game; it took them a year and 2 months after its release to do so.The likability of the characters in the story is very hit or miss. The base game story sucks but the game play somehow makes up for it. Looting and shooting is very satisfying. The action skill abilities are fun to use and vary widely. There are quite a few noteworthy side missions and cultural references that are clever and funny. There is a good amount of in game cosmetics including new ways to customize one’s vault hunter’s gear. The game is best enjoyed co-op. Unfortunately bugs like getting stuck in the map after using your action skill ability, story progression blocked by npcs glitching out, and multiplayer lobby stability issues still exist today. IF YOU ARE A BORDERLANDS FAN, get the game on sale. It is certainly good for a run through, especially with friends. It will scratch the itch of wanting more borderlands after so many years. For 30 bucks you will get your moneys worth. It does feel a little empty without the dlc season 1 add ons (stories, weapons, and class mods).IF YOU ARE NOT A FAN OF THE BORDERLANDS GAMES OR ARE NEW TO THE BORDERLANDS FRANCHISE, your time would be better spent playing something else. If you want to experience this game anyway, buy it on sale. I can’t in good conscience tell you that for 30 dollars you are getting your moneys worth.Shadow warrior 2, according to its steam page, was released in 2016. It would be a better choice. I have only played 1.9 hours of it. My friends absolutely adore it. I’ve watched a few lets plays of it as well. The movement feels more fluid than in bl3. Shadow warrior 2 seems to have challenging, interesting and varying styles of boss fights that bl3 REALLY SHOULD’VE HAD. I can safely say despite shadow warrior 2 having less weapons, it has a better weapon modification system than borderlands 3 end game does. I don’t know if the things you slot into your weapons are story progression or rng based, but you can choose what you slot into your weapons. It is easier to cycle between weapons and you can cycle between more weapons than in Borderlands 3.

Maybe Rhys, Ellie and Moxxy are the only ones, who are done better than others.Also do not expect any big backstory revealing except for  and even that is done poorly because IT MAKES NO EFFING SENSE NEITHER FOR BL3 NOR FOR THE PAST GAMES!Forth of all, bugs. _childDocuments_.review: I don't like to write reviews, but I felt I needed to this time. Borderlands 3 is a game with solid gameplay, and okayish story, and somewhat meh characters. This is kind of par for the course for Borderlands games. However, this game is crippled by a number of technical issues. The first is matchmaking. It is dependent on the Shift servers, which seem to go down constantly. This often prevents any kind of online play. The second is its extreme lack of optimization. Certain zones lag, some specific areas in zones lag, lag spikes in combat, etc. No amount of changing the gfx settings has done anything to alleviate any of this. On top of this, their attempt at DX12 was very, very bad and often makes these problems worse. I can play games like Monster Hunter World with no problem, but BL3, even on lowest, will stutter and lag. As far as I can tell, its some sort of issue with how they handle texture streaming. And the final issue...the bugs. There are a lot of them, ranging from minor all the way up to disruptive/crashing. In light of these issues, I just cannot recommend the game until they are fixed.tl;dr - It has good gameplay, but a plethora of technical problems. Would advise waiting until they are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: There are games where the writing will make or break a game. Think of Last of Us or Guardians of the Galaxy. Those are games where the narrative is a big part of its appeal. Then there are games where the quality of writing is inconsequential; because the gameplay can singlehandedly carry the experience. Borderlands is the latter for me. A long time ago, I played Borderlands 1 and enjoyed it, even though the plot was basically non-existent. The gun play and loot grinding was more than enough to keep my interest. The huge improvement in writing quality was a nice bonus to Borderlands 2, and that made it my favorite game in the series, even today. But the writing in Borderlands 2 did not make or break the experience; I can enjoy Borderlands 2 divorced from the narrative. For that reason, I enjoyed Borderlands 3, even though its writing quality took a sharp nosedive from Borderlands 2. Does Borderlands 3's narrative and character writing suck? Absolutely. Is the humor cringey? Yep. Did that hurt the experience for me? Sure. Did it completely ruin the game? Hell no. Borderlands 3's gameplay is a massive improvement over Borderlands 2. Guns look and feel better to shoot. Movement is more responsive. The new character classes are great - though I would've preferred more character classes to choose from. I loved being able to travel to different planets; a welcome improvement after spending so long stuck on Pandora. To me, the gameplay of Borderlands 3 is what carried the experience and that was the aspect of the game I focused on. And its for that reason I recommend Borderlands 3. If you do play this game, I highly recommend you skip any cutscenes and tune out the cringey dialogue; you're not missing anything worthwhile. Just have fun doing missions and grind some loot.

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 offers a thrilling and chaotic experience with its trademark blend of first-person shooting and RPG elements. The game introduces new planets to explore, each with its own unique environments and enemies, keeping the gameplay fresh and exciting. The vast array of weapons and character skills allow for diverse playstyles, encouraging experimentation and replayability. However, some players may find the humor and writing to be hit or miss, and occasional technical issues can detract from the overall experience. Overall, "Borderlands 3" delivers the addictive looter-shooter gameplay the series is known for, making it a must-play for fans and newcomers alike.Borderlands 3 is an absolute masterpiece of a game! From its vibrant, cel-shaded graphics to its adrenaline-pumping gameplay, every moment spent in the Borderlands universe is a thrill ride. The vast array of diverse characters and weapons keeps the experience fresh and exciting, ensuring that no two playthroughs are ever the same. The storytelling is engaging, filled with humor and heart, making it impossible not to become invested in the world and its quirky inhabitants. Whether you're exploring the expansive open-world environments solo or teaming up with friends for chaotic co-op mayhem, Borderlands 3 delivers an unforgettable gaming experience that will keep you coming back for more. Gear up, vault hunters, because this game is an absolute blast. Recomended to play 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, where do I even begin? Where do you even go from here? Over 50 hours invested into a game with such diminishing returns. For all the crap they hyped this game up with it fell flat on its arse in its opening hour. So bad in fact that my group and I called it quits on just the base game alone. By far the most childishly easy entry into the series that offers no challenge, depth, nor reward for anything long term because Gearbox felt like "a million guns" was more important than functional infrastructure.Pro's:- Completely overhauled engine with much cleaner and vibrant visuals.- New places to explore besides boring old Pandora.- Upgraded vehicle customisation.- Some interesting choice driven side quests.- Actual lore, to a degree.- Upgraded controls. Cons:- Appallingly easy combat loop.- Overly complicated and cluttered UI.- Extremely shallow gameplay incentive and design.- Extremely ham-fisted 'comedy'. - Extreme overuse of wacky and zany aspects.- Extremely annoying and irritating characters. - Extremely dumbfounding character choices.- Extremely uninspired and uninteresting antagonists. - Extremely non-sensical plot. - Extreme overload of legendaries, diluting the loot pool.- Extreme lack of any outstanding music pieces. - Extreme over population of guns that feel way too similar.- ClaptrapHonestly, the worst entry to the series by far. There was absolutely no challenge to the game structure, whatever gun had the most fancy fandangled effects was guaranteed to get you kills. It was a game that actually had you, rather than shoot enemies, simply shoot AT enemies, because nearly everything is designed to be AOE or splash which just completely negates any accuracy penalties the guns have. It speaks volumes when the most fun the game ever got was a horde-esque sidequest in an arena that actually threw us into a den of chaos against enemies that actually out levelled us. Because this game suffers just like all the others, in that, these games feel like they were designed for people who have the attention span of a goldfish. Doing everything the game allows you to grossly over levels you. We were thwomping bosses in mere seconds. They were a fizzling, farting, bubbling mess before they even uttered their second voice line. All the while the screen is just constantly flashing and fizzling because everyones gun shoots bunker-busting fireworks displays. By the first hour of the game I had a level 12 shotgun that stuck by my side for far longer than it should have. I had no common/uncommon/rare drops outperform it until 40 levels later. This game seriously has some baffling design choices, besides the cacophony and catastrophic lightshow that is the gunfights, the audio was a hot mess with numerous character lines either overlapping, or just interrupting and cutting each other out. You could never properly immerse yourself in the story unless you sat in only one spot any time an audio cue triggered. To top this off, all the previously established characters now have the IQ of a walnut and make absolutely inane choices. The new characters are obnoxious ♥♥♥♥♥ that just drone into your ear at supersonic volumes because SCREAMING is just all the rage in humour these days. This game seriously tries so hard to pass as comical it's actually pathetic. It's a disservice to all the genuine moments we experienced in the first two.To sit through 50 hours minimum to reach the conclusion we got, and then be told the real "challenge" was just around the corner was insulting. My suspicions arose immediately when the only two difficulty choices you are met with are "Normal" and "Easier".This game was designed by idiots, for idiots, and you can see that as plain as the dust on Pandora with the ludicrous dlc setup they have. Designers cut, Developers cut, doesn't matter which way it gets cut, it's never gonna be a clean one.Most people wanted another serious overhaul much akin to the transformation that occurred between the first and second games. What we essentially got was a volume tweak, a shiny new paint job, and a whole bunch of particle effects that just completely break your immersion because you can't see ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ passed your gun barrel when it fires. The most interesting the combat ever got was when I used the most boring, bland, functional, and sensibly designed gun that actually required me to aim somewhat. What a steaming, convoluted mess of a game. Waiting 7 years for this soiled wetwipe was hardly worth it. I have less remorse purposely giving myself blueballs, because at least I get to walk away with a happy ending. There was absolutely no such pay off for the testicular torture that is the grand experience of this game. Avoid, even on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a free-weekend, so I played a story playthrough, and I have to say, I'm done with this game. I'm not interested in grabbing another toon or engage in any of the higher difficulties or "end-game", in large part to the mediocre story, the unlikeable or annoying characters and the clunky UI. I also don't feel like thowing money at epig or denuvo. So, if you only care for shooting stuff in style and nothing else, pick up this game, you will not be disappointed. If you are undecided and haven't played any of the Borderlands, pick up BL2 instead. Maybe throw some of the community patches on there, "gib" your toon if you want to skip some of the egregious grindwalls and you'll have a far better experience.Shooting stuff is stupid fun, weapons are wacky with lots of BEWMS and EXPLOSIONS and wonderfully designed gore and mayhem! Audio and atmosphere are awesome. Maps are ok and the fighting-areas are awesome and well designed to minimise backtracking. (that does not apply to the quest design however, you're often sent around the large maps with lots of backtracking)To preface, loot'n'shoot games rarely have a compelling story, they don't need to, but what it has to do, is give the player enough motivation and understandging to invest just enough emotions to continue playing. For me, this game fails at this "simple" premise. The story is ok for a 'maniac of the week' and I'm surprised by how tame it is in regards to the anti-SJW outrage that has surrounded this game. I didn't particularly empathise or care for the new characters or their struggles and how they are presented. Plot-holes, lore retcons and reveals are frustrating. Some sidequests are fun and flesh out story archs others are fun allusions to literature or pop culture, but those are too few and far between. Then there are these selfaware meta quests that devolve into meaningless posturing, especially when the game and developers are engaging in the same tactics. I might have cared a little more if this game was the first in a franchise and I weren't a gullible and naive consumer i.e meatsack throwing money. The Tales from the Borderlands transplants in particular were annoying.The actually likeable characters are cast aside to be one-line questgivers, and expendable comic relief are main actors in the story. That's like 16 layers of irony, "Pot Thoughts" sums up what I think of the story overall really well. I was surprised at the science-minigame voiceover and I respect what gearbox are going for.UI and menus are beyond bad, it spans through the weapon selection, to stats, to map, to quest & markers and selection over to "social" features, to the various cosmetic options. What might have been ok in 2009, mildly inconvenient in 2012 is now an utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Basically I've reduced interacting whith menus to a bare minimum, adding abilities and upgrading when weapons didn't deal high enough numbers. For quests and finding my way through the maps I've had mapgenie.io up on a second screen, I just don't give a damn for these types of deliberate obfuscation anymore.I've had no technical issues, game always stayed at 72 fps (manually capped). No screen tearing or fps drops (on my ryzen2700 rx1080 32gb ram and NVME-storage). I've only had considerable stutter, on explosions, entering new areas or opening UI or selecting weapons, basically anything that demanded adhoc asset loading. Sometimes Audio crashed in intensive fights and could oly be fixed on restart, but that was only twice in my playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more Borderlands, what do you expect?The story, especially compared to its predecessors, is really bad. Plenty of retcons, inconsistencies and unlikable characters. The villains lack depth and charisma, making it difficult to enjoy their presence in the story as "the bad guys". In other words, the Calypso Twins are no Handsome Jack. The pacing of the story also feels inconsistent. At one point you're on a planet for a grand total of 45 minutes, then you're on another planet for 6 hours. I could go on about other negatives to the story, but that would include spoilers. There's plenty of videos out there critiquing the story already. Suffice it to say, I don't play Borderlands for the story alone, which would limit the enjoyment the game does offer.Which leads me to the positives! The gameplay is fantastic, probably the best in the series. Every gun feels unique, despite having no red flavor text. Makes you feel as if there's a seemingly endless choice of weapons. There's also a lot of quality of life additions we haven't seen before, such as having access to the Fast Travel network anywhere you're standing, and being able to fill your ammo supply with a press of a button near a vending machine.Overall, I would wait for a sale and not spend $60 on the game. I breezed through the base game in about 20 hours (and I tried to do every side mission, so it'll take you even less time if you choose to skip most of them). Otherwise, if you're a fan of the series, pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let my hours fool you, I left the game open for a good chunk of time, plus unless gameplay is downright terrible I am normally inclined to finish a game and its expansions (or at least most of them).I'll start off on a good note. The gameplay is the highlight of this game, and I personally enjoyed it quite a bit. The level design was done pretty well, there was tons of enemy variety, and the areas were set up in unique ways. On top of that the gunplay is incredibly crisp, the sound effects are perfect, and its just so much more fun to run and gun in this game than the previous iterations (some of which are still pretty good in their own right). I think I enjoyed the combat in this game more than any of the others. The art also looks great, and is pretty much exactly what I expected from the game and its unique graphics.However, the game has plenty of flaws. In terms of gameplay it's just... easy. To start with you have difficulty options unlike the other games: Normal, Easy and... no hard mode unless you beat the game so that you can either restart the game in TVHM or abuse the mayhem system to a bloody pulp to get the best loot for barely any extra effort. Normal is still pretty easy, and if you played the previous games you'll notice how much less you'll be going into second wind or dying outright. The bosses for the most part are laughably easy, with more than I can count on one hand being killed in less than a MINUTE. With the right weapon you can kill some of the harder enemies in one or two hits easily, and in the end you get good loot. Speaking of loot legendaries are incredibly easy to find from red chests and bosses and you're basically assured to find one or even multiple in every area. This effectively makes white and green items completely useless once you're past the beginning levels of the game. Although more of a challenge is presented in the DLCs it is still fairly easy. The difficulty also affects the weight of anything in the story the bosses are tied to.Speaking of the story, boy do I have a lot to say about it. The story is a first-class premium example on why you should never let Redditors make things. It took the beautiful world-building being built up by the other games and launched a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ meteor into it. It is so terrible that it actively distracts from the gameplay enough to ruin any sense of immersion and is one of the worst video game stories I have ever had the displeasure of playing.For starters, many of the characters you know and love from the previous games never show up. At most they might be mentioned in an ECHO log or two, and if you're lucky they might show up in a DLC you have to pay for. The characters that never show up in the base game are:-Axton-Salvador-Fiona-Sasha-GORDYS-Loaderbot-Zed-Gaige-Krieg-Athena-Janeyand more minor characters! On top of this many corporations, even if they have defined personalities which is still a 50/50 chance they do, never show up either. BL3 is drifting in a sea of missed opportunity where it never addresses many of the long-standing questions from the series (it actually just adds more) or expands upon ANY of the endings in other games, besides BL2 kind of. Additionally the game often contradicts current lore as well as lore it builds up on its own and will often leave you dazed and confused if you pay attention to the world at all.The new characters are all terrible. The villains are literal edgy twitch streamers and the bandits are their followers (I wish I was joking). The artstyle may be good but whoever designed the character's looks really needs to never touch character design ever again. Most of the characters look fine but others, especially the new ones, look like they just came straight out of a Starbucks in California. They're bland at best, ridiculously annoying at most, and evoke no reason for you to care about them. Every single character has no development whatsoever including the villains. The best characters are already established in the series and often show up for a short period of time before being totally forgotten about for the rest of the game. The major character deaths that occur, unlike Roland in BL2, are utterly needless, senseless, and only made me hate the villains even more as characters.But the worst part about the game, which makes it impossible for me to recommend this game, is the sweeping, soggy, smelly coat of ♥♥♥♥ over the entire game Randy Pitchford would like to call the series' "charm". I enjoyed the humor in the other games, even if it did get kind of stale at times, and they knew when to have serious moments and spare the comedy. This game cannot go five seconds without some cringy joke assaulting your ears. I am being stone-cold dead serious when I say you will get the same sense of humor browsing the front page of Reddit. The humor in this game is not only abysmal, but it cannot take itself seriously for ANYTHING. The character deaths, the intense moments, it doesn't matter, EVERYTHING is coated in this humor that is honestly worse than any of Amy Schumer's Netflix specials. It doesn't help either when some supposedly huge, intense boss battle ends up taking you a minute or two to absolutely assblast the thing you're up against, or when the reveal of some character or situation about to happen is extremely cliche and predictable. Even when the game finally decides to cast off the Reddit-tier humor for a moment it is extemely cheesy and showcases more of its horrible storywriting.Lastly, would you believe that BL2 had a higher variety of environments? BL3 does have some variety but only deserts, swamps, cities and Eridian areas. BL2 had all this and more in its base game, and BL3 only had Maya's homeworld beside this which was a SINGULAR AREA (The events she ends up involved in later in the story makes this decision so much worse). Going through swamp and jungle over and over on EDEN-6 eventually became a little boring, and I couldn't help but notice BL3 never attempts to go to an area from previous games or even mention them beyond a few voice lines. A small disappointment, but quite noticeable.If you are looking for engaging gameplay, you will be dissapointed. If you are looking for new expansions to the universe or its story I urge you to never go anywhere near this game. However if you truly do enjoy this game and want more, I will recommend the DLCs*. The artstyle is actually pretty unique and you get a much better story out of them, and the gameplay is still good.*except the hammerlock dlc, its pretty gay3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Borderlands 3 ReviewTLDR: Worthy sequel to Borderlands 2 and great addition to the Borderlands Franchise. Highly Recommended especially for fans of the franchise. Do yourself a "flava" and buy yourself the DLC as well. More about that later.Total disclosure, right now, most countries are locked down and thus a lot of us are getting antsy or cabin fever. This is definitely your solution (you know along with doing actual productive things like learning a language or writing a book of course.) Note: If you're reading this in the future, I'm talking about the Covid19 pandemic which for me is ongoing but will, hopefully, be over by the time you read this. I’ve split this review into several different parts, the (current) state of the game, the story, the gameplay, and finally whether you should buy the DLCS.State of the GameAnyway, first of all, this game was probably one of the most hyped games of possibly the past five years when it came out last year in September. I was fairly hyped as well to be honest. Following the mini games on their website, replaying Borderlands 2 as well (more comparisons to this later.) This, however, really died down upon release and I feel like the game struggled a little to live up to said hype. I would reckon that it was because of its limited release. However, that all ended a few months ago when the game was released, to much fanfare, on Steam, the biggest or at least most common gaming platform. With a large discount, nonetheless. I think it not an exaggeration to say that the game has really taken off now. Right now, the game is in a great position, with updates coming pretty much every week and a large patch incoming in about 2 days (from writing).All in all, it’s a fairly exciting time to be playing the game now.StoryFor those of you who don’t know anything about the game, you play one of four glorified treasure hunters and fairly quickly get embroiled in a war with two cult leaders. Luckily, you and your plucky friends can stop these maniacs before their plans of ascendency can come to fruition. There are a few things to note about the story. Firstly, there’s a great sense that you’re part of a big galaxy and that your story does quite matter on a galactic scale. For those who played BL1 and 2, we’ve finally left Pandora even though it still features rather prominently. There are quite a few other planets now, each of them with their own unique creatures and environments. The design of most of these planets is on point and, really helps with the world-building aspect of the story. One of the planets, for example, is basically a Louisiana Bayou with dinosaurs. I also do have to note that even on the meagre moderate to low settings that I’m currently running the game on, the game really does look beautiful.There is one big fault with the games and its in the writing. The writing of the game is such that its very 2019. A lot of the jokes will just not age well and there are others that are just bad. Some of the new non playable characters (NPC) do have quite a bit of potential though a lot of the better ones are in the DLCs. The antagonists, however, are just horrible. They’re modelled after streamers/youtubers who have amassed a literal cult following the world. For some inexplicable reason, they’ve decided that they want to become gods and rule the galaxy? Its never really that clear either that or I just wasn’t paying too much attention. This would be fine if they were a) entertaining or b) just DLC characters. But 30+ hours with these halfwit irritants is really more than enough. I confess that I have not played the True Vault Hunter Mode and this is partially because I really do not want to subject myself to the main campaign again. Especially before the inevitable level increases. The real problem here was that after two games of one of the best villains in video game history (Handsome Jack, a villain who was hilarious and just despicable at the same time), these two are just a plot device really I guess. There are some attempts at twists and turns. Some of which are quite unexpected. Others just fall flat.That brings us to the larger problem of the NPCS. I would wager that they’re completely hit and miss. Some have quite a bit of potential (Clay) or are otherwise interesting (Wainwright Jakobs), others are just play horrible (the antagonists, Ava. For the record, she really is the worst.) Why introduce new irritating characters when you could build so much on other more beloved characters? Yes, I know that the Borderlands world isn’t literally ten people but if you’re going to introduce fan service characters either spend some time with them, giving us cool missions that build them up or just save them for an entire DLC when you can do that. GameplayAs is oft mentioned, Borderlands was probably the first game to combineI would wager that in terms of gameplay, Bl3 is the best in the series by far. Unparalleled among the games. It’s vibrant, hyperactive and, at times, psychedelic. It’s also colourful, sometimes silly and choke a block full of visual jokes which I really enjoy.I do have to give credit where credit’s due and say that the guns are amazing. Every gun has an amazing just feel to it. There are so many different designs and each manufacturer feels unique. There’s a great sense of being an all-powerful wrecking ball that destroys everything in its path. You could say that it can get a bit overwhelming of course but I wouldn’t say that that’s a bad thing in itself.Oh and something that’ often overlooked, but the music is just on point throughout the game, really helping create the mood for whatever little arena or map you’re in.Overall, the gameplay can keep you entertained for hours, days and, I think their plan is, years. It’s incredibly fun to just prance through the little worlds and shoot hordes of nameless bad guys. Should you buy the DLCS?If you’ve read the summary, I’ve started the review with, you’d know that the answer is (currently) a resounding “yes, absolutely.” Other than the obvious part of the guns (more guns! Most of them good! All of them quite unique!). The writing seems to be quite a bit better in the DLCS and the stories are a bit more condensed and a bit more interesting. That is not to say they are perfect or anything but they’re definitely contenders for the best DLCs of all of Borderlands. The environments in the Lovecraftian themed DLC2 (Guns, Love and Tentacles) are probably some of the best. I think the best thing about the first two DLCs is that they are indicative of the quality coming out of the studio. I know its dangerous to speculate about the future but if the developers maintain this or exceed this standard, I’ll be quite chuffed. Now the missions themselves are fairly standard, the usual do this and that, I can’t say that the main campaigns in both DLCs are unique but there is one side mission that does stand out though. Or should I say a series of missions. Its in DLC 2 and its worth buying the DLC for the mission alone. I find that some of the characters in the DLCs are quite enduring with some that I’m hoping that they’ll develop a little later on. The antagonists, however, are not. They’re just there to give you a mission though, they are much better than the aforementioned base game antagonists.ConclusionDespite its flaws, Borderlands 3 is an incredibly fun game that you can play with your friends or by yourself. If you’re a fan of the series, there’s absolutely no way you can give this a pass. If you’re new to the series, don’t be too overwhelmed. It’s a simple concept. Shoot things to get guns to shoot more things to get better guns. Trust me, there’s nothing quite like it. The cost might be a little steep at first glance but the amount of content you’ll get is nothing to scoff at and is an incredible bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is trash, the main antagonists pale in comparison to Handsome Jack from BL2, and Ava makes me want to neck myself. However, in spite of that, the amazing game play more than makes up for it so if you're into looter shooters, do give the game a shot. Post game content is kinda limited tho so do keep that in mind.I only played through as Zane and I can say that if you wanna truly enjoy Zane and feel OP you sorta need to get DLC. From the Designers Cut DLC, you get the 4th skill tree (MNTIS cannon). The MNTIS cannon is the only Action Skill that starts and ends instantly and is very spammable (Ideally, you would want the barrier, STNL, and digiclone to last indefinitely thus never triggering Action Skill start/end anointments). Thus, it pairs incredibly well with anointments that trigger on Action Skill start and Action Skill end. In addition, If you pair this with a fully spec'd out blue tree (Seein' Red is a must for this), your kill skills will be up 24/7. When you consider that Zane only gets stronger the faster he moves and Fugitive from the purple tree literally lets you sprint and shoot at the same time, it really does feel like this skill tree should have been in the game from the start when you're running around at mach 5 tearing through everything (try barrier + redistributor for maximum fun). When it comes to class mods, all of Zane's base game class mods are pretty awful and all the good class mods are behind DLC. Seein' Dead (Handsome Jackpot DLC) is kinda OP with letting you randomly trigger ur Kill Skills with 25% effect bonus and Hustler (Psycho Krieg DLC) lets you 1 shot bosses.  Literally Zane gets turned from the worst Vault Hunter to the best Vault Hunter with the power of DLC, its kinda insane.Overall though, 9/10 game that I can wholeheartedly recommend. Especially if you like looter shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't Borderlands anymore, having pre-ordered both BL1 and BL2 way back in the it pains me to see what this franchise has become.The positives:- When looking at a technical standpoint it's great, it runs buttery smooth, no screen-tearing, all the video options you need and overall it's very optimized.- Lots of build variety with the skill trees.- Some nice QoL's got added which are nice when coming from the older games.- The new character models look excellent, Lilith and Maya for example look great.The negatives:good god where to begin- Probably the biggest issue for me personally is the extreme amount of visual pollution, apparently it got reduced but it's still beyond insane how much clutter there is, from the texture work to the light flashes to the insane amount of explosions, it's a nightmare when trying to look for the enemy or anything really at times.- The horrendous writing and the awful story deserve an award for being the worst I've experienced in the 100+ games I've played, it's laughably bad and whoever is in charge should be ashamed. The characters are unbelievably cringe and just blurt out random XD voicelines half of the time talking about bagels or some ♥♥♥♥.- The audio/mixing is terrible, 90% of the time you got voicelines playing which reduce the sound making you barely hear the music or anything else.- Visually it looks incredibly cluttered, Eden-6 for example just looks terrible with the amount of clutter it has.- The absurd amount of loot you get even when just starting a new character, you don't have to do much and you get showered in legendary loot making you never feel rewarded. There are now pearls or anything to get excited about, when getting loot you won't feel anything.- It's laughably easy, you'll be fine by just playing through the game without doing and side content, check the vendors every now and then for legendaries that are cheap as piss and you're good to go.- The maps overall are bland, some good like Athenas which you visit for maybe 1 hour.- I could go on but this last one kills all the fun, you have to wait every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TIME FOR SOMEONE TO STOP TALKING BEFORE YOU CAN PROGRESS, it's infuriating how often you have to wait for a character to stop yapping before you can progress in the game. Also having to return to Lilith or any character really for basically nothing doesn't make any sense and slows things down.I can name a lot more but what stood out to me is I got little to no positives because there isn't much if anything it does better than the predecessors, Borderlands 2 still is the peak of the franchise and Borderlands 3 doesn't come close.At best this is a 5/10, just painfully average.

The biggest pros are just the polish and feel. Things that sometimes are hard to explain. And some things that you can put in to words, like in BL2 a gun with, say, 50% accuracy would pretty much have a chance of shooting backwards, in BL3, 50% accuracy means there's a distinct deviation but the guns is still very much usefull.  Things like this make the game feel more modern. I can't see myself putting much time in the older games except for quick playthroughs for the story after getting used to this. Most of the complaints I have so far are stupid things that are prolly easily fixed that for some reason are still here, among them are: - Not possible to turn  of map rotation. So if you wanna keep oriented, face north before opening map. (come on, add a option for this, srlsy)- Inventory is sluggish and sometimes abit bugged, the icons are exchanged for a "loading" circular spinning arrow everytime you trash/favourite something, comparing, click and drag are also semi-broke.  It's easily avoided by slow and methodical movements but pretty annoying, gamers wanna click click done. _childDocuments_.review: Going into the game, Borderlands 3 serves as a pretty well-received sequel to the proceeding game, Borderlands 2. It's easy to see the general visual, sound, coop, and overall gameplay improvements to the final product. If you are looking for a sequel to Borderlands 2, then look no further than Borderlands 3. However, one of the most significant difficulties of being a direct sequel to Borderlands 2 is inheriting the pitfalls of the proceeding game.The story is one of the biggest culprit put simply, lacklustre and inconsistent. For the sake of adverting from spoiling any significant plot details, it's reasonable to establish that any amount of effort the player or their allies puts into the game is immediately flushed away as the antagonist gets their way "just because". This struggle is funny at first but becomes cumbersome fast as the player never truly has the upper hand until the very end of the game. Another point of failure is the general scriptwriting of the game though I understand the broad audience of the game may be for a younger audience; the game never seemed to cause me to laugh as the humour stays within this fine line of being utterly inappropriate. I would love to see the team deviate from this line and possibly explore other means of amusement.The gameplay of Borderlands 3 is one of the strengths of the game compared to its proceeding instalment, Borderlands 2. The enemies of the game explore many more forms of attack patterns, general shape, and initiative. The gameplay is much more involved than the previous instalment where the enemies hit much harder on normal with some pushing more towards flanking and ambushing rather than tucking away and firing from a distance. Going off of the issues with the previous section, this is fun at first but quickly becomes quite cumbersome. The battles rarely deviate for long periods meaning, that the only way to induce more pressure is by launching many foes with vast amounts of health, all set to surround the player at once. As you can imagine, this leads to a perpetual pursuit around the stage, acting more on the defensive while anticipating your shield to restore.From my experience in the cooperative, it's mostly a cut-and-dry clone from Borderlands 2 with a few developments such as the introduction of cooperative and competitive styles of multiplayer. There's not much to dissect as the experience is much of what you would expect from Borderlands 2. A vital issue worth noting is that the game does not keep a consistent track record of a guest's mission progression and found areas in the relation of the host's progression; it appears you retain the host's current stage. To bring more perspective, I often play coop as the game is much more fun with many people playing at once. Unfortunately, I disconnected at the end of a play session, when I returned to my campaign, I discovered I couldn't complete the mission as the objective was in an area I have not yet located. This issue led to a total mission soft-lock; the only way to fix the problem was hoping to join a player at the start and replaying the whole mission. It would be kind for Gearbox to add a mission reset feature to fix these soft locks. (valve plz fix)The overall presentation of the game is absolutely marvellous. It's easy to see a whole slew of graphical and auditorial improvements as well as new assets the artists behind this game took so much time to create. However, the art team may have over-focused on the overall theme. Every area of the game is much too cohesive to Borderlands. I was packed with excitement when learning that I would be crossing to new planets to explore what new designs the artists had up their sleeves. When I got to these planets, I didn't feel the slight alienating effect I thought I would feel travelling to these planets. Instead, the areas felt much too grounded into the design of Pandora. Though with exceptions such as Athenas. I could never shake the impression of still being on Pandora.

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever I can say has been said before, and with more detail. The bottom line is this:The game is enjoyable in light bursts. I can play it for a few hours at a time, and then forget about it for a whole year.No, seriously. I've replayed the beginning Pandora section over and over to play with friends, simply because once we get to Sanctuary I've clocked out. The story and characters (besides the classic ones) are too cringe to not be intentional. Nobody talks or acts like this. No Gen Z I know has played this game and went "I relate to that!"It reeks of suits trying to appeal to a younger crowd by going "How do you do, fellow kids?"The gameplay itself is actually solid, and while I find 3 of the 4 new hunters to be annoying/obnoxious, I do like how intricate their builds can get. The guns are varied, to a fault, so you're never sure what you're gonna get.The tonal shift is somehow worse than the one between BL1 and BL2, and maybe even Destiny 2 between Witch Queen and Lightfall. The only saving grace is Lilith managing to still be badass, while also maintaining a straight face amongst a bunch of clowns.Overall, I don't even know if I can personally recommend this game. As a huge fan of the franchise (even the Pre-Sequel), I don't think I can even recommend it on sale. It's 9 bucks right now, and to be frank you're better off just buying BL1 and/or BL2 for a friend who hasn't played them. Or buy a 5 dollar taco bell cravings box, and use the change to buy an extra baja blast.
