_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've "played" about 6 hours so far. I deliberately played in "" because the game crashed or got stuck 3 times during this time and I was more busy listening to Anna and the others. But I'll get to that in a moment. Since I read a little before buying, I already knew that the game is now more open world and actually doesn't play in the metro like the other two parts. That doesn't have to be bad, does it?Nothing has changed in the controls. To play I still need what feels like 20 fingers to be able to somehow operate all functions. I didn't like that in the other parts, but  I don't know what it's like with the controller, I've never tried it, but I am of the opinion that it could have been solved differently or the inventory that you carry around with you could have been divided up or put together differently.The NPCs in this part look much better and more realistic than the ones in the previous parts. There are also new mutants like the beastmen, which at least has convinced me.From the other two parts it was actually clear to me in advance that there would be some speech scenes, cutscenes, stories and conversations, but: Either I watch a scene or I have to run after someone or listen somewhere.Even when I am supposed to fulfill a task / mission, I always have someone in my ear who has to tell me something.I just want to play, nothing more ...Speaking of which, I think it was a huge mistake to get involved in such an apocalyptic drama with a woman.Anna !To be honest, it really gets on my nerves and provokes slight aggression. Apart from the fact that she definitely has the say in the relationship with Artyom and he only seems to do what she says or wants, she just keeps talking, giving commands or having something to whine or complain about.Furthermore, I have the feeling that the game has mutated even more into a sneak game. Even if I run it doesn't last forever because I'm out of breath so quickly, puff and have to run slowly again. In the open world it's kind of tiring and exhausting. Since I don't just have to get from a to b, but in between I always have to go somewhere else, on foot or in a boat that feels as fast as you walk, it all somehow drags on so unnecessarily.At least now I definitely know that we are not alone and that there are other factions and peoples on earth.That was actually foreseeable, only why there was no contact so far was not clear. But we've already solved that. I suspect that in the next few hours I will meet one or the other faction and probably eliminate them. There are still too many people on earth after such an apocalyptic event...Well, almost 4 hours and a few more falls, I've left winter and the cannibals behind and I'm here, hm, well, I think it's summer, but the desert is more likely to hit it, I think. Apart from the fact that everyone else always has a lot to say, she annoys me mostly and extremely ...Somehow I'm bored of the game right now.There are phases in which you are challenged for a moment, be it with the fight against other factions or against mutants, but most of the time I run or drive around slowly to reach my next goal.Before I can do that, however, I'll be sent on side missions with more stories. If it could go a little faster it probably wouldn't be that bad after all.In principle and for the sake of the story, these are also good and expand the gaming experience. Because of the slow flow of the game and the speed, it's really difficult for me at the moment.So, actually I wanted to  today. Unfortunately, I had to find out that due to the last gamecrash yesterday, there are no more save states in the cloud so that I should / have to start from the beginning. Great game, honestly ... Fortunately, the saved games were still in the Steam Cloud, so that I could download them by hand and now can "continue playing" where I left off. Then let's wait for the next one to crash ... I have now returned to the metro. Since Anna is terminally ill in the meantime, she has been shut up for a long time. That's why Miller, her father, speaks all the more now. Worse still, I have to tour with him and no matter what he sees, he knows exactly what happened and has to tell me immediately. Apart from the fact that I am not absolutely not interested in what happened somewhere, at least 20 years ago, I thought, you are quiet when you are on a mission where mutants or other opponents can appear all the time? Miller was really cool in the first two parts, now he's a complete disaster. I wish he was only a third as cool as Miller from "the Expanse" ... honestly.So my friends, I finally managed to finish the game and paid the ultimate price and saved Anna.The whole time I thought about whether I should rate the game positively or negatively. Despite everything that annoys me so much, I decided to rate the game positively.Basically it's a good game and (almost) ties in with the other two and I just think who played the other parts should still play that because of the whole story.It's a shame that the game often crashes on DX12. There is some information and help on the various game crashes on the net (if necessary).For my part, I would have been happy if it had been possible to skip the cutscenes and all that I didn't want to know, see and above all hear. Well, I've got it and think about whether I will still do all the other things like collecting postcards, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: takes players on an unforgettable journey through a beautifully crafted post-apocalyptic world, offering a fresh and immersive experience that captivates both newcomers and long-time fans of the series. Developed by 4A Games, this enhanced edition serves as a remarkable upgrade to the original game, showcasing stunning visuals and improved gameplay mechanics.One of the standout features of Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition is its breathtaking graphics. The developers have painstakingly created a visually striking world that is both desolate and hauntingly beautiful. From the dark, claustrophobic tunnels to the vast, open landscapes, each environment is meticulously detailed, bringing the post-apocalyptic setting to life. The enhanced lighting and ray-tracing effects further enhance the atmosphere, making every moment a visual treat.The story of Metro Exodus continues the narrative of the previous games, following the journey of Artyom and his companions as they seek a new home in the devastated Russian landscape. The game successfully maintains a sense of tension and desperation throughout, as players encounter various factions, mutants, and environmental hazards. The well-paced storyline keeps you engaged, with emotional moments and unexpected twists that add depth to the characters and their relationships.Gameplay-wise, Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition introduces a more open-world approach compared to its predecessors. Players are given more freedom to explore the vast environments, complete side quests, and scavenge for resources. This change in design adds a sense of exploration and discovery, allowing players to make choices that impact the story and the world around them. The survival elements, such as managing resources and maintaining weapons, add an extra layer of challenge and immersion.Combat in Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition has also received significant improvements. The gunplay feels more refined and responsive, making each encounter thrilling and intense. Players can choose between stealthily eliminating enemies or engaging in all-out firefights, adding variety to the gameplay. The AI has also been enhanced, making enemy encounters more dynamic and unpredictable.While Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition offers an exceptional gaming experience, it does have a few minor drawbacks. Some players may find the pacing a bit slow, especially during the game's early stages. Additionally, occasional technical issues and glitches can detract from the overall immersion, although these are relatively rare and not game-breaking.In conclusion, Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition is a must-play for fans of the series and anyone seeking an immersive post-apocalyptic adventure. Its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and improved gameplay mechanics make for a truly unforgettable experience. Despite a few minor flaws, this enhanced edition showcases the dedication and craftsmanship of 4A Games, solidifying the Metro franchise as one of the best in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the publishers decision to move this game to the epic crap store the game itself is incredible. The developers really poured their heart and soul into this game and it is evident all over.The game stays true to metro in every way starting from the opening sequence which is more linear, to its semi-open world sandbox levels. The game constantly keeps you uncomfortable (depending on the difficulty you play on. I am currently doing a hardcore run through.) and there is a solid variety between clostraphobic and open settings.The open sandbox areas are incredible. You can truly get lost just exploring, fighting, creeping, and living in these large areas. The more linear missions are standard metro excellence as well.Some cons:The open levels don't really let the player know what missions will trigger the player leaving the level. I know it might be "gamey" if they prompted the player but it would be helpful. In the first open area I had spent probably 5 hours in the level and only explored about half of the map before completing a main story mission that triggered leaving the area.Another con is there are a few bugs but this is very minor for me. None have been game breaking and I have not encountered many bugs at all. The ones I have encountered have been graphical bugs like some enemies clipping for a few seconds etc.Really those are the only cons in my opinion. In closing this game is incredible. 4a have dumped their souls into this game and I can't recommend it more. I am very glad I pre-ordered it on steam!

_childDocuments_.review: I Highly recommend this game!If you have followed the metro series and enjoy the work this studio puts out this game is no different.I would say it is an even better experience than everything prior. This game has a mad level of immersion and feel to it.It has so many lovely details, quirks and unique tools that elevate the experience immensely.It has a few bugs and kinks here and there as always happens, but most of them have already been ironed out and but the overall experience of this game has so far been incredible.It has a really good story, great atmosphere, several smaller open worlds that makes each location unique and challenging in different ways.The customisation of your weapons and tools brings along a great flexible and adaptive game-play that forces you to change up your setup to match the situation regularly.Despite all the controversy surrounding the launch this is a fantastic game that I think anyone interested in story drive fps/single player experiences should try. I feels like a contender to game of the year to be truly honest.All stalking/exploring/shooting/surviving/scavenging/interacting with a beautiful and meaningful story.For the best experience possible, play through the recently revamped Metro: Redux and Metro: Last Light prior to playing this edition. ++++Story ++++Graphics ++++Immersion ++++AI ++NPC ++++Gameworld ++++Weapons ++++----Fairly slow controls (immersive but stiff at times) --Whole Epic store debacle ----A few bugs and crashes -Can sometimes start in windows screen without a way to change back to fullscreen ---No volume control buttons work in-game --No Tab out possible without ctrl+alt+delete and open task manager. --

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD-A crisp chill perturbs the leaves of the auburn trees. A single string of golden light caresses the bolt shaft, the usual shimmer muted by a delicate crust of dirt, invisible regardless, through the cracked scope. The target, a curious individual, covered tip to root in a motley of dried brush and bramble, stands as if to sniff the surroundings. You observe it's absentminded ambling with a stately gaze: it appears the target is as bemused by the forest as it is awed by the sunset. The cool, rough finish of the spring trigger glides pleasantly over your finger, beckoning you to commit the shot, to free the bolt from its tensioned cage.A deep throaty roar sends tremors through the very earth! The bolt flies wide and dives for the river as if dying of thirst. The forest dweller, abandoning all pretence of injury or innocence, starts and sprints into the nearest cave. You curse silently as a thunderous pack of wolves force you back into the tree hollow. Watching as they zealously rip and tear the virgin foliage asunder, you notice a flash of light atop the opposite cliff. A mirage? No, it repeats in a pattern. Could it be?The long-awaited third chapter in the Metro saga has arrived! It does indeed boast much larger worlds and vastly improved visuals (even over its predecessors), while sticking true to its brand of rich, driving, environmental storytelling. It feels as though the series has evolved to the next plane of narrative gaming. In many ways, it feels more engaging and genuine than the best AAA titles of today, and that is saying far more than something.The devs have outdone themselves in a big way, with a world that lives and breathes around you. Every character, human or beast, has a life and routine to follow and a story to tell. The story beats unfold themselves seamlessly around nearly every corner. The atmosphere is palpable and ripe with just the right mixture of fear, apprehension, dread, sorrow, rage,  mirth, hope and joy as each situation prescribes. This is one that you can lose yourself in without even realising it.Whether you choose to indulge in the modern Raytracing (Dare I say it?) paradigm or not, the worlds in Exodus are drop dead gorgeous. Filled with disarming weather effects, lifelike (albeit mutated) beasts, meticulous design details and far too many secret crevices, it cannot be played through only once, if you hope to experience it all. Every vista is bursting with visual splendour that both calls you forth with awe and demands that you trade haste for curiosity. Indeed, no matter how much you might pride yourself as a speedrunner, Metro Exodus, evermore than its progenitors, commands your explorer's spirit. Period.THE BAD-This is where things get serious. The game has been publicly available for two years now and it still suffers from some, not insignificant, freezes, crashes and heavy frame drops in places. It also occasionally fails to trigger story beats, which often requires you to reload a save in order to progress. Part of this may have been my eagerness to play on a new generation of hardware with drivers that may have literally been born yesterday, but these issues did persist (at a noticeably lower frequency) well into my binge - I... I mean playthrough!This one has been well documented, so I'll be brief: Metro Exodus was one of the original 3 games to utilise first-generation RTX tech, and while it certainly pushes the lighting fidelity to unprecedented heights, it failed to allow for DLSS at standard resolutions. This may have been a limitation of either the game, or possibly, the infamous Nvidia drivers themselves. Either way, it does diminish the experience of the technology to the player, without logical reasoning. At time of writing, an update to DLSS 2.0 and Raytraced reflections is on its way, so I'll definitely be taking a look when it drops for PC.THE VERDICT-Metro Exodus vastly outstrips its predecessors in every way: The levels are far larger and reach a level of detail and fidelity most games struggle to achieve even today. In true Metro fashion, it provides a compelling narrative, lifelike characters and living environments.While it does deliver on its promise of a rich, meticulously crafted world, the experience is inconsistent. Stability issues have slipped through the cracks which, if encountered, will break your immersion, if only briefly.All of this eye candy does demand a lot from your system, though, so many sporting older hardware will need to make some settings sacrifices that they didn’t have to on other titles of the day. Something to note before jumping in.With all of that in mind, Metro Exodus is a necessity if you've already played, or watched, the previous games. For those who haven't, you'll definitely get more from the game's lore and character development, if you go back to the older titles first. That said, it's still an excellent standalone experience that imparts what you need to know about the world as you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this the way the game was supposedly meant to be played, ranger hardcore mode.At least don't if you actually want to enjoy the game, since it disables quicksaves.The autosaves are inconsistent as all hell and you will often continue for what varies between 30seconds to an hour before the next autosave, and usually leaning on the 5-10 minutes side.You need quicksaves to actually have fun playing this game, the autosave system is terrible.It was bad but bearable until the forest mission attempting the "forest child" achievement.The last autosave I got is the cave. Then, I have to listen to 2 guys talk for like 5 minutes so that 2 other guys start to talk for 5 minutes, then if I get spotted at all (and enemies sometimes seem to just see you through walls/floors), you get to restart the whole process over of waiting 10 minutes before your next try. Lots of fun.Every time I think, "Wow this game is great!", the glaring issues rear their head and pull me back into a pit of suffering. The frustration of this game and loss of progress pales tenfold in comparison in 2033 and last light, despite being newer and seeming more modern, but with a save system even worse than the old games. Playing this game actually gave me a stress headache and I've had to stop playing out of rage due to bugs & saves several times, not difficulty.Allow quicksaves in rhc and the main problem goes away, just a suggestion. That system exists for a reason, and it isn't added challenge when the saves are this bull, it's just wasted time.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro 2035 is damn near my favorite Atmospheric FPS serie ever. This time they tried the "OPEN WORLD" formula but did they succeed ?:, many said this is one of the only game pulling an unreal engine 5 type of performance on Unreal 4, and they arent lying! Maxed out; the lights, particules, smoke and so on, are really, really well done. And all of that with excellent performance on a good PC. (RTX3070ti / i5 12600k 4.2ghz / pcie4 SSD / 4x8gb DDR4 3200mhz), Metro keeps its truely unique aesthetic with litteral tons of attention to details. Recharging the flashlight to make it brighter, pumping my tikhar rifle to send those pellets at deadly speed, wiping the gas mask, patching it with a piece of cloth in an emergency, GOD I SWEAR I LOVE THESE LITTLE QUIRKS AND FUNKY MECHANICS SO MUCH !!!, every sound is near perfect, satisfying, makes sense. Don't care much about music but the SFX ? Omg, great stuff ! are top notch.. , the 2nd act in the sandy desert feels weird in the serie's context but that's what they were going for. The game picks back up after that, but the middle part of the game feels a bit out of place for what you'd imagine a metro game to be like., specially in the caspian sea level.  Even on a blind hardcore difficulty 1st playthrough! Overall, exiting the metro to get back up to the surface was one of the best aspects we lost with this open world formula.  but you're left with the impression that they missed the boat on what they could have done. An ideal open world Metro game should take place in a big moscow like city, with more explorable devastated buildings, landmarks, covered in that eternal snow, less sun, less desert. I know to make a game as visually polished as this one, you have to respect certain limitations but I just wish they'd stick more to the original look of the first 2 games.:•  campaign : . Starts fantastic with a real moody underground clean up with your flamethrower, then a way too long narrative sequence kills the rythm, I wish the entire dlc campaign was more about burning everything in dark gloomy underground tunnels but no, they tried the typical "learn more about the main plot through someone else POV's" of which I don't really care much. Just let us burn more stuff next time ok ? ;p •   campaign : . Really good all throughout, less story focused, more exploration based. Perfect DLC campaign to me !

_childDocuments_.review: The story is engaging, the switch from a linear game to an open-world one felt natural. All the characters are incredibly human and even likable (Even Artyom on loading screens.) So why the thumbs down? Two reasons: First, the crafting system. While not strictly  per se, it's an unwelcome change from previous metro games where you used ammunition as currency. Balancing your ability to deal damage against purchasing much-needed supplies. It's swapping something wholly unique for something everyone else does. It's a downgrade in every sense of the word and I find myself hating it more and more due to the following reason.The bugs. Randomly getting softlocked due to inputs not registering. Controls refusing to update. Filter time spiking down to zero in seconds rather than minutes. Hits just not registering. Guns jamming whilst fully cleaned. Frequent freezes for seemingly random reasons. Enemies detecting you through walls. Constant save corruption.Functionally, the game is a mess. Metro: Exodus is an exercise in form over functionality. The game can have the best story, the prettiest world and some of the most compelling characters, but all of that is naught but ash when the game itself plays like absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Note that I am not actually saying "don't buy it's a bad game", in fact I think it's a pretty good game but there's a few things about it that rubbed me the wrong way. I'll give an overview with possible minor spoilers but avoid major spoilers.First, the gameplay and movement is very clunky. It looks really clean but it actually handles like a truck. I also don't like how the inventory/combat/regions work. You'll be crawling around the map and exploring (it has limited open world segments as well as linear segments) to collect a handful of gear upgrades, gun attachments and the 2 ubiquitous resources that you can turn into anything. But you really only need these resources to craft more ammo/medkits/repair that you use up by searching for them, and most gear upgrades are inconsequential. You can buff the weapons up, but then at one point you just lose all your gear you built up! So overall the entire inventory segment of the game seems pretty wasted.Which is the next issue, is that as a metro game it has a karma system to get the good or bad ending. Now the way this game operates and portrays people and the situations it puts you in, you should really be gunning down most people unapologetically, right? I mean if they're hostile and trying to kill you, and they're cult wackos or slavers or bandits it should be no problem to kill them, right? WRONG! BAD ENDING! The way they implemented this was horrible and feels extremely forced. "Oh no, you didn't show mercy to the slaver scum that tried to kill your whole crew! Oh no, you knocked out some forest weirdos!" It's even worse when an ENTIRE REGION in the game forces you on this path of, "oh you gotta sneak around and can't engage anyone or bad karma". They also take your gear away for this part as a sort of *hint hint* thing to say "no killing". But it makes this entire sequence way less fun than it should be, and it's still one of the highlights of the game. And the game seems to equate nonlethal takedowns with lethal force, which is all the more annoying.And the last problem is, it's really not very true to the metro series. It's more open world style and takes place... not in the metro. The story and characters are not all that interesting, with a few exceptions. Many plot points feel forced or just nonsensical. The more funny and gallows humor side of the series is almost totally absent here, with only a couple nods. And the entire story just has no emotional impact until the ending sequence. Overall, it's a pretty good game especially by modern standards, but it's bogged down in many aspects (including some technical problems like crashes) and is a pretty weird (presumably) ending to the metro series. I'm mainly being contrarian with my downvote but I'm pretty annoyed having finished the game, which had more generic preachiness about "oh religion bad" and "blindly trusting military authority/ charismatic leaders can actually turn out horribly!" than any actual interest in the dialogue or story.

_childDocuments_.review: The only case where you should buy this game is if you're a fan of the series.This is not a well made game. _childDocuments_.review: OverviewMetro Exodus is the third installment of the acclaimed series, inspired to the books of Dmitry Glukhovsky, and set after the events of Metro last Light. Once again impersonating Artyom, players will soon leave the cryptic tunnels of the Moscow Metro to journey on through the entirety of Russia, ending up in a variety of places ranging from deserts to lush forests - accompanied by Colonel Miller and his elite Spartan team. What initially begins as a daring escape soon turns out to be a journey for survival, as unexpected turns of events one after another come crashing down on the squad.🟩 ProsIncredible visuals with excellent art direction.Realistic, satisfying and unforgiving combat system on higher difficulties.Meaningful exploration with many secondary locations.Excellent narrative and character building.Overall good variety of content, situations, enemies and tools.🟥 ConsKarma system, which determines the ending, was reworked in a bad way.In Ranger Hardcore mode, Autosave frequency is inconsistent and can lead to significant progress loss.Rating: ExcellentClick here for the complete Rating ChartExodus' visuals are amazing, possibly the best available on PC to this day. Each environment is recreated with masterful art direction. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterStarting with the good points, the strongest feature of Exodus as it was with the prequels, is the atmosphere and world-building, which deliver an uncompromisingly realistic take on the nuclear post-apocalypse. This time it's not confined to the cramped Metro tunnels, but shows in full the entirety of Russia's wastelands, and does so flawlessly. Fighting any kind of enemy on the higher difficulties is a tense and unforgiving affair, where all but the weakest attacks mean certain death for both yourself and most enemies.This realism is complemented by accurate gunplay and good variety of murder tools to use. Exploring the wastelands is not only spectacular but also worthwhile, as every map contains a bounty of secondary locations often hiding unique upgrades for Artyom's suit and weapon mods. They will make your life easier once acquired. The narrative and characters stay true to the excellent book series and do not disappoint in the slightest.There are however a few dents to an otherwise flawless execution. The Karma system has been reworked and forces players to take on the majority of situations with complete stealth, without also killing anyone in order to get the good ending. This goes as far as penalizing you for killing someone that shot first and is openly hostile, while the consequences will influence your companions' very lives as if some "higher power" was there to punish you - which makes no sense.Overall, Metro Exodus remains an excellent open-world FPS that delivers the quality already made famous from the previous chapters, at the same time enhances the gameplay in new ways bringing it to a new level that surpasses the previous ones in almost every department. It took me around 25 hours to finish the game on Ranger Hardcore, while exploring thoroughly every map and completing all side content. For the price of 40€ and excellent quality, I can recommend buying at full price.Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out Tamaster's Review Archive to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.Weapons make up the lack of variety with extensive modding possibilities. Most parts will be found while exploring secondary areas. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterIn-Depth Breakdown🎮 Gameplay AnalysisGameplay is divided into Exploration, Character Management, Quests and Combat.ExplorationIs performed on foot most of the time, except in a particular map where there will be a truck at your disposal. Ziplines and boats are also used sparingly to traverse otherwise impossible paths. While exploring, keeping an eye out for mechanical and chemical components - both used in crafting - is one of the primary goals, as you'll need them to craft supplies. Of course you can also find already made ammo, medkits and filters, but that's a more rare occurrence.Certain specific places hold unique modifications more or less hidden, and this is what makes exploring every corner worthwhile. A global map will display your position and all the discovered points of interest, highlighted on the map by using the Binoculars on a high place. Safehouses are sparingly set around the world and they can offer a safe refuge to wait night or day, craft at the workbench and more importantly save the game if you play Hardcore. There is no fast travel.Character ManagementCan be done on the fly with the portable workshop in your backpack, or in a more complete manner at a stationary workbench in a Safehouse. You will be able to modify any of your weapons with previously acquired mods at any time, as well craft simple ammo types such as arrows or steel balls, medkits and filters. More complex crafting requires a full bench and that includes changing your suit upgrades, crafting bullets and as well throwables like grenades, cleaning weapons to prevent malfunction.QuestsAre not numerous in the game and usually are about retrieving a specific item for one of your travel companions or another character. They do not always award anything other than achievements or Karma, but still they are worth doing for the sake of storyline and to explore new places.CombatIs one of the most consistent elements of the experience and at least on the higher difficulties, is a brutal and unforgiving affair where even just one shot can instantly kill you, as well as enemies. Ammunition is fairly limited, while grenades and throwables are powerful bit very expensive to create - using all your resources, stealth as well, is key to prevail against overwhelming numbers. Nothing prevents you from going in guns blazing but on higher difficulties it's a good idea to take out at least some enemies silently before doing so.Foes range from your average bandit with a shotgun to nine feet tall abominations with the strength of twenty men, passing from mutated shrimps and venomous giant worms. Each foe has strengths and weaknesses for you to exploit, for example most animals will be scared by fire or your vehicle. Human enemies are definitely smart and use tactics such as flaking, cover and grenades to overpower you, other than having swift reflexes and excellent aim - on Hardcore at least. Being accurate, fast and conservative are the pillars of Metro's combat.Not only humans, but also all kinds of beasts mutated by radiation will be your enemies. Some of them will act as powerful bosses. A Screenshot of Metro ExodusBy: TamasterTechnicalPC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4Critical Problems: None.Optimization: Resource usage is within expected parameters for the quality, no problems to report.Performance: The game runs without issues in 1440p, 85Hz on Ultra settings.Bugs: Key rebinds do not work properly for certain keyboard configurations.Other issues: Save system on Hardcore difficulty has frequency issues, might be a bug, unconfirmed.Final ThoughtsMetro Exodus is definitely a worthy successor that expands the prequels' gameplay, taking it to new heights, but not without some drawbacks. Fans of the series and those who like atmospheric games will not be disappointed.

anything.Artyom listens to about 30 minutes of unskippable dialogues in the first hour of the game, and won't speak a single word, not even nod or shake his head.The game looks above average in terms detail when you get close up to things.Since there are so many forced dialogues and unskippable cutscenes and such, how do they hold up?well, you might enjoy them if you're drunk.dialogues are very _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Not a great story and clunky game mechanics. Difficult to immerse into. Some good 'oh ♥♥♥♥' moments though.I bought this game thinking that it would be a good continuation of the previous ones. However this has not continued the story quite as well. The books were an excellent read but this game feels a little hollow and it is difficult to motivate myself to play it. I think because this is not following one of the books it's not as immersive and kind of relies on your knowledge of the books to stay attached to the main character, where as other similar games you become attached to the character because there are elements of customisation and personalisation alongside character development.Most of the conversations that occur between characters I want to hear but it feels more like a chore. The dialogue doesn't flow and there are short pauses between characters replying to each other that make it feel drawn out. I'll probably update again the more I play but that may take a while.....The game play feels like it is trying to be really gritty and immersive but is actually just achieving clunky. Your character model gets caught on so many different things that mean you mostly bump your way over terrain to find the flat parts. The 'vehicles' (kayaking especially) feels just as clunky with the combat elements punishing you for the poor design as you get stuck half the time. Don't get me wrong, its a good idea and I see how they are trying to make it feel like a real kayak but it just achieves it in a very clunky manner. The combat is pretty good but again doesn't feel like it flows quite as well as in previous games. The character movement impacts on this feeling a little clunky. There are some classic 'oh no' moments where you've accidentally alerted everyone and it is fun but the fun seems to be a bit of an exception rather than the rule.The 'health indicator' is actually just quite annoying. This is probably because most games have conditioned me to see the edge of the screen going red as recently taken damage with it slowly going back to normal. Where as in metro it stays bloody which just feels more like a niggling distraction than a 'my character is injured'. I'm not saying a health bar would be any better but maybe the character having blood on his hands or wiping wounds or something may have been better. Like i said, the current 'edge of screen red' is just an annoyance in my peripheral.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5 / 10 ( 8-8.5/10 if they fix the numerous bugs ). A great game that I will certainly play again. Depending on who you ask this could be the best or the worst metro game to date so opinions are varied. Personally don't think it is better than the previous 2 games, but it is certainly worth playing. Most of my issues with it come down to personal opinion or ( i think fixable ) bugs but some things just felt average. Pros:- Graphics are great ( though heavy on your system so be sure to have decent cooling )- Nice variety of maps- The story was solid but not as good as previous games - On the spot crafting was a nice addition- The unmarked side missions gave areas a bit more back story and never felt like a chore. You can skip them without problems but some do impact the main story.Minor complaints for elements that are generally good:- Audio was generally good though I found that the audio certain areas not as good as it was in previous games as I found it lacking atmosphere that the audio is often responsible for. Audio had some bugs in some areas too but that could be due to the fact I turned on the Dolby Setting.- Didn't like some new creatures like the "zombies".- Some elements felt a bit unpredictable which could result in annoying one hit deaths ( at least on hardcore difficulty ). Luckily the new save system avoids losing a lot of progress with the game generally auto-saving every 3 minutes. - New save system, while in a way a great addition as you never lose much progress, it removes any real feeling that a wrong move might lose a lot of progress and that feeling of stress or panic that might come with it. It does change how you would play the game in a minor way. - Personally felt that many area's didn't have that metro vibe I was hoping to find. I think peoples wish for more open areas have not resulted in more enjoyable maps. Other people really loved those so its really down to personal choice.Cons:- Bugs. So many different ones. From failing to start to enemies shooting through walls to screen overlays being smaller than the screen and human enemies that couldn't be killed with stealth and failing to start sometimes. My biggest immersion breaking bug was that adjusting the FOV ( no ingame slider ) resulted in screen overlays being smaller than the screen and thus looking buggy. So like the binoculars or damage overlay would not fit ( aka be smaller than ) the screen as well as some others. - Save system: While quick save is a nice addition, the automatic saving is buggy. It can result in horrible situations where it saves while you are being attacked. In some cases people have had to restart the level as the save game was unusable.- AI isn't too great. While it wasn't perfect in other games I feel the AI had more issues in this game. In one specific situation the AI said they saw me, but they never even came to attack me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've ran into a bug that when you load up your save game, the interface (HUD) is broken. You cannot bring up your weapons, gas mask, light or interact with anything. I did some research and this bug has been in the game since the start (last year) and has never been fixed by the devs. You can fix it by restarting the chapter you're on but doing so, resets your weapons, gear, and the amount of supplies you had. I went from having around 2,000 of both supplies and when restarting the chapter, I had about 100 of each. This happened when I got to the "Caspian" level.This is the best looking Metro game and I really love the gun play in this game but this bug really is a game breaker for me. If the devs don't fix it, I might just not finish this game.Edit 1: The official Metro twitter did tweet out that they are aware of some in-game bugs and do plan to release a fix for them but the COVID-19 virus is delaying them to do so.Edit 2: I decided to completely restart my playthrough and see if it was going to bug again. When I got to the "Caspian" level again, I did NOT bug out and I still had my weapons and materials. So it seems to be either somehow triggered or it was just bad luck and something broke in my save. Either way, It could still happen to you so just keep this in mind when purchasing this game.Edit 3: Finished the game and both DLC's and without the few bugs I had, this was a fantastic game to play through. Story was good and the graphics were great. Almost got all the achievements but one of them requires beating the game on the hardest difficulty which I could do but I've played through it two and a half times already so maybe in the future I'll finish it off. I've also changed my review to recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm punching the "Recommend" button so hard I think it's gonna be stuck and cannot be undone (and I didn't  just do that because I'm listening to Jerry Cantrell's new song [Vilify] while writing this review — I promise). In any case, I'm pretty sure everyone in my contact list heard the noise I just made. One of them, by the way, told me to go to bed yesterday when spotted me out of bed playing "Metro: Exodus". What am I supposed to say? You, mere mortals, don't understand me — I mean, anyone in this review section giving thumbs up. I have new missions in life: save Anna, my beautiful wife, defend my train, sneak past ghouls and rescue teddybears for Russian kids. (Hear that, Soldy?).Ok, so what's in the game that's making me as zombified at night as the ghouls I had to sneak away from in this vast snowy wasteland? Listen to Little Bran and take notes:- Tons of games are known for magnificent gameplays or graphics, but few satisfy you by just letting you BE there. Yeah, just be. Just exist. Feeling the environment, the noises, the snow, the ambience. Up to this point the game already deserves a thumbs up, and I'm not even talking about gameplay and graphics. YET! The devs wanted to make you believe and FEEL you ARE there, left behind, hopeless, walking, crawling or just allowing your senses to do the work for you.- Graphics? What can I say? I forgot how many times I dropped my keyboard, left my mouse and just stood there, drolling. One thing is for sure, if Neo was fooled by Matrix, this is another level even for him. - Gameplay? If doing nothing wasn't immersive enough, the devs took a good look at the mechanics. If Metro: Last Light was amazing as f00ck already, they perfected the moves even more. - Difficulty? THE MORE YOU DIE, THE BETTER YOU GET. Mark Little Bran's words: the game WILL NOT give you a moment of breath, for every moment, event, is gonna lift you outta your chair. Playing in hardest difficulty is simply outstanding, with a total of zero seconds of boredom. Every time a freakin' monster shows up is a WHOOOOOAAAA moment, where you scream of excitement. _childDocuments_.review: Post-apocalyptic games may have been done to death, but Metro Exodus still manages to generate a new spin on the genre, due at least in part to its uniquely Eastern European worldview.It's a fine game too: beautifully crafted, intelligently placed, rich in terms of story and endowed with gameplay that is both satisfyingly varied and nicely fettled. Sure, it doesn't break much new ground (although its weapon-customisation system will surely be copied), and there are those who will argue that, format-wise, it's a throwback.But if you like your shooters to tell the sort of story you would enjoy in a movie, and to ooze distinctive personality, you should find it very satisfying. If you're looking for a multi-player romp, however, then you'll need to look elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game!!! Just completed for the 2nd time a few moments ago... what an absolute masterpiece!!!One of the best story driven FPS ever made!!!Other game developers could learn a thing or ten about game design and depth of lore from this game!!!!!!!Brilliantly crafted characters, deep emotional story and dialogue, beautiful and dramatic landscapes, a huge, exciting and emotional rollercoaster of a journey, I would recommend to anyone that loves gritty post-apocalyptic adventures!!!So much detail everywhere, everything feels logical, real life, organic and decayed, wild and desolate, with isolated moments of beauty and tranquillity, so many different biomes the graphics can be outstanding if you catch the sunlight in the right way while crawling out of a dark hole into the world above...A decent mix of linear and semi-open exploring with scripted action and random encounters, but its the story and world itself here that really excels, the shear amount of detail and lore in this game is incredible, you can sometimes spend hours just exploring the world see what you stumble across, or relax just listening to the stories of the various survivors in your group between each mission, go smoke a cigarette with your friend at the front of the train as it chugs across the land, or discuss the plan with another, it really helps set the stage as your group slowly grows in size!! Missions involving team mates actually feel worthwhile, the team plays a genuine part in the mission, covering you, or assisting you with enemy scouting or info on your objectives, You can customise and service you weapon loadout in a ton of different ways to suit your playstyle, stealthy or guns blazing, long range or close quarters,Choose to kill anything that moves and suffer the judgement and dislike of your group, or go the humanitarian route and try to avoid unnecessary bloodshed...its a really cool game!!!!A few negatives... I got a bit of stuttering as the game autosaves and sometime loads areas, which is a little annoying, I've had two crashes on but who knows whether its the game or my PC..hahaAlso some of the initial loading times are inhumane!!!!Overall a fantastic, in-depth, gritty post-apocalyptic experience with some very minor forgivable quirks, well worth it!!!!I give METRO: EXODUS a solid: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first Metro game, but this game did not feel nearly as good as the others. The main issue is the inscrutable "morality" system that the game doesn't tell you about at all, aside from a few hints at the start of each mission. The "good" ending requires you to hit multiple objectives that you're often not told  about at all, and are incredibly easy to miss, even if you're following a guide online. I missed one small side quest in the second mission, and by the time I realized it, it was too late to go back and the game only keeps your last four save slots so I couldn't even restore an old save to fix my mistake. The game often expects you to use stealth, or sometimes not use stealth, and doesn't tell you which. Getting it wrong will get you the bad ending, every time. See those guys trying to kill you? Better not kill them, or maybe you can, it's hard to say sometimes without looking it up online. This is broken, frustrating, and this isn't really the way a game should play - it should let you play according to your own styles and as long as you accomplish the stated objectives, consider it successful. Deus Ex does this really well, unfortunately this game does not.

Instead we just got a visual upgrade period.Invisible walls that kill you are still there. The character still handles like a truck. Controls weren't improved. Items clipping through characters, vehicles, walls are still present (sometimes characters even clip through each other) and the worst offender for a game that is heavily based on stealth: The takedown button often doesn't show up which prevent takedownof enemies (whom on occasion will even detect you through walls).Buy if heavily discounted. _childDocuments_.review: (I AM A PRE-PURCHASER OF METRO EXODUS AND HAVE THE ADVANCED ADDITION CURRENTLY ALL ON THE STEAM PLATFORM)Ever since I was young Metro has been an amazing and heartfelt series for me exploring the underground metro as Artyom, you experience an abundance of mutants, rebels, and things so otherworldly the only way to understand them is to play and see for yourself. At the time of this review I have around 3 hours on record for Exodus and up until this point I have noticed the game kept its core single player roots from previous titles while incorporating a but more of a fallout style side quest extra mission feel to it. Exodus is different from 2033 and Last Light in the sense that you do not follow one path and continue on it until the end of the game, but instead Exodus adds another layer of sleeping to change the time of day, collect scrap materials you may later use to upgrade and craft certain weapons, and collecting a teddy bear for a young girl desperately trying to forget about the current life they are living in this post-apocalyptic world. Exodus is so far a very very well made game and I strongly encourage anyone to try it for them selves AFTER playing the other amazing previous titles brought out by 4A Games.WITH THAT BEING SAID, There has been much controversy about the publisher Deep Silver and their decision to move the game onto the Epic Store my take on this is that if you do not have the game pre-purchased on steam PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE wait until 2020 to wait and grab this masterpiece. Epic Games does not deserve any type of recognition for this and the decision by Deep Silver was one that was rooted with deep greed and should not be given the light of day what so ever, besides purchasing the game I strongly suggest those who would like to continue supporting these AWESOME and INCREDIBLE developers, 4A Games to find means to donate to other future projects they may have and just put out a good word for them. A developer should not be punished for the stupid and greedy decisions brought out by the publisher. ALSO ONE MORE IMPORTANT NOTE,Exodus is a game created and published in 2019 I am currently running the game on a 1080 TI with an Intel core i7-8700 CPU the game is fantastic graphics wise and continues to amaze me even after hours of game play so before purchasing the title please keep in mind that if you are running anything lower then a GTX 1050 your game play and experience may not be at the most optimal level. Those cards are currently going for around $120 USD and isn't too much of a wallet killer, before committing make sure that your hardware is up to par for the best possible experience.CONCLUSION,All in all Exodus is a breath of fresh air for me and many others alike, besides lets be real with the big cloud of battle royales, MMOS, and overall other multiplayer games reining supreme over the gaming community, single player deep story experiences have been left in the shadows and seeing a developer do it right like 4A games has with this title is truly amazing to players who want a break from the repetitiveness of BR's and multiplayer games alike. Exodus is an experience you won't want to miss out on if you are feeling like traversing the lands of MOTHER RUSSIA, battling mutants, taking out bandit camps, and killing 50 foot long crab-whales, then Exodus is definitely a must-play for single player fanatics and casual video game players alike. With that being said thank you all for taking the time to read my review and I hope that this review can clear up some questions or concerns many may have before purchasing this title, have a wonderful day and have a great time exploring the Motherland!

_childDocuments_.review: As ever with the Metro series this is a very story driven game, but this time with wide open spaces. It has a rather different feel to it considering the different map style and the fact that most of it happens overground, but the core elements are the same: cool bodge guns, moral choices, rich backstory, mutants, thick Russian accents and a secret "good" ending which you have to be REALLY morally good (and a little completionist) in order to obtain.I would have liked the game to be longer (I would say its about 30h per play through of the main story atm) but mainly because I didn't want it to end, and considering the already massive game size (77GB with the expansions) I suppose I'm just being greedy.If I had one REAL criticism, it would have to be that there are a lot of what is essentially cut scenes, but they are scripted in-game interactions meaning they can't be skipped, so I spent some time playing on my phone waiting for the touching guitar jam session between buddies to be over so I can play again, or that painful 2 minute scripted fight scene with a mutant where I just have to mash "E" and died 3 times because I apparently wasn't doing it enthusiastically enough.All told this is a great game, I got halfway through then started again from the beginning because I decided to do a "good ending" playthrough, and I just finished the game, and Im already considering doing it again on Ranger Hardcore and New Game+ (which gives all kinds of options to make it harder) so it doesnt get old.Though its a bit of a departure from the other 2, its a great 3rd game I would highly recommend to lovers of RPG driven FPS games and fans of the Metro.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't do reviews and I don't like long ones sooooTHE GOOD:- Took me nearly 18 hours to finish on hardcore and didn't even realise because of how intense and captivating the game was, 10/10.- Stealth system is a major improvement over last light- The dialogue is amazing, and the stories the characters tell really immerses you in the world, you start acting as if they are all your real friends.- Story is great. The ending was satisfying regardless if you got the good or bad.- Customisation is endless, I found so much gear and after talking with other people, they had gear I didn't even know about.- The maps are detailed, each area is unique with its own mutants and factions, tons of Easter Eggs, tapes and diaries scattered around bring detailed history of the land which provides deep context for each faction and how they came to be.- Graphics are excellent. Needs a decent rig though, my GPU made my room a nice toasty 35C when playing this game.- So many russkies speaking English that I've perfected my Russian accentTHE BAD- Isn't true "open world" it's more of an "open map", you travel to different areas on the train but there is no way of going back to previous areas.- The dialogue, while great, sometimes seems to repeat itself, just using different words to describe the same story, resulting in rather lengthy conversations that just go around in circles as if meeting some kind of word count.- The timing of character lines also seems a bit off, Miller would be talking about "THOSE BANDITS" and at the same time start talking about the weather.- THE WEAPON CLEANING MECHANIC.- To get the "good" ending you need to know who to kill and not to kill. There are some parts were you can't kill anything, and have to sneak around, if you are caught they shoot to kill. Can get frustrating when in close because of the clunky stealth (cyka pirate level).- oh yeah, the stealth. While it is a major improvement, still feels strange. You can sometimes run literally in front of someone and they won't notice while other times you're behind a crate and they "feel like something is off about this area". HOW DO YOU KNOW THIS CYKA.- Occasional bug. The only one I encountered was in the car, if you looked at the map you suddenly just broke your neck and got into a weird camera angle.TL:DR Solid 8/10. The cons are inconvenient at best. The story, graphics, and just general feel of the environment makes this one of the better games I've played in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Boring game, holds your hand through out, not scary, not as good as previous game for atmosphere, cutscenes-a-plenty, terrible A.I soldiers, weak enemies, optimised by the apprentice, wait for sale 6.5/10.Oh dear, what went wrong?Bland story, you know what happened when RR Martin left GOT? It's basically that. Now that the books/Dmitry Glukhovsky are no longer there to guide the story & 4A Games are left to their own devices, it's really lost so much depth and soul.Generally the game is "okay" It just feels a bit lifeless compared to the previous titles. It feels like they went after a wider audience with this one & commercialised the brand so to speak. It feels like Rage 2 but Rage 2 is the better FPS game. Enemies don't stagger, so you shoot them point blank they just shoot back like nothing happened. Hitboxes are messed up when enemies are climbing up ledges, edges and ladders, you miss shots because of it and it feels sloppy.The A.I, mainly the enemy soldiers are just immersion breaking, they are brain dead. They run right up to you but can't see you or they just aim at random things. Sometimes they are looking one way but shooting in the opposite direction, sometimes they don't move when you shoot them and sometimes they go in to "cover" but have a leg or their brain dead little skull popping out of said cover, making said cover utterly pointless.Stealth doesn't really work with the semi open world. You are in a dark place, not making a sound but the blue dot says you are visible, you move 2cm forward, now you are invisible to the enemy! Seems rather crude. Then you have the problem of enemies seeing you though solid objects. I have no idea how the stealth in this game works, roll the dice & see.Boss fights, shoot shoot, run run, shoot shoot, run run, you get the idea. Bland, generic battles with bullet sponges. I completed the game on Ranger mode in 15 hours , that's with some exploration, mainly exploring the first 2 locations as the next 2 locations are pretty small and linear and don't really allow for you to go anywhere.Maps are bigger but there's no real reason to explore them, so what's the point? You spend some resources to find some resources, if that's your thing then cool but for me it just doesn't work. The places you find are almost copy paste locations. A few soldiers on a crane or at a little base, no depth to the exploration. Too many cut scenes, there's more cut scenes than gameplay. Every few minutes the controls are taken away from you in order for you to watch or be apart of a cut scene. It's annoying. Do we buy video games to watch the cinematics, if you do then buy this game.Another issue with maps is there's loads of non physical objects, you if you try to jump on them you just fall though them, often you will end up in the water or falling to your death. They are there in front of you, you can see them, but they are only there visually and not physically, very annoying. You are not alone! I am here with you! For a lot of this game there is some annoying character following you or covering you, I don't need or want their help but the game already made that choice for me. More control the developers haven taken away from the player.Maybe I want to play ranger hardcore mode so the A. I is stronger, but I also want to go Jon Rambo, guns blazing, well I can't because the difficulty options are all or nothing. You can have easy with plenty of ammo or harder options with less ammo, you are forced into the broken stealth system on harder difficulty because of this, once again developers not allowing the player to enjoy things their way.Poorly optimised, this game on a console is capped at 30fps, it doesn't even manage a steady 30 there, on my PC (Ryzen 5 1600x OC'ed, RX 580 0C'ed, 16gb ddr4 3200mhz and SSD I could run the game on medium, 1080p and get between 40-60fps, many areas are not optimised at all, resulting in sub 60fps, dx12 dx11, all the same & didn't change a thing. One of the least optimised titles I have played in recent times. Weapon models look great but I wouldn't say the visuals warrant the bad performance, some of the textures look like 8bit.Loading times are quite long also, as I said above, I have an SSD, but this game, especially on the first load of a map after start the game could be 1 minute long.  A "quick load" can be 20 seconds after each death which becomes quite tedious. No idea what kind of loading times people with normal HDD are getting.  Just changing the the graphics settings via the video options resulted in a 2 minute loading screen "changing settings 16%".The best FPS save I found was to change "r_foliage_shadows" to "0" via the Config folder. Demons useless, these flying beasts are just not scary in this game, they are just overgrown pigeons now. Demons & their laggy looking shadows will take a few swipes at you & that's really about it. They die very quickly.Spiders, same as the Demons, they seem weak in Exodus. Some "fire" rounds from the BB gun, one shot and they are dusted. Thought they were armoured on the front/top & you could only kill them by flipping them with exposure to light previously? Not scary & too easy. Plus the flashlight has about 20 years worth of power so the spiders are pretty easy to deal with. I feel going up on the difficulty modes should cut the flashlights run time considerably so you need to use it wisely. Blind Ones, what the hell are these and why? Why would some gorilla type beasts evolve into blind idiots? They are useless, Librarian(s) is a superior enemy.  Meeting the blind ones should have been an event, instead it's just another poorly executed enemy that you can avoid with ease.  You don't even need to sneak, just walk normally & throw an old tin of Heinz baked beans at a wall, they are defeated. Humanimals, the generic zombie enemy, every other game has them, so why not? basically just some sort of stand-in enemies, instantly forgettable.This game feels like it needs another year of development/finishing.  It's a bit rough around the edges even though it's had a year since the release on the EPIC Store. You would think they would have used that year to fix any issues, instead they created some DLC. Priorities in the wrong places it seems?Press & hold E, this pretty much does everything, open boxes, go though small gaps, go under fences, pick up weapon, strip weapons/take ammo from enemy gunns, load save etc Press E-xodus. An enemy jumps you, press EEEEEEEEEEEE until the QTE is over.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through this game about 3 times now, still working on all of the achievements (one of the only games ever where i loved it enough to decide to grind for all the achievements). But lets get to the bastard pos elephant in the room ... THE EPIC GAMES STORE >:( !!! by no means am i saying that you shouldn't download the Epic Games Store for this game, as that is your choice completely, but I am am gonna suggest that you don't for various well reported security issues and Tencent *shivers* being majority share holder in epic. I myself was lucky enough to pre-order this game on steam when i heard about Epic poaching it off of Steam, i normal don't endorse pre-ordering games due to how games have been releasing over the past couple of years, but i was not sorry or disappointed when this game was released as it was released finished with only minor glitches. The developers 4A Games do amazing work both story and graphics wise and i highly recommend that you purchase this game when the Epic 1 year exclusivity deal is over, and it is back on Steam (probably 20% off just out of spite XD)But now to the game, and my opinions and gripes  on different aspects of the game.(AVOIDING SPOILERS as much as possible BUT SOME MIGHT SLIP THROUGH)Story: Overall the story is good and enjoyable, worthy of multiple playthroughs to see things that you may have missed on your first playthrough. While the story is well written and has good ups and downs, it doesn't consistently flow through different chapters with the very first chapter seeming to speed along a bit to quickly for me to catch everything on my first time playing, and the final chapter seeming to just be very very drawn out with multiple different section setup in a linear layout (which isn't a problem for me as i have played the other metro games ((which is how both of those games where from start to finish)) but may be a bit strange for newcomers to the series.) Overall a great story with pretty good voice acting with each character having their own personality even if some kinda fall flat *cough cough* Katya and Stepan *cough cough*. Gameplay: While the core gameplay is a bit clunky and a bit dated in 2019 (with "press E to" prompts everywhere) it is something that you get used to pretty quickly, and the slow intentional movements works great with the survival horror aspects of the game and with the majority of HUD elements such as a geiger counter, detection light, and filter timer (along with other upgrades you can find through out the game) being displayed on Artyoms wrist watch .         - Gunplay; while on the lower difficulties the combat becomes quite at bit easier and less of a risk to supplies as on easier difficulties supplies or much more plentiful, where as on harder difficulties the every bullet counts and stealth mentality becomes your best friend. There is also a weapon cleaning aspect in this game as the dirtier your weapons become the less reliable and more likely to jam up in combat.        - Gear Progression: Metro Exodus does not have a leveling system as it is trying to be "realistic" in the way that people don't gain more health and stamina by doing random ♥♥♥♥, instead to improve Artyom's kit you need to explore and look for upgrades for both Artyom's weapons and equipment. The weapon upgrade and hot swap mechanic is pretty cool but a bit shallow as once you find certain upgrades there is no point in using any other upgrades, i wish that it was more of a this or that sort of thing like a trade off         - Supply Management: As i said before on lower difficulties this a much less of an issue but on higher difficulties your gonna want to avoid large scale gun fights and mutants of any kind as much as possible/ other than when it is the only choice depending on the chapter. you will want to scavenge for supplies but will need to learn to make it quick, best spots for supplies seem to be in red zones, mutant nests, and bandit camps making planning and/or stealth a necessity for every situation.         - Enemies: same as before on lower difficulties human enemies aren't as big of a threat as the accuracy and range seem to drop off on difficulties lower than normal. On higher difficulties human enemies are much more accurate and deadly. Mutant enemies seem to be a hassle on all difficulties as fighting mutants just wastes supplies as mutants (other than the purple leech things in the putrid tunnel) don't drop anything, avoid mutants when ever possible.Graphics: Just like both of the previous games the graphics are truly a benchmark for pc performance with there being a special extreme graphic option ment for future hardware. while to graphics are extremely good you can still get good preformance by lowering graphics( i have a laptop with a 1060 and play on a mix between medium and low graphics to hit the 60-80 fps range, but the graphics are still amazing)Sound design/ Atmosphere: with all of the sounds in the game tied to one volume slider it makes a very atmospheric and immersive experience as when your around loud things in will overpower quiet things like voices and movement in a very realistic way, only downside is that you really have to listen to what people say which can be hard with there is alot of different sounds going on. Some of the most creepy and atmospheric moments in this game is when your alone in a dark dreary tunnel as there is usually no music in these sections making every little noise very audible and creepy (HEADPHONES HIGHLY RECOMMEND) Weapons sound awesome and powerful, and hit with alot of force. Final overview: Overall Metro Exodus is an amazing game with great graphics, fun gameplay, and a good story. Its only fault is that it is a Epic Games Store exclusive. _childDocuments_.review: After beating the game, I can finally write a review. However, I can't recommend the game.First, I'll mention the things that I disliked about the game. The most important thing is the terrible optimization. This game should not be as taxing as it is. I have a 1070 Ti and an i7-4770k and I could barely make it past the loading screen. I had to turn the settings all the way down and change settings from the NVIDIA Control Panel that I've never touched in over 200 games that I've played. With an hour or so of research and troubleshooting, I was finally able to play the game, but there were still horrible stutters even after capping my frames at 60. Again, I've played many graphic intensive games and never had this issue. Another thing is that this game is a bug filled mess. Hitboxes are wonky and sometimes bullets will pass through enemies. Some objects have hitboxes that are too big and you can't shoot through something that's clear. Also, sometimes when you're running, you'll hit a bump and fly into the air and take fall damage. Sometimes you'll run down a hill and fly through the air and take fall damage. The fall damage in this game is no joke. Two centimeter fall and you're wasting a medkit. Not particularly an issue unless you're taking fall damage a lot from bugs like I did. Lastly, upon exiting, the game would usually say my save data was corrupted and ask if I wanted to overwrite it. I always said yes and nothing ever happened, but it's not reassuring when you dump hours into a game for your data to become corrupted.Now for the good things about the game. Even with the graphics all the way down, the game still looked decent. Also, this was my first experience with a Metro game and I did just fine on normal difficulty. Resources were plentiful and I never died too much so it's definitely a game everyone could enjoy. However, the single redeeming factor of this game is the story. Even if you haven't played the previous games like me, it's still very easy to piece things together and become attached to the characters. It has one of the best stories I've seen in a game for a while. With that being said, I still can't recommend the game. It's been out for an entire year and rather than fix bugs and optimize the game, the company would rather prioritize money and keep putting out DLC. Also, lets not forget that they prioritized money over their players when they removed the game from steam and went to EPIC for a year. Overall, a lot of bugs, terrible optimization, great story. 6/10 experience

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the enhanced edition which doesn't have it's own steam page. The extra ray tracing made a great looking game look even better and i appreciated the implementation of DLSS 2.0 and an FOV slider. As for the game itself, it's great. It has minor flaws which hold it back from being amazing to me and i do think Last Light is still the best in the series because of it's strong pacing and well written story. The open level design in Exodus allows you to take in the environments more and be more immersed but i do think the pacing slightly suffers compared to the other games. The slower moments where you are looting, exploring and travelling between areas were never boring because of the amazing atmosphere the game has but it's not that tight concise adventure that the other two games were. The crazy amount of dialogue in the game is a little extra in my opinion and it doesn't help with the pacing. You can listen to these characters babble on and on for hours, some of the dialogue is good and adds extra world building, but a lot of it feels like padding and just pointless. The worst offenders are all the one sided conversations between a character and the protagonist because artyom doesn't speak in game, so the characters feel like they are just talking to themselves and it's not engaging or interesting to listen to. I thought the story was good but it's heavily segmented into mini plots between each area while having a very loose over arching plot in the background. It doesn't have that one big story it's trying to tell. But i did think the story was a great way to end the trilogy and it felt satisfying. The gameplay is great, the customisation has depth, the shooting feels impactful, the stealth feels satisfying, exploring and looting is engaging and immersive. All of the small details help with the immersion too like wiping or patching the mask, checking the map or the compass which is all done in game etc. I appreciate games doing this and i wish more do it in the future. The little things make a big difference in getting you immersed in the experience. I also recommend playing all the metro games in Russian because of the added authenticity and the english voice acting isn't very good. I'm glad i waited for the enhanced edition to come out, i did play this game previously on the microsoft store when it came to game pass and it was a blast to replay this game.8/10 (Great)

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: ★★★★★ Metro Exodus showcases a significant leap in graphical fidelity compared to its predecessors. The game's environments are breathtaking, ranging from the hauntingly beautiful post-apocalyptic landscapes to the detailed interiors of makeshift settlements. Dynamic weather, day-night cycles, and realistic lighting contribute to an immersive visual experience that elevates the Metro series to new heights.Gameplay: ★★★★☆ Metro Exodus maintains the series' signature blend of first-person shooting, survival horror, and atmospheric exploration. The addition of semi-open world environments introduces a new level of freedom, allowing players to tackle objectives in a more non-linear fashion. The variety of weapons and the emphasis on resource management contribute to a tense and strategic gameplay experience.  Story: ★★★★★ The narrative in Metro Exodus continues the compelling story of Artyom and his companions as they journey across the post-apocalyptic Russian landscape. The well-developed characters, moral choices, and the exploration of the Metro's rich lore create a narrative that is both engaging and emotionally resonant. The evolving relationships among the characters add depth to the storytelling.  Soundtrack: ★★★★★ The atmospheric and evocative soundtrack of Metro Exodus complements the desolate beauty of its world. The music, combined with ambient sounds and the haunting cries of mutated creatures, enhances the immersive experience. The attention to detail in the audio design contributes to the overall sense of isolation and tension.  Level Design: ★★★★☆ The semi-open world design introduces a refreshing change to the Metro series. Each environment feels distinct, featuring a mix of urban ruins, frozen landscapes, and desolate wilderness. The level design encourages exploration, and the dynamic nature of the world, including day-night cycles and weather changes, adds depth to the gameplay.  Replayability: ★★★☆☆ While Metro Exodus offers multiple endings based on player choices, the linear narrative and scripted events may limit replayability for some. However, the variety in approaches to missions and the moral decisions throughout the game may motivate players to experience different outcomes.  Overall: ★★★★☆Metro Exodus successfully evolves the Metro series, delivering a visually stunning and emotionally charged experience. With its engaging narrative, atmospheric world design, and strategic gameplay mechanics, it stands as a worthy addition to the post-apocalyptic saga. While some series purists may miss the confined spaces of the metro tunnels, the expansion into a more open world proves to be a welcome and refreshing change for the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: pros:- Volga chapter,- graphics,- weather and day/night system,- some of the weapon customization options,cons:- very, very slow and boring start (throughout first hour you have control of the character for about 5 minutes, rest is just cutscenes),- very, very linear gameplay (even the "open" world parts),- every chapter, apart from Volga, was disappointing,- minor technical glitches (while in car open map and put it away, the car will try to leave the screen as well, being detected through walls, character makes a jump when stumble upon small obstacle or wall, objects floating in the air, dragon picked me up off the roof and never dropped)- weather system is triggered by game events, so it's not actually open, living world,- a lot of times there is no clear signal when you take and lose control over your character,- some of the mechanics are not clearly explained during gameplay (f.e. how to switch between ammo types, while picking up weapon which weapon will be replaced, etc),- some of the tasks you have to deal with are not clearly explained (like how to trigger next bit of the terminal mission in Volga),- the open world bits that were advertised are still very linear and don't give you much chance to explore (except Volga chapter) - you will visit every single location in every chapter as part of main storyline, if not, it's just a camp you can raid,- waaay too much linear wondering in the dark, underground corridors for open world game.The bits that they took from Stalker games (weather, day/night cycle) are pretty good, but insistance on using unskippable cutscenes for narrative and constantly being stripped of my gear is just so f*ckin frustrating - I mean how many times can I be captured by someone, isn't there another way to push story forward?It's not a bad game, but since it was suppose to be open world title I was hoping for far more freedom and not as linear story as in previous titles. _childDocuments_.review: Making a new part of the Metro is a difficult task. Making a new part such that it was more successful than the previous two is an almost impossible task. In this part of the trilogy, players will leave the dark world of the Moscow metro and get to the surface in order to board the Aurora train and explore the regions of the nuclear post-apocalypse of Russia, and together complete the adventure of Artyom, Anya and his friends.Graphics and sound have improved significantly compared to the previous two parts. The linear level design is mixed with a small open world, and a more advanced weapon and equipment modification system has been introduced.The story is short, but it makes you think about life. Namely, about the horrors of nuclear war and all the consequences that follow from it. When every day survivors worry about how to live on. People go crazy not knowing where to find water, food, medicine and even some temporary habitat. When there is almost no living place left in the world and everything is covered with some creatures, and radiation exceeding the norm several times on the surface.I also recommend you to take DLC Two Colonels. It tells the whole ins and outs of the history of Novosibirsk in a concise manner. The turning point is very exciting, and the ending will not leave you indifferent either.

_childDocuments_.review: Exodus is a beautiful game.Stunning graphics, amazing gameplay and an open world done right!Unlike most Open World games this one doesnt just copy pasta objectives all over, no! Each of the open world maps, there are 3, is handcrafted with unique objectives and POIs.intermixed into the open world sections are linear levels driving the story, aswell as the train levels that are purely optional but let you listen in and even interact with your fellow Spartans, the friendly troops you fight alongside with.on the grpahics aspect this is most definetly one of the best looking games i have ever played and the followup Enhanced edition is even prettier altho not much, but locked behind raytracing.Gunplay feels solid, combat feels great and enemies feel challenging, definetly a step up from the redux versions but luckily not broken like in 2033.The story is somewhere inbetween 2033 and last light. my personal opinion is that it peaked with LL but it is still solid and especialy in the train levels show you the depth each character you regularly interact has.The DLCs both take the core concept and push it to its peak.Sams Story feels like Metro Exodus at its best. Open world with a well written story, however the boss fights could be better.The Two Colonels is Metro at its peak aswell, less open world and in the Metro system of an entirely different city it could easily stand on its own legs as a seperate game and succesor to 2033 and last light. however its rather short, so doesnt overstay its welcome, but leaves you wanting for more!If you Have Exodus but are unsure about the DLCs, go get them!
