_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a post-apocalyptic first-person shooter that takes you on a harrowing journey through the ruins of Russia. As the third game in the Metro series, Exodus continues the story of Artyom, a survivor of a nuclear war that has devastated the planet.The game is set in a beautifully rendered and atmospheric open-world environment, which is a departure from the linear level design of its predecessors. The world of Metro Exodus is richly detailed and filled with danger, from deadly radiation to hostile mutants and human factions. The game's survival mechanics, including scavenging for supplies and crafting weapons and gear, add to the sense of desperation and urgency that permeates the game.One of the standout features of Metro Exodus is its storytelling. The game's narrative is expertly crafted and driven by a cast of well-developed characters. The game explores themes of hope, sacrifice, and the human condition in the face of extreme adversity. The game's story is both emotional and thought-provoking, and it is sure to stay with players long after they've finished the game.The combat in Metro Exodus is intense and satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons and tactics at the player's disposal. The game's stealth mechanics allow players to take a more strategic approach to combat, and the enemy AI is challenging and unpredictable.The graphics and sound design of Metro Exodus are stunning. The game's world is beautifully rendered, with an attention to detail that is second to none. The sound design is also exceptional, with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack that perfectly complements the game's atmosphere.Overall, Metro Exodus is an exceptional game that delivers a compelling story, intense combat, and a beautifully rendered world. It is a must-play for fans of post-apocalyptic games, first-person shooters, and immersive storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is hands down the crowning achievement of the Metro franchise. It brings Artyom and company out of the claustrophobic metro tunnels of 2033 & Last Light, and into the daylight of POST-apocalyptic Russia, in all its glory. Never before has a game so effectively blended the polish of a linear FPS with the freedom of a reactive open world, while capturing a Slavic atmosphere which rivals that of blin-kingpin S.T.A.L.K.E.R. itself. Exodus takes Metro to fantastic new heights while cutting out nearly all the lows, whether that be in gameplay, world-building, or storytelling. As a fan of the series for years, I’m happy to report that this  the sequel we were waiting for.Metro Exodus begins with the protagonist, Artyom, plagued by the suspicion that there is still human life left on the surface beyond the Moscow Metro system. You, as Artyom, have been making frequent dangerous excursions to the surface since the end of the previous game in the hopes of finding a radio signal to validate this theory. This causes strife with your wife, Anna, who is fearful that one day you won’t arrive home still breathing. As a consequence, she decides to come with you on one of your trips to the surface to watch your back. On that fateful day, Artyom and Anna discover; not a radio signal, but actual people who claim to hail from outside the city… as well as an operational locomotive train, capable of taking them – and the Spartan Order – across the country.Shifting to the graphics of Exodus, I have to say that they are entirely up to series standards. The art style is identical to that of its redux-ed predecessors, but every visual detail has been tweaked to breathtaking fidelity. Textures are photorealistic, faces are way beyond the uncanny valley in a positive direction, animations are fluid and numerous, the lighting is gorgeous to the point that its beauty exceeds real life, and all other technical components are practically flawless. The soundscape is noticeably (mostly) unchanged from the previous games, however there is a whole new soundtrack which accompanies Exodus’s atmosphere terrifically. As for performance, the game is demanding, but still well optimized. All in all, I’m absolutely taken by Metro Exodus’s presentation.Exodus is divided into roughly three separate maps throughout the course of the game, as well as a few more linear levels. While the settings themselves are gorgeous to the eye, from the swamps of the Volga River to the deserts of the dried up Caspian Sea, there’s also a lot to do. Each region has multiple objectives and locations, with secrets to uncover and loot to seize. There is a disparate theme to the individual provinces too, giving Exodus a real sense of variety. Notes and audio journals dot the world-space as well, revealing the history of a place and its people following the war. The several environmental stories told are enlightening, and sometimes even heart-rending. Altogether, Exodus’s environments are impeccably designed, and reward intense investigation.Metro Exodus, among other secondary features, utilizes an all new crafting and modification system, which I’d say is… a mixed bag. The crafting component of the game feels lazy, as there are only two materials to work with: metals and chemicals, which (annoyingly) functionally constitute 90% of the games lootable items – meaning most valuable consumables must be crafted. On the modification side of things, there’s a lot more to like. There are roughly ten base guns in the game, but each can be radically altered to work more effectively in different scenarios. Gear modification serves as the progression system, so it’s important to stay up-to-date with your weapons and accessories. There are a few more gameplay mechanics such as stealth, radiation, and vehicles, but all can be roughly summarized as ‘well implemented.’The Metro series is known for its atmosphere, and the immersion of its combat is a central element. I truly believe Metro Exodus has perfected the first-person impact of firing a gun; between the recoil and sound design, and even on down to the stopping power of each individual weapon. And good news – from bandits to mutant beasts, and slavers to the eerie humanimals, there’s a whole host of new adversaries to blast away across the scarred face of Russia. The AI of human enemies is quite sophisticated too, being able to call out your position to their allies if they spot you; relative to the objects around you. It’s also worth noting that you can defeat humans non-lethally, and that combatants will surrender if routed. Intricacies like these nested within Exodus’ combat system are what drive the gameplay, and make it uniquely satisfying.Refocusing on Exodus’s story, it’s a much better tale than that of the previous titles. For reasons I won’t spoil; you, Anna, Colonel Miller, and the rest of the Spartan Order travel eastward through post-apocalyptic Russia in the train found at the beginning of the game, which is quickly coined the . As the crew trek across the scorched earth of the motherland, seasons change, and new societies are discovered. The survivors of the nuclear holocaust have become vicious luddites, bandits, cannibals, and slavers – but a rare few have preserved their humanity. Eventually the Order’s goal becomes to find an untainted land to call home; a place where a civilized society can rebuild, and Artyom and Anna can raise a family.Whereas in past Metro games the supporting characters were side-pieces or even something of a nuisance, Exodus is much more character-driven in its storytelling. The blank stares of Bourbon and Khan are gone; replaced by the sensitive compassion of Stepan, cockiness of the impressionable Duke, and the  love of Artyom’s wife, Anna. The Aurora’s crew grows and changes with time, developing through the experiences they endure and the trials they overcome. If you care to bend an ear, your comrades will talk it off, expressing their thoughts, plans, hopes, and fears. While the translation of dialogue to English can be clunky at times, the character writing itself is just magnificent. The inspiring humanity of this small group of characters truly bring your goals as Artyom into perspective. The people of Metro Exodus are what make the whole experience.On a quick narrative note before my final verdict, I’d like to clearly express that Exodus tracks your moral status throughout the course of the 25-odd hour campaign. There are particular actions you can complete that will give you positive karma, and specific crimes you can commit that will accrue negative karma. How you interact with the game world and its characters will have consequences – not only in the form of separate endings, but in a cascade of different narrative outcomes. The Order’s exodus is a treacherous one, but the most perilous war is that of the one which rages .I feel my opinion on this game has been made fairly obvious by this point, but that doesn’t mean I won’t praise it further. Metro Exodus is one of the best games, period, that I have ever played. Its the culmination of what already was a phenomenal series, and Exodus pulls no punches in giving the trilogy a stupendously vast, enjoyable, meticulous, touching, and downright impressive send-off. I couldn’t have imagined a better way to conclude Artyom’s journey.

_childDocuments_.review: The Metro Series is based on the novels of Dmitri Glukhovsky. It is clear to me that the writers of this game took the origin of the story very seriously. You can tell that they didn't want to just insert a story into the game just because - they want the player to care about it as well. The characters themselves, as well as the dialogue alongside pretty much everything else is written , you can really tell that they treat their source material with outmost respect. While Artyom is mostly silent (except for loading screen dialogue/diary entries), his role as a passive protagonist isn't as bad as I orgininally thought it was going to be. Rather than just getting told what to do by every NPC, he has moments where the plot is developed through his actions - or rather through the actions of the player.This is outstandingly done by the "karma" system of the game, which means the story will follow a different path, depending on the players choices. You can choose whether to mercilessly kill everything that stands in your path or carefully approach the situations given by the game and respect its virtual residents These choices are done not by merely pressing a button, as in "Would you like to be bad? Y/N", rather it's done through action - or even the lack thereof.This way it doesn't just feel like Artyom defines the story that is told, but that the  is pushing the plot forwards.In short, a beautifully told storyline with interesting characters.Let's get to the juicy stuff. It's a FPS so naturally you'd expect a fair size of shootin' action. While that is true (and it's good shooting, we'll get to that in a bit) it's not the only thing you do and depending on how you play, might even play a rather subelemental role.The levels that the players find themselves in are not a linear row of corridors, which was a point of criticism of the predecessors (2033, Last Light), but are big, open and fully explorable areas that differ wildly throughout the game's journey. You get the usual dark and atmospheric metro tunnels, as expected, but you'll also get desert areas, swamps, citys, forests, etc. It's a huge step up in scope when compared to the previous titles.These levels aren't just big for the sake of being big  but are carefully crafted to The game is a realistic apocalypse; you're not running and gunning, spamming the "E" key to pick up loot.I played on hardcore and every mistake I made was punished accordingly.  - Shot down in seconds. - That's on me. - Crafting stations are plenty, ya dummy. Your guns are heavy and feel powerful, while avoiding pinpoint accuracy and unnecessarily big magazines. Doing maintenance on your guns is crucial if you don't want the aforementioned gun jamming to happen to you.Another mechanic to further immerse you in the apocalypse.Metro: Exodus is not without flaws though:- While guns have a natural inaccuracy to them and it's mostly fine, sometimes you'll just get these Your crosshair is right on target but your knife throw still misses.- Minor bugs here and there, such as a buggy POV driving a car. These are mostly rare and minor inconveniences though. If you care about story, have played the previous titles, enjoy a slow paced FPS based on immersing you into the beautifully crafted world and its environments: It's a no brainer, this game will provide many blessed game hours.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, Metro: Exodus (MEx) might seem like a typical FPS with a couple of twists, and while it doesn’t really offer anything groundbreaking, it is a perfect example of a whole package being greater than the sum of its parts.::Unless you want yet another FPS with some extended features, you should most definitely play this game on . Having played through the game twice, I decided to try Normal and, let me tell you straight away that this is most definitely not the way you should experience MEx.Not only is the game too forgiving but , which makes it stand out in the oversaturated FPS crowd, become basically non-existing. Just imagine if Dark Souls had Skyrim’s quest pointer.If you’re uncomfortable with a very challenging setting, pick the one that you’re OK with and go a step above in order to maintain the pressure and the idea of a harsh and unforgiving post-nuclear world. I’ve heard someone saying how , and I could not agree more. With that being said, let’s dig in, shall we?The Franchise previously known for its predominantly claustrophobic and linear levels becomes very open-ended in its latest iteration. From this, it’s easy to assume that there are going to be some big changes, and, I for one, welcome and absolutely loved those. Thematically, this is still a Metro game. There are even a number of linear sections and levels, such as the game’s opening, where you have to play as it is intended and have little to no say so in how things develop. Gameplay-wise, the foundation is there, just that it has been expanded and improved upon, but the overall feel was quite different for me. Being dubbed the best scout in the unit, Artyom, the game’s protagonist, has a lot to live up to, and MEx provides plenty of opportunities to do just that. Wandering the outskirts and the wilderness, scouting for points of interest and noting them down on your map for later exploration is a very important and big part of the experience. In fact, depending on your playstyle, scouting, exploration, and scavenging might as well be the major part of your MEx playthrough, and this is actually pretty cool.Now let’s add a high level of immersion to this. I’m talking about no HUD. This means no objective tracker on your screen, or a mini-map full of colorful icons to pop. No distraction whatsoever while exploring. You go where you think that something of interest might be. Of course, you can still access the map and check the objective tracker. You have your visibility indicator for stealth and the Geiger counter as well as many other indicators. The thing is, they’re presented in a very immersive way. They’re all gadgets, mostly on your wrist, audio and visual cues which are a part of the game world, and when you see or hear those, nothing is reminding you that while all of this is cool, you’re still playing a video game.Even though MEx puts you on an open level, it is still not an open-world game. In fact, these open areas are big levels that, once you’re done with, you may never return to. This is why you might want to let your FOMO take over and take your time to make sure you’ve visited every nook and cranny. Why? Because this is how you progress, for the most part. The game will  so pay attention to what your comrades are saying!You don’t exactly level up in MEx. There are no perks to unlock or XP to grind. However, there are still ways to improve your character, like gadgets, suit upgrades, and weapon parts. Finding new weapon parts is a big deal, as the game lets you customize guns in the field. Considering various enemy types, different weather conditions and the impact that the time of the day has on the world of MEx, this is quite useful. Need a medium-range rifle instead of a silenced pistol? Strip down your revolver, and make a couple of adjustments! Swap the silencer for a long barrel, add the 2X Scope on it's rail, and you've got yourself a rifle. If you've searched thoroughly, you will have everything you need, and can improvise to adapt to any given situation. Once obtained, these upgrades can be used through the entire game.Others are given to you as the story progresses. You might actually want to stick to the main objective until you’ve obtained the binoculars, at which point you’ll be properly equipped and have everything you need to explore the world on your own.When it comes to the story, perhaps more than the content of it, I like the fact that it’s rather believable. Listening to the Artyom’s comrades speak about what was going on is what I enjoyed the most, as they were all lovable characters with a lot of personality.The adventures of Aurora’s crew and their objectives feel like they are happening spontaneously. They were logical conclusions and decisions based on the current events and situation that I never found to be forced on the game simply because the developers needed some excuse to blow things up or shoot someone.  Player choices and their consequences, which the game always had (to an extent), are done better and more clearly telegraphed to the player this time around, although there’s still room for some improvement.  The exploration, which I’ve brought up so many times already, also extends to the story as some story-related things require to be found first. It is also the best way to gain additional Karma points which will determine how the story unfolds and eventually ends.  Of course, I am recommending this game. I’ve played it multiple times and actually plan to give the recently released raytracing-only version a go sometime down the road.  However, keep in mind what I’ve said at the beginning: unless you make this game unforgiving, you’ll be mowing down enemies and playing a post-apocalyptic shooter, which is not really that impressive nowadays anymore.  My impressions are based on the very specific Ranger Hardcore mode with Minimal Interface. This made the game slow, methodical and unforgiving, which is something that I very much enjoy. Ammo was scarce, just like the resources, I had to make every bullet count, and when I made a mistake, it was punished severely. At times it reminded me of the good times when I played Metal Gear Solid 3 back in the day on my PS2. When I scoured around for resources and ammo, waiting for the perfect opportunity to strike. MEx is, in many ways, just like that, and if this sounds like something you’d like to experience, then, by all means, get it, play it, and love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright! Finished the Main Story, 2 Colonels DLC and the Sam's Story DLC. Let's start off with the main game without the DLC.You play as Artyom, a special operations soldier of the Metro, after the bombs dropped eliminating the entire world except Moscow. Yet Artyom still explores the outside world, wanting to see if there is anybody still alive outside of the metro. Eventually on the surface Artyom discovers a train just choo chooing down the irradiated tracks. (That's all I am going to say about the story, as I don't want to spoil any of it.)Now with the story out of the way, let's get to the gameplay. (This review is my experience on the 2nd hardest difficulty, although I am doing a run on the hardest difficulty)Now I have not played Tarkov, but the movement reminds me quite a bit of that game from the videos I have watched. It also can be a bit wonky at times, just like in TF2 if you hit a ramp just right at high speeds you can fly up it. And by fly I mean FLY. I have launched myself off of buildings with this (Ability?). I love it so much though and if the devs remove it I will be so sad. Now for the main attraction, the weapon customization! It is done so well, screw finding stupid things like cans and scrap to fix up a sight for your rifle (Screw you fallout 4). Effectively the bag your given can carry infinite stuff, so collecting parts is easy. Just scrap the weapons found on the field and the attachments will be added. Find a workbench in the world and customize your weapon with whatever you want on it. Thanks for not making it needlessly annoying or time consuming (Still hate you fallout 4). Now, the difficulty comes from Ammo management and weapon sound. Ammo is barely found in the world on the difficulty I was playing on. If it is found, it's one or two bullets. Crafting is also high on ammo and it does not yield much ammo. Which is usually not a problem, unless you have those scripted events coming up that are unknown. I remember having around 200 rounds and thought I could take on anything! I ended up burning though those rounds in one scripted event and barely made it out alive. Just to let you know, this happens a lot. Along with that, suppressors are very useful. Who knew that attracting the entire base with a shotgun blast doesn't bode well for your survival.I also forgot to add these with my post. Filters and fall damage. Make sure to have at least 5 minutes of filters on you. I got stuck on two sections because I forgot to make some new filters and ran out. Also fall damage is really annoying in the game. The slightest falls will bring your health down to the red and because there is no auto heal a med kit will have to be wasted on your inability to use the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ STAIRS. Oh, and that leads into health kits, have as many as you can on you. They are worth more than ammo. Try to save them for as long as you can, because on the field you will not be able to find them, at least on my difficulty. Also there are multiple endings. Basically being a psycho will yield a bad ending and being somewhat honorable will yield a good one. The good one seems to be cannon according to the Sam's DLC, but I only got the good ending so far. I can't really say anything about the ending, but note your actions can lead to different endings.That's all I got on the main game, so let's hit the Two Colonels DLC.It felt really short. It did plug up some plot holes with the ending of the main story, but if your not invested in the story it's kinda not worth it. It allows you to go ham with a flamethrower tho. So that was fun. It was very linear, but that can be said with the entire Metro series. If your into the story of the game, you will like it.Let's just go with if your a long standing member of the Metro series, the Two Colonels DLC would not be a bad idea to pick up. Otherwise it may not be. See if you like the main game first before buying it, or just get the Gold edition. That's what I did.Sam's StoryThis is by far my favorite DLC. It adds two new weapons (An 1911 and a Sammy Rifle) which will be given to you for playing in the DLC. The story goes that Sam is homesick (He is American) and travels around trying to find a way home. Eventually he stumbles upon a town and finds a few people that can help him get home. (That's all the story I'm giving away).This was a well formulated story and has multiple mini stories in it. Overall it is very fun and has my favorite mechanic in the history of Metro.A Harmonica, which Sam is able to play at certain areas! It inspired me to learn how to play mine and I quite enjoy it! Overall I love this DLC. Not as much as the main story, but it is so much fun.To sum it all up, this is one of the best single player games I have played in forever. I loved Fallout NV and wanted something that can live up to that experience. I think this game has actually done it. While linear and has little to no room for player roleplaying it does tell the story of Artyom very very well. I usually hate stories like this, but it was done in a very great way and I dare say that it was one of the best to do it. Highly recommend this game to anyone wanting a good Boog of a loo game. Send those demon spawns to hell comrads!PS, screw epic games. Deep Silver if you ever pull that crap again I will not be buying the game no matter how good it is.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the previous Metro games, I can not recommend this game to veterans or newcomers to the series. While the story of the game is nice, and some of the set pieces are fun, there are just too many issues with this game that outweigh the positives. This game runs awfully, I had so many technical issues running the game. To name a few, there was an issue where when I took out my map while driving a car, it would put my head in the roof, I had one cutscene where the audio desynced, so everyone was talking over each other, and a major boss fight toward the end of the game broke for me where the boss kept charging at me. While the previous games had issues in their game logic or performance, this brings it up to a new level. Also, the feedback while playing this game is all over the place. Boss fights feel awful because your just dumping bullets into them without any acknowledgement that you're doing something. There was so many times I would be sneaking around and the noise for being spotted would play in it's entirety and nothing would happen. That sound effect sometimes would go off multiple times in a min, and I couldn't see anyone spotting me. Finally, and I wont get into it greatly due to spoilers, but the ending mission feels so rushed and awful to play. The boat segment feels miserable, the enemies you fight there are hard to spot or hard to deal with, and god forbid you get the bad ending to this game, you will feel so unfulfilled. (I am still confused how I got it since I followed what not to do on the wikis pretty closely)At the time of writing this, it is a year and a half after release, so I can not see the devs fixing these bugs so far past release. I'll just say I'm disappointed as a fan of the previous games, and I can only hope their next game is in a much better state. Stay away from this game, replay the previous two for a much better time.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Good game would recommend if found on sale, don't pay MSRP.As a player who usually doesn't play story based open world games this was an enjoyable experience. Now the game has a few bugs here and there, and the dialogue can be a bit clunky, however the game itself is really well done. The in game environment is extremely well built. Levels are challenging even on normal, and the story progresses in a steady but well paced manner. There is a good balance of stealth, action, world building, and exploration that can be had throughout the game. I enjoyed listening to the tapes and reading the letters of people as I navigated through the levels, with details that I was able to string from one stage to the next to discover what had happened to the characters despite not having played the previous games in the series. The game encourages exploration as you pickup resources which are vital for your survival which can allow you to complete tasks before the game tells you to do them which helps immerse you in the world. I have a few gripes with the game. It is quite a short play through (first run was 15 hours). Often instructions can be unclear mid level if you miss a piece of dialogue (it makes the game more challenging but can be annoying after the 10th time). Some of the stages feel a little repeatetive once you get really into the game.Overall I would recommend if you can find it for a good price, I paid around 12CAD and I am very happy with my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: They really went the extra mile with this one.  The other two previous Metro games were great and all, but this one brought it to the next level.  Great character development, a tighter story, and connects them all with a wonderful ending.  If you liked the first two, but not loved, this one will bring it home for you, and bring those emotions on you wanted to feel in the first two, but never got a chance.  If you've never played the first two, no problem, this one handles itself well as a first game and you can always go back and play the previous reduxes.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the previous games, and this and its DLC's.All I can say, is this series was worth every bit of my time, and I'll say, I have a pretty short attention span and I struggle with some things that take way to long.I don't know how, but Metro somehow pulled me up and made me take in what's going on, and made me involve myself with the environment.The atmosphere? Is breath taking, and the graphics are just mind blowing, some scenes are just pure eye candy, and always makes you stop to look around to take it all in. if there's one thing this game has won is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ graphics!What about the characters? The NPC's feel like real people, I can't believe you were able to create a fictional character ran by strings of code to have this amount of emotion and personality put into them, the passion here really shines.Story? I'll say its a bloody tear-jerker all the way through, and I must say Metro is by far the best story driven game I've ever played. I strived for that good ending, and bloody hell it was hard trying not to cry with my brother standing over my shoulder, and man screw that two colonels DLC, how dare it pull on my heart-strings that hard.Gameplay? It really depends on the difficulty, you can go for normal or easy which turns it into a more faster-paced shooter and harder difficulties for a slower, plan-of-a-attack gameplay style. Only one flaw I have with Exodus's gameplay, is sprinting onto any slight slope will send you flying or you'll float across the ground and end up falling to your death.Immersion? Turn that hud off and its like real-life. Always loved game mechanics where everything you need to worry about is on the characters body and not floating text on your screen.Navigation? Can be pretty irritating sometimes, cause they made it look so realistic and boundaries can be very difficult to judge and I ended up drowning/breaking Artyom's legs more times than I can count. For people going for the hardest if you turn the HUD off completely, I hope you know all the key prompts and know where to go...Replay-ability? Exodus took a more open map direction instead of a stream-lined map design the previous titles had. Exodus has achievements, collectables, different karma choices, many attachments, guns and different play-styles you can choose, there's a lot of replay-ability here, and due to how much I loved the story and the mechanics, I'm going to be replaying this.Bugs? at the end of a tunnel the terrain vanished and I couldn't continue, restarted and it was fine, crashed a few times on me, but this didn't bother me that much. It happens.Conclusion, its a bloody great game and I really honestly suggest playing the previous installments before this one.Thank you 4A games for such a masterpiece.Go buy it full price, on sale what-ever you prefer.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another huge leap forward by 4A. To get this over with, yes, the game is buggy, it crashes, the AI is dull, story written by a russian teenage-oriented pseudo-military author, the voice acting and general sound design is rather horrible to hear in 2019, some textures come straight out of 2000-ish and the world limited with invisible walls is right from that era as well.With that out of the way, if you are still kinda into it, here comes the good stuff. Overall looks of the game is plain amazing to gaze upon in all the dynamics of beautiful views (if you are not into close-up texture hunting). Technologies behind that picture are top notch and a really welcome addition to an Nvidia gamer. Gameplay mechanics are dripping over the top ( for a Metro game it is ) and a road-movie style of the story leads to amazing setting changes over the course of the game. No more one dark tunnel replaced with another, even darker tunnel. Those two make this game entertaining from start to credits.Open-world'ish maps are packed with content with over 100 unique items to collect, stories to read and scenes to imagine. No more empty space-fillers. The story carefully leads you around but totally encourages to take a detour. And that is what curated  level design is all about, not just empty space generating to make you waste your time.The story itself leads you through those epic authentic environments and while being plain simple and even childish with a great part of satire , raises those warm filings in your gut, the thrill of the unknown and the rush of a pursuit, asking tough questions and telling unique stories of people surviving after it all truly came down. And while everything else seems to be, well, mediocre at best, all of it combined into 4A game seem to just work and be a good fun, throwing you from one gameplay and setting into another, from STALKER to Mad Max, from Metro to right out Half-Life, you can either hate every single part of this game or enjoy the damn out of the full picture.And I also want to say that the true way of playing this game imo is on hardcore ranger, just because it makes the game so much more thrilling and challenging, somewhat hiding HUD and AI problems from you, making you scavenge for every drop of materials and ammo, thinking about your approach to your enemy and shake every time you finish an intense fight or barely escape overwhelming enemy force. In conclusion, this is not a perfect game by any means, but it moved the franchise a dozen steps up and I'm really looking forward to the next game 4A 'll throw at us. P.S.: I don't care about epic store thing, why would I? I'm here to play the game and I don't care where to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is one of those titles i really struggle to find honest words for...Maybe the best way to review it is like this: Unless you're a really hardcore fan of the series, you should prolly pass on this one. If you are, read on. Metro Exodus is a beautiful story wrapped into a bad, or at very few occasions, mediocre game. Somehow it feels like being stuck between an fast paced action game, a shooter and an exploration-focussed walking simulator, and Metro Exodus doesn't do very well.In comparison to Metro 2033 a few nice features have been added, and for themselves they seem to work as one would expect, but in total the game tries to be everything at once, yet struggles to be anything at all.- Is there much to do in this game?-- I haven't finished the game yet, but to this point it's a mix of scripted sequences, sneaking around while being punished for trying to solve missions the stealthy way, and unfair shooting sequences. It's basically Metro 2033 taken to a few open world levels. Yet, if you rush through the story missions you can probably finish the game easily in under twenty hours. The levels are really large and have a lot to offer visually. Storywise, as well as in terms of loot, it feels unrewarding to go exoplore. You constantly use more resources to explore the area and fight your way through than you find while scavanging. So better don't waste your time, it's not worth it. Even Fallout 76 has better loot than Metro Exodus.- What about the story...-- It's loosely based on the ending of Metro 2035 and pretty much continues where the book ended. If the game was a better one, the story would be much more enjoyable. Even after the first patch the voice lines often overlap each other, making it hard to follow what your companions or other NPCs are trying to get across. The game often annoys me to the point where I just leave the scene of the dialogue.- ... and the atmosphere?-- Well, the atmosphere is the thing that keeps me playing Metro Exodus. It's different, maybe not quite as good as Metro 2033.- Is this a Horror game after all?-- Not really, as I mentioned before this is rather a mix of fast paced yet clunky shooter and a slow paced walking simulator, and it's doing neither part particularly well. I feel like it's too slow for action players, and too fast for people enjoying exploration. The horror that Metro 2033 still had has vanished. Where Metro 2033 thrilled you and gave you chills, Metro Exodus just stresses you out.To cut it short: If this was just a pure exploration game, it would be quite ok. Not good, but ok. But the shooter part makes it really unenjoyable. The gamepad integration is poor, even on max. sensitivity it takes about 2,5 to 3 seconds to do a 360 spin, auto-aim doesn't help, and enemy AI is wiggling alot which makes it hard to headshot them (if people playing this on consoles have the same problems, I really feel sorry for them). Granades tossed by enemies fly through walls, enemies are able to penetrate areas that you cannot shoot through, stealth is working like meh... Sometimes you can down an NPC with another one standing only few steps away without being caught, other times the enemies spot you across half the map and even hit you while you struggle to see them at all. Plus, this drastically affects a few missions. I found it impossible for me to complete a single mission in total stealth, sooner or later the shooting starts, so I can also pass on sneaking and go in guns blazing. Dialogue system is messy. Really not a good game. And I'm sorry to feel this way.

_childDocuments_.review: I prefer to leave "Neutral" as recommendation but since its yes or no I'll just leave it at yes.Let me get this out of the way first.This game has MANY issues when it comes to its gameplay I will talk about it after all the good things about it.This game is a mix of between Linear and open world experience, you'll be thrown into this "world" tackling a lot of side missions and you're free to do them in any order you wants but the main story will drive you along in a linear path.They really puts a huge amount of efforts getting the players to immerse in this world everything the player does the world take notes about it and reflect about them through NPC's dialogue and the main character's diary. Every interactable objects are part of the world itself ... they may go a little too far in this department but I'll talk about it in the gameplay part.Graphics .... is an icing on the cake for this believable world. It is gorgeous on High settings, lower than high and it starts to get blurry which is not ideal but seeing the game engine itself is very well optimize most PC should be capable of running this game in high settings.Now here is where it all fall shorts...the gameplay.Starts with character movement slight incline low or high they are potentially lethal to the player. High inclines slows you down maybe that is how it works in real life but then you notice this happens with every small hill and everytime it happens you'll hear that sound effect which appears to be a character sliding sound effect. Try your very best to approach low inclines slowly otherwise you'll notice you get a lot of air time by simply running off them highly lethal in some area.Weapons now jam when they gets dirty ... awesome this is a fine system until you realize that it doesn't just jammed. When the weapons get dirty their performance also drops so it doesn't matter how buff your gun is if it gets dirty it won't delivers what you wanted it to do combine that with weapon jamming and you get the idea of this mess. Its like they don't want the players to use any of these cool looking metro design firearms.Objects interaction...I'll just refer as "animations"A lot of the objects in the world can be interact with....all of them has mostly the same animations and it is not a fast one. Sure for the very first time the character has to interact with the object they have to inspect it closely that explains the time it took for the character to do his things BUT some objects like Electric Motors and a Generator the character interacts with them all the time and when there's an enemy making all the noises and in some cases RIGHT IN FRONT OF THE CHARACTER and he doesn't show any sense of urgency to...you know FINISH whatever he's doing FAST to respond to life threatening situation !?Yes this is about "muh immersion" but this can ruin anybody else's when there's a disconnection in the subject of "realism"Vehicles....ESPECIALLY the boat.Yes the players get to drive around in a vehicle in this game but whatever you do try to spend as least amount of time as possible on a boat. The boat moves SLOWLY.... make sense considering the player is basically rowing it until you realize that there are enemies you have to fight on that small of a platform. To make matter worse the enemies you're fighting are the one that do RANGE ATTACKS which if you happens to be on ... I don't know A BOAT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE RIVER ? Have fun.The game has a moral system for you guess it.... them endings.From my experience it doesn't really force the player to play the game in "the only way possible" as many would implies.The player can approach the game with "If its hostile, you kill it" mindset but remember NOT everything is hostile.This way you don't have to force your way to play the game "the only way" which happens to be stealth.Still it could've been better I don't like the idea of "Do good deeds to be rewarded" as this is not a good mindset for anyone.That's all I have to say some may notice that I did a review for the game not too long ago but I see it as a full negative reviews which is unfair towards the game with this amount of effort put into it so here it is a hopefully a better one.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the third game in the Metro series and represents the biggest leap forward.Graphically, the game is a 10/10. It's fantastic. There's no comparison to its already visually appealing predecessors. The story once again surpasses its predecessors and casts them into shadow. Exciting, incredibly immersive, and extremely emotional, it's one of the few games that brought tears to my eyes. It's a journey that everyone should experience at least once.However, the gameplay differs from its predecessors and might deter some old fans. There are now small open-world or rather open maps. These are extremely well-crafted, highly detailed, and offer a lot to do. The beauty of it is that there are no unnecessary side missions; there's no simple checklist to complete, and the story unfolds beautifully within those areas. At the same time, there are still plenty of tight and horror-like passages that target the hearts of old players.Metro Exodus is a game that shouldn't just be played through; it should be savored and experienced. There are so many beautiful dialogues and details that the game thrives on exploration and soaking up as much as possible. The replay value is also much greater than in its predecessors.For me, the game is a 10/10 and my all-time favorite game. I can only recommend that everyone experiences the pinnacle of the Metro series for themselves. Play it, and you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited:Finished the game. This is my first full review of a game. First off, this game is marvelous! Thanks 4A team for delivering this masterpiece.( - ) Let me talk about the negative things of this game first:Metro Exodus is a great story-driven game. Graphic is top notch. However, there are few minor problems with character animations and audio bugs. People talk over each other sometimes and if you're going to play without subtitles, it's kind of hard to follow the dialogue. Facial animation was not that great, some of the cutscenes were a bit off for me but most of the time they were good. I guess it's not originally for the English version, playing this game in Russian version could be better but I would never know for sure. Still, these are some minor issues that didn't really affect too much of my experience playing this game.( + ) Let's get to the good part:This is definitely the best single player first person shooter with a great story for me! It's been so long since I really enjoyed a game like this. The character development is one of my favorite things about this game. The game does a great job of making you feel connected with the NPCs. Everyone in your Aurora squad has their unique personality and you can easily tell the difference.The new crafting and modding system is interesting. I love how you can change the mods on your guns while you're doing quests because it affects the gameplay a lot. You have options to choose your loadout before and during the missions. However, if you decide to play this game on Ranger Hardcore mode, the resources are pretty scarce which forces you to play this game on stealth most of the time.  Cleaning your guns is very important because the dirtiness affects your weapon's stats (accuracy and fire rate). Your guns could be jammed many times if they are too dirty.New quest-finding system is great too. The game doesn't show you where the quests are, you'll have to discover those points of interest on your own using your binocular. Those high grounds are the goldmines of intelligence if you take your time and look for places. It will be shown as a question mark on your map after you stared at a specific location for about 3 seconds.I love the day-night cycle in this game. The game gives you options to select day or night time. There are many safe houses around the map and you can use them to heal yourself, use the workbenches or sleep. It changes the whole game of how you choose to approach your next mission. Day time means less monsters and the human AIs are quite harder. They can easily see you from afar and alert the other guards so for example, if you want to take down a bandit camp, night time is much more effective. However, night time in this game is horrifying (more monsters to deal with). There are also anomalies in this game and it gives me S.T.A.L.K.E.R vibes. It only happens at night and will hurt you if you get too close.The atmosphere is one of the best about this game. It's breathtaking with 4 different seasons and environments that the game offers you to explore. Different biome has its unique feeling into it. Just take your time to explore every corner you go through, there are many surprises that won't let you down.Just like the old Metro games, your playstyle and your decisions dictates the outcome of the game. In my opinion, the karma system in this game is one of the best I've seen so far in all of the games I've ever played. You will see the consequence of your decisions during mid game and at the end as well.There's no need to say about the soundtracks. They're insanely good and fits the theme well.I got the bad ending even though I tried hard to get the good one. There are things that the game won't tell you but you have to think carefully before you act. Therefore, I'm still working on my second playthough because I missed so many things on my first playthrough and I'm trying to get the good ending this time.Thank you 4A! Solid 9/10.Edit 2:I just uploaded a GMV that I made for Metro Exodus.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro exodus is a good game overall and worth the price for about 20+ hours of game play if you familiar to the series. Starting with the positives, Exodus adds on a lot compared to the previous series, it adds: a couple sandbox areas, several linear sandbox maps like last light, a crafting tree for all items (weapons, ammo, armor, attachments), two paths for bad and good ending plus dialogue trees through out the game based on killing or sparing(weapon holstering on some events), day and night cycle, bandit bases, mutant nests, a LOT of dialogue from your teammates and characters, boat and car driving, weapon degradation, enemy surrendering, and way more. The sandbox areas really shine for me like: what time of day makes certain enemies more active, bandits on guard in day, mutants roaming the night, safe houses to sleep and resupply, side events like the main enemy of the area setting traps, and points of interest (bandit camps and mutant lairs) for weapon/gear addons. The crafting system replaces trading system and gives better flexibility instead of going to a shop to remove components (and hope it works for this area), and its simply two materials that are used for making ammo and items. The story is about above average but makes up with a lot of side quests for your crew and the other characters who join you. The side characters who "join you" in missions usually take a back seat as supporting fire which is preferred over "tour guiding" as the first metro did quite a bit. The side characters are tied with the karma system on whether you went full bloodthirsty mode or mercy/stealth and can die based on that decision, along with a change in attitude/tone especially for Miller. Graphics are good when I played on minimum but on ultra pretty good if you have a high end PC. Voice acting great, sounds great, cutscenes are superb, small details just awesome (like weapons getting dirtier, small animal wildlife, and enemies talking about your actions).For the Neutrals well there's a decent amount of written lore that I don't bother too much with it. There's no real new enemy types as their reskins of previous (games) mutants with slightly different mechanics. I'm not fond of collectables regardless of what game. Stealth is harder as enemies are more aware of their comrades, see in the dark, and have bigger field of view in general especially in day. I have no idea how to switch ammo types for certain weapons so that annoys me. Certain weapons aren't available till later on, which shortens the amount of use you have with them which I guess is expected in survival games.The negatives rise a bit from the PC end so consoles may fair better. I played on minimal settings(gtx1060, i7 3770, 8 gb ram, windows 8.1 pro) and my pc was huffing and puffing so this is a demanding game, so take it with a pinch of salt to buy on PC. The custom keybindings aren't solid as it messes with cleaning guns, disassembling and silent killing binded with the use medkit button! Quickloading seems to glitch out the game the more you do it and leads to some weird bugs (my favorite is being launched out of the moving train to the sky box and dying on the way down). Hit detection is a problem it reminds of stalker clearsky, freaking bullets dancing around the enemies head. Of course Artyom remains a mute, really annoying me as why have him voice over the mission loading screens? The dark ones are hardly mentioned(I say this as its too subtle) and don't make an appearance, pity. This is just a general overview of the game so not everything is greatly explained in detail or I might of missed (especially in the negatives department and reviews have a character limit) but the positives outweigh the negatives and gets my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the third entry to the post-apocalyptic Metro game series, following Artyom's footsteps and his companions’ journey across the continent of Russia. Exodus features an atmospheric survival-horror gameplay with its own mixture of non-linear, gorgeous and deadly environments to explore. Exodus features an improved weapon system with more in-depth customization options and a few newly introduced features to the series: crafting system and a day/night cycle coupled with a dynamic weather system.Highly recommend playing the previous titles  before Exodus as I think Exodus doesn’t truly introduce series’ newcomers to the world of Metro and the metro environments itself as Exodus focuses more on non-linear open levels.

_childDocuments_.review: My first playthrough of Metro Exodus was 25 hours and I went straight to the hardcore difficulty when I started the game. Which is unusual move in my over 30 years of gaming history because I pretty much always start with normal difficulty and later rank up the difficulty level when i replay the games. Then again, I have been huge fan of the previous two games and played both of those atleast 5 times. That is one of the reasons why I started straight away with hardcore mode because I knew what is the most intense and rewarding gameplay for me with Metro series. So... How was the 25 hours of first playthrough? Awesome. Terrifying, And most of all, intense as f*ck. There were so many moments when i was calculating my bullets, desperately collecting stuff to make either more ammo for my guns or supplies to stay alive in this deadly environment and trying to kill the enemies with the little I had. Exploration of the grim open world maps were super fun and those open world maps really elevates the game on a whole new level because all I wanted to do between missions was to explore if I saw something interesting in the distance with my binoculars and learn the background story of the place. One of the reasons why this game is so much fun, is the the pacing which is top notch. First two levels in Moscow are familiar radioactive atmosphere from previous games, then it follows with open world map with lots of to see and explore, suddenly game falls back to claustrophobic/close quarters level design and once again hooks the player with bigger open world map and so forth. Which means the locations have tons of variety and it keeps the game fresh and the crafting system is welcome addition because now you can change your playstyle on the spot if you want to.Is it perfect? Sadly no. One particular boss fight left a bad taste in my mouth because I didn't have enough ammo when I squared off with the beast for the second time and after several deaths and stupid mistakes, the brutal boss fight suddenly turned into a movie because I was standing in the correct place. Important lesson to the game designers, that's not how you design a boss fight. Anyway, timed exclusivity deal with Epic robbed me from last years game of the year but I'm not mad. I'm very glad that I finally had the option to play the game on store front of my choosing. Highly recommended for the previous Metro players and those who likes FPS games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphics, promising gameplay and distinct maps. All are drowned out on how much of a buggy mess this game is even though it has had time to remove such simple crashes. I have never spent a day playing this game without it crashing, that isn't even the worse part of the game either. Every other quest or area in this game has a hostage you can rescue that barely factors into your reputation with the locals as if you went loud or stealthily killed one person you are permanently vilified and have become evil incarnate. This then leads into the biggest failure of the game, if you don't want me to kill enemies where are all the non kill approaches? I have not encountered any weapons that do not kill and I am trudging through the natives map where it is almost impossible to clear it until I sit there or sleep for it to become night. Another great game edition is removing the inventory you already had to start fresh on a new map. No one in this universe likes this overused mechanic, if I have perfected my favorite gun at least let me keep it good lord. I love the Metro series but the repetition of trying to be the good guy in this game is on such an unbearable level combined with the failure of trying to evolve gun play makes this an unworthy addition to the absolute gems that are the other Metro games. Gorgeous maps though!

_childDocuments_.review: The open world is just... bland. Don't get me started on the way enemies respawn. You have to pass through a group of enemies - you kill them. 5 minutes later, they come back. There were some nice moments and story pieces with her. There were some obvious things that the characters - military people, didn't catch on. I mean - what the hell, who wrote that? _childDocuments_.review: Alright where do I start?Let's begin with the graphics: In dark areas, Metro Exodus is not too impressive, but in well lit spaces, the game shines with amazing textures, effects, lighting, it looks absolutely incredible.Sound design is also great, especially since it is an important tool to figure out whether enemies are nearby.The story of the game continues after the second part of the series, but most of the characters in your team are new additions. If you are one of those people who enjoy a game which adds a lot of story and simple ambience, you're gonna love this one. There's a lot of that here. As it is tradition with the Metro series, you can constantly choose between "good" and "bad" options, which this time actually have a more significant impact on how the story progresses before the ending.For the gameplay, let's compare it with the previous parts of the series. Instead of rather linear areas, you now operate mostly inside of a half open world. There is now a day / night cycle, which has a significant impact on the environment and on your options to approach a situation. You can still upgrade and change your equipment, but this time it is less centered on gearing up between missions. Instead, the whole equipment system has been turned upside down compared to Metro 1 and 2: There is no more military ammo and no more shop owners, but instead you now constantly scavenge two main components for crafting and utilize them at a workbench or in the field. This allows for regular weapon / equipment maintenance (yes, there is weapon decay now) and changes, and you can also craft new ammo and other equipment with it. To unlock new weapons and equipment, you take them from enemies or find them hidden within the world, instead of buying them from vendors. As with the other parts of the series, you always have the option to choose a more aggressive or stealthy approach, with stealth mostly being the better option. The gas mask, which was almost a permanent companion before, has now become less important and is only used in a few "critical areas". Stealth works the same as before, but can be a bit weird at rare times (such as not being able to knock out an enemy because he's standing 10 centimeters above you). If you enjoyed the feeling of dread and general darkness of the first two games, you will find a significant change from that here. However, the game definitely deserves all the praise it has received and I strongly recommend it to everyone who enjoys (half) open world shooters with some equipment management.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to recommend this game for two reasons. - Big design flaws, like the boss battles which are highly annoying (first bear encounter doesn't make it clear you shouldn't unload everything on him)- The path to good or bad ending is poorly designed, it's baffling and killed my enjoyment of the game. The game expects you to judge who deserves to live or die based on who the devs thought deserved to live, stripping all your experience from free will or judgement. You want to play your way ? Get punished with the bad ending if we don't like it. I didn't want to play a game that teaches me what it is to be good or bad with such stupid sense of morality. Let me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ think by myself and don't punish me with bad ending because I think some character is evil and deserves to die. Some games like Dishonored will offer you two paths that are equally fun, problem is, being stealthy in Metro Exodus is not fun at all, so requiring you to be stealthy in some areas where it is way more fun to go all action is counter-intuitive. I enjoyed my time with this game as an action shooter, but hated it in the same time for its stupid game design decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I recommend this game only when on sale, and only bundled with it's DLC.That said...I do recommend Metro Exodus, but it is a very flawed game.Not in gameplay from moment to moment, or in story or characters.More it's in how it's laid out overall. For a game that prides itself on exploration and it's vast world this time, it honestly feels like it runs out of open world steam quickly. Not to say that their can't be linear sections or that the open world is bad. But thought the game tye two beat parts are the vast open world sections.Then the rest is linear and one semi linear section. It's a shame, because it really shines when it opens up. The closed in sections are interesting, especially the one after the first open area. That one is the right one gtg for an inbetween section. And the last area is really solid too. But then you have the semi area, and it just feels clunky.Frankly each part is good in its own way, except the semi open section which has cool ideas but feels like a half assed watered down attempt to fit more open world but still be railroady. It's a shame cause I thought it would be an interesting new vast open zone, but it ends up being just a way wider corridor. It's just kinda a bummer.Really it needed another major open world section to lead into the last area. It just feels like it's rather abruptly short. Like the best portions ended to soon.I recommend it, but man, I still feel bummed by the lack of more vastness to explore. Go into it knowing your only getting 2 open world maps, and then corridors, some wider then others. The DLC are interesting though, especially Sam's. The DLC are solid expansions of the worlds story. Overall not a perfect game but solid enough, with some disappointing failures that will bug ya till the end and leave ya wishing they'd expanded the world just a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming to metro Exodus and seeing some of the problems that you encounter in 2033 and LL persist here is a real kick in the balls. I'd give this game a sideways thumbs up if it was possible. TLDR; buy the game on discount. Dear god, don't pay the full price.+ Gunplay. Not talking about combat over all, but how weapons feel in general.+ Visuals. Game looks absolutely beautiful graphics wise, and runs pretty smoothly too. Enviroments are clearly made with love and care. Character designs are great, and so are the level designs. Alot of details are squeezed in everywhere, and the maps feel like there's very little filler areas, instead every map and all parts of them feel hand-crafted.+ Sound design. Weapons have some real punch to them. Ambient sounds are plenty. Music is great.+ Weapon/gear customization. Something that you couldn't do on the fly in previous games. Weapon attachments can now be swapped mid-firefight, and useful consumables can be crafted if needed, like health, ball bearing ammo etc. Huge amount of variation in weapon tuning.+ Map. Huge-*** maps with alot of stuff to explore and search. Big variety in enviroments, from dry deserts to snow-filled cities.- Voice acting. Holy f*** the voice acting. The english voicelines are so lifeless that most players opt in to  That should be a big enough of a red flag. From what i've heard from russian players, the russian voicelines are equally terrible. But if you don't natively speak russian, might as well listen to gibberish instead of NPCs that are dead and hollow inside.- Exposition. Unskippable talking taking place right before your eyes. 50% of this game is you, sitting on your ass, listening to other people talk. And talk. And talk. If you're not a Metro superfan, these are the times where you exit to desktop to watch Youtube or take a piss while you wait for the NPCs to shut their mouths and allow you to keep playing. Ridiculous.- Bugs. Floating objects everywhere. Characters, objects and items clipping through eachother. Player physics are also screwed up, sometimes if you run and jump into an object in weird angle you get thrown up high into the air like a rocket.Apparently some game-breaking bugs stop people from progressing in the game altogether, but I haven't encountered this, thankfully.- Collision. Bullets sometimes get magically stopped mid-air when you shoot near certain objects due to their oversized collision boxes.- Weapon balance on certain weapons. You can bang a guy 3 times in the chest with a .44 magnum and he'll just do a silly tumble. He proceeds to shoot you 3 times with an AR, and you're a bunch of steaming s**t on the floor. Frustrating. To some extend, you can explain this one away with game difficulty.- AI. Combat against humans is a never ending circle of: enemy peeks -> enemy stands still -> pop them in the head.- Character animations. Their eyes and mouth moves, nothing more, nothing less. Expect moments where you're wondering aloud if your friends are androids or actual human beings. Occasionally, you wonder if your wife Anna is a bag of skin with pneumatics inside.- Lore. Shocking. _childDocuments_.review: Seems like a great sequel to the Metro-franchise.I played both previous games and loved them, I think I've played both of them through twice so far. I love the story behind these games and how the games present the story and the world their based in.+ Open world feels good, even though the side missions are pretty basic+ Weapon and equipment crafting system adds options and variety+ Story seems interesting and engaging, at least so far...- Enemies on the Volga-level (shrimps, tsar fish) are extra annoying and there's never a boat when you need one- Something seems to be off with the "screen safezone" and the blood decals which appear when shot are not scaled to fullscreenBUT.Putting aside the fact that the game was Epic Exclusive for a year after being presold on Steam, which angered a lot of people. That is not why I don't recommend the game. It's because the game is buggy. I don't mean the Bethesda-type buggy; literally game breaking, hard crashing buggy. In the Caspian Sea level there's a bug that hard crashes the game. After looking for a solution or a patch, I found out it's been there for a long time and that there are some work-arounds that work for some, not all. And this is just one of many. Before these types of game breaking bugs are fixed, I can't wholeheartedly recommend this game, no matter how great it otherwise is.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After the release of the DLC content and the free Enhanced Edition I decided to change my review to positive.I think if you can buy the complete game during a Steam sale for a price 25-35 euros then it's totally worth it. Alright I pre-ordered the game before this huge Epic store drama! I finished it today and I'd like to say a few things about it.I do not buy games too often because I work most of the time and games don't excite me that much anymore. Maybe I'm getting older (I'm almost 30 years old)Sometimes I do find interesting games that catches my attention and I buy them.So this is what happened with Metro Exodus. I really liked the previous two games and I've read stories about the rough conditions that the game devs were facing during the development period of the second game (Metro Last Light) so I was like I'm gonna support them and I will appreciate their hard work and knowledge.Okay so here's a few things. I think the graphics is phenomenal. The models, textures, weather effects and other visuals are super dope. Every weapon gets dirty after a while and it effects them. They are stop working in a middle of a gun fight and I understand the concept but I think it's a little bit annyoing. We can clean the weapons but it takes a specific crafting material.It's not a 100% sandbox game, because there are 3 big open maps and a few smaller, linear ones. I had a strange feeling that they cut out a big map to put it in the DLC but I might be delusional.There is no quick travel, you can use a car and a flat boat to travel quicker. The car is available on the Caspian Desert map and the boat is on the Volga level. Maybe it's just me but the controling the boat is annoying. It slow and it's rotates really bad. I think they should've work on this a little bit more.You are forced to use the boats because Artyom can't swim. I'm not quite satisfied with the enemy models. We've got a few human models and you will fight against them, it's justr weird when you see the same enemy character model for the 100th time.There are not too many monster models either. Maybe five? They are always look the same. They have the same behavior so fighting against them becomes repetitive. The weapons are great and you can modify them but most of the time you will stick to one weapon and you will use the rest when you are out of ammo.The story is quite predictable and it has a lot of cliches. I think Last Light has a better story overall. Paying attention to the details. This is a really weird topic because there are things such as swiping the mask that shows the developers are paying attention to the details but I've seen oposite things as well. For example when an NPC walks through a deep snow it leaves a trail behind him, but we won't. The same thing happens when you are running through shallow water, sand, or just jump on a muddy surface. There was a scene when an NPC was pouring tea in a cup but there was no "fluid simulation" the tea just appeared in the cup. Boom magic.Discovering the big open maps are also weird because sometimes the monsters are just standing next to you and they don't do anything. There are no unique side quest.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- Game breaking bugsThis game is extremely fun and I enjoyed it quite a bit. It's had its problems, don't get me wrong. The save system on Hardcore is a bit iffy and they made some strange decisions with mechanics, but thus far I've overwhelmingly enjoyed the game. However, the game is in a HORRID state when it comes to bugs and glitches. There are many inconsequential bugs, from physics bugs to clipping and so on. But those are mostly fine. You can deal with stuff like that... usually. The reason this review is negative is that the game freezes at a specific point about 15-20 hours into the game for an overwhelming amount of players with no reason why. Upon exiting a cave in the Caspian Sea area (on a main mission no less) the game freezes without warning, either crashing to desktop or forcing a task manager close of Metro. As of now I've reinstalled the game, verified game files, reinstalled my drivers, disabled Steam Cloud on Metro, cleared my cache, tried all graphical settings, have launched the game in safe mode, and every other possible fix or remedy posed online. None have worked. This bug is prevalent enough to find multiple threads with a quick google search and even a few articles on PC sites attempting to provide solutions. Until this bug is fixed, I can't recommend this game, because if you end up getting it, you'll spend over a dozen hours playing only to hit a wall that can't be passed, and seeing as how this bug has been around over a week without a word from the devs, I'd say hold off for now.

_childDocuments_.review: As i grow older, i tend to lose motivation to play games since alot of them aren't even fun anymore and i usually have to force myself to play them. But THIS game is an absolute must play, i absolutely loved every second of it. Some people may be scared off because of the change from linear gameplay to a more open-world type gameplay unlike it's predecessors. But i think they executed this change of pace perfectly.The gameplay is basically the same as the previous games, they added a cool crafting system (that somehow magically turns some random chemicals and metal into gas mask filters and ammo). Your guns can get jammed if you don't clean them often and you have to manually unjam them, sand, snow, and even falling in water affects how fast your gun gets dirty. Your gas mask can get damaged too, and if it cracks you can repair it with duck tape (it's only temporary though), and unlike the previous games you can't pick up a new mask, you will have to repair this one at a workbench.The morality system makes a comeback, but there's not alot of moral points to be earned in each chapter, most of it is straight forward unlike the previous games (also as a tip, listening to dialogues won't give you morality points, but it can give you sidequests and cool marks on the map).The locations are really cool, there's a chapter for each season of the year, and you get to experience quite some interesting landscapes, ranging from snowy landscapes to desert places. I'd say the first chapter (The Volga) is probably the Highlight of the game, but that does NOT mean the other chapters are boring.I haven't encountered any major bugs, most of the bugs i've encountered were physic bugs, and those were extremely rare, there are some game breaking softlock bugs supposedly, so make sure to back up your saves as you progress (i made a special folder where i kept all my saves from the beginning of the game to the end)The best aspect of the game for me is probably how immersive it is, i haven't been immersed in a game like this in a really long time, in my opinion, i'd say it even takes the spotlight away from the first game.And it's not only the "horror" elements of immersion, it's the family and friends aspect as well, drinking and playing the guitar with your friends on the train was one of the most real scenes i've ever seen in a video game, and i am so glad that a video game could capture that beautiful feeling.Okay i'm getting quite stupidly philosophical there, to wrap it up, this game is AMAZING. It absolutely blew my mind, i thought it would kinda disappoint me after the first two amazing games, but it's quite the contrary. I think this is my favourite metro game, and i absolutely recommend it even at full price.P.S. I highly recommend playing this game on the Ranger Hardcore difficulty as with all the metro games, not only does it help you immerse better, but i think it's the best way to experience this masterpiece of a game.R.I.P. Андрей Корзинкин
