_childDocuments_.review: About halfway through this game I regretted purchasing it, I was looking for a good post-apocalyptic shooter and what I got was a bunch of verbose NPCs telling me not to kill anyone. Of course when I didn't listen to them and earned the "bad" ending as a result, it was like a ****slap to the face.First off, the features are lying to you, this is not a sandbox survival, the world is not beautiful, the levels are not non-linear nor are they particularly huge. Your "arsenal" of weapons consists of a few moddable weapons that essentially do the same thing, some eat up ammo faster than others, most are silenced, they all kill with one headshot, but if you want to achieve the "good" ending, you should probably plan not to use any of them at all. Allow me to elaborate:Each area of the game features set locations you will visit to advance the plot and several side locations that can range from key plot point areas to simple monster nests, the game ambiguously represents all of these locations on your map with a simple question mark. In order to even know about these places you have to "scan" the world with your binoculars until you hear the "click" that updates your map which sometimes works and sometimes doesn't. It is important you don't wander off from your primary objectives or you can miss entire sections of the plot, some of which will lock you out of the "good" ending without even knowing about it. So while you technically can roam the map at your leisure it's better to approach each area in the linear fashion it directs you.The weapon system was by far my biggest gripe with this game. You can mod your weapons but all the mods you find are just basic upgrades of their previous iterations. Like the basic revolver holds 3 rounds and you can find a 6 round cylinder and then an 8 round. The stocks are the same way, adding stability and accuracy in various tiers and you'll usually just go with whatever gives you the best bonus. For some reason there's 3 different laser pointers which don't really do anything but replace your aiming reticle with a different colored dot. Typically you'll just use whatever headshots people quietly, the AI is so dumb their allies never seem to notice, and if you do get in a firefight the AI likes to find cover behind objects where their entire body and head are exposed. If you're looking for challenging dynamic fire-fights, you're not going to find them here. And besides if you approach the game that way, you'll get the "bad" ending, apparently you're supposed to just sneak through 80% of the game. Fighting critters is another matter entirely, you'll use a shotgun for those, but the videos above tease critter fights as a kind of tense cinematic experience, when in actuality you'll just mash the E button until the situation resolves itself. Ammo is pretty scarce though, especially shotgun shells, and if you use your main weapons to dispatch critters you'll find yourself running dry pretty quick. It seems like you should have some kind of backup melee weapon like a machete or something for close encounters, but you don't. For your "arsenal" of weapons you carry around two main weapons and then a 3rd special weapon that you can't replace. This is a shame because that 3rd weapon (the air rifle for most of the game) is kind of boring to use and isn't very reliable in a firefight. Weapon maintenance is also an issue, if your gun gets dirty it loses rate of fire, damage, and tends to jam up after 3 shots. While you can mod a weapon in the field, you can't clean one in the field, and you'll have to look around for the few "workbench sanctuary" locations around the map, these are few and far between and quite often you'll find yourself not using a weapon because you got a little water splashed on it and it went from fully functional to complete garbage just like that.Story-wise the game isn't terrible, it's not Mass Effect or anything like that. The characters, most of which are entirely forgettable, will jabber your ear off for DAYS about absolutely nothing of consequence in this annoying faux-Russian accent. Nothing they say advances the plot, nothing they say really means anything to you, and the funny thing is that you never say anything back to them even though Artyom does speak in the between mission summaries. Like, how hard would it have been to have the main character take part in the conversation? Obviously they put a lot of time into making these conversations and I'm sure the voice actors made out like bandits if they charged by the hour, why doesn't the main character get a voice? It makes all the character interactions awkward and one-sided, like that weirdo who sits next to you at the bus stop and starts going on and on about their pathetic life without giving you a chance to speak about your own.Another minor thing is that moving around in the game can be glitchy at times. Sometimes when you're walking you get stuck on ankle-high terrain, other times you find yourself launching off minor inclines in the geometry as if the engine was designed for off-road racing games. The game wants you to complete objectives in a fairly linear fashion, but it also wants you to explore every last nook and cranny of the map, the areas aren't huge but they're large enough that this becomes extremely tedious. And while you're wandering around you might stumble into an area that fast forwards the plot leaving out key details.Overall I'd say it's not a bad game, but it's not really a good game either. There are definitely some memorable moments and the bunker level was pretty fun. But for a game that brands itself as a guns-heavy shooter, there certainly seems to be way too large of an emphasis on just sneaking through most of the content. For a game that bills itself as a non-linear sandbox it's really more of a linear story-teller and a linear story-teller with a silent protagonist is just lame.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to say this, but this game just isn't good. I had very high expectations from the game since the first two were great, but this just doesn't cut it.The story, while not deep, makes sense for the most part and it felt natural to transition to above the ground. Characters have more backstory, and you meet some interesting folk out there. Locations are interesting and quite different between each other so it feels fresh when you go from one chapter to another. The world setting is something that I've liked.Graphics is of course very good, but even that has its downsides. More on that later.But then there are tons of problems with the game. One of the worst things in the game is the terrible voice acting. It's just so cringy and immersion-breaking, it's unreal. Of course, I've tried to play in Russian with English subtitles, but subtitles bugged out at one point and I was stuck with the entire game with two lines of stuck text on my screen. And no matter what I did, I couldn't fix it. So I had to switch back to bad English voice-overs and turn off the subtitles.Animations are the next bad thing. They just don't look nor feel good.AI is terrible. Enemies are either stupid and blind, or once they spot you, they know the exact location of yours for the entire time.Voice quality is overall not really on point, sometimes it desyncs, sometimes it just bugs out so you don't hear anything and sometimes it just doesn't sound good.There is mouse smoothing turned on which can only be turned off inside the .cfg file, including some other performance-breaking options.I was constantly encountering the bug where if I open up the map while inside the car, my head gets stuck in the car's roof. So every time that happened I had to exit the car and enter it again.My save file got corrupted four times in total. Thankfully I didn't lose to much progress, but still, it was very annoying.I also experienced a game-breaking bug in the Caspian level with the lighthouse. I had my game crash more than ten times there. Eventually, I've managed to get past it with the help of Reddit and other people who were experiencing the same problem.Graphics while very nice, there were some clipping textures and slow loadings of textures, or straight up not rendering/loading properly.All the mentioned problems are just unacceptable. Especially because they took the Epic's money and behaved as they did. After a year out I was expecting a high-quality product, but what we got is just a broken product. Shame really, because behind all the problems there is a good game, but it's burrowed too deep.

_childDocuments_.review: In the grand tradition of Russian apocalypse simulators, I've always been more of a STALKER than a Metro fan. I found the stealth mechanics of Metro 2033 and Last Light to be needlessly obscure and the shooting largely unsatisfying. The exploration of linear cramped environments was also rather dull, and the writing appeared to be either bad or lost in translation - or both.With Metro Exodus, 4A Games continues its crusade against the FPS mainstream with another grim-faced Eastern European epic. Given its underwhelming prologue with overly familiar metro crawling, lots of ham-fisted dialogue and a couple of rather silly (not to mention all-too-convenient) plot twists, it's fair to say that the game didn't make a very good first impression. But when the Aurora grinded to a halt on the banks of the Volga and Artyom got to explore the frozen wastelands around him, the whole game shifted gear quite dramatically.For a series defined by its granular approach to FPS design, it's more than a little ironic that the emphasis on (bad) storytelling and elaborate set pieces has so often drowned out the methodical, slow-paced gameplay which Metro actually demands. The fact that the new game includes expeditions into vast open areas (with a fully dynamic day and night cycle, no less) to be explored at the player's own pace makes a huge difference. While slowly making my way across the desolate landscape - constantly on the lookout for groups of scavenging monsters and enemy patrols - I found it much easier to take in the scenery and appreciate the exquisitely hand-crafted remnants of a civilization long since consigned to dust.Of course, it goes without saying that its ground-breaking graphical wizardry has something to do with my enjoyment of Exodus. In 4K on Extreme settings, the overall experience can be quite breathtaking. I found the introduction of ray tracing in and of itself to be quite subtle, but there are individual scenes (for examples, dimly lit indoor environments interacting with the daylight outside) which definitely stand out. Even if it's hard to put into words exactly what's going, it does feel like a rather seismic shift towards a new level of realism.Fighting bandits in a rain storm, discovering a gargoyle's nest on top of a water tower and sneaking through an abandonded factory to avoid being swarmed by a veritable army of mutants were some of the more memorable moments during my time in the Volga area. What really stole the show, however, was the exceptional design of the environments themselves. And while graphical fidelity can sometimes be dismissed as a superficial concern, the artistic integrity of what 4A Games has accomplished here is arguably inseparable from the sheer amount of polygons and layers of post-processing etc. which makes this simulation of Russian post-apocalyptic decay feel truly alive.While I knew Metro Exodus wasn't going to be an actual open world game, my sandbox instincts got the better of me and I broke away from the main quest as soon as possible. After having methodically explored the frozen Volga wasteland for several hours on my own, I finally got back to the train and started picking up the actual assignments associated with that region. This resulted in a lot of backtracing, since all the quests were naturally associated with places I had already cleared out. The pacing thus got somewhat weird towards the end of my Volga expedition, but at least the game recognized my deviations from the intended path with some additional dialogue (and also mercifully refrained from repopulating said environments with fresh enemies!).Making my way through the following sandbox area (the Caspian desert) was associated with a not insignificant amount of gameplay-related frustration, as my stubborn and mostly failed attempts at stealth resulted in a lot of protracted trial-and-error. A few times it was legitimately the game's fault, when the situation suddenly went from bad to worse as a result of some minor glitches combined with the lack of hard saves (only quick saves and autosaves, which at least is an improvement on earlier titles in the series). Also, the enemy compensates for their unstable AI by being unrealistically excellent marksmen, even at absurd distances (at least on Hardcore difficulty).On balance, though, the second large environment in Metro Exodus still provided a more memorable experience than the majority of first person shooters and open world games out there. The more linear sections related to the story missions were all quite enjoyable (while never overstaying their welcome), and thorough exploration of the region's many ruins was consistently rewarded with genuinely useful gear and weapon attachments.After having lived and breathed the Volga region's sublime desolation for an extended period of time, I was ready to declare Metro Exodus one of the best action games in recent memory. Alas, my enthusiasm slowly diminished - albeit never completely disappeared - during the remainder of the campaign. By the time the last level turned out to be a tedious and claustrophobic chore pared with a clumsy narrative climax, I just wanted the game to be over. But despite unsatisfying stealth, bad dialogue and some technical annoyances there were still lots of memorable moments during my intense 35 hour playthrough. Exodus represents a radical step forward for the Metro series - and in some ways even for the FPS genre itself - and 4A Games has clearly moved from scrappy underdogs to industry heavyweights with their latest release.

_childDocuments_.review: Its alright, I prefer the story of the older games though. I feel like they sacrificed intense moments and character relationships for a lazy open world attempt. Many other players have had the same issue and this game has been out a couple years already with no fixes as 4A Games seems not to listen to me or anyone.I can't recommend this game on the PC side of things, the console versions don't seem to have this issue. The game is amazing but If I cant even play, I can't recommend it to anyone at least on PC.If you own a console I'd suggest getting Metro Exodus on PS or Xbox.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro returns with Exodus and continues to be one of the best single player story driven FPS experiences in gaming. Staying true to its core mixture of intensely varying emotions throughout well-paced chapters and exciting gun play. Exodus story starts where we left off in Moscow and expands all over Russia in its lengthy story that is longer than the previous two games combined. The open world levels were slower and less intensive game play with moments less true to the Metro brand, however they were a smaller part of the game with developing story lines crucial to the game, locations worth exploring and ambience you could really soak in. Throughout the chapters you are faced with different objectives and out comes depending on play style that may affect and shape your teams survival and outcome of the game, these details are refreshing and worth paying attention to.Any moments you may feel the game begin to slow down are met with extreme bursts of action and classic Metro game play.9/10 and advised to be played on Ranger Hardcore.see here for Metro 2033 Redux reviewsee here for Metro Last Light Redux review

_childDocuments_.review: While i know the Metro series is very popular, i personally felt let down by this title. From the amount of bugs i encountered to the lack luster gun play, repetitive enemies and poor voice acting ( translated i know, its no excuse for horrible voice acting.) it felt very generic with characters always praising the protagonist for doing what ever task the leader set him on. I dont know much of Russian culture so maybe this story went way over my head but it still felt artificial. I dont rate games on graphics because honestly its a very artificial aspect of a game, especially story driven one. So that aspect doesn't affect my rating. This game has been out for a while now and i encountered so many cliping bugs, Areas i could enter i literally had to reload my previous save because i couldnt get out. and a very lack of diffrent weapons. it was, for lack of a better term, boring. compaired to the previous titles of this serie, it felt like a downgrade and a let down. 6/10 slightly above average and im being generous because i know alot of time and effort went into it but thats the best i can do for this title.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could do a neutral review.I love the Metro Series, I remember the first time playing Metro 2033 10 years ago, the scarcity of ammo, constantly fearing for your life, sneaking from enemies. It was one of the few horror games that really did it right. Metro Exodus has those moments, but in all honesty it is few and far between. They opt to go with an open world aspect of it, which I understand why they did it from a story perspective and where it was going, but the best parts of the game are the ones that are similar to the first two. I found the open world aspect in all intents and purposes lack luster, tedious, and just not fun.I really only recommend the game if you absolutely love the first two and are committed to seeing the end to Artyom's story. As a standalone game it is terrible because you are already 2 games deep of heavy story telling.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a solid 4/5 Game. The Atmosphere and level design is nothing short of exceptional. The environments are absolutely stunning. The weapon design and authenticity is superb. If i were to recommend to anyone anything about this game. It would be to play the game in Russian with English subtitles. Don't get me wrong, the game is entirely playable in English it just some of the pronunciation and language used is a bit well... off at times. Playing in Russian is definitely the way to get the best experience. The campaign is a little short if you just play it in a straight line without exploring. My only gripe is that it doesn't have the same sense of fear as the metro tunnels of 2033 and last light. There is no fear of not knowing what's round the corner or where your next filter will be. Also to play this game on Ultra at 60 fps 1080p you're going to need at least a 1080ti. I have a GTX 1080 and was playing on very High and my GPU was pinned at 99% almost the entire time. But boy is this game stunning. Easily one of the best looking games of this generation. definitely a game not worth missing

_childDocuments_.review: Critical Wall Of Text.  Hope it's interesting for those who care...I really liked 2033 and Last Light Redux and have played them multiple times now.  I didn't get to play this game until 2021 because I didn't have a good enough PC to run it.  I was aware of the developers taking the game off Steam upon its release to be sold on Epic.  Which I thought was a real jerk move and clearly done for money reasons.  It pissed off Steam users, me included.  I got the game on Steam with the 2 DLCs for a decent price since it's considered old now.  I've seen recently too that the developers are releasing an "Enhanced... Remastered" version of this game now.  Stating that it is for high-end PCs.  Which just made me laugh.  The game as it stands is for high-end PCs.  I ran this on an RTX 2070 Super with max settings.  The Ray Tracing looks terrible and makes NPCs/Enemies look like Sparkle Dust Ponies or TV static or something.  I ran into my fair share of glitches, stupid AI, FPS drops, and crashes.  I constantly had this glitch occur where I would be in the truck/van and go to look at my map.  The viewpoint in the vehicle would shift way up so I couldn't drive properly.  I'd have to get out and get back in to fix it.  Pretty game-breaking actually when you're getting your ass kicked because you can't see.It plays like Evil Within 2/Dying Light, mostly.  Leveling, crafting, side quests, open world, etc.  Although to me not as engaging or fun.  I guess I prefer a linear/tighter experience with Metro.  Having played my fair share of the Stalker series.  I feel that is what this game should have been and not a Metro game.  If you like Stalker but find it too hard, then I guess this is for you.  The game's ending was not satisfying to me either.  The game felt padded and just somewhat bland in areas.  I felt a real lack of a horror element too which may be because of the openness of the game.  It looks and sounds great aside from the Ray Tracing issues.  I do have to mention the AI again.  Not that the other games have super AI either.  I just wanted more from the enemies than Exodus provided.  I've played the Two Colonels which was fine and all, it was more like the original games.  Short and sweet, also surprisingly easy.  Not sure about the other DLC yet till I play it.  I am sure it will be decent.As for this Enhanced/Remastered thing that is coming out.  Just seems silly to me.  This game doesn't need a Remaster, it needs more updates/patches.  It just says to me that it was released too soon.  I haven't heard whether it is gonna be free to people who own the game already or not.  It's not something I will be buying.  It just makes you feel like you were taken advantage of.  A point of concern is... Unless you are really into Metro and this style of Metro.  You may only play this game once or not for a long time, due to the game's length.  So if you just played the original of this game then you are getting a lesser experience.  So no, it's not a bad game by any means.  It's just not what I wanted or expected from the series or its developers.PS... I don't know about those of you that have played through the main campaign.  The NPCs always seemed to feel like they were stating the obvious.  The means of telling you what you need to do and how to do it.  It's better than being confused or lied to I guess... lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus (ME) is a first-person shooter game with survival horror and stealth elements. It has been developed by the company 4A Games and published by the company Deep Silver.++ Journey across the post-apocalyptic Russia on a train with your heavily armed friends. Revisit the claustrophobic tunnels of Moscow, shake hands with cultists on Volga's frozen tundra, liberate slaves in the desert of the Caspian, play hide and seek with the tribes in Taiga's lush forests, and sneak around blind gorillas within the irradiated ruins of a dead city.+ I like most of the characters because they are well written, and the game gives you enough opportunities to support them. My favourites are Stepan and little Nastya; I could not refuse her plea for the heroic rescue of a teddy bear.   + Solid addons. Both of them illuminate the events around side characters that you will encounter during the main storyline. - The depiction of Colonel Miller, a hardened veteran and military leader, as a naive and irrational commander lacks credibility. And believe me, thoughts of mutiny crossed my mind several times.- Occasional FPS drops, irregular crashes, and corrupted save games. I have experienced all of it, and it boils down to... *switches to a Russian accent* completely normal phenomenons.-- Taking the game out of the Steam store, two weeks before its release, is referred to as a d*ck move in the gamer scene.I consider ME to be a great continuation of the series, and the strongest part of the franchise. It has surprised me with its open world aspects and gripping storyline. Alas, the overall impression is tarnished by technical issues, and the rushed cooperation with the EPIC Games Store for temporary exclusivity. You can do better 4A Games and Deep Silver.Recommended for fans of the post-apocalypse and gas mask fetishists. Estimated time for 100% completion: +50 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 68Multiplayer achievements: none

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a captivating and immersive experience, characters and interactions are very charming and abundant, the story is REALLY good and impactful - especially if you've played the previous metro games to have more time with the world and characters. _childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is A fantastic game, Despite me reading some reviews that say its glitchy and doesn't run well; after completing the game on hardcore I can tell you that it is a masterpiece. To sum up some of the things I loved about this game I would have to say that the world design is great along with the sounds in it, from the guns to the creatures the sound has to be one of my favorite things in the game because it makes guns loud, Like how they are suppose to be which some games fall short on.To address the glitches in the game, which every game has, the glitches I had mainly game from alt tabbing which is a pain to deal with when I want to check discord or something but I'm usually so engaged in the game I don't even check other apps. Other than alt tabbing I only had a few visual bugs which are hard to notice unless you really try to spot them.In most games I play that have story I don't normally pay attention to it and rather speed run through the game; But with the game play fully revolving around the story unlike some open world survival games (far cry). to not spoil, it was a very captivating story with a emotional ending. I noticed that some people in other reviews complained about the resource management and stealth system, While the stealth could get annoying at times I really didn't mind it and actually had fun trying to do that one challenging stealth move without being caught although I could see how its not for all people. The ammo/resource management for me was easy, that's mainly because I took my time searching every nook and cranny (which I do enjoy doing), but at times it especially near the beginning when I needed 10 more chemicals to fix up my weapons it did feel tedious, but that feeling goes away later on in the game. Ammo management is easy, just hit your shots and avoid targets that can be avoided.This Game is made for those who like Medium-High amounts of resource management, Fantastic Gun-play, Open world stories, good Character/story/sound/and world design. Overall I would rate this game a 9/10 Because some of the stealth was unpleasant and because I couldn't alt tab without the game crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro is one of my favourite franchises, so I was really excited when this game got announced. I had a good time playing this, and I do recommend it. Still, it was not exactly what I was hoping for. Compared to the last games, that actually took place in the metro, this game mostly takes place on the surface. They do advertise it as that, so it wasn't surprising. Trying something new doesn't have to be a bad thing.While the surface experience is still cool I personally prefer Metro to take place mainly in the metro. The other Metro games give an unique experience down in the metro (And a little bit outside of it), which they do so well that no other game compares. But this game taking place mainly on the surface, it doesn't do as many things that makes it stand out from other games. It just feels like another post-apocalyptic shooter when you're shooting at these raider-like bandits and humanoid ghouls. It advertises the open surface areas as non-linear sandbox levels, but they are actually quite limited at times, with a clear line to where you need to go. You get a few different paths to the place you need to get to and the freedom to reach it, but calling it "non-linear sandbox" is a bit of a stretch. There's two levels that actually feel open and invite some exploration, but one limits you with a lot of water, and the other is just pretty empty. Trying to complete parts stealthily can also be extremely frustrating because that system does not always seem to work fairly.The game still did a lot of things really well, which is why I do recommend it.Atmosphere is still top notch, and the main reason I love these games so much. The sound, the lighting, the world, they're all really good and immersive and really draw you into the game.Metro's graphics have always been really great, and that did not change in this game. The gunplay still feels good, and weapon modding is bigger and better than ever. Like the other games the story is well done, and there is plenty of lore to be found in your diary, collectibles and by listening to conversations.Having the Aurora (train) and its crew to come back to after the lonely and sometimes claustrophobic missions is really cool. There's a lot of dialogue with your crew, and they're all fun characters. There's some things you can interact with that add to the immersion, without actually doing anything for the gameplay (Shoveling coal, taking a sip from your canteen, smoking, checking different frequencies on the radio, etc.). Like the other Metro games, this game features a similar morality system and multiple endings. I personally like both of the endings, and enjoy the ending in general. The final mission was probably my favourite one.Also the game gives you a wife for the lonely under us.There's also a well received DLC that actually takes you back to the metro, and another DLC releasing in the upcoming months.

_childDocuments_.review: What it's not:Fallout. Here's what it is:A very visual and cinematic game that follows a man and his struggle for a better, less dystopian way of living. Tired of being in underground Moscow, after Soviet Russia faced nuclear destruction, our main character, Artyom, sets out in search for an oasis among the radiated, post apocalypse Russia. With a very good story and many options to approach different scenarios, I highly recommend this game for those who enjoy a good post-apocalypse RPG.  While the game is some-what linear, it plays very much like a movie and breaks from the cinema enough for you to feel as though you have the freedom to roam and create your own story.

_childDocuments_.review: Not delving into deep details, I'd like to recommend this game to people who have played the previous games. If you haven't, I'd suggest playing the older games first. To begin with, the deep atmosphere we love is present, and the world is expansive and intricately detailed. The graphics are top-notch, gameplay is solid with satisfying gunplay, and there are plenty of upgrades to tailor your playstyle.Now, let's talk about the story. I'd rate it 10/10, but it's important to note that this isn't your typical linear shoot 'em up game. You need to take your time, immerse yourself in the experience, explore extensively, read notes, listen to audio logs, and engage in dialogues. All of these elements contribute to the story, making it meaningful and providing the rich atmosphere you're seeking. I enjoyed previous games just as much as I enjoyed this one, and it's becoming increasingly rare to find a well-crafted, story-rich single-player experience these days. Ukrainian game company 4A Games has done an excellent job. (Thank you; I've had a lot of joy.) I've played the game twice now, and overall, I'd give it a solid 10/10. I'd even place this game alongside titles like Half-Life.

_childDocuments_.review: - Miller doing probably the best roundup of Artyom's misadventuresAfter many years of waiting I finally came around to play , the third part of the  trilogy. Prior to this, I already read all of the novels and spin-offs released in the west, played all the games plus the pre-4A stuff like the  franchise. So it's no wonder I was very excited when a few years ago 4A announced a sequel to the events of , vaguely based on parts of the  novel.Before the release I made sure to look up no footage, content or whatsoever about . What made me kinda skeptical though during the period of its development was the hype this game stirred up in the mainstream media. Let's be frank, the original  started as an genre underdog to a first quite unknown, though highly acclaimed Sci-Fi novel from Russia. Today, now almost 10 years later,  grew to a AAA franchise that doesn't need to hide itself from the big players of the industry.But eventually I'm happy that my worries turned out quite unfounded - in the end 4A Games delivered a solid singleplayer experience that stands true to its roots and predecessors. The doubts of other players who expected a lazy open-world clone of  or a Bethesda   also didn't come true. Metro Exodus is still a linear, classic-to-the-core FPS experience in the likes of  but with several small quirks and well-implemented ideas from open-world games.The story is quickly explained: After the events of , Artyom desperately searches for signs and ways to escape his miserable existence in post-apocalyptical Moscow of the year 2035. Together with his wife Anna he soon reveals a major conspiracy that changes his whole perspective about his life in the Moscovite Metro. Thereafter he embarks on an adventure that takes him thousands of kilometers across the Russian landmass...Of course the game puts you again in the shoes of our hero Artyom. As in the predessecors the game lets you use several pieces of firearms like the iconic Bastard submachinegun, the trusty AK or, the all-time fan favorite, the pneumatic Tikhar rifle. Unfortunately, I was dissapointed to see that some weapons from the first two games didn't make it to third game, like the Saiga-12 or the Abzats. Looking at it objectively, it can even be assessed that  has the lowest number of featured weapons in the whole trilogy.But interestingly the game makes that up by introducing the new backpack feature to the franchise. At any part of the game you can open up your backpack and modify your guns with scavenged parts. Weapons now also can get dirty which causes them to jam in critical situations. On workbenches, which are scattered on some parts of the levels, you can maintain your weapons and craft new ammunition and equipment.But still, don't expect a mindblowing plethora of micromanagement and gun-geekiness - the whole inventory and upgrade mechanics are pretty simple, straightforward and a far cry from  or similar games.Where  ultimately shines is in its level design and atmosphere. The outdoor maps are beautifully crafted and brim over with details, life, hazards and wonders. 4A Games made a great decision to move away from the dark tunnels of the Moscovite Metro to the green of the Russian taiga or the dust of the Caspian Sea, all while still keeping true to the post-apocalyptic vibe and stereotypes. Some sections of the game will also remind you of 's driving sections, with many places to stop by and to explore. And for all of you who missed the creepy and dark tunnels from the first two games, rest assured: The designers made sure to build in classic tunnel sections into each of the big maps as well, so  old-timers should feel at home just as well as newcomers.Combat is pretty much the same as in the first two games - you can either go in guns blazing or you can take the stealth route and knock out enemies from the shadows. As in the predecessors,  borrows the iconic light meter from the  series that helps you hiding in the dark. But then again, I thought that not all stealth sections of  were that well designed. Often you get detected without even knowing who could have possibly seen you and other times you laugh at the stupidity and blindness of the AI enemies. For me, this was a bit a hit-or-miss.Shooting common mutants and monstrosities is also quite straightforward and true to the franchise - nothing much to complain if you already liked  and .The story and character development on the other hand is really well written, and I go as far to say that it is the best of the whole trilogy. You will certainly empathize to Artyom's friends and their stories, and once more it's possible to achieve either a good and bad ending. This of course makes a second playthrough all the more tempting, all along with the legendary Ranger Hardcore difficulty, which also makes a comeback in .The only drop of bitterness was the terrible and sudden decision of Deep Silver to release the game exclusively on the Epic Store and therefore ♥♥♥♥ over all players who wanted to buy the game on Steam on the day of release. Their excuse to release the game a whole year later on Steam doesn't justify anything, nor does it help to cultivate fair competition among PC gaming launchers and platforms. Personally I don't think it's correct either to review bomb this actually excellent game, but what Deep Silver and Tencent did was way beyond dirty and is putting a lot bad light on 4A Games and their bright minds. As long as this trend takes place, I would recommend to boycott platforms or launchers that do ♥♥♥♥ like that until they learn to respect an equal and fair market. I know Steam / Valve is not an angel as well, but that was just terrible.Apart from that I experienced a polished, intense sequel to one of my favorite FPS franchises ever made. Personally, I still rate the original  a bit higher for a lot of nostalgic reasons, but  surely delivered what it promised. pump-ups on the Tikhar rifle

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the third installment in the Metro series and it is the first one to have an open world setting.  This open world setting does have its negative experience such as:- You are encouraged to explore the many place of interests BUT do take note that most of the time, the amount of effort taken to kill the enemies surpassed the reward that you will potentially get. In other words, if you don't mind this and just loves to explore/immerse into it then that is fine.- Some of the chapters may feel like a slog (it'll get worse if you plan to explore as many place of interest as possible)There are also some mechanics in the game that can be annoying for example:- The car feature in the desert is good but can be a pain to use it, it is quite clunky to be honest - Too many animation when changing, reloading, pumping weapons, getting into/out the car etc etc. Animation does helps with the immersion but in some of the chapters these behaviors is downright frustrating as the enemies just keep popping out of nowhere to deliver surprise cheap shotThere are some things that are done right but I've got to say that overall the general feeling for the entire play through is quite a slog and there are still a number of not so satisfying things that could be listed down. Some sections are nice and reminds us of the previous two Metro settings that we love for example the linear subway environment. Perhaps Artyom and company should have just stay underground.Metro Exodus is definitely the weaker one among the three but still, I'll recommend this game though because it still can be enjoyable but stick to the following tips and you'll be fine:- Focus on main objective- Do not go out of your way to explore the places - Some map or areas can be very confusing, in this case just slog through I guess

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, not really enjoying it.  Here's the major sticking points:The caption of the game says: "Explore vast, non-linear levels, lost yourself in an immersive, sandbox survival experience..." Well I'm three hours in and this isn't sandbox at all.  You are forced on a very linear path for a few hours before you even reach a location that is sandbox.  However, you're still only given one quest, so the "sandbox survival" is quite literally shoot stuff until you run out of ammo and die.  Following the quest is still the only option.In terms of the questing experience, oh my goodness do these NPCs talk... and talk... and talk.  Like, hey, shut up and let's go!  I don't need to hear your whole backstory, just point me to the zipline and lets get out of here!  There's no option to skip their dialogue or "uh huh" your way through it, you just have to stand there and listen; and in some cases, that means listening to them bicker back and forth, then share a toast, name the train... like, seriously.  We just got shot at, let's MOVE!Controls are weird, maybe a controller would have been better, I dunno.  Running out of ammo in the field is a pain (and thus limits the sandbox completely until I assume you unlock that gadget).  And unless you're running your cursor over every box, wall, cabinet, dead body, etc., then you have no idea if you're near something to loot, or near something trying to kill you because you're trying to find gears for crafting the only ammo you can in early game.Overall, not my thing.  I definitely expected more sandbox and less railroading quests (pun intended).

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is overall a positive experience, but not without flaws.The biggest selling points are still here, the lore, the narrative, the characters and the story. It all clicks and it's the core foundation of Metro for me, as it's what keeps the game in shape despite its flaws.I didn't enjoy a lot of new aspects which differ Exodus from previous games. The "open world" looks more like the one we got from Mafia 1 - sure, you can divert a little from the path and explore, but that's it, the linear progress is still here and will close behind you almost all the exits, you can't just "go back" and collect missing stuff or finish open cases. Speaking of those, there are no side quests of any kind, the "best" you can have are a few small activities which all look the same - go kill/knock out everybody around and retrieve an item or pull a lever, that's it.The open world on the other hand is completely empty, the only thing that exists are enemy encounters, you can't get rid of them even on the easiest difficulties where they just spawn and you have to kill or sneak past them, there is very little opportunity to explore, it feels more like a chore of the main quest that makes you visit almost all of the point of interests that are interesting, because everything else is not. I think I found literally ONE location at caspian sea which looked interesting yet the main quest didn't make me go there, and I explored whole map on each level.Personally I enjoyed the linear story of the first metros more, the "affair" with the open world didn't end well in my eyes, yes, the game is indeed located mostly in open areas as opposed to claustrophobic metro tunnels, but that's pretty much everything the game has to offer - the locations are indeed designed well and unique as the places you find yourself in, but the moment you start exploring you notice that it's all empty world that tells no story at all, even Fallout 4 did better job here by having a lot of locations that were simply interesting to explore without any quest forcing you to go inside.I'm still leaving Exodus a positive note, because it's still the Metro universe I love and it'd be unfair to put equality sign between badly designed "open world" or underwhelming crafting mechanics and the excellent narrative, story and the lore. It's still a very good game to play, but personally I enjoyed the claustrophobic prequels far more, where you could feel the struggle of living and explored locations were polished to perfection, as opposed to the "open world" we got that feels rushed and boring.If you've enjoyed previous Metro games and you're into the lore, you certainly won't be disappointed. As a starting point, I discourage, you'll get thrown into the middle of action with characters you don't know, and the mechanics won't keep you for much longer alone.---If you liked my review, you can find more of them on  and on my .

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the metro series, and have even went as far as actually reading the books after playing the first two games (which I loved, last light especially). Unfortunately, as much as I regret it, I can't recommend this game, though I see why people like it. First things first, the stuff that I like. **The stealth**  has been somewhat improved when compared to previous games, though sometimes the takedown prompt won't show up even when you should be able to get it. Enemy detection is still insane at higher difficulty and sometimes flat out makes no sense, but this game is better at making you feel like the "special forces" Artyom is supposed to be. **Gun modifications** adapting your weapons for a particular situation on the fly has got to be my favorite thing in the game by far, even though it is not very deep. **Shooting** Is decent and feels good, though I have seen better. **Morality system** Finally it makes more sense. Onto the bad - **Characters** Specifically one dimensional side characters, paired with the fact that the audio is of such poor quality really kills the immersion for me more. Each of the side characters on the train feel like the game could have been done without them and nothing would be missing. Voice acting could have also been done better imo. **Open world** Is so open it feels empty, especially in the Caspian level. Miles and miles of open desert to be crossed with (what has been for me) a buggy mess of a car. To top it off, there is little incentive to explore as all the loot you'll find at most locations is the same generic stuff. A few bullets, some scrap, some chems. The locations for gear upgrades are static, so once you know where they are you're golden.**Story** Is not bad at all, but many things feel like "padding" to make the game longer. I prefer the story of both of the previous entries in the series over this one.**Bugs** All minor, but annoying after a while. The game also tends to crash for seemingly no reason at times. **Verdict** It could have been the best in the series by far, but the bugs, with the iffy voiceacting and audio kind of killed all the immersion for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is the last game in the Metro Trilogy and is based on -and inspired- by the Novel Metro 2035 from Dmitri Gluchowski.   You once again slip into the boots of Artyom, who is married by now and a well-established Soldier, with a desire to find out if anything outside of Moscow survived the great War. And to most people’s surprise, there still exists life outside the Metro.After a, more or less, successful rescue attempt of his wife Anna, Artyom and a handful of his comrades escape Moscow with an old train. Will they survive? Will they find a place to live in the wastelands of Russia? And what is still out there?   Metro Exodus has pretty much the same gameplay loop as the two previous games. You explore the world, gather resources, craft ammunition, other necessaries, like health packs and filters for your gas mask and improve your weapons.Exodus has one massive difference thou from 2033 and Last Light. You spend most of your playtime on the surface and in three big semi-open world levels, you are free to explore and tackle objectives to some degree in an order of your choosing.  The levels are well made, and fun to play through, but they do not have the claustrophobic spooky atmosphere of the Metro obviously, which I really missed. But of course, the devs stuck to the source material, and they did a good job. But it is something to be aware of, since Exodus has a way different feeling through this.    The game looks and sounds absolutely gorgeous. The world feels and looks good, the underground levels have the classic Metro atmosphere and design we all love.  The weapon and background sounds are great, and the English Voice actors doing an amazing job in my opinion.   This is only for the Enhanced Version which I played, and I regret that I did.Thanks to the Raytracing which can’t be disabled in his version, since it is build around it, I had to play most of the open world areas with around 30-35 fps, which wasn’t exactly fun. I had Raytracing on the lowest levels and graphics on normal, but apparently a GeForce 3070TI + an Intel i7-12770k and installing it on a M2 SSD clearly wasn’t enough to handle the game. So be aware of that. If I would play it again, I would definitely choose the Normal version of the game.     Exodus has 2 DLC’s :  This DLC’s is maybe my favorite part of the entire game. It plays a long the final Chapter of Exodus to go deeper into what happened and explore the other side of the story. The entire DLC has the beloved Metro atmosphere. Loved it.     This DLC’s Story begins after the ending of the main game and follows one of your comrades who leaves the group in his dream to travel do San Diego in the hopes to see this dad again.  Also, a great DLC with a nice story a lot to explore, but it is set in an open world environment again. Can definitely recommend playing through it.   Metro Exodus is a great and well deserved round up of the Trilogy. I liked what everything leads to, and it feels like a good conclusion to the entire Story. The gameplay feels great, the characters are well written once again, and you feel satisfied to end your Metro experience with this game. If you can’t warm yourself up to the open world levels thou, I can’t recommend Exodus.  Personally, I prefer 2033 and Last Light but Exodus still deserves a recommendation.  (Since the review playtime apparently only displays the playtime of the non Enhanced Edition, my playtime as of wrting this review is 62h)

_childDocuments_.review: First, ignore my hours. The original and the enhanced edition of Metro Exodus share a Steam page, but reviews only show hours played in the original version. Any hours in the original were just me leaving the game running for cards. I put 17.2 hours into the enhanced edition.Overall, the best thing about metro is the graphics. They really are pretty. Being the first ray traced only game, I was surprised at how well it ran. At 1080p with DLSS on quality mode and ultra settings, my 2070s averaged about 80 fps, with some areas as high as 130 fps, and basically no where dipping below 60. Unfortunately, A large part of the game takes place in dark areas that require the use of nigh vision goggles, painting the world green. While I really like green, the night vision goggles really made it hard to appreciate much of the beauty.Another thing the game did really well was the AI. Enemies would regularly tell others where I was, for example “over there! Behind the barrels”. I thought that was really cool and made them feel much more like real people.Unfortunately, the gameplay didn’t live up to the graphics. The actual gameplay consists of a lot of slow walking across vast landscapes with limited supplies, which at times got really annoying. I get what the game is going for, it just not something I liked.The characters are another area where the game fell flat. After spending almost 20 hours with them, other then the 2 women, the leader, and the driver, I could not tell you who was who or anything unique about them. They just weren’t memorable or unique, but maybe that’s the point since they were all soldiers.Overall, I enjoyed the game enough to finish it, but I wouldn’t really recommend others try it unless they want to test out their new ray tracing card or really enjoy slow paced games where you spend a lot of time wandering around.

_childDocuments_.review: Having already completing this multiple times, on steam and on Epic, I cannot suggest buyinh this game unless you are a die-hard fan or it is on sale. I would give this review a sideways thumb if I could. It is the weakest game in the trilogy in terms of game play and story. When I first heard this game would have open-world parts to it, I knew that was a bad sign. Instead of sticking to the claustrophobic atmosphere and enviroment that made the original games so good, it decided to go open-world in order to cash in on how popular is with the crowed. So now Metro is a loot and shoot game, making it no different to most games being spewed out these days. One of the uniquest ideas the Metro series came up with, was using military-grade ammo as a currency. This offered the player to use the military ammo on enemies (as it is more effective than regular ammo) at the cost of not being able to buy better/ more equipment, or save it up, at the cost of being weaker. Now it is good, it's just harvesting things you find on the floor, which is plentiful. In terms of level construct, the best chapters are the linear ones, with the final chapter "Dead city" being the best of, as it resembles what a Metro game should be like, with the worst chapter being Caspian, for the opposite reasons. The chapters follow a pattern of: Linear, open, linear, and open, with the 'Taiga' chapter being a mix of both, and the final being linear. Gunplay is alright. If you play it on hardcore, humans are as delicate as you, making it fun to fight them, But mutants are sponges, and will often take more than several rounds just to take them down, which is really cancerous. Another thing is, Artyom seems to have brittle bones, as falling from 1m in the air or running down the stairs can either kill him, or wound him quite badly.Story? It pretty much sucks. The story is that you're finding a new home after escaping Moscow. However, there are no real stakes outside of Anna. This would have been fine if you consider the fact Last Light had you blow up D6 (with you inside) in order to save it from the Red Line if you got the bad ending. You can't really top it. That being said, nearly all the characters in the game are boring and 2D. The Colonel is a grumpy old man, Anna is there because she has tits, and Artyom is a plank of wood that is too shy to speak, and has to write his inner thoughts in a diary. The side characters are forgettable. None of them hold a candle to the colourful personalities that both Khan and Ulman had, and they either died/ went missing after Last Light. So you're stuck with more planks of wood. Supposedly, Pavel from the last came was supposed to be apart of the crew. He would have been the only interesting character amongst the crew, especially considering his role in the last game.The DLCs are actually worth getting.Two Colonels is what you'd expect from a Metro game, and fills in gaps for the last chapter and offers a great mini story with a very touching ending-scene, which is just as good as the ending for Metro Exodus. Sam's story is a open-world expansion, with Sam as the protaganist. He's the only member of the crew to be fleshed out, and is unique in the fact he's American. What makes it rather funny is that if you play it in Russian, he speaks English in a Russian accent, and comes off as quite humourous when he starts insulting people. The expansion offers a interesting map worth exploring, new weapons, new creatures and an open-ending. The thing I liked about the expansions is that both characters talked. This actually gives them character, and helps the story move along, as opposed to being a mute. Please make this a feature for the future instalments that are being made.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, where to start?   I went in expecting something like Metro 2033, and kind of did get that.  However,  with that came a hell of a lot more.  Incredible graphics and story telling.   Cold, gritty, solemn and scary at times.   In my time of 18 years of playing First Person Shooters there have been a handful of stunners.   First was "Wolfenstein 1992.  Second  was the game "Marathon" for Macs in 1994, and it's multiplayer ability.   Third was Halflife from Valve (1998?).   Make this the Fourth in that lineup.Metro Exodus drags you into the game from the start and you stay there in depth the entire time.  The storytelling is superb.   The game action is outstanding and can be frustrating sometimes.  It's departure after two Chapters to a semi-sandbox atmosphere is a gloriously fun change.   I got a little shooting crazy and ended up the sad ending and I still think it is the best.  Completely emotional.   I went back and played again and was more friendly, because I just had to see the happy ending.  It was good but as expected.You will be tested.  If you play over the level of "Normal", I pity you.   Hell, you'll be tested at "Normal" too.   To be honest I found it necessary to go to the internet twice to help.  Yeah, I cheated, but I still loved it anyway.  I can't say enough for this game.  I went in expecting to be bored with a game completely like Metro 2033 and came away changed.  I know that sounds corny, but it's true!

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered Exodus very early on so managed to avoid the Epic store kerfuffle that went on. I can see why it ♥♥♥♥ off a number of Steamvets, however.My main concern with the new direction Exodus was to head in was that there was the potential for it to lose too much of its "Soviet Soul". I really enjoyed the claustrophobic confines of the Metro of the previous 2 titles, as well as the games linear nature.  New open world format aside there was still enough metro spaces to get into, with Novosibirsk/Dead City in my opinion being the highlight of the entire game.Overall, the game managed to retain the magic of the previous titles for the most part, though as time goes along and replays are done, I still pine for the old metro. There is still so much story to tell back there that I hope somehow that we can return there in future. Granted many of the old characters from the previous titles remain back there so my fingers are crossed that we will see them again in some form. Perhaps the same emerging threat that has taken over Novosibirsk in such a slimy and disgusting manner since the civil war could be a good antagonist in the Mosco metro, requiring Artyom to return there.The new crafting system is quite good, though I think they should have retained military grade rounds and that currency in some format, it would have complimented the crafting system well.Graphics, as per usual, are AMAZING and you can spend much time wandering around appreciating such a well constructed world.All in all I highly recommend Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus, the final game in the post apocalyptic, survival shooter series made by 4A Games. And without a doubt this is the premier Metro experience. From action to world design, to crafting, and customization this title really brings home the core ideas of the metro series to a satisfying conclusion. With a jump to an open sandbox style experience similar to the original Crysis, and retaining the survival aspect of the first two games is frankly sublime to play. Semi open sandbox type experiences are my personal fav way to play FPS games. So when I realized Metro Exodus was doing this, lets just say I was very, very excited! Full props to 4A Games, because they really pulled it off with a large verity of locations, events, and side content to play. This time around Metro's story is decent with the iconic choices that the series is known for, and surprisingly some really decent emotional moments. Not something I was expecting from a title such as this, so it was nice to see some decent dramatic payoff. Some criticism I have is that some of the dialog is a bit cheesy, and sometimes the dialog would overlap in scenes breaking my immersion. Really kind of nit pick issues in my opinion. But the one noticeable flaw is that the game has glitches. While playing I noticed quite a few small bugs that weren't game breaking, but enough to be noticed. So would I recommend Metro Exodus to a friend? Of course! If you PC can handle playing this game, its a strong buy. Really a new high point for the series! Both the main game and DLC are fantastic. 9/10 Incredible!

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 9/10Genre: First Person Shooter THE GOOD:+ Graphicly, each level features rich detailed environments with plenty of graphic and accessibility options. A photo mode can be toggled anytime to take beautiful pictures of the scenery or gameplay. + Every level has its own unique atmosphere. Some levels are more open world while others are more linear. Each level has some great cinematic story segments that highlight the dangers of living in the world  + The game has a sense of realism with its gameplay that you don’t find in many other FPS games. Weapons can get jammed if they get dirty, you have to wipe your gas mask for visibility, charge your battery for your flashlight or night goggles, some weapons need to be pumped for maximum efficiency, enemies surrender when they realize they’ve been beaten, etc. Non of these are overly obtrusive either so you don’t feel overburdened or frustrated by these mechanics but they do a good job of reminding you that you need to be a bit more aware of what is happening. In addition, there are no traditional menu screens or traditional HUD so your entire focus is always on the game. The game does a brilliant job of keeping you immersed in the world. + NPC’s act very realistically. They have conversations with each other about the situation or the world around them in between missions. The developers did a good job humanizing the NPC and in general I liked sitting down and talking to them.    + Like previous games there is a hidden morality system which does affect how the story unfolds. Killing people indiscriminately usually results in loss of morality while sparring people grants you good morality points. Each level is designed to encourage both action or stealth depending on your play style.   + Much of the gameplay revolves around scavenging for materials to upgrade and fix weapons. Being prepared prior to battle is important and adds to the tension of combat. Different weapons types and upgrade parts further facilitate different play styles. +Both story DLC”s are excellent further highlighting the world of Metro Exodus and add many more hours of enjoyment. THE AVERAGE:+/- The main character is a mute character during gameplay which is really odd and distracting given that he narrates the story during loading screens and given how many NPC characters interact and talk to him during gameplay segments having him stay silent feels like a very odd design choice which doesn’t really work in this case.  +/- In between missions you have to listen to many NPC characters talk and as realistic and cool as it is, non of this is un-skippable making subsequent playthroughs frustrating.  Conclusion: One of the most immersive games I have played all year. I loved exploring the world scavenging for items while trying to survive every combat encounter and seeing the story unfold. Highly recommended for any fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing and soul-stirring game! I fell in love with the gripping story, soundtrack and brutal combat. The story is about human connection and sacrifice. Without giving too much away, the great lengths that Artyom goes for his wife Anna culminates in a very satisfying ending and is sure to tug at your heartstrings.I will say though, you will need a little patience with the game. It develops a little slowly in the beginning and the combat takes some getting used to but, given enough time, the storyline comes together really well and the characters end up being memorable.The combat is BRUTAL and stealth-driven. You will need to be on high alert every step of the way because ammo and work benches are limited. The horror element is very well done and lends itself to the gripping nature of the game.Oh and did I mention how incredibly good the graphics are? I played the PC enhanced version (highly recommend) which allows you to fully customize raytracing settings. I cranked those settings to "extreme" thanks to the powerful 6900 XT and boy do the environments really transform. Since this a post-apocalyptic game, the everything around you is almost always rusty, dilapidated and just plain dead or mutated. This is in my top 5 of the most graphically beautiful games I've ever played. If you're looking for a stealth-based post-apocalyptic game that you will have you at the edge of your seat throughout the entirety of the game, look no further! You will not be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The crowning jewel of the Metro franchise, showing that a sequel can still be in touch with the heart of the originals without becoming formulaic.Metro Exodus is, in my opinion, a solid 8/10. It has solid, fun gameplay. Great difficulty (if you're into that), amazing graphics and a heartbreaking story. Know that I feel that this game is just about perfect in every way except for some few things that I will now list:- Annoying movement bugs that can have you stuck for a couple minutes as you wiggle out of it- Unstable areas such as Caspian that are prone to crashing with the wrong settings (V-Sync, etc.)- Not being able to listen to cassettes while moving, and not being able to have conversations on the train near the workbench. There is a lot of story in 1 on 1 dialogue and diaries in this game, and there is basically no way to make this more engaging in game, you just have to sit through it if you want the entire story. Being able to read the diary entries you find in the game at your workbench while listening to the radio would have been nice.- Linear weapon upgrades for a lot of weapons. The later upgrades are usually just straight up better.- Not enough clues and relevance to the locations for rare equipment. You basically just have to scour the (quite big) maps to find these, which gets a bit annoying.- Quite apparent Deus Ex Machina shenanigans. VERY CONVENIENT gas mask filters during story sequences so you don't run out of air, etc. Wish they had found another way to do this.- NO FOV SLIDER- Messing with the FOV in the settings messes up the graphics for the binoculars and damage indicators. Going to 90 FOV (bare minimum for PC gaming IMO) breaks weapon viewmodels.- Messing with the FOV also seems to misallign some of the scopes, especially at long ranges, with the bullet going above where you're actually aiming.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still a fun experience, because it's still Metro. But, Metro Exodus is definitely the weakest entry in the series.Voice acting is horrible this time around, something the previous games were at least competent, or great (Pavel in Last Light) at. The story is very bare and the horrible direction and line delivery killed any possibility for it to be interesting. This is especially jarring since the intriguing stories are what originally helped the Metro franchise succeed.Every open world set piece is essentially exactly the same with a different coat of paint. You go to a zone, there are lunatics there, you do a small quest chain to allow the train to keep driving and move on. There is barely any side content, and what is there isn't meaningful. And don't get me wrong, I'm the last guy who wants side content in Metro, I hate that they opted for an open world game in the first place.Then, you have the bugs. New Game+ is still bugged to this day, where at a certain point in the game, there is a very good chance that you won't spawn with any weapons. DX12 crashes are as present as ever and sometimes the game just freezes to 1FPS for a minute or two and it just might catch itself again, but it also might not. Some of this is fixed by simply switching to DX11, but then you miss out on the beautiful raytracing. Oh well, better safe than sorry when you are doing an Iron Mode playthrough.The human AI also kinda sucks. You feel that the hardest when you are playing on any Hardcore difficulty and sniping an enemy position from a solid 100-150 meters away, only for them to have pinpoint accuracy on your head with their Bastard guns and killing you in an instant.Because the story is so mediocre, the endings aren't impactful either way. In the bad ending In the good ending, well, it's obvious how it will play out if you've seen the bad ending. It's similarly uninteresting, especially compared to Last Lights amazing ending(s).But, the game has its merits. When you're not in one of the open world levels, the story moves at a nice pace and things speed along. These areas are where the game shines and the most important and interesting plot developments happen. Gunplay is also quite interesting, you can modify your weapons on the fly and add/remove attachments at will. You can also craft some stuff in the open. More sophisticated crafting requires workbenches. The game is extremely gorgeous as well. Raytracing certainly helps but even without it, you can't deny that it's a beautiful game.All in all though, this game  qualifies for a positive review. I just hope that for the next entry, 4A Games decides to go back to a linear, more focused approach. And please, ditch Artyom for the next game since his story should effectively be over. And give the next protagonist a voice. It gets increasingly annoying how they work around Artyom being 'silent'.

_childDocuments_.review: Oooookay, then. This is a tough one. Let it be known before we proceed forth that I've been an avid fan of the entire Metro series and the universe it's based in since I played the first game all those years ago, though, let's switch to the game at hand before this turns in to a drawn out description of all the fond memories I have of 2033 and Last light.Like its predecessors, the first thing I noticed as the game opened with the starting scene, was the eye catching visuals. The atmosphere was much like what I'd remembered from my prior experiences, the subtle glare reflecting off the mask, the vision obscuring splatter of viscera that you'd have to wipe away every now and again (or just leave it there if you're in to that sort of stuff) is all there.I began the game in high spirits, expecting a great adventure, a hero's journey, and while I did get much of what I sought, my largest qualm was with the fact that every interaction between/with NPCs is horribly presented. The voice acting's good, but executed poorly, conversational progression left me feeling largely disconnected from all the characters in the narrative, and it felt as if the words being said merely for me to listen, and not to tell the story.The gameplay's good, though plagued by some pretty severe bugs that'd need to be resolved before the game's fully enjoyable. For example, I played the game and traversed through some pretty tedious bits of the first map, only to find my save from 1 minute ago deleted, and my progress set back by 40 minutes instead, which is highly aggravating.I've always been a fan, I will remain one, but I've been a fan of the story, the narrative, the fact that Artyom and the characters felt more alive in the previous games than they did in this one, and I think that's what  they need to go back to for any future endeavors. As for this one, I'd say it's definitely good, but well.. I guess most can't buy it on steam for a year or more, and I hope all the issues are resolved before then.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Stalker and the Metro games following it, I loved the Slavic take on the post apocalyptic world-building compared to that of the rest of Europe and America with it's mostly Happy-Go-Lucky games like Fallout, Borderlands (not in America but an American developer anyways). Something about the cold nuclear winters, frost kicking onto your visor as  you wipe it off with a dedicated hand button and the constant ticking of the Gieger counter firmly reminded you that the world with the now-deranged mother nature is far more dangerous foe than anything you will face. When it is shown that the new Metro game will take place mostly outside of Metro, fans were rightly skeptical as one of the core series strength was always the dark interconnected tunnels of the Metro stations of Moscow which drenched in atmosphere which other games in the genre could hardly come even close to. After having played this game in hardcore difficulty, which took me around 30 hours as I took my time as I usually do in these sort of games; I am happy to say that the new open environments are not detrimental to the series core, in fact the the claustrophobic metro sections are still there in the game and elevated up several notches in atmosphere.This game at its heart is probably the closest to Half-Life 3 and a true Crysis sequel we are ever going to it. The one year journey as the game takes you across the desolate Russia with your wife and the people of your ‘Order’ evoked me feels of Half-Life which I have not gotten for so many years, damn I missed that. The maps are not open world, but many are very large, giving you multiple ways to tackle problems, just like Crysis. Also debuting is a on-site attachment system, again similar to Crysis in many ways. That is not to say the game simply borrows everything and calls it a day, there is still the Metro atmosphere which really gels everything together. You have a mobile hub, a train called the Aurora. Here the game becomes a little bit like immersive sims like Deus Ex. Here you get to talk with your crew and play with the weapon modifications. I was surprised how lengthy dialogue can get with you or when the crew is talking amongst themselves. It is a non-issue as you are forced to listen to everything, but I like how the dialogs were often long and felt ‘real’ as opposed to a minute or two conversations. These Aurora sections bring the much needed downtime, especially when you consider how brutal the game can get at times. The thing which bothers me a lot unfortunately is the English voice acting, it is simply not good most the time, minus your wife Anna. It feels like an amatuer person reading off the script, also the voice writing is off for me as well. I heard it sounds a lot better in Russian and it does, however it hurts my gameplay as I constantly checking the subtitles will force you to the bottom third of the screen a lot of the time as you would be missing out a lot in front of you. You don’t want to miss out on that one as Metro Exodus, just like it’s peers, is gorgeous. It now has a dynamic day/night cycle and RTX users can enjoy true Global Illumination which makes the game look even more realistic. Even if you don’t have RTX GPU, the game is absolutely jaw dropping on my GTX 970. I get a good 45-60fps on high settings and the frame rate mostly stays high during combat so it doesn’t bother me. Although bear in mind that the frame rate can vary a lot depending on the location you are in and what you are looking in front of you. There are some off low resolution textures on certain objects here and there, which is a shame but not a deal breaker but overall though, this game is a stunner and easily one of the best looking games out there on the PC.I played it Hardcore difficulty and I suggest everyone to start playing from this difficulty as it tunes the game the way it is meant to be played. Ammo and crafting supplies will be scarce, I had to make difficult decisions like breaking down my ammo for some materials to craft a filter for my mask for example. On this difficulty, you will regularly making such decisions, although it never it felt like it is the focus like a disaster management game. It made me appreciate the gameplay systems even more. The gunfights can be very lethal on hardcore difficulty. 2-3 shots or a shotgun blast can kill you, same rule applies to the enemies. The enemies are challenging because of this, but unfortunately the AI isn’t that good. They take cover and aim pretty good but they never force you to fall back rethink your move. Careful planning and the right gear with the right modifications can make all the difference.Speaking of gear, the weapons and items in metro exodus looks and feels very real. It has that raw look which tech and junk strapped together to make it function which I love. Weapons will degrade overtime in the weather, and will cause it to jam or shoot off the mark when it happens. So it is always a good idea to take note of your gear before heading out. There are also crafting stations outside of the Aurora which will allow you to make ammo and clean the weapons.I did not feel much for the story but in the end it truly grabbed me. It shows the desperation of how far we will go for the people we love. As someone who lost the love of his life very recently, it teared me up. Rachaelle my love, if you read this, I am sorry I failed you.They simply do not make games like this anymore. It was longer than I expected as it took me around 30 hrs to beat in my own pace. It is very unfortunate the steam/epic thing blew to the point the game suffered in the public view. For those are waiting for the steam version of the game, trust me this game will be worth the wait. Make no mistake, this is a great game...one which I wish my girl friend watched me play from...wherever she is...=========My System=========Windows 10 proIntel Core i5 4570GTX 970 OCed16GB RAMSamsung 840 EVO SSDGame installed on a Western Digital Green HDD

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off as a bit clunky and slow for a modern game and takes its sweet time setting up the premise, but when you're let loose into the postapocalyptic wasteland, there's no going  back - the atmosphere sucks you right in and doesn't let go.It's not the extreme open world I was let to believe in advertising, but it's actually better for it. It's the perfect blend of open and linear. There are several quite big open maps with each it's own postapocalyptic style and within these maps there are more closed off linear levels with more horror elements. They even put normal action levels between the open levels.The looting is a little half done for a postapoc game, with only two crafting elements to make everything, but scavenging for these everywhere might also get you better gear and weapon upgrades. The weapon system is very cool and extremely wastelandish: You can for instance take a simple thing as a revolver and build it into a sniper rifle with the right mods.And then there's that constant fear of not having enough filters for the gas mask or that your weapons get so dirty they won't shoot properly. Not to mention your headlight running out of battery as a mutant jumps you in a dark corridor.What this games lacks in size and quality to games like Fallout 4, it makes up in sheer atmosphere. At the moment I can't think of another game with better Mad Max/Wasteland feel than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is an interesting final piece to the Metro Series, it changes some aspects of the first two games by introducing the crafting system and better  customization options for your guns, although not a major change, it allows the game to be a bit easier in some aspects as you can now craft some ammo on the move. Metro Exodus for the most part is still a great game in my eyes and doesn't let my hopes down, staying true to the same aspects of the previous two games. But occasionally the crashes and the look sensitivity the game has to offer occasionally made me want to put the game down.
