_childDocuments_.review: This game, was amazing honestly I enjoyed most of it as not to say this game is perfect 10/10, most games will not be, always gonna be that one glaring issue and in my opinion in metro exodus that one glaring issue is just bugs!THE GOODThe good is that most of its good, the story makes sense and safe to say its really action packed and really has no issue, sure some parts could be boring some parts may be found a bit difficult/you may have to think of some other ways, but this may be for specific people as I rarely got bored of the game, I really got tired and really recommend taking breaks as well, don't get me started on the scavenging and crafting, the scavenging is great, need a weapon and pick it up? hold e, need to grab ammo from a weapon or just the attachments? hold r, although sometimes I do recall there being an issue with looting corpses by guns, which obviously when you kill an npc/enemy they drop their gun near them, so that may be hard and cause some issues, but the attachments you get by pressing r can be used via your backpack, which I wanna point out I appreciate that the gun fight dosent stop making it feel like a "game" it continues as a real life gun fight would, it wouldn't just stop. Whole point is with the backpack system you can change your attachments instead of in previous games where you would have to either use military grade bullets, or pick up enemy weapons, but maybe take some compromises, or do a mix of picking up weapons and spending bullets, you can do what you want alongside crafting some other small items like cans, and it mainly eliminates the need, dont get me started on how your gun can jam now and where at one point my gun was so dirty during a fire fight, it basically made my ak a burst gun where I had to pull the charging handle back after a few shots, stuff like this makes you consider your resources if you should clean or maybe craft more ammo for your next journey, knowing your gun might jam more often, alongside that you can pick up stuff like green mushrooms to use in crafting/ scavenge lockers, boxes, corpses for any craftablesOk, I wasnt always a stealth guy whatsoever always going in gun blazing but some missions stealth is full on required, or just recommended for the amount of enemies, but I never went stealth that much so I can't comment on it, but it seemed ok and kinda punishing if even one guard spots you, but that would be how it works if someone sees an enemy they are gonna scream and make sure all the guards know, you also have cans and throwing knives to assist you if you decide to go stealthThe story really isnt a mess, the total gameplay I found is around 15-20? hours and it depends on how you spend your time what you explore what you don't, which I also really like how you can explore the world and hows it a bit less linear than the previous games, although you don't have to do them if you want to and progress with the story, although if you do more content and all that, you also have to consider the fact that people speak/do stuff that you may wanna listen to as it adds to the world and makes you feel like your part of the world, and not just the whole word, people having normal convos a drink yata and some of it can be interacted with. _childDocuments_.review: It took me a long time after finishing the game to decide whether to give it a positive or negative review. However, since the game suffers from many of the problems plaguing previous Metro games and the scarcity of gameplay improvements, as well as the constant annoyances and performance problems, I can't with clear conscience give it a thumbs up, even after buying it at a decent discount. Unless you're a massive fan of the previous games- you'll feel right at home here. All in all, this game has a lot of unrealised potential, if only the devs had more time to polish it and courage to make this game something more than "Metro 2033/Last Light (mostly) outside the actual metro". I do hope the new Stalker game eventually comes out and shows them how it's done. Strong points:+ Atmosphere and environments - as expected in a Metro game, Exodus is still pretty creepy and full of that post-apocalyptic atmosphere the series is known for. The change of scenery did little to change that thankfully.+ Visual/sound production - the game is a marvel to look at and listen to. The environments really come to life thanks to this and they do a great work in supporting the game's atmosphere.+ Save system - one of my biggest grievances with the previous games was the awful checkpoint system. I'm not a fan of those in general, but the Metro series had one of the worst ones I've ever seen. It actually stopped my Metro LL Redux playthrough since the game saved just as I was suffocating due to having my mask damaged in a boss fight. Fortunately, one of the biggest quality of life improvements 4A Games made in Exodus was the introduction of quick saves and multiple save slots (although shared with checkpoint saves). It really made a huge difference to the game's enjoyment. I'd prefer a full-blown manual save system but I'll take what I can get+ The weapon modding and crafting system is a really good inclusion, even if a tad unrealistic.Weak points:- Performance and stability - par for the course for this series, it's bad. I was getting regular hitches, particularly in combat, on a fairly beefy PC and medium settings. Even worse, the game would freeze fairly regularly in one of the big open areas at the start of combat, forcing me to manually restart. I didn't lose much progress thanks to my constant quick-saving habit, but it was really annoying.- The game is missing vital settings; for instance, there is no FOV slider - you need to edit the config file for that; and even then, some HUD elements did not scale at all. Moreover, since the game has stability issues and really does not like being minimised it benefits from borderless window mode a lot - however, it's not possible to select in-game. You need to modify the the config file AND use a 3rd party app to force a full screen window. That's not ok.- Human AI seems to only have 2 modes: "completely oblivious" and "you breathed a bit too loudly so now everyone know exactly where you are". In a game which emphasizes stealthiness it's a big deal.- Ranger Hardcore difficulty is still a joke. This one is a pet peeve of mine with this series and I was hoping they'd finally change it since it would add to the immersion; but no, it's still as idiotic as ever. Removing the HUD is cool and all, but then you get stupid crap like not being able to see the selection menu for throwable items. This whole thing needs a deeper rethink.- The gunplay is only alright. It involves mostly either peeking out of cover for a moment and headshotting ranged enemies or blasting mutants charging straight at you. It's the bare minimum to call this game an 'FPS' but it gets old fast.- The ending of the game isn't great in terms of gameplay. It has great atmosphere but it's a slog to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sadly pretty disappointed with this addition to the Metro Catalogue. They really missed the mark on what made Metro special. I wish that the last 10% of the game was the entire game, that is the only part of this game that met the feel of Metro. Everything else feels like Far Cry. I like that they have moved this toward as a more open world experience, but I want to explore post apocalyptic nuclear winter Russia/Ukraine. Why they felt the need to bring us to a desert and a taiga is beyond me. There are a few core things that really made me not enjoy the game over all...- The crafting at first feels cool... but then your realize... oh I can just craft a med-kit, or ammo, or filters almost anytime I need them. Completely killing that tension that the original Metro's builds by having to manage your very limited supplies. Hell, even having bullets as a currency which was such a cool idea, was scrapped.- This also kills stealth. Stealth in the original Metro games were not entirely optional. You were out gunned and out manned. You took stealth more seriously because you couldn't afford to waste supplies in a gunfight. Gun fights in this game felt like a joke. The AI is far too dumb, the supplies you have are plentiful and as long as you have cover, you pretty much have unlimited heals. I never felt at risk, there are even times I would just charge the enemy head first knifing people.- Crafting also killed the tension of gas mask as well. This was such a core part... the gasping for air... the feeling of not being able to linger because you only have so much oxygen. Pretty much completely gone and almost entirely un-utilized for the majority of the game- Are there even any gas mask effects anymore? I don't remember getting my mask smudged with blood or water or snow in this game... only patching a hole and leeches.- They pretty much killed the psychological horror aspects the game except at the very end - super disappointed in this. I loved the idea of the horror being so significant that it is imprinted on the location. I wish they had expanded on this.- I found it way more difficult to be invested in the story. I don't even know why. Almost every dialogue with the exception of the end of the game felt more like roadblocks and filler than something meant to be there. I always felt like I wish I could skip it and get back to the game or wanting NPC's to get out of my way. I never felt this way ever with the original Metros.- The in-game chatter dialogue felt was too sanitized... like this is a supposed to be an adult game, but the insults sound like something out of a pixar game.- Some of the weapon design felt good, but some of it felt a little too steampunk and unrealistic. Even the AK just seemed to have a weird design.- Also, forgot to mention that there are still some game breaking bugs. My first play through I like 80% the desert area and had a bug that prevented me from progressing the only fix was to restart the whole level from the beginning... which is like 60% of the entire game. My second play through was less buggy, the only major bug I had was being dropped out of the sky and getting stuck falling under the ground forever - I was expecting there to be a teleport plane, like most games if you somehow glitch under the map, but no dice here. Had to reload - not a huge deal but kinda breaks immersion.- What I enjoyed was the combat and weapon customization. Although the AI was bad and didn't feel challenging or intelligent, the gun play felt fun.- The desert map did feel a bit disjointed compared to the taiga map, but from a design aspect they did a good job even if it wasn't what I was looking for.- They clearly put a lot of time and thought into the maps' progression and flow. I very rarely ever felt like I was picking up an new inferior attachment. Almost all attachments were actual upgrades.To be clear this game isn't bad by any means. It is good for what it is, but what it is, is not a Metro game... It just isn't. The tone, the feel, and the core elements are just not there. I want to see a open world Metro game that has handcraft areas that are seamed together through a metroidvania style progression. I want the same brutality that existed in the first games. The starvation for supplies. The feeling of being at the bottom of the food chain. The uninhabitable unforgiving surface. Way more psychological horror elements. I want do dredge through the underbelly of the Metro. I don't want Far Cry in Metro. Sadly, I doubt I will ever see this game.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------DLC's>The Two Colonels: I enjoyed this way more than the main game. It wasn't perfect, and definitely felt like a bit of a theme park ride; taking you from 1 point to the next. However, the vibe was very Metro in comparison. The story telling was far more compelling in my opinion than the base game. I really enjoyed it for what it was, and the storytelling made up for the fact that it felt like a theme park ride.>Sam's Story: So far, I hate it. I haven't finished it yet, but I will, and will update this... There is so much pointless dialogue that (at least appears to be) unskippable. The main character doesn't sound like an American who has lived in Russia. He sound like someone reading lines who has no idea what they are saying. He is constantly mispronouncing Russian words... just annoying, but not detrimental to the game play. Also, this constant acknowledgement of Sam being American and constantly being addressed as an American is super cringe. Really feels like the devs were just trying to placate to an American audience... which is fine... but like... can you be a bit more subtle about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 10/10I've never been a fan of story-driven games, but the Metro series, and especially Metro Exodus, touched my heart in ways I never expected. It's not just another game; it's an emotional journey through the Moscow Metro and into the harsh Russian wilderness in search of a new home. that hooked me from the start.Metro Exodus offers a gripping narrative without feeling overwhelming. It strikes the perfect balance between storytelling and gameplay, making it accessible and engaging even for those like me who typically prefer action over plot.The characters are well developed, and their relationships evolve throughout the journey. The choices you make carry weight, making you genuinely care about the fate of Artyom and his companions.Lastly, the graphics and audio are top-notch. The game's visuals are stunning, and the sound design immerses you in the eerie and dangerous world of Metro.This game proves that even if you're not a fan of story-driven titles, Metro Exodus can convert you. It's a rare gem that transcends genres and offers an unforgettable gaming experience that touched my heart and will stay with me for a long time. Don't miss it.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a first person shooter set in the aftermath of a nuclear war, where a small group of survivors live in Moscow’s underground rail network. This is the third game in the franchise, following Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light. The player once again controls Artyom, as he leads a squad of soldiers on a quest across the country.• Combat is enjoyable and fairly challenging on normal difficulty.• First 90 minutes feels very restrictive, with lots of lengthy dialogue scenes broken up by a few short combat sequences, during which you have an AI partner constantly saying “hey go over there, do this”. Thankfully, when you reach the open world sections, the game finally backs off and allows you to explore at your own pace.• The world is a dangerous place, inhabited by several different types of enemies including Human bandits, Humanoid mutants, dogs, Watchmen (large wolf-like creatures that hunt in packs), flying demons, giant shrimp that live in lakes, giant spiders hiding in dark tunnels, and some boss level creatures that I won’t spoil. Occasionally you’ll notice the bandits and monsters attacking each other.• Weapons feel great to fire, and include pistol, shotgun, assault rifle, sniper rifle, crossbow and the Tikhar, which uses air pressure to silently fire metal balls. Each weapon can be upgraded with mods to improve damage, accuracy, clip size, as well as changing how they function, such as different types of zoom sights or silencers. You can carry three weapons, which allows your loadout to have a nice mix of short range, long range and stealth.• Its often a good idea to use stealth if possible, take out enemies silently, or avoid them completely to conserve ammo. Going loud usually attracts more enemies, and you can’t recover ammo from looting monster corpses, so you could quickly run out of ammo. You can craft more ammo, but crafting resources are limited and probably better spent on medkits and gas mask filters.• Open world has a day/night cycle, and weather conditions like rain and sandstorms, which reduces visibility both for you and your enemies. Some areas are heavily irradiated, requiring you to wear a gas mask and change the filter periodically to avoid suffocating.• Main story took 19 hours to finish. There are two different endings depending on your actions during the game. (I got the good ending :D)• Main story is mostly well written.• Voice acting is fine, but I’ve heard better. • Your squadmates don’t just exist to shoot stuff, they’re living their own lives.• Artyom is a silent protagonist like Half-Life’s Gordon Freeman, which feels very weird because the other characters constantly talk to him during cutscenes. Its especially ridiculous every time they try to call him over a radio while on a mission. “Hey, Artyom, are you okay?”. Do they expect him to answer?• I suffered some frequent stuttering, even though my PC (i7 6700K @ 4ghz, 16GB ram, GTX 1080) is comfortably above the recommended spec shown on the store page. After adjusting some settings I had a constant 60 FPS, but occasionally it would freeze for half a second, which was very noticeable when turning my mouse sideways. Strangely, this was worse in the narrow underground tunnels at the start and end of the game, and it actually performed better in the open world areas. It never hurt me during combat, but it was annoying while exploring.• Controls are fully rebindable, however there is a quite annoying bug. I prefer to use arrow keys for movement (yes, we still exist), but there are some scenes where you sit down while listening to an NPC talk and you have to use WASD to interact with objects, or to leave the conversation, meaning that I had to change my keybindings back and forth several times.• When exiting back to main menu I frequently got a message suggesting that my saved games had been corrupted. I never actually lost any progress so I always just ignored the message, however you might want to research this further before purchasing. Maybe I just got lucky.• There are two DLC missions where the player controls different characters. The first takes place during the last mission of Artyom’s story, the second is set after the end of the main story.• Combat is the same high quality as the main story. The first mission adds a flamethrower to the player’s arsenal.• The stories are less detailed compared to the main story.• The first mission is quite linear and lasts around 2 hours, while the second mission contains a new open world area and took me around 7 hours to finish.Metro Exodus has enjoyable combat and a good story, but is let down by some technical problems. As the game has already been out for a year on the Fortnite Kids’ Anti Consumer Store, I doubt these problems will be fixed now.Still, its worth playing for fans of the FPS genre, and the Metro franchise. I bought the game plus DLC for 40% off, which feels like a fair price. If you’ve never played Metro before, I’d recommend picking up 2033 and Last Light, because they’re also really good.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very good game. The game brings in friends from 2033 and Last Light rewarding long time players of the series. That being said, it is still a complete game even if you haven't played any Metro before.The game was surprisingly jam packed with content. Easily over 10 hours by just focusing on main missions and omitting side quests. But way more if you explore the maps to the fullest (which is pretty rewarding in this game). The story is rich and full of character; there are lots of times where you can simply listen in to characters having full dialogues. The game feels so alive and like you are actually part of it so it's very immersive. The combat is pretty fun and if you wanted, you can go full stealth except for a couple of scenarios. There are lots of cool guns, attachments, and upgrades you can receive just by exploring the maps which made combat feel fresh even towards the end of the game. There are 2 endings based on basically being a better person (good ending) or a bad ending in which you don't respect others etc. It was easy to get the good ending without a walkthrough so just pay attention and be smart and you can get it.Anyways, the game certainly is worth it and I was totally immersed and invested in the story. There are a lot of challenges you face and have to overcome and it gets pretty emotional at times. I think this is the best Metro released to date and it feels like all the work from Metro 2033 and Last Light has paid off and you complete the dreams of the characters you have come to know and appreciate. Now besides the story, the game was very heavy to run at times and I'll admit it was a low fps slideshow during some encounters and I have an above average pc granted I am playing at 1440p. I also crashed probably 10 times from start to finish, maybe more. Make sure you are running dx11 in settings and try to save often so you don't lose progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is solid, unlike half the objects in the game. The "open world" gimmick is based on a single handful of levels. MG rounds are absent entirely.Crafting is very bare, and is a bandwagon thing. Do it proper, or not at all. My biggest letdown though, it ends out of nowhere. Absolutely out of the blue. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: An interesting experiment that pushes the franchise into new ground, while stubbornly repeating old mistakes.Exodus is an ambitious game. Whatever else I say about it below, I want to put that out there first for  context. The first two games were ambitious too, of course. What they managed to achieve with their limited budgets was, quite frankly, astonishing. However Exodus is ambitious without that caveat. They have taken the leap in moving from a pretty corridor shooter of 7 hours duration, to a somewhat prettier corridor shooter of 15 hours, to full AAA level Odyssey adventure of 30 hours spanning multiple unique semi-open environments, with boats, vehicles, and several dozen different enemy types. So, whatever else you might have to say about Exodus, nobody can accuse the team of failing to deliver enough content, or enough play time. And nobody could say that they weren't brave enough in trying out new ideas. The developers should also be commended for sticking with the immersive, simple UI of the original games. In moving into the realm of the semi-open world genre with crafting they did not simply unthinkingly adopt the tropes of that genre, but made their own version of it. The in-game backpack and craft table UI is excellently done. The weapon attachments and choices are also well balanced. The scarcity of resources in hard core mode was really appreciated. Although a larger budgeted, more mainstream product, Exodus is still willing to make its hard mode actually reasonably hard for the most part. One of the gripes I had with Metro II was that it was so common to find you had more ammunition than you could actually carry, especially when fighting other humans. In Exodus I actually found myself counting my bullets. The paucity of supplies works well with re-usable weapons such as the knife and the crossbow, rewarding you for patient play by giving you more leeway for those sections when you really need some reckless firepower. There are also some really nice simple improvements that I appreciated after coming from Metro I and II. Some of the gripes I had, such as the simplified UI being -too- simple, so that you could not even see how many bullets you had by holding tab, have been dialed back. Something else I really appreciated was the environments. The first open area, the Volga, in particular, is my favorite. There was a point early on, maybe after I had spent an hour wondering the Volga, where I felt that Exodus was -the- grim apocalypse survival game I had been waiting for. Something to rival a nicely modded Stalker game, or a heavily modded Fallout 4. There were multiple places of interest to explore. The flow of looting, sneaking, shooting, and scouting all flowed so nicely. The atmosphere was cautious. A little grim, but a little relaxed. While in the first Metro games you often find yourself overwhelmed by the stress of 30 minute sections of terror, here we had that pleasant interchange of tension and relief, that I love about open world games. It was executed perfectly. I was in love. If you would have asked me for a score, 4 hours into Exodus, I would have said 9/10.Then it all began to fall apart. (Warning, some mild spoilers about the main plot follow.) Firstly, the story... Things got concerning when I realized my beloved.... I honestly forget her name and I have just completed the game... had developed a cough after exposure to a toxic gas. It was immediately obvious that the game was going to turn into a McGuffin search to save our darling. I felt very disappointed. The stakes were laid bare. The mystery shattered. We are going to save the damsel in distress. And this will supposedly be the emotional core of the game. Going forward that turned out to be entirely correct. Unfortunately, if anything the story of Metro III is therefore the weakest of the Metro games. While the first two have some interesting ideas to explore about the Dark Ones, the third is literally just "rescue the girl." If, and this is a big if, the game succeeded in making you actually care for that character... (now I remember, her name is Ana...) Unfortunately you don't really have a reason. The game takes you through all these sequences that are supposed to be emotional, especially towards the end, but for me at least they failed to resonate. The Metro series has always been fairly juvenile in part because of its source material, and unfortunately Exodus is no exception.The second area where the game falls flat is the world / level design. The early Volga map is excellent. It is perfectly balanced. However the subsequent maps have major flaws. The Caspian desert map is simply too large. They wanted a car, so they made a map big enough to require a car. But driving itself simply takes you out of that nice loop of tension, between exploring, fighting, looting, and instead gives you "drive to A." The Taiga map is really a wide corridor, with some very frustrating sneaking sections. It has a nice ending, and I do appreciate the overall concept, but the execution is just not very good. Dead City is... well... a return to the original Metro Games, but with perhaps even less player autonomy. It opens with what feels like 20 minutes of simply following a guy and hearing dialogue. This is not good. Taking away freedom from the player has always been an issue with this series. Unfortunately Exodus seems committed to repeating these mistakes for the sake of doing something a little fancy looking. Sometimes it works. Usually it doesn't. The final ten minutes of Exodus... well... it is an excellent negative example of what game developers should never do. Similarly, in order to get the good ending, there are sections where the game requires that you kill nobody. At the same time, stealthing some of these sections is a challenge. Two sections in particular I had to repeat dozens of times. Simply because I was not "supposed" to hurt any of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who were willing to kill me on sight. Write it on your liver guys. Depriving players of autonomy is always bad design. Punishing them for failure by making them reload is bad design. Thirdly, there are some little AAA tricks that I did not appreciate. The original game was quite brutal, and I understand if the edges needed smoothing off for a bigger release that would reach a larger audience. But I certainly noticed when, after dying to a large beast in a certain section and re-loading, those same beasts were now mysteriously all dead. The game had decided that it needed to do some behind-the-scenes lowering of the difficulty level, so that I wouldnt feel frustrated. Given I was playing on "hard core" difficulty I was not impressed by this decision. The whole point is that I -want- to be challenged. If I die, then that is an opportunity for me to learn from my mistakes and try again. I'm far more interested in that aspect of the game than in getting to the next spoon fed story segment.It is a shame to begin a game with such strongly positive impressions and end it on such a low point. I want to emphasize again that, overall, it is a good game, and it is am ambitious game. If it has some very glaring issues, it is in part because it tries to do so much, and this left some key weaknesses exposed. They wanted to have both a very strong, linear, narrative arc, and also an open world exploration game. A better choice, I think, would have been to commit more to the latter, and to try and allow the interesting world to do more of the talking. There is talk of a fourth Metro game on the way. I hope that in hindsight Exodus turns out to have been a bridge to wherever they are ultimately heading. A bit like AC Origins was a bridge for AC Odyssey. There are elements here in this game which are simply superb, and I would love to see them integrated into a more refined package. But that may be difficult when there are some ingrained design habits that still seem to need unlearning. We shall see!

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is what I find a perfect ending to the Metro Trilogy, with you finally leaving the tunnels and venturing out into the rest of Russia and seeing how the Nuclear War effected it. Each area you visit feels unique from the last in more ways than one. I'm glad that the game follows a storyline that is Linear in nature and not just one giant open world, as those end up being overwhelming and too much, with a narrative dissonance that comes into play, but with the way Exodus handles its flow of Linear Section>Open Map>Linear Section>Open Map it perfectly breaks up each of the sections so you (probably) won't get burnt out on a section, and I wish more games would do this instead of just having one giant open world. Admittedly, I find the first open section on the Volga River a weak way to start the game after your first Linear section, as the main way of travel is incredibly tedious to do but you can (almost) completely ignore that.The game feels incredibly immersive with all the first person animations being well animated and thought out, world building for each area is great. The addition of the crafting system is a nice change, as you'll be scavenging for supplies rather than buying them with bullets, and being able to customize your guns on the fly ala Crysis. My biggest gripe with that is it lacks the amount of gun variety from previous games, especially from Last Light, thought you can make the Kalash into an RPK and somewhat into an AKSU, and the only shotguns that exist are the AShot you can turn into a Single, Double, or Quad Barrel shotgun but unfortunately because of that the Duplet is no longer a thing, and the Shambler can be upgraded in ways to where it fits the role of the Saiga 12.If you're going to play it, I highly recommend playing the game on Ranger or Ranger Hardcore for the best experience.The DLCs are both fantastic as well, with Two Colonels highlighting the more Linear gameplay as seen in earlier Metro games and Sam's Story highlighting Exodus' more open gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting 80 hours into the game, exploring as much of the amazing and beautiful world as I could, playing through the main game and dlc, and after getting all achievements the game has to offer, I can say without a doubt this has been the most fun in a game I've had for the year of 2020. This game looks amazing, has an incredible story, great characters, fun mechanics and an overall great and immersive world. There are quite a fews bugs here and there and I've had my fair share of crashes, but I think my overall enjoyment surpasses the minor problems the game has. I'd recommend this to everyone, and if you can listen or read the books along with this and it's predecessor games.

_childDocuments_.review: TBH, I would have given it thumbs up if its review score was less that "very good" at the time of writing. . It gets the atmosphere right each time, it has great and varied environments, fantastic sometimes unbelievable level of detail, a mostly good cast of characters, many things to see, explore and do, challenging difficulty (hardcore), some fun moments, and two gripping endings. I got the "good" one, which was very well executed, bitter-sweet and satisfying. Yet, the game was a chore to finish. Some were due to gameplay. Imho, the first open chapter (Volga) was a bit steep in difficulty. Also, on hardcore level, you lose most of your resources between chapters. Fair, but it was not very clear to me until a few chapters in. And maybe, the game overstayed its welcome just a bit. However, . BUGS/ISSUESTake down prompt. This was the most annoying one. I choose to go non lethal with take downs. However, the prompt very often DOES NOT appear. The solution is to turn away from the character and back. However, by the time you execute that extra manoeuvre, you are often spotted. Also, it makes cool setups fail one to many times. Frustrated to no end.Jumping and climbing. Artyom can climb onto walls and even roofs. But I remember getting on a roof quite easy to enter a room within the building, and after returning I needed to re-try like 30-40 times. That was fun.Movement. Movement is fine until your press the sprint button. Artyom becomes so floaty that he becomes hard to control. Especially when sprinting and jumping, you'll witness some weird physics.Line of sight. Although this only happened a handful of times, enemies were able to spot you even it should have been completely impossible (through walls). Minor issue.All seeing and knowing enemies. Sometimes the game seems unfair. In some instances, enemies know your exact position and can pinpoint you from extreme distances (remember the backup ). Respawns. Human enemies stay death, monsters respawn, in full strength. Fair enough I guess, but respaws can happen so quickly after clearing an area that it can be highly annoying, surprsing and immersion-breaking. Imho, it makes free exploration at the start of the game harder than necessary, especially when you are low on resources. And doing the same area stealthy in a row is a chore.Craches. With DX12 (in this case for RTX) there were some crashes. These crashes are hard. You need to kill the game somehow, which is no easy feat given that it remains on top while accessing the task manager. Be warned, shoveling coal in the train is dangerous :-) Seriously.Misc. Well there is more. I remember visual artifacts in the sky in the east of Volga, I remember the sky being fast forwarded for a while after sleeping, ... and some more random and/or smaller stuff that I don't recall now ¯\_(ツ)_/¯That said, most of the bugs would have been forgive-able if not for that take down prompt. This seems something fix-able. Pitty it did not happen. In some cases, when the bug was mostly absent, things could be really fun and satisfying. Oh well.RTXSince I have an RTX 2080 I decided to play with RTX on (G-SYNC 1440p), DLSS off. This too has been rather disappointing. With RTX some environments become extremely dark and washed out (gamma issue too?). An issue here seems that light sources are not correctly configured, or that there are not enough light sources for "real lighting". Also, lighting from the sun or ambient lighting is not always convincing. This is most noteable in the train. That said, FPS remained acceptable and at least RTX ON made some difference (*cough* Shadow of the TR) and could be fun to watch from time to time. The only games that have been impressive so far are Control from Remedy and ofc Quake II RTX which goes all the way with path/ray tracing.

_childDocuments_.review: after playing 10+ hours I thought it was time to write a brief review:Before, I couldn't recommend the game because of crashes, and yet I have to discover if it will still crash so now and then after validating game files in steam. (PC specs for the matter are: i7 7700K, 16GB RAM, GTX 1080)For now I can only say that you can see there's put much work in this game. The graphics and scenery are amazing, the story is compelling, the atmosphere and dynamic weather/day-night system with it's different playing-approaches and overall gameplay is one of the best I've had in the past few weeks or maybe months. To me, honestly, this game can be my number one game I played past year.I really hope the devs will patch the game against crashes or system-hangs.For now I will definitly recommend this game but keep in mind you might end up with the desktop view all of a sudden during an infiltration in a bandid camp. Not so pleasant as you may understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a good game but there are certainly places it could have been improved.The story is great and the graphics are amazing, but you've heard that before.The gameplay isn't half bad. There was tons to explore and loot. Once the game opens up it felt "fallout-ish", there were many points of interest and with many weapon & armour upgrades it was well worth checking them all out.Customising weapons was really fun, with multiple different ways to modify a weapon and certain modifications changing how the weapon played entirely. Managing equipment and keeping your gear clean was an interesting mechanic and forces you to keep track of how much gear you have & if it's a good idea to engage certain enemies.Stealth was a viable option in Metro with certain paths lead around & behind enemies so that you didn't have to engage at all. But if you play like me and want to takedown enemies then you can do so with enemies looking straight at the one you are taking down. The AI didn't seem to recognise that there mate just got clubbed and they would stand there and watch me do it with no reaction.I had a very few crashes but they were there. Couldn't figure out why. And I had a few game sessions where it didn't save so I played the same part twice.Apart from that, Exodus was pretty fun and I would recommend.

name: Spelunky 2
detailed_description: Spelunky returns in this greatly-expanded sequel to the original roguelike platformer! Meet the next generation of explorers as they find themselves on the Moon, searching for treasure and missing family. Spelunky 2 builds upon the unique, randomized challenges that made the original a classic, offering a huge adventure designed to satisfy players old and new. A Bigger and More Dynamic World, with So Much to See and Do Spelunky 2's world is even denser than the one in the original game, offering many more areas, characters, traps, and items, as well as new ways to interact with them (and for them to interact with each other). The world has expanded in other ways, too, with branching paths and multi-layered levels adding a third dimension to the classic 2d platforming. Animals can also be tamed and ridden. And dynamic liquid physics create new challenges and make the world feel extra reactive and alive. Build a Community, Make Friends Back in Base Camp, characters you unlock will mill about and relax between runs, offering encouragement and advice. As you explore, your camp will expand and develop into a thriving little community to welcome you whenever you need a break from exploring. While there, you can also access shortcuts and practice your moves in safety. The Game is Yours to Explore Spelunky 2 is not just about 'getting good and beating the game' - more than that, it's an endlessly replayable playground to experiment in and find your own way, creating stories against the backdrop of an expansive, deeply-interactive world filled with secrets. The more you play, the more the game becomes yours! Key Features, Summarized: A Bigger World with all new areas, monsters, traps, and items! An Extra Dimension is added by allowing players to access a second layer behind the normal playfield. The second layer might contain treasure rooms, hidden passages, and other special places. Multiple Routes Through the Game will add variety and give players more ways to personalize a run. Find and Ride Mounts (like turkeys!) that have special abilities. Enemies may ride mounts, as well! New NPCs that you can help, hurt, or ignore… to make each run feel even more like a unique story. Variations and Changes to Classic Spelunky Concepts like shops and ghosts that will make veteran players rethink their strategies. Improved Liquid Physics allow water and lava to move and pour realistically, which drastically affects the playfield (and looks cool) Deadly Poison and Curses can be inflicted on players and enemies alike. Build a Permanent Home at Base Camp as you do runs and explore the caves. Improved Lighting and Special Effects are paired with richer visual and audio design. Deeper Mysteries that may require a community effort to unravel. Possibly More Eggplants

_childDocuments_.review: Precision is the key....Precision in movementPrecision in decision makingPrecision in time managementYou waste time...you'll dieYou make the wrong decision...you'll dieYou act too greedy and it will catch up with you and...you'll dieLuckily for Spelunky 2 every part of the gameplay is enjoyable and meaningful. You can never feel sad about losing a good run as the next one might be even better.It's also worth adding that the "scenarios" you find yourself dying within are so complex and surrounded in chance that each one feels...natural. The laws to which this games works are so well written that the unpredictable nature of death is replicated perfectly. It is truly magical in that after 50 hours you'll see it coming a mile off and still not be able to stop it. You will shout "I knew it...!" over and over again! It's simply beautiful programming...9/10 - As near to a perfect game as it could get. I just feel that there is still room to make this even greater by adding more depth and complexity to character choices (different stats and skins) as well as end game options/challenges aside from the inbuilt achievements. The quality of the game overall rivals Nintendo's approach to gaming quality...rock solid mechanics and smooth animations for distinct characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Game's super addictive-VERY replayable-Has a learning curve, but easy to learn-Always learning new stuff-Always something new to experienceCons-Sometimes the game seems to be based off of luck rather than skill-Can be really unfair at times (for example, a mole out of the sky and hitting you giving you 0 time to react, or hiding a spider in the foreground banner, or an explosion or something happening outside of your control out in the distance pissing off the shopkeeper)-Needs more variety in the OST, especially for the first world. Seriously, you'll be seeing the first world A LOT if you are trying to get through this unseeded, the least they could do is add 2-3 more soundtracks in world 1 so the one soundtrack they have (which is really good, btw) doesnt become ultra repetitive for you. Seriously, I can't even listen to the soundtrack by itself on youtube without feeling... pain.Overall, really fun. Ragequit and rage inducing, too, lol

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is as good a sequel to Spelunky HD as one could hope for, it maintains the originals charm and character, without becoming too derivative.  The gameplay holds up well, and while some of the total fault placed on the player has shifted, certain enemies or traps can be unfair, a very large majority of deaths are still your fault.  Spelunky's difficulty was actually increased for the sequel, the number and ease of death is even more brutal than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: The design of the game, completely contradicts how it is meant to be played. Spelunky 1 you had to plan out your moves as you went, the enemies and traps were well thought out and well placed, designed to be difficult but be beaten and the game was good because of it. Spelunky 2 throws unfair ♥♥♥♥ at you just to do it, just a big screw you, there was literally nothing you could have done to save yourself. Enemies and traps are more abundant, not designed to be difficult, designed to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but the same rules of Spelunky still apply. So if you get hit one time by any of the dozens of enemies crammed in a tight space then you are dead. Most times they don't give you an out, it's a "here we go I guess" type of situation that ends in you dying 90% of the time. That is bad design. I bought it, played it nearly 2 hours, then promptly refunded it months ago. Spelunky 1 does many things better and is leagues better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of posting I have 197 hours for this game and all of it's achievementsDo I recommend this game?NoRight off the bat I'm going to be very honest in saying that if you haven't played Spelunky HD, or if you're someone who looks to play games for a short while and have moderate success and put it down feeling happy - this is not the game for you and there is going to be plenty for you to complain about.That's not a slight either - this game is very hard, and you're going to have to play it for awhile for you to learn most of the crucial things the game is trying to teach you, as well as for you to get comfortable finding creative ways for you to deal with an innumerable amount of unique situations you will encounter. It will be unfun for you if you only plan to play for a short while and never get to see any of the zones that go beyond the starting area of the game, "dwellings". Beyond that I have to be honest to you and say that this game at the time of posting is being patched very frequently [multiple patches a week], because there are a lot of bugs being fixed and changes being made and as requested by a large part of the playerbase. Just to name a few that I've run into: Textures in the Super Super Secret Spoiler area tend to flash and appear in and out of the game: You can't see your own score on the daily challenge leaderboard even when you press the "Me" button: at one point a sticky bomb exploded almost as soon as I put it down in the dwellings without there being any cause for it in context of what I know about this game in 197 hours. Currently at the time of posting the feature of multiplayer is not a part of the game, which was a huge selling point to me - but if it is the "only" selling point to you and you wish to play it casually I would suggest waiting. In the games current state, I can say that I've enjoyed it but the numerous bugs I've had to endure in the line to actually posting this review is been more headache, and heartache than it has enjoyment. Some people believe it adds quote "depth" to the game that the forward swing of your whip has very little utility. A bat can be coming at you from above - and you can jump and time a swing you believe to be perfect but it literally has to be the tip of the front of your whip that makes contact with something - the swinging blur of the whip reaching that point has no hurt box. But that's not even the worst part: the back end of your whip - which is a startup animation and in theory shouldn't hurt anything at all because it's a wind-up is 1000% better and has a larger hitbox and greater consistency than the front of your whip. To fully explain what I'm saying here - you will have to train yourself to turn around in many instances to hit arrows/enemies/objects with the back end of your whip because the front end of your whip can't do much at all.In summary, the games difficulty and harsh learning curve will be a turn-off to a lot of casual players. But even for the "hard core" playerbase in the games current state with all the issues in the game being patched and reported on a daily basis, as well as the missing addition of multiplayer: I cannot in good faith recommend this game. The constant patching for bug fixes and changes is an indicator to me that this game is not yet finished. I will update my review in the future in things change but this is a present day review and my thoughts on the game. NOTE: I have other gripes with the game such as the graining dwellings song and the lack of variation in the music that was a feature in Spelunky HD: but the soundtrack is dynamic in Spelunky 2- meaning that the song changes or transitions while keeping many elements of the base song depending on whats happening in the game. So I can understand it would be difficult for the developer team to orchestrate numerous songs for every zone because of this. Again, I could just be nitpicking, but a lot of time will be spent in dwellings- especially at the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky messed around with this design philosophy where the game is just a set of rules, and having cool and interesting interactions between stuff is more important than being super balanced or even fair. I think the first game was pretty careful about upsetting people with this since there was no way of knowing the game would be a hit. Spelunky 2 goes wild and adds obstacles not because of their difficulty, but because they add something new to the playground. Chain reactions of harmless objects will launch you into spikes, enemies will accidentally release the ghost at the start of the level, hired hands will pick up your weapon and kill you with it, and you will get softlocked by lava, but at the end of the day each death is a product of rules you already knew about and you learn to predict and defuse the BS before it happens. Sometimes, the chaotic nature of the game will cause something memorable and help you out, like a caveman picking up and throwing an item you can't reach or a shopkeeper shooting his own bombs and blowing himself up. Not everyone will enjoy this game and it's probably more frustrating than the first, but if you push through it's extremely fun and offers tons more depth and possibilities.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 200 hours (including non-recorded) and after just beating the (final) boss, I can say that this game is defenitely worth your money. It's addicting, it's frustrating, but most important of all: it has random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that could end your run in mere milliseconds, and even though I want to punch the screen out of anger, that is also what makes it great. _childDocuments_.review: Six years of practice in Spelunky 1 has finally paid off. I don't die to bats anymore! Now, I die to lizards and moles. Damn it, Derek!EDIT: After beating hard ending on around 230 hours mark and many great QoL updates, I can safely say that this is the best game ever made for me. It hits everything that I love: randomly generated levels each run that always keep me on my toes, no in-game progression that makes my win purely based on my skill and a little bit of luck, and simple mechanics that chain together into a hard, but winnable challenge.What I dislike on many modern roguelike games are in-game unlockables that makes the character stronger, thus giving an illusion of the players become significantly much better, even though their skills only increase a little. Spelunky will make sure that each challenge that you overcome are the result of you learning from past failures, correct threat identification, and correct response to such threat. You will feel your own skills increasing as you beat the seemingly insane and impossible challenge.This game may frustrate many players. I can understand that. Due to random nature of the game, sometimes Spelunky just throw a few bullsht at you that you can't respond in time. I too had my fury with this game's bullsht in the past. It's also because it's the first time someone encounter a particular threat. But, most of the time, it's due to the players' own folly. Taking things slow (most importantly, by changing the default movement into "walk" instead of "run"), identifying threats, and act accordingly, are the only things that you need to beat normal ending every time. Hard ending is entirely a different thing, though, and only players who truly enjoy Spelunky will attempt doing that.If you can't imagine enduring Spelunky by yourself, good news, Spelunky online multiplayer is ready and great to use. Find yourself a friend or two or three and try to beat the game together! It may make the game slightly easier, but everything is much more fun with friends and you can all laugh at your undoing together. You don't have friend to play with? Go to  and find someone to play with there.In conclusion, Spelunky 2 is a worthy successor to Spelunky HD and a testament to Spelunky's game design. This is the best game ever for me and I truly recommend it for anyone looking for a pure challenge.I still hate moles. I hate witches. I hate cats. I hate curses. I hate trap blocks. I hate egg. Derek Yu, bless your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ soul for making me pass all this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so desperately to enjoy this game, but every time I tried to play it I ended up getting pissed off. When I first played this game I thought it was just difficult like the first, but after playing it for a while, 90% of the challenge comes from pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I honestly don't have a better way to phrase it. A run could be going perfectly, but no matter how perfect and careful you are one single wacky hitbox or miscalculated jump could throw that whole run out the window. It's very easy to get wombo-combo'd by almost any enemy since you get knocked down for about a second and a half after taking damage, if there's more than one enemy coming after you when you get hit, you're almost always just dead, even if you've stocked up on hearts and equipment, one wrong move and you're done. I consider myself decent, if not pretty good at games, one of my favourite genres is rougelike/rougelite so I'm used to having "bad runs" and "good runs", but almost every damage taken/death feels undeserved and stupid, over time it turns into anger and overall unhappiness. Although there are things that make Spelunky 2 fun and charming, besides the gameplay itself.The art style in this game is great, even if it is simple. The OST is also very good and really makes you feel like you're spelunking! There's also tons of characters to collect and play as, most have different ropes which is a nice attention to detail. The different areas that you can explore are really pretty and are much different than each other.The main problem I have with this game is the gameplay, as I've already stated. There are mechanics that I really like, for example the ghost and the ghost pot, but there are others that, in my opinion, make it frustrating to play. One quick example of that is how the dart traps work, when you dodge the arrows they will hit a wall and bounce off, yet even if they bounce off and just nick your bum you still take two hearts of damage, when this happens I have the urge to kill. It just feels unfair.OVERALL - If some gameplay mechanics are polished a bit, I think I would love this game, but how it is now it's just rage inducing. Everything other than the gameplay is great, but that doesn't excuse the gameplay (which is in my opinion the most important aspect of a game). A lot of time and effort obviously went into this game and I wanted to support it, but after about 10 hours of playing, all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just starts to come to a boil and it just got to a point to where I decided to write this review.Putting this into a score, I'd give Spelunky 2 overall, a 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: In a vacuum, this game is easily good enough to get a thumbs up. The problem is, that for newcomers and fans of the original alike, my advice is "Your better off sticking with the original."Basically, there are 2 things that differentiate this game from the original. One good, one bad. Sadly, the bad outweighs the good.The good is that there is a branching level path. At the end of World 1 and World 3, there is a split in the path, so you can proceed to worlds 2a, 2b, 4a or 4b to bring some variety to the table.The bad thing is that the game is predictable. The original gave you  a grab bag of different tools to gather from the shop, which made each run feel different from the last as you improvised your way forward.Those tools are still present, but there are new features you can consistently rely on. Every level has a dog and a ghost pot, which optimally you just carry to the end of the level for extra health, and extra money respectively. But you can only hold 1 item at a time, which makes this tedious. And even worse if you want to grad another holdable item to bring with you. Sometimes, there will be a golden idol in a trap, that you also want to bring to the exit or shopkeeper, which again, just makes the errand running back and forth worse.Levels 1-2 will have either the udjat eye, another carry item from A to B quest, or wild turkeys. 1-3 will have the other scenaria. Wild turkeys can be bombed or otherwise cooked for extra health, or ridden to enable a double jump and slow falling until they take too much damage and die. Then when they die, you bomb them for extra health. If you're feeling adventurous, you can kill turkey fetish man to grab an extra turkey and some extra treasure. You really shouldn't give him the turkeys though, as they're just more useful than his rewards.The really big problem with the turkeys is that they largely invalidate many of the items that you would ordinarily have to rely on. The double jump means you need to use far fewer ropes, or the climbing glove, and straight up don't need the spring shoes. The slow falling renders the cape redundant unless you switch mounts or your turkey dies. And since you have access to these every run, the items they invalidate rarely have time to shine. Oh, also, the spike shoes don't work while you're on a turkey.The game is still a tough as nails fun roguelike platformer. But the predictability really kills the strengths of the roguelike genre. The original did not have this particular issue. Both will kill you a lot though, in a mix of fair and unfair manners. I want to say Spelunky 2 is substantially harder, but it's been long enough since I played the original that I can't say for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels more like Spelunky 1.5 than 2. The good parts of the original Spelunky are all in here. Tight controls, fast entry into gameplay, and a lot of fun treasures to play around with. The art is more refined than in the original Spelunky, and the music is good, though there aren't many song tracks in this game. The game is also nice on my 144Hz display, where I believe the original Spelunky is capped to 60 FPS.Unfortunately, it feels like there's very little innovation going on here, and instead there are simply newer and more ways to game over. The one thing I had truly hoped to see was fewer ways to meet instant-death, or better ways to recover from situations where you effectively are punched to death without being able to regain control. That didn't happen. I don't think this is just me, either. I was able to get better at, and beat, the original Spelunky. It took some luck, sure, but I felt the progression. But I'm already familiar with the Spelunky brand, so I have a baseline experience to rely on. And yet somehow I feel like it doesn't matter how much I improve at Spelunky 2, there will be something which subverts my expectations and makes me feel not that I made a mistake, but that the game was eager to punish me.I haven't had a chance in seven hours of play to really explore the new weapons or secrets, since I lose so frequently. But now with the cursed ghost jars, damsels, and mounts, and weapons it feels like I'm doing a lot of Spelunky's version of inventory management rather than playing the game. It just gets tedious, and my own time isn't so worthless to keep at it.I'd been hoping for a Spelunky 2 for a long time. And since it's quick and easy to launch the game and start playing, I find myself doing so frequently these past few days. But I am just as quick to find the exit, because I'm not having fun. I suspected as much when I first started playing, but I thought I'd give the game time to slow burn its way in. I'm regretting not following my immediate instinct to issue a refund request after the first hour, because the experience didn't grow more enjoyable over time.

Feels less fulfilling.Update: Having played a handful more in multiplayer and singleplayer, I would say that the game is currently a little too unpredictable, such as:Overall, at 160 hours played, I feel like Spelunky 2 is less of a game about skill or speed but rather being prepared for every possible way a game could suddenly kill you in - many of which are a little too exotic to practice without modding the game. _childDocuments_.review: I really liked the first Spelunky, which I played when it was a free Gamemaker game. I actually own the Spelunky Wiki, though I haven't done much on it in years. The first remake was worth a buy even if it didn't appeal to a lot of people because it added quite a bit to the overall game. This one, however, doesn't really do enough to stand out as a separate game. It feels more like a mod.In general, Spelunky 2 feels like a game trapped in 2012, when roguelikes that were based on RNG screwovers were considered good. Thank god we (mostly) got over that. The first game had its share of issues, from the dark levels (which no one liked) to the fact that RNG played a huge part in how successful your run was. I was hoping that Spelunky 2 would fix that, but instead it doubles down on the difficulty while not doing anything to alleviate the issues the first game had.The first area of the game is now full of enemies that may as well be invincible unless you throw them into spikes. In the first game, this was more or less exclusive to one enemy (the caveman) who didn't always show up. Now you're guaranteed to have full hallways of them, and with Spelunky 2's more compact map design you're generally going to have to fight them in tighter quarters. It also seems like item drops have been severely cut from where they were in the first game, which kind of makes no sense as now everything that isn't on the direct path to the exit more or less requires bombs to access.Other than that though, this is more or less the exact same game the first one was. The whole "City of Gold" chain that starts in the first area is still in, the areas are set up exactly the same as the first game's were (Caves, Jungle, Ice, Lava) and it's just.. too much of the same thing. The only way I'd buy this is at a steep discount. Otherwise, just play the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Spelunky HD, but with more content, improvements and deaths!Spelunky 2 is a roguelike platformer, a very challenging one at that.You make your way through different areas, each containing various deadly traps and enemies that can end your run in an instant if you're not careful or prepared. Every death can be frustrating, especially when it happens out of nowhere (Spelunky moment) but with knowledge and new discoveries comes confidence. What might have made you panic or anxious before, not knowing how to overcome it, is now only just a small problem in a bunch of other complications.The improvements are quite nice, like better graphics, more precise movement and local/online multiplayer (Co-op/PvP).Though if you're going for 100% completion you probably will be playing alone most of the time since a lot of the achievements require you to play non-seeded singleplayer runs.It is an unforgiving game that will actively try to kill and break you, but once you know everything and are confident enough it will become a rewarding experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 340 hours into Spelunky HD, and it is one of my favourite games. I REALLY wanted to love this game.Spelunky 2 is a consequence of the developers mistakenly thinking people liked Spelunky solely because of its difficulty. Early levels, especially those in the Dwelling, play like Frozlunky (for those unaware, it was a Spelunky mod that could drastically boost monster rates, among many other things) levels instead of an intro section. I don't think people want 6-10 arrow traps on every level, or extremely unfair levels of stunlocking. Many people in the community have said without any exaggeration that the hardest section of the game is the Dwelling. This really shouldn't be the case. I should also point that this is being written AFTER the first patch on the Dwelling. It was even worse before.This is coupled with the fact that it feels like you're doing the same exact thing every run. The lack of variety in the early levels (which you will be spending most of your time in because of the nature of the game) makes it feel like I'm doing my taxes before playing the game each time. It lends itself to being quickly frustrating and dull.Artwork and music is fantastic, and later levels look stunning. The initial items, branching paths, and (most) of the new enemies are great. The game suffers immensely from incredibly poor design in the first few sections. I'll happily return to the game if these issues are addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: The first stage(Dwelling) is my problem with Spelunky 2. I enjoy most of the game greatly; the gameplay is as fantastic as ever(with maybe some questionable hitboxes) and while most of the areas are harder than stuff in the first Spelunky they feel good and manageable. Visuals and music are both fine though music especially doesn't really hold candle to the first game. The rest of the audio is great with various sound effects mixing perfectly.But yeah that Dwelling sure is a doozy. It's just too much in too small of a space and playing it I feel less like I'm powering up to face the meat of the game and more like I'm trying to endure past a massive speed bump(at the very start of the game!). There are just so many gotcha-style enemies and traps that the game keeps spamming. It takes too much effort and patience simply to get through let alone gain some advantage/actually building an interesting run that I'm exhausted getting out of it.And it's one thing to have this intense of a stage later in the game when the player can prepare for it; get some advantage to exploit against the worst stuff. Those stages are here(haven't explored the game at all fully; I have beaten it once in a full run) but as the first stage Dwelling is kinda miserable. There is so much variety and secrets in this game but I'm being slowly drained by the first area and it's such a shame.Now all that said I'll keep trying and maybe with more time I'll start to understand it better. But for now I don't see it and at 20 hours and with a pretty deep understanding of the core mechanics from the first game it sure feels like I should not have to be spending so much time and effort just starting a run. There is some other stuff in the late game I could praise/complain about but in short it is pretty good once you get there; way WAY better than the beginning.EDIT: Welp I gave myself up until 100 hours to beat the Yama equivalent of this game(so not the extra secret boss), didn't get it done and then gave myself more time. Got the kill at 121 hours and now am done with this game for a good long while if I ever play it again at all. Dwelling is still IMO by far the worst stage in the game even with the balance changes; largely because of how tedious it is; but it is more manageable now. On the whole I still greatly prefer Spelunky HD but I'm sure for people who wanted an even more hardcore instakill experience Spelunky 2 delivers that in spades. For me the added bs does sway the balance of the game to a point where it's just too much for me; even now that I've gotten decent at it. The gameplay/destruction is still fantastic though and carries the mediocre bits well enough which kept me going; but I never got past that frustration and as such am keeping this review negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a sequel to Spelunky which in of itself is the HD remake of Spelunky Classic. In Spelunky 2 your goal is to make it to the bottom of a perilous floor to get to the next. Each floor is procedurally generated and filled with many horrors that sometimes do 1 damage and sometimes kill you instantly. The satisfaction that comes from self-growth displayed through just a little bit more progress, or discovering a brand new thing you hadn't seen before is what makes this very challenging game special. You're going to die, over and over and over again, but more often than not you'll come away with new knowledge that will help you get to the next floor, or the next area. That's what makes this game so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.

_childDocuments_.review: While there are a lot of things that I do like about this game, there are just too many things that I don't like about this game to actually give it a thumbs up recommendation. For one thing there isn't a ton that differentiates it from its predecessor, the stuff that was added feels pretty inconsequential and are mostly in service of making the game harder than its predecessor, and while there's nothing inherently wrong with wanting to make the game harder, the way that Spelunky 2 was made harder wasn't an improvement in my eyes. The original Spelunky is a hard game, but it was hard in a way that made you feel like the fault of dying was your own and that you could overcome the game by learning more about it, cheap deaths were rare and the difficulty was more satisfying, but Spelunky 2 doesn't feel like that, there are a lot more cheap deaths and a lot more instances where you feel like you were put in a situation where there was nothing you could have done differently that wouldn't have resulted in your death, there were a lot more cheap deaths.Spelunky 2 is also missing some key usability features. In the original Spelunky upon start up you had a quick start option which would start the game using your last used setting, and allowed you to skip all the menus and other stuff and get playing right away. Spelunky 2 doesn't have this, so you are forced to go through the menus each time even if there is nothing you are changing from the last time you played it.To me, there just isn't enough of an improvement over Spelunky to really recommend Spelunky 2, and in some aspects it feels like a downgrade. If the only thing you were looking for was a more difficult Spelunky then you've got a new game, but for everyone else, just stick with Spelunky.

_childDocuments_.review: Your liquid physics are all cool until you get soft-locked in a corner of a level because of a lava flow that no amount of ropes or bombs will fix.The core of spelunkly is still there, and it's still good, but jesus christ this game needs a rebalance. level generation/design is worse, with more areas being way to claustrophobic, filled with traps and enemies, and areas requiring the use of bombs and ropes. More enemies lean towards instant or certain deaths (infinite stunlocks) than the first game.I really hope this gets some patches in the future to fix these issues, or at the very least fix the enemies being right on top of doorways. there's thoughtful hard and there's exercise in futile frustration hard, and spelunky 2 is the ladder whereas the first was not this way.Edit: The later levels such as Tide Pool are shockingly better than the first one, which feels imbalanced even when the level generation dosen't suck. some minor adjustments like forcing no lava to spawn under the drill's path in volcana would be welcome and make getting to vlad's castle much less rage-inducing since the aforementioned lava has a chance to make that path suicidal.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts my heart to give this game a negative review but this game does not give me the fun vibes that Spelunky 1 did. Rather than laughing at a series of unfortunate events, you are constantly wondering how the F did that happen. Nearly every monster will one tap you, but not like it sounds. If you get hit by a monster they will then rapid fire hit you over and over again while you lay unconscious, so it might as well be a single hit to kill you. The moles are unnecessary. _childDocuments_.review: Is this a worthy sequel to Spelunky? NO, NOPE, NO WAYSure, it adds a whole bunch of new visuals and general stuff, -what you might expect from a mere expansion pack perhaps, it does not improve on or fix anything that was wrong with the original game.-Difficulty is way, way up-many things now feel deeply "unfair" in ways that the old game didn't-shopkeepers (and now other NPCs, yay) are still ridiculously op, and can be turned forever hostile by monsters rather than the player-the whip seems to have a smaller hitbox, and doesn't seem to whip above or behind at all like it used to-the rope doesn't seem to harm enemies like it used to-enemies still can have multiple HP, and cannot be hurt while they are stunned, worse, there are more multiple HP enemies, and they're harder than ever.-meanwhile, YOU can still be hit any time, and can still take damage while stunned, meaning that stunlock issues haven't been fixed since the last game.Don't let the improved visuals fool you, this game is less polished than the first one, not more. This is not a sequel, more of a collection of new content stapled together.This game makes me want to go back to the first one.Despite the long development time, it feels thrown together in 5 minutes.Avoid this game, I'm stuck with it, but you can avoid my fate.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game to bits but damn is it difficult. The game has no real buffs or items that carry over runs, just characters that are cosmetic only and shortcuts that are more used for experimenting with stages since you don't get all achievments from using them and you can't really properly beat the true ending. I really like this though. There is no doubt that it is YOU that is getting better, not the game that is getting easier. The beginning is rather rough, but after a bit everything just clicks and it feels great. Also the game is not very luck based since items matter a lot less than in games such as Binding of Isaac and Risk of Rain 2 (not that those games are bad in fact I like them both a lot). This can be really nice since you don't get those boring mediocre runs with just meh items. Definitely one of my favorite platformers and roguelikes! I can't really think of any cons within the game 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun, and the thing about spelunky that separates it from other rogue-lites is that every run you have is different. The controls feel amazing and the physics are fluid (no pun intended). As for difficulty, this game will kick your ass and spit on your face. And I know a lot of people like to say "ohhh in spelunky when you die you always feel like its your fault nothing is ever BS in this game" but that simply is not true, There are a lot of moments that will happen where the game works against you, like an arrow trap with nothing nearby to set it off, or a kali altar that just decided to explode into a million enemies. (SPOILER)  If you rage easy or get very impatient, this game is not for you. But if you have patience and are interesting in testing your 2D platformer skill or just want something fun to pick up and play, get spelunky 2. The game came out 3 days ago and I already have 38 hours. It's just such an addicting game.

_childDocuments_.review: My point still stands, EVERYTHING CAN KILL YOU.My first review of this game I had made within my first 10 hours of playing it. I was very quick to make a review, but it didn't go into depth at all. And honestly, I'm still going to avoid going into depth about this game. Trust me, you'll want to experience EVERYTHING for yourself. DO NOT LOOK UP VIDEOS ON THIS GAME, PLEASE TRY TO FIGURE STUFF OUT FOR YOURSELF. It has so many secrets, and they're all incredibly rewarding to find out. This game will really try your patience though, as it is extremely unforgiving. Be constantly aware of the fact that stepping on the wrong tile can instantly kill you regardless of your health. If you don't like difficult games or having to lose all your progress in a run and being set back to square one, this game isn't for you.Alternatively, if you want a challenge that will last you hundreds of hours, hop in! I think even after putting in nearly 100 hours I still haven't seen much more than 50% of the content in this game. I can't wait to dig deeper!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so addicting. _childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2: Electric BoogalooSeriously, this game is Spelunky HD turned up to 11, including the deaths. You will die a lot, and have nothing to show for it. This is a true action roguelike, just like the original Spelunky, albeit harder, a bit more punishing, and occasionally unfair.Overall, Spelunky 2 feels a bit unbalanced, at least compared to the first game, and has a few kinks the developers need to work out. Online multiplayer is not currently present, but in development. I can't really think of any other cons at the moment.Pros are abundant. There's more content here (items, enemies, levels, secrets, and plenty of familiar stuff from Spelunky HD as well), the controls are tight and responsive, the core gameplay loop is ultimately satisfying, and there's a high level of polish to the music, art, and overall game design that, despite my frustrations with the difficulty, warrant a recommendation.If you want a game that truly challenges your skill, look no further than Spelunky 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 250 hours in Spelunky (the first one).  It's an amazing game.  If you are an experienced Spelunky 1 player, you will be decent at Spelunky 2 right out of the gate.  However, the movement mechanics in Spelunky 2 feel gummy compared to the first game.  In the previous game, the mechanics felt tight and reliable.  Here, they feel like you're trying to hold a bar of wet soap.  Also, the first 4 levels are too hard.  Everything is so tight and compact, making it super easy to die.  And yea, maybe I should just "get good."  However I would imagine this level of difficulty is pretty frustrating for a new player.  If I am having trouble (even after 10 hours), new players might be turned away.Those are the only reasons for this negative review.  If Spelunky 2 is your first Spelunky experience, it's worth the buy--on sale or full price.  The devs at Mossmouth did a great job, and props to Derek for coming up with such a great series.  If you're interested, read other reviews to see what's great about this game.
