_childDocuments_.review: A good roguelike is harsh, but fair. You die a lot, but each death teaches you something you can use to do better next time.Spelunky 2 is not a good roguelike.Yes, your skill matters and you'll do better as you keep playing. But your success in any given run is far more dependent on luck than on anything you can do as a player. No matter how well you play, most of your runs will end because the level generator screwed you over.Some people enjoy that sort of thing. I don't. I kept playing because I'm a stubborn completionist who will pour hours into a task I don't enjoy just to say I "won".A few of the standout issues:- Wonky level generation. Impassable lava pits, self-destructing Kali altars, key items trapped behind multiple layers of walls, lethal traps that can hit from off-screen, "drought" runs that leave you without useful items or shops, etc.- Absurd stunlock that forces you to twiddle your thumbs while your character is slowly tortured to death.- Wonky collision detection, especially with falling objects. I've had multiple runs ended because my feet touched a falling object. Cue damage and stunlock.- A bizarre difficulty curve that places some of the toughest enemies and traps in the very first section of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky controls, non-intuitive gameplay, false difficulty, extremely repetitive.  Controls are sketchy for picking things up + riding things.  Leads to multiple attempts for what should be very simple level navigations.  You can get a turkey mount - kinds fun?  But turns out double jumping on an turkey and trying to duck/enter a tunnel seems to work like 20% of the time for some reason.  Want to pick something up?  Better hope it isn't buggy or just hop off, pick it up, get back on.Difficulty... you can be doing extremely well (lots of health built up) and there are multiple ways the game will random you to death (essentially stunlocking you).  Multiple other ways to die instantly, that you can't avoid because they aren't intuitive.  So you need to learn by dying and hoping to avoid the next time.  This would be fine, if it weren't so repetitive.This is a rogue-like which I usually enjoy, the problem is when you die you start at 1:1 and the first few levels are incredibly the same.  Not all that difficult, but they also take time to get the $ and health you need.  Not worth trying to get to new areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★Derek Yu and the team at Mossmouth have once again outdone themselves with the masterpiece that is Spelunky 2. As a sequel to the acclaimed original, Spelunky 2 not only lives up to the lofty expectations set by its predecessor but ascends to new heights, delivering an unparalleled rogue-like experience that is as challenging as it is captivating.One of the game's most outstanding features is its procedurally generated levels. Each descent into the depths of Spelunky 2 is a unique adventure, an uncharted territory filled with traps, treasures, and creatures that defy expectations. The genius of the procedural generation lies in its ability to surprise even seasoned players, ensuring that no two runs ever feel the same. This dynamic world-building keeps the game endlessly engaging, fostering a sense of discovery with every step.The meticulous attention to detail is apparent in every facet of Spelunky 2. From the charming pixel art style that retains the nostalgic essence of its predecessor to the vibrant and diverse environments, the game is a visual feast. The personality injected into each character, be it the determined spelunker or the quirky denizens of the underworld, adds a layer of charm that makes every interaction memorable.The level of difficulty in Spelunky 2 is both punishing and rewarding. Learning from mistakes becomes a fundamental aspect of the experience, and the sense of accomplishment after overcoming a particularly challenging section or boss is immensely satisfying. The game encourages creativity, forcing players to think on their feet and adapt to the ever-changing environment.The addition of new characters, items, and secrets elevates the gameplay to new heights. The variety of playstyles and strategies that emerge from the expansive roster of items and characters allows for a wealth of replayability. Spelunky 2's depth is not just in its caverns but in the strategic choices players make, creating an immersive and dynamic gameplay experience.The multiplayer aspect of Spelunky 2 deserves special praise. The cooperative mode adds a whole new layer of enjoyment, fostering camaraderie as players navigate the challenging caves together. It's a testament to the game's design that multiplayer doesn't feel like an afterthought but an integral part of the Spelunky experience.The soundtrack, composed by Eirik Suhrke, is a perfect accompaniment to the perilous journey. The music seamlessly adapts to the on-screen action, creating an atmospheric soundscape that enhances the emotional resonance of each moment, from tense encounters to triumphant victories.In conclusion, Spelunky 2 is a triumph in game design, a shining example of how to craft a sequel that not only honors its roots but surpasses them in every way. It's a challenging, visually stunning, and endlessly rewarding adventure that will keep players spelunking into its depths for years to come. Whether you're a fan of the original or a newcomer to the series, Spelunky 2 is a must-play, setting a new standard for the rogue-like genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I HATE THIS GAME. I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE IT.Spelunky 2 has the incredible ability to kill you in the most annoying and horrifyingly creative ways possible. Every levels are filled with carefully placed hazards and enemies to make you slip and mess up, instant kill are everywhere and all it takes is one wrong input from the controller to literally end your run. EVERY SINGLE mechanics in this game are meticulously designed to kill you in ways you wont ever be able to predict. There are no checkpoints, no save, no overpowered items that lets you breeze through the levels, no meta progression that makes the next attempts easier. IT IS BRUTALHowever what makes Spelunky 2 stands out from the rest of "haha hard game go brrr" titles out there is how.....brilliant it is at killing you, most of the time when you die you know exactly why it happened, but it's still surprise you everytime just cuz how insanely over engineered the game's mechanic is. Spelunky 2 doesnt play dirty, it just uses everything it has at its disposal and it uses them to the absolute extreme, it is insanely hard by design, and Spelunky 2 is horrifyingly well designed.....The one silver lining to all of this is that with enough observation, practice and determination, one can learn to avoid every death in this game. Spelunky 2 has a near infinite skill ceiling and despite having almost 400 hours now and beaten the game multiple times, i still have not begun to scratch the surface of what can be pulled off in this game. For the hardcore players looking for a game you cant truly master, none does it quite like Spelunky 2.Fantastically awful, play at your OWN risk.

_childDocuments_.review: Some would describe Spelunky HD as the perfect game, and I would agree. So then, how can you possibly improve upon perfection? The team found a way.Spelunky 2 features much of the same gameplay loop the previous entry had, yet adds variety and player agency by having options for the zones the player can head through. While Spelunky HD had a linear game from mines-jungle-ice caves-temple, Spelunky 2 has a split path from the Dwellings (zone 1) and the boss fight of zone 4. This isn't the only innovation however, as the area between the character select and core gameplay features a hub where you can interact with characters that have been unlocked, each with their own personalities. An improvement over the last game's characterisations (which had no interaction and they were all named after their predominate colours).These aren't the only improvements though, as much of the game has been refined, better balanced, and more variety to objectives, as there are mini stories one could progress through the game. For example, one can meet a vampire hunter locked in the lave area, and meet him later when you confront the vampire, and a few more times for a small arc.Every death in Spelunky still feels like it was a learning experience, and the same holds true for the most part in the sequel, although there is the occasional sky bombing mole that you couldn't possibly see.Ultimately though, Spelunky 2 shows what a great sequel can be, and definitely worthy of carrying on the Spelunky name.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely excited for this game! The previous Spelunky HD is one of my all time favorites, and my gold standard for modern roguelike games. I can understand that Derek Yu wanted to make his sequel more challenging, but Spelunky 2 goes way too far with it, to the point that it isn't even close to fair anymore. But to be fair, the game does some things better than its predecessor, and I wanna list some stuff off, both good and bad.There's lots of new characters! Each character has a unique kind of rope that they use, which is a nice touch. I also really like the newer character designs and the big influx of new characters to unlock. I like the new golden idol altars in zone 1 more than in the original. The giant pillar is much more manageable than a giant wild card boulder of death that could easily ruin a run by crashing into a shop or a vault far off screen from you.There are many more zones to explore this time. Not only that, there are two different paths you can take at the end of zone 1! I love that! I love the turkeys and other mounts that you can use and even keep between floors. Those are cute and I love them.There are now mini game shops that let you enter a special challenge room where you can earn money and prizes. Sweet!As for the bad things....Moles are an obnoxious new enemy that can chase you through walls and floors. I've lost count of how many times they've dropped on me from seemingly out of nowhere because I can't see everywhere at once, or I ended up stuck between a gopher and another hazard and couldn't avoid taking damage because I can't watch the the whole screen.There is a now an equivalent to the tiki trap that shows up in zone 1, and that's pretty neat! But the arrow traps are now 2 or 3 times as frequent as before. Staying on alert for them means you basically can't ever stop being paranoid about them. The first one wasn't nearly this stressful about that. Enemies are far more frequent now, and avoiding one enemy very frequently leads you straight into something else.  The first zone has an actual boss enemy that will very easily instantly kill if you aren't extremely careful, and that got old really fast. Sometimes a level will just randomly be HUGE. That wouldn't necessarily be a big problem on its own, except...The ghost in this game is much more punishing for players who want to explore a bit. And the thing is, it already WAS punishing for players in the last game. It's just even more so now. It now splits into multiple faster ghosts if you aren't quick to get out when it arrives. The previous game already didn't really give you that much freedom to explore levels, so this change seems needlessly aggressive. I could see this being a feature in a version of the game meant to challenge speedrunners, but having it in normal runs seems cruel. This game feels a lot like one of those "insane brutal challenge designed to make children cry" challenge mods made for the most dedicated fans of a game. Except that's just the standard game here. And its just not that fun to me. This would be a whole other thing if the game had a difficulty option, and this were merely the hard mode. But there isn't an option to make any of this less of a chore.I gave it my best try! But I just can't justify playing it anymore. I sank over 600 hours of my life into the previous game, and I had a blast with it. I'm putting Spelunky 2 down after 30, because it's just not worth playing any more.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a while, especially if you're familiar with the original, but you're also more likely to notice how much content is rehashed from the original (i.e. basically everything, making it feel more like a Spelunky 1 expansion pack). While the new content and plentiful secrets are generally pretty exciting and entertaining, the still-poor platforming physics and hitboxes will slowly erode away your enjoyment, as will the decision of the developers to focus more on funny death potential than quality of life (every throw of the dice in the gambling den threatening to either damage you when it falls on your head or get you murdered by the bouncer if they land one pixel outside the door, shopkeepers and NPCs becoming aggroed as soon as you enter the level by procedurally generated objects damaging them or their goods before you can take one step, teleporting enemies that can telefrag you no matter how much health you've stockpiled), the sad part being that many if not most of these problems were imported from Spelunky 1 and were intentionally left unfixed for the funny Twitch clips.Of course, the new content has plenty of its own problems, with enemies too fast to reliably hit with the floaty, momentum-lacking jumping controls, enemies that damage you as soon as they see you regardless of how far you run away, and progression-necessary rooms and items that are generated in locations unreachable without using all of your resources and simultaneously angering instakilling NPCs (or they might as well be, as taking most damage stuns you long enough for most enemies to stunlock you to death no matter your health) for the rest of the run. Overall not the worst roguelite on the platform by any means, but a very disappointing follow-up that doesn't improve on its predecessor in any meaningful way and seems more concerned with producing funny clips for streamers that it personally calls out in the hopes they will generate more buzz for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointed in lack of official Linux support, maybe we'll get there.Works OK with tweaks in Proton, check out ProtonDB, otherwise it works for me with custom Proton version Proton-TKG 5.18 – without any further tweaks.Overall for any long term fans of Spelunky this game is a mustI'm going to add a caveat here.If you play rogue-lites to beat them:I'd advise checking out the first version if you are new - this one is extremely difficult.If you like sandboxes, laughter mixed with pain and absolute hell breaking loose, this game is far better. The game will teach it's mechanics by killing you over and over. If you don't like dying, check out Spelunky; but if you want a game to master through brute force and hilarity, check out Spelunky 2.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who spent quite a few hours with Spelunky 1, I find the difficulty of this one to be pretty fair, however, people who are new to spelunky should know that this game is extremely hard and  Don't just give up and assume you suck, practice a bit everyday and you will improve.The first area has some nasty new enemies but nothing you can't handle once you learn what they do. Some people are arguing that the first area feels overcrowded with enemies and traps now because the new enemies are added on top of the ones from the original game, but I disagree, there's no more enemies per level than in the original game, there's simply more variety of them, which is clearly a good thing.The new art style is brighter and more simplified, the environments feel a bit flat at times,  , however I think the characters and creatures look generally nicer now, a good example is the cavemen or the bats. They also added some pretty nice looking lighting effects which look awesome specially in dark levels.Hilariously enough, you can see your "win percentage" on your player profile, as if anyone is gonna have a win percentage above 0,01%.Overall I just feel excited to explore this game and find all the secrets and alternate paths and what not, so far this feels like a worthy successor to the first one.

Yes, Spelunky is a very highly rated and difficult game. I'd recommend this to people of all ages, as there is limited blood or gore. I've been playing Spelunky since I was 6, and it's the best!

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Spelunky 2 is easily the most difficult game I've played.I'm no stranger to difficulty. I've conquered the Dark Souls series, Celeste's final chapter Farewell, fellow roguelike Enter the Gungeon, all but the final two pantheons in Hollow Knight, the best ending of Cave Story, and the Ku'lero Temple in Crosscode.But Spelunky 2 doesn't really care how good you think you are. It will beat you down, over and over, time and time again until you learn your bloody place in the world, and if you ever forget it will very swiftly remind you. Beating the game AT ALL is an incredible accomplishment, and getting to some of the secret areas is borderline nightmarish. Completing the Cosmic Ocean? Forget about it, you aren't going to.If you're planning on buying this game, know what you're getting into. You're going to die. You're going to die again. You're going to get frustrated, and quit the game. But inevitably, you'll come back to it, because you want to show this game who's boss. And one day, maybe, you will. But you need to WORK for it. You need to play, and practice, and die, and try again. It might take you 100 attempts. 200. 300. 1000, even. Or you might be a god gamer, do it in 20, and say "that's not enough" - and go for the Cosmic Ocean. And then THAT will take you 100 attempts, 200, whatever.The point is - this game is a commitment. You can't cheese your way through. You can't breeze your way through. And you sure as hell aren't winning on your first try. If you're willing to take on the challenge, you'll love this game. If not, you'll probably hate it, and that's totally fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Twice as hard, but only half the fun.I put in hundreds of hours into the first game and consider it a classic. It was difficult, but after a couple dozen hours of gameplay you got most of the game down and can enjoy the real fun, being able to relax and explore each level at your leisure.  The game was cruel, but fair.Spelunky 2 is not a game that offers that experience and sadly after 89 hours of playing I've had to come to terms with that fact. The game is overly difficult, the music isn't very good, the gameplay changes from the original are practically a detriment, you never feel like you're able to really accomplish anything because of how much easier it is to die, and most importantly its just not much fun.The game never allows you to really relax or explore like in the first one, The crackhead moles on the dwelling area who you pretty much have to spend the time to kill because it takes twice as much effort to run away from them at times. The ridiculously small hitboxes of the mosquitos from the Jungle area are almost as bad as the thorny walls that you're gonna bump into with your last one or two hit points.The lavamen and the lava liquid spread from the Volcano will randomly end an amazing run in an instant. Keep in mind these are JUST the first 2 levels of a run.If these weren't bad enough you also have to now deal with unreliable hitboxes on both enemies, lava, and traps that will end a run faster than a black out. You can be just out of range on several of these and the game will still say you take the hit. Sadly ladders, ropes, and platform edges can also be unreliable and at times, especially when they count.The level design now has removed a lot of the more open exploring feel the first game had and instead has everything whittled down to maybe two paths and a few dead ends and the game feels incredibly claustrophobic and lacks a more open feel. While the original had a lot of claustrophobic design in the level layout it still maintained some open areas, several settings lack this in the sequels randomly generated map layout and it lacks variety in a lot of the maps as a whole. The Dwelling is especially hit by this.The games soundtrack is hit or miss. I loved the music in the original and while this games soundtrack does have some really nice tunes, several of them feel flat and bland. Also I was surprised that each setting now only has 1 soundtrack, where as in the first game each setting had several ones which helped create a really unique feel and was always a pleasure to listen too. But with the same soundtrack just endlessly looping until you finish the setting and move onto the next it gets pretty monotonous. Shout out to the Tide Pool soundtrack actually making me want to go to sleep -_-But the real irritation is you cannot play this game the way you played the first one. Thats an instant death. You have to practically start over and if you spent a couple hundred hours on the first one you have that muscle memory kick in and get penalized for it. Thats not exactly an easy adjustment to make :/There was an lot of anarchistic to the first game which was a lot of fun and kept you on your toes, but unfortunately this game takes that concept and gives it a steady supply of crack. There are times when you'll find out its just easier to commit suicide in a run rather that continue on and thats honestly a very depressing thing to admit. It feels almost counter productive to try to learn how the game works as I did with the first one because no matter how hard you try, this games randomness will just keep you from ever really going anywhere.I'm no slouch to Spelunky and its not easy to say that a game is too hard, and I don't want to sound like a games journalist but Spelunky 2 is way too hard. There is an amazing game inside here, but the new design approach to trying to kill you every strep of the way combined with random elements that never allow you to really relax and have fun with the game, isn't fun at all. I'm saying this after the Mole enemy changes from a few days back too.This isn't a game you can sit down and really have fun with as I did with the first one, and despite all the things in this game I really love, the new Olmec fight, the Temple of Anubis, the hidden levels within each level and the side quests, the non stop difficulty keeps me from getting to savor these moments because you can't enjoy what happened if you die a quarter second later from a Mole, or Lava, or flying saucer that got blown up across the map and ended up launched at you.Spelunky 2 needs a lot more adjustments to it than just the mole issue on the Dwelling setting. If Jesus Christ was in a world made of video games then Spelunky 2 would be both the nails and his cross.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me question whether I ever actually enjoyed the original.  The original was challenging, but here everything has been cranked up to 11.  The first set of levels, which in the original were a way to ease into the game, are now a nightmarish slog, ultra dense with traps and enemies, including new enemies that are far more difficult than their predecessors.  They take multiple hits to kill (which cannot be done quickly as they are invincible during stun) and have fast, erratic movements.  Then once you graduate to the later levels, your health effectively becomes meaningless because 90% of your deaths will be 1-hit instakills, or effective 1-hit kills where you are stunlocked, thrown around the screen, and juggled to death.  The game does not even appear to be aiming for the "tough but fair" label that Souls games often get.  I experienced many deaths due to bizarre enemy interactions halfway across the map, or objects flying at me suddenly from offscreen.What all of this added difficultly results in is a game that is at odds with itself.  It must be played with extreme caution if the player wants to have any chance of success, but this slows the pace of the game down to a crawl and draws out the length of each run.  This being a roguelike where all progress is lost upon death, this makes every death as painful and disheartening as possible.  The balance between fun and frustration has been completely lost here.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is interesting to talk about a few years later after 100%ing it. This is a sequel that does a lot right but adds a lot that just adds frustration in many scenarios, but is overall a great experience.To get things out of the way the "community" aspect in the trailer is literally just seeing all the playable characters you unlock walking around nothing more.This game is structured similarly to HD but adds a lot more shop variants, areas/alt paths, npc interactions, and different secret areas. a lot of these add way more gameplay variety and run choice but some choices are just straight up better than others. IE: Vlad's cape, going to Tidepool in many cases, etc etcThis game does give even more player choice via learning skips and exploits, such as being able to skip the entirety of the requirements for the hard mode ending if you're really good at jetpack movement.The biggest negatives I can give this game are how some items were changed + a late game area: Cosmic Ocean...Jetpacks and other backpacks that are electronic/ will ignite and explode dealing 10 damage to you, this wouldn't be that crazy if it weren't for the fact that lava as a fluid is very fickle and unpredictable in many scenarios. The real offender in this case is the hazards in Neo Babylon, but are entirely dodge-able. This is just a skill issue on my part but it can be quite annoying to acquire a great item for a heavy cost/risk just to instantly lose it. This sorta leads into Cosmic Ocean and a few other area caveats.Cosmic Ocean IS designed as the ultimate challenge, but being screwed over time via a single mistake, whether it be poison or curse status and NOT be able to remove it ever in this zone is poor design. You can often be boned without the Kapala (item that lets you heal via blood) and just have a slow agonizing trickle down.The only other area in the game that can often be straight up unfair is Volcana in a singular instance. When using the drill to reach the castle the lava flow the drill impacts can often leave you just... waiting.... sometimes you can't even get through and have to give up on going to the final area if you don't have enough bombs. This rarely happens thankfully due to some restructuring of level generation in patches.Despite these two area negatives this is a great game with so much depth, my only biased negative that isn't gameplay related is that HD's soundtrack, which included easter egg songs and multiple tracks per area really added to the run variety and general vibe.TLDR; Fantastic game but lacks in many areas compared to its precursor.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun for sure, but there are still tweaks I think could be made. I think the first world's generation might need some fixing, as there is an abundance of traps and the spike falls that are almost always never used. The combat is fun, but being blown up with a jetpack by a torch is annoying. Dead bodies also knock shopkeepers unconscious when live ones dont. The whip got nerfed, and the male//female damsels got removed from the game. Don't get it twisted, I got 100$ of the achievements for Spelunky 1, and have beaten Spelunky 2's normal section already, and will likely 100% it as well, but I wish all the minor inconveniences for the sake of making the game more difficult I could be without (Everyone has been Derek'ed before). Otherwise, this game has a whole new diagram of secrets, paths, enemies, items, and npcs! It's a challenge to really master this game because of how much more dynamic and alive it feels. It's like trying to get good at running across a balance beam. You have to go fast enough that you don't die unnecessarily, or bore yourself, but slow enough that you can come up with plans to tackle the level, and all its traps. I 100% don't regret a single cent of what I paid, and highly recommend any players, casual or not, to try out Spelunky 2 to experience something that few 2d platform looters have accomplished.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll always recommend either Spelunky game, of course.  After getting Ironman in this one I decided to replay the original a bit to see how it compares (I got to the City of Gold for the first time!), and here are my main takeaways.Spelunky 2 improves majorly on the variety and scope of the original game, with far more areas and even branching paths that allow you to take different routes to reach the same ending.  There are also several additional "quests" that can be undertaken for an additional challenge.  This length can be a detriment however, making having to restart even more frustrating.The art style and music are a bit different as well.  I prefer the original in these regards, but I understand I'm in the minority.The main thing to note here is the difference in level layout itself: the best way to describe this game's levels in comparison to the first is   Levels have far less open space and far more enemies.  This is the main factor in the sequel being more difficult, the other being that it is simply longer.  Having played both back-to-back, I will definitely say I prefer the spacious levels of the original to the cramped menageries of the sequel.TL;DR I would recommend everyone I know play both of these games, but the sequel's levels are a bit crowded for my liking.  And the increased length improves the variety, but comes at the price of making restarting feel even worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a phenomenal game in my eyes and the best of the 3 current spelunky games (expectedly as it is the latest instalment). The greatest aspect of the spelunky experience is the quality replay-ability the game has to offer with its randomly generated rooms throughout different world types, the complex game mechanics that are simple to learn but take extensive time and dedication to master. Spelunky 2 is a rogue-like game, (this works well with the randomised rooms), therefore as you play you cant rely on any form of power ups for the player character across games, but you need to learn how the world around you works and how to thrive within it, this would lead the skill ceiling to be even higher.The game has well rounded graphics and a colour pallet that is not too vibrant or abstract. Each world also has a unique theme that really makes each new location feel different, this consists of the music that seamlessly transitions through levels (10/10 but can be disabled), the huge variety of enemies that all have their own attack patterns and the style of the terrain surrounding you. These aspects lead each level to feel alive and not just a chore to get through.This game is packed full of npcs to interact with, quest lines to do and secrets waiting to be found. And all of this is documented in a well thought out journal that can provide insight into how far you have progressed through the many hours of content waiting to be explored.There is also a co-op mode for up to four people and this can be accessed locally or through an online feature, with this you can access the standard adventure game mode and the arena mode to battle your friends to become the ultimate spelunker.

_childDocuments_.review: Arite so, where do I A recent release at the time of writing (version 1.18.0), Spelunky 2 has kept my attention for the two months it's been out, trying to plumb its depths for gold and glory. And whilst other things have been giving me less time to play the game, it's still in the back of my mind for a number of reasons.The sequel to Spelunky HD has some loose ties with regards to story - characters from the HD version ended up with backstories and friendships that makes having idle chatter with 'em in the base camp a neat little distraction between runs. Whilst they all play functionally the same, there's a good spread of characters you can play as, who all have neat things like different ropes, sometimes different whips and even unique sound effects for some actions, so from the 20 characters you can find, there's sure to be one you'll cling on to when you unlock 'em. As you progress further into the game, a fair number of things such as enemies or locations are discovered that puts some  twists on things that existed in both the Classic and HD versions of the original game. To put it lightly, if you expected the final boss (normal AND secret) to be like , then you have a better understanding of ancient history than I do!In terms of gameplay, Spelunky 2 feels very similar to Spelunky HD (who would have expected it?!) with minor tweaks here and there. For example, enemies can't bump into you from below if you're hanging from a ledge - your ability to stomp is no longer explicitly tied to your downwards velocity. The addition of back-wall regions can potentially double the amount of stage you have to traverse to find gems and trinkets, and helps compress level progression somewhat without making Special Stages too common by having unique regions in the same place as regular stages. There's also a new challenge for high-score runners as the ghost is feeling a little more sprightly up on the Moon... The numerous patches the game's had since launch have helped tighten up other mechanics here and there, though this does leave the game in a weird state of flux where something that seems like intended gameplay (eg capes deactivating during a throw animation and reactivating when the animation is done) suddenly gets patched out in a following update.The constant patching also helps to keep some of the more  technical bugs at bay. From major things like achievements not working and all controls being mapped to "Up" on the left analogue stick, to minor things like small gems all using the same emerald graphic, and then the standard ol' hard-crash here and there, Spelunky 2 is still rough around the edges, but Mossmouth is putting the work in to buff things out and leave the players with a sparkling diamond.Visually speaking, Spelunky 2 feels cleaner than HD, with lots of softer colours in the stages as a contrast against the more violent parts of the game. This pairs well with the more subdued and dynamic musical stylings of Eirik Suhrke that sets it apart from previous entries. The actual physical requirements of the computer needed to play the game can easily catch folks out, however there's settings to make the game run on less-than-ideal builds. Some of the challenges the game offers can be made more difficult thanks to this visual style though, as money or hazards you were aiming to avoid are hidden behind set dressing you didn't register as a threat, and without warning another run is over. With the increased size of stages, this makes some challenges rather difficult to surmount.Which leads me to the main caveat of recommending this game. Whilst I have a lot of good to say about it, Spelunky 2 feels far more unforgiving than its predecessor. A full run to either of the game's end-bosses can take a good while to accomplish. Going fast is generally a recipe for disaster, as dart traps or spikes or any number of stage hazards will catch you out in some way, and the myriad new creatures you can encounter on the way through the depths will take some getting used to before they go from "instant death evil" to "oh those guys again". It takes a  of learning, and finding out where all the moving parts hafta go in order to get a "Hard" or "Special" clear can take quite a while to accomplish - either in terms of the initial discoveries, or how to actually  everything without being violently kicked to the "Game Over" screen again because turning off the hypervigilance for one second meant you missed the flaming UFO that's hurtling towards you. This is part of the whole "roguelike" genre, of course, so if you like punishing difficulty, Spelunky 2 has you covered.If there's one thing I definitely do  like about Spelunky 2, it's one of the final areas of the game, the . After 30 or more minutes putting everything together to clamber through nineteen hazard-filled stages, four major bosses, and any  of minibosses on the way there, your final reward is an "endless" stage type that sends you traipsing through previous stages with no walls, three targets to clear and a new hazard that blocks the path to the next stage. I say "endless" - it caps out at 99, at which point you're rewarded with  commemorating your hard-won victory. If this had been a side-game you could unlock after clearing the hard-mode boss, similar to Arena Mode, Seeded Runs and so on, I'd probably look on it a bit kinder; a kind of distillation of the game where you keep going until you die. As it stands, it's the end-game that seems to stretch off into infinity, encouraging unhealthy gaming practices with the promise of a fancy reward at the end of it all, whilst the game does everything it can to stop you from achieving this goal.In short, Spelunky 2 is what you would expect from a follow-up to the HD release of Spelunky with seven more years of experience under the devs' belts - great fun, punishing difficulty, fantastic music, pleasing visuals, and overall a great experience provided you can weather the storm.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a spelunky game before, you might be thrown off by the art style or apparently simple gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Maybe my opinion on this game will change if I play it more, but Jesus Harold Faltermeyer Christ, it is too bloody hard. I don't mind a game being tough, I completed Hotline Miami 2's Hard Mode, played the ♥♥♥♥ outta Nuclear Throne, and generally prefer difficult games. This game, however, is too hard, and the gameplay isn't fun enough to justify that difficulty. If I allowed comments on my steam reviews, i'd expect a flood of "git gud"s about now. If a game doesn't entertain me enough for me to "git gud" i will not attempt to "git gud".It is far too easy to lose health, and far too hard to regain it. You can knock yourself out with your own bombs and throwables if you don't aim them right. The most common traps take away 2 of your 4 precious health points in a single hit, and although the dart traps can be avoided or disarmed if you throw an item or lure an enemy in front of it, sometimes you either won't have any items to throw, or be at an angle where you just can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ throw a thing in front of it. The game is just not fun. Maybe it will get more fun if i play it more, but at the moment... No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to say, but Spelunky 2 is decidedly worse than classic and HD. Enemies, traps, spike pits, etc litter 80% of the real estate of a level, They are so densely packed that there is no breathing room to ever slow down. Whether it's tons of moles and arrow traps in dwelling, or 10 rotating electric traps in neo babylon, or instant death blocks flying at you from every angle in Temple, there's a never ending mishmash of garbage being thrown at you that feels poorly thought out and spammy.Repetitive tasks like saving the sisters in Jungle or farming blood in Vlad's become a grindy chore as you go through runs, and the constant revamps of the Olmec mean you never know what you're going to be dealing with after a patch. Sad to say it's strictly worse than its predecessor, and not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the first game, everywhere I was on the internet I would suggest SPELUNKY (I even always spelled it like that), on r/PatientGamers it was my answer for almost every question when someone inquired about what game they should play next. I had the first game on PS3 and PC but my laptop was so old that it would constantly overheat just playing that small game. Now I have a new laptop as of Christmas 2020 and I finally get to play the one PC game I had been waiting for for many years...and I'm almost about to give up on it. The easiest example I could give about the difficulty is something like Dark Souls, people want to be punished but also learn to be skilled, a nice balance in the gameplay once you hit a certain point then many feel the games are second nature. Not with Spelunky 2, I've literally played 60 hours of this game (I can't even think of how many hours I've put into S1) and still feel just as stupid and weak as the first day I started, every pixel of this game is made to be as unfair as possible, if I was a big PC gamer and knew all the ins and outs of modding I would love to edit the gameplay to make it so I could at least make it to Olmec on the first run for once. I absolutely loved the game Hollow Knight which many compare to the Dark Souls game as a sort of 2D version, that was just a lot of pattern recognition but also, the game was FUN. I find that I had waited so long to just play any Spelunky again that I'm putting all my time into S2 in hopes of feeling the joy I had from the first but no, it's easy to just "quick restart" and try again and get lost in getting further until I have to just just off my laptop in the middle of a game because I'm so upset.

_childDocuments_.review: When I originally left this review, I found seeded runs helped me progress so I wanted to re-evaluate how I felt about Spelunky 2. But this game still feels closer to a neutral recommendation for me. Playing with friends is a lot of fun and alleviates most of my gripes. Playing solo is still mostly only fun if you have speedrunner levels of dedication. Be prepared to reset your runs. Sometimes early and often to get a good start. If speedrunning is not your thing and you don't have friends to play this game with, recommendations are with those caveats in mind. Maybe if you're willing to mod the game for variety, it could be worth as the platforming and level progression are very good overall (assuming you can progress). Please do not mod your Spelunky 2 install directly to avoid cheats in direct relation to Steam and all that. There's gonna be some spoilers here, but I'll try to keep it vague.At it's base, Seplunky 2 is a solid 2D platformer. It comes with various upgrades and tools to navigate through the caves, along with various enemies to work around. The movement feels a bit too fast and spastic at times, with hitboxes that can be unforgiving or feel inconsistent. But overall, it can be very smooth. It combines the unforgiving nature of Dead Cells, the utter bullcrap of Dark Souls, along with the obscure pathfinding of a Hollow Knight, all into one (I said this in my original review but still feel it best summarizes the experience). On paper it sounds great. But in execution, it's a bit too brutal at times.Getting to new locations can be quite rewarding, especially with the struggle just about every level can pose. So many runs can end at any moment to a split second decision, so you want to be on guard at all times. Money can be useful for upgrades, but also a distraction which can put you in situations that whittle away your health or combo you to death.I've restarted 1000-ish times and beat the first-ish boss, got all the shortcuts, unlocked seeded runs, looked up half the game I'm missing, checked out speedrunner strats, checked out the devs reacting to speedrunner strats, tried to figure out if there's anything new in any area I've been already, and I still don't know how this game was meant to be played. Shortcuts seem best only for bragging rights and a little practice. There are achievements which require you to do them in what I would consider the easier way. (Beat the game without shortcuts? Which shortcut is even good?) I tend to not always piece things together the first way one should, so there's probably a few things I'm being dense about.The first couple of worlds are where I normally worry about money, as I can't find shops anywhere later on. It starts to give this strange sensation that getting money normally just leads to lost health, so robbing a shopkeeper just ends up helping me navigate the worlds and fend off enemies. Later levels start to follow a trend of more hazards and enemies in tighter spaces. While a nice change of pace after running through early worlds, it gets to be a bit absurd when the level is too busy killing itself and all you need to do is stay out of the crossfire (takes care of the shopkeepers for me). Which a lot of the game in general will kill itself and then blame you for it. Sometimes you can be the culprit, but I've delivered turkeys for Turkey Man (definitely his name) and he dropped a key for me on his turkeys and then killed me for it. The game seems very unable to actually kill the player efficiently, so it makes up for it by sharting damage and aggro for no reason the longer it goes. And for how much I'm expecting things like making the shopkeepers mad or whatever else to kill me, often times I'm getting one shot by terrain. I've even been killed by a flying arrowhead that did zero damage but dropped me onto a conveyor belt which delivered me onto spikes. I wish I could say this doesn't happen often, but that's pretty much how most runs go. Something benign turns into a stun which delivers death. I'm still going back to 1-1 all the same.For the other half of the game, you still need to go through a couple sequences in the first two worlds for 2 items. Both required for just about any path other than the first-ish boss (give or take advanced tech and/or cheese). At first, it seems fine, but it gets so incredibly tedious to constantly redo these sequences, hoping to find your change of pace in world 3, only to be done in by instant-death mechanics. I've never been a fan of instant-death mechanics. At best, they're annoying once in a while, and at worst, they start to feel like a lazy way to keep the game going. Half the things on screen are likely to kill you at any moment. Along with combo chains that can easily snowball. It is possible to commit no mistakes and still start world 5 with an explosion careen from offscreen the first second the level loads and end your run. That is not weakness. That is Splunkying.This game is not dynamic enough for it to focus on the singleplayer aspect this much. Multiplayer focus would have been nicer, as it helps alleviate just about all the issues stated above (dividing tasks for the two sequences, not having to restart on one minor error made 5 worlds in, etc...). But couch co-op doesn't have split screen and online doesn't seem to have access to shortcuts, unlocking characters, and arena bots (I believe, but I also still don't know what unlocked my seeded runs). Instead, a lot of what the game offers is something very clip worthy while livestreaming. It is a lot of fun. I livestreamed with friends for my birthday. But 1000 restarts solo is just too much for what this game actually is. Clip worthy, speedrunner ready, solid platforming, and great cooperative shenanigans. And that's the high note I'll leave it on.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally getting all the achievements in the game, I think I can effectively say I've experienced all that Spelunky 2 has to offer. To summarize my thoughts: this game is fantastic if you're looking for an extreme challenge. Just like the original (Spelunky HD, that is), this game will beat your butt no questions asked. Just like the original, you'll feel yourself getting better every run. Just like the original, it has near infinite replay value. Unlike the original, Spelunky 2 expands upon that feeling of discovery and strange locations. The introduction of backrooms, as well as split paths was an excellent choice, and really added a lot to make this game stand out from the first.That being said, with more content comes more issues. I'm sure it is evident to anyone who has played the game for more than a couple of hours, but the dwelling is certainly not all that it could be. The addition of a special level on 1-4 is a great idea, but some of the new enemies that weren't in the original really should've stayed out. The magic of Spelunky HD was that when you died, it was ALWAYS your fault, and you could only really blame yourself. But in Spelunky 2, some things just feel unfair (moles, horned lizards). That sense that the game is unfair is most concentrated in the dwelling, but it can affect you in other areas, too.Don't get me wrong, though. I still absolutely love this game. I wouldn't keep coming back to it if I didn't. The challenge that Spelunky 2 brings is addicting. If you loved the first game, chances are you'll love this one. If you have a lot of time to be frustrated at yourself, but slowly get better, chances are you'll love Spelunky 2. However, if you get easily annoyed at occasional unfair RNG, this may not be for you. While I think I can safely say that just about everyone can enjoy Spelunky HD, this game takes the difficulty to an extreme that many players would avoid. Even still, this game is a thrill, and I highly recommend it.

And new players can feel the joy of trying to traverse the levels while figuring out how to not die so easily, new players will also feel the excitement of trying to uncover the mystery of the caves and all it has to offer, and no run will feel the same as the levels are half auto generated and half authored which is a genius way of making it so you never get tired of the game because of how replayable it is. _childDocuments_.review: What is the one difference between Spelunky 2 and Spelunky HD? Probably the appeal to different demographics. Spelunky HD was hard from the very beginning. I didn't unlock the jungle until my 20th hour in HD. Spelunky 2 may not be easier, but it has a better difficulty curve. For casual players, Spelunky 2 is a godsend for anybody that wanted to get into Spelunky but lost interest after many deaths. There's even an online multiplayer for those who want to play with friends. For the hardcore gamers however, you may find Spelunky 2 to be unbalanced. If you want to get to the first ending, the game is fine, but if you want to get to the hardmode second ending, the game restricts your choices to where you can only go a certain route, making the playthroughs boring. Only a handful of earth's gamers have had enough patience to beat the third ending, that being the Cosmic Ocean. I recommend Spelunky 2 to any players who play the game to see how far they can get over players who play the game to get the farthest. In my book, though, this game is one of the most entertaining action roguelites to date. Even after 92.2 hours I'm still making stories to tell to my grandchildren! 10/10

Spiders can hide behind the little cloths on the ceiling that appear sometimes in the dwellings, 2. m o l e s, 3. how poison works. A run can be utterly destroyed because I accidentally had a scorpion lunge into my jugular because I couldn't see in the dark? Better rescue a pet or looks like the run is flushed straight down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In fact, the run is already in the pipes! Better fish it out from a sewer using a pet so you can finally stop being in constant pain. While those are the bad things of the game, I'd like to talk about the good to great to absolutely amazing. First off, it feels so good to be genuinely surprised when you find a secret. Having a game make me say "woahhhh" is pretty rare and its super fun seeing the red place (can't say the actual name because of spoilers) and then meeting the big but not bigest man. What I also love about this game is that it will break you. This game is really mean to its players. Not like a mean where it randomly restarts, more like a brutal mean. It is relentless, and you will never catch a break. You can have 99 bombs, be at the final level, and have 10 billion health, and somehow die to a regular spider. Anything can kill you. And when I finally beat this gem, the only thing I'll be able to do is play it again.In summary, buy this game or beg someone to gift it to you if you like a challenging, 2D, and brutal but fun experience with good music. _childDocuments_.review: I remember when I bought the first Spelunky 3 years ago. I played the freeware Spelunky Classic, thought it was a blast, and was curious about the HD remake. I figured that I would return it after an hour and realize "Oh, it's not worth it." 150 hours later, I can say pretty confidently that it was. I'm not gonna say that it was some grand revelation, but it tweaked the near-perfect formula, while adding plenty of new features, and it came out as the truly definitive way to play the game. I'm barely an hour in Spelunky 2, and I can already feel that same process happening again. The differences between this and the original, compared to the original and Classic, are too numerous to count right now, but the heart of the core gameplay hasn't changed a bit. It still has that systemic, dynamic, risk vs. reward gameplay that the original nailed, but adding more features and tweaks to make it even better. Every single attempt so far taught me about some new interaction, new system, or new technique, and that's almost exclusively in the first area of the game. This doesn't reinvent Spelunky, but I feel like this is the new definitive way to play, just like Spelunky HD was before. I'll update the review after I've sunk more time into it, but if you're any sort of fan of the original, or just want a ball-crushingly hard roguelike to sink your teeth into, you can't go wrong with this.Edit 28 hours in: finally beat the game once with the last shortcut. can't wait to dive in for more torture tomorrow

_childDocuments_.review: Quite disappointing. Spelunky HD is & was such a great game, almost perfect. I had been anticpating the sequel since the announcement a few years ago. The sequel seems to try and cram so many new mechanics in that all the fun has been pushed out. In Spelunky HD, you always felt like a death was your fault & that made you eager to press on. In this sequel, there is so much to keep track of that the best way to move forward is to slow down to a crawl so nothing pops up and kills you cheaply. Some of the level 'chunk' designs are really confusing. You'll see these spots where there is a gem or pot placed in such a way that forces you to use resources to get to them. In Spelunky HD these situations were few & far between & were there as a 'bonus' in case you had some extra bombs & ropes. In Spelunky 2, the level design is constantly trying to milk you for your resources around every corner.Health is pretty irrelevant - because everything now reacts to everything else, getting hit once usually means stunlock-bouncing around until all of your health is depleted, & that feels really cheap. Maybe I just need to put more hours in, but unlike Spelunky HD, this game doesn't give me any motivation to press on, because I know it'll be more & more cheap deaths that are beyond my control. If you're a fan of Speluky HD, I unfortunately would have to say stick to that one and pass this one up. This game is suffering from sequelitis quite a bit, & that is a real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: wow, this is a phenomenal gameok, so after writing a few reviews i learned that it REALLY isn't for me but this game is so amazing that i'd feel like i'm doing it a disservice by not reviewing it.when i first played spelunky, i failed, i triumphed, i learned, but most importantly; i died, a lot. the thing about spelunky is that it does not hold anything back, and i was not dissapointed to learn that the sequel is very much the same, but even harder. this game can manage an incredible balance between being extremely difficult and yet fair. through my hours of playing and countless deaths, maybe once or twice i felt like a death wasnt entirely my fault. enough with the basic overview, let's see what's changedchanges for the worsei don't want to end this review on a sour note, so we'll get the things i didn't like about this game out of the way first.first of all, the music.spelunky 2 expands on nearly every single thing that spelunky 1 put on the table, more enemies, more areas, and many more ways to find yourself dead. the only thing that it didnt expand on was the music. the first game had maybe 4 tracks per area that would each have a random chance of playing so you dont have to listen to the same song every time you die. i think this is a great thing, and i was slightly dissapointed to see that it didn't appear in the sequel. the music is still wonderful, don't get me wrong, and maybe it's a little nitpicky, but i don't really know the reason for this change.second of all, the lag.this game is beautiful. the effects that appear are amazing and make for a great and immersive experience. however, if you have a low end pc they might be an issue for you. i dont run an amazing setup, i play most of my games on a laptop and i usually don't get lag or graphical issues. however, i noticed that in dark levels and levels with liquid the game would slow down to a crawl. a day or so later a patch came out that made the game feel much less laggy and everything is playable again. im not certain on this so you'll probably have to check up with someone else but if you have a really old and bad computer you might want to look in on it. changes for the better now, there's a lot to pick apart so i'll be as concise as i can.first of all, the rides.the rides are a newly added mechanic in the sequel and i like them quite a bit. they offer unique mobility and attacks to enrich your run, and anything that makes your life easier in an even harder game is certainly welcome.second of all, the new areas.spelunky 2 adds several new areas and has most of the old areas at least somewhere present from the first game. thematically, the new areas are great. the new traps, obstacles, enemies and music are pretty sweet. most of the new enemies are very interesting and very few of them are annoying to deal with. the few new items that we did get were all pretty nice and interesting.third of all, the charactersspelunky 2 adds a bunch of new characters and most of them are cool and well designed. ana spelunky and LISE are some of my personal favorites. it's also nice that we've gone from a male/female damsel or a dog/sloth to a hamster, cat, or dog.so, should you buy spelunky 2? yea.if you have to choose between spelunky 1 or 2 i'd say you should go for 2 since there's more content in general though both are great choices and phenomenal games.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the original Spelunky, and put in a good 50 hours or so which is a good chunk for a game of this sort. Of course I would want more Spelunky.Spelunky 2 feels like a mod level pack or a DLC add-on to Spelunky 1.It definitely brings in tons of changes and new things, but it re-uses so much from the first game that it hardly feels like there was any form of innovation and it feels more like a rehash.The game still plays well and is as addicting as the first, but there's a lot that feels off.Difficulty: They definitely ramped up the difficulty level, making it much cheaper than the first game. I also feel like, while increased difficulty can make the game be a huge challenge to returning players - it will alienate newer players. I think it'll be harder for new players to get the hang of this game, without having played the first one.Rehash: The zones from the original game, all the enemies, all the traps, all the items return to this one. I would have preferred a "sequel" to actually do everything new. Instead we got all the exact same ♥♥♥♥ with some minor adjustments and visual changes. It feels incredibly lazy and hardly like a sequel. For a price higher than the original, I was expecting the content to be more original.Music: Spelunky classic had some great music. It was super chill, very retro style and fit the game beautifully. Its only downfall was being somewhat repetitive as there weren't many tracks for the game. Spelunky HD completely redid the music into this funky jazz style that was forgettable, had awful instrument choices, and simply wasn't enjoyable.The music of Spelunky HD is one of the only things I didn't like about that game. I found myself modding it out to be my own custom music packs instead. Fortunately, the game was easy to mod so that I could do that.Spelunky 2's music isn't quite as bad as Spelunky HD's, but its somehow even more forgettable. The soundtrack is really as generic as they come. It sounds like they just went on a site with royalty-free background music and used tracks off of there. Why they don't go back to the original musician and have Spelunky have great music again is beyond me. A lot of us are just modding the OG music back inThe music was a huge letdown, though my expectations were low after Spelunky HD.Truly horrible soundtrack once again. What a shame.Visuals: Spelunky HD looked great. Its artstyle was very charming, it had tons of color, and the environments were nicely detailed.When I first saw Spelunky 2 in the trailers, my initial reaction was "wow that's hideous."This game's artstyle is much more clean, which isn't a bad thing. What is a bad thing, is how incredibly washed out and desaturated the visuals are. When Spelunky HD was so colorful, I don't know why they thought it was a good idea to make this game look as drab as it does. You can find comparisons online of the original game's maps versus this one's and its night and day. The jungle is the easiest example. That was my favorite zone from the first game because I found it very cozy and liked the art. On here, its just a gross washed out puke-green color. I really don't know what they were thinking with the visuals this time around.This game isn't one of those indie games where people are going to praise its visuals.Its actually a bit of an eyesore.Overall: I haven't given Spelunky 2 nearly enough time to actually give a verdict if I like the game or not.Its possible I'll end up loving it and praising it and I fully intend on playing it more.edit: Scratch that, I refunded it. I just didn't think it was good enough for the price. I'd rather play the OG again.I don't think a rehash product warrants its price point and I'd strongly suggest newcomers to buy the first one instead.I'll edit this if I change my mind, but right now the game feels like it rehashes way too much from the original and the awful music and visual art do not help its case at all.Only get this if you absolutely loved the original and want more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't possibly recommend Spelunky 2 for a new player.  It has little to no difficulty curve, immediately ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you straight in the face with a lot of mechanics.  Do yourself a favor, just play Spelunky 1.If you're a returning player, I submit that this still sucks.  I do not find it enjoyable to play, and unless you're looking to punish yourself with a more challenging Spelunky right from the get-go, the fun factor here is questionable.  I don't like looking at the game's drab color palette, the movement speed on some of these enemies is crazy, and if the thirty different mechanics in the first world don't get you, some suited for advanced players, its mini-boss has a good shot to do you in, too.  The rest of the game keeps going in that direction, and if you want to know what something does, experimentation pretty much means death.I played a giga♥♥♥♥ton of Spelunky 1, and it's one of my favorite difficult games of all time.  If I had known that this was actually git-gud masochism and not a balanced, fluid experience like the first game, well, I, uh, still would have bought it.  But I can't say that you should, too.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a good game in there - the design principles that allow you to interact with almost every object using the same rules and the permutations that creates are impressive. But the incredibly punishing game-play and arbitrary deaths actively discourage you from experimenting with these cool systems. Why bother working out what a new item does when doing so might kill you and send you back hours of painstaking gameplay?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still waiting on the multiplayer, but even so, I've had a blast both playing and watching this game. It's frustrating some moments, goofy in others, and everything in-between.Spelunky 2 is a skill-based roguelite platformer that is all about managing resources, tackling deadly situations quickly, and once in awhile, some silly Rube Goldberg death. Core gameplay revolves around exploring randomly generated levels with certain guaranteed setpieces and stage themes. Players learn through experimentation (and maybe through a wiki, because some stuff is pretty obscure) and death. It's a tough game- newbies to the genre will find it hard to make it past the first few stages. There is insta-death nearly everywhere, and there are few things that can completely take that part out. You need to be decisive, deliberate, and deadly.Good luck out there, fellow Spelunkers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is brutal, painful, and makes me very depressed. And yet... I wouldn't trade it for anything.This game is stupidly difficult, if you are going in with no Spelunky experience it won't be easy. Your first runs will probably last less than a minute, maybe a couple minutes if you are lucky. But through each run, you will learn. It'll be the big things first, like how arrow traps work, or how the enemies function. Maybe you'll realize that if you bring that animal you found to the exit you'll gain more hp. After a little bit, you'll reach 1-2. You'll see the shop and realize the importance of money. This cycle will keep going, you making it further and further each and every time, getting better and smarter. Even if you die in a hilariously stupid manner, you'll improve. You could have the perfect run with great items and lose it, and it'll hurt. The pain never fades. Yet with every failure, you learn. You get further. And maybe, just maybe, you'll beat it. And every run, every loss, every heartbreaking failure will make the victory ever sweeter. It'll be a glorious moment in your life, but there's more. Secrets litter the game, with the primary secret being an expansive route leading to a whole new world, and a new, difficult, powerful boss. There is more secrets, and throughout the game you may see snippets of it. You can look it up, but going in blind is a very neat trip of discovery, with each step drawing you in further. This game is packed with content, with multiple different worlds hidden beneath the surface and many more challenges to find. This game is an absolute masterpiece. The controls are incredible with (most) deaths feeling like it was an error on your part. I'll be playing it for a long, long time.TL;DR: I got PTSD from playing this game, 10/10.Seriously though, this game is incredible, get it, you won't regret it, except you will regret it when you lose a great run, but regardless it'll be worth it in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 has, at its core, flawless gameplay, flawless graphics and music. It's one of the few true roguelike platformer, where  your progress is not shown on an XP bar, but in your growing skill as a player and your knowledge of the maps. On paper, it has everything I love in video games. So why don't I recommend it?It's rather simple: it's the ''rng bullcrap''. One of the main feature of the game is also it's downfall. This was an important feature in the first Spelunky, but I found that in Spelunky 2, it's out of control. Though getting killed the second  you enter a room by your NPC ally because he went berserk after seeing an enemy can be "funny" in a slapstick kind of way, it's less so when it's extremely frequent and you find yourself not even being able to get out of the first level without dying and starting over 5 times. You can take shortcuts, but the requirements are often a huge pain in the neck to get. I played nearly 40 hours at the time of this review and I feel like I haven't even progressed that much. It was definetly NOT the case when I played the first one, in which I made great progress and discovered tons of secret in barely 14 hours. When I play a game, I don't like to go on reddit or YouTube to figure out how to play. I like to do that myself. I strongly do not recommend you do this with Spelunky 2. It's clearly a comunity based game, which is not bad in itself. It's a very valid design choice that has been widespread with the rise in popularity of hardcore games. But after finally looking at a few videos, I realized that this game was going to take a long time to learn all it's secret and techniques. I wouldn't mind to do that normally, but the thought of following guides for hours while I get unfairly killed by enemies, traps and allies sounds like something I don't have the patience for anymore. If someone would come to me and say the love the game as it is and that it's a masterpiece, I certainly wouldn't reject their opinion or question their tastes. As I said in the beginning, It's fundamentally a great game. Who knows, I might go back to it one day and maybe it's gonna finally click for me. But even if it does, I would never recommend it to anyone but the most patient, hardcore and (most importantly) dedicated gamer.EDIT: After an additional 15 hours of play, the help of a few guides, I managed to finally beat the game and get to the basic ending. My opinion on Spelunky 2 was only reinforced, as much for the negative aspects as for the positive. If I can end this review a positive note, I must say that despite everything, it did manage to have me go back to it untill I finally reach one of the final boss. It's a testament to the rock solid gameplay that is so good that it keeps you coming back despite the infuriating nature of the RNG. I still wouldn't recommend it to the vast majority of players.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew from hating Spelunky 1 to liking it a lot. it was a game that will take you a lot of time to learn, and to understand that it's hard but it's fair. Spelunky 2 is actually not very different from 1, so do expect to spend quite some time if you want to really get to know the brilliance of the game. What's really good about Spelunky 2 is that it doesn't fix what's not broken. It doesn't add what's not needed just because some believe that a sequel must be bigger, nosier, crazier. Instead, it just continues doing what it is good at, and brings in more of the same, but also different.  It's still balanced, challenging, and fair.Bottom line, it's a well made rogue-like platformer. It rewards patience, dedication, and skill. It's not very fancy, but it has a lot of variations, so it takes time to learn. It's quick, responsive, and very satisfying when you overcome the challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game last October and after playing around 20 hours I got bored and put it down for over a year. Just recently picked it up again out of boredom, and after 3 weeks and 40 hours I finally beat Tiamat.  This game is a treasure if you put in the correct work and effort into it. The joy you will feel when getting deeper than you ever had is great, but that is not to say that you won't want to rip your hair out. I don't think I've ever felt such polar emotions than in this game. 99% of the time I want to throw my computer out the window and that 1% of unadulterated joy is what makes it all worth it. This game is a game that you must be willing to figure out all of its ins and outs to get your true enjoyment. Spelunky will punish you in the most brutal and unforgiving ways, but it just makes beating  it that much more pleasing. There are loads of secrets to discover (unless you're like me and just looked them all up on Youtube) and there is way more content in this game than any regular person has the capacity to get through. In all, this is not a game for everyone, but those who are up for a souls-like cartoony dungeon crawler, then go right ahead. EDIT: Finally beat Hundun after what seems like a year. . I now feel I am truly done with the gam , but I cant recommend the game more to those who are up for a challenge

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it just feels... tedious? There are a ton of items, maps, secrets, and so on, but the actual game itself just isn't engaging to me on a moment-to-moment basis. The actual act of moving, jumping, and navigating doesn't really involve much skill at all - about 90% of the game is just about looking around, taking note of your surroundings, and being careful, but once you do that, executing your moves isn't particularly fun or exciting. And consequently, about 90% of my deaths came because I walked into an arrow trap I didn't notice, a spider dropped from off-screen onto my head, or I broke a pot that had a snake inside, and not because I mistimed a jump or reacted too slowly to a new challenge. Maybe that sort of slow, methodical style is fun for some people, but I personally just found it frustrating and artificially difficult.Really, Spelunky 2 feels more like a "meta-game" about discovering secrets and fooling around with interactions than an actual platformer - it's a little like Fez, if you could also die at any moment because the game is full of contrived threats that are only dangerous because avoiding them is so tedious that you'll end up getting too bored to properly defuse them. I just didn't find it that interesting, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play a Spelunky game, Spelunky 2 is the best place to start. It has the best understanding of how to make its grand systems feel tangible, and it complements that understanding with a host of new content. Conceptually it is awe-inspiring and it manages to deliver on that awe. That's the core of what I need to say about it. I have other things I want to say, but I don't want them to complicate my core message: Spelunky 2 is amazing and well worth experiencing for yourself.It's not very deep lore to point out that Spelunky 2 is actually the third "Spelunky", but I think that's worth stating since it's easy to think of Spelunky 2 as just a sequel. To simplify, Spelunky HD (Spelunky 1) was a commercial release of the already existing Spelunky Classic, iterating on its graphics and controls. Spelunky Classic is available for free online if you want to check that out and get an idea of what Spelunky is without buying in right away, although the games are well worth their sticker prices.My amazement with Spelunky 2 isn't just at the newness and quality of its content. Spelunky HD also felt new and high-quality when I started playing it (about half a decade after its release). Spelunky 2 is the first time I've been so aware of Spelunky as a communal thing. The wiki is still a work in progress, commentary from fans is currently free-flowing, and when online multiplayer is finally added I have at least one friend who I'm going to make play it with me. Spelunky HD has been my favorite game and I imagine that will remain true in a few years, but Spelunky 2 is new to everyone and makes a lot of the things I love about Spelunky even better. It would be a shame to ignore that for the sake of some nostalgia and familiarity with a game that benefits so much from feeling fresh and alive and visceral.

It needed to veer far more confidently into a new direction, forsake the old and welcome the new, but its cowardice in that regard yields a depressingly familiar experience that fails to captivate in the way the first game managed.

If you liked Spelunky 1 you'll love Spelunky 2 (unless you suddenly became uninterested in challenge for some reason)I'm going to be honest it makes me sad to see negative review with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ arguments like "first one runs on my pc but not this one", "wip is smaller", or "doesn't add anything"Here is my response to those people, and to the people wondering if there is truth in it:Gameplay-wise: yes there are some differences with Spelunky 1, the wip feels a bit smaller, but it's hard to know for sure, I'm glad there are differences, it's not the same gameRequirement-wise: yes you need a better specs than spelunky 1 to run spelunky 2, but I mean 7 years between the two, of course requirement went up, it makes total sense. _childDocuments_.review: It's somehow the same, yet entirely different. I marvel at how close Derek Yu paid attention to all the things fans loved and did in the first game, then expanded and changed those things to give you a fresh experience all over again. I'll admit, having played so much of the original I went in a bit cocky thinking it won't take me too long to get a win. But holy ♥♥♥♥ just the first new area kicks my ass even now. All my muscle memory from the first game became immediately useless in the second game. The whip feels different, you run by default, all the little nuances in gameplay feel different requiring me to completely relearn and adapt.It gave me everything I was hoping for in this sequel. New areas, enemies, items, secrets, and endings. I just wanted more of the same but expanded and worked upon. Its delivered this is in spades. Brutal, relentless, and unforgiving, Spelunky 2 has to be the current pinnacle of roguelike games for me. The sense of progression, getting better, and overcoming odds to achieve that ultra feeling of gratification is second to none and only rivaled by something like Dark Souls. Yet this can all happen IN THE SPACE OF 30 MINUTES. Then you cry and do it all over again. I'm over 1000 games in as we speak, nearly 100 hours on the clock (on PS4), and am currently playing almost exclusively with friends on PC due to its new online coop mode.
