_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, Spelunky 2 is a good game, but I honestly don't know if I would recommend it to anyone that owns the first game. If you don't own the first Spelunky, you should definitely pick this game up. It's a fun roguelike exploration game that's super punishing with a  deep set of gameplay mechanics to learn. However, I don't feel like the game offers anything substantially more than the first game, and for 20 I'm really disappointed in the amount of content it offeres. The differences from what I can tell are: 1. One alternate area for each level (past the first level) so three new levels in total, plus some side areas. The areas have new enemies and traps. There are also bosses at the end of each level. 2. 5 or so new items (Powerpack, Telepack, Hoverpack, Bow, Chicken, and some items for the true ending runs) as well as mounts that you can ride on.3. The true ending run has been changed so theres more stuff to do. 4. New character skins, some with their own skins for the whip and rope.The new levels and the changes to the true ending runs are basically the meat of what's been added, but everything else is basically the same game. The old levels are almost indistinguishable from the first game, and I'm disappointed that there are so few additions to the actual gameplay. I wish they would have added more new items that actually change how you play the game, and played around more with level layouts and map designs. Overall, the gameplay is so faithful to the original that none of the new content makes you play the game any differently than from the first game. A lot of the fun I had from the first Spelunky came from mastering all the different aspects of the game, and improving every time. When I played this, there was basically nothing new to learn. It just feels more like a DLC for the original game than a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review because I'm ecstatic that I FINALLY beat the first (and easiest ending) after 50+ freaking hours. I still have a LOOONG way to go if I want to experience the other 2 endings, but man it's so incredibly rewarding seeing myself actually win for once.Yes, yes, I know there are speedrunners that can accomplish the first ending in less than 5 minutes while it took me over 40 minutes, but hey I'm proud of my accomplishment.Now, I am warning you all, this game is HARD and can be very frustrating at times, but that's the joy of it. There are many rogue-like games that as you get better,  the game makes itself easier by rewarding you with better items, better abilities, better characters, etc each run. However, Spelunky 2 has NONE of that. Getting better at the game IS your reward. The reward is PURELY INTRINSIC.Every death is your fault (well most of the time at least). You learn that you play the game better when you take your time and refuse to be greedy. It's an enlightening experience, honestly. This game literally taught me things about myself, if you can believe that. It taught me to be patient, to not be nervous, to not freeze up with adrenaline and instead concentrate, to be observant.Spelunky 2 is the definition of a SKILL-BASED game. You maxed out your health and feel unstoppable? Well, oops your hubris got the best of you and you fell into spikes and got insta-killed anyway. You rushed too quickly and don't notice a bear trap in the ground? You're dead. The tiniest mistake, can ruin your entire "perfect run" and leave you feeling absolutely heartbroken after being so invested in an hour-long run. All you have left to do is stare at the screen in utter shock and yell "CURSE YOU DEREK YUUUU" from your bedroom.But guess what? You take a breath, stop, close the game, and play the next day.  Eventually, your patience and frustration pays off and man it FEELS GOOD. That is part of the experience. Whenever you die, you often learn something new, like a new mechanic, a new trick, or a flaw about yourself. Compared to when I first started playing the game to now, I am insanely proud of how far my skills have gotten. I would often get extremely nervous in new areas at the game, and that would usually lead me to my death until I finally learned to be more confident.The game is all about being in constant competition with yourself to eventually get better.So please, do not get discouraged from the difficulty of this game. Take your time, relax, and try again. There have been days where I would play for hours and wouldn't even make it past 2-1 once. It happens.I promise eventually you will win.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Minor frustration with the level design aside, Spelunky 2 is a triumph. It improves upon the original in ever single way while adding new gameplay elements. If you love roguelikes, you owe it to yourself to buy this game. Be warned though that the game is pretty challenging, but if you are willing to learn Spelunky 2 and how it works you will be rewarded. BEST ASPECTS: GAMEPLAY, MECHANICS, VISUALS, CUTE STORY.WORST ASPECT: OCCASIONAL CHEAP LEVEL DESIGN FINAL VERDICT: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to one of my most-played games of all time. It retains everything that made the original good, and adds lots of new and interesting items, characters and mechanics. The difficulty is generally much higher in Spelunky 2, especially in the first set of levels, the Dwelling. All in all, it's everything I hoped for in a sequel, and then some – I'm already as addicted to this as I was to Spelunky HD. Game of the year for me, easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an amazing game. Difficult, but amazing. Knowing that your progress and how far you go is all due to your skill and any piece of damage or death is almost 100% the players fault. Whether you don't notice something, or you throw an object that ricochets and hits you, or you throw a pot too close and it has an enemy inside. The game is completely fair but sometimes really mean. For example when you barely have any health and the dog is generated in the sub-area or in a wall. So to get the dog... just use a bomb. Resources in this game are meant to be used. Don't just use them all willy-nilly, but use them. In my opinion, Spelunky 2 is an "objectively" perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a rougelike, hard platformer that will kill you, over and over again relentlessly, but thats the beauty of the game itself."What does this trap do?""Whats the best way to steal from the shopkeeper?""Can i abuse this mechanic...?"The game wants you to experiment with pretty much everything, and upon doing so you either just straight up die and get rewarded with knowledge of the game, or end up with rewards to get to get further in your run (or well, you take damage)The gameplay never gets old. The game offers 16 biomes, in which a number of them require you to do specific objectives, in which again encourages expermentation. When doing a run, there are branching paths (as seen in the trailer) so every run feels fresh and infinitely replayable. Oh, and multiplayer is really great for this game lmao, its of those type of games that end up in a chaotic playthrough with your friends sabotaging one another or just dying hilariously. And if youre lonely with no one to play spelunky with, theres a discord server for this game and you can simply find people there to play with youLastly, this game has mods! And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, i love the mods in this game (ill put a link of a yt tutorial video i used on how to do so at the bottom. Youll need it.)So in conclusion, really, really.good game with infinite replayablity and about the price... in my opinion, buy it on sale, i bought mine during the chirstmas sales though, not sure when its gonna have another.(Link for spelunky mods! _childDocuments_.review: This game is designed for you to fail but in the most fun and consumable way possible. If you have patience or temper issues, you'll find this game very challenging. However, if you love precise movement and controls, secrets, fun physics, fantastic art, great music, then this game is a must. Just stay positive, be relaxed, have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is very much an old school sequel to Spelunky, it assumes you've mastered the basics of Spelunking and ups the ante in every way while still keeping very close to the format of the first game. It's unforgiving of mistakes and requires 100% of your attention, and can often feel unfair. However, if you're willing to put the time into it, to learn it's systems and know where to tread lightly then you'll continue to make headway, and in time you'll become accustomed enough to occasionally get to the end. But you also need to be willing to accept that you will die, a lot, often from completely out of the blue, and especially so when victory is just within your reach.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a lot of fun, but doesn't quite recapture the magic of the first to me.There's just too much repetition with the new bosses. The new cave system also tends to result in cheap deaths when you get hit by enemies you can't see on the other side of a door.It's not a bad game, but it has more flaws than the first game and loses the endless replayability, which is a shame since there's so much added content.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: After a decade from the first Spelunky, and after 7 years of waiting (for me personally in hopes of a sequel), it's finally here.I spent countless hours in the first Spelunky, yet I don't think it prepared me for how absolutely PUNK'D I would find myself playing Spelunky 2. This game is harder and more enjoyable than the first, while still retaining the "Innocence" of a simple delving platformer. You'll rage as you make your way through different levels, meet friends who you'll become attached too, and get upset every time you fall onto some spikes or through 2 arrow traps in a row before getting a sense of what happened.Enjoy your deaths and learn from them so you can continue to make the same mistake over and over again.Solid 9.5/10 Rage Compilations
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Developers have impressed me with being able to follow up and surpass the first one with this sequel. The remake of Spelunky 1 was a joy to see of those that fell in love with the pixel version all those years ago. To see what there is on offer in Spelunky 2 just makes me happy. Them doubling down on all the secrets. making one of the more punishing yet extremely enjoyable rouge-lite platformers to ever exist.Highly recommend for fans of the original 100%. for those just coming in, there is no need to play the first one to get what's going on in Spelunky 2. The story is very minimal and Spelunky 2 has a bunch of newness and more stuff going on over the original that it really can stand as it's own thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game has something that not a lot of 2020 games have: fluidity. This game literally does not even know what a 'loading screen' is, the sound design is phenomenal, for example, the drums become louder as you approach the miniboss is 1-4, and it overall feels like a very smooth game; I have had almost no frame rate drops. Can you improve upon perfection? No, but this sequel provides a lot of new mechanics that helps differentiate itself from the first one, while capturing the same charm. Once again, I face palm from every death, but because it's my fault, that makes it ok. Definitely my favourite game from 2020, and will be my game of the year too. Can't wait to play online with my friends over the probable second lockdown!

_childDocuments_.review: You wrecked something I loved.  Tantalizing me with better graphics, more options then throwing the balance out of whack and making it both randomly unfair and too much harder.There's a phrase "the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results" - well the original Spelunky free classic and the Earlier version I could have played like mad till I did all the impossible runs if I'd had nothing better to do - and loved every minute, just relaxing, no biggie.THIS game I do regret wasting any time on - it is just frustrating.  All that art and options to make it nightmarishly difficult even for normal play then plenty of ways to get stuck even when careful and have gear, like floors of nothing but lava and no alternative route or easily trapped in caves without enough bombs.Plus - you removed the "Damsel" with pets, putting a playable character that looks like her but where few will reach. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and I really recommend it, but fair warning it's very hard. And there are many complaints that the game is much harder than the original but I think it's because the is so new and we haven't gotten used to the new mechanics in the game and with time it'll get better... but I think that even after getting used to it, it'll still be appreciated if the difficulty in levels could decrease. With all that said, Spelunky 2 is a great game and even without playing the first one, you can still enjoy it but since this game is about trial and error, those with little patience might find it hard to enjoy this game. And those who came from the first game might find it even harder to adapt to the new one because of being so used to how Spelunky 1 works. Even now, a long time after the game was released, it still holds up really well even when people already learned techniques.

_childDocuments_.review: The secrets and satisfaction you gain from uncovering them in this game is more than enough to last you many years of replaying this game over and over. _childDocuments_.review: I have around 300 hours and all achievements in Spelunky on pc alone. Prior to September 29, 2020, It stood as my favorite game of all time. I like games that reward learning various mechanics and games that have secrets and puzzles you have to dig for. Spelunky was a beautiful mix of the 2. Every time I reached a new milestone (i.e. killing Olmec, killing Yama, getting the no-gold run, getting the eggplant run), I got that feeling of progress, but I wasn't satisfied to the point where I could happily stop playing. That is, until Spelunky 2 dropped. In the dwelling, the differences felt fairly minute: cave drawings on the wall, a turkey here, a horned lizard there, updated arrow trap visuals, etc. It still felt more the same than different though. The same tight controls, meticulous platforming down to the end of each level, and the ridiculous/brutal rube goldburg machine that was dying in the first game. It felt familiar yet fresh. It wasn't until I dug deeper that I saw just how Spelunky 2 set itself apart from it's predecessor. And that's exactly how, it goes oh so much deeper. I won't spoil even a little bit of Spelunky 2 here, as I feel puzzling your way through  the treasure trove of secrets in the game holds a lot of it's charm. I've been blown away by said secrets thus far, and I don't believe I am even close to seeing the entire scope of this game. Derek Yu is an artist and has claimed the silver and gold medal on my podium of favorite games with this franchise alone. Thank you Mr. Yu.TLDR: 10/10 game. Guaranteed to have you scream with joy and agony in the same breath, and still say, "Just one more run"
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 overall is a pretty ok sequel to Spelunky 1. This includes many refinements to the original, such as what feels like slightly more responsive controls, more content and balancing which encourages you to use a larger variety of items than in the first game. However, some of it's additions weren't exactly good ones. While accessing the background of a stage appears to give another layer of depth to a level, it mostly isn't used in interesting way (although does have a few good uses). Also, there are a lot of levels that will always have a certain shop or miniboss area, which does make the game feel repetitive with how frequent these are. Overall, I feel like the charm of random level feelings from the original has been forgotten in this game, with the strength of the procedural generation of the levels being downplayed significantly in this sequel.  Another thing to note is that I would say that the music definitely does not live up to that of the first game, with many levels only having one track that plays rather than 3, making the level themes much more repetitive.Even though Spelunky 2 has more in terms of content than it's predecessor, I would recommend that you play the first game before this one. Otherwise, most things that made spelunky great are still here, while the increase in difficulty should be fun to tackle for more veteran players.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing is more fun than dying over and over again. If it isn't the Moles that keep spawning out of no where to kill you then its the incredible hit stun that locks you place that allows enemies to keep on killing you. Whats that? You made it to Olmec? Congratulations, you now get to die because his bombs turn into heat seeking missiles and automatically stun you and kill you in one hit even if you're across the map. I get you're supposed to die, but when most deaths are because of an enemy hitting you and an arrow trap hits you then a snake bits you, it gets kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Wait for better patches before buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an incredibly difficult game, much more difficult than its predecessor Spelunky HD. The game will make you rage, a lot, for hours. However, this game is still incredibly fun. With lots of content you'll probably never get to see!The visuals, levels, enemies, bosses, and almost everything else is an incredible improvement over Spelunky HD, apart from a few things.That mainly being the music, the music is still very good and is actually dynamic now which is great. There are many amazing tracks you will likely love... however, they all fall short when compared to Spelunky HD. This is likely because that game didn't need to focus on dynamic music and only needed to focus on happy jingles to nod along too.Another criticism about the game actually stems from 2 new features, that being the back layers and fluid physics. The back layers are a very interesting concept that just isn't used very effectively, with there not being much content or anything interesting to explore there. The other one is fluid physics, while being a great concept, the lava causes more annoyances that great times, blocking level paths and making the drill in volcano slightly more RNG heavy as well as making the game significantly more computer intensive.Despite this criticism, the game is still amazing and one I heavily implore you to try. While it doesn't have the exact same feel as Spelunky HD you will still have an incredibly, painfully fun time! (Especially, if you enjoyed Spelunky HD.)The new areas are great to venture through, and you can finally play with your friends online if you can manage the input delay. I have completed all achievements and it took me 61.9 hours, the achievements are varied and great and I am almost ready to hang up mining helmet, however I still crave to do one more challenge, that being the endless expanse of pain after those 22 levels of turmoil. You should play the game to understand what I mean, because there is a greater challenge hidden away from the achievements here, one you will likely never complete...I give this game a solid 9/10 - great gameplay, difficulty and challenges with good but not excellent music. The game is slightly more RNG dependent than the previous game, but this still leaves room for a lot of fun.Well done to Derek Yu! And remember always to "ransack those shopkeeper's pockets" while Kali watches!

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun but here are a few caveats that imo are game ruining. Firstly, the mole enemies are ridiculous, annoying, and unfair. So many runs would end because some random mole enemy would jump onto the screen from above or to the side of you without much or any warning and my character would take damage, it feels very broken. It isn't a fun game mechanic to play around and it encourages the player to have a slow approach. Second, the tile in the forest biome that kills you instantly looks almost identical to a regular tile. If it kills you instantly regardless of your health, surely there can be something to differentiate it from other tiles.Lastly, when you take any damage, you are unable to move. You're still able to take damage though, so this leads to a succession of hits by one enemy, or you just being juggled by enemies and there's nothing you can do about it.It is hard for me to be invested in each run when you can die so undeservedly and it makes me reluctant to play, otherwise the game is really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Sick of defending this disappointment, horrid design changes really ruin this game.Awful new mechanics (whipping from ledges, critters cant be used to activate traps anymore so whats the point of being able to pick them up)Dreadful balancing (first stage is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess, the patch helped but its still the least enjoyable part of the game because you will take damage to something really stupid and decide to just restart because you took damage so early in to the game its just better off having a fresh start with better RNG)Lackluster music selection (its pretty barren)Garbage stage generation (unlike the previous game there are many times you will have a stage generated where you are forced to use resources or take damage to progress, previous game was very convenient and this almost never happened especially falling from long heights but also being able to use critters to activate traps, oh and not to mention the damsel generating in areas where you are forced to use a bomb being more than half of the time they spawn now, the first area is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, way too much crap going on and virtually nobody enjoys it)Honestly feels hard to believe the same person made the previous one, this game just feels like some sort of fanmade mod. its playable, it can be fun but dear lord its just infuriating and can really ♥♥♥♥ with you if you were a fan of Spelunky HD, its not for every fan of the original, its probably worth picking up but don't surprised to find that its a disappointment and the only thing to enjoy is that there is more content.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that Spelunky/Spelunky HD basically wrote the book on the modern rouge-like and Spelunky 2 certainly follows in its footsteps, however i feel it has a few stumbles along its path. To be fair, the few issues i have are drops in the bucket compared to what the game does well, but once noticed they never quite go away. One annoyance is the world generation, especially for the first area, the Dwelling. World generation in spelunky works on a sort of grid system, with hand created "rooms" being strung together randomly (with a few failsafes to ensure the exit is always reachable), and the ones for Dwelling often result in boring and samey levels with pointless dead ends, sometimes having most of the level not even accessible unless you use one of your precious bombs. Even then there's often nothing worth searching for. This issue is somewhat lessened in other areas, but still very much present, and if your hunting for secrets in a few areas, being constantly cut off from what your looking for and needing a bomb or item to get there is tedious.Another is the ever known risk of getting "spelunkyed". Often Spelunky 2 is rough but fair, rewarding quick thinking and attention, but sometimes it will place you into true no-win situations due to no fault of your own, or a single slip up will send your battered body flying into multiple enemies and traps then finally into a boiling pool of lava, all with no chance of recovery. In these instance the most you can do is try to marvel at how horribly your life was just ended and try again, but if your luck is bad and the game is placing enemies and traps with no remorse it can get annoying.One of my last issues involves the new "Background Caves" and the fluid dynamics, but is a bit of a nitpick. The fluid dynamics is mostly just interesting, but with lava you can sometimes end up screwed either by your own actions, or random things just happening around you (this ties in to the concept of getting spelunkyed). Meanwhile the background caves are just sort of... there. often they have nothing of interest, the small ones often having nothing but a bat or two, while the large ones MAY have a special shop. However, the shops include a caveman run shop who sells rocks and skulls more often then not, and while the other shop you can run into often has a few choice items for grabs the actual chances of FINDING the entrance to the back caves is seemingly totally luck based (I have seen nothing online about there being ANY way to reliably find the things if they exit past getting a bit lucky with an exposed entrance, if a way exists i dont know it)I front-loaded this review with the things that annoyed me, but i think my hours played can attest to what i think of the game overall. If you think you reach the skill floor for this game (I recommend starting out not really caring too much about finding secrets or playing perfect, just start building your skills to see if you can git gud) and are interested in this type of game, I 100% endorse this one and recommend you buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is an experience inferior in every way to its predecessor. Just play Spelunky 1; unless you are the sort of challenge-addict who does eggplant runs for fun, Spelunky 2 adds nothing of value for you.Spelunky 1 was charming for the minimalism of its design and the extremism of its gameplay. The experience of being struck from an arrow-trap at the far edge of the screen and sent flying into a row of run-ending spikes was novel at the time; the consequences of errors were severe and would heavily punish careless play, but nearly any foreseen and understood threat could be avoided with only moderate platforming ability. The combination of those two traits was important: if you got stunned and sent flying, the wacky exaggerated physics meant that the consequences could range from slightly-damaging to fatal, but threats were sufficiently noticeable and telegraphed that this result was generally due to a significant and understandable misplay on the player's part, or the punishment for a 'greedy' maneuver. This also meant that the game could get away with various little clumsinesses; because the game's challenges were only moderately mechanically demanding, it didn't matter so much that some parts of the execution were awkward.  Spelunky 2 treats the game of Spelunky as though it needs no basic improvements or updates, and only needs increased difficulty. Much content is shamelessly unchanged; for someone expecting the new game to be a *new game*, navigating the same old caves with the same old enemies and even collecting the same old Udjat Eye is a disillusioning experience. As for what content is new, it uniformly departs from the old design philosophy of predictability. New enemies move more chaotically, are harder to hit, have larger and less-avoidable methods of attack, inflict crippling and difficult to remove new status-effects. Additionally, they are more-densely packed into less-open spaces, multiplying the probability that any misstep results in a wacky chain-reaction of unpreventable fatal damage, especially given that old boons like the jetpack now often become explosive liabilities instead. The final region of the game's normal route embodies this chaotic premise wholeheartedly; a bullet-hell landscape of perpetually-circling fireballs not only turns normal enemies and their corpses into high-speed projectiles fully capable of stunlocking and juggling away whatever amount of health the player has managed to accumulate, but will make cheerful pinball-game sound-effects on each impact to emphasize the whimsical unpredictability of having an exploding UFO chucked at you from offscreen. In Spelunky 1, physics-driven instant death was always a possibility, but even near the end, it was the norm for most hazards to just deal a reasonably proportionate amount of damage and then allow you to act again. In many of Spelunky 2's areas, suffering a hit and 'just' taking damage cannot really be expected.Making matters worse, the game's chaotic new portfolio of threats is not matched by any improvements in controllability. The slightest variation in D-pad input will still arrest the player's movement on ledges or ladders they had no intention of stopping against or flipping over; the climbing glove in particular frequently spells death in the game's chaotic later areas, introducing deadly undesired pauses into the necessarily-rapid navigation of constantly crushing elevators and eternally-milling fireballs, because the game still insists upon a minimalist control scheme for increasingly demanding platforming challenges; overloading the 'move left or right' control with 'also cling to the wall' just doesn't cut it when you have to sprint through a series of narrow, twisting, moving horizontal-and-vertical passages. Sometimes this insistence on control-minimalism makes very basic actions impossible; suppose an item the player wishes to pick up is located on a 1-tile-wide platform which can be descended through, but there is a rope passing through the platform. The player *cannot* pick up the item, because they cannot crouch on the platform to do so, because the crouch-input navigates the rope instead. But Spelunky 2 wears these clumsinesses with pride; mechanical awkwardness is a proud feature with a long history, not a bug to correct. While not a control scheme issue, this proud embrace of pointless problems is best exemplified by the Hired Hand. 'Rescuing' one of these 'allied' NPCs and attempting to actually traverse the dungeon with their 'help' invariably means being killed shortly thereafter by their wild, reckless attacking and throwing of objects; one learns just to not bother rescuing them, or if they are accidentally released, to simply kill them before moving on rather than to suffer their 'help'. No gameplay function is served by having a 'benefit' that is actually a strict liability, but that's just what kind of punitive-for-its-own-sake gameplay Spelunky 2 thinks it's supposed to be about. The first Spelunky was fun. This one just feels tedious. There's little joy, after having one run end due to some offscreen lava-spewing explosion, in setting off again to discover what Kaizo-style configuration of hazards will be thrown together this time. In the first game, losses felt mostly deserved and victory felt achievable with attentiveness and a *little* luck; even the alternate Hell route was enjoyable enough to both discover and to conquer without outside spoilers. In this one it's hard enough to put up with the normal game, much less embrace the even-more-random conditions dictating whether following an alternate route is feasible on a given run. So if you're a punishment-craving veteran of unforgiving precision platformers who doesn't mind intentionally-awkward controls in a game willing to punish anything less than a perfect run, go for it. Otherwise, there are other better games for sale.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've thought about this a while, the review and all, and here's my heavily summarised sentence; I love this game, but I wouldn't recommend it unless you're either a content creator, or have friends to play with; though, The sole exception to this is if you've completed Spelunky 1 and want more. *Spoiler warning Below!* To Summarise: The Good-  There's a lot to do in this game, it's got a really good amount of secrets and discovery; it captures the theme of adventure incredibly well. - The animations are very smooth and the art is great, a clear and concise visual upgrade from the previous title and a game that's almost always nice on the eyes- The gameplay is still really enjoyable most of the time, with good controls and satisfying movement- The Multiplayer is simply incredible, and easily the best part of the game; It really is better with friends, The deaths become funny and the run isn't immediately over when one person makes a mistake. not to mention, outside of other players' movement, lag is nonexistant. It's really incredible how Mossmouth did it.The Bad - Dwellings is Incredibly, violently repetitive and if you do not have the drive or skill to constantly get past it, You won't enjoy the game. - In spelunky 1, most deaths were fair, and the few Rube's Machines to send you to 1-1 were at least, rare enough to be funny, but in spelunky 2 I often find myself not even reacting when one kills me.- Neo Babylon has the most, cheap and out of control deaths of any area in spelunky history with it's combination of UFOs, Reflecting shields and crushing Elevators. It's not fun; no sane person is arguing that a UFO going mach 9 to teleport you to 1-1 is Well designed and fair - While Discovering the secrets is great, Actually doing them is a different story. Spelunky 2 feels as if the Udjat eye spawns in resource-demanding locations so much more than 1, and Olmec's 3 phases still drag on way too long; for something essential to progression - I lose brain cells everytime a Shopkeeper outpost spawns with a ghost jar in it. Seriously; Why is that even possible, they always shoot it and it summons the ghost and forces you to speedrun an area with shopkeepers in it - I still don't understand why shops don't have a door, or some form of, Entry protection; Firemen, Lizards and Dart Traps can often spawn in front of shops, and if that shop has a bomb bag in it then it simply ceases to exist when the shopkeeper channels their Inner Mr. Sir, and uses a double barrel shotgun to take out a lizard. Seriously, the only reason I can assume this exists is because it generates those "Family Guy Funny Moments" compilations where a lizard rolls into a shop and proceeds to blow up the entire shop because of a powerpack and oneshot the player inside of it. It's funny the first 5 or 6 times but, it gets old fast- The Music, now, don't get me wrong, the Music is Incredible, an OST worth buying, however; each area has one track, unlike 1 where each level has 3. this contributes to the problem I mentioned above, where the dwellings are repetitive, as the music is always, Always identical. Overall, I can't recommend the game unless you have friends or an audience. A lot of the downsides are negated by that; The violently repetitive nature of it, the unfair deaths that stop being funny after a while, etc etc. It's a good game, but, Get spelunky 1 instead, and *then*, only then, if you really desire more, get spelunky 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a overall fantastic game. It builds a lot after the already amazing game and adds or refines an insane amount of content. The game allows you to play in varying ways depending not only on what you want to achieve (as in score, time, distance), but also with your skill level. Levels are filled with various tasks that you can complete, that aren't directly instructed, but optional if you see them or wish to complete them. You can skip collecting certain items that are used for progression in the late game, items to temporarily help you, or items to permanently give you a boost. Spelunky 2 can be very difficult due to the need to manage your resources and evaluate risks. The game can be brutally difficult and does have a large learning curb because of this. The only form of permanent progress is shorcuts to areas farther in the game which do not allow you to go for hard endings or special endings. What you do gain from deaths and runs is experience on how the world that you are playing in functions, and how to evade or predict certain dangers.tldr: Overall, Spelunky 2 is an extremely fun and challenging game that allows you to play in many different ways. It's procedurally generated and you never play the same game twice. It's well rounded and allows you to learn and improve at the game. Online multiplayer is extremely fun w/ friends and hopefully deathmatch will be released soon

_childDocuments_.review: Unpopular opinion and I recognize that. The game is amazing. When you watch someone else play it. This allows you to get hooked on the game so that when things get difficult, grindy, or "rage quitty", you still want to see things through to the end. I recognize this is not a typical platformer and the intention is you replay it from the beginning.. A LOT. Yet, this game is terribly difficult right out of the gate to the point of being just un-fun.  Having almost logged 10 hours on this game and still only having been to level 2-1 less than what i can count on 2 hands, sucks the fun out of this game completely and takes what should be a relaxing gaming experience and makes it a horrendously frustrating, hypertension inducing nightmare. Maybe I'm not the target audience, but come on bruh. make it a little easier to get to level 2-1. AND FIX THE WHIP HIT-BOX, IT'S ATROCIOUS.Look man i'm pissed because I'm an adult and i don't have enough hours in my week to build up the experience to actually be good at this game. This ain't no mmorpg. I should have to play for 30 + hours to make any damn progress.My advice. Unless you are the Buddah or Ghandi and have achieved eternal zen, don't buy this game, save yourself the coronary.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, but don't play this if you're expecting a typical rogue-like.This game demands a ton of attention from the player, as practically anything can end your run.The strongest point of the game is its unique learning curve: there's so many interactions and techniques that can change the way you play, and learning all of them feels like you're really mastering the game. It's a feeling you'll find in very few non-competitive games. (unless you're a speedrunner, that is.)The sense of progression, however, isn't going to be everyone's cup of tea. Newer players (especially those new to the series as a whole,) will often find themselves dying repeatedly until they've gained their bearings, which can be an incredible mental-hurdle to overcome. I know that it's cliche at this point, but I'd actually compare this 'difficulty'/'learning'-curve to that of Dark Souls (provided you didn't power-level and cheese everything lololol) as, the majority of the challenge can be erased with clever planning, mechanical-familiarity, and skilled execution.Overall though, playing this game is an experience you'll find almost nowhere else. Especially not with the quality that these games provide. I highly recommend this game, so long as you're masochistic enough to survive the learning curve.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 feels like a try-hard version of the first game, where too many mechanics/difficulty were inflated for the sake of it. Hit rules are inconsistent (you get hit multiple times in a row and always take damage even if stunned, but enemies get invincibility frames after one hit). The first game was also like this but Spelunky 2 ups the ante to ridiculous levels by increasing enemy spawning to uncontrolable levels.Enemies like the mole or the armadillo can basically stunlock you to death regardless of your heath points. I have had armadillos kill me at 10HP because they stunlock me with roll attacks or launch me from one side of the level to the other onto spikes due to the poor physics.I feel the random generation of the levels themselves has also gotten worse. level paths are often blocked by enemy placements that make it impossible to progress without taking damage or outright block the way forward unless you can use bombs or ropes, which often means you do not start with enough resources.All of these are problems that the first game already had but which were made worse in this sequel. The path forward got harder but the player gets no rewards or incentive. If this works for you, great. I does not work for me.It feels like I paid good money for a poorly balanced difficulty mod.

_childDocuments_.review: spelunky 2     :   I was excited to see a new spelunky 2 and bought it at full price!  it's on the moon apparently?  There are new elements and things you've seen before, if you played the first.  I enjoy the spelunky world but it is not for the faint of heart or sensitive souls who just want to have a nice gaming experience because it is very difficult, and often one wrong move will set off a chain of events leading to death.  I don't have a controller which makes it more difficult.    There's a lot to look at.  I enjoy the lil dun beetles and piles of bones that you can whip.   Plus now there is a second dimension to the map, where you can go behind the scenes in a way, or in lil holes to a second, darker area.  I love the lil ghost jar you need to carry around, not wanting to wake the ghost.  It does feel like more of the same, which is a good thing, in lots of ways.  In other ways it feels like an unfinished game, in the sense that there is only this extremly difficult speed run mode, when i want a more chill mining experience.  The AI is interesting but pretty dumb, it's trying to jump on the plants that eat you in one bit, or jump in lava that annoy me.  The insta deaths are pretty annoying, and there are times when its hard to wake up in time to prevent the same enemy from repeatedly getting me till death.   I don't want to be a complainer but it's way to hard for me.  Maybe it's better in co-op, probably more fun.  Most things are insta death anyway, so i feel like im wasting my time with the dogs and turkeys.  I do like the changes but it's still basically impossible to beat this game and that is why i find it... not as fun as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: It handles like it's predecessor with some minor hitbox changes to enemies and the whip. The art style has been changed up a bit to be a bit more crisp. Controls feel smooth and responsive.I won't claim to be the best at the game but, this game wants to kill you with haste. It has a tendency of wanting to stunlock and kill you for a simple mistake. For certain hits, you stay down for a while and get knocked back a fair bit, which can trigger enemies that remove the remaining HP within seconds. There are also certain scenarios where the level generator decides to force you to use a bomb or force you to take damage.I'd still recommend it, just not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is both magnificent and the worst imaginable gathering of unfortunate events that are 100% out of your control.Spelunky 1 was a breeze compared to this clustertruck of weird, BS moments where no matter what you do you will get stabbed in the shins by 3 moles in a 1 tile-high corridor outside of a door. There is no way to see it coming, there is no way to dodge it, and you will get hit at least once. And yeah, sometimes in Spelunky one, you enter a new level, and something happened, and the shopkeeper is mad, or you die instantly. Sure. it happens.But in SP2, EVEN if the shopkeeper doesn't get mad at you for unrelated accidents (most of them anyway), and EVEN if there are more ways to get HP now, guess what? Doesn't matter. because 50% of your runs are ruined from the start. Hell, one time I restarted, and a skeleton spawned right next to me. Sure, I should have spammed the whip right away like a pro speedrunner, but also HOW ABOUT TUNING IT DOWN ON THE 40 ENEMIES ON FIRST LEVEL?I don't mind Dying. Dying is fun. Dredmor taught me that, and Dredmor killed me a thousand times more than this game ever will (probably) but at least in Dredmor, 95% of the time it's my fault. This is not difficulty. This is cheap.  It's engineered to kill you. It will kill you. and half the time, you won't even know what hit you.My pet peeves (in no specific orders)-Moles being invincible when they emerge and being able to move INSTANTLY after said invincibility phase.-Moles emerging under you in a 1 tile high corridor-Stages with many moles. By that I mean 3-4-Lizards hitting you 3-4-5-6-7 times in a row (see 1-tile high corridors where you come out of a door for additional rage)-Cavemans tripping over something. That's fun. The following 0.8 seconds stun phase right after that is not fun at all. make it longer. 2 seconds is all I ask. but no.-having 5 ragdolls in one spot, and having anything happen to it with you being close to it.-Having the pet behind a 4-wide wall, in a corner way up there-Having the key behind a 4-wide wall, in a corner way up there-Having the ghost jar behind a 4-wide wall, in a corner up there (you get it)-Having any important area completely isolated by the level, inaccessible behing walls, usually by a shop as well.-Having the drill over a shop, or any other important areas. -5 enemies behind a door, literally 2 feet away from you. -Any of these scenarios, but with a ghost jar.-Ghost jar getting broken when you enter a stage (how about making the jar indestructible the first 5 seconds? I mean come on man!)Any of these (and there are a tons more trust me) will usually put you in a horrible spot, or straight out ruin your run or kill you. And there is NOTHING you can do about it. I don't mind you cranking the difficulty to 11 out of 5, that is perfectly acceptable, I eat Dante Must Die runs for snacks, but just like there shouldn't be unavoidable instant hits in beat em alls or fighting games, there shouldn't be situations that are 100% out of your control THIS OFTEN. having 1/10 of my runs ruined is understandable in Spelunky. Not half of them. Some of these shouldn't be impossible to fix as well.The balance issues by itself is also wonky. In the first 4 levels, there are snakes, bats, scorpions sometimes. these are understandable threats. The scorpion poisons you now (the poison status effect shouldn't do what it does IMO, but whatever) but okay, that's fair somewhat. Then you have cavemans, moles and lizards. In order:-Cavemans: slow, dumb, can't jump or stop running once it does. Abides with the rules of the game and is understandable. Has 3 HP.-Moles: Fast, digs in dirt. Unpreditable, incoherent, an absolute threat. invincible when emerging from said dirt, difficult to deal with. Also has 3 HP.-Lizards. Attacks on sight. Cannot be stopped once it goes, except by stronger weapon or throws object. Will murder you if in a 1 tile-high corridor because you can't stop it with your whip. ALSO 3 HP!so when the game spawns 4 cavemans in your face, at least you can stop them with your basic attack or do something about it. If 4 moles spawn in your face you might as well expect to trade 3 HP to get away or fight them, depending if the game boned you on level generation as well. Because sometimes it does, thank you for your money. At the very least, it makes for some excellent entertainment watching. Waving at you Vinny Vinesauce Man! Watching you turn into a duck out of frustration in spelunky is always the best times. For us, sorry for you.I could rant for ages. So should you get the game? Niuhg. Like I said it's awesome, but it makes me bitter every single times I boot it up. I have fun, but I feel worse about it. Every streaming session I did of it so far has been pain, no exception. So despite the high praise the game gets (and I really understand it and agree with it), let this post and review be a warning for you all. Because this game is unfair. it is infuriating. it is ABSOLUTELY BRUTAL!!!! I CANNOT recommend it as I would other difficult games, because it is an unfair mess of garbage scenarios that will test even the most hardcore of Spelunky veterans, except the kids who eat raw coffee beans for breakfast. However, if you read all of this, and the pain you imagine excites you, then by all means... This game is pretty dope.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the first one a lot, my review is gonna sound unfair at times but bear in mind despite all the cons I'm going about, I'm giving it a positive review since the game is obviously good and a great purchase choice, especially on sale.Spelunky 2 builds up on all the hard time you had before, making it incredibly hard to go through the game. It's still fun and addictive as hell, bringing a lot to discover and fresh ideas. Also great artwork and animation. And fantastic gameplay. Seriously the game's really good, let me just vent out a little:Where the problems start, at least for me: the game is somewhat obtuse every now and then. Some sections break the momentum and you're in the middle of something that's not that fun at all, like when the elevator goes through a lava pool, or those infuriating moles don't make up their minds, or having to search for the correct statue, and so on. The number of traps, plus the two ghosts mechanics, get in the way of wanting to search an area better. I get it's part of the difficulty, but it's still something that keeps someone from exploring the game, which I would debate is a good idea. And still the game finds other ways to punish you, like losing Qilin to the ceiling lasers and ruining your run.Spelunky 2, for me, unfortunately ended up being more frustrating than fun. If you're just playing for the regular ending and not touching it again, then I'd say the game is on point in terms of difficulty and punishment. It's said every death in Spelunky 1 is by your own fault. I'm not so sure about that, but that's definitely not the case here. The game will be upfront unfair now, expect that, and try to laugh in the process. A great game to play with some friends watching your pain.

_childDocuments_.review: I triple dipped this game on PS4, Switch, and now Steam. I don't like platformers much but this game has very crisp controls and deep mechanics. It's not like Hollow Knight but I would put it on the same tier of platformers with an exceptional game feel.The world design of Spelunky 2 is so neat, drawing from various cultures. The game also has a souls-like system for side quests. Quests are cryptic, the quest NPCs will just show up in unexpected spots as you dive deeper into the caves, and all NPCs can be killed. The implied connections between the various characters are delightful as well.The game is hard as dirt, truly unrelenting, but generally fair (except for the Low Scorer achievement). There is no meta progression to make the game easier like you'd find in other roguelites. And as a general rule the more powerful or useful an item is the more dangerous it can be when used by inexperienced players. The teleporter lets you bypass large sections of levels but also allows you to teleport yourself into a wall, resulting in instant death. The jetpack lets you fly over dangerous obstacles and avoid using ropes to ascend but it also has a tendency to explode when exposed to fire or if punctured. Your only hope of surviving the brutal cycle of death and rebirth in the caves are your wits and experience accumulated over hundreds of failures.Good luck, and take care of your mental. You'll need both for the journey ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, I really do. I had some fun with it but there are some serious level design and gameplay issues, some of which ported from the 1st game, some new, some not in the 1st game.Here's is the list of BS:#1 : Shopkeeps get pissed when a trap or enemy hits them or damages their shop. Derek, make them pissed but not at you!#2 : Arrow traps on ground-level that appear from off-screen horizontally and shoot you but you couldn't see them in time. This is a level design flaw. Make it so they're always positioned in visible range.#3 : Enemies covering exits or too close to entrances. #4 : Whipping while grabbing a ledge sends you flying. Da ♥♥♥? Remove this entirely please. When on ledge it should do nothing when pressing whip button.#5 : Gently dropping a bomb next to a dead turkey to cook it sends it flying to kingdom come.#6 : Moles dropping from ceiling is mostly unpredictable and frustrating. Make moles less dumb please. They should dig out up & sideways only. There's enough ♥♥♥♥ to deal with without having to check ceilings all the time.#7 : Why in god's name do jetpacks explode now? When you wear them you're one hit from being BBQ. Please no. Just NO. AT LEAST, AT THE VERY LEAST make them not explode instantly when you get hit.#8 : Poison is a ♥♥♥♥♥. It will keep ticking your health away until you get a doggy kiss. Considering how bloody hard it is to get one in most levels, and the time it takes, getting poisoned generally means your run is over. Make poison expire after 3 hearts so it's less OP please.There are some other issues too but these are the essential deal-breakers for me. They are all things that I think Derek and his team could fix in an update and I sincerely believe doing so would make the experience more enjoyable for everyone, while still being a very punishing game. It would at least feel less unfair.As it stands though, I cannot recommend it in it's current state unless you are masochistic.I will keep trying to beat it, though I fear I may send my monitor flying in anguish and rage.

_childDocuments_.review: I do NOT RECOMMEND this game and here is why:1) Unlike Spelunky 1, this one has a lot more random factors that you have no control of and those could ruin your runs in an instant(UFOs in the ice caves, dumb Olmites in the Neo Babylon, traps in Neo Babylon, etc). You can just spawn at the entrance of the level, and all ish goes bananas without you even interacting with anyone/anything.2) Levels became more complex - it feels like a true challenge to survive 1st 4 levels, let alone Jungle or Volcana. Game only becomes harder and harder as you go deeper - and not in a good(pleasant) way like it was in Spelunky 1. Enemies overwhelm you in some areas - and if you don't have any way to work your way around(or through them) - you are screwed and it's a 'Restart'.. In some cases levels are built in a way that you will most certainly die if you don't have at least 1 rope or 1 bomb,3) You have to *know* certain aspects of the game in order not to screw it up(and end it at the Tiamat's Throne) - like for example not to blow extra blocks near the Waddler or not anger Tun(though mobs and level design can do that for you). To reach the Sunken City, you have to be NOT ONLY skilled like hell but also very-very-*VERY* lucky.. And the Cosmic Ocean - oh boy.. If you are up for some serious BDSM action and 2-3 hours of your life wasted in blood, sweat and tears - I tip my hat to you..This game was created for nerds - not for people who enjoy casual(classic) spelunking like in the 1st game. I tried to love this game - I really did, but all I got was only negative emotions as a result of each *screwed* walk-through. And they don't go away that easily.If you really want to play this game - be warned: IT DOES NOT FORGIVE ANY MISTAKES and it will most probably make you feel miserable at some point.. I would advice buying the 1st game instead - I guarantee that you will enjoy it more than this insanity stimulator.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand, and appreciate what the game is about.  It's very challenging, and was made to be challenging which harkens back to the old school 8-bit/16-bit games.  However, the difficulty in some of those games were due to technical limitations, poor design choices, port from an arcade game trying to screw you out of quarters, or other issues.I am  like these so please be aware of that when seeing my recommendation and review.  In terms of positives and why I got this game?  Simple!  For the co-op play.  I found the co-op with friends to be .  Going through the challenges and running around was a blast!  Graphically this games is great.  The art style is easy on the eye, and overall very smooth on my increasingly aging computer.  I am of the belief games with art style such as Spelunky 2 will age better than those who go for realism.  Especially since technology is so fast and realism dates itself quickly. What I distinctly didn't like about the game  was the fact that once you lost all your lives you start at the .  We'd reach level 2-1, lose all our lives, and start at level 1-1 all over again.  At first it's funny but, after the 10th time playing with 2 other people of various skill level  it quickly loses its appeal.  The 8-bit era had memory issues hence why progress couldn't be saved in some games.  We don't have those issues today for games. So not being able to save my progress showed how little patience I had.Another issue?  One hit deaths or worst - fall deaths on blind corners / platforms.  The stages were procedurally generated so this meant you can die in the most tragic, unlucky way.Like I said just not my kind of game.+ Fantastic artwork, and style+ Co-op mode+ Simple gameplay mechanics and controls- One hit deaths, no continues, and no saving progress- Frustrating gameplay (which many may see as a positive)- Very difficult- Having start all over again once you lose all your lives Not a fan of this frustrating, "git gud" type of game 4 /10

_childDocuments_.review: carries with it much the same spirit of its prequel, being a 2D platformer with roguelike elements. In comparison, it comes with a more expansive world and more secrets. The baseline difficult exploring platforming remains. There are perhaps a bit more predictable spawning of certain items/creatures on certain levels with the way the game is set up, but there's enough variety and sudden death opportunities to always keep the players on their toes. Once again, expect to get frustrated from all kinds of different mechanisms, just so that you can start over again with more knowledge about the game.At baseline, it's a 2D side-scrolling platformer where your goal is to progress from level to level --entrance to exit, and deal with the enemies along the way. You will explore different biomes and deal with a variety of enemies, each with predictable patterns of movement and reaction to you. You will run, jump, whip or throw climbing ropes or bombs, both limited in supply. You will come across money that you can use at shops for additional gear, or you can steal or kill shopkeepers for them if you truly want to not play by the rules. At the end of the day, you will die many times trying to make it to the end, and occasionally you might just succeed.The game is hard, because of the way it's set up. While you can unlock some shortcuts through playing and fulfilling certain requirements, many players will start from the beginning and work their way through each time. Every time you turn the corner, you could face an unexpected event that completely destroys your run, and you will have to start over. Even using shortcuts you will face certain variety in level generation to make the individual levels feel different.There are also more ways to die in this second  game because of a lot more aggressive enemies, more traps, more potential explosions, etc. Derek Yu heard all of our complaints about how long it took to spawn the ghost and how slow its movements were. Instead, now the ghost (plus other enemies) are on steroids, coming after your very life.There are more bosses in this game as well, that's probably why the game sometimes feels a bit more predictable. This doesn't make it more easy, you can just be sure to expect certain things to always show up in specific locations. I remember playing through the first game and always thinking that it was odd to only have one boss, unless you took the string of secrets through various pathways in order to get to Hell. Of course there are still secrets and pathways to string together in  but there are a lot more branching pathways to make life interesting.Anyway, I have one win under my belt so far, after 77+ hours, and who knows when I will get my next. I have done almost all of the exploring on my own, because that discovery and trying to piece things together has been incredibly fun. Having played the first game a lot, I was definitely keeping an eye out trying to discover any potential secrets. I found some, but not enough. The biggest draw for a lot of people to this game was the promise of online multiplayer. This is not yet available, but we are all hopeful that it will be soon. In the meantime, there's been a lot of tweaks here and there, so it's been interesting to see the game get some major and minor changes during its infancy based on player critique.What stood out for me about  was its platforming, with such responsive controls, predictable movements, and precise actions, everything felt so right. With  that feel has remained the same. There have been other tweaks to the smaller details that people will noticed between the two but they both work well and are responsive in their own ways. Once you get used to the control scheme and become comfortable with expected movements and outcomes, you will find that everything feels to be more or less within your control--a small percentage of the time. That feeling is good and brings me back to these games for repetitive playing, even though I know I will likely fail.2D platforming with roguelike elements.Very responsive, some people prefer keyboard, others prefer controller. You definitely want to experiment with both to see which one works better for yourself. I personally use a controller.More child-friendly artwork compared to the first, deceptively so. I do not think this game is easier, in fact, I think it's more difficult. Animations are really awesome.Music is quite good, though not quite as magical as the OST from the first game. Sound effects are mostly okay. (I personally think that there was one major change in one important hidden-pathway sound effect that got almost muted and hinders my own game a bit.)For those who want a hardcore 2D platforming experience and every run being different. For those who don't mind dying repeatedly in order to learn the game's mechanics in order to have a better chance at further progression.Absolutely worth the price. made a lot of people wait, and it was worth it. It's such an enjoyable experience, and Derek Yu delivered on the promise of a game that can be fun and refreshing for new  players and returning veterans alike. No matter who you are, get ready for an exemplary and hardcore platforming experience. It will be frustrating at times, but you will ultimately learn the mechanics of the game through repeated deaths so that you will give yourself the best shot at winning against the odds.Absolutely recommended for the single-player experience alone. I cannot wait for online multiplayer to be implemented, to be able to play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: After dumping in many hours into the PS4 version prior to the release of the Steam one i can say this game is not for everyone but could be if everyone is willing to learn what Spelunky 2 is and what it has to offer. Essentially in order to for me to get the most out of Spelunky 2, i had to put in the time to learn every mechanic, every monster attack pattern. Spelunky 2 is a game about intense learning. The way i look at every encounter is almost as a mini puzzle in itself. The game is unforgiving and does not hold back. The amount of obstacles in a claustrophobic area is daunting but when I manage to get through them i  feel awesome. I was a MASSIVE Spelunky HD fan. I played that game for years before I defeated the "Hard" ending. I've told many of my discord buddies about Spelunky and they all scoff. I tell them, if you love games, and you want to feel real accomplishment, pick up Spelunky. Spelunky 2 brings back some familiar areas from HD and also all of the same items. However, they all feel massively tweaked and different. For instance the boomerang feels actually extremely useful. The jetpack is still amazing but now it has a FATAL flaw which makes choosing to proceed with it a hard decision in itself. That is just 2 items I've listed and i could go on and on. The way all these items and enemies as well as traps interact with each other can equal a glorious death, however frustrating it might be. The Devs also put in branching paths, which makes the game feel incredibly open and replayable. If i don't feel like spelunking through the jungle I can take the new path. If i say "nope" to the temple I can go to a new place. It just feels fresh.I've seen other reviewers saying the music isn't as great. I mean sure the slapping jazz track that played randomly in Ice Caves for Spelunky HD doesn't make a comeback but that doesn't mean the music is bad. The music is awesome and there is also dynamic sound design with many of the items. *Pick up the chest from the dwelling after you get the eye and throw it against the wall and you will hear some great dynamic sound design*I think some of these folks that are complaining are people that got frustrated, this is a significantly harder game.I myself was getting pretty upset at some points, it took me a week to beat the basic ending, so i do understand some of the frustration. In conclusion:Spelunky 2 is crafted with so much love it hurts. The amount of secrets and things to discover are literally out of this world. The amount of cool playable characters to collect is awesome. Derek and the rest of the Devs deserve awards and even more success. They have made a game that i will be playing for years. The stories and things that happen from run to run are some i will always remember and "beating" Spelunky 2 will always be one of my greatest gaming achievements in my 29 years on this planet.P.S. i you haven't watched the Spelunky documentary head on over to YouTube and search Spelunky documentary. It was made by NoClip and its a great watch, not only to learn about Spelunky HD but also about game design in general.P.S.S My apologizes if this is to long, i just LOVE this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't mind true unfairness, RNG elements, and unreadable chaos in your skill-based platformer rogue-like, you might be able to tolerate this game, and even appreciate it, just know that no matter how good you are, you physically won't be able to predict and avoid some of the stuff that can happen in this game, it is basically a core tenet of how this game was designed and can be felt throughout the entire experience. I personally absolutely despise playing this game, but I have a lot of respect for the solid and single-minded design choices throughout it, the main creator of the game, Derek Yu, really knew what kind of game he wanted to make, and as a result, this game feels consistent and coherent from beginning to the end... Even if that makes you consistently hate playing it, like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit January 2021:the Multiplayer Online component.. it's super fun WHEN IT WORKS.  Random Matchmaking never finds anyone (unless you invite a person you know) and it constantly disconnects throughout the match, all the time.  So you'll be 10-15 minutes into a run and another random disconnect.  No option to rejoin the game either.   I would give a thumbs down review if I didn't know they were still working out the bugs.My ONLY gripe with this game is that it doesn't support 21:9 Ultrawide resolution.  It does show 2560x1080 but it only goes up to 16:9 I'm sure because of game balancing.  This game would've been perfect had it also put in Ultrawide support.  I was confused as to why I didn't see online co-op or pvp in the game but after I read the launch patch notes I understood.  Online MP is definitely tricky so no problem there since we all know it's coming.  Let's just pray it's not a Doom Eternal situation where they promise Invasions and then months down the road never deliver.  We know Derek Yu isn't the type to promise something and then not impress the fans with polish and skill.This game is essentially a perfect sequel to Spelunky.  The game runs above 60fps and looks beautiful with it's new art style (I wish there was an option to turn on or off the shadow effect from the first game to give it that original look again, or an option to replace the music with OG stage music), and the controls feel even better.  If you're a Spelunky 1 veteran though I'm sure it will take some getting used to, but I like how the sequels new controls and movement feels.  Way smoother and more fluid, it's hard to describe but playing them back to back you'll understand.  The best way I can describe it is your movement and jumping feels way more immediate and less delayed than before, so it comes even closer to those Super Meat Boy levels of perfection.  Honestly, I think this game is at that level.Otherwise nothing else negative I can say about the game. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews out there praise Spelunky as the be-all, end-all of rogulikes, the perfect manifestation of the genre that solved all problems and deserves a golden throne as the king of games. That's an exaggeration, the game is far from perfect, but it is amazing, and everyone should at least give it a try.There are plenty of people out there explaining why the game is great, so I'd like to talk about a few things I didn't expect when I picked it up, so you can ask yourself if it suits your tastes.Firstly, it's less of an action platformer and more of a side-scrolling puzzle game. The game is made out of rooms, and each room is hand crafted, meaning that it already has at least one solution built into it. Your task is to figure that solution and perform it with perfect accuracy. It's a hell lot of fun to do that, but it's a bit different type of fun than many people expect.Due to that form of challenge, the game follows a somewhat realistic approach to its logic. The infamous dart trap is a great example: it triggers when something gets near it. Once you realize that something means anything, and you can throw pots and rocks you find around, the game clicks. This is the sort of challenge you'll be facing a lot of the time.Finally, it's not a perfectly balanced game. There's some RNG involved to the events that take place, mainly due to the dumb AI of creatures populating the dungeon. They can kamikaze into you and jump into spikes, they can fall on you from off screen, there's a lot to watch out for and many things you just won't see coming. I believe this AI behavior is the only reason why you have health points in this game, as everything that's not an enemy will always kill you in one hit. This being said, having extra health often makes little difference.The biggest offender among AI are shopkeepers. They will decide to kill you for dumbest reasons, like a rodent entering their store while you're inside. This is supposedly a remnant of the previous game, but I find this memetic behavior so frustrating I'd rather they fixed it already, even if the optimal play is to always kill the shopkeepers anyway.Oh, also, "always run" is turned on by default. If you haven't played the first game, change it to walk immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent over 19 hours on this game, and with no exaggeration, I can count the number of times that I've made it beyond area 1 on the fingers of one hand. I have never made it past level 2-1. Maybe I just have spectacularly poor hand-eye coordination, or maybe I'm just too old to be able to cope with so much mayhem (I'm 37). But the fact that I've spent so much time on a game that I'm clearly incapable of mastering in reasonable time says a lot about how much fun this game is. I know I'll probably never be able to devote enough time to this game to become good enough to even see level 2-2, let alone area 6. Yet for reasons that I can't explain, instead of this making me want to kick Derek Yu in the nuts, it makes me admire the fact that he had the balls to make the general public pay to experience such unrelenting cruelty. It also somehow makes me want to spend even more time playing the game. Is this the feeling that drives people to throw money away on the lottery every week? Whatever it is, it's such a unique experience in my game playing history that it's moved me to write my first review.I recommend it to people who have no interest in progress.

This had a really cute intro, better music/writing/graphics, and could be fun to explore, if my progress wasn't 2% skill, 98% Random Number Generator; it makes the player feel like they have about as much control as while playing a slot machine. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love the McChrist out of this game.It's new content is a breath of fresh air that keeps the player engaged. There is so much new stuff to do, so much to explore. Every nook and cranny is filled to the brim with secrets. Getting tilted is heavily punished by the newly introduced enemies and hazards, as they are as deadly as they come. All of this juicy new stuff, while keeping the core mechanics super close to its predecessor (Spelunky HD), keeping the familiarity people have with the previous game.After playing Spelunky HD for 278.8 hours, and finishing the game many times over, it becomes a bit stale. The only ever actual hazards are the shopkeepers and your own occasional lapse of environmental awareness. It’s path is fairly linear, whereas Spelunky 2 has multiple roads leading to victory (but mostly hilarious deaths). The high amount of danger makes sweet victory taste even sweeter. It’s a big upgrade in every sense of the word. If you are, however, easily triggered by hard-to-accept intakills and stun loops that result in cheap deaths, I’d recommend you to stick to Spelunky HD, as Spelunky 2 might be twice as unforgiving. Something that absolutely stands out from the rest, even past the introduction of mounts, is the ghost jar and the ghost itself. The ghost has always come to kill you if you dillydally too long on one floor, but they made him a ‘teensy weensy’ bit harder to kite around the area. Now there’s even a ghost jar that summons the ghost when it breaks, whether you like it to or not. It does give you nice sum of money in the form of a diamond though. It’s the new chief among hazards. Some love it (like I do), some hate it.Of course, there are a handful of things that I don’t like all that much. The absolute first and foremost thing that comes to mind is the new mechanics behind the climbing gloves. I don’t really know why this was changed  (maybe they were way to strong in the previous game), but it’s done more harm than good for me, being my main cause of death almost every time I pick it up (because sometimes you really have little choice, when your bomb blows the shop items into a large pile or you’re out of ropes). Of course, one might argue that it just takes practice to master using them again, but in the face of danger my autopilot and reflexes are programmed to handle the situation Spelunky HD-style, which is extremely difficult to adjust. I’d pick Spelunky HD’s climbing gloves over the new ones any day.My other few complaints are fairly minor, and I won’t list them here. I love Spelunky 2, and I’d love for it to blow up even more among a large audience, so it gets the recognition it deserves.P.S. One last thing, since you’ve come this far. If you’re convinced and buy/play Spelunky 2, please not become these 2 archetypes:-	The crybabyThey become upset about their deaths, and go complain on forums/ the store page’s reviews about how the game “is unplayable in its current form”. The game can be really unforgiving, but every death is avoidable, and the danger is often a reaction to your own actions. Some dangers cannot be avoided, but must be dealt with. And yeah, some lessons are definitely learned the astonishingly hard way. Try to reflect on what happened, how to deal with such events in the future, and move on. If the tilt is too heavy, quit for the day. If you need to vent, do that without posting something hateful. In the end, you won’t look like some hero of justice that changes the game for the better. You’ll simply look like a fool that wants the game to be adjusted to your skill level, and not the other way around.-	The ‘Git Gud’ guyThey feel the overwhelming urge to point out that any complaint about the game is just the result of bad play. As much as I hate the crybabies, these guys also suck. With their logic, the game could never do with any improvements, simply anyone’s opinion about something undesirable in the game is just false. Of course you can tell complainers they’re overreacting, I’m just saying there are ways to do that without coming across as a douche. Nobody will thank you for your contribution to the conversation if all you ever say “that’s just Spelunky being Spelunky” and “git gud”.

_childDocuments_.review: If the amount of hours is not an indicator already: This is one of if not my absolute top 1 favorite game of all time.   - The controls are very good, both on controller and keyboard  - The art style is unique and great  - The mechanics are great and responsive  - Gameplay in general is great. The progression and increasing difficulty feel natural and have a good pace.  - No handholding. Only a basic tutorial explaining controls. The player figures everything out for themself (or looks up certain mechanics on the world wide web).  - Basically all rogue-likes (-lites) have that mechanic but I'll mention it anyway: Replayability is great due to randomly generating levels and different paths the player can take, each having their own set of obsticles, rewards, ambience and so on  - (Almost) all deaths can be narrowed down to skill-issue and the player learns something new for the next run    ^ Almost every run the player learns a new mechanic, which there are a lot of (what certain items do and why but also some secret ones as well like  )  - 3 endings of which two have a bossfight (  )  - The questlines are good but I usually don't really do most of them, I have a set of questlines I do almost every run  - Ignore following point to avoid spoilers: .Overall I definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a 2D platformer and rogue-like with great mechanics, controlls, progression (in learning the game) and overall design but also for those looking for something new and fresh to add to their libraries consisting of only a single genre of games.

_childDocuments_.review: As you could probably surmise based on the previous title, this game will challenge you to your core. The entire game is a teacher. There are no pop-up dialog boxes explaining what you should do in a situation, there's no NPC to tell you what to do. It's all there right in front of you to learn. It's a game-designer's dream to be able to teach the player entirely with the gameplay itself. Everything can be done, you just have to die a lot
