_childDocuments_.review: For me, Spelunky 2 was quite a revolutionary game. I had never really heard anything about the series, and for the first two years after its release, I had actually assumed it was some kind of farming colony sim that just happened to take place on the moon because of the cute animals in the trailer. Really though, this game completely changed the way I think and how I approach video games in general.Spelunky'ing is a really goofy, but interesting premise. For one thing, many of this game's mechanics seem almost paradoxical by design. You have limited time in a level, but have to play very carefully by watching for traps, dealing with enemies, and looking for secrets to boost your success odds during an expedition. If you take too long, an invulnerable ghost will appear and turn you to smoke; yet, if you go too fast, you're probably going to get killed by an arrow trap, or conked by a totem pole, or melted by magma, or cursed to death by a shaman, or shot by an angry shopkeeper... You know, this game isn't very fair in all honesty.Mechanically, this game makes total sense. Everything you do can be logical, everything that an enemy does can be understood and prepared for. Traps have specific and learnable triggers, and the player has their own tools for disabling, triggering, or straight up obliterating obstacles in your way. However, there must have been quite a surplus in the trap section at Lowe's because when you first begin playing this game, there seem to be more traps and enemies than can possibly be accounted for or dealt with in quick succession. Truth be told, this game challenges you... to die. A lot. Spelunky 2 as a roguelite is about iterations of runs, playing again and again to refine your skill. Every time you die, that's one more lesson to pick up on and understand. As a player, you'll define your own protocols for maneuvering around every trap, approaching every level type, and defeating every kind of enemy. Your actions and inactions both determine whether you'll spend 20 hours in the first two worlds or going on to win the game and its multiple endings. I've found that the entire experience made me reevaluate how I would react to challenges in video games, and it made me consider what it is I want to enjoy in video games. Every scenario is a puzzle, whether or not it is an FPS duel against a sniper player or a survival-exploration of an uncompromising world. Each setback is an opportunity to learn from your mistakes and iterate on a solution for next time. This philosophy is something I apply to my life almost everyday, and it's boosted my enjoyment of genres in which I used to become very frustrated with such as multiplayer FPS. For that, I thank Spelunky 2. Bless it for catapulting a flaming caveman into my jetpack run of a life.

_childDocuments_.review: Nayb's Notice #12 (I think...): Spleunky 2Spleunky 2 is the sequal to (you guessed it) Spleunky, an indy game that took the online gaming community by storm. It keeps much of the same format as the first game, such as the maddening difficulty and the sense of adventure, with some more subtle changes to overall improve the game.The original Spleunky is well known for how hard and unforgiving it is, and that tradition continues on in the sequel. From the second the tutorial is done this game does not care if you die or get frustrated. Whether it is getting hit by a mole that came from underneath you to getting hit by an arrow that makes you fall into a pit of spikes, you will die in this game, and you will die a lot. But over time you will slowly start to get a fell for the many different worlds Spleunky 2 offers, whether that is the forest world, lava world, or others that you go through during your adventure. Each area has unique enemies and traps that will, again as mentioned previously, kill you.Overall though I have enjoyed this game, even though at times I want to uninstall it. Highly recommended!

The game is one of the most difficult games I've ever played, and a lot of that comes from the immense amount of knowledge required. I can't recommend this if you're the kind of person that gets mad at video games, but if you're willing to sit there, learn from hundreds, probably even thousands, of little mistakes bringing your demise, and push forward through it, Spelunky 2 is a fantastic game and my nomination for Game of the Year.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of the rogue-like genre for many years now, starting all the way back with the Binding of Isaac. From there, the genre has exploded into many different variations of randomly generated levels and perma-death level difficulty; where the stakes are high and the rewards of succeeding feel that much sweeter. Spelunky was a title that, in certain variations, has existed even as far back as Isaac and it was a game i had always heard about, but never really knew if I would enjoy it.With Spelunky 2, I decided the time was right to take the plunge; this quirky little platformer could be a bit of fun. Little did I know, this game would bring me immense frustration, laughter, elation, anger, excitement, and feelings of discovery. This game is unforgiving and doesn't hold your hand; it drops you in and leaves you to find your own way out. Maybe that's not for everyone, but at this point in my life, this game has become my favourite in all of the rogue-like genre.Being able to overcome a level or boss brought me incredible satisfaction; being able to discover secrets and secrets within secrets probed me to dig deeper; getting to a point in the game when you think it's all over only to discover that there's much more. These are the things I've experienced from this game and being able to play with friends and seeing their exact same emotions as mine is something that makes me want to share this with everyone.With most rogue-likes, there is usually a large slew of items you can pick-up that gives you a unique "build" for each run you do of the game. The lack of items in Spelunky means that most of the variation exists in the way the levels are generated; and sometimes, that variation is cursed. I've found that having a small pool of items makes almost all them useful in some way, so no matter the seed that is generated, you know that when you pick up an item, it will prove to be helpful to you in some way.In regards to the level design, you're fighting against the RNG; sometimes it works in your favour, sometimes you're left to figure out the best escape route possible. Sometimes, the items you need are generated and easy to pick-up or purchase from the shop. Sometimes, the only clean way out is to go down a route and avoid traps and enemies. The more you play this game, the more you are able to navigate the variations in levels better than you ever thought you could.In almost 100 hours played on Steam as of writing this, and not to mention the time i've spent on the Switch and PS4 as well, this game is an experience for those looking for a meaningful one. If you are patient and determined, I feel like this game can reward you for the time you put in and will keep you coming back to see if you can beat it again and again. I would recommend this game to everyone and hope you, too, can beat this game, even if it's just to say "I did it".

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 500 hours in the original Spelunky.  I've beaten that game multiple times, know all the secrets, and have almost all the achievements for it (the last two don't look fun to get, so I've not really tried).  I played the original, OG Spelunky before that...though I didn't start coming into my own with the game until the more modern version.  I'm no master level player, but I know the game well.  I adore it, and it's one of my favorite games for relaxing.   Win or lose, I find most of my playing really engaging; I laugh at my deaths and take glee from my successes.  As a result,  I had my eyes on Spelunky 2 for a while, and the pictures made it look like just what I wanted.Then I played it...and I kind of wish it had stayed on my wishlist.Spelunky 2 isn't a bad game so much as it is a sequel that is at odds with the game play of the first title.  Strong among the first game's qualities were, as you got good, you were able to take your time and really build yourself up.  The level layouts rewarded mastery, while still being stuff that greener players could traverse and get to the end of.  Traps were designed in such a way that the vast majority of my deaths in the original game felt like my fault and only my fault; it felt fair, while still being cut-throat.  I was the one who failed, the game didn't 'trick' me.  The end of the level ghost was a problem, but a more clever player could circumvent it and even kite into gems to increase their value, creating this interesting risk/reward dynamic...making the end of every stage a calculation of what you could do safely...and what you could do if you were willing to risk it.All of that is gone now.The traps are much more frequent, and feel designed for cruelty rather then a rewarding game play experience where the challenges feel designed to create a good time.  The physics have changed, meaning you can throw a stone in front of you and not hit what is in front of you....so not only does that make no sense?  As a vetran of the first game, I have to unlearn what the previous game taught me for what feels like no good reason.  The ghost isn't something a skilled played can circumvent and avoid...and even use for profit; the ghost is much faster, so it's so much closer to a standard time limit without the nuances of the original title.  The money is now more sparsely laid out, so building yourself up is harder and more challenging....without actually feeling more rewarding; I never feel like my inability to buy things and build myself up is a fault of my choices...but a fault of level lay outs that now spawn less money.  You used to be able to cling to ladders and ropes and fire a gun, allowing the methodical and thoughtful players a chance to use the terrain; now the kick back shoves you off...presumably to make game play more "interesting".I'm not interested.The game feels like it wants to just be harder for the sake of being harder alone, when the original game was still very challenging and engaging as it was.  The design was pretty flawless.  What I came to Spelunky 2 expecting was that core design, while getting new content, stage lay outs, and concepts.  What I got instead was Spelunky for the irritating and toxic "git gud" crowdAnd there are lots of fun things in the game.  The little fire beetles are brilliant design.  The Boarcupine boss is well designed, and fun to try and figure out.  The cave systems are great, and how doors interact with bombs presents fun challenges and interesting options.  The new level short cuts are well designed.  I'm just upset that all these fun, new features are now in a core game experience that I nakedly despise.I would have returned this thing, but I accidentally missed the cutoff window by letting the game idle while picking up a family member from their job.  So I stuck with it longer then I would have otherwise....I started being able to get into later stages, and facing the traps there.  The problem is that it isn't fun or rewarding.  It's a miserable slog. Even when I succeed...I never get the sense of triumph the previous game give me; my reward is only ever a new piece of tedium to throw myself at.Honestly, I wish I had my money back instead.  This game just misunderstands what made the previous game fun, and I sort of hate it.  It represents all these ideas that I wish I could bring back to the original Spelunky.  Until someone makes a mod though, Spelunky 2 just represents a waste of my time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2:This game is about the rouguelike experience. Now what do I mean by that, well I believe this game has four main sections that I believe are worth discussing, Movement, Items, Level Design, and Difficulty.To start I will be discussing Movement. In terms of movement options, you have a walk, run, jump, clamber, and that's it. The movement is very simple, although this incentives the use of items, so that you will have more movement options or other various power tools at your disposal.Items: The items in Spelunky 2 have many utilities, and purposes, to start I will go over the basic items you start with bombs, and ropes. Bombs and Ropes are both items that are consumed over a gameplay session each providing different utilities, the bombs blow stuff up, whilst ropes let you climb up to higher locations. The next items are equipment, these items are applied to the player character similar to a backpack and each can provide different helpful tools to a player, for example a jetpack to fly, a cape to glide, or a power pack to power up your attacks. Speaking of attacks, the final item type is the weapons and items that you are able to pick up, these items consist of guns, weapons like boomerangs, and even magical weapons that have special properties.The level design is a short and simple discussion. The game is a roguelike and as such will have a nearly random generation for every level in the game even having special locations that will appear in certain locations if you know what to look out for, but new to the series is a choice between different locations, for example the jungle, or the volcano areas.Finally there is the difficulty, what I feel is the greatest part of this game. To be absolutely honest, this game loves to not through it's punches, and is absolutely brutal. The tutorial shows you the tools at your disposal, but the rest of the game you have to figure out how to do tasks, you have to learn so much about this game, and you are more than likely to die on your first run-through of the game, but if you stick with it, you will get good, and you will learn to overcome so many obstacles.To finish out this review, I hope you will join me on this adventure, by buying the game, as I believe this to be an excellent game, and the extra content that I chose to leave out as I believe it is a discovery when you learn how to do a lot of it, will be worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 14/04/2021: Revised my review from Negative to Positive.Initially when I bought Spelunky 2, it had no Windows 7 compatibility. While I understood the decision by the developers not to support an old OS, I was bummed out not being able to play as a Windows 7 user. Luckily a patch was soon released by the community, and I was able to play the game. Still, as the devs pointed out, "any future patch may break Windows 7/8/8.1 compatibility". Therefore, I couldn't recommend Spelunky 2, as a warning to others still using an older OS.Having now played 80+ hours, I want to revise my review. The game never broke, and it is better than Spelunky 1 in almost every aspect. It's more dynamic, bigger, and a bit more difficult (which is a plus). There is a lot to explore, especially in terms of the end-game. While reaching and beating the main boss might be fairly difficult, it is nothing compared to some of the very specific achievements, such as entering the Sunken City. And even though this is a challenging, sometimes brutal game, it almost never feels unfair. With the rare exception, dying is always the result of a mistake you made, making it a truly rewarding experience to finally reach one of the several endings. If you enjoy easy-to-learn, difficult-to-master games, Spelunky 2 should be right on top of your list.

_childDocuments_.review: High difficulty only works if the game is fair, unfortunately, Splunky is anything but. Though the first world functions well, however moving onward to further floors a lack of careful playtesting becomes very apparent. No level makes this clearer than the Lava world (2nd floor). Beating the floor feels like a lottery ticket, most of the time, the floor is mindnumbingly easy, however, on occasion, due to some freak accident of random generation, it becomes nearly impossible. I kid you not, one time I spawned in above a pool of lava, and the only way to advanced was to expend all my ropes. unfortunately due to a spike trap hitting a robot on the head in the next level, the path became impossible and I could not advance. On other occasions, I've spawned in only to be immediately chased by a ghost (no idea why, probably because of a poorly spawned robot). Not meeting the minimum requirement of five thousand hours in game, I died jumping into a spike trap while attempting to get away. Additionally, lava monsters in the stage randomly drop onto your head, more often then not, immediately killing you. Though rare, sometimes there are impenetrable walls of firebugs. The game all to often falls back on the existence of ropes and bombs to smooth the absolutely randomness monstorsity which is the random generation system. Even in the most deserved deaths, death still feels kinda random, simply because of how fast you die in comparison to the duration of a run. As opposed to playing to win, your playing not to lose, and it isn't nearly as fun. Another issue with the game is how steep the learning curve is for new players, even the hardest of games tend to give players places to learn and practice, shortcuts simply aren't enough. Though steam only shows I have 9 hours in game, steam doesn't log hours in offline (it internally logs them for refunds, but won't log them publicly), I have is likely have something along the lines of 30-40 hours. Because of this, I can say with absolute confidence that the game is in desperate need of a practice or seeded mode (yes, a seeded mode already exists, but you have to beat the game to unlock it, not very helpful is it?). Splunky aritificially extends it's run time with stupid unpredictable deaths (cough cough moles), the only way to learn the mechanics of an enemy, is to repeatedly die to it. Though speedrunners and youtubers have proven that it's possible to consistently beat the game, if you scroll through the run of the day leader boards, you will see that the vast majority of people struggle with getting through the 2nd floor, THE 2ND FLOOR!I will happily change my review as changes are made (It's possible that multiplayer will invalidate my review, seeing as the local coop does iron out some of the toughest parts of the game), but as of right now, I cannot possibly recommend a game in which runs go on for tens of minutes and runs end in tenths of seconds (often to unfair feeling circumstances).

_childDocuments_.review: Spelunky 2 is a highly-anticipated, much-needed revival of one of the original Roguelike classics that defined the genre. Released a whopping seven years after the first installment's HD remaster, Spelunky HD (Most commonly known as just Spelunky), the sequel to the roguelike classic delivers on many aspects, with some minor flaws. Every enemy can be very punishing while some border on plain unfair . You can and will get stun-locked to death constantly if you're not careful as no matter how much health you have, there's always something that will end your run swiftly. The platforming mechanics are simple and easy to learn, though difficult to master when certain items get involved. If you're like me and you want to keep everything a secret, you will have a very difficult time as the game is filled to the brim with cryptic details and secrets.Just like Spelunky HD, Spelunky 2 is  with secrets and the game tells you nothing. You are expected to either look them up or find them by trial and error or complete accident. It even includes an absurdly complex secret path to reach the "real" final boss. And if I didn't know about that path from Spelunky HD, I am unsure if I would ever find it. If you don't want to use Google, you should expect to keep a keen eye out for the finest details and make many experiments with the risk of ending a powerful run.Both very much and very little. The sequel succeeds in delivering "more" Spelunky by keeping the majority, if not all of the old enemies and traps and gameplay mechanics. With a roguelike, it can be challenging to make a sequel whilst avoiding selling what is practically a re-release of the same game. With Spelunky 2, it feels more like a remaster of Spelunky HD with an abundance of new items, secrets, and bosses. It even presents a few alternate stage paths to explore, each with their own set of challenges. Put simply, if you're wishing to see much of a change in the gameplay style in Spelunky 2, you've come to the wrong place. But if having  Spelunky is appealing to you, then this may be a worthwhile purchase.If you intend to play with friends, you may not expect to get very far. Spelunky 2 supports up to 4 players locally and (soon to be) online which provides an intensely chaotic but extremely entertaining experience. Unless you and your friends try-hard and take the game seriously, you will likely spend your time throwing each other around and hitting one another with rocks and pots. But you will surely get a good laugh out of the accidental friendly-fire deaths.As of the time of writing this review, Mossmouth had forgone the implementation of online multiplayer to provide an early release. But, the developers are hard at work in developing this feature and are openly communicating with the playerbase on the subject. For now, if you have a reliable internet connection, Steam's Remote Play feature is an excellent medium to play with your friends. Even better, your friends do not even need to own the game to play with you through this method. Only the host.+More Spelunky, if that's your jam.+A modernized, expanded experience.+Full of laughs in multiplayer+Active Devs+Brand-new stages and secrets to uncover+You can pet the dog/cat/mouse+Substantially more variety in:Level generationEventsEnemiesItemsNPCs~Brutal difficulty~Well-kept secrets~A "Just Okay" Soundtrack~Similar Graphics-Some enemies are just plain unfair.-Nigh devoid of story.-Level generation  ruin a run.I cannot explain Spelunky 2 in any better way than "More Spelunky." After all, the game has so many secrets that I can't say much about it. Many roguelikes thrive on replay value and the sequels retain a familiar feel for that reason. It is a brutally difficult roguelike platformer with tons of secrets that will be hard to find. I would recommend Spelunky 2 to both new players and veterans, though new players may have an easier time if they try Spelunky HD first. For those desiring enjoyment with friends, it is a hectic experience that will either make you rage or laugh, depending on your style. Mossmouth are actively working to make Spelunky 2 a more balanced game and it is working wonders.

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty scaling in this game is awful compared to previous titles and should only be bought if you really want an improved version of 1 or are willing to use mods, which is a shame as nearly every other aspect of this game is amazing.The first area extremely difficult compared to nearly everything else in the game only challenged by  (area 4) and alternative harder paths such as the  or alternate endings, but those are only hard because you'll so infrequently reach those areas and it'll take many tries to properly learn them - which is fair, those are meant to be harder. But having the first area so brutally punishing is laughably terrible game design compared to the perfection of the rest of the game.The music focuses on different aspects than the first Spelunky's, removing multiple tracks and instead focusing on the overall quality and transitions of the tracks, which works out surprisingly well. But they also gave the first area the worst music - the area you'll likely be spending 90% of your time in unless you use shortcuts (preferably with mods). The gameplay however is (almost) a huge step up in every regard - all of the stages have their own quests which are all interwoven into one much larger reward, the alternate endings, which I won't cover. Not only that, after every boss there are also two stages to choose between, making the game far less linear than the other Spelunky games. Both with unique rewards, challenges, enemies, graphics and music. Which is a shame, because the harsh welcome of the first area and it having arguably the most important quest item literally drags all of this work down.Maybe I do "suck" but when your difficulty curve starts extremely high, then flatlines before spiking again, it just screams poor game design.If you are happy with a bad start that gets far better, this is the game for you. If you are happy to get mods to get past the bad start, this game is for you. But if you don't want to put up with these and are still interested in the game,  or get the remake of the classic, Spelunky hd. The curves there actually make sense.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I'm a sucker for platformers. Now see there are games like Celeste that are good platformers and then there are games like Super Meat Boy and both Spelunky games that just make movement feel so good (don't get me wrong, Celeste was still a good game with the most relatable story I've ever played). Sure this game has some bs and a lot of luck but that's what you get from random generation. I've beaten the game with shortcuts and I'm planning on doing two other endings as well. With that said, this game has a lot of replayability, especially in terms of content. There is enough content for new players to enjoy, and hard core players to explore. My only complaint at the moment is the difficulty curves. I feel that the first two areas should be a bit easier and less chaotic. When going through the game I noticed that it never gets progressively harder. In fact, I think the first two areas are the hardest of them all (aside form the secret areas). If you're going to get this game there's something you should know; it's going to be hard, this isn't Mario Bros so please don't come back complaining that you cant get pasted the first area and leave a negative review just because of that. You will die. A lot. So get ready to practice. With that said, if you like platformers, rouge-likes, and/or you're just interested in the Spelunky franchise, I'd highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: (but in a good way)The characters feels really nice to control while being hard to master at their full extent, the different objects scattered throught the world are usefull but dangerous at the same time, the enemies can easily end your run, but have paterns that will help you mastering them, and the world is filled with traps, items and more that will intrigue you during your whole playthrought.They require skill and thinking to get, while still hinting at their existence, so that you can more easily find them. A lot of items and places will feel out of place, almost useless, but in spelunky, NOTHING is useless. This makes the world feel alive and mysterious, there's always something that will make you say "". This leads to a lot of goals that you can set to yourself, which helps to get involved on the game. Don't feel discouraged by the difficulty of spelunky, because every mechanic are well-tought to help you understand the game, it's traps and it's enemies. Every death is a lesson on how to survive next time, and feels fair, you harldy never feel cheated (well in the beginnings at least, it would be a lie to say that I never got killed unfairly, but it's stuff that happens...) Even if you find hard game not fun, Spelunky will help you to change this opinion, has it is made to make you learn and accept.If you don't know if you should get the game or not, ask you 2 questions :if not, then it might not be worth it to get spelunky, since it requiers time and patience to enjoy itLike I said, if you really hate dying, Spelunky might not be for you, but if you want to challenge yourself (even if you don't like hard games), this game is a great start, since it's fair and fun.Spelunky is a game about difficulty, mastering, secrets and bombs (a lot of bombs), and it's one of the best rogue-like I've ever seen, let alone one of the best GAMES I've ever seen, so hesitation doesn't have it's place here. If you like rogue likes, hard games, plateforming games, or just want to torture yourself a bit, this game is MADE for you. It's really good, like  good, so just get it, you won't regret it ;)Sry, that was a bit long, I just have LOTS to say about this masterpiece, which is and will always be one of my favorite games of all times... there are a lot of helpfull guide here and there on Steam, and some will help you enjoy the game even with all the frustration, so I'd recommend reading them. Thx for reading this, if you see spelling issues here and there, be sure to let me know (I'm not english so it's hard for me to write perfectly), and on that note, have a nice day ;)

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Spelunky 1 or Spelunky 2, my best recommendation is to play Spelunky 1 to the fullest and only even consider acknowledging this game's existence until you get completely bored of Spelunky 1. When this game was just a trailer and a couple of gameplay demos, I couldn't even imagine writing a review not recommending this game, but it's clear that after playing for as much as I have that Derek Yu doesn't understand the magic and fun that came with Spelunky 1. The main issue is that the game is needlessly antagonistic towards the player for no reason other than what seems to be, "Hey, you! Player! Stop having fun!" Why is it that the jetpack now must explode with contact with fire? In Spelunky 1, the jetpack is far from a victory guarantee and despite its utility, there's still plenty of opportunity to find yourself with another loss with it equipped. Yet, regardless of the result win or loss, the jetpack is such a joy to use. In Spelunky 2, the jetpack retains its familiar maneuverability, but the "contact with fire and it explodes" gimmick leads to removing much of the enjoyment of encountering it in a run. And I think that's how I'd describe most of Spelunky 2's additions from the first game: player-punishing gimmicks. In Spelunky 1, the game is completely up front with all hazards and really the only re-occurring element of surprise is enemies in pots or damsel-disguised enemies (but these are only found in a secret appropriately difficult alternate world). In Spelunky 2, we've got enemies hiding behind scenery, run-ending traps hiding behind scenery (although, thankfully, after an update there's now a small gold piece to make bear traps a little less blending into the background), and enemies in pots that poison you. Poison takes one damage at regular intervals until you rescue a damsel (and good luck finding one after you get poisoned usually), which is a far harsher punishment than taking one damage from being surprised by a hidden enemy in a pot in the first game. The first time I encountered the poison and curse debuffs I thought they were interesting additions, but then when you really think about it/try to deal with it in game, you realize they just don't really mesh at all with the core gameplay. The only thing that even comes close to being a constant burden like curse or poison in the first game is getting the ball-and-chain debuff from destroying too many Kali alters, but for the most part, you have to purposefully go out of your way to make this happen. Even with a random alter being destroyed by something out of your control, I always either had enough favor with Kali for it to not matter or quickly rebuilt favor to avoid the harsher ball-and-chain punishment (and the odds of alters being destroyed twice by RNG are extremely low anyways). Either way, I think I only got the ball-and-chain punishment maybe twice in thousands of runs. Meanwhile, I don't know how many times I've gotten cursed or poisoned in this game, but frequent enough for it to really sour the experience of playing.At some point long ago, I started playing Spelunky 1 with the music muted and I've resumed that with Spelunky 2 after many hours playing, but I will comment that the music in Spelunky 2 is highly repetitive and not nearly as enjoyable to listen to as the first game. This is more of a disappointment than something that I wouldn't recommend over. I think the adaptive soundtrack is an interesting idea, but hearing the main dwelling song again and again with little variation on every run shows how badly this works in practice (it doesn't help that the main dwelling song is probably the worst in the soundtrack). I think my return to Spelunky 1 one night after many lackluster not so fun attempts at Spelunky 2 runs says it all. That night, I managed to get a victorious alternate ending run in Spelunky 1 less than ten playthroughs and I had a load of fun in the process in spite of the hundreds of hours I've had in that game. I sort of walked away with the feeling of, "Oh, I forgot there is a version of Spelunky that's actually consistently fun to play." Perhaps the only good thing I can say about Spelunky 2 is that online co-op is a lot of fun because most of the player punishment I discussed above doesn't really matter as much since dead players can be revived on the very next level. However, personally, my main interaction with Spelunky 1 or 2 is through solo play, so I hold with my opinion that I don't recommend this particular iteration. I'll continue to play Spelunky 2 if only to get to one of the game's endings, but after that, I'm not sure I'll play that much aside from co-op and the random one-off session.

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating and tremendously unfun, Spelunky 2 looked at Dark Souls and went "HEY, I CAN DO THAT!" and *thought* it was ramping up the difficulty. It was even partially right.Truth be told, the game is imprecise as HELL. I can try to pick up a bomb I just dropped to lob it and the graphics do overlap like I should be able to - but I don't. Skeletons pop out of boney bits (that are everywhere in level 1) or helmets to get a cheap shot on you. Sometimes the level generates inescapable damage situations - another cheap shot.The ghost wasn't menacing enough so now after 15 or so seconds it splits into two, making gem farming a weirder proposition. Hit detection is very dodgy. Worst of all, I can jump and press towards a ledge to grab and sometimes my character just decides he doesn't want any of that ♥♥♥♥ and falls to their death. I have tried to goomba stomp numerous enemies only to be touched\damaged by them despite landing from above. [TODAY was a day where they apparently adjusted various instances of this to be less egregious..didn't work].Spelunky 2 is not funstrating like the first one was. It's just *frustrating*.  The first area, as many correctly state, is among the hardest in the game for how weak, unequipped you are, the utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RNG, the *constant* harassment of enemies (of which there are more of, in a tighter space) isn't helping.Cavemen now have 3 hp. You have fast, irritating guinea pig\mole looking ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that dig through the ground to get at you, also 3 HP. They *will* follow you and hurt you and jump out of the ground before you can react some times. I'm sick of the first area. it's music, its enemies, it's *MEMORIZED*layout. I had to play it a lot with the restarts because bad game design but I'm also just siiiiiiiick of it. You recognize how the rooms are cut and pasted by the engine because you'll get almost identical configurations *very* often.Just bad. Avoid it, don't buy it, make the developer give a ♥♥♥♥ and fix these issues.This game makes me actually angry, but I didn't realize how lazily "LOL DIFFICULT GUISE!" it was till I was past the refund window :-\.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people have already said this, but I feel the difficulty has passed the point of  "fun because it's hard" from the last game and is just "hard because it's supposed to be". It almost feels as though the developers forgot that they're really good at Spelunky now, and didn't realize they were making it too tough. As of this writing, only 23.5% of players have even cleared the first zone. My experience so far has been frustrating, constantly being caught in world generation dead-ends where there's no way to move forward without taking damage or using resources, and that's not including the un-dodgeable enemies in doorways.Beyond the difficulty though, I'm actually more disappointed in the music. I remember the original having multiple tracks for each area, or at the very least for the world 1 where we spend most of our time. Now each world only has one track, and in just over 3 hours I've already turned off the music and replaced it with my own playlist.I really want to like this game, and I'm going to keep trying at it, but so far it has felt like it attempts to pack more onto the original title, without realizing the space is way too tight. I feel I would enjoy this a lot more if the first world was nerfed some. Every zone after has felt easier, but because of the way the secrets work I can't just skip past the garbage part.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've loved the Spelunky series for over a decade at this point. I had thousands of runs on Spelunky classic, and about 50 or so hours on the HD remake. When the sequel came out, I was extremely excited! And then I wasn't, because it's hard as ♥♥♥♥. I considered it a miracle to get to the jungle area in Spelunky 2 when I first started playing it. Anything beyond that was absolutely unreal to consider. I played for about 5 hours before dropping it completely. But my problem was that I was expecting Spelunky HD (Part 2), rather than a proper sequel. The old tricks won't work, there's too much that has changed for me to expect to be good from the start. And this is a good thing! The sequel changes enough of the formula to stand apart from the other two games. But I didn't appreciate that at first, hence why I ragequit. After playing it for a bit more, I still haven't beaten it, but I've made it past Olmec, past the Ice Caves, into Neo-Babylon. I'm getting better all the time.I actually thought that maybe my skills had deteriorated for a bit - but I downloaded Spelunky HD and beat it on my first try. It just goes to show you that Mossmouth has done a fantastic job of adding variety to the game and increased the difficulty so that people like me who've played Classic and HD will not just stroll through this in a few playthroughs. Buy it at full price - this is a game well worth it. Buy it for the difficulty and attention to detail!
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great achievement of tough but fair design across the board, from the levels to enemies to bosses. Pretty much anything can (and will) kill you. The progression is solely gated around your skill, and you will get better as you play and learn more about the game.My major issues stem from the multiplayer co-op. the online interface sucks, some issues include:-winning a run in multiplayer boots you to the main menu-cannot change an settings (audio/video) mid multiplayer runThe multiplayer has issues but is perfectly playable, and is a great time with friends. If you're looking for a challenging game with tight controls heavy replay value, a lot of unlockables/secrets, and dopamine coursing through the veins (if you can handle some frustration), I can recommend Spelunky 2 easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: A masterstroke from Derek. A sequel that lives up to the original game and then goes even further beyond that. The Spelunky 2 much the previous games combines rewarding game play with a grand sense of exploration and progress, so many areas to discover and items/enemies to interact with. There are many secrets and challenges to overcome in this incredible experience. I would absolutely recommend this game if you want a challenge worth mastering and you have the patience to master it. great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Spelunky 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really expected more gameplay polish and pacing/balance to the game. I haven't beaten it (or gotten close to seeing all that it has to offer) and will update this review when I complete the game and get all its achievements, but that may take a while since I really have not had any fun playing this sequel thus far.It feels like they completely missed the highlights and allure of the thoughtful challenge that Spelunky/HD offered to players, and decided that object density equates to interesting level generation.I would wholeheartedly recommend you to play Spelunky (1/HD) instead, and return to this sequel afterward if you feel as though it was not busy enough.

name: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem
detailed_description: You are one of the three survivors of the slaughter of Castagath. Rescued by Grand Inquisitor Heimlock, you were drafted into the Republic’s Army of the Purifiers at a very young age to be trained in the military academy and become perfect soldiers against the supernatural. You also had the chance to benefit from Heimlock’s occasional advice and training, which led you and your childhood friends, Valeria and Edric, to be called the “Children of Heimlock”. Recently, the Brotherhood of Dawn has infiltrated the Crimson Keep, a mysterious republican fortress lost among the northern deserts known as the Red wastes. While the purpose of the attack was unclear, the republican Senate voted a retaliation act against all known locations of the Brotherhood. Led by Grand Inquisitor Heimlock himself, troops are soon deployed on the Coast of wrecks, near the city state of Stormfall, to terminate a camp of Brothers. You are, with your two childhood friends, part of operation Dawnbane, under the supervision of Justicar Maëlys. Key features: Free character development Wield a great variety of weapons and find your own playstyle thanks to their unique stances and combos. In Wolcen, there is no class, only your weapons set the rules for your skills types. Three types of resources Rage and Willpower interact with each other, using the Resource Opposition System. Stamina allows you to use a dodge-roll to avoid danger or travel faster. Item diversity Gear up according to your offensive and defensive choices with common, magical, rare and legendary items. Break the rules and unlock new possibilities with Unique items and rare affixes. Rotative Passive Skill Tree Make your own path throughout the 21 sub-class sections available in the Gate of Fates to customize your passives and make them fit to your play style. Skill customization Level up your skills with your character or alternative resources to gain modifier points and create your own unique combination of skill modifiers. Change your damage type, add new functionalities, grant buffs or debuffs, change the skill’s mechanics completely. The options are limitless. Strategic fights Wolcen’s creatures have complex patterns including deadly skills. Pay attention to various markers and to animation anticipation to avoid lethal attacks using your dodge roll ability. Aspects of Apocalypse All characters can shapeshift into one of the 4 Celestial incarnations available, each of them offering 4 different skills, and one devastating ultimate. Endless replayability Improve your gear by looting or crafting, gather resources to unlock rare missions, face advanced challenges for special rewards, experiment new builds, become the greatest achiever. There is always something to do in Wolcen: LoM. A taste for beauty Using the Cryengine technology makes Wolcen an immersive and beautiful game with highly detailed armors and weapons. In addition, 8 hours of epic orchestral music will accompany you during your journey. Unleash your fashion sense Customize your appearance by switching the visuals of your armors and weapons. Loot more than 100 different dyes and tune up your armor to have your very own unique style. The asymmetric armor system will also allow you to change your appearance for left and right shoulder and glove. Difficulty modes Choose how you want to make the campaign with 2 different difficulty settings: the Story mode and the Normal mode. The endgame is shaped to allow a progressive increase in difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: So, despite all of the bugs and server issues that have happened since the game released (which are being actively worked on and updated!), I would  recommend this game to any ARPG fans. The game has a simple and enjoyable story, the artwork is beautiful, the music is stellar.And the gameplay  ROCKS. With a myriad of builds you have access to, and a ton of super fun skills/spells to play around with (each with thier own sets of mods that can change them even further, not being bound to items based on class, because there is no class, it makes for an enjoyable and dare I say, addictive, gameplay loop. If you want a game with hours of fun either solo or in co-op this is a solid choice, and these guys put a ton of work into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! it is so much like Diablo 2 at its core.But there are some horrible and i do mean Horrendous problems with this game.The bad.-Sever crashes.-- Too many network issues they should have fixed BEFORE release.-bugged Skills/Passives/Talents/Items.-Bad decisions/ wrong priorities by the devs.-Control (no forced move on mouse 1)-lack of skills.-lack of item variation.-No real end-game goals (the unique to legendary should have been End-game goal but apparently that was a bug)the good.+Visually stunning for a Arpg this game tops them all with EASE!+Mechanical combat feels done Right! its fast pace, there is no sluggishness its just spot on.+the amount of build diversity is there its just that a lot of people just copy-paste builds now-a-days which makes me cringe when there is so much false information about builds out there. Bleeding edge still works perfectly fine as of patch 1.0.7.0 Either you understand it or you don't that simple.(as of 1.0.7.0  that is more then enough for 187 levels.)+the amount of effort required for good gear is right there, be very lucky with the rolls or just grind endlessly.+there is a lot of good potential for this game, But. the developers REALLY have to work harder on this game now more updates, more content, micro transactions on stash-tabs/ cosmetics etc..+Can't wait for new DLC's, Arena fights, Pvp content and much much more.I would recommend this game if you are patient.if you are not i'd recommend you to wait until the first big major content releases come out that way you skipped the whole bugs/errors/exploit era because that seems the area we are in right now and this will continue for several months to come.This game was too early for a official release, they should have delayed it can release the press-kit to 20k+ people for pre-release testing this way ALL of these problems could have been avoided.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who initially pirated the game to check it out, after playing it for 40 hours I had to buy the actual game.I don't know exactly what everyones gripe is with the game, that it's not Diablo and it's not PoE? it honestly strikes a happy medium in between the two, while not on the level of PoE in terms of customization and content, its head and shoulders above D3 and if you changed a few characters and lore around would probably be Diablo 4. There are obviously some things that still need to be worked on, Melee seeming almost unstoppable compared to ranged/magic early and mid game and there are some strange FPS drops on some of the maps, but iv'e found that atleast class wise they all have their own charm points.I personally found myself enjoying this story a lot more than I expected, they've done a great job of world building in a small amount of time whilst also making it a linear experience instead of just jumping between acts with random stories.TL;DR, if you want a game more enjoyable and customizable than D3 or a game that isn't as chaotically customizable as POE, or you simply want an enjoyable story to play through, the game ticks a lot of boxes and I think its only going to get better with time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 35 - 40 hours into the game. If I had to rate it on a stars rating, it'd get 3.8. Here's a rough breakdown:PROS* Pretty good hack & slash * Making the skills for all classes simply droppable/purchaseable is amazing and I've waited for ages for a game to do this.* Class tree progression has depth and is pretty fascinating. That you can rotate the rings of the tree to make a more linear path for progression is fascinating and a great idea.* Graphics in general and those for skills and spells do a good job to make you feel pretty awesome* No issues with my save game getting messed up/corrupted/lost, but I am playing "online".* Story gets a 3 out of 5. It's not amazing, but it's enough to keep you moving.* All the components to make this a 5/5 star game are present, but the developers made choices that detracted from this potential.* Allowing the ability to reroll character points & class path points for a reasonable price is most welcome.* The interplay when your character and Valeria is well done and the only emotional lynch pin this game has, sadly. There is Hemlock, but his voice acting is flat so I just don't feel it.CONS* I don't know why hack & slash games, especially those trying so hard to be Diablo, make legendaries exceedingly rare or level blocked, but this game does. That greatly hampers the excitement of loot rather than building it up. Getting a legendary per session in Diablo is a pretty great cadence IMHO.* Dropping crafting components with no mention or hint of a crafting system is maddening* Having literally 1 NPC that sells gear is super annoying especially when there's no clear conveyance of when his loot changes. If you log off and log back on, he'll have the same stuff in both cases. That's incredibly underwhelming.* The lack of variety in NPC loot vendors lends to gold hoarding. Seriously...I have over 100K gold and nothing to spend it on.  A gamble NPC would be welcome, but only if you could get legendary from him...which you probably couldn't if one did exist.* I've come across 2 NPC's in the world that sell a single unique item. The first time I didn't have enough gold. The second time, it wasn't something I wanted. I have yet to see any such NPC again. That's maddening.* I found the equivalent of a treasure goblin...once. Just...why make that so rare?* The game really does need an ingame codex for some of the affixes you discover because it really hard to know what they do specifically. Adding +9 to my critical score....does what? By what percent does that actually increase my crit chance?* The only stat worth a damn IMHO is Ferocity. I've dumped all my character points into it for the most part. My crit chance is about 44% and crit damage around 250%. The over simplification of character stats is a detriment to the game.* The acting for Hemlock is sub-par. The voice is right, but his lack of emotion takes away from some moments that are supposed to be more impactful. He just comes off as flat.* In one scene early the game Eadric is all about "We'll do this together, sister. NO matter what." In the very next level, he's like, "well if they're going to execute you, that's your fate. Accept it." Wait, what? There's no good explaination for this.* Crafting is an end-game component that happens after you essentially beat the game...Yeah, this is trying to come off as the premium product but ending up like that My Pillow guy. So, like I said. The stuff to make the game amazing exists. In short do this:* Make legendaries drop at a cadence of once per session * Build crafting into the game from the start. Revamp crafting to whatever degree needed to make that possible.* Add a codex to explain affixes or quantify the pros/cons of equiping one piece of gear over another * Revamp the character stats and how they work. Take that back to the drawing board.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you put all of the bugs and the offline issues aside, this game is no more than a 5/10. 1.) The Itemization is boring. When will devs learn that bigger numbers do not mean more fun. You want some uniques that change the core of your gameplay, maybe making your skills do different things. It was one of the biggest issues that Diablo 3 faced in classic, you just equip things because they have better stats, but once you have your skills, it ultimately feels like you are playing the same build the entire game.2.) No endgame. You can beat the storyline in a solid 8 hours with an average build, probably faster with something really solid. The story is so lackluster too that I have no urge to even want to go back through it either, so it leaves me with just endgame. The endgame feels like they took some inspriation from Diablo 3 and Path of Exile and tried to merge them together, but it just feels like a Path of Exile map that has winding paths that always seem to lead back to the same spot, leaving a lot of backtracking.Even aside from that part of the endgame, the city building is just not that intriguing to me. Granted, I have only leveled my city up to 3, so I have not spent a whole lot of time in it, but I just can't bring myself to play it anymore, I feel like any progress I make means nothing.3.) Poor QoL. Right click is a left click while in your inventory so you have to have your mouse completely in place to sell things to the vendors. No move only bind. Can't upgrade gems. No skill tree search. Bad hitboxes.These are things that if you play other ARPGs and you play Wolcen, you will almost immediately notice.4.) Apocalypse Forms are terrible. These things do not scale very well, so by level 40ish~ it is only useful to survive boss mechanics if you accidentally used up your dashes, and to look badass, but everytime I would enter them, I would pretty much immediately toggle it off once I evaded the mechanic.Luckily I hadn't bought this recently with all of the hype, and had it for a couple years now, so the disappointment is a lot easier on me, but I really hope I can steer some PoE players away from wasting their money here. Buy a stash tab, it is a better investment.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big ,  and  fan,  has been on my radar for a long time, and plenty of people are understandably hyped that this could be the next big thing in the ARPG genre. On the other hand, I'm usually very wary of early access games.  The game started it's development three years ago and still leaves a lot to be desired leaving me torn between recommending it in order to support its promising future and waiting a bit for  to work more on this unpolished gem.  is overall a successful game especially for an early access period. Graphics, animations, gameplay and the skill system is pretty good for both hack’n slash and RPG lovers. There are still things to work on like the music and the main story. But when it comes to reacting according to the feedback they get from their players,  does a great job. So expect them to make this game better and better after each update they plan for the future. If you do decide to check out the game – as always with early access titles, keep your expectations in check and keep in mind that If you are not a fan of ARPG's,  in its current state won't change that – but for the fans of the genre, you are sure to find plenty to have fun with. _childDocuments_.review: I have been playing aRPGs and RPGs for nearly 30yrs. I think it's always good to start with a bit about your personal tastes in a genre so readers can see if they relate. Certainly for me, when comes to aRPGs, my most notable titles I hold in high regard (in no particular order) would be Diablo 2, Dungeon Siege 2 and Grim Dawn. I like classic RPGs that aren't complete fixated on the rng of items, be it drops or crafting. I do currently play D3 and PoE as well,I am fortunate (based on what I has read about the problematic launch) that I did not pick up Wolcen and start playing until patch 1.1.0.8. I have 17 hours in, I am a level 27 character focused on Arctic Spear and can honestly I am very impressed. I am only going capture a few bullet points here with the intent of writing a full review later.The GOOD:the most visually stunning aRPG to datecombat - dodge roll, right out of the box. Puts the "a" in aRPGskill progression via skill levelling and modifiers (no cookie-cutter builds)character attribute spending and respec (like how it's directly tied to dmg).Gates of Fate (passive skill tree) - well thought out to encourage build diversityBloodtrail - really nicely integrated into story campaign (love the modifiers)The BAD:The CRYENGINE will be very hard on systems more than a generation from today's hardwareBugs - while I have only encountered 2 (one really a QoL, one a defeated boss not recognized 1st time around)Long cut scenes, 1st time around you have to experience all the lore (and it is pretty good)Load times. I have a SSD, but new region loads can be lengthyCommunity Presence - since Bloodtrail, there has been a tremendous amount of hot fixes however you would not know it based on their forums as it appears there is not much sign of a community manager in several months

_childDocuments_.review: hi,I'm playing the game offline so I don't have much trouble with any lags but I understand that the game experience suffers much if you play online and you have trouble to control your char due to input lags.The game really had a rough start and I played it on early access, on launch and after the bloodtrail patch. For me, with bloodtrail the game feels like it should have been on release day. there are still some bugs (had a few crashes in  a certain area) and sometimes mobs don't feel balanced right but in the end I enjoy the game.I like the much darker atmosphere (graphics) more than in diablo 3 but this is just personal taste. To keep it short the game has the right mix for me between POE and D3 and I think that's where the devs wanted this game to be, in the middle of those both games. It has not the variety of a POE but still more to grind and experiment with while playing D3 where your char already feels finished after 20 hours and the skills are more streamlined. In the end I like all 3 games (POE,D3,Wolcen). For the moment Wolcen fits my taste because I can easily jump in and play for short sessions or even half the day without learning much about the mechanics and without routing your char before you start it. Just jump in and level the class how you feel it is right and this way it plays without any problems for me (lvl 64 dual wield pistols). In the end Wolcen was unfinished on release but has become an enjoyable ARPG since last update and I keep playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very poorly made Diablo 3 clone with none of the qualities of life implementations you would expect to see from a game like this.- Loot stats are RNG heavy to a point wheres stats do not make sense.- Mage has only 1 off-hand available to them and there is no main-hand specific to the mage. Equipping the main hand weapon like a sword or dagger actually gimps the mage class.- Loot on the ground disappears for some reason and you need to constantly hit alt to see what your missing.- The UI is ripped straight from Diablo 3 along with every active skill being the same. I guess they couldn't come up with any original ideas for skills.- Sometimes you cannot click on creatures to attack them but they can sure attack you.- As a Ranger, you miss 90% of your shots for some reason. Even point blank you will miss hitting the enemy.- The game graphics are terrible. Diablo 3 has much better graphics and animations. This game boasts detail but its just not there.- The passive skill system is a poorly done rip off of Path of Exiles passive skill system and the skill paths force you to take skills that are meaningless to your character.- Selling items you don't need to make money is a hassle. No mass sell button, 1-second delay when selling an item which turns what should be a few seconds tasks into minutes.- The Offline mode just means you can't play the game. When you click offline mode the menu options to play the game disappear and say "you are offline". Not sure what the point of that button is.- You cannot drop in play your friends multiplayer game. They have to back out. Join your group then you can play which sucks when you are playing and get disconnected from the servers and have to fully back out of the game so your friend can you join you again.- No options to teleport to your friends on the map you gotta run!- No trade options or loot sharing.- When trying to invite a player to join your group it's hit or miss if they will receive the invite.- Clicking to enter a dungeon or next level is awkward there's no indicator to where you are going and there is about a 5-10 second delay after clicking the entrance to go to next level where it seems unresponsive.- You cannot move around the mini-map and there are no indicators short of a little start to tell you where to go. The starter only shows up if its within a minimap view.- Sections of maps/dungeons are constantly re-used within the same map/dungeon making it very repetitive and tedious scenery within about 10 minutes of gameplay this is pretty obvious. I understand this is a common thing to do for devs but come on you couldn't design past 10 minutes of scenery really?- Devs raised the price of the game from 30 to 40 bucks USD. This is FAR from AAA title game and is very much still an early access game despite them trying to pass it off as a full-fledged game.Overall just a very disappointing game with no redeeming qualities.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretext: I LOVE the ARPG game style.  I have almost 6k hours in Path of Exile.  Another thousand in D3.  I try just about every game of the genre since Din's curse/FATE.  That being said,Wolcen is a letdown in several key aspects, and I cannot recommend this game if you're looking for anything more than going through the initial story and maybe an additional 10-20 hours of end-game gameplay.  If those are your expectations, great!  If not, beware.Pros:Great story!  I thoroughly enjoyed the writing, plot and execution of the campaign.  There is a lot of "charming" humor in the story and I thoroughly enjoyed it the first two times through.Graphics: pretty good.  A lot more detail than most iconic ARPGS.Co-op: party play is good and well balanced.  (Glares at Path of Exile...)Dodging - actually decent interactive gameplay as far as responding to enemy attacksCons:Character builds are shallow end-game, and mechanics are bleak.  For how simple it is, I'm surprised it doesn't just hand you a build like the set bonuses in D3.Controls/Gameplay: Controlling your character doesn't feel good.  the aiming and targeting system just feels clunky and leaves a lot to be desired.  They even have their own targeting system, and a "classic targeting" mode in the settings.  Both feel bad.Design/Theme: (warning: bias) Looks very "Warhammer-y" - seriously, just look at the armour.  too many spires and spikes.  Nothing looks practical, and all of the combat animations look very forced and unnatural.  Not my cup of tea.  This was not how the game originally looked when I purchased it.Design/Theme pt. 2: When I bought this game, it was actually called "Umbra" - the name of the in-game mana (now called Willpower.)  Back in the Umbra days, the camera could rotate 360 degrees.  I understand that they removed this feature as it extended development time and graphical demand, while not adding much to the game.  I agree on this.  However, the game didn't make a lot of developmental progress and was pretty stagnant for about a year before (I think) a new team took over and scrapped all of the developed world and re-wrote/re-branded it to Wolcen and wrote the campaign.  This whole process took a year, then the game was released to Beta.  This whole process was VERY rushed and not transparent at all.I feel that what was gained in development progress was lost in character.  The original "Umbra" game, whereas it didn't have much of a campaign, had WAY more character, feel and charm.  That was the game I purchased, not Wolcen.  I would not purchase Wolcen today if I did not own it already.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential, but with all the ISO ARPGs coming out this year, there's a lot to compete with. That doesn't mean you have to overwhelm your audience with so many menu options and character customizations. Keeping it simple and intuitive - in my opinion - is way more compelling.1. The game already has great looking graphics and artwork going for it, but one thing I absolutely hate (for whatever reason) is when developers give me the flexibility of moving the camera around. I prefer it to be fixed and appreciate the art for what it is. Also makes it less distracting. This is primarily why I stopped playing (in additional to the grim-dawn-like complexity) ... it just got really annoying to deal with.2. Character models looked incredibly goofy when I was playing last and they looked disproportionate to the environment. We all like to gear up and marvel at our appearance like narcissistic sick **cks, but when my character looks like a lump of jello it really takes me out of the immersion.I appreciate the challenge the game has to offer...although, sometimes it is a little unforgiving when you die, get respawned far away in a city not even close to where you were, and have to walk all the way back to your death location and give that battle a second chance.Going to give it another try. Looking forward to future development.

_childDocuments_.review: So... Wolcen... Where do I begin. The gameplay is SOLID, your attacks carry a certain impact with them and your enemies are sent flying away. The game gives you certain freedom in customizing your character's abilities and appearance. However, when it comes to little details in the game that is where the fact the game is in early access shines through. First of all while the slider system in the character creation allows you to have huge control over the appearance of your character, it is greatly flawed. By which I mean you can make your character look a certain way and only that way otherwise your character ends up looking grosteque. When it comes into combat the game parades the depth of using environments in combat yet when using lightning in water I don't really notice any differences (other than this spark thing they do when they die). If anything it should electrocute the water... And me in it. This would add a level of strategic thinking when playing, adding depth and decision making in combat. Reading through what I wrote I can't help but feel I'm complaining about what I don't like and I think that is the case, nonetheless I do think such details would make the game better.adding to this, the first few spells you find lack variation. They either spray, shoot or laser your enemies. Thats mostly it. TL:DR/ conclusion They made a wonderful game with a wonderful engine and loving environments but when it comes into the nuances of a game there is much to work on. The game as it is now is not something I'd invest myself in but there is certainly a lot of potential for its growth.

_childDocuments_.review: So,  and  had a baby, then hired  to be its nanny. The result is . If you're a fan of either of the first two, then you won't find any real surprises, other than how well they've taken the strengths of each and leveraged them together here. Active skills are learned and leveled up, with additional features selected as you progress them (similar to ), while Passive abilities are selected via a "web" (similar to , but with the ability to rotate the three rings of the web independently of each other, thus making different paths easier to grow into). The addition of a dodge mechanic makes combat all the more active—particularly boss fights, which feel more like an MMO Raid.As I write this review, it's still the early days since launch. As many might expect, there have been definite problems with scaling the server infrastructure to match the number of people trying to play. This has resulted in disconnects and some lost data when syncing to the Online servers, and you cannot use the same characters between Online and Offline play. This also means that playing together with others can be problematic at times. However, I have faith that these initial issues will be sorted out soon, and we'll be left with just the gameplay, which stands tall on its own.I'm really enjoying the game so far. I'm sure I'll like it even more once I can reliably play with my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game some more, I am changing my review to positive. I originally gave a negative review based on technical issues at launch. However, it seems they have managed to patch it up well enough, at least with regards to offline play.About the game itself, this is essentially a linear action game with some RPG mechanics for levelling. It will send you through a number of corridor-like levels where you are supposed to kill everything with an impressive arsenal of skills and spells, and pick up vast amounts of loot, most of which will be sold off in town for a few gold coins. It is fun to play, and looks rather pretty. The RPG elements are very light, and there is not really much choice besides how to level up your character. The leveling is decent, if a bit overhelming in how many options there are. Going up a level is not quite as big a deal as in many other RPGs, but it does happen more frequently, and gives a nice feeling of steady progress.Original review:"I'm sorry to have to thumb down a game I backed on Kickstarter, and which I think is both gorgeous to look at and fun to play, but...it deleted my (offline) character and all progress I had made in the game. There is no manual save option in this game, and if I can't trust it to keep my progress, I am not willing to play it.EDIT: I managed to restore my character. After some research, I found out local characters are stored locally in JSON text files, and the file for my character contained a bunch of binary data which had overwritten part of the description of an inventory item. After removing the binary data and the damaged item, the game managed to parse the file and load my character. I will not change my review to positive until the numerous technical issues have been resolved, though."

Lastly (for now) I'd like to talk about the sound design and animations, they are AMAZING, I'd advise you (especially at the near end of Act:1) to pay attention to enemies animations and the sounds being created during battle.  I can tell, they put in a lot of hard work to make this masterpiece.  It's like they're trying to make the game ideally exactly what you would want it to be, feel, sound and perform like... almost perfect.  I'd like to review the game more after I complete it when it releases, but for now.  What are you waiting for?  Your journey to ultimate power awaits and your enemies don't sleep.  So get Wolcen now and become the god you deserve to be.

Personally, my grips stem from an inability of my character leaving the town after the patch because the teleporter despawned; therefore I am unable to finish the story quest without remaking. Almost half of my skills do not work properly (missing aoe buffs, missing talent buffs, missing element buffs, etc), which is utterly useless for my support build. There is almost no endgame content, and once you can beat 187, your progression is over and it becomes a grind for efficiency? (Which is redundant). And lastly, the skills that somewhat work have been nerfed to the point that they are useless, much like the other 90% of skills that simply dont work anyway. Overall, I would give it a 6/10, and that is only because the storyline and concept of character development and customization is fun. However, there are better games with similiar customization that dont carry the pricetags or bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid ARPG. Very well executed for what it does, which is standard. But it's a really good feeling and fun enough standard. If you're worn out on D3 or any other ARPG this will be a refreshing time.There are some inconsistencies with being able to auto attack target really small enemies like bats and rats, they also get stuck pathing in circles because their turn radius isn't small enough. So auto attack builds are really annoying against those kinds of enemies. But if you have AoE this doesn't feel like a problem.I've barely used the apocalyptic form, maybe pressed the button once. It just feels kinda out of place in an ARPG. Unnecessary. I hate having that feeling of, oh no i dont want to waste my cooldown...need to save it for a good spot....and then i just never remember to use it. No idea how to switch to other forms? Later in the game? End game?The potion and resource system is kind of interesting, it's a see saw that you can toy around with for min maxing builds. IDK, interesting to see what kind of ways to exploit it and tune it people find. For casual players it just feels like D3 resource system.So ya...good holdover game. Not that many skills in the game....but like they all have a bunch of modifiers and I think with the passive tree and unique items there's enough variety. Also the skills are really dialed in, they feel good. Ya, I'll see how it fairs in the long haul. The enemy density and game pace is lower than D3, but it might ramp up as I get more into the game. Hopefully it doesn't scale into number gobbledy ♥♥♥♥ like D3 does.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much an average game and no longer bad, but far from lving up to its potential. It started as a buggy, overhyped mess with major issues, especially with its online mode (which still to date make the game feel laggy, so if you do not plan to coop this game, jsut play it as local single player and not on the server). Despite the initial problems, the developers showed dedication and steadily improved the game over the years. While it didn't reach its full potential even now, Wolcen evolved into a decent ARPG, offering engaging combat mechanics and great visuals. Although it may not be top-quality, the game stands as a testament to the developers' commitment to fixing their creation. I have played the game thru almost every stage every alpha/ beta stage the game whent thru. i have seen this game completely change down to the very fundamentals, from small things like how the runes page used to look or how character screen had only two options, to stuff much larger for example we no longer have massive maps with random generated mini dungeons that hold what seemed then involving side mission or small tide bits of lore or even the campaign. or how there was a game mechanic called arena where you can due challenges to get awsome rewards there was even a  competitive dungeon mechanic where people compete on who completes it faster or how difficult they can make it.with that all being said here is my reviewPROS: - awesome sound track.-beautiful environments.-voice acted cutscene's and main campaign dialoge.-in depth character class system(wide varity of ways to play and make it unqiue to your play style)-(for now) no micro transactions. -its easy to learn hard to master and will become harder at launch.-beautiful AMTX visuals for abilities - end game does not involve prestiege farming (paragon farming in diablo, level in poe).CONS:-shallow game play( really only use two abilities)-shallow passive tree( to easy to being op and reach endgame status)-not enough content and no side quest making the game really shallow.(pre-launch)-they removed option to make a home( removed in the beta hopefully they being that back was kinda nice)-only three classes at start yet can only really start playing two of the three early on. UPDATES:(stuff will be included) -diablo skin system(♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥)-dozens of new skills -adding an additional endgame with challenges that have rewards worth getting.-a much more in depth character customization almost on a level of code vein( please read latest news to see more)if there is more they are adding please comment it down below.With that all being said my score will be a 7/10 its a good awesome game it looks really polished and i love being able to play how i want it and being able to look how i want, but even though it look and sounds awesome, the game is really shallow with being op and reaching late game status by the end of act 1, bosses being so easy i used only one ability to kill them, you will die far more often to enemy's than bosses, lack of exploration, there is no reason to explore because there's no mini dungeons and no events to get you side tracked for a bit. and on top of all that the tiers of gear is so shallow in difference the only thing making a red tier item or legendary different than a purple tier item(uniqe) is red tier has less stats than a purple tier item and that purple tier looks cooler.I know its  a mouth full of negitive stuff but dispite that its honestly a fun game and you have to start some where to make a game stand out and it honestly does, how will they make if this game become better or bigger in the future who knows i just hope they look at a proper competitor like grinding gear games(devs of poe(Path Of Exile) and not blizzard(devs of diablo series). thank you for reading my review i hoped it help and i hope you have a awesome day.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is unofficially still in Early Access. I gave them some time (more than a year) since I last tried it, and it still suffers from the same issues.I will keep it short and simple:- Combat clunky and unintuitive. Animations, sounds and general feel are good, but it just doesn't flow. No diehard ARPG fan likes left-click attacking that is also your movement button. It's precisely the reason why moving around enemies feels so awful. And that's just one of the issues.- Variety is a myth. Looks to me that this game could really use a serious overhaul of the skill system. It's so basic in its nature, even if it's unusual and "new", but it's so easy to decipher but on the other hand also confusing (or rather obscuring) af. You will find yourself building characters that all feel the same, with just different shiny explosions you throw at enemies. The fine distinction between how a melee character and a mage are supposed to feel is just not there. And seriously, I really dislike resource management in this game.- Map orientation is confusing with huge icons that make no sense and give you a false sense of where you actually are. This has always bothered me so much and it's still there.- Performance-wise I haven't had a problem on my part, but I also only ever play Offline Mode. Some crashes the last time I played it, but in my last short session I had none. Maybe I haven't played enough to notice much.Summary:Overall, the game feels rushed and unpolished. Polishing a game is not just about looks, as this one does look really pretty, but it fails to deliver in other aspects. There's so much to be filed on and improved upon. The state of the game reminds me of "Vikings: Wolves of Midgaard" levels of quality. Both games suffer from pretty much the same problems. Right now, I cannot recommend this game as a contender for any other popular ARPGs.
