So I changed to the mage (the one that fits the story) and suddenly I was overpowered...There are lots of ways to change and improve your character during the game (armor, weapons, huge skilltree, spells and allignements)The ending is a bit disapointing (story-wise and action-wise), but overal I had a blast playing this one.If you like arpg's, give this a try (as mage). _childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since its Early Access days. As reflected in the Steam user review ratings, it has been a rocky road for Wolcen Studio and their flagship title. I've played it off and on since very early in its development. I've seen it go through some major changes and overhauls. The game we have today resembles the original very little. At one point you could even build your own house to display your trophies. It seemed that Wolcen didn't know which direction to go.  They wanted a dark and grim fantasy world ARPG. Hardcore gamers themselves, they wanted to make what they thought Diablo 3 should have been, a lofty and admirable goal. It took them some time to figure out what the fans wanted, but they did, and now it finally shows. This is one of those titles that would have been better off waiting for full release rather than making it available in early access, since current ratings reflect earlier stages of the game. It's a win for players, but the devs take it by way of long-standing negative reviews that remain long after they become irrelevant.  What we ended up with here seems like a compromise between the dev's vision and what the fans wanted. The game is much more like D3 than the devs would probably like to admit, right down to the voice actors and their lines.  ,who apparently does all the female lines in every video game now, is still "unstoppable!"   A little history out of the way, the game is currently a solid ARPG experience that fans of the genre are sure to love. If you were disappointed by the early state of the game, now is a great time to dive in and start working a build. A big endgame update is on the way this month, offering 4 new game modes, and I'm excited for that.  What makes Wolcen different from D3, Grim Dawn and PoE? The classless build system. You choose a starting weapon and from there you can adapt your build however you like. Stats are determined by items, equipment and gear. You get your 10 attribute points per level, and passive skill points, to allocate however you like. Certain gear set-ups allow you to hybridize and optimize across different skill sets. You can use both magic and melee if you want. And you can switch it up at any time. This allows for an unprecedented level of freedom in your build. So far I've made a Void Witch, a Toxic Assassin, a Blood Baron, a Holy Crusader, a Pyromancer, and more, some of them from the same character. Skills and abilities have real impact, they feel nice and weighty, very satisfying to play. Certainly there is a difficulty curve between mobs and bosses. Clearing mobs is no indicator of your ability to take on a big boss. While I haven't had to grind over already tread paths, the option is there if you need it. If you falter at the bosses, it is 100% your build, which is easily remedied by grinding and/or trying something different. The latter is not easily achievable, if at all, in other games in this genre. In Wolcen, you can switch up gear and tweak stats a bit, and voila! a whole new class to try without starting a new character. The game looks amazing, built on CryEngine, it is more detailed than any top-down isometric I've ever played. It is truly stunning to explore the different environments. The gameworld is a work of art, and the 3D models for everything from gear to actors are no less aesthetic. This is a labor of love and it truly shows. If you tried it before and walked away with a bad taste, try it again, you will be pleasantly surprised. Wolcen is a must-play for any ARPG fan.*My ReShade preset

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a 5/10. This is a very Diablo-like game but doesn't really meet the bar for the genre. A lot of the abilities and movement are clunky. The pathing on some of the spells and warrior abilities is terrible. You can be facing and enemy and your character will randomly turn the opposite way and hit nothing. There is a glaring lack of fluidity between skill chaining. Its almost like their is a passive global cooldown that exists between all action whether it be combat abilities, healing, dodge rolling, or just moving. The boss fights are very unrewarding. I enjoy high difficulty games like Nioh, Soulsborne series, Sekiro where the fights are very high difficulty but also high reward. Wolcen fails hard in that area. It seems like the developers tried to hard to make a challenging game and just ended up making it frustrating and unrewarding. A lot of the fights are just unpredictable cluster$&#@s of endless waves of units while dodging 1 shot mechanics. Its just cluttered and there is no real enjoyment to the fights.The story is not that impressive either but that's not too big a deal since these types of game are normally combat focused.I don't really find there to be much in the way of viable customization for your character. When i first started the game and saw the talent point system and all the different abilities I was hopeful. But  as i progressed It seemed to me like there are a total of 15 abilities in the game. That's it. They are divided by weapon and class type which means that you are limited in the skills you can use depending on your playstyle. All in all i am very disappointed in this game. If you like games like this i recommend Path of Exile, Diablo, or Grimdawn. They do it much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is a great game. But this is only true in single player (online) and even then not always. The game is totally immature. If you play a run on 150+ it is a no-go to do it together with other players. Although the game is actually made for it, it doesn't work at all anymore.I have a more than sufficiently performant PC and also my internet connection is very good, but the lags always kill the game.  Reliable. The game is fun when it runs. But as soon as a lot of enemies appear on the screen the danger of crashing is always present. That gets on my nerves and is a reason why I slowly lose interest in the game.Shortly before a stage can be completed a bug appears. No matter if you are suddenly teleported to an infinite chessboard, an opponent who is not strong enough to kill you but still hits you infinitely and you can't get away, a superlag with slide show until your own death, sudden messages "Your group has been defeated", etc. Unfortunately the game is still too much fun for me that I let it stay until now. But much is really not missing any more. The developers should release a release that removes these real game-breakers as soon as possible. Whether a bleeding edge build is too strong or too few uniques that are also usable should not matter at all. Please fix this game and make it run permanently without all the bugs and crashes. Everything else is unimportant at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10Apparently abandoned by the developers. I bought it on sale for like 5 bucks and enjoyed the story so far. It's fairly easy to switch between skills/builds. Visuals are good, gameplay is good. The skill tree borrows a bit from PoE, but is more convenient to use because it doesn't have generic Dex/Str/Int nodes. I didn't encounter any bugs, but am playing Singleplayer in offline mode. Not sure if Multiplayer works as well. Enemies could be more diverse from area to area in the story, and the movement speed is a bit too low for my taste. Side content is clearly indicated, which looks a bit lazy but is more convenient from a gameplay perspective. I eventually stopped playing mid-story because swapping builds is too expensive mid-story.Overall recommended for a small change from the usual grind in PoE/Diablo, but as always, at some point, it will turn into more of the same, and once you reach that point, the game is dead. No devs, no players, no community.

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy and dull.  Needs quality of life improvements like nobody's business.  I personally think the skill system is poorly executed.Edit:  Just to emphasize a key complaint with the game, I have to say that the "classless" system is incredibly misleading.You don't have a class in the game, yes.  However, the idea of pairing this with a system that limits what abilities/skills you can use based on weapon type is INCREDIBLY contradictory.  The current system is actually far, far worse than if you had to pick a ranger or warlock or any of the psuedo-classes on the [incredibly boring] skill tree.  Want to be a paladin? Tough. No spells for sword users.  Magic archer? No spells for bows.  Monk? No attacks for staves.  And the skills that you can use are all dull.  The rune system is dull.  The back-and-forth resource generation that should be super interesting is dull.  It's all "Wolcen: Lords of Beige".  What a waste of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This review really should be a neutral, the game has come a long way since its alpha and they have made a very fun experience with a solid core and fun combat. The single player offline mode is working well and I haven't ran into any major issues with it, though there are still minor bugs that can be frustrating that require you to restart a boss fight or have to back out to the main menu to fix map clipping, which can cause you to fall through the world. However be warned that the online component of the game is a disaster at the moment with the servers having sever issues when I was trying to play with my friend. There also tends to be the occasional failed to create game session, which I assume is due to server spots not being available. Anyway long story short if you love ARPG's and don't mind playing the single player offline while waiting for the multiplayer to get fixed then get it, but if you want multiplayer then I recommend waiting and purchasing it when its all fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to post a thumbs up, but really this game is right on the fence for me, even having bought it on sale. While the story gets a lot of positive comments, I found it pretty up and down. Act II was quite good.It does have some promise, and a few things it does quite well:-The voice acting is generally top notch-The mix and usage of spells is generally pretty interesting- most of the cut scenes are well doneIn the end though, most of it is just so-so.  I didn't lose a character as some did, but I did experience a few notable bugs. At one point my shared gear chest was wiped out.  Frustrating, but frankly most of the gear especially at low/mid levels is just eminently replaceable.  The other bug was that all my spell effects and enemy spell effects seemed to disappear entirely around 1 hour of continuous play.  I didn't test it enough to confirm that it was time based, perhaps it was just certain issues with Act II / Act III, but it did seem to happen around 1 hour both times (which highlights that most of my play was short sessions)Most of the higher quality gear I did get I bought off a vendor, with only very few drops in 16 hours that were worth keeping, and none that were powerful enough to convince me to change builds.I think my biggest frustration as I transitioned into the end game is the shared move/attack for mouse movement was a real problem (for me) on some maps because of uneven map desigh and mob clustering.  Dodge + movement based spells became more reliable to make sure I was moving when I needed to, even if burning them just to move was not particularly ideal.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable ARPG.Anyone who's played other such games will instantly recognize many elements, yet they're all handled slightly differently. A talent grid similar to Path of Exile, but much more manageable; skill modifies like Diablo 3's runes, but more plentiful. All skills can be learned, though their usage is tied to equipped weapon types, and while the game does seem to favor hybrid builds due to the Willpower/Rage resource tug-of-war mechanic, there are ways to make more pure character styles - just perhaps not until you work through the talent grid a bit.As someone who doesn't care for the Titan Quest/Grim Dawn talent system, and doesn't care to rebuild and relearn my characters in Path of Exile every time I go back to try and play it, Wolcen is a fantastic option. Don't regret the purchase at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game and it has a lot of potential. The free character development (when it works) and art style are awesome. I typically cut a lot of slack to indie devs and try to be understanding. Unfortunately the numerous severe bugs are too much to bear on this one. The biggest one I've encountered is; I've tried beating the final boss of the story 15-20 times and it bugs out every time (even post patch 1.0.5.0). So, I can't even access the "end game" mode. I'm tired of wasting my time on this game. This game is a complete mess of bugs, some of which are game breaking. I've encountered several major and minor bugs including but not limited to; UI mouse clicks not registering, movement and skill mouse clicks not registering leading to deaths, hard crashes to desktop, characters spinning when leaving dungeons, skill tree nodes not doing anything, bugged final boss fight (making the game unbeatable), audio glitches were sounds get stuck in loops. These are just the bugs I've personally encountered. There are several other critical bugs being reported such as character resets, story progress resets, loot tables getting stuck at X item level below you, mobs and items disappearing, etc. These are just unacceptable for a full released game. I'm giving up on this title for now. Maybe I'll come back when they fix it, but I doubt it. I wish I could get a refund, but after slogging through 25+ hours of "meh" story mode game play and bugs I'm stuck with it. I'm very disappointed because this game could have been something special to rival the competition.
_childDocuments_.name: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so confused about this one, really. It's beautiful, it has a certain grittiness that we've longed for and seems to check a lot of boxes, at least for me. I've played a bit from the alpha, previous beta and now this one. To be honest, the only game-breaking bugs I've experienced are from this beta. I'll start with the bad stuff first, since that's the only point of testing things out, anyway. - Clunky pathfinding that sometimes, miraculously, teleports me into a wall or some terrain obstacle with no way to unstuck myself. Haven't tried with the teleport skill since I didn't have it at that time. Once, it happened when that Soul Demon ( or not sure what the name was ) boss thing at the end of the expedition ported me via his bone-grasp-prison-thing and just dumped me in a gooey snot-egg and left me trapped. I died, of course, 3 times, not being able to move and target him. Which leads to the second bug that pissed me off more than once ...- Targeting. It's like every other expedition - the big boss at the end can't be targeted. Sometimes, even, the beams and projectiles pass through him with no hit indication or damage floaters. While he's just standing there damaging me. Then, the spells and attacks would do some damage, then they'll stop and that leads to a 20 minute fight where half of the time I can't target him. There's also no health bar on the top of the screen. Only when the spells hit, and the damage is shown, does his mini-health bar appear, giving me some hope that eventually, we'll get there. - Which is hyper frustrating, because most of these bosses, and mainly those Alpha Sivirs, hit like a hadron-collider powered mack truck. Then they spew their poison all around them and a melee char could be insta-gibbed. Also, there's a beam from one of the Soul Demons again, that can't be dodged and I'm pretty sure it's a bug again. It just STICKS on my char and follows me with the speed of light. I'm sure it's not intented, because it looks absurd and ridiculous, since the boss gives no indication that he's targeting me. - I've respecced through a few generic builds, but there's nothing special to be seen here. Why is the third wheel removed? Am I remembering it wrong, or was it available in the last beta? - Loot. The most important thing in a game like that. For now, it's also the most disapointing and frustrating. As far as I understand, the focus of this beta phase is to test some replayability aspects, which for me - logically - could be achieved with a higher loot diversity. I've had one legendary drop that seems no different from a random rare. I can't try out different chars and builds, since I got like one or two good drops. Buying stuff from the vendor constantly makes respeccing a chore, and financially impossible, so ... - The skills and spells themselves look cool, they have IMPACT, there's a certain satifsaction from blasting mobs away with fireballs or shattering them into frozen bits and so on. My bet is, we'll get some pretty cool-looking stuff as far as spells are concerned. However, the leveling system is a bit of a downer. Most of the time you get to choose from ''more damage'' or some other less important stuff that's almost always going to be ignored. I don't feel any diversity here. At least we've got some different types of damage and, I guess, ailments that go along with them. Which are cool, by the way, I've rarely seen such gorgeous looking way of shattering of mobs.  - Crashes. I get them all the time, not sure if there's something wrong on my end. Probably not. I'd really like to see more contant, to get a hang of the world and the act/quest aspects of the game. Apocalyptic forms? Would be nice to check them out. I won't regret buying it, I even recommended it to some folks, heartedly, yet I don't see myself playing much of the game if it's just a diablo 3 clone with flashy visuals and spells. Still has the air of a tech demo about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Steam once again couldn't take long texts...TL;DR: Wolcen: Lords of Mehham is not worth it, it still feels like a BETA product, as it's so shuddily built up, alongside the 4 years of development hell, it's basically a Duke Nukem Forever situation, but as a small studio, probably have to fix the game before they can begin on another project, as it's just so uninspiring, unoriginal, and lack of overall view about the game as a whole. Never recommended at full price, or 50%, instead go for a cheaper price at current state, and possibly  future state. Actually also makes Warhammer 40K: Inquisitor Martyr seem good, considering that also has its fair share of problems...Wolcen: Lords of Mehham, a game that was initially called "Umbra", but later became what it is now. A shallow instant gratification "ARPG" with a lot of items being thrown at you just to seem like a good game. Even from this 1.8 hours of gameplay, I encountered a lot of what I expected... graphical errors, unfinished character creator, missing and/or wrong/missing words in subtitles, ranged attacks (for bows at least) seems to attack from behind your character and seems to prioritse attacks from your character's right side, a lot more I'll uncover...As I mentioned, the character creator features barebones, redundant character creator, as if it was just slapped together to feature a character creator. It has all what you need to clarify it is unfinished, by using male portraits of options like hair, face model option window button, and a colours of some few things. The character creator is also pretty much redundant, seeing as you'll basically never see your character's eyes, face or hair... It's go for it, or make it bare with either a male or female, and that's it, not feature SOME things that quality for bare minimum character creator.As I said, subtitles can be inconsistent, as usual for this day and age... but I do have a problem disappearing immediatly after death, which just feels like it's for optimisation of the game, but just goes to show they focused on the art, rather than the gameplay.Abilities are activated immediatly upon clicking or pressing assigned button... which can and will result in a waste of ability (cooldown), unlike in Grim Dawn, where you'll be in range (your character moves close to the enemy) to use them before it's being activated.The pacing... is comical, ranging from a serious to boombastic change, as if there was no thought put into to process on how things should change, it did give me a good laughter however.Hitboxes/clickboxes are a large issue, ranging from annoying to frustrating, where large enemies will be easy, whereas small targets running around spastic making them hard to hit, and can force you to use AoE when not actually necessary.Online elements are present in offline mode... like a warning saying "an event is about to start, do you want to wait for other party members?" or something like that, when you're offline...As I mentioned with the ranged attacks starting from behind your character, this can be an issue when you need to focus an enemy down, because your projectiles which should've launched from the point of your weapon... are launched from your elbow? Why do bows act like rocket propelled grenade launchers? This is an issue when you're surrounded and need to take an important enemy down.Another issue is when you need to use your health potion, which is default assigned to Q, at times when you press your designated health potion, it will not be used, which makes a minor panic to you in terms of needing that health potion urgently.The sheer lack of context is insulting, explaining barely anything of what options do, "Auto-dash", what does it do? Make your character run? No, probably auto-roll on dodge? No. What it does is immediatly launch yourself toward your enemy with melee attacks. Context are also severely missing in the settings menu. Who was responsible for this?! It's been early access for 4 years! And it's like WOLCEN Studio has learned nothing of testing and questioning users about what things mean!And the classic good old missing models... what were supposed to be tree stumps on the ground, are just floating discs of the inner wood whilst missing the bark... UI loss of focus, how does this happen? This is usually something for the desktop where you have multiple windows, Wolcen should focus on one thing when you open a window, example: The inventory window can and will lose focus, having you to click on it, so you can what you wanted to do in said window.Weapons: The pistol is wielded on your main-hand and a melee on the off-hand, which is weird, seeing as the character you play as seem to be a right-handed person, which would mean most of their trained hand would be focused with better strength, this would mean they should wield the sword on their dominant hand (right hand) and the pistol on the left hand, as the pistol has a constant power.And to top it off with... the classic Crash to Desktop, which just happened because of whatever reason, I was just using the ability window to upgrade my teleport ability, and all of a sudden crashed...To end it all with... Wolcen: Lords of Mehham was not ready to be released, it still feels like it's in BETA in terms of quality assurance of the product, and it's basically just an instant gratification "ARPG" which is just so bland that you can turn off your brain like you'd watch TV.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential, but there's too many issues that really ruin the experience for me.  The first issue is unresponsive ability and potion buttons. The potions are also used up way too fast, only a few uses and they empty.  Which killing enemies refill them, but still it's a pain during boss fights, where you pretty much have to spam potions.  Then there's the massive balancing issues that exist.  Bosses have virtually no cool down on ANY abilities, which would be fine if there was enough damage mitigation or dodges, there isn't.  Many times a boss will have half the field covered in persistent aoe and then starts throwing cleave after cleave with zero C/D.  The cleave on it's own takes 1/2 to 3/4 of your health.  During this madness where you have almost nowhere to dodge, there's infinite ads that either do ranged aoe or crowd you so you can't move on what little space you have left.    The final issue is load times and lag.  The game takes forever to load in, I'm talking like go make dinner and come back and it might be done.  Then the lag... I run way more graphic intensive games on my pc with absolutely zero problems.  This game tends to bog my pc down even after adjusting graphics settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I think that the negative backlash for this game's issues is completely overblown and while I don't disagree that there are plenty of bugs and issues the developers need to fix very quickly, the underlying game is excellent and is worth supporting and waiting a little longer for. The developer team is full of passionate people that want this game to be a long term success and when I see people refunding the game because there are some bugs, I have to question their mental state.Anyways, on to the review.Story: The game's story follows your main character and the characters around it that are each given some time to develop and understand their motivations. So far there hasn't been any moment of the story that feels jarring or undeserved and while not being the most engaging story at all times, it has set in place an excellent base line for future lore and I am looking forward to how the story progresses. The voice acting is excellent and there are a number of cinematic choices that work very well for the game.Gameplay: Currently, this is a mixed bag but I can see the future being bright. Magic and melee skills are incredibly satisfying and diverse, giving the option to mix and match skills as long as you have the required weapon type or an item that allows skill use without the associated weapon type. But sadly, the ranged skills are currently lacking in choice and in satisfaction. The skill you get when creating a ranged character shoots multiple projectiles but does not have target seeking AI which almost all other ARPGs have implemented for multi-projectile skills. I found it more efficient and fun to just use the normal attack until I found an area of effect skill that vastly out-performed the first skill. Monster packs are very literally 'packs' of monsters that seem to be quite far apart even at endgame, making the fluidity of combat feel a little off. That being said, the groups of monsters tend to be well organised into few large monsters that hit hard and take longer to kill and smaller monsters that die quickly and are numerous. It's a good balance but I'd like to see the density increase as you gain character levels.Customisation:There is plenty of customisation to be had for your character in the form of the passive skill tree, skill modifiers, limited but effective crafting systems and appearance customisation with armor dyes. These all feel great already except for the main form of customisation, the passive skill tree. There are currently big issues with nodes not functioning or providing false values that can make this area of the game unsatisfying. But once they have ironed out the issues, this should be an incredibly rich part of the game.Graphics:Beautiful. Probably the best looking ARPG on the market. Buuuut if you have a lower end system (5+ years old), be prepared for some framerate issues in some areas. Personally, I've had to dig into the game files and lower some of the values manually to get to a playable framerate so I hope that the game can be further optimised in the future or even be given more effective graphical options.Overall for me this is a solid 6/10 with current issues and probably 9/10 if they fix the issues and do it well. As I mentioned before, the bugs are numerous and this should be treated as buying an early beta version but it's an incredibly promising game and I would like to see it succeed in gaining momentum as the underlying game deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily guided and scripted early game play. I just want to go kill monsters, level, and get gear. I could seriously care less why the monsters need to die. I am not playing ARPG for story, dialog, and cut scenes. This is why I love Grim Dawn, you don't need to follow the story.Original review:So far the game feels good. I am hoping that the game will give a high replay value. It has good variation on the old style of arpg. The skills feel effective and can be freely modified with more and more options as you and the skill levels. The resistances and most stats are done in an interesting and diverse way. The armor is not restricted to class type like some other games. I am free to be a caster and wear heavy armor. This is due to how the base stats on the armor works. There is no "armor" stat, physical resistance is not independent of other damage types.I have seen very little that I dont like. which is saying alot, as I am generally very critical of games. One small thing that stands out is health orbs dropping from enemies. I dont like how this feels and prefer to use potions to restore health. Hoping to use mods to remove this mechanic in the future.I also find that I dont really enjoy the transformation into a super amazing primordial thing. I grow all fancy and pretty and get new super skills. While this looks really good, and maybe even sounds good in principle. I find that being thrust into new skills and being invulnerable for a short period to be distracting and disruptive. I am building my character with the skills I want to be effective at killing enemies and bosses. Why would I want to transform into some super ultra thing? Thankfully this is not a forced mechanic. I will try to learn to use it more, but I expect it will be something I ignore.Still a long way from the end of the game and Ive only played as a caster so far.

_childDocuments_.review: [As of writing this review, I just finished Chapter 2]The game has potential, shouldn't have been released yet though. It's fun, challenging and fast paced. Most of the time. The skill system is somewhat simple but unique, has a lot of similarities to Diablo and Path of Exile though. What's not simple is the defence system. Nobody ever explains to you what differnet defences do, there are like 8 kinds of resistances which is very overwhelming for a new player, so many stats on items that are super confusing and don't seem to make much sense at all etc. The bosses very challenging, which is a good thing. What's not a good thing is, that the bosses aren't challenging for themselves but the hard thing is dealing with the ads they spawn. They bodyblock you, screw you over because you roll into them or they just straight up kill you. I have found so many gamebreaking bugs already that I wouldn't be able to list them all in this review, and I only played for 5 hours. Some enemies are untargetable and still damage you and you have no way of dealing with them, sometimes you roll into some rocks and you're just stuck there and have to restart the mission, some enemies pull you and no matter where you stand they will hit you, even if you're way outside the pull range (you can stand behind them and they'll still pull and stun you), the health potions have a delay so often you'll just die without being able to use the potion because of the input lag and sometimes they give you life, then retract that life for a second, then give it to you again so you have a small window where the potion didn't have any effect ... (too many to list)The movement system in this game feels very bulky and unpolished, you sometimes attack when you just want to move somewhere, the passive tree seems very underwhelming and some nodes don't seem to work properly, selling items is a pain because you sometimes have to click 4 times for it to sell the item and the shops are just straight up useless. They're just there to be there, not to actually sell you anything useful. I'll continue playing this game for a bit but if it doesn't see polishing and HUGE fixes I'll probably quit until the game is ACTUALLY released. I wouldn't recommend playing it as of now.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start out by saying I am new to the Action RPG genre, and having little to no experience in the genre I rather enjoyed my time playing Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem. Before starting I saw the mixed reviews and was not sure what to expect, but right from the early going I was delightfully surprised to like and even be impressed with many aspects of the game. The game play was fun and I was kept mostly engaged throughout the story. Wolcen isn't the most challenging game even on the harder mode, but I didn't find this to be a drawback. The end game does become repetitive but still offers ways to up the challenge. The combat was solid and even in the end game it was still fun mowing down endless hordes of enemies. There are many enemy types and some have a really cool design to them which helps keep the game fresh. There are many types of weapons and spells to choose which all can be tweaked to your own liking to better suit your build. The perk tree is massive but doesn't feel overwhelming, you can even rotate the perk tree to allow even more customization to your character. You can make some really OP builds and there are a lot of possibilities. I enjoyed the story even if it was a little cliche and predictable, but it had some depth to it and was on the longer side. Some parts of the story were hard to follow but still in the end I was satisfied. The graphics were a strong point of the game. From the cinematic like cut scenes, to the detailed environments and enemies, its a pretty game. The music suited the game nicely and added to the medieval feel of the game. There were some parts of the game that reminded me of The Lord of the Rings which I thought was cool. That being said there were some aspects of the game that were inconsistent and held the game back. The game lacked polish in areas, there were some graphical glitches and audio glitches but nothing too severe. On occasions a piece of loot could not be picked up off the ground. I did experience infrequent crashing though the game did a good job of keeping your progress. Some parts of the game like the hub area and project map felt a tad bleak and lifeless. There is an online component to the game with an related achievement that allows you to play Co-op, but that feature will be removed September 17th, 2024. The price is fair for the quantity and quality of the product, though there are games in the genre that are free and many would argue better games. However these negatives weren't enough to deter me from liking the game and my time playing it. Wolcen might not be winning any awards for best in category but I still thought it was a good game and one I would recommend.

The only things I can really complain about are the fact that the bosses are mostly unbalanced versus the regular enemies. That needs to be addressed. You will feel almighty until you run into an Act boss, then you will proceed to be destroyed. I dont think the boss difficulty is unbalance tho, I think the enemies are way too weak and don't help you master the mechanics you will need to beat important parts of the game. The pacing for levels is pretty good tho. But one thing is that if you micromanage your gear, you will spend hal the game doing that, you hav to learn to let go of gear and just move on since there is so many pieces available that until the end its not all that worthy to socket them real good for example. _childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential.PROS-super sweet visuals-the physics are really cool-great spell effects and particles-great mechanics like spells being affected by the environment-gameplay feels fluid-great viarity of gameplay styles (the skill tree system is super cool and diverse)-dainly dungeons-housing system-very cool features that will be in game later on like socketing and forging weapons, as well as transformations and co-op multiplayer-Devs listen to the playersCONS (lots of these can be attributed to the early state of the game)-poor optimization-story hasn't been very interesting so far-bugs-crashes sometimes-rare weapons don't seem worth it a lot of the time as magic (blue) weapons often have better stats that outweigh the unique modifiers the rare ones do.There are loads of things I didn't mention but those would be the most obvious PROS and CONS.All in all most of the cons are due to the early state of the game and loads of new features are already planned and being worked on.

_childDocuments_.review: edit (24th feb 2020): playing with other players rely heavily on the host's hardware and how the servers act at the time. if you want to get a normal gaming experience all the time then don't buy this game right now. but in all the darkness there's still light. the dev team tries to make the player's experience always better and most of the time they find success. i still think that wolcen will be one of the best action rpgs on steam, on pair with grim dawn (imo)!mad edit (22th feb 2020): don't buy this game if you think about playing it with friends. skills are dsynced, bugs appear to get more and more the more the devs are trying to get rid of them and it just doesn't feel right anymore. it never felt right but at the moment it is just a mess. i'm sorry...i will remain the review on a recommendation cuz i still think that the devs can make it playable. don't disappoint me.pre-release review: wolcen is a pretty solid game with nice graphics, effects, gameplay and sounds, not gonna lie, but some things really lack in this game. here are some of them:- stiff point of view (not adjustable like zooming in and out)- sometimes you can't use skills (probably server problems)- sometimes you get stuck in place and can't roll and jump (with skills) through certain floors and pixels (probably also server issues)- if you revived a teammate you'll get stuck in place for 1-2 seconds- sometimes you can't see the stats when hovering over an item with the cursor- german, maybe other languages aswell, aren't correctly translated (one item i got has + damage to spells in german but the same one has + damage to attacks in english)- if you are in a group and already were ingame with character x and you go back to the menu to switch to character y then you'll still load in as character x- you can't change the key bindings for m1 and m2 (m1 = basic attack, m2 = main spell - i would love to switch my basic attack to another key. i often can't move out of a big group of enemies as a mage and i don't need my basic attack)- damage calculations of spells don't really make sense (spell x has 99-129 frost, 74-154 lightning, 0-20 aether and 20-26 sacred damage. switching lightning to sacred damage with a skill modifier makes the spell heavily occult damage biased but you get more damage when you go for elemental than occult damage. so sacred damage (occult) will get stronger if you're using elemental damage)suggestions:- npc who rerolls one stat of each item (like in diablo 3)- training dummies in the city would be awesome to test build changes- a search bar in the gate of fates (to find the bonuses you want to have)

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is graphically a great achievement in the ARPG genre.  The gameplay feels visceral and carnal.  There is nothing better than seeing a monster explode into pieces as you crunch through them with a weapon.  From what I've played of the story I can't wait to see all of it, sadly with not a lot of time to play games these days I'll be waiting to play until the multiplayer is available.  These types of games interest me the most when I can play with my friends and show off the fun builds we designed.  As for the launch of the game with multiplayer, I'm guessing the developers weren't expecting their game to get so much traction going into the launch.  Even IGN wasn't promoting the game and it still managed to rake in thousands of ARPG fans the first day.  Servers are actively being worked on and the developers have been very open as to where they are in getting them fixed.  It's been years since I've seen the launch of a new IP have perfect online support day 1 or even by the weekend.  Kudos to the Developers for including an "offline mode" so people can play if they really can't wait for the multiplayer support.  Definitely a game I'll be sinking a lot of time into once the "online mode" is active.  As for now I'd give the game a solid 7/10 with no multiplayer available.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good graphics- A few decent skills- Skills got a moderate amount of customization (but also a lot of %x damage or crit etc)- Really good graphics- Most one shot skills from mobs are telegraphed so you don't get poe'd- Gold/currency actually matters and you got a base to upgrade which gives some benefits and promotes trading- End game activities show stats, like your damage/healing/damage taken etc.- Passive skills are fun, not great but okayMeh:- Items got a decent amount of modifiers but they are not very interesting- Additions to the one above, uniques are not that interesting aswell- I like the primary weapon skill (basic attack) because it has decent animations and actually useful but you can't disregard it or modify in any wayCons:- Too few skills, like not even close to PoE or even Diablo games- Too many copied skills from other arpgs that are not interesting at all- Movement/Dodge skills and potion usage do NOT override your other skills which is very stupid because that gets you killed a lot and makes fights very random- Campaign was extremely stale for me, had some moments but mostly a stale campaign that has the most common plot twists on any games/movies- Huge polish issues like game-breaking bugs (like I can't progress due a campaign bug) and imbalances all around the game- Unique rng can define your early game progress A LOT (i had a physical weapon drop as physical build and I used it for 25 levels without a replacement that is even close)- Lack of item crafting. There are some orbs to modify current items but you can't craft items from scratch (at least in campaign, as far as I know)*AS I WRITE THIS REVIEW, GAME HAS ABOUT %70 ONLINE DOWNTIME (including constant dcs/crashes during gameplay and progress losses) AND BECAUSE OF HIGH POPULATION SERVERS CAN'T HANDLE THE PRESSURE*Conclusion: I'd wait for some time before purchasing to see if they can get their s*** right. Otherwise there are much better alternatives out there. You'd have a value purchase if you see this on a -%50 discount though.ADDITION AFTER 119 HOURS OF THIS REVIEW: 1 end game build ONLY, people dupe currencies left and right and there are exploits to obtain uniques very easily. I'd certainly avoid this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. Yeah, it's got a couple of bugs, but so do many new releases and we love them anyway. Nothing that a quick log in/out won't fix. Yeah, it had some trouble with its servers at the start - and none for me since. Are we really going to fault an Indie game for being so good that it was too popular for its servers?I've been playing with my spouse and we LOVE it. Within 20 minutes we had vastly different characters, and he's switched his build entirely. The game is forgiving if you want to try new paths. I've stuck with my Ranger Bow build the whole time and am having a ton of fun. It's like Diablo 3, except with a good story and actually hard - the first *real* boss knocked us on our asses for a solid hour, yet every attempt was still *fun.* We didn't get angry because even though the boss is punishing, it rewards skill and teamwork.The classing system is deep but also approachable - basic descriptions help you pick things early on with the option to refine later once you have a better understanding of what's going on. And the ABILITIES! Speaking for my ranger build, the five I've selected are great fun and have great synergy for both single and multiplayer - marking targets benefits everyone, while my other skills let me deal massive damage AoE while my partner focuses on single target.The characters are engaging, the voice acting is on point, the story makes me want to know more (even if I'm a little confused about what's going on right now), and it made me feel a few feelings - things definitely not true for other games I've played like this.All and all, fantastic first experience with it - can't wait to go to sleep so we can get up and play more tomorrow morning!

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm just over 60 hours into Wolcen, I've finished all 3 main story acts and I'm deep into end game with my dedicated spell caster, so I feel I can give a pretty good opinion and review of the current state of the game.Firstly I want to say the game has not had a perfect launch by any means, server issues and bugs have plagued the experience for some players and obviously tainted their experience badly. I am not one of those players, server issues are a pretty much staple with game launches these days so its almost to be expected but as long as the devs are communicating they are aware and patching aggressively to get things stable and fixed then I can forgive that, which is what they are doing. I also have not been effected by any serious bugs (character stash/progress deletion, etc) I've only experienced hilarious things like dying and having my body ragdoll around instead of res and ive had to reload my game or a game crash here and there. Nothing I would consider stopping me from recommending what is an excellent ARPG and again the devs have communicated and pushed patches to hot fix the bugs the community is reporting fast.I enjoyed the main story of Wolcen, its voice acting can be a bit cringe at times but I felt it was engaging enough for me to enjoy playing through for the first time. Once you finish the main story you move on to the Champion of Stormfall mode which is the endgame of Wolcen (Think Diablo 3 style Rift Running but with a unique twist) ..now.. I just want to say I have seen a few negative reviews that are talking about builds and that there is only one viable build or that spellcasting sucks or what ever and then I look at their time played or see them talking about how they didn't even make it through act 2.. and I just shake my head. ARPG builds do not come online until the endgame so at least make it their first please before commenting on this. Okay back to the positive..WOLCEN IS GORGEOUS, seriously.. the game is so pretty, the spell effects and lighting are awesome and I am absolutely in love with the art style! I love the aesthetic of the armours and weapons in this game! I find myself spending so much time in the Character armour customizer dying and making my character look as badass as possible, and so many times I've just walked a map edge just to get a look down at the little details. It's stunning.Wolcen definitely could use some extra polish in niche areas which I'm sure will come, things I'd like are deeper stat breakdowns for characters and Items, you definitely have to do some mob killing testing to see if an item or ability is actually doing what it says its doing sometimes because you cant see it on the stat lines but I don't know.. i don't necessarily hate doing this? also there are some imbalances on nodes of the gates of fate that I'm sure will get adjusted in time, but in my experience there seems to be a good amount of choice when it comes to build variety in this game! In the end Wolcen has definitely given me my moneys worth, and I'm definitely not finished with the game by any means, I'm really enjoying it. There are so many builds I want to try, gear to experiment with (I've only had a handful of uniques drop so far!) and expedition pushing to do!If you are a fan of your diablo style ARPGs then I don't see how you can look past Wolcen.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen is a hidden gem:It’s got a bunch of unique mechanics that make it stand out. The story is solid, with engaging cinematics and lore that pull you in. Like the ailments system, which means damage over time for some types. The crafting system follows the basic recipe of unique loot and gem socketing.The late game in Wolcen is tied to the story in a unique and interesting way. It had a rough start with bugs in the early access and 1.0 release, but don’t let that fool you.One of the best things about Wolcen is the character customization. You can use any weapons and armor, which means you can create all sorts of builds. The skill tree is interesting, and you can reset everything as you play (for a cost). So, if you start playing one way and don’t like it, you can change it up. This level of freedom is really nice.Furthermore, the skill system in is also flexible and in some cases unique. You can take a skill and change its damage type or even how it works. For example sunstrike-like ability for a caster could be changed into cold damage and/or a targeted location instead on caster. You can even add to that the ability to move it around. This was probably one of the first arpgs where I played as an ailmentalist mixed up elementalist wearing a mixture of mage, rouge, berserk and heavy plate(s)...Finally, despite some initial challenges and b-rated aspects it's a good contender in the ARPG genre. Developers should take a page from Wolcen’s strong points and look at the customization and player freedom. It's probably a good time to give Wolcen a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game and could tell pretty quickly there were a lot of red flags, especially for a 3.5 year old game. I wanted to stick it out and try to get my money's worth but I'm not sure if I'll ramp it up again to finish or leave it. It's unfortunately a general rule now that most games from low quality developers need a couple years of polish. This game needs about 8-10 more years if this is as polished as it's gotten from a namesake studio 'WOLCEN' after 4 years.  If you play enough video games you can tell which developers actually play their own games and which do not. Wolcen studios does not seem to play Wolcen, in its current state and maybe not ever. I'm not sure if anyone play tested the game in fact. It has some redeeming qualities but never before has a game just jerked at me to stop playing it as much as Wolcen has. I think I have finally given after 24 hrs. Was gonna try to make it through the last act (that was added later, after what would be a lackluster 3 original acts) but they decided to completely change the game in Act 4 and it's initially really not interesting looking. Acts 1-3 play normally like an ARPG with mission flow and were quite easy. On my first playthrough I managed to not die once and beat the Act 3 boss with my 2h melee build pretty easily. Then in Act 4 after 3 consecutive awkward frame drops and redirects with black screens with no other transition you are ported into a new game where you report a mission table and have to pay gold (why? i have money but why?) to unlock additional quests from that point on. It's a shame too because I really wanted to see my build 'through' before I put it down because I feel like after this many levels I've finally unlocked enough stuff to make the clunky hot mess feel fun and fast paced at least. Sigh. From here on out the review will transition to my pro/con list that I diligently kept while playing...///+++PROS+++\\\=Skill customization is a cool feature. Lots of options to tune and tweak your skills on the fly for free.=I don't care for Transmog really at all but I checked it out and it seems decent aside from buggy non loading textures (con).=Cinematics are underrated and can really help set scenes, break up gameplay, develop stories. They are mostly well done.=Damage conversion built in as a toggle to your baseline abilities is a cool feature to increase access to variety.=Voice acting in general is really well done in this game. It's a shame the gameplay doesn't match. Well done throughout. =Speed- I started having fun when I got my build juiced enough to leap everywhere and smash everything with high uptime on rage. Slow before that but that can be any type of RPG. ///---CONS---\\\=Vendor UI- accidentally buy something? Bummer. Pennies on the dollar to sell back. Not friendly to check out gear. Or accidentally hang out around if you are early game with no funds.=Portal system is really clunky. The first time I used it to return to the map I clicked on the waystone instead since the buttons are on top of each other and thought you just had to run back, which sucked. Then i tested it again and saw it's just poorly designed. =Quest rewards in mini dungeons pop up while you are still in combat and can't be closed without picking something while enemies wail on you and half of your UI is muddied up. =Often times the interaction buttons for multiple portals (exits next to mini dungeons etc) are right next each other and so large of an interaction range that you will misclick into the wrong place. =Stat allocation on gear. Wtf is going on in this game? One class gets HP, another resistances, another a health shield? It's so incomparable in general.=No movement speed on any gear except rogue gear. I found one pair of boots that were bruiser class and had MS for a short time that I used. Movement speed is such a great stat in any game and especially a slow clunky game like this, and yet the only class with inherent bonuses (on multiple pieces, helm chest boots legs) is rogue? Makes no sense. Again, did anyone test this game?=Chaining spells and attacks is a bit clunky and their appears to be no animation canceling.=Wonky scaling and rolls on items and quest rewards, often. Low level gear way out performing high level gear and quest rewards that don't scale so they usually suck even though they are supposed to be nice pieces.=The vendors and mission table guy talk smack if you wait more than 0.1 seconds on the screen without selecting anything any it's really, really annoying. Build an atmosphere I enjoy. Not one with a coughing dying woman in the background hacking up the same audio file lung every time i port back and the vendor pressuring me into hurrying. =Pathing is just bad. Enemies and NPCs can jump over walls with precision while you will constantly get stuck on corners and jump in place.=The Wolcen website sucks. Other games like Diablo or Grim Dawn have amazing online communities. Really limited information and interaction and poor UI.=The late game scaling on xp is obviously imbalanced, a sure tell of a game looking to waste your time with fake grind.=Poor stash tab UI. Drag and drop items is slow, changes tabs. Just throw the item in there. =Bad fixed camera. Not a fan of fixed cameras in general but don't also stash chests and boxes in hidden places when we were already feel like we have no neck. Rotate cameras.=Skill system makes no sense at the start. Random RNG drops from mobs and then if you look around you can also buy them...?=The dialogue between players and even alone is always jumbled and doesn't queue properly. The player cutting themselves off and moving on to the next line. Again. Play test. Anyone? Wolcen developers playing the game ever? Unlikely.=Inventory size is abysmal. The loot filter is meh and still you end up with a lot of junk constantly running you back to town.=The damage conversion is cool but pretty inconsistent. Sacred damage for instance, is on every melee ability but that's the only one I saw like that if you were to make a build around it. Would get less value from other skills with non similar conv.=This is apparently the revamped campaign but the transition from act 3 to 4 was atrocious and disorienting.=Mission table based game in act 4 where you pay to unlock quests with gold.=Difficulty curve is non existent. Not sure how the actual 'endgame' is balanced but I made it through act 1-3 with no deaths, killed Heimlock pretty easily and then got 1 tapped 3 times in a row by some random hero mob on my first expedition in act 4. uh what? it was so easy the entire time I wished for a hard mode available earlier or anything at all and then you get randomly tapped by some assassin mini boss.Compare the Pro cons.. I wouldn't recommend it for much more than 5-10 dollars. Even then, there's many better buys for that price range. I could list em off but they're everywhere. I might try to finish the campaign but this game is tough, not in the good ways.*EDITED* never went back to play this, never will go back to play this, much happier. bad game.

I have played Diablo 2, Diablo 3, Grim Dawn, Titan Quest, Path of Exile, Torchlight 1, 2, etc.I don't pretend to know the above games in detail, but I have played them for hundreds of hours combined.I won't go into details because they are not arguments but rather personal opinions.I can say that it took the best from each of those games, like captured their essence and combined it into one amazing game.Of course it's not polished, of course it's full of bugs, of course it has have issues. No, I'm not trying to defend them, they NEED to own up for what they did, at least they look like they're doing for now. But one patch a week it's not going to cut it, however it was quite a lot of improvement in the last one. It seems to be quite a popular opinion that just because they're a small team they weren't allowed to ♥♥♥♥ up so bad. But if you think about it, I'm pretty sure that most of us know quite bigger ♥♥♥♥ ups from quite larger companies. I'm not going to give specifics, I don't like to point fingers.So if bigger companies, with more experience, more money, more employees, more knowledge in the field, more of anything really. We are speaking about BIG studios and big corporations that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, and we STILL give them our money for their ♥♥♥♥-ups, but we're not going to help a new developer that actually has a chance of doing something good in the gaming world. What kind of a community are we ? I'm am sorry but this is my opinion and I stand by it. To clarify things: - I'm not in any way associated with this game, it's developers or so on, I just heard about it from a well known youtuber, I bought it and this is my opinion about the game and the dev team.- Do I think it's worth it £30 now ? Well... not entirely, I think you should wait one-two weeks for them to fix the game properly if you are the kind of person whom expects a smooth experience, otherwise go ahead.- I never experienced any gaming breaking bugs but I did experience a few, also the first chapter boss was buggy for me, I had to wait for the patch to be able to beat him, after the patch the fight was too easy.I don't know if it was because I would've learnt the entire fight or because a critical bug was preventing me to be able to kill him, but the boss one shoted me quite often, after the patch none what so ever. _childDocuments_.review: I cant recommend this game in it's current state. 25 hours played. Clunky combat, broken passives, and oh my are there bugs. Certain channeling skills have to much wind up and kill the fluidity of combat. Mouse targeting is just god awful. Hit boxes need to be fixed, some enemies can be near untargetable. Most of the time a simple basic attack is more than enough but those damn hit boxes are so small you cant target the things. Channeling skills (with the exception of the laser beam one) in this game just don't work with how they want you to play. Enemies have patterns and you have to be active and position around them. The fact that you're stuck in place waiting for your character to take a huge deep breath, hands in the air then pushing forward to then then do damage....... just feels so cluncky/slow. By the time I got to actually doing damage the Boss/Mob had already move and is pummeling me. Single target channels replay the animation each time you select another enemy. So if you try and rely on the mouse hovering over enemies to auto cast you can get stuck in a loop of doing not a damn thing. Because said enemy will move and you trying to chase around and oops you selected another... and another ... and another.Moving well attacking or using another skill in sequence can sometimes cancel out skills resulting in wasted resource. Pressing to many actions can CTD or main menu. Talking to Store Npcs and running away well using skills crashing. using  skills with interacting with things can cause the skill to act like its still being pressed down. Glitching outta the map in parties.Players already found what is op and so on in the passive tree. They've also found out that a lot don't work as intended, or flat out don't work at all.  I like the over all concept of the tree but seriously needs a fix. Server bugs and dupes. Constant disconnects Etc.Overall the game Isn't finished. Cool concept and it has potential, but it's just an overall poor release. Hold off on this game until the bugs are fixed and receives over all polish to its gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: A more powerful and immersive story than any other ARPG you'll find.-indepth skill system that gives you a lot of customization with both skills and talent points to toy with-fun combat as long as you're mage class-You level skills up akin to PoE skill gems except they don't have a dumb gem system, the skills are also insanely customizable at higher levels.-really dynamic fights, and you do have warning with attacks so enemies don't end up steamrolling you without consent-Voiced side characters that actually fight well, too bad they can't come for end game-A very comprehensive end game that is both customizable and feels like "The End is a New Beginning" with custom map modifiers, talent-like speccing for end game challenges and very challenging combatCons:-Some skills are useless until higher tiers, and therefore a pain to level -Weapons aren't all equal-I haven't figured out a need to make a melee or rogueish build because they're so clearly inferior-despite having the system recommendations the game still chugs a bunch, especially in later acts and endgameOverall I can tell a lot of work and love went into Wolcen. While they still need optimization work, it's a ton of fun to play as is. Balance is the main issue they face though.The fact I completed all 3 Acts without dying makes me think the Staff is the most unbalanced weapon. I had trouble with this game playing with ranged and melee weapons. Gave up. Restarted character with the Annihilation Beam and the Staff and just face-rolled the entire game. Seeing as only 3.3% of players completed act 3 without dying says a lot, probably staff users, I'm not sure though obviously.Otherwise, a lot of effort went into endgame and if everything is addressed the end game could be better than anything else that's come along for ARPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently gave Wolcen another shot after a three year break. Played through it back when it first released and saw that it had severe issues back then. They devs had several years now to address problems in Wolcen and finish the game properly as initially the compaign basically stopped suddenly after act 3 and just threw you into a boring endgame. Along the way the player encountered huge problems with balancing (bosses way overtuned, very few usable skills and so on) as well as technical issues.First let me state that I'm actually positively surprised that the devs didn't just take the money and run. They still worked on Wolcen trying to fix and finish the game. This is something I can actually respect. Unfortunately the result still is not good enough to justify a thumbs up. In terms of rating the game it would looks something like this:Act 1: 7/10 (pretty solid in terms of story and basic gameplay - my biggest issue is the gates of fate talent system which I absolutely hate)Act 2: 6/10 (still okay, but some technical and gameplay issues become more prominent)Act 3: 5/10 (the technical and gameplay issues become more prominent)Act 4: 3/10 (the game is just trash it this point again with huge balancing issues)So as you can see the game gets progressively worse the further you get into it. My gripes with the game in act 1-3 (which remain in act 4) are basically:1. The gates of fate talent system is basically a modified version of the Path of Exile talent system. I hate both systems because they are difficult to read and understand and overall force new players to use guides so they get a decent build. In terms of the concept you are apparently supposed to look for the "big nodes" in the tree that are essential to make your build work and which depending on the color of the notes usually synergize well with specific classes. The problems is that it's to much information in a screen all scattered around and most abilities you will not understand just by reading through them. In addition the abilitiy to move these wheels around creates way more options to combine thinks which makes it even more difficult for average players to grasp the system and fully utilize it. 2. Early on the gameplay is usually pretty fluent and straight forward. However the further you get into the game and the more abilities you find the more difficult it becomes to actually keep fluent movement as a lot of abilities and combinations require you to wait for animations to finish before you can do something else. The issue already existed at release and I heavily criticized it back then because even healing potions were bound to that. Luckily potions are disconnected from that now from what I was able to see which means you can drink potions while using abilities. Still as a melee using blade storm build it can become very annoying when you jump into a group of enemies use a shout and if you want to start spinning you have to wait for about 2 full seconds for the shout to complete before your character actually starts spinning. And it becomes worse if I want to jump in => shout => activate shield => start spinning. Usually my shield activiation gets completely ignored. I actively have to stop the attack press the shield at least 2-3 times to see it activates before I can resume my attacks. This is just unacceptable in terms of the combat behavior. This is especially the case in endgame when your character ends up in a ton of area attacks that sometimes kill you before you even have the chance to do anything because you're stuck in an animation...3. Technical issue - I've seen disconnects from the onlines service. I've seen animation errors where my abilities didn't show the animation anymore which required me to basically guess whether something hit or not. I've seen my character get stuck in the environment tons of times due to invisibles walls which btw. makes quick navigation through maps pretty bad.4. Dungeon design is very simple and usually consists of a few corridors where the path at times splits into two routes which then are being merged again a bit further down. You have sometimes minor side paths with dead ends. Some of those dead ends may contain optional bosses. There is basically almost no real interaction with the environment. You have some boxes lying around which you can destroy but those are specifically placed and are not really of the environment. Also in some fixed positions you may have something blocking the path which then will be removed through a static event. You can also always see whether something is a randomized or pre-made map. Every pre-made map ia already completely visible when you expand the map showing you the complete layou. When you enter a randomized map you actually have to explore it. The minimap usually shows the direction of the next mission objective though (yellow star) which means if you want to go straight through you know where to go.5. Classes have a limited number of combat abilities which then are combined with some support abilities. It narrows the number of viable builds considerably though. Wolcen wants to provide options through the talent system but in the end the number of usuable builds is very low. Wolcen is a game pretending to be deep while actually being pretty shallow.Let me also say something about act 4 as well as the "endgame".After finishing act 3 the story cuts off suddenly with a time skip while it's not really clear what happens with you or your character. You end up being in control of the hub city while moving the story forwards with a very simple approach. You select a project to drive the story forward. Then you do one random map and then you jump into a pre-made story map to continue the main story where initially nothing is really said about what happened in the previous acts. It feels completely disconnected. The process is repeated several times until you defeat a major boss and then you start playing random maps only for a while until the main bad guy arrives which then triggers the final fight. You are supposed to build up the defenses of the city to defeat the bad. The concept of building up the city was already the endgame initially and was basically centered around the endless cycle of => clearing a map => get loot => improve the city to increase difficulty and get better loot => clear a map => and so on...It basically the same principle now in act 4 where the better loot is missing though. My character was level 53-54 in act 4 when I quit and I still got level 41 items ever since I started act 4. This pretty bad as the enemies have been getting stronger due to them leveling with me while I'm not progressing with my gear though. The only power upgrades I get are from the new levels on the abilitries and additional talent unlocks. I've run into balancing issues here thought because of this as the enemies have become so strong that they suddenly can kill me very quickly while I can't really do anything about it or even teleport out of the map.I finished act 1-3 without dying when I started a new character in the current version and even till the first part of act 4 I was able to complete it without actually failing a mission. I got knocked out once or twice in some fights but still managed to complete the achivement to survive the three acts. The difficulty has been spiking though without giving me the tools to counter it. This leaves me extremely frustrated in preperation for the final fight you're supposed to defeat maps and small arena with lieutenants of the main bad guy but there is so much stuff thrown at you (especially in terms of area attacks) that you simply get overwhelmed. It's either you defeat the boss quickly with a lot of damage output or you will get overwhelmed. Most of the time it's not even clear what kills your character as there is just things thrown at you from everywhere.Anyway I still can't recommend Wolcen.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game could have been amazing but it doesn't work most of the time.The gameplay is fantastic (when it works). The story is uninteresting and the level design and AI are sub par. Yes the launch was rough but really it would be a great game if they could fix the multitude of problems/bugs during combat. Throughout the game playing co-op we've experienced hit-box problems, enemy attacks going off before their marker is on the ground, soft locked bosses/mini-bosses, and most notably player attacks not registering. There are other minor problems but this is the big one. We've experienced anywhere from about 25% to 100% of our basic attacks not landing over the course of a few seconds of attack animations. This also means we cannot generate resources to use spells. At $40 this game would be an outstanding value if the combat worked the way it should. But two full weeks after launch these problems persist and take so much enjoyment out of the game to the point where it becomes an exercise in patience that simply makes it not worth the time. I assume these issues will be fixed in the future but the campaign is short and I see little replay value, making this an unfortunate flop on what could have been one of the best games of its kind.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't recommend it because it has a thing that needs to be changed, and has to stop in all future games. And that is the idea to make the final chapter a grinding, generic chore with no story whatsoever. I encountered this nonsense idea for the first time in Middle Earth: Shadow of War and got terribly disappointed with otherwise pretty decent game. The same goes for Wolcen - it's a well decent game with nice gameplay, amazing skill tree with endless combinatorics to suit every style you can imagine and once again the same amount of styles you cannot even imagine until you start exploring...Story is a so-so, but for this genre it is not that important, and graphics are superior.All in all, it feels like an amazing game until chapter 4 starts... where it literally breaks. Sad.All my prospects for my character turned useless at one point, and all progression in vain, unless someone is satisfied with yet an other short RPG to kill time with, it is otherwise forgetable and only good for the genre collectors.

That was something totally unexpected and unpleasantly surprised* The Multiplayer option is DEAD! Either very long times to connect with someone or not working at all in specific regions.* The loophole involving rising in level for no reason and doing the same thing over and over again, just to get stronger and bigger is so cheeky and ... disgraceful. Probably developers were having a meeting regarding new content release or DLC's and decided to just give as a way to continuing playing the game but without NEW chapters, maps, stories, viable MULTIPLAYER option or something much more exciting. BREADCRUMBS. Anyway! I believe it's first time in my life when i give a thumbs up or good review to a game which has more cons than pos's and the reason why is simple. I enjoyed playing it for those few 65h aprox and i still reckon it has a lot of potential with a proper team and funding behind.I'm not a professional gamer or critic, just writing my opinion in a personal way, describing with my own words the experience i had, not trying to be to fuzzy about specific content. Before buying something i read most of the times reviews by amateurs like me as i do not trust nowadays the professional youtuber's or gaming websites for simple reason that they get payed sometimes for those reviews and this have a tendency to influence the decision about rating the game itself. Always trust the "little people" as they will have no hidden interest behind their decisions of rating a game in a good or bad way, at least most of them/us. _childDocuments_.review: I think the dev team right now is thanking their lucky stars that this game caught on so well. After multiple years of development they release a vapid, generic ARPG that has top of the line graphics and it blows up into a multi million dollar product for them.This game is solid, the gameplay is quick and impactful, there are telegraphed attacks and dodge rolls, the skills each have individual customization options, the passive tree is sprawling, the unique items allow for interesting build ideas, but I still don't recommend it. Why?It's more of the same, repackaged and rebranded with a shiny wrapping paper on it. Mostly though, I don't stand for its development process. I'm tired of how "Early Access" is some sort of free pass to allow scrutiny of your game to go unpunished. "The game will be finished at launch/wait until launch etc." It's launch now, the game is still unfinished. The money may have ran out after such a long time and they just needed to push out some semblance of product, which is understandable, eventually, you just need to call it quits. I'm so sick of people buying games like this, unfinished, but showing potential, and then feeling justified in their outrage down the road when the developer has moved on and no longer supports the game. Your purchase is final, there is no obligation for the game to get better or worse, they have sold their product. Whether or not they have the grace to take advantage of a situation such as this and continue work on this product is a question remaining to be answered.Anyway, you still may get joy out of this game, it's not bad by all means, and I won't discredit the development team entirely, like I said the game is solid. What I'm recommending against is getting swept up in the Twitch/Media hype cycle of jumping on an unfinished project, consuming it mindlessly and moving on to the next hit of outrage/endorphin rush.Blah blah blah.
