_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled upon Wolcen Lords of Mayhem on Steam a few days ago. The price was 19.99USD for the Alpha Access (not cheap for a game that is still in development). Been playing rpg games since I stopped playing wow, the solo idea of grinding forever at your own pace and getting those godly drops is exciting. Playing on and off d3 (last season’s not a single update), Path of Exile (which is amazing in support, updates and content), Grim Dawn (loved it but somehow, I got bored), and now I decided to get my hands onto Wolcen.First, CRYENGINE, says it all. The world includes a large open world featuring various environments, from swamp to mountains, to ancient ruined cities, forests and villages. If you want to spend a lot of time exploring the world and performing side quests, it is up to you.You can build your character as you want, picking any skills, weapons or armors and making the combination of your choice. There is no class restriction. However, there is a price:Resource Opposition SystemThe gameplay is balanced by three resources:Rage: Used for powerful melee attacks. You gain Rage by attacking enemies.Stamina: Used for escape and assassin type skills. Stamina Regeneration is effective when your character doesn’t take any damage.Mana: Used for magic skills.My Experience in the gameMy experience as a melee character hasn’t been that great in the alpha access. I feel that the game is favored in range classes, but I guess is too soon to make that justification. I decided to go with whirlwind, the spells and attacks are drops as Tomes, so they must drop for you in order to use them.A Beginner tip as a melee, on the first waypoint, basically as soon as you start the game, you must fight a boss with lots of adds. All you must do is be patient and kite, kite, kite, use your range spell, yes, you have one, do not attack boss with melee attack, you will die. Walk around the room clockwise or anticlockwise, use your space bar if needed to dodge / roll your character ahead (you only have 4 stamina points).I noticed as a melee character I must use spells to get the attention of a boss, or a rare mob and kite, I rarely used my whirlwind on a big boss, that’s instant death for me. Whirlwind did not last long enough, so whirlwind, hit, hit, whirlwind, hit, hit, you get the idea.The class point system is very interesting, visually and at the same time its overwhelming #pathofexile. Maybe I am a noob, but I noticed on the same tree there isn’t any amazing defense nodes, maybe I must rotate the tree to pick something else.lots of character icons don’t have a mouseover explanation, for example the portal is a tiny little blue dot under the character’s health pool to the right. Same thing with skill points on the tree, but as this is alpha all is reasonable.I honestly believe this could be my 2go rpg game to farm forever, explore the world in stunning visuals.The only thing I disagree with is, if you walked to an area and discovered a hidden door or a dungeon, once you step in and if you die, expect to die, you will be resurrected to the town portal, and not at the dungeons entrance. I hope they fix this or find a better solution as it is time wasting and its frustrating for the player.Overall, I loved the visual exploration worlds, melee combat and survivability needs huge improvement, skill tree needs to be looked again for melee, considering the bosses and rare monsters are NOT friendly for melee. Is it worth to buy the game when it comes out? HELL YEAH, I am sure they will listen to their community and improve the game. OH did I mention ARENAS?

_childDocuments_.review: What's rather good: Yep, that graphics!What's not soo good: All the rest..First, the game is annoyingly buggy and unfinnished. Not only will triggers deny to execute, forcing you to reload the game several times. No, the whole "game" ends without any proper message. Having received the quest called "@ui_A1_Q5_S12_StepNameLabel", you will have to deduce on your own that you just experienced all available content and might want to close the application. Moreover, the minimap is buggy (does not save revealed areas, or turns completely black on a regular basis), enemies are stuck in stairs, checkpoints are not saved correctly (you sometimes must repeat a mission after quitting the game), and, and, and.. many minor bugs as well..But.. well.. I would still oversee such flaws and really look forward to the final version of Wolcen.. ..if the game itself would be fun to play. But unfortunatelly, Wolcen lacks the most important aspect of quality: A good game balance and game design.I actually LOVE to grinding creeps. I can collect items and compare stats for years. But there is nothing to love about in Wolcan! All the items barely vary in a meaningful way at all. There are 5 rarity levels, but rarity levels 3 and 4 seem not to exist at all. Unique items are super boring, especially compared to PoE or D3. You will definitely find a sh*tload of "rare" items (rarity level 2), but you will just have no fun digging through that garbage over and over again. I find that remarkable how the developers achieved to make the stat comparison of items a boring, nearly frustrating experience. Uh! Oh, and of course you can sell items for gold.. ..but you won't need gold for anything! All shop prices are completely imbalanced. And all shop offers are completely pointless. Let's put that in clear words: This is a grinding game, and I even had NO FUN finding unique items and upgrading my gear.But well, what's maybe even much worse than the lack of a nice item variety:There are NO real strategies for a possible character development and there is literally NOT A SINGLE tactical element while playing: It's just so super easy to pick ONE good skill and kill all the monster-filled floors with just that single skill. There is no real "skill" you can develop while playing the game: Just evade the enemy attacks (when they surround you, you are dead; when they do not surround you, you easily win..). Just keep button-smashing that one overpowered skill to clear every stage. In my case: I played as a hunter, and just setting up a single turret cleared the whole screen for me, INCLUDING BOSS ENEMIES! The game even to easier and easier over time! Not that there ever was a challenge at any given time. It's just that the game starts non-challenging, and then continues to get even easier with every single minute!But well, at least the skill tree looks nice.But, yeah, that's exactly it: It LOOKS nice.Having checked out the actual opportunities, even the skill tree turns out to be absolutely shallow and pointless. Yes, you can add some percentage of damage here and there. But again, there is barely any tactical and/or strategical impact. You just get stronger with ever level up. Simple as that. No increasing complexity. No meaningful decisions. No unique style of playing a character. Nothing of that at all.Plus, all the novel elements introduced by the game appear to make no sense at all. For example: In Wolcen, skills are gained by looting skill items that you will find occasionally from time to time (as normal loot from any creeps). But you will have found all five relevant skills for your class within an hour or so. And from then on, your inventory is just spammed with skills you already own. You can actually sell these skills for skill XP in order level up your skills. Nice idea. But here, again, there is NO BALANCING at all: You will have to gather and sell 30+ of these non-stackable skill items in order to successfully level up a single skill a single time.. ..but you won't do this, because all your skills already progress more than fast enough just by playing. The whole feature is implemented in a completely pointless and boring way. And the same goes for all the other features. Well.. "All the other features"? Sorry, I have to correct myself:There barely are any other features! The game has about 90% less features than PoE and/or D3, and it seems SO FAR AWAY from being finished. The release date of late January 2020 should hopefully be a joke!Currently, Wolcan is more a TECH DEMO than a proper game.It's a copycat that looks beautiful, but has nothing relevant to offer under the surface. The whole game design is boring and the game balance does not exist.Oh, and just a short word comprising the narrative design: Random. It's so random and boring I can not even tell. The dialogues are basically just a concatenation of stupid fantasy words and I never felt so disconnected to a game universe. Humm.. What else.. Boss fights are 10-20 seconds showdowns without any suspense or challenge. Winning fights in general is purely due to keeping up attention, not having any skill. There is never ever a moment where you actually have to use more than 10 of your brain cells. These are needed to match the creep allocation on the screen with your one good skill. Oh, did I mention that there is no challenge??!What else.. Dungeon generation is boring. Some sounds are just weird (VERY russian voice for african king, I actually had to laugh). Act 1 was super fast to play through (without bugs, it would have taken me 2.5 hours, I guess) - so even with Act 2, 3 and 4, there would not be enought relevant content. Yeah.. More does not come up to my mind, right now..Summed up:Wolcan is not challenging AND not rewarding at the same time.Do only buy if you'd like to see a tech demo for a hack'n'slay game made with the cryengine.

I have 4 face options for the female character and none of them look appealing. Then we have around 8 horrible hair choices and the eye color. Male characters also have a beard choice. Its not worth it, unless they increase the options in the future. But right now it would have been better to just use one generic character for each sex that at least would look good. _childDocuments_.review: There has been a lot of hype surrounding this game, and a lot of negative reviewing based on the.... rough launch. My perspective however is one from someone who had no idea about this game until basically launch day. I have been playing D3 on my Switch for weeks now, and a next-gen ARPG? Absolutely. I bought it, played online that first day, and let me tell you this game is great. Bugs aside, because I will also transparently say I haven't experienced any game breaking bugs at all. The story has been captivating and makes me really feel (And I am not even done with Act 1) that I am both unimportant to those around me but integral to some fate-specific goal. I love the general feeling gaining power. The spells are fantastic. Melee feels really impactful, and ranged makes you feel like a rogue/ranger. DPS wise the bosses are tough and the cannon-fodder make great gore-explosions. The aesthetic is great, the abilities feel cool. Gaining gear feels like it changes how you play. Being a hybrid and changing how you play is also pretty easy. Rough launch aside, I've loved every moment of this and would absolutely recommend it at this price point. I don't know for sure, but there have been whispers of new difficulties, end-game content, and possibly other updates. Even without those updates I recommend it but I see great things for the future of Wolcen and would adore having more people to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is decent. Overall 6.5/10 or so. Definitely worth on discount for $10. I wishlisted this for a long time and I'm aware of the history of terrible bugs and lack of improvement. However, the story is...fairly engaging, surprisingly. Visuals and audio are nice. You can see there was definitely passion put into this game, at least by someone. However, there's just a lot of wasted potential, beautiful areas you don't really immerse in, environment you don't really interact with, no secrets; mostly just a lack of content. It appears some parts of the game were invested heavily in and then suddenly they ran out of time, money or ideas. One should buy this game just to see what was so close to being a really good game, what a good structure can look like without well-executed development.   It's not very difficult to play, the UI is easy to understand, the mechanics are pretty straightforward, and mob clearing feels good, but the bosses were too easy-literally giving me their doom speech as they crumbled to dust. The only bugs I encountered were couple game breaking fights when I used my transformation and warped into some corners. So, just try to avoid sketchy terrain, or using your ultimate.  Pet build (pleasantly surprised yet again) is one of the best I've run in any ARPG. Most just don't feel very good. I won't be playing too much more as it's very story-driven but I might give another build a try. I hear melee builds feel clunky and the end game content is too meta dependent, so if I get to that point I'll hop back on another tried and true game. If I had to judge...9/10 Visuals8/10 Sounds5/10 Mechanics/Difficulty7/10 Fun GameplayMinus a couple points for bugs and lack of content, plus I'd weigh the gameplay to be the most valuable aspect.Meh... about a 6.5/10 At discounted price

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's a maybe right now, which will be a yes IF the major launch bugs are taken care of.  I'm hesitant to say No, but you need to know what you're getting into if you say yes.  Please note, you're going to be reading only the bad (bugs) but once these are resolved, it probably will be a Yes recommendation as it's a solid ARPG without the bugs.Current bugs I've seen or heard of:Characters getting deleted, both Online or Offline (The two modes toons / inv are seperate btw)Storage chest inventory deleting items (had a couple myself after going to a new act)The controls can have significant delay (especially online) which can be very annoying and get you killedMany bosses have a one shot mechanic even with high HP, so the delayed dmg passive is almost a requirementSeveral Act Bosses and NPCs required to continue in Story Mode can bug out, leaving you unable to do anything but restartI can't complete the last fight in Act III right now because of the bug above, not sure how it got launched in this state tbh, you can see in Store discussions tons of people are having this issue, I can look past many things on launch week / give a free pass but that's the sort of thing that is literally game breaking / deal breakerFix the magic shield mechanics..it's a buggy mess.  It constantly goes away and redraws itself, and I'm pretty sure most of the passive skill mechanics don't work for it, gotta fix that pronto.Mouse over on gear in inventory doesn't show, you have to click in an empty spot to get it to workThe final buggy issue that matters to me, is the fact that currently, the only viable way to build a character is to get the highest dmg 2H you can find, and build melee spin to win.  Ranged and Magic are lackluster in comparison in terms of dmg.  I'm an altoholic so I've played all playstyles, both online and offline and this is the sad truth.  Which is sad, because several of the other playstyles are fun as far as animations, so once that gets balanced it will be good, they did well with the passive skill tree.Now the good thus farDecent storyDiversity in skills (although I will say that more Active skills are needed for the 'Pure' builds melee, ranged, magic as far as not having to use a catalyst to mix abilities)The End Game modes are engaging, very similar to Diablo Grifts, POE maps, and its own city building mechanic (Unlocks once you beat the story and only way I can do it currently is offline by changing the flag due to the bug mentioned above)You can skip cutscenes by holding space, which is niceWhat I want to see once the critical bugs are squished:No more lag when using active skills / potions, makes an ARPG unplayableInventory auto-sortOptions which creating a new toon to get them to the furthest story you've achieved or better yet, let them just start in the other non-story mode without having to complete the story, the wall just isn't needed.More Active skills and the other builds to be viable compared to 2H aoe, personally I want more mobility skillsSpeaking of skills...they need to have no cooldown, you already have a resource mechanic limiting it.Pet AI to be controllable (mainly the Mortis tank, as he tanks well (taunt works really well), but not controllable)Gem removal cost needs to be toned downThe one shotting mechanic needs to go away, period.  If you avoid the red, you shouldn't be able to be one shot.There's no logs indicating what exactly one shot you or what damage type is hurting you the most, how are we supposed to know what you build resist against?Speaking of resists, if you build pure tank in the classic trinity sense and damage resist...it's laughable because it doesn't help much, you should be able to stand there and afk almost if you're a pure tank build, low dmg to balance it of course, but currently, there is no tank build in the classic sense, fix that please.Better armor reroll mechanics and include the components to be used on red armor or have its own component that's not rare.  Gear reroll is a staple in ARPGs.Gear sets for all the buildsThe higher you go in delves, you should auto get higher gold / magic find before the extra gold amplifiers.  Risk vs reward.Custom loadouts for saving your different builds, that auto-equip the saved armor in those sets'Sell all' of different rarities or 'Sell junk' with a button to mark gear as junk

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem is an isometric 3rd person Action RPG, in the style of games like Diablo or Path of Exile.In Wolcen, your character is not defined by a class, but rather through your selection of weapons, active skills (swappable at any time ala Diablo 3), and passive abilities (selected from a massive skill tree ala POE). There is a lengthy campaign, followed by the Champions of Stormfall mode, similar to Adventure Mode from Diablo 3. The game can be played solo or in groups of up to 4 players, online or offline. Offline characters cannot be used for multiplayer.Initially developed and Kickstarted under the title "Umbra", Wolcen was developed by a small indie studio (Wolcen Studios, how original) out of Paris, France.After a lengthy period in early access, Wolcen was recently released. Unfortunately, the surge in players proved too much for their servers to handle, and offline play was unavailable for two days after launch. The team added more servers, and online play has been stable since.While not particularly novel, Wolcen is generally fun, with excellent graphics (courtesy of the licensed CryTek engine), decent sound, and generally "punchy" mechanics. It does suffer from a lack of animation canceling, which sometimes makes the game feel unresponsive.The largest issue at present is the abundance of serious bugs. These range from performance issues and crashes to item and gold dupes to abilities that do not work at all. How significantly these will impact your enjoyment of the game is entirely a matter of personal tolerance.Personally, I can't help but feel that despite all its flaws, there is a spark to this title that makes it truly charming. It is clearly a labor of love from a small team, and what they have achieved is impressive despite its failings. I believe it is likely that the team will continue to address bugs, but that the game will probably never be as polished as its AAA competitors.If you are a fan of ARPGs and don't mind some bugs, this is a title to check out. If you never got into Diablo or you can't stand "unfinished" games, you might want to skip it.

Their motivation works: remove/bypass a dimensional barrier so that demons rule the planet. Their methods do not work in my mind but hey magic *shrugs*. last point is that the story ends on a cliff hanger "to be continued."Loot: numbers go up. The legendary pieces are so powerful that they lasted me the whole campaign while the iconic pieces became too weak to use in later levels. Pets are useless. _childDocuments_.review: Brings together some of the best ideas from PoE, D3 and Grim Dawn, and sprinkles it with some fresh touches. Recommended as one to watch, although at the beta stage it's hard to know if it has the legs in the late game.  The combat is just plain fun, and its tied together with a stronger narrative than its competitors. It has a fresh take on some classic mechanics (especially attribute points and stackable skill modifiers), good graphics/sound and I have found it to be stable. I have been spoilt by the vast array of build options in PoE, so by comparison, the passive skill tree looks a bit limiting (although PoE's complexity ain't for everyone). They are adding active skills regularly and the passive tree is still in development so I'm hoping that they keep fleshing out the range of character build sub-types and play styles available. One other little point - it's pretty obvious there's no women on their dev team. I've played this periodically through the alpha, and the beta is really progressing well. If you are a fan of ARPGs my view is it's a safe buy - it's fun to play now, and I have enough confidence the Dev's will finish it well.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start... I started this game the day it launched. Ill say the game is fun with actual friends. my brother and i would play in the end game and that was much more enjoyable. the ♥♥♥♥ talking made the repetitive actions with zero rewards much more enjoyable.my biggest complaint is two fold. but it rests squarely on the shoulders of the developer. 1 - They are, and have always been unreasonably slow with hot fixes, releasing pertinent information, and general follow through on what they do actually offer up. and 2 - in their first content update, they required you to create a new character in order to take part in the new stuff. with almost 200 hours on a single character that sucks. but ok whatever, ill give it a shot. the content update was bland. bland. bland. tremendous waste of my time.they shouldve found a way to integrate existing characters into the update.for those of you interested in picking it up for the first time, and avoiding the headaches i encountered, i think you could have fun. at least as you play through the campaign. dont expect to get groups thrown together as fast as diablo though. youll likely play the game solo almost exclusively. so if thats your speed, then enjoy! youll get a sold 30 hours of enjoyment in the story at least.

_childDocuments_.review: As a modern ARPG 2020 I feel It is able to stand-up on its own within the genre. Although the content at the current moment of the games launch leaves me to desire more, this game and its development team has true potential. But as more updates and content routinely rolls out, and this game keeps getting more and more polished, I believe a true ARPGem will be built. The graphics are great, but that is to be expected when your game runs on the CRYENGINE. The music and atmosphere is good and what you would expect from the themes this game portrays. I would consider the Voice-acting to be good, but not great. Although this is mainly due to how the dialogue was written. The main story is comprehensible but very forgettable, but the story wasn't where my general focus was throughout my play-through. The Combat is fun and engaging. its probably the most enjoyable aspect of the game. On first impression I initially found the new character creation options to be shallow. But in hindsight when looking back to other ARPG's I've dedicated my time to in the past, I realise Wolcen gives you more options than most. Your character is not locked into any specific class, although there are only 3 general prototype classes that you can build from within the skill-tree. Warrior, Mage, Rogue and all the various archetype classes that can become of those are open for you to decide what kind of character you want. Skills and Spells are either purchased or dropped from mobs, and are only limited by what weapon you chose to use. Skills can level up, and can be modified with skill runes (similar to Diablo 3) and be buffed by passive skills from the skill-tree. Then once completing the first chapter, you gain an aspect point which you can then use to chose an Aspect/Apocalyptic Form, which is friggen cool.All in all, im enjoying this game. The few negatives I find, dont really blemish my overall enjoyment of the game. I wish rendering was quicker for the cutscene LOD. I hope they add more skills, and i wish i could play my Online characters offline. that's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: ARPGs are meant to have fun combat, good customization, and fun grinds for loot. Overall, Wolcen is worth the $40 price tag for its fun combat and amazing customization alone.+ Combat is fun+ Vast amounts of customization to cater any playstyle you'd like+ Gorgeous graphics and VFX for spells/abilities+ Good content for its price+ Unique story, not a Diablo clone+ Interesting mix of fantasy, scifi, and other themes+ Pets can pick up loot; auto-pickup gold+ Boss fights feel unique and are fun. Later acts have more challenging bosses to make-up for the insanely easy act I and early act II "difficulty"+ Beautiful level design and badass or gruesome looking enemies.+ Awesome music+ You can take on the form of an apolocalyptic deity. Albeit, not that often. However, each one is unique and have some fun abilities.+/- Clunky movement (animation cancelling) compared to other ARPGs. Once you're used to it, you can manage around it.+/- The game is too easy for the majority of the campaign. Difficulty spikes suddenly happen when you start reaching act II bosses. There's only Story & Normal mode. The game needs higher difficulties. This may have been due to the initial playthrough is treated as a longtime tutorial, slowly introducing you to more game systems. Perhaps the devs want to avoid the typical artificial inflation of difficulty that plagues this genre. Still, my boredom from lack of challenge was forgoed by combat's sheer fun and my curiosity to experiment in different ways of obliterating enemies with combos of spells and abilities.+/- End-game systems revolve around city management as a mechanism for end-game systems for continued skill and gear grinding+/- The game apparently has crafting. I never used it and it was never explained to me by the game.- Bit rough to learn at first since there's so many stats and the game just throws you into it without much guidance. A lot of combat metrics/stats could benefit from more tooltip info. What's the difference between attack power and weapon attack power? Do they interact? Etc.- Campaign ends on a cliff hanger, leaving you unsatisfied with the story.- Movement bugs will sometimes trap you forcing you to teleport to the city hub. Or will make some mini-dungeons completely unplayable as you cannot move past invisible wall- Desync of mouse cursor, character, and your movement--- Always online required. You cannot interchangeably play your online character with offline mode. They are completely separate. Wtf??
_childDocuments_.name: Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the range of bugs and rocky release Wolcen isn't a terrible game and with its Chronciles finally out it really freshens it up. I'm just going to review aspects I feel comfortable reviewing so I wont be talking about the technical aspects of it as I am not to familiar with coding and what not.The new Hunt Mechanic: This. This is fun. I like that your choices tell a small story as you hunt the monster. I like the risk and reward you get from it. Wanna increase the reward output? Get ready for the fight of your life. I have had two bugs occur in this mechanic though: One was that after activating the hunt there was noway to progress it (during the story) and when I am downed my character goes into an infinite loop animation of a downed state. Besides that this is a great mechanic and gives me some hope of what they will do in the future.- The character progression: There's not "classes" in this ARPG but it has a more similar progression to games like PoE as it allows you to play you character however you feel suits you play style.- The combat: I felt this was a little clunky and it could be because I am playing online and not offline but it does feel a little out of sync. Besides this I feel that the abilities play really well into the combat with the ability to dodge attacks manually something you dont want to be caught without in times.The weapons you wield can also really change up how you engage in both the abilities you use and the approach to combat you take which I really enjoyed and led me to experiment with different combinations and powers.Abilities: I have to say I really love the update on this. The ability to change the damage type of your skills has allowed me to really tinker my character to play the way I want. Each ability feels unique and I am yet to try them all. I do wish they added more in their first Chronicle but this isn't too disheartening.Story: The story is okay. I have finished it before this update but I never really cared much for the story is this kind of genre. The theme seems to be centred around family and it follows a pretty basic tale, it doesn't do anything "wow" but this doesn't take away the enjoyment for me.Endgame: This aspect of the game I have not reached in the Chronicle update, but in the past when I hit the endgame I found it just okay. It was fun for the most part but there was really only two active endgame mechanics; both which are just dungeoun runs and "Kill X Boss". The passive aspect which worked as a city builder lite was a great aspect and I hope their are changes to it with the Chronicle update and may update this review when I get there again. I just hope they add more variety to the end game.So now do I suggest you buy this game? Well it's your money do what you want with it. But I would suggest buying it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolcen may just be the biggest waste of money I've ever played. Wolcen is a linear trash compactor of a game. Minimal skills, minimal customization, minimal enjoyment. When you're not fighting through waves of trash mobs that are 2-3 levels below you, you're fighting bosses that will fluke the living daylights out of you: refreshing health on downs, random attack registers that make no sense and mob spam that does nothing but piss you off as you try and maneuver around them with the god awful controls. The game's story is so banal that the only thing redeeming is the cutscenes. (basically TES: Oblivion story but with flesh demons). The pacing of the game is dreadful. You complete the game at roughly level 33 (assuming you get past the utterly dreadful boss mechanics that leave you tearing your hair out), leaving you with 40+ levels or so to continue through the game. After the story is complete your reward is to be forced to run through countless dungeons doing the same thing over and over: kill enough mobs to spawn the boss, kill the boss, return to town, rinse and repeat. I'd rather push my face into a powered lawnmower and go live in the woods than do that over and over again. The only side quests as you travel through each zone is the dungeons you will spend all your time doing in endgame. Totally not worth buying unless you want this non-contact alternative to a lobotomy.

name: Factorio
detailed_description: Factorio is a game in which you build and maintain factories. You will be mining resources, researching technologies, building infrastructure, automating production and fighting enemies. In the beginning you will find yourself chopping trees, mining ores and crafting mechanical arms and transport belts by hand, but in short time you can become an industrial powerhouse, with huge solar fields, oil refining and cracking, manufacture and deployment of construction and logistic robots, all for your resource needs. However this heavy exploitation of the planet's resources does not sit nicely with the locals, so you will have to be prepared to defend yourself and your machine empire. Join forces with other players in cooperative Multiplayer , create huge factories, collaborate and delegate tasks between you and your friends. Add mods to increase your enjoyment, from small tweak and helper mods to complete game overhauls, Factorio's ground-up Modding support has allowed content creators from around the world to design interesting and innovative features. While the core gameplay is in the form of the freeplay scenario, there are a range of interesting challenges in the form of Scenarios . If you don't find any maps or scenarios you enjoy, you can create your own with the in-game Map Editor , place down entities, enemies, and terrain in any way you like, and even add your own custom script to make for interesting gameplay. Discount Disclaimer: We don't have any plans to take part in a sale or to reduce the price for the foreseeable future. What people say about Factorio No other game in the history of gaming handles the logistics side of management simulator so perfectly. - Reddit I see conveyor belts when I close my eyes. I may have been binging Factorio lately. - Notch, Mojang Factorio is a super duper awesome game where we use conveyor belts to shoot aliens. - Zisteau, Youtube

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a great game that won't suck up all your resources if you're a casual gamer or have a budget gaming PC. There is a TON to do in the game and you can be as fly-by-the-seat-of-your-pants or analytical about it as you want. I really can't recommend it enough; however, you should know that it takes A LONG TIME to play. So, if you have other obligations, this may not be the best game to choose. If you enjoy strategy games where you need to plan and manage a lot of different things, then you'll love Factorio. One of my favorite thing to do in the game is build a tank and drive around exploring the map and killing bugs. It's a wonderful pastime and you can totally lose yourself in the game play. I hope you enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game before Steam about a year already.- Most stable game I've played. ever.   - I've run a server a headless 32-bit linux machine with 128MB RAM, worked perfectly   - Haven't found a bug thus far- Hours of fun already, I have been playing this game mostly together with friends, never gets boring there's always something to do or to optimize. - Would recommend if you love sandbox games and building factories that, in their complexity, are only limited to your own imagination (and that of your friends)!

_childDocuments_.review: This game should absolutely win the category for older games with plenty of new updates. It has the most active developers I have ever seen. I find this most impressive.Now for the review part:Factorio is an easy buy for everyone who likes building games. In this game you are always working on something which isnt perfectly automated. Absolutely a game for perfectionists! I dont have that many hours compared to others but thats due to being someone who likes to play with others. I can for sure say: I recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is near perfection for any critical thinker, problem solver, or logical analyst. You build, and then you optimize. Scarcely do you find a title that exercises the brain as much as this. You'll find hours upon hours of content here, further proliferated by consistent and appropriate updates by the developers as well as the extensive modding community working tirelessly to maximize replayability. Your ability to progress and withstand what's thrown at you is largely an extension of your own ability, dedication, and understanding, making Factorio perhaps one of the most satisfying games to conquer. A strong recommendation for anyone looking for a new longstanding favorite made with the utmost passion and skill.

_childDocuments_.review: So I wanted to play a game for half an hour one night. The next morning, I had... something. An eldrich monstrosity of belts, smelters and arms. Something that - had I had but another half an hour - I was sure would summon the flying spaggetti monster himself. So I gave it another half an hour. I'd played for 10 hours straight, what harm could half an hour do? A week later I still had an iron shortage and had wired plumbing into my desk so i didn't have to get up to drink.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this I put nearly 120 hours of game time in Factorio within two weeks of purchase.Is Factorio really that good?At first i would of said no, it isnt, but as time went on and the sheer madness that is Factorio begun to unfold, I knew this would be a serious addiction. On par with crack?  Mmm... Possibly. So what changed my mind?Well, let me start by saying the tutorial is not a good representation of the game and the two hours steam allows you before refunding is of no use to you here. You could never come even close to grasping what this game has to offer in that amount of time.To answer my own question... the Map editor changed my mind.The Map editor is loaded with not just map settings but difficulty / enemy settings kind of intertwined.For example: The more trees you add the less your highly toxic factory pollution seems to spread.Little or no trees.... well, the alien locals get a sniff of that fancy chemical factory then go mad with Envy as you bask in your glorious complex accomplishments. I Cant really say what happens next, sadly- Let me tell you all straight, I'm a sucker for punishment. I enjoy playing games on very hard settings, and I have to admit Factorio does NOT disappoint.The first few attempts i kept thinking to myself that "Factorio is too easy", "it doesnt know what kind of game it wants to be".The turret defense side of things felt mediocre at best, which made the building side of things feel pointless.However, after starting over and cranking up the settings this game feels Godly and chaotic as hell.Trying to build very advanced manufacturing setups while being hindered by my own OCD / need to refine my BS sloppy building methods, AND.... finish up tech trees / SUPER advanced science manufacturing, coal, oil, solar, nuclear setups/ upgrade all sort of weapons, armor modification, trains, and robot tech, while trying to fend off the SUPER jealous alien life so i can launch myself back into space....I have NEVER! been so entertained. The panic of trying to get your factory functioning is intense on harder settings.But enough of that.-Factorio is as complex or as easy as you want it to be, meaning, you dont need to research every science / tech to have a good time. If some military tech is confusing you feel free to skip it or come back to it when you have a better understanding of its basic systems. You use, belts, robotic arms, power (electricity), ore smelters, and a whole slew of other material / liquids, including crafting stations, to create manufacturing setups. For Example: you need a mining machine to mine coal, you then use conveyor belts and robotic arms to transport that coal to a smelter which will be used to smelt the iron. Same process to get the iron ore to the smelter. Your smelting that iron to make iron plates. you will use belts and robotic arms to move the iron plates to a crafting station where you can make iron gears. Kind of see where im going with this? three items to make one, then ten of that, plus three other items to make something new, then take three new items plus three other new items you created with your factory to make a new, new item...lol it just keeps going like that till you have this giant complex system creating tons of different materials that contribute to the overall layout so you can produce highly advanced products... like a robotic exoskeleton that makes you run super fast :)-Intuitive UI.-Vehicles and of course trains.-Enemy progression. base building/spreading, consistently upgrading enemy units.-player progression.-weapons like machine guns, flame throwers, turrets, laser turrets, rocket launchers, and many others that i dont want to spoil.-unintentional puzzle solving mechanics. meaning you are constantly trying to improve your set up in a space that you accidentally made too small and is now too far long to change but also surrounded by other complex manufacturing setups. true you could tare it all down and fix it, but wheres the fun in that.-why wait for the enemy when you can go on the offensive and hunt them down, i mean spread compassion... with your new arsenal. Very fun btw. has kind of dodge bullet hell kind of vibe and very player skill based.-Game is really balanced.-functions and scales well in co op. never had a disconnect. not one. good job devs *golf clap*-servers are easy to set up and have easy to understand options.-addons for armor. dont want to spoil it for you, but there is some fun / cool items for sure.-map exploration. really big maps to explore.-combat feels fluid and responsive.-Factorio doesnt hand hold. some may see this as a negative, but not me. Huge positive.-you can customize the color of your character, and create all kinds of map markers to simplify scouting in co op or just to mark ore. lots of neat options and icons for marking. -you can zoom way out and in.-Giant mod community.-when you die everything your wearing and in your inventory stays on your corps till you go get it, and yes it can disappear if you take too long. i love it. Reminds me of Asheron's Call.-Map editor/level creator is great, easy to understand.-Great community of helpful people.-good music/ sound design.-tons to build-If you like a layout you made you can save it to a schematic than later use it like a building guide/reference  -The Car movement is absolute garbage and will drive you crazy! worse than any game i have played and the Devs need to fix it.-Certain armor upgrades increase inventory space when you equip them, however if your inventory is full and you missclick the armor, you remove the armor, and drop everything that was in the extra slots the armor gave you on the floor. Which is crazy. The end game armor adds a huge amount of inventory space and can drop several THOUSAND items on the ground un-stacked. picture that for second. it fills huge a portion of the ground. you have conveyor belts everywhere, full of items, robotics arms flailing about, and you left click your armor instead of right click (because most things require left click in factorio) then huge amounts of items spill out everywhere that are now mixed in with all the factory garbage that is going on. So now when you go to pick your stuff up, you end removing tons of unwanted sh** from the conveyor belts taking space your full inventory didnt have in the first place. Now you have to sift through endless amounts of crap just to pick up the stuff you didnt mean to drop. Its happen to everyone ive played with multiple times. A simple fix would just be to make it to where you have to Shift+left mouse click to remove the armor.Please do it devs.-Texture color pallet tends to get a bit stale over time. The Dev has added some color to the trees, and new drills which is much appreciated. Other items need some love.-Doesnt have a very Sci-fi feel. A lot of the time you forget that the main character crashed a space craft on an alien planet do to most of the things you utilize in your factory looking like average everyday items and not like futuristic space travel kind of gear. For a hot minute there i thought i was playing a 1900s gold rush sim lol.-No story.-No campaign .-advanced oil and nuclear power is rather confusing at first.-tutorial isnt very helpful.There you have it folks. Not much for cons considering the complexity of this game.Ill be sure to add anything else i think of as it comes to me. Im sure ive forgotten plenty.  It is well worth the price and can expect to get hundreds of hours out of Factorio.Id give Factorio on harder settings 8.5 out of 10.On standard settingsa 6.5 out of 10We'll see though. Ive seen devs destroy amazing games in early access.  written July 3rd 2020

_childDocuments_.review: Well, since Factorio is now released from the chains of "Early Access", it's about time to do a review.This topic is a bit controversial. At first, the devs wanted to implement a full story campaign for this game, but in the end they gave up, which is sad, but nothing can be done about it. The only story aspect of this game now is present via a set of "tutorial" missions and i'd like to say that if campaign followed the same pattern as they did with this "tutorial" - it would be amazing to play.But what's done is done. I hope one day they will reconsider this decision.Essentially, the bread & butter of this game lies in "Freeplay" mode, which allows you to generate map/resources/enemies to your liking via many available options. For more interesting challenge, i recommend you to set enemies up to the max, especially if you want to play multiplayer mode with friends. Personally, i like playing with a lot of resources + enemies. Because, it's quite boring to build A TANK when you don't have anything to kill, right?But before you dive into the complex building system, you need to know about the most important mechanic of this game - Pollution. Pollution is essentialy your "aggro" parameter, that increases with every building you build. Surrounding Trees and landtiles absorb a certain amount of your produced pollution, but most if the time it can't absorb all of it. So, what will happend if your Pollution increases? The answer is rather simple. The local fauna aliens will attack your base directly. The strength of attacks are dependent on how much time passed in the game, how much alien bases you destroyed and some other aspects. This is the "Evolution" factor in the map creation, you can increase or decrease it, but i prefer it to stay at default values.Early game get your Machine Gun ready and start mass producing MG ammo as soon as you can. I don't like using a Shotgun, since you'l get Piercing MG (better damage than normal ammo) rounds soon and Turrets also use MG ammo. So, by producing MG ammo, you will supply both yourself and your defense MG turrets. Two birds with one shot.Setup a defence perimeter. You can scout nearby locations to check how far are enemy bases, be careful since they will attack if you'l get too close. Since you will not have an access to Stone Walls immediately, there's a great way for improvisation ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°). Pipes are one of the best ways to setup a defence perimeter early game, as an example it looks like this: You won't even repair them, just replace a damaged part with a new  one, easy.Build a Car, since you will not be able to destroy nest with Spitters on your foot. You can see those small worms nearby enemy HQ's. There's some unique enemy types in the game and Spitters is like a defense towers at the enemy base. Their projectiles also use a smart aim patterns, which means you'l be testing your driving skills, because you'l need to dodge at high speed + fire at them at the same time. After securing your early game base, start research developments and base expansion. Good luck!People from Factorio community deserve a special mention. Simply put - this game got an amazing community and mod support. With a wide range of mods available, it can change the game's experience dramatically.If you only purchased the game, i recommend you to play Vanilla version for awhile, before setting up hundreds of mods.I'l list a few of popular mods here as an examples with a small commentary from me:-  (A tool for locating input starved machines)-  (less building sizes, that can block your movements)-  (VERY IMPORTANT MOD, that can helps dramatically when you wait for X to finish)-  (this mod is essential for a battle-maniac like me, because i can see evolution/pollution stats there and prepare accordingly)-  (more variety is always nice)Factorio is a fantastic game, both in single and multiplayer. If you enjoy building long lines of production, railways, while battling a lot of enemies using your own Tank, then you're at the right place.- This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Computer Scientist Donald Knuth once said: "Premature optimization is the root of all evil"."♥♥♥♥ you!" said the developers of Factorio, and optimized the heck out of their game right from the beginning.If Sim City 2k, Minecraft, Transport Tycoon and Dwarf Fortress had a beautiful, bugfree baby, and that baby only inherited the best features of its parents, it would still suck ass compared to Factorio.Jokes aside, this game is really well-made and you can tell that the creators care about quality. Despite its alpha-status, it's already practically bugfree and heavily optimized. It can handle huge factories even on outdated hardware, and if that is not enough, they constantly tinker on their own game engine to make further improvements to the games 'performance.The Gameplay itself is addictive to say the least. Many strategy and planning games let you automate at least some things, but not too much because the developers probably thought that it would take away the fun. Well, Factorio let's you automate literally everything, and guess what: (clever) automation is more fun than anything! Buy this game, it's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've enjoyed games like Satisfactory, Dyson Sphere Program, MegaFactory TItan, or any other in that vein, then you need to play Factorio. I believe it's one of the best in that genre, even though It's not the prettiest to look at, and the price rarely drops below $29.99.I was never smart enough (nor willing to watch YouTube vids about it) to build a ridiculous logistic network fully automated mega base. I never evolved much beyond conveyor belts. But there are so many creative and technically workable solutions in this game, that if you put the time and energy into it, you can unravel the most convoluted of spaghetti monsters and feel like you're making real progress.There's an expansion coming out, Space Age, which I will definitely buy. I will now happily retire my old base and I now consider this one of my all-time favourite games.

But each iterative improvement and new trick learned makes your designs better and better, as you continually improve the factory. _childDocuments_.review: Probably one of my favorite games of all time. It's one of those games where you can't explain it to someone without them playing it for themselves.You start the game by manually mining and smelting resources to make parts but you quickly begin to make drills, inserters, conveyor belts, and more to begin automating the process. Eventually you begin allocating resources to laboratories and researching new machines and upgrades to improve efficiency. You start automating every aspect of the game in its entirety from crafting ammunition, getting base resources, rebuilding walls, and launching rockets at aliens.Oh yeah, this game has aliens too. As you play, your "pollution level" increases aliens will begin to attack your factory in large groups, forcing you to always be on alert for them. Making turrets and crafting ammo automatically becomes a must eventually. You can even build drive-able vehicles and go to destroy the enemy bases yourself using ammunition made by your machines.Overall, this game is a 9/10. The progression is slow at the start and the game is a bit hard to learn but it's very worth it. I also feel the $35 price-tag is a bit high for this game but with the amount of content you get it's very worth it. Just hard to get friends to buy it because of the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. There is a large amount of content that will keep you hooked for hours, especially if you are into resource management games/factory games. There is a lot to do and in the end you get to feel the great satisfaction of creating a huge automated factory that you can sit and watch grab resources for you. Then, when you're bored of that you can get mods that expand the game even more. Highly recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I usually play mainstream stuff.  RPG.  A puzzle game now and then.  This game is different.  Its about completing / building an efficient machine. _childDocuments_.review: After about 60 hours of gameplay, I took a break from the endless cycle of improving the   production, to look around my industrial Empire. A frightening thought suddenly struck me- what have I done here? I have built an enormous complex of steel and concrete, far bigger than what one, including my own, could hope to understand. I have stripped the planet of it's resources, and burnt down forests for space. I have even industrialized the eradication process of the local inhabitants-- sure, they may look like bugs and can attack me, but wasn't I, who invaded their planet and polluted it, the real aggressor here, and were their attacks not justified as self defense? How could I not see that the only thing that I can not mass produce is the same tree that I have carelessly ran over?I was in that moment that I have realized that one of my mid-level production facilities is not running at full capacity. Following the belts backward, I have been horrified to learn that the train did not arrive fully stocked. I have abandoned my previous thoughts immediately. After all, the production line that builds production lines of production lines of production lines is not going to build itself without my direct involvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: There is a free demo. Check it out if you are unsure about buying this game. The developers have specifically stated that they have no plans for this game to go on sale, so don't wait for one.Factorio is the definitive 2D base building and resource management game that was designed from the ground up to allow for massive factories.You can get a DRM free version of this game off of the Factorio website, even if you buy the game through steam.There is a built in mod browser and auto installer that makes community content seamless with the core game.It has multiplayer support for literal hundreds of people on a single server.The game is incredibly stable with even trivial bugs being patched literal hours after being introduced.If you enjoy 2D base building and management games then you owe it to yourself to at least try the demo for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely off the spectrum. The idea is to ascend from planning and decision making to repetitive checking of every building and unit and feel good about it. For me personally, the real challenge starts when you add aai programmable vehicles mod and try to make the game being played 100% by itself. Machines use enemy pathfinder, and that's make them 'stuck' if the path is too long or not obvious enough. In order to resolve it, you have to expand this pathfinder by dividing the path in smaller ones that are easily understood by the pathfinder. You have to calculate distance, angles, maybe assign safe-to-travel chunks that do not contain any cliffs or water. You also have to make units wait for each other and move out only with enough inventory, and you may want to make them retreat at certain point, because for example a suicide squad of tanks every say, 5 minutes, is a massive hit for economy of your factory(a single tank with 100 red magazines costs like one train wagon of iron ore or so, I had 10 tanks and it wasn't fun to lose them frequently) Best simple tactics for ai combat in my opinion is to prioritize worms. You can make them move out to newly scanned resources, clean up the safe zone around these resources, so a miner can move there.All of this is a lot easier to write as a code. But to 'draw' code in pictures like with logical circuits in Factorio can be very-very challenging(at least it was for me). Every picture(combinator) stores or passes some variable and you can't see these variables unless you click on combinators. Which means you have to memorize a lot more in order to analyze/edit the code. And it is very easy to make a mistake at first until you get used to this way of coding.The only nonvr game I have truly enjoyed since 2017

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, it's about building and vindicating a "defense factory" on a planet full of bugs. The first 30 minutes you still have to craft a bit by hand, but this phase is over very quickly. As soon as the first small mining drills are running, the game starts to be really fun. Everything is centered on the automation of production processes and the establishment of resource chains. I would even say the game is a bit like the old “Die Siedler 2”, which is meant as a compliment. By using circuits, triggers, drone settings, and so on, the game still gains in depth even after many hours. Moreover, the bugs (which are attracted by pollution from the factory - great game mechanic! :)) also give you a kind of Starship Troopers feeling. The story is not a super crazy one, but that's exactly what I personally like a lot.-> Factorio is my best single player game since FTL and there is even a MP mode here (which I haven't tested yet).-> 10/10 points, great game, totally worth it

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Factorio.My favorite thing about it is the progression. Everything flows perfectly into the next tier, adding layers of complexity. It's like a massive puzzle. Overall I've thoroughly enjoyed every moment of Factorio. It's extra-good with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: For Christmas I purchased Factorio from steam. I first saw my grandson playing it and I was intrigued. The premise is that you have crash landed on a planet that has natural resources and hostile aliens. The game is to build factories and research labs to construct a space ship to escape before the aliens kill you. This is defiantly a way to indulge your inner OCD. It is a little pricey($30) but I think it is worth it for a totally new concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game off and on for years and through different versions. This game has kept the same core mechanics yet improved some of my least favorite aspects, incredibly. I'm not sure how much longer it will be in early access, but it feels like a full fledged game right now. The mod community has very active and lots of good QoL or even game changing mods are available. Game changing to make it dozens of times more complex, which some people might like, or even automating railroad building. If you've ever liked Sim City or any other building and resource management game, you will love this. There is a learning curve to it, but you will be insanely in love right at the 1-3 hour mark.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Re-review of Factorio, Just after playing the game for 8 hours and completing the vanilla 'free play' mode of Factorio for the second time in my life. I can say for the money I paid, this game is a bargain. Sure the price tag is pretty high, around 45 dollars and never goes on sale. I have enjoyed it a lot, if you enjoy any kind of other automation game, or colony management game or even games like unpacking you'll probably enjoy the logistics and transport of items. I would say out of any games in this genre it's the best, this game does have a tough learning curve though, even if you have played other games like satisfactory. You have to learn to build your factories more orderly in order to be able to expand without destroying parts of your factory, you have to learn trains and signals (If you have ever played Satisfactory they are the same as in that game with block and chain signals). You also have to learn how to use circuits with pumps for advanced oil cracking and some other production lines. It does take some grit and determination to learn it, but it's very rewarding and each discovery helps you progress faster.The game runs pretty smooth for all games even when you have launched your rocket, but when you start going past that into 'mega base' territory it can stop you from progressing further. The menu's and systems are also pretty easy to use, however they should give you the four hotbars by default without having to crawl through the 'interface' options. It also doesn't teach you that you can switch the top hotbar to access up to ten of them.The game is pretty solid and doesn't have many bugs (Except for the ones trying to eat me and my walls), however I do have some issues around how personal logistics are handled. I do personally love them, it's the best QOL feature that allows you to automatically be supplied with buildings and dump unwanted items by logistic bots from the factory. However I wish that personal construction robots could automatically dump items into the logistic trash slots when your inventory is full. Also I tend to get stuck alot in pipes and have to delete a pipe or a storage tank to escape.However most issues and gripes you have with the game can be solved with one thing.The Ingame mod system!Whether you want power armour MKIII or an entirely new experience the mods tab in the menu has it all, however using them of course does take away the ability for you to unlock steam achievements but can still unlock them and see them in game. Though It would be nice if it had a system similar to Deep Rock Galactic, where you can still unlock achievements using only approved mods by the developers.So if you couldn't tell or skipped through the review, I absolutely think you should get this game. Factorio's highly addictive, runs well on most machines (until you have pass endgame or use lots of mods), has lots of great community content such as overhaul mods such as Krastorio, Space exploration (very popular) and pyanadon's modpack and other mods. With no bugs to boot.The Factory Must Grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game does most things right. It's highly addictive, but in a good way - it makes you think about your factory even while not playing the game. Any shortcomings, which are really just small quality of life issues, can be fixed by mods. The game has a built-in mod browser, and savegames can install mods automatically. The game is in active development, and gets patches regularly. The developers also publish regular blogs, which are always very interesting to read.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Absolutely brilliant game. In addition to the obvious sim, survival, and strategy components, there is a genuine science and even software engineering component to this game. On some levels it teaches logical networks, distributions, data flow, and also more general scientific and engineering principles. But more than all that, Factorio is great fun with endless creativity and replay value. The factory must grow.

_childDocuments_.review: It's all fun and games until bugs the size of buildings come to destroy you and your stuff. I'm serious. The enemies in this game can be slow to wake, but once they're up, you don't want to get in their way. The game takes the phrase "If you build it, they will come" and tells you to keep "them" at bay. The tutorial is very involved, good for starting out, but the games main intent is for you to see what works and what doesn't.All in all, as long as you are able to stay on top of your supply and demand, avoid getting killed by angry bugs and, for the love of the almighty, look before crossing the railroad tracks, this game will be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people won't see this as a survival game but it's one of the quintessential survival games. It challenges you to optimize everything from how you think about laying out your base to how you think about playing the game. It's simplicity is wonderfully pleasant. It is surprisingly fun to play co-op or PvP with friends. It requires a LOT of patience. Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a very addictive game of mass production. There is never a dull moment as there is always something in your factory that can be improved or expanded. The developers have several options allowing you to customize your game for the challenge you want, whether it be defending against hordes of biters or building the megafactory of your dreams in peace.If you are a perfectionist, this game will grab a hold of you and never let go
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most polished games I've ever played - and it hasn't even released yet! The art style is gorgeous, the gameplay is addictive, but varied and non-repetitive.It's infinitely replayable no matter if you want to start a new optimized factory learning from your previous mistakes, or if you continue forever optimizing and expanding your current one. Even if you somehow manage to get bored of the base game, there're lots of polished and well thought-through mods and scenarios available.During my 200 hours of playtime I've never encountered a single bug, and it ran silky smooth even on my business laptop! It definitely set new standards for me at how a game should look at release.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, if you like complicated games with lots to do. It's all about optimization, design, and balancing inputs and outputs. You can spend hours running back and forth across your factory, chasing things to fix, and it's the most consistent fun I've had in a factory simulator/sandbox game. A lot of the recent negative reviews don't have anything to do with the game itself, rather some apparently controversial things the developer said. If you can't separate the game from its developer when deciding whether to buy it, I hope that you miss out on a game this great.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a fastforward for your life. You sit down then next thing you know it's been 10 hours, you haven't eaten, moved or looked outside but you just need to do 'one more quick thing' before you can leave the factory for the day. Highly reccomend multiplayer so you can ignore the world together.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Have you seen all those praising reviews? Did you wonder how a game that looks so strange at first view could achieve something like this?The reasons therefor are multifarious.Factorio itself is a masterpiece and plainly the best in its genre and there is by far no other that could compete.The developers are genius. They deserve a monument for their transparent and responding behavior. Do you remember playing games where the community was toxic a. f...?The majority of people who play Factorio are helpful, friendly and interested in contributing their knowledge to make the game even better. How do I know you ask? I am constantly reading the forum entries on the website and here on steam. Even the controversial topics are exciting to read because of the many people arguing smart and reasonable. I already told you about Factorio being the incumbent in the genre and here is why. The gameplay triggers your brains to a level where it might even hurt a little bit and it has an incredible smooth learning curve. Something I find refreshing along all those mindless games. I have played quite some games in my lifetime but no other kept me engaged and thinking about it while not even playing. tl;drOf course this game isnt for everyone. No game can be that perfect. Factorio is nevertheless one of my favorite games of all time.I truly hope that everyone who is deterred by those first impressions will overcome their aversion and give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not very deep into the game, still feel like I have a lot to learn. Apex of its genre, based on what I have seen and played of its contemporaries. Unrivalled mod support to keep things going long after you launch the rocket. You don't need a big brain for the game, once you get going you will feel like you have one, regardless of the elegance of your solutions to the games presented problems. I do recommend you know what you are getting into. Not everyone can plop down squares on a grid for hundreds of hours, as that is ultimately what actual mechanical game-play primarily consists of.Don't wait for a sale, it isn't coming any time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing since before it was on steam and I have never felt bored with it. This game is worth the countless hours you will sink into it.Update for Space Age. I didn't know you could improve perfection. Then the DLC happened and I found out you can. I don't know what to say more that my hours logged in the game won't already tell you, this game is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Your factory will never be efficient enough. Your mines will always run dry. You will never be satisfied with anything about your factory - ever. You will neglect friendships, relationships, obligations with work. You will become the factory. Your life will now be about efficiencies, logistics, and killing native alien species to fulfill your twisted desires to launch countless rockets- thousands of them.10/10 will continue to pollute and genocide an entire planet for a dopamine fix.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, functional and mostly bug free even though still in development.  I usually avoid early access games, but this actually a GAME, not just some moving parts in a toybox.  Crash on a planet with a pickaxe to show for it.  Remember how to build a few things, like mining drills, furnaces, and conveyor belts, and go to work.  End up with a multi-screen factory creating flying drone-bots and laser turrets defending the walls of your mighty empire from the hippy bugs who hate pollution while you build your rocket ship to get out of there.  Fly for home!Crank up the settings... and do it again. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Well made, extremely optimised (so very playable on low end PCs) and ADDICTING!If you didn't know there's a free demo you can try. I'd guess that is way above average but my point is you'll hardly run out of content.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game will outright ruin gaming for you. It's a puzzle/base building/RTS/top down shooter hybrid that will make everything else you play pale in comparison. _childDocuments_.review: 186 hours in about a month and I put in 44+ hours of RL work 6 days a week. My house is in shambles and the cats are starving.  Master of orion 2 achieved this, Xcom apocolypse achieved this, Minecraft achieved this, Fallout 2 achieved this. Also lets not forget the recent, Stardew Valley and now we have Factorio. "one more turn , more more build, 3 hours later,,, crap, I gotta be to work in 4 hours and I havnt slept yet.". The thought and execution of how this game works and how it is put together is astounding to todays standards.It has a balance and flow that doesnt force a player into a instant meta as in "you have to do this like this all the time" but instead says, "it is your game too, play on.".  , then again why would you want to? Some folks have over 500+ hours on one map! I have one that has 96 hours currently. , you can feel it by how the controls and overall game mechanics flow seamlessly together. A lot of thought and some pure old school genius is at work here.If you loved the games from the 90's that relied on game mechanics and getting the most depth out of a little space then here it is.Parts of this game remind me of, Roller coaster tycoon, Minecraft, Sim city, and oddly Commando from a over head view "old NES version". It even has the flavor of a train simulator. It also is a puzzle game and really makes you think in a good way. _how can I build this-how can I make this better-how much bigger can I make it.I gotta add the negitives as well but there are not much to add; At first the game can seem daunting or even overwhelming when it comes to figuring out how things go together and work but that soon passes.  Starting the tutorial campaign helps with this. I would give this game a easy 10/10 but I give it a 9/10 because it is not finished yet.I strongly reccomend this game for those who like a building sandbox game where you feel you are achieving somthing every step of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to say anything that hasn't been said by everyone else, but this scratches the OCD organised optimisation itch like pretty much no other game out there. If you like the idea of starting with nothing and ending up with a sprawling automated system of finely tuned production where everything is about finding that next bottleneck, fixing it, and then working on the next level of complexity, just to rip out half of what you've done when you find a different way of doing it that would be about 20% more efficient, this is the game to play.Sure, there's monsters you shoot, and with the recent updates you can turn them from being "minor inconvenience" to "pain to stay alive", but the game shines in the way the complexity is steadily added from simply "mine stuff and turn it into other stuff having transported it on conveyor belts" to managing liquid production, using wires that turn stuff on and off with logical conditional statements, making new bases and building an automated rail network to send large quantities of stuff over large distances, then robots capable of carrying stuff through the air, then ... etc etc, every time you get a bit further you get faced with new opportunities, new problems, and new complexities to incorporate into whatever spaghetti network you've alread got.It genuinely takes a long time to get through a game to completion, and even when you feel like you've basically seen it all some of the mods add huge amounts of additional layers and tiers of complexity (such as the Bob's mods collection).SummaryIt's like a dynamic and evolving randomly generated puzzle game mixed with a colony builder, where a single playthrough can genuinely take tens of hours (the higher level achievement for speed play is to complete within 8 hours of game time, which gives you some idea of how much there is to do). Replayability is mixed (lots of settings you can change, map is randomly generated, but essentially you'll still be doing the same thing), but I've come back to it time and time again to try doing things differently or have more aliens attacking me or less resources to work with and so on.Very highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is the difficultty curve. It starts easy, you smelt some ore, no way you will ever run out of space, suddenly its night, plastic production is low and you need to figure out how to route more coal to it to support the growing production area. Then its suddenly afternoon and how in the hell are you supposed to manage to transport all the stuff to the rocket. Suddenly its a week later your family is having an intervention to get you away from cracktorio, but you missed it because you are almost at the one rocket per minute mark.In short, if you have time, download the demo, try it out. if you dont have any time, try it too anyway, factorio will teach you to optimize everything, including timeusage only to eat it all up anyway :D12/10, but be warned it will eat up your time like its nothing
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a thinking man's game. From the time I've spent with it, I can immediately see why there are so many positive reviews. There is always a better way to do what you're trying to accomplish, and the tools to do so are always at your disposal. It's a learning process that doesn't seem to cease nearly as quickly as in other games of these genres you could say this game taps into. If you're reading this review, my guess is that you will be happy you spent 20 bucks on this game no matter how much time you spend with it. This game is worth it

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough!In the domain of automation builders, this stands out as the most optimized and playable. It runs and looks great. You can play this alone, with a friend or in a group of 100.The vanilla game can keep you busy from between 50 to 150 hours, depending on how steep you want your learning curve to be. You can customize the difficulty extensively. Then there are several overhaul mod packs that each boast 100+ hours of progression.There is an element of PvE against the biters for players that seek that, and here you can follow several play styles. _childDocuments_.review: This game is truly brilliant it requires you to plan ahead and think about the long term. The graphics may not be the best in the gaming industry but it goes back to an era where graphics weren't everything and where gameplay and amounts of content were. The whole premise of the game is to get off the planet you crashland on and you do so by building machines to automate the process of researching the technology needed to build a rocket and leave the planet. However that's not how most people play this game. Most build extravagant factories that they just sit back and admire.
