_childDocuments_.review: When I discovered this magical game it was like nothing I had ever seen before it. Everything in this game is simple enough to understand as a brand new player but has enough depth to allow several thousands of hours of gameplay. While building your factory you run into problems left and right and that problem solving is so incredibly rewarding when it’s successful. I cannot see myself ever getting bored of Factorio, and if I ever tire of the base game there’s always a vast sea of content that is the Factorio modding community. One of the biggest things that I always take for granted is that Factorio has one of the least toxic and most friendly communities I have ever seen. There’s never and hate towards new players who don’t quite know what they’re doing yet, instead I see players giving productive suggestions to nudge them in the right direction. Everyone is always welcome to changes and new ideas and growth. Factorio is probably the best game that I have ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Why just choose one job in real life when you can abandon society, crash land on an alien planet and take up the mantle of civilization yourself. You are an aristocrat, engineer, and warmonger. You will dish out punishment with grenades at machine gun speeds and eerie precision to those who deserve it (trees, aliens etc.). You will literally throw railway tracks out the window of the locomotive as to construct the railway in front of you while riding at dangerous speeds. You will feast on fine dining fish and nothing else because it is the finest of foods a gentlengineer can consume. You are a god and no man or alien will stop you.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game... Spend over 1k hours in it and keep playing or coming back to it after months.The best game - a lot of fun, nice gameplay, nice mechanic, a lot of new features added from time to time, multiple different play style - you can keep grinding or just have something small and almost play like idle clicker :DBe warn though, you can sink in it for days.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: mining drill, mining drill, belt belt belt belt belt, inserter, burner, inserter, belt, belt, belt, belt, belt, inserter, assembling macine (iron gear wheel), inserter, assembling machine (science pack 1),  inserter, belt, belt, belt, belt, belt, inserter, lab(zapzapzapzap), reasearch complete. then comes science pack 2..... not gonna go therethis game will take hours of your time and make it feel like minutesconclusion: fun game
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine this, you crash land on a foreign planet, you awake to the sound of bustling trees and vivid wildlife. Now if you're a natural red white and blue blooded American such as myself the first thing you thought about this new planet is 'colonization and local genocide'.So you start chopping trees and burning coal to fuel the furnaces, then the dirty filty hippies (aliens) show up to spoil the fun. Naturally you shoot and kill these dirty hippies who want to stop you and your giant carbon footprint on their planet. So you go all starship troopers on them with machine guns, tanks, flamethrowers you get the point. Oh I also forgot to mention you are also allowed to liberate these filthy mongoloids from their oil too. But in all seriousness this game is amazing, it's one of my favorites and there's really two ways to play. You can watch some videos and learn the meta blueprints or do what I've done and only built things using your own thoughts and creativety. I have over 300 hours and have yet to look at any video that wasn't teaching me about the game(trains and how to automate them to run your ass over). Every component gets more complicated in terms of the recipe and you're always on your toes if you play with aliens on and try to expand too fast. Even if you beat vanilla the amount of mods to make your play through easier or harder gives this game almost unlimited replayability. If you enjoy solving problems and never truly being satisfied with your answer (always trying to improve a little bit over your last design) this game will scratch that itch. It's an absolute marvel and something that can only be copied and never surpassed.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I won't do the independent zones of the game, instead I'll try and summarize what you're actually doing and why it's fun playing a very nastalgic looking game like this.Summary: You're a lazy piece of crap that decides to crash into a planet inhabited by giant bugs, and in doing so completely strand yourself with no knowledge of how to build a ship, even though you're an engineer and just flew one.Back to being lazy. You're so lazy that you decide that creating a furnace will save your life. Well it didn't, but hey lets slap some iron in there because we're bored. Woah, iron plates, cool I'll just put that in my incredibly large pocket. Oh ok, a big a$$ bug is here, wonder wh- K my hand is gone, lets make guns and turrets and cranes and drills and conveyer belts and explode because you decided putting hot coal on oil would be a good idea.In Factorio, you are an engineer who crashes on a planet with very little resources to begin with. Your ultimate goal is to fly the heck out of there before you're bug food, but you need to go through multiple technologic advancements in order to build a Rocket Ship. The tech tree, art, sounds, and gameplay all work so greatly together to deliver an old timey ps2 2000s feel, you just can't help but feel happy when playing.Also, if something works....Please for the love of engineering, don't touch it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:This is a game about automation. If you enjoy setting up efficient systems that do all the tedious work for you, this game is gold. I've had over 200 hours of fun this far and I intend to keep playing. There is also a lot of mods that add tons of content.Long version:Start out with nothing, build some basic machinery to extract and refine materials and expand your factory until you eventually have all you need to send a sattelite into orbit. Beware that the local, semi intelligent animals are not fond of pollution, leading to a war between you and nature.Setting up and expanding your factory is the key part of this game. Finding joy in building complex networks and tuning it to achive efficiency is important, since there are few other ways of enjoying the game. There is a bit of combat and exploration, but without the factory you wont survive for long.Regarding difficulty, there are ways to customize that before starting a new game. For new players there is a tutorial campaign, but I don't recommend it. Instead you should start a game where you've set the aliens to being not a threat (you can get rid of them enirely if you want) and play around until you get a feeling for how stuff work (or check the wiki).There is great mod support for this game. Some mods add things that helps with completeing the normal game. Some add completely new stuff that makes things more complicated. Some make the aliens stronger. I am currently playing with some of Bobs mods and ArchAngels mods, making the game f*ing complicated, but if there is something you would like to see in the game, there might be a mod for that already.I have had some trouble with lagg, but that is probably because my graphics card is getting a bit too old and bad. Otherwise I have not encountered any technical difficulties.This game is Gold (but there is no gold in the base game)
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommend. I played Satisfactory before this and while they are both factory games, they play pretty different, and which to pick depends on what type of experience you are looking for. Factorio has higher stakes, with enemies that will attack your factory (if you keep peaceful turned off.). There is also limited resources at each node which require you to expand in search for more. In this way the game sort of dictates a pace for you to play at, which can be fun as long as that's what you want. If you want a more relaxing/immersive experience, then I would recommend Satisfactory instead, with unlimited resources at each node and enemies that don't attack your base, You can go at your own pace, and if you are a perfectionist, you can really spend the time to build your factory the way you want to rather then rush to get things up in running like I found myself doing in Factorio. The world's that you play in also differ quite a bit, Satisfactory has this beautiful hand crafted world, that even after playing for 200 hours I haven't seen everything in, and really inspires you to build something cool in, and also is something that you have to plan around. Factorio on the other hand has generated worlds which are nice in that they are extremely customizable and allow you to play in different ways from one game to the next, however don't really tend to pose much of a challenge building in one area versus another, atleast not in the same way that it does in Satisfactory. I also personally think that making things "efficient" and trying to load balance machines like you would in Satisfactory is a lot more difficult, but to the point where it's almost not worth it and just better to go for good enough. The ratio's are constantly changing and once you get to endgame I would presume that you could, but for a large portion of the game, it's just not really super feasible. Whereas in Satisfactory the ratio's are a lot simpler to work out for most things and you can better plan ahead to make sure that you can upgrade it easier down the line. Which is also probably more important than in Factorio because in Factorio you can make blueprints which allow you to easily rework large portions of your factory rather quickly, and even though they exist to an extent in satisfactory, they are much much much less capable. Honestly making blueprints in Factorio has been one of my favorite parts because they really give you a chance to dial things in exactly how you want them, and do it really well once, and then utilize that for the rest of the game. Overall I would definitely recommend you give it a shot, especially if you have a friend to play it with.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass in development.  Lots of people will tell you about how great the game is for it's gameplay.  I'll tell you about how great the dev team is that supports this game.  Consistent, thoughtful, meaningful updates and communication to and about the game.  The effort from this small team is second to none.  If you're sick of supporting half-finished AAA titles riddled with bugs and half baked ideas, look no further than this gem.This game is an absolute steal at twice the price, do not look at their "Never on sale" policy as greed, but as people deserving to be paid properly for good work, and the team at Wube absolutely deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game with at least 50-60 hours of gameplay before you start including mods or absurd factory optimization. There's a demo if you want to try it, although keep in mind the gameplay before you start the factory up and running is different to the rest of the game. Also, the devs are based in a way that keeps external ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ influence out of the game, so you know it's not gonna get shafted by stupid decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty damn good, definitely one of my top 5 games of all time. More crucially, this is a game I can definitely see myself having 1 run or two played per year for the rest of my life. Bang for buck is unrivaled, give the demo a shot, and if it activates your neurons the way it activated mine then buy it, and never look back.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing sandbox game. I can not tell you how addictive it is. I would recommend for literally anybody, however be warned it's not a pick up and play kinda game. From my first spaghetti factory to my feeble attempts at a megabase, I can strongly vouch for the replayability of this game. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: From the constant communication and dedication between Devs and Players, to the ever-growing amount of possibilities and adventures to be had, Factorio has turned the concept of labouring survivalism on its head, by removing basic human needs, and instead focusing on building the perfect fully-automated American Work Force Simulator, complete with environment-crushing pollution and pissed-off locals.11/10 Would kill natives for factory expansion just to mass-produce nuclear radioactive technology again.P.S. Yes, there is oil. A lot of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a top-down 2D game, where you play as a shipwrecked person and must build machines to survive. You start by mining some iron, copper, stone and coal to make machines, but then you use those resources to turn into drills, assemblers and conveyer belts to build it all for you. You can then reseraach techologies to scale that up infinitely.A very good game, also with a very easy to access modding community.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: It's too hard. It's all a big head game. Defending makes it harder. Letting them live makes it harder. Killing them makes it harder. Upgrading makes it harder.  Not upgrading makes it impossible. Doing nothing makes it harder. It just gets way harder all the way and you are always weak. It makes you think upgrades did something at first.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you Factorio
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!I've yet to launch a rocket, mostly because I haven't had time to play the game consistantly enough to get to the end game before a new patch came out (XD), but with the hours I've sunk into this game... it's definitely worth the money, and it's great fun.The multiplayer works great, and the dev team has done nothing but awesome things, and I feel like they really listen to the community to give them what they want :)My only regret is that I have but one thumb up to give!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Years of updates and bug fixes along with the 2.0 update brushing up the experience with an exceptional level of polish makes Factorio the title deserving of the Labor of Love Award.The core gameplay of Factorio is deceivingly simple but there is a substantial amount of depth to the challenges one faces when building out their factory. The difficulty and overall experience of the game can be tailored to one's liking through the map generator settings and tweaked even further through the use of the built-in mod manager.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, keep in mind this is no light thinking, easy going, no problem game. It requires large ammounts of logical processing. Factorio is a game about logistics and efficiency. You have to design and manufacture large lines that produce certain goods to procede in the game. But even if you aren't the best engineer or mathmatician you can still find enjoyment to learn how things work.Over all it is very intreaging to the people who like to problem solve. But it takes time to learn
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just one of the best Factory based games.You start small and expand big (very big if you want to)There is no "wrong" way to do anything, Yes, it could be more optimized, but do you have to? no!If you like everything nicely organized, you could satisfy your OCD like no other game Or you could leave it as a big spaghetti construction and explore your factory over and over again trying to find where everything was made :)For those who like some combat in these types of games, They have bugs! loads of bugs (if you let them) So prepare yourself for some "Tower Defence" mechanics while trying to expand! But be aware, the more you expand, the more bugs you will piss off!and for some other people; They have trains! and yes, trains need dual locomotives if you want them to be able to reverse, they do not magically go through each other on 1 single track, they will crash and you can actually sort a smart routing track with signal that you manage yourself!All in all this game has everything you could want. Add some mods to the game (BOB's and you are in for a long ride of building your factory.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: A game that draws you in with straightforward mechanics and simple premise will consume you into a world of bots, trains, and biters. For an early access game it's incredibly polished and each release leads to more and more optimization. The devs are very active (check out their weekly blog) with the community and have created an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an engineering masterpiece, no questions asked.The premise is simple: mine resources, crafe them into different items. These items can help you automate mining, automate crafting, and eventually The design of the game is incredible at taking complex tasks, breaking it down into simple components you can focus on and over time you will be able to achieve everything! Every single complex item is broken down into a tree of smaller, easier items, which in turn can be automated further. Never in the game you're dealing with an overwhelmingly complex problem that you don't know how to handle.A usual playthrough of a game will take around 40-60 hours, depending on the person. If you want to see what type of person you are, absolutely do download a demo, it's around 4 hours of content for absolutely free.In addition, an "average playthrough" doesn't have to stop at the final task, like killing the ender dragon in minecraft doesn't end the game; it's all a sandbox, do what you want!The game is incredibly optimised, I've been able to run pretty large factories on my very very old laptop. People have constructed absolutely enourmous factories, nowhere close to what I can do, it's a fascinating watch on youtube, I highly recommend checking them out. There are always things to optimise, the number of things to do will grow way faster than you can handle them, which can lead to some decision paralysys. What helps is that time is not of the essense and this is an amazing game to get lost in and spend a night or two without sleeping just expanding your factory. As everyone in the community says, The devs are amazing and respond to bugs so fast. There've been patches that fix a single visual glitch because somebody on the subreddit said "literally unplayable" that a shadow goes behind a rock and not in front of it. The Factorio Friday Facts are an amazing long read going into details of what the devs have been working on over the years and it just makes me appreciate Wube team even more.Overall, 10/10 engineering simulator, probably the most niche sandbox I'll ever play, but I love every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the most well-designed, well-maintained video game ever. It sparked the entire "factory game" genre and still stands on top as king of that genre a decade later.The base game and its DLC are 100% worth their price tags. However, it is not a casual game. Not hardcore, either, but... play the demo. If you like what you see, you will like the full game. It's just the tip of the iceberg.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Design your own factory to the last machine.Sit in a comfy chair and enjoy the experience... or tryhard by calculating crafting ratios, designing the perfect layout and creating the most efficient contraptions, the game ensures that you'll enjoy it no mater the playstyle.Amazing 'quality of life' features suggest that this may be one of the few games where the developers actually played their own creation and weren't limited by the studio to add whatever they felt was necessary. It's what I miss in gaming nowadays.Spin it up, the factory is waiting for you... and the factory must grow!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive, endless replayability, huge active player-base and endless mods. Factorio is one of the best indie games i have seen, let alone own, and always keeps my brain thinking of more efficient, compact, Etc. ways of building. I would go so far that i would say it has improved my thinking of real world situations.Worth the price, endless fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: "I'll just update this part before I ... (do anything)"several days later"Well, that took longer than I expected. Let me just finish this little thing before I ... (do that other thing)"several days later"FFFFFFUUU, where did the time go!? ?!?!"This game is like a time machine. It takes a person makes him/her disappear for hours or days without them noticing.just awesome[edit: With the new version 2.0 (and Space Age DLC) this game hasn't lost any of it's good vibes. This game is still awesome, and the developers deserve all praise for keeping working on this!]
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: this game... don't do it, your life loses meaning. you dream of belts and efficiency. And then you discover the mods! O.o The devs have made an incredible game they update it regularly with fixes and it has one of the least toxic communities I've ever known in gaming. Unless you take a screenshot with your phone camera :)
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 would get addicted again.But seriuosly, this game is just awesome. I can't wait for the official release and the features that come with it!You can do soo much with this game.  Small, casual, inefficient factories or go all in and mod it hardcore. You even have the ability to mod yourself because the mod API is easy to understand and mods use lua (remember ComputerCraft? - thats also lua) in my opinion a very easy to learn programming language.Have too much time in your life? - Get Factorio!Just do it!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: If you like setting up huge factories just to scrap them down and build them all over again once you get better tech, well, this game is for you.100h in and still it feels like I'm scratching the surface, not even touching mods or alternative game-modes beside freeplay.The game is still under development as of this review, but it already offers what feels like the full experience, and they may even expand on that. No doubt I'll be playing this on release.All in all, a solid game, very well done, for those who like optimizing huge factories spanning kilometers, building lines of self reloading and repairing turrets, and also exterminating aliens with the power of mechanization. Just don't buy hoping it to be a top-down shooter because you might be a little bit disappointed
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my friends. The game was not for me, but when I joined my friends world I could see the hours of dedication they had put into it. Specially if you are a fan of making a game automative so you can collect all your resources and do nothing at a point, but the grind to get to the point must have been something. I would recommend this game on that point.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: So I went into this game very excited for a survival-esque game where you crash land on a planet and using science and machines, eventually build a rocket and escape back to space. So I began the very addicting process of mining, building, automating, and repeating. I spent many hours learning of locomotives and how to make the signals speak to each other to make a smooth system. I researched faster speeds at which to automate and move resources more efficiently. And most important of all, I researched increasingly deadly weaponry to fight back against the alien scum. Man those bugs are annoying. The fight to survive went on, sometimes desperate, but I always managed to pull through. The factory grew larger, I expanded for more resources, and the planet got sickly. My factory went nuclear and the rocket began to be built. Soon I would be able to leave this little planet and it's residents. Then the aliens attacked and destroyed part of the factory. Enough was enough. I took my tank and decimated the vermin. And out of spite I took my flamethrower and burned all the forests I could find. I pumped as much pollution I could into the water and air. (Imagine that song "How bad can I be" from The Lorax). It was at this time the rocket finished. After many hours, I was about to escape from this planet on the rocket and win the game. Preparations complete, I began the launch sequence. As the rockets fired up its boosters, I contemplated as the trees burned in the distance the sacrifice, dedication, and risk it had taken to get to this moment. I was victorious, I thought as I watched the rocket I would escape on launch into space...Turns out you don't actually leave on the rocket, it's just another way to get a lot of science for your research. I'm sure there is a lesson to be learned here as the planet burned around me... but who cares, the factory must continue to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Simply the best strategic build simulation gameplay I've ever had. Its game engine is simply a monster, it can simulate gigantic factories, with millions of objects interacting (factories, components, conveyor belts, trains, enemies, etc) with no frame rate drop. I can say multiplayer coop gameplay is really cool. The game has a huge tech-tree, which is well balanced. The modding capabilities of this game adds so much to it: if you get tired of playing vanilla, the modded version simply transforms this game into a huge complex game, with tons of new challenges. If I could recommend this game twice here, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, my only criticism lies in how the multiplayer handles latency hiding. Whenever you shoot in combat or drive vehicles, it breaks the latency hiding making it feel absolutely horrendous to play at times. It seems to apply mostly to everyone except hosts, and mileage may vary depending on your latency. I have some friends I play this with and it's an amazing experience, but this latency hiding breaking during combat and driving heavily dampens the fun and just makes it frustrating at times. So while my overall review remains positive, I feel compelled to post a disclaimer to anyone purchasing this game to play together with friends. While you will still have a fun time building your base together, the combat and driving may be heavily delayed and laggy depending on your latency. This has been an issue for years (The oldest post I could find about this on a simple google search was back in 2015) and I hope one day the devs will get latency hiding working for combat and driving, as this is a frustrating and frankly disappointing blemish on what is otherwise a great multiplayer experience. Of course if you only play single player then none of this applies to you, the game is great regardless.

Sure, You may have figured out the optimal production ratio for green circuits, but now how do you fit it into your factory? And then how do you fit ten more? And then three hours later, can you squeeze in another one?This game gives you little to no guidance, an infinite canvas, and a well developed toolbox for you to build your wildest factory designs. If you don't like such open ended games, maybe move along.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, let me just state this right away:  If you're bothered by the game's price, dont be.  This is more than worth the $30, no question about it.  Frankly, for something this good, I'd have gladly paid double.  Factorio is something very, very special.  Incredible, almost unmatched depth and complexity and an absolutely staggering amount of content await you here.  And fun, lots of fun.The game's trailers do a good job in showing you what it's all about.  Stranded alone on a strange planet, you need to find a way to call for help.  And the only way to do that is to get a satellite into space, via a rocket.  But a rocket isnt something you can just craft.  Nor can you just build it out of blocks like in other games.  Such an incredibly complex thing demands far more than just that.  No, in Factorio, the only way to reach your goal is to design an entire factory to produce all the things you need.  A really HUGE factory.You start off small.  When you begin a new game, it's just you, and the surrounding landscape.  Grab a few resources, and make a pick, Minecraft style.  Gather a bit of iron, coal, copper, and so on.  You'll notice that this is an incredibly slow process.  This, though, is a game about automation, not mining by hand.  Right away, you'll start crafting and placing machines to do the mining for you, and fueling them with coal.  And you'll start to automate further than that.  Why fill each machine with coal by hand, when you can use conveyors to send it to where it needs to go, and "inserters" (robot hands) to grab it and put it in the machines?  This is where the automation begins, and where the game starts to show hints of it's brilliance and potential.  Getting even just this little, simple setup going for the first time feels great, and is the point where many players will suddenly find themselves hooked.From there, the complexity mounts ever further.  You soon have electrical power, and once that happens, the game really gets going.  You'll be setting up entire arrays of mining devices and smelters, with conveyors going all over the place to get things where they need to go.And by "things", I mean ALOT of things.  Something I found surprising was the sheer scale of this game.  Factorio isnt the only game to have you building a factory... heck, even Minecraft does it with mods and such.  But this game has a total focus on it, and factories are about mass production... emphasis on "mass".   At first, 100 iron plates might seem like alot.  But a couple of hours later, and you'll be going "I only have 2000 of these, I'm running out!".   You'll be producing items by the thousands, tens of thousands, whatever.  And chances are it still wont ever truly be enough.  It's extremely daunting when you're first starting out.  There's a sense of "oh wow, this might be too much for me".  But stick with it.  The tutorial is... lacking, to say the least, but I find that the game's overall flow works nicely.  You'll gain new things to make from an utterly monstrous tech tree, and each new thing will build upon concepts you've already learned.  You have alot of opportunity to experiment with each thing and learn what they can really do.And there's so many of them!  Mining devices, smelters, boilers, splitters, a whole array of different types of inserters, trains, and even things like assemblers, which take a crafting recipe, and repeatedly makes that item, provided you give it the components it needs.  Suddenly, instead of just crafting inserters yourself, you've set up an automated process to just make them for you.  You can even have the assemblers make more assemblers!  And with a game of this scale, you'll probably end up doing exactly that.  There are all sorts of things you can build and use, and a million different ways to use them, and this is where the game's challenge shows up.  A factory is a complicated thing.   VERY complicated.  You can see that even in just the trailer.  All sorts of situations will appear to challenge you.  You need some pre-made gears and copper wire going at the same time towards some assemblers, but you've already got lots of other machines around and conveyor belts going all over the place.  How can you fit it in there?  You'll puzzle through stuff like this constantly.  And you'll be constantly looking for ways to improve your factory.  After all, a good factory is efficient, yes?  The best part is, with so many different parts available to you, you have extreme freedom in how you go about things.  You can play the game YOUR way, come up with your own designs and ingenious builds.  And however good they may be (or not so good) there's always room to improve, always chances to try new things.   The depth here is astonishing.  As is the sheer amount of freedom you have.Better yet, everything is "smooth".  The game is freakishly optimized, for one.  But also, it's stuffed full of convenience and anti-frustration features.  For instance, if you want to craft an assembler directly, it needs specific components.  But you dont need to waste time making each individual one.  The game will automatically queue up every little thing it needs, and craft them, and finally put together the assembler.  And your character can still run around and do things while this is being done.  There are MANY things like this in the game, making sure you have a good time instead of an irritating time.And best of all... there are no dull moments.  There is ALWAYS something to do, and all of those things are engaging, interesting, and challenging.  You'll even be going to war against swarms of monsters who arent too happy about you being there.  While the learning curve here is very high, I think it's more than worth it.  You'll find yourself addicted quickly, and having a great time every step of the way.  There's very good reason as to why this game is rated #2 on Steam.  And hey, there's even full mod support!  Customize the game however you like!  A great deal gets even better, yeah?Overall, just incredible.  Absolutely incredible.  It's hard to find anything negative to say about this.  But I could praise it all day.  Easily one of the best games out there right now, and it's only going to get better from here.Just be warned, it'll eat your time.  There's another review somewhere that says something like "I had a family, now I have a factory".  You'll quickly grow to understand what they meant by that.  You've been warned!...Really though, just buy it.  You'll be glad you did.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. That is undeniable. Do you want to know how I discovered Factorio? Through an old SsezthTzeentach video. I was interested, so i pirated it. I finished the game once on the pirated version and it took me 56 hours. And it felt like 2. And now I'm reviewing it, because after i finished it the first time, I bought it from here and finished it again so at the time of review, I have maybe 150 hours in this game.I want to start by talking about the tutorial. I highly recommend you take it, because it is a good way to ease you into the game.  The genius of the tutorial is that after the first level, each stage puts you in the ruins of a base, with some of it being active. This is amazing because the goal of "JUST START A FACTORY BRO" does not seem as daunting, since you have half of it made and the ruins let you know what it looked like before. From then on, the tutorial feels like it just lets you play the game with the tools you get from green science. The one complaint i have with the tutorial is that it does not, in any capacity, cover oil. I feel like since oil is so important to win, the tutorial should have maybe given you a ruined oil processing plant with light heavy and petroleum and told you to fill your car up with 10 blue circuits or something.Now what's it like to actually play the game? Well, if you get invested, It's the most addictive and time consuming thing ever. The stated goal of the game is to build a rocket and send it to space. The real goal of the game is to optimize and fine tune your logistic system so that your factory does 2 things:1) It works completely automatically, with products eventually becoming science2) It performs task 1 efficientlyOne thing you must always remember is that at one point, the factory will come to a stop, for 2 main reasons (assuming it is achieving goal 1)a) Your resource patches run outb) You've run out of things to researchAnd lastly, the biters. These serve as your enemies during the whole game. Since the map is infinite, so are your resources, but so are the biters. These guys are pretty simple at first glance: All your building produce pollution. If pollution reaches biter nests, they will gather up their forces and launch attacks. However, the more time these guys spend in pollution, the more they will evolve. They will get harder, better, faster and stronger. Additionally, they will also expand their bases, generally coming closer to your factory.  And that is why these are a piece of brilliant game design, since chances are, the worse you are at the game, the less your buildings will be active and you will produce much less pollution then the typical Factorio player.Well that's pretty much all I wanted to say. I'll leave you by telling you that my most played genre's are Mobas and FPS, and yet I still adore this complicated game, so I recommend you give it a shot as well. Additionally, the mods for Factorio are amazing. Rule 34 for Factorio is that if you can think of it, there's a mod for it.And remember my Texan brothers, THE FACTORY MUST GROW!

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:Surviving a crash landing, the protagonist of Factorio finds themselves on a resource-rich planet. From iron ore to coal, the planet offers the chance to rebuild and find a way home.Pros:- Rich Environment: The game starts with a plethora of natural resources like iron ore, coal, trees, and stones, setting the stage for crafting and building.- Evolutionary Gameplay: From manual resource collection, players quickly evolve to creating transport belts, automation arms, and more. It's a balance between manual tasks and automation.- Dynamic Threats: The planet is not uninhabited. Local creatures are not fond of the new industrial intrusion, posing a threat to players.- Creative Base Building: Multiple options for defense (e.g., walls, turrets) and ample ways to structure your base, offering a fresh experience each time.- Complex but Rewarding Tech Tree: As the game progresses, newer technologies keep the production chain exciting and challenging.- Massive Community Support: Many online resources, such as guides and videos, help new players adapt and learn.- Constant Sense of Progress: The game rewards forward-thinking and strategy. Each step feels like progress.Cons:- Overwhelming Complexity: With so much to learn, some players might find the game's steep learning curve daunting.- Limited Campaign Missions: The campaign could benefit from more structured missions, especially for endgame content.- Information Overload: Some in-game information and graphs can be hard to digest and understand for beginners.Conclusion:Factorio, primarily a building game, provides a unique twist by personifying the builder in a survival scenario. The game's strength lies in its detailed crafting and building systems, complemented by a sense of constant progression. While the complexity can be overwhelming, the sense of achievement and an active community make it a game worth diving into.

_childDocuments_.review: The Factory Must Grow!    Factorio is a game about automating everything. _childDocuments_.review: If you love being creative and building huge automated bases then this is the game for you. Factorio offers a unique blend of survival and complexity management without being repetitive or grindy. Unfortunately, the game isn't without its flaws.While the complexity may feel overwhelming, once you compartmentalize these the game becomes a matter of sticking together components that take in resources and give out resources. This makes the game rather simple and more grindy as it requires you to expand to get more resources to build more factories. The problem with this is that expansion is hard as you need to put down turrets to expand (aliens on default are aggressive and everywhere). Luckily, most of this process is automatable by using construction robots.The addition of train cannons in 0.16 made expansion vastly easier. The cannon automatically fires and clears areas of aliens so you can move in.The game should have more components and complexity, as it's quite easy right now to reach end game once you know how to build everything. One aspect I'd like to see is perhaps food with real-time mechanics (e.g. it takes a week in real time to starve). Another thing would be glass processing and "Sea Block" (a mod for the game that adds ocean-based elements) to be in the base game.Another problem with the game is the lack of builtin tools to aid factory management. We can only see production statistics but not what is bottlenecking the factory. In addition, a builtin ratio calculator would be neat. As of right now, you need to look up the crafting recipe and calculate factory ratios manually which can get cumbersome.Overall it's a very enjoyable game and I'm looking forward to seeing new developments.If you finished the base game and enjoyed it, go get the DLC

_childDocuments_.review: Coming up to 5000 hours playing this game, and im still learning new things in multiplayer.  The devs are by far the best ive ever seen.  FFF (Friday Fun Facts) is a blog post they write up every Friday.  Every. Single. Friday. For the last ... 4 years?  look at them on their website, its not a 2 min blurb, its a full review of what they've done that week, and where they're headed, what their plans are, current iterations they're going over, complete with pictures and sometimes *chuckle* hand drawn graphs.  Their IRC channel (there is a link on their website) has someone on the dev team there pretty much 24/7.  Not just "community manager" nitwits (Trangar, te he), but guys like Rseding91 (their C++ guru) that are programming the actual updates.  Oh.  There are updates.Are there sometimes bugs in the patches?  Sure.  Which is why you sometimes see 2 patches in the same day.  Bugs get quashed immediately whenever possible.  While this review doesnt speak much about the game, the team behind it deserves the recognition - its amazing, thoughtul, and incredibly well done because of them.In a nutshell, its similar to RTS games like starcraft, where you build up and gather resources.  But instead of spending 20 minutes to build up a base to have the game end in 2, you keep building.Building Bigger.Making things more efficient.Tearing down and rebuidling.Im almost 5000 hours in and sticking with vanilla until I can personally say Ive mastered it.  Once I stop learning new things almost every time I play, ill start fooling around with mods.  And there are lots of them.  Is this game worth $20?  It absolutely was for me.  This single $20 purchase brought me thousands of hours of entertaintment, frustration - when things didnt work planned, and absolute delight - when things get fixed, and I can reflect on my orchestra of 500 machines working in harmony.  Whether or not it is worth it for you is up to you.  But I would be remiss if i didnt impore you to give it a try, get the demo, fool around, commit an hour or two.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  Sandbox "build your base" kind of game, designed around the premise of automating all of your natural resource gathering and production.  I like the concept a lot, but after playing for a few hours I realize it's just not my bailiwick.  It's one of those games where it feels like you're doing work rather than enjoying a game.  Think of the Sims and how much work and annoying it got to balance your work/home life in it.  Think of Super Mario Sunshine and how annoying it got to be to have to clean up all those annoying blights on Sunshine World.  This game feels worse than that.Mind you I enjoy Rimworld.  I enjoyed Minecraft.  I like the kind of game where you build your base around survival and creativity.  But this felt like rather than building a base for survival, you were doing it as a job.  You were doing it for the sake of doing it.  Something doesn't feel "fun" about that to me.Cool concept, nice features.  But it just falls short of giving me an experience where I'm playing a FUN game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Great game if you like resource management combined with base building and logistic systems; think prison architect for building but then with a character, and spacechem / infinifactory with regards to management.Gameplay: Gather resources (manually at first, automated later) and build stuff with it! The main goal is basically survival, where you need to defend everything you build from aliens who become more aggressive overtime (nothing too zerg in the beginning, you've got time and it’s nicely balanced). Build mines to help you gather resources, build conveyor belts to transport your resources to things that use those resources and make a nice system out of it all... or don't and have chaos :DGFX: So it’s a top down view with some good looking GFX for the kind of game it is. I THINK most of the gfx are pre-rendered sprites which have a 360 degree render pass done on them, but that definitely can’t be hold against the game.Story: You get dropped on an alien planet where your main goal is to survive, build a base, research technology to keep you alive and build a base strong enough to sustain launching a rocket into outer space.Pros:  - Good GFX - Great Gameplay - Awesome Co-op experienceCons: - Interfaces are sometime unclear / unclean. - No clear tutorial yet explaining late-game stuff, it takes some time to figure out, but don't let it hold you back.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw factorio on steam, I wasn't to sure about buying it. It was then when I watched the video I thought "hey. I would like this." It was the biggest decision in my life on steam. I never thought I would enjoy rebuilding, remapping, and repairing sevral times due to new technology and constant alien swarms, I actually quite enjoyed it. Don't get me wrong here, the things I mentioned above may sound like cons but the pros outweigh it a truckton. Something I would like to state is that, late game (but not end) alien artifacts couldn't be more overpowered. One artifact makes 10 alien science packs. And that's it. No smart inverters, no advanced circuits, just alien artifacts. To construct the rocket silo you only need 100 and within gaining the car and some armor piercing bullets you can get about 200 from 14-18 spawners, and those are relatively easy to kill, considering once your attacking spawners you should have at least a submarine gun but that's pretty early game. What I'm saying is that you may want to either make more tech that requires alien science packs, lessen the drop amounts from spawners, etc. But other than that the game mechanics are pretty balanced, aside from the worms which can still be countered. Some new things I would personally like to see would be: better exosuits, so you can storm into enemy bases, mk 2 and mk 3 tanks and cars, so you could have more health or more speed when driving around, advanced trains that consume more materials or an electric train, more types of robots, boats, planes maybe, better breaks for tanks (you don't know how many pipes/poles I've broken), and more diverse and plentiful enemy types. Overall, factorio is an excellent game and I've recommended it to all of my gamer friends and would recommend it to anyone else. If you've got 20.00 $ you've got happiness and creativity through factorio. Something else I also forgot to mention was that this is literally the ONLY game that has opened up my mind and forced me to think more than I do in math class. 10/10 Best game of its kind ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the best games I've ever played.  I'm about 12 hours in so far, and there's more and more ahead by the looks of it.I'm sure the intro and other reviews cover aptly what the game is all about so I won't rehash any of that.  What I will list however are the things I see as good points, and why I like it.Firstly unlocking a tech tree is always something I like doing, and having the various items aid the next step etc helps.Next, the contruction/destruction.   There's plenty to place in Factorio, from belts to trains, but it's nice that is usally made very easy, and even better, there's no penalty for destroying and rebuilding.  This leads to endless tinkering and optimising.  It also means you don't always end up building yourself into a dead end, so planning to the nth degree isn't required (though for mega structures, a change can of course have massive knock ons).The game is really quite easy to understand, it's pace is down to you, you can just leave it all sitting there doing nothing if you want, or keep it running 100%.But it's not something that requires you to sit and wait for ages for something to happen.  Sure there'll be a few minutes here or there, and the reasearch can take quite some time, but there's always something to do.   Mining asteroids in Eve this is not.So easy to understand, no penalty for changes, lots to change and optimise and all at your own pace.  It's utterly brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 2nd most played game on Steam (as of writing this). Seemingly complicated at first, taken piece by piece, everything falls into place. Constant troubleshooting and problem solving as you continue to increase the size of your open face factory. As you build, you have to keep an eye on the native "bugs" that will come after you for your pollution atrocities. However,, clearing out their "camps" will keep them at bay, as you push them back as you expand. The mechanics are simple yet effective, and even before 1.0 this game felt amazing. I can see them adding more to an end-game situation in the future. But even once you launch that rocket, you're more than happy to start again from scratch and do it bigger and better.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what I can say that others haven't. Factario is deceptively fun. The gameplay is structured so as to steer the player towards their own natural short, medium, and long term goals. There's so much to do and so many ways to do it, it's easy to get in enjoyable multi-hour distractions to improve your factory before remembering that you actually intended to build something specific.I was hesitant on what to expect but I've really enjoyed the game.Update: Space Age expands on the game a lot, it's easily one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game. Don't think, just buy. This is one of them games that looks good on paper, but turns out to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing! I am completely hooked. I haven't played any game to any extent other than factorio since purchasing a week or so ago.I think this is the second review i have ever written on steam because i feel the devs deserve it. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in 2016 and enjoyed 52hrs of gameplay just learning it without enemy attacks activated. Someday I'll play it again with some friends and try to beat it with the aliens on hostile. I think I got my value out of it already but there are still more hours of content when I am ready.Now I'm writing this review because although I enjoyed this game 5 years ago it has become apparent that now is the time to tell the world that it is a great game and it is worth your investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRIf you like sandbox games where you can just build a giant factory for the sake of having a giant factory, this is an amazing game.If you actually need a purpose for building said factory, maybe spend your 32 bucks elsewhere.I love automation games, and am a sucker for working out logistical problems in a factory.But when it comes to Factorio, it seems to me like it has such great potential.Even the high pricetag seems to be reasonable at first if you consider the shear amount of content it provides.But in the end it is laking one very big important thing for me.A questline. Or any kind of guide to tell you what to actually do in the beginning.My Buddy tells me we can build a railsystem.I say for what, we seem to have everything we need nearby.He says we could research rifles.I say why, the wildlife only seems to get provoked if we come to close, and otherwise we aren't threatened by anything.To me the campaign just feels like sandbox with a reasearch system slapped onto it so you can't build everything straight from the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a great game.There's a solution for everything in this game, and it all has to do with machinery. It's like a puzzle, except you're in control of what goes where. There is no guideline or specific way to do anything in this game. The game doesn't really feel repetitive, although there are times when you can simply sit and watch your dense factory produce bullets and pollution. It always seems like there's so much to do, which is awesome for any game.The UI is incredibly simple, and gets straight to the point. No tabs, everything is grouped in a way that makes sense, and is readily available at any point in time. There are some situations that can be a bit confusing, as most slots have no label. SHIFT + Click sometimes sends items to an unexpected place; however, this particular issue is to be solved very soon.The visuals are quite nice and everything fits pretty well. It's fun to watch the machines work and produce stuff.There are enemies in the game, and they scale with your progress. As you pollute the world, the aliens get more aggressive, to a point where they'll send big hulking aliens that'll try to rip your factory apart. You also have weapons to defend yourself with. The presence of aliens will eventually force you to focus your factory on military purposes, such as grenades, bullets, bombs, armored cars and tanks, and power armor which can become so strong you can stop a train by standing in its way. Combat is simple, but seems polished. Vehicles take a bit of time to get used to, especially when trying to stop and reverse, but they're not borked or difficult to use.The progress in this game works very well; you start with simple coal-burning machinery and work your way to more advanced machinery. Over time, you unlock better machines that are more efficient, which forces you to re-design parts of your factories. I have personally re-designed my science facility 3 times already, each time improving it's efficiency and reducing its size.The developers of this game are absolutely, hands-down the BEST developers I've ever encountered; they are always transparent, they work hard and enjoy what they do, they explain what they do to the community, they listen to what players want/need, they test their game and don't add features that do nothing. I'm currently playing on the most recent build of the game, which is oddly called "Unstable", even though it's more stable than any other game I've ever played.Did I mention trains? Yeah, there are trains too.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I'v been playing factorio now for a good 2 years almost 3 now, and so far its been an amazing game that has some really good replayability as well. you start off small manually mining ores, but quickly begin to do basic automation. which then becomes a snowball effect untill you have mega processing areas that just pump out goods, which are then used to make even more things and so on. This game is extremly stable, through out my play time i'v only had the game crash once. but other than that one small bump in the road it has ran extremly well. Pros:- lots of replayability- very good progression/tech system- nice graphics (my opinion)- trains!!!! and robots to move stuff around- can create blueprints then have robots build stuff based on blueprints- good map generation as well as lots of options for the map generator- in game map editor/scenario editor - large variety of ways to reach end game ( IE kill all the natives and take their oil and rapidly expand, or build small and compact base and try to deffend from the natives if you p*** them off)- Ai are well balanced but could do with a few more variety- lots of ways to deal with the natives such has tanks, rocket launchers, or gas grenadesCons- end game isn't fully completed altho its still being developed- As I said before could use a few more types of nativesAll in all its a really good game for the price they are asking for and they have a friday facts where they talk about everything they have done in the week so you can get an idea of what the next update is going to be about. if you have the money and you think you'd like this then buy it, and its even more fun if you can get a server going with a few friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! I was not expecting it to be this expansive and rich with things to do. My only issue is with the enemies; they're just bugs. The variation of those bugs is just color/size. I would prefer if they were more thought out. However, whatever brain power that wasn't devoted to the bugs was sure as hell devoted to the game-play. 9/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game with interesting gameplay.Gameplay is well optimized and interesting almost through all parts of the game. The main gameplay is in building your base to produce some technological stuff, to build a bigger base that can produce more technological stuff. Sounds simple, but you will create your own little factory with a power plant by yourself, developers give us a lot of different types of items and buildings, which you can manipulate, and optimize for building some unstoppable production.You will solve big problems in your factory such as: optimizing your resource delivery conveyor or delivering iron ore by trains, creating fire turrets for defense, or enriching uranium for a nuclear reactor. Sounds really hard to do and boring, but the game makes you feel fun from these problems and make you happy when you find some genius way to use standard things better. And this game fit well for a lot of kinds of players, from hardcore one to some lazy people which just want to chill after work. Also if you get bored from the main side of gameplay you can make a tank or car with a machine gun and just drive a little outside your base and kill some biters. And it will also help you in the main part of the game because you will spend less time defending your base from attacks.Nice optimization and interesting mechanic with pollution and biters adding into your game another side of gameplay, the part which is interesting too but not so interesting as the main part of gameplay, because we don't have a lot of weapon types and some parts are not so effective for battle as you think when you collect resources to produce them. But you can find a lot of opportunities using buildings for your battle. Actually, they probably were made without any thinking to use them in the battle directly, but it's great that you can use them effectively in it so that it will open a big window for different manipulations.One problematic time period was when my base had already grown up a little and my base was almost like spaghetti. So it was a little boring to rebuild all this stuff. So it's the biggest problem of the game.A little disappointing is the ending, I think they can make more tools for the end game era to let players feel like a god.And also I can mark one thing: the game world is endless so you can't get some happiness from your in-game tasks such as: killing all biters, researching the whole planet and etc. It looks like a good point for multiplayer or for some experienced players but I don't think so for new players it's good too.Anyway, it's a great and unique game, so I recommend it for purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Simply an amazing game.  I have hundreds of hours played on it before the Steam release, and I'm still planning on hundreds more.  The addiction is unreal.  You'll be seeing conveyor belts in your dreams.  There is always something you could be doing better, some tweak you could make to be the tiniest bit more efficient.  It is simply incredible how much content this game provides, along with a ton of replay value, especially considering the very active modding community.10/10 would sell my soul again.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a fantastic game with a large level of creative depth in terms of a constructing a factory. That said, every time I see news for it, the sound of multiple inserters starts up in my head. To say this game is a hidden horror game would be nothing less of a joke to most people (minus those who've played it for as long as I have and or way longer). 11/10 would recommend to a friend who wanted to never sleep without hearing those infernal machines at work.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Weird to get used to but its actually a really fun and challenging game. I always get deep into it then restart my game to build my world even more efficient than the last one. I do really enjoy this though, its very user friendly and once you learn it, its pretty easy to progress in terms of you really just need time, patience, and figuring out how to best plan something.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game for many many hours before it was on steam. The dedication and attention to the quality and details of the mechanics by the Devs is incredible. I strongly encourage anyone interested in the game and how it's made or why things were done a certain way to read their Friday Facts. I have always found them to be very interesting reads.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game about 6 months ago and have played around 100 hours before the steam release. This game is so polished and ive never even had the game crash on me once. I love this game, there is so much depth on the base game and there are tons of mods that help to lengthen playability. The developers are fantastic and share a ton about the development, there should be no hesitence in buying into this game. And heck, they have a demo on their website if you have doubts.This isnt just another survival/crafting game, it truly has a unique and original spin that works incredibly well. If you are discouraged by the complexity of the screen shots, dont be. The learning curve is incredibly rewarding as you slowly discover how to play the game. There are also hundreds of video tutorials that are fantastic. You will not be dissapointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and despite being in a fairly niche genre can appeal to a lot of players' interests. It teaches resource management, it tests your ability to plan ahead, it lets you come up with creative solutions to logistical problems, and lets you roleplay a planet-destroying alien that decimates the local populace and exploits their resources. This game strikes so many balances perfectly as well. There is a lot of room to experiment, but the tech tree is staggered enough that options don't become overwhelming. The game has so much depth to it, but much of the complicated bits (trains, circuits, etc.) aren't required to launch your first rocket. The replay value is insane, thanks to the thousands of mods available (and surely more to come, now that it's out of early access). Options to expand parts of the game you enjoy, add entirely new kinds of constructing, and anything else you could imagine are super easy to download within a few clicks. I have far too much to say, so while this review does not do the game justice, I highly recommend at least trying the demo out.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: i Bought this game almost a year ago before it got on steam....And i guess i have played it for like 300 hours! It's a Great game! I can best describe it as transport tycoon towerdefence. But your transport lines are not just 2-4 steps long! they might be 15 steps long!You should buy it!I guess its worth pointing out this is a very complete game regardless of the version numbers and early access tags.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I may never need to buy another game again. I've played through the game 5 times now, and about halfway through each run I felt I made a terrible error in my factory and wanted to restart from the beginning. But each time I held off until I launched at least 1 rocket so I could learn more about the game before starting over again to hopefully make the perfect factory.Pretty soon I'm going to be on my 6th factory, and I already have a plan to make it even more efficient right from the get go. I also know I'm going to discover a thousand horrible flaws in my plan, and that about halfway through I'm going to hate my factory and want to restart so I can do it right this time. And I'm so excited.This is a game about growth; not just the growth of your factory, but the growth of you as a player. Every time you play this game you'll learn a little more about logistics and gain new insights into the various mechanics that you can use to overcome various obstacles in the game. And every time you overcome an obstacle, you'll create brand new ones to conquer. Hell once you get good enough at the game you can even edit it to add in whole new challenges; stronger biters, less resources, more costly recipes, whatever you need to do to keep the game interesting.Best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game I've ever bought, and they keep updating it to make it even more satisfying and addictive.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly what else needs to be said?  One of, if not *the*, true greats of the genre.  Factorio's the OG and is an excellent example of Indie software development, and is an incredible game to play.  As long as you're a fan of automation, of course.The music, graphics, and general gameplay are always winners, and the developers' mod support and outlook is hugely positive.  I can't gush enough about the game, it's just that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a game like Factorio before. It is so different to any other game I've played, it's hard to compare it. My first impression when friends told me this game is great and I saw some endgame screenshots with "motherboard alike structures", I thought: "How can this even be fun". Some time later I realized, , so let's give it a try. And I said to myself: "When I'm still playing after like an hour, I will buy it".I bought it after 30 minutes.Well, it's a game where you build a factory. Optimize processes and workflows. Fix issues like bottlenecks, build a train network to deliver more materials. etc. etc.The story is quite simple so far: You crashed on an alien planet with almost nothing and have to find your way to escape from that planet. So the last "task" of the story line is to build and start a rocket. But there is so much more. Most of the time you should set your own targets. Some people do speed runs and getting better and better in it, some building mega and giga factories that are very very big. Some build factories for special purposes.The game is highly moddable what gives it a very high replayability. Almost everything of the game could be changed. There are already a ton of mods available, some with very high quality and a total conversion alike. Also a lot of mods that just provide QoL.The performance of the game is very good. It's a 2D sprite based game, with a perspectival topview. In more than 250 hours I rarely found any bugs or glitches. It never crashed so far.In a nutshell, if you like to automate things, find ways to fill bottlenecks or solve problems: This game is nuts!I can highly recommend to buy this game, or at least try the demo, if you can identify yourself with some of the gameplay explained above.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Factorio is one of the most successful indie games ever created.  It single handedly spawned a new genre.  Since the critical acclaim and success that Factorio has seen over the last few years, the factory automation genre has blown up.  I am fairly late to the party, but am just glad to have finally stumbled upon this very special game.  I played Satisfactory and Dyson Sphere Program first, saving the king of the genre for last.  It was worth the wait.  All 3 are spectacular games in their own right, but Factorio is my very favorite.  I loved every second of the vanilla base game, and have enjoyed small mods that change minor things as well as massive game overhaul mods that radically increase the complexity of the game.  I have loved every minute of this extremely unique and engaging experience.Consensus:-Best of the Best (Tier 1 and makes up 5% of my reviews).  This game is a true masterpiece and one that anyone that enjoys games should experience at some point in their life.  I was one of the lucky ones that bought this game for $20 back in 2017.  It took me almost 6 years to give it a try, and my only regret was waiting so long.  At it's $35 price tag, it's an absolute steal.  Although I'm not a fan of the price increases, it's well worth every penny.  If you haven't played this yet, pick it up right now.  It's so good, so challenging, and offers such a unique gaming experience.  I love going back over my sprawling base and seeing how it evolved over the course of 70-80 hrs.  I've had two extensive playthroughs (1 w/ a mod overhaul) and feel like I'm just hitting the surface of what this game has to offer.  There are Youtube videos of players putting in thousands of hrs and creating earth shattering factory fortresses.  Whether you are looking to play this casually or for years to come, this is a must play game for all gamers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10To be honest, I did not expect much coming into this game and had no prior knowledge of it and oh boy it was an unforgettable experience. Its concept and gameplay is really hard to sell to players because of the steep learning curve and messy UI but it is actually a really well-structured game. I can't find words on how to describe this game as the experience and enjoyment evolves with the player himself. Whether you play it as the base game or modded (Bob's and Angel's is the way to go) the experience will still be top notch. Definitely an underrated gem for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: The old school Diablo II style graphics are complimented with keeping the game approachable and simple. Progression is straightforward but always pushes the player for one more thing. As a result, it becomes very engaging with players finding it easy to lose time or quickly accomplish 1 task and log off.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that stays on my computer no matter what. You can always drop back into a factory to fix up your production of something, expand mining, un♥♥♥♥ that weird part of the power grid over on the south side, or just drive your tank around the wasteland shooting up aliens.This is THE building and logistics game. Nothing else comes close.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my addiction.I make games for a living, so problem solving on my free time sound like hell. But more than any other game, this game gives me that "just 5 more minutes" feeling over and over until it's 5 AM. Maybe because things are difficult enough that makes me feel like I accomplished something when it works, but easy enough for me not to give up.I don't have that many hours in this game just because of sheer discipline. If not for that, I would hardly play anything else.It's even better with a friend on multiplayer.10/10

All of this in just one map.If this doesn't say "Best game ever" than what does?First I thought: Looks like an interesting concept but boring and ugly to play. But believe me it is the opposite.
