_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Just when you thought you got the hang of the flow of the game, more science and technology are needed, so you spend a bunch of hours on optimising the piping of materials to the necessary components of the factory, Time that you don’t have.Just when you are comfortable with the things, you run out of material so you go look for some, but there are biters around it, so you spent a bunch of hours clearing up the biters, and setting up your first train system. Time that you don’t have.It goes on until normal life has lost its meaning, time that should have been spent on growing the factory. Factory must grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have too much time? Play it. Are you lacking time? Make time. The factory must grow and your life does not take precedence. The factory must grow and according to your grandma you've grown every time you see her so you clearly know how to make that happen. Studying Computer science? This game might even teach you a little bit and help you get the right mindset.This game deserves all the praise it's gotten and more. Play it right now, for the sake of the factory, for the sake of your insanity, for any time you have too much of.That being said, its very easy to lose a sense of time and you should only play it if you have nothing important that day and the next, because you will forget what time it is and go to bed wayyy too late.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Perfection is an ideal which is worth pursuing even though it can never be reached. Factorio gives you the satisfaction of constantly moving forward towards higher efficency as you build your sprawling machine city. Try to reach perfectly efficency with a giant machine which takes raw materials from the earth and turns it into finished products to build a rocket to leave. Blissful, fun, sometimes hilarious, sometimes frustrating, but always eats hours of time."Oh, I fixed that problem! But now that the system has enough plastic, it needs more... advanced circuit boards. Which need more... copper wire. I can do that! Let me just run over to my copper factory and increase production, which... hmmm.... these conveyer belts are inefficient. Let me just fix that, and... what was I doing again? Oh! I can fix this power system to be more efficent!"And three hours later you need to leave for work because it's morning and you're still playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game (base game is good, though the mods make it epic!). You start with building a small base, and 20 hours later you are tweaking a huge industrial powerhouse. The game gives you the choice to play with/without enemies, you can change all settings of the maps and generate the world you prefer. With hunderds of games in my library i always keep comming back to Factorio. Not conviced yet? Play the demo and you'll be sucked in Factorio before you know it.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game in 2018 and it remains my best game purchase before or since. If you have an analytical mind and you are looking for a game that is relaxing while still challenging, Factorio is for you.Build your factory from the ground up to enable you to build a rocket in order to escape a hostile alien planet. The game is well supported by the devs and they are constantly improving the game, usually based on mods created by a dedicated community.The Factorio community is one of the most helpful and least toxic in all of gaming and they are always willing to help other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: You know that feeling when you watch those "Satisfying Video" compilations on youtube? You know, where you see like pasta being made, chain links being linked together, fairy floss going onto a stick and all that sorta stuff?Well when you figure out Factorio and get your first big factory up and going, it's like living in an eternal state of that feeling. You just sit there, staring at your efficient designs, admiring your belts (and/or robots) and just generally revelling in your ability to cleanly automate everything you worked so hard for up to to that point.Buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Personally i love the game its fun difficult and is the first game in a long time that made me really think about how to improve on my own design rather then just doing what i know works there are many ways to come to the same conclusion in essence if you like to build and something relaxing to spend a couple hours a day doing then this is the game for you... also i will always support anyone who is willing to stand against the cancel culture ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is going around as the creator said "Take the cancel culture mentality and shove it up your ass" Love you man keep up the great work
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: The factory must grow.In my opinion, this game isn't for everyone. You have to have a certain aptitude for systematic thinking and planning, and take enjoyment in a well-made solution. If that niche suits you, you'll quickly see why this game has such a high rating.In addition, Wube is an incredible developer. After reading their Friday updates for years, I've been amazed by their passion and attention to detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favourite base building game, fun and so satisfying. You never feel like you're wasting your time, everything can be automated and the factory is always growing. You know your goal is to launch a rocket, and you get sucked into all the complexity along the way. When you finally decide to finish up a playthrough you can look back and be impressed by the huge factory you created bit by bit. Great both solo and in online coop!Lots of respect for the devs as well, with the Friday facts you can see what they prioritize. They are always making improvements to performance and quality of life. With this attention to detail, things always do what you expect. I also don't believe I've ever encountered a bug while playing, other than the biters!
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the Early Access tag trick you.I'm one of those guys that never goes for early access games. If you are that way too, let me just tell you that this game does NOT play like an early access title. It was in development for four years already before it came to steam, and it is VERY solid. It already has 50+ hours worth of content inside, and after my 90+ hours of gameplay I have yet to encounter a single bug.Plus, there is a huge modding community that produces some great stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best logistics game I've played, and the team continues to add content. Already over a hundred hours of gameplay, and I'm looking forward to many hundreds more.Updated for Space Age:Spent the $45 on Space Age and have already gotten another 100+ hours. The additions are all welcome and the game is even more slick now than it once was.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio is a game about building and creating automated factories to produce items of increasing complexity, within an infinite 2D world. Use your imagination to design your factory, combine simple elements into ingenious structures, and finally protect it from the creatures who don't really like you.
_childDocuments_.name: Factorio

name: Golf With Your Friends
detailed_description: INTRODUCING: KING OF THE CASTLE New DLC Available Join the Discord Community About the Game Why have friends if not to play Golf... With Your Friends! Make sure your skills are up to scratch as you tee off against 11 other golfers in simultaneous online multiplayer. Themed Courses! Go head to head on courses with unique mechanics and holes. _childDocuments_.review: While I enjoy playing it, I'm not sure I can recommend it. The game play is very light. Almost every online game you join will have "super jump" enabled. True it is a lot of fun. But the game is effectively a miniature golf game in which you avoid playing the course. You do this because the course design is often bizarre. Bizarre to the point that it really is a better game with super jump. Also on a personal note, I'm not a fan of the game's public chat. Because I cannot mute it, in case I end up on a course with creeps or one with a personal conversation between two or more people whom I don't know. True you can try and ignore it, it is only on the left of the screen, but I'd be just as happy playing with strangers whom aren't going to derail a conversation into political screeming or grapphic and lewd context. I know in an internet with 4Chan we're all supposed to jaded cruel shock jocks but I am not all about that.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, but I can't recommend this. I purchased this game to play "Golf with my Friends". I can't see how this would take more that a couple of days of programming to get it working, but instead they've spent months on a level editor. Shame, because the basics are very good, the hole design is decent, and the game would be fun if I wasn't limited to playing local single player.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is infinitely more fun with friends playing. Just make sure you know someone that has the game or is willing to buy it to play with you, because that's what makes this game its most fun.Side-note, that 10k put achievement is legitimately the longest grind ever. Even if you can rack up a 100 put game going quickly, you would need to play through 100 games before getting the achievement. In my experience, I could get through a map after about 10 minutes, which means that this achievement alone takes anywhere from 16 to 17 hours going quickly. A bit brutal, to say the least.EDIT: They devs are now locking achievements behind playing courses that are paid DLC. You can technically get them by playing in public lobbies that have people who have bought them, but good luck getting below par on a one off game. Fun casually, absolute nightmare for people looking to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is infuriating. If you have infinite patience and are ok with a super glitchy, poorly made game you might be ok. I'm usually a very calm person, but I can only play this game for short periods of time with my friends before I get too angry to see straight. Granted, I'm not the best at this game, but I am also decidedly not the worst. There are far too many bugs to fix or address; the game would have to be completely re-written to fix them all. Most notably, certain positions are impossible to get out of (you will receive the maximum strokes on the hole because you are stuck), and if you are a new player, or its been a while since you played a course, forget about knowing how to get to the flag. _childDocuments_.review: I normally don't comment on any forums, but I feel this amount of frustration can be taken care of being hopefully reaching the developers. While I love this game, and spend lots of hours practising, but it seems the game has a lot to do with lucky and skill. I can take criticism time and time again and improve my scores only so much on a recognised course, but I fail to see how some unthinkable score cards are a reflection of my ability to play your game. We all have very basic access to the likely basic controls of the game.This has led me to understand and notice some understandable yet doable updates. 1. Improve the speed at which we painlessly can watch our ball roll to any place on the map that isn't in the hole. Yes this would include out of bounds areas that auto glitch to last play position. I am aware there are sweet points off grid course. I don't need to see it roll along...or float...I know this is possible as older games have it. Just a thought. please.2. More direction on the course. You offer a brief ability to skim the course ahead. 15 sec. In many cases this is not long enough for me. In turn, I fail to get an appropriate angle at a shot. Assuming I haven't used all my view time. If there is a way to keep the flag option on during play that would make a huge difference.3. The roll and bounce of the ball is a little too much. I'm not sure if there will or can be settings which would allow for more realistic bounce. Its a little tricky to gauge the need of shot at times. Even with the meter level reader. The problem may be in the environment settings and not the game play. Shot which roll in different points of any course have varying effects. Not sure if a settings open in general can be added to reduce realistic values if this is a standard mode. Perhaps a more relaxed version.4. Great game Overall. I would enjoy it more if it had more holes by steam as well. Super awesome this came out. A nice way to sit back and hound away at a ball. or Puck. _childDocuments_.review: Whatever you do, do not pay full price for this. It's some janky shovelware, and the level designers do not understand how to increase difficulty without making things exasperating. It seems the majority of these holes haven't been play tested, and if they were they weren't tested for player fun or enjoyment. The game makes utterly baffling choices like only allowing freelook at the course for 15 seconds before you're back to the (often obscured) first person view. Instead of increasing the challenge in an engaging way I guess it's easier to hide where the end of the hole is, or put in ridiculous, impassable hazards? The levels themselves are some 2000-era ugly, and overall it seems like an explosion at a warehouse of old Team 17 assets. I am sure there are great minigolf games out there, but this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the game Golf With Your Friends draws some interesting parallels to Tiger Woods overcoming sex addiction. Much like Tiger Woods' journey towards recovery, the game involves navigating through various challenging courses that require patience, skill, and perseverance. Overcoming sex addiction demanded self-control and discipline from Woods, just as players need to exhibit precision and focus in the game to achieve success. Golf With Your Friends is a fun time and the Steam Workshop gives a ton of cools maps. Don't eat that.

_childDocuments_.review: You're trying to put a ball in a hole by touching the ball the least times. You can change spin or strength, and the hole is marked with a flag. If you meet the suggested number of times touching the ball, it's referred to as 'par.' The winner touches the ball the least. It gives a game structure most people are familiar with. With that said, good luck jumping over saws; freezing yourself out of mid-air to land a perfect hole-in-one; ensnaring others in glue traps; and trying to figure out exactly how to hit a ball so you don't end up floating away on your rubber ducky in the pond.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty fun a few years ago, but it felt a bit under-polished. We still played it anyway, because of it's upbeat cartoony style and hilarious gameplay customisation. Over the years myself and others have played the game quite a lot, for a game that only offers very simple gameplay (shoot ball in hole to win). But the gameplay customisation adds quite a bit of replayability. Everyone hates the cone ball. Or you could have super low gravity and player collisions. Just to name a few things.They added some extra game modes, like hoops. And they slowly added new maps over the years. More official maps would have been nice, but we get by pretty well with what we've got. And there'e community workshop maps too (but they aren't as good as official maps). However, the game still felt a bit under-polished in some areas and not completely bug-free.But then, Team17 bought the developers out. Which wasn't a bad thing! They've massively improved the user interface, fixed bugs and added some cool new maps. Now the game really feels worth recommending to anyone - not just those who need their funny game fix. But I suspect there is still more content to come!It's a great game to grab a few friends with and have a reliably good time. Sure, it's not the most sophisticated game, but it offers pretty satisfying gameplay that should appeal to a lot of people.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 49 year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my son, who is now 14. My son recently downloaded Golf With Your Friends and in less than a week, he had already played for over 20 hours. This was terrible for me, as it was already hard enough for me to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching videos on Tiktok. So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought my son and I closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories
_childDocuments_.name: Golf With Your Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This probably isn't the kind of game you expect to have sentimental significance to people, but it does for me, so I'm going to get that out of the way and then focus on the more objective stuff.So I was in an abusive relationship throughout 2021-2022. I won't get into the details, but it was pretty extreme, and included controlling who I could speak to/the friendships I could have, for how long I could be with them, and so on. I was very trauma-bonded to this person - I could not see how bad it was. I knew I was miserable, I knew it was abusive, but I was making excuses and I couldn't bring myself to leave or even to stand up for myself.I was finally 'allowed' to have a game night with my best friend for an hour, and on that game night we played Golf With Your Friends. It was the first time we'd played (though we'd both seen YouTubers play it before), and we started off with the Forest map - and it was the hardest I'd laughed since my relationship began. Tears in my eyes, hysterics, non-stop laughing. I later found out that my mother had been outside my bedroom door listening, because she hadn't heard me laugh in so long.That was one of the first steps in realising I had to get out, and the best friend I played with that night is now my fiancee.Less heavily, this has been the background game for so many good conversations with my friend groups. It's always so much fun - often people will be reluctant to try it because, well, 'Golf With Your Friends' doesn't sound like a very appealing and exciting game on the surface to most of them, but once we're in it everyone is yelling and laughing and asking me when we can play it again.The official courses are pretty good and have a decent amount of variety, but once you're done with them the real fun is in the custom/Steam Workshop courses. Sort by popular/most liked, check the comments to make sure there are no glitches that might prevent you from finishing, and go wild. There are some genuinely creative gems in there.I've played other golf games, and this one has my favourite controls and general graphics. They're pretty smooth and easy to get accustomed to in my experience, and I very rarely, if ever, got frustrated with the game for making me ♥♥♥♥ up as a result of a glitch or bad gameplay - any errors I make are entirely my own.The customisation is cool - loved the cosmetics you can unlock for finishing courses, and my ball is now rolling around with a halo and angel wings. I also enjoy my little swan-boat float.
_childDocuments_.name: Golf With Your Friends

The game's completely appalling at how poorly done it has turned out. Golf It seems like a good alternative when it comes to this game type's genre without the some of the quite honestly already stated problems that people have been talking about and experiencing quite often.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very quirky fun take on mini-golf that you play with your friends, strangers or even by your lonesome (trying to figure out the hole-in-one strats, you know who you are.) Currently has 2 courses available with more planned on the way, a few quirky modes currently on the experimental version and possibly some of the best devs I've experienced despite only being a 2 man team. They are very active on updates and have a roadmap in the forums if you want to see where they plan on taking it. They are very friendly and active on the forums and is taking community ideas and advice to make the game even better while also adding more to it in a fast enough manner.I highly recommend this to someone who wants a game that is more casual but has the options to make it a stressful race to the hole against others. There are plenty of Youtubers that have videos on it though they might be dated because of the constant tweaks by the devs but you can get an idea of what you'd be getting into from the videos, still though I think it's worth the price in it's current version with only 2 courses so when everything else eventually comes out it'll be more than cost efficient! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Golf with Friends is an arcadey putt-ing game in the sense you dont get any simulated golf green with uneven or grainy surfaces. What you do get is an array of hilariously themed courses with loopty loops, speed boosters, black holes and more! AND optionally you can play as a hockey puck, basketball ball, or tinker with the physics (eg. bounciness, stickiness) to make your very own gameplay.Gripes:1. If your ball lands next to a wall or underneath something, your view becomes obscured, you can try zoom in/out but that don't help sometimes. 2. Each hole you can press c to free cam for a limited time to scout the hole, but that timer runs out pretty quickly considering how complex some holes are, especially when its over multiple floors. 3. The reset ball feature doesn't work for me. Very frustrating as I had to incur maximum penalty strokes on many occasions as the timer runs out while my ball is still flying out of bounds.Overall, super fun and relaxing. I did have trouble finding games on oz server but maybe its just that specific time I was on. Great putt putt game for you and ur fambam. It has a little something for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Learning how to build and publish levels in this game is like having a child. You may have all the best intentions in the world. You may do as much research on the subject as you can. You may have seen how others have succeeded. However when you attempt to execute your plan, the world says no, that isnt hole 1, this spawn you placed 3rd is actually hole 1. No, how that item functions in the main game does not matter, it CANNOT be used in the same way in the level editor. NO, just because the level editor has a snap function does not mean what you spawn will in any way line up with each other. You will lose sleep and subtract years from your life trying to create levels. It is a genuine struggle to play and enjoy this game. If I met the person who optimized the level editor I would slap them with my paraplegic dog's otherwise useless hind legs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the worst imaginable physics that I've ever seen in a golf game. The ball behaves as though it is on a near-frictionless hard surface as long as it is on the course, regardless of the actual material it's sitting on. Grass? Wooden floors? Tiles? Everything barely slows you down. Balls bounce as high on hard glass as they would on soft leaves. Balls glitch through walls on the Oasis stage if they're travelling fast enough.Trash game. Only redeeming feature is playing this with friends after a few drinks. Or many. Perhaps enough to make you forget about what you're playing, and the match just devolves into a chatroom.Don't buy this. Waste of your hard-earned cash.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf is a club-and-ball sport in which players use various clubs to hit balls into a series of holes on a course in as few strokes as possible.Golf, unlike most ball games, cannot and does not utilize a standardized playing area, and coping with the varied terrains encountered on different courses is a key part of the game. The game at the usual level is played on a course with an arranged progression of 18 holes, though recreational courses can be smaller, often having 9 holes. Each hole on the course must contain a tee box to start from, and a putting green containing the actual hole or cup (4.25 inches in diameter). There are other standard forms of terrain in between, such as the fairway, rough (long grass), bunkers (or "sand traps"), and various hazards (water, rocks) but each hole on a course is unique in its specific layout and arrangement.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game to play solo or with friends. The different courses are varied in difficulty, but if you play enough you can find shortcuts for the different holes. The different modes keep the the game from stagnating. Use the explore mode for practicing the shots; you can learn the courses so you can play to get achievements, hats, tails, and floats. You can also build your courses to share with your friends or through the workshop. It's a good game for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with 3 friends and had the time of my life. This game is just fun. There's really no other way to describe it.Pros:Customisation - Balls can be customised to a colour and the lobby host can change the physics of the game by changing the ball shape, gravity, bounce height, toggling collisions with other players, etc. Makes for a laugh with low gravity, bouncy eggs.Simplicity - The game is simple with a minimalist art style, runs on pretty much any machine very well. Do note that 'Medium' and 'High' settings have their FPS capped, where as 'low' is uncapped.Fun - Just, fun. Like a game should be.Affordable - Definitely worth the price, an absolute blast to play.Cons:Maps - only two maps at the moment, however these are very cool. I especially like the Oasis map as it has some really cool features like the river section.Dear devs:Please add workshop compatibility later in development, it would be awesome to have the community make custom maps, also please make more maps of your own as I love the level design currently in game!Overall verdict:Fun, easy to run, affordable - get it, especially if you like mini golf.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated 12/2023We just tried to play this on LOCAL multi-player, but it will not accept 2 or 4 controllers, whichever controller starts the game, it will only use that 1 controller, this must have been broken on the last update,. so pi55ed off with Team 17 for not sorting this game, why not just copy the system from Zen's infinite Mini Golf, the controllers and avatars in that are perfect, shame the game is screwed, we use to love that too! Just played this for the first time with Remote Play Together - we played the 1st course without any issues, great fun and lovely graphics.We then played the Worms course, OMG it's full of bugs guys - the ball lands out of bounds, it stays there, making you lose that hole. The views on the ball are shocking, it was ok to hole 15 then it was shocking, like the camera was sat on the ball, impossible to see where you aiming/shooting and the clipping on the ball was terrible, like the camera going in the ball. During playback, all players can take control of the ball, this needs to be isolated to each player like Infinite Mini Golf, otherwise another player could sabotage your go, either on purpose or by accident.I have been told by Team 17 this is down to Remote Play Together, I will try on I.M.G. later and see if the same issues arises as we know that does not happen in local multiplayer normally :) Even though the option to ALWAYS SHOW FLAG is ON, the flag was not always shown, on the larger courses on Worms Levels this made it total guess work to know where to aim :/ It did not always show where the other players ball was on the course.It is V1 so hopefully this will be fixed very soon, but I bought this game in Alpha and got refunded due to the amount of bugs, so very surprised to see it hit retail and still be buggy - Luckily Team 17 are an awesome bunch and I have faith in them to fix this game :) I will say I recommend this game as it has massive potential, we play I.M.G. every Thursday but this could be our new go to Golf game if the bugs are fixed :)--------------------------UPDATED -------------After revisiting the game after several months, I've just posted this - read it before you buy it! Issues on Local OFFLINE ModeThis week my partner and I have had another go at this game, but still inundated by bugs that are infuriating.Firstly, the players turn ends prematurely, so we cannot see where we are ending up on our go. We just played the level Space Station. and on Hole 17 I think it was, neither of us got the chance to steer in the water as it returned to the next player despite us not finishing our go, this meant we both got stuck and could not possibly get to the hole. On the same course my partner went out of bounds and her ball did not respawn, so she just had to waste her go.The controllers still control the other players go, something I reported when I first got this game which was ages ago.Player 1 always goes first, it should be whom ever won the hole goes first!No RESTART HOLE option, much needed for when it glitches and leaves a player off the course :/--------------- UPDATE ----------Played quite a few courses now locally with family, the go ends prematurely on all levels - just now on Hole 18, I got the ball in the hole but my go and ended so and it came up that I had run out of shots - pretty crap considering I got in the hole! This needs fixing urgently!Also, aside from the issue that all controllers work all of the time, the game remembers the last players camera angle, not each players, this could do with fixing too.If you want to see how this should work then play Infinite Mini Golf, this game has the turn system perfect.It would also be much better if players could have names and it remembered the settings for each Player instead of having to change the colours etc every single time we play.This game has potential but it's faaaaar form being right!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game. For the early access, it also means the price is low (as the author has said in the notes the price will raise). I can't understand at the moment the 'negative' comments for an 'Early Access' game, it's not a AAA title. I like the little touches, like the 'glowing balls' in the darker areas. While it's not clear at first were the hole is, you get it eventually. The more times you play it, the more confident you'll get at doing things like distance, ball power, ball direction and all that fun stuff. I'd suggest putting it on your wishlist incase it goes on sale again, like when I bought it. If the price then goes up, you've got a bargain. Hope they introduce 'bot' mode or local play. At this stage, I would give it 8.5/10 (but, it IS early access)Two years on, I'm still playing this game, at least twice a week. They have updated a lot, they have now got a map editor within. It is still early access, they still have some tweaks to do (as you still hit a white/invisible wall at times) and hackers still manage to get in now and again and ruin the experience.I'm still sticking with it though, it's a really fun game with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through 4 18-holes. Visuals are bright, joyful, a bit crazy, but all in nice fun. The fact every course has its own entirely distinctive theme is simply awesome. There are enough courses and modes of play to keep you occupied for a while. Control over the ball isn't too bad in itself. Mechanics are relatively simple and clear enough, but there are a few issues. Notably, the camera seems to get stuck with objects at times and make you look much closer at the ball, making judging proper velocity a pain. Then there's the design of the levels. I was quite impressed by the first set of holes, which simply worked well and offered at times obstacles typical to what you'd find in a real minigolf course. Other levels were much more problematic, mostly in terms of difficulty. The first 9 is usually quite fun and shows interesting challenges, but the last 9 gets insane and too unforgiving at times, requiring way too precise inputs. I don't mind getting over par, but I do mind having to guess the almost exact force I must use for the ball to then roll on some accelerator platform and fly away through a ridiculously small hole in a wall, or on a minuscule platform. On the other hand, there is much space for the player to progress with practice. Thus, for anyone with the patience to go through those difficulty spikes that will certainly ruin your score sheet up until now, there's something really cool to play with. _childDocuments_.review: Golf With Your Friends is what happens when you mix golf with chaos and then add a bunch of people who have no idea how physics work. Imagine trying to play a serious game of golf, but instead of a nice, quiet course, you’re on a map filled with ramps, ramps, and more ramps—oh, and black holes.It’s the kind of game where you’re either laughing so hard you forget to hit the ball, or getting so competitive you end up taking your shots way too seriously, only to get launched into the stratosphere by a trampoline. There’s no such thing as a ‘normal’ round—every hole is an adventure, and sometimes the adventure is just trying to avoid falling into a literal volcano.10/10, would recommend for those who want to play golf... with way more explosions and way less focus on the actual golfing part. Bonus points if you somehow manage to beat your friends without losing your mind first.

_childDocuments_.review: My friend made it so every time you lose due to time expiration, it gave you plus sixty points.  I ended the game with something around five hundred eighty points.  10/10, would get 580 points again.This is just one example of various I have available.  As for a serious review, my friends and I play this game when we need to get away from serious strategy games that require intellectual thought and planning as a way to "unwind" of sorts and be stupid, and the beauty about it is, after a relatively short amount of time, you're ready to play whatever game you were playing initially again.  For example, a group of friends and I were playing Men of War: Assault Squadron.  After getting steamrolled by the Germans for the third time in a row, we were basically fed up and needed time away from it.  It was looking like we were just going to call it a night and get off till a friend decided this would be a good idea, and bought me a copy while it was on sale.  What followed was about fifty minutes of utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and cancer.  It turned from a game about golfing with friends, to a breeding ground of divsion where the main goal was to sabotage the other player's efforts to win by sacrificing yourself and wasting your own time to knock them away.  After those fifty minutes, we were ready to go back to Men of War.  It should be noted, fifty minutes is a comparatively short time period, whereas otherwise we would have gotten off and the time would be measured in hours, rather than minutes.  If you're looking for a "filler" game to play in between gaming sessions where you and your friends can cool off and have fun (or lose your ♥♥♥♥ and ragequit), this is an excellent option.  Binge-play hours in a major title, take a thirty to sixty minute break in Golf With Your Friends, and you're easily ready to go back.  Or, simply play the game on your own, or, as the title suggests, with your friends.  The game is well off enough that it can stand independently and not as simple in-between filler.  The oftentimes challenging level design will encourage you to stay up, similar to a game of Civ, where you must get in that one, last turn to succeed.  It's well worth it, but prepare to lose your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: "Golf with Friends" is a fun and entertaining multiplayer mini-golf game that is perfect for casual players looking for a light-hearted and fun experience. The game is easy to learn and play, with simple controls.The graphics are basically hard to fault for this type of game, unfortunately some assets seem to be flawed. For example, the ball sometimes bugs in walls or obstacles. The variety of different themed courses adds variety to the game and keeps things fresh and interesting.However, the game also has some drawbacks. The physics engine can be a little inconsistent at times, leading to frustrating moments when shots don't behave as expected. Thus, a game that was already thought to be won can unexpectedly turn around again. The ice hockey and basketball modes are particularly prone to errors. The game would also benefit from a few new official maps. Although you can download countless courses from the workshop, they are often even more error-prone.All in all, "Golf with Friends" is a decent and entertaining mini-golf game that is well suited for occasional play sessions with friends. While not the most polished or challenging game on the market, its simplicity and multiplayer capabilities make it worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started playing with my friends we had a lot of fun. It was a nice and relaxing game you could play while talking to other people. Everyone was happy and we had a really good time. After playing for a couple of days we started to be more and more competitive which wasn't necessarily a bad thing. Instead of just playing, trying to have fun, we now focused on winning and beating each other. After a few more days things slowly started to go south and what started out as a fun activity became the reason why I lost most of my friends. We didn't play to have fun anymore, the only reason we played was to win and to find out who was better at the game. Death threats, insults and tears replaced all the joy we first experienced playing together. Over the course of time more and more of my friends started to quit the game because they couldn't deal with the fear of being humiliated anymore. To this day I still don't know what happened to some of the people I used to talk to on a daily basis, they simply disappeared and no one ever saw them again. I personally feel responsible to inform the public about the risk of buying "Golf With Friends", because it ruined not only my life, but the life of the people I was closest to as well. I'm dealing with severe depression and anxiety attacks on a daily basis because of the insanely competitive environment that surrounded me. I still recieve death threats and letters from people I won against because they want to take revenge. If you decide to buy "Golf With Friends" speak to your parents if you're not at least 18 years old and make sure they are aware of the possible long term effects this game can have on you. If you are old enough please take the time and ask yourself if playing a game is worth risking your health.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot has changed since I've posted my previous review in 2019 (see below), Team17 first seemingly cooperate with Blacklight to bring the game to other platforms and then bought the IP and Assets outright at the end of 2020 / beginning of 2021. A game that did receive regular updates and bug fixes from a team of 3 developers is now withering away under the ownership of a publicly traded company with 200-ish employees that couldn't even be bothered to post patch notes for the last update. I hope that £12 million buyout was worth it... well, it probably will be once they'll shove GWYF 2 out the door.If all you're after is a simple mini golf game and don't plan on anything other than playing it, this is still the version to get. When you're done with the official maps, the workshop has content for days which you'll not get on other platforms. I'd still recommend it, even with it's obvious faults that should be long gone with the resources that T17 could throw at it, as long as it's not at full price. Stay away from the editor though...Coming from someone who build 10 maps over the span of 2-ish years... no. Just no. It feels almost like they're purposely sabotage the editor. Whoever was given the job of working on it is either incompetent, doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ or simply half-asses it. Known bugs (e.g. pieces will just jump outside the map when you look at them wrong, breaking the map) won't get fixed. Responses by their support on the Steam board are worthless copy/pasta. Formerly working stuff in the editor is now broken (can't rotate assets on more than one axis, manually entering values doesn't work, ...) and, this is the best IMHO, scaling/position values on existing assets were changed so much that already published maps on the workshop were unplayable. No QA, no patches, no ♥♥♥♥♥ given.--- Old review:A nice relaxing mini golf game... that is until you miss a shot that you should be able hit blindfolded. For the 3rd time. _childDocuments_.review: I am really torn between giving this game a thumbs up or down, but I chose thumbs down for two big reasons.  The first is that there are only a handful of maps, and it simply gets boring fast, I am sure this will change with updates however.  The second and largest reason is that it seems to be too difficult.  Let me explain: as with every golf game the goal is to get the ball in the hole in as few moves as possible and each hole has par, anything less is a good score and anything more is a bad score.  The problem is that it's almost impossible to hit the ball with the right amount of force because the ball either rolls a lot or a very little and is hard to get the exact force you want.  Secondly you have to be a perfectionist when playing, there are several holes where if you make one mistake you'll get over par.  There are also some holes where it is almost impossible to get under par because the hole is seemingly designed to make you go out of bounds or get lost.  I'm looking at you egyptian level.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that it's out of early access, this still feels like a promising early access game. It needs a lot more polish -- for example, the camera angles often get annoyingly blocked by environment art, which in a professional and polished game you would expect to fade out to allow you to line up your shot. More thought also needs to go in to the speed and responsiveness of the game, as you often end up watching out of bounds balls rolling very slowly to a halt, with no apparent option to just skip the rest of the turn or immediately reset the ball.A level editor is always a very nice feature to have and could potentially give ongoing life to the game and community, but sadly it is broken and doesn't come with a tutorial or even any balloon tips, so it's unlikely that anybody but the most die-hard fan will use it. They should look at the Trackmania Forever level editor for inspiration if they want to improve on this.The frustrating thing is that all of the games problems are very obvious and shouldn't be too difficult to fix if Team17 had any interest in the title, so the fact that they've come out of early access without these fixes suggests to me that they've cut their losses and won't be providing much in the way of ongoing support or fixes. If that is the case they would be far better advised to release it as a F2P title to populate the servers and allow a community to form, which they could then monetise further down the road. It occurs to me that the game may have been designed whilst loot crates were still de-riguer, and now that that trend has thankfully passed they just don't know what to do with their product.It is still a fun game, the sort that could occupy an hour or so with friends at the end of the evening. It can be played in turns around one screen, but it really shines in its online mode where everybody can take their shots simultaneously. Sadly I've only been able to find a server with more than one or two people once. I would very much like to play Golf With Your Friends with my friends, but I can't in good conscience recommend that they all spend £6 on a copy. If it gets reduced to <£3 in a sale I'll buy it for them and we'll have a good laugh.

_childDocuments_.review: Why Golf With Your Friends Is the Best Game EverIn the world of video games, there are countless genres that cater to different interests and skill levels. Some games are built for intense competition, others for storytelling, and some simply to relax and enjoy time with friends. Among the many multiplayer games that exist, Golf With Your Friends stands out as one of the best. It is a unique, fun, and lighthearted game that combines the relaxing experience of golf with the excitement and chaos of multiplayer action. This essay explores the reasons why Golf With Your Friends is the best game ever, focusing on its accessibility, engaging gameplay, humor, and social experience.1. Accessibility and SimplicityOne of the greatest strengths of Golf With Your Friends is its accessibility. It is easy for new players to pick up and understand the mechanics. Unlike many games that require hours of tutorials or complicated controls, Golf With Your Friends has a very straightforward gameplay system. The objective is simple: get the ball into the hole using as few strokes as possible, just like traditional golf. However, the game introduces fun twists that make it anything but conventional.The controls are simple—players adjust the power and angle of their shots, making it easy for anyone to jump into the game without having to worry about complex mechanics. This simplicity, however, doesn’t translate into boring gameplay. The developers have designed the courses to be fun, with each one introducing new obstacles, ramps, and strange, creative layouts that keep the experience fresh and exciting. Whether players are new to golf games or veterans of the genre, Golf With Your Friends welcomes everyone to the table.Additionally, the game is available on multiple platforms, including PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch. This cross-platform functionality ensures that friends can play together regardless of the device they are using, removing barriers that typically arise in multiplayer games. The accessibility of Golf With Your Friends makes it an ideal choice for casual gamers who want a game that is easy to enjoy with no steep learning curve.2. Engaging and Creative GameplayGolf With Your Friends takes the simple concept of golf and adds a twist of creativity. The game features a variety of courses, each with unique designs that range from whimsical and surreal to challenging and wacky. From obstacles like giant moving platforms to ramps that send balls flying into the air, the courses are filled with surprises that keep players on their toes.One of the most enjoyable aspects of the game is the variety of power-ups and game modes available. The game offers different modes like "Classic," where players play a standard round of golf, and "Crazy Golf," where things get even more unpredictable. In Crazy Golf, gravity may change, or balls may randomly teleport, adding a level of chaos that keeps the game exciting. These modes shake up the traditional golfing experience and allow for a lot of fun experimentation.Additionally, the game includes a variety of customization options for the players’ golf balls. From changing the color and texture of the ball to applying fun skins (such as a basketball or a star), players can personalize their experience and make the game even more entertaining. The ability to customize their avatar or ball gives players a sense of ownership and fun, further enhancing the appeal of the game.3. Humor and Lighthearted ToneUnlike many competitive games that encourage serious play, Golf With Your Friends thrives on its humor and lighthearted tone. The quirky course designs, bizarre obstacles, and comical animations provide a sense of fun that keeps the game from ever feeling too serious. Even the sound effects and the exaggerated motions of the golf balls as they roll across the screen add a comedic layer to the experience.This lighthearted approach allows players to enjoy the game without feeling the pressure of intense competition. Instead of focusing solely on performance, the game encourages players to laugh, have fun, and enjoy the chaos. For example, when a player’s ball falls off the edge of a course or is sent into an unexpected direction, the over-the-top reactions and humorous animations often leave everyone in fits of laughter.The game’s humor is one of the key reasons why it has become such a popular choice for groups of friends. Whether you are playing with childhood friends, family members, or even strangers, the game’s tone ensures that everyone is having fun, and the stakes are never too high. It is a perfect escape from the more stressful, competitive gaming environments that dominate other genres.4. Social and Cooperative ExperienceAt its core, Golf With Your Friends is about bringing people together. While other competitive games focus on defeating opponents, Golf With Your Friends places a strong emphasis on social interaction and teamwork. It is the kind of game that can be played casually with friends during a laid-back evening or in a more competitive setting, depending on the group dynamic.The multiplayer experience in Golf With Your Friends is second to none. It supports up to 12 players in a single game, meaning large groups can enjoy the game together. The ability to chat and communicate with teammates or opponents allows for a fun and interactive experience, with players joking around, making friendly banter, and celebrating each other’s successes or misfortunes. Whether you are playing with close friends or meeting new people, the cooperative and social elements are what make this game truly shine.Furthermore, the game does not require players to commit to long sessions, making it easy to fit into any schedule. A round of Golf With Your Friends can be as short as 20 minutes or as long as an hour, depending on how many holes the group plays. This flexibility allows players to enjoy the game without feeling pressured to dedicate long stretches of time, making it an ideal choice for casual gaming sessions.5. A Game for EveryoneUltimately, what makes Golf With Your Friends the best game ever is its universal appeal. It doesn’t matter if you are a seasoned gamer or someone who rarely plays video games. The game’s accessible mechanics, fun and creative gameplay, humor, and social experience make it enjoyable for all types of players. Whether you’re looking for a relaxing experience or a game that is full of surprises, Golf With Your Friends has something for everyone.The game’s inclusive nature also extends to the diverse player base it attracts. Golf With Your Friends doesn’t rely on complicated strategies or competitive skill levels, meaning that players of all abilities can participate and enjoy the game together. This is a rare trait for many multiplayer games, which often exclude newcomers or casual players.ConclusionIn conclusion, Golf With Your Friends stands as one of the best games ever due to its combination of accessibility, engaging gameplay, humor, and social interaction. It is a game that encourages fun, creativity, and lightheartedness, making it perfect for groups of friends looking for a casual yet exciting multiplayer experience. The game’s whimsical course designs, customizable avatars, and variety of game modes ensure that every round is unique and full of surprises. Whether you are a casual gamer or a dedicated player, Golf With Your Friends offers a delightful escape into the world of wacky, fun-filled golf. Its simplicity, charm, and inclusivity make it a game that anyone can enjoy, and that is exactly why it deserves the title of the best game ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Lord of the Rings and the Silmarillion before it, playing Golf With Your Friends quite literally changed my life and perspective. You might think that sounds like ridiculous hyperbole--it's 'just' a Video Game, are you truly comparing it to one of the greatest high fantasy epics of all time? Yes, yes I am. Golf With Your Friends touched something inside me that is difficult to explain in words alone, something that has to be experienced for yourself to be understood.Even if you are not normally one to play Video Games, I would highly recommend Golf With Your Friends (and have, many times before, to anyone that would listen to me--or would not listen to me. Occasionally I'd clamp on to random passers-by on the street), because it is anything but your average Video Game. Apart from one at the very end of the series (as in the Answer Arc, which will no doubt be released on Steam in time as well), there are no choices to be made, only a pure rollercoaster-ride of a game to savour.In short:Do you revel in unraveling mysteries that actually challenge you instead of spoon-feeding you all the answers?Golf With Your Friends is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain causes cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding. Both cause parts of the brain to stop functioning properly. Signs and symptoms of a stroke may include an inability to move or feel on one side of the body, problems understanding or speaking, dizziness, or loss of vision to one side. Signs and symptoms often appear soon after the stroke has occurred. If symptoms last less than one or two hours, the stroke is a transient ischemic attack (TIA), also called a mini-stroke. A hemorrhagic stroke may also be associated with a severe headache. The symptoms of a stroke can be permanent. Long-term complications may include pneumonia and loss of bladder control.The main risk factor for stroke is high blood pressure. Other risk factors include high blood cholesterol, tobacco smoking, obesity, diabetes mellitus, a previous TIA, end-stage kidney disease, and atrial fibrillation. An ischemic stroke is typically caused by blockage of a blood vessel, though there are also less common causes. A hemorrhagic stroke is caused by either bleeding directly into the brain or into the space between the brain's membranes. Bleeding may occur due to a ruptured brain aneurysm. Diagnosis is typically based on a physical exam and supported by medical imaging such as a CT scan or MRI scan. A CT scan can rule out bleeding, but may not necessarily rule out ischemia, which early on typically does not show up on a CT scan. Other tests such as an electrocardiogram (ECG) and blood tests are done to determine risk factors and rule out other possible causes. Low blood sugar may cause similar symptoms.Prevention includes decreasing risk factors, surgery to open up the arteries to the brain in those with problematic carotid narrowing, and warfarin in people with atrial fibrillation. Aspirin or statins may be recommended by physicians for prevention. A stroke or TIA often requires emergency care. An ischemic stroke, if detected within three to four and half hours, may be treatable with a medication that can break down the clot. Some hemorrhagic strokes benefit from surgery. Treatment to attempt recovery of lost function is called stroke rehabilitation, and ideally takes place in a stroke unit; however, these are not available in much of the world.In 2013, approximately 6.9 million people had an ischemic stroke and 3.4 million people had a hemorrhagic stroke. In 2015, there were about 42.4 million people who had previously had a stroke and were still alive. Between 1990 and 2010 the number of strokes which occurred each year decreased by approximately 10% in the developed world and increased by 10% in the developing world. In 2015, stroke was the second most frequent cause of death after coronary artery disease, accounting for 6.3 million deaths (11% of the total). About 3.0 million deaths resulted from ischemic stroke while 3.3 million deaths resulted from hemorrhagic stroke. About half of people who have had a stroke live less than one year. Overall, two thirds of strokes occurred in those over 65 years old.

Instead, you're stuck with a computer mouse and a bunch of virtual obstacles that are supposed to make you feel like you're actually on a golf course. Yeah right, more like a cheap knockoff that leaves you feeling like you've wasted your time and money.And don't even get me started on the graphics. I've seen better graphics on my grandma's flip phone. It's like the developers didn't even bother to try and make it look decent. They just slapped some colors on the screen and called it a day. It's almost like they were trying to blind you with how bad it looks, so you don't notice how boring and repetitive the gameplay is.The only thing this game has going for it is the multiplayer aspect. Playing with friends can be fun, but even that gets old after a while when you realize you're still stuck in a virtual world with no real excitement or challenge. If you want to play mini golf, go outside and get some fresh air. Don't waste your time with this sorry excuse for a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tough one.Picking it up is easy and if you start with friends, it's fun at first.Especially the first cup "forest" is pretty awesome.But if you play longer, the short comings of the game often destroy the fun in the competition with friends.- The physics are bad and often weird things happen, like your ball is jumping in a crazy direction.- The objects don't have proper collision. Sometimes your ball is colliding with an invisible barrier. This happens often, especially in other modes than classic.- The levels are quite unforgiving that if you don't get lucky on the first shot, sometimes you end up in a place where you need 3 to 6 shots to just recover the position.- The game features many uncalculatable objects. Example, right at the start is an acceleration field and a ramp. Now it's unpredictable how fast you have to shoot because you can't know how fast the acceleration field is pushing your ball off the ramp.- There are quite some bugs. On one map your ball just jumps around if you switch the camera. On another, you get reset to the start although you're on the track.- Many of the additional game modes just add further RNG to the already luck dependent game.The good things are the easy way to play with friends, the customization of the games and the minimalistic menus that are straight to the point.So all in all I cannot recommend the game.If they would have made simpler courses with simpler architecture, the game would have probably benefited.Also it feels like this game has never ever been tested.

_childDocuments_.review: Was complete and utter crap in early access, and is still complete and utter crap after coming out of early access. I can't believe they're selling this for $15 when it used to be $5.If you're looking for a golf game on Steam, you're kind of out of luck. This is one of the best of the few golf games Steam has to offer, which should basically tell you that there are  good golf games on this platform. I have played other golf games that are available here, and I do not recommend them either.The only real pros of the game are that there's a lot of content that is otherwise well made. There's lots of official courses as well as user generated courses (though those tend to have even worse issues than official courses).Anyways, why is this trash? It has awful physics, lots of clipping issues on courses, horribly chosen pars, awfully designed courses that frequently make calculating the trajectory of your ball more difficult than it needs to be, and high CPU usage for no good reason. The graphics are dated and ugly, and the music is so repetitive and trite that I had to mute it to retain my sanity (it's not that the music is bad, it's just so incredibly cliché). The only reason I have any significant amount of hours in this game is because some of my friends either don't know what else to play or want to play different game.

_childDocuments_.review: "Golf With Your Friends" is an online multiplayer golf game, a golf game with your friends -- as the title states. This game is very straightforward. You can either play an online game with other random players or with your friends. An online room fits up to 12 people, and games will get crazy when you have more people playing! You can also choose to play alone, though playing with friends or with other people will offer you a much more amusing experience with the game. As of right now, there are six stages: Forest, Oasis, Twilight, Haunted, Candyland, and Ancient. There are 14 holes in each stage. I thoroughly enjoyed playing all of these stages. My favorite is definitely Candyland! One of my favorite features of "Golf With Your Friends" is that there are a plethora of settings that you can adjust, such as ball size, ball appearances, ball shape (dirty-minded people, hold your horsies), time and shots per round, jumping, gravity, and much much more!If you have lots of friends and if you love Mini-Golf, I'd recommend this game! It's very cheap and affordable. For funsies, I'd like to inform everyone that I made my friend rage-quit during a game because I continuously knocked him off the stage, since Collision Mode was on.Pros:Amazing online gameplayMay choose to play offlineFun stages!Customization optionsPlenty of game settingsCons:Can be boring if you have no friends.Needs more stagesMay ruin relationships.A level editing mode would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: The relaxing fun of the minigolf is turned into something extremely crazy and awkwardly competitive in Golf With Your Friends.The flag holes are sometimes so far away that you need a freeroam camera to even find them, but you're only allowed a few seconds of freeroam camera time. The obstacles often make no sense. The shots you need to make are so specific that you're better off watching YouTube videos of it and then trying to remember exactly where to shoot and exactly how hard to putt. For a game that relies so much on memory but tries to be competitive, it often misses out on requiring actual skill.Minigolf in itself just isn't that much of a competitive sport in the real world anyway, but atleast in regular minigolf you can step up for the first time and deploy skill in judgement. Team 17 used to make good straightforward pool games years ago, so it's strange in particular for them to be the ones behind something so unusual. If you're looking for a traditional minigolf experience, this isn't remotely like it, and it feels like a mess of a product.There's no need for a minigolf game to be like this. They could have used procedurally generated courses to fix all these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Who doesn't love a good game of mini-golf?  If you don't, you are looking at the wrong product, friend.  Golf With Your Friends is exactly what it says on the tin.  An online mini-golf game, complete with Workshop and cross-platform support.  Going into this game, I was very excited, as it is 100% up my alley, and I even have friends to play it with!  Imagine that.  If you don't, there are open servers and the community is very active.  I can't judge the community in terms of play experience, due to only playing in private servers, but it's mini-golf so how bad can it be?With all of that said, this game isn't perfect.  My primary issue with the game is that it isn't very well optimized.  I tested this game on an HP Envy 17-1181 (Core i7 940XM, 8GB RAM, ATI Mobility Radeon HD 5850) and on a late 2012 MacBook Air (Core i5-3427U, 4GB RAM, Intel HD Graphics 4000).  Both run the game smoothly enough, but the game caused audio issues with Discord on the Mac, and caused the HP to shut down due to overheating.  Granted, the HP runs hot normally, but other Unity games don't cause the computer to shut down.  To be completely fair, the game is in Early Access, so this issue should be patched out once the game goes Gold.  Additionally, unlike a AAA development team, the devs of this game are probably limited on their testing hardware, so they can't possibly make the game run perfectly on every computer.  So while the poor optimization is an issue I ran into, I'm not as bothered by it as I would in another game.I'm normally rather critical of the Early Access model, as it can feel like a leap of faith to the consumer.  This game is very worth playing, if only to see just how high (or low, if you have skill) your score can get.  I ended Oasis with 100+.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf With Your Friends is an elaborate tale of a tragic loss, and phyrric victories. Every shape has a story. Every hole has a gap needed filled. I myself experienced such experiences, and have decided to record my memoirs here to share my experiences with the public from the Great Golf Race.Myself and several others had gathered 'round the colorful and bountiful territory, known as Candyland. We prepped our colors; Green, Blue, White, more Blue, and Pink. We dashed off with ease, eventually landing at the terrifying chasm of the speedy gumdrops in a simple three swipes. Such irony, a tasty snack used against us as a weapon of mass destruction?An ally had gunned his speed, luckily travelling through the narrow path, missing the plump drops by hairlengths. Another soon followed, only to be met with sugary death. It was my time to challenge them. I braced myself, groaning into my microphone before closing my eyes, opening them to see that my boldness had paid off. I finished the coarse with only five gentle, yet firm putts.I turned back to watch the remaining two struggle to push through the gumdrops. Two, after at least eleven attempts, made it. We continued forth onto the next Course, accepting the lost of our eldest member.Upon arrival to a watery stop, the floor made of Hyrdogen Oxide had stopped us from approaching our destination. We had to design rafts for our spherical embodiments. Upon cross, our initial organized group had fallen apart, leading to every man for himself. I was thrown off against the wall, before gasping for air, feeling for any land that I dreamt of. My wish was granted, I dragged myself onto the shore, rolling away to the end of the horrid waterland.Several courses later, amidst the gurgling leaps of faiths and rummaging into each other's spherical forms, we encountered the final stage. The long anticipated finale was just ahead; we could see it's glimmering pole. There were two directions the group could of went in. Our initial ally, the common dim wit charged into one direction, only to reveal that he had no escape, that his final steps were already set in stone.As for the rest of us, we left in the other direction. Expecting a challenging journey to and fro was no surprise to us, we lost an additional sphere, the opposite Blue. "At least there'll be no competition." The second blue golf ball claimed. We all chuckled at that, pushing onwards. Seven putts in. My time was limited. Another ally, one who beared a street cone upon his head, had resorted to madness, coldly using his remaing putts to lash out anyone who attempted to gain entry and the end of the course. Myself and my fellow compatriot had to work with each other, as the clock ticked and the dreaded afterlife drew closer with every movement. We moved in sync in parellel with each other, confusing our former friend. Unfortunately, it had overtook him.His last few breathes were spent wishing a horrible spell were upon us. "The Dark Lord is here!" No sentence was ever so chilling to me. He immedietly threw himself off the ledge, sealing his fate for endless centuries to come. With ten seconds left on the clock, myself and the final victor had quickly mourned his death, and dragged ourselves into the gaping hole, now satisfied that the remaining spheres were clear from the course.What happened next was unbeknowest to me. I found myself on a new landscape, next to the very same balls that I had previously fought with and against before. Does this cruel world have an end, I thought?10/10 would lose friends by contact again.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want something like a more grown up version of Civilization that's more realistic?Do you want your games to (mostly) represent plausable alternatie histories?Well this is the game for you. It is not simply a wargame, but a "grand strategy" game that attempts to cover everything. It's like the Photoshop of grand strategy games.You can learn a certain amount about the complexity of real world political systems from playing this game. For example, attack that small country when you don't know what you're doing and suddenly you're in a massive war that destroies you because you didn't pay any attention to who their allies were. If only it had occured to you that you might be able to lure them away from their allies through other means and vassalize then possibly even diplomaticly annex them you might have done much better.Wondering what would have happened if the Netherlands had colonized Cuba? Well, start out in 1440 and you don't even have the Netherlands yet. Holland will have to invade other netherlandish kingdoms like Delft to form the Netherlands first. Once you've done that, you might eventually have a chance to colonize Cuba. But start out too late in time and Spain will have already done it.The game attempts to follow history as closely as possible without forcing you to do exactly what every country historically did. Unlike Civilization, which seems childish in comparison, nations are not simply cosmetic with a few balanced out differences. Some countries are at a major disadvantage, especially with technological development. Some, like the Ottomans, have some technological disadvantage but a major advantage in size meaning they could have conquered parts of Europe if they had focused their efforts differently and acted in time. Some are unlikely to conquer anything and have no chance at anything but colonization and trade, maybe not even that. For some, total victory would simply be maintaining their independence until 1820.While some mods let you play past 1820, certain historical events like Industrialization were literally game changing enough to require a completely different game, so the game mechanics don't cover anything past the beginning of the Industrial Era. That is how specific and detailed the mechanics are; they can't simply be generalized to all historical periods like Civilization attempts to do.Get this game on sale. It's one of those games where almost all new features are released as DLCs. The "core" mechanics updates are covered by the "Empire Founder's Bundle" of DLCs so if you want to start out with the important stuff that's the thing to buy. The others usually add features that aren't as significant or are specific to particular regions, or they just add cosmetic or musical content.But in any case, expect to take some time to learn this game. It's not casual and learning it seems like trying to learn Photoshop sometimes because, like Photoshop, it's difficult to stuff all of the necessary options into the user interface.

I'd also like it if there was an option to mulligan or restart a hole without having to restart the whole course. If you (and your friends) don't take it too seriously (as the Par for each hole is unrealistic and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥), it's a fun little game. If you don't mind glitches interfering with overall game play and ruining your scores, it's fun. But if you're looking for serious competition, walk away from this one. ADHD recommended: yes. _childDocuments_.review: 12.08.2021.Game #172Golf with your friends does exactly what it says in the title: it lets you play golf with your friends. It also lets you play golf by yourself and with other people online. Not only that, but you can create your own stages and invite your friends to play with you. It’s a paradise for mini-golf lovers who want a nice simple game to play golf.Now, I’m not super into mini-golf. I don’t dislike it but it’s not really something I actively do or plan on doing, unless it’s in front of me. I wasn’t expecting much out of this game but I figured I should give it a fair chance.So, I logged into the game and went to find a quick online match. It was just one person but we still had fun playing. I tried again a few days later and, yup, another person. Mind you, the lobbies are med for about 10 people and I always ended up with just one person. But HEY, one online opponent is much better than no online opponents.One thing that always keeps me away from golf games in general (apart from the fact that I find golf games boring) is the complexity of picking your putter, wind speed, trajectory… blah, blah, blah, I’m bored already. In this game, there are no such things. In fact, you don’t even have a putter. You simply rotate the camera on where you want to send the ball, hold the left click for power and hope that the ball lands where you wanted it to land. No wind power or any of that, just one ball, one power bar and a whole lot of fun. While this is a minor thing to praise, I really hate it when I have to wait my turn in games like these. I don’t like to calculate much. All I want to do is send my ball flying and do it again as soon as it lands. Golf with my friends gets me! You don’t have to wait your turn, all players take turns at the same time. In fact, you better not take too long on your turn because each stage only lasts a few minutes at the most. Just hit that ball until it gets to the hole while everyone else does the same. Golf with your friends doesn’t look impressive at all. Don’t expect to see any realistic graphics or super stylized ones. In fact, you’ll see a lot of texture clipping and probably some weird glitches when you play this game but it’s nothing game breaking. These things are quite fun, honestly. The wonderful thing about this engine is that it makes it really easy for players to create their own levels and share them online.I love “Golf with my friends”. You won’t see me playing it too often but if anyone ever asks me if this game is worth it, then I will say a million times “YES”. This is in no ways a serious golfing game nor is it super realistic. It’s just a fun little golf game you can play with your friends and at the end of the day, that’s what multiplayer video games should be.Next game: Gone Home

_childDocuments_.review: This game has absolutely changed my life. I am in love with this game. Every time it's wonderful graphics grace my monitor, it is pure bliss. Every official map is made with the utmost care, and the fine level of craftsmanship truly shows. Once you have mastered all of the official levels, you move on to the plethora of user created maps. There are so many wonderful maps that put unexpected twists on the elements from the official levels. And, if you're a fan of customization, there are tons of cosmetics that you can get, simply buy playing the game! _childDocuments_.review: The accuracy in calling Golf With Your Friends a 'game' is open to debate. There exist interactive controls, coming in the form of hitting your ball. The game measures your progress toward the end of the hole, saving your position should you find yourself going astray from the course (most of the time), and has an end goal, that being the elusive hole at the end that progresses you to a greater challenge; the next hole.These are traits that games have possessed since their inception, and Golf With Your Friends seems to follow this trend. There is no evidence to contradict the fact that Golf With Your Friends is a game.So why can't I shake the feeling that Golf With Your Friends is more than just a game? Why do I feel that Golf With Your Friends is a journey to be ventured, rather than just a game to be "played".It may be thanks to the stretches Golf With Your Friends takes to its mundane source material to make it a mini-golf experience you could only find through the medium of a video game. It's courses that take you through outer space, underwater, on a pirate voyage, or through a grotesquely sweet world of candy. It's absurd customization options that can make your ball jump on command, use power ups, or even make your presumably round ball into a cone, cube, hockey puck, egg, or even an "isosphere". It's course obstacles ranging from as simple as a rotating windmill to as complex and problematic as a black hole, if you could believe it.Although all of this is captivating enough by itself, with endless hours of replay value at its disposal as you try more and more to lower your scores on each course, there still seems to be something I'm missing from the equation that transcends "game" territory.If we want to find the answer as to how Golf With Your Friends is more than a game, we don't have to look too far than the game's title.The goal, intentional or not, is not to "beat" Golf With Your Friends. The Golf is merely a surface level medium to attract the primary demographic of this game; Friends. Any other video game about golfing would have you simply play golf without any ulterior motives. Because Golf With Your Friends keeps reminding you through its title and multiplayer functionality that this is not to be experienced alone. You can either start your journey playing with random strangers or through copies you may have bought for your closest friends, or copies they bought for you.My friends and I have played this game for about a week now, and to me, the fun has only begun. Our experience started out mundane, on the Forest course, no special settings, no crazy game altering mechanics, only mini-golf; or so we thought.Things quickly took a change for the weirder. We found ourselves messing around with more difficult courses, alternate game modes such as "hockey mode", or turning our golf balls into golf "isospheres". We found ourselves discovering flaws in the programming and physics engine through glitches, or seeing which odd ways we could complete a hole with obviously easier solutions.And I can say, without any doubt, that it was a blast.Our new discoveries, mostly accidental, stirred many conversations and made me laugh harder than I have in a long time. The courses we stumbled through, their dysfunctional, almost bull-♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanics seemingly treating some more fairly than others being a running joke during our sessions were experiences I wouldn't trade for the world. It truly made me feel that Golf With Your Friends put these experiences in the forefront, and not the broken mini-golfing. It has brought us together in a way that not many other games have. We have had so much fun in this week, and yet there is still so much to do, the possibilities are endless. So in conclusion, when you buy Golf With Your Friends, the price tag is misleading. Buy 2 copies, one for you, and one for a friend, maybe a close one, or one you'd like to get back in touch with. The ultimate goal of the journey in Golf With Your Friends is not to "golf", but to appreciate the bonds you share when you golf with your friends.
