_childDocuments_.review: Golf is a club-and-ball sport in which players use various clubs to hit balls into a series of holes on a course in as few strokes as possible.Golf, unlike most ball games, cannot and does not utilize a standardized playing area, and coping with the varied terrains encountered on different courses is a key part of the game. The game at the usual level is played on a course with an arranged progression of 18 holes, though recreational courses can be smaller, often having nine holes. Each hole on the course must contain a teeing ground to start from, and a putting green containing the actual hole or cup 4+1⁄4 inches (11 cm) in diameter. There are other standard forms of terrain in between, such as the fairway, rough (long grass), bunkers (or "sand traps"), and various hazards (water, rocks) but each hole on a course is unique in its specific layout and arrangement.Golf is played for the lowest number of strokes by an individual, known as stroke play, or the lowest score on the most individual holes in a complete round by an individual or team, known as match play. Stroke play is the most commonly seen format at all levels, but most especially at the elite level.The modern game of golf originated in 15th century Scotland. The 18-hole round was created at the Old Course at St Andrews in 1764. Golf's first major, and the world's oldest tournament in existence, is The Open Championship, also known as the British Open, which was first played in 1860 at the Prestwick Golf Club in Ayrshire, Scotland. This is one of the four major championships in men's professional golf, the other three being played in the United States: The Masters, the U.S. Open, and the PGA Championship.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf with Friends is a game that promises to be a fun and relaxing experience for anyone who loves miniature golf. Unfortunately, it falls short of its promises and ends up being a frustrating and tedious mess.The game's controls are clunky and unresponsive, making it difficult to get your ball where you want it to go. The physics engine is also wonky, leading to situations where your ball inexplicably bounces off of walls or flies off into oblivion.The courses themselves are poorly designed, with obstacles placed in seemingly random locations and little thought given to how they affect the gameplay. This leads to situations where you're stuck in an endless loop of bouncing your ball off of the same wall over and over again, or struggling to get your ball up a steep incline.Adding insult to injury, the game's online multiplayer is a mess. Lag and connection issues make it nearly impossible to play with friends, and the lack of any kind of matchmaking system means you'll often find yourself playing with people who are way out of your skill level.In short, Golf with Friends is a game that's more likely to leave you frustrated than entertained. Unless you enjoy the feeling of repeatedly banging your head against a wall, it's best to give this one a miss.\\ Just kidding I'm just bad //

You can shoot along a wall and get your ball bounce directly back, because there's just pinaccle that extends just a tiny little bit out of the wall.This game is just poorly made. I do not recommend.

The later fields for every course are challenging, and there are a few bugs to be worked out: like in the history museum course, where the tar pit is just before the hole, you can get your ball stuck in the rock area, below the right side of the ledge leading to the tar pit. Or the stuffed bear's head in the wall, the ball will bounce off of its teeth and off course. Both are still bugs as-of this comment.  Overall this is an entertaining pass-time game with a lot to look forward to!

_childDocuments_.review: You know those times where everyone is in discord and no one has any idea what to play? Maybe everyone has had a long day or possibly has had a few beverages... you know that kind of night, right? Golf with your Friends is the PERFECT game for those kind of occasions. It is another one of those games that does not take itself seriously and does not expect you to either. It is a simple game revolving around blasting your golf ball towards the hole. There are like 2 controls, 3 if your friends are sweaties and play with jumping. The game is graphically simple, yet the cooked-in maps are visually interesting enough, especially the later ones. The game has memorable/memeable music with plenty of funny sound effects. The golf balls behave like you would expect. The game is very, very straight forward. The fun of the game really comes from turning on collision and colluding against your friends. GwyF is really just golf if you have no friends to play with and the game really cannot carry itself without you and your friends making your own fun from what the game offers. Don't think about it too much, don't be too sober when you play, and I guarantee that this will be a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: INTRODUCTION[The scene opens with Hulk Hogan, Macho Man Randy Savage, Mr. T, Tommy Wiseau, and Arnold Schwarzenegger standing in a living room that looks like a mix between a WrestleMania ring and a 1980s arcade. They’re huddled around a gaming PC with the words “Golf With Your Friends” glowing on the screen. On the table? Protein shakes, popcorn, and an inexplicable pile of sunglasses.]HULK HOGAN: Listen up, brothers! Today, we ain't body-slamming or saving the world. We're hittin’ the greens! (flexes dramatically) The Hulkster’s got the moves to dominate this course, dude!MACHO MAN: (snapping into a Slim Jim) Ooh yeah! The Macho Man is bringing the madness! The greens won’t know what hit ‘em, brother!MR. T: I pity the fool who thinks I can’t putt! Golf ain’t just for rich folks—I’m about to make this my turf, suckas!TOMMY WISEAU: (smiling awkwardly) Oh hi, guys. Let’s play... golf, huh?ARNIE: (wielding the controller like a shotgun) It’s not a tumor; it’s just winning. Let’s GO.[They all slam "Start Game" together like they’re launching a rocket. The first hole loads up, and chaos begins.]HOLE 1 – THE START[Hulk Hogan, brimming with confidence, lines up his first shot. He flexes, aiming carefully before swinging the controller like he’s bench-pressing the moon.]HULK HOGAN: Let me show you, brothers, what it means to Hulk-smash this ball![The ball rockets off the tee like a meteor—straight into a tree, ricochets off a fence, and lands in a pond full of cartoon frogs.]TOMMY WISEAU: (in dismay) You’re tearing me apart, golf ball![The camera zooms in as Macho Man steps up, wearing sunglasses on top of his sunglasses.]MACHO MAN: Ooh yeah! The Macho Madness is coming for ya! Watch me hit this sweet spot![His ball soars through the air, bounces on the green, rolls majestically toward the hole... and promptly drops into a sand trap.]MACHO MAN: (still confident) That’s just part of my strategy, brother. Sand power![Tommy Wiseau picks up the controller, holding it upside down.]TOMMY WISEAU: Oh hi, ball. Let’s be friends.[His ball immediately vanishes into a glowing vortex. Everyone stares at the screen.]ARNIE: (mocking) You didn’t just miss the hole—you missed the planet!HOLE 2 – THE TRICKY SHOT[Mr. T approaches the controller, his signature gold chains gleaming like the sun. He glares at the game like it owes him money.]MR. T: Time to show you fools how precision works. Ain’t no jibber-jabber in golf![He lines up a near-impossible shot. The ball ricochets off six walls, bounces over water, and dramatically rolls into the hole.]MACHO MAN: (jaw dropping) Oohhh yeah! That’s some real A-Team action right there!TOMMY WISEAU: (clapping too hard) What a story, Mr. T!HOLE 3 – TOMMY’S TURN[Tommy Wiseau crouches dramatically, whispering to the ball as if it’s a long-lost friend.]TOMMY WISEAU: Oh hi, golf ball. You are my favorite customer.[He takes a swing. The ball shoots up at a 90-degree angle, hits a seagull, and plummets into a nearby lava pit. Everyone groans.]ARNIE: (deadpan) You just introduced the ball to Judgment Day.HOLE 4 – ARNIE GOES TERMINATOR[Arnold Schwarzenegger steps up, holding the controller like it’s a bazooka. He squints at the screen, muttering Austrian curses under his breath.]ARNIE: (in Terminator voice) Hasta la vista, gravity.[He hits the ball. It defies physics, bouncing off every obstacle on the map—bridges, windmills, even a virtual squirrel—before landing perfectly in the hole.]MACHO MAN: (stunned) That ball ain’t a T-1000; it’s a T-perfect!HULK HOGAN: (grumbling) Beginner’s luck, dude.HOLE 5 – MR. T SHOWS OFF[Mr. T cracks his knuckles, glaring at the screen like it owes him an apology.]MR. T: This hole’s mine, suckas. Watch and learn.[He swings the controller like a hammer. The ball sails majestically across the screen, bounces once, and lands directly in the hole. A rainbow animation erupts.]EVERYONE: (cheering) The fool-pitying champ!MR. T: (grinning) That’s right, suckas. I’m the real A-Team!ENDING – CHAOS AND FRIENDSHIP[The group plays through several more ridiculous holes, with balls flying into volcanoes, spirals, and occasionally outer space. Laughter fills the room.]HULK HOGAN: (cry-laughing) Brother, this is the most fun I’ve had since WrestleMania!MACHO MAN: Ooh yeah! The madness and the mini-golf magic, brother!TOMMY WISEAU: (nodding sagely) What a story, golf.ARNIE: (laughing) Forget the greens—we’re bringing the boom![As the game ends, they all high-five, surrounded by chaos: overturned furniture, a shattered protein shake, and Tommy sitting in a golf cart for no apparent reason.]FADE OUT:[The screen shows "Game Over," but the fun isn’t over yet. These legends have proven that mini-golf is more than a game—it’s a battlefield of hilarity.]THE ENDIn a world where regular golf is slow, boring, and way too quiet, experience Golf With Your Friends—the game that asks: “What if mini-golf had jetpacks, lasers, and friendship-ending chaos?”Get ready to tee off on a wild ride through insane courses that look like they were designed by a hyperactive toddler with a candy addiction. From haunted castles to space stations to volcanoes, nothing is off-limits—except for normal physics.Play with up to 11 of your closest friends (or sworn enemies) and watch as your wholesome group chat devolves into an all-caps shouting match. Master the art of timing, precision, and blind luck as your perfectly lined-up shot ricochets off a wall, misses the hole, and lands somewhere in a completely different dimension.Marvel at the truly unfair power-ups! Turn your buddy’s ball into a cube, cover the green in honey traps, or activate the most diabolical invention of all: collision mode—because nothing says “friendship” like sending someone’s ball flying off the map on purpose.Featuring:    >Holes so outrageous they’ll make you question reality.    >Customizable golf balls that scream “style” (or just “hat”).    >And the most epic soundtrack since Caddyshack!So grab your clubs, gather your squad, and prepare for the real challenge: staying friends after Golf With Your Friends!"Golf With Your Friends"—because nothing says fun like rage-quitting on Hole 18.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings as I hope all is well! Below is my Steam Review for Golf With Your Friends, thanks for reading as I wish you well in all your gaming adventures...STORY/LORE - N/ANo story or lore here ladies and gentlemen, just a fun amateur golf game that’s great with friends. If anything, each different course has a distinctive feel to it, so in essence, each course has its own unique little story. Does that count?GAMEPLAY - 8/10Golf With Your Friends is a pretty fun game if you enjoy amateur golf. Obviously, if you have a group of friends to play with, this is the perfect game to chill with on a Friday night. You know, grab everyone on Discord, sit back, and hit the amateur golf course. Golf With Your Friends has a good selection of maps and different ways to play by either using the Dunk or Puck mode, to add a little variety than just a traditional golf ball. You can also customize your golf ball with all sorts of fun different things from dinosaur bones to different kinds of trails. It’s not a whole lot but just enough to make it stand out when playing with others.GRAPHICS - 7/10The graphics are decent in Golf With Your Friends but keep in mind, you’ll find some clipping and glitches here and there. It wasn’t enough to ruin the game or anything but the graphics are fine here but nothing that’s going to look real or break your rig. This is a fun little amateur golf game to play with friends, it’s not real golf or anything like that.SOUNDTRACK - 7/10The music in Golf With Your Friends is fitting for an amateur golf setting as every course will have its own unique soundtrack to it. It’s nothing that’s crazy immersive or anything, just simple and good for background noise as you golf.MULTIPLAYER - 8/10At the time of this Steam Review, it does take a while to use Quick Play to find others to play with. This is most likely the case because it’s not an insanely popular game here on Steam. That’s why I recommend getting this game if you have a core group of friends that are looking for a chill kind of game to play with on the weekends or something. It’s very easy to host a game and you can customize it in a lot of different ways.FINAL SCORE - 8/10Golf With Your Friends is a fun little amateur golf game that obviously, is a lot of fun with friends. The golf courses are fun and unique with extremely simple controls to sit back and enjoy. The soundtrack goes well with this kind of game and overall, I enjoyed going through all the different courses, modes, and customization settings. I tend to play this every now and then with friends when we’re in the mood and it’s definitely created some funny moments when fueled with alcohol. I definitely recommend this game if you love amateur golf and want to get your friends together to try something different when you game.

_childDocuments_.review: Basketball is a limited contact sport played on a rectangular court. While most often played as a team sport with five players on each side, three-on-three, two-on-two, and one-on-one competitions are also common. The objective is to shoot a ball through a hoop 18 inches (46 cm) in diameter and 10 feet (3.048 m) high that is mounted to a backboard at each end of the court. The game was invented in 1891 by Dr. James Naismith.A team can score a field goal by shooting the ball through the basket being defended by the opposition team during regular play. A field goal scores three points for the shooting team if the player shoots from behind the three-point line, and two points if shot from in front of the line. A team can also score via free throws, which are worth one point, after the other team is assessed with certain fouls. The team with the most points at the end of the game wins, but additional time (overtime) is mandated when the score is tied at the end of regulation. The ball can be advanced on the court by passing it to a teammate, or by bouncing it while walking or running (dribbling). It is a violation to lift, or drag, one's pivot foot without dribbling the ball, to carry it, or to hold the ball with both hands then resume dribbling.The game has many individual techniques for displaying skill—ball-handling, shooting, passing, dribbling, dunking, shot-blocking, and rebounding. Basketball teams generally have player positions, the tallest and strongest members of a team are called a center or power forward, while slightly shorter and more agile players are called small forward, and the shortest players or those who possess the best ball handling skills are called a point guard or shooting guard. The point guard directs the on court action of the team, implementing the coach's game plan, and managing the execution of offensive and defensive plays (player positioning).Basketball is one of the world's most popular and widely viewed sports. The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the most popular and widely considered to be the highest level of professional basketball in the world and NBA players are the world's best paid athletes by average annual salary per player. Outside North America, the top clubs from national leagues qualify to continental championships such as the Euroleague and FIBA Americas League. The FIBA Basketball World Cup and Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament are the major international events of the sport and attract top national teams from around the world. Each continent hosts regional competitions for national teams, like EuroBasket and FIBA AmeriCup.The FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup and Women's Olympic Basketball Tournament feature top national teams from continental championships. The main North American league is the WNBA (NCAA Women's Division I Basketball Championship is also popular), whereas strongest European clubs participate in the EuroLeague Women.

_childDocuments_.review: This pretty much sums it up. You will hear so much swearing, cheering and laughing playing this game the way it's supposed to be played - with your friends.Here is my shortcut - the hole in one of this review.It's Golfing - as easy as it gets - you hold the mouse button, move the mouse to change the strength and direction of your shot and release to hit the ball.Additionally, you can choose to play a kind of basketball, where jumping (default 'Spacebar') is enabled and the holes become hoops.You can also zoom in and out to get a better idea of the location of your goal. Beyond that, even if something obscures your vision you can use the free camera (default 'C') to get a better idea of your position.Currently, there are 6 different levels: Forest, Desert, Moonlight Park, Spooky Mansion, Candyland and Jurassic Park.Something I really enjoyed to see is the progression you can observe going from level to level.Each map contains 18 holes and at least in the forest level you can finish it with 18 shots - but this will take a lot of practice.The design is really neat and most of the time you can take more than one approach to hitting the ball.With to the many possibilities comes a big part of the replay value and the whole fun of the game. If you manage that one insane hit, none of your friends even thought about and you leave them wondering how you managed the hole in 2 strokes when they are on the 7th.Creating and joining a lobby is super easy, as well as setting up modifiers. Another big part of replaying this game will come from setting up different modifications - such as 'random ball shapes'. When the unlucky one with the acorn hits the hole in one - a ♥♥♥♥ storm will be unleashed :D before even going into multiplayer, I advise you to paint your ball under 'Customize' - so you can be recognized by your friends. Just don't take the same colors. Press 'L' to light the way for your friends.All the levels are really neatly designed and have a really cool air about them, to match a certain theme and bring you in the mood.I really like the sweet melody in the background, my friend, however, turned the volume way down because he couldn't stand it - so it's really a preference thing.If you have friends willing to play this game with you - by all means you can have a good time., there isn't that much content in the game yet. Of course, you can aim for the hole in one on every map (if this is even possible; I don't think it is), hone your skills by trying new hits and playing with funny settings but it depends on how long you and your friends will stay motivated together - because if the first one loses the interest, the others will probably follow.If you have read this far - .I hope this review helped you in deciding to buy this game and if it did, I would be grateful for a 'thumbs up', if you didn't like it, you can give me a 'thumbs down' but I would be glad to hear your opinion on what you didn't like.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I mean I've played this a lot, had a lot of laughs, even did a couple courses on par completely.That said, the reason im giving this a thumbs down is well deserved in its own right, let me tell you what bothers me.Clipping, Yes, sometimes at some levels its possible to clip through walls, and lose.Physics : Not always accurate as other play throughs (So I guess the game becomes more luck based).Pars : This is my biggest annoyance, whoever set the par rate in a LOT of courses, set it straight out on "If you're really lucky this should be right!"The game is actually pretty fun, but the creators (Team17) should've made the par chart a bit more on par with the course itself, like the barrel level in Forest should be a 3 par instead of a 2 par so that it's not completely luck based of hitting the hole in the barrel but more so for people that don't get that (Super lucky shot), btw this comes from someone who finished THAT COURSE on its par limit already.Beyond that, the physics are often wonkey, and in some levels (like space station and the haunted course) you can legitly get your ball in place where there's sadly no more saving it, since the level see's it as a "legit part of the course", while factually you shouldnt be able to get there.Lastly the camera can go completely wonky on you (especially close to walls) making shots or even looking at your screen a headache, and in levels with minecarts, or other moving objects, they sometimes just decide to go invisible, making it a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ playthrough.Also, more often than not you get disconnected from the "Rare already" Multiplayer sessions because of a "Network Error" which is just sad.Can't believe that we're now sold a singular DLC map for 3$ and it's a garbage map too.Lastly, Snowflakes for instance sells in marketplace for 1100$, but as far as I know its unobtainable, it's an effect from what 2019? or so and has since been unlocked since the game doesn't do "holiday events" or something.Still thumbs down for me.

And let me tell you, nothing brings a group of friends together like taking turns hitting a little white ball around a virtual course.But fear not, because there's plenty of ways to sabotage your friends' shots, like bouncing their ball off a moving target or knocking them off a tricky ledge.Of course, the game isn't perfect. Sometimes it feels like you're in a never-ending game of putt-putt, trying to hit that one pesky hole that just won't go in.But despite its flaws, Golf With Your Friends is a fun and hilarious game that will have you and your pals laughing and joking around for hours on end.So if you're looking for a game that will bring out your competitive side while also making you giggle like a kid, give Golf With Your Friends a try. Just make sure to watch out for your friends' sly attempts at sabotage."

name: A Fold Apart
detailed_description: A relatable, true-to-life story of a long-distance relationship. Over 50 handcrafted paper folding puzzles. Beautiful 3D graphics with a tactile, “homemade” paper aesthetic. The ability to choose the couple that best represents you! Lightning Rod Games presents A Fold Apart: an award-winning puzzle game that explores the emotional rollercoaster of a long-distance relationship — in a world of folding paper! After career choices force them along separate paths, a Teacher and Architect vow to make their long-distance relationship work at any cost. Experience both sides of their story as the couple navigates the complexities of (mis)communication and the emotional ups and downs that separation brings. By flipping, folding, and unfolding the paper puzzles in their handcrafted worlds, you can help the couple overcome the emotional barriers of their relationship — but will love endure...?

short_description: A puzzle game that explores the emotional rollercoaster of a long-distance relationship — in a world of folding paper! Flip, fold, unfold and rotate paper puzzles to help a couple navigate the complexities of living apart.

_childDocuments_.review: (Leans more towards neutral than positive)A Fold Apart focuses on the difficulties on a long distance relationship between two characters, which you can switch around the genders of if you want to before starting. To make things easier, I’ll call them Red and Blue. After meeting at a library, they hit it off pretty quickly as they make many memories together, start dating, and soon enough live together. However, they hit a snag one day as Blue is offered his dream job of designing an important building in the city. After talking, Blue decides to accept the contract and temporarily move to the city until the job is done while Red stays in the country and begin her dream job of being a teacher. The two communicate with each other through text messages, but it only takes a couple weeks for problems to arise.A Fold Apart gives us snippets into Red and Blue’s relationship, showing us the times when problems emerged for either of them. Each chapter starts you out with controlling either Red or Blue and right when they’re texting each other. Every so often you’ll be able to choose between two choices to send out, but it doesn’t necessarily change the story. It all seems like everything is fine until something brings them over the edge, whether it be a text or their own doubts. Thus, we’re taken into their thoughts where they’ll walk through their mindscape as their thoughts are both shown with the changing scenery and text. This is also where the puzzles reside.As you can probably tell, the puzzles here are focused on folding paper. Most levels require you to figure out a way to get to a star to advance. It starts out pretty simple. At first, you can only flip the paper to see what’s on the other side and fold a side or two to get you used to combining platforms together and knowing that you can overlap obstacles. The only thing you can’t do is folding the paper over Red or Blue. As time goes on, more elements are added in and becomes a bit more complicated. Soon, you’re able to fold all sides, fold the corners, flip the paper, and have to deal with platforms that disappear if folded. Of course, these aren’t introduced at the same time, but by the end you have to solve puzzles with most of these in mind. If you do come across any trouble, there is a hint system that you can access through the pause menu, but the hints are more doing a step for you rather than giving you a nudge in the right direction with an actual hint. It also resets the puzzle to the beginning. So it’s good news if you’re just completely lost on what to do, but not so much if you just need the last push and would rather not be giving the solution outright.I did have some troubles with A Fold Apart though. Sometimes, I had trouble climbing onto platforms despite being right beside it. Making me try multiple times before it registered me being right beside a platform ledge (and in some cases had to use the hint system). On puzzles that let you fold the sides and the corners, I also had some problems of the game thinking I wanted to fold the side rather than the edge.Also, it may just be me being inexperienced in the dating scene, but I found the conflict a bit silly at times (which evolved into annoyance). You’re told pretty early on that they prefer talking face-to-face rather than over text, but we never see them doing the next best thing by talking on the phone or video chatting. Another was that they read way too much into some of the texts. Like at one point Red says that Blue should take care of himself so he doesn’t get sick. Blue gets upset and goes on about how long work nights are for her before realizing that Red means well. It also doesn’t help that they don’t really communicate. Like Blue wants to rest up during his visit instead of during a bunch of things Red has planned, but he keeps it to himself rather than telling Red since he thinks it would cause a fight. I’m sure Red would have understood especially after telling her that he’s been working long hours and he’d be incredibly stressed once he gets back.I don’t know, maybe I just didn’t resonate with the story as well as others have and expected them to work more on their communication and other problems that popped up rather than ignoring it and blaming it on the distance (or on Blue for taking the job). I do see how it’s realistic, especially since I’ve had times where I get anxious when texting or just sit on a message for hours combing through it despite knowing it should just take a couple minutes, but I guess I expected them to actively improve their communication and try visiting more (especially on Red’s end) rather than (spoiler) defaulting to Red having Blue choose between his job or the relationship.That said, I do love the aesthetic and how it stuck to it. I love the art style and how bright and colorful everything is even when it darkens up during the low points. It’s great how the environment when we’re going through the character’s thoughts change as well. Like when Red mentions that she hates the city, all the buildings start to swarm her to express how it makes her feel cramped. Lastly, I like how it stuck with having this take place on paper rather than just having it only during puzzles. Each piece of paper is one area snippet and the next area is placed down so you can walk on it.While I did enjoy A Fold Apart for the most part, I’m not sure if it’d necessarily recommend it. While I do love the art style, how paper is used throughout, and how the mindscape was used to link towards Blue’s or Red’s thoughts, there are some aspects that can turn you away. If you’re looking to get the most bang out of your buck, A Fold Apart won’t help in that regard. It’s only about 2-3 hours and there’s not that much replayablity. It also depends whether or not you want to play through a story about a long distance relationship that’s pretty lacking in the communication section and where both sides often look too much into things. I also won’t recommend A Fold Apart if you’d get annoyed at the constant reinforcement of long distance relationships being hard and how often the inner dialogue kinda repeats the same message. Otherwise, look out for a discount or consider picking it up on iOS.

_childDocuments_.review: There is something really to be liked about this game. The graphical style and the melancholy music are really lovely. But - in this jaded gamer's opinion there are a few issues that are just too big to ignore.The story is a somewhat saccharine tale of love divided by pressures of work. Okay, I like the idea that a story could be inserted into such a simple puzzle game and it does hold together, but to me it just felt a bit too much. Tug gently at those heart strings if you want to produce an emotional response, don't swing on them like you're Quasimodo.The movement could be frustratingly slow at times and the text message sequences were positively painful. The puzzle mechanic was a really nice idea and I loved the concept, but it was just too simple. For all its imagination, moving towards a glowing star while avoiding badly animated stop things (actually, what were those??) all felt a bit Mario Cart and somewhat out of place in a game like this. Could we not have been looking for things from their relationship? Elements of their live together? Or pretty much anything other than glowing stars.Finally, as others have commented, there is just not enough in here to justify £15ish. This feels like a mobile game and if it was priced accordingly I would be a lot more forgiving. I hate to leave a negative review. The industry needs more games like this and fewer like Call of Duty. In the end, for all I really wanted to love it, it just didn't come together for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game because the content does not justify the price of 16.79€.The puzzle mechanics are interesting as you have to connect separate parts scattered on both sides of a sheet of paper by folding and rotating that paper in certain ways so that your character can move towards the level goal. Yet in my opinion the puzzles fall sort of flat because there is no real difficulty involved. In the vast majority of puzzles the positions of those separate parts make too obvious what you are supposed to do, especially because the options of valid actions are kind of limited.There is a story which I, however, did not really care for, It is about the hardships of a long-distance relationship due to one partner getting a significant job in another city. In particular I was turned of by the quality of the internal struggles both characters face. C'mon, if you make a decision then stick with it and don't constantly whine about it / doubt it over and over again! On top of that, as far as I understood it, in the end the couple "makes it work" by one partner just giving up his/her dream ... seriously? How does that solve anything?Finally, I felt that the controls were a bit too slow for my taste which made puzzle solving a bit tedious but I can see a potential reasoning behind that on the developers' side. Nonetheless it added to my overall dissatisfaction with the game.All in all, I feel kinda bad for not recommending this title because the core of the game is a really neat idea. But to reiterate the pricing is simply over the top in relation to content and overall the gameplay experience was not exactly satisfying. If this title looks interesting to you I strongly recommend waiting for a sale at 10€ tops.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game about a topic not explored very often in games. The puzzles are interesting. It takes a while until it includes mechanics that are less common in games, but once they do, it's a fun challenge. I wish the mechanics were more tied to the narrative: (mild spoilers) I REALLY loved the final part where you play as both characters, as I found that it was where the story was the most in-sync with the gameplay. The rest of the time, it felt like a puzzle games with non-related cutscenes about a long-distance relationship (or the other way around). I found the artstyle lovely and pretty unique, I just found some environment a little bit empty. I don't know if it's just me, but I found the conversations between the levels a bit awkward to play: both because I found it annoying that the characters didn't talk more openly about their feelings (but then again, some couples really do talk like that in real life), and because you had to use the arrows to walk with your character, at the same time as you had to choose dialogue options with those same arrows. Maybe there is something I didn't understand controls-wise. To be honest, I think I loved the concept more than I loved the actual game, but I still had a pretty good time. I'd recommend it to anyone who wants a somewhat casual puzzle game with a cute-yet-sad story on the side.

_childDocuments_.review: A Fold Apart is a sweet puzzle game with its mechanics and visuals well tied to its themes. The game could use some quality of life improvements and a smoother learning curve, but it's worth it.  The folding paper puzzles manage to match the allegorical emotional landscapes of a long-distance relationship cleverly. Some of the mechanics didn't click for me and I think it could use a few extra steps to ease you into new stage gimmicks. At least the game has a solid hint system. The game looks great and I love that you can pick through presets of different couples making it more relatable. I'm not a big fan of the writing though. The story is fine, but some of the lines and conflicts didn't click for me. It runs fine out of the box and the requirements are relatively low. It also instantly recognized the controller using Steam input. It's worth the price. Recently they even added a new bonus chapter for free so maybe more content will come. It's a nice game you can finish in an afternoon and I like how it tackles a subject that isn't that common in the medium. Not only that, I'd say it nails the tone in both its puzzles and visuals most of the time. One negative point though is that I feel almost everything in the game is just a tad slow, from menus to animations. But overall, I enjoyed my time playing. You can check my profile to read more about my review policy.

The story emphasizes a lot on the importance of good communication and the dilemma between lovers when it comes to balancing the needs of your significant other and a work that you love. Through the experiences of these fictional characters, I daresay I've learned a lot about long distance relationships and the amount of effort both sides will have to put in... the compromises as well... to make it work.Part 1: (had to take a break because my brain stopped working :P)Part 2: Story aside, the game has a very intriguing yet simple enough puzzle game that seems to serve as a tool to move the story forward. That is not to say that the puzzles aren't fun enough to stand on their own. In fact, I really liked how many new and unique game mechanics that the developer/s have managed to come up with to supplement the existing folding-based mechanics. However, for those who don't enjoy solving puzzles but love a good love story, A Fold Apart offers a Puzzle Hint feature that basically guide you through (step-by-step) the solving process, essentially letting you skip a puzzle if you don't feel like solving one. As a side note, I don't have any game dev knowledge but I'm pretty sure it's not as easy to program a virtual paper that can be folded in all manner of ways and not only for only one time either while having movable and animated elements in it, so needless to say, I'm very impressed. I also would like to commend the artist behind the brilliant art work and the composer for the amazing music in this game. Both the visuals and music go really well hand-in-hand, and they really illustrate whether, by sound or art, the emotional turmoil each character is going through. So, TLDR?+ You can choose which type of relationship you'd like :)+ A relatable (if you've been in a long distance relationship with someone you truly love before) story about two lovers who were in a long distance relationship and their struggles to keep their relationship afloat.+ Fantastic art and music. Really helps to bring depth to the story as it is being told.+ Great writing! The dialogues are very well written. You can actually "see" their love for each other only through the lovers' texted banter. Some of the internal monologues can be pretty spot-on, and that ending is just so heartwarming.+ Unique gameplay. The many different obstacles that are gradually introduced into the game slowly ramps up the challenge as you play, but...+ Simple puzzles. Especially if you're a veteran puzzler, this game would be child's play for you; for others, the game provides enough brain teasing, without going overboard. However, it's not the type of game to play if your brain's shutting down due to tiredness... as I've found out personally in my first stream :P+ Puzzle hints! If you tire of solving puzzles and would like to just experience the story, you can basically skip a puzzle by using these hints. They are unlimited.+ Allows multiple ways to solve a puzzle. It's rare for a puzzle to have more than 1 way to solve in this game, but to my delight, I found that there is such puzzles and you can solve it whichever way you can.- A bit of a glitch here - take a look at the Part 1 video - As amazing as the game is, I'm not very sure if there's a lot of people who would shell out $20 for a relatively short puzzle game that only offers a single playthrough (around 2 hours or so; I accidentally idled the game for a bit when I tabbed out to pause my stream and take a break). The price is rather steep.- Not a "choices matter"-type of game despite letting you to, at times, choose between two dialogue choices. Dialogue choices give you the illusion that you get to control the narrative but that's not the case. The story will play out like it's designed to. I think this is a missed opportunity that the dev could have used to slightly extend the game's lifespan/replayability. A couple's love may not be a topic that some would be able to relate to or understand, but if you do, A Fold Apart manages to really show the struggles that even two people who very much love each other may face, even if they aren't in a long distance relationship. There are many valuable lessons that one could obtain through this game - the key points being "the will to make a relationship work", "the willingness to compromise for a loved one" (both sides have to compromise or it won't work), and "thinking before you speak" (your words may hurt your loved ones more deeply than you think). The gameplay is also fun and interesting, especially when new elements are being added in, and best of all, the puzzles aren't designed to completely and utterly stump you. If you get stuck, you can always use the Puzzle Hint feature to skip a puzzle. However, due to the price, I'd recommend waiting for a discount before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Awful storytelling actually ruins the entire thing.The story is not compelling to begin with: Two snivelers physically separated for a few months wallow in self-pity.The narrative goes full sappy, shallow, becomes nauseating.The urge for skipping quickly arises.But there is so little you can skip.Most of the whining is done while walking, and you have to make them walk yourself.Your participation to this fiasco is imposed.The walking is sedated.A crawl.And because things can always get worse, the storytelling opts for pocket phone conversations.That's right, texting.Not video calls, not phone calls, texting.Because these two jerks, who keep pretending they miss each other so much, are too cheap for a call, I guess ?Texting, the least cinematic device since the invention of power outages.And you have to click to advance the texting too.And because things can always get worse, you also have to choose some of the schlock they type.It's draining and infuriating at the same time.This is supposed to be a puzzle game, yet it feels like 90% of what you do is drag the miserable protagonists while trying to ignore their prose.Which is constantly and uglily spattered all over the screen in large quotations, by the way.Let's assess the actual game then. The puzzles.There are few of them.They are too simple to be challenging.The only difficulty lies in trying to fold corners instead of borders with a gamepad.The folding isn't free, the paper doesn't fall exactly where you want it to, and the limitations are not clear; It often refuses your move for no discernible reason.Plus, walking and climbing are excruciatingly slow, as mentioned.Here you go.The devs design efforts were plainly spent on the wrong component.There is just too little actual play, and it's not good enough, to justify your torment.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a while. I like cute puzzle games and the story and art looked so adorable I had to check it out. What followed was a short but charming game that I'm glad I got to play.Prior to starting the game, you can choose between 4 different variations of the couple that the story follows. I love that the developers put that in there, major points on that. The story follows a couple who are madly in love. One of them gets an amazing job opportunity overseas for construction and takes it. The game showcases how their love tries to survive the harshness of long distance and if they can still be a couple by the end.This is a puzzle game with a very interesting premise. The goal is to get the character to reach the star in the picture. The only way to make this happen is to manipulate the stage by folding it (you get it!?). It starts off very simple by just folding it side to side or up and down. As you progress, you'll get corner folding and rotating it as well. Most of the puzzles are fairly simple to solve, but some of them did take some thinking to solve.The overall theme and look of this game is perfect. I loved the music, I loved how the story played out, and I loved how the style of the text was used to convey their thoughts. I was grinning from ear to ear whenever they showed dialogue between the couple but also felt sadness when the long distance really started to strain their relationship. Luckily the game is not super long, so it felt like it was just long enough to enjoy the entire package.I don't have any gripes with this game. The developers did a smart thing by adding a hint system in case you get stuck. You can use as many hints as you want, heck, you can use the hint system to solve the entire puzzle if you want. They really wanted you to enjoy the story and not let the hard puzzles ruin the experience and I respect that. I did not incur any glitches or anything game-breaking.Final verdict? This was a sweet puzzle game. It'll take you around 3-4 hours to beat. After you finish the main story, you can do the two bonus chapters that add more gameplay elements if you really want to test your mettle. Being that it is so short, you might wanna wait to grab it when it's on sale since I think $20 is a bit much for this one. Other than that, I highly recommend it if you want a fun puzzle game with a very cute couple. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: I guess this is a tepid thumbs-up.Pros: The game looks quite lovely and the puzzle mechanic is fun and pretty fresh. The puzzles are fairly simple, so this is a game much more about the experience than the challenge, and that's fine. You can customize your couple's genders, which I appreciate.Unfortunately, then there's the major con: for a story-based game, the story sucks. I played this over Discord with my long-distance fiancée thinking it would be a cute thing to experience together, and-- was anyone involved in the creation of this game ever in a long-distance relationship? The story is full of contrived, annoying arguments caused by misunderstandings and lack of communication, and none of it feels realistic to the deep amount of commitment and communication inherent to LDRs.It's a pretty game and if it looks enjoyable to you, I'd recommend it, but only on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting puzzle concept. I got stuck in a few but never enough to look up a solution. Some puzzles (especially early ones, but also some later ones) are very easy. _childDocuments_.review: You can follow me @GameAcropolis on Instagram.A Fold Apart tells the story of a happy couple who are quickly torn apart when one of them get a job opportunity in another city. They assume that their happiness and devotion to one another will help them get through any obstacle, but they quickly struggle to cope with the loneliness and emotional toll that comes with a long-distance relationship. They rely on text messaging to stay in touch, resulting in miscommunication that triggers immediate frustration and sets them upon an emotional journey to navigate their thoughts and feelings.The visual presentation instantly stands out as it is a work of art. The colour palette perfectly contrasts the rural and urban lifestyles, but they are also used to depict each character’s emotional state of mind. Their inner struggles are also visualized with on-screen text to help capture the increasing toll that a long-distance relationship is having on them.A Fold Apart features over fifty puzzles where players will have to fold, unfold, flip, and rotate paper in order to complete each puzzle. These game mechanics are introduced as you progress, which adds to the overall complexity of each puzzle. The addition of a hint system is welcoming as certain puzzles require several attempts to gain an understanding of what specific actions are needed in order to succeed.A Fold Apart has been in the making for several years and I can say that it was worth the wait, even though it was short-lived. It took me on an emotional journey where I shared laughs and frustrations with each character. The ability to choose which couple to play as is also a nice touch that fans will greatly appreciate. It was also confirmed during the virtual launch party that post-launch content will be released in the near future. A Fold Apart comes highly recommended and it can currently be enjoyed on Steam, Nintendo Switch, and Apple Arcade, while it will arrive on PS4 and Xbox One in the near future.The narrative is based on the cofounder of Lightning Rod Games’, Mark Laframboise, own personal experience during a long-distance relationship and the obstacles that needed to be overcome.Pros:+ Stunning aesthetic presentation+ Impressive paper manipulation game mechanics+ Numerous puzzles of varying degrees of difficulty + Ability to select between various couples    Cons:- On the shorter side with only 6 chaptersThanks for reading,  Dave/Game Acropolis

The puzzles are super fun and increase with difficulty as you go, but aren't so challenging that it feels impossible.I've had two minor glitches; once, after getting shocked, the character stopped responding to the movement keys, and at one point  the map disappeared but returning to the main menu then continuing the game returned me back to my current puzzle.So glad that this game is out and that I can enjoy it's beautiful graphics and heartwarming story!

I really enjoyed my time with the game - the story was sweet and well-told, the art style was unique and beautiful, and the puzzle gameplay is very creative and fun. _childDocuments_.review:
Lightning Rod Games presents A Fold Apart: an award-winning puzzle game that explores the emotional rollercoaster of a long-distance relationship — in a world of folding paper.

Featuring:
- A relatable, true-to-life story of a long-distance relationship.
- Over fifty handcrafted paper folding puzzles.
- Beautiful 3D graphics with a tactile, “homemade” paper aesthetic.
- The ability to choose the couple that best represents you!

After career choices force them along separate paths, a Teacher and Architect vow to make their long-distance relationship work at any cost. Experience both sides of their story as the couple navigates the complexities of (mis)communication and the emotional ups and downs that separation brings. By flipping, folding, and unfolding the paper puzzles in their handcrafted worlds, you can help the couple overcome the emotional barriers of their relationship — but will love endure...?

name: Omen of Sorrow
detailed_description: Monsters of classic horror and mythology clash to take back the night! In a hidden underworld ruled by creatures of the night, a new terror has awakened! Omen of Sorrow brings monsters of horror, literature and mythology together for a fighting game experience unlike any other. Inspired by numerous arcade classics but offering its own unique innovations and mature aesthetics, Omen of Sorrow positively bleeds style! Featuring a roster inspired by such icons as Frankenstein’s monster and Egyptian high priest Imhotep, this traditional 4-button fighting game rewards or punishes players based on how aggressive their playstyle is, putting a skill-centric spin on combat while keeping the experience accessible to newcomers. Powered by Unreal Engine 4, Omen of Sorrow’s 2.5D brawling spans a multitude of detailed locations with handcrafted animations and cinematic finishers, all set to a masterful soundtrack by composer Francisco Cerda. The previously downloadable bloody countess Erzsébet now joins the main roster, alongside a massive blood dragon at her command. With a dozen vicious combatants at your command, who will you lead to victory, and who will fall to your bloodlust? Features: Select from a varied roster of characters inspired by horror classics. Use cinematic finishers to take down opponents in style! Explore single-player modes against the CPU or challenge friends online. Strategize on the fly and turn the tide of battle through aggressive play!

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm I have very mixed opinions on this game..   As of now this game has been on Epic Game Store for about 2 to 3 years.. When it launched it had a story mode.. For whatever reason the devs took it out of the game and said that they would replace it with a better story mode and to just wait.. Well 2 years go by and they rereleased this game on Steam and consoles with a whole bunch of fun things like story mode, arcade endings, improved gameplay and i think more unlocks.  One of the people said it best Epic was the beta testers and Steam got the final version.. As far as I know this game has not been updated for Epic games store, so people who owned the game on that store don't get all this new content and have to buy the game all over again on steam or console to get it again..   Now to the game review.. The graphics are very nice and each character looks cool and unique in their own way.. The fighting system is very cool you have this thing where when you attack and hit the opponent you have a chance to regain health back and so do they so the game encourages you to be very aggressive..   The fighting system is very complex and easy to pick up but hard to master..  The new added story mode and endings to arcade mode is epic and I have been waiting for it for 2 years.. I enjoyed the story mode and am still trying to get all the endings.. The game is really fun for people who like terrordrome 2 or mk games, even fun for people who like darkstallkers and such..  The only thing i think they did that made the game a bit meh compared to epic version is i think they did some things with graphics that made them look a bit more worse then the epic version.. But this is the best version to have by far as it has story modes and bunches of things added.. I would say the game is complete enough now to get it and be happy with what you got.. For the devs i would love to see more dlc characters as well as the supermoves actually killing the opponent on the final hit, maybe some blood spatters out and on the screen and they stop breathing at least..

name: LUNA The Shadow Dust
detailed_description: Buzz "It’s only the start of 2020, but I can see this being a strong contender for Indie Game of the Year! " 5/5 - Rapid Reviews UK "An impeccable soundtrack, challenging gameplay and exciting story ... The game will be another benchmark to the golden rule of visual stories: show, don't tell." 5/5 - Omegascopio, Brazil "A magical point and click. Beautiful cinematics make us go through all the emotions, without letting out an ounce of voice. LUNA The Shadow Dust is quite simply a nugget that we were pleased to discover, and that we can only recommend." 10/10 - coupleofgamer, France "LUNA - The Shadow Dust enchants with great art design, wonderful music and well thought-out puzzles." 85 - 4players, Germany "A small work of art, well-made and compact, flooded with colours and bittersweet feelings. Unfortunately, it doesn't last longer than a Saturday gaming session." 85 - ragequit, Greece "LUNA The Shadow Dust does not reinvent the wheel, but it is a game that I will remember for a long time. Classic gameplay mechanics combined with phenomenal, quite specific graphics make it difficult to tear yourself away from the monitor." 8.5 - gram, Poland About the Game Inspired by the adventure games of old, LUNA The Shadow Dust is a moving tale of two playable companions drawn together in a hand-animated puzzle adventure, featuring a breathtaking original soundtrack and beautiful 2D cinematics. To light a candle is to cast a shadow Behind the shadow of reality, an enchanted world awaits illumination. Experience the magical journey of a young boy and his companion as they solve puzzles and trace back the memories of old, brought to life with visually stunning, wordless cinematics. Enter the ancient tower that stands at the edge of the world and discover the hand-drawn cinematics, intricate puzzles and haunting music of this indie gem. Traditional frame by frame character animation 12 frames per second, 3 layers per frame. Over 250 animations and 20 minutes of cinematics. A nostalgic and time-consuming process - but really worth the challenge for a small indie team of four. Single player mode with dual character control Solve puzzles from different perspectives. Discover a story of true courage with two playable characters drawn together through an inseparable bond. Think outside of the box Spark your imagination and solve a wide variety of puzzles, presented in gorgeous hand-drawn environments. Puzzles work standalone, requiring no 'hidden items' or player backtracking. LESS reading, MORE cinematics We replaced a dialogue system with a series of beautifully hand-animated cinematics telling a mysterious story. Engaging Original Soundtrack Our composer created an original soundtrack, designed to immerse the player in the emotional highs and lows of the story, kindling goose-bumps along the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: (Point & Click Puzzle)Options include separate sliders for music and sound, plus full-screen/windowed.  Cutscenes can be re-watched via the main menu.:As darkness consumes the land, two friends ascend an ancient tower in their quest to restore their world and banish the shadows.There is no journal, nor in fact, any dialogue at all. There didn't seem to be much story at first; just short cutscenes... Until you progress to a point where you're familiar with the characters, and then you'll be presented with a scene that lasts probably 7 minutes.  There are two super-long cutscenes during the game, and luckily, you CAN pause if you need to!  I didn't notice a skip button, but I see on the forums that the dev was going to add that option once you've played it through once.  All told there is nearly 30 minutes of animation to enjoy.:This feels more like an escape-the-room type of puzzle adventure than anything else.  You'll be working with a couple of scenes at a time, and will need to find a way for both of you to progress before you can leave the area.  Each character has their own skills and weaknesses.  For instance, the boy can flip switches and move objects, whilst his companion can enter small spaces and morph into the shadows as if they were as solid as the real world.The puzzles themselves are logical and fun to figure out, although there is specific  that you'll have to remember from early in the game... I played through in multiple sittings, so I had to resort to a walkthrough to get that info.  I recommend , since it explains where the original solution could be found.: There is no way to make your characters move faster, BUT, you can click to get one moving, then swap to the other to get them to move at the same time.Unlocked chapters can be replayed from the main menu, which is super-helpful to get any of the  that you might have missed.:If you're looking for action, this is not for you.  This is a charming point and click game for those who would like to relax for a while.  I really enjoyed my time with LUNA, and hope that these devs put out more games soon!  Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Take an Amanita game, blend the artsy style of GRIS in and give it a room-escape twist: this is what playing  essentially feels like. For me, this was an unforgettable experience: it’s a unique and magical game with an emotional and heartwarming story and an amazing soundtrack. I am a big fan of Amanita games, and  takes the best aspects of their specific style (the way the puzzles are built, charming characters, whimsical machinery with all sorts of cute buttons that do unexpected funny things etc.) and tops them up with with a watercolour hand-painted 2D art and a haunting soundtrack, both reminiscent of GRIS’ unique artistic design. And just like in GRIS, the enchanting story is told without words, through images and an immersive, moving soundtrack, extremely fitting for the game setting. belongs to the point and click genre but at its core, it’s basically an escape-room game. The nameless protagonist (we find out his name from the achievements description - Üri) sets on a spiritual journey to reach the top of the tower that holds the balance of the universe. He starts at the bottom, making his way to the top one room at a time. Each room represents a self-contained puzzle and the locked door that leads to the next room can be opened only if the puzzle is correctly solved. The difficulty remains pretty constant throughout the game (apart from the last puzzle which is substantially more difficult than the others), but just like in Amanita titles, the player often needs to pay attention to details; because of that, the solutions are not always obvious and sometimes one has to  and try unexpected things. Even if the objects that you can interact with are highlighted on mouseover, one needs to trial-and-error a bit in order to understand their logic or how / in which order they need to be combined.Shortly after he starts his journey, the main character meets Layh, a charming animal who instantly develops a strong bond with Üri after he is saved by him. From that point on, the two friends have to join their strengths together in order to solve the tower’s mysteries. Layh is tiny and can crawl into small spaces, but he needs Üri’s help to reach higher areas; Üri on the other hand can push or pull boxes on which Layh can climb; later on, new abilities of these two characters are revealed, but one thing remains constant throughout the game: they will always need to work together. The player controls Üri and Layh separately, one character at a time with the ability to switch between them (by clicking on their portraits or by pressing space), no matter if they’re in different realms or close to each other and they will often have to interact with other adorable animals, like this little fellow here:As it is often the case with tales that are told without words, ’s story leaves a few aspects unexplained and there’s quite a lot of room for speculation. “Why did the boy fall from the sky at the beginning of the game?”, ,  and many others. The secret ending sheds a bit of light on some of these open questions and gives the story a mystic, spiritual connotation, therefore I highly suggest unlocking it (and the extra cutscene that comes with it) after you finish playing the game. The player can go back anytime and revisit any room, therefore triggering this additional ending is extremely easy. is one of the games I would definitely nominate for this year’s Game Awards. It’s a creation of love, beautiful and heartwarming, mysterious and challenging, and it deserves all the credit it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: Superior hand drawn artwork and an award winning sound track make this game memorable. As a puzzle game it proves to be mostly a rewarding experience although the story is a little confusing.   Throughout the game we are treated to some wonderful cut scenes and cinematics culminating in a very dramatic ending.  predominantly is a puzzle game. It does have a story but it is a bit confusing and although the artwork and music was superb it is difficult to tell a story with no words. I think I would need to play this game again in one sitting to understand the story. Even with this confusion onboard, I still felt moved at the conclusion however. The puzzles are very clever and the mechanics are easy to use. Most puzzles only have a few elements to them. It is a game of experimentation. Press that button see what it does; Turn that wheel see what happens; turn on the light etc. then try to piece it altogether. The answers are very logical. Some clues are visual and are hidden in the environment whereas others are associated with light and shadow, and this is a theme we see repeated throughout the game. There are about fifteen rooms of puzzles to tackle. Out of these fifteen, I got stuck on two. One of them took me hours! There is no hint system. If you get stuck you won’t be able to continue. I would urge you to try and try again and don’t give in too easily. These puzzles are well designed and give you a sense of enormous satisfaction when you finally complete them. I wouldn’t say the puzzles were too easy but most of these puzzles are housed in one room with only a few mechanics to try. Sooner or later you will solve the puzzle through experimentation. Further into the game, the puzzles become slightly bigger with more locations and multi layered tasks to complete. The characters are extremely endearing and you would need a heart of stone not to fall in love with them. The boy and dog have to work together to solve puzzles and this creates a bond between them. If you are familiar with puzzle games then this might not prove to be too taxing on the brain. There are a couple of doozies that I would say were difficult but achievable with logical thinking and perseverance. It will take you anywhere between 3-7 hours to complete depending on your expertise (and whether you cheat and look up the answer) so it may appear a little overpriced. There is an obvious amount of effort that has gone into this game and the production value, with its wonderful soundtrack and charming graphics, will certainly impress.  The story is a little confusing. It is very dramatic and the cinematic scenes are awesome, but at times I was wondering what was happening.  and I don’t think they quite managed it unfortunately. The obvious bond between the boy and dog is certainly apparent, and this in itself delivers enough emotion and trepidation to entertain.  The game doesn’t feel disjointed. The puzzles are embedded in the story so it flows nicely and creates suspense as you climb the tower. The game is heavily influenced by the escape room concept. The objective is to find your way out of a locked door in a room. In the room will be various contraptions, levers, buttons, switches etc. which you will need to interact with and ascertain their purpose. There are no red herrings. Every item that you can use will need to be used. It sounds easy, and in some cases, it is, especially early on when we are learning the mechanics. During the story, you meet a companion. An adorable little dog like creature who will help you solve the puzzles. This is when the puzzles start getting more complicated. The dog is small and nimble so he can go through holes and gaps in the environment and appear in other rooms. You will need to work together to get out of the room and both of you must exit for you to proceed. The characters are easily switchable by either pressing space, pressing the character on screen or if off screen, pressing their face in the top right of the screen. It is effortless. Objects that are in the puzzle are highlighted by moving your mouse around the screen. If something can be interacted with, a hand will appear. If something can be entered or jumped upon, a foot will appear. The space bar does not highlight active objects but it is not needed as the rooms feel uncluttered and objects are not hidden. On some of the longer puzzles there is a bit of backtracking to do and even though the rooms are small I would have liked to have seen the character move a bit quicker. Perhaps a double click of the mouse making the boy or dog run would have been welcomed. It is only a slight annoyance and does not prove to be too frustrating however.There is no hint system at all. If you get stuck, you are stuck. I suppose it would be difficult to implement this in fairness. Mostly, puzzles were reasonably straightforward and achieved through experimentation and thought. The puzzles containing light and shadow were the most difficult. The boy can cast a shadow in certain circumstances and the dog can jump on his shadow. Sometimes you need to move the dog between the light and dark to progress. There is a lot of switching characters and lots of layers to the puzzles. The boy can push certain objects which the dog can then interact with. Combine these elements with buttons that turn on lights, switches that move platforms, and mini puzzles then you get the idea. Occasionally, you can interact with mice or other creatures to help you out with puzzles.  The soundtrack is awesome. The cutscene and cinematic choreography is beautiful and you can understand why it was nominated for awards. During the puzzles there are background noises and a catchy tune playing.  The graphics are one of the highlights. Beautiful hand drawn artwork which portrays emotion and drama. It was a brave decision to have a story-based puzzle game with no dialogue whatsoever. Even though the graphics are superb they don’t quite manage to tell the story effectively without voice acting or subtitles.  I was suitably challenged by . The puzzles are clever and well designed and completing them felt satisfying. The graphics and sound are superb but the decision to balance the entire story on visuals alone could prove to be confusing to many. _childDocuments_.review: Luna The Shadow Dust is a point and click puzzle adventure game by Studio Lantern. You play as a boy in a rabbit onesie who comes across a mysterious door on a strange plane. After lighting a lantern above the door, a dark tower appears to you and you go inside. The game sees you travelling up the tower by completing puzzles in each room, by yourself to begin with and then with the help of a small rotund creature. I wasn’t entirely sure what to expect gameplay-wise going into this game, but the best point of comparison is a Amanita Design game, this feels a lot like a combination between Chuchel and Samorost.Luna is undeniably beautiful, and its art is backed up by fairly enjoyable puzzling but its similarities to other properties does detract from its uniqueness. If you appreciate good art, or the genre, I’d say it’s well worth picking up, perhaps not at full price though.If you found this review helpful, please consider following my curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: Luna: The Shadow Dust is a point and click puzzle game in which we control two characters which work together, a boy (Luna) and a weird dog-like creature, to progress up the floors of a mysterious tower with an exotic, gorgeous hand-drawn aesthetic.Each level represents a unique puzzle / escape room set against a beautiful, hand-drawn background. The art is incredibly talented and has amazing detail, with a clever focus on light and shadow play. There was always something small that caught me by surprise, even just looking at the screenshots makes me realize there were small details that I missed. The story is in these details, for you to extrapolate and imagine, for there’s no dialogue or text in the entire game. I’m just utterly charmed by the art from start to finish.The puzzles are logic and detail orientated puzzles, following the tried and tested methods of point and click adventure games. You need to find what you can interact with on the level and then try to work out what you’re supposed to do with it. This is mostly working out what order to do things in and I found it mostly an enjoyable and relaxing experience. Not too taxing, but with enough thought involved that I felt satisfied every time I completed a level.The developers have tried to tell a full story without using any words at all, through dramatic music, twenty minutes of cinematic cutscenes, and these beautiful tower levels. Whilst I think it all looks utterly amazing, I didn’t feel much cohesion or driving drama in terms of the story. As someone who really likes words, I honestly think that a narrator would have improved Luna: The Shadow Dust. The wordless story is a design choice that the developers fully committed to, an interesting concept that wasn’t quite there for me.Even without really knowing, or caring much about why I was traversing the tower, it was still an awesome and enjoyable journey, so Luna: The Shadow Dust gets a big thumbs up from me.Note I received a review copy through Curator Connect. _childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful and magical journey. Charming, fantastic artwork, too, which is the game's forte. The accompanied musical scores are delightful and fitting to its fantasy theme. The background story somehow brought a few drops of confusing tears at the end, perhaps thanks to the emotional tune and the ever-touching act of love. The major issue here is the gameplay which demands you finish too many tedious a task in order to complete the puzzles. You climb the stool, climb the ladder, push the box, and repeat some or many of those again. About 20% puzzle and the remaining 80% walking around. When a puzzle was finished and I advanced to the next level, I thought to myself, was that it, that's all there is to the puzzle? And admittedly I felt horrid thinking so since the game is downright gorgeous. There is for me the relaxing, immersive playing pace, but this game didn't hit within that range. If you are drawn to the game's artistic beauty and don't really mind anything else, then go ahead. But I don't think I can really recommend this to any of my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it, maybe even dropped a few tears near the end, although I admittedly did not understand the story as the game mostly focuses on visual storytelling. It's a point&click puzzle game, not to be confused with adventure games - there is practically little to no exploration aside from a couple of creative achievements. I think it took me around 3 hours to finish without any help, so it might be a lot shorter depending on your speed. Now I didn't get stumbled or anything, which is relatively surprising because the puzzles were very creative, I can see someone having issues with the logical interpretation. To be fair, most of the puzzles had an obvious solution, or at least it becomes obvious after you solve them, there was only one that I don't fully agree with. Ultimately you probably buying this game to see some hand-drawn animation, and it had a decent amount of cute cutscenes between the gaps.I did not run into any glitches, so I can't speak for whatever is going on with other players. I will say that targeting and visual indications could have been better. For example, you can push or climb on the box, I think that could use better icons, additionally, I had a hard time rolling the circles in the clocktower because I could not stop them when I wanted. Some of the puzzles allow you to play with them after you already beat them, that can be a little confusing because you assume they still have a purpose.  There were parts of the game that I felt were very slow for some reason, I guess they were trying to build atmosphere, but in this case, it did not work for me just because nothing was happening. Minor criticism aside, I do think the game excels in terms of creative puzzles, I really liked the time-travelling segments and utilizing of shadows. + very creative puzzles+ hand-drawn cutscenes, adorable visuals+ some cool achievements  - these gave me the most problems, if the puzzle is solved, I should not be able to play with it because I end up the second-guessing myself when looking for solution (mostly clocktower). I know a few of them have achievements, so once you get those, the puzzle should become disabled.  - there were many small issues with spacing, not being exactly on point to interact. You can also make nice little icons for things like climbing up so you can tell the difference between walking and interacting. On that note, having the hand icon over the character kinda confused me because I often felt like there was something around me I could pick up, but it was just telling me that I could select the character. For me the creative puzzles were the highlight of this experience, I thought the story would be the most interesting but as I said, I am not exactly sure what happened. Considering the price of the game, I would expect the gameplay to be more polished - there is room for improvement. But as expected, the animation was very cute and I ultimately don't regret playing through it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Even with a few obvious roughnesses, mainly related to some gameplay decisions, «LUNA The Shadow Dust» leaves a very warm and pleasant feeling. I would not call this game a purebred point-and-click adventure, it is rather a puzzle game that rotates around the axis of a very good plot. If you try to somehow describe the universe of the game, then everything in it literally speaks of love for the "Little Prince" by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, where space-scale adventures are combined with incredible humanism and vivid emotions. The adventures of our little hero, at some point finding a strange furry friend, unfold in a giant tower, each floor of which is fraught with new secrets. And why I was inclined specifically to the puzzle belonging to the game, each floor is a separate puzzle that needs to be solved. There is no inventory in the game, so everything is tied to the mechanics and logic of behavior in a particular area, and there are no problems with a variety of puzzles. Riddles with shadows, puzzles with mandatory teamwork, riddles for memory and many others. The level of difficulty of riddles is quite normal, there are no particularly hardcore things, but you will have to sweat a few. And if you remember that there is not a single word in the game, then to solve puzzles you have to turn on intuition.The pace here is quite slow... Ah, about the unhurried pace and I want to say how about one of the few big drawbacks of the game. The fact is that the heroes walk unusually slowly, and if you are greeted by a big puzzle or a riddle to several rooms where you have to move a lot, then you begin to suffer. I guess that the lack of running was done in order not to ruin the measured and comfortable gaming experience, but it can always be done with a double click, for example, so that the player himself can choose his own rhythm. This is a completely non-critical remark, but it begins to be felt very quickly when you move along the plot, probably starting with a puzzle in the kitchen. Some may find the game quite childish because of the plot, although I really liked its presentation and mood.The game looks and sounds absolutely incredible. As I wrote above, there is not a single word in the game, so it’s very important to use the rest of the dramatic art tools here, which the creators do great. Hand-drawn locations breathe life, they are all unique and create the feeling of a real fabulous adventure. The videos are almost full-length cartoons with incredible animation and elaboration of scenes. The only very small drawback I would call is that in the opponents we again have the Terrible Shadows, which look like pterodactyls, but this is a trifle. I honestly admit that I completely immersed myself in this game, with great pleasure going through the adventures of two friends. My heart is always pleased with such sincere good adventures that can touch something inside you, I hope that there will be more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I liked everything about this game BUT the puzzles! lol I agree with other reviews saying that the character moves too slowly and that the puzzles involve a LOT of repetition of the same action to be completed (the thorn being a notorious example). Overall, the game was beautiful enough to motivate me to unlock all achievements, but the puzzle-play experience could definitely be improved. With all that said, I'd recommend this game when on sale!
