_childDocuments_.review: If LUNA The Shadow Dust would have been priced at around 5-10 euros, this would have been a much easier game for me to recommend. As it stands, I can't justify spending 20 euros while there are much more enjoyable adventure/puzzle games in the same or even lower price range. Games that I ended  up enjoying heaps more than I enjoyed LUNA. First the good: the game looks great, although the animations can be a bit choppy. That didn't bother me because it somehow adds to the games charm. I loved the use of colors and I especially liked the soundtrack that had some wonderfully enchanting moments (especially near the ending where it made me think of the Ori games). What I really didn't enjoy were the meaningless puzzles. Most of them were incredibly easy to figure out but still took a LOT of time to solve, running around in circles to throw switches and push blocks. Some of them were quite frustrating in its execution and took WAY too long to solve, because I had to repeat or reset certain cycles again and again or switch between the two characters to solve the different steps of a puzzle. I never felt that I was figuring things out, or exploring a cool setting, but I was instead forced to do menial tasks to get to the next chapter. Meanwhile, the two characters move at a snails pace, only adding to the frustration. And then there is the games length. I managed to solve the game in three hours (even with the characters moving so slow). I don't believe how much time you need to beat a game is really important (I love shorter games!) but overall LUNA I just felt like a bad deal to me. I considered getting a refund when I was nearing the 2 hour mark but I do believe the developers can do better. With some better pacing and more interesting puzzles LUNA could be a great game. But it is really not at the moment. 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: +Story, quite an accomplishment considering there is no dialogue!+Atmosphere+Graphics, breathtaking+Musical ScoreThis is a very polished Point and Click game. It is eye-candy, surreal at times, and is backed by a heartwarming story. Who would have thought that a game with no dialogue could move you to tears? There are a few scenes where your eyes won't know where to look first. When you first began playing, you may not know why you are doing what you are doing; you won't care; the game carries you away that much. The game will prompt you on how to play.Sometimes you play a game that is so beautiful you want to sit back and just watch for a while; this is one of those gamesIt’s hard to write this without giving you a spoiler but:Puzzles: This is the heart of the game. You and your companion will solve several puzzles on your journey. They are smart well thought out puzzles that require thinking outside the box. Once you realize how versatile your characters and environments are you will get the hang of it. There are many visual clues for puzzle solutions in the game. Look at the walls, look at everything. Part of the fun in the game is figuring out what the puzzle is; the prompts will help you along. Some of the puzzles are challenging. Actual play time, thus far, is six - seven hours, which includes replaying one chapter. Due to a mouse issue I've left the final puzzle undone. This review will be updated when the game is completed. Purchased games on the release date has become dicey. So many must be patched and patched again. This game must have been well tested, it ran perfectly.  No game crashes, lock ups, no errors were encountered.LUNA is family friendly. It would be too difficult for most elementary age children to play alone but is a great game to play together.In the menu options you have the regular audio and video features, plus, the ability to replay animations; there is also a chapter selection feature. Thank you so much for this devs!The characters do not quickly zip round; you need to be patient and enjoy, not speed-run the game.LUNA uses an auto-save function that allows you to continue playing the level from where you left off.Excellent job Devs!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Even without its serene music and sharp visual design, LUNA would still be a decent point & click adventure game. It strips down to the basics of the genre by culling traditional storytelling and replacing it with voiceless cutscenes and painted murals. With no inventory and minimal backtracking, it puts emphasis on the raw puzzles that use two characters with complementary skills. While the initial challenges are easy, the later ones are clever because they split up the characters in interesting ways. If you are keen to return to the genre but daunted by the prospect, LUNA The Shadow Dust is a good way to get your foot in the door.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Voltaire* I’ve never been a big fan of point & click games, and to be fair I don’t think that I will ever become one of them. attracted me with its incredible picture: warm colours and the locations which I just wanted to observe, not play. I honestly think that this game has one of the most beautiful settings I’ve ever seen. I can talk and talk of how the graphics are incredibly beautiful. However that is only the picture, I don't want to play a game only for its landscapes. I need something more.Despite the visuals, something called a game, should have something else to play for. Unfortunately, the game doesn’t provide anything except that. In total, I completed the game in about 4 hours, but to complete the four-hour game took me about two weeks. The reason for such a long play through of such a short game is to what degree the game is wonderful visually to the same degree is exceptionally boring. I was frustrated all the time while I was playing the game. The characters move very slowly. That affects the puzzles solving: it takes tons of time when one character would move from one side of the screen to another to press a button (or a lever for a change) and then back again. And that’s the only game mechanic of solving the puzzles. The same repeatable actions all the time made me really exhausted so I couldn’t tolerate more than 1-2 levels at one go. I would play the game even less per day but there is no in-level saving option – the game saves only between levels. But there is a possibility to replay single levels to get some missed cheevos, which is great because I don’t think that I would ever want to replay the game again.One of the features of the game is the lack of voice acting. It is something unusual and unique but in terms of this game the feature doesn’t help much – it only made the game experience even more exhausting and tiresome. There are only terribly long cut scenes which show what is going on here but for me they were really hard to follow. In addition, there are no subtitles or notes or basically anything which could help to understand or to remind me (especially after such breaks of playing the game) what is the point of the game.Yes, I understand that support of independent indie developers is important. I’m not diminishing their visuals and the amount of the work done but I believe the price for the game is exceptionally high for such little and not that enjoyable experience. I really recommend the game for its visuals and highly discourage buying the game for the full price for the rest of  dimensions and for people who are not interested in the games where visuals predominate the gaming pleasure.*Uolsh, I. A. (1984)  Russian-English Dictionary of Winged Words. University of Michigan, p. 54.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like good art, this is the game for you... unless you actually also want a game. The characters move laboriously, which is made worse by the amount of times they have to push a block from one side of the screen to the other and back. The puzzles rely on repeating actions in the correct sequence: make a mistake and you have to start over. Each of these actions comes with its own animation, which fills a few seconds and thus pads the playing time even more. The whole game is a series of escape rooms, with one puzzle to solve in each room to open the door, so all in all, it's repetition upon slow repetition. Might be worth it if you have a couple of weeks to kill, a lot of patience and you get it in a 50% off sale.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: "There can´t be light without shadow"A statement so plain and yet so insightful that represents the whole atmosphere in LUNA The Shadow Dust. Melancholy and an unfamiliar sensation of nostalgia overcame me while playing and especially finishing the last part of this game. It sounds paradoxical, since there is nothing to be nostalgic about and yet there is this certain feeling which tries to bring back unknown, nonexistent memories from my past. The story is as deep as you want it to be and as shallow as your imagination can allow. If you are not willing to invest yourself in it, then a disappointment is inevitable. There are no dialogues or monologues that would spoon-feed you the story. And even though the art and the animations are one of the cutest, best out there, I could totally see how the somewhat stale gameplay could ruin the experience for some impatient folks. Most puzzles are well made and despite their low difficulty, its accomplishment feels rewarding. I rather enjoy an easy but solid puzzle than one that leads to frustration and eventually a drop out from the immersion and the game itself. In the end, whether this game is for you or not, depends on how much you are willing to immerse yourself and sympathize with the characters, their bond and the overall universe and its almost philosophical dilemma. You should take it slow and be patient throughout the game. I recommend it for everyone who can turn a blind eye to relatively easy puzzles but instead focus on the world itself and its myths.

_childDocuments_.review: + Great art and music- Puzzles lack any sort of depth- Overly tedious puzzle designLUNA is a game that shows that you don't need high production values or even dialogue to tell a story. It's a simple point and click adventure about a young boy and his animal companion, with a brilliant art style and soundtrack to accompany it. The result is a very aesthetically-pleasing game. However, it doesn't necessarily do this without sacrificing a lot in return.As a fan of the genre, I have to say that I am disappointed. LUNA is a fantastic-looking game with some great music. However, it pairs this with puzzles that not only lack depth, but are overly tedious in their design. The result is gameplay that just feels like a cycle of chores to complete until the credits roll, hardly something you'd want out of a point and click adventure. The story, while decent, isn't enough to warrant slogging through such gameplay, so you're better off looking elsewhere.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: LUNA The Shadow Dust is a point-and-click puzzle game presented in a completely hand-animated visual style. We take on the role of a boy, and after a few minutes into the game, we also have a small and funny-looking pet companion join us. We need to use them both to solve puzzles ahead. Each puzzle we solve, we ascend higher along the large tower. We're not given a backstory at the beginning, but it gradually starts to unravel over the course of the game. There is a sense of mystery at all times about what's going on. It’s a small story revolving only around a handful of characters. There is no dialogue spoken throughout the whole game. Everything is shown with actions and character emotions. The story, however, mainly takes the backseat and allows the gameplay to lead.We go through the tower stage by stage, with each one being a unique puzzle that we must solve. There are no items to collect in order to use later, and there are no special abilities for us to remember to use. Every puzzle can be solved right there and then by studying the environment, doing some experimentation to see how everything works, and then to formulate and execute a solution. Most of the puzzles were pretty fun, fresh, and unique. Some of them were multi-stepped even and had different stages, where solving one part of it then led to another. Perhaps the thing that really stands out when it comes to puzzle-solving in this game is that we have to make use of both characters in order to solve the puzzles, as they interact with the environment differently. The boy is able to press buttons and pull levers, as well as push some objects around the room, while the pet companion is able to do platforming on various objects, including the shadows. This means we have to alternate between them when executing a solution.This game has an outstanding visual style. Its characters, environments, colours, and story cutscenes are all beautifully crafted. The music conveys the emotion of each scene and area in place of any dialogue and it does it very clearly. It's a well-polished game and the devs have put a lot of passion into it.Overall it's a fun and well-presented game. Its only drawback is the short length (it took me just over 4 hours to go through it, but it might vary depending on how fast you go through the puzzles). The puzzles all feel fresh and different from one another, so there's no filler content, but I think a bit more game time on the story could've been good or some additions to the gameplay that could make the second and other playthroughs different to the first.For the full review and a short gameplay video, check here:

_childDocuments_.review: A short, poignant, wordless tale wrapped in a series of clever room-based puzzles.Pros:* Beautiful music* Intelligent puzzles* The later puzzles , likely, make you scratch your head where to even start.* Except for the 1st few (and the very last), each room takes ~15-30 min to solve.  Great for a quick distraction.Cons:* Short - 3 hrs, for me.Meh:* Can't save mid-room - if you have to quit the game, you'll have to restart the current room.* Start menu is mystery-meat icons - they make sense after you click them, but expect no explanations.TL;DR: If you like puzzles and wordless tales, 8/10 (due to length); else, avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Luna The Shadow Dust is a lovely spinning of a fairy tale into a game. The art, both in-game and in cutscenes, is beautiful and detailed. The story was carefully crafted to work with no dialog. The music is whimsical and soothing. The game took me a little over three hours, which I think was a good amount of time for the story and gameplay. Some of the puzzles were fairly challenging, but most had consistent logic. There was only one puzzle (room 9) involving a mechanic I did not know how to trigger that I looked up.My only complaints didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game. The controls are a little bit awkward. The movement speed is slow and some actions take more work than I think they should (for example, getting down from a platform and walking around requires one action to jump down from the platform, and another one to walk around). The developers mentioned in a post release update that they are working on improving these issues.I do like that it is possible to visit each room individually after it has been completed, especially since there are some achievements that I missed during my first playthrough.This is a perfect game to play during a weekend. I finished my first playthrough in a single day, and it was a sweet and relaxing way to play the game. I played it on Steam on my computer, but Switch might be the better choice, just because it would have been perfect to play in bed.

_childDocuments_.review: I entered the game anticipating more of a conventional point-and-click adventure in the inventory management manner, but what I experienced was special. You’ll be asking yourself “what or WHO is Luna and what, exactly, is shadow dust? And why am I climbing this tower anyway?” while being consistently rewarded with enjoyable puzzles and cutscenes. Did I mention how beautiful this game is? Everything in the game is lovingly hand drawn and you can tell. This includes over 20 minutes of actually animated cutscenes. The graphical style of a game is usually a secondary factor for me when it comes to video games and yet the artwork is fantastic in Luna: The Shadow Dust.  The artwork creates a truly immersive world and characters that you want to explore.The absence of any spoken or written words throughout the entirety of Luna The Shadow Dust is one of its distinctive features. Instead, the locales and characters in the game themselves tell the story. This is an intriguing method of delivering the story since while some video games rely heavily on ambiance to tell their tales, I don't think I've ever played one that does so completely. Due to this reason your enjoyment of the story is going to depend on how close you pay attention to your surroundings. The game isn’t going to outright tell you what is going on. Instead you will get a lot of the story from looking at various paintings and other objects you find in the background. If you’re a fan of point-and-click adventure games, but want something more focused on puzzle solving and storytelling, then absolutely. Just throw your money at it. There’s no inventory management, mindless backtracking, or obtuse progression gating here, and honestly, I’m not sure if I’d classify Luna: The Shadow Dust as a point-and-click first and foremost. It’s more of a puzzle adventure game since you have direct control over the two characters, only pointing and clicking to interact with objects in the environment. The game may not revolutionize the genre as it plays like your typical point and click game. Despite that, it creates a really engaging game. The puzzle design in the game is fantastic. The puzzles are well crafted and the solutions are quite clever leaving you with a sense of accomplishment. Supporting the puzzle design is the overall atmosphere which is fantastic. The game utilizes a hand drawn style that feels like playing a game inside an animated movie. The story is mostly told through the environment but it creates a visually stunning world that you want to fully explore.Overall, Luna: The Shadow Dust checked off a lot of my personal boxes and I thoroughly enjoyed the five hours it took me to finish. I’m not sure I’ll go back and play it again since the big story reveals would lose their impact and the puzzle solutions would likely remain in the back of my mind, but even for a game I’ll only play once, I can still highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited about playing this game, because of the stunning artwork and because I love point-and-click games. But I'm very disappointed with it. The art is amazing, but that's about it. The puzzles are boring and tedious. Finding the solutions is relatively easy, but the execution of those solutions involves so many repetitive actions and everything moves incredibly slow. The story is forgettable. I can't bring myself to finish the game, getting through the puzzles feels like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Ever had those days where you want to distract yourself with an evocative setting but not burden your mind with overly complex narrative and mechanics? Chances are you're looking for a game like Luna.The best comparison I can think of for what kind of game it is is a 2D Myst or Riven - just like in Cyan's acclaimed work, Luna is an inventory-less point-and-click where the puzzles are unfamiliar mechanisms that you must figure out the workings of. Except in this case you don't have to look around for someone's text-heavy journal - the puzzle is self-contained in a room and you figure it out by interacting with it. Figure out one mechanism, and it's onto the next self-contained room. Each one telling a small story with its intricate contents and serene music. The collage of puzzle rooms is tied together with an overarching story, told through the various murals and inscriptions you find, as well as cutscenes.The combined result is roughly 4 hours of taking in the game's atmosphere and visuals whilst learning the workings of a multitude of puzzles. (Or more, depending on how quickly you grasp those puzzles) Depending on your tastes, that length might be a bad thing, or a good thing. My suggestion is watch footage of the game's demo and see if it's the kind of short experience you're willing to pay full price for.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has gorgeous aesthetics, but the actual puzzles are a mixed bag.How long it takes various animations and transitions to play out makes figuring the puzzles out more frustrating than I think they should be, so that when the solution is a bit obscure and requires some back-and-forth to figure out it becomes very tedious.If you can deal with that, and really like pretty hand-drawn graphics and an emotional soundtrack, I think it's worth trying out, but it's not an easy recommendation because of the frustrations.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: In two words: absolutelly lovely.It's a short adventure and puzzle game, and every minute is worth it - from the work that went into the graphics to the music. On every level I was amazed by the - hand drawn - illustrations.The level of detail and care on this game shows how much love and creativity went into it - this game is an interactive work of art.You start out with very simple puzzles, and slowly grow into more complex ones.Controls are simple, so gameplay is quite easy - there is no inventory involved, just clicks, pushes, moves, jumps. Every level is mostly independent from the previous and the next one, but some levels have multiple rooms.I see this game as fitting for all ages - well, maybe with some adult help on the later level for the younger players.It's a refreshing game, a calming break from all the action packed stressful games on the market.The full price (€19.99) may seem a bit high considering it was a 4 hour experience for me, but those were some very enjoyable 4 hours.Recommend to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: From a completely visual standpoint: This is an absolutely gorgeous game with a beautiful soundtrack that makes you feel like you are traversing through a children's book. The artwork and animations where 100% what drew me to buy the game to begin with.Unfortunately from a game play standpoint, the puzzles are very bland. The most challenging aspect about a few of them is how tedious it is to do certain repetitive tasks again and again with characters that move very slowly. I never really had a moment where I felt accomplished, clever, or pleased with myself after finishing a puzzle. Mostly I would finish puzzles and feel surprised that was all there was.It's a shame, because the art made me want to like it so much, but the gameplay's tedium frustrated me enough that I decided to stop.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I played through this game within 5 hours. Its way to easy. The most difficult part  was most of the time to figure out, what the game wants from me and not how to do it. It took me a while to realise the little cat could melt within the shadows. I bought it to play a puzzle game, but I prefer a game, where I need to figure out how to do something and not what to do, because there are no words in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly relaxing little point-and-click.  I really loved it.  Fun to do, not too long, casual, nice visual style, love the handdrawn, cartoonish feel. Nice to have the two characters who can do things together, and cooperate on the same problem while in different places. And no dialogue is very restful. Music is good too (though I mostly play games with volume off or down low). Some minor drawbacks in my view: I'm a raw beginner in games, and found some of the puzzles a bit too subtle. Like I'd get the main thrust of the problem and solution, but then something had to be done in a very specific order, or tweaked just so, or there was some really subtle visual clue a while back. So had to resort to guide help a bit. One room required fast and precise platforming, which I'm really bad at and found frustrating. The cutscenes are long. No manual saves means a bit of backtracking if you quit a room before solving everything and unlocking the exitdoor. Some parts a little bit scary so maybe not for the smallest children.

Can you at least warn a person or something next time? I spent twenty minutes today trying to calm down a five-year-old who was crying unconsolably at the end :(The game was pretty great until the last few minutes.Apparently Steam won't let me post a review without giving it a thumbs up/thumbs down... I'd still recommend this game but maybe don't repeat my mistake and use it as a family bonding time.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: - A lovely puzzle game where you climb a tower with your animal companion, solving puzzles in each room to progress further while learing the reason you are there. While we have seen the premise before, it's done in a very good way where artstyle, music and gameplay flows together creating one of the better puzzle adventures i played in a while.   - Story is told entirely wordless throughout cutscenes and backgrounds. Not the most creative or unique story, but it doesn't matter in the end and isn't that important a part of the package.  - There are a lot of different puzzles that use a wide variety of styles and problems but they are not especially hard, and you will be able to figure them out if you just pay attention.  - Absolutely lovely, with a handdrawn animated movie look and feel.   - Great dreamy soundtrack. Fits the artstyle very well  - Fairly easy 100%. No achievements are missable, you will be able to go back to a scene and replay it without erasing your overall progress. One of them is a chore, you will need a spreadsheet or follow a guide to be able to do it in a resonable time. A great puzzle game with stellar artstyle, aesthetics and sound design. One of the strongest in it's genre in the last couple of years.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I said 'yes' to the recommendation, but really it should be a 'maybe'. This game cost £15 and I only got 5 hours of game play out of it. It didn't feel like it was worth the money.Positives:  The art is pretty nice, although I am not in love with the styleThe puzzles are good - just challenging enough most of the time. They put a lot of thought into them which is refreshing and the puzzles themselves feel artistic.The music is lovely and sets a nice atmosphere.The game play is entertaining and I like the extra challenge of two characters.Negatives:I didn't follow the story completely. There were a lot of long cut scenes and I wasn't entirely sure what was going on. I got the gist of it, but not enough to be invested in the story.Some of the puzzles were too challenging. It pushed me past the 'okay, what am I missing?' stage to the 'Seriously I have tried everything and I don't understand what you want from me?!!!'The character walks slowly so a portion of the game play is just watching them amble across the screen.The last puzzle was disappointingly simple and very anti climatic.Overall the game is worth a try, but the story wasn't engaging (because I didn't understand it or it wasn't strong enough) and it felt short. However the puzzles are good and the soundtrack is relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: LUNA The Shadow Dust is a point and click puzzle game that took me by surprise by how amazing the artwork and animation look. It is very reminiscent of older anime as well as the classic Studio Ghibli look. It being point and click in nature may be a turn off to those who want direct control over their characters or faster movement speed in games.That element aside, the gameplay itself is pretty straightforward and well done. You are climbing a tower room by room and slowly recovering your memories. Each room has a different puzzle to solve before you can exit. As you climb the tower, you gain a very adorable cat like creature as a side kick and you can alternate between the two. The puzzle solving elements are interspersed with adorably animated cut scenes.The puzzles are not difficult to solve and most are presented in a manner where you can quickly figure out most of them at a glance. It took me around 6 hours to beat the game and around 2 more hours to obtain all the achievements. The Master Chef achievement is the most tedious achievement in the game as it is very time consuming and can be difficult to figure out the requirements.Overall, LUNA The Shadow Dust is a very solid point and click puzzle game wrapped in amazing artwork and a solid sound track.Video Preview: Additional Info:Game Received for FreeGame Playthrough: CompletedTime Played: 8 HoursAchievements: 24/24Achievement Difficulty: Moderate (Master Chef achievement is time consuming)Recommended For: Fans of point and click puzzle games, 2D animation

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: While I did not buy this game at the Steam Store, I did pay for it through Kickstarter.I've been following this game since its Kickstarter campaign of 2016. While development was slow and there were numerous struggles, the developers never failed to keep us updated and in the end they came through with this neat, little, handpainted gem. I seriously regret not pledging 15 pounds, which would have gotten me the soundtrack too. Oh well ^ w^This game is short, slow-paced and overall not too challenging, which makes it a great play for a rainy Sunday afternoon (or any day / weather condition when you feel like spending about 4 hours on a game). The music is nice and relaxing, the visuals are absolutely stunning and there's not a lot going on.Or is there?On the surface this may seem like a simple puzzle game, going from room to room, solving puzzles to progress, but it's far more than that. This game manages to convey a story without a single spoken word, which means that you can enjoy this game no matter where you're from! All story elements are conveyed through cutscenes and scenery, all painted by hand and it shows.Let's move on to pros and cons:+Very pretty artstyle that is very easy on the eyes (not too dark, and certainly not too bright).+"Simple" puzzles where the solution is a journey of its own.+A nice and relaxing soundtrack.+A super adorable fluffy sidekick, with the power to merge with the shadows!+You can replay a room as many times as you like. Just return to the main menu and click the Book icon.+Not heavy on my (old, non-gaming) PC's processor!+24 Achievements which are easy to get (I only looked up four of them, one of which I could have figured out on my own)-The game is a little short. I would not have minded if the game was longer.-While the shadow-merging mechanic was fun, I think I would have liked it if it was used more.-The characters move slowly, which fits the pace of the game nicely, but in some areas it would have been nice to have a run option.-In some puzzles the solution is a little repetitive.~Minor nitpick: Due to the game not having any dialogue or readable written words, I cannot for the life of me remember the names of the characters. It doesn't really help they're not the easiest to remember. Couldn't help but stick to Finn for the boy... That is really more a shame-on-me than a shame-on-the-devs.Overall I can really recommend this game. The cons are definitely not severe enough to not enjoy the game anymore. It doesn't even really bother me ^^Thank you for reading my review, I hope it was helpful to you!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: LUNA The Shadow Dust was a game that had me hooked from the START. Do you like cozy games? Do you like cute art? Do you like thinking ( a little bit)? This game hits all of those. The art and music is just so, so good. The storyline is beautifully tied together at the end as well, so if you like all of those things: this game is meant for you. The puzzles are simple yet thought provoking, a couple of them definitely stumped me so I had to think abstract and outside the box which is really what makes a game for me. I loved how the puzzles were designed and though I said simple, I didn't say easy. You definitely need to use your brain which I really like. The game had it's challenges yet overall was super relaxing and fun, I had a smile the whole time I played!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: It's very short. It could so easily have been twice as long and not lost any of its momentum or appeal. It fleshes out a lot of its time with animated interstitials telling a story, which is a simple but effective and emotional one. The puzzles are straightforward, and sometimes too simple, but have a lot of variety in how to apply their solutions. The art is beautiful, and very evocative. I recommend it, but I would have preferred more: more story; more puzzles; more difficulty; more variety.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game.LUNA is a point-and-click puzzle game.  It's not a standard inventory-based adventure game; it is more a series of rooms which are all self-contained puzzles.The hand-drawn style gives the whole experience a very cinematic feel that has stuck with me long after the credits have rolled.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful - absolutely stunning! Hand drawn artwork and an original sound track to go along with it. Both were just lovely to listen to. It had a very Samorost 3 feel to it - which was brilliant. Each level represents a new puzzle to complete - the puzzles aren't overly hard - enjoyable. The story was beautiful - the secret ending even more so! There is no dialogue - but you could understand everything the game was trying to say - very impressive! I had NO idea what the goal was, or what I was aiming for -- but it honestly didn't matter - it was very well designed!! My advice would be to play the game slowly and just enjoy. Good note for achievement hunters is that if you miss one during the play through (I recommend just playing through and enjoying the experience) you can choose the level you need to get the achievement in without playing through the entire game again. Would definitely buy if I hadn't received a Review Key :) At time of review, two achievements were borked - but devs acknowledged and are working on a fix :) VERY interactive team! Thank you..
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly a big disappointment.Yes, the art style and the soundtrack are amazing and beautiful, the characters are nice and you like them on first sight. But the gameplay is absolutely horrible: just boring in every imaginable way.The characters move awfully slow; you see the solution of a puzzle, but to solve it, you have to wait and watch as the pcs take their time to move - seemingly forever.The real problem for me are the "puzzles" - if I was a child under 10 years, I perhaps would really love them, because they are not too hard; but for me as a grown up, who has played lots of puzzle and escape the room games, these not in any way innovative puzzles are just annoying. So I lost interest in this game after about half an hour and hope to get a refund. Possibly the difficulty is increasing etc. but it also is a task for the devs to get you hooked in the first minutes. And that didn't work for me. I have no interest what so ever to find out, where this game leads. Normally in cases like that I would at least go to youtube and watch, what happens in the end. But here I'm not even interested in that.So, I think this game is perfect for kids, not for teenies: for kids. Or for people, who really like a very slow relaxing game with no pressure at all. To others, like me, who were blinded by the style: stay away, you'll regret it, if you buy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Luna is a beautiful game! Absolutely one of the best-animated games out there. There are so many small details to view throughout. I also love when bright colors are introduced to balance out the somber lighting. It's dazzling!This game is more about solving puzzle rooms and following a linear path up a tower. This provides a ton of variety because each puzzle room is so unique. They cover all kinds of ideas from music puzzles to aligning images. But each room stands alone so there's no carryover between them with something like items. Luna has relaxed gameplay, and you can take as long as you want to solve a puzzle.Made a video if that's your thing,

Some puzzles are easy and some puzzles will take a bit before you will understand what you have to do. The animations are cute and the artstyle is really well done. The music is very atmospheric. _childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really did.And there is much to like. The art and animation is excellent. The music is soothing and works very well with the visuals of the game.But the game itself is frustrating. Not because the puzzles are difficult, but because they are often quite boring to solve. Many of them require you to repeat actions over and over, and many of those actions are often slow. And if you're trying to figure something out the frustration will grow even worse as you're forced to watch slow (but beautifully made) animations play out time and time again.The story, such as it is, is fairly interesting, but lacks the emotional weight it tries to deliver since the game is quite short. And for such a short game it relies quite heavily on cutscenes, which I found surprising.All in all I was unfortunately disappointed with LUNA The Shadow Dust. It's a good looking game, but it's all surface.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles in this game are very easy, and it purposefully makes you move slowly. I tried to get into that, to feel the vibe, but I never could make it. The cut scenes were very long, especially at the end. If you're a fan of puzzle games, like Myst, I'd skip this one. If you like little cartoons that try to tug at your heart strings and you want an easy challenge, give it a try. It wasn't for me.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a review that criticized the simplicity of the puzzles, but I think that it matches the overall theme. The game does bank heavily on its graphics and music, but the use of the two characters is often ingenious and a feature of adventure games that's often underused. Like many recent adventure games, there is no inventory. I wonder if having one might not have made a deeper experience, but it would have been a radical change.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A really lovely short and sweet experience.  I fell in love with the art style back when it was a Kickstarter and I'm so happy to see what it became.  No puzzles were too challenging, but all unique and clever, and each area and character was stunningly animated and designed with so much care.  Absolutely recommend this game, it's a wonderful example of a small team creating something they loved just for all of us.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a beautiful design, but finale wasn't fair, because they didn't give the answer in some place before to solve the puzzle.The soundtrack is awesome too, but the story was poor.I remembered Dark Tower at the end, seems like a copy.But even there, it was not satisfied for me.Sorry guys, this game is not worth the price it has.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This game was less than 3 hours and all the puzzles were fairly simple except maybe two. Some of the puzzles, you would figure out, and then need to tediously hit the same buttons to rotate/change things with annoying animations. _childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, This is a good game that gives me Ghibli nostalgia and does not overstays its welcome. Positives:1. The art work has a story book quality to them and are amazingly hand drawn.2. The music is excellently composed which is a great asset to any puzzle game.3. The puzzles are not the most difficult in the world but they are well thought out and avoid pixel finding like some of the other games in the genre does quite often.Negatives:1. The control does take some time to get used to when the 2nd character is introduced as you will need to control both of them separately.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This game is along the same lines of games like Machinarium - simple point and click to solve the puzzles. However, it has a wonderful dynamic of dual control, so you have some really interesting puzzles to solve. A couple are a little tedious as is always the way, but the art is lovely and it was captivating enough that I played it all in one sitting.My only real issue with is was the cut scenes - they were long and you couldn't skip them. Frankly, I found them a little odd and unnecessary.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork for this game is really beautiful - so beautiful that my first impression was that it's a shame there's not more to do in each scene. For the artwork alone I would recommend it... but I gotta say the cut scenes really killed the vibe... it seems like there's a lot of interesting mythical backstory here, but it's sort of only hinted at. The main story, revealed in cut scenes is... meh. The music for the most part is nice, but there are points where the synth strings are just cloying.I'd like to recommend, but I probably won't play this game again. I just kind of felt annoyed at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: My goodness, the art in this game is lovely! The pace slows you down and really makes you appreciate the details. This is fine when you are correctly solving puzzles but a bit more challenging when you struggling through and not quite getting it. However, there is only one puzzle in the game that was complex enough that the pacing became frustrating. I am glad I spent the time I did with this story and world.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful Point-and-Click puzzle game with gorgeous hand drawn visuals, an enchanting soundtrack and an emphasis on light and shadow puzzles.Luna The Shadow Dust has a storybook feel throughout, helped handily by the visuals and soundtrack. The story follows Uri and his companion Layh as they climb the Tower and try to reach the top to restore the light and discover what happened to it. The puzzles range in difficulty but are never so difficult as to be frustrating. The game took me around 3 hours to complete, so this would be the perfect chill puzzle game for a spare evening to play through in one! I recommend Luna to anyone who enjoys a mystical soundtrack and a relaxing point-and-click adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is viewed as a simplistic puzzle game that turns into a heartfelt journey. The puzzles are not too easy but not mind boggling either so after you complete each section there is a strong sense of satisfaction after completing each puzzle. Most games like this have a tendency to get lost in it's own plot, much like the game Iris Fall. But Luna however does a great job storytelling without dialogue & even if we don't get the whole picture. I really hope this company tries to flush this out into something more. I see a lot of good potential in it story wise.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Luna: The Shadow Dust is a point & click adventure puzzler that has been fully hand-drawn and animated. The art style appears heavily influenced by Studio Ghibli’s stuff and yet still manages to stand out on its own. The music is equally as beautiful as the visuals and the two combined craft a wonderful interactive artwork that is simple to use, challenging at times and fun to play through.Feel like I can certainly recommend this game to folks that enjoy puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Full review at: The general experience of Luna: The Shadow Dust is definitely an enjoyable one. The world is beautifully realized with sight and sound even though not a single word is used to explain the story, but much like its puzzles, much of it is intuitively understood. Climbing up the tower is definitely designed more as an experience devoted to exploring a simple but interesting plot through visual storytelling than providing strong point and click gameplay, but enough of the puzzles do provide interesting concepts or decent challenges to make getting to the top a mostly enjoyable experience. Movement is too slow for its own good and a few puzzles are much too simple, but these are easily overlooked thanks to the moments that do have more involved problem solving or are just a chance to appreciate the artistry featured throughout this title.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Overall i think this game deserves praise mostly for its art.Music is also a plus, even tho it kinda felt like i was listening to the same song the entire time, but it was a nice song.Storytelling was very confusing, i finished the game and i still don't understand the donut in the sky or the cat lady or anything really.Dificulty curve could be a bit better worked on, as the early puzzles are very very very easy, but then the last puzzle is some big brain legendary dothraki warrior kind of play.There's also a level where you just go up stairs, which felt kinda....pointless.Overall for kids, i think it is a good brainteaser, but other than that, it's just a pretty game to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: If you like chilled out puzzle games with beautiful, hand-drawn animation/art, a gorgeous score and mysterious non-verbal storytelling, then LUNA is a MUST BUY. Something I love about the game is that the vast majority of puzzles are 'perfect information' - i.e. you know that all the tools you need are in the room you're in, which means you can focus on observation, experimentation, and using your wits. The solutions aren't necessarily hard, but you either feel great for figuring it out ahead of time, or the process of experimenting is logical and fun, so either way you end up feeling good. Don't expect a traditional point and click game though - there's no inventory, and no exploration - but LUNA is not trying to be something it's not - and it therefore excels in what it does do. The way the enigmatic story slowly unfolds gives extra motivation to solving each puzzle, as well as the excitement of seeing a beautiful new area. All told, LUNA is a streamlined, polished and beautiful narrative puzzle game. Of course it's not perfect - for example, it wouldn't hurt if the walking/activating animations were a tiny bit faster, especially since one or two puzzles rely on timing (only a little bit though) - but it's a unique experience and the tiny ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do nothing to take away from that.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: is a beautiful and very well-made puzzle game involving two characters that you'll be alternating between, namely Uri the kid and Layh the cute pet that joins him on his journey after he helped it. They are making their way up the very imposing tower in hopes of reaching a floating island of sorts so that they could stop it from sending monstrous shadow creatures that currently plagues the land, including the town Uri lives in, below.+ Mostly easy and relaxing puzzles that can be solved without any guidance from the game. The puzzles are also very well-varied from room to room. Solving puzzles in this game is nothing short of a delightful experience!+ No hand-holding but you can probably figure out how most puzzle works and what you're expected to do pretty quickly.+ Beautiful art, animation and music+ A heartwarming tale about a young boy's quest to save his people+ Suitable for kids- Might be a bit pricey considering the hours you can get out of it. If you're on a tight budget, maybe you'd like to wishlist the game first and check back in during a sale!- Not suitable for hardcore puzzlers - you may find the game boring.P/S: I've got stumped in one of the later levels (and also the boat level but I got through that by luck and a bit of common sense) but I'm sure I can figure things out in the end. LUNA: The Shadow Dust is a brilliant story-driven puzzle game that's not only beautifully made, it is also one of the rarer puzzle adventure games where the puzzles aren't just the same mechanics or designs over and over again. The variety here is amazing and the puzzles are simple enough to grasp to the point where the game doesn't even need to explain a puzzle and you can "get it" after playing around with some levers and stuff. I really can't recommend the game enough! If you're a huge fan of casual puzzle adventures, you'll want to wishlist it if money's tight or if you can't wait to play the game, buy it outright.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the game is REALLY beautiful, sweet, simple, and the story is lovely... but, for the price of the game, it is VERY brief and (while the magic of the graphics is captivating and the intermittent story elements are endearing) the actual gameplay is pretty restrictive and honestly kind of boring!If you just want something that's pretty and simple and you only want to kill a few hours, it's probably a perfect game, but it just didn't win me over.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully drawn, but infuriatingly repetitive and dumb...basically, the artwork is MUCH better than the gameplay.  This game is too slow and frustrating for no good reason, which is a pity, as it had great promise that failed to materialize.OK, I've finished this - the artwork and effort is GORGEOUS, but there is MUCH too much time in which the player is passive watching a long, pretty incomprehensible/illogical sequence of stuff play out. _childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game in the point-and-click style I prefer: 2D, no text, & no VO. The art is quality, and the puzzles are just the right amount of difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: An almost joy from start to finish.  I've been playing games like this for, oh, more than thirty years now - I played The Manhole back in the late 80s which was probably the first of these "no interface, just explore" concepts.  One of the particular benchmarks in this genre was Samorost, which brought an extra style and unique graphical feel, and that is what Luna most reminded me of but takes it a bit further.Which is both high praise (as that's already a high bar) but also a criticism, since it feels merely as though this is an Amanita game with some very, very good cutscenes.  So what you get is a slow-paced puzzle game (with one exception, which I will come to) that will annoy an enormous number of people who demand instant gratification and, all too often, a bit of violence.  This game has neither of those things and if you want them, or you have no patience, then you should look elsewhere.Instead, it conforms to all the tropes of the "single-screen back-and-forth" form, with a couple of tricks of its own.  But everything holds together beautifully, with coherent internal logic and proper forehead-slap moments of realisation as you piece together how the various sequences are meant to work and then execute them correctly.But - and it's a big but - there is what I felt was a genuine design mistake about half way through, with a room that requires fast and accurate clicking, which is the antithesis of what this genre is all about.  There are a couple of other sequences that need a certain amount of timing but on the whole the game is pretty forgiving.  Except for the bookcases, which not only takes a long time to tumble to the trick (which, to be fair, is a very good one), but then sends you back to the start again if you make a tiny slip up.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not finished the game yet but these first two hours were a very pleasant experience:+ the graphics are very interesting, the color palette is relaxed and the animations are cozy.+ the sound effects are on point and the music is very cool !+ the puzzles are quite interesting and they get more complex but not annoying nor tiresome.+ the story is very intriguing and slowly developing through leveling up and Luna's memories.- i wish i had something to complain about but.. i don't ! maybe the price.. ?
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: What do we have here?  I'm not sure, exactly.  The character design makes you think, "Empathy!" but then you end up using a small lost child to shove heavy things around, slowly and repeatedly, and stuffing the little cat/ball/lizard thing down radiator pipes and up against evil magic bramble spikes, when you're not leaving it outside in the winter to get fossilized.   The drawings make you think, "Miyazake moved farther east?" but it's hard not to notice that it is a towering, terrifying conglomeration of code violations and fall hazards.  The play starts out as a gentle puzzle game with a soundtrack appropriate for a slightly unsettling spa experience, but suddenly there are time-trial exercises that had me mashing the trackpad in a non-relaxed way. There seems to be some kind of mythos involved but it may be all stained glass and glowy things rather than a holy book of I don't know what and at this point I'm not sure I want to know.  The gentle feeling may just come from having to watch the characters walk very, very slowly.  I just have the feeling that the heart of this game is more brittle and unfeeling than can be camouflaged by all the lovely hand-drawn everything that adorns it.  It's too late for me to return the thing so I may march through to the bitter (although perhaps heartwarming, who knows?) end, but it's not too late for you not to buy it.

_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Too easy, too simple, and more often than not, too dull and slow,  counts on its beautiful, fairy-tail, dreamy graphics, and soothing OST, a bit too much than it should. It’s not a bad point-and-click adventure, sure, and those who can look past its heavy flaws will be entertained for about two to three hours, but if it weren’t for its stunning hand-painted world, few would give it a second look.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt, LUNA The Shadow Dust is the most beautiful game I’ve played in a long time. A scintillating yet simple story told with no words, only the deepest emotions conveyed through glorious art and hypnotizing music, I was legitimately moved to tears multiple times. Of course, a few of those tears shed were in frustration over a puzzle or two, but in the end, it only extended my time with a phenomenal masterpiece crafted by video game artisans. A powerful, cautionary tale of those who forget that the brightest lights yield the longest shadows, LUNA The Shadow Dust is worth every single penny and will no doubt stay with players for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs to be enjoyed with hot cup of tea.Delightful puzzles in a wonderful, magical world, the art style and music creates a quite relaxing atmosphere.A very nice touch to the puzzle mechanic that you need to control both characters individually and have them work together, as only together they can solve them.While - depending on how good you are solving the puzzles - the playtime is not too long, but that time you do spend in the game couldn't be any better.So, if you like puzzles and are looking for a comfy experience and a nice story that develops over the course of solving those rooms, do look at this.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Great art but that´s about it. The game is only about 3 hours long and it would have actually be even shorter if you didn´t have to do the same thing multiple times for most of the puzzles. It doesn´t help that while good looking, the animations are slow and you have to wait for them to complete before you can switch characters or input another action. Another negative point is that the puzzles rarely make use of the shadow mechanic and the small creature you have with you and if they do they never use it in a clever way. All in all this made the puzzles a chore to go through and bored me to hell. The puzzles, while they do establish that you are in a magical world, they barerly, if at all, are related to the story. The story in itself is simple and has quite a few plotholes but this is a magical world so everything could be explained somehow I guess.The music is pretty good but nothing I would come back to listen to. I really can´t recommend this game unless you like the artstyle and want to support indie devs.

_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointing. Mediocre puzzles, with built in delays of characters needing to walk or manipulate items all at a snails pace. To be fair, I think it's intentional (they want a leisurely "ambiance-heavy" style), but a 20 second long animation of you riding cart each time you try to click on an item is an example of how to turn a 2 minute long puzzle into 20. Story was... fine. Music was good. But the puzzles are weak sauce; embodiments of the downsides of poor point-and-click stuff (little finicky things you miss ending in puzzles that actually don't require you to think too hard once you find the button to click; very little logic required, just hide and seek)
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning. Beautiful designs, well executed animation, thoughtful game concept.If you are looking for inspirations for your next game or art. I recommend it.But the slow and limiting in game movement was too frustrating to deal with.The best part of the game, (use of shadows) was't implemented enough. And the story wasn't satisfying. It gives a hint of a larger, beautiful world that remains separate from the main story. The main story line misses a few story beats to feel strong enough to holdup an otherwise beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. The music, the art...it's reminiscent of so many of my favs (ghibli, gris, etc) while still being unique and having its own story to tell <3 At its core, LUNA is a point & click escape room...progress is linear and you mostly just go from one room to the next by solving puzzles. However, there are also some really gorgeous and cinematic cut scenes between levels that add a lot of depth to the story, and keep it from feeling like you're just solving random puzzles one after another. And if you're worried about the difficulty, I'd say 85% of the rooms didn't make me wanna tear my hair out ;) My only gripe is that character movement is quite slow, which made some tasks a bit tedious if you had to do them over and over again (especially so when achievement hunting). I'm ADHD af so I expected this to bother me more, but there were enough beautiful details and animations to keep me (mostly) entertained. TL;DR: My only regret is how many times I dropped my little companion guy. Sorry, buddy! But seriously, just get this game already.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Nice point-and-click game with lots of puzzles and a heart-warming story. You and your pet needs to go up the tower, to infinity and beyond! The art style is gorgeous, the puzzles are smart, the soundtrack is so beautiful. This game will stay with you. I would say it is similar to "NAIRI" or "Little Briar Rose" for its art style and warmth. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

More seasoned gamers may find it boring, but I would still recommend just to experience the art and the story! <3
