_childDocuments_.review: Boring and tedious. The character is so slow. You have to repeat actions so many times, e.g. climbing the last ladder takes forever as you have to wait between each steps (yes this is the kind of tasks for have to do: climb a ladder by clicking up many times)Cut scenes are so looong (I guess this is why some may enjoy this game but I could not relate).Amanita games and even Gris are so much better.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, with a nice storyline that had me shedding a few tears at the end. If you enjoy beautiful animation, escape room like puzzles, and lovely soundtracks, this game might be for you. I certainly enjoyed the journey. The only complaints I have are that I found some of the puzzles a bit repetitive and that the price might be a bit steep for the game's length. I would suggest purchasing when on sale. If I had to give the game a rating, I would say...4/5 and recommended to those who enjoy slow paced puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What can I say? Such a beautiful game that absolutely drew me in (pardon the pun) with its hand-drawn animations, calming music, and an emotional storyline that is sure to take you on a rollercoaster if you're a big empath like me. I'm obsessed with intricate puzzles, and this ticked it off the list too. You get put into an ancient tower that is built on many levels, and you need to go through each level/building part one by one in order to get yourself out from the very top and restore the order of the world. You start off as playing Uri, but will soon have a companion that you must also control (both have different abilities to be able to do certain tasks/techniques). That's all I'm gonna say, no proper spoilers. Overall, I think this is one of the best games I've ever played, and I hope one day there'll be sequel or something!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy point & click puzzle games and I particularly enjoyed this one! It is very story rich and the puzzles are challenging without making you lose patience. The sound track was fitting and calming although it could have had a bit more of spark. Finally the design was absolutely beautiful, all the way from the colours to how paintings would unfold when the pieces of a puzzle were set right.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game... but with a bit of caveat.  The art and music is well done, but the story itself is really meh. I suppose if the target audience is younger then they'd enjoy the story more... except the puzzles of this game isn't exactly easy to solve, so I wonder how many kids can actually beat the game without using a guide. I really dislike the clock tower puzzle since there's little to no hints. Also, later puzzles tend to waste our time, like the books/library one. Or the 4 season one. Yes, we get it, we need to do cycles, but repeating the same sequence just so we can get to the other sequence is NOT fun. And the achievements are also very conflicting. For example, there's an achievement for releasing the bee for all seasons in the 4 season puzzle, that I found out after beating the game. The thing is, you only need it for one season. So, once you figured out the puzzle, why would you not go solve it, but instead keep releasing the bee? This achievement was designed to reward players who do trial and error... but then there are other achievements that reward the player for completing the puzzles without error. It seems that the devs just wanted to add replayability for the sake of replayability, because the achievements designs are not consistent.But still, overall it was a *nice enough* experience, so I think it's worth playing, especially since it's relatively short. But compare to the Looker that I also just finished on the same day, the Looker felt more fun to play, and it's free. IDK, I feel like giving this a lukewarm 6.5/10... but I can see someone might really enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little indie puzzle game! The universe and art style are magical, a mashup between the vibes of Amanita design and Studio Ghibli, with an equally magical soundtrack! The setups are so cozy and warm and the hand drawn animations are simply stunning. I recommend getting this if you’re into this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: THE MOST BEAUTIFUL and ENGAGING point and click I've ever played. puzzles still make you think and require good timing/"skill" even though the controls are so simple. the storytelling and myth-weaving is so artistic and just gorgeous visuals and soundtrack. this game gives me the same warm fuzzies as watching the first 2 harry potter movies over and over when I'm sick, just magical fantastical wonderful worldbuilding, such an enjoyable aesthetic to find comfort in again and again. unlike a lotta other point n clicks the story really keeps one-upping itself and it really goes in completely unexpected directions fleshing out  the story and myths of the world much more than games like Growbot (which i also love but the story is far more  confined  and the plot takes place in  one setting, unlike this  game  which really goes  all over). PLEASE TRY THIS GAME  IF YOU APPRECIATE ARTFUL/CREATIVE GAMES!!!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A unique and very enjoyable experience to remember.Luna the shadow dust stands out for its atmosphere but also the gameplay works very well.Graphics and music are executed very well and fit together. The story is motivating . Characters are driven by good intentions and care for each other. When playing, the mood is always good and relaxed, not stressful.Regarding the gameplay, I appreciate it very much that this game is not about repetition and chores. Every single puzzle is different with a special twist. The puzzles are not very difficult but still not trivial as well. Some are amazingly clever .If you are experienced with this type of puzzles, not everything is completely new, but this game is still quite unique.The length of the game is not very long, but this is good, because the time spent playing is enjoyable. This is much better than an artificially extended playtime through repetition and chores. About the ending: The structure with different rooms allows to play one puzzle at a time, perfect for playing with limited pace.I recommend this game to people who have a sense of art, like using their brain and are looking for a relaxed game experience. It is suitable for children with playful imagination and creativity as well as for adults who prefer to relax for a few hours using their brain actively and of course to any fan of point and click adventures who want to see a bit beyond their own nose.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and quick game. The first handful of puzzles are very easy and straightforward but towards the end of the game they get a little more tricky. Beautiful artwork. Surprisingly long cut scenes the few times they occur. It was a nice play. Definitely something to play if you want something more easy, quick, and laid back.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I have a condition/disability that makes me physically and mentally react slow. That's why I like to play point and click adventures and this type of puzzle games: I can actually play a game myself. Not this game tho. I am in the room where the lantern falls from the ceiling and you have to react faster than my disability lets me. I am physically not able to finish this game except for when I get my husband or a friend to play the fast parts for me. I wish games would have ratings or notes that would tell for which disabilities it isn't playable, or even better: Have options to make those parts easyer or different for disabled people. I would not have bought this if I knew of this.I am angry, disappointed and sad, because otherwise I really love this game. I like the art style, the music and sound effects. Just another game on the pile of "If I wouldn't have this disability", if no one helps me I have to try to refund it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, short game. Beautiful art and atmosphere, and I really enjoyed the puzzles and their light/shadow concept (a few of the last ones were a bit too much trial and error perhaps, but nothing too frustrating and still fun). The story develops slowly, but might even cause some tears in the end!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little game! Beautifully drawn, every room has a new captivating aesthetic! Has interesting puzzles, that have a "discovery" method of solving. The game-play was smooth, and straight forward. It has very nicely animated cut-scenes, and a simple yet effective story. The only thing that may bother some people is the time is takes for characters to walk, but I was fine with it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificent animations in cartoon style. The music is beautiful.The story of this game is a little bit mysterious, but that's the typical touch of this kind of game. Also an emotional atmosphere during the end of the game.Most puzzles are logical and easy; but sometimes you just have to think/look a bit further.In my opinion 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Luna is pretty. I'll give it that. Sadly it's too worried about it's looks and not enough about gameplay. There are two faults, either of which on their own I could forgive but not together. As I said it's about looks. Every action has an animation, usually too long. Some tasks like picking up a book in the library can take about 15 seconds and you have to repeat that one at least four times. The puzzles are also about experimentation and discovery rather than deduction. Not a problem in itself, Amanita Design can do that well, but combine it with the lengthy animations and each room becomes a test of patience more than anything else. In the end my 3.9 hours to beat the game was too long and felt like a lot of time wasted.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Luna is a hand drawn, slow paced puzzle game with a touching story, told completely visually, with no dialogue and simple controls. Definitely worth playing, with some beautiful scenes and music. If you're a fan of point and click adventures with a distinct art style like Samorost or Machinarium, you'll enjoy playing. However, the game is very short and  can be finished in under 5 hours. Despite the high production quality, it's not worth $25, so add it to your wishlist and grab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely little game - the art and music are both GORGEOUS, and really transported me to another world. The lore was beautifully detailed and felt really unique, like it belonged more to a novel than a game (though I would have liked more backstory about how the tower integrates with the rest of the world, but I think that would have been hard to do without using words - which obviously the developers are trying to avoid).I also enjoyed each of the puzzles - I liked that there wasn't too much to click on in each room (so you couldn't just click everything until you found the right answer), but rather that you had to take your time to look around and figure things out.If I have a complaint, it's that I'd have liked the game to be longer (partly because I wanted to continue the enjoyment, and partly because I think it was a bit short for the price), but I'd still really recommend it. I found it very soothing to play, and it got my imagination going too.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adore this little gem! The art style is just right up my alley and I still come back to the soundtrack every now and then.+ Graphics, Soundtrack, Story- Price vs gameplay timeThe  is beautiful (just look at it) and the flow between gameplay and cinematic cut scenes feels near seamless. The wonderful  adds to the overall whimsical, cozy feeling and you'll get why it got nominated for awards right off the bat. , LUNA offers escape-room-like puzzles, which in most cases are fairly easy to solve, while the  is told completely without words. The  is be a bit high for the few hours of playtime (including achievements), but considering it is hand-animated, I get the idea. I recommend sitting down on a Saturday with a cup of tea and playing through in one go if you have the time!Maybe  you prefer challenging Point&Click Games, tend to skip cut scenes or cinematics or want more out of a game than a Saturday evening amount of gameplay hours.I think  you like cozy, dream-like games that clearly took lots of work and love from their developers, if you don't mind a game being short as long as it takes you on a journey or if you love Point&Clicks and prefer classic mechanics over difficult, time consuming ones.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet, classic point and click game with a bit of puzzles that require (sometimes) an effort to solve without any walk-through. I love the story line so much- you get to play as both characters, a boy and his animal (?) apprentice, and it somehow grows on you, the duo. You'll find yourself attached to them both as the story progress. Amazing art and concept, and with no spoiling intention: I CRIED AT THE END. Happy tears? Sad tears? A combination of both? Man, who knows. Would totally recommend this to those who love puzzles, p&c, and great story & artwork!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique game, and I really enjoyed it as a fan of point and click games.You can tell a lot of work went into the art, animations and the music, which are all superb.The puzzles are not very difficult but the pacing is good and it's a lot of fun to follow the story (which is told without using any dialogue, a very nice touch) until the end.The little pet character is super cute too, and I want a plush version of it ASAP.NOTE: I played the game on a different Steam account, which is why the number of hours played is showing as very low. I enjoyed the game so much that I purchased it for myself on my Steam account as well.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The art style in this game is really cool! Music is great, animation is adorable. Although, there was a point when i wasnt able to do anything except move around because the game was bugging out, and i have to reload, but besides that it was fun, kinda wish the ending was more of a playthrough rather than a couple cut scenes. Overall, a fun game, and the puzzles later in the game took me a bit to figure out.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice point and click puzzle game. Puzzles were good. A little hard, but usually enough to take some thought and make you feel clever that you solved it.  A few took me quite a while not quite understanding what I was supposed to be doing, but then when I solved it, I thought, well that makes sense I should have thought of that. Nice Indie art style. Not too many cut scenes, but I thought they were too slow and dramatic. No words, just silent movies. The one at the end was way too long and dramatic for me. You get a cat and can toggle between using the girl and the cat, and they have to work together to overcome the obstacles. The cat can walk on top of shadows and that is often the key to figuring it out. I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A short puzzle game with heavy focus on atmosphere, visuals, and sound. Everything is very well done here and overall leaves a good cartoon / cinematic experience. Some of the puzzles can get overly frustrating with timing, light / shadow, and odd mechanics between the two main characters. Add to this that all character movements are slow and drawn out for authenticity, so there is no speed running at all. If you go in with this expectation, you will enjoy the slow ride that this game is about.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Look, i love me a hand-drawn puzzle game. But this game. Man, this game is so boring i just wanted to get it over with. It's a short 3-hour game and i still couldn't wait to finish it. The characters walk VERY slowly and every interaction is too long, so if you mess up a few times expect to spend a lifetime in a puzzle. Especially the library one, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that animation was SO LONG.Also, there are 3-4  animations throughout the game which give you the backstory, but these are also SO FREAKING LONG it felt like i was watching a movie instead of playing a game. I mean i'm all for a little cut scene but damn these were too long.Overall, would not recommend. Just play other games.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: It's SUCH a cute game, and so beautifully made T_T <3 it's a bit short for the price it was imo, but the art and the intricacy of the puzzles makes it worth it. I was never stuck to the point that I wanted to give up, it was just the right amount of challenge while keeping it a chill game. If you're a hardcore puzzle game fanatic and need to be challenged 1000% then maybe this isn't for you, but if you like to enjoy your puzzles, like pretty artwork and a cute yet sometimes sad storyline, then this is definitely for you!!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A young boy falls from the sky and at the last moment lands safely on what appears to be a beach. When he gets his bearings he notices a blue flame following him, and it appears to be casting shadows, shadows of things that aren’t there. It’s when the boy finds a door, with an extinguished lantern over it that the real adventure begins in LUNA The Shadow Dust.This is a point and click adventure game where you will be tasked with conquering rooms/floors of a large tower. Obviously your objective is clearly to get to the top of the tower, but along the way you’re going to have to conquer many puzzles, and chances are you’re going to have to attempt some of them quite a few times. The complexity of the puzzles does ramp up as you ascend the tower, and a new wrinkle gets thrown in early when you encounter some sort of cat-like creature that you will “tag-team” with to solve most of the puzzles. I have to admit that some of the puzzles drove me crazy because you really had to have your timing down, and then there were others where at first I didn’t know what to do and then I had a very satisfying “ahha” moment. This game really boils down to two concepts: light and shadow, and I have to say that the developers pulled it off. This is even shown between levels as you’re progressing to a new floor/room, you are slowly returning light to the tower. I love the look of the game, from the different environments you’ll have to go through to the way the characters look. There were also the cinematics that were sprinkled throughout the game that gave, in my opinion, the player a chance for a stronger emotional attachment with the story. Not all games need to have a narrator or characters voiced, it's difficult, in my opinion, to successfully pull off, but there was just enough in each area that there didn’t need to be any type of spoken or written “handholding”. I’ll also say that the music that went along with the game fit perfectly, it didn’t take away from the look of the game, and it didn’t take away from the quality of the game.This is not going to be a game for everyone, but there’s definitely a good chance that those out there who like point and click adventure games filled with puzzles will enjoy this game. I feel like too many times we, gamers, base the greatness of a game on the time spent, and I will tell you it took me around 2 and a half hours to beat, but I really do feel that I got my money’s worth. I felt satisfied, if not a little sad with the ending, and I recommend this game to others.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. Enchanting graphics full of loving details and great animations. I also really enjoyed the story and was left wanting to talk to someone about it. The puzzles are very easy at the beginning, but become much harder and more extensive at a pleasant pace. But they can always be solved with a little thought and logic. Only the last puzzle I personally found a little too difficult. I would have liked to play much longer and was almost sad when the game was over. I think that's one of the nicest compliments you can make a title like this. Absolutely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: this game is aesthetically beautiful, and the puzzles are clever and interesting. it's a fascinating challenge to work both luna and the cat at the same time. moving through the game is an unfettered delight. some of the story scenes are a little long for my taste, but that's my only complaint. the story scenes are also really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite what I was expecting, but still enjoyable! (Albeit for a discounted price)If I had only one negative thing to say though, I think a clearer worldbuild could have helped. The no dialogue is fine, and it's not completely difficult to follow, but there is quite a few details that are never fully explained; or portraits and rooms that seemed like they should be something really important (And there's a secret ending to back this up?), but don't offer a whole lot besides some cool aesthetics. Which I suppose it's fine too. It is a really short game, but I can't help wondering what it could have been if it was extended out just a bit longer.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing puzzle game with calming music. The graphics are beautiful and the cut scenes are nicely designed, drawing you into the lives of the characters. While a few of the puzzles are not overtly intuitive, I liked that the game is designed to allow you to try multiple options to figure out the process without any setbacks. I hope there will be a sequel in the future. I would definitely purchase it. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The drawings are really successful. There are too many details in the game and sometimes you may not even notice them while you are playing especially for the first time. Overall I liked its nostalgic nature. Game soundtracks and drawings are a complete piece of art. I also liked the shadow details very much. I love this kind of relaxing, adventurous puzzle games. I highly recommend it.   Be careful! Emotional content! The game contains material that may be devastating or traumatizing to some players. :(
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: About 4 hours of game play but there is a good amount of puzzles and a good amount of fully hand animated cutscenes. This would probably take a child a good bit longer, but I had to click everything for my 3 year old anyway so the puzzle solving was a bit quicker. There were 2 puzzles that just didn't have a clear enough hint for me, or too tedious of a hint to discover that I looked up the answer. The rest of them I think an 8 year old would find just about right for most of them. Really nice sound track. I am looking for others like this to play with the 3 year old.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully and lovingly illustrated, this classic puzzle adventure game has a soft color palette, gentle soundtrack and idyllic design. Each scene feels so warm and comforting that whenever I finished a puzzle, I felt a twinge of sadness to be leaving them behind.  With a simple, sweet story and wonderful characters I ended this game both weepy and happy. Playing Luna: The Shadow Dust felt like getting a warm hug or sitting in my favorite chair. It was simply brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the puzzles and story of Luna. The fact that the entire story is "told" without words is pretty cool, and the environments are really interesting. There's a lot more going on with this game than meets the eye. I'm glad I got to play it, and I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys point-and-click puzzle games.(Game received for free, but not with any expectation of a positive review.)
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Do yourself a favor and PLAY THIS GAME. Every aspect of it is stunning. It's amazing that this was accomplished by a team of FOUR. The art is amazing, the puzzles are fun, the characters are charming, the story compelling, and the soundtrack is really really good. I'm not sure why you're still reading my review instead of buying this game?
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: LUNA is one of the most Magical and brilliantly crafted games I have ever seen or played! As well, the creators of this game are remarkably authentic and kind souls! They put their hearts and souls into this creation and it shines through! The puzzles are interesting and even adorable at times. The Artwork is superb and astonishing! The storyline keeps you totally immersed and makes you think and wonder the entire time. It also has quite funny moments, too. I am pretty much referring to any moments spent with the mice. lol 10/10! 100% recommend this game to everyone who loves proper storytelling without needing to say a word of dialogue and for anyone who truly adores games that are both made BY and FOR those of us who do not want to just burn through gameplay but find ourselves feeling deeply instead!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad a game, but you know, something is missing that after playing it you just have that small unsatisfied feeling. I can`t blame the game, but maybe it is too simple at some points and also closer to the end it becomes tedious: the main difficulty goes from intricate idea to just a lot of moving around and the main characters (you will have move two separately) are moving too slow, for my taste.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: The graphic was awesome, the puzzle was great but sometimes I got frustrated from how slow they moved. 7/10 because I'm not really into the story, it's pretty cheesy. But if you're to play with a kid and play as you tell them the story, I think that would be pretty good. Great game tho, nice work, Dev team!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Luna will transport you. I rarely write reviews. But I had to for this game. Three hours of gameplay. It is one of the most clever, beautiful games you will play. The point and click puzzle games can sometimes get very frustrating but this one was just difficult enough to be fun but I never found myself rage quitting because I couldn't figure it out. This way, I got to thoroughly enjoy the story, scenery, and music of this amazing game. 10/10 AMAZING GAME. Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming little story!It's not a long game, I played over a couple of evenings. Most of the puzzles are fairly straight-forward and just require a bit of tinkering and paying attention to the clues. This is perfect if you just want something low pace and feel like getting lost in the ambience, it's beautifully illustrated. I enjoyed every minute of LUNA.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: is a short, delightful, beautifully hand-drawn puzzle game. The puzzles are relatively easy, but not to the point of being trivial, and are incredibly rewarding -- partially due to the charming visual style. The music is wonderful and the entire game is told through visuals as opposed to through narration or dialogue. I particularly appreciate this, as it puts emphasis on the game's splendid art. Additionally, I could see this as a great game to play with a young child; akin to an interactive storybook. I definitely recommend picking it up if the store page has piqued your interest.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet.  The hand-drawn animations are gorgeous and the soundtrack is beautiful.  However this is not your typical point and click, more like escape room on each screen.  It is very short and the story left me a little confused, yes I get the story, but I don't fully get it if that makes sense.  I would probably not replay this game again and I would suggest getting it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully drawn and animated light adventure game that allows for a few hours of point and clicking around to solve puzzles and fully uncover the story behind a mysterious tower that the protagonist is trying to ascend.Only "flaw" the game has (if anyone were to call it that) is the fact that it very often feels a bit too slow since you have to repeat certain actions and watch the characters very slowly move from one place to another. If you are used to double-click ~ teleport adventure games, this is not your thing. This is more the sit-back-and-relax kind of adventure game rather than the intense-point-and-click-paired-with-really-hard-puzzles kind of thing.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that it was an amazingly beautiful game with charming puzzles and a story that lets the visual do all the talking (the 4 seasons puzzles was by far my fav! )My only complaints for this game has to be at the end... if you dont want some spoiler i suggest you not read the rest.At the Clock tower puzzle i didnt understand why the developers would include the ringing of a bell if the time for the puzzle isnt set at the start of a new hour like most Clocktowers... but thats just a nit pick.The 2nd one has to be when the main character and your buddy fall of the ledge. after that scene it just cuts to both of you back at the altar! no transition nothing, i do thank you not having me climb the latter of subtle wind signs but it just kinda dragged me out of the immersion.All and all great experience cant wait to see what else this company comes up with!!!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Great game; the art style really drew me into wanting to buy and play it as I really enjoyed a similar game, Broken Age. Puzzles aren't simplified, so it makes you really think, while also being able to still enjoy playing the game itself. The soundtrack is beautiful and so are the small cinematics that they added in. Truly a beautiful and relaxing game.I definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing artwork and beautiful cinematics. Gameplay is challenging but not too challenging to the point of frustration. The game nicely builds your foundation of the necessary skills so that by the time you get to the harder levels, you are well versed in the techniques required. Very cute story line. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: LUNA The Shadow Dust

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful! From the illustrations, to the story, to the background music.. and of course the puzzles that got me dusting off the neurons <3 I'm not a fan of point & click games since I feel they are quite obvious as in "where to click" but not this one, this challenged me to think a bit out of the box and I loved it! Will definitely keep playing to unlock all the achievements and keep enjoying it a little bit longer.

_childDocuments_.review: LUNA The Shadow Dust is a stunningly beautiful game and one worth playing for the aesthetics alone. The entire game has been created with hand-drawn animation giving it a look and feel that is reminiscent of a Studio Ghibli film. I was also reminded somewhat of Unforeseen Incidents, another beautifully drawn game I played a few years ago. The details are incredible and the use of both color and lights throughout really brings the rooms and puzzles to life. The soundtrack (composed by Wang Qian) is also beautiful and adds a lot of extra depth to the story.I really enjoyed playing LUNA The Shadow Dust and found that the puzzles fell into that ideal zone of being hard enough to be challenging without being so difficult that they caused frustration and made me want to give up and walk away. I noticed that I was talking out loud to myself as I worked through them, and could see this game being a great choice for a couple or some friends to work through together—I will be suggesting it to some family members who love to play mystery puzzle games along the lines of those from Big Fish. Solving the puzzles is decidedly more tricky than mastering the controls and I will admit that I needed to consult walkthroughs sooner than I would have liked! Many of the rooms will contain a clue somewhere so it is well worth exploring everywhere in order to figure out the solution. However, the puzzles can become repetitive, especially if you cannot see the solution immediately.There’s also a lot of humor to be found in the game. One puzzle involved fattening up an adorable cartoon rat by cooking him various dishes that caused a different reaction when Layt boinged off his head. Another, one of the most impressive puzzles I have yet to come across, involves hilariously multiplying Layt to create a number of duplicates who could each sing a different note of a tune. With this puzzle, the gameplay and the soundtrack blended together perfectly to create something both visually and audibly incredible.LUNA The Shadow Dust is a relaxing game ideal for snuggling up with on a cold night. It is not an especially long game, but this could be a good thing because it stops the puzzles from becoming overly monotonous and it makes completing the game feel achievable for casual gamers who only want to dip in and out for a short time in the evening. I’m definitely hoping to see a sequel in the future.Full review on GeekMom.

_childDocuments_.review: By far, LUNA is one of the best, if not the best, puzzle games I have played in a while. The puzzles are moved by a strong story, which kept getting more interesting as time went on and you figured things out, and even though some puzzles were quite long or difficult, I never found myself walking away from it. There was no repetition or boring moments in this game, and the bits of humor they put in here and there, such as Layh falling and the mice worked so well. Everything was inviting. The art was beautiful, the soundtrack and noises were perfect, and the characters were cute and likeable. I really enjoyed the no dialogue; it made the story much more moving. It felt very much so like fantasy, but it had grounding moments that a lot of people feel or have flt in their lives. such as the found family aspect. All in all, I highly recommend LUNA. Very anxious to see what else this awesome studio puts out in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Luna: The Shadow Dust is the type of point and click puzzle game that can be difficult to talk about, not because it’s bad or has controversial materials, but because the magic of the game is going in with little knowledge about the characters and story.To keep the game a mystery this review is going to be short and hopefully convey what players are jumping into. Is Luna a good game? Yes. Is it short? Yes. Is it worth adding to your ever-growing collection of games? That depends on if you want a game that tells a story or a game that has something to say.If you’re here for the latter, I’m afraid Luna isn’t going to cut it. But if you enjoy a game simply being a fun game, you’re in for a sweet treat.Luna: The Shadow Dust takes place on a mysterious floating land that has an erected tower that can help lead to the truth for a young boy, who has no known name, who has woken up with no memory of how he got there.Along the way he meets a strange cat-like creature that doesn’t cast a shadow, together the boy and his new companion will climb the strange tower and discover a darkness that threatens the world, and they may even learn something about each other.That’s basically all this review should say about the story, because the story is front and center alongside a hand drawn graphic style that helps the game stand out.What’s more, the game is completely vocal free, there is no dialogue spoken by the characters nor are there any vocal tracks in the music. Luna is so confident in telling its story that it doesn’t give the characters exposition dumps and relies completely on the characters emoting and interacting with the world around them.The animation is so well done in-game that you can mistake it for an animated concept video, each level looks like a pitch for a new animated show that you would want to watch on Netflix. The characters are expressive, and each level feels different from the last, no two levels feel like a remixed version of an older section.Luna: The Shadow Dust knows what it wants to do and does not implement annoying backtracking in an attempt to pad out time, it wants to show players the story and keep them moving forward, this help gives Luna a great sense of pacing and satisfaction.Gameplay is rather simple, every room in the tower has its own puzzle that players will need to figure out, there are no time limits or monsters trying to harm the two protagonists. Instead players are encouraged to take it slow and explore the room for clues, this could be in the form of a note in the background or an NPC that interacts with certain items.One of the greatest things about Luna, other than the animation and music, is that the puzzles are well thought out and makes sense (for the most part). Only a couple of puzzles felt arbitrary with how things were laid out, they didn’t fit with the other logical puzzles, but those were very far and few.One moment players changing lights to open secret doors and the next players are using time travel to change seasons, no matter the puzzles they all follow themes based on the room, including a boiler that requires the use of steam.Of course, not everything is perfect with Luna. While the animation is nice, it’s very limited, there are no running animations, so the two characters are always moving at a snail’s pace (luckily many of the levels are small).Cutscenes in the game lack the same fluid animations as the actual game and feel like animated storyboards or unfinished scenes, it’s a bit of a whiplash when the game switches to a cutscene and small animation mistakes like missing frames sour a fun moment.The big thing for many will be the amount of time it will take to finish Luna: The Shadow Dust, which isn’t long, the game will take between two in half to three hours to finish. And even then, that depends on how long certain puzzles (the two illogical ones mentioned earlier) will take to figure out.Luna: The Shadow Dust is a fun beautiful game that is short on levels but doesn’t overstay its welcome, it doesn’t waste the players time and it has a heartfelt story with great characters that works without them having to say a single word.

Enjoyment of this game is heavily dependent on how appealing the artistic elements are to you. Requires a fair bit more patience than average and often uses arduous movement of the controllable characters to set pace and tone of an area, which may not be everyone's cup of tea. _childDocuments_.review: my initial draw to this game was that it was visually gorgeous, with a style that reminded me of a studio ghibli film or a european comic book. LUNA the shadow dust doesn't disappoint in this area; every room is stunning, the hand drawn animations are perfection, and the game is full of exquisite small details that make every levels feel lush, like a real world you could spend hours in. the audio design is especially good, with a gorgeous soundtrack by wang qian, dominated mainly by strings, and there are some levels (the organ puzzle) where the combined visual and audio experience made me physically gasp. i'd gladly play a 40 hour game from lantern studio with the same visual and audio style.the puzzles start relatively intuitive, but become deeply complex by the end, bordering on slightly unfair-- expect to need a fresh second pair of eyes and to take a while with trial and error on the later puzzles. the game requires you to inspect seemingly insignificant elements in the room, and sometimes to remember previous information. for hardcore point and click fans, which i admittedly am not, this is probably fine and not as much of a challenge as it was for me.however LUNA the shadow dust's story is where it really shines, an unexpected star of the show as i've been disappointed by wordless narratives before. in many ways it reminds me of the arrival by shaun tan, one of my favorite graphic novels. the game starts out seemingly as only a very charming puzzle game, but by the time things get real you can look back and remember many details that foreshadow or tie into the main story, and it feels like a tale you've been dropped in the middle of rather than an excuse narrative. without words LUNA presents a world with its own lore and backstory and gave me several moments where i was genuinely emotional. the cutscenes are especially charming; they're quite long at times and again, they really do feel like shots from a ghibli film.overall i highly recommend this game to point and click fans and anyone who's interested in the aesthetic-- it's a lovely little tale that feels like your favorite illustrated book or animated movie come to life, and left me satisfied, but wanting more from the world and more from this studio.

name: Fury Unleashed
detailed_description: Fury Unleashed was created by combining inspiration from modern roguelite platformers, like Dead Cells and Rogue Legacy , with nostalgic memories of old-school platformer shooters, like Contra and Metal Slug . We have spent five years polishing our creation to make sure that your experience with the game will be as memorable as those titles and we really believe that you won't be disappointed. Explore the pages of a living comic book where ink is your most valuable resource and each room is a comic panel. Find out why is John Kowalsky, author of acclaimed Fury Unleashed series having a creativity crisis and see if you can help him deal with it. Kill enemies quickly enough to unleash your fury and rip through everything in your way without getting injured. Learn to play flawlessly and beat the entire game in one, epic combo! Choose either challenging Hard mode, which will put your skills to the test - or Easy mode, where you can adjust the difficulty parameters to your liking. Go solo or bring in a friend for a co-op session. Choose your hero's skills to match your playstyle, customize their appearance or even replace their face graphic with your own! Discover worlds created by a mix of hand-designed levels and procedural generation algorithms. Choose the best items to assist you in your playthrough and unlock permanent upgrades when you'll die for your subsequent runs. Play through the pages of visually distinctive comic books, each with its own enemies, and overcome a total of 40 bosses. All that accompanied by epic soundtrack composed by Adam Skorupa and Krzysztof Wierzynkiewicz, the creators of music for The Witcher, Bulletstorm and Shadow Warrior 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t do a lot of reviews, but I felt compelled to a proper one because this game is really, really fun.Action/platformer/roguelite/RPGFirst of all, I’m on the wrong side of 45 and still gaming strong, but it presents a quandry:  I love “old school” games, but  - I am too old and can’t game as well as I used too.  The secondary problem I run into is “loving the idea” of old school games but after the novelty of pixilated graphics wears off, I can’t see them as anything but ugly.  Fury Unleashed effectively beat the hell out of those problems.  It has an AMAZING amount of customization of difficulty allowing for old people like myself to really enjoy it as well as the crazy kids hat love games being 25 viagra hard.  The graphics are really sharp and not extravagant, in short it’s pretty and runs butter smooth.  It really seems like they thought of everything up to and including a pet peeve of mine where games that use the Steam Workshop make you download the workshop stuff outside of the game, but this integrates it into the character select screen so you literally see the cosmetics you can dl from the workshop and simply select it in-game.I am a big fan of another rougelike “Undermine” and I thought it was perfect, but this is even better.  Undermine was the perfect Zeldaish rougelike and this is the perfect Contraish rougelike.Pro’s-	One of the best things about this game is that it rewards you for trying different weapons/skills/armor as opposed to punishing you if you pick "wrong" It rewards trying new things, making the replay value much higher.-       Old School gameplay without pixilated graphics.-	All of the weapons feel fun to use and worthy of using.-	There is always something that can salvage what is shaping up to be a “bad run.” Many times I *thought* a run was doomed and since it “didn’t matter” picked a power up or item I *thought* wasn’t worthwhile I’ve found said items to be incredibly useful-	Easy mode makes it accessible and is customizable so if it makes it “2ez” or not easy enough, you can adjust individual aspect of it to scale the difficulty.  -	A lot of FREE cosmetic changes are available to keep things fresh, including community made skins that you can equip in-game as opposed to having to dl them from the workshop before launching.-	Movement is accessible with a high amount of variation, sprints, stomps, double (and triple) jumps air dashes etc.  It is stuff that would normally be out of my wheelhouse but the control scheme works well and I’m moving like a freaking champion.-   Allows you to carry 2 weapons so you can feel free to experiment with different guns without giving up your current weapon.Con’s-	I don’t have any yet, and I’m over 30 hours in.  There is literally nothing I would change.TL;DRThis game is awesome.  If you like Action/platformers and Rougelite games, you will love this freaking game. It is a 10/10.  It’s a STEAL for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like Rogue-like's.  The exception being Spelunky.  Watching the videos of gameplay, this looked like Spelunky but with guns.  I bought it on this basis and....IT IS just like Spelunky with guns!!I can't really recommend this game enough if you like, or like me, don't even like this genre!!  It's very arcadey, but with the proc-gen randomness that makes some runs easier than others.  You are rewarded for playing fast and consistent due to the "Fury" element.  Chaining kills together before the combo timer runs out grants attack and defence bonuses, so it's actually beneficial to be a gung-ho most of the time.  This is of course more fun than constantly being tentative!The game is still in development and the devs says that it would take about 12 hours to complete in its current state.  I've played 16 hours so far and only just starting on the last level.  Maybe I suck!!  Having fun though!!!

_childDocuments_.review: focuses on an intense run and gun combat with combo-driven mechanics to encourage the player to move fast to reap the combo benefits. You’ll find and unlock new weapons that are satisfying and effective to use as you maneuver around enemies to avoid getting hit. It seems to be inspired by a few older run and gun games mixed in with some rogue-lite platformers as well.• A hectic run and gun rogue-like that encourages fast and intense gameplay• There are loads of guns to try out and unlock• Comic book styled graphics• Skill tree can be altered by removing skills points and requiring them in different skills• Minibosses are plentiful• Music gets more intense the bigger your combo is• Harder difficulties get rid of leveling up between runs making it less rewarding and encouraging to play• No indication of how many bullets are left in a clip or how long the reload time is is nothing short of a hectic run and gun game that provides a lot of flexibility to how you play. Weapons are the bread and butter of this title, giving you a wide variety to choose from and unlock new weapons as you progress. Since there isn’t an overwhelming amount you’ll be able to test these new weapons that you’ve unlocked and decide which ones you like the most. Some of them have a random chance to come with additional benefits such as having flaming or poison bullets to the rarer cases of finding weapons that have infinite ammo.This title encourages players to be quick on their feet to keep their combo going for as long as possible by giving them additional benefits. Your combo will increase with every enemy you kill and the time before the combo expires will be reset when you shoot an enemy or an object that breaks. By default, you’ll gain an ink multiplier that can double the ink you pick up as long as you keep your combo going. Another useful combo skill is the ability to gain a shield that protects you from being damaged, every time you achieve a combo of five you’ll gain this though it only lasts if you can continue your combo and with the right skills it can stack up to three shields.You’ll encounter a lot of different mini-bosses throughout each run of , each of them suiting the environment of whichever comic book you are in. Both the main bosses and the mini-bosses aren’t overly complicated and don’t have much variety to their attack patterns. However, you can definitely tell that most of the time was focused on creating these bosses with very high levels of detail and creativity to make them all unique from one another.Throughout each run you’ll be collecting ink which is your experience points to level up between runs. You can obtain ink by killing enemies, bosses and absorbing it from weapons and armor you don’t want from chests. Between each run you’ll be able to spend your skill points to acquire new abilities, some of them seemed a lot more beneficial than others. You are however able to reset your skill points at no cost so your free to mix and match different skills to see which ones suit your playstyle.As well as leveling up, you’ll have the opportunity to unlock new weapons for later runs which definitely gives a sense of progression if you die a lot and struggle to progress to the next area. These weapons can seriously pack a punch sometimes and gives the player more of a chance to find these rare of better weapons. You’ll unlock these weapons as you play through each run and don’t necessarily have to go off the beaten path to find them, after obtaining the black and white drawing of the weapon you’ll have to give it to another guy who can create it in this world in the same run. I never really had any problems with this and it was a nice sense of progression compared to just leveling up and gaining new skills and abilities.Upon completing the game on Hard mode you unlock the next difficulty with is called Incredible. This is where the game felt a lot more luck determined and got more frustrating the more that I tried. In this difficultly, the game resets your characters level to one when you die in a run, it gives you three random skills to choose from after you’ve completed a chapter if you’ve gathered enough ink to level up. Therefore dying at all in the mode doesn’t give you any sense of progression and is based on skill and luck of finding decent weapons and being offered generous skills to choose from. Furthermore, the game doesn’t feel like it encourages you with new unlocks or anything upon completing this mode (as far as I’m aware) besides the personal feeling of beating the game on a harder difficulty.This title does an interesting with its soundtrack, the combo meter determines how intense and dramatic the music gets to add more intensity to the combat when you have higher combos, and this pressures the player in some way to keep the combo going. Apart from that, the music for the bosses again just added more pressure to the player as they fight this massive creature or mechanical structure.Each area is definitely unique and different from one another, though you might get a bit bored of how an area looks if you’re stuck on it for a while. Apart from that, I liked the look of each area, it really suited the theme of what enemies you’ll be encountering and was a fresh experience when you first entered a new area. However, the final area which is just black and white which posed some problems for me, it was hard to figure out where bullets were coming from as they blended in with the black and white background. was definitely enjoyable to play through for the first time, it’s a hectic run and gun rogue-like that will take a couple hours to complete and leaves you feeling satisfied. However, despite trying multiple times on the harder difficulties there wasn’t enough content to encourage me to complete them. Sure there are a load of weapons to unlock there are powerful and fun to use, but by the time I had finished the game I  had unlocked the majority of them anyways. I would still recommend getting this game though, even if you just complete it on hard.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Heck, they needed five years to make this simple roguelite run and gun game, this simply MUST be a masterpiece. And it IS a ♥♥♥ in' masterpiece! I love it.Arriving deep in the Amazonian jungle, you shoot everything that moves while avoiding deadly traps. Then you die, but you gain points to permanently improve your hero. It is a twin-stick shooter, your (primary) ammo is unlimited and you carry a powerful melee weapon with you. Killed foes splatter their blood and bones around, quite satisfying in a strange way.You gain bonuses (health or other stuff) when killing foes fast and chaining hit-combos without getting hit yourself. Find random upgrades through the levels or gain extra ink (=gold) when passing special trials. (Double) jump, duck, or dash as long as you want (you still take damage), throw grenades or use a special power when not shooting or slashing enemies. Platforming is not very difficult, the challenge lies more at not getting hit. Enemies attack you on sight, and the traps that came straight out of an Indiana Jones movie (sawblades, fire spitting mouths, spikes,...) can reduce your healthpoints very quickly, while regaining health is not so easy. The game contains many bosses, no idea how many but I saw a lot of them. Most of the time they killed me. The game is divided into three comic books (=chapters), all of them feature completely different terrain and enemies. After the jungle come some heavy weapons and nazis, finally some aliens. You need to kill the bosses of each chapter to unlock the next book.Local two-player mode is supported and great fun. Played with controller, no idea if this game is fun with kb+m. 3440x1440 works fine.Just one more run. Just one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic roguelike 2D shooter that is well worth the price of entry, on discount or not. Far too many roguelikes feel like players need to be punished for dying, they believe that taking everything away is a fun concept, but they often fail to properly balance the game in a meaningful way that doesn't leave the player feeling like their time is being wasted. Every new game of Fury Unleashed I get better, I get further and I am always grinding on those ink blots to upgrade my player for the future. They are often generous with the drops that you are given and even when you don't find an upgrade, you can convert them to ink. The game also allows you to carry at least two firearms to swap between and I really appreciate that. This is what you'd get if they combined metal slug with a RPG and they've done a very good job.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers of Fury Unleashed clearly put a lot of effort into making the game play smoothly. You can fully remap the controls (plus some novel and handy extra options, like dropping through platforms or jumping just by pressing down or up), shoot in all directions (an aspect strangely absent from even modern games like this), and actions like jumping, stomping, and dashing all feel appropriate and responsive.It's hard to even remember all the times I've thought something was considerately handled by the devs while playing (the most recent example being that extra objectives you sometimes get are paused when fighting a boss). You can teleport around the map, which is both convenient and keeps your combo counter going. The combo timer mechanics are fun, exciting, and flexible enough that I don't feel super stressed playing with it (I usually struggle with that aspect). Upgrade points can be reallocated at any time, a feature I really appreciate. The game is definitely challenging, which can be mitigated by upgrading, but between being able to remove upgrade points and improving my own skill with the trickier mechanics, I feel like the game will be enjoyable for a very long time.There's quite a variety of weapons, and I've liked all the ones I've tried in different ways. In other games, it's often a bit disappointing switching to a new weapon with better damage but less fun mechanics, but I'm generally pretty happy trading up here. The armor is a tad boring, but useful. I've seen several superpowers, and like all of them better than the starting one. I'm surprised they didn't include an option to switch what you start with.The game looks and sounds good. You can pick some customization options for your character's appearance and their starting weapons. The music ramps up with your combo counter. The comic book theme is well integrated and charming.It's a really solid, fun game. Easily recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING ROGUELIKE! GREAT VISUALS AND GAMEPLAY.JUST BUY THIS GAME BUT FIRST READ MY TIPS AND LEAVE A LIKE OR AWARD.CHEERS- Feel free to start on easy if you're not familiar with the mechanics but if you have played games like Neon Abyss, Hades or Enter the Gungeon, it should be second nature barring any button remapping.- Focus unlocking and upgrading skills that involve the Combo Meter and Ink Gain. The meta progression revolves around gathering Black Ink from defeated enemies and the Combo Meter will increase the amount of ink you earn as you increase the combo.- Combo Shields are your best friend! Once you unlock Combo Shields, you gain a shield up to a max of 3 for every increment of 5 in a combo. A shield gained at 5, 10, 15, etc etc. These shields block one hit each and make it so your combo isn't broken. You can regain a shield by reaching a multiple of 5 in your current combo. If you're at 19 combo and lose a shield, when you kill your next enemy, you will gain back the shield.- You can refill the Combo Meter in many ways such as: Shooting/Hitting/Killing an enemy, picking up ink, teleporting, standing next to a chest/Inkmaster/Vlad/etc.- Starting ranged weapon choice is mostly up to personal preference. I recommend the Shotgun, the spread is nice because even if only one bit of the shot hits, it keeps the combo count up.- Starting melee weapon is personal preference, they all have the same damage.- When playing, you can get new weapons and armor. Pay attention to not just the damage or the armor rating, but also what bonuses they have. It might be best to keep a piece of armor that has a lower armor rating or is even broken, but has a great bonus. For example, you can have gloves that have a Lucky Reload bonus which is a percent chance to auto-reload your weapon, even if the gloves have no durability, the bonus stays. For weapons, you can get an idea of how they function by paying attention to the clip size, DPS and Single Bullet Damage. Something that has a low clip size and low damage per bullet, but has a high DPS means it's most likely a shotgun style weapon.- Use the environment to your advantage and remember that you don't always need to be running or dodging. Slower movement can help with better positioning to dodge enemy bullets.SHARE YOUR TIPS PEOPLE

_childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed:~~~~~~~~~~~~As a young tadpole, I couldn’t wait to get my three fingers on my favourite monthly comic books. I used to devour them like a hungry beast as soon as I had them in my little green hands. I always found it amazing how these comic book creators could come out with new stories and twists so quickly and publish books month in month out for decades. Others were not so lucky. For instance, the creator of the dashing hero, “Fury”, only published 3 comic books before running out of creativity. But boy, they were something! This Fury guy came up against incredible armies, villains from different eras and even from space. The guy could do some damage, and you are going to relive those adventures in Fury Unleashed! Fury Unleashed is a fast-paced action roguelike side-scrolling platformer game developed and self-published by Awesome Games Studio on the 9th of May 2020 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on Xbox One, PS4 and Nintendo Switch. The game consists of 3 comic books that have four chapters each and include a main boss fight. There are 4 levels of difficulty in this game, but you’ll only be able to play in the easy or hard difficulty at first. The other 2 levels would probably be a lot harder, but I can’t tell you in detail as I have not yet managed to finish the game on the hard level of difficulty.  After selecting one of the two heroes available to you on your first attempt (there are nine heroes to unlock and you can create a personal hero through the Steam workshop), you‘ll be fighting either solo or with a friend on your local machine in the Amazon Jungle first, then in a secret Nazi base, and finally in an Alien mothership for your last adventure. The game is challenging to say the least, and I strongly suggest playing in the easy mode of difficulty for a while so you can level up your character after each attempt and earn skill points which you can use to upgrade him/her, hopefully making your next playthrough easier and moving on to the next book. The gameplay is basically moving from one room to the next, collecting as much black ink as possible by killing all the enemies within the room and, of course, avoiding being hit too frequently. The trick is to keep your combo alive so each time another foe falls while the combo is live, the enemies will drop more black ink when they die. They will also drop gold but in a small amount. Make sure you collect as much gold as possible as you will need to purchase health and some other goodies.  These goodies will come through chests and personality icons throughout the chapters. The conventional chests will usually give you either a new range weapon or armour, and by the way, they are free but are not necessarily better than what you are currently carrying. The red chest will usually give you stunning items/skills, but it will cost in life points, sometimes quite heavily; you might lose up to 80 per cent of your health for these items or skills. Do think twice before you take what is on offer as you really don’t know what the next room looks like. It will be the same when you meet the Devil Icon and Vlad the Peaceful, There are a few other character icons, as well as portals, but I’ll let you discover them as you play.  The other things to be careful of in each of the room are the obstacles. For example, you’ll have skulls on walls spitting fireballs or acid and giant circular saws (fixed or moving) in the Amazon comic book levels, wall-mounted machine guns in the secret Nazi base, and lasers on the Alien mothership, to mentioned a few.  Each room will also have breakable items, such as vases and crates, and some of them hold gold which is always good, so don’t hesitate to smash them as you see them. In each of the books, chapter one is usually the easiest to navigate, although that also will depend on what upgrade you might acquire during the chapter, such as new weapons or amour. But as soon as you manage to reach the second chapter, the difficulty will increase rapidly, and you might enter a few rooms that hold a mini boss. In fact, there are two mini bosses’ rooms in chapters two and three, and you might take on severe damage fighting those bosses ahead of the ultimate fight in chapter four. Between the three comic books, there are 30 mini bosses as well as 9 main bosses to defeat (3 in each comic book), which dramatically increases the replayability in this game. What is also very important to know is that when you die, you restart the game from the first comic book until you manage to beat the 3 main bosses of that book. If you manage to do so, you will be able to start your next playthrough from the second comic book if you wish. And it will be the same if you beat the three main bosses in the second comic book; you’ll be able to play the third comic book straight away on your next playthrough. Personally, I prefer to start from the Amazon book as it will take quite a while to level up and therefore earn an extra skill point. I played Fury Unleashed solo and must say that it is staggeringly addictive, and if you love tough games as I do, it will be very hard to drag yourself away. As far as I’m concerned, it’s bloody MARVELLOUS!   Fabulous comic-style graphics and the soundtrack is a cracker! Stacks of enemies to fight against, including 30 mini bosses and 9 main bosses. Significant Skill tree upgrade and fabulous gamepedia which includes hero and enemy statistics. You have full control support but can play with your keyboard if you like. Positives:~~~~~~~+	Fabulous artwork+	Stacks of enemies to fight within 3 comic books+	Stacks of weapons and armour+	30 mini bosses and 9 main bosses+	9 different heroes to unlock and the possibility to create your own in the Steam workshop+	Single-player, local co-op and remote play via Steam+	Each playthrough is different+	Good skills tree and excellent gamepedia+	very addictive and bloody MARVELLOUS+	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Give us more Fury comic books!Let’s take on armies from a different era! Smash goons, mini bosses and main bosses; it’s time to let loose the Fury Unleased!9/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!Review written by THE CPT FROGGY for

The game is meant to be hard but if you're finding things a little too difficult, you can lower the difficulty with the same rewards (Aside from a few achievements), which is a much more enjoyable approach to the game. I didn't run into much trouble while playing, just the end game grind. It's recommended to have enough levels before facing the end boss, he can be difficult, even on the easier mode. Can't complain about anything else, just enjoy this faced paced game for a fair price.Total Score = 76/100.GAMEPLAY:Fury Unleashed is a combo-driven roguelite action platformer - each kill you score increases your combo. Hit certain thresholds and your damage resistance and healing powers will become more noticeable. The game was created by combining inspiration from modern roguelite platformers, like Dead Cells and, Rogue Legacy with nostalgic memories of old-school platformer shooters, like Contra and Metal Slug.SIMILAR GAME LIKE THIS? / REVIEWER PREVIOUS EXPERIENCE:Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy■■■■■■■□□□ 7 / 10A fun fast paced game!RECOMMEDED SPECSIt'll run on anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading a review is not enough? Want to see some footage? Check the link and watch some game footage for yourself and decide if this game is worth your time:Currently, the Humble bundle Choice offers 3 Great games, one of them is Fury Unleashed. A 2D side scrolling action shooter with a lot of RPG elements and epic Boss fights.Do you know Awesome Games Studio? Well let me tell you I did, while playing Oozi or Yet Another Zombie Defense. Thinking that this game studio pretty much sucks and will lose itself in the mundane world of average games. Well now after Fury Unleashed I have to think differentlyAh! PEW PEW PEW! Shoot them, slide along, buy some guns. There is the Giant tarantula, you lost 3 times to her! Kill it!It is amazing how simple a game can be but yet so amazingly difficult and complex. When I started this game I just expected shooting and running. But the game delivers so much more. It starts with a customizable character, level ups and the best parts weapons. So many Weapons, they did a great job here. Every weapon feels completely different, the grenade launcher feels so impactful when he hits. The Laser gun with it rapid fire feels tremendous. Now lets talk about the Gameplay. You jump, you stomp, you crack heads with melee weapons, and you dash around. The Game is settled in to segments, and you run from map segment to map segment killing everything and getting your Combo timer high. The higher it is, the more money you get and the higher the chance of healing orbs and potions. But the best feature are the bosses. They are massive and everyone needs a strategy, sometimes its just dashing and shooting but then again on other parts they have different forms and patterns to memorize. In total this game is awesome and not what I expected when I initially started to play it.+ a lot of different enemies every unique in their skill sets and attack patterns+ Unique hero with customizable body and level up system+ Different Bosses with unique skill sets+ Grenades and unique special skills for your guy+ hard mode+ levels have different build-ups with treasures to find+ special missions during the normal gameplay- Bosses are far too much of bullet sponges- RNG based item finding can ruin your day (I got 4 different grenade launchers during a game)Fury Unleashed offers an addictive 2D action game with unique enemies and a giant effort to the action-roguelike games. There is not much to say only that you need to live with the fact it's done via unity game assets and can look a bit awkward.So who will enjoy this game? Do you like Roque like action games? Need something more modern than Roque Legacy? Did you love the gameplay of Skul the Hero Slayer? Well in this case this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I had first played Fury Unleashed almost a year ago when it had a different name and was still in early access.  I thought it was pretty cool, but I moved on from it pretty quickly.  By the time I was ready to come back to it the devs had almost finished the game and were exiting early access, so I figured i’d wait.  Glad I did, as the current version shows all the time, effort, and listening to player feedback that the developers put into this game.The presentation looks great, controls are smooth, and the gameplay in general is a lot of fun.  I also love the way you can scale the game’s difficulty to suit your tastes.  This is necessary because once you die during your playthrough, you go back to the beginning and lose all the cool power-ups you’ve acquired.  There are permanent upgrades you can buy with the skill points you accumulate, but they are more about health and keeping your combo meter lasting longer.  If not for the ability to scale back the difficulty, I would have been discouraged to abandon this game a lot earlier.Overall, even with the difficulty scaled back, there’s still some grinding involved to get your character to the point where he can survive long enough to beat all the bosses.  But I found it to be part of the fun, rather than a chore like it is in similar games of this type.  Plus, there’s a good selection of bosses to defeat, only some of which I came across.  I’ll definitely be coming back to this one for more playthroughs to see the rest of them.To the developers - great job.  I hope this game finds its audience and we see more great titles from you in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is like if Dead Cells and Metal Slug had a baby where that child is raised properly but doesn't necessarily succeed its own parents and just exists as a good and fun product.While I've played plenty of games of this genre by now, I think this game is pretty unique with how you are playing a comic book character, named Fury, who explores different pages and panels of a comic book that gets filled out as you progress through it. It's a cool idea for level design and storytelling where you see Fury's journey as they experience the typical lifestyle of a comic book hero as they slay villains and save the world, but Fury is in distress because he gets contacted by a mysterious entity who warns him that his creator is moving on. This sparks Fury to go on a quest to prove himself worthy of more material. It becomes the character's desperate fight to stay relevant. As is pretty standard for comic books, the character being named "Fury" is very identical to the naming convention for these hero-like characters. This is not at all a bad thing, however; as I think it makes it all the more natural to the idea of the game being played out in the style of a comic book, and even the enemies he fights are sort of typical and what you could expect. The game spans across three books (or levels) where each level has three chapters to it. Each chapter has a miniboss or two and the book's final boss is located within the third chapter. There is a fourth comic book as well that you reach once you have beaten the boss of each level, and this fourth comic book is what concludes the story and reveals an interesting twist. The first comic book focuses on bugs and ancient creatures, the third comic book focuses on an alien invasion . . . all typical stuff for a comic book. The second book, which is also kind of typical? It features Neo-Nazi's who apparently developed a time traveling machine. I'm pointing this out more specifically because I always thought it was interesting that in storytelling the Nazi's are always of a genius intellect and technologically advanced. Just look at Captain America or the Nazi's in Call of Duty's zombie mode where they developed laser guns and stuff.With this being a roguelike, you start over from the beginning of the level if you die but the game has an XP and level-up system where you can empower your character after each run. Killing enemies drops ink that you collect to spend in the skill tree and part of the gameplay here is to build up and maintain your 'combo' to increase the multiplier so that ink drops in larger quantities. Even better is that it is completely free to respec your build in case you want to try something new, which I took advantage of if a build I opted for didn't seem to work very well. Something else that I liked was that you can skip ahead to the next level from the character screen once you've beaten the boss of the previous level, preventing you from having to replay entirely from the first comic book. This can allow for speedier or less tedious progression but you may find yourself underpowered since you skipped previous levels and therefore would not have collected as many weapons and gear.Speaking of weapons and gear, I feel like this is where the game was truly lacking. What makes games like this so great, where there is the RNG factor to the drops you can get, is the game having hundreds of drops to collect and pray upon should you come across something really good in previous runs. It's what made a game like The Binding of Isaac so fun, you never knew how your run would go. This game has a good variety of weaponry but I didn't like that you had to 'unlock' the blueprints by locating a specific NPC somewhere in the level, where they didn't always spawn, and then you'd have to take the blueprint to a separate NPC, who was guaranteed to spawn somewhere in the level after you collected a blueprint, but there's always that chance of dying and losing your new gun before you can unlock it for future runs. A lot of the guns seemed very situational, weak, or just overall worthless where you quickly learn that the winning combination is really just a standard rocket launcher and grenade launcher. Your starting weaponry is between pistols, an SMG, and shotgun, so you'll have to find any other weapon you like through chance as you play the game. The armor as well is lacking and there seems to be even less of it to find or look forward to. It adds protection to you, where you can take a few free hits without losing your combo, but a lot of the passive bonuses or effects to the armor also seemed rather pointless most of the time. While the game was fun, it was pretty easy at least for me. It wasn't really until the fourth comic book level that I was met with some challenge, as this level mixes it up and plays differently to the previous three levels you will have conquered. It's very important to learn how to stomp the heads of the more basic enemies as this will be an instant death for them unless they are shielded, and the rest of it is generally just dodging around the map as it becomes somewhat of a bullet hell, especially with the bosses, but as is the case with games of this design, you'll get better the more you play and familiarize yourself with the patterns of the enemies you come across.Of course, I died a few times before reaching the final level due to taking too much damage and not finding methods to recovering my health, but it's not too hard of a roguelike and I did still have a lot of fun with it. The developer here doesn't seem to have very many games in their portfolio but I think they have a winning recipe if they focus on games of this nature. I'd be interested in playing more games like this coming from them as they improve and become more experienced.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best (but also one of the hardest) platformers I've ever played. You defeat enemies with both your gun and melee weapons, and by doing so without getting hit your combo meter rises. The higher your combo, the more perks you get to help you to beat the game. This works surprisingly well, and the game offers a huge variety in weapons, enemies and bosses to keep you hooked for many hours. The default (hard) difficulty is very hard imo and requires a lot of practice (and luck). I've never managed to finish the final boss of the second comic at this difficulty setting. Luckily there's an easy difficulty available, where you can tweak all settings to your own liking. This is really great to prevent frustration, more games should offer this. Very, very recommended!
