_childDocuments_.review: I had a fun time with this one. The hit-box on your dude seems slightly smaller than the model, similar to those crazy shoot-em-ups with the giant bosses. That helps in making feel like you're a badass; zipping around, wracking up combos and avoiding damage by the skin of your teeth. They put a lot effort into making this accessible too, with Easy Mode having sliders which allow you to adjust how much damage you take, the health of the enemies, etc, letting even terrible players like me finish these things! If I have one complaint, it's that it doesn't take too long to unlock all the starting options and there's no more than four choices (unless I missed something). Would've been nice to start with some of the more powerful options.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a very long early access phase in which even the title was changed. I've played it back then, wasn't fully convinced, but definitely saw potential in it. Now, almost a year after its release, I came back and found it pretty satisfying. The developers really did a good job in fleshing most parts out. It's difficult (as I like it), the artwork (especially of the bosses) is great and some effects are insanely cool. I also like the amount of weapons, although they don't change much of my playstyle. But my praise comes with some reservations. The skill tree is not super convincing. Points are received slowly and the skills are generic. I usually knew, which things I wanted to improve and never saw a reason to reskill. I don't like the music so much, it could also have more variety. And last, the randomness of the appearing items can be frustrating. Sometimes, you have to play through a chapter with an old weapon, but since the enemies HP are increased after every chapter transition, it can then take long to kill them. Over all, I enjoyed the 13h I've played this game, but would recommend it for half the price (i.e. 10€).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for May 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 1st, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Take the rogue-lite genre, add in a comic book aesthetic and story about a comic book character coming to life and you’ll find a rather solid and interesting game.  Players are here to take down enemies, and there are more than enough of them for players to fight through.Fury Unleashed is a hard but fair rogue-lite.  The game will require a high level of precision at times but also offers numerous bonuses and upgrades as players play through it.  Player’s builds are mostly customized by the weapons and items they find. Fury Unleashed looks great too, the boss battles feel quite epic, the enemy choices are solid, and something was making me want to keep coming back even after my session.  I wish the developers went a little further with the comic style, but there’s enough here to shine.Pick this up if you want a solid Roguelite.  This will never rival the top tier of the genre, but it is extremely enjoyable.  There’s also a difficulty option if you want an easier playthrough and the game becomes too challenging.  If you’re not a fan of roguelites, this one might not speak to you. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, only buy on sale. Definitely not worth 20$.Fun for a few hours with friends but very quickly a lot of flaws come in to play. You end up fighting against the extreme oversaturation of environmental damage rather than the enemies and for a game that incentivizes fast gameplay and keeping up your combo (which expires pretty fast, even with upgrades) the amount of fireball or poison traps laid out directly in front of each doorway you enter or daisy chained back to back is frankly unacceptable.For the first chapter its manageable at least to some degree, but once you get to the second chapter things get exceedingly worse. There are many times where you will get quests that involve you having to only use melee for the next few kills to get a reward and on the second level it seems like half the enemies explode into 3 grenades the second you kill them, making melee unviable and the quest practically useless.The worse issue however is that co-op seems entirely like it was patched in just to say there was co-op and no balancing was done to make it actually good. The game revolves around keeping ur combo up and although each player killing something will refresh the timer on the other players combo; both players combo counters are separate. This forces you to have to compete for kills to keep ur shields up rather than work together. Also for some reason all resources and quests progress are shared but only 1 person can claim the quest reward or use the resources, making you extremely stretched thin on firepower. If not to make it worse, if 1 player dies, they will be revived on the next level... with none of their items. 250 gold you spent for 1 player to get 10% bonus crit rate? completely gone and wasted.That being said, I think this game has potential to be a super fun game with friends despite its flaws but I strongly recommend not to buy this at full price, you will not get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it is a fresh change of pace from what I have been playing recently, but this game really hits the spot for me!! I like to think of it like a platformer 'binding of issac' type game. I am sure there are many other games out there but this does everything well!! You literally are running and gunning jumping dodging and melee-ing in a very smooth fashion...Each of the worlds/comics have 3 levels with increasingly difficult enemies and then a final boss. You also collect new weapons, armour and abilities as you progress too so it evens out. Every time you die you can level up your hero too and allocate points for perks that you keep each new run. For me, the starting weapon is already really good so I don't think RNG plays too much into things as you can play to your playstyle and equip what you want on your various runs. One thing I am not super hot on is the combo meter, where you gain more ink (currency or points, I think) the higher yours is. But that forces you to really blow through some of the rooms in hopes of keeping your combo going, and the downside to this is there is a lot of stuff that will kill you. Stuff will pop out of the walls, enemies will aggro you and there will be a bunch of fire or acid being shot from the walls or spikes on the floor. All of this leads to a slower play for me, but regardless it doesn't really affect too much for me since I have beaten all 3 first world bosses and can now begin a game on world 2.Anyway, this is a good pick up and play for an hour game. It has enough progression and enough replay ability to keep you coming back, as I will be too !

_childDocuments_.review: Not a good rogue-like. Too little changes between runs and when you inevitably fail, you only get points to spend in a skill tree. Progression in the skill tree is fine at first then it's too slow, this is mitigated by the fact that the skill tree is mostly useless aside from upgrading critical damage and a combo shield which is the only real defense you have, aside from getting good, because you get very little health refills during a run.Also, difficulty spikes considerably at the second comic book (each level is a different comic book) because enemies take double the time to kill and your character doesn't scale that fast so it all becomes too slow and grindy. Switching to Easy mode barely helps.I was also unimpressed by the story and how it's delivered, I'd have preferred a dumb story to this uninspired commentary on the struggle of comic book artists.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a huge number of side-scrolling shooters out there, quite a few of them are roguelites too. Fury Unleashed doesn’t do too much to shake up the gameplay in either department, but it does have a design and aesthetic that makes it stand out. Fighting your way through the panels of a comic book ends up being a really enjoyable way to experience a game.Abbreviated Review: Each level of Fury Unleashed takes place across the panels within the pages of a comic. You start in the top left and make your way to the bottom right with whatever path you choose. Not every panel is connected to every nearby panel, so some paths may funnel you one direction. Whichever way you go though, enemies will be ready and waiting to take you on.The aesthetic isn’t necessarily in your face in most parts of the game. At a glance, it might be hard to even tell that it was meant to be perceived that way. However, a quick look at the map makes it easy to see. There are tiny bits throughout that help make it more obvious. Pickups and mini-quests are displayed as little animated icons that look drawn onto the levels. Once you move to these, you can see what new gear or mission they obtain. The same icons are used in some scenarios when enemies are spawned in on the screen.The comic book design plays into the experience just enough to keep you invested in the way things happen in the game and the narrative it conveys. Rather than typical pickups, killed enemies drop different types of ink used to upgrade your character/level up and purchase upgrades at shops throughout the game. Also, when you head into a new level, it’s a whole new comic book with an entirely new set of environments and enemies. That is, of course, pretty typical, but the use of a comic book with a little lead-in gives it just enough flavor to make it interesting.Roguelites are inherently supposed to be difficult. It’s sort of their primary function to keep you failing early on so that you keep trying it. Fury Unleashed delivers on that, but maybe a little too well. Each comic is split into four levels including a final boss level. I spent several hours just trying to make it through the first set of levels in the comic. Sometimes I wouldn’t even get to the final boss - each of which you face with whatever health you had going in. Without many health pickups, this was very difficult. I ultimately had to turn it down to the “easy” difficulty just to get out of this monotony.Once I made that change, I managed a ton of progress very quickly. Much like Wargroove, you can manipulate this difficulty making it as challenging or easy as you wish. Even on the normal setting, it made things significantly easier – perhaps due to all of the practice I had failing. What this allowed, in part, was for me to gain levels and get upgrades at a significantly faster rate. This made it possible for me to do a lot more in the normal game mode. Unlocking ways to maintain my combo (and gain more from having combos) showed me how important this feature was.Combos, as you would expect, are garnered from you dealing damage to and killing enemies. Each one raises it by one. The higher your combo, the more ink you get from each kill, and thus the more progress you’re making in the upgrade system. Many of the upgrades allow you to keep your combo longer, protect you from losing the combo with ‘shields,’ and most importantly allow you to get more health pickups. Health is a hot commodity in Fury Unleashed. Very few things return it, and one of the first upgrades is increasing your max health. While it’s possible to survive with raw skill, being able to survive more hits (especially on bosses) is key.If it wasn’t for my discovery of how important combos were or that a bit of time in easy mode, I might have given up on this game. I didn’t enjoy getting stuck so early for so long. One thing I find beneficial in roguelites is giving you the ability to get reasonably far and seeing more of the game early on. Even if you still have to play many more hours to actually in. If you’re going to fail, that failure state should come with learning more about the game as a whole, not just the half dozen enemies in the first levels.The somewhat subdued story that goes along with Fury Unleashed takes a look at the nature of being a creator. It explores how fans and critics can influence people and how frustrating that can be. It appealed to me because I also deal with that to a small degree. While it’s certainly not part of my day-to-day, it can be a tough experience. Mixing that in with the cool aesthetic of well-crafted sidescroller shooting and fun enemies to face off against makes this game well rounded. It may not be the best of its genre, but it is certainly worth checking out if you get the opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is .  If you're looking at the screenshots or gameplay videos and think this might even be remotely up your alley, you're probably right.While your first few rounds may leaving you feeling a bit confused or concerned about the combo system, once it settles in I think most will find it sufficiently rewarding to push the action along at breakneck speed, while not being so forceful or punishing to push you away.In a similar vein to how DOOM (2016) rewards the player for aggressively engaging the combat system, so does Fury Unleashed.  Health is rewarded for pushing yourself harder and faster through the action, with the ever increasing risk of not being able to handle what the game will throw at you while you're frantically trying to maintain that combo.  It feels frantic, but in a good way.The game also does a great job of making your character feel like a bad ass out of the gate, and then amping that up even further as you progress through finding additional upgrades.As far as Early Access goes, this feels like a winner already.  Well worth the current price, you really can't go wrong here.

_childDocuments_.review: I first picked up Fury Unleashed when it was still known as Badass Hero. At the time, I thought a it fun little run-n-gun rogue-lite with much-needed persistent progression, making it a bit addictive, but its central combo mechanic made it feel more punishing then other entries in the genre and even with the upgrades it didn't feel like I made much progress. After trying it again sometime after launch, I can say it has improved. I was actually able to finish the first world finally and see part of the second. Since updating this review last, I was then able to finish the remaining worlds on hard (the game's "normal") and the final boss on easy. That fight in particular is a massive difficulty spike I wouldn't mind seeing tuned a bit in later updates.Since the first time I played it, Fury added a story: A metaplot about the author of the titular character's action-packed comic book that rings not only believable but poignant to a fellow artist like myself. Once a staple series, Fury's comic has come under fire in recent years by internet hecklers and the artist is suffering burnout. As Fury battles his or her way through their greatest hits, glimpses of the real world are shown through notes and social media posts. The kind words from Fury's fans left a big smile on my face.My original thoughts mostly hold true on the mechanics: Remember to use your air dash and stomp, they help a lot, especially since dashing on a flat surface allows you to sprint until you run off the edge of something. Rewarding you with health drops for keeping your combo up is interesting, and at least better implemented then trying to get health back in most other rogue-ish action games. However, there are always points where you are taking so much incoming fire its difficult to keep your combo up, though some of the upgrades can alleviate this. As in Rogue Stormers or Immortal Redneck, the unlockable weapons and persistent upgrades make the difference towards actually being able to complete a run. Presumably if I kept at it I could beat the final boss on hard.It has surprisingly tight controls, an exaggerated, colorful art style and a wide variety of nasty weapons to try out, though some have to be unlocked first by finding sketches of them and successfully carrying them to the "inkmaster", one of the shopkeepers. When I originally played there was no option for a female player character or coop play, but these have since been added. There is also Steam Workshop support, allowing you to download and use custom head textures for your character.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest problem this game has is that it doesn't have any I frame moves, no roll, dodge or similar that gives I frames. An roguelike can be played without it BUT Fury Unleashed is pretty much a bullet hell/roguelike with very small rooms. Small rooms are great for platform Roguelikes, Bullethell games want/need big arenas. The amount of Stuff flying at you (sometimes literally unavoidable when you enter the room) is obnoxious. Thats why this game sorely needs a dodge/dash/roll with I frame. They could still patch it in for the dash you get, but why they didn't do it is baffling.The core gameplay is fun and it looks really good, but the amount of projectiles kill the flow of the game completely. Also too few Item choices/powerups. Starter Weapons are greatly underpowered if you start a comic book after the first one.The game could be 10x more enjoyable with a few tweaks, I Frames for the dash, Unlockable stronger starter weapons, maybe less projectile spamming, and Health globes that actually give a decent amount of health.

_childDocuments_.review: A very satisfying, tough and fun though somewhat one-note roguelite. I had a blast with Fury Unleashed and it provides a VERY polished and difficult core experience that is highly rewarding to get in grips with. While constant upgrades do help Fury is heavily action-focused and fast; and is so in a glorious fashion. As said that's the one thing Fury does though; for a roguelite even with the different weapons every run feels pretty much the same. But as is Fury doesn't outlast itself either, I got through it way before getting bored and do intend to jump back in for a bit more. Audio-visually Fury is busy to a point of being obtuse at times but the spectacle is worth it. Good time all around as long as the players reflexes are in order still. I played solo only and the default difficulty is balanced plenty well and I didn't feel like I was missing anything by not playing coop.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I find it very strange, I have to give a negative review to this one. Generally I don't like roguelite games, even elements of them - for many reasons, but it does not really matter. Sometimes I give them a chance if I find them appealing enough to try, and sometimes, they do surprise me (like Children of Morta).Fury Unleashed, for the first 3 hours, really felt refreshing, and I finished the first world on a good note, expecting a good ride for the rest of the game.But as soon as I went to the second world, things turned to ♥♥♥♥ rather quickly, and all the flaws of the game surfaced right away.1. Starting loadout is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can select only one melee weapon out of four, and one gun out of four. All of them, though, are very basic and useless for the harder enemies of the second world2. Since levels are randomized - so are weapons. Chances of finding something good are very slim, and what is even stranger is that in the first world I used to find better weapons than in the second one. Logic behind this is unknown to me...3. Power-ups, both in-level and the ones which are a part of progression are mostly useless, and are something like '+5% damage resistance', or '+50% increase of the orb collection range'. Needless to say, picking them up does not help at all4. Progression after the first world gets veeery slow. You can literally spend 30 minutes playing only to get 1 progression point which would not even be enough to upgrade something5. Levels themselves are often very small and cramped. While the first world is tolerable - in the second ♥♥♥♥ is flying from all sides and often you find yourself simply unable to escape any damage. There are enemies which explode upon death, but they may be positioned in such a way that you will be hit regardless of how you decide to approach them6. There is never enough money to buy anything, and strangely, again, in the first world I used to get more money than in the second. Why? Who knows7. The game also gives almost no chance to heal yourself. Even with upgrades for health orbs - when you get them you will only get a few health points, which, while having 200-220 max HP, does not help at all. This means that if during a pretty good run you encounter a cramped room with a lot of enemies (some, maybe, legendary ones) - you can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the rest of the run, since it's easy to lose almost all your health in such situations8. Legendary enemies, by the way, give almost no reward. You would expect them to be actually worth all the hassle - but no. Some XP, 10 coins - and there you go, enjoy the rest of the runOn the upsides, the game looks great, controls well, and bosses are amazing (with a few infuriating exceptions). But the strange shift in quality after the first world really put me off. I don't know what devs were thinking

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Has a lot of potential, but work to do. Only get this if you want to help forming the game!*Video contains gameplay, below is the reviewSince it just released in its early access state, there is still a lot of content missing. This isn't that big of a deal, if you don't mind following the state of the game and help shaping it up. Also meaning that the current version keeps you amused for a couple of hours at most, till the next content patch comes up.I personally play with a controller and I do think this game is made for it. Although, if wanted, it can be played with a keyboard and mouse. As for the controller, it feels smooth, has a valid standard layout (which can be changed if wanted) and suits well with the learning curve of the game itself.Unlike a few other rogue-likes I played, the missiles projected by enemies can't be dodged in any way (like dashing, down stomp) and must be avoided at all costs. This took me some time getting used to, and in some occasions due to RNG being a ♥♥♥♥♥, gave me unfair situations. Rooms filled with enemies, with projectiles coming from everywhere, nearly impossible to avoid. Be that as it may, it seems to be a core element of the game and in general works well apart from those few instances where you get blown to pieces (or atleast lose half of your HP when you where just doing so well!).Regarding RNG, there is a lot of it in this game, even the bosses are randomized by changing the layout of the environment. Which feels refreshing but as mentioned above, in some occasions can be a bit unfair.There currently are just a few different weapons (amongst others: smg, shotgun, bazooka, minigun) which are randomized by things like different reload speed, more magazine ammo, freeze/burn effect etc. You do have unlimited ammo, and only shoot with guns (atleast so far, no melee of any kind). While playing you find these weapons along with other items that you can either use for that playthrough or redeem for experience instead.The enemies feel very different from each other and the animations are well executed. Giving you that learning curve improving with each run you make. Meanwhile leveling up unlocking new abilities like more health, more drops, longer combo time, faster reload speed, etc. (mostly passive). Keeping your combo count up is also pretty important, advancing quickly from one stage to the other getting bonuses from the abilities you unlocked by leveling up in your previous runs.The music in its current stage is very boring, linear, its basicly one soundtrack that gets more intense when your combo count goes up. However, they mentioned in their early access FAQ this will be completly reworked and is just a placeholder for now. So all in all, this game has a lot of potential. It might be a bit steep for its current state, but may definitly be worth it in the end. I would only recommend getting this game if you want to try it out for now and help building the game to a solid final release.

_childDocuments_.review: It's seriously so good. Fury Unleashed focuses on run-n-gun and bullet hell elements, while using a rougelite platformer as a base. It's probably why i'd say it's the best rougelite i've ever played. There are like, two or three things with this game that i'd say are issues/annoyances. That's it. The vast, VAST majority of this game is just that fun.I have to say that hands down, this is one of the coolest and most unique settings for a game ever. You play as a comic book character running through his own comic series. The rooms you enter are comic panels, and you start from top right and exit bottom left. Each comic book has three chapters, and there are three main books to play. I sadly can't talk about the story without spoiling at least something, but trust me when I say it not only fits the style, but also isn't just about the story of each comic book - it's about the comic's fictional author.Gameplay time, and right off the bat, the movement feels incredible. It doesn't exactly have a high skill ceiling, but slowly optimizing your precision and timing is about as deep as it gets and that's honestly that's as deep as it needs to be. It's fast and smooth, and once you fully understand the movement, you'd be hard pressed to find any sort of jank or clunky feeling interactions.Now combining the movement with the combat, that's where it gets good. The vast majority of the massive weapon selection feel powerful and fun to use. And this game being a rougelite, there is a subtle yet noticeably increasing power curve. Enemies are more tanky and powerful, and so is the gear you find. I appreciate how it's not a huge jump in stats from the start to the end of the game. You could probably beat the game with your starting gear honestly, it would just take more time.There's also a lot of other systems at play that really enhance the gameplay, if not outright hold the whole thing together. There are merchants that generate randomly in various panel of each chapter, for example. Weapons, health, stat boosts, there's a lot of helpful stuff. There is also a pretty extensive skill tree you will slowly fill out that applies to each run (except the unlockable and side gamemodes). One of the more interesting mechanics, which is a HUGE part of what makes the game fun is the combo system. The higher your combo, the more gold and health drops you get. Maintaining a combo also keeps a upgradable damage shield up, so you have a little bit of leeway in maintaining your combo. Using the combo system isn't completely needed however, as your HP bar isn't measured in terms of single hit points, but rather a normal damage number-based hp. So you start out with a base 100HP which you can upgrade in the skill tree. Using the combo system is obviously the way to go however, and really speeds up the XP farming process for the skill tree (which didn't require grinding actually).Yeah 100% completion is actually really doable. By the time you get around to attempting the harder achievements, Your skill tree will be mostly complete and your power level will be WAY higher, not to mention your skill at the game. The unlockable and side modes are actually not that hard to complete (except for one which I WILL get to later....). The two unlockable modes are way more traditionally rougelike. Instead of a persistent skill tree, you get a random selection of skills at the end of each chapter based on how much XP you got. Definitely makes the game way harder, but this being a bullet hell game, it's more about dodging than being tanky. The combo system is your best friend in these harder modes.All the other achievements are challenge-based, and the hardest three achievements sound REALLY daunting, but by the time you get around to trying to get them, it's actually way easier than you'd expect. Even the rarest achievement according to steam's list didn't take nearly as long in comparision to other rougelikes i've played.That thing being the Superhot side mode. Nothing in this game comes close to the difficulty of this mode. I didn't expect it to be not only hard, but extremely annoying as well. The sad thing is it's not even the whole mode that's bad, it's specifically the second book. The hazards, enemies, and bosses are all horrible with the gimmicks of this mode. The main part is pretty easy - time only moves if you move. And although it can be helpful, it actually doesn't really come into play that much. The other little detail that completely ruins this mode is you have 1 hp. No upgrading it, no getting around it, nothing. You better get REALLY good at the bullet hell part of this game, because it will be the sole reason you die over and over. The main strat is just memorize enemy and boss attack patterns, and then also hope you get good enough rng with the weapons to minimize the time and chances you give bosses to kill you if you mess up with your dodges. This is the game mode that will teach you how to speedrun the game. Because you will eventually lose patience with being thorough exploring the chapters and just beeline to the exit. If you accidentally stumble into this mode before completing everything else in the game, you will be stuck on it until you get good enough to actually beat it. I finished this mode before trying any of the other modes, and then proceeded to destroy all the other modes with ease. It's so unreasonably hard relative to everything else in the game. I'm so glad it's just a side mode, but the fact you gotta finish it for one of the achievements does bring the whole game down if you're going for 100%.Despite Superhot's issues, it pales in comparision to how FUN and stylized this game is. It's the perfect blend of multiple genres, extremely creative aesthetic, and well thought out mechanics. And I didn't even mention the fact this game has Co-op!!! Absolute banger through and through, and I'm so sad that this game doesn't get nearly enough love and attention as it deserves. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game with amazing gameplay.Everything is so fluid, the traversal in this game is fantastic and the versitality that the player has is wonderful.Each room is modeled after a panel for a comic, but the comic aesthetic it's just that, an aesthetic, a particular art style of sorts, and I like it to remain that way because it doesn't get in the way of the actual game but instead helps it by complementing it.Then there's the beautiful and incredibly unique art style, I feel as if this is what puts a lot of people off because its different, not because its bad, I feel as if sometimes a lot of people might feel afraid by what they might not be familiar with, so if we're talking about an indie rogue-like without pixel art, then this is something that stands out a lot.But as I said it is a shame because the aesthetic is beautiful, its one of the things that I enjoy the most about the game.At first the only thing that truly bothered me about it was the actual face of my character, I just didn't liked him.But thankfully you can customize your characters color of skin, and face, you can add different masks that you unlock as you play along, plus you can also make use of the workshop, or even do what I did and add unique masks, and/or helmets from your favorite games.The gameplay it's really where is at as it usually happens with video games, and thankfully the combat system of the game is fantastic, as it is the rogue like progression.I don't really comprehend the complaints towards the difficulty of the game, maybe they aren't contemporary because the game as of the time that I'm writing this review includes, thankfully, different difficulty options, one of which is "easy" and lowers the difficulty of  the game significantly.It does this artificially by reducing the enemies health, and making the player take less damage.But suprisingly and once again, thankfully, the game also gives you the ability to customize this level of difficulty in case you want to make it harder, or easier.I'd like to really applaud the developers for giving this option, and for implementing it in such a way that the overall experience doesn't get affected in any negative way.This is really what has made this title one of my favorite rogue-likes right next to something like The Binding of Isaac.I specially enjoy how fast-paced, "cartoony" and gory the combat is.You can throw grenades, use an equipped melee weapon, and of course your main weapon is a gun, something that fires bullets.At the start you don't have much but naturally this being a rogue like, it has wonderful progression throughout the different levels, which eventually you'll find are filled with enemies, traps, and even mini bosses.See what I enjoy the most is the so called "flow" of the game, everything keeps the player going and not once did I felt constrained by anything that was happenning around me.I can even go as far as to say that I enjoyed this gameplay even more than something such as Dead Cells.The movement and flow of the combat systems, and the way that both of this systems work together is very satisfying, you can also find upgrades for your armor that change the aspect of your character for the current run.It is a wonderful game so far for what it offers and at the price that it offers it, I really wish the devs don't abandon this game, so far it doesn't seem like anything like that will happen but I really hope it never comes to something like that I wish for the game to become fairly popular to have more modding capabilites, perhaps even get the tools to create our own comics (levels) and allow for greater experiences than the already fantastic one that I had, and hope, other people will have.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 7/10This was on my wishlist and something i wanted to play for a little bit. I liked the artstyle of the game and i like roguelikes. Well after 15 hours of playtime and doing most of the achievements i could, here is what i liked and disliked. Fury Unleashed has a very weak story that fills very much like filler then anything structured and well made, but that is to be expected of a heavy gameplay focused roguelike. Artstyle was gorgeous and really well done. Black and white sections are a nice change of pace. Bosses are fun to figure out and fight. Each boss has their own like one pattern and they are copied into different elements which increases the boss variety. Example in comic 2 you fight 2 or 3 choppers and tanks each. so like 5 or 6 bosses but they are the same expect different elements they are based around like fire or acid. I mostly played on Easy and i think the balance of the game falls of massively in Comic 2 since enemies have more HP and take longer to kill whilst weapons and everything else seems to do the same amount of damage in terms of your damage output.  So the fast paced nature of killing enemies in Comic 1 is not possible from Comic 2 onward on Hard which is a shame i think. You can't really break the game and do insane amount of damage. Everything is in a controlled environment pretty much so it feels specially when i tried the final boss on Hard that the damage output i was doing was not enough. Like i started the Comic fresh ,or pistol start meaning i selected it without playing any of the previous comics before hand which you can do and you can tell the game was not really meant for this type of pistol starting ,so starting from scratch. You get a legendary weapon to choose but most of those weapons are useless and don't do enough damage. I think the combo system is flawed. Instead of focusing on just killing enemies it expect you to do it no damage which is kinda silly in my mind. Would make more sense to keep the combo going just by killing enemies instead of taking random bit of damage breaking the combo. I tried a few times on Hard to do it fast paced like in the first comic but it was not working which sucked. It also seems like the game has no synergy or connection between melee and weapon attacks, meaning if you attack with both melee and your weapon there is no bonus damage which is a bit of a shame. Items list is generic, weapons are generic i mean everything about it is stock roguelike stuff and nothing to really note about it. You can spend 2 to 5 hours on this just randomly playing or more if you want some of the achievements or most of them at least. I also think the game might be also be more co-op oriented which would explain the damage falling down the pipe in comic 2 and just the entire game being kinda meh. There is no good way to grind ink to level up and get skill points besides beating the game on Easy a bunch of times. No reward for it though like no achievement so it's a bit useless and the game might have the issue where if you upgrade everything then it becomes more fun and balanced but i could not be bothered to do that and if that is the case then bad choice/idea.So overall this is really fun and solid roguelike though it focuses more on gameplay then story. The balance is questionable it can still provide some resemblance of fun despite it's flaws. I would recommend getting it on sale or cheap and trying it out. I personally had so much fun playing through it for the 15 hours i did play. It's one of those games you kinda have to try to see if you like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed is a 2D Sidescrolling Stick-Shooter Run-and-Gun Rouge-Lite Comicbook Adventure. You play as the comics hero Fury, who is customizable. As Fury, you're on a quest to make your writer feel better about his trade. To do so you must blast and hack your way through the Comicbook pages and become the ultimate Hack and Blast Hero. Don't let the Gameplay and flow fool yourself. It's a "RUN AND GUN" Type of gameplay where it definitely shines the faster you are and the most combo you do. It's a combo-type of game.The game is therefore heavily set on kill combos and fast-paced action. You can even run a whole level on a single combo if you're fast enough. With a ton of weapons, and enemies the game is a non-stop action fest. Being a Rouge-Lite it's surprisingly forgiving in what you lose on death, but every time you die, you get stronger, and off to the pages of the comic once more and put your skill points into yourself in order to upgrade. You will be in a constant state of Die and Retry, but this only furthers what you're capable of. The Game definitely shines in co-op - I've played this Game with my brother for 5 hours and completed the game on hard with 80% Completion.The soundtrack is perfect for the mood and keeps the pace rolling. The graphics are creamy smooth, even in the most intense times. The controls are super responsive lending way to very satisfying gameplay. There is an easy mode, that's customizable, allowing you to tone down the game, great for new players. One of the most intense Run-And-Gun games I've played in a long time. Either new to the genre or a long time fan Fury unleased is a treat of a game.Only con: The price. I could've finished it way faster but I'm also playing videogames since I can think. You might need longer if you're a casual but videogame veterant will complete the game in less than 4-5 hours. I personally think its too much on what it asks without a discount but I got this game in a fanatical bundle and paid less then 50 cents. Absolutely worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: A high-octane platform shooter with a strong aesthetic. This review is my initial impressions after a few hours.While not quite reaching 'bullet hell' levels of danger on the screen, Fury Unleashed throws hell at you - at any one point, you'll be juggling fireball traps, blade traps, enemies, flying enemies, hidden enemies, and so on. Your task is to blast and slash your way through, and to do it quickly and efficiently. Building up your combo metre is key here. The balance on most weapons feels pretty good, with each having a niche, and with all of them being viable. There's no massive gulf between melee and ranged attacks. Your superpower and grenades can come in clutch, too.The progression is, perhaps, a bit slow, but there's plenty to unlock - improvements to your character, better drop chances, new starting weapons, new weapons you can find in the levels, new superpowers, new aesthetics, and new levels. There should be enough to keep you going for a long time in this game.The aesthetic is pulpy action comic, with a meta-narrative about the author's struggles with depression. It's fairly interesting, but don't get this game for the story. It's not a story game.Overall, I think this is a fun offering. It's part of the May 2021 Humble Bundle, so get it there rather than here.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very interesting. As with other roguelikes, the evolution persistence is limited to the character, not in the story, but it is realized in a way that being stuck in the same "chapter" is not too depressing or boring. The game blends classical elements present in classical roguelikes, such as mixing static enemies that plague the screen with small shots and moving enemies that do quite harm, with modern experiences, such as handling a lot of different range and melee weapons---classified by rarity level. The result is a nice degree of situation familiarity inherited from experience with other roguelikes and modern shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed really nails what it sets out to do as a fun, fast, action-oriented platform shooter, and the devs seem to have their heads on unusually straight, because the game isn't just good and fun, it also usually does exactly what it should do, a depressingly rare attribute that adds to that feeling of quality and enjoyment.If you like the video, it will deliver.  There used to be a free Prologue version here, as well, that let you play the beginning of the game and even save all your upgrades for the real game.  Seems like that's only available via itch.io now: Solid mechanics, with lots of nice action-oriented nuance, and a well-done hit chaining system that lets you just play for fun or really get into the game and work to keep your combo alive.Has metaprogression, which is both a positive and a negative, but the progression is not unlimited (so, once maxed, the rest is player skill) and generally enhances play as you unlock mechanical upgrades, like certain combo chain levels granting a safe hit, getting more XP for finishing an enemy with your grenade, or getting a hit chain timer extension for stomping enemies (yeah, you can stomp enemies).  You can also freely redistribute your metaprogress points, so you're never locked in and can use that to play with fewer bonuses or only specific upgrades if you like.  Like I said, the devs usually do the right thing.This is not kind of roguelite where you stack a mountain of passives until they play the game for you.  This is the kind where the core gameplay is so good that you're glad you have procedural levels to justify coming back more and more.Looks good, plays well, and delivers the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: Really enjoyable action rogue-lite that I have no problem recommending+Steam trading cards (5 drop, 9 to make card)Steam achievements (47, require luck, a lot of grinding and finishing the game on all difficulties)Local co-op (can also work in remote play, so technically even online) A huge amount of weapons and armors (all of whose can be 1 of 3 rarities)4 chapters (10 main bosses ) with unique minibosses (30 in total) and enemies (52 in total)The really enjoyable gameplay loopRPG elements with skill tree (earn exp in a run to improve your character for the next one)Steam workshop for new visual items2 bonus game modes - Superhot (world moves when you do) and Crypt of the Necrodancer (rhythm-based) If you are playing on easy you can adjust the game midflight (enemy hp, damage taken, hp received, gamespeed)  - more games should have this featureSome achievements are not pointless - they unlock new characters (9)You can customize starting loadout Ingame challenges I am really a fan of the soundtrack Random generation of levels and challenges in them (kill enemies in time, melee kills ...)Flawless boss kills matter (you will get to pick from 2 items instead of 1) You can customize your characters (male/female - hair, accessories, beard, war paint)Leaderboards (if you are into that)-I am not a fan of the self-reflective story honestly, especially the ending Unlocking new weapons is a choreThere is no point in replaying the last epilogue - it is hard and after the first fínish it doesn't offer anything (it has no weapon unlock and enemies drop minimum exp)Higher difficulty doesn't offer better rewards (it should really be higher difficulty = more exp or unique unlocks)some hits feel unfair (enemies spawning into existence behind you or dropping into a floor right into a trap)+/-I consider the first world to be the most interestingSome of the weapons look really unbalanced (damage is bit all over the place)The game is much faster than your average roguelike (supported by combo system that gives you exp multiplier)I would really like "flawless boss kills" in bestiary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem. _childDocuments_.review: Damn, this game is really good and the artwork is fantastic. It's a platform shooter with some twists. Basically you play through cells in a comic book and your goal is to make it to the final cell without dying. You can explore every cell if your really good and kill every bad guy or if your like me you try to find the quickest rout, skipping some cells, so you don't die. Each bad guy you kill drops ink, I assume this is the ink that was used to draw them, and if you die you can use it to level up your hero so you can make it further the next time.The implementation is fantastic and the gameplay really fun  ...but... it's really hard. I played it on easy and still kept dying over and over. The game play is designed to be this way though, your goal is to level your character up and see if you can make it further and kill more bad guys than the last time.I think it's great and it now has local co-op mode as well. The price is $12 which is really good for the quality of the game but the developers have said this on the store page..."At the current stage of development it would take about 12 hours to complete the game. The price will likely increase as we develop and add more content to it."So get in quick!Take a look at my video to see what some gameplay is like....Thanks for watching, please like, subscribe and comment.

_childDocuments_.review: My thoughts on Fury unleashed:In the duration that I have had the game its quite challenging especially for a 2D platformer. In the beginning its unforgivable as you won't have much, but once you gain momentum through leveling skill points, they boost your survivability. In a way it reminds me of Dead Cells as gradual progression is key to reaching the other stages or the end. On the contrary, there is a plentiful amount of weapons to choose from to use in slaying different enemy types that are diverse to each chapter. Lastly, one major component that keeps you standing are the allies that appear in random rooms who provide the player with a myriad of items or other things to traverse mass swaths of enemies. Even though there's parts that can make it tedious, a difficulty parmeter on easy  is a fantastic touch that you can adjust to fit your needs of how you wish to handle the game before moving to hard.Overall, to me the game is quite addicting if completion is the main goal here in an effort to grab everything availible at hand. Sure games like these aren't for everyone but if a game that has an underlying plot and levels that are filled with action and the unknown to be a combo racking machine then this is the perfect game to give a go.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR  10/10 Xom howls with laughter!What would the product be if you mixed together the creativity of Comix Zone, the unrelenting action of Metal Slug, and the audacity of action flicks from the 80's? Probably this. Fury Unleashed is the first game I want to review, and rightly so.To begin with, the Hero starts off with one SMG, one choppy blade, grenades, and boots of stomping. Throughout the course of the story, you get all the silly loot you could want and more. Freezing shrapnel grenades? Got 'em. Rocket launcher with poison warheads? Sure! Unholy blade? No problem. Triple jump boots? Go wild! In addition to this arsenal of fun, the enemies you face are varied and challenging in distinctive ways. In fact, the same deadly shenanigans you pull on them can just as easily apply to you. This is most noticeable in the second comic book, where enemy soldiers can (and will) use the same weapons you do.The RPG-style progression is another part of the game which really appeals to me. If you don't like the points allocation, or just feel like you use some game mechanics over others, disable or reduce the stuff you're not feeling and transfer to what you do want. Simple, to the point, and reinforces the comic background: You get to sketch the Hero. Aside from the goodies you grab from hacking and blasting bosses, you can buy more at the purple portals. This also includes stat upgrades for your damage and life bar.Audio is fairly simple in terms of both the Hero and the opposition. Where the audio really shines is the music. Not only does the background music for every comic feel very appropriate for the level it plays in, it swells and becomes more rich with your combo meter! Very gratifying, and a good way to add to gameplay.Level designs are fine, with panels ranging from basic transition hallways to death rooms with spikes and traps aplenty. The arenas you fight bosses in are suitably grand, and drive in the whole point of escalating your game right to the pay off. Environmental hazards also serve to keep you focused on your own movement, especially so when deciding whether to blast away the three small fry gunning for you or to close the gap and deal with the big mook first. A good thing in level design is that very few threats can take you completely off guard and even when they do, you quickly learn what to look out for. Rather than screw you over with cheap shots, the game will motivate you to become a more skilled player. The one random factor that can be a problem is the item generation, but even this is rarely enough to bust your playthrough.Awesome Games devs really put out a title that lives up to the studio name. I can't recommend it enough! Despite being an early access/development title, I only really found one bug worth mentioning. Sometimes, when transitioning down from the first panel in comics 2 and 3 (the very first), your Hero will slow down to a stop before falling into the second panel. That's it. Everything else is smooth and polished up.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently a good friend of mine turned me onto this game and this was a true gem of a find.First and foremost the game uses INK, yea INK as an in game currency. Considering my handle, I find this a very fitting game for me right off the bat! Let's talk about what this game isThis game takes place within 3 comic books, at first you will only have access to one as you need to beat 3 bosses from each comic to unlock the following comic. Oh and the bosses? They won't always be the same because each run in this game is different't. Considering how many weapons, items, enemies and bosses are in the game you won't get bored easily.One good thing this game does that a lot don't is gives you the ability to re spec your skill points at anytime. After any run you can either invest in new skills, unlocked skills. Or in this case "downgrade" a skill and take the points into another skill. This can make for some unique skill builds.When it comes to your character who you can play with there is a wide array of how you can customize how you look. Hair, skin, war paint, starting weapons as well!Here is the icing on the cake as well, if you are a streamer like me that has a community that likes to see you suffer. You are in luck because this game has Twitch Integration! Your Twitch chat can vote when certain chest are found in the game. 3 options will appear on screen and the chat will have 20 seconds to vote on what you get. This aspect of the game was a lot of fun!Overall this game is fast paced, amazing and one you don't want to pass up if you like Rougelike games! 10/10 easily!

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access has been totally worth it since day one: full price worth it.Each update has been significant, pulling me back into the game to see what's new, and to learn whatever tricks they've added.The developers are obviously committed to every aspect of the game, UX to SFX.I would spend more money for Fury Unleashed DLC without hesitation.FWIW:Played entirely on Solo. Not tried Co-op.Keyboard and Mouse. Guessing it's better with analog sticks, but it's a skill game and I haven't wanted to retrain on different controls.Most of my hours logged on Hard mode, which is the default setting. I've not tried Easy, but I enjoy Incredible a lot. Incredible mode starts the player without progression bonuses, emphasizing skill over raw stat improvements -- you still earn progression bonuses at the end of every chapter, but they only persist for that one playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest negative is the design of the combo system forcing a more aggressive playstyle. For me only two of the weapons (Rocket Launch and Assault Riffle) have been enjoyable because of this dictated pacing and the only time I play differently is switching to melee if I come across more ink or health drops from those kills. Not a fan of the having to beat three bosses to be able to start at the next comic, it got to be a very boring first few hours in the jungle time and again, would much rather see a system that if you make it even once it's unlocked. Also had some occasional slow down where saving and quitting a run and restarting cleared up. Overall though really fun game despite not being a fan of the genre. Has an amazing art style, polished options and extras, fun gameplay, varied enemies, and loved the bosses and mini bosses but wish I got to fight them more often.

_childDocuments_.review: So, to be perfectly honest, this is not my usual type of game. But I was in the mood for a story-light, easy to pick up action game, and Fury Unleashed delivered in spades. It's not the prettiest or most polished game, but it's really fun, and it truly gave me the sense I was improving as I replayed the run over and over again trying to beat that final boss. It's one of those game where it will take you 30 tries to beat a big boss the first time, and then after you've beat it once, it's like something unlocked in your brain and you'll beat it 9 time out of ten.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know any person who has not at one point seen themselves as the avenging hero, charging across the battlefield as a one-man army and Fury Unleashed opens up the possibility for you to do just that. You play as Fury in this rogue-like game, hacking, slashing and using your ultimate (and some dodgy deals) to get yourself through strips in a comic bookWith a game that manages to be both challenging and perfectly balanced at the same time, keeping me going when I would have easily given up in other games, the idea is excellent and perfectly executed and the little challenges in between manage to spice it up enough to inject some variety without losing the heart of what this game is.It is worth mentioning though that this game is designed to be hard to beat and it can be frustrating at times, they counteract this by allowing you to even further adjust the difficulty you begin with, to make the runs smoother. Unfortunately this doesn’t help the fact that you will be losing you gear and badass boots when you die.All in all this game truly is a gold mine, offering way more in advantages than it ever will in disadvantages and winning just makes you feel so powerful because it is so notoriously hard. All in all there isn’t a single person I wouldn’t recommend this to, it has something for everyone and is well worth the investment

_childDocuments_.review: It's too bad I have to strongly recommend against this game. A lot of effort was done by a small development team, the game is smooth and entertaining - even addictive. Graphics is and sound is ok. The story is mediocre. But, here is a list of the things that frustrated me:1) Lots and lots of unavoidable damage!! There are MANY places where the damage is simply unavoidable, you enter a room and you are surrounded by many enemies who all shoot you at the same time, and you don't have any room to escape! Or, you enter a room and you are pinned down the very moment you enter. This game is a platformer in which you play room by room, or sketch by sketch of a comic book, and all those rooms are very small, so it's hard to escape or avoid the damage. 2) THERE IS NO CONSISTENT WAY TO RESTORE HEALTH. On hard everything hurts you for lots of damage, and the healing orbs are too rare and too insignificant. There is simply no way to keep up with the damage you get. It's a very bad design decision to give shields and health orbs only when the kombo times are active = meaning, you have to constantly chase the kombo and never let it expire to get shields and health orbs. 3) This game is for kombo fanatics!! When I bought this game, I didn't know that this is a niche game made for kombo maniacs. Developers had to write it down in the description, but of course they didn't do it. If they did, only people from the niche of kombo games would buy it. I'm not a kombo guy, and I don't like games that force the player to play in a certain way - in this case the game forces you to play very aggresively!!When I play platformers, I like to play slowly, carefully, defensively. I really don't like when a game wants me to play aggresively. Why didn't the developers respect other styles of playing? In this game you always have to chase the kombo time and you actually have to rush forward like a maniac. This game wants you to rush and kill things like rambo, but at the same time every damage you take hurts you like a ♥♥♥♥♥ and you don't have a way of healing!!! 4) BOSSES!! Omg, the bosses of this game feel like Metal Slug bosses with their bullet hell. Of course, not every boss is hard. Some bosses are ok, but many of them are bullet hells. You simply have to memorize the patterns. Some bosses simply fill the space with bullets and you don't have where to go.5) The game has only 2 difficulty settings: HARD and EASY! Why on Earth did they decide to exclude the most popular difficulty = Normal?? On hard it's incredibly hard. On easy of course you can beat it, but even on easy it's challenging, mostly because the bosses will take away the majority of health. It's a roguelike so all the weapons and armor are randomly found, so it depends a lot on luck and on finding a good DPS weapon. I don't like to play games on easy. I never do that. With this game I had to, because on hard it's only for maniacs, so now I don't feel the satisfaction I usually feel when I complete games on normal or hard. 6) It's very clear the developers didn't play test this game properly. Many people told them the game is too hard in the forums but they are stubborn. Buy only if you are a kombo maniac.
_childDocuments_.name: Fury Unleashed

_childDocuments_.review: A roguelite action-platformer that offers quite a challenge while demanding a lightning fast pace but also doesn't hesitate to let you make the game easier, and doesn't overstay it's welcome.The story is, surprisingly for roguelite, simple but intriguing - you're a comic book character, as in, fictional within narrative itself, going trough comic book pages, trying to reassert yourself in the mind of an author who's burned out, is low on ideas, and is pondering about fully abandoning life's work. It's quaint, there's a nice twist there, and it does touch upon creative's struggles regarding validation and sense of direction. Also there are small comicbooky details like how areas go from top left to bottom right like a comic book page there, and labels by items reference past issues that obviously never existed but imply a very labyrinthine lore with magic, technology, ancient gods, aliens and time travel all in.Gameplay, what originally intimidated me was that the game is touted as pretty combo-centric, which it is, but it was more lenient than you would expect, you get quite some time, and you get a lot of options to kill enemies quickly, things like melee and Mario deal a surprising amount of damage, and sprint and air dash are quick to pull off with minimum restrictions so you just need to remember to use these as frequently. Everything is snappy and smooth, too. Lategame bosses can turn this into a Touhou with how many projectiles they launch, but for majority of game the hazards aren't that many.On other hand the roguelite aspect is pretty light. Sure enemy placement and layouts and random objectives are randomized, but it's not as much of a game changer. On other hand bosses are actually varied, each area will have a variation of them, and even final area boss is one of tree, and there are a decent variety of hostiles, so that helps keep runs fresh. Also, while items and upgrades you can find are usually welcome additions, there's a surprisingly limited selection on them, but guns? Guns are all varied, while majority require unlocking ingame in involved way, each new type feels distinct and interesting, while most of time being pretty useful or having a cool redeeming feature. Wish other gear and upgrades were as varied, really.Also, the soundtrack slaps though I worry it may be repetitive if played for longer, the dynamic soundtrack changes from ambienty to heroic heavy action solely based on your combo, so you'll hear it go back and forth between three or so tracks.This is nice, if you want a replayable action platformer where you can and even get to encourage to just run and rush wrecking everything in your way, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good throwback to 90s arcade games and comic book craze of yore :)I got this game from a bundle and didn't play it until much later as from screenshots it looked like "yet another generic gamepad action platformer with procedural levels" but once in-game the production value shined through. It feels like Dead Cells with guns, the feel, sound and animations are on similar level but the progression is a little bit more on the generic side (even though you unlock fun new items through quests in-game, there is a "Hero Upgrade" screen that just gives you passive upgrades like "more HP", "quicker reload" for all future games which only make the game easier)Overall very solid game of it's genre, worth it especially on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review feels very strange to me. You see, after 6 hours playing I would have put thumb up but at 7th gameplay hour my thumb turned to negative.Why? It's an odd design change, but before we get to that point I want to talk overall of this game with good stuff and odd/ negative stuff.+ GameplayThe way this game wants you to play is FAST. Like, REALLY FAST. And it works.You see, in this game when you get your combo meter high enough you gain shields which absorb damage; making fast paced movement really profitable.+ Lot of equipments, items, enemies and side bosses (though special power items felt weak/ disappointing).It's nothing even close to something like Enter the gungeon or Binding of Isaac but like with Rogue Legacy I never felt bored by the lack of content.But now, let's get to odd/ negative feedback.- Defeat 3 bosses to move to next area, even when you already do automatically by defeating one...?I'm not sure how easy/ hard it is to explain, but once you defeat the main boss of area you get straight up moved to next comic-book/ level.HOWEVER, if you want to get start new run from the next comic-book/ level, you have to defeat previous comic-book 3 times as they have 3 variants of the main boss from each comic-book.This design choice felt like intentional gametime prolonging for me. Personally I probably would have tried to courage player returning to previous comic-book with cosmetic/ in-game gear instead of this "you must do it 3 times with very slight difference"-style.- The amount of ink (permanent upgrade material) you get from 2nd and 3rd comic-book is not scaled up from first comic-book?I'm a huge fan of roguelites and thus I started to play this game with hard-difficulty as recommended for players with experience. And 1st world this felt well tuned with difficulty/ reward perspective. When I managed to get further I got more upgrades and so on.But when I moved to 2nd world I felt like that despite killing nearly same amount of enemies as in the 1st world I didn't anymore get new upgrades. And this wasn't just because after every level up the amount of ink required grows.I changed to easy-difficulty for rest of my playthrough and then amount of difficulty/ reward felt good again.So what's the odd design choice that turned my thumb down?After defeating 3rd comic-book boss you are moved to final comic-book right after the boss like with the previous comic-books. But in final comic-book things change quite dramatically.You see, there are made two dramatic changes to the game.EDIT 2: In September 2021 update they changed it so that you get ink in the final comic-book.EDIT:Awesome Games Studio commented on the original review and told out that after 3 times dying in the last world you can teleport back to previous comics to grind more if you need to.Fury Unleashed is excellent example how to reward/ encourage player to be fast and keep the combo-meter up and running. Some of the final decisions of final comic-book are not something I personally agree with, but despite that there are at least 3 comic-books/ levels to dive into and unleash the fury inside you.

_childDocuments_.review: Fluid gameplay, good difficulty without feeling unfair or frustrating. Very readable and pretty graphics. One off the best roguelikes I've played.It's simple enough that you can just hop in and play, you don't need to know any meta data, just shoot stuff and dodge stuff. Despite being so simple and straightforward, it doesn't get boring because the weapons you find are quite diverse and you get different act bosses/minibosses every time. The bossfights are really pretty and well done and never frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like games like Contra or Metal Slug? Maybe have an affinity for roguelites? If you do, you'll enjoy this game.Everything about it is very polished. The gameplay is very satisfying and fun because of a combination of good, responsive controls, really cool visual effects and great audio (I have good headphones, and the bass during is really meaty).It's a great game to pick up and play, and have quick, fast and intense burst of fun. The name really says it all. It's Fury Unleashed.Not only all that, but the game is multiplatform as well! It supports pretty much every platform you could imagine.I'm playing the game on Linux - the Linux version is great, I haven't encountered any problems.The devs are friendly and are obviously very passionate about their work. Playing the game, you can tell that it's a passion project for them and that they cook a lot of care to create a really fun game that has style.Playing this game evokes the same feeling as playing classic old arcade games. Everything just screams 'Fun!'.

_childDocuments_.review: (I received my copy of this game as a review copy)The game itself is fun but the paper cutout pieces kind of make it hard to enjoy. It's part of the aesthetic but it's not an aesthetic I particularly care for. It has this look and feel of clunky-ness despite functioning perfectly fine. The character models are ugly though.The gameplay is what gets me to keep playing. It's fast paced, twin stick, action shooter, plays like metal slug but on smaller instance based stages. I like the permanent progression system and even on the "streamer" mode (easy mode, ouch my feelings) it still felt challenging. _childDocuments_.review: I've been trying to find a good roguelite to replace Rogue Legacy for years. It's early on but I think this one will fit the bill.It's the first game I've played since Rogue Legacy in this genre that really nails down the progression. So many other games, Rad, Wizards of Rogue, even Dead Cells, get this wrong. In those games, it's entirely possible to sink upwards of an hour into a run and get nothing in return. Not here. After every meaningful run (more than five minutes, really) you earn the chance to level up your characters stats.And those stats make the game's action more managable immediately. It doesn't make it easy, it's still a hard game, but the difficulty never feels frustrating or unfair. A fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off as a high paced roguelite and through subsequent completions you can even change it into a full fledged roguelike (if you don't know the difference then this doesn't matter!).Somewhat overwhelmingly uses the entire controller as a means to slaughter the enemies on screen and a seemingly useless combo meter fully evolves over a few plays into a tight control scheme that fuels your murder rampage and the combo meter turns into a mistake rectifier as you gain a free pass if your combo is high enough. Combine these elements and you get a super faced paced run and gun style shooter.There is quite a large variety in guns which do have to be unlocked so you can't start off with the super overpowered ones but it is a roguelite so that's the be expected. The item variety is a bit lacking but in this sort of game it really doesn't matter. This game also has a bizarrely captivating story which I didn't expect and its very much ignorable if you don't care.The biggest downsides to this game are A) every single end-chapter boss is a huge bullet sponge and is more infuriating to fight rather than difficult and the final level being... really boring. However, the majority of this game is excellent well worth a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Badass Hero is a challenging sidescroller shooter roguelite. The combat is a lot of fun. The controls are tight. The enemies vary in difficulty and appearance. It also needs to allow you to edit controls. It says to hold shift as you launch, but that does not work, and besides that, there's no way to edit controller controls at all, even though it works fully. Overall the game is good, it's fun, and if they add background music and the ability to change the controls (Left trigger to jump is the stupidest control ever. A is to jump. A.) then I will say this could have infinite replayability. The tiers in content are revealed in "Comics" which is a nice change from "Floor 1-1, Floor 2-1, Floor 3-1, etc", plus they are all different themes. One is in space. The first one is in an Amazonian Mayan looking village. I would probably give the game in its current state a 7 out of 10, and definitely recommend it for the small price tag. If it adds music and control editing I'd give it more of an 8.5. The lack of music is deafening in a game like this.Edit: There is temporary background music that is barely audible, but the dev says they're adding some soon. And the next update should have control mapping. So with that said, I'd give this game an 8.5

_childDocuments_.review: Would you rather watch than read? Me too. Check out the highlights of the gameplay here:You get to move through a comic book world. Each time you run through you have to start from 0 (rogue-lite) but as you go you'll get perks / permanent powerups. The guns are varied and different enough that each time you go through you're playing a completely unique run. Also, Mr. Doodle is terrifying. As your combo meter climbs you start to get HP back and get more INK / powerups and some of your perks will start to trigger. The game encourages you to go QUICKLY. You can go slowly and play defensively but you'll lose out on the bonuses that the speed would give. That really makes you have to balance speed and defense.With the combo system and the various powerups and weapons, each run is going to be wildly entertaining. _childDocuments_.review: Fury Unleashed is a rogue-like BangBangBangBOOM! game with a few bullet-hell bosses.  Beat it in 4.4 hours (half on hard mode and half on easy, with a few moments trying the other modes) using a game controller.  Difficulty can be set in game.  When I started I had to go through a line of, "Ugh, not another Rogue-like..."  and kept dying in the first comic in order to level up.  I almost put it down there, but I liked the feel of screaming through enemies at a fast speed with the music making me feel awesome while doing it.  Glad I stuck with it.  Love this game now, and will definitely play in the future.  This game has a good pace to it, and enemies aren't too unfair in the thick of things once you Get Gud.  Even the bosses are fair once you figure out their patterns.  Everything goes by at a fast clip, and there are tons of weapons, armors, and upgrades to choose from.  The more skill points you use, the more ease you'll have mowing down swarms of poisoness insects, crazy nazis, and alien menaces.  The story behind the game is also good.  In fact, the story is the entire game, from the animation to the badguys to the very plot, itself.  It ties itself really nicely into a bow at the end.  There's a bloodless option to make it cleaner for younger people.  There are a few other modes, including Co-op, one-hit-kill, and a Necrodancer one that was nice (though switching to it changed my hero and kept them that way, which was a small nuisance that showed me more character skins I unknowingly unlocked...  So that's all good).   It's got a ton of achievements to try and get.  Yay replay value! The music is rad.You can gun down nazis as a maniac furry.** Epilepsy Warning: The Necrodancer mode will probably trigger you.  And there's a lesser chance the last level might as well.  Proceed with caution.  For all the knuckle-dragging roguelikes out there where it never seems to end and you're trapped fighting the same levels and bosses ad nauseam, Fury Unleashed is refreshing and gives you a sense of solid progression instead of slapping you back to the beginning every time.  It's one of the first Roguelikes I've actually beaten.  I'm glad I got this game.  Was a solid thrill.

_childDocuments_.review: The shooting feels good and the platforming is alright, and with functional co-op + roguelite elements it's a good time. I always appreciate infinite ammo so that I can keep focus on just reload tempo and maintain the fast pace that the game is going for, which is very important here because of the ever-ticking combo meter, but what breaks that is having to stop and pick up the enemy currency drops from every single enemy. It would be nice if after all enemies in a chamber are defeated it would all magnet to you, but on top of having to manually pick each drop of ink up it's on a time limit so it despawns if you don't immediately go over to it, and with the black/red/gold coloring it can be hard to see against some backgrounds. Enemies will drop that ink currency mid-fight so when it flies towards the character (much like enemy projectiles) it is just more visuals to distinguish between in a split second. There is no colorblind mode but it is possible to toggle off foreground decorations and background decorations which helped avoid melee attacking explosive barrels and getting my eye on the currency drops before they despawn. Why is the [Kick Explosive Barrel] the same button as reload instead of Melee? I have melee'd a barrel that I've wanted to kick, and I've kicked a barrel that I didn't see when trying to reload, just have the kick replace melee instead of reload, I don't think anyone ever wants to melee an explosive barrel! I usually don't like 2d action platformers that have such tight modular combat encounters, and the claustrophobic chambers here can have you pinned against the entrance as soon as you step into a room, or getting immediately sniped from off-screen when you first step into a room, or just falling down a single platform because the next room is down but the floor below is spikes that were too low to see from any platform, and taking damage breaks your combo which a lot of benefits are based on staying in combo, I'm actually changing my mind this is not recommended, it's getting in the way of itself too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Opinion is subject to change during development.I expect to get more play time with Badass Hero, but I feel confident recommending it in its current Early Access state after 4 hours.Badass Hero is a hard game, expect to die and restart plenty of times, but it does become easier little-by-little thanks to a permanent character progression system often found in other similar modern roguelikes.My first dozen runs of Badass Hero were about getting acquainted with the controls, enemy types, and character progression system, all the while "oohing and aahing" at the wonderful comic book graphic style. Once I was comfortable controlling my badass, it opened up advanced platforming techniques like air dashing while wall-bouncing grenades and shooting at baddies.After choosing a comic book (thematic set of levels) to play, each run had me discovering and equipping various weapons and armor pieces, found with both numerical random stats and special effects: rocket launchers that could freeze enemies, machine guns that could make enemies explode on death, and armor that made me invulnerable while air dashing, just to name a few. This item system aided in making each run feel fresh and surprising.There are moments where the random level generation went against me, creating what felt like unfair, near-impossible to beat rooms, but with the right items, health pool, and skill, I felt there was still a sliver of chance. But the game is made to play over and over again.Does the thought of finding a shotgun with piercing bullets and chance to ignite enemies excite you? Go on then, be a Badass Hero.
