_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything superliminal is not.That sentence comes from having played the games rather close together and having thereby a pretty good comparison from the genre. My praise will therefore reflect my grievances with the other game, consider it a 2 in 1 review.Exhibit A: Manifold garden is beautifully consistent: any rule you learn once stays that way for the remainder of the game, never flinching even if a puzzle would be easier to do without it or even if it´s presence may confuse you about how to actually go about solving a puzzle. Now that might sound either duh or mildly inconvenient if you have little experience with physics bending puzzle games, but believe me, it´s crucial. It´s what makes portal so enjoyable, aside from the characters. Every single puzzle you feel like you had all the tools and all it took was a bit of ingenuity to put them together correctly. Furthermore, you might be asking why that is praiseworthy, aren´t game mechanics supposed to be consistent? Well, it is praiseworthy because of how far the game goes outside of normal physics. Portal manages to stay consistent with, well, the titular portal. Other physics puzzle games manage it with the tried and true cube, beam and occasional light platforming. Manifold Garden manages consistency with 1. changing the direction of gravity 2. infinitude in basically every direction at almost all times 3.flowing water and 4. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ timestop mechanics (I´ll elaborate later) on top of the standard boxes! Not to mention ...Exhibit B: It never feels gimmicky! I cannot stress enough how natural the rules of this peculiar little (actually infinite) world feel. You have multiple opportunities to encounter mechanics before they become crucial for a puzzle, like encountering the flowing water and thinking at first it might just be decorative, but uuh boy it sure isn´t! Whenever expected to learn a new mechanic you are put into a situation where trying it out is designed to feel just plausible enough to not feel like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but presentet ambivalently enough to not feel like the game is trying to hold your hand. Later on, old mechanics (with arguably exactly one exception) do not get forgotten but are expanded or made to interact with the new ones in increasingly creative, fun and frankly mind-blowing ways. The consistent feeling adds to the world´s authentic ...Exhibit C: Atmosphere. From the graphical presentation strongly reminiscent of Antechamber to the subtle yet fitting and all the more impactful when intensified musical score, this world is pure Art. You feel like contributing to the creation or at least cleanup of a hyperdimensional  art installation, or the titular garden. You are rewarded for completing each "gauntlet" of puzzles by jaw-dropping sights so beautiful you will sometimes actively stay in a "solved" room and infinityfall through it some to look at what your work has amounted to. Not many games of this genre manage to make rewards for puzzles more than the inherent satisfaction and the ability to continue, this one does. This feature is also strongly supported by ...Exhibit D: The freedom. This game, except in obvious cases where your further manipulation with the world prevents it, basically lets you backtrack or get anywhere within it you were or can see (except for glassed machines but hey, them´s the breaks). You do not have a path charted out, you do not have to go on, you can and will loop back again and again to some places, changing some each time you visit and you start looking forward to visiting again! At one point the game had me searching feverishly for a sollution to a puzzle, backtracking to somewhere I was 2 hours before in seconds, before realising that 1. there was no way i could solve my present problem with any material in the previous room and 2. the fact I even thought this might be the sollution to a puzzle shows just how interconnected and, just, whole this world with quite alien geography and geometry to our own feels. EDIT: While writing I wanted to backtrack to a specific point way back and found out i couldn´t for no obvious in-universe reaseon, guess there had to be some issue, eh? After all the designers are still only human...The last bit is somewhat spoilery, therefore only read on if you want to hear about something that might quite possibly makes the dicussed elements feel way less authenticbecause you heard my vague description of it. You have been warned!If you made it to the end, I both sallute you and am sorry for making such a wall of text. The game has left a genuine impression on me and I had to vent somewhere. If this review motivates a single person to get the game or finds some resonance in another player looking for other´s experiences, it will have achieved more than enough to justify it´s existence.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of physical puzzle games, don't think - just buy. Manifold Garden is a masterpiece - at once terrifying and spectacular in its design. The feeling of immensity is breathtaking and unique among puzzle games. For that alone, it's worth a purchase. While the puzzles themselves are on the easy side, the experience of the game is something amazing.The basic mechanics are simple. Essentially, move the colored blocks to the correct locations to unlock the next area. The twist is your ability to rotate the entire game world, changing gravity to help you traverse the Escher-like, infinitely recursing levels in different directions and move blocks. Overall, as puzzles go, they are on the easy side. It took about 5.5 hours to complete the main game, and no single puzzle took more than about 20 minutes. I'd estimate the total number of puzzles is about 50 - so some of them are quite trivial. But, it can be easy to get disoriented, especially on some of the larger levels, which to me is part of the experience of Manifold Garden. I noticed only one bug:  Unfortunately, unlike some other physical puzzle games, there is only one way forward. If you get stuck on a puzzle, too bad. You can't go to another puzzle and come back later. Given the structure of the game world however, I can't imagine how it could be any other way. It's easy to imagine puzzles in Manifold Garden that would have been deviously hard, and perhaps that would be an excellent extension of the product at some point. There are certain game mechanics that, strung together, would have been truly mind bending. Actually, most of the puzzles can be solved in only two or three "moves" and near the end, I did feel like the game could benefit from one or two truly challenging levels, combining some of the more space-twisting mechanics together with a more complex series of operations required to solve them. But really, I can't think of another puzzle game that captures a similar  while playing it. Manifold Garden is truly a one-of-a-kind game, more than just the sum of its puzzles, a game worth experiencing just for the sense of immensity, the technical accomplishment, and the opportunity to explore a kind of 4-dimensional space in a satisfying and unique way.

_childDocuments_.review: ------------Gameplay-------------- ☐ Magnificent☑ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksManifold Garden is a game where you traverse non-euclidean spaces and infinitely repeating rooms to solve puzzles. The game play loop feels very similar to the first portal where you would solve a puzzle and move to the next room, but unlike portal the main feature of the game is changing the direction of gravity. It seems simple enough but the insane amount of stuff that you can do kind of suprising.------------Graphics--------------☑ Magnificent ☐ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe graphics of the game are the main reason I picked up the game myself, and I was not disappointed. The graphics themselves are just like any modern game and I would expect that the average computer could run it, but the artistic style of the game itself is outstanding. There were points in this game that absolutely amazed me. If you like Escher or geometry this is a perfect example of a game that got it right.------------Sound----------------- ☐ Magnificent☑ Amazing ☐ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe music is good, but is very atmospheric and dynamic which is very nice to hear. The main reason the sound score is so high is because of the effects. Wow. It's best to experience it for yourself but all I have to say is its a treat.------------Story----------------- ☐ Magnificent ☐ Amazing☑ Great ☐ Could be better ☐ No thanksThe game doesn't have an outright story or narrative, but certain things in the game write the story for you. Without spoiling much all I can say is you need to read in between the lines on this one, but once it clicks its an enjoyable story.------------Difficulty------------ ☐ Absolutely insane ☐ A good challenge☑ Fairly difficult ☐ Casual gameplay ☐ My grandma could beat thisThe main difficulty is puzzles, and oh man are they good. I got stuck plenty but I never really got stuck for long. Thinking outside the box and being creative rewards you as most of the solutions, just like the game itself, are a bit wild. Despite the difficulty, I never felt frustrated or annoyed with a puzzle and after every one I had a smile of satisfaction on my face. It was just the right difficulty for a game like this.------------Game Length----------- ☐ Single Session☑ A couple days of gameplay ☐ Average game length ☐ Longer than most ☐ Infinitely replayableI beat it fairly quickly, taking under four hours, but it felt much longer during the play sessions. I did spread it out over a couple days but if your someone who likes to spend more time on a game all at once, you might be able to beat it in a single session. Of course being a puzzle game, completion time will vary between people depending on if they get stuck on puzzles and whatnot.------------Should you buy--------☑ Yes ☐ Wait for a sale ☐ If theres nothing else to get ☐ No ☐ Absolutely notFor anyone who likes a spectacle, puzzles, or having your mind blown this is the game for you. Should you buy it? Yes. Should you wait for a sale? Maybe. If you don't like games that take a shorter amount of time to complete, maybe wait for a sale. I myself got it during a sale and had I known what the game was like, I would have easily gotten it full price. If your not someone who enjoys puzzle games, wait for a sale or for a rainy day when you have nothing to do, but try it out, it really puts a twist on the genre and I think anyone can enjoy it. In conclusion, Manifold Garden is a game that, in my opinion, rivals portal as one of the best puzzle games I've ever played and my only complaint is that I couldn't have played more of it. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This one kind of hurts to vote down. There's clearly been a lot of love put into the aesthetic both with the fractal-like level design (which I can imagine took some serious math), the fleshed out photo mode, the mellow and contemplative music, and the general audioscape of the game (big echoing footfalls when you run, little geometric bird flocks chirping, the ball-in-a-tube pulsing on beat with the music, etc), but I couldn't bring myself to finish the game because... I just didn't think it was that fun. My main reasoning for saying so is that the puzzles felt less about being clever and more about awkwardly shuffling around the level until I saw a way to walk my cube from point A to point B; I didn't feel clever but just kind of exhausted by the time I managed to coerce the cube to where it needed to go.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and potentially short puzzle game that plays with gravity in 3d spaces. the puzzles are fun and build well on previously learned mechanics, the only complaints I'd have are that sometimes the levels are so big you can get lost not knowing where to go, and that if you get motion sick easily you could have some serious problems. Other than those 2 things the game is really beautiful and has good puzzles throughout.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend once described FLCL to me as 'Excel Saga on Excel Saga'. In much the same way, this game is Antichamber on Antichamber.A bit more seriously, this game is quite impressive. Unlike Antichamber, this game operates heavily around a sense of scale. A lot of the places in which puzzles are solved are literally infinitely large with huge structures floating in an endlessly repeating void that loops at the edges, often with some of Antichamber and Portal's signature non-Euclidean doors thrown in. Unlike Antichamber, none of the mechanics ever really feel oddly hacky. In Antichamber, especially later in the game, I'd often find myself wondering if that was really how I was supposed to do something, but never really had that in here.Unfortunately, the game is not perfect. None of the puzzles are particularly difficult, and basically every single one can be done with little effort past figuring out where and what all of the pieces involved are. Still, they are fun to do. The bigger problem, by far, is that the game is  short. I beat the entire thing in slightly over 4 and a half hours,  Edit: Never mind. There is extra content.The bottom line is that the game is very fun but extremely short. It's not too expensive, though. If you've been looking for another non-Euclidean puzzle game that'll have some neat woahs in it like Antichamber, or maybe'll even surpass it a few times, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a puzzle game with some neat art around it and more got an art gallery to walk through with some puzzles sprinkled in it.  Not quite what I was looking for. Also as far as the puzzles go, they were generally pretty easy, but some of them in the larger areas are obscured by being more of a hunt for where the puzzle starts, or hunt for the cube you need to solve the puzzle.  And movement speed is a tad slow.  So really to enjoy this you have to really like the idea of looking at the scenery a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Manifold Garden

_childDocuments_.review: Visually fantastic game, great sense of non-euclidian space. The puzzles were never frustratingly difficult, except one spot for me, and that was because of a bug. For anyone else who might encounter this: in the red area, a yellow tree fruit didn't spawn, and I spent an hour or so thinking I was doing it wrong. Restarting the game caused the fruit to spawn and I could continue without problem. If the devs see this: sorry, I don't have any repro steps, I had just been playing from the beginning for 2-3 hours.The music was great, but it was a bit disappointing that for most of the game it was overly subdued. I think if the majority of the game's music followed the style of the last bit of the game and the end credits, it would have made for a fantastically groovy experience. As it is now, though, the bulk of the game's music is too low-key and chill for my tastes. A Groove Mode where the soundtrack tone is closer to the credits song, but for the whole game, would be amazing.All in all, a great puzzle game. 10/10 (11/10 if there was a Groove Mode).

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! Get ready for some pretty unreserved gushing. This game is AMAZING!The most obvious feature is the infinitely looping space. This core mechanic makes for some interesting (and beautiful!) environments. It's like exploring the inside of a kaleidoscope!This game is billed as a puzzler which of course it is, but I also loved the exploration aspect. You have to understand the space and resources in it before you can go about solving anything. This initial portion of discovery in an abstract world was very compelling!What got me as I played through the game was the no-so-obvious cosmetic or UI elements that really showed some lovely attention to detail: The informative use of colour to indicate orientation; the tesseracts; the 4D➜1D before the credits... All just beautifully done.It's hard to find criticism of this game. But, if I could change anything it would be to make the latter levels a tad more challenging.While I acknowledge that this is of course very subjective, personally I found the pacing for the early parts of the game (as you're getting familiar with the mechanics) very good. But, once you grasp how things work, there were times where I just flew through a level and was almost surprised that there wasn't more to do in order to complete it.Admittedly, this is a nightmare to "balance". I did get lost once and it took me a while to find my way back to where I'd wandered off from. Depending on how much you like the exploration aspect, this could get frustrating.My biggest wish is simply for MORE! I don't want this game to be over! I'll likely play through it again at least once. What I'd really love is procedurally generated levels! That's a tall order I know. But, I think it would suit this game perfectly. If offered with a few user selectable complexity options to ideally accommodate a wide variety of players, I'd likely never uninstall.Hope the devs see that last bit. I'd definitely pony-up for a procedural generation DLC :-)TL;DR If you like clever puzzlers with unique mechanics and gorgeous minimalist graphics with great attention to detail: BUY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Manifold Garden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a TRIP! I first got it on Switch and finished it, but I wanted to experience it with no hardware limitations so I bought it again here. That's right, folks - this is a game so good I bought it twice!The broad gameplay loop is that you'll enter a hub room with a puzzle that can only be solved by solving other puzzles in the rooms adjacent to the hubs. Some of those adjacent rooms are hubs themselves. The world is navigated on flat planes at 90-degree angles, but you can't jump. You can only turn the world... or are you just turning gravity?The puzzles are based on getting a cube to the goal point, but the cubes don't move unless you're aligned with their parent plane. Manifold Garden is kind enough to ease you into it with a wordless tutorial that teaches you the basics on how to solve puzzles, but after a couple of hours I hit some puzzles that I had to sleep on.The visual design is... well, William Chyr *is* an architect. Sometimes when I traverse the levels, I feel like I walk from a modern skyscraper office building, through a doorway, and on to the steps of a Mayan pyramid or into an Indian well. Almost all of the levels repeat in all directions, and if you're "outside" you can traverse the level infinitely. With the repetition of cream-coloured geometric structures with purple outlines, Manifold Garden achieves a kind of psychedelic experience.The music helps too, with a chill atmosphere and synth effects right out of the movies Blade Runner and Annihilation.I cannot recommend this game enough.However, I must note that if you have trouble with visual-spatial awareness, you might struggle to navigate Manifold Garden. On the other hand, what a marvellous challenge it would be to overcome your troubles and finish the game!

_childDocuments_.review: An enthralling Mobius/Tesseract inspired exercise in walking simulation. From the simple idea of gravity manipulation comes something truly exquisite, and the sound design undoubtedly plays a major part in the experience. name: System Shock
detailed_description: System Shock is the fully fledged remake of the ground breaking original from 1994, combining cult gameplay with all-new HD visuals, updated controls, an overhauled interface and all-new sounds & music; it even has the original voice actor of SHODAN, one of gaming’s most iconic villains. Witness the rebirth of one of the greatest and most influential games ever created. SHE IS SELF-AWARE AND AWARE OF YOU Meet SHODAN. The psychotic AI has taken control of Citadel Station and turned the crew into an army of cyborgs and mutants; She now plans to do the same to Earth. You must explore and battle your way through the depths of a space station gone to hell. Stop SHODAN and avert humanity’s destruction. HER TERMINATION IS OUR SALVATION FEATURES - Fight to death in the depths of space - Face off against the forces of a rogue AI gone mad - Improve your skills and adapt to take on your foes - Discover a non-linear story unfolding at your own pace - Jack into cyberspace to hack the system and open other routes - Innovative art style combines retro future design with modern technology Become fully immersed: shoot, brawl, crawl, climb, leap and think your way through Citadel Station.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a triumph!I am making a note here, huge success!It's hard to overstate my satisfaction!To borrow the words of Shodan's little sister.SS1 has kept its spot in my top 10 for 30 years or so. But it really showed its age, being in particular the 3rd immersive sim and the last one without mouse look. For a long time, I had dreamt of a modern remake, and what a remake we got. As I am running throughout Citadel station's corridors, I am panting and sweating, and also making a lot of happy noises as I appreciate how good the original game was, and how lucky I am to play this masterfully executed remake.All the right choices were made (or nearly so). It's faithful to the original where it matters: the story, the game design, the chilling atmosphere. And it improves really well where it was needed: UX, graphics, sound design, and so on.Bravo to the dev team, it was absolutely worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I was an original Kickstarter supporter for the original funding campaign. So I didn't receive this game for free I did get it at a significant discount.The original System Shock was one of my favorite video games growing up. This remake is an amazing update on a foundational video game. I have played through the original game more times than I can count. They did an amazing job on updating the station to take advantage of the new technology. The new station felt extremely familiar to the point where "I remember a secret door being there..." and boom still there. And yet there were a lot of times that I got thrown for a loop when they had updated the formula to keep you on your toes. For instance the Cortex Reapers in the original game weren't very intimidating. A single concussion bomb and they were done. In the remake they represent a serious threat on the station and in cyberspace. Because of how the cyborg works it doesn't matter if you have turned off the cyborg conversion system. If you die fighting a reaver you lose. Which brings up my only real gripe, an unskippable cutscene plays when you die. When doing some of the more difficult fights it can be really annoying.I really love what they did with cyberspace. It plays pretty much like the original but it is a lot more fast paced and tactical. Also the visuals are stellar. It feels exactly like how William Gibson describes cyberspace in Neuromancer.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a rather slow paced FPS where you need to keep your brain active. The mood is great as you walk around a space station filled with hazards, trying to conserve ammo and resources to achieve your mission. Oh, and there's an AI on the loose that really, REALLY wants you dead.-I really like the art style and visual design of the game, but it comes with some flaws. It's very easy to miss an important lever or switch in a room if your pass by too fast, and it is rather easy to end up having to walk around trying to find where to go next (or looking it up online).Similarly, if you don't play the game for a couple of days, it's hard to remember what you were up to last time you played, and since there's no mission log, you just sort of have to figure it out and/or go through your audio logs/emails.There's some puzzles to solve and not all of them by firing a gun. There's also some quirky 90's game design, but I find that rather charming. Just make sure to bind your implants to keys so you can toggle them without having to open the menu every time. It will make the game a lot more enjoyable!You'll need to pay attention to your surroundings and listen to audio logs to figure out where to go and what to do when you get there. If you can live with that and have some patience, I recommend this game!...Your will serve SHODAN well as a cyborg if you fail.

_childDocuments_.review: Controller support needs some polish and the ending could've used better treatment, but overall the gameplay, art style, audio, and damned gorilla tigers worked just great.What a fun game!I remember playing the 1994 demo on my friend's computer, and being awestruck. You could look up and down, you could pick things up, you had an inventory, and it was even  It was practically real life, on the screen! We taught ourselves how to pkzip recursive directories across multiple disks that we'd scavenged from his dad's boxes of old work floppies, just so I could take it home with me. The remake felt very respectful to the original. Time to slap a NG+ mod on it, and go again!

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is one of the most important games in my life, although i never played it until the Remake.Let me tell you i'm an imerssive sim-fan, Thief and System Shock 2 where my firsts, shortly followed by Deus Ex. leading all the way up to Prey in modern times.Seeing that night dive was remaking this had my hopes up, I ignored it for many years hoping to not spoil myseflf, and missed the entire drama. And hey it was totally worth it.If you don't know what an imerssive sim is, it's a game where systems integrate into eachother to make emergent gameplay. In system shock this takes the form of a dungeon crawler, designed by an angry AI that you just released the ethical constraints off.... Yeah... It be like that.This is game requires you to integrate with it's systems, it won't hold your hand and you have to pay attention as it sprinkes clues to what to do all over the game... There are no UI guiding elements, although alot has been modernised, like the map is a million times better than the original for example.Anyhow if you like exploration and the idea of playing like a bad ass hacker solving the pussle that is citadel station, then sign right up!

_childDocuments_.review: If there was any game that needed a remake, it was this one.The original System Shock was an incredible game that pushed the action adventure formula forward, and to which many other similar games owe their heritage (Deus Ex, Prey, Bioshock, to name a few). Unfortunately it came out in 1994 and at a time when computer graphics were struggling just to play "Doom", and the UI and control scheme was quite terrible and not well thought out. It was an absorbing but incredibly clunky game to play, which would have turned many people off. You would be forgiven for not having played it.This remake is clearly a labor of love, and something that brings this classic into the modern era. All the UI issues are gone, and the game looks a million times better. That said, this is not a game that will hold your hand. You are alone on a huge space station, and you have things to do - just what you are supposed to be doing will only make itself clear if you find and read the logs left behind by other crew members (a much used gaming cliche which System Shock pioneered) and immerse yourself in the story. This may not be to everyone's taste because it means a bit of light puzzle-solving. In addition, the space station is akin to a huge maze, and even if you can figure out what to do, you are going to get hopelessly lost initially.It's not all just wandering about. There are cyborgs out to get you, and you'll eventually find a number of weapons and guns to engage in melee or ranged FPS combat. There are cyberspace sections where your hacker has to fly through computer systems, akin to "Descent", and there are some wall puzzles to re-route power which break up the action. Also there are some memorable discoveries you'll make on the station so surprises and jump scares wait at every turn.There are a few subtle nods to other games with some original changes too. System Shock has back-ported Arkane's "Prey" junk recycling mechanic back into this game. This is a bit like coming full circle, as Prey was directly inspired by System Shock itself!Persistent players will be rewarded, and if you think you have what it takes to survive this nightmare - step right up. In short it's a must-purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original, but as a fan of the many, many games it inspired, this is a great way of getting a taste of what all the fuss was about. The atmosphere and level design is on point. I found myself annoyed by the labyrinthine maps and obtuse objectives until I realized that that lack of hand-holding was half the fun. Being dropped into the station and having to figure things out was refreshing compared to the typical linear "follow the glowing arrow" gameplay  I've become used to. Each level is a little puzzle with delightful little details and quirks hidden about; I never felt bored traversing the map (even if I got lost sometimes).Combat is enjoyable and the weapons are delightfully hefty, from a gigantic wrench to a plasma rifle. Enemies can take you down very quickly, but you also pack enough punch to make things feel fair and strategic.  I also <3 the grid based inventory management and recycling mechanics (I spent far too long hauling random junk across maps just to amass credits that I never spent). The only downsides for me are the cyberspace sections; I found them to be an annoying interruption to the otherwise superb exploration and combat.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a remake of the original game of the same name from 1994. It shares the same story beats, a lot of the layout of the levels is the same, as is the traversal.The modular difficulty system makes the game accessible to basically everyone, as parts of the game can simply be switched off.The levels are generally all layed out in the same way - 4 quadrants placed around a central hub - and are very labyrinthine. It is, despite a useful automap feature, relatively simpleto get lost in the levels. This is a fact already present in the original, so in the remake, some parts of the levels were removed and the confusing layout was mentioned in an audiolog.The station spans 10 levels, one of which has 3 sub-levels, all with specific uses and contents, making them distinct from one another. Resources are scarce in the beginning but later on areplentiful.The player can be upgraded with cybernetic implants (or "wares") which give new abilities, ranging from soaking more damage to effectively flying.The main resources are health, energy, ammo and trash. Trash can be converted to credits which can in turn be converted to patches, food, ammo and weapon mods.Energy is an interesting resource, as it is used to power wares and as ammo for certain weapons. It can be recharged with batteries and charging stations, the latterare found on every level of the station. When carrying an energy weapon, the reload-button can be used to use a battery, which is a good mechanic, as it necessiates fewer recharge pauses.The game proper begins with the player on the medical level, finding out that some greater tragedy has occurred, for which they are responsible. The player then spends roughly 20 hours fighting throughmutants, cyborgs and robots, all while being taunted and berated by the antagonist. On every level there are cameras and computer nodes which need to be taken down to open the way to the next.In the original, destroying cameras could prevent some traps, so far, this has not been confirmed for this game.During the game, the player must enter cyberspace to open locks. The cyberspace is a descent-like play, giving full freedom of movement in all directions. All enemies have the same freedom and that makes the cyberspace sections fun to play, as they are relatively simple to navigateand contain some interesting combat challenges. Dying in cyberspace boots the player back into the real world with a severe chunk of health taken away, except on Cyber-3 difficulty, which explicitly states:"If you die in cyberspace, you die in real life".On almost all levels, there are cyborg coversion chambers, which take severely injured humans and turn them into cyborgs. These can be turned off and restored to be medbays. On most difficulty settings, dying afteractivating the first medbay returns the player to a "near" medbay, even if the one on the level is not yet active. Since respawning bears no penalty, dying on the early levels is not a problem,however the two final levels plus boss fights do not allow respawning and lead to a game over.Near the medbay, there is a dumbwaiter, which can be used to transport or hold minor items between levels. This is helpful, but not necessary, and the lift can not be used on the last level.The story is conveyed through audio logs and emails, which are almost all voiced, making them easy to process. They can contain key codes or hints on where to go, but mostly they carry exposition.The final boss encounter happens in cyberspace, however this time the controls and behavior are more akin to realspace. There is a nice exposition dump while moving towards the boss arena, and the fight isinteresting but strange. However, it is a step up from the classic "throw stars at some grey squid while your screen fills with image pixels", which was mostly difficult only through time limit and strange controls.Some people may be put off by the blend of hi-res and lo-res textures present in the game. This was already visible in the demos and is still present here.It does help the games atmosphere overall, but especially in the beginning, this may seem jarring for some.This game is dark. Sometimes, too dark, and the lightswitches do not much to help it. While this is intended, as this is a dead space station and not a busy hallway at noon, it sometimes makes things hard to see.Some wall graffitis are all but invisible. On the other hand, sometimes the light sources are just too bright, especially when doing a wire puzzle and some of the lines carry around a 4-6+ charge, they get really bright.The fight is confusing. It is unclear where to hit and how to end it, the only indication that a section is "done" is no more respawning enemies. Also, at least on Cyber-2 difficulty, it seems impossible to "die" and get a game over, as one continuously respawns.Despite the fact that I personally enjoyed the original cyberspace sections, they have been changed for the better. Rooms are actually visible, there are some nasty surprises in there and there is no question where you can go. It is easy to get disoriented, due to full freedom of movement plus rolling, but I never had the feeling to be lost.Also the fact that there is no longer a time limit and it is possible to play conways game of life on the walls is a really fun change.The arsenal is huge and contains some very fun guns, like the rail gun and the laser rapier. Most weapons have multiple ammo types, and switching them happens with a single keypress.An auto-reload option is present, and disabling it can lead to some very embarassing moments.Depending on what you want to do, these range from laughably easy to extremely difficult. Cortex Reavers, while dying quickly to laser rapiers in the original, are nov very dangerous, as they packa punch, have their own arenas and are .I really enjoyed those fights, and I loved the fact that when dying during a boss fight, no med bay will save you.While player agency has been reduced a bit, there are still a lot of possibilities.You can end the game prematurely in research, you can ignore some parts of the story, and you CAN dump all your guns and ammunition in a "secure" place and make it inaccessible.The fact that these things are not oversights, but intentional, is something that makes the game fun - you can't softlock easily due to simple mistakes, but you can deliberately cause it.Apart from the modular difficulty setting, the game also gets progressively more difficult. Being greeted by a mutant cyborg and a cyborg elite guard,knowing there is no active medbay and no room to maneuver as one is in an elevator, is its own level of difficulty. Also the lack of medbays on the higher levels creates a lot more tension.The fact that medbays work across level boundaries on Plot-2 and less is great for first time players, as it allows much more leniency than the original - but this advantage is stripped away at higher levelsand during boss fights, making this kind of cheesing in the late game impossible.All in all, this is a VERY well made game. It does show its roots very clearly, and is definitively made for fans of the original - but it can very well appeal to all audiences.True to the original, the game does not hold the players hand, and when using default difficulty, having a pen and paper handy is recommended.I enjoyed it very much and can only state that this is, in my opinion, a must-buy, even if only to have the opportunity to relive what has influenced so many games and tropes since its release.TL;DR: Great game, 10/10, would recommend. Does not hold your hand. You will be frustrated and love it.

_childDocuments_.review: OK , walking around seems great for the first hour. after that not clear what to do.  the map is useless, it's hard to read any text in the game.   there seems to be no story after walking around on the first level,  not clear at all where to go next. Useless game. makes no sense at all. Poorly designed. A poor remake of a poor 1990's game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the original KS backers I have to stress that I am bitterly disappointed at this game as it stands.So let's look at some things yes, the audio is choppy and not that overly immersive, pretty much plays like any other FPS from the late 90's or early 2000's.Yes the cyberspace zones look nice but you won't care when you cannot navigate them.And the map, holy crap, is this what fans played way back? HOW!!! How are you supposed to play this? Sorry but I need navigation markers and arrows because hell if I know where to go!You simply WILL NOT navigate that map, sorry it's not going to happen, at least a game like Skyrim had markers.Furnace vents turned out to be lift structures, why do they look like air vents then?Proximity mines, OMG that damage radius is WAY too overpowered, your nowhere near it, you shoot it and you take damage.Look it's not all bad, the visuals are generally ok and seem to follow the original game with minor deviations.But the rest is a mess, you will enter a room and the Unreal 4 engine will use physics animations on the corpses.And Shodan, seriously why are we playing this KNOWING she survives into SS2?Achievements, hard, not worth the effort.Puzzles, hard even on easy, don't let that game choice fool you, puzzles take work EVEN on easy!I'm not impressed, and I waited 6+ years for this.If you like it, great, your welcome, I did not mind being a backer for this and I hope some of you CAN enjoy it.For everybody else, sorry but this is not the remake you asked for and deserved, Nightdive let you down and I amsorry about that.Edit - Comments shut down because idiots decided you need to be able to know or have played the original game or perhaps even the second one. Sorry but this feedback is unfair and some of us would rather play this on it's own merits without system shock history getting involved. Oh and no gratitude for us backers without whom you would not even have this game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say much about the accuracy of the remake insofar as recreation of the original goes - I played all of five minutes or so of the enhanced edition years ago. What I can say, however, is that System Shock (2023) is a solid immersive sim experience, with foes and puzzles aplenty, and a solid, if a bit old, story. Graphics are crisp, just at the right balance of retro and modern, physics are predictable and immersive, optional rooms are appropriately rewarding. It also ran perfectly on linux (albeit with a proton container) from day one, which is a plus. Incredibly optimized, minimal disk size bloat, no significant bugs that I noticed. Some puzzles were a bit of a challenge, but that is a good thing, really. Can't recommend it strongly enough to anyone that enjoys the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Your system will be shocked! Yeah this game does NOT hold your hand and paying attention is key to finishing the game. And do not play when you're buzzed or drunk. You'll probably forget a few things. Puzzles... will drain you mentally. REALLY good brain exercises. Some are easy and some are like WTF?? Combat is alright but it will punish you if you play recklessly. When enemies spawn, they enter very quietly and sometimes in the same room as you're in in the form of hidden square compartments rising from the floor. I recommend playing the game on all 3 difficulty settings except the mission scale: you got 10 hours to complete the entire game if you put it on 3. It can be really confusing the first time around but it gets better. I hope NIGHTDIVE STUDIOS remasters SS2.

_childDocuments_.review: Great remake. Nightdive proves that they cannot only make very faithful remasters but also keep the essence of a game while at the same time giving it a tremendous upgrade. The art style is something of it's own. They really managed to make everything feel modern while at the same time keeping the crunchy blockyness of the original low res textures as a stylistic coice.Highly recommended, even if you've never played the original.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake, thoroughly enjoyed from start to the end-excellent atmosphere-smoother controls, really plays like an fps now-addition of vending machines from where you can buy weapon upgrades, ammo or medical supplies by using the originally useless vaporize function to make recyclable scrap from junk items, then recycling it at stations for credits-graphics and art direction..with former, post processing is somewhat overdone at times, but latter? Oh hell yes the cassette futurism look is still here and improved no less-weapons that were previously either to be used sparingly until last few levels or were just too crap are now no longer so-game is very small, not many gb -there's a demo available for those skeptical of the game-power panel puzzles are more varied nowThe bad: -ending is somewhat lackluster really
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin?I never played the original and I had always avoided it because of the age of the game with others saying it hadn't aged too well. I always wanted to play it because it is known as one of the greats, but it never pushed me over the edge.In comes the 2023 remake demo and I got hooked. I left the game on first death and waited for the release.I ended up playing day of release in a dark room by myself and was instantly immersed into the world. The vibe and atmosphere of the game sucked me and I forgot about the outside world as I was trawling through the space station, surviving Shodan and her evil androids.Even though the two games are different, this game gives me the same feeling felt on my first play through of Fallout 3. This is something I've strived to re-capture and only a few games have lived up to that.The combat, enemies, story, atmosphere, puzzles... everything makes this game one of my top favorites and potentially my game of the year for 2023.I think more people should be playing this game and if you're reading through reviews wondering whether or not to buy, you should just go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I played on release so there were some technical issues, including a few softlocks, getting stuck on geometry, and other odd bugs, but they may be patched out by the time you play.Visually, the studio has designed to make the game look appropriately retro, being a one-to-one remake, this includes purely rasteurised lighting, and textures with a pixel shader applied.The music and sound design/scape is stellar, which is no surprise considering its origins in Looking Glass Studios.Gameplay mainly consists of solid FP shooting, with breaks between consisting of exploration, puzzles, a flying hacking secondary mode, a frankly ungodly and unwelcome amount of inventory management, and running up and around and back and forth through the levels completing various objective tasks you can discern from the audio logs.Generally these audio logs provide enough direction, but one could easily get lost if you don't find them all, and further, they can be quite obtuse at times, which actually forced me to consult a guide on one occasion.Despite its obvious flaws, the remake has made System Shock generally accessible and for me was compellingly immersive through my 40 Hour playthrough on medium difficulty. I fully intend to play it again on hard eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful remake of the original System Shock, with some extra improvements to make the game in line with the modern standard. This also means it still carries some of the originals problems, like the level design feeling very maze like and similar, and the cyberspace sections are still really bad. But overall its still good, and a very good remake.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Definatly a great and needed revamp of a classic game. The puzzles are trickier, the maps are easier to navagate, and the controls are significantly better than the original. The puzzles and cyber space might seem a little annoying to new comers, but they don't define this great game. I just wish the earth shakers and concussion bombs were in this version, but i can understand why they were not implemented.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An absurdly faithful remake of the original granddaddy of survival horror, the System Shock Remake is well worth the bang for your buck. From combat to puzzles to distilling and refining the very essence of what the original game was all about, this remake took it to new height and deliver something very unique: the crispy graphics and gameplay of the modern age with all the old -shock goodness you'd come to expect. Truly phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a full rewrite of my review that I made after my first playthrough.After beating the game on 3333 difficulty on my 3rd playthrough, and not getting tired of it at all, I can safely say, that not only is the game GOOD, it's AMAZING, easily a contender for one of the best games I have ever played in my life.Replaying the game on the higher difficulties, including the 10 hour timer, is what brought out this game's true colors. Lets start, because like the game, this is gonna be a mess of a ride.Starting off, visuals and music. Flawless, 10/10. The combination of high-detailed models and weapons operate alongside textures that are, up close, lower res. Is this bad? Absolutely not. Too many games forget that better visuals often mean static or dull envrionments that look pretty and kill performance. This game has both, with unique, colorful details, full of 3d models that give the world depth, while being playable at 100+ fps even on higher settings.A beautiful game that, despite being on a single station, never looks tedious or repetitive.The soundtrack is a banger, flipping between haunting ambiance to classic System Shock electro music in combat. I've been listening to it on walks and at work, and it is great, not just in the game, but out of it too. Get a solid audio system to hear that deep bass in Bridge, it's beautiful. Gameplay. What a fluid, tight combat system. Every level introduces new enemies and weapons, EVERY level is a maze that stresses you out. Enemies are tough, their attacks hurt, and using the wrong weapon, or even wrong ammo type on the wrong enemy, will quickly drain you of resources. It makes combat itself into a puzzle, forcing you decide when to play it safe with energy weapons or play it hard with ammo for faster results. Boss fights WILL.KICK.YOUR.ASS. Even items that otherwise help cheese them, like the slow-motion patches, only make it bearable, as opposed to impossible. Good, bosses should terrify players with failure. And lets give the most important part: exploration and storytelling. In any other game, waypoints and paint jobs would tell you where to go, a quest log would give you step-by-step instructions on what to do, and exploration would basically be "go from A to B, but you get options of A1, A2, or A3 to get to B"This game will force you to think. Listen to the audio logs, pay attention to the messages and environment for what to do. This game will not hold your hand, it's actively trying to kill you. And that 's the best thing about it, even after 3 plays now, beating it under 9 hours, the constant stress of remembering what to do, how to get there, how to deal with puzzles and enemies in a time-efficient manner gets into you.It's a phenomenal experience, every trap and boss you survive, every puzzle you solve, every major mission objective you finish, feels great, because it was YOUR thinking and combat skills that made it happen, YOUR careful management of time and resources, YOUR spatial awareness to notice hidden areas and items. Even the boss fight, for all the flack it gets, is still relatively straight forward, quick, and intense. I would recommend this to anyone that wants a breath of fresh air, a new experience that will actually push you to your limits in terms of patience, mental fortitude, and feeling like a small insect fighting a god. Heck, i'd recommend it to anyone in general. Also SHODAN is A-Tier Mommy material, and that alone is enough. She is unironically a fantastic enemy, who's traps, taunts, and constant comments in audio logs are phenomenal writing. Get the game. It is wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Not only a really faithful remake, but also just a really fun Immersive Sim. Great animations, sound design, voice acting, it runs well. A good time! But be aware that this is a remake of an old game. This game HATES YOU, it will not hold your hand let alone give you an idea of what you are doing. Explore, Fight and Pay Attention and maybe you can right your wrongs on this ship, and maybe even save the world! This is how you let a game cook, give it the time it needs. This is how you remake an old masterpiece, bringing it to a new generation (me) but also satisfying the people who played it way back when. This is how you literally make it so noone will ever play the original System Shock ever again! It's that good! Well done NightDive. I hope you can continue to do excellent work! Would let SHODAN step on me again 10/10. Underrated game of this year tbh
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on Kickstarter back in 2016 with little to go off of other than concept art and some 3D models, fast-forward 7 short years later and now it's what I personally consider to be the most faithful remake i've played.I've only played the original System Shock once (around the same time I backed the project) so this was a fairly new experience to me with only a couple of recollections here and there, that being the case, I love the classic 'no waypoint/guide' approach they took with this.Running around the ship and exploring rooms on a whim while reading and re-reading text logs scratched an itch I didn't know I had, in that junior detective kind of way. Little "Eureka!" moments like piecing together the code for the Storage 9 door, or picking up the severed head I already walked passed a dozen times for the retina scanner (or using a chess bot online to tell me which moves to make in the chess game in Delta Grove, because i'm ass at chess)Many moments felt ultimately more gratifying because I got to figure them out for myself, definitely my biggest take-away from the game. All in all the gameplay feels like it delivered what was promised, and personally, what was expected.My only nitpicks are that I personally feel the cargo lift for storing items should've been a little bigger? and there were a lot of times in combat when the music would kick in right as I get done killing the enemy, so I'm kinda just standing there above their corpse jamming out to the soundtrack (which is really good btw)Also big shoutout to Nightdive, I emailed them asking if I could swap my Playstation key for a Steam key, due to the console version being delayed, and within 30 minutes they replied back with a key for me. Thanks a bunch, guys
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly faithful remake for an incredible game with some changes where it makes sense, the way the art style of the original game was adapted for the remake may be my favorite part, it's incredibly neat and a visual treat.My only real complaint is that the cyberspace bits and the final boss are a tad lackluster, but this was even more true in the original game and they take up so little overall playtime that it doesn't detract too much from the core experience.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best remakes I've ever experienced. So much respect to the old Looking Glass team who created the original and Nightdive for updating it for new generations to enjoy (and for their work preserving the original game too!).

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry, but i am not a Fanboy of the Original, and this Remaster is just notas good as it could be. Only 18% of the gamer completed this game. That says it all.The only good thing is how to use the different ammunitions to the various typesof enemies. The enemies themselves, act like stupid "Kill on sight" Bots. So sad, but at the end the final Boss was also just a bad joke. I thought the game crashed,but then the credits appeared.The possible Remake of the second part has to be so much better to convince me.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This and RE4r are easily my favorite video game remakes from the last few years.RE4r takes a slightly flawed masterpiece, melts it down, and chemically reconstructs it into a brilliant gem, and this takes the blueprints of the original and builds it up in an almost identical way, but builds it from much stronger materials.To get to the point, this is a nigh perfect remake.  It captures the style and vision of the original game, and pretty much maintains every mechanic... The chief difference is that this game entirely removes the clunk of the original.  Nightdive has impressed me; not only can they make good remasters, but they can make good remakes as well.There are a few minor issues (simple bugs like dead enemy ragdolls occasionally falling back into place when you re-open a door, as if they were in the air a second ago... that kind of thiing), but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I think its awesome, but I recognize it won't fit everyone's tastes.  I think the closest recent game on the market is Prey (2018).  So if you liked that, you will like this.  The core gameplay is exploring and solving labyrinthine levels.  So I would recommend this to gamers who love puzzles and exploring.  The combat can be a little bit awkward, considering how claustrophobic the levels are and how fast you can die.  But also rewarding when the sandbox style approach to taking the initiative in combat clicks together.  Finally I think its just an exceptional and worthwhile effort by Nightdive and I would love to see what else they can do.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Excellent remake. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A grudging recommendation. For the most part, enjoyed the throwback gameplay of a sprawling map and the return to SHODAN. I did not play SS1 but played the sequel several times. I will likely buy the remake of SS2 after enjoying SS1, but I will not finish the remake after 20 hours of playing it because of the hell that is Beta Grove.Even with a radsuit, Beta Grove constantly taxes your health and energy. If you're low on both, the game gives you few tools to address it. Energy and medkits are in short supply, so I'm supposed to, what, sprint through the level until I learn it, dying over and over so I can "speedrun" it later? Apparently I suck at the game because I'm apocalyptically low on the items I'd need to make this level playable, much less fun.Two other quibbles: 1) the 2D map is an unwelcome throwback when trying to navigate a 3D space, and 2) the primary fire button (mouse 1) sometimes does nothing at all (this is reported by other users as well). 20 hours for $40 is fair enough, but holy HELL make sure you hoard health and energy packs for Beta Grove. Liked the game, but did not love it well enough to go back and replay it to do the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth full price, as long as you know what you’re purchasing. There are a lot of quality-of-life updates, but also the basic design is that of a mid-90s game. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10. Not too bad, and I don't mind giving it a thumbs up, but also kind of glad it's over. Very true to the 90's ethos - no tutorials, no quests, no objectives. A great many story-critical items you have to just stumble upon (blink-and-you-miss-them). The ending also dragged on (a lot) - a few too many bosses, IMO, and the final boss is a complex, multi-phase, that doesn't allow saving at any point. Sometimes, you die and you just respawn, but around 40% of the time, I just died died, and had to restart the whole thing. Never actually figured out the pattern. Also turns out that most of the online content re: the final boss fight is no longer valid, due to a couple of post-release patches.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I recommend you play it on easy, i liked the puzzles and the exploration but the combat feels iffy and the cyber space its the worst.It's a caution recommend,For years i had known of the legend of system shock but i also knew of the reputation, its a great game but it does feel archaic in some parts, the maps did not age particularly well, its true that it feels like a real place instead of a videogame level but it does test your patience in some places, for me its the respawning enemies, the game its very quick save and quick load intensive, you pretty much have to fall into traps to know are there and while its not always bad it does interrupt the flow of a modern game design, the controls are ok but some details like your (very weak) flashlight using power always irked me in games.There is not really an ammo economy, you can't buy more ammo, you rely on finds and drops, the enemies are tanky and when they respawn it's just a drawn on resources, the directions you get are vague since you are out of the context of the conversations in the game, you get very little directions. It wouldn't be a bad thing but the game it's more on a action direction than a horror or stealth directionsI feel its hard for new players to explore since many games like bioshock, dead space or dishonoured have come out with the evolved game design integrated already.I recommend you play it on easy, i liked the puzzles and the exploration but the combat feels iffy and the cyber space its the worst.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing short of masterpiece, Nightdive out did themselves with this one. I can only hope with some more polish to iron out some of the bugs and glitchs are ingame will make this a possible GOTY.And I feel I need to say this: that a game studio thats willing to put out a demo should be trusted from the get go of making a damn good game. If they're willing to show what they're giving in a form of a demo, and one they were willing to keep up during a games development show's they have the competence and confidence within their product, and to put their best foot forward. _childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: If all you're looking for is what's, effectively, a graphics overhaul of the original? This game is for you. It is a very faithful remake to the original title that doesn't shy away from its roots or reinvent the wheel. This is great for people who are nostalgic for & really want to relive the 1990's experience of System Shock with refreshed visuals. For anyone else, this is a mid-tier experience that's held back by all of the same issues that make the original game, from a modern standpoint, frustrating and disengaging.I would have less of an issue if the store page was honest about this. The game sells itself as "the rebirth of one of the greatest and most influential games ever created." A rebirth is a revival, a renaissance, or a reinvention. My impression is that this game has suffered the same fate as the Enhanced Edition of Planescape: Torment. The creators were so averse to "repainting the smile of Mona Lisa" that they adamantly refused to seriously rethink & resolve some of the key issues (narrative, combat, QOL) plaguing the original title.I wouldn't call it a regurgitation, but it definitely feels closer to it than a rebirth.If you are expecting:* Snappy, responsive, and weighty combat* Well-structured storytelling & plot* Basic features native to modern games (autosave)* A game willing to take five seconds to explain core mechanics* Standard QOL features (a vaporize all button, allowing recycling of unwanted weapons, etc.)This isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A 10 out of 10 Immersive Sim game, taking me ~19hrs and 12 minutes to beat (more like 19hrs and ~35 minutes counting the final boss), and a fantastic way to experience the magic of the original System Shock made back in 1994 by Looking Glass Studios with improvements to everything across the board. Nightdive Studios *knows* what they're doing.But that is to say, the game is improved in its systems, but still keeps the original game's difficulty. Overall the game feels like a Immersive Sim-Metroidvania, as you back track to different floors often, the path to the endgame gets slowly less linear, and you find gear and items at wildly different paces to other players. You will be confused, and lost, because the game asks you to engage more than simply point click shooting and opening doors until the credits. You'll have to remember codes, solve pretty difficult puzzles, listen or read closely to audio logs, make sacrifices to your loadout as you can't bring *everything* you find, and scour almost every part of a given area. All to your benefit yes, but nothing in this game is ever just *given* to you without you finding either the means to get it, or locating it (sometimes just stumbling upon it too). So prepare a notepad, either pen and paper or a file on your computer, even screenshots will do. You won't remember everything, and anything that looks or sounds relevant IS.The game is definitely a must buy for anyone that likes a FPS that makes you scratch your head and is willing to dig around, and even Metroidvania lovers who want a new game to puzzle their way through, it's very worth it if you're willing to struggle a little, fail a *lot,* and try again.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who experienced in the golden age of PC gaming (late 90s - early 2000s), this game just scratches an itch that hasn't been scratched in a very long time, and it's oh-so-satisfying. The original System Shock (1994) was created in part by legendary game designer Warren Spector (Deus Ex, Thief: Deadly Shadows, Epic Mickey). System Shock (2023) is an extremely faithful remake of the original 1994 classic. The story is the same; you play as a hacker who finds himself in a space station against a rogue, killer AI who is out to get you. Your job is to survive. The levels are designed in nearly the SAME exact way as the original; which is incredible. The level design in this game feels so fresh despite its age. Forget about going from point A to point B and having your hand held everywhere you go as is the norm in modern gaming. You aren't told exactly where to go, there's no waypoint to help you, nor is there regenerating health. You gotta figure stuff out by yourself and search for audio logs, listening for clues to progress further. It's up to you to make your way through the maze-like Citadel Station, but watch out because enemies lurk and you can find yourself being overwhelmed quite quickly. The gameplay is slow paced, which is something I appreciate. I often find myself taking my time in the game to really search every room as best as I can. By searching properly you may find the rare but valuable credits, ammo, upgrades, or even guns and gear. If you rush through the game you might miss out on some special gear. The game rewards those who take their time and enjoy the ride; savouring every sip of this glorious soup. The enemy encounters are fun, but tense and sometimes challenging. Every enemy has a weakness that can be exploited, so it works to your advantage to use certain ammo and guns against certain enemies. This way, you can conserve your ammo and use it to its fullest potential. The atmosphere in the game is really something special. It's creepy, but not too scary. The music is present, but not overbearing. It adds to the creepiness of the game while being catchy and easy to listen to. You also often hear enemies growling, or talking to themselves as you are exploring the station. This can be extremely nerve wracking (in a good way!) when you do not see where they are. The graphics have a charming, pixelated look to them that evoke a sense of gaming's golden age, but the game still looks great. The lighting, shadows, and fog all come together to create an ambiance that is just delightfully creepy, tense, and visually appealing. If you are a fan of classic FPS/Immersive Sim games like Deus Ex, where you have to take your time, explore, and literally take out a piece of paper to write down notes of hints you find in the game, then this masterpiece is for you. If you aren't sure this is your cup of tea, give it a chance. Play it for the two hour Steam trial and see how you like it. It's likely that you haven't played anything like this before. In 2024, it's rare to find a new game that plays like an old school FPS. Here's to hoping there are more to come. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I bought & played the original way back in 1999. I got about three quarters through the game before I got stumped. The game was amazing but the graphics and dated low resolution interface was often a struggle. This was very much a game that would have benefitted from VESA. The maze-like maps looked greatly the same and the way you moved took some getting used to. In other words, a classic but with some flaws that made it harder to play than it needed to be.Almost 25 years later and now we have a pretty faithful remake that removes most of the annoyances of the original. Proper modern FPS controls, better gun handling, improved interface, a better map and of course much improved graphics that make the game a lot easier than you'd think.I didn't expect to complete the game right away. I usually delve into a game for an hour or two and then come back at a later time. However, something kept me playing and I realized it was the way the game is designed: in floors. It's easy to play a full floor at a time, going from room to room, solving all the puzzles and ending the game after you've done a complete floor. Leaving behind map marks for areas you can't reach (yet) makes it easy to keep track of open ends.While the combat is still rather basic, it serves its purpose and the fun of the game is in the puzzles, piecing together all the clues and discovering what to do next. In this I had a real blast. I recall the original being a real maze but I didn't have this feeling in the remake - I don't know if they improved the level design or if the new graphics & controls just made it less of an issue but it only bugged me a few times (the Executor level being the worst with the repeated need to go through a very long crawling corridor half a dozen times).But besides a few small minor issues, this is one of the best remakes I've ever played. The fact I completed it in a few days shows how fun it still is today.

Nightdive outdid themselves with this remake, to the point I hope they perhaps make their own ip and not let this be a one and done, I'd love to see what they could cook up with such thorough experience with one of the ogs. _childDocuments_.review: an outright improvement over the original game in every way possible. The team clearly worked hard to ensure that the game was not only a visual treat that blows the original out the water, but also ensured the game remained faithful but greatly improved in terms of its gameplay and presentation of narrative. If you've only ever seen System Shock 1, I highly suggest this game. If you've played the original game then I highly suggest this game. If this is your first time experiencing the series then I suggest the game with a few caveats; you need to enter it knowing that its a remake of a very early shooter game, and comes with a lot of the baggage a game like that would come with. Levels are maze-like (although the visuals help a lot with clarity of where to go in the station), combat is relatively simplistic overall, but given a major overhaul with its great gore systems and its story is presented to you mostly within audio logs and emails that are written incredibly well. _childDocuments_.review: It took a while for it to release. That may have upset some people, especially the initial backers who were maybe expecting a different kind of game. That's unfortunate. I'm not here to convince any of those people. I will say that from a technical aspect, the game is polished AF, has not crashed or really bugged out on me except once, where an elevator didn't work. a save and reload solved it. Some reported the usual unreal 4 caching stutter. I only noticed it during level loads, which are "seemless" in that there is no loading screen.   What this game is, sometimes to a fault, is a faithful redesign of the initial game. It takes advantage of a lot of modern game design without compromising what made the original great, which is the claustrophobic feeling of exploring a space station come to life where everything is trying to kill you. As such the maps are the same maze like levels with increased fidelity where possible and slight tweaks and rearrangements where necessary. Same thing can be said for the weapon and items, and enemies. Most of these return, with some new inclusions and exclusions and modifications where it makes sense. The black mesa standalone game is the perfect comparison. Everything feels familiar, but also fresh. Finally, the hand holding (there is none) and difficulty aspect mirror that of the original title for the most part. The difficulty sliders themselves make for a varied and customized experience that can appeal to many kinds of people.I did mention "to a fault". Expect lots of backtracking, some confusing design choices like not having a total ammo count easily visible, not being able to vaporize all scrap items at once. The latter is quite annoying as this mechanic (unique to this itteration) is essential for purchasing weapon upgrades (also unique to this itteration). The FPS aspect was not the original's strong suit, with enemies feeling dumb and not really that varied aside from how beefy or armored they were. Things are a bit better this time around, but the enemy ai still leaves something to be desired. If you loved the original system shock, I highly recommend this game because it is essentially that game if todays technology were available in 1994.If you're new to this, this is an opportunity to experience a remake of one of the first examples of an immersive sim, with all the gameplay philosophy, and none of the dated graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Beautiful visual that brings to life Citadel Station in all its glory, lights and colors are especially vibrant and immersive+ A sprawling, immense station to explore and conquer filled to the brim with puzzles, cyberhorrors and resources.+ One of the best villaness in video game history voiced masterfully by her original voice actress, Terri Brosius+ An almost perfect respect for the original game, this remake keeps the journey from 1994 as faithfully as possible while making it possible to enjoy without having to learn how to pilot a space shuttle just to control your characterCons:- While incredibly improved from the original, cyberspace sessions might feel disorienting and confusing- In late game it becomes quite hard to manage the coin economy since your inventory will probably be 90% full all the time- While i can see the appeal of it, the chess minigame feels quite unwelcomed, i do not want to learn chess to have a shot at getting a quite important, even if optional, character upgrade.Nightdive has outdone itself in delivering the definitive version of probably one of the most important videogames in the medium history. System Shock is a masterpiece that will wrap you in its Cyberhorror enviroment and ask you to switch on your brain to defeat the magnificently villanous SHODAN before she remakes all the inseec...humans in her twisted, cyber children. Some younger players might find the lack of handholding or objective tracker quite disorienting but if you focus on what is around you, listen to what the doomed crew of the station left behind in their logs, you'll have no problem in understanding what to do and how to do it, A must play for all gamers, thank you Nightdive!9/10
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: [Early impressions]The original SS is too primitive for my taste, so this is nice. It has most of the conveniences of a modern game, such as (almost) full controller support. The interface makes sense instead of being a strange artifact only 40+ bearded dudes and turbo nerds understand. No disrespect to 40+ bearded dudes and turbo nerds. It has good atmosphere and the graphics look nice, although I'm not sure if I would have gone with the blocky look. At least not without a CRT filter like Prodeus has, or like the Quake 2 remaster has. I'd even go so far as to say it's a bit creepy thanks to Shodan's voice and dialogue. The story is even more relevant considering we're currently weighing how to deal with AI and its ethical constraints. One of the super interesting aspects of it is how you can see the DNA of games like Prey 2017 and Deus Ex. In fact, there are rooms/areas of Prey 2017 that I'm almost sure were inspired by if not lifted from SS1. It still takes a bit to get accustomed to how it works. It's mostly comprehensible without too much fuss, but the problem I have with it is knowing where you're supposed to go next and what you're supposed to do. From what I've read, you need to pay very close attention to what's being said in audio logs and make sure you read everything you pick up. I suppose this isn't an unreasonable ask, but a very common complaint you'll find online is that people don't know where to go or what to do. Sure, not having a big dumb marker on the map may cause some players to skip exploration, but not everybody. I know if I just go to the marker and skip everything else, I'm going to have a bad time because I won't find ammo, guns, healing items, and other goodies. So it doesn't _prevent_ anyone from exploring. For me, a quest marker is simply a way of saying "If you wish to progress the story further, go here". I know having quest markers might look poorly on your gamer cred report, but sometimes old game design is a pain in the ass. Besides, the quest markers are an option.Until they fix the damn patch. Currently, the patch that's supposed to add waypoints doesn't work. Aside from waypoints not working, there are a bunch of other bugs. While I appreciate Nightdive's creation of this remake, making a big announcement about a patch that has bugs with a major feature and then taking days, maybe weeks to fix it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks. And that's why I don't recommend this game...yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never been able to play the original so picked this up in hopes I could find out what I have been missing out (or not). So I cannot give any opinion on the "faithfulness" of the game as a remake but purely on the fun I got out of it.My initial fear was that this game is too close to the original to appease fans of the series and therefore comes with the clunkiness of early 90s games. But this is not the case. I'd definetly say that the game feels "modern" in terms of gunplay and usability while it definitely has a retro charm to it. :The game has a good length to it (approx 25h for 95% of the content) without any parts feeling like filler. The story is good and doesn't try to make itself cleverer than it really is. :The game is 99% voiced, decent accustics, beautiful retroesque graphics and some ambient music which does the trick. The art-direction feels unique, retro yet modern and unique. Definitely not the average "let's use a pixelation-shader and call it a day"-average.:Like I said, the gameplay feels quite modern in that the guns have a decent kick to them, hit-boxes are crisp and movement is precise. The "interact" butten is bound to right click by default which is odd but makes sense simply because interacting is probably your main action in the game. The layouts of the levels are fantastic and never feel like a haunted house but much more like a real star-ship with sensible architecture.I heard the hacking was the weakest part of the original and I can say that it still is. If I had a button to skip them I would've. They never feel fun or rewarding but easy, simplistic and a chore, I guess Descent was the hot-property back then and everyone needed to have a 9DOF shooter-element by law.All-in-all if you haven't played the original like me and wondering if this game is worthwhile without nostalgia-goggles then yes, I can recommend this game. It's a fun, atmospheric, light-horror exploration shooter where gameplay goes hand-in-hand with the story.
