_childDocuments_.review: A Masterful Revival of an Immersive ClassicSystem Shock,stands tall as a testament to the brilliance of the original immersive sim. As a old school 90's kid gamer diving into this remake (only playing the second system shock before)  I was captivated from the very start.This game stays true to its roots as one of the pioneers of the genre while effortlessly appealing to contemporary gaming sensibilities. The strict ammo and inventory management mechanics add a layer of tension and strategy that keeps you on edge throughout your journey aboard Citadel Station. Every bullet counts, every item matters—forcing you to think critically about every decision you make. (I play on hard combat difficulty, it may be easier at other difficulties and not as edgy)The atmosphere in this game is ridiculous. From the eerie, cyberpunk-infused corridors to the haunting audio logs that unveil the station's dark secrets, every aspect contributes to an immersive experience that few games achieve. The developers have painstakingly recreated the immense and oppressive atmosphere of the original, ensuring that every flickering light and distant sound adds to the sense of isolation and impending danger. (Enemies can actually spawn at any moment, making back tracking for energy or health an actual challenge not just a chore)The gameplay itself is a delicate balance of exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving, all woven together seamlessly to create a narrative-driven experience that grips you from beginning to end. The level design is intricate yet intuitive, encouraging exploration and rewarding curiosity with hidden secrets, items and lore that enrich the overarching story.Visually, System Shock's remake is not bad. The updated graphics breathe new life into the iconic environments and characters, while maintaining the retro-futuristic aesthetic (also block style) that defined the original game. The attention to detail is evident in every facet of the game world, from the gleaming technology to the decayed infrastructure, making Citadel Station feel like a living, breathing entity.Overall, System Shock is more than just a remake—it's a homage to a genre-defining classic that manages to feel fresh and relevant in today's gaming landscape. Whether you're a fan of the original or experiencing the world of System Shock for the first time, this game delivers an edgy  journey filled with tension, atmosphere, and thought-provoking gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: I remembered System Shock from when I was a kid, but I had never played it.  Prior to the remake, I had managed to get my hands on an copy of the original game.  It had not aged well, and quickly lost my interest.  So beyond a couple hour's worth of playtime, I, unlike many here, didn't have any great amount of nostalgia for this licence when I grabbed it on sale.  Honestly, even with the up-rev of the game to newer beautiful graphics, the impeccable voice acting and the many quality of life upgrades that were put in, some things are still not where they should be.  Shooting from around corners can be frustrating.  Enemies always seem to be able to nail you if you don't catch them unaware, and they aren't always alone.  Some boss fights are pretty hard, even on the balanced difficulty, until you read on how others cheese them and then they become trivial.  However, for those flaws I found in it...  I really liked it.  There were a couple times I jumped as a cyborg snuck up on me.  The puzzles are well executed.  But what really got me was the very last fight, and how it knocked over my expectations and really giving me a sense of tension that I really did not expect.    And then, having the Order of Death playing as the end credits rolled...  That's when I understood with absolute certainty that these people who remade this game knew what they were handling.  You see, That song was also used in the 1990 B-movie "Hardware", a movie about a killer robot (it's probably worth a single watch, but I'm a sap for that kind of movie).  They understood, and that's why they shelled money out to license that song playing at the end of their game.  And while they could have done some things better, I understood that it probably wasn't talent or vision that hampered them, but time,  I salute what they have done.  Should you buy this?  On sale definitely.  Full price?  Depends on you budget for entertainment.  But these guys deserve recognition, and this game is pretty good for its money.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game blind, I've seen videos before vaguely about this game and I've heard great things about it but never got around to playing the original. I was eagerly awaiting this remake to be released after keeping an eye on the kickstarter and watching all the teasers and trailers.After putting in around 30 hours or so and completing the game I can say that this is an instant classic. The game play and overall game design is well thought out and I've heard it's extremely similar to the original also so that just proves that old game design can still work in a modern game. The level design was fantastic but mainly corridor based with some variation in openness. One drawback which annoyed me quite a bit was the amount of backtracking needed and a lot of linear corridors/crouch spaces which you had to go through multiple times. Things like this could have easily been fixed and improved upon. Apart from these small issues the overall design of the station was amazing and it really made you feel like wanted to explore every single nook and cranny of each area. The puzzle design was also quite cool. I felt like it wasn't too tedious and actually took a few tries to complete them and they actually made you think. The combat was also fantastic and there is a wide variety of weapons and gadgets you can use as well as skill/equipment that you can upgrade by finding the higher tier version throughout the station. I did find that the key binds for these were missing so if you don't check you won't know how to use them so make sure to bind these. I'm eagerly awaiting the Enhanced edition of System Shock 2 and I really hope they do a similar remake of that in the style of this one. Overall, I'd recommend to buy this If you're a fan of old school RPGs and great game/level design and you're fans of games like Prey or Arx Fatalis.

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people will want to compare and contrast this with System Shock: Enhanced Edition, so I'd like to provide an analysis.  System Shock EH/CD version was a big part of my summers as a kid. System Shock is a wonderfully remade version of the original System Shock game.  The labor of love involved here is obvious in every detail.  The textures are an interesting mix of modern technology and throwback textures that strongly resemble the originals, sometimes down to having low-rez edges.  This serves a double purpose; running this application at 4k on a 60" monitor with all settings maxed stays at at least 45 FPS. Enemies in this game are the same as in the original, but with updates of course. The Humanoid Mutant looks truly freakish, and Hoppers now have the ability to hover into place instead of just slowly hopping.  They also fire beams instead of a pulse shot.  The Serv-Bots look FANTASTIC and are a bit bigger than they were.  Security bots remain terrifying opponents but now they can fly, like really fly and are also larger.  Enemies in the cyberspace interface are more varied and interesting and the combat there is faster.  Cyborg Humans now carry SPARQ beam weapons, though they are usually broken when they fall.  I haven't run into a Cortex Reaver in any way yet, but the enemies are more intelligent and attentive to sound, so I'm a bit worried about dealing with the one in the launch bays when I get there. Zero G mutants are spiky and look a little like something you can pick up, so be careful when you hit the Research level.The weapons are still the same, though I found a shotgun I don't recall from the first game and I haven't found a flechette machine pistol yet.  There's also a massive wrench that can replace your pipe weapon early on, and it serves as a fantastic melee weapon.  The wares for the implant you have in the game appear to be the same as the original, just updated to match the new environment.The story is still the same, though the severity to which SHODAN is corrupted is less obvious when you first wake up other than dealing with two angry robots and getting your first message from the TriOptimum agent.  Additional lore items have been added, including new audio logs and stationwide broadcasts from a fully aware Cyborg Edward Diego and with a SHODAN who has embraced her hubris to extremes early on.  The script is, however, followed faithfully otherwise, including every time SHODAN calls you an insect or otherwise taunts you.  Rather than severed heads laying everywhere, you'll see the victims of the station's events as intact corpses or walking around as mutants or cyborgs, still dressed as they were when they died.   You also start in your apartment and do the hack (just a keypress) that starts your problems yourself, and get to enjoy the entire prologue from a first person perspective instead of a VO over a travelling shuttle in space.   The game is darker and scarier, more akin to SS2, and while I was worried at first because the infamous medical level hissing broken door was no longer broken, there are other doors where they grind loudly and spark because their mechanisms are damaged.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting 15 hours at most but this damn near took me 25, wasn't expecting the length. When you're read off all the levels at the beginning, I assumed some you'd skim through or whatever, but no, you're doing the Citadel station top to bottom and it's gonna feel like it. It's good too. You're getting your moneys worth with this,Being the proto-immersive sim it's pretty light on the genre elements, it feels a little more metroidvania-y than anything. Every level is a sprawling, looping, overlapping, short cutting, crawl spacey maze and you're going to be back tracking A LOT. There are no quest/mission markers or any objectives journal. You figure out what you're doing through audio logs and messages. The goal is to stop SHODAN and the game just asks that you pay attention and be methodical to do that. Most of it is intuitive, but you have to go slow, rushing through or trying to speedrun sections will only cause you more headache later when you're missing a key item or piece of info. I felt I was pretty thorough, took it slow and listened, even then I hit a wall twice where I just had no idea and had to Google because I didn't wanna spend an hour wandering around with no clue what I was looking for. When I did do that it always turned out I was somewhat close to figuring it out anyway, but, be warned, it's that kinda game. It can eat up a lot of time when that happens, so my advice is, if it's really got you stumped: don't be a masochist, just google the detail you need and move on, otherwise you might sour yourself on a great game for petty purist bragging rights.Save some rail gun ammo for the bridge section towards the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah good game....BUT there's a lot of little tiny things that kind of annoy me when I play it:-default controls are a bit strange IMO and I find I'm constantly tweaking them as a TON of things you'll use a LOT aren't even bound to a key.-some of the UI stuff seems messed up control wise (see media section of MFD)-auto-saves being practically non-existent later in the game after lulling you in to a sense of security by having a bunch on the first 2 floors-scrolling through media section for passwords is stupid, game needs a "known passwords" section-a ton of icons on the map aren't labelled at all and doesn't get any info when you mouse over it, the legend has like 5 things in it, yet there's well over a dozen different map icons, This drives me INSANE.-game just completely lacks an overall ammo counter which seems like an oversight.This stuff can and should all be fixed with a patch or two Nightdive, please.MAYBE some of this stuff is due to it trying to be like the original? _childDocuments_.review: Where you would like Nightdive's remake of System Shock heavily depends on whether you want to experience the original faithfully. If you do, as most reviews have said, the remake is fantastic. The modernized pixel graphics are iconic and I think it might inspire other game devs to take a similar approach.But if you expect the gameplay to also be modernized, then you might be disappointed. There is a very good reason why immersive sims have evolved now that we are in 2023 (and for the most part in a good way, looking at Prey here). I can get past the fact that you really have to dig deep into the hints and pieces of info you gather to find out what to do next. But I absolutely hate the inventory limitation and ammo management. The frustration of need to manage these things really slow down the immersion. Another shortcoming of old game design is clearly evident in the final boss battle. You only have one weapon that shoots slow. Your movement is frustratingly slow so it's a die-reload-fest. You repeat the same process for 4 times. It's just not fun at all.All these flaws in the eye of modern games are kept in and not improved on. That is a design choice so while frustrating, I can accept it.Overall, this is still a great game and a real classic. I can look past some flaws in the outdated design of the original game because Nightdive has done an amazing job recreating the original System Shock.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played the OG System Shock before, but I played the 2nd game first and now got the chance to experience the remake.This is before and after the 1.2 update; Nightdive Studios delivered a better OG game experience. SHODAN is still as terrifying as the 2nd game, but more HD, and her voice acting was on point; SHODAN remains one of gaming's most unforgettable villains, a malevolent AI whose twisted logic and megalomaniacal ambitions constantly threaten humanity.The ending fight improved after the 1.2 update, with more weapons to use and a slight puzzle-solving in it.In conclusion, System Shock is a shining example of how to modernize a classic while staying true to its roots respectfully. _childDocuments_.review: I had to write up something because of the rollercoaster this game had put me through. It's rare for a remake to maintain the difficulty of something made from the era, but even on 2/2/2/2 difficulty (normal?), this game will absolutely grind you. You'll be starved for ammo and health and energy...until you're not. Eventually you're granted no-punishment respawns (in a sense to lull you into thinking dying is okay) before the other half of the game asks you to save scum every door. Writing down notes because sorting and relistening to audio diaries gets taxing. SHODAN's cheapness as a computer that despises you balances well with the meta of the game hating you. Enemies will pick the most inconvenient places to spawn (spawning enemies right after boss fights in the same room), hit-scan you without notice and you'll be backtracking so much that eventually you'll have a diagram of the ship in your head. The final cyberspace fight wasn't even reflective of the other cyberspace battles, nor the combat in the game. The atmosphere, the puzzles - all in all fantastic. Really carries the weight because despite QOL improvements you are going to be battling every aspect of this ship non-stop. I came in at 25 hours with some decent backtracking; I couldn't imagine how anyone could beat this on the hardest mode with a timer. Straight up not sure how to beat this game without a laser rapier.As a game, I felt myself constantly being frustrated and trolled by this machine and that parallel really threw fuel onto the fire of my desire to beat it. I knew SHODAN would throw everything but as I got more powerful weapons, more powerful tech the survival horror turned into horror survival and a memorable game that I don't really wish to replay anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the most frustrating games I've ever played. It actually started of rather fun as I wandered around and explored. But the more I played the worse it got. There is practically no story beyond "computer went psycho". I find myself constantly walking around pushing buttons and flipping switches without knowing what they do or why I'm doing it. I encountered areas where another character supposedly solved a problem, but for some reason I also have to solve the problem which has already been sorted out. Characters who died seemingly reappear after being killed as if nothing happened. I found myself in dead ends numerous times because the game wasn't giving me the slightest hint as to what I had to do. At this point I've practically given up on the game. I have come across too many dead ends to really care about it anymore. I have to find a code, but where is it? No idea. It could be anywhere in any of the maze like levels. It's like trying to find a needle in a haystack.On a more positive note though I will say that the action part of the gameplay is quite fun and can be challenging at times, the controls are pretty decent though using right click to activate things did take a bit of getting used to.The visuals are very nice, it looks like a pretty decent update on the way the original looks.

_childDocuments_.review: Look at you, hacker....  And welcome back SHODAN!  How I missed this franchise!System Shock 2 was one of the seminal games I played growing up, still on my top 10 list of greatest games of all time.  Never got around to playing System Shock 1 mainly because the game was already dated by the time SS2 arrived, and games have only gotten better since then. Always wanted to go back and play the orignal, and with this remake I was finally given the opportunity.I'd forgotten about the remake I pre-ordered years ago, and was pleasantly surprised when it arrived, and exceeded all of my expectations. Sleeper hit of 2023 for me.I expected the game to be vastly inferior to SS2, and boy was I surprised. It's very similar to SS2 gameplay wise and story wise, it's just missing mechanics like weapon degradation, item research, and RPG elements. Other than that it's the same basic immersive sim, you crawling from deck to deck slowly figuring out what's going on and trying to make your way off of this doomed space station.This isn't a 2023 AAA title, and as a "remake" it shouldn't be expected to be. You're playing System Shock because you want to experience it's well earned reputation but on modern hardware. To me this boils down to 1) compelling story and universe, 2) immersive sim gameplay, and 3) SHODAN.  This title delivers 100% on all 3 counts for me.The story was great, and filled in some of the blanks from SS2 for me. Hearing SHODANs after all these years (voiced again by Terri Brosius) was just one of the things I didn't expect and I was thrilled to discover.From a gameplay standpoint, it's downright impressive how well the core 1994 gameplay holds up in 2023. This is the granddaddy of all immersive sims, and playing it in 2023 reminds me why it's so highly regarded. The interface has been upgraded to modern standards, but the core gameplay remains the same.Graphically it's great. I love the modernized but classic "semi pixelated" look that reminds you of 90's games without getting in the way. It's not trying to be a 2023 AAA title, it doesn't need to be. It's updated, fluid, detailed, and definitely "feels" very much in the System Shock universe to me. That's all that matters.Playing this game reminded me why I fell in love with the franchise to begin with. SHODAN is definitely one of the greatest game villains of all time, the original inspiration for GlaDOS (hey Valve we need a Portal 3!). The SS universe is compelling and really deserving of more games in it's future (here's to hoping).Crossing my fingers this makes enough money to justify a System Shock 2 Remake, and additional titles.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock 2 was my introduction to Shodan. It was a game that I've measured everything up against, ever since. I'm telling you this because I can't compare it to the original SS. What I can tell you is, I am really loving this!

_childDocuments_.review: Game has fantastic atmosphere and general vibe.  I love the modern lighting with low res textures, a little bit like Amid Evil.  Story is simple but cool.  Game design is old fashioned and tricky.  It's sometimes unclear where to go and what do to.  Don't be afraid to reference a guide if you find yourself wandering aimlessly for too long.  The enemies get spongy and difficult quickly, forcing you into careful resource management.  It's not a run-and-gun.  More like a skulk-around-and-gun.  I despise the cyberspace sections.  Set them to easy mode when you begin the game so you can spend as little time on them as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play this game with a controller you'll find that, much like the original System Shock, this game is just begging for a remake with better controls and a modern interface.This can be addressed on the user end by using Steam's controller settings to map keyboard and mouse inputs to the controller instead, but given System Shock was already a great game with lackluster controls, this reads as a mission failure to me.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. It's a bit crazy when you play this to see how little games have advanced aside from graphics. This game still holds up wonderfully in the current generation. It's like playing the progenitor of Prey and you can see all the game-changing ideas the team had back in the day. Props to Nightdive for recreating the game faithfully. I was worried it'd be like the Gothic 2 remake but no, it holds up and I loved it. The only downsides are a few crashes (especially around the chess game and the cyber levels), and I felt like the music was a big downgrade from the original. Aside from those small points, I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I walk through this game so far and there are many things that have me think "I can see with this is a 9/10 game in many peoples minds" Then there are the moments where I question it heavily. Progress is a drag, the coin and garbage system is trash. There are NO explanations on how to do anything, and its not intuitive either, there is no clear telling of what to do, where to go. Its horrid. A harder enemy difficulty just makes the enemies super spongey, and as a result in a game where resources are scarce, it makes it a very annoying experience, where you feel pulled to use your wrench or pipe, which is the most boring ass melee combat imaginable, with the most unpolished animations and slow ass time to kill. Its boring, so boring.One thing you can respect this game for is staying mega true to the original. I think it hurts it more than it does good. These new graphics and the direction it took I found questionable, and the nearly unchanged mechanics made me wonder if some things should have been changed. Some remakes and stray from the original path. This game feels more like a remaster almost, because of the little changes in many core things. It feels weighty, clunky even. As someone who has played System Shock 2, this is simply just a let down to me, I hope going forwards they will remake it, without changing much like they did this because SS2 is perfect. This game, felt aged, and did nothing to fight that aged feel. The hacking floaty levels are annoying, disorrienting, and boring. Level design is ok, but its all over the place, and not for a single second do I feel like it gets interesting enough to move through it as little of it changes massively. Feels like randomly generated rooms slapped together. Once again, this game should have got a different kind of remake treatment that is all.8/10 - this is one of those red sevens or eights I give rarely. The whole "I think this game is good but I dont like it" scenario I rarely utter. This game may be the perfect rebuilding of the original to the original fans, but for me, I see a game that needs more polish, a game that needed to be built on more than just a near perfect recreation. The original System Shock was not a wine, and this shouldnt have got the wine treatment in my opinion. I really wanted to like it, well, I tried.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great game. Just finished it - I had a weird bug or glitch happen on my first playthrough at about 90% of the way into the game. The game was just so addictive and exciting that I ended up playing through it again just to get to the end. Totally worth it. The final few levels are a ton of fun and I really enjoyed the action-focused approach that it built to. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The original was my favorite game in the 90's, and with this remake it comes back to my top 10. It looks gorgeous, has that perfect creepy atmosphere, and I just love those claustrophobic corridors. But it's not perfect.1. The intro is dull and lacks music in the right places. Nothing like the original.2. No visual or audible feedback in combat when you hit an enemy. Especially not with melee weapons. The original did this better too.3. The chess puzzle. It's complete BS. 4. The cyber space sequences are too long, and you forget what you were doing once you come back to Citadel station.With the latest patch it also seems to have become a buggy mess:- Start it up into the main menu, and it runs at 1 FPS sometimes.- Click "Continue" only to find yourself in a place which definitely wasn't the latest save game, and with the wrong protagonist (the female instead of male).- Try jump up on a chair, and get killed by the physics engine going crazy.- Try to place a map marker and pat yourself on the shoulder if you succeed.- Crashes.- Get stuck on the final boss fight, because the game doesn't trigger a certain event.The remake is generally much more difficult at the same difficulty setting. I die a lot. Take a jump, miss the platform and you'll die from fall damage. Open a door, not ready for the surprise on the other side, and die again. And again. Some areas were like that - take out one enemy, die, and go back to take out the next, die and repeat again.My overall impression is positive though! It's extremely immersive, and for me that's quite much due to the slow pace and the exploration. Even if the levels are chaotic mazes, I still enjoy the navigational challenge. The music is great too.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A remake that really shines; fully remaking the original, even the enemy placement and behaviour, even the little bit of jank from the 90's PC games - I love this game! I played a lot of the demo when it came out and I was blown away by it then. The full game lives up to the potential, the artstyle is very much like the original - but in 3D. It's somehow the way I remember it looking and feeling, but comparing them side by side the graphic overhaul is extremely noticable. It looks good, it plays well, I highly, highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything a game needs in a remake. There is no filler, no cutting corners, and no nonsense. This is the original game improved while retaining all of its charm, even including the actual voice of Shodan, Terri. Among all of the fantastic dialogue and world immersion, I noticed a bunch of goofy, messed-up stuff that raised the game even further, not because the bugs were awful. They are what made classic games amazing, a randomly placed NPC swinging from the ceiling to greet me on a return trip through an area I had entered multiple times and had never seen him before as if the game was mocking me but in a classic way like "welcome home."It goes by old school means. You pick p a key item and drop it somewhere? Good luck finding it unless you're recording your gameplay for streams or content. There needs to be a quest item map locator or something. I've spent so many hours backtracking very important key items. Thank god you can return to the groves once jettisoned if you have dropped key items there.I intend to finish this game once I have some free time and am not suffocated by all the games I have to go through, but my god has this been entertaining and nostalgic, maybe a little bit exhausting but that's due to the long session and games getting to me, the games great!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original. But have both waited and been excited to play this for a long time. I'm sorry, but after playing just that little bit (under 2 hours) I feel like my money should be put towards something else to play. It just isn't doing much for me and I'm questioning but interested in learning later what actual remake changes and improvements have been made. Because the UI controls just piss me off and I wish they were better.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive did an excellent job with the source material but the awful level design is just frustrating. Generally not fun to play. I think everyone should stick to the easy difficulties for a first playthrough.+ Nice graphics, performance is fine no hitches or other Unreal engine problems. TAA is a bit blurry but I'm ok with that. + Nice atmosphere and music, weapons and animations are nice. - Quicksave spam is mandatory- I have to dry heave whenever I open the map screen- No FSR so Radeon users are stuck with the resolution scale decrease if their system can't handle 4K.I played a lot of 90's games but 90's game design is not fun anymore kids.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!!! There was a time that I wondered if this will ever see the light of day and if it does, is this another Duke Nuk'em Forever but man Nightdive really pulled it off. The atmosphere was taken from the original and they successfully enhanced it while keeping it true, accomplishing this in my book is probably the most difficult task of a remake, to retain the original feel. The enemies are much stronger and better fleshed with resistances that almost made me cry from happiness when I discovered the speed boots. Run Forest, RUN!!!!!The most impressive part is the world of Citadel station, the re-imagined space station is mind blowing, the sheer amount of painful detail that went into recreating each map that make the station an entirely believable but terrifying place. I've finished SS1 more times than I care to count and I got lost!! (now where did I put that noob badge.) What also blows my mind is how the redesign has really brought out the genius behind the level designs, I will never look at SS1 the same way again. Its not perfect, but its close. All in all, Thank you Night Dive for keeping your promise, Thank you for not c***ing up my most treasured game and for doing it so well that it felt like a brand new experience mixed with nostalgia. I take my hat off and bow my head in respect of your accomplishment.System Shock 2 is going to be awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Played the original years ago - this remake retains everything that made the original great...but be forewarned: it retains much of the difficulty of the old game, too. It's been upgraded with the controls of a modern FPS, but there is no quest log or markers and no friendly assistant telling you where to go. Turn off the strict 10-hour time limit your first playthrough, however, and you will have a blast. There are several new additions to the game (recycling, for example) that make it more interesting and the level design - although archaic and convoluted - has some truly dramatic and memorable areas (ex: the security level), enhanced now with Nightdive's slick modern graphics. It's hard to improve upon a classic, but they've managed to do it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The action is a delight, Terri Brosius is amazing as SHODAN, they succeeded in adapting the old-resolution visuals, and the 90's level design manages to surprise me as I play.  There's a sharp drop-off in enemy sound with distance which means I can't hear their creepy audio without being deafened by anything close-by, but otherwise I feel fully immersed and I love every minute on Citadel Station.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic remake with impeccable art direction.  Cool to be able to play the first system shock, which I initially avoided because of its age. It seems it's the definitive way to play the original game, rather than a new game altogether. The main game has largely been preserved, while UI, cutscenes, and bossfights have been retooled and improved.  Most notable for me, however, is the game's visuals, which were produced in conjunction with the original game's lead artist. The result is a very authentic and heartfelt reinterpretation that embraces the idiosyncrasies of the 90s classic.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an incredibly pretty game that does an amazing job at upgrading citadel station graphically to the original, overall game play however I believe is a downgrade. Guns look great and have good animations but the act of shooting and the enemy getting hit does not feel all that responsive. Melee feels clunky and it doesn't feel like I'm hitting anything while swinging. There's also a few other gameplay things that are changed like "bosses" removing the ability to regenerate after you die which feels cheap in a bad way especially since they tend to do way more damage than enemies resulting in a quick and off guard death resulting in unnecessary time loss. I also feel like the inventory management feels like it's only there because it was in system shock 2, I don't think it fits the game all that well and feels like it only slows the pace of the game and serves as an annoyance. Another huge loss I personally feel is the music, while whats in the game is not bad on its own, it fails to give every floor any kind of unique atmosphere. It ends up making a lot of the floors end up feeling the same in terms of atmosphere which was the opposite in the original. Maintenance always stood out in the original because of its dark hallways and its droning song, now it reminds of the other floors, missing its dark hallways and having minimal soundtrack, like all the other floors.Also there's a handful of rather annoying bugs and soft locks I've encountered from energy draining when all the left modules were off, and to what killed my play through, items not staying in the elevators and not appearing the trash chute in reactor which is where I kept all my key items needed to progress which I didn't realize till 5 hours later in my play through.Overall, the game has an incredible presentation but lacks beyond that, it looks and runs like a 60$ game should but it plays and lacks the some of the atmosphere the original had that will cost only you 10$ on steam so I'm unsure to say what price this game should be, 40$ felt like too much but anything under feels like too little for how much effort went into the remake.Note: Also I will mention cyberspace is a big improvement over the original although I feel some of the sections drag for a bit and it's a bit mindless
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest remakes of a video game of all time.It's the perfect resurrection of a game, there's just so much to it honestly, it's really hard how to describe the worth of this game and how good it is in the eyes of a original System Shock fan.Outside of the perspective of a System Shock 1 fan, it's still an amazing game
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A remake that preserves all the good parts of the original and removes all the clunky controls from a game that came out a month before I was born. It's surprising how modern the level design feels, surpassing stuff made today by miles in a sort of metroid-vania exploration of a single spaceship that inspired the likes of Prey and Dishonored. Satisfying to puzzle out in a way few modern games achieve, even some of those that bill themselves as immersive sims.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is a real master piece. The musics are awesome, so is the ambient sounds and the level design.A truly good remake and the game don't hold your hand and that was refreshing. Shodan scares me way too much but that adds to the greatness of this remake. The maze design can give you headaches sometimes if your have the memory of a goldfish but if so you'll find guides and playthroughs without any doubt.10/10 (keep a notepad or a paper and a pen to note the different codes and pay attention to all the logs)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original a lot when it came out in the 90s. Some parts are very familiar - I remember playing the cover-disk demo which was about half the first level more than 10 times - but it all feels fresh. Love the re-imagining of the puzzle locks.Shodan has always been my favourite video game 'villain' and the one thing I was worried about in this game was that it would have been made less sinister - fortunately it is just the right amount of evil and scary.Normally, I am not a fan of games where enemies re-spawn out of thin air for no apparent reason in an area where you are sure you wiped them all out but at least here it is 'explained' with the floor rising up and a caged zombie or bot being released.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive does it again! Though this is not their usual Enhancement like we are used to. Now people don't run away in fear when I mention System Shock and how amazing it is. Did they make the game easier? No. Has the plot been changed to suit a new future narrative like Dead Space did? No. Is this a remake a love, sweat, and blood? YES! You can feel it in your veins, that they fought tooth and nail to give us System Shock without any modern shenanigans and just modern innovations.The $40 price is well justified, and could of been one of those $70 games that people claim the gaming industry should be moving to. If this is your first time hearing the name Nightdive please go look up some of their amazing Enhanced games! Especially Quake which is make in their custom KEX Engine and is such a treat for people like me at my age.Download the demo, if you like it buy the game. If not look up a few YouTube videos and spread the word of System Shock.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock: a game I heard a lot about but never really knew why. I heard bits about what made it great.The remake was my entry into System Shock. I had seen the DF video but waited until it was on sale. And some other games I was playing weren't as interesting.I like to game, so I started to play on some settings as hard. Man, did I not like that experience. Enemies rushing and respawning right in front of you all the time. If this was going to be the experience throughout the whole game, no thank you.I was only on the first level, so I restarted, putting some stuff on medium difficulty.But why did I decide to keep the puzzles on the hardest difficulty. On this playthrough the first puzzle I come against, I am stumped. The puzzle is way harder than the previous ones I encountered. Partly because I don't know everything yet to solve these puzzles. There is no lead into it. So what do I do? I start the game again. But this time just on medium difficulty.Let’s go over the actual review. But how do I start this?The station feels alive, or rather felt alive. Mutants, dead corpses, and audio logs.However, localization is a pain. Binding of keys is a travesty; I use AZERTY. So the hotkeys on the toolbar don't work. And no way to rebind them. How fun when you try to heal in a panic.Also, unbinding the interaction key from the mouse button and then putting F on bind 1 while it was on bind 2 breaks the game. No F at all for you. And then when you unbind 1, it no longer shows up on the tutorial hints.This game is also not like other games. No objectives, no clear path forward. You have to go through the logs to see what the next objective is. I kind of like it. But it has some flaws. Or what I am missing is a log of the random things the machine says. For example, the diagnose machine says something about 428, but I missed what exactly. Which made me look up where I am supposed to find this relay. This is also a flaw of the maintenance area. It's not clear unless you know that you can hover over the relay to see what its purpose is or if it’s number 428.Talking about being stuck, I had to look up an answer twice because I don't trust this game. First time was when I got into a dead end. But apparently, there were hidden doors. Something I had never known about before. And was never aware of as a possibility.Second time I was stuck was because I did not see the level 3 boots because they were obscured by a dead body and next to a charging station.Inventory space is a pain. It looks good on paper, but man, does it become a limitation near the end of the game. I have guns but no inventory space to pick up items to go to the recycling to make some money. Unless I do specific runs to do this. This kind of screws with the game loop for me. And wasn't really what I was looking for. If they just did the Minecraft thing, it would make it more pleasant.Energy is another big part of the game. We have guns and our suite that work on the same energy. I can’t say i hate it. But it’s rather annoying that energy is taken of you when it in not actively being used. Turn on hazard control without using it well there goes your energy. There is also no way to calculate or see how much these suite abilities use. I only used the abilities near the end of the game because i was forced. The hazard ability also only seem to mitigate part of the problem and never worked as good as detox. Even when turning it on after you ran through radiation doesn’t work as good as just taking detox in the same scenario. Which makes me question. Is this thing on?But man, all of this seems to pale against the story of System Shock. The station, the AI, and the people. It just all works together. The people on the station trust the AI because it has ethical constraints. It does erratic things. Not because it's crazy but because it's brilliant. At least that's how leadership hails it. But not the people who actually have to work with the changes.While the difficulty was set on medium, some parts were still a challenge to get through.So overall, I liked the game. But I don't really feel confident in the studio. They were able to put the game back on the map. But don't really feel like they succeeded in dialing it up to 11.

_childDocuments_.review: I played all the originals and at that time, those boxy bastards captured something special in early 2000's in gaming that honestly has been quite lacking these days. This feels like a remake and i barely remembered the game but it was really a great remake. The engine and visuals really brought to life Citadel station. And that crazy psycho Shodan is still awesome. The graphics were quite impressive, the team could have made it perfectly HD but they had this aesthetic that just screamed retro "enough". What a great job to the team and sparking some memories.Now it wasnt perfect, some loading crashed the games and some bugs here and there existed but nothing to the point we see nowadays in all these AAA games, at 40 bucks this was a steal and worth all the time i put into it. Its a no brainer to try it and get in the System Shock world.If they remade the second one, already on the wishlist and next time i will take that go fund me more seriously as i was hesitant it would even come out shame on me.

_childDocuments_.review: Or System Shock (2023) is a first person space horror shooter.You're a hacker. In exchange for not prosecuting you, you remove the ethics filter on the AI for a space station. To sweeten the deal you also get a military grade implant.You wake up after the implant surgery and find out that maybe removing the ethics filter from the AI might not have been the best thing you could have done. No one is there when you wake up and you are attacked by mutants that look like they used to be human.Full disclosure, I backed this on Kickstarter and my name is in the credits. I backed this because of how much I enjoyed the original System Shock. I was not disappointed in the remake, though I was frustrated more than once.It starts of like your normal shooter. You start off with no weapons, upgrade to a melee weapon and then finally to ranged weapons. Along the way you can purchase upgrades for your weapons, more damage, faster reloads, less power usage, and so on. In addition to weapons upgrades you can find implants to give you abilities and protection.You earn money by recycling "trash" you find around the station. You can either take it to the recycle center or vaporize it, for less value, normally about half. You can also find money on the corpses you find laying around, though nowhere near what you can get from recycling.As the game progresses you have start working to fix the mess you started by taking down Shodan. You work level by level to reclaim the station. The goals you need to complete are found by discovering text and audio logs. The logs will give you clues, combinations and objectives. The combinations are random, per play through, so you will have to find these files.You are frequently required to back track to a previous level. The Maintenance level was the one that got me, there is a head that you need to open a door, but you can't access the door until you reduce the security below a certain level, which cannot be completed until you perform another task on a different level. I had to restart the game because I knew I needed the head, but after a few hours I put it in a "safe" place and couldn't find it when I was at the door I needed it for.There are several mini games you will need to play. Two of them are used to open locked areas, most levels have three of these type of puzzles. They come in two flavors, a railroad type game where you have to switch the tracks to route the power between two square lights. The second is a level game where you need to hook power plugs to available outlets and route the power to get the required level. If you are having difficulty, some of the robots will drop a logic bomb, which will auto solve the puzzle for you. There is also a cyberspace game where you fly a ship and have to shoot data streams to open or unlock doors. Most of the cyberspace games weren't that difficult, but there were a few that game me fits. If you fail the game, by dying, you have to start over from square one. Most of the cyberspace games have more than one target that you need to clear. Some of the cyberspace doors are required to advance the story, others are just armory doors for weapons and bullets.Your ammo is restricted. Some of the ammo runs offer your suit power and there are recharge stations for you to charge up. You can also find batteries to partially charge up in the field. Energy weapons were my favorites as I would frequently go back to the charging stations resulting in unlimited ammo.Health is a lot like ammo. There are patches that will partially heal you, with a big up front heal and a trickle over time. Then full first aid packs that will heal you to full health. There are also medical beds that will also heal you to full health. The medical beds are not on every level, so you will need to either back track to a level with a bed or use one of the other healing options.As the story progresses the difficulty of the mobs also increases. Inventory management is a large part of the game. You can quick slot four weapons, but they take up space in your inventory, along with the ammo needed to use them. You will need to find the four weapons that work best for you and take them with you. You can store weapons in places where you can find them again, I highly recommend either the med bed or recycler on the Reactor level. As ammo is limited I found myself using a single weapon and changing to a different weapon when I ran low on ammo. There are two inventory increases to find and one requires beating a chess puzzle. Like the codes you will find the chess puzzle is unique for every playthrough, mine the opponent had three rooks (castles).You are given very little information on what you need to do, or how you need to do it. There is a lot of backtracking to places you have previously been. All codes are random, so a guide is of minimal help.CPU: AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X3DMotherboard: Gigabyte X670E AORUS EXTREME (rev. 1x)RAM: G.SKILL Trident Z5 Neo Series (AMD Expo) DDR5 RAM 64GB (2x32GB)Video: ASUS TUF Gaming GeForce RTX 4080Or

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game on easy mode.  I tried it on "normal" but got tired of dying every five minutes.  The game is really stingy on ammo.    It is retro and contemporary  at the same time, which I like.    And the maze layout is kind a cool.   But the best part of the game is the "save anywhere" feature.  Can't beat that.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, would recommend. But please do yourself a favor and don't play with Cyberspace difficulty set to hard. I love Descent and even I think Cyberspace sucks in this. Maybe it did in the original game too. There's no good visual feedback on whether you're hitting things or if you're being hit and you're annoyingly slow. You can't change difficulty after starting the game so set that ♥♥♥♥ to easy. The puzzles aren't great either but they're not offensively bad.Also, the OG system shock would let you write notes on the map and that's missing from this. The recent 1.2 update broke the functionality of map markers but even if they worked, you only get one kind of marker. There's no way to indicate what the thing you marked is. This game has a lot of going back to previous floors to find a quest item and not being able to mark a thing you think will be important later sucks.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Great reboot on this classic but it shouldn't have taken 7 years . The original game was done from the ground up in 18 months. Still , praise to Nightdive for producing the enhanced version and this modern SS1 restoration. Looking forward SS2 enhanced and curious if they will have any involvement in SS3. Currently playing SS1 enhanced and 2023 version levels back to back and it's been a great time. The original SS1 classic is abysmal to play today but fascinating and fun to reflect on. I remember playing it when it was first released on floppy and running into Origin play testers when I lived in Austin TX. Absolutely one of the best games ever and still is. If you like reboots from this Era of games definitely check out Descent Overload as it is excellent as well. All and all great Job Nightdive. You guys just need to pick up the pace a little.  Don't follow the Robert's Space Industries model.  This project shouldn't have taken more than 3 years to compete.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A great SciFi survival horror style FPS, awesome aesthetic, great music, and game/map design from another time. It's not without a few warts/frustrations, but it's a masterful recreation of a masterpiece of a game. It holds up if you've got the patience for the older game design philosophies that challenge you to pay attention and don't hold your hand. That can always be a bit tricky if you don't have time to play often, I made good use of the new Steam Notes feature and made it through without too much trouble, although this was my second play through (the first was SS:Enhanced earlier this year). The Enhanced Edition was good enough to rivet me to my chair for my first ever play through, 30 years after the OG game came out. I would absolutely recommend this version, they have done an excellent job faithfully recreating and lovingly updating the original.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. Congrats to Nightdive, this game is an achievement. It respects its roots and builds a contemporary version that's sleeker, faster, and quite beautiful. I'm seeing hard surface in my dreams. Terri Brosius is back as SHODAN and Eric (her hubs, the dude who did the music for Thief and Deus Ex IIRC) did the processing of her voice too. So excellent. The VO performances are fantastic.I never write a review until I've finished a game but this is an exception. It's too great to miss. Play it immediately for the love of Looking Glass. Their legacy is on full display here.Do yourself a favor and turn off "toggle aim" and then bind aim to right mouse. Then just use F to interact like you would in Dishonored/Thief. E is lean right and you should definitely use Q and E to lean if you want to survive. Folks know the name of the game with oldschool immsims but in case you don't Q/E are your good good frens.I also found it useful to manually bind the... augs? Hardware you install. Having easy on/off is great for shields and boots and things, and mine didn't come auto-bound. I'm sure you all know to do this but JIC. _childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent, even coming into it with no prior experience with the System Shock series. For me, this was the perfect balance of challenging & mysterious yet not so challenging or mysterious that it's frustrating. There are no quest markers, no journal, no nothing. On settings above easy, the game delivers all its instruction in the form of audio and text logs that you have to find around the station, and it's the task of the player to keep notes and figure out how all the various things work. It even goes so far as to not tell the player which items are quest-related!The audio and visual design is stellar. Everything looks suitably retro but still very pretty, a nice retro-futurism that I haven't seen since Alien Isolation. The sounds of the environment are great, but the sounds of the weapons are even better (the magnum being the best). This is especially impressive considering that despite the game being more-or-less non-linear and about 20 hours long, it takes up less than 10 gigs of hard drive space.In terms of stability, there are two minor issues and one semi-major issue. This is all describing the release build of the game, and it's refreshing to see only a couple problems in a game released this recently.I don't have performance problems in very many games so I'm not sure if this is the game being well crafted or my PC being souped-up, but the performance of the game is perfect. No framerate drops, no areas that mysteriously run poorly, not even so much as a frame rate hitch (outside of a momentary one when saving). Saving and loading is practically instant.All in all, if you are a fan of immersive sim type games, retro futurism, AI apocalypse stories, or survival horror, I would strongly recommend picking this one up. At a time where games are now being sold for $70 USD or more, this one is absolutely worth the $40 they're asking for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played both original games, this remake sticks with what worked with both, and alters what didn't so that it isn't ridiculously complicated. Adapt to those hurdles, and System Shock will prove to be an incredible experience found nowhere else.Strong recommendation, and if you're still not sure, the demo does a decent job showing you what you're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: All's well that ends well? Not quite. But there is an happy end, dont worry!Regardless of the actually quality of this game, we should not forget or turn a blind eye to the fact, that the development of this game was a mess. Unfortunately, this  kind projects are the reason why many people are disapointed with Kickstarter and Crowdfunding in general. Thats bad for the overall reputation of all game developers who want to kickstart their idea and projects and its bad for potential backers, fans and gamers as well. NightDiveStudios did a very poor job developing his game with the community. The game was successfully funded in 2016 and the estimated release year was in 2017. Its 2023 now and it took this much time to actually finish and release this game. The original was developed within 1-2 years, the remake took almost 7 years, just to tell you how long it actually took until the game finally released. I am still very disapointed with NDS, their poor communication style with the community, the way how they managed to report on updates, problems and delays, the way they treated Beta-Backer and many, many more things. If you want to know more about the problems, go to their kickstarter page. You will find everything there if you interested. Unfortunately gaming journalism did a poor job as well and didn't covered the problems of the game and only wrote and talked about the game  after it was released, At least mostly. Shame on you as well!But now to the actual game: Is it a good game after all this problems and delays? YES. IT IS. Fortunately! :) Many other Kickstarter-Projects that had the same infamous development history like System Shock Remake weren't so lucky. (Aquanox Deep Decent for example) But in the end, the Remake did a very good job remaking the old concept of a great sci-fi horror immersive sim game, that was way ahead of its time and inspired many games like BioShock, Prey and many more.I do not encountered any bigger bugs and/or problems in my entire playthrough and the game was very polished right from the start. The graphics, design, lighting, sound and atmosphere is great. Of course I liked the gameplay, weapons, levels, puzzles and every other aspect of the game as well. And to encounter the iconic villian AI SHODAN after all this years, really was great!A fair warning: This game did not hold your hand by any means. You dont get an obvious questmarker for every single step, you need to do to proceed in the game. You have to explore the different areas, read logs and e-mails, experiment with the existing tools, items, machines and technologies and find the points of interests YOURSELF. Some people call this "outdated design", but for me its just an execution for people who only want to follow a quest arrow and didn't want to think for themselves. Thinking for yourself and figuring out things on your own will NEVER be outdated. Additionally: You dont need a doctor in PhD to solve the games puzzles and tasks, but you need to read instructions carefully and think out-of-the-box sometimes to get across an obstacle. If thats a problem for you or if you think thats an "outdated design", you wont have much fun with this game. So be warned!For anyone else: You will have much fun with this remake of a true gaming history masterpiece. There are  some smaller issues(like wobbling and hilarious ragdoll bugs) and smaller graphical glitches, but nothing that will destroy this great experience. SHODAN is back, after all this years. And thats actually great! :)tl;dr: Development of this game was as mess and I am really disapointed with NDS and the way they treated their backers. But the game is great. So I can recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to releases from the last few years, most of it being absolute garbage, the titles I've been enjoying oddly enough are indies, remakes and remasters, just older games in general. This game honestly really surprised me being in a genre I have a love-hate relationship with, that being the Immersive Simulator genre. Yet this game just clicked and pulled me right in. While it is a remake, as far as I know it's only a huge HUGE graphical overhaul. The gameplay is pretty much kept intact. It very much is a clunky FPS game that can be pretty hard at times, and that isn't even the most difficult part. What will absolutely rip your balls off (assuming you have any) is the fact that you have no objective markers pointing you in the right direction and instead having to read audio logs to understand what to do. It's a little hard to recommend this game because it is so old school and archaic, but in my opinion it is not a bad thing that these gameplay aspects are like this. Hell it's like they are intentional and almost extremely faithful to the original 1994 game that was way ahead of its time. I do recommend it as someone who really enjoyed their time with this remake and got all the achievements for, just know what you're getting into is not here to hold your hand. Welcome to Citadel Station, Insect.

You managed to recreate the feel of the original, meanwhile streamlining all the UI bits that made it hard to play and somehow managed to retain that special feeling. I'll be spending some time on Citadel Station, once again.

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid this game if you like playing with a controller, or if you expect the polish of a Dead Space Remaster, Dying Light 2, or Prey 2017 for combat, movement, and managing the environment.  As of 05/31/2023 this game is seriously lacking in polish and smoothness of movement, inventory management, and world management in general.  Case in Point #1: If there are 20 items to collect you have to hand aim at each one of them tediously with your controller to collect them one by one.   Case in Point #2: Because the retro textures have the same 'depth' you cannot easily distinguish a button from the rest of the walls in the room. Ditto for door handles, etc.  It looks like someone threw up Neon and Pastel's everywhere, and then Ravers went on a bender and then decorated the station with it.  Nothing on the walls or in the world makes immediate intuitive sense.Another problem is the game does not have good FOV adjustment for wide screen monitors either.  What did they code & test on, 4:3 or 16:9 monitors?!I'll take another look at this game in a few months and see if they have patches to deal with gameplay issues, or if modders have improved this.Play with KB & Mouse and I assume you will have a better experience.  Avoid for now if you are a controller player.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a hard frustrating grind. the level layout is very painful, there are no objective markers or journal as such to show you what your next objective is, You have to listen to audio logs and try and figure out from there what you're meant to do. You will wander around aimlessly for AGES at a time until you stumble onto a room you didn't go in before or find a switch or button you didn't flick last time or you come across an enemy you didn't see last time. You are frequently scavenging for weapons and ammo too but 95% of the items you pick up you will find useless (they're even marked as junk). The combat feels clunky and awkward too.The graphics aren't bad but for a modern day remake they are very sub ordinary, thankfully you can more or less run this game on a toaster so if your PC specs are low then this is one game that you won't have an issue running.Overall, I did not enjoy my time playing this game, can't recommend it sorry. Too hard, too frustrating, too cryptic. Maybe in 1994's standards it might have been fine but it's a formula that just doesn't work today.

_childDocuments_.review: System Shock is a remake of the 1994 classic of the same name. This game was a beloved cult classic and had major influence on other games going forward. Widely regarded as one of the first Immersive sims and survival horror-eqsue games, this remake had alot to live up to. It took around 8 years after this game was announced for it to finally be released. So, did they deliver on this product? I've never played the original game, so I will not be viewing it in comparison, but as a standalone product.I absolutely enjoyed this game and was hooked within the first four hours. This game is essentially a horror rpg with item conservation and metroidvania level design as it's primary loop. What you end up getting from this is a story that is told almost entirely by the environment alone and the audio logs left laying around the station. You can very much see the influence this game would go on to have on Both Bioshock and Prey with this presentation and level design. Both this form of storytelling and the level design really encourage the player to explore and learn every corner of Citadel Station. The game has many great narrative moments and is a blast to play with all the weapons and abilities. The visual style is also very unique, with the characters appearing to be high resolution, but still having stylized pixels as the textures. I think this was a great homage to the original games visuals and they look pretty good for the vibe and atmosphere of the game. Overall, I ONLY recommend this game to people who are fans of Immersive sims or more older punishing design. This game does not have any quest markers or objective lists, only giving you a map and notes to take. The narrative and objectives are all told in voice calls and audio logs, leaving it all up to you to immersive yourself in the atmosphere and perceive everything. It is not casual friendly.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a brain and enjoy using it , you will enjoy this masterful remake of a legendary classic from the golden age of gaming. It does have a few flaws but they are pretty minor in comparison with all that it does better than the original. With chris avellone on board it's no wonder this game came out so amazing. Great work on this gem nightdive.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's alright. Would I recommend it as a new game? Yeah, probably.Would I recommend it as a remake - Probably not.I played and LOVED System Shock. It's easily in my Top 3 of games. So probably my review is biased by nostalgia and comparisons between the versions. Then, however, it is a remake, so that may be fair game. I even still play the Enhanced Version of System Shock from time to time, and enjoy it very much. Yeah, so the graphics is blocky and dated - who cares? Its fun! And while I could always go for another round of the Original, I fear I will have to force myself to keep playing and finishing this. Keep in mind - I'm only almost through the second level. Lets start with something positive:They certainly could reproduce the atmosphere of the Original. You feel right at home on Citadel.Now some things that annoy me:- Recycling: If you're a loot hoarder like me, you'll hate it. You can recycle junk stuff at a machine for credits. Or you can 'vaporise' it for junk, roughly worth half the credit value of the machine. So you're either running around with an inventory full of junk, going to the recycler and back, or you always have the feeling of wasting money. It's especially bad if you're on a new level and havent run across the recycler yet .That's a personal thing, granted, but it takes away from the fun for me. What's NOT personal is that you can recycle and vaporise broken weapons - but not working ones. I don't need a third Mini-Pistol, thank you. But I can't t recycle it unless its broken? Bollocks. - The station design. It's somewhat more realistic, maybe. Useful? No. In the original, you could spot at a glance if there was a button or a useable object, since the background was rather uniform. In this, there are lights and screens all over the place. Can I press this lighted button? No. This one here? Yes. This one over there? No.Once again, a matter of personal choice, but I think a bit more clarity would have been good.- The puzzles: I like puzzles. But if you randomize your puzzles, and if the first puzzle I run across on my second game I get stuck on for 15 minutes and still can't solve it - it kinda stops me from playing further. In the original, I believe the puzzles were set. The first one was easy, a couple of clicks - even on the hardest puzzle setting. (Later ones were tougher, but you get logic probes later on that will let you bypass them, if you felt it necessary.) Also, I said it during development, but still: I hate that the puzzles, keypads etc. have to be used in your usual viewscreen. Press those buttons with your crosshairs, don't even think about having an enlarged HUD window version for easier access!And last, and most certainly the biggest issue: - Cyberspace.Yes, I'm one of the thousands of people complaining about cyberspace. Sorry. As others said, it's empty. Big empty halls, spawning enemies in an arena-shooter way. Thats about it. And if you fail the CS level, you will have to redo it from the beginning.Now, in the original, there was a lot of stuff in there. Keys, notes, software upgrades, data files...  and if you were beaten halfway through, you could reconnect, and the enemies you had already finished were still finished. Which means, even in tough CS levels, you could grind your way through if you healed up in between. Now? Succeed - or retry.And, seriously, who thought that Shock needed an arena shooter part? "We're remaking an atmospheric survival adventure game - so of course, we need a part where you tape down the fire button and strafe around with lots of enemies"Then there are a couple of little annoyances for me: No quick-heal button. No button to play the last unplayed audio log.  No auto-junk, junk all or whatever. The ever repeating annoying animations (using a medbed, using a keycard, grabbing keycards, audio logs, etc) which you WILL at some point wish to be able to just skip. If you want to quickly grab three things, but the first one is an audio log, and you will have to wait for the animation to finish before you can pick up the keycard, and wait for that animation to finish before you can pick up the third thing - you'll know what I mean.Also, the occasional lack of info: Like many, it took me some time to notice that on the puzzles the plugs had different power. And you don't know what setting your weapon is on or what ammo you loaded - if you don't already know it. For example: The pistol has normal and Teflon rounds. Loading one you see the ammo count. Loading the other, you see a circle around the ammo count. Thats it. Would it have been so hard to put a little "Teflon" below it, or a "T"? You know, like the Original did?All in all: This certainly isn't bad, but I recommend you play System Shock Enhanced Version, if the graphics dont bother you. I find it much more fun and actually even somewhat easier to get around in.Edit: Almost through now. Not feeling better, rather worse.There are so many QOL things that just weren't added, it baffles me.- You can't split stacks. Recycler gives 1 credit for each 10 scrap. You have 57. Well, get ready to waste 7, or don't recycle.  You want to stash half your ammo pile? Tough luck.- No quick-heal button, I think I already mentioned that, but it still bugs me.- You can't add notes to the map. Like in, for example, you know... SYSTEM SHOCK!?!There's a door you can only open after level security has been dropped? Just search for it again! You need one digit from the CPU cores on each level for a code. Better write it down on a piece of paper, because you certainly won't in your high-tech Computer hacker gear! Text editors are dead, man, dead!!- The inventory. Dear Lord, it's small. In the Original, you could keep 7 weapons, with all the ammo you got, 7 types of grenades, 7 healing and boosting salves, and 7  misc items (batteries, severed heads, c4, etc.) In this? Well, everything takes space. I have like 5 weapons, ammo for them and other weapons, a couple of healing items, some batteries, emp grenades, some quest items and credits, and my inventory is full. Get a new weapon? One you (yet) only have 3 shots for? Well, either skip it or drop one of your "old" weapons. Oh, and your ammo stack for guns x and y has reached max capacity, so either use it up or skip the rounds you just found.- The recycler. Ohh, the bane of my existence. The bigger, more valuable broken weapons are 2x4. The recycler is 3x3. Yes, you're right - you can't recycle them directly. It's nice that it says recycling will give you 5 credits, but in fact you are just not able to recycle it. Ever.- I feel better about the recycler and scrapping mechanics now, though - mainly because I am now able to ignore them. You get credits, but there's not a lot you can spend those on, so recycling is just a basic thing and not really worth it. Mostly you'll need it for weapon upgrades you can find 1-2 on every level, I think. Then you can buy some healing and aid patches. And ammo, which is really, really sparse (each vendor has two ammo items, and there are like 2-3 of them  per level). You don't really need to buy ammo, though, IMO - and if you do, the little there is to buy likely won't make much difference.Besides that, all you can spend your credits on is... snacks. Great.Edit 2: Done, finally. And let me just say... ugggggghh. The last level, beating SHODAN.I feel like now I owe an apology to Shock 2 for what I thopught about its last level. Its just...bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game if you like atmospheric sci-fi horror shooters with a immersive sim element. The original was too outdated for my taste, however this version is an excellent blend of old-school gameplay with modern quality of life elements.Exploring and figuring out what transpired to the space station is very engaging. Trying to stay alive while managing resources and navigating around obstacles is a very compelling gameplay loop that had me quite hooked until the very end. The audio logs and e-mails provide a paint a bleak story which keeps you hooked in the story. The villain and the station itself are an entity of its own and honestly a unique antagonistic force against the player.System Shock looks and sounds great, maintaining a smooth gameplay experience. Guns kick like a mule and enemies have a tangible sense of weight behind them. The inventory management is always a challenging puzzle, as well as interacting with objects in your environment.There are some minor flaws but overall this is a definite recommend for me. Melee is bit underwhelming but you won't be losing it for long because guns become prevalent quite quickly. There is a cyberspace section which acts as a hacking mini-game which is a very faithful recreation from the original but frankly it is quite boring and repetitive. Usually killing the flow of the game but luckily they aren't very common. The game doesn't have any journal or clear ways of indicating your objectives. Most information has to be extracted via audio logs or dialogues with others. This is certainly very immersive and quite a fresh change but if you take an extended break from the game, you won't really know where you left off. I had this happen and did look up some walkthrough for my first run. Hence, the game won't guide you around the station and there are no objective markers to speak off.Take a notepad with you, write down codes and jot down some notes. These reminders go a long way to figure this mess out, the game really requires you to pay attention.Overall, SS is a really great game that blends old-school gameplay philosophies with a modern touch. The game also allows you to adjust the difficulty options to your liking. I recommend playing on the standard mode but taking down the cyberdifficulty to easy because they are tedious. Also the puzzles are actually tough in this game, so having it on easy makes it smoother if you don't feel like bothering with it (except you really like chess).There are some nitpicks here and there but it's just refreshing to play a game that harkens back to games such as Deus Ex, Thief or the original System Shock.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original and would never care to with how archaic it is. I definitely respect it though, especially for giving us the immersive sim genre as we know it and being SO unfathomably ahead of its time. But DAMN, this remake is something else. Can't describe the level of satisfaction I get from every little part of this game, be it the puzzles, the exploration or combat. This game is definitely NOT for everyone, but patient people who get high off those dopamine hits from solving things will ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this.Edit: Going further and further into it, this game is bar none one of my favorites of all time. I can't believe how good this is. Edit 2: Scratch that. This  my favorite game of all time. Don't get me wrong, I can still see the flaws in some of the bugs and technical issues here and there, but that's inconsequential to just how masterful of a game this is. Imagine every genre of a game put into one, but with all of the soul and integrity of each genre somehow still intact. Dungeon crawler, immersive sim, sci-fi cyberpunk RPG, FPS, puzzler, survival horror, Metroidvania. This game literally has it all, and hits on everything it does with so much competence. I've always been jealous of those people who love certain games like Skyrim so much that they can replay it over and over again and feel at home, feel at peace, because they found a game, a thing, that can be their comfort food or warm blanket when life gets tough and an escape is needed. I finally found that game for me. I beg of you, check out this game and surprise yourself with something a little bit different.
