Not racist just don't like reskins.'Ate them Bioshocks too. Not racist just don't like reskins.Simple as.EDIT: To add a more serious tone to this review, this feels like an absolute TREAT of a game. The majority of the trappings of the classic game are still here for modern audiences to get mad at and the older players to get confused. I've forgotten everything so getting lost again on Citadel Station has felt glorious and refreshing.I like how Cyberspace ain't wireframe no more, instead more like the 90's corridor fighter games like Descent and Hellbender. So many times despite me getting wiped out fast I've been smiling, especially when the Death Machine caught me out all over again. That line traumatised me as a kid, just like the Sim Units on Shock 2. Seeing people freak out over the sudden lifts and repops as well has been fun.Compared to everything that has followed while the puzzles can be a little hard to work out and there is some requirement to have pen and paper handy, (not had that since RE2make. I love that stuff!) core mechanics are a lot more straightforward and not short on the serious RPG elements drowning the game like its sequel had. These games prepared me for a lot of storyline mechanics and betrayals because the rogue AI SHODAN was that brilliant a character.If you've played Prey 2016, or anything Bioshock, time to meet the mother. Go in expecting the game to kick your ass and make you think and you will be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having such a great time that I simply couldn't wait until I complete it and had to drop a positive review immediately. It's so engrossing every time I boot it up. Absolute master class of non-linear gameplay and a stunning remake. Edit: Having just finished the game, I'm just gonna double-underline the above. It feels like a massive privilege to be able to play the game in this state. It was hard to put it down, every play session, reliably. It's very true to its roots, maybe to a fault. It does feel like I've just played the original game so - mission accomplished. But it would have been nice to add some QoL changes - at the very least bigger cargo lift and better inventory/item management in general (I ended up solving this issue with mods halfway through the game). It could end up being a monkey paw situation but honestly taking a few lessons from Bioshock's book (quick healing, quicker access to special abilities, etc.) might have done this remake a lot of good (and would make it halfway playable with a controller). But either way, game is great.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I had never played the original, but I got through some of SS2 back in 99. I did, however, beat Bioshock 1 and 3 so i was curious to see how a re-imagining of the original game that started it all would be. Edit: Just finished it, I really dug the retro cyberpunk in space vibes, the atmospheric music, and the sense of unease even in safe places. The first person Hacker design is full of great, personable animations. The inventory system and story progression could be a bit of a struggle sometimes, but did my best to keep away from walkthroughs. From what I understand, the hacking segments are an improvement from the original and I enjoy the junction box puzzles. I highly recommend it if you are looking for a good sci-fi themed dungeon crawler that's loaded with baddies and gadgets. (PS Spoilers: there's no end credits gag and there's no way to skip them, unfortunately)
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10Played this game wanting to see how this inspired Prey 2017. Wasn't completely disappointed. Prey is still better since it released later and expanded on what immersive sims can be. SS1R is an extremely faithful remake of an old classic but because its so faithful it didn't improve on the genre at all, only modernized the original inspiration. I appreciate this, but I would've preferred if they completely reworked some parts of the game, like what the team that worked on Black Mesa did with Half-Life. The way they remade the HL1 boss fights were waaay better than how Night Dive remade SS' boss fights.Regardless, I enjoyed the game. The setting and art style alone carries most of the game for me. Being alone and trapped in a space station controlled by a crazy AI trying to constantly kill you, combined with a retro cyberpunk aesthetic, it gives an extremely unique atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent remake. Does a good job of keeping the same feel (as seen through nostalgia-tinted glasses) as the original, but modernized greatly.Main criticisms would be that there isn't much impact sensation to the weapons (especially melee ones), and that it could use a few QoL features like autosort and autovaporize of inventory items, and maybe a warning of the (new) point of no return.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game.Whenever I tried to play the original System Shock, I was confused, it wasn't because of its age, I've played plenty of DOOM, Quake, and Half-Life, fairly old games, DOOM being older than the original System Shock. I was confused by its presentation and gameplay, I had no idea what it wanted me to do, I had no idea what was even going on.But this remake changed that, made it more understandable, made it one of the most investing games I've played, although still frustrating at times, I took about twice the normal gameplay time, because of this games difficulty too.It's also not too friendly to regular computers, my old laptop which I played this on had no struggle playing DOOM Eternal, a very good looking game, on regular settings with 60 FPS, Urdak aside. but System Shock chugged a lot. This game also has a great story, filled with horror and comedy, balancing them both great. I love SHODAN, System Shock wasn't my first rodeo with an insane, rampant, opposed to humanity, female AI as a villain, Portal and Halo 5 had them, ignore Halo 5. Nor was it my first rodeo with an immersive sim set on a Space Station that's had a terrible accident on it, and with someone with a name having Sho and Dan together, Prey  had that, but System Shock did not fall below them, SHODAN is just as good a character as GLaDOS, while being way more aggressive, even if Prey is the best game I've ever played. And the fact that somehow, The Hacker won, though how impossible it feels at each step.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: pretty good but theres a lot of bugs that kind of ruined my game. for one, the healing pod bugged out and can't be used anymore, so I had to play through the entirety of medical in instadeath range. combat also isn't great. ammo is scarce, which would be fine, except even the weaker enemies take 3-4 shots to kill. enemies will occasionally respawn or show up in already explored areas, which puts even more of a drain on your ammo. currently stuck in research, unable to heal, replenish my energy, or kill any of the ranged enemies that oneshot me if I try to progress. still a pretty good game, though.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand the positive reviews, 2 with the graphics update mod is a MUCH better game.The graphics are I suppose loyal to the first but are still really ordinary, the whole game is bright light city inside a space station which makes it very hard to select or see the buttons which open things and so on. The combat is meh, a lot of things make it annoying, hitting things in melee doesn't make enemies stagger or interrupt their attacks which leads to a lot of getting beaten up, even on lower difficulty there is a lot of enemy spawns all over the place which just becomes tedious. Example in 2 Medbay you might expect to encounter 1-2 enemies spawning when you enter a level, in this a previously cleared area had 12 in mobs of 4 so you get to play do I use all my ammo or lose a lot of health.The inventory system is 1. annoying 2. Even more annoying, you can vaporize pretty much all the junk you find which is a lot and then turn it into credits in a recycler when you find one you have to vaporize each item one at a time there's no automation to this. The need to complicate this from the nanite system of 2 is just baffling. It makes it an enormous chore to collect vaporize and then credit things. There are corpses everywhere, aliens, human robots, almost all of them have nothing, at all, but you gotta search em all and generally can't remember what you've searched or what you haven't.The puzzles were designed by someone who hates you and hates fun. They're irritating, poorly explained and really difficult with multiple options to fail and spend 20-30 minutes figuring just the right combo for each one. The cyberspace is some huge shoots things with magic lasers and get through a gigantic maze with no idea what exactly you're supposed to be doing, also with no navigation to objectives you're just supposed to figure it out while getting progressively more irritated and lost. I was expecting something more, as it is it's really tedious and for me not very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for the faint of heart.  It won't hold your hand and tell you where to go and what to do.I haven't loved and hated a game this much since darksouls3.  A remake that just remade the game with minor ui enhancements (from what I remember playing the original) and updated graphics.  A great game that won't be everyone's cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: would like to first point out that this remake of system shock is the first title i've played from nightdive studios, so i'm not familiar with how they structure and design their gamesi've had a tough time with enjoying how the game is progressed. it was pretty easy to familiarize myself with the game, since it is a first person shooter. but even my prior knowledge and instincts weren't enough to get me through the story. the player is guided through the game with audio logs and occasional dialogue when certain points of progression are reached. it's very easy to miss what you need to do if you weren't paying attention. and if you do, you can listen or read the logs again... just skim through the 50 other logs you've already picked up.resources were another core mechanic i had a problem with. the game is designed to make the player search rooms and enemies for resources. in return, the player is rewarded with ammo, medical items, weapons, and upgrades. there's no telling when you will get more resources, so you're forced to be conservative with what you have. though there is a problem to this- the enemies respawn. and it becomes an even bigger problem if you get stuck on what to do. i reached my limit when i found myself relying on energy weapons and going back and forth to the healing pod in the medical bay. because i couldn't figure out what to do in the research floor, i ran out of ammo and healing items from the enemies that respawned.the cyberspace sequences were rather tedious. you travel through a series of tunnels and rooms while fighting enemies. by destroying the giant mega energy core thing, you gain access to locked areas or get a code. traversal is disorientating and you can lose your sense of direction when fighting a group of enemies. the combat in cyberspace isn't very good. most of the time it's hold movement keys while spamming attacks. the game would crash at times as well. sometimes happening when changing floors on the elevator, and one time where i had the escape menu open for a few minutes before running into a "fatal error". thankfully whenever the game did crash, it was moments before an autosave. still annoying to relaunch the game and get back to where i was though.finale spoilers below:i can't say i never enjoyed the game for what it is. the visuals were very appealing, i really liked the 3d pixel artstyle. the music was great, although the combat themes were a bit cheesy and inappropriate. the elevator music is a banger to say the least. the gunplay combat was fine. some enemies were really tanky. i keep forgetting there's a lean mechanic, but i died trying to use the grenade launcher so i never utilized it after that. maybe i should've played on the easiest difficulty and that everything here is a skill issue, but man it's frustrating how easy it is to get lost and resort to online guides.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake of System Shock with superb graphics. Could never get into the original, this brings it up to snuff with today's games. A few old design choices show through - back tracking a lot but the worst is just the simple lack of a current objective. Overall that's minor because it's so good and is worth every bit the wait for this remake! If you never played the original and like Action RPG definitely pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A solid remake of a 90s classic, the System Shock remake mostly succeeds in updating the original. The graphics and artstyle are fantastic, and citadel station feels more "alive" than ever, with a gorgeous window view to boot. The combat is alright, and the level design is maze like, though the vague objectives are pretty frustrating. The ending is pretty abrupt though, which is disappointing. Overall I'd recommend this to system shock fans, but I suggest newcomers play the original game before tackling this one. Though I will say that this is worth it just for SHODANs voice, seriously man, some of her audio logs are legit ASMR to me. And remember, this is what you want, this is what you get
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: As everyone else has pointed out, this is something special. I'm a sucker for immersive sims, and even after all this time, it doesn't get much better than this. The DNA of so many games can be traced back here, and this remake proves that the original had some serious staying power. So much fun to explore the horrors of Citadel, with all the quality of life improvements. Feels like a modern game with a retro sheen, more than a retro game with a modern finish.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of the original, both in spirit and tone. The graphics are fun, as they are designed with a slightly pixel-like retro theme. The audio and music is spot on. Most levels are familiar and expanded upon in a way that doesn't feel out of place. Enemies are great, and varied throughout the game. This is everything you'd want from a remake and more.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: While a troubled development and handling of the kickstarter left a sour taste for backers this has become, after patching, a worthwhile game to carry the SS name.For me SS has always been more of an FPS quest game more than anything else and as such how you interact with the story and the world around you is paramount. in remaking SS they've managed (IMO) to keep the feel of that while also upgrading the graphics, sound and various game mechanics.- The Game -It's the great story of System Shock with as probably a fateful of an adaptation as you can create. there are a few differences from the original SS but overall this is the same game in all the ways that matter.the sound design in this game is excellent and the atmosphere they create combined with music feels right at home amid the corridors of citadel station. it's a visually striking game but kind of misses the mark for me since I feel like it should have been leaning a bit more to the horror or derelict station vibe with a bit less bright lights and a bit less clean.combat is there to serve a purpose but that's fine since the story is what matters and while it's a fist person game I don't remember SS fondly to how amazing the combat was. while it's relatively basic there's a enough variety to keep things interesting.Cyberspace can be a bit confusing at first and might seem a bit dull later but honestly it's not different in purpose to what was in the original.All of those elements combined deliver a great way to experience SS in modern times.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great both on its own and as a remake. It is almost a 1 to 1 interpretation of the original game with some changes. I like it when the game just tells me how to do my tasks, but I have to figure out where they are and what exactly I need to do. The art style is great and gives the game a retro vibe. The story is also good, you can piece together a lot of events that happened after listening to some audio logs.The gameplay, in my opinion, is more complicated than the original. I feel like I could fit more items in the original game. Either way the balance on Hard feels really good, I never felt overpowered or underpowered.This game isn't perfect either, so let's talk about problems. I think this game has two big problems. First, the music. They remixed the original music, but that's not a problem as such, the problem is that it almost never plays when I explore and I REALLY hate it because the original game has a really great soundtrack in my opinion. From what I understand they chose dynamic music mechanics where it plays a combat remix of a track in battle and very rarely plays an ambient version of the same track while exploring. Because of this, I can't properly rate the soundtrack.The second problem is with the weapon upgrade system, it forces you to stick with that one exact pistol that you upgraded, or that one shotgun that you upgraded, when in the original game, if I couldn't find ammo for a weapon, I could throw it away to save inventory slot and find the same gun elsewhere later when I stock up on ammo for that gun. It takes away a little from the feeling that I'm using everything at my disposal to survive.This game is greatly optimized, but it's just a little raw, like a ragdoll bodies respawn in the air, and you can see that when you enter a room you've already been in, or for some reason I see the audio log UI after loading a save. Everything else was bug-free, and I'm truly grateful that this isn't another game with a kilometer-long list of issues at release.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully faithful remake of the original System Shock. To an audience unfamiliar with the game, perhaps it will be TOO faithful!Most of your sense of what to do next comes from paying attention to audio logs, some of which you can miss if you aren't checking carefully. The environments are (faithfully to the original) maze-like. The wall panel puzzles aren't explained and while you can definitely figure out how they work by messing with them, some may grow frustrated, particularly by the power level puzzles. For a new player, there's no shame in picking difficulty 1 for puzzles if you aren't a puzzle fan, and difficulty 1 for mission, which as I understand it gives you a couple hints/nudges in the right direction for how to proceed with the main objectives. You can bump up the difficulty with combat or cyberspace to give yourself more difficulty elsewhere if you wish!This game is FANTASTIC for the type of player that is ready to slow down, take their time exploring the station, and maybe pull out a piece of paper and pencil in case you need to write down a door code or two. I played the original version when the enhanced edition released, and am blown away but what a great job Nightdive Studios did here.Few criticisms I have are mostly quality of life stuff - I'd love to be able to label pins I place, I'd love an in-game notebook I can write notes in, I'd like a way to empty a weapon I found on the ground of ammo without having to place it in my inventory (because I horde things in games and my inventory is constantly full). There's probably a couple more but overall I am happy this game exists and am looking forward to finishing my time with the System Shock remake. Well worth the wait!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A must play, it`s very rare to get games this impressive nowadays, it reminded me of alien isolation, amazing games with low attention.Received the same treatment as the remake of Resident Evil 4, a very good game. You can feel the love the developers poured into it.Animations, graphical department, the progression, the variety of weaponry and upgrades, tools to help you progress the game, this game has so much to offer for the people that like a good challenge, the game is unforgiving and expects a lot from you.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: SHODAN still relevant all these years especially with Artificial Intelligence taking the world by storm in 2023. Who knew....SHODAN is honestly without a doubt one of the best villain's in gaming history. System Shock remake certainly lives up to what Nightdive studios was dreaming about when they announced this game back in 2016-2017. A faithful remake with some great Quality of Life additions. It's a great game if you are familiar with the 1994 version of the game. Combat is where it changes the most here. Now that we have established where First person shooters are in Gaming History we can now go back and give the good ol games more of the identity and proper care which is what Nightdive studio does well. With that the enemies are also updated and are more aggressive than the 94' counterpart. Also changing how to "Hack". I really enjoyed this as much as the 94' counterpart as it had a lot of wiring and I wasn't sure where the wall was lol. I really appreciated the art style here where it looks modern from a distance but it retains its pixelated architecture from the Original. Cyberspace will always have a place in my heart and I really owe it to Warren Spector who produced the original to getting me into Immersive Sim games.The difficulty is what you expect with the tweaks on Mission, Combat, Puzzles etc. I did 2 all the way through and there were times I was confused where to go since its been so long and Old Guides still work on this game to my surprise lol. I do wish that there was a more QOL improvements in the Objective base difficulties. Although I heard switching to 1 on mission gives you generic waypoints, I do wish that was overhauled to give new players who have never played System shock a comfortability into understanding what OBJs have been completed so they do not run around for an hour forgetting weather or not they turned on a switch or forget to write a number they saw on a screen. This is probably my only gripe I have with remake honestly which is it remains too faithful in the difficulty which may turn off some folks.I really LOVE System Shock Remake! SHODAN presence throughout the game make its seems like she is toying with me at every corner as the "Hacker". A pathetic insect infiltrating Citadel Station. A pleasant surprise to be sure!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original but damn she purdy now. For those not in the know, it took over a decade for someone to attempt to rip it off and that game was called Bioshock. Plenty of other franchises took pieces though... looking at you Elder Scrolls.Edit: Finished the game at 32 hours. The only issues I found were on the bridge at the end. Plenty of enemies t posing into the environment. I agree with most the reviews here that mention it, but the ending is drab and dull. very anticlimactic. It just runs out of gas before the final bossfight, if you can call it that.Id really like to see more remakes from this developer. Heres to hoping for an actual remake of Daggerfall...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is well-made and quite interesting. I would recommend it for anyone whom is a fan of Prey (2017).However, I will say I have had my nose in a guide for most of this game.The environments are gorgeous and mechanics solid, but the puzzles and ways you progress the story can be very difficult to follow.Important objects are given almost no context, unless you find the right audio logs, and you can find them quite early before they can be used.I have had a large object stuck in my inventory for hours because I was maybe 10% close to being able to use it, but the game won't let me drop it because it is a story item.So if you are patient, or don't mind looking at guides, then I do recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: The remake of System Shock  is one of the most enjoyable games I have played for a long time, The puzzles are hard but doable. (except the chess Game where the AI is too clever by half). The Bots are difficult and I lost count the number of time I died and was reborn. But doable. the story is great but certainly doesn't lead you by the hand, you have to read everything and explore everything. 35hrs and still going. I have seen a full play though for 8hrs? But I don't know how they did it, and I don't care, just love the play though.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Move over Deadspace. The Graddaddy of sci-fi horror wants its crown back.For those that enjoyed the original, this is a must buy. 9/10. There are some problems and there are some segments that are....weird.For everyone else, probably an 8/10. A competent shooter and a good, although obscure, story.The lighting and general atmosphere are amazing, minus some segments where the music is absent and others, forgettable.I would really have liked to see some basic objective remembering/tracking panels. Also, a Hud element to track remaining ammo in inventory vs what is just in the gun would have been nice. Plenty of other QoL features would be appreciated but altogether it works pretty well.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: A Solid Remake of an amazing classic, albeit one overlooked due to its barrier of entry. If you can only play one version of System Shock 1 play this one. If you can play both ask yourself what is your barrier to entry. If nothing comes to mind try to play the original first, it deserves your love insect. This is not a perfect game, there is a bug the devs need to fix in cyberspace maintenance that forced me to pause the game a few times for like 30 seconds each in the final area so the game could unscrew itself. Oh and the ending was a little flat, please if possible add more.DEVS THIS IS A NOTICE FOR YOU TO FIX IT YOU GUYS ARE DOING GREAT DON'T ♥♥♥♥ IT UP. (Edit: The maintenance bug has been fixed, good work guys.)But overall I have had alot of fun with this version. There are occasional frame drops and ragdoll jank and yet this is still better then most of the "new" games i've played as of late. DO NOT BE FOOLED. While this is a bit easier then the classic game (at least on Normal), they have revamped a few things to prevent total cheese. Boss fights disable medical respawning for one thing. This is *mostly* the old game with a fresh coat of paint, some fat trimmed and a *minor* amount of re-imagining. Also for the sake of making everyones stay on Citadel a little easier I will spoil that there is  You are welcome.Now the combat is pretty standard fare, none of the weapons feel like spitball launchers so that is actually really cool though id have liked to see the dart gun and MG of the original just to see how they would have designed them, whatever, spaghetti. The guns are good, hit pretty hard though the Assault Rifle feels like an odd duck if you have the Skorpion and the Ion Rifle feels overshadowed by the Mag Pulse and Sparq Pistol (side note that thing got BEEFED up I love it) and Gas Grenades just feel a bit like a little puff of liquid and then nothing. Much prefer using the shotgun for organics. Ah right see? The Shotgun was not in the original but it blends in well enough that i sortof forgot for a second.Okay but how is the music? I am glad you asked. Its not a "remake" soundtrack where they just do remixes of the old ost. Almost everything here is new, most of it is pretty ambient and pretty quiet so i'd say turn up master vol and turn down game volume a bit until you find your preferred balance. I quite like it. The ambient musics have a feel that seems to fit with the post tragedy feel of Citadel Station and the Combat music is the Ambient ramping up as SHODAN attempts to turn "post" tragedy into "present" tragedy. Good stuff. Also the main theme and Cyberspace themes are remakes of the original so don't get too huffy on /v/ about the game being soulless.This neatly (for once in this rant) leads into Cyberspace. Easier to read for newcomers and veterans alike. Have you played Decent? No? Go play it Zoomer. This plays a little like that with the ability to roll,strafe,control altitude and all that. Aside from the previously mentioned glitch in Deck 3 (NIGHTDIVE GET ON IT PLEASE) I have thoroughly enjoyed my dives into Cyberspace.SHODAN as always is incredible. Alot of love to her writers and Terri Brosius for making her an absolute delight to listen to. There is a reason a section of the fandom is down bad and its because the work put into SHODAN is like the rest of System Shock: One of a Kind. Thank Terri once again for her awesome work.Overall the System Shock Remake has some teeth. It comes to the table bringing one of the most well renowned but underplayed games in the medium and updates it to allow newer generations to play it without having to fight with things like mouselook. Some people complain it is "too simple" those people should go back to chasing and killing their food with sticks as modern cooking is "too simple". Others complain the design is too archaic or that it doesn't hold your hand. This is a machine from a lost era of games that expected better of its players. You can do better, don't undersell yourself, do better. Also some people complain about the Hackers "new personality" in a cyberpunk game. Read more classic Cyberpunk literature.System Shock in total is like one of SHODANs Cyborgs: Not Perfect. But the basis for a better model.Buy it Insect.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:Alright, they fixed cause of the sequence break I had. Wanna know what it was without spoiling anything? It was not me using quick load!Game has a certain thing you have to do way past midpoint. If you do it, you get a steam achievement. This game for some reason used STEAM ACHIEVEMENT to check if you can do the thing.Meaning even if I had started all over again with new playthrough, I'd still be stuck.That's hilarious! Was that some kind of placeholder method to check if you can do the thing or were devs really thinking they'd get away with shipping game that checks if you have STEAM ACHIEVEMENT wether or not you can do a thing to progress the plot? Did they think nobody would do second playthrough of this game or what?You'd think just normal boolean variable would be enough but nah, let's check for steam achievement! nothing could go wrong!----------------------------------------------Should I recommend this game?In one hand, I had absolute blast 70-75% this game.In other hand, I managed to sequence break my savegame by quick loading while I was dying. I can't progress anymore, I think I got through 70-75% of the game. I've tried loading much earlier saves and continue but no luck, if I want to complete this game I have to start all over. I don't think it's excusable that using basic game functionality like quick load bricks my playthrough ... so ...I think I'll give this game thumbsdown for now. If I ever have time and energy to replay this game without sequence breaking it and experience this game completely, I'll come back to give this game a thumbsup.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely faithful, well polished, well done remake of System Shock.Hackers back, SHODANs back, Cyberspace is coherent. The only thing missing is the OG music but honestly that helps a lot to keep me terrified while I dodge a Cortex Reaver.Issues: -Melee is lackluster, but I drop it by the time I get a shotgun. -Kleptomaniacs/Loot goblins will spend a lot of time scrapping all misc items. (You don't need that many credits)-Dead Enemy Models will flop a bit when you re enter an area, might spook ya but it doesn't hinder game play-NEW PLAYERS to System Shock, Faithful recreation means lots of big corridors and rooms with no objective markers please, unless you enjoy problem solving by reading and paying close attention to audio logs, glance a guide when your not sure what you need to do.

The reputation of animations adds a tedious yet realistic feel to the world. It adds a great deal of tactics and forces me to pay attention my surroundings. It has very few issues. _childDocuments_.review: Great game for solving puzzles, being a punk, and killing the underlings of both corporations and "God"I can see why this game has the legacy it has. I honestly think a bit worse of Dead Space now, since being lost is such an interesting way to explore, and Dead Space doesn't let you do that.I can't get enough of the art style mixed with the level design.My biggest issue is that there's 90s adventure game design at play, and I'm not smart enough for that. :(Looking forward to playing System Shock 2 coop!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This one is very hard. System Shock is one of my favorite games of all time. So, I am going to review it both compared to what I remember of the original and as a modern game.Short story: If you liked the original System Shock, just buy it. But *do not* set the combat difficulty on hard, because it is too hard, unless you really like to suffer.Long story: This is a very good remake, and yet, I think that I still prefer the original one...* The graphics are great: They keep all the spirit of the original game, in a retro but modern way.* The audio soundtrack is average. I still remember some sounds and music of the first System Shock. I didn’t notice anything special in this one. Also, I really don’t like combat music that is too loud and prevents you from knowing where the enemies around you are, which is just stupid.* The gameplay is both good and bad. The gameplay is silky smooth like in modern games. And here lies the problem: everything happens too fast. You are not encouraged to take your time and read the logs properly. This is a bad thing because you really need to read the logs to understand how to solve the game. In other words: because of the smooth and quick gameplay, you might not enjoy the story as much as you should, and even be stuck without understanding why…* The difficulty is odd. I remember having completed the first System Shock several times, with probably one walkthrough with maximum difficulty for everything. In this one, I made the mistake of setting the combat difficulty to hard. And that was too hard. I mean: So many instant deaths when you don’t know somebody is going to fire at you right behind a door. Unfortunately, you cannot change the settings afterward. So, when I understood my mistake, it was too late, and I had to suffer for 20 more hours to finish the game.I don’t like the end of the game. I don’t remember that part of the original, but the end is just awful. There is no RPG or exploration game anymore. For several hours you will just fight wave after wave of powerful enemies with no real reasons for them to be here. I mean 80% of the game is very well-architected: the levels make sense, and almost every robot makes sense. But the final levels do not make sense; they do not resemble the bridge or the security sections of a space station…Also there is something strange with the gameplay: Some parts of the original game have not been properly ported. I remember a level which was very dark, and I had to manage my energy to light things up and my other items to solve it. In this remake, I never had to use any of the vision enhancement modules! Also, the drugs are useless. Aside for stim packs. The enemies are “too” strong anyway, at least at the hard difficulty, I had to find the best weapons to burn them in a few seconds because none of my equipment would make me tank their DPS for more than a few seconds…Conclusion: In the end, it is very hard to decide if you should buy it or not. This game is a nice remake, but it has lost something in translation… Just take your time, and do not set the combat too hard or you will probably regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - The gameplay is old-school in a good way and focuses on claustrophobia in maze-like levels. After two big patches: a 9/10. (This review has been edited and re-edited after the patches, currently 1.2.18887)PRO:- Gripping Frankenstein-like story. It is also the sci-fi version of the Sorcerer's Citadel: You are fighting against the odds from the lowest levels up to the top to confront the root of all evil.- No hand-holding: Everything you need - objectives, hints, puzzles etc. - you find in the environment and the audio logs. No quest marker, no map icons.- Good amount of play-time, doesn't overstay its welcome. Backtracking depends on the individual level of claustrophobia. You don't have to grind, but it feels more safe.- Excellent level design, with great attention to detail and interactivity.- Gorgeous cyberspace design.- Interactive take on the introduction serves for better immersion.- Unlimited save slots, save anywhere + Mod support.- Patch 1.2.18883 and 1.2.18887: All relevant bugs have been fixed.Prevailing Issues:- Fonts are way too small and thin - you cannot even decipher the key prompts.- The audio mix for the logs has been improved, but Rebecca's messages (which are of seminal importance) still have to be amplified in volume. The audiologs should be remastered as a whole, make them louder, and increase the master volume as well.- Scripting of the combat music has been addressed, but could be improved further.- There should be an option for the original soundtrack.- Unshackling Shodan at the beginning should have been a hacking puzzle, so that it becomes even clearer that you brought the genie out of the bottle yourself.Design issues:- Melee combat is clunky - just like in the original game.- Hilarious respawning technique with hidden compartments all over the levels. Who has built these? And why? How are these replenished with new enemies? This is in strong contrast to the immersive realism.- Inferior voice talents compared to the original, except for Shodan and Rebecca (whose actors are the same as in the original).- At first it is very unclear how the puzzles work.NEG- The end fight is a tedious chore, and patch 1.2 hasn't improved on it. Make this one a hacking mini-game - we are playing a hacker, remember?- Cyberpunk aspect is drowned in survival mechanics. This is my second real beef: The new realism sacrifices a lot of the original's charm.- This game was in pre-order for one and a half years. That's a no-no.AnalysisThe original SysShock was a great cyberpunk adventure, basically a first-person shooter with tacked-on RPG-elements and a well working physics engine - all in all very progressive for a game in 1994. 'System Shock Remake' is more like a survival-horror game, nothing more, nothing less. Instead of fast shooter gameplay, everything is a slog - in a good way. You slowly work yourself through the corridors and search every room, progressing through utterly claustrophobic environments. You are supposed to take your time, because the game wants to work on your nerves. In short: this is not a modern action game. It wants you getting bogged down in Shodan's "death-machine". And this is what makes the game great: We have one of the ultimate villains in the history of entertainment. Check out the trailers: "Modern technology - making life easier. What could possibly go wrong?"Some design issues set apart, the positive aspects strongly outshine the negative ones. My verdict: 9.0/10 - on par with 'Resident Evil 2 Remake'. Original game (1994 & Enhanced Edition): 9.5/10, on par with 'Half-Life 2'.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. Visually it punches above its weightclass thanks to its style, the remake offers a lot of modern quality of life features (including a difficulty that uses waypoints), runs flawlessly. the game itself is a mix of Soma (the fact that you have to actually explore and be aware, no handholding, no waypoints by default, puzzles), Metroidvanias (maps looping in on themselves, unlockable shortcuts), dead space (item management and limited ressources, without leaving you without options), descent (360 degree action combat in cyberspace segments) . All whilst predating all of those games. Great stuff, absolutely adicting.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: When this game came out I was negative 4 years old, therefore unable to play games. Even without nostalgia, this game is very good. Graphically it still feels retro, many textures are 8 bit, but the game still uses Unreal to the fullest. Environments are not only "high tech" in terms of engine (lighting, some effects) but also interesting stylistically. Overall it culminates in a well-lit environment that is vibrant, retro, and atmospheric.The game-play loop is cool, though you might want to write things down if your memory sucks as much as mine. There is a lot to explore between varied encounters with a wide variety of enemies. Every individual combat mechanic (how to shoot, throw nade, etc.) IS simple, but you have so many options that it stays fun. If you liked Bioshock, you will probably like this. I have enjoyed the medium difficulty where there are no clear "objectives" like most games have, even though it can be confusing. There's no glowing arrow or even a checklist, you just need to be thorough, listen to all the audio logs, and maybe write codes down somewhere outside the game. The future is dark, a glados-tier AI antagonist wants to end humanity, and you're just a dude who got arrested for hacking. If you've always wanted to feel like a well armed rat in a maze, this is your chance.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: It's the original game but better in  every way.I'm not going to gush over the actual game itself, because I already did that for my Enhanced Edition review, but this remake was incredible, and turned out, much like Dead Space, to be one of those remakes that you should just play over the original.The combat is great, the music is great, the art is great.SHODAN's redone dialogue is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.The game is great.Do not be deterred by the game's maze-like nature and lack of objective markers.The best way to play the game is use your map, clear every room you can, pick up everything, press everything, and pay attention to audio logs. If you get stuck, just use a walkthrough (even a walkthrough of the OG game works lol),10/10 game, perhaps my favorite game this year.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: This remake shows AAA creators that a good game can be great even without fancy realistic graphics. The graphics can be described as timeless and not looking outdated even after 10 years, as realistic graphics deteriorate after just a few years Total game downloads are only 3 gigabytes, which is much smaller compared to Hogwarts Legacy, which is just under 80 gigabytes.People say the gameplay is "normalized for normies", but I'd say it's up to date for modern FPS standards. If any COD player tries this game, they will feel right at home without feeling like they are playing the same game again.I hope more people decide to play this remake because it is definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: I think this games biggest strength is stopping Shodan is 100% your responsibility. No markers or anybody telling you what to do. All you can do is hunt down the audio logs of the long dead crew and put their old plans into action to save the day.A remake that's as 90s as the original system shock, that goes for visuals, gunplay, level design, everything except the music. My adventure through the sci fi labyrinth was a pretty fun time. It's a claustrophobic maze filled with mutants, cyborgs, robots, locked doors and puzzles. The remake has gibs and ragdolls for dead enemies which are always fun. Shodan is a great villain thats actually a bit unsettling. Great "Unstable AI" character. The "cyberspace" part of the game is a cool minigame with a huge visual overhaul from the original.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, good job Nightdive!Even though System Shock 2 gameplay was not very standard, I really loved the game ( since I loved Bioshock, deus ex and Prey 2017, I had to try the source) and since the remake to the original was already announced, I preferred to wait for it and worth it.Amazing job to improve the original game while preserving the essence of the original instead of reimaginating.Really enjoyed the retro graphics, gameplay, puzzles, story.I have some minor complains about the game, and some of those I think Nightdive could fix in a update for future buyers ( I already finished the game):URGENT Problems (these ones to me NEEDS to be fixed):- Before you go to the Bridge, It needs to appear a popup saying you would not be able to go back. What happened to me is, I didn't save a lot and got a problem with ammo, since I only was carrying the submachine gun and the railgun(no melee rapier). This lead me to not be able to continue, forcing me to use a cheat to get more 9mm ammo to be able to complete the game(I don't like to use cheats, so at least I only used the railgun ammo that I had/found). THIS IS BY FAR THE WORST PROBLEM OF THE GAME.- The death scene needs to have a skip button, dying is already the punishment( the scene is very good, but I don't need to see it everytime).Minor Problems:- Enemies barely feel any shot or hit, this could be improved.- Enemy AI doesn't behave very well when you are on a different height, making it easy to kill enemies bellow.- To make it easier for everyone, have an option to show your objectives. I've been stuck two times in the game where I didn't knew what to do, no matter what I red in the emails. It could be something to add a checklist when you open an email that contains some information to at least point you where you should go. Making it optional to enable/disable in the gameplay options would be great, could be shown in when you start a new game, something like: "Would you like a enable an Objective List? ( This is not the original experience of System Shock, but also can be disable in gameplay menu during game at anytime ).That's it, thank you Nightdive, I would really like you to actually re-imagine what a system shock 3 would be, since this one was more of a modernization of the classic and you guys already announced an enhanced version of the 2. You guys did really well! Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: There really does need to be a "Yeah, kinda?" recommendation.I never played the original, I would have been six. But I love the concept and the recent Prey game got me excited for this.It feels like a great game wrapped inside some design decisions that HAD to be included... otherwise the 90's kids would be angry. The difficulty decisions are smart, but once they're locked in... that's it. That means if you're 10-12 hours into the campaign and can't keep 80 things in your head at once? You're swapping between a browser and the game every thirty minutes to know what to do.There's a reason almost all Immersive Sims now come with an Objective Tracker (You don't need to give us waypoints... just an idea) mandatory. That could be switched on and off happily in a setting somewhere, with no actual effect to gameplay.The weapons are great fun, the laser rapier is hilariously fun to slice things to pieces with.The enemies are terrifying and SHODAN is the POS you remember. She's very over the top baddy and I love it.It's just the small niggling frustrations around the difficulty sliders and in game. I think I got to the exec suites... and just gave up. I guess it's a good game? I know how it ends as I played SS2, but I just deigned to stop caring about it after a while.Oh, don't think about asking for help on the Steam forums/community either. Good lord, you'll get bombarded with boomers going "This is what's wrong with gaming these days!" at you... despite the fact that it's a 30 year old game and QoL was almost deliberably obfuscated for these chuckle♥♥♥♥s.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: First level is great, research goes downhill (the cyberspace section is so bad it made me want to restart with the CS difficulty set to 1), and I barely got anywhere in the third level before just giving up. I was already low on health/ammo and the aliens that can just appear out of thin air in front of me just kept wiping me out. Enjoy the demo but leave the full game alone.Also, to anyone who says it's an immersive sim, you're wrong. There's usually only one way to accomplish any objective and only figuring the answer out will let you proceed. That's very different from the "Play your way" style of real immersive sims like Dishonored or Deus Ex.
_childDocuments_.name: System Shock

_childDocuments_.review: [Also known as "System Shock Remake"] You're a renowned hacker, the most notorious cyberspace thief in the corporate world. Caught during a risky break-in, you become indentured to a greedy TriOptimum executive. After six months in a healing coma, you awaken to the twisted aftermath of a terrible disaster. Where are the surgeons? Why is the station in such disrepair? Slowly, the chilling realization that something is very wrong creeps over you. Once a prime corporate research facility, Citadel Station now teems with mindless cyborgs, robots and terribly mutated beings, all programmed to serve SHODAN, a ruthless A.I. There's scarcely time to think before it unleashes the first terror...

name: GTFO
detailed_description: FINAL EDITION Rundown 8.0 – Duality brings the story of the prisoners in the Complex to its riveting culmination. With all rundowns available in GTFO: Final Edition you and your team have more than 80 nail-biting challenges to suffer through. More than most people ever will be able to endure. About the Game Your team of prisoners is dropped into the Rundown when a new Work Order is issued by The Warden, the mysterious entity holding you captive. The Rundown is a series of expeditions, each one taking you deeper into a decayed research facility called The Complex. You descend level by level, scavenging tools and resources that help you survive in a perilous network of tunnels where gruesome creatures lurk in every shadow. Complete all the expeditions to fulfill the Work Order and clear the Rundown. GTFO is designed for prisoner teams of four, putting cooperation at the core of the experience. Bots can fill your lineup if you’re short one or two players. They’ll follow you through expeditions, sneak when you sneak, collect resources, and fight alongside you. They’re a good fallback, but the level of communication and tactical combat in GTFO means it’s best to play with people. A strategy is necessary to clear the Rundown. Before you drop into The Complex, your team needs to decide what gear, boosters, and weapons to bring. You must also balance the team, identifying the function of each prisoner so that you know what to do when things go wrong. And they will. They always do. Stealth and coordination are necessary to survive as you maneuver through The Complex. Many of the creatures of GTFO are suspended in a state of hibernation, so light, noise, and vibrations can easily wake up these Sleepers. And if one of them knows you’re there, they all know. That’s when things get messy. You’ll need heavy weaponry and a clear mind when the shit hits the fan. Check your line of fire, force them through bottlenecks, set up your kill zones and reload every chance you get. These creatures stop at nothing, and neither should you. Once the mayhem starts, you have no choice but to put every last one of them down. Clearing expeditions and Rundowns will reward you with new cosmetic gear. Wear it with pride, as it proves to your peers you’ve been to hell and back. The Sleepers, on the other hand, will not care for a second.

_childDocuments_.review: *Played on free weekendI only played one level by myself with three bots. Not a bad game, though my frames skipped occasionally, but I like to play FPS games with my controller and this game requires some work with a keyboard to complete objectives, so it's not to my taste. If you don't mind bouncing between mouse/keyboard and controller or just play mouse and keyboard you might enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: GTFO

_childDocuments_.review: Needs saves on checkpoints, once the devs add this feature, I will say 8/10.Right now, 6/10 - some of the levels are sloppily designed, unbalanced, and over-reliant on weapon selection. The later is a good thing (usually), but the weapons themselves are not balanced in terms of damage/supply/etc. You can play with bots, but sometimes they bug out and do not get resupplied or just get stuck in place during the security scan phase (very frequently happens when it is a moving one).In terms of previously mentioned sloppy level design let me elaborate on one such occasion:Level C2 of Rundown 6. You have to start up  the generators to get rid of the green poisonous gas. Some of the rooms have it, some of them do not. And sometimes, when you open one of the doors (while you have multiple choices of which one to open), there just happens to be a gas leakage which puts gas into rooms which did not have it in the first place. Checkpoints are sometimes too far apart, and a general playthrough of mid-high diffiulty levels solely relies on how those checkpoints were placed (evenly, or absolutely randomly). Such playthroughs may take from 1.5 hours to 5 hours, the latter of which require too much time and dedication to sit in one go.Yes, the biggest downfall of this game is the absolute complete disregard of the devs towards the player time. You cannot save on a checkpoint to continue on a later day. Nope, Either ruin your sleep and nerves trying and memorizing everything, or just quit with no progress done at allSo yeah, right now, advised only for those who do not value their time or have an exceptional team to coop with.Just add the saves on checkpoints devs, bruh

_childDocuments_.review: So far I think this is a really good gamePros-          -Great stealth mechanics ( even with it being multiplayer )         -Great scary atmosphere Cons-           -Not really a con but it took me and a friend 5 hours to beat the first level, so warning noobs / more beginner type players this game can be difficult with only 1 or 2 players           -Easier for 4 players Overall I would say this game is a must try!

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that it doesn't have matchmaking actually makes the community a lot better than most co-op games. Players tend to be more committed to the game because if you aren't playing amongst friends in your friends list, you have to actively search for players on GTFOs discord channel. With promise of changing rundowns weekly to monthly, that could keep the replay value of the game quite high. I highly recommend this game to anyone interested in the survival horror cooperative genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased GTFO some time ago, but honestly, the lack of matchmaking is a deal-breaker.  I don't have time to hang out on the Discord chats looking for players.  They need to fix this immediately.   Otherwise, this game is just made for people who got bored playing LFD2, etc.  It is dark, scary, and requires teamwork.

_childDocuments_.review: i've been wanting a hardcore co-op shooter like this for awhile now and despite all the setbacks from one mistake in a mission it keeps me coming back for more, the game doesn't scale in difficulty if you're not playing in a full group so either get friends to play or trust random online strangers on the discord

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome co-op game if you've got three other people to play with. Match making is on the road map but not in yet. Wide selection of guns and equipment, constant updates and map rotations. Even if you beat a mission you can replay it, spawns and loot change up every time. Good game to play in a dark room with the headphones on!

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, work together or die together. The motto definitely applies to this game, and it's definitely a good time when you can get a 4 man team of friends together. While each mission can take a fairly long time to complete (upwards of 1 - 2 hours depending on the difficulty of the mission you choose to try complete), it's an immensely rewarding sense of completion when you finally do it. Mechanics such as using the terminal to find objectives is rather fun (personally) since I enjoy coding. And the whole concept of a rundown offering limited time content helps to keep everything fresh I believe (albeit I could be talking out of my ass, I started with Rundown 4).

Not boring even if it has like 6 levelsMy suggestion is the sound effect of the guns should be a littlie bit.. louder? _childDocuments_.review: This game hits like a mix of Left 4 Dead (except the enemy are all Witches) and Dead Space. It is violently difficult and the randomness only adds to it. The audio, and visuals are +AAA. The story is hidden away in terminal logs for now and I think the story is real cool. Curious to see if they will incorporate more of the story as an actual element of the game as opposed to just being a couple audio logs and a ♥♥♥♥ ton of emails. I don't like the stiffness of the animations regarding the gunplay because somehow the guns also feel very loose. like we aren't gripping onto our guns when they recoil. So the gunplay just needs some bare minimum tweaking. Otherwise the game is scary, difficult, and loads of fun with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is smart and needs a lot of sneaking and planing.It has ok graphics and is most fun in a team. Actually when you want to play this game you have to play in a team even though you can play it solo.But the enemies are so many you will have a hard time with the limited ammo and resources in the game.The big downside of this game is the time.It takes almost 2 to 3 hours to finish a challenging map if you are not in a well coordinated team that knows the map already by hard.Played 3 maps so far.Took me about 1,5 hours to rush them and about 2.5 hours if I wanted to do almost all objectives.Its just such a time sink for one playthrough that I know already I wont be spending a lot of time in this game.Most fun for me was the terminal, cause I am already coding linux servers in my job, so those queries are kinda super smart and familiar.

It is specifically designed for team play, and if you don't have friends who play the game, just go to the discord server, or if you want even more of a challenge, play it solo or with 2 people. filled with strange enemies to fight, new objectives to do, reactors to start up, stealth situations, combat, and is fast paced. It is worth every single penny spent. they also take suggestions from the community and such.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I ever reviewed a game. I'd recommend to have at least two friends with you to play to enjoy the game and actually have a chance at it. It is very difficult which makes it (at least to me) very fun to play. Never spend so much time on a game arguing which is the best strategy to go to finally beat a level. The game allows for a lot of different ways to beat it and it forces you to really think about your options, the equipment your taking with you and it requires team play and communication, otherwise you're just being overwhelmed by enemies and you're getting your ass kicked. 10/10 (although so far you cannot replay the old rundowns as mentioned by other reviewers before). _childDocuments_.review: To learn a game, you replay the sections you fail until you understand it. This is a core learning loop, and is a big part of what makes a game fun and engaging.GTFO has very long missions, often over two hours a pop. Multiple times in this game, we've cleared the first 1.5 hours of a mission with relatively minor pain, only to fail at the 11th hour. To replay the final section, we'd need to replay the entire 2 hour mission, which feels like a massive waste of time.Games address this problem using checkpoints, which allow players to progress through a piece of content gradually. Checkpoints allow developers to dictate the pace at which their players experience their game's core learning loop. They allow games like GTFO to have long missions, with non-uniform difficulty throughout.GTFO has checkpoints...but it might as well not. The checkpoints in GTFO are too far apart, often well over an hour. They are also confusingly inconsistent - in one mission, we got a checkpoint after 15 minutes (after ~one big fight), and then no checkpoint for 2 hours (after ~four big fights).This game is fantastic for those who want to grind out a mission for dozens of hours. The gameplay is pretty good. Melee feels weak (but on purpose), ammo is scarce (but on purpose), turrets and foam and mines and setup in general seem strong (also on purpose). It offers some incredible highs, and is an awesome base platform for future updates. It's easy to see the developers adding new weapons, new tools, new enemies, etc.But the checkpoints are too far apart. The game did not respect my time, and it won't respect yours. If that's okay with you, great, you can find a lot of enjoyment here. But there's a lot of games out there my group of 4 can enjoy. We'll likely gravitate towards those other games, at least for the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric but ultimately incredibly repetitive and dull.Every run is the same, save for a few environmental hazards. You stealth, melee, loot and then open another door to repeat the cycle all over again. Sometimes you'll have an alarmed door to open where you'll get to experience one of the games few standout moments of brief Aliens-like action set-pieces but these are few and far between as your team meanders through foggy copy-paste rooms filled full of terribly designed monsters.The much talked-about difficulty isn't even an issue as watching a few Youtube videos will fully prepare yourself for everything the game will throw at you. As for the "horror" aspect of the game, honestly, it doesn't have one. There are no real moments of terror and the only tension comes from spending 40 minutes clearing a run to end up with no ammo on the final door or hastily inputting console commands in as your team eagerly waits in the background.Ultimately the problem I have with GTFO is that the actual game play loop is just tedious and boring. There is no real progression and the content refreshes mean that you're unable to return to any of your favourite runs after they update. The game would benefit from more engaging objectives, a persistent horde-style mode or just something to break up the tedium.3/10 - Only buy if you're the type of gamer to enjoy repetitive tasks for little in-game progression. Also don't bother if you don't have any friends on Discord as the games MM community is utterly terrible and few people use microphones.

_childDocuments_.review: After 50 hours of gameplay, i figured it was a good time to leave a review.1º - As you might know by now, this is a team based game, and by team based I mean there is no way you can play solo. The difficulty doesn't change if you take one or four people, to the point where some levels are near, if not completely impossible doing solo. So yeah, expect to play with alot of randoms or some friends.2º- Despite being able to play as a team, the game has no automatic matchmaking system ingame. Most of matchmaking is done via the official discord server, and despite having a chat ingame you'll should have a mic to do voice chat in with your team, since there is alot of coordination and cooperation in this game.3º- This game is hard, even if you are new or a more experience players. unless you have a perfect team that can ace everyting, you will have an hard time in most levels, for each "♥♥♥♥-up" will cost your team much needed resources that put you guys in a rought spot later on4º - Some levels are more stealth based while others are more gun play, but the majority of the game is stealth(sometimes quite stress inducing, in a  fun way ) with some mandatory gun play in some parts. What i mean is that, this is not "Killing floor 2" or "COD zombies" kind of gameplay. Usually, the less you are forced to use your guns, the better things are going so it can be quite a slow gameplay that takes time. This might sound a bit boring but the "slow" gameplay is usually filled with suspence that makes one being "on edge" almost all the time, and the quiet gameplay can easely turn into a "spray-and-pray" ambient of chaos and despair in a moment so ... thats fun XD5º - Performance wise, i never had a problem. No crashed, just some minor bugs  and the games runs well enough on my pc (1060gtx , i7 processor, 16gb ram). you might have a bit of lag if the party host (or you) has internet problems, but nothing game breaking in most cases, and you can chose the region the host his in the official GTFO discord, so it should be fine most of the time.6º - The updates, despite being few and far between, change alot of stuff and had a bunch of new content, to the point where all the levels are completely new with a variety of new mechanics and more options for your loadout, keeping the game fresh.Overall,  despite being in early access, GTFO already feels like a complete game with an amazing and challenging team based gameplay. I recomend this game if you like to work a strategy or cooperate with your team to clear the levels of GTFO without you all dying in a chaotic demise that the enemies can bring upon you.

_childDocuments_.review: : , as the description is in the store, is an extremely cooperative first-person shooter. If we know anything about the game, it is due to the information we found on the game's official page, as well as what the game offers: a mysterious, ambiguous, terrifying climate, whose places are depopulated and instead habited by unknown creatures. We will play as prisoners who are awakened from their hydro-stasis state, from the . The Warden will drop us into the depths once awake to fulfil certain missions of the expedition. We walk through the corridors of the complex that are infested with sleepers, unknown creatures that remain attentive to the sounds and lights of our footsteps. Once the mission is completed, as the name of the game indicates, we must from there. As we progress, we discover a bit of the story behind the game. We will find the evidence in each scenario that reveals what hides in the depths, and with the tasks that we must achieve. All of that is protected within the complex: dark and atmospheric locations that allow for immersion and suspense of a sci-fi horror narrative. Each place with an organic structure and with the resemblance of a maze proposals that challenge where every corner is lurking enemies, which allows that tension with that feeling of absconding. A game to some original and pretty challenging, with adequate graphics for the purpose; although it still needs some corrections and graphic bug fixes, but nothing serious that prevents play.: The game's tagline reads «work together or die together». The game consists of performing certain tasks. Carrying out the tasks make up the main mission and, in turn, the expedition. The game is not all about shooting, but it also involves strong teamwork. The teamwork of this game will be extremely substantial to complete the expedition. It will be necessary to create strategies to carry out these tasks, from managing resources well, advancing in stealth mode or planning escape routes. Although the game is quite difficult for newbies, it is recommended to play the «tutorial» in which the basic rules of the game are explained to you. Once you are done with the introduction of the game, you will be able to access the levels of the game. The levels, tiers, will be unlocked at the end of the previous expedition. Each level will be more interesting and with more obstacles, whose tasks range from simple to challenging. Just as you will have obstacles, you will also be able to do that and gain time to continue advancing thanks to the use of tools, power-ups (gifts from the guardian when obtaining a certain number of artifacts —solids with anti-Euclidean geometries) and the variety of weapons that you can use. This game has a reward system for the effort at the end of each expedition. Keep this in mind, without persistence and strategy, the game will become extremely challenging.: The game is atmospheric, whose ambient sounds predominate. Although that is apparent. The ambient sounds are reflected in the enemies when they are about to wake up. Or there are ambient sounds within the complex, as if something is there waiting for our presence. Some sounds are almost organic which hardly spoils the immersion of the game. Silence often rules at every moment that is sometimes interrupted by the characters' dialogues. That is why the importance of playing this game without a microphone, although it seems to be the opposite when playing with people. Although not all the time environmental sounds predominate, on some occasions we will listen to horror sci-fi dark ambient music that generates tension at certain times. That music is presented in a timely manner at certain moments, for example, when reaching the starting point of the expedition or ambient pieces with short duration that immerse you in moments of exploration on the complex. The music becomes vital when the enemies wake up or the battle begins. The music generates tension and uncertainty, which they have achieved with that combination of dark ambient horror and dark minimal-classical music. Despite the fact that the music pieces are short, the game offers that mix between environmental sounds and the ambient music well integrated into the game.: In appearance the game will seem short, but the difficulty adds a great challenge to the players. The developers constantly add improvements and updates, without forgetting the excellent idea of bringing the first expeditions-rounds that were in early access. Also, the game enhances that challenging difficulty for every level map you manage to complete. So it can be said that the duration depends on your strategies and skills to complete the expedition. You may complete a map in 2 hours or less or it may take days to complete it. Each completed map you will get a reward. This game can be played with bots or with friends, which, bots have decent AI and quite useful when facing difficult tasks. Although it is advisable to play with people and there is a community on Discord so you can find your team and thus be coordinated during the expeditions. At the beginning, in my personal opinion, I thought that the game had the logical similarity of a Rubik’s cube, since there are different combinations of the same elements with which they create more possibilities, in this case, maps. _childDocuments_.review: : GTFO (Yes, get the ♥♥♥♥ out, this game will ruin you. Jk, it's great) is a 4-person cooperative, stealth based, tactical shooter with horror elements, developed and published by  At game start, you pick your load out for you and your team (Or solo, if you're a madman), and you are sent down into an underground complex by a mysterious entity called “The Warden”, to explore your subterranean prison and complete objectives, or fetch quests for the said Warden. Which from what we can gather, you're prisoners who are expendable, hence being sent down to the long abandoned complex that's now filled with these grotesque mutants that will eat your face off to do the Wardens bidding. GTFO has a HUGE emphasis on stealth, exploration and strategy, and if those aren't you're forte, you're not going to have a good time on this.: I love how streamlined all the assets are. The game is beautifully designed, and how  manages their assets is honestly amazing and will never cease to impress me. Each level, despite using the same assets in a lot of places to streamline how well the game runs, each level always feel unique enough to be completely separate to one another, whilst still being part of the same facility. : Eerie, unsettling, and then battle music when you know you've f*cked up. It works, it doesn't need anything more, anything less. Every sound in the game is so well done, crisp sounding and in your face when it needs to be. One sound I need to specifically highlight and give extra credit to is; Chargers. OHMYGOD, they sound horrific and I absolutely love it! Their movement sounds, breathing, it's so unsettling even when you've heard them a 100 times before. I love them so much.I also feel like I need to add context; Creatures will essentially give you a warning with “flashing” (a glow on certain parts of their body whilst they're sleeping, as a warning that they are aware of you), and a “beating” sound, when they are now quite aware of you moving/making noises/flashing your torches at them. You get the 2 stage warning before they scream and wake themselves and everyone else around.: Extremely clean, great intro into the game and honestly sets the tone extremely well. A nice array of settings to fiddle with, and they give you every option you could want to add friends into your game. Copying lobby code, invite through steam and/or matchmaking which is still in it's early stages.: I finally owed writing a review for this game, considering it is in my 10 top favorite games of all time. GTFO, does not care for your incompetence, if you cannot learn from your mistakes, learn how to deal with the enemies that are presented to you, maps, tactical placements of your gear, you will not win. I like to annoy people with calling this “The Dark Souls of Shooters”, and honestly whilst I started that as a meme, It's fairly true. GTFO is difficult, and it takes pride in being that. It takes pride in the fact you will spend up to 4 hours on a run, to make one mistake and have to restart the whole thing, but somehow, it's never punishing enough that you don't want to play it, you see exactly where you went wrong, and how to correct it when you try again.. Not many games have that, and it's one of my favorite parts of this game that shines above most.Further things I want to highlight; no perks, no cosmetics, no DLC's (they update the game with new rundowns and get rid of the old level packs as time goes by, so you have a constant variation of levels to play through), the whole game stands well enough on it's own and has solid gunplay, gameplay and even just that smidge of story hidden amongst the cracks to make it a well rounded, fun, engaging experience. Nothing beats that “Expedition Survived” screen though, and once you've triumphed through it all, that screen is the best thing you will ever see.Now with all that aside, this game definitely isn't for everyone, and it genuinely plays and feels better when you have a consistent team. You build new strats together, communication flows better, I can't imagine this being fun with randoms, but they have a tone of servers for players looking for people to join them, and now they have matchmaking through popular demand. I understand that having 3-4 people to play with isn't an easy thing to have.Also something else to note; GTFO does NOT scale. It is the same difficulty all the way through (They have added even more content and challenge with extra higher difficulties and areas to explore and complete). Enemies also are partly randomly generated, but levels will have specific caps and requirements (e.g 1 scout, 1 titan, 20 sleepers) so enemies will not be in the same place, unless it's one of the level specific mutants, even then it can still be in a different area. Whilst I've seen this game get a lot of flack over not scaling to less players, it honestly would not work, and it would not be the game they have wonderfully crafted to this point. It needs that brutal, cooperative experience, that will probably start arguments with your friends.This is a labor of love, you can tell. I can't praise the developers enough for making an early access game feel more polished and be one of the best co-op games I've played to date (Which by the way, there are (last I checked) 9 developers working on this game. 9!!!) GTFO honestly deserve so much more praise and love than it gets and I highly recommend it to anyone who likes tactical shooters that offer a challenge with friends!

Seems and gaps in the world let you look out into the black void and nearly every room has a place where you can wedge yourself to escape the enemies. In total, most every rundown we've beaten has relied on one or more game breaking exploits that we've ACCIDENTALLY discovered while running around. We weren't even trying to break the game, but glitches are seemingly everywhere.The reuse of assets was understandable during rundown 1 - 3, when the gameplay itself was a fresh and new experience, but now it just seems lazy. The same few rooms remixed and sometimes filled with thick fog, repeated again and again and again. Why are cold storage rooms connected to an atrium? Why are server rooms connected to botanical garden rooms? Nothing makes sense, and they hide this fact by masking half their levels in FOG.The developers also seem to have been bitten by the Dark Souls bug; in which they conflate harsh difficulty as it's primary identity; crafting rundown levels that are stress gauntlets lasting sometimes over 2 hours to complete, and having no decent ideas or alternative content to throw at players, simply resort to making their enemies INVISIBLE. There better be a DAMN good reason in lore for that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥—but seeing as the developers don't seem to care about their level design, I wouldn't surprise me if they are just making up the story on the fly. OH and lastly; the game is one of "THOSE" games, where the story is hidden in the details, but mostly in audio logs you find on computers (which new players will be unable to access because they are locked into previous rundowns.)The enemy variety is stale now, we need more common enemies to fight, unlike the mother who we only encounter every few runs.Don't buy the game until it has more varied content.
