_childDocuments_.review: Each update seems to introduce features that the vast majority of the player base seems to find either frustrating (respawn rooms), unenjoyable (stamina), or takes away from the learning curve (hammers now have 5x stagger and can 1 shot stun all giant enemies). Let's go through some history.R1 was release. The game was "spooky" at best but it was fun.R2 released a ~ 3 months later. It stepped up the game's mechanics, introducing infection and environmental hazards like spitters. It also introduced the "E Tier" levels where difficulty is at it's peak. Great rundown, though quite dated now.R3 releases just 2 1/2 months later. Referred to as "baby's first R2" as it was basically just R2 but the levels were easier. Massive downgrade in quality of content. The rundown was out for 4 months and was so bad that it spawned the GTFO Modding community because it was so unenjoyable.R4 releases and introduces "optional difficult content" except it's not optional and progression is actually locked behind this content, so they weren't able to actually make the optional content hard like it was promised to be. This update also introduced the "precision" system, which allows different guns to deal different headshot multipliers. They used this system to... nerf every single gun in the game by setting all of the guns below 1.0x headshot damage. Cool.R5 releases and adds an enemy that can be created in quite literally 30 seconds with no interesting new content, but serves as effectively a "level pack" as a rundown does. "Respawn sacks" were shoehorned in to try to force a new game play mechanic that prevents backtracking. The mechanic's tell is that there are cocoons on the ceiling. There is no audio or visual effect tied to these to suggest that they respawn enemies, and new players often think that the enemies respawning is actually a bug and not an intended feature. This rundown was out for 8 months. You read that correctly.R6 releases and adds a stamina system that the community simply tolerates because it's impossible to enjoy and doesn't truly solve the issues that it was meant to solve. It simply makes the game play slower, which doesn't make it play any better. The skill ceiling of melee was massively gutted in this rundown (see: solo gameplay of R5 vs R6 for melee comparison). Sledgehammer becomes a mindless instant stunlock monster but not very great against small enemies? Somehow this is backwards from what it was prior. Broken checkpoint system added that bricks runs, and might as well not be introduced until it's actually working properly. Massive enemy position desync bug added in a hotfix, massively complained about, but not reverted. This is important (bug introduced January 27th 2022 via hotfix).R7 releases as a free weekend. The enemy position desync bug has not properly been acknowledged or addressed in any capacity. Steam reviews plummet with free weekenders complaining about bugs (most of which are actually long standing bugs) and getting objective items stuck in their hands, ending their run. The developers finally after many months publicly address the enemy desync issue and checkpoint objective stuck bugs that make the game extraordinarily unfun to play before they go on vacation.So where does this leave us? The game has long since started to go down hill long ago. New features added are not great, often unfinished, or straight up broken (host migration). If you couldn't tell by my hours, I obviously enjoy this game a lot more than I should. It might be worth mentioning that a lot of my hours are actually just me on the rundown screen with VSCode open creating custom modded content to not have to tolerate very lengthy content droughts. This game has an absolutely incredible core structure, but the devs seem to introduce interesting mechanics in the most unfun possible ways. R7 is probably even their best rundown to date in terms of quality of content, but the state of the game itself is absolutely at it's worst it's ever been since public release. I want to, but I can not recommend GTFO in the current state. At this point, I blow through their 6 months worth of content in a day or two depending on how much attention to the lore I give, then exclusively mod the game for the rest of my play time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen quite a few bad reviews for the game over concerns there is a lack of content and I'd like to give my personal experiences withe the game. _childDocuments_.review: Incredible game! Having played through the first few levels now, with live players and bots, I can say this game is the well rounded breath of fresh air that the horror shooter genre needed. Even with friends this game has the tension needed to really drive your heart rate up the wall, just make sure you stay out of the range of the sleepers when this happens.GTFO makes you feel powerful and vulnerable at the same time. The limited amount of resources available in each level are strong when used wisely. The game has a learning curve in this regard and may take a few attempts to get past the later levels as new mechanics and enemy types are introduced. This learning curve is much less steep when compared to other difficult games as the mechanics work beautifully when applied correctly; if you take a few failures to learn how each tool works, you will have success in the Rundown.World building... don't even get me started. The devs have found a reasonable way to make updates to the game and not replace the world building, but further the story line. This may not be the hardest method to implement in a game but the way it's approached in the Rundown is ingenious! Every piece of a level has a method of telling the story, even objectives in the game are progressed by the player LITERALLY typing in commands into a console... no "Hold E" to progress, you gotta input commands under stress! All of this makes the Rundown feel real!I excitedly await what is in store for us from the developers at 10 Chambers as they think of more tools, weapons, enemy types, etc.. to add, adding to the incredible world and mechanics of GTFO.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game,  however you will quickly find that the gameplay becomes very 'same-y',  you have your stealth portions and in certain areas,  you are forced to prepare for a wave of enemies. Although,  this might seem like a negative,  the way this game makes you feel and cooperate during those moments is what is really fun about this game.  This game is really about coordinating with your teammates, and surviving through the environment you are forced into.  Once you get down to the C-Tier rundown missions,  the game has unique missions than what you are used to.The only negative thing I can think of for this game is the lack of progression anything at this moment in it's development.  The only form of progression in this game is the rundown.  Once you beat Tier A,  you work your way up to much harder levels and objectives.  Seeing as this is the only form of progression,  I feel like this game's longevity and replayability is severely lacking.  Eventually once the community understands how the game is supposed to be played... completing rundowns will happen more often- there won't be any new content or anything to work for until the next rundown (a entirely new set of tiers and missions).  There's no form of matchmaking yet,  but the game isn't suffering because there isn't.  I actually believe the GTFO discord is all you need for matchmaking needs because you're bound to find other competent individuals that are willing to communicate.  An automated matchmaking system would reduce the effort required to find parties,  but I feel there might be a little more disconnect in the community that this game currently has going for it.This is an early access game-  this review should tell you that this game is still in a very bare bones state- however,  is very polished at that.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly unique experience, 10 chambers should be extremely proud of themselves for creating one of if not the most genuinely fun games I have ever played in my life. First of all the I love the atmosphere of this game just by getting into the menu you know what you're in for. It really sets the tone of the game and immerses you immediately into this unknown world with lots of lore to be found through the game play and setting rather than the game telling you through a campaign. Combat is fun as all hell because of things that really bring up the tension such as: Alarm doors, and defend area's. The game also found a way to make stealth super fun for players like me who are not really a fan of that kind of the thing, and its something you will be doing a lot of. Team work is very essential to success in this game as it requires planning and critical thinking for every level. And I love it.Though some may be scared of the the 4 player co-op because of the lack of friends who own or are interested in this game, luckily the community discord that 10 chambers has set up is filled with lots of friendly people just looking to have a good time, and even if you are nervous about talking to randoms like I was I highly recommend getting involved with the discord you will have a good time.There are very few problems in this game for something in early access and thats something these developers should be praised for. SO many triple A studios love to hash out these half assed lifeless games with 0 love put into them, and the only thing important being money, This game is clearly a passion project by a small team of hard workers who wanted to bring something new to the table and it's so clear the amount of love and work that went into this game. On the topic of bugs the only thing i've ran into in my nearly 12hrs of playing are a few model glitches that I have only seen happen twice other than that I honestly can't say anything else negative personally.Though it's a tad more easy to miss the voice actors did a fantastic job bringing the four prisoners you play as to life and deserve praise in my opinion, along with the writerall in all GTFO is an absolutely amazing game that is truly special in many ways, And I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun engaging experience that will leave with with great memories and even better friends.Thank you 10 Chambers Collective10/10

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is the sleeper hit of the ages. Regardless of the problems you may have it with, the fact is that it's a highly refined, stealthy, extraction shooter. The goal is usually, as one does in an extraction shooter, to grab various important items for the higher ups that just yanked you out of Cryosleep. Why? You gotta find that out buster.Quietude is king here. You can get extremely close to the toughest enemies, and a couple don't even respond to your movements (i'll let you figure out which ones~), just make sure you really practice your hacking minigame.Loud gameplay is tense, and you and your team be they bots, players, or a mix of both, need to come prepared. You will be massively rewarded if you understand how to utilize choke points, c-foamed doors, and controlled shootings in rooms. Terminals ask players to be a little computer savvy and have team leaders. Having someone chase down a key item with repeat pings makes precision a lot easier to achieve, and is one of the prime reasons one would want other players on their team.That's largely the basic gameplay loop, don't worry much about other basic mechanics, everything looks good and feels good, and that's what matters. Don't pass this one by, and drop by the discord, we always need new blood to keep the game alive!

And that it is an unplayable disaster zone in literally any other scenario. The bots are certainly a step in the right direction but with friendly fire and limited resources you cannot afford poor performance. The matchmaking seems to delight in matching up trolls and microphoneless aimless players who drag your run into the grave.Much like all cooperative games, if you have a group of 4 dedicated to getting it right, this game rocks hard. Otherwise it actively punishes you for wanting to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: tense, brutal, fun 4 player team coop, where you need to coordinate or you'll die! New content releases periodically keep the game fresh.The game uses a "Rundown" system where there's a tiered level system, getting more difficult the further you drop into The Facility, with more difficult enemy types. Every few months the Rundown disappears and the developers release a new one. This gives some urgency to complete your current rundown and also keeps the game fresh with new levels.Currently in Early Access, each new rundown also includes new tools, weapons and enemies.The game is brutal. Recommended play with the same group of 4 so you can coordinate better (although matchmaking is now in beta stage) - you'll need to coordinate well, otherwise one mistake after an hour of sneaking and stealth can wipe the whole team in seconds. It's this edge that really builds up the tension. The balance is great - stealth most of the time to conserve ammo, but when things go t*ts up (after your mate runs to a resource locker and wakes all the sleepers!) you also need to lock and load and utilise your tools and weapons to keep the team alive.Highly recommend, feels like a finished game already even in Early Access

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from balance issues and difficulty spikes. As it stands, players are encouraged to use Discord servers and microphone to communicate, but often Discord doesn't pic up microphones even when they are installed. There is also the option to use voice communication through Steam, but then you end up having to navigate through the game itself, Steam and Discord just to play one or two sessions. All in all, more of a hassle than is worth it. Lack of variety in weapons is also a problem and you often feel that they don't pack enough of a punch. Areas are often dark, which is atmospheric, but it also means that you lose your teammates. This takes away most incentive to explore. Enemies are sometimes erratically triggered into full aggression even when you sneak up on them, cascading into all monsters on the map to come awake. They then launch homing missiles that can track you around corners, whereas your own pistol feels like a pea shooter.All in all, the concept is good, but doesn't hold up against the extreme difficulty spikes. You are forced to use microphones and hope for everything to connect properly, which it often doesn't, and then players are punished for losing the group. It all means that you end up with a gameplay experience that is not balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the concept of a stealth/zombie/weapon/equipment manager-type game. But I think it was designed for the most part poorly. This game is VERY challenging it is very easy to die with bots so you better have friends.Stealth 6/10The game revolves around stealth because you don't have enough ammo to go loud on every engagement. I like this it creates tension and fear because you don't know how much you are risking while going close compared to going loud. But it really just means coordinating charged melee attacks with friends while crouched and moving when the sleepy baddies aren't glowing. That is to say after some experience the experience doesn't really change at least in strategy. Sometimes when you go loud and use firearms some units in a bigger room don't wake up. Which is strange to me, considering there is a unit that screams when you touch its tentacles it screams and pulls units that just spawn in from "outside" of other rooms to come and storm you, which can be VERY punishing. That is also annoying when you take precautions to clear the previous areas just to have them storm from those areas anyway.I was hoping for some sneaking that was similar to "the last of us" where you had baddies that were at different levels of awareness with much different body language to communicate this to the player. The player's advantage is that we have more methods of "seeing". Including different states of awareness would add much more depth to baddies. Especially one that could "smell" the player, meaning as soon as the door opens they begin hunting until they have eyes on or equivalent then become aggro'd. Zombies 9/10The baddies are very well done, they are up there with AAA games. The way they move as a single unit and in crowds really adds a dynamic fluidity to combat (they move so weirdly in crowds that it's hard to pick out a target). It is difficult to get consistent headshots as it should be. The baddies are TOUGH, even the standard units. They have range/projectile units as well as rushers who have significant range on their melee attack. All this to say without a proper team with proper preparation and coordination, any engagement has the potential to wipe out the team. The addition of glowing parts helps target acquisition but is basically necessary because the game is so unforgivably dark.The only addition I can think of is if the new "boss" became a regular hunting enemy that can kidnap players and put them in different rooms by themselves around the map.Weapons 3/10They do weapon classes in a very weird way that I do not enjoy. Its system is similar to FO4 where weapons that shoot fast do less damage and have more ammo but weapons that shoot slower do more damage but also have less ammo. Weapon calibers aren't addressed in any way so its not like there is a weight value given to the ammo per round. You are just limited to a certain amount based on the specific weapon. Ammo is also refilled based on a percentage of ammo not by round. There is a generic ammo refill pack that gives 20% capacity of primary and special to the player regardless of how many are left. So if you really like your primary and barely touch your special you could potentially be wasting ammo by refilling when your special is already full. Weapons also come with predetermined sights and accessories. One of the only thermals is on the semi-auto high caliber rifle which is unfortunate because there are few scenarios that allow a slow-shooting weapon to shine where as the fast-shooting LMG-likes would be best with the thermal, but since they shoot fast they do terrible damage anyway.I had hoped there would be a level of customization on par with like COD, FONV, or even better like Tarkov. A system where you can collect weapons, resources, and accessories to constantly improve your loadout. All while weighing the options of carrying too much ammo compared to other resources that you could have instead. The argument could be made that players would just bring obscene amounts of ammo and dump them in a weapon cache area. But this could be regulated by the price of ammo in the game or by an increased range of enemy earshot for firearms. But I suppose that this "improvement" in customization might clash with the theme of GTFO and the story where you are basically a prisoner sent with minimal gear. Equipment 1/10The equipment in the game kinda seems like an afterthought. There are few options for equipment but there are basically four options. The first is a bio sensor that allows the player to sense bio signs in the form of white dots on a small screen within a short area and the ability to tag ONLY moving bio signs. The first option is basically useless because the sleepy baddies glow in the dark periodically so you can see them farther away in gameplay than you can on the biosensor and if you were planning on avoiding them you can't even tag them in case something goes wrong so at least you know exactly where they all are. It's mostly used to see if there are baddies behind a door. But opening the gigantic loud doors does not wake any sleepy baddies up or even alert the one baddy that walks around blindly, HUGE missed potential IMO. The second option is an elephant toothpaste dispenser gun thing. It secretes a substance that reinforces doors and slows down enemies that walk through it. It's okay but the grenades that do the same thing are waaay better for reinforcing a door because they reinforce the door fully and in an instant. The dispenser is also a hog on equipment refill packs. It slows down enemies fairly significantly but the baddies are really tough so might be better to option 3 or 4. Option 3 is a laser trip landmine dispenser that dispenses landmines on any surface. It is also a hog on equipment refill packs but they do a lot of damage but considering they are landmines there is not a lot of collateral sometimes they kill just one baddy. which annoying because the one tough baddy you wanna kill is often in the crowd so you need to place high on a wall so only the tall baddy will trip it. Or ya know just shoot the tall guy far away with a slow shooting gun, it takes way less preparation and is often more effective. Option 4 is really three options and IMO it is the only real option, which is sentry guns. There are three varieties shotgun, machinegun, and sniper gun. They all perform as you might expect but they are damn effective probably more so than the players. In fact, they are probably the only reliable way to handle a horde without risking a ton of invaluable HP. They all carry waaaaay more ammo than your personal weapons which makes no sense to me, they are easily deployable and easy to pick up, and the single most important thing about them is that they will be ignored by the horde. So you can place them wherever and they will whittle down the horde while taking no damage and only expending a moderate amount of ammo. Then the guys that slip through will be few and hurting so they get absolutely destroyed by the player posse. The best method I found is to have only sentries and use them as often as possible, have only one sniper sentry while whatever mixture of the other two works best. Landmines feel like a waste everytime I use them and an extra sentry annihilates the horde instead of moderately slowing them down with the elephant's toothpaste dispenser. At most have one bio scanner. But there might be a surplus of equipment ammo if you do that, which I find annoying because I want to have that slot open for med packs instead.If the player had to choose between supplying ammo to his sentry or to himself this would be a more interesting dynamic. Like if a player had to worry about ammo compatibility in his loadout. Computer terminals are a thing but they have no real impact on gameplay. They are only used to locate things. You can't use them to hack defense systems (which don't exist) or open doors (which you can break).

_childDocuments_.review: A courageous idea with bad executionGTFO is a 4-player co-op shooter with heavy emphasis on stealth. The gameplay is mission-based; you and your teammates are thrown into handcrafted dungeons filled with humanoid monsters in order to complete an objective and make it out alive – nothing out of the ordinary so far.The premise is the sheer horror of the high difficulty. Any misstep can escalate the mission to the point where your team either dies or takes heavy casualties in terms of resources like ammunition and health items. Combined with the brutal darkness and the sound and level design, it creates a tension that can only be experienced very rarely in co-op games.Sadly, once this facade drops, a game flawed by bad design choices steps into the light – or darkness if you will ;)See, the developers praise inaccessibility as one of their core design philosophies. I respect this decision. We need more games that expect at least a modicum amount of engagement of the player but the way GTFO did it is simply not right.Let me elaborate:- The game can only be played in a group of four, no less, because there is no scaling.- There is also no drop-in/drop-out system which means that if a teammate got disconnected, prepare to restart a 3+ hour long mission.- Even with missions of this length they cannot be paused and continued another time.- The game has a lot of systems that have to be learned and mastered but no systems to teach you these. That means no tutorial and no dynamic manual – a part of the design philosophy, I guess.- Testing via trial and error is discouraged by the massive punishment received if something goes wrong.- The game has about 50+ missions but only about 8 are available at a time because “they are tailored specifically to the player’s taste”.- The game has a lore but it is somewhere hidden in the log files, so I didn’t bother.- The game has no soundtrack.- A mission fails once you and your mates agree not to restart at a checkpoint because you wouldn’t make it anyways. This happens at about 3 hours into a mission. Then you get nothing, no progression, not an experience bar of any sort, not even tips on how you could improve the next time around.These reasons keep the game in a constant spiral of frustration instead of an interesting challenge. But it is fixable, with minor tweaks even. The technical basis of the game is sufficient and polished.If the players would be given access to the earlier missions with less complex systems, so that they can learn the game in smaller steps. If the players would be rewarded with cosmetics for retrying a mission over and over again, to communicate that restarting missions is a part of the process instead of a failure. If the missions were shorter, so the players could try out strategies instead of sticking to the combat-approved tactics.If all of these improvements would be made, this game could be a decent like Deep Rock Galactic – oh, have I mentioned that Deep Rock Galactic costs less then this mess?

If you want the true GTFO experience, you need to play with 3 other people that have never played the game before. And (at least for me) that is unrealistic. (without sales) This game is $30. Having your group spend a total of $120 on a game that you might not even like, is a bit to far fetched for me. If you REALLY want to play this game, Just play modded. And if you have to turn to a modded community for good content, I wont recommend the game. All of that being said, I will not stop playing this game anytime soon. Wouldn't recommend if you want to play solo or cannot do voice chat via Discord or some other app. Just trying to beat the beginner level with 2 people with extreme coordination has proven to be fruitless.Review after full release:Most of what I said in my old review still stands. However there are some changes.4 players is no longer required and most levels can be beaten solo without severe exploits or cheese (I've beaten all but the final two missions and the bonus objectives for C and D-tier missions of Rundown 6 without another human player). This is due to one of the full releases new features: bots.Every one of my first completions for levels this Rundown has been in a duo with a close friend and with 1 or 2 bots. And we've nearly full cleared the Rundown, likely will in a week or two (my friend only has 1 night on weekends to play). While the game is certainly easier with real players, bots do an somewhat adequate job of making up for the lack of a full squad. This opens the game up to many players who can't find 3 other masochists to bash their heads against the wall till the conquer a level nor do they want to use the new Matchmaking system or use the official Discord to find other players.They've also added Checkpoints to the game, which have been controversial, but overall they're a positive addition to the game. If you feel this takes away from the hardcore nature of the game, you have the option to not use them. Using them also leaves a green mark on your victory screen to show you used a Checkpoint so if you want that extra glory over others they can't fake it.Checkpoints have salvaged what was becoming of the game; where missions became very long taking multiple hours often with large swaths of the level being relatively simple with the random difficulty spike you'd run into. This was frustrating as you'd lose hours of progress due to not being prepared for a 10 minute sequence and would now have to redo the hours of easy content just to try the difficult section again which you could easily fail again. Now with Checkpoints you lose maybe 20-30 minutes of time and they're often positioned so they're before the difficulty spike. Allowing you to practice this part over and over without having to repeat simpler boring segments. The biggest reason Checkpoints are so important is that they allow people who don't have as much free time (my friend) to enjoy the game more since we don't simply get a couple attempts at a mission per week taking us multiple weeks to complete, instead our time is spent on figuring out the hard part giving us 1 or 2 completions per week.1.0 has also brought a lot of improvements that were needed for bringing in new players and making them stay. The game is far more new player friendly due to the progression objectives in missions that tell you step-by-step what to do to progress forward. Rundown 6 is also one of the easier Rundowns released since the initial Rundown 1. Rundown 6 feels like the antithesis of Rundown 5 which is by far the most difficult and unforgiving Rundown which turned many players away from the game due to it explaining almost nothing while throwing things you aren't prepared for at you while expecting you to spend hours on a single run of a mission.I recommended GTFO to people who want a hardcore FPS PvE co-op experience with stealth, strategy, and horror elements but only if they had the group willing to take the plunge, but that was during Early Access. Now I recommend it in general to people who want to enjoy everything before the but of the previous sentence because that but is no longer needed as you can enjoy the game solo, duo, trio, or with 4 people.I'd give it a 8/10 as it stands (there's a decent amount of bugs tied to the new features, but what do expect when none of these features were in the EA and didn't have a year to have players iron out the bugs). Could the game be improved? 100%. There's still some QoL features and variety that could be added; but thanks to the Rundown system, all that could be added in the next update thanks to new content being added with each new Rundown.

(This issue is very, very compounded when it was someone else who messed up and everyone has to suffer for their mistake.)TL;DR Game looks and sounds really good, but game uses the ultra-punishing kind of difficulty instead of a fun kind of difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: /edit: 1.0 Version: I played this game another 50 hours by now and with 1.0 released I have to say that the devs really stepped up their game in terms of level design and pacing. So, why keep playing if as the developers say 98% of tries fail? Interestingly enough the gameplay loop is very satisfying because the game is so very very difficult. On top of that it is a game that like no other is in dire need of coordination with your team, which may put of some people but with some of my best friends and sometime a very supportive and lively community its an absolute blast. Consider this however: You need sometimes about 2-3 hours to actually finish a level, and more often then not you will fail at the end only to see no progress at all for your effort. Because of the random enemy and item placement not to tries are the same which makes planning on the fly difficult or well, almost impossible sometimes. I have played this 40h - and I will play more certainly and only made it through 3(!) of the levels. I guess the game could use more variety and some progressions system to motivate more players, but the fact that the devs deliberately decided against this is commendable in this day and age. I think there is no other game out there quite like this. So, if you are in the marked for an absolute HARDCORE horror shooter this is possibly the best you can get.

_childDocuments_.review: You and 3 prisoners are sent deep into the core of the earth to play 'Red Light, Green Light' Wack-a-mole with some mushroom people.Designed by some of the main original Payday developers, GTFO is a challenging, team focused survival horror with a nice blend of stealth and shooting action segments. The game almost requires you to have a full team of 4 and with no difficulty slider it can be pretty punishing. My friends and I always joke that the game makes you talk like how people do in Ubisoft multiplayer reveal trailers (if you don't know what I'm talking about, watch the division gameplay trailer from e3 2013) with constant callouts and organization. When you're not shooting and running for your lives during the onslaught of enemies, you're sneaking around, stealthily killing, planning, strategizing, organizing yourselves and scavenging for supplies to distribute evenly amongst your team. The game almost feels like a puzzle game at some points and is best experienced when none of your teammates know exactly what to do for a given expedition.The stealth segments of the game are characterized differently than other popular games such as Payday as the enemy detection is based off of player movement when they're breathing rather than traditional line of sight detection. I find this to be a much better improvement to stealth as there's no goofy cliche of guards seeing you run past them but not fully detecting you so they just simply think to themselves "Must have just been my imagination" or something like a Skyrim NPC. However some people can find this to be a drag as there's periods where you're standing still, doing nothing, waiting for your teammates to figure out how to navigate towards you for a coordinated stealth kill on a group of enemies like you're playing Modern Warfare 2.The guns and equipment feel great and all have really unique pros and cons which are fun to experiment with and use. And the visuals, graphics and environment are all stunning and immersive even for an early access game.The largest drawback in the game’s current state is its lack of matchmaking, with the majority of players using the dedicated discord server to organize teams. I don’t find it much of an issue but it's an extra hoop to jump through and can be discouraging to some.The next biggest concern with the game is also its most interesting, unique feature: Rundowns.In GTFO the missions available to you are on a fixed timer for the entire community, this is a rundown. When the next rundown goes live at the end of the timer, the previous rundown is removed and can no longer be played. These missions are designed by the developers specifically for each rundown, and are to be done in a linear order, getting progressively harder the further you go down that given rundown. The rundowns so far would take a fresh team of competent players roughly ~20hrs to fully complete. As of writing this, the game has just started it’s 3rd rundown after being released for 6 months (This isn’t including alpha/beta stages and also doesn’t account for the holiday break the devs were on). So the game has a planned content life-cycle that’s constantly being maintained by the developers. If they can maintain this and keep it fresh and unique, the game will be fantastic I imagine. However I'm prepared for lots of copying and pasting as the game’s life goes on, as I don’t see the devs being able to constantly create unique brand new content consistently - but here’s hoping it’s enough.The devs have an active roadmap that they expand upon and post their thoughts about in their discord, with matchmaking, player and weapon customization and gear progression all being planned developments in the future.Should you buy it? Well if you’re going to pay $30 and get ~20hrs of gameplay for your first rundown, you’ll probably be disappointed. So it depends how patient you are and what you’re expecting out of the game - Personally that’s what I would expect out of a game in early access.If you like a challenging co-op FPS experience, especially if you liked Payday, I would definitely recommend this game to at least try. If you don’t have 3 other friends with the game, it doesn’t take long to hop in the GTFO discord and find 3 other people to give it a go with.If you really hate the idea of one of these things, you could definitely always wait as the game gets further developed in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: You have to join the official discord server in order to play. Don't play with bots, your experience will suck. If you have  and You will have to communicate a decent amount while playing this game. It is very fun and challenging. If you like playing hard video games, this is the game for you. I have 21 hours in the game and I haven't even beat half of the levels in this game yet because there's so many missions. There is no difficulty setting in the sense that the mobs will always deal the same amount of damage no matter which mission you choose. You cannot go from "hard" to "easy". The difficulty however lies in the mission you select. Each mission has a depth, and the deeper you go, the more enemies you will encounter and there will also sometimes be secondary and "overload" objectives that can heavily increase a mission's difficulty. Currently, the only purpose for doing these side objectives are for personal satisfaction. Granted, it does feels great when you beat them. Some missions contain harder map conditions like intense, thick fog, poison gas, pitch black darkness, or a lack of resources.If you have any basic experience with command prompt for Windows OS it will help a little bit. You have to use the in game computers to locate items and resources. I recommend watching a guide on terminals if you aren't familiar with command prompt at all. You can also just type "commands" on a terminal and it will tell you all the functions you can do at that specific terminal.The guns are fun, and the stealthy melee combat aspect feels fantastic. There are some missions where you are forced to go "loud" the entire mission where you defend an objective such as a nuclear reactor. Some missions you should preferably stealth as much as you can to conserve resources like ammo/health and extract after you gather the required materials in order to unlock extraction.Out of the missions I've played so far, the gameplay loop is basically this:1. Stealth to enemy zombie and bash it in the back of the head.2. Communicate with your teammates on where the zombies are, and if necessary, 3-2-1 a group of zombies at once.3. Progress through the level and eventually you will reach a door with an alarm. This means that you have to now go "loud" for at least a few waves of zombies that will rush your position. These zombies are omnipotent in the sense that you can't hide from them (just like all zombies that are alerted of your position in this game.)Alternatively, you could also go loud in every mission, for the entire mission, but this isn't recommended as you will run out of ammo for the alarm doors. Some missions have tons of alarm doors.Teamwork based horror game, 9/10. Shame this game doesn't have more players, I think the price tag and lack of advertising is what is making it feel unpopular. There is also no PvP in this game, although there is friendly fire so technically, there could be if you and a friend are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around at extract.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is a hardcore, team based, co-op survival shooter. It is very challenging, maybe even 1 of the most challenging online team based game i have ever played.The game requires teamwork and full coordination, as every mistake could spell the failure of the match. Every step taken must be deliberated with your team. No bold move you make should not be communicated with your team as when things go awry because of your move being a mistake, the team would be confused and in disarray. The game requires meticulous resource management, this includes your ammo. consumables, tool capacities and most importantly, your health. Do not go charging in melee-ing enemies to save ammo if there are more than 1 of them as them depleting your health is far worse than you depleting your ammo fighting them. The game features tools as i mentioned above, and players should bring different tools for different purposes. There are 5 tools so far, C-Foam launcher, Biotracker, Burst Sentry, Shotgun Sentry and Mine Deployers. The ideal tool for a team of 4 should be a biotracker, a shotgun and burst sentry and a C-Foam launcher, but they can of course be changed depending on your needs. You'll learn how to use them as you go. The game is a shooter, which usually means it involves the use of guns. The guns in this game feel pretty good, and the accuracy on them are also alright. Ammo is pretty scarce so it is important to use them sparingly. You can bring 2 weapons. a main weapon and a special weapon. They should be a mix of ammo efficient weapon and a high damage low ammo count weapon, but you can of course mix and match according to your playstyle. The game also has a melee weapon in the form of a 2 handed hammer, which you can use to stealthily kill enemies. This is the best way of conserving your ammo while killing off enemies in the process. If there are multiple enemies in close proximity to each other, you will need to coordinate with your team to kill them off with the hammer at the same time so as to not alert any other enemies in the vicinity. To summarize, here is a list of Pros and Cons:- Unique gameplay elements- Requires the team to actually work with each other in order to succeed- Good number of guns and tools available- Challenging (A pro for people who wants difficult games)- Different ways to complete objectives- Still missing key features such as matchmaking (Devs said its coming at a later date and the current alternative is the GTFO official discord server to pair up with other players)- Challenging (A con for people who doesn't like difficult games)- Some minor gameplay bugs and exploits (Nothing serious that will affect gameplay so far)- Not many missions available (But every level is challenging so advancing to the next level will not be so easy)- Only caters to a certain type of playerIn conclusion, GTFO is definitely a must buy for people who like challenging, team based gameplay. Do not expect being good at this game the moment you play. You will die, a lot, and learning from the mistakes leading to your death will be key for future runs. Good luck and Get The ♥♥♥♥ Out.I rate 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun, but it has some key details that hold me back from recommending it. See below:-Very scary and atomspheric. The fog to the ambient noises, this game is really creepy and has a cinematic vibe to it unlike anything I've ever played.-Great sound effects and voice acting. The character VAing, or what little there is, is very well done and the sound effects of the monsters are bone-chilling.-Very unique menu and intro. I usually don't make the menu a pro in my reviews, but the menu and opening cutscene to this game perfectly illustrates what type of game it is, and sets the mood perfectly.-Gets updated frequently. This should really be a given with most EA titles, but here it is present moreso. Weapons, levels, and enemies are updated pretty frequently and they have a lengthy list of features they will add to the game and if it all gets added, this will certainly be worth the price.-New Rundowns come fast and are completely new levels. The Devs tailor make new batches of levels and release them depending on what levels people have finished. Each are pretty unique to eachother and offer an amazing challenge.-Long levels. Each level takes an half hour to sometimes an hour and half to finish, especially the harder levels.-VERY challenging and it takes careful planning and communication to finish each level. The levels here are extremely tough and make each person a necessity to carefully plan and finish levels using the right tools, as well as careful communication. Voice Chat is a NECESSITY to beat levels here.-Little to no bugs. In my entire time playing (which isn't too long but I will still keep this on here), I have encountered only one bug which is miraculous for an early access game (monster got stuck in the corner of a door). They clearly worked hard on optimizing the game, which most EA developers put in the backlog so they can roll out more P2P content.-NO MATCHMAKING!!! Fanboys may defend this by saying to use discord, which you need to find others to play with, but asking people to download another program to match with other players is absurd. If you have friends however you should be fine, but no MMing really hurts this game's playerbase as well. It is coming in the future, but as of now not having it is devastating.-No unlockables. I hear this is coming in the future so I might change my review then, but as of now there really isn't a reason to keep playing after you beat all the levels (which are long, but there are roughly 8 atm that are updated every few months.-Barely any enemy types. There are like 4 in total right now, but some levels have only like 2 types show up in TOTAL. Some variety could really help here.-No way to play old levels. Once a rundown ends (even if it was up for quite a while) you cannot play those levels again, which is a shame if people really like levels from the first rundown and wanna play them. I'm not really seeing this in their plans anytime soon either, so I don't think this will be added.In conclusion, GTFO is certainly interesting, but I would wait a few months for more essential features to be added before buying into this game. However, if you have some friends and want a fun game to jump into, this can be a fun time. Just be aware some major features are missing, and that you are buying this to help the developers finish their game.

As you progress you learn how to play smarter, and with each rundown the game gets more and more interesting. If you don't have any friends with the game, don't fret, there is a very helpful player base on discord who is more than happy to help you learn. Finally, the game gets lots of support and constant updates with new rundowns, gear, new enemies, bosses, etc.  I highly recommend getting a group of friends to buy this together as it will give you hundreds of hours of fun and is well worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is actually so good it pisses me off.Here is a game with dynamic mechanics, a very high challenge level, an overwhelming sense of reward and an atmosphere that practically permeates through your monitor.Strap on a headset and team up with 3 other skillful (and doomed) souls as you face a variety of challenges standing between you, your goal, and your escape. What are these challenges? Who knows! Sometimes it will be a pitch black room filled with monsters you must somehow ninja past with almost nothing in your inventory to assist you. Sometimes it'll be loud blaring alarms summoning endless horde waves, which you must cut down as fast as possible with automatic weaponry. Sometimes you'll have to search through fog for keys and items as your body is slowly overtaken by an airborne infection that will literally leave you gasping, or hack into a network by inputting unknown codes into a computer with a command line interface. Sometimes it will be some or all of these things at the same time. The challenges are constantly coming, and they feel fresh and innovative each time.Do you like Dark Souls? Do you like MMO raids? First person shooters? Stealth? Action? Exploration? Do you like talking to people with common interests? Organic horror? A sense of reward? DO YOU LIKE VIDEO GAMES?If you answered yes to any of the above, you'll find something to like in GTFO. How this game has not already taken the industry by storm is beyond me. Anyone who wants a challenging, rewarding, immersive online gaming experience needs to make the investment in this game (which includes not only buying and playing it, but also getting a headset and socializing with the community). Do these things, and you will be glad.

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth it. Despite the lack of matchmaking and VoIP, they've still made arrangements to help players find a group through discord and use the host id from the clipboard to join the lobby.The game is intense and teamwork is a must. Communication is key in winning in this game.Edit Rundown 2:I'm changing my review because I cannot in good conscience recommend this game.Why? Well, it is a fun challenging game that is very demanding in teamwork and skill but at some point, I can't help but think that the devs cannot beat their own levels and just create some parts of the level at a whim. While working on the GTFO Survival Guide, I can't help but think it's a lazy way to design their levels by simply adding more of a certain enemy like the Scout. There are a lot of things they have done right but there's a lot of wrong and if you complain, you start to see how toxic the community can get. "Git gud" as if that's an answer to all of your problems but to have a 3-4 hours of effort lost into a level? And that's only one playthrough until your team is wiped. The starting levels are good and challenging with an average of 45 minutes of gameplay but the later half? Expect over an hour of gameplay per level. You'll need a lot of time in your hands to play them and I understand that many people don't have that. So not only does the difficulty stops some people from accessing all of the content but their allowed time to spend on it stops them as well.I'd change my review back if they add a difficulty settings for those who seek the challenge while allowing others to experience the content. Normal - Hard (2 scouts vs 6 scouts)Or take for example the C1 Nerf, it was hard and fun for some but for a lot of people, the devs had to nerf the level. And even now, for a C level difficulty, it is still D-level hard.And maybe if they set up a level design rule that a level shouldn't take over 2 hours to complete. I think 1 hour is the sweet spot.Also, the devs should make up their mind on their battle mechanics. If the combat is supposed to be high-paced, the player wouldn't be locked to move at a snail's pace and weapon switching would be a lot faster but it isn't. The combat mechanic is daunting and heavy while you move in slow motion and your enemies move at high speed. The last few levels at the deepest part of the complex requires to be high-paced especially if you're restricted to a countdown timer but you move at a crawl. It's contradictory...All of that makes me think that they haven't completed their levels so the perfect balance it had in Rundown 1 is lost in Rundown 2.Edit Rundown 3 :I finished Rundown 3 and I saw that most things of what I said for rundown 2 has been fixed on this rundown. Most missions are around 45 minutes and there's more variation compared to before. There's a few minor stuff that needs to be fixed like the balance in the firearms. In this rundown, you have the HEL Gun, Rifle and the DMR that are too similar to really set them apart from each other but there are other weapons. It's just too bad that there's no Special Weapon with automatic fire and lots of ammo like the Machine Gun.

_childDocuments_.review: For people interested in this type of game, I  do recommend you buy this. Sure, it might be a little up there in price for some, but there's nothing locked behind dlcs, no in game pay-to-win purchasable items, and it's an all around quality game. The general gameplay includes you and your crew (now able to be played single player with the addition of bots who are actually decently smart) sneaking around an underground facility completing objectives, gathering aid packs, and fighting off the enemies. If you're into a fun and, suspenseful, and sometimes rather challenging experience, this game is for you.On a side note, GTFO does have an official discord server which is great for people new to the game who want either a little bit of help or if they don't have friends who own the game, but don't want to play alone or with random people.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game so far has been with a full team, keep that in mind as you read this review.GTFO is truly a masterpiece, I mean that with utmost sincerity. GTFO  does not do a whole lot but what it does do is so incredibly well executed I cannot help but be overly impressed with the amount of detail and effort 10 chambers has gone through to create a truly unique  and challenging experience.Let me just say this game is hard and it will punish you for every mistake, your hand will not be held. Despite this, the game is incredibly addicting with a team. Planning out each and every move and praying our next locker or chest is an ammo box or med kit is a fantastic experience to share. The levels are very well designed and the atmosphere of the game can simply not be matched by any other game in its category. It is eerie and the opening of each and every run really reminds you just how screwed you really are. The decent into a pit of darkness to what is most likely your doom, feels so damn good.The level of detail the game has is a testament to true passionate game designers. Being able to see your teammates flashlight, having to actually type in commands at terminals in the game and being able to actually see what your teammates are typing, opening the map and seeing your teammates cursor so that you can more easily communicate your plan, and the scratches you see on your screen when passing by light reminding you that you are wearing a gas mask are just such fantastic touches that really have made this game for me. Also the characters talking to each other or commenting on things happening is also a very nice touch and have made for some good moments with friends.As an early access game 10/10 as a completed game I give it a 7/10, 100% worth the price in its current state with some buddies, assuming you all enjoy a challenge.Here's what I would like to see added to final game, keep in mind i have not looked at their road-map while listing these things.1. Glow sticks: I want glow sticks to last much longer so that they can be used to mark an escape route in missions where we need to gtfo as quickly as possible. Right now the current time that they stick around is simply too short to make them useful enough to be excited about them. I see their value but I'm more excited about their potential.2. Character progression: I would like to see some sort of minor character progression that played off of your current mental state, infection rate, ect. Such as an unstable mental state making monsters appear where they are not and a higher infection rate making the character cough or have their vision become slightly yellow. I think it would be cool to have these problems reset after the RUN DOWN changes and apply them only when the character fails. Offsetting this by giving the players awards when they complete a mission (such as more starting ammo on their next mission or a perk or unique device of some sort) would be very interesting.3. Consumables and tools: Keeping consumables and tools in a stash after successfully completing a mission for future use in missions you are having problems with I think would be a very valuable addition. I would want this stash to be very limited to keep the game difficult and discourage hoarding but adds to you progressing with the game as you go deeper. 4. Terminal interactions: I would like to see more terminal interactions, such as activating a venting system in rooms to get rid of fog, but also have the draw back of enemies being more easily alerted in that room. Or activating disarmed sentry guns in an area. 5. Lore/story: I would like to see more of the story and lore added into the game more directly. As I've said before the atmosphere of the game is very good, and the idea of why you are down there and why you are doing all this is very interesting. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. I've only played through one mission but i'm reviewing it now since I dont know when else i'm going to get the opportunity to play it since it requires a group of pretty close knit friends all around the same skill level to get the most out of it, due to it being a really hard co-op game. I can see the game potentially getting repetitive to some people due to there not being an overwhelming selection of guns and tools, but to me that kind of adds to the charm and allows you to get a base understanding of each weapon really quickly and figure out level strategies faster. Despite being really hard I don't find the game overwhelming at all; the only part that is kind of confusing is how level progression is structured and the whole "rundown" bit, which isn't really explained well to new players. But the actual gameplay itself is surprisingly straightforward and easy to jump into- my friends had played the game before and I was brand new, we just started a level they were stuck on and I got the hang of it pretty quick.I enjoy how the levels don't randomize very much between runs, the structure and doors remain the same so you can actually plot out strategies by playing a level over and over again. The gunplay is fairly standard but feels good and it's super satisfying to hit an enemy in the head with a sledgehammer. There's a half & half split between "stealth" and "action" so it never feels like you're doing the same thing for too long and there's a lot of on-the-fly thinking to figure out what strategy you should use in what situation. If you mess up and get hit you don't die instantly; you actually have a pretty generous amount of health and ammo given to you at the start... the challenge is that you have to make it last nearly the entire mission since there are very sparse resources.Overall if you like survival horror games and want to play a heavily co-op themed survival horror game this is probably the absolute best game for you. I never felt super scared while playing it but there definitely was a tension that never let up during the whole game, similar to early survival horror where you have extremely limited resources and hate having to take any unnecessary fights.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is a lot of things. It's you and 3 of your least favorite people plunging into the unknown because a hostile computer has dominion over your meat. It's putting turrets up at an alarm door you have no choice to trigger. It's huddling in the dark around a fog machine while clicking noises sing your nerves into stuttering live wires.GTFO is tense. White knuckles on mice, exasperated breaths, high fives over discord tense. Watching others clear rooms, killing sleepers, simultaneously hammering the tall boys. Chucking a foam grenade at the walking Olive Garden before sprinting in to finish it off, you will terrified of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up. You won't, most of the time. But when things go Triangle Shirtwaist, it'll always stir up right before you bring the hammer down.GTFO is fluid. The alarm is ringing, the doors are closed. Dave uses the motion tracker to find the horde. Before they break through the door, the turrets are up, and the mines are down to meet them once they break through. Nobody has said anything. When it's done and nobody has gotten hit, and there's plenty of ammo, there might even be some jokes. If things were less loving, everyone knows that the flow has to be better during the next alarm.GTFO is cinematic. Klaxons and whirring red lights cast long shadows off of twitching bodies. Glow sticks color the worst possible configurations of teeth and skin and claws. Fog traps everyone into twisting corridors with nightmare sounds squelch every crouched foot step. Hammers make delicious crushing noises. Enemies rip apart in delightful splatters of guts and gore. The noises, the scenes, they all offer a single feeling. A feeling that you're not supposed to be here, and you need to leave.GTFO is challenging. Raids in Destiny levels of communication, with opaque mechanics, and unexplained nuance. Details are important. The hammer works, you didn't kill it because you didn't hit it right. Glow sticks, fog repellers, lock melters, everything except for the long range flashlight, it's all important. Scouts parade around, casting noodley promises of an early death. You'll want to learn, after you play a little bit, but crucially I think discovering this stuff with your friends is the best of the time in the deep.  GTFO is growing. With new rundowns, new puzzles, new challenges, and more on the way, this is a great time to get invested in what I think is the best time you can have with 3 people over the internet. As a warning, it is essential to have 4 people to play this with. If you don't, don't buy it, you'll never get to play. Other than that, I don't think I've ever been so enraptured with a video game product. I think about the twitching things below the jail all the time, about the whir of doors opening, about the tearing of a door frame, about the coldly delivered objectives offered with no context. The machine hates me I think, but I'm going to go down again, I can't help myself.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is among the best of any 4-player co-op experience. Each of the 80+ maps now available (post Rundown 8) help to evoke the highs of MMO raid progression in learning mechanics, devising and refining strategies, and executing them successfully in collaboration with your peers.Decidedly different than other games in the genre are the absence of leveling systems or skill trees to artificially gate progression through grind - there are also no unlockable or paid elements to shortcut your path to clearing content. All weapons and utilities are available for use on any map and experimentation of your team’s setup can alter your ability to succeed as you balance resources available on a given map and enemy compositions with the strengths and weaknesses of your tools for their range, DPS and burst abilities, penetration, and ammo efficiency. The skill focus extends to the way the weapons operate – the weapons with the best ammo and damage efficiency have explicit limitations (longer reloads, larger spread, shorter damage falloff ranges) that significantly increase their risk to use or require relying on your team to cover situations that you cannot.The levels (“Rundowns”) in GTFO follow a similar philosophy to the loadout in delivering a fair and skill testing experience. Total resources (ammunition, tool refills, health) per map have fixed total values but are scattered and split randomly between varying positions on the map. Objectives do not change, but their locations do. This complements the static high-level strategy per map with a dynamic one that changes based on your group’s situation and resources and how successful your team was at clearing tasks and executing the plan. The flow per map is also dynamic in how you frequently switch between stealth or active combat and your group’s decisions to do so based on the current objective or timed challenges – stealth isn’t always the correct answer, nor is clearing or engaging a room at all for its resources. At a macro level the objective variety is strong with over 15 types of map objectives with new mechanics gradually introduced through game progressions and twisted and reframed to make the experience interesting and fresh. The atmosphere, characters, and environmental lore are also excellent and coupled with low light and dense fog keep situations tense.The tagline of the game “Work together or die together” truly defines the game. From theory to practice in the context of personal experience the game is incredibly challenging, fair, and the sense of accomplishment felt after spending 20 hours of attempts on an individual map is truly rewarding. Hundreds if not thousands of hours of gameplay are present here and if you vibe with the theme and enjoy a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone. That is not a mistake, that is a specific design decision on the developers part. My friends and I used to joke that "GTFO is the game made by the developers FOR the developers, and along the way someone jokingly said "Hey why don't we sell this to people? Maybe they'll like it" and they decided to run with it.The jokes aside this is a really niche, yet very beautifully crafted game. The gameplay loop is very unique in the sense that is discourages rampant guns blazing tactics in favor of a strategic approach. You WANT to avoid loud confrontation as much as possible and when you are left with no choice but to GO loud, have a plan set in stone to help you get out on the other side with your resources and health in tact.Where are they coming from? What doors can we block off to slow their approach? What traps can we set to take out chunks of them before we open fire? Any escape routes we can take if things go south? GTFO is 90% planning and 10% shooting but that's what makes the game's loop feel so satisfying! When you manage to take down a horde with as few resources as possible it feels so great because you know that you now have more ammo and health to work with if things gets worse further into the compound.Gameplay aside, with the 1.0 release they really nailed some of the QOL update. The bots are really good. They are not without quirks but you have command options to make them do and perform certain actions like setting up turrets, foam walls and even hold resources for you. Their aim is also godsent and they are going to make every bullet count.The checkpoints was a much needed part to make the game more approachable for some people. In the early access, a single mistake could spell doom for your team and that meant going back to the beginning of a map and try again. With the checkpoint system they at least make it more manageable to try again without having to start all over. They do this without taking away from the difficulty of the game.The new melee weapons are also fun and really allows you to tailor your playstyle more and more. Do you want a strong, slow weapon for taking out enemies silently but from a range? Do you prefer a much smaller option where you really need to get close to the enemy but the kills are fast to pull off? There's enough choices for anyone to have a preference.And then there's the story. In the past most of the story came through reading logs and listening to audio recordings. They were mostly a side thing for those interested in diving deeper into the story and universe of GTFO, but with Rundown #6 and the 1.0 release they are putting a lot more emphasis on telling the story directly as part of the gameplay and it's worked really well thus far. It leaves you asking questions and trying to seek answers for those questions, encouraging you to keep going deeper and deeper into the complex. I can't wait to see where they take this story!So overall: If you are prepared to face trial and error and accept that the game is difficult then certainly try the game out! It's become one of my favorite releases in recent times!

This game in reality is a coop stealth horror game with (very well made) shooting as the punishment for Fing up the stealth. The stealth gameplay revolves around crouch walking, standing very still occasionally and timing melee kills with your teammates before somebody F's it up and everybody starts blasting. As good as the game is, the stealth and melee overall feels less polished and like it had less care put into it than the shooting aspect did, which is strange considering the game discourages shooting as much as it possibly can.It's a very strange game and the only thing I can compare it to are Payday 2 stealth heists on the harder difficulties, but with better gunplay and the ability to return to stealth as the reward for failing stealth. I love the atmosphere, I love the setting, I love the CMD Prompt computer usage and the main menus being themed after DOS style computer interfaces.The only real complaint I have, and I'm not very far into this game at all so this could be a non-issue, is that I'd really like to do more shooting because the guns are cool and the shooting mechanics are insanely well done. _childDocuments_.review: 'Uncompromising' is the one word that sums up everything about this game: the levels, your objectives, the foes you will face, the Warden which sends you down again and again, and even the Complex itself which you are sent down into.You, unfortunately, must be the opposite: you must learn to compromise with your comrades for the best of the group and for the objective; you must learn to compromise when your situation becomes less-than-ideal (a common experience during your expeditions into the Complex); and you will compromise yourself to meet the demands of the uncompromising Warden. No cost is deemed too great to reveal the mysteries of the Complex.I've played this game since the first rundown during Early Access, and while I missed an entire rundown (and partially missed another), I did get to finally fill in the gaps when the game properly released. My admiration for it has never abated, and I will forever sing it praises for being uncompromising during an era where game experiences are more often than not compromised for a population that refuses to meet a game on its terms.This is not for the faint of heart, those who seek a less demanding experience, or those who refuse to work with others. If you can accept that and meet this game on its terms, it's one of the most memorable experiences of its kind.Get in, work together, don't die, and Get The F- Out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is pretty solid. Definitely a must buy if you like co-op games, or games that are difficult. I only have two real gripes with the game. One, the missions can sometimes take . I'm talking up to 4-5 hours for the later missions. And two, there really isn't a reason to go back and replay missions. For me, once I beat one of those 3-5 hour long missions I seriously don't feel like ever doing it again. Even for the shorter missions I don't feel like replaying them because there simply isn't a reason to - at least there isn't for me. If you can enjoy replaying missions without getting anything to show for it, then this probably wouldn't be an issue for you.The actual base gameplay is simple and easy to understand; the game chooses to build difficulty through the mission design for the most part instead of through gameplay. Each rundown has a different theme (currently anyway), and each mission within the rundown tries to do something unique and challenge the player in a variety of ways. One mission you could be trying to carry multiple batteries through a level, while another you could be in infectious fog that barely allows you to see. Each mission being an unknown challenge is half the fun of the game to be honest, so I recommend trying avoid spoilers from people outside the ones you're playing with.While the game currently does not have matchmaking, I'd say in a strange way it sort of  the game. Having to hop into the discord and join up with groups of people advertising their lobbies feels almost like walking into a stereotypical DnD tavern or guild looking for people to quest with. It also ensures that everyone is generally communicative - or at least talking to one another. You don't always get the best team this way, but it's fun meeting all kinds of people while trying to accomplish some of the later missions like D2.  Plus, if you hate the people you keep joining into you can always just host your own lobby and do your own advertising in the LFG channel. I personally went from joining random lobbies to always hosting my own, and have met some hilarious people by doing so. Definitely don't write the game off because it has no matchmaking, or because you don't have a group to play with!If doing missions that can range from mechanically difficult to tests of perseverance with four other people sounds like a good time to you, then you'll love this game. If you don't like having to retry missions a lot, missions that take a while, or having to find your own group (if you don't have one) then you probably won't like this game. Me personally, I recommend it a lot. It's a unique experience that you don't get with many games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a glutton for punishment with a twisted sense of teamwork, GTFO might just be your digital masochism paradise. Picture this: you and your buddies, armed to the teeth, tiptoeing through hellish corridors infested with Lovecraftian nightmares, all while trying not to scream obscenities at each other. Welcome to GTFO, where the only thing scarier than the monsters lurking in the shadows is the prospect of coordinating with your friends.Let's talk about frustrations. Oh boy, where do I start? Ever had that heart-stopping moment when you accidentally alert a horde of grotesque creatures because someone sneezed into their mic? Yep, GTFO's got plenty of those. And just when you thought you had the perfect plan to stealthily navigate through a level, someone decides it's a brilliant idea to go full Rambo on a group of sleepers, triggering a cacophony of chaos that would make even the bravest marine wet their pants.But hey, it's not all doom and gloom. GTFO is a masterpiece when it comes to showcasing the fragility of human relationships under pressure. Remember that time Steve forgot to refill his ammo before a big fight and you had to sacrifice your last health pack to keep him alive? Yeah, good times. And let's not forget the classic "who stole my glow stick" debate that's bound to erupt at least once per session, sparking a heated argument that makes the monsters outside seem downright cuddly in comparison.In GTFO, communication is key. Or so they say. In reality, it's more like a cacophony of conflicting commands and panicked screams that would make a kindergarten teacher weep. "Shoot the big one!" "No, not that big one, the other big one!" "Who has the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ keycard?!" It's like trying to orchestrate a symphony with a bunch of tone-deaf cats.But amidst all the frustrations and co-op dramas, there's a strange beauty to GTFO. It's the kind of game that makes you question your friendships, your sanity, and whether or not you should invest in a better headset with noise-cancelling capabilities. So, grab your friends, steel your nerves, and prepare to descend into the depths of madness. Just don't forget to pack extra ammo and maybe a couple of stress balls. You're gonna need 'em.

It can be buggy, frustrating and confusing at times, but never feels unfair. It is a niche product for a hardcore audience. But if you are intrigued by it's premise and have buddies or no problem with looking for them on the Discord then it is an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric but ultimately incredibly repetitive and dull. Every run is the same, save for a few environmental hazards. You stealth, melee, loot and then open another door to repeat the cycle all over again. Sometimes you'll have an alarmed door to open where you'll get to experience one of the games few standout moments of brief Aliens-like action set-pieces but these are few and far between as your team meanders through foggy copy-paste rooms filled full of terribly designed monsters.The much talked-about difficulty isn't even an issue as watching a few Youtube videos will fully prepare yourself for everything the game will throw at you. As for the "horror" aspect of the game, honestly, it doesn't have one. There are no real moments of terror and the only tension comes from spending 40 minutes clearing a run to end up with no ammo on the final door or hastily inputting console commands in as your team eagerly waits in the background. Ultimately the problem I have with GTFO is that the actual game play loop is just tedious and boring. There is no real progression and the content refreshes mean that you're unable to return to any of your favourite runs after they update. The game would benefit from more engaging objectives, a persistent horde-style mode or just something to break up the tedium. 6/10 - Only buy if you're the type of gamer to enjoy repetitive tasks for little in-game progression. Also don't bother if you don't have any friends on Discord as the games MM community is utterly terrible and few people use microphones.Recommendation - If you're looking for ACTUAL tension in a co-op FPS then get Ready or Not.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not like the game. I am a fan of Co-op oriented games, and have gone so far as to say that all games are made better by Co-op. I love difficult games, I often try to play on harder difficulties and I also am a fan of games playing with lighting as a mechanic. Lastly, I like slower paced games.With all of that said, I was expecting GTFO to kind of be a perfect storm for me, and yet I asked for a refund.Ultimately, I find the game to be too slow, but I think it's better explained as needlessly slow. Rooms are very large but contain little loot or enemies, movespeed feels on the lower side out of combat, and I couldn't get any tab autocompletes to work in ingame terminals. As I mentioned that I refunded the game, in my 117 minutes of gameplay I wasn't able to complete the mission with 2 friends, one experienced while the other and myself were not. Part of this, in my opinion, is due to the game having too little ammo. I like ammo management, but I do not personally find it engaging in GTFO. Stealthing the game, which helps you conserve ammo, I consider more tedious than engaging, looting I find to be very boring, as it's a lot of nothing with some things sprinkled, and things you want being fewer.I didn't enjoy the game's darkness, I didn't feel that the visual impairments added to the game, and moreso made looting and other such things more annoying. Personally, I find that Deep Rock Galactic does a far better job of playing with the light levels, but the two games are of different scopes.I was a little disappointed to find out that the game doesn't have very much in the way of unlockable progression, as I feel like with it's difficulty it would be neat to unlock some rewards for it. But this is moreso a personal gripe on my part.
