_childDocuments_.review: The best way to summarize my opinion of this game is that I think about it more than I play it. While I love the game as a unique experience, it's just really inaccessible. This is a very difficult coop shooter. It's characterized by long missions, slow pace, heavy resource management, and "oh ♥♥♥♥" moments. It's not something you can just get on and play because of lack of any tutorial, need for 4 players to have a "balanced" experience, 1-3 hour mission times with no checkpoints, and high level of teamwork requires things like mics and reasonable teammates, both of which don't lend themselves to matchmaking. This is a game where a single person making a minor mistake can wipe the entire team. I think this naturally makes playing with randoms difficult. But having a steady group of 4 is not something many people have. It sucks that this is the main consideration when considering the game, because the game does create some novel and memorable moments. The game also has kind of a seasonal approach, the game has a strict set of levels that are not random and very hand-crafted for you to do. There's not a lot of them, but they are long, hard, and have bonus challenges that incentivize coming back to them. They also completely replace the entire set of levels with fresh ones a couple times a year. The new sets of levels also come with new tools and new guns. So it's a game you'll want to be returning to over time.  So what's the secret sauce? For me the big upside is the atmosphere, which really comes in two flavors. The first flavor that you'll be experiencing most of the time is the constant sense of dread and foreboding that comes with navigating the high risk rooms in stealth, trying to preserve health and resources, knowing that a single mistake at any moment can cost the whole team. The second flavor is panic. This doesn't just happen in predictable scenarios where you KNOW there is going to be an alarm. It also happens when your stealth fails and now you suddenly have a horde to deal with. These are really the best moments of the game, because I feel like this is one of the best horror games at creating panick in a group of people. Normally coop ruins horror vibes. But There's a caveat to this. Most panick moments are created by the level design of the missions. There are specific surprises and challenges built into each level. If you group with experienced people on the discord server, they will spoil a lot of these moments for you. Honestly, when I played with a group of friends going in blind, the experience was VASTLY superior to playing with people from the discord server. People who look up youtube videos of the levels and know all the surprises going in are seriously undermining the core experience of the game just for the payoff of beating a level. But this game is just not that special when you reduce it to the pure mechanics of the game. When this game becomes just a kiting/aiming exercise, that's really when it starts to fail. So yeah, I recommend under specific conditions of being able to play with at least 2 other friends (my friends and I were able to enjoy the game and even beat some levels with three, and adding a single person into a tight nit group we can usually socially enforce no spoilers). But unfortunately, people's desire to master and beat the game kind of robs of it of the horror magic it's trying to hard to create. And unfortunately, most people on the discord server seem to value people who will increase their odds of WINNING. Of course they do right? It's always like that in any game, especially a game where failure could mean you "wasted" an entire hour.You gotta STOP thinking like that with this game. This isn't a game with grind. You don't win loot or progress your character by beating levels. You don't "waste time" by failing a level. You progress by learning the game. The fun of the game is in discovering the mechanics and experiencing the surprises. This isn't a game where you're missing on loot or progression because you aren't playing optimally. When you've got some scared buddies with you and you're timidly crawling through a dark scary place and then suddenly you hear that scream and things go loud and you're panick run/shooting and lose track of what's going on, that's the magic of the game. I think it's a pretty unique experience when it isn't meta-gamed.

Enemy animations can appear ragged and choppy.-gun play feels disconnected, I am not sure how best to describe this maybe its the lack of sound on bullet impact or the weapon animations and sound but something is off.-Enemies always behave the same way. Scouts are creepy and a good change up but the rest of the enemies once alerted just make a bee-line to the play and start attacking in a line for the most part. _childDocuments_.review: It’s clearly designed for a party of four, but how’s the solo experience?Managing resources and determining which rooms you need to clear is the crux of solo play. As a result, missions are decently replayable since the methodical approach to clearing rooms depends heavily on randomized resources enemy spawns and your melee skill. The bots aren’t great, but they don’t actively get in the way like many other coop shooters. You can clear most missions easily with bots, though they seem to struggle with heavy gun-play and you obviously can’t split up for separate objectives. Honestly, my main complaint is that the game doesn’t seem to let you play solo without an internet connection. Bugs:- The game can fail to launch or make lobbies sometimes, I haven't identified if this is an issue with the game itself, network or proton layer stuff yet.- Enemy animations can go a bit goofy.- Some maps have environment clipping.- Resource boxes can spawn in inaccessible places.- Occasionally the entire environment can get culled out for a second when going through doors, which is a bit weird and jarring.- Bots often stand outside the warden exit scans.- Bots can phase through gooed & closed doors, which can ruin a run if it happens right before a full-team scan event.- I’ve had the game crash twice after completing a mission, but I didn’t lose any progress or artifacts. Clunk:- Some tools like glowsticks require a left-click charge to throw, these inputs don't seem to get buffered and can be lost when swapping between weapons/tools.- The hacking tool can fail to unlock doors if you swap away from it after the last hacking input.- Commanding bots through the 'q' menu is generally too slow to use mid-combat, but I don't think there's a good fix for this, as even a gesture wheel could be awkward.Assuming 10 Chambers doesn’t abandon this game, and you’re okay with methodical stealth into excellent gun-play, this game is great!

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, the work of a critic is easy. We risk very little, yet enjoy a position over those who offer up their work and their selves to our judgment. We thrive on negative criticism, which is fun to write and to read. But the bitter truth we critics must face, is that in the grand scheme of things, the average piece of junk is probably more meaningful than our criticism designating it so. But there are times when a critic truly risks something, and that is in the discovery and defense of the *new*. The world is often unkind to new talent, new creations. The new needs friends. Last night, I experienced something new: an extraordinary game from a singularly unexpected source. To say that both the game and its studio have challenged my preconceptions about fine digital entertainment is a gross understatement. They have rocked me to my core. In the past, I have made no secret of my disdain for Ten Chambers famous motto, "work together or die together. " But I realize, only now do I truly understand what they meant. Not everyone can become a great developer; but a great developer *can* come from *anywhere*. It is difficult to imagine more humble origins than those of the genius now developing at Ten Chambers, who is, in this critic's opinion, nothing less than the finest developer in Sweden. I will be returning to GTFO soon, hungry for more

_childDocuments_.review: Lets just start with saying, I love this game. Coming from someone who doesn't consider themselves a hardcore gamer (GTFO is my most played game by far) I think its a great experience and highly recommend it. HOWEVER, this game is not for everyone.As many other reviews will tell you, this game is one of the best at creating a sense of dread and impending doom. To this day it is probably the only multiplayer game that can still scare me. The gun play is responsive, rigid but not restricting, and truly hammers home the idea that you are not the apex predator. The stealth combat is fun, perhaps even more so than the shooting, and doesn't bog you down or make the game feel too slow.However;There is a lot wrong with this game. While I personally haven't been put off by it, there are a lot of bugs. Compounding this problem is the fact that your average level in this game takes around 60 - 90 minutes, with even the shortest ones being around half an hour. Spending all that time on a game to have a bug ruin it will definitely sour the experience. Personally the length of the levels is the biggest problem and the reason that after over 300+ hours in game, I can only stomach one or two levels a month. The A Tier of the game (The first and easiest of the levels) is far too easy for a veteran, the B Tier is similar but has some tense moments and some bad RNG that could result in a wipe, I feel the C Tier is this game at its best. Beyond that the game becomes nearly unplayable for your average user. I understand that the niche and main draw to this game is the hardcore nature of it but come on, 8 of the most difficult enemy in the game followed by 4 of the second most difficult enemy in the game on loop for 3 hours isn't fun. 2 or 3 deaths is fine, encouraged even, this game is supposed to be hard, 4 or 5 I'll take, skill issue right? But 15 + hours on one level is madness, even for a vet. And then they go and add secondary objectives.These devs are some sadistic mfs.So why after all that trash talk would I still recommend it. Because I keep coming back. After all these years I still load up the game and play another mission or two. With the new bot mechanic I can beat A and B tier and I still think its pretty fun. Every once and a while I drop in with some friends and we hammer out a C level, maybe even a D level if its not too bad.For 30 dollars, you can at least give the game a try. I think its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO is a tactical PvE Coop team shooter. It's very fun and genuinely one of my favorite Coop games there is. But it is NOT for the regular person. This game is best played by two people: Masochists, and people who genuinely hate themselves. This game's levels require cooperation, strategy, and the willpower to stop yourself from smashing your keyboard in pain when you die and have to redo a mission that took you several hours to do. The mission in this game can take between 30 minutes and 3 or more hours, depending on the mission. If you don't have the right plan, you die. If you don't have enough ammo, you die. If you brought the wrong weapons, the wrong tool, the wrong boosters for the job, you die. Sometimes you have to redo missions just because you didn't bring the right stuff. _childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a very split review so I want to get the important bits out of the way first. GTFO is fantastic. It's beautiful in a horrifying way with fantastic visuals, the sound design is on point, it's a cooperative 4 player PVE game. But Enek, you might be asking, you downvoted this game, so what's going on? It's because I also hate this game; not for the accompanying frills to build upon a game, but the core of it in which everything is built.+This games been making waves again lately with the new "rundown" coming out, what that means in a more understanding, tldr phrase, is a new map is being released, with some new enemies, even some new weapons. Fresh content drip into a steadily releasing early access game is a beautiful thing. Beyond that the stealth action and puzzle solving is rather fun. There's coordination in everything you do, as you move from room to room sweeping things out and collecting all you can. Unpolished gem that is already shining to a degree.This however is where things get messy. The game is hard, and punishing. There is nothing wrong with challenge, but this alone can be a make or break for people wanting to check this out. This is not a Left 4 Dead, or a Payday style game. This is not run and gun gameplay.-You WILL spend 80% of your time crouched and slowly walking about, until the game gives up on it and you have to pass a security door. At which point the game throws out stealth and it now becomes a defensive hold, against a flood of foes. In any other game this could be fun, but gun-play in GTFO is not. Hitboxes can feel strange, as does damage dealt to enemies; you can blow an enemy open with a shotty, sending viscera flying, and it's still smacking you. There's a lack of feedback to taking damage and being downed; a defense hold will start, and you'll discover one of the naruto running or crabwalking bastard is just standing next to you lashing you with a tongue annnd you're down. Compounding the problems of the game as other comments will no doubt show, is a lack of matchmaking. It's steam friends or, ironically enough, gtfo. The problem being even if matchmaking WAS implemented, it's be fairly unbearable as voice coms are a necessity at every stage, and one persons mistake can endanger the entire squad.-I break this into the next section both as a negative in the game, but to draw attention to it as a potential to curve the growth of the game moving forward. There is no player growth. There is no chase or advancement. After playing through stages, there is nothing to do other than just playing them some more for the sake of it. No weapons to unlock, no perks to spec out a character, no dumb cosmetics to show off to friends.-As a final aside, the puzzle solving aspects with the hacking are a fantastic take on the whole thing, but they're also very bare bones. The method you go about doing it is wonderful, there just isn't anything additional to do with it aside from ping objectives mainly.I don't want to give this game a scathing review because there are parts of it I do genuinely enjoy. This is a review of disappointment out of something I hunger for more of and to be better, not because it needs trashing on. I WANT either a tough as nails pure stealth gameplay, or there to be a more classic run and gun style option. I want a chase to keep me going through stages. I want GTFO to kick ass; but unfortunately with the rave reviews it's getting, I don't ever think it will for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what would happen if you put Payday: The Heist, Resident Evil, and Neon Genesis Evangelion in a blender. Keep at it and you'll go from being crippled by simple mistakes to quickly mitigating the consequences of colossal screw-ups, but don't get too complacent because it will eventually throw a curve ball at you.If you're wondering WHY you're crawling around a foggy underground hell hole you're about on the same page as the people you're playing as. Those pods they get pulled out of at the start of every mission damage their memories so they have only the faintest idea of who they are and what they're doing, so don't worry too much about it.Matchmaking is a bit FUBAR as I'm writing this, so you might have to go poking around the game's discord to get a full group if you don't have friends to play with already. You can play alone with bots and probably manage to complete at least Rundown 1 if you equip them properly. They do make extremely stupid decisions sometimes though so be prepared for that. On the bright side: With the right weapons they can be relied on to hit their targets. Just avoid giving them low capacity guns and you should be okay.

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO in it's current state is a rough diamond. The game is brutally difficult they aren't just blowing smoke with that description. The game punishes mistakes heavily often ending the run on the spot. But that level of risk comes with an incredible reward for strategic play that very few games can achieve. So far I've cleared only a single rundown with my group and a group is absolutely necessary, we tried for a long time to clear as a duo and while it felt possible it felt like it required a flawless run, a full group felt like it allowed a little more wiggle room but still very punishing. Despite this extreme level of difficulty almost no games gave me the rush of excitement this one did at the end of the level. Failure feels like a learning experience never unfair you know exactly what you can change on the next run. In a world saturated with procedurally generated challenges and levels, it's very refreshing to get structured levels with a great challenge that you can work towards completing instead of failure meaning relearning certain aspects. Overall I think this is one of the most promising games in early access and I can't wait to see how the devs expand on it's already very strong foundation.Pros:Fantastic atmosphereSome of the best lighting in horror games, dark corners and foggy corridors hide everything in them.Enemies are powerful but not unfairVery satisfying to execute a successful planGame play loop is great and feels like a slower more horror focused left 4 deadCons:Guns are kind of floaty at the moment, lack impact when fired.Melee hit tracking can get funky when aiming down at enemies have to aim a little under the target.I highly recommend giving the game a shot, even now it's a great investment in a game that is obviously loved by it's developers and it's just a very solid framework at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE FOR 1.0:This game is MASSIVELY different than what I remember. It runs better, there's more loot, the gun variety is like 2-3x higher than before.Havent dove into a game with friends yet, but this review is probably largely rendered obsolete. I already liked the game a lot but it's been improved upon greatly. Still positive review as it was good before and is better in all regards now.Update for Rundown #2: I dont know if I'm better at the game, if some updates to hardware made this game run better or if they've improved performance, maybe even just made the levels better as to not have as much of an impact on your resources. But this game runs better.New missions are fun, different and I'm actually beating some with the performance improvement. New mechanics are fun, new consumables are fun, new guns-... Well the burst rifle is a great add, rebalanced guns are alot better too.. It's everything I wanted in an update for this game.This update gives me ALOT of hope for the future of this game. How all the mechanics can come together with new hazards, new enemies, new consumables, new tools can make this game incredibly deep.You think an item like fog dispenser wouldnt really help that much, on a level you can see everything already. But then you use it and you're like HOLY CRAP I CAN SEE. So you use them all. Then you find rooms FULL of fog and you realize you either need to go around this, find more fog dispensers or be VERY careful going through it (if its not the infection clouds).On top of that, glow sticks were like useless before, now they're nice to find when dangerous rooms random alot of the lights off.---------Original review:This isnt like upgrading to killing floor 2 where everything is flashy, faster and more energetic. This is like if those custom maps in killing floor 1 where you cant buy items, you have to find them, were made into a stand alone game with more emphasis on being careful, tactics and cooperation. Not that you can find guns, but you have to search for ammo and health ect.My first game, I went in without reading anything or looking at the video in a few months. We just ran in the first room and go "I see em!" and start blasting. Literally died in the second room in the first level.Second game we try taking it slower. Read that it said they react to light while we were dropping into the level. Found some glow sticks. Turned out flashlights off, scouted out all the enemies in a room before we started shooting. It was easier. But we still died in the second round of fighting.Everything in this game takes a careful approach (or maybe 4 players) otherwise you're going to die or lose a large amount of resources. I dont want to spoil discovering anything, because it's a cool experience to think one item is useless and then see how incredibly good it is was a big laugh for us.After about 15 tries of learning the mechanics and trying new guns/strategies, we've yet to beat the first level with 2 players. But it feels fun still. The maps change periodically, the actual content in the maps change from run to run. The rooms will be shaped the same but the items and enemies in them will be different. I forgot to check how long the first set of maps are going to be set in stone before they change but I'm looking forward to it. There's a bit of weird stuff going on with aiming for me. I dont know if its because I need to upgrade my PC or if its on the game's end but it doesnt feel as snappy to aim as I'd like. But this just makes it all more tactical to me. You cant just flail around and be an action hero. You have to be careful.The guns could 1000% use some balancing, as some seem weaker than others, but there's still a good few loadouts that can fit multiple playstyles. Really excited to see what the progression systems bring. Really would love to customize my character, which I saw was on the roadmap. This game is going places, I'd say get it while it's hot. _childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is HARD. You will need patience and squad tactics to survive. Its not a game for lone wolfsFor most of the match you will be low on either ammo, health or equipment charge. You will need to communicate with your team as enemy spawns differ each map and a previously safe route will suddenly be overrun. The first level took me about 6 runs to get through, the challange on the next map really picks up. Its kind of Left 4 Dead meets Dead Space meets Splinter Cell. You have to time your attacks with your team and use your load out to your advantage. Battle plans can fall apart as soon as the fight starts so you have to think on your feet. Once you get the needed item it gets really tough as you have to fight your way back to the start and hold out for a short time.The lack of matchmaking is kind of annoying but it is bringing people together in Discord. Met some cool people pretty easily but setting up a match from scratch sometimes takes a little bit of leg work.

_childDocuments_.review: playing as Hackett, game gave everyone in my squad Hackett's hood except for me. I got one worse looking gas mask.10/10 even the cosmetics have it out for meIn all seriousness, This is a 4 person co-op game. This is not like the Left for Dead games or the Vermintide games. This game is about teamplay. The focus is not how accurate you can shoot, or how much DPS you can get out, it is about how your group of 4 people can create and execute your own plans, under stress, to beat difficult odds.This game is hard on purpose, and it is handcrafted to that goal. You will fail missions. You will give up on levels. You will spend hours and multiple attempts grinding at the same levels until you finally get through it.Some levels you may not get through.I have completed at least 60-80% of the levels in the rundowns I participated in with 3 person teams.Some levels we could not complete without that fourth person.If you rely on bots, you will have problems. The solution to those problems is not to "fix" the AI, it's to replace it with another human.If you do not have 4 people, you must be willing to find people to fill or the game won't be worth it. On that note, if you rely on matchmaking you are again handicapping yourself. Voice communication and familiarity with each others' play-styles are almost necessary to complete some levels.

_childDocuments_.review: "GTFO is seriously hard, you need dedication and teamwork to survive!"Yes, but...Having a four man squad makes a difference, the ability to talk and work together will provide a definite edge. And dedication is definitely required as the game tells you nothing, rather it drops you in a pit with little ammo and a flashlight. I like the premise, the game reminds me of titles like Resident Evil, Left 4 Dead, and Dead by Daylight, but lacks the polish and shine. Gun battles are filled with lag spikes and frame-rate drops, leaving you shooting madly at hordes and praying to make it out with enough health and ammo to go on. Much of my time playing was spent lost in the labyrinth, running from room to room trying to figure out where to go, where to take power packs, how best to split up loot... Nearly every room looks the same, getting turned around and lost is a frequent occurrence and made my play-through rather aggravating.There are moments in the game where you'll defend a doorway from a horde, turrets are planted, foam deployed, bullets go flying, tension is high, and everyone is fighting for survival. These are the best moments in the game and they are short-lived, and far too few. The majority of the time you'll sneak or pounce sleepers with a hammer (It's like wack-a-mole, except not fun?...), and try to loot lockers before your team-mates so you can have a little more of that ever so precious ammo or health-packs. I have to disagree with the developers when they say the game is "hard", I didn't find it 'hard' at all, rather very tedious and unnecessarily uninformative. I don't need a game to hold my hand, but some kind of guide as far as what to do, how things work and where you should be trying to go would be nice. I shouldn't have to watch hours of YT videos just to understand or enjoy the game, and at 30$ there are better titles on the market (IMO I wouldn't pay more than $10 for this).If you have three other friends willing to do the research and stumble around in a damp, dark basement, grab this at deep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for 2 years for GTFO to release for purchase. I did not hesitate when it opened for alpha. I do not regret it.At only 4 hours (at the time of this review), I can tell this game will hit 400 with me, no sweat. Gameplay is spectacular, and the use of lobby join codes is ingenious, where the game will recognize a lobby code that is copied to your clipboard.The game is very, VERY challenging, but never hopelessly difficult. Whenever you fail a level, there is always something you and your teammates can look at and say, "we can improve this". With each attempt, enough things stay the same that you can rely on & perfect your process with. Likewise, enough things change to keep you on your toes & require you to communicate with your team.WARNING: This game is BEST with a full team of 4 players. Luckily, the GTFO official discord allows for players to hook up quickly & easily. Also, the game has no gamma setting. I'm pretty sure this is intentional.OVERALL RATINGS:Core Gameplay: 5/5 (stealth & strategy & occasional gunplay and/or pants-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥)Content Variety: 4/5 (needs more equipment, progression. alpha makes this excusable to me)Replayability: 5/5 (I failed the same level 7 times in a row and still was ready to go again)Multiplayer Accessibility: 3/5 (Currently must have discord, but finding a team isn't hard)Multiplayer Community: 5/5 (Encountered no toxicity, most seem friendly & cooperative)Difficulty - Stealth: Medium, Easy to master, although failed silent kills can end your whole run.Difficulty - Combat: Hard, Combat is a last resort, and low reserves & long reloads can make it brutal.Difficulty - Strategy: Hard, Easy to learn, hard to master. This is where you will always want to improve.Difficulty - Level Progression: Very Hard, right now, completing even the first level (A1) will require a good crew and a perfect plan.FINAL RATING:10/10 I love it, and I want more of it. Absolutely worth the buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really does have a ton of potential. I can't tell you how much fun i had with my friends diving in when the game came out. However, after a little bit you really see how flawed the gameplay is. There really isn't much fun to sneaking when you have to stop every two seconds cuz the enemies start to alert. It doesn't help that, with a team of 4, you have so much risk to dying outright because of one mistake. The lack of resources is a problem, mostly the ammo. I do agree with the design philosophy that giving us too much ammo will take away from the point of the game. However, the game just isn't fun if you can't go loud when you inevitably make mistakes. Another thing i dislike is that the big beefy bois are notoriously hard to stealth kill and just as inconsistent. Some of them die in two fully charged hits when all four of us are attacking, and other times 4 fully charged hits barely even scratches them and then alerts the whole area. It's unfortunate that there's no risk/reward system with the tougher enemies. Screamers and Beefy bois are annoying to try and stealth kill and theres no benefit to trying to shoot them premptively because you'll likely die in the very likely event that the screamer summons a horde. Ultimately i like the game, but as it is I don't think it's particularly fun to play. I really am looking forward to the updates and I will certainly play every one that comes out.

"innovative gameplay".After that *yawning* experience Im rewarded with an apparel style that ads a red stripe to my clothes *yawn*.Most of the games from bigger studios during these times are so bad, that not having microtransactions, grindy mechanics (you own everything from the very beginning) unoptimized visuals put this game into a "very positive" state but the gameplay itself is mediocre at best, tedious at its worst.I may give this game a positive review if I really wanted to persuade my friends to play this with me, and i didn't want to look like a sucker for spending 30E on a horde shooter with 4 enemy types that all look like a raw chicken that ate a flashlight.TLDR: fun for the first couple hours with its Intriguing atmosphere of being a prisoner sent to industrial hell and plenty of cool guns to switch around, then it turns into a reptetive, tedious, yawning simulator

_childDocuments_.review: GTFO still feels like a "proof of concept." It's the bare-bones basics of a game idea that's got extra added in to feel like a fully realized game. Just enough to hide the loading screen, but not enough to hide the cracks of incomplete animations, placeholders, lacking the absolute basics for it's gameplay, and untested gameplay. (Which makes sense, it's been one patch since their release in 2019.)GTFO has some interesting concepts going for it. More-so that while inebriated, the game is legitimately scary. Though, when you have three other people talking about their kids and how much whiskey they've had, the “horror” aspect of the game is that much more difficult to put through, and getting most of the way through a level, only to due due to lack of resources... An hour and a half of struggling! Will not make for a good community once the matchmaking patch drops. Already, there are Steam Community Guides saying “Don't do X. It's completely useless. My Strat is the best!” Lone players will probably be in a similar situation they'd find themselves in PayDay 2. Kicked out of almost every lobby because they don't have the “Crossbow of anal pounding +7.”In terms of Graphics and Aesthetic, GTFO does a lot of things interestingly. Underground ruins look dark, and lack of light and overabundance of fog puts you in interesting scenarios where you can't see anything. This adds to the challenge, and when you have items to counteract it, such as the fog device, their short lifespan puts into question the best time to use them. A notable downfall in this stage is the lack of animations. There is no animation for a team-mate charging his melee weapon, and monsters will often jutter back and fourth. Are the hitboxes where they should be? I hope so, because I've only got three mags for a woefully ineffective submachine gun.Finally, this is something new. It's fresh. I can't recall another game where I have to input commands in a DOS prompt, and then relay that information back to my friends. A game where we have to prepare for a security scan, only to have all of our own plans ♥♥♥♥ on, because it took an unexpected turn. I like games that challenge you with on the fly thinking, games where we have to all sit down and plan something out. This really isn't your average CoD, where you can get high and still expect to come out on top. That being said, I haven't looked into their discord community. If you have friends who are all willing to eat the cost of a new, difficult Co-op game with a great atmosphere, it's a great buy. But if your friends get frustrated easily, don't have mics, don't know how to form a plan, or couldn't navigate through Half-Life's tutorial... You might find yourself stuck on the first level, hating it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of GTFO can be difficult to grasp. In order to fully understand the story, you have to find lore logs (collectibles) in the terminals throughout the missions, and read them, and pay close attention to when the characters in the game are talking. It takes place in an underground prison called The Complex. When your team is dropped into the Complex, you enter the Rundown (episode). A Rundown is a sequence of expeditions (missions/chapters) issued by the Warden, the unknown entity holding you captive. Survive all the expeditions to clear the Rundown. The environment in The Complex is mostly the same. A dark underground facility with a bit of variety from time to time. The variety of enemies is good enough. You and your team need to use different strategies and weapons depending on which type of enemies you're up against.GTFO is a very unique, strategic, co-op horror game like no other. It has up to 4 player co-op, and is a very difficult game, especially if you are not playing with a full group of people with voice chat. You cannot choose the difficulty level in GTFO. Instead, the expeditions are divided into different tiers, which is basically how difficult the missions are. These tiers go from A-E. For example if you take the second Rundown, the missions are as follows:R2A1R2B1, R2B2, R2B3, R2B4R2C1, R2C2R2D1, R2D2R2E1A rule of thumb is that the deeper you go in the Rundown the harder the mission, in this case R2E1 is the hardest. Another Rundown may look different. R1, R3 & R6 don't even have an E-tier mission, and it varies how many missions a Rundown has. It can be up to 4 missions of the same tier. There are a total of 8 Rundowns.It can be enough for one person in your team to make a mistake and the entire mission is lost, which can be both fun, exciting and frustrating, given that many missions are very long without checkpoints. You have to be careful with the ammo, and going in guns blazing is not always the best as it can have fatal outcomes. Practice, planning, coordination and stealth are key to beating the game. Even with very good planning, things can go south and you and your teammates' skills are put to the test. Always have a backup plan if something goes wrong! Simultaneous stealth kills with your group are a big part of the game if you're into that sort of thing.When it comes to weapons, there are many to choose from. Some weapons I loved, some weapons I loathed. Some weapons have insane recoil and are very difficult to handle because of this. But overall, most weapons are pleasant and fun to use. You can have one Main weapon, one Special Weapon, one Melee Weapon, and one Tool.There are 4 different Tools to choose from: Sentry Gun, C-Foam Launcher, Mine Deployer and Biotracker. On top of this, there are 4 different Sentry Guns to choose from: Burst Sentry, Shotgun Sentry, Hel Auto Sentry and Sniper Sentry. All have their pros and cons. C-Foam Launcher can be used to shoot foam on the ground, doors or on other places in the surroundings to slow down the enemies. With the Mine Deployer you can put trip mines on doors, the ground or on walls. Biotracker is a tracking device that you can use to scan rooms for sleeping enemies and also tag the enemies so they are easier to see if they wake up. Enemies that are awake and scanned get a red triangle above their head, and this triangle can be seen through walls.To gather boosters, the players need to pick up Artifacts, which are scattered throughout The Complex. Boosters provide bonuses to the player and last for the entirety of an expedition, usually at some cost or requirement. Boosters can be applied to the player in three different slots, Muted, Bold, and Aggressive — corresponding to the rarity of the artifacts. Some boosters can also have negative effects or certain conditions that have to be met for the booster to take effect.  A Muted booster can only be used once before it expires. A Bold booster has up to 2 uses. An Aggressive booster has up to 3 uses.Every time you complete a mission for the first time, you unlock cosmetics in the form of Helmets, Torsos, Legs, Backpacks and Palettes (Colors), to customize your character.I would have liked to see more detailed information for the weapons. For example, a gauge or numbers that show how much damage a weapon does, the size of the magazine, fire rate, reload speed, etc. The only thing that is displayed when you choose the weapon is, for example: High damage, Medium range, Hard to control, Fully automatic, Low ammo capacity, Overpenetrating rounds, etc. I want detailed stats of the weapons so that you can compare them easily, and see which weapon you should bring to a specific mission. I don't wanna have to google that...Something that is very strangely designed is that the host does less damage to bosses for some reason. Why? I have no idea.The list of collected Boosters could have been much better. It's a very confusing list of strange titles for the boosters. You have to click on the booster to see what effect it gives and the conditions that have to be met for the booster to take effect. You can't sort the list in any way either, instead it just expands with the last booster you unlocked, which ends up at the bottom of the list. An example of how a title, effect and conditions of what a Bold booster looks like, is this:Title: PROTEC+ - MEL-R RQ/72 (2 uses left)Effects: ↑Melee Resist. [+10%] ↑Projectile Resist. [12%]Conditions: Health > 50% (Subject must have 50% health or more for booster to be active)That title tells me nothing. Just confusing.The game also has some game-breaking bugs. These bugs do not occur often, and can be avoided by restarting the game every 3 hours or so. I've heard that memory leaks or something is the issue, but I don't know. The developers don't seem to want to patch it either.One bug is that when you shoot C-Foam with the C-Foam launcher on a door, the shots just go through the door and does not reinforce the door.Another random visual bug, is that a small part of your screen starts going black. It starts as a small black hole that just gets bigger every second until the whole screen is black. This goes away after a few minutes, but can really screw you and your team over if this happens to someone at the end of a long mission. You can still run around and shoot and such, but you can't see anything. This bug only happened to me twice in my 215 hours of playtime.The game also has some audio bugs where suddenly the sound of your own footsteps gets really loud and you hear less from the other in game sounds.There are some more bugs, but I'm not gonna list them.The game can be a bit confusing, and it can be difficult to figure out where to go and what to do sometimes, until you get the hang of it. This is a game that you really have to immerse yourself in, together with three other people, if you want to get really good. So if you are interested in doing that, and have three friends to try this game with, I highly recommend this game. Or join the GTFO discord to find players. I consider myself and my skill a bit above average when it comes to this game, and it took me 215 hours to beat every mission in the game and unlock all achievements, and I had a blast doing it! If you can look the other way when it comes to the game-breaking bugs (that rarely occur), then I highly recommend this game. Time to Get the ♥♥♥♥ Out!

_childDocuments_.review: The headline pretty much sums up the game. GTFO is an interesting attempt on stealth coop horror game and feels a lot like a mix inbetween PayDay, L4D2 and Dishonored.Right now what happens is you get to choose a loadout pick some friend and take the elevator down in a undeground complex and be greeted by horror itself. Only be told to get and collect something. So well me and my friends ended in dark rooms full of funghi zombies glowing and sleeping trying our best to get arround without unleashin chaos and dead. Guess what.We died.GTFO is in Early Access and is developed by a very small team. In a few days is an update which contains more content(new levels, equipment and perhaps enemies). So i need to take those infos into account. And i might be a little harsh.Right now GTFO leaves me with mixed feelings. Lets say mixed in a positive way. This game has a huge amount of potential. To way some good and bad things. While the level design and atmosphere is horrific and terrifying and absolutely suited for the game, its not very deep lore wise. You are a prisoner. Ok. You go down and get stuff. Ok. There are infected people sleeping and deadly. Ok. Good start for a setting. But why are we getting those thinks. What happened to the world. And what even is this place. I would say the world is beautiful from a curtain perspective make it feels alive.Another thing is to point out and that is some off a more serious issue i had is the way of the coop stealth gameplay.Basically what you are doing is gathering some infos of what is where and then move still and slow from room to room. If you find the dead you stand still while there a scanning and move while there sleeping. If you are close enough a deadly swing with a hammer makes the dead stay dead. Room clear next room repeat until you are forced to shoot or you finished the level. Some enemies require different tactics but the usual way there is to move around them and avoid them.Its kinda repetitive. You are always short on resources and the gunplay should be tweak a little bit. Since guns are not feeling powerful enough against the dead. And you are wasting way to much ammo to take down the threat. It is not a real option. At some points you are forced to use your tools and weapons to protect a point while breaching a door. That is cool. I like the fortification tools you got. But weapons in general are surrounded by a weak aura. But most importantly,never make a mistake. One mistake can easily cost you the game. You find yourself in a bad spot most of the time and if you or a friend triggers an enemy the whole floor is about to lit the party up. Recovering from that is almost impossible. Twice the mistake is double the trouble and the end of what life the prisoners had left to live.I am curious for matchmaking and i think this game needs a lot more consistent feedback in order to grow into the right direction. Right now i can be frustrating at times of failure and if you are able to complete a mission there is no reward only do that again and get more stuff.Right now i only recommend it for player groups of at least 3 people. Solo is pain in the butt. As a duo you can handle it but one strike and you are out. Be aware of the price. For some it might not reflect what the game should offer. But as much i can tell right. I await what will happen next. I wanna see this game grow bigger and be successful. The potential is real and the devs seems to have a vision about what to come next. Join on your own risk and be a part of it. Only restriction. You must own brown pants.

They also added checkpoint doors, which some people might hate, but hey, if you're skilling through maps with no issues anyways, there should be no problem with adding in a potential time saver to people who are less good at the rundown.Games are meant to be fun, and for people who aren't good at them or don't have people to play with, the checkpoints are a good accessibility option.With that out of the way, the game is still a great stealth-horror game and is still pretty difficult if you don't prepare before a horde. The bots are great for me personally because I hate playing with randoms, and not many of my friends are willing to play a map of it. Although, the bots are about as smart as an old shoe and will often get themselves stuck behind a door that you just closed, but hey, at least they can take and use (on your command) their equipment.The audio still freezes sometimes, and the outdoor zone lags on higher settings, but other than that, it runs pretty smoothly. Sound design is still great, letting you know exactly where an enemy is just by sound alone.If you plan on buying this game for solo play, wait for a sale. If you're planning on playing with friends, obviously still wait for a sale, but it's still worth it. it's great when you can blame someone for missing a melee attack instead of blaming your own incompetent self!

_childDocuments_.review: Once a manager asked me what I disliked about my job.  I told him the work had become increasingly tedious.  He attempted to "culturally manage" away my objection with "I understand that work is difficult at times but..." I interrupted him.  "No," I said. "I didn't say work is difficult, I said it was tedious."  He asked me to explain.Say you walked into a conference room with an open 40lb box of loose staples and flung the box end over end at the wall, staples everywhere.  Difficult would be: you tell me to clean that up but you don't care how. So maybe I would drag a big magnet across the carpet to collect them, maybe get a stiff bristled push broom to push them out of the carpet, maybe rip up the carpet and roll it up. The task would be difficult, but I could find multiple solutions and the solution would be its own reward.  Tedious is, you hand me a pair of company approved tweezers and tell me I have to pick them up one by one per established company procedure.GTFO at times feels too much like tedium and not enough like difficulty.  Sleepers, follow the procedure, use the hammer one at a time, wait for it, wait for it.... Find the mcguffin, follow the procedure and use the terminals, list, ping, list ping.  How will you get there? Procedure, find the doors that are passable and use them.  Door alarmed? Follow procedure and follow the line on the floor as proscribed. Gun fight? Follow the procedure, use the long range weapon for long range, the medium ranged weapon for medium range, the short ranged weapon for short range, but never the long for short or the short for long or the medium for short or the medium for long because this violates the established procedure and so you will be harshly and arbitrarily punished with inaccuracy and reduced damage at ranges not significant enough to warrant variation.Gameplay in GTFO doesn't challenge the player to be imaginative, to problem solve, to be rewarded for the solutions they devise. Instead it forces the player to learn the "policy" dictated by game mechanics and adhere to them, and that isn't difficulty, it is tedium.   So grab your tweezers--I mean hammers--and creep along picking up those staples. But don't deviate or Human Resources is going to punish you because you’re not doing it right.Hopefully this changes because there is amazing potential working for the warden.

_childDocuments_.review:
GTFO is a 4 player action/horror cooperative first-person shooter for hardcore gamers looking for a real challenge. Players get to play as a team of prisoners, forced to explore and extract valuable artifacts from a vast underground complex that has been overrun by terrifying creatures. Gather weapons, tools, and resources to help you survive - and work to unearth the answers about your past and how to escape.

KEY FEATURES

* 4 player cooperative PvE gameplay that puts you and your teammates through the ultimate cooperation and communication test.
* Explore a massive underground complex with a dense and dark atmosphere.
* Plan your expedition, equip and operate tools, combine your firepower, communicate and coordinate as a team - every detail counts if you are to survive the nightmare.
* Search the complex for information and resources to help you and your team solve your objectives and come back alive.
* The Rundown: New expeditions released regularly that always replaces the old expeditions. Our goal is to invent new ways of challenging you and your teammates in new and interesting ways.
* Nightmarish atmosphere accompanied by music from acclaimed composer Simon Viklund.

name: Martha Is Dead
detailed_description: WISHLIST MEOW! 😻 Accolades About the Game Martha Is Dead is a dark first-person psychological thriller, set in 1944 Italy, that blurs the lines between reality, superstition and the tragedy of war. As conflict intensifies between German and Allied forces, the desecrated body of a woman is found drowned… Martha! Martha is dead, and her twin sister Giulia, the young daughter of a German soldier, must alone deal with the acute trauma of loss and the fallout from her murder. The hunt for the truth is shrouded by mysterious folklore and the extreme horror of war that draws ever closer. What will prevail? FEATURES Unashamedly authentic voice acting in Italian The first Indie game to launch using the native Italian language as the default setting – for full immersion into the story and the characters. From the creator of The Town of Light The second game from LKA, the award-winning developer of “The Town of Light” and specialists in reality-based narrative games focused on tough subjects. Deep and dark multi-layered narrative Martha Is Dead is an exploration of loss, relationships, and the psychological undertones of a dark period of history through the eyes of a young woman who seeks the truth, but who also has secrets of her own to hide. Explore a detailed recreation of the Italian countryside Freely explore the breathtakingly realised Tuscany countryside on foot, by boat, or by bike. Grounded in reality, Martha Is Dead’s setting and historical context are inspired by real facts and places that have been faithfully reconstructed in true LKA fashion. Play with dolls Play with numerous marionette sequences in the puppet theatre to remember repressed memories. Mixing folklore with superstition Unlock symbols and use tarot cards to unveil new aspects of the game and summon the spirit of The Lady. A backdrop of War Collect newspapers, and telegrams and listen to the radio to keep updated on what is occurring in the world during the war. Virtual photographic greatness Take pictures for the sheer pleasure of doing so, and also to progress through the story and discover more about the game world. A simulator will guide you through 1940s photography, where you’ll be able to develop your actual photos through a fully working in-game darkroom! Authentic Italian music of the era Immerse yourself in a deeply evocative and atmospheric soundtrack containing underwater music specialists Between Music and their Aquasonic project; The Town of Light composer Aseptic Void and his moody yet spinetingling tones; and held together in true vintage style featuring reimagined versions of classic tracks including Schubert's Ave Maria, O Bella Ciao, with original tracks written and sung by Francesca Messina, AKA 90s disco star, Femina Ridens.

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving a recommendation to play it as a HORROR GAME ONLY, but with the following warnings:1. This game begins with a crisis information website. There's a reason for it. Trust me on this. 2. The game is filled with triggering images and disturbing scenes/themes/topics. It covers everything from homicide to war crimes to miscarriage to animal abuse to child abuse to suicide. If you are a survivor of any of those types of severe traumas or may still have PTSD from combat or abuse, I would highly suggest you consider finding a game that isn't this one. It's likely to bring up some very negative memories and feelings that could re-traumatize you. Better to be safe than sorry. Lots of games out there are horror that don't go this deeply into extremely disturbing topics like these, especially in the detail you'll experience them if you play this game. It is TRIGGERING to an extreme. Just a warning on that.3. There's a LOT of Nazi imagery in the game. This could be upsetting for some people. 4. I work for a suicide/crisis hotline. This game was mentioned to me because of its triggering nature. I played it mainly to see what it was about. As a person who works in the field of mental health, I am very cognizant that a game of this type, portraying these types of images, and immersing the player in a lot of horrible situations...may be extremely difficult for many people. If you are suffering from any severe mental health disorder, especially depression or anxiety, I would suggest again that you consider playing something different. This game would likely make you feel worse. You don't need that.And if you play this game and feel like you're having a hard time coping with the game or its topics, please stop playing it. If it is damaging to you (and you should know what that feels like) or puts you in a sense of mental health crisis, PLEASE turn the game OFF, uninstall it, and then...reach out to a friend, a loved one, your doctor, your therapist, etc. You can also contact one of the many crisis/suicide hotlines available worldwide. Some even allow you only to talk via text.So, if you are inured to violence and none of the topics I mentioned above are something you have personally dealt with (or have been traumatized by in your past), the game itself is beautiful, mesmerizing in many ways, and the story is very engaging (almost too much so). The soundtrack is really great, too.  With all this said, on the basis of it being a HORROR GAME ONLY with its strong story, great soundtrack and gorgeous visuals, I can recommend it. However, PLAYER BE WARNED....that's all I have left to say about it.

_childDocuments_.review: 1944. Italy is ravaged by the misery of war, with Allied forces moving up towards the Tuscany region while Axis troops mount a desperate defense. Protagonist Giulia K. is the daughter of a high-profile Nazi officer, but even this privileged position doesn’t save her from tragedy. One day, her twin sister Martha is found dead in a lake - an overwhelming loss. She always was her parents’ favorite, unlike Giulia, so the latter decides to take her identity, pretending to be her from that moment forward, to gain the love so far denied to her.MiD mostly takes place in and around a countryside villa outside the village of San Casciano, Tuscany. There’s a remarkable attention to detail in the realization of each location, from the interiors of a typical upper-class 1940 Italian household, with luxuries such as electric power and a phone line, to the verdant woods and sun-beaten dirt paths commonly seen in the rural areas of the region even today. The marked contrast between these idyllic landscapes and the brutality of war, or the horrifying visions in Giulia’s mind, creates a rollercoaster of varied atmospheres that works out very well.Apart from the protagonist, there’s a small roster of relevant characters that, however, never happen to dialogue directly with you at any point: a consequence of the recent events, and of the pretense Giulia decided to put up. You’ll hear conversations, read missives, listen to telephone calls, but never engage in active dialogues save for some phone calls at specific points. The writing feels plausible, with an Italian voiceover that accounts for the different mannerisms and speech patterns of the time. Most situations feel plausible and realistic, even if (probably by design) you’ll end up questioning the veracity of some of them as the game progresses. The story plays out through a number of days, each having a primary objective related to the events at hand, and a series of optional activities as well. Generally, you’ll be able to explore the world freely at any time, with the primary areas being the villa and its courtyard, the nearby forest and the lake. Some places will be locked until specific events happen, or certain quests are triggered by your findings. Your trusty camera will be of paramount importance, as it will not only allow you to collect evidence in order to shed light on your sister’s death, but also to use filters (such as infrared) to reveal the unseen. There are a vast number of interactable objects that reveal more about the family’s past, the general lore or the people related to you in some way, each of them is voice-narrated by Giulia. Those looking to do everything will find much information in these optional interactions, they’re definitely worth the extra time spent.While your focus remains finding the truth about Martha’s death, there will be other things to do as well. For instance, hidden riddles can be found by photographing specific objects in the world, optional points of interest that reveal dark stories, or trigger quests altogether. These missions may be optional, but contain a good chunk of unique content, such as puzzles, minigames and sub-storylines regarding parallel ongoing events. Some of these elements also can be missed, since the game progresses in a series of days alongside the main quest’s evolution: after certain events unfold, some areas may not be accessible anymore, thus locking the quests out forever (unless you reload an earlier save). Going just for the main story is something I wouldn’t recommend, as these secondary missions, even if a tad annoying in pacing at times, prove overall interesting and expand on the narrative considerablyThe most frequent type of puzzle will be associated with photography: relevant items to frame, both primary and secondary, will be highlighted on your HUD, and it will be up to you to use the right camera accessories, such as filters, and set the right zoom level, exposure and focus to get the perfect shot. Not only that, but photos also need to be developed in a dark room, which involves a simple button-pressing prompt as QTE. Other than that, you’ll eventually be decoding telegraph ciphers, finding items such as keys to unlock doors, boxes and passages containing critical items, or figure out the right things to say in a phone call to extract information. There are also a few quick-time events here and there, but they’re fairly simple and not demanding in skill or reflexes at all, in line with the genre’s expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all,Those that are saying the game is "unplayable" are false. My computer is nothing special and it ran the game on high settings with 0 issues. I don't really know what to say after completing this game - I've never played anything remotely close to this in terms of realism, graphics & just down right disturbing. This game is not "scary" its a true psychological horror game, it will make you do things you truly don't want to do or experience, if you don't have a strong mindset i would recommend that you don't bother playing this... it will truly push you to your mental limits & there are things you will see / do that can actually haunt you for some time. Its also extremely sad... it will open your eyes a lot in the matter of mental illness & mental health.In conclusion this game is one of a kind, but it's honestly not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? After a brief flashback from your childhood (1929), a 15 year time jump without any remembrance of the time between, the game begins in mid-1944 and you find your (deaf) twin sister Martha floating dead in a lake. Was she killed? Why is she wearing your clothes? Why can't you remember anything? After pulling her out, your parents think you are Martha, and so you switch identities. For reasons only known to yourself, you do not tell anybody that you are Martha's sister, Guliana. While your father always loved you (Guliana), your mother loved Martha, but not you. The game takes place in Tuscany, a region in Central Italy around the beautiful town of Florence. Your mother is Italian, but your father is a General in the German army. Quite an interesting (and strange) setting, for a supernatural horror game. Or is it a thriller? Or just an adventure?The controls work a bit like in Heavy Rain or the newer Vertigo. Press a mouse button and move the mouse in a direction to start actions. The game plays in first person perspective and makes heavy use of head bobbing and focusing/defocusing  to create suspense. In my case this mostly creates nausea and hurting eyes. Items in your inventory are used automatically (at the right spot). You carry a camera around with you and have to take pictures at certain spots. I hope you understand a bit of photography (in the pre-mobile phone days), because the game expets you to control aperture, exposure, focus, use different lenses, filters, films, flashes and whatever on your camera. After taking pictues, you have to go in the darkroom to develop them. At least this process has been considerably simplified compared to real life developement. I mean, I am playing a psychological horror game, and I am not taking a historical photographer course. Most of the game consists of walking around and examining your sourroundings, using items at the right spot. There are also some action sequences, when you fail one, you start again at the beginning - until you pass it. Or quit. The game is saved automatically at certain checkpoints, or you can save manually. You can always access a map, your objectives, an album of the photos you made or a log of the text read so far. Using a controller is possible. The story is told by a (rather good) narrartor. The graphics are close to photorealistic. And the environement is detailled. Really detailled, I have never seen such a realistic environment in a game. They stutter a bit on my PC (GTX 1070) when I move too fast, though. The houses and everything really look (and sound) like in real life, not something that has been made just for a game. Not even the visuals in "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter" came close to that. Really nice. At least the visuals are certainly a masterpiece.Graphically superior psychological thriller taking place in rural war-torn Central Italy of 1944.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, this game is awesome. In practice, it falls short in almost every department. Before you call me a 'hater' please understand I spend my own cash playing this type of game to then list them as part of the only '' fan club i know of on Steam. So I have a lot of experience with these games: what makes a good experience or a bad one. This one has been terribly mediocre. I rarely complain about performance because I have a great rig and i regularly repaste it. But here, The graphics are good  without being great , yet they come at the price of strange, unwarranted performance cost (something the the developers are aware of). On a machine that can play CP77 at 70 FPS on ultra with DLSS set to 'quality @5k in SUW mode of all things, here I'm struggling to get 20fps in 'high performance' while locked at 1440p (so SUW option). I even had to drop the quality setting to 'high' to make the game playable. Objects pop into view (a clear sign of VRAM swapping despite having a card with 8GB of GDDR6 and 64 gig of RAM matched to a socketed i9900k). This is not acceptable. And the framerate drops constantly even if you drop the graphics to medium, meaning the problem is not rendering but elsewhere.I can't even imagine what the people who usually complain about framerate will say about this one! In addition, there are numerous crashes, geometry locks, and other annoyances that will force you to reload. So save often, no quick save is available however.None of this would really matter if the story was captivating - but it's just an awfully complicated, strange mess that initially give you the illusion of an open world only to place you on rails and never letting you go . At some point, you're given a chance to dial phone numbers. That opportunity is taken away from you and never given back if you 'trigger' an even by 'walking' in the 'wrong' place. Likewise, the game give you this amazing camera with TONS of options. They get used twice in the game, and the myriad of options are just an in-game toy to take neat screenshots. How disappointing. Imagine someone telling you 'hey i have this special filter that can see... ghosts' so you go around and take pictures of all the graves and nothing happens. But walk on the right 'trigger' and suddenly the same graves that didn't give out ghostly pictures will suddenly do so. Everything is on rails.Everything is scripted, and badly so. There are weird running labyrinth were you have to proceed by trial and error. There are underwater scenes where you can't go to the surface because it's a hidden boundary but you could in the previous scene. There are elements that are extremely hard to locate and I overall I felt I spent more time working around all this than actually playing a game.I would only recommend this game sub $10 AFTER they fix all the patches. It's short, it's clunky, and quite frankly we have so many alternatives in the walking simulator genre today, we have the right to demand the best. Look at Observer: System Redux if you don't believe me. Look at games like the Stanley Parable ultra deluxe. Heck - even the aged "Ethan Carter" still feel more modern than this.I feel about about giving the game a thumb down because some elements are really well done and conceptually, the idea was neat. But numerous technical issues, a lack of flexibility forcing people to reload old save to complete 'side missions' and a general feeling that the game is not finished stop me from recommending this title. Better luck next time.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, DO NOT play this game if you are squeamish to gore or sensitive to topics such as abuse, self-harm, and the like. Martha is Dead has multiple trigger warnings, some people chose to ignore those warnings and then had the audacity to complain when they witness something graphic. It’s laughable but I digress…Martha is Dead tells the story of…well, how Martha died. Going any deeper than that will probably spoil but I can definitely vouch for this game's story. It takes place in 1944 Italy and it’s not just about a young girl's internal struggle. It also portrays the tragedy involving World War ll and how people were affected by it. It’s like a historical-psychological-thriller mixed genre and I am all for that.  Gameplay mostly involves walking, biking, taking photographs, and developing those photos in the darkroom. There are different dialogue choices you make and you can explore the semi-open world, which is gorgeous by the way. The performance was not that great. There were a bunch of bugs and the stuttering was so bad I had to wait a couple of weeks for the game to be patched by the devs and they did. It now runs much smoother compared to its first week of release. They were on top of it, listening to everyone's requests/issues, and now the game is playable with some minor issues I’m sure they’ll fix with some future patches. This game is not for everyone. There are some scenes where even I, a horror lover, was shocked to see but no way would I wish for it to be censored (like it was on ps). The devs were kind enough to give people who bought it on ps steam keys if they didn't want to play the censored version of the game. I applaud them for doing that and for not playing it safe by sugar coating how brutal the war and people's ideologies were like back then.

_childDocuments_.review: is a psychological horror game heavily driven by its story. LKA Studio is tackling mental health issues and disorders and is doing it so brilliantly. The game takes place in Italy near the end of World War II. You will play Giulia K, the daughter of Nazi General Erich K, and while on a routine walk near the lake you find the floating body of your dead twin sister and embark on a journey to make sense of it and explain her death.We should start this review by saying that I would not recommend this game for whoever doesn’t like the sight of more graphic content, some scenes are disturbing, shocking, and not something you will typically see anywhere. With some pretty heavy trigger warning sounds, you will know when something is about to happen. With that in mind, Martha is Dead will not leave you indifferent on that aspect for better or for worse while exploring the world through Giulia’s perspective and her camera lenses.This was a truly horrifying experience, in the good sense of the term, without much context and not knowing the extent of what I was getting into, I expected ghosts, terror, jump scare, even zombies at some point. Instead, I got to go through this adventure with my imagination as my worse enemy. Not knowing what was going to happen, even trying to stop my character to do things at times but just being powerless and watching as everything unfolds.Throughout our investigation, Martha is Dead feels like an adventure-walking simulator with impeccable graphics, design, atmosphere, and an amazing system to immerse ourselves into it. Some sort of open-world is offered to us in the confine of our map, to find more elements of the story, more context, and details to read, analyze, think about to piece it all together. On top of that, we are free to take pictures with our camera as we please and go and develop them in the black room. This feature was really enjoyable with tons of different variations, lenses, and extra components added to the camera as we progress through the story. Photography is the hobby/passion of Giulia, an extensive amount of work was put into making it a core element of gameplay. Furthermore, the game is graphically stunning and will leave you in awe with the level of details. It contributes to a lot of the immersion and when most of your job is to take pictures, having some sense of artistic freedom and realism just seems natural. I was not expecting such high-quality work done on that front. The story is extremely well-written, the plot gets only better with time and some choices will have to be made during the journey. Whether it is through discussing with other characters of impact or for deciding your future actions on your own. It is unclear whether these have any impact on the story but it added some extra content to a game that can feel somewhat short to play without it.The ambiance is really well made and the exploration is rewarded, from the music, radio, pictures, paintings, everything has their own part to play in the world of Giulia and every room, corridor, and conversation mean something.The voice acting was really well-made, but only in Italian. It was pretty mediocre in English, the translations were accurate enough but had some mistakes, do yourself a favor and play the game in Italian with English subtitles, you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a truly fantastic looking game with some great multilingual audio and an intriguing story to boot.While not extremely heavy on the scares, the game does a great job at building atmosphere and dread as the story progresses. Set against the harrowing backdrop of WW2, you'll play as Giulia, adopting your dead sister's identity after a misunderstanding. From there, Giulia will begin living a lie as she tries to discover who (or what) killed her sister. There will be many opportunities for you take different paths and make different choices. Some are meaningless, but others might have dire consequences. For a couple of examples - now that you're Martha, will you wear her clothes or you own? If you find secret information, will you keep it to yourself or tell the authorities?If you're a fan of vintage photography, this game will certainly scratch that itch, allowing you access to many accessories, lenses and a full-fledged dark room for you to use. Taking photos is an integral part of the game so you'll want to keep an eye out for little camera icons along your journey. It's an in-depth and intricate part of the game which I enjoyed using.This version is the uncensored one, so it does include some rather gruesome and unsettling scenes, so you have been warned.The game will likely last you at least around 4-5 hours. If you decide to investigate everything and try different paths, then I wouldn't be surprised if that number nears 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Martha Is Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a really long time to play this.  I am one of the patient (cheap) gamer crew, so I waited for an eternity for this to go on sale.  I’m glad I did because its pretty pricey for what it is.  It still gets the thumbs up though because it is a pretty good slow burn horror game that has virtually no jump scares and relies more on narrative and a visceral feeling of being in the shoes of the character to make you feel uneasy. I am glad I finally got to play this.  I think it is too much of an asking price and definitely recommend on a sale.  If you are in the mood for a dark walking sim with some puzzles then its pretty good.  As I mentioned before, there are horror elements to the game but it doesn’t have a single jumpscare.  It is creepy because it immerses you in the life of the protagonist and it does a good job of keeping you engaged in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is without doubt something that doesn't pop out from every corner - and for a reason because it is one of if not even the most terrifying psychologically challenging game I've played. Through the game the player is pushed to situations and visions that no sane person would like to watch too long. I mean that there is more than a handful of something caught from the worst nightmares and I'm not only talking about how gruesome they are but they stimulate almost too well of human mind which can snap in the wrong position in the most fatal way. Martha is Dead is the most miserable tale of how monstrous one can become if the current environment and the past direct so.The game takes place in the small villa in Italy's countryside near the end of WW2 where Allies are pushing forth and the country is more or a less in chaos reigned by National Socialists' Germany. Without spoiling too much of the remarkable story I cover the beginning where Guilia find's her twin sister Martha's corpse in the lake and as terrified she is she is also righteous and wants to find out who killed her twin. Nevertheless through fast twists and turns she also becomes anxious and haunted by the happened events and constantly falls deeper and deeper into state where both player and Guilia question what is actually true and what is not.Thus it is enough to say that the game is story rich and so rich that the layers within form a stack so huge that it is actually meant impossible to make any proper conclusions for protagonist's morals, fate, visions and past are left open. When I completed the game I watched a couple of analysis and I found out that there might be as many theories that there are players. But that much I know that the feelings I had changed from pure pity to utter rage towards the main character - there was a tiny moment I felt that I had to actually close the game, maybe uninstall it for I barely could watch this circus any longer.Martha is Dead isn't just psychological creep show though because there is some simple, but entertaining learning matter as well. The biggest feature is gorgeous WW2 era camera, which player uses to proceed in their objects but can use it freely to take pictures whenever and wherever they like and these pictures are developed in old fashioned way in a darkroom with thin red light and devices. The procedure is documented in detail from the beginning to the end also underlining the parts where it would take longer in real life. The telegraph is another thing which is used few times and I definitely know better now how to write Morse code if I ever need to. There is also lot of walking in the small but nice looking area and sometimes the game can feel rather a walking sim than a psycological horror/thriller, which it is but the more peaceful parts work as a good variation at least.  The icing on the cake is default Italian voice-overs and I do recommend to play it with those and English subtitles to fill the immersion. English voice-over is available option though.Even when I had played LKA's previous game 'The Town of Light', other controversial game still giving me creeps, Martha is Dead delivered something unforgettable. The most hawk eyed players have even seen some connections between the games. However, I hold no shame of playing this although  I would never recommend this to everyone because Martha is Dead is not for everyone. Period. It is an honest, uncensored and merciless ride into twisted and despaired human mind and I can't judge who is going to 'like' it or not, but for me it was dancing in the nonexistent line of sick taste, art and documentary finally making it over the finish line.If you should start this game, be honest with yourself and listen to your feelings. If any worse vibes emerges take care of yourself, refund the game and hug some of your loved ones.

_childDocuments_.review: "Martha Is Dead" is a psychological thriller set in 1944 Italy amidst the Second World War.Not really a jump-scare game, it is rather a look into the darkness of a troubled mind using horror and macabre, unsettling imagery.The story is very well written and the plot intelligently developed.  It has the feel of a "who-dunnit?" novel.I decided to play the game using the Italian voice acting (with English subtitles), which for me enhanced the experience from a historical location point of view.FPS drops in a few areas forced me to lower the graphics settings, because it resulted in your character being instantly turned around, going back the way you came from instead of continuing on to your goal.Overall, the game was well worth experiencing.
