_childDocuments_.review: I really did a step out of my comfort zone with this game but it was nothing but worth it. The last week I was on vacation leave from work. I wanted to play a story game to have something to do my initial plan was to replay one of my favourite games in Witcher 3. While traveling through the world I intended to watch my favourite German Youtuber, Gronkh, again like in the good old days. When I stumbled over his playthrough of Martha is Dead I remembered hearing quite a lot about this little game. After 5 minutes of gameplay plus looking at the store page, I decided to play it myself. Coming into the game I didn’t know what to expect. I hoped it to be atmospheric but not so scary that I would ♥♥♥♥ my pants (I am very easy to scare…) and holy hell it was atmospheric. The game came out in a time where we have a new war on the European continent so everything was to be handled with care, this in combination with the game talking about topics in a way a triple A production would never dare to was a supreme combination. The trigger-warning at the beginning and in the middle of the game made the promise for this game to be graphic and so it was. However, this was nothing short of a brilliant way of supporting the story. In general, the game design was brilliant, between beautiful landscapes a scary but also awesome forest and the beautiful yet scary mansion and the morgue in a very sharp graphic the game also offered something more cartoonish which did still not break the dark atmosphere. They really found a perfect balance. I believe for everyone who usually plays horror games this will be nothing… but the game never wanted to be a horror game it wants you to feel unpleasant and this it achieved it for me in nearly all situations of the playthrough. This is also accomplished by the brilliant use of music, not good music in particular, though the game offers some good tracks via radios which are always turned on within the main area of the game those are nothing more than some background noises. I am referring to the music and sounds used when we get to the scarier parts of the game. For example, the use of only a very wrong and shrill played violine while doing something ethically not right did have me shivering. The sounds of the world in general are well done and good used. Well placed wild life noises could make you turn around one more time than you would like because you feel unpleasant. Gameplay wise this game has more to offer than I would have thought going into this adventure. Generally speaking, I like those so called walking simulators but this game had some fresh takes I rarely saw within other games. If it is to develop photos with the description how it would have been done historical speaking or the use of a morse code. Taking photos never was something annoying to me. The game offers a docent of different lenses and other shenanigans to use which gives you a nearly unlimited amount of possibilities and simulates the art of taking pictures back in the 1940s quite well. Story, wise I don’t want to say much, but the story is very winding and makes many turns. As the daughter of a top German General in 1944s Italy, close to the ever more progressing Allies we see the world through the eyes of someone who neither has much to do with the war nor understand it. However as always, we are forced to make decisions based on our hearts. However, this is not our most important task, because we try to solve the murder of our twin sister. We have to deal with beings whose existence we can't understand, and we have to process the new information we receive, while someone seems to be trying to kill us. Everything is under the question Martha or Giulia or is there another possibility?This game did catapult itself into one of my all-time favourites almost immediately. LKA wrote a great story with well thought out characters, side quest, one of the best atmospheres I ever experienced, a great plot and good-looking game, which at the same time doesn’t lose out on the gameplay side of things. The formula to go for such open and no taboo approach, by LKA and Wired production, is brave to say the least, but it was worth a 100%.The game wants you to think about your actions and sayings. Everything you say might have more effect on a person than you could imagine. It is very deep in telling you to watch more for your doings. I want to close this review with what I take away from this piece of art of a game. My learnings are to watch more on my behaviour and not put people into boxes and come to conclusions to fast. Not every one is in a healthy state of mind or feeling as good as I am. Some people have to deal with ♥♥♥♥ far greater than you could ever imagine. It is nothing short of unimaginable what the human brain can do to shield one from what it believes to be dangerous. This can come in an unthinkable amount of different signs and symptoms we might never be able to understand the full function and capacity of the human anatomy. Thus, all I want to say is that “We are nothing but a puppet of our mind” Thank you and if you need help, please reach out for it. You are never alone.~sincerely SVPPweeB

_childDocuments_.review: DISTURBING BUT ERRATIC JOURNEYIf you want to play "Martha is dead", don't expect a horror game, it's a mixture of different simulators with a creepy premise. Despite being a bigger game than their previous "The town of light", "Martha" shouldn't cost 30 euros, because as an experience it cannot rival other AA games."Martha is dead" includes: - Countryside simulator: ✓- Walking and running simulator: ✓- Photography simulator: ✓- Puppeteer simulator: ✓- Tarot reader simulator: ✓- Telegraph simulator: ✓- Bicycle and boat simulators: ✓Apart from that, I would urge the devs to eliminate all "running scared" scenes (especially the ones with words in them) cause they don't add anything at all to an otherwise serious, deeply disturbing tale. Get rid of these fake Alan Wake sentences, and the silly Lady in the lake scares, cause the core of the plot is much more important and disturbing than any horror nonsense. Devs could have created a really memorable mixture of WWII and psychological insanity by relying on the strong aspects of their plot: child abuse, insanity, violence, war, vengeance. Instead, they wanted to explain many films at once:- A half-arsed war story- A half-arsed family drama- A half-arsed ghost story- A half-arsed tarot reader story- A half-arsed love story- A half-arsed asylum storyIt's way too much. By the end, none of the simulators nor none of the stories seems developed enough to leave a lasting impression. On the bright side, each and every one of these ideas, stories and simulators is really interesting and fun, but together they don't make much sense. I would love for the devs to develop in depth seven different stories and games instead of this convoluted mess..As it stands, "Martha is dead" doesn't make much sense and doesn't scare much, in spite of all the gorey scenes that, to be honest, never stroke me as crucial to the plot. I'll play more games by you, LKA. But you can still fix this one! It shows so much promise and it crumbles under the weight of its own ambition! Don't add so much, but instead develop and explore the possibilities of one idea. Explore layers of one idea, go deep into the madness, just like Bloober Team and Frictional Games and Red Barrels and Red Candle do. I know that you can do it cause you've got the vision, the talent and the knowledge.

_childDocuments_.review: My main complaint is the game-play. It has no real choices and it doesn't make you feel immersed until the end. Someone else in the reviews put it perfectly as a "Walking Simulator". Being a semi choose-your-own-adventure is misleading; most of the time it feels like you're just in the backseat rather than making choices as the character Martha.I Also couldn't tell if the intentional language setting was to be Italian or English. Both didn't sync to the characters models, and never pulled the weight of what exactly they are saying. Martha at moments has some dead-pan, emotionless voice acting. And some of Martha's dialogue could've been cut as well, with it being the trope of "Telling the audience instead of showing it" most of the time. Most of all this game feels like something you should watch a Youtuber or Streamer to react to. The empty game-play gives me the impression that it was ment to be commented over; for a Streamer and their audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Updated: March 4, 2022Do I recommend this game? Short answer: Is this game for everyone? No.  ...but if you want a reality-slap about your mental health, go play it.If you are like me, who has been searching for a good game with dark/heavy themes... this game is for you. In its core, Martha is dead delivers an authentic experience. The ambiance and the music perfectly encompass each scene.  The voice acting is splendid! But the way they frame the main character is hauntingly realistic. She's perfect. The devs have been working hard to push updates and fixes the past week. _childDocuments_.review: I just completed Martha Is Dead today, after less than 6 hours of gameplay. I took my sweet time exploring most options (finished 79% though). Overall, it was a disturbing visual novel with very few actual mechanics to make it feel like a video game. That's fine, but for $30 I expected a bit more enjoyment. And once you've completed the story, there's no real reason to delve back in...unless you're a completionist (which I'm not). If you have a weak stomach or get triggered easily by extreme violence and self-harm, steer clear. If you're a horror fan who likes this subgenre, and you can snag it at a deep discount, it's worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: (Steam says I have 50+ hours in the game.  This is incorrect.  The game apparently failed to exit properly more than once.)I really wanted to like this game.  I love story games, I'm okay with minimalist game play while being led through a story with no branching.  I'm good with an unreliable narrator.  But Martha is Dead really just falls flat.  The attempts to add game-play elements makes the game frustrating (the telegraph made me want to scream, being forced to do click-drag type actions to mutilate a dead body more than once instead of just watching a cut-scene).  There are too many points where trying to figure out where to go and what to do made me bored with the game. I got stuck on a telephone pole, unable to get down, unable to figure out why, until I happened to _look in the right direction_ at something completely unrelated to my reason for being on the pole.  If you delay certain actions, you get locked out of completing them by story events.  The puppet show was torture... again, making you click and drag and push your way through multiple cut-scenes.  It would have been _less_ tedious if it hadn't been interactive.The sets are well-developed, with a large amount of detail.  The English voice acting is great.  The main character has a beautiful voice and listening to her for hours is easy.  And the story started out as very engaging... but then it all fell apart and it lost my interest, and the ending told me there was no point to trying to figure out what happened, as it was all meaningless.And despite all the poor game-play, that wasn't what ultimately put me off.  The story itself was confused and confusing, and in the end, I disconnected from the main character and _stopped caring_ about her because the unreliable narrator had become so unreliable I wasn't sure about any of the events that had been portrayed, and I just wanted to get the game over with because I hate not finishing a game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was not easy for me to make a decision on how to rate the game and what to write about it (and I've been sitting here for quite a long time, changing parts of the text again and again, rereading it and changing it again and so on. ..).- I really wanted to play the game and my decision to give a thumbs up is based on the fact that I found the game to be quite good despite the later following things. - For someone unfamiliar with the genre or these types of games, the ~$30 could well be a waste of money, so I'd have to give it a thumbs down.- For a concrete recommendation, I would actually prefer a neutral rating, because in my opinion it really depends, for example, on whether you because you could say that the game is more like an interactive audio book novel that comes with lots of text and voice-over. I didn't buy the game on Steam and the $10 i have paid, I think it's still ok. Anyone who knows such or similar games can roughly guess what to expect. As for the differing opinions on playability, it seems that the game actually performs better at some setups and worse on others.  In this context, I cannot say whether it is due to the hardware used, the game settings or what else is done on the side. I also had stutters and frame drops during the game, but I have to say that I played the game in windowed mode due to the situation and used a lot of ALT+TAB, which this game doesn't like at all. Maybe it's due to bad or missing optimization, I don't know.As the brief description on the store page says, the game is a ““, and it is. .  The horror in this game only relates to the "coming" war. But nothing more.If you decide to play the game, , but also bring a good portion of patience with you, since the game is not (yet) completely error-free. It can happen that you often have to reposition yourself in the game before you can interact with something or have to load a save game because you get stuck somewhere. It's not tragic, but can be a bit annoying at times. By the way, there is no jump button, you just walk (run) or ride a bike.I played through the game as much as possible in one go and would also recommend it because of the atmosphere, even if it can be "tiring" at times. I would say the playtime is somewhere between 6 and 10 hours. But it simply depends on whether you complete all (side) tasks and the associated achievements or not. Getting lost and wandering included.If you get involved in the game and the emotional, sometimes confusing and bizarre story, it can be quite captivating and exciting.The game design and the mood it captures is really great and you can see the love for detail on every corner. Graphically, the game is a real eye-catcher. When it comes to the story, it's more up to you to decide whether it's satisfying for you or not.✅ stunning (level) design ✅ great mood captured✅ lovely details✅ bizarre story❌ too expensive ❌ some bugs ❌ possible performance problems

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead, begins with a heavy disclaimer and rightfully so. The game covers ethically heavy topics such as war crimes, child trauma, pregnancy and mental health. Should you as a player, in any time or point, experienced any form of severe trauma, do please reconsider playing this game. This game excels at story telling and it provides stunning graphics. The narrative is driven and doesn’t feel boring. Thus, you are constantly engaged with the story. As an amateur photographer I loved the mechanics behind old school photography, I have never come across developing photos manually so I loved it. I managed to beat it under 6 hours, would have preferred a longer story. Coming from a medical background, it didn’t seem all too disturbing to me but please do heed the warnings. Maybe I’m just too desensitized due to work. Quick takes:+ Story is great and it provides a few plot twists,+ Graphics is absolutely stunning once you crank up the settings, the game looks okey on medium settings but I did encounter a few visual bugs. Perhaps due to the lower setting. + Taking photos can result in you grabbing a many stunning photos. + The tasks in the game is at period, difficult until you get the hang of it. + You must complete some morse code puzzle, in which was a fun experience. It too took me a while to figure out how to read the morse code map thingy. +/- The soundtrack is on-point but does become "meh" at times. - Walking can be tedious between locations.- It wasn’t scary to play the game and horror aspect of it is lacking. - The story is rather short  Overall, I recommend this game and perhaps we will see a similar game from this game studio in the future? I rate this game 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A few things to know before you buy:1. It’s short. I don’t rush my games but I still finished it in about 3 sessions of play.2. Don't let the beautiful rural surroundings and old-timey photography and telephones fool you: this is a very gruesome, morbid, tragic and miserable story. And there is a lot of gore, violence and other unpleasantness. This is not a subtle game. It keeps getting in your face, like it’s determined to find some way to upset you.3. There isn’t much interactivity, and what’s there often feels pointless. Like, you’re directed to make the character do something but there’s no way to mess it up, so why make you do it at all? Only, it seems, to make you feel complicit in her actions. There is also a long-ish sequence where you need to uncover the story through controlling a puppet show, which is just incredibly cumbersome and annoying.4. The camera stuff is cool but a lot of the equipment you’re given is superfluous. The photo developing process is boring. And there really isn’t enough to take pictures of that will have any effect on the game.5. The world is small and claustrophobic. You only have the house and the grounds in which to manoeuvre, beautiful as they are.I did finish the story, but only out of a desire for completeness. I was really willing it to end for the last hour or so. All in all, disappointing. Glad it was on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead was an incredible journey. I went into the game extremely excited from the trailers that I had previously seen before release. I highly recommend this game. Now, let's get into the pros and cons.The developers weren't scared of delving into incredibly dark topics that normally most developers will avoid like the plague, . This can be a turn off to some, and that's okay. That just means the game isn't for you. The soundtrack and atmosphere were both magnificent and well-done. The story that was told in this game is probably one of the best stories I have ever experienced. I found myself crying, almost to the point of an uncontrollable sob when watching the ending and having the credits roll. I found myself to be somewhat relatable to the main character and it just hit very different. If you're looking for a game with a great story, this game is for you. Just be warned, there are some very gruesome scenes.The game definitely needs to be optimized. The developers are aware of the problems that everyone is experiencing and are working on it, as far as I know (per Steam Discussions/Forums). There also appears to be a form of a memory leak when having the game running for several hours at a time. Simply restart the game and it'll be working again. When utilizing the camera to take pictures, any movement with the camera can cause it to jump or stutter, which kind of got annoying but I got used to it. I didn't really encounter any game breaking bugs or glitches.All in all, this was an incredibly fascinating game with a beautiful story to tell. Do I recommend it? 100% yes. But, I recommend waiting until an optimization patch is released, which should hopefully be soon. Thanks for reading! 🥰  🥰

_childDocuments_.review: ‘Martha is Dead’ is a game created by LKA Studios (authors of the excellent ‘Town of Light’) and was released in February 2022. It tells the story of Giulia K., a young girl who is trying to find out who killed her twin sister Martha. The game is 7/8 hours long and the plot is truly intriguing from the start as we quickly realize that something’s wrong here. Really, really wrong.The game is a walking simulator in a semi-open world: we’re playing as Giulia (in FPP view) and we’re spending most of the time at exploring and looking for objects that are crucial to the story. We can also gather additional informations about some events or characters by reading notes and newspapers and sometimes we have to take photos of certain things to advance the plot. Gameplay-wise it’s just a typical walking-sim, so if you have played games like ‘Firewatch’ or ‘The Vanishing of Ethan Carter’ you know what to expect. There are also few QTE in the game, but they are very simple and almost impossible to fail, so they are not annoying.The in-game world is quite large (list of locations includes the house, the forest, the lake and several other interesting and sometimes also quite surprising places), but navigating through it is easy, because Giulia has access to the map and her diary, so we always know where we are and what to do next. It’s also worth mentioning that there are few optional side-quests available. They allow us to get a better understanding of certain events, but we also can completely ignore them and focus just on the main plot - it’s totally up to us. The game is set at the Italian countryside during World War II and the protagonist is a daughter of an Italian woman and a Nazi general. This alone gives quite an unusual (and basically unseen in video games) perspective, but there’s more - as it turns out, Giulia seemingly has absolutely no idea that Italian fascist and the Nazis are the bad guys (!) and she’s genuinly surprised that partisans are constantly fighting the Axis armies. Developers did a really good job here showing not only the girl's different (and ridiculous) perspective, but also how blind to the facts she is, because there’s enough evidence lying around to know what Mussolini’s and Hitler’s people really do. This whole thing is basically a detail always subtly appearing somewhere in the background and it’s really easy to miss if we’re not exploring carefully enough, but it is really well done. And now it's time to talk about the best thing about ‘Martha is Dead’ - absolutely fantastic story. I'll write it right away to make it clear – this is NOT a normal story about solving Martha's murder. The plot is really dark, heavy and reaches into the deepest, darkest parts of our minds making us wonder what's real and what's not. We’ll witness a lot of strong and very violent scenes (and I woudn’t be surprised if some people call them shocking or disgusting), but all of them make sense and are justified by the story the developers are telling. The story that at some point turns into the absolutely fascinating and messed up journey that keeps us hooked to the screen the entire time and does not disappoint at the end of the game. On top of that devs treat us like adults, so there is not just one simple explanation to everything and we should pay attention to details as some of them can totally change the way we’re understanding some events. Moreover, the atmosphere throughout the entire gameplay is simply incredible, because developers are revealing next layers of the story in very smart way and we know something unexpected is going to happen sooner or later.There’s also one thing that should be mentioned: even though the game is not a horror, it has some jump-scares in it. There are literally few of them, but I know some people hate them, so I think it should be mentioned. As for the technical stuff – ‘Martha is Dead’ looks stunning, especially on the ultra graphic settings: the textures are razor sharp, the lights and shadows work just like they should and some of the views are simply gorgeous. It’s basically one of those games where we can just go from place to place and spend hours taking screenshot after screenshot. The same thing can be said about the soundtrack as the music is simply phenomenal and complements what we see on the screen in an incredible way. I played the game with the Italian voice acting (it’s really solid) and English subtitles and I think it’s the best way to do it, but English voice acting is available as well (can’t say anything about its quality though). And it’s also worth mentioning that we can save game anytime we want plus there’s also an autosave feature.Now the complains and luckily the list is not long. First and foremost - ‘Martha is Dead’ was released 2,5 years ago and the technical state of the game is still.... Well, disastrous. Regardless of the graphic settings and DirectX version (we can choose between DX11 or DX12) I was experiencing constant stuttering, freezes, FPS drops, texture pop-ups and a whole bunch of other problems, such as camera jumps, crashes or the fact that sometimes after closing the game it turned out that I have to manually kill the process in the task manager because it was still running in the background. I have really decent PC that allows me to comfortably play games like ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ or ‘Elden Ring’, so it's not a hardware problem on my end and there’s a lot of topics about it on the Steam forums and it’s constantly mentioned here in the reviews. It’s kind of surprising to be honest, because previous LKA game (‘Town of Light’) worked like a charm and I had no technical issues with it whatsoever. Obviously I know every game is different, but I just didn’t expect that ‘Martha is Dead’ could be THAT messed up technically.Apart from that I can complain about literally two little things. First – sometimes during the exploration ambient music just stops and restarts only after saving and reloading the game. Not a big deal, but still an issue. Second – backtracking is a little bit annoying sometimes. Developers seem to be aware of it, because there’s a bike available in the game, but because of the technical problems I described earlier it becomes completely useless, mostly due to the sudden camera jumps as they make it impossible to drive straight even just a few meters. To sum up this review – ‘Martha is Dead’ is really a great game. Dark, thought-provoking, incredibly intriguing and sometimes simply fascinating. And yes, it’s a mess on the technical side, but in my opinion the story makes up for everything. Give it a shot, I’m pretty sure you won’t regret it.-----TL;DR? Here's the short version.Pros:+ Fascinating story with many unexpected twists+ Creepy and disturbing atmosphere+ Graphics are absolutely stunning+ Beautiful soundtrack and really solid voice acting+ Manual saving system (and there's also autosaving feature)Cons:- Constant stuttering and framedrops- Random freezing and crashes- Backtracking can be kind of annoyingIt's a great game with a lot of technical problems, but the story IMHO makes up for everything. Is it worth giving a shot? Totally.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have been aesthetically pleasant but it was boring and for the price, I expected it to be twice as long.  Most of the interactions were irrelevant to the completion of the game so it seems they were placed in there to just waste time.  It was basically a photography game where you learn how to develop film.  What was the purpose of all the filters for the camera when none were needed?  If the game occurred in 1944, why were there mausoleum plaques with deceased dates in the 1980's on at least 2 of the sarcophagi?  Why was Giulia's closet and bed in Martha's room while Giulia's locked room only contained that puppet show?  Why did the explanation of how nanny and Lapo differ from what actually happened during gameplay?  If the bicycle was only needed to ride to San Cristiano, why were you able to interact with it prior?  Did anybody try riding that thing before it was necessary?  I did!  It was terrible to control and moved slower than she ran....and she ran slow.  This was all nonsense.  The transmission quest would have been irritating because I couldn't read the chart, but luckily for me, I copied morse code in the military so that was not difficult. _childDocuments_.review: *Slight spoilers to follow so be warned but if you want my immediate takeaway, this is one of my least favorite gaming experience of all time. - In it's short play time Martha is Dead juggles themes of child abuse, animal abuse, familicide, suicide, mental illness, fascism, and more - all with the most superficial depth and subtlety of a sledgehammer.- The first 4-5 hours are a tedious slog through walking sim exposition with the clunkiest controls and slowest movement to pad out the run time as it spoon feeds you unreliable narration that hardly ties it's plot points together. - To pad out even more time none of the dialogue or constant monologue is skippable. If you read fast, you'll spend a third of this game waiting for it catch up with you. - The final hour or so amplifies the previous problems just by bathing the story in unpleasantness and a marionette play that despite looking kind of clever, manages to slow exposition down even further. - All plotlines are explained away as mental illness with a shrug - Incredibly weird this game cuts to black to hide gun violence several times, gives you the option to censor a scene of self harm YET makes you partake in a lengthy QTE minigame where you undress the corpse of a teenager and cut a deformed fetus out of her with a pair of scissors a'la Inside. - All the constant grief and trauma in this game leads up to a suicide that quite honestly feels earned for the pain it's endured and given to others - but this the game has the audacity end on a "suicide is never the answer - good things are always around the corner" message right after staring into the dead eyes of it's truly horrendous protagonist. I don't know there's a ton more technical stuff pertaining to the awkward movement, the inconsistent lighting, and the fact that despite looking dated and mid it somehow put my PC thru the wringer but still the tone deaf ending that never seems to end just had me screaming "OH FFS..." as it stumbled towards the finish. Absolutely hated this experience and would not recommend for even a "hate watch" playthru.

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially one of the most disturbing games of the year, Martha is Dead unfolds as a slow-burn, first-person, psychological thriller. The main premise of the game entails Martha, the identical sibling to Giulia, of course, dying; and the rest is comprised of how people in her vicinity are affected by this, which is also interjacent to your eventual descent into madness. It certainly does surprise you with more than what seems plausible on the surface.The controls are easy enough to grasp, being mostly point-and-click interactive with movements assisted by a WASD keyboard format. You, obviously, can use different layouts or a controller if you please, and you can play the game in a multitude of languages—Italian being both the innate choice and possibly the best one. The game includes a log for missed dialogue and subtitles, and while some documents in-game might be in English, they're mainly in Italian, so it isn't completely immersion shattering. There are also extra details that I appreciate, such as the daily tarot divinations.Regardless of whatever technical choice you make, you will eventually assume the role of a twin sister situated in the Italian countryside of the 1940s, who is engrossed in a web of war, abuse, grief, and psychotic delusion. You are simply a victim of circumstance. This game definitely requires quite a heavy trigger warning prior to playing it, as there are a few pop-up messages preceding specific scenes. Martha is Dead is an ordeal that is RIFE with both realistic & gratuitous gore. The experience is heavy on atmosphere and accompanied by an eerie soundtrack, and the graphics are the icing on the cake. With that being said, the character models, along with environmental textures, can sometimes look wonky up close. Still, the game is capable of everyone's favorite buzzword, a.k.a. "ray tracing," and can easily result in your system heating up to some extent (it's probably necessary to mention here that I am playing on a laptop with an i7-9700 Intel Core, 16GB of RAM, and an RTX 2070.) In addition to that, it's worth saying that my playthroughs were significantly glitched, with me being unable to proceed with certain quests despite my position in the story. There were many occasions when I'd fly through the map after trying to do something as simplistic as riding my bicycle over a dirt hump. While hunting for the last two achievements, I would have to close out my game just to reset the location of my bike. As you'd guess, this ultimately became very draining after figuring out that these problems were not unique to a single condition and would recurrently show up. My game would, on occasion, have somewhat of a stuttering problem as well.Martha is Dead begins with a view of a bedroom window, amongst a doting nanny retelling the story of a local cryptid: a homicidal wraith who slays a young woman every time fog descends upon the lake nearby. The reason for this stems from a traumatic event involving the drowning of the "White Lady" during a domestic situation regarding her and her significant other.Although you may interpret this as the main focus of the game, the White Lady is predominantly made available in fleeting moments and photographs, most of which you have to actively try to discover. The other times she appears are within metaphors and coincidences parallel to the story; an eternally repetitive imprint on reality, i.e., "The house was a place of suffering."One of the teeming questions that plague this game is having you navigate between major parts of the story through either the lens of a camera or from the audience of a puppeteer show at the theatre. Some of the first items & areas you're presented with either involve or consist of being gifted a camera, alongside your own personal darkroom to develop whatever tokens of interest you capture with it. If you're confused about how to progress, all you really have to do is keep an eye out for the hand-shaped button prompts, which routinely fill up with red. There are also collectibles, requiring you to pick up rolls of film and camera modifications that you find in and around your family's estate. This feature leads me to reminisce a lot about Fatal Frame and its mechanics with picture taking.(Spoiler warnings from this point forward.)Overall, Martha is Dead was an encounter I mostly enjoyed, as long as I wasn't forced to figure out how to progress through game-breaking bugs. Luckily, the developers seem to be pretty focused on staying on top of patches and updates, so I doubt that any of these hiccups will survive for very long. It's a gripping adventure that will at best make you uncomfortable and at worst cause you to be confused, depressed, and sick to your stomach. I'd recommend it to anybody who isn't particularly sensitive to these things.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic horror tale that’s bound to sit with you. One that feels like it’s using the medium to tell a story, not just to shoehorn in the usual suspects of video game tropes and slapdash mechanisms. At times, it actually comes off more like something you’d experience in 70’s horror cinema: A slow-burn that starts out more akin to a social drama, but carefully turns into something more sinister and makabre during the latter part. In fact, one of the things that make Martha Is Dead stand out is how it’s a little bit less concerned with giving nods to the player. It’s not a game that fits the modern mold of streamer-friendly gargle -- even though there’s no clear elevator pitch here that would convince you otherwise. There’s just something about how no one’s trying to impress or scare you for the sake of scares alone. No one’s monitoring your heart rate. No one’s using algorithms to inject jumpscares. Instead, gore and horror feel more like a natural, deliberate extension of the storytelling.It’s a confidently produced and directed game; laser focused in its mission to create a believable and chilling atmosphere. And the setting really is one of the highpoints for me here. It’s beautiful. Especially how the whole WWII-backdrop looms in the background, grounding it. Also, how the environments and attention to details manage to transport you into this beautiful European period piece. I wish more developers would allow themselves to use their native language as the default spoken one. It’s a huge part of why Martha is Dead works for me -- and why I’m in Tuscany and not at home in front of my computer.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a one of a kind experience.As a psychological horror fan, I went in with certain expectations. I said "one of a kind," because what I got to experience is something I haven't in any video game before. It is not afraid to push the ladder a bit further than you're used to in games or even movies. It gives you a fair amount of warnings - for a good reason. But the true horrors of this game are not those in jumpscares and disturbing imaginery, they are those within mental illnesses (trauma, self-harm, abuse) and war (I would like to put an ephasis on drug usage during WW2). The unspoken, beneath the surface horrors. And that is where it succeeds the most. The game is running on UE4 and despite of being made on an Indie budget, the visuals are stunning - partly photorealistic.It is set during the late years of World War 2 in a small fictional town in Tuscany. The attention to details representing this time period is fantastic. From the landscapes to the house interiors and decorations, everything was crafted with the utmost care. The title also uses "metahuman technology," which made it possible to render pretty realistic character models. Attention was also paid to the lighting of specific scenery, which I consider an important aspect of a good horror game. But what ties everything together and makes it complete is the soundtrack. And it's great. It fits the game's environment perfectly and was well incorporated to add tension when needed.The gameplay itself is consisting more or less of puzzle and mystery solving, exploration, and has a really extensive photography mechanic that was fun to use. But the gameplay and some other issues are where this title falls a bit short for me. Walking as a whole was kind of clumsy. Later on you can unlock a bike to travel longer distances with, although I chose to walk rather than ride it due to its riding mechanics. It also felt a bit repetitive at times. Some chapters felt like there wasn't much going on. Now, Personally, I like slow burns so I didn't mind it that much, but I can understand why it might be a problem for some players. Just remember - in the end, it will all make sense. Everything, is building up to it. The optimization is just simply, bad and could have been polished. Randomly dropping frames, stuttering, getting stuck in objects on the ground, game crashing after loading a save file, cutscene not loading properly forcing you to reload.. Final verdict : I enjoyed the game and don't think I'm gonna forget about it for quite some time. Through all it's flaws "Martha Is Dead" is a piece of art, and I recommend it to anyone who isn't overly sensitive or is a fan of psychological horror. Special thanks to LKA and Wired Productions for bringing us and allowing us to experience this unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: FULL REVIEW --->  Not in the typical jump-scare sense we see all too much today though. There were many moments during Martha is Dead where I truly gasped in horror. There were things the game requires you to do, that you DO NOT WANT to do in the game. There are several moments of truly graphic visual horror that many people will not get past.It is a true psychological horror that will get in your head. Days after finishing, I continue to reflect on the game. It sticks with you.All serious elements are dealt with respectfully and tastefully and are there for developing the story (although you may not realize it yet), not just a gore ‘shock effect’. They help place you into the character and doing these extreme actions in a game will push your own mental boundaries. Again, this game will NOT be for everyone. I personally feel exploring these topics respectfully in a video game is a step in the right direction. Much respect to the developers for bringing light to and allowing people to experience the torment of these issues in the safety of a game, that many people experience every day in their real life.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is an indie walking simulator set at the end of World War II (1945), Italy, where you play as Julia (Giulia) whose identical twin, Martha, is mysteriously killed. The protagonist fakes as her sister and you will see her journey of finding out the truth behind the death. This game has some good ideas in terms of gameplay and an obscure yet unexpected story, however, falls short because of the execution and technology implementation, making it kind of a niche experience where you must endure lots of clunkiness before you can see a story that may or may not appeal to you.For most walking simulators today, the story is moved forward by the change of space. The course of walking and the interactions in between are the gameplay, which makes this genre tend to have weak playability. I think the dev of this game saw this weakness, so instead of walking, they designed the gameplay around exploration in one big map. It is a very good idea and supposedly makes the game more interesting with higher playability. Unfortunately, the execution is not there.The assistive designs around exploration, such as map design and movement are very poor, further disincentivizing players to explore. It is a result of poor implementation of technology.The interactions are unnecessarily complicated. For example, to open the camera, you need to do almost everything you need in real life, all of which are followed by a set of interactions. Some of the interactions give a good opportunity for internal monologue to happen, but more of them are just filler contents – to make you do a series of button pressing for the sake of having more things to do.There is one puzzle session in the entire game, which is to translate morse code. Daymare 1998 also has the same translation puzzle and I criticized it for the same reason – making a real-life implementation as a video game puzzle is just lazy, and morse code translation is just too complicated and uninteresting. I had to google a tutorial to translate the puzzle.This game keeps reminding me of The Beast Inside, another walking simulator that uses similar exploration as gameplay design. That game has its own problems, but in terms of gameplay, it has genuinely good puzzles and some interesting map interconnectivity for exploration. By comparison or not, Martha is Dead is just a very underwhelming experience.The storytelling, on the other hand, is much better than gameplay. Martha is Dead uses a non-continuous narrative method that jumps from scene to scene, similar to montage in movie. You might find it difficult to understand the story due to the jumping, but with this, the story is able to simplify unnecessary plots and more importantly, works really well in creating mystery and smoothing the transition. Speaking of, I think the scriptwriting is pretty good. It is one of those stories that is unexpected but also perfectly makes sense, as the mystery is well set up and leaves small hints in different sessions if you are able to notice them. The story also leaves some ambiguity smartly, allowing players to have two different but interesting interpretations of the story.I do think the good and bad of the story come in the same form, which is obscurity. Because of the scene jumping and using inner monologue as narrative (hence the very limited perspective in viewing the entire event), the story takes effort to understand. On top of that, the gameplay can greatly distract players from sorting out the information they gather. Therefore, I think only a certain group of people will appreciate the story.As for the presentation, the game has good sound design that enhances the atmosphere very well, but the visual design is kind of a mixed bag. The interior design of the house is very detailed and believable as a house of the 1940s, but outside the house, the game doesn’t look so good. The environment seems to be designed with assets from Unreal Engine Marketplace, hence they come in low resolution, look particularly bad up close, and have no environmental effects (like the leaves don’t move with wind), yet the optimization is atrocious with lots of random frame drop (frame rate cut in half with RTX on but visual difference is minimal). Also, the FOV is kind of uncomfortable and needs lots of time to get used to (motion sick warning). I played the game in mid-March and there were many bugs (I had the game on Day One but a game-breaking bug prevented me from advancing until a patch came out). To their credit, the dev released patches that fix bugs and optimize the game quite frequently.In conclusion, the story of Martha is Dead is not for the majority yet can attract people who enjoy psychological horror and obscure storytelling. But as a video game, the story is not enough to redeem the unexciting and disappointing gameplay. I really wish it is a movie instead of a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free!Initially, this game was a big yes. At least as far as the story goes. But ultimately, Martha is Dead makes for an interesting story that really lacks any fun gameplay elements, is optimized horribly, and goes on for just a bit too long. - StoryReally the majority of the story is very interesting. You're often wanting to know what happens next and occasionally scratching your head over certain puzzling elements. However, there's times when the writing doesn't make sense in areas where maybe I missed a small piece of it, but certain dialogue choices don't make sense. There's some twists and turns and some of them are neat, but holy Shyamalan Batman, I was left rolling my eyes at yet another "twist." By the last few twists, I just didn't care anymore. The clunky gameplay also gets in the way of the story to the point where by the end of it, I just wanted the story to be over. - Audio The voice acting is mostly superb. The main character is voiced beautifully. There's maybe a few heightened emotional moments that didn't really sound great, but overall, it was great. Some of the supporting characters are lifeless, but you'll spend most of your time listening to the main character's voice which is great. The music in this game tries way too hard. I'm also of the opinion that vocals in music in games are often distracting and out of place and this is no different. Like this follows the trope of the *violin intensifies* and it's really just obnoxious especially when the scene doesn't warrant THAT much tension. - GameplayMy biggest gripe with this game is that it tries so hard to be a complex game and add all these little mini games, but it doesn't do any of them well or it over complicates things for no reason. The camera is the main part of the "gameplay" and it really just throws all kinds of film, lenses, and accessories at you and allows you to adjust focus, aperture, and exposure which you would think means you're going to be taking some super Instagram worthy shots, but really any story elements are locked to a particular exposure, focal length, and lens to the point where there is indeed a wrong way to take a photo. Not only that, but the incredibly tedious and boring task of developing photos is slow and not engaging at all. You have to do it correctly, so no framing shots in a way you think looks cool. And the game over explains everything and wants to tell you how developing photos was REALLY done back in the day, but it's simplified for the game. I can respect the game is trying to be educational, but the task is still tedious and talking to the players directly takes me out of the immersion. There's all sorts of mini games like this, but I don't want to write an actual novel here so I'll move on. -VisualsThis game looks beautiful...when it works. Let me preface this by saying I have a Ryzen9 5900x and a 3080. There's very little my PC struggles to run. However, this game in 1440p on ultra is literally unplayable. I know I know, there's some games that just aren't meant to run maxed out, but even with some settings turned down, my PC struggled to keep up with it. To the point where there were large frame rate drops and stutters as the game loaded sections in. But the BIGGEST problem is the Morse Code mini game. You'll have to press your mouse with long and short sequences...neat right? Nope. Not if the game isn't running smoothly. One message was fine, but then another just would not work. I was getting so frustrated, I literally held up my mouse to my microphone for chat to hear a long press, followed by short, only to be met with an error telling me I was doing it wrong. I was going to lose my mind. I had to quickly jab the mouse like it was too hot to touch. The stuttering frames meant the game wasn't reading my input correctly either. After noticing the audio kept cutting out, I realized it may be because of the game's poor performance that it was doing this. Finally the last bit here. Horror.So this game isn't really horror. At least not in the traditional sense. I see it's tagged as psychological horror which...I mean...that doesn't seem to be entirely accurate either. It's just gore. Very gory. I don't mind gore, but this was just shock value gore. There's sections of the game that just seems to throw in gore and nudity for no real reason. It was just a bit over the top and though some parts served the story, I felt like most of it was just a bit much. TLDR; Martha is Dead is a beautifully horribly optimized game with tedious and boring gameplay mechanics and excessive gore for shock value. The story was questionably worth it, but by the time it was done, I was just relieved to be done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest: I usually love games like this. But this has been an exercise in patience. _childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to play this game. The idea of playing as an Italian woman living in the Toscana region during the 1940s (a very particular time period for Italy history wise!) was very attractive. Taking that and mixing it with a very suspenseful premise for the main plot and very ominous title (you know, Martha is Dead). And even more, adding a very strong analog photography element and even a little bike ride (not just any bike, but an old big bike, like the ones your grandpa may have lying around).Going in I think there were a lot of things that are recognizable in one way or another to a lot of people around the world in this game.Indeed this game has a lot of good things going on for it, first one is: the attention to detail and the graphical fidelity are amazing. Not just from a technical standpoint of view but from a craft and artistic one too. Waking up for the first time in your room, looking at things, the rest of the house as well and the nearby woods is like transporting to another place, and another era.The dialogues in Italian with subtitles (if you play the original audio) is very well done and helps a lot getting you immersed.The initial premise for the story, is very attractive and promises a lot.Sadly, the game then fails to meet many of these promises or at least falls short of the enormous potential it does have.The photography element, which is one of the main points of interest in the game, does look very well, (your camera, your accessories, you have a lot of them) they all look and feel great, but in execution..... that's where it kind of falls short... taking the picture, you do have your manual focus for example, but the game tells you then with a big red message when your picture is in focus. A the very beginning of the game you do have a special "precise” focus tool in your camera, but you never really use it after that. The same can be said about exposure (aperture, speed) You do have manual controls for that too, but the game camera shows you how the picture will end up looking, and a big red sign lights up telling you when it is well exposed or not enough... which kind of makes the whole point of having the manual controls not really necessary in the end... It is a shame really, the tools are there, but the implementation does not really favours you trying, making experiments, because its really difficult seeing your manual focus on screen without a focus tool like the one in the beginning and then using the filters. At least the “Dark Room” part in which you develop and print your images is a little better, and you can play with longer exposures if you choose to do so, while still advancing the main story.But I’m going on a tangent about photography perhaps, you'll have to excuse me as I was at some point a photographer, and all these things ring very near to me. Perhaps, most people won't even notice many of these things.Moving on, the bicycle is another great touch to the game, which gets terribly underused. You'll probably ride your bike once or twice in the whole game, unless you just want to go in circles around the house. And it is a shame because the bike mechanics are very good (at least the few times I spent with trying them) Specially the sounds, I love the sound the bike makes when you’re going at full speed downhill, you hear the chain roll, just like a real old bike, you can just let go off the pedal, and the bicycle will go on alone without you doing anything, which of course doesn't happen when going up. Little beautiful touches that make all these interactions so special.And then there's the story... the ominous title, your sister's mystery, the historical political context surrounding everything, can it be related? Your German father with its Nazi affiliations and your mother.Without spoiling the story, I would say that I personally didn't like the way the story went, or at least, how it went in the later parts of the game, especially in the end. It could have been so much more. All the elements are there, it just feels like a wasted opportunity.The game also makes some narrative decisions (as to how the story is told) specially towards the end which left me wandering if maybe they ran out of resources, and they just had to resort to a very minimalistic (and frankly poor way) of telling certain key elements of the story while at the beginning of the game it was done much better with maybe less crucial scenes (which were beautifully told) but still, all that effort put there, and all the immersive historical elements too, and then what happened to the story?In a way, having all these beautiful visual achievements, photography mechanics and historical accuracy showed to us at each step, undermines how little the actual story in the game makes use of all of this.As much as I like all the comfort food, the story should have been more predominant, the player more involved with it. However the main character sees to it of course. Doesn't matter how radical the story gets in the end. IT should FEEL more as a road taken. Not just something that appears suddenly and that's that. Tell us more. Make us understand more our main character. However improbable.   One thing is certain, I like LKA game worlds, they tell us (imperfect) interesting stories and I think the potential for a great well told story is there, latent, like a photograph taken on film, just waiting to see the world one day.This very inflammatory but respectful review is

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is an absolutely remarkable psychological thriller. If you appreciate games with complex unravelling narratives and strong emotional content, you will probably really enjoy this game. It is set in Italy in 1944. You are Giulia, a young woman. Your twin sister Martha is deaf. Your father is a German general overseeing the war in Italy. Your Italian mother despises you. She adores Martha but has been profoundly abusive to you throughout your life. Your father did love you and try to protect you from your mother, but he was increasingly absent because of the war. It begins as you are gathering film in the forest near the lake. You had set up cameras on timers and want to develop the photos. As you are focusing one of the cameras, you realise that there is a body in the water. You frantically swim to it. It is Martha. You drag her to shore and just sit with your dead twin. Impulsively you remove her locket and place it around your neck. Your parents find the two of you. But they believe that it is Giulia who has drowned. It is at that moment that you decide to live as Martha. It's one of the best narrative hooks that I've ever encountered in a game. As you live as Martha, you begin investigating her death. Giulia knows that she's psychologically damaged and is working to overcome that. She wants to know that truth. What unfolds is a series of revelations, some of which are very powerful. The game has some really strong moments andI don't think that I'll forget it. This is an excellent game. If you love a strong narrative and powerful emotions, then play it.At the beginning of the game, you are in the beautiful Italian countryside. You had set up cameras on timers and you

_childDocuments_.review: Length <5hrMartha is Dead is a strange game, on the box it seems like a horror game set in World War 2. I saw the trailers and thought, Wow this is going to be some occult horror of a monster in the lake. Nope! The game is completely Psychological Horror, with random and at times what feels like over the top horror scenes glued on. Do not come into the game with the expectation to be scared, the horror visuals are few and spaced out. The game is more about the player understanding what is actually going on, and the player will only realise this later into the game.I would say the game is closer to The Remains of Edith Finch and The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, than a full horror game.Most of Martha is Dead is a Simulation game, the player will be completing random actions in Giulia’s daily life. While later the player will support the war effort, this gameplay is mainly fetch quests or go to set locations.The player will also have to complete some morse code puzzles, which was a fun experience. It took me a while to work out how to read the morse code map, as I attempted to read it from the bottom at first, till I learned it was a branching path from the top. The rest of the game is exploration or narrative plot, you are not going to find any real action in the game out of a few moments. At times the player will also need to make use of their camera to take pictures asked of them, this is a little tedious as you need to find the perfect angle and use the correct lenses and focus. The player can also find items to take pictures of in the environment that will reveal more. Once the player has taken pictures they will need to develop them, which is done through a little mini game. Now the visuals are amazing, especially the horror moments, they stand out and definitely worth the time to see them. They out match a lot of horror moments in games, and would be scenes I would expect to see in the original Texas Chainsaw Massacre.Before Spoilers I just want to say Martha is Dead is a good game for people who just want to experience a game, it is closer to a walking simulator-esque game, go in expecting that and you will enjoy the game. I did not, I saw the game marketed as an over the top horror game, and thought that what I was buying with countless times being told of how dark horror is.. Sadly this was a tiny amount of my gameplay and I feel a lot of the horror moments are not really needed for the narrative and are only there to make visual stand out set pieces.Martha is Dead is solely reliant on its story and we perceive the story through Giulia, the only problem is, she is an unreliable narrator. This extends into the whole game, everything you see, everything you hear has a high chance of being her false reality, and as such the game is completely subjective to what the player thinks is real. I am not even sure if any aspect can be perceived as real.So my best guess, Martha is dead, she has been dead since birth. Your mother had pains during pregnancy and only one child was born. I believe this is the case as Giulia says that her family is cursed with twins, and is seen in the fetus. (Your Mother also states you were alone at the lake, having a breakdown).This led her mother to have mental problems post birth where she abused Giulia, but also treated Giulia as two people declaring her as Martha and may be the origin of Martha as an identity, this can be seen in the puppets where each time punishment was dealt it was to solely one child. Your Mother also refers to this later during your confrontation. This caused Giulia to create Martha as a separate personality, one that cannot talk to her mother, and in doing so did not receive further abuse. It was Giulia who was blamed for problems and received the abuse instead. You were taken away from your mother when she was meant to be in a mental ward, you can hear that in the ending when the mother talks to the priest. It also explains why you were alone with Nanny, as there was no abuse removing the need for Giulia to rely on Martha to protect herself. This leads to the start of the game, where your mental state further deteriorates after your miscarriage and Giulia wants to become Martha to avoid the pain she is in. Also potential on meeting your mother again.You could also perceive that your Mother preferred Martha as a personality because she could not answer back, meaning your Mother rewarded the Martha part of Giulia. While other characters only interact with Giulia, such as Nanny and your Father. This can also be reinforced when people can not identify the difference between Martha and Giulia because there is not one, it solely what personality is dominant, with no physical change.Now if I was to take my theory as real, then so much of the game is probably just Giulia’s reality and never happened, to the scope of this who knows. It might be everything, she may have not done anything but walked around talking to herself. Core moments like being shot, the injury just disappearing, all newspapers she reads mentioning Martha, conversation you hear from soldiers or even the doctor. The phone call with Nanny, and any picture that you had taken. None may be real, this also renders all horror scenes as part of her delusion and not being real. There is even a chance that all actions you do for the war were not real, as did you even receive the first note from your lover as that also mentions Martha. I just don’t know.This really comes to light in the endings, where you are effectively having to piece together your reality. What you submit at the end is Giulia’s reality.Here are some more points for you, the White Lady (Ghost in the lake), a fairytale from your nanny that you do when you play with your puppets. Any scene she is in is probably a delusion. Why Martha had a bed and clothes, I have no clue. Why you are restricted from your old room, I am still not sure, really on this one I think I missed some context for all I know the roof was leaking. You may enjoy the game, but to me, the game leaves a foul aftertaste where it feels like I am going to have to fully break down all moments, just to find out that nothing makes any sense because Giulia throughout the whole game can not perceive reality. This has been so annoying. I have thought over the game repeatedly, I wrote this review on release and have redrafted it endlessly. The story of Martha is Dead, is confusing solely on the fact that you cannot build a grounded reality from anywhere because everything you perceive is potentially unreal.Here’s the last thing, did your Mum and Dad die, did your Nanny die? You carry your Mum’s head under the bridge but was this reality? Your Dad is killed but his body is taken, and there is nothing left on the floor to prove he was even there. The moment plays off fast in the story and the only visible sign of it can be seen as the injury to Martha’s face. Your Nanny’s death is told through exposition, exposition that directly references Martha.I would not recommend the game unless you want to just experience the game. Really experience the game for what it is. Now I have a headache and need to leave this game in the past, it’s been a long time writing this and now, I’m free. Still lots of cool moments, it’s worth buying for those.If you want to have a look at the game here is the start of my playthrough:For some good horror games check out my Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some performance annoyances, Martha Is Dead makes excellent use of its layered narrative to tell a complex story involving the mental health of its main character. While Giulia searches for answers about her dead sister, players take photographs, explore a slice of Tuscany, and interact with objects via some amazing first-person animations. The subtle horror themes and war backdrop just add flavor to the complex narrative, and we’re always wondering about Giulia’s mental state. It is a tale that will keep players thinking after completion, and when a story is able to dive into the mind like that, it must have done something right.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game meant for everyone. If you are a fan of The Town of Light you will likely enjoy this entry. Something I enjoyed about both games is the way in which it depicts and explores mental illness. It is not taken lightly, and the game designers clearly have a deep empathy for people who endure mental health issues. Game play  is limited, but given the nature of the game itself this is not an issue. They do a good job of exploiting the medium to tell an effective story. There were some elements that I found needlessly complicated, but these are optional. Taken as a whole everything serves to move the story forward, or immerse you in the narrative until you feel as one with the protagonist. The last part is crucial for me. I haven't felt like this since I first saw the film Session 9. The way in which the narrative unfolds leaves you questioning what exactly happened until the very end. The denouement is touching and a great send off. Performance wise I feel like this could have been optimized a little better. For being a limited narrative experience it really made my computer chug at times. There were some texture loading anomalies, and some inconsistent pop-in. Nothing super extreme, but it's worth mentioning. 8/10 would strongly recommend.  Definitely play it alongside Town of Light as they link together in a sort of meta-narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay spoilers follow, no substantial plot spoilers. This is a strange game, but, unfortunately, it is not strange in an a particularly interesting or thoughtful way. It's less a traditional "horror game" and more an unfocused mash-up of early-00s era adventure games like Nancy Drew, the modern first-person narrative "walking simulator," and a historical drama with psychological horror/thriller elements. There's also a weirdly (kind of hilariously) detailed camera simulator for some reason, which the developers take great pains to explain is similar too, but not exactly like, the way a real camera works. The main problem is that it is full of half-executed ideas and mechanics, as it jumps between these influences abruptly and without warning. After a promising start, the game quickly loses steam. The long middle of the game is largely just wandering the environment looking for stuff and taking pictures as the story unfolds. The story is interesting but not exactly exciting or unique (unless you are new to any psychological horror tropes). There are some places where you make "choices" but if those choices have any consequences for the story itself, I'm not sure. As is often the case with psychological horror, you quickly realize your player character is not a reliable narrator, and what you seem to be doing might not be what is actually happening. Unfortunately the game wastes the productive narrative tension and gameplay dissonance from this most basic trope of psychological horror. Instead, you walk through the woods for the umpteenth time to look for a thing to do a thing, etc. It's very tedious and strange.To the earlier Nancy Drew comparison, I wish this game was half as cozy or well-designed as those games, which, are under-appreciated puzzle masterpieces. Unfortunately this game consists of a few Nancy Drew-esque puzzles (including an incredibly frustrating telegraph machine) that ultimately seem to be optional or at least have no bearing on the story as experienced by the player.There are a lot of bizarre choices and elements in this game. One is a bike, which you gain access to sometime in the first half of the game, but is basically unusable because riding it feels like bobsledding while drunk and wearing binoculars. The other is the camera -- introduced as a main item for our character, a part of her characterization, and also as a portal into the narrative drama and horror elements. As I mentioned before, the camera simulator is laughably complex, and was pretty clearly someones labor of love. Unfortunately this game really fails to deliver on any of this. You forgot you have the camera until you need it to advance the story. And you only really need to use it a few times. You're given a ton of camera accessories (lenses, tripods, flash, camera skins, etc) for pretty much no reason at all. I think there was a version of this game that was about capturing paranormal things on camera, which may have been an interesting concept, but got pushed to the side in favor of more (half-baked) ideas.In terms of the scares, they aren't really there. The horror element opens the game, and then disappears until the final act. There are two or three memorable, macabre scenes, that I actually admire the developers for including. This would be fine if the game spent that long, ponderous, middle section actively building tension or atmosphere, but it simply does not. Instead you are just checking boxes and solving pointless puzzles.If you're really into the psychological horror walking-sim thing, like, be my guest and buy this game. But definitely not for more than $10. Just don't expect good puzzles, any scares, or a finished, thoughtful project.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I definitely wasn’t expecting this one. Then again I normally don’t have expectations going into horror games since I tend to avoid any real context on what it is about, so I was quite pleasantly surprised with this being a different kind of horror.ProsA well crafted slow burn tale of grief, trauma and mental illnessWhile normally irrelevant in horror, this is a different kind of horror game and the good graphics enriches the experienceWell executed atmosphere with music, radio broadcasts and news articles that help you feel you are in 1940s Italy and feel the somber tone of what Gulia is going throughIn depth explanations as to how actual photography at the time worked despite the simplified methods used for the game playNeat little puzzle involving the use and deciphering of Morse codeConsThis game gets really dark with its theme, so if you are sensitive to the subject matter the game presents then this is probably not going to be for youSome tones of the voice acting, particularly with the father, feel like they may have been lost a little in translation, recommend playing in the default Italian language with subtitles for the best experienceSo would I recommend this? Absolutely! This is a well crafted experience, however as I said previously this is not going to be for everyone especially. While not really a con, there is almost no replay value for this game outside of achievement hunting or maybe wanting to revisit the story sometime long down the road. Though that’s not what this game sets out to do, it sets out to give you an experience that will linger with you long after the credits roll. That being said this one will be sticking with me for a long time and I rate this game 4 GO HUG YOUR PETS, YOUR FAMILY, YOUR FRIENDS, ALL YOUR LOVED ONES RIGHT F***ING NOW out of 5
