_childDocuments_.review: On paper this seems exactly like my type of game: a scary, narrative heavy, messed up story with critical acclaim. How could this not be a hit? I ended up playing this game twice because initially I felt that my conflicted opinion stemmed from the fact that in my first playthrough I thought this was going to be a ghost story. While there is an element of this, it only makes up a small portion of the story. This game is more of a dramatic story about struggle with mental illness, which is fine, it was just not what I was expecting from watching the trailer. I did find it frustrating though as the initial hook is so unique and interesting I found the premise wasted on what the game actually ends up being. I am not a fan of discussing spoilers in reviews, but the ending has to be discussed in order to provide the context for the entirety of the game and thus my review of it. So warning - heavy spoilers ahead:While the ending is vague it is essentially explained that your twin sister does not exist and she was a manifestation of your character's imagination as a result of a traumatic upbringing with an abusive mother. I think. The ending certainly leaves room for interpretation, but despite me playing this twice, reading the wiki, and watching youtube interpretations, it is not overtly clear what part of this game actually happened. Some people maintain that the game happened but your character created this elaborate “fake twin” plot to deal with the trauma of the actual narrative, but I disagree with this take - the game leans heavy into the “there was no twin” plot twist towards the end, essentially leaving two spins on what the ending is. 1) None of this game happened and your character was just in a mental hospital the whole time. Or 2) Your character never had a twin, she was a manifestation of your character’s trauma. For the sake of breaking down the plot I interpret the game’s ending to indeed suggest that your character’s twin was imaginary, and that most of the game is the result of an unreliable narrator presenting false events to the player. The game does commit to this ending the most, so let's talk about why it is horrible. Quick plot point to provide context: The twins in this game are Gulia and Martha. In the beginning of the game it is Martha who “dies”, with Gulia then pretending to be Martha, so your parents and the community actually think it is Gulia who died.If Martha is imaginary, somewhere like 90% of this game did not actually happen. The first few chapters are about dealing with Gulia’s (but actually Martha’s) funeral: there is a body in a casket and a funeral your character makes preparations for. You listen to your parent’s deal with the grief of losing a child. Multiple other character’s acknowledge that in some capacity you had a sister. All of this has to be hand-waved away as just straight up lying to the audience. The “twins” have their own rooms and own clothes in the house - an argument could be made that your parents were trying to maintain the facade of your character having a twin - but then why later on are they surprised when Gulia reveals to everyone that it was in fact Martha who died. What difference does this make as they only have one child? A portion of this game also deals with Gulia discovering that her boyfriend actually slept with Martha and got her pregnant. Again, fantastic plot point, but this is of no consequence because Martha and Gulia are the same person. This is the recurring theme, the game will present some plot point that may or may not be intriguing, but regardless of what this point is, it ultimately doesn’t matter because it never really happened to begin with. I love a good unreliable narrator twist ending. A great example is “Braid”, where the ending changes your entire perspective on the game up to that point, yet the story still makes sense in this new light. Braid is a terrific case of the unreliable narrator technique being used constructively. Martha Is Dead uses the unreliable narrator technique destructively. So much of the game’s ending is impossible to reconcile with literally every character's behaviour. On my second playthrough I kept an eye out to see if there was clever wording that hints at the ending - but no, every character behaves in a way that is contradictory to the “twist” with no attempt made to explain this contradiction. And at the very end you get a cinematic where your character explains that she recovered and is fine after “everything”. That’s great: what did she recover from? What arc in the story led to this recovery? Moving past the story you are left with some very basic gameplay elements. When not dealing with the plot, the gameplay will consist of:- Dialing the phone (yep…)- Riding a janky bicycle (which is frustrating and got my character stuck a couple of times resulting in my having to reload an earlier save)- Sending and interpreting telegraph Morse-code sequences, where your character deciphers the code by just looking at a piece of paper - Taking and developing photos with your cameraYeah, gameplay is light. Usually I can forgive this if a game’s story can make up for it, but that is not the case here. Now I actually liked the photograph gameplay component of the ones listed above. There was something fun about setting up a shot, using the right attachments, and spending the time to develop the photo. It was mostly automatic but it was cool going through the whole process and seeing the final result (and the photo’s did look very nice once developed). The telegraph quest is by far the worst offender - it is so boring and as much as I hate to admit it, I just turned to a walkthrough guide to quickly get the interpretations. The worst part of all of this is the wasted potential of this game. This is my 2-cents on how to fix the narrative: Commit to the twins existing. Commit to the mistaken identity of which twin actually died. Use this plot point to justify the existence of ghosts and layer this game with creepy ghost sequences and haunted house moments. Use the unreliable narrator technique to confuse the player into which twin you are playing as and which twin died. Throughout the game it can bounce back and forth, and you the character discover things that make you question who you are and why your twin died. Commit to everything in the game happening, we just don’t know which twin it is happening to. This makes the boyfriend plot more interesting (did he cheat on you, did he ever love you to begin with) and the mother plot more interesting (I personally would use this as the ending of the game, your mother meant to kill Gulia but ended up killing Martha - her favourite daughter). This naturally cycles back into the game’s premise of your mother being a terrible person. You then sacrifice your mother to the White-Lady ghost (I didn’t talk much about her as this review is getting long enough as is, but she exists…) and you, your twin’s ghost, and White-Lady reconcile over the similar grief you have felt and the trauma you endured, healing together and allowing everyone to be at peace. This leads to your character’s recovery and justifies her ending monologue about her being ok now. Boom - a satisfying narrative with actual character arc’s and the perfect playground for this game to deliver creepy moments.A couple quick positives: visually the game looks quite nice (not amazing, but definitely nice). There are a number of graphic moments you play through that do hit hard (but are wasted on the game's ending of “not really happening”). The house design is cool, and is complemented by great sound design (and a wonderful soundtrack as well).I am surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews for this game. I love these types of games and I did not enjoy my experience with this one at all.

_childDocuments_.review: was a unique horror game that caught my interest when I first heard it was getting censored on the PS4 due to  current stance on censorship. I, of course, love horror games and I wanted to see what kind of game this would be, there is also a disclaimer that the game gives as soon as you boot it up. This is not for the faint of heart and definitely not for the squeamish, I myself like to explore these types of games so my interest was definitely caught. The game also had some really high ratings on other review websites, so I was expecting something amazing.However, when I played it, I got something else, and I am honestly quite disappointed by the shallow experience that I have gotten, which is what made me put the game down. I will be going into all of this in the review and why I personally think that  is not a horror game.I should also probably make this clear, but I do not play , however, I will not be giving this game a negative review simply because it is one. I am someone who will play any game as long as it’s fun. The only game that I have played that is part of this genre is  and that was an enjoyable experience. I am judging this game with the experience that I have had and nothing more.The story starts out in the year 1944 in , with , who is at a lake taking photos when she sees a lifeless body floating in the river. She swims out to go and rescue the person for her to only find that it’s her sister  and she is dead. However, when her parents come to see her, they mistake the dead body for  and think that  herself, who is alive, is . assumes the role of  so she can feel the love that she never got, as she was abused by her mother, and her father is a soldier who is working with the  in .  will try her best to find the truth as to why her sister died, while she deals with trauma and the loss of war.The story of  had a very interesting start and then it turned into something that I was honestly disappointed with. There will be segments where you can choose how to progress through the story, like one of those choose your own adventure kind of things. However, none of the choices you make matter in the grand scheme of things. If a story allows you to choose your own path, the story should reflect on that and divide different outcomes and endings. You don’t get that in this game, and you only get one ending where nothing you do matters. Also, for some reason,  likes to leave the front door open whenever she leaves. Perfect for any person or demon to walk in and haunt the house. I did like the segment where we enact a recap of the story so far with this grim reaper puppet. The overall design and layout of the segment are really interesting, and I liked it overall. he one thing I will give praise for is the voice acting, it’s really well done, and I even hear that one of the voice actresses is being nominated for an award for their performance. The entire game takes place in  so you will be hearing everything in Italian while you read the subtitles.Now, there is not a whole lot to talk about in terms of gameplay for . That’s not to say that is a bad thing as the game is a walking sim. There is a camera that you will have to use to progress through the story- you will use it to take photos and then you will have to develop those photos by going into the photographic darkroom. Which is rather cool, I liked this feature as it showed us how to develop them.Although that’s all of the positives I can think of in terms of  gameplay. The game has these on-rail moments that make you choose certain words to progress, however, if you choose the wrong one, you must redo the entire segment again. There also are other on-rail moments and none of these feel fun. The issue I have with the gameplay is that there is no failure, even the moments that you think have failure don’t. I don’t feel vulnerable at all in certain situations or threatened. For a horror game like this, I think a sense of dread should be included to make the ghosts you come across threatening.However, the worst aspect of the game is the lack of actual horror elements. It relies on jump scares; these are not considered horror in my opinion unless done correctly. The content is more of a thriller than horror which leaves the feeling that something is not right. The game is disturbing on some levels with the gore, but it is not presented in any new or interesting way. With this said, everyone may not be as used to gore as I, so be cautious with what the game does have in store.The graphics are honestly really beautiful, and I would have loved to spend time admiring the clear-like fields if my experience wasn't affected by a few performance issues.First, I will mention gaming performance, mainly low FPS issues. Even after lowering the graphic settings the problems persist. Draw distance is another issue, it is absolutely horrible; I can stand a few feet away from something and you can see the low resolution with the screenshot I provided.One last issue worth mentioning is the camera movement can end up in pretty awkward positions when panning around with a mouse. I should note that the developers are aware of these problems and plan on fixing them.I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50, with 16 GB of RAM. is an interesting idea on paper, but the execution didn't pan out. I think the experience would be different if they are able to iron out some of the issues that currently break the experience.I ended up putting the game down due to all of these issues and the fact that I was also locked into progressing at a certain point. I know I could have just reset the game to resolve this, but I simply didn't have enough interest in the game's current state. If you truly do want to play it yourself, I recommend getting it when it’s on sale, as the current price of 33.89 CDN with only four hours of content is just not worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: While the historical accuracy of the game is spot on and the lack of censorship is commendable, the side quests relating to the war as well as the developers focus on realistic fascists of life in WW2 Italy, (telegrams, red room development of pictures, and decoding morse) lead to tedious tasks that detract from the main horror theme and eliminates any suspense through long periods of unrelated and boring game play. At its best points the game is a atmospheric and shocking horror with interesting character dynamics and shocking imagery. At it's worst, which takes up most of the game, it is a scatterbrained camera developing and rusty-ass bike riding simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a lot of good and bad things. Starting with the good.It had a great story line. interesting with small twists here and there. It showed difficult topics in a respectful way. Meaning, any difficult topic that was shown was done for story purposes and not to overly upset or intimidate the viewer. It even had trigger warnings on the most intense part and offers a selection to censor it. I enjoyed the story enough to want to play it again. The Bad. It honestly should have been a movie. There is a lot of "gameplay" where youre just sitting and watching and not really controlling much. When you did have control, the game tended to be a bit glitchy and difficult to interact with the enviroment. It had fun minigames, but the tediousness in which the minigames were carried out took away any fun that was had. For instance there is an optional quest where you must send a telegram with morse code. The first part of sending the message was fun and easy. but you then have to decode the telegram and it becomes a little bit more frusterating. Each of the situations like this alone are not too bad and would be minor if every mini game and quest turned into this annoying chore simulator. Even the picture taking mechanic was fun at first and so was developing the photos but it turned into a chore when you had to do this for every single photo you took. overall i would play the game again if there was some of the bugs fixed and the games changed a little bit. Maybe making photos in batch, or what have you.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you play Martha Is Dead? Yes, when it’s patched.In the crowded market of first person indie horror games, Martha Is Dead stands out with its breathtaking visuals, historical setting, and haunting atmosphere. Gameplay-wise, it’s about what you’d expect from a walking-sim. But the camera mechanic is a fun little distraction, keeping the experience from becoming stale. My misgivings about the second half aside, I can definitely say, overall, that I found the story engaging, and Giulia makes for a darkly compelling protagonist. It's a shame that the performance is so unstable. The frequent stutters, frame drops, and freezes prevent me from recommending the game at full price. Give it a few months, then pick it up. _childDocuments_.review: Clear case of suffering from over-ambition. Strangely disproportionate usage of resources and effort can be seen all throughout this title. A lot of budget seems to have gone into cloth physics and the player model but not into NPC facial animations. If this game is striving to be artistic, then it has a pretty funny idea of what that looks like. Yeah it's art. The art of hiding characters from the player while trying to sell this immersive tale all at the same time.Had they cut out one or two thirds of this game the pacing and overall quality would've been better for it. Aside from that... The Town of Light is easily the developer's better experience with a much more iconic atmosphere. I care about atmosphere and presentation a lot when approaching the horror genre. And this just made me feel nothing more than what I could've gotten out of a random WWII Italian drama.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for such a long time for this game to come out. So much so I had planned on scheduling this game entirely around the launch.I am a full time horror streamer, and have been passionate about horror and stories revolving deep topics since my childhood.This in short, is one of the most massive misses I have EVER experienced. I would much rather play one of those god awful off brand $2 horror thrown together messes than ever giving this a second thought, and my god have I played some pretty AWFUL games. Both laughable, and in taste.You all had so much opportunity to tell such a beautiful story, to touch our hearts with something we could relate to, and even wrap it up in a really interesting time piece. It could have been meaningful. All you did was use trauma as a crutch and not only that but continuously shoved it down our throats until we got sick and tired of looking. I had to literally close your game during the stream in the middle of one of the scenes as the only place it was going, was down. I kept pushing through about 7 hours just in hope that there would be some point to it all.To top all of that off, the mechanics were absolutely AWFUL. It was broken, and beyond poorly optimised.I'm extremely disappointed in you guys, to my absolute core.Next time, please take a lighter touch with trauma.Edit: This is specifically referencing shoving the dog in a boiling pot of water and forcing her daughter to eat it, and slapping her until she did. This has nothing to do with the setting of war, or the undoing of her mental state because of it. The plot was understood and I was on board with it from the beginning, until we hit that part of the game. As it was completely irrelevant to me and unnecessary.So when I say "a lighter touch" I mean stick to what's relevant in telling the story. I'm not sure boiling dogs and forcing kids to eat it...pushes that..

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely, this is a horror game. But this is not a screamers case. I tell you about suspense and feeling of approaching something horrible. She starts her own investigation to find the truth. The game is not for everybody because of disturbing content. The developers say about that everywhere. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A walking simulator with an overall weak plot sold on "MUCH DISTURBING, VERY EDGE" marketing.Pretty much what it says on the "TL;DR". Most of the "disturbing" moments within the game are, quite frankly, neither disturbing nor meaningful, but rather tasteless and exploitative; the game's plot consists entirely of these scenes and an ending twist, which I assume everyone over 18 saw coming from a mile away.The only saving grace consists of a few moments with interesting imagery, especially near the end. _childDocuments_.review: Last night I started Martha is Dead, streaming some of it on BEAM. Today, I had a feeling that it wasn't the best sort of game to stream, due to the subject matter: Mental health.Today I finished it, and I have to say that I am glad I didn't stream the rest. It covered some horrific issues and didn't shy away from any of them.Martha is Dead is a walking simulator with some simple exploration puzzles, but nothing that proves too difficult.Everything in the game is designed to push the story forward, allowing you to make certain choices (most of which still push you into the direction of the main plot) that range from the banal chores of everyday life, to the gruesome triggering horror that seems all the more disturbing because it's based around the mental health of the main character.After you find your twin sister Martha dead in a local lake you are taken on a trip in a stunning Italian landscape in the grip of World War II. Your family tries to carry on as the world around falls apart and as you progress through the story you get hit with one shocking twist after another.I thought I had the story figured out pretty quickly, but as is the case with well-told tales, I was wrong. The darkest thoughts in my head - the ones that should never see the light of day - are what this tale is about. The taboo of a person's mental health deteriorating at a drastic pace, when it was probably never great to begin with. I've played a lot of harrowing tales, but this is only the second time that I felt horrified at the things that can happen to people (the first being another Italian game called The Town of Light) when they really have nowhere to turn for help.All of this torment is covered with a veneer of a stunningly realised rural Italy, with a soundtrack and environmental audio to match. Walking in the woods, you could close your eyes and swear you were there. Walking through their rustic home, you can hear clocks in another room and floorboards creaking as your weight bears down on them.Little touches like realistic fabric physics on your character's clothes are something you rarely see, but if you look at her shadow whilst walking, you can see the flow of the material. There is so much love poured into this game.But there is one caveat to all this.There are performance issues galore in Martha is Dead. The longer you play, the worse they get, leading me to think there are memory bleed issues (and I had one crash with an error code that said as much). The odd thing is that whilst in the dense woodlands, the frame-rate was better than inside the house.If you can persevere, it's a tale worth being part of.Another word of warning though. There are scenes of graphic self-harm and stuff that is much darker, so if you are in a fragile state of mind, you may find it hard to stomach.If you are okay with that, and the performance drops, I'd say give it a go. It's not happy, but it's a story that has a lot of heart and hard work behind it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be frank about the game. Do I recommend it? Surprisingly yes. But only to people who were fine with narrative games like Hideo Kojima's Death Stranding.To me the game narrative was amazing and the gruesome interactive sequences did make me squeamish and uncomfortable. But the game also heavily advertised on horror and paranormal folklore as much as it did on the mystery narrative. To me that was a mistake and feels almost clickbait-y. I bought the game excited for the horror sequences after playing the demo but the horror and gruesome moments occurred very solemnly and spanned across hours of gameplay between one another. I took maybe 16 hours to complete the game and I think I could count all the gruesome scenes on one hand where maybe only 2 of those moments were actually interactive if I remember correctly. As a narrative and story driven game it's fantastic, as an exploration game the scenery and audio is mesmerizing. But the game falls flat for me on the horror.I was expecting something like the game Layers of Fear, a game that will keep you on your toes with tension while being capable of finding a way to either release that suspense without cheap jump scares or a game capable of building off it. But anytime the game seemed like it would pick up horror wise, it'd soon find myself back to walking around and photographing/locating things that would help continue the murder solving narrative. This honestly made the game come off as boring at times. There wasn't enough interactive gruesome bits and the white lady of the lake while frequently mentioned is barely interacted with.10/10 narrative plot10/10 sceneric/audio visuals7/10 on the horror. And this is me being modest because of how well the few scenes that were scary were delivered. There are better horror games for cheaper, and at this price I seriously only recommend this game if you're interested in a narrative, almost cinematic experience because that is the only thing this game manages to deliver amazingly on

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I would not recommend the game, I will start with elements I liked about it, as I do appreciate the massive effort going into such productions even if the end result is not something to my liking.I think the setting was done very well, and it was an interesting choice. In general I do not enjoy war-themed stories that much, but it was used here as a background rather than a focal point. I really liked seeing the general's house and what kind of standards were considered as being well off in those times. I played with Polish subs and Italian voiceovers and the voices were done really well I thought. I cannot understand the language, apart maybe from a few words, but I enjoyed the voiceovers a lot still.When it comes to why I would not recommend, I want to start with gameplay side - which was very scarce. There were a lot of moments where interactiveness did not seem needed, and was even annoying (like the marionnettes). Tons of scenes could have been cutscenes really and at the end I felt maybe it would have been better as a movie than trying to be a game.The graphics are very nice, but the game isn't optimised too well, even after few patches made since the release. The bicycle riding was quite unpleasant, so I barely used it, and saw in some other reviews people were getting stuck and needed to reload.How the menu UI works isn't very intuitive and simple actions like objectives checking was an annoying task as a result.Taking and developing photos mechanic was kind of nice to start with, but I did not enjoy that much repeating it too many times. I was glad some parts of it were skippable.I had some trouble with the telegraph puzzle, it's possible Polish subs were not optimal to make it fully cohesive.The plot was intriguing and I liked a bit of uncertainty whether paranormal was the actual activity in teh setting, or just the character's imagination. However, at the end I felt robbed of conclusion and understanding what has really happened.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game that unfortunately didn't stick the landing, especially given the 30 dollar price tag. 5/10This game has a lot of fantastic ingredients- An interesting camera mechanic, some beautiful art, a few novel ways to convey a story. But it just doesn't pull them together well enough in the end for anything to really stick with me. Ends up falling into some unsatisfying psychological horror cliches that left the story lacking for the substance needed to carry the dull gameplay loop. The last minute of the game gave me tonal whiplash, feels like the devs realized the ending they'd cornered themselves into wasn't something they weren't comfortable subjecting the general public to (fair enough, I can definitely see where they were coming from given one of this game's major themes is trauma) so they had to quickly make a U-turn.Ultimately the game ended up being 'meh' for me. _childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead is not a horror game. If you are looking for jumpscares and the likes, look elsewhere. Martha is Dead is not a shooter, not a RPG, not an action game. If you want to 360 No Scope, talk to a lot of NPC's or smash buttons, look elsewhere. It is also not for the faint of heart. It's not without reason the developers have put a warning at the beginning of the game, provide a  for those that feel the need to seek help and have censored certain parts of the game. The game deals with some very serious topics, not in the least child/animal abuse. So please, heed these warnings before you play!So what is Martha is Dead? In my humble opinion only one of the best games ever made. It tells you a psychological story. A story about a young woman (Giulia) in 1944 Tuscany. A story about her mind and what goes on inside of it while she tries to find out what happened to her twin sister (Martha). You are taken on a trip deep into her mind and at the end you're left wondering what was real and what wasn't. What really happened to Martha and if she was even real in the first place. Personally, I couldn't help but feel for Giulia at the end. For everything she had gone through in her life and what that had done to her mentally.The game is visually stunning. The devs have really captured the feel of Tuscany during summer. I love how you walk around the area and really feel like you're there. The music is absolutely beautiful and fits every scene. The implementation of the camera into the gameplay is one I found very interesting. Taking pictures, developing them to further the story is a very nice touch. A few collectables to get, a couple of side quests, but these aren't too difficult. All in all you can play through and get all achievements in about 6 to 8 hours. I'd recommend to play without a guide the first time to really immerse yourself into Giulia's mind.Seriously, play this game!10/10 (I've just started to play this on Steam. I have 40+ hours on Xbox in this game)

_childDocuments_.review: While the advertising focuses a lot on the shocking and horrific elements, it would be more accurate to describe this game as a mystery thriller set against the backdrop of Nazi-occupied Italy during WWII (which is a bit of a mouthful so I guess psychological horror works too). The story is the game's greatest strength, focused on the journey of Giulia as she uncovers the mystery of her sister, Martha's, death. It really manages to hook you from the opening once you find her body in the lake, and as you discover more details related to the event it pulls you deeper in until the very end where all becomes clear, relatively speaking. Honestly given the themes and topics this game tackles it makes sense that the ending is unclear, as well as the events that transpired; it allows the player to fully process the story as a whole and it opens up to repeat playthroughs to appreciate how the greater reveal works as you play with the ending in mind. The way it handles mental illness and struggling with trauma is both haunting and sad, and the time period is incredibly important in making this work when you look at certain details (like the prescription drugs found all over the house). Even as I type this I'm still thinking about it and trying to understand what is real and what isn't, but with Guilia as our narrator we truly won't know will we? And as she accepts her actions in the end, neither will she. But the hope that she has grown and moved past those events is the light at the end of an otherwise bleak narrative. I genuinely appreciate games like this that bring to light struggles that comparitively few people face in order to have the majority reach a wider understanding. If I had to compare this to another game it would be Hellblade in that it uses a genre (psychological horror/action-adventure) as a vehicle to tell a deeper narrative.Although the gameplay isn't the focus of these games, I unfortunately must mention how the gameplay in Martha is Dead is pretty straightforward and poorly optimized. I don't have the current top of the line rig, but an i9 and 3070 gtx should be more than enough to have this game running smoothly. And yet I would have egregious frame drops as the map still has to load in, times where dialogue would run over a game running 5 frames a second until its all loaded and it starts to play catch-up, and multiple times where I would see the map loading in real time from a blurry mess to the gorgeous graphics it touts. Make no mistake, the game is beautiful, but it needs a few more minutes after it's done loading to actually be done loading, if you know what I mean. Also, performance issues aside, as I mentioned the game doesn't ask much of you as a player to do. It's a walking sim through and through where most of the time you're exploring an environment to find the next piece needed to progress. For the story it wants to tell this is more than fine, but for it to have performance issues when it doesn't demand that much? It does bring the game down a bit for me.All in all, if this game does interest you, I would advise to wait for a sale, solely because two years after its release it still has performance issues. But I do believe if you push through it you will find a good, unique story here that is well worth the time to invest in.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Martha is Dead' is an incredibly well written story with a few twists down the line, some more predictable than others, all the while diving deep into the human mind and how it could lead us down a twisted path. There were a lot of unique elements that I've never seen in a horror game before and were used up to perfection to present the story at hand. Some of the quests felt like chores but they didn't take away from the overall experience. Played the entire game in Italian and I was surprised how good the voice actors did, certainly added a lot. The dialogue/monologue is interesting and keeps you invested the entire time. There is a lot of explicit and gory scenes that I feel were needed to explain what the human mind can conjure up. The graphics look amazing and a lot of detail and attention was poured into small things that you don't often see in most indie titles. Definitely recommend picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator and it's a little bit slow at first but the descent into insanity will hit you hard. One of the very few actual "psychological horror" games. That is to say it is the actual psyche of the character that turns on itself. Rather than most games were some external source is being applied to the character causing insanity or some other issue. The gameplay is about uncovering a mystery and it consists of mainly walking around and interacting with various objects. The story of the game is the focus here so actual gameplay takes a backseat, but that is ok for games like this. There were alot of warnings when you start up the game about "graphic scenes" that will upset some people and apparently this game got media coverage for some graphic scenes or something but I dunno to me this game was very lax in terms of graphic depictions. It does have some pretty messed up things happen in the game but if you can watch a standard R rated movie im sure nothing in this game is going to upset you. The story is really good and dives into actual mental illness as well as how war can directly affect innocent people that have nothing to do with said war. I read some reviews saying the game length doesn't justify the price and that is completely insane to me. This game has actual heart and soul put into it, and for 6+ hours of entertainment with a story that you WILL be thinking about for weeks to come the price is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha is Dead follows a new yet familiar take on horror games, staying away from cliche jump scares and predictable plots.The game combines puzzle-solving, semi-open world exploration, and even QTE (Quick-Timed Events) sequences.The story told throughout the game was phenomenal. This aspect of unraveling the unknown is what I genuinely love about the genre of horror and mystery, may it be through movies or video games. The game tells its story in memories that the main character can remember. This writing and storytelling style is a genius way of sparking the curiosity from players, leaving them with the itch to play more.For a non-triple A title, the graphics were top-notch. Everything seems polished from the beginning of the game up to the free-roaming segment. The details and lighting are crisp, clean, and well presented. There are parts of the game where I was like, "This looks realistic as heck."Martha Is Dead's sound design is one of the game's best aspects for me. It presents constant tension throughout the game when it's needed (i.e., exploring the woods at night.). With the birds' melodic chirping to the ravens' harsh grating sounds, the game truly feels alive even during day time.The atmosphere provides a safe yet constant feeling of distraught through certain game moments. When that continuous feeling of distraught is about to break, it doesn't bring out cliche moments like jumpscares to burst the bubble per se. The game does an outstanding job of not opting for a jumpscare; instead, it goes for a more creepy and memorable horror moment.Martha Is Dead is an excellent psychological-horror game with its unique tackle on the horror and mystery genre. It's sure to deliver a great and memorable experience to horror fans out there.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I was looking forward to this game, I can't recommend it.Graphically the game is beautiful. I ran into a few places where elements of the terrain didn't line up properly and grey light shone through, I had to disable Ray Tracing after day 2 because the reflective surfaces became super-luminous, and despite playing on my GFs i7/3060 PC on a 4k TV the only resolution option I was given was 720p even with RT and DLSS disabled. But the level of detail is amazing and the world is well crafted and completely believable. Exploration can be frustrating. Walking speed is comparable to other games crouch speed and sprinting is comparable to other games walking. There is a bike that is supposed to allow you to cover long distances faster but it's barely faster than your sprint speed and can only really be used for two short sections nearer the end of the game. There are also many invisible walls that impede exploration that can make navigating the woods were most of the game takes place incredibly frustrating.Many objectives are missing markers or waypoints and interactive elements in the environment can be very finicky to position for the contextual prompt to activate. On the positive side, the camera and telegraph mechanics are actually really well done and were some of my favourite parts of the game. Whilst the game starts out seeming as if it will be dealing with more classic spooky horror, this mostly falls away within the first 20 minutes or so and largely deals with shock and gore horror, either relating to the characters mental health or the horrors of war. Whilst this is a great concept and something I was aware of before purchasing, the game seems to lose it's direction about half way through and becomes increasingly incoherent in its story telling. There are a couple of "side quests" whose progress is locked out until new areas become accessable but this is never communicated to the player leaving you wandering around until you give up and return to the main quest. Things do greatly improve in the last 20 minutes or so, but doesn't have the intended impact due to the previous half the game, as well as a couple of side quests which if incomplete, the game assumes they weren't started leading to characters saying things that don't make sense given the objectives that you have completed.*MINOR SPOILER WARNING* The end sequence is also slightly ruined by a pop up content warning advising of scenes of self harm, which seems completely pointless when the game has already showed execution by hanging, shooting, death from explosion and several graphic scenes of corpse mutilation.*END SPOILER*If you really want to check this out, I'd recommend waiting for a hefty discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the gameplay aspects, the graphics were gorgeous and it really did evoke a sense of being in Tuscany in 1944. I do think some things were missed that added a lot of context; for instance, the medication her mother was using is methamphetamine. Which explained so much about the mother, but unless you know that or google it, it's lost on the player. Similarly, seeing it beside Martha's bed on the floor and in the box. This has implications which are potentially lost to the unaware which could provide more context for character actions.Pros: Beautiful graphicsGood voice over (highly recommend keeping it in Italian)Fun gameplay mechanics - camera, Morse code.Very time capsule like - It's like stepping into the time period, a lot of love was put into ensuring this was accurate.Haunting atmosphere without the need for jump scares - refreshing in a jumpscare-tastic gaming industry.Cons:Some parts dragged on a bit too much, the puppets for example.The area is far too big with not enough to do in it. - The woods are sprawling and beautiful, but there is not that much to do within, so it made the woods seem a bit lifeless in terms of it just...being there to walk around in and admire the graphics.It seems to villainize mental health disorders - It surely seems like a cause to be celebrated; greater representation in the media of mental illnesses and mental health. But. despite warnings and links to mental health sites, the game does, at least in my opinion, villainize mental health disorders, namely DID and/or schizophrenia/Paranoia etc. I didn't feel like it was telling a poignant story about the struggles of mental health and what that entails, but more that it was leaning toward the cliche of 'mental health disorders turn people into raging murderers with delusions'. The focus seemed more on the gore, rather than what abuse and living through a horrific war did to the main character and the fear that must have come with being the daughter of a high ranking German official (It was touched on, but not much and the game says nothing on this fact other than showing us a lot of Nazi flags when in reality, it could have served as being much more thought provoking. It lacked any underlying substance). I think, if it had been accompanied by more concrete evidence rather than hearsay, it would have been more thought-provoking and shined a much better light on mental health. Instead it seemed to skim over the abuse and trauma for the main character to remind us that she was 'crazy'.As it stands, it's following a classic media trope of stigmatizing mental health disorders into simply 'this character is mad/insane'. I do not feel that the game shed much light on the complexity and fragility of the mind with regard to the subjects in the game. A lot of mainstream media show various mental health conditions personified as evil and I feel Martha Is Dead has, unfortunately, leaned into this trope. For decades, horror films and games have used 'madness' and 'psychotic' as their variation on evil and horror and falsely perpetuated the notion that mental conditions commonly lead to violence against others. Something Martha Is Dead leans heavily into.Martha Is Dead also seems to perpetuate the continuing confusion about the relationship between schizophrenia and dissociative identity disorder, as the game seemingly teeters between the two with its implications and hearsay, with a lack of solid evidence and research. Compared to games like Hell blade, who put in a lot of research to ensure Schizophrenia was portrayed accurately, I feel as if Martha Is Dead pulled a trope from a hat and simply went with it. It feels like little thought was put into the consequences of trying to depict mental illness without enough research backing it up. This is not to say that it was done on purpose, more that it feels like a smaller team with a large idea perhaps didn't put in as much thought as they could have with regard to what they were trying to portray. Sadly, at least in my opinion, Martha Is Dead is continuing a stigma on mental illness. As a result, I feel the story, while starting off strongly with a lean toward the supernatural, fell short and could leave people feeling frustrated. There is no real satisfactory ending, rather one which makes you feel like what you did was meaningless while you try and piece together a story with parts missing or without context. People with schizphrenia or DID or severe mental health disorders, don't flip between types of symptomatic behavior like a rolodex and the fact that mental health is the big reveal at the end of the game is really disappointing.Quite frankly, I was disappointed that it didn't stick more with the mother and her addiction or just go full supernatural. Dramatization of mental health may serve as entertainment for many, but the impact of that is far reaching and harmful. Do I recommend this game if you're looking for something impactful about mental health? No. Do I reccommend this game if you're just looking for gore with little substance and/or reasoning behind said gore? Haunting music and atmosphere and beautiful scenery? Yes!

_childDocuments_.review: ★½Let me start this review by stating that I truly enjoy the walking simulator genre. My favourite game of all time is Death Stranding, which obviously isn't your conventional walking simulator, but I also love games like Layers of Fear or Firewatch. Now, this game has some incredible graphics, an unbelievably realistic art style, and one of the most hauntingly beautiful soundtracks that I've heard in a video game. The setting is also interesting and allows for some interesting character backgrounds and motivations. However, that is about where my praise for the game ends. This game was seriously exhausting and excruciatingly boring. Firstly, similar to many other reviewers, I experienced horrible optimization issues and was plagued by low FPS throughout my entire playthrough. I also experienced multiple instances where I had to close and reload the game because it either completely froze or questlines would break and would not allow me to progress. To relate back to my original comment about walking simulators, I think many of the gameplay aspects of this game should have been left out of the game (and allowed it to only be a walking simulator), as many of these mechanics were either inconsequential or excruciatingly tedious. There are game components that I do not think that you should have the player do, and should just perform them for the player. The camera was an interesting mechanic for the first few times, but is only used 4-5 times throughout the entire story, but the worst mechanic was the telegraph. You had to fully code and decode morse code messages, which took an incredible amount of time and was not fun as a gameplay mechanism at all. I also played the game in the native Italian language and I thought the voice acting was subpar, where the main actress did not feel emotionally invested and provided emotion and enthusiasm in the wrong places. Furthermore, I feel as though the story is more akin to an audiobook than playing a video game. The main story beats are told through text on a black screen and major plot points are either told in this method or skipped over so quickly you are not given enough time to emotionally process them. Similarly, I don't think the story itself is meaningful, powerful, or important in any way. The story is terribly shallow and told in  way that does not properly emphasize or draw importance to . Finally, the ending is probably the worst part of the entire game. The last ~30 minutes are probably one of my least favourite video games moments ever. The entire story is poorly summarized in a puppet show (telling the story that we have already seen and telling it in a really poor medium). The ending itself does not pack the deep emotional punch that they think it does or that it should based on the subject matter. Moreover, the gore and extreme visuals feel as though they're added just for the sake of having them present rather than beginning importance to the story or themes. Ultimately, I expected a lot more from this game and felt like it severely underdelivered and was definitely disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: While everything below are things I stand by, I finished the game today and it actually got way, way better. Even though those small issues that annoy me are still there, the story is absolutely worth it. The puzzles are good, the story got me intrigued, the atmosphere is superb. So wonky gameplay aside, I like this game. 7.5/10This game confuses me...POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD, READ THE REVIEW WITH CAUTIONThe game does some things well and some things not so well. But the thing is that the things it does well, it does really well, but the things that it does poorly it does atrociously bad.Take for instance the morse code section; when developing photos, the game tells you at least 4 times, if not more, that it's more complicated in real life but they toned it down in the game for the sake of the player. Then about 45 minutes later you have to communicate using morse code, and you actually have to decipher and decode the messages you get back. So, they "dumb down" one part of the game to make it less tedious for the player, but they keep another part as real as possible which just really made me want to refund the game instantly because that section was painfully boring and annoying.Also, the majority of the cutscenes are way longer than they need to be. Instead of just saying "Hmm, maybe I should go to the shed", your character might say "Me and my sister used to spend so much time at the old shed. If I should go anywhere, it's there. The shed is the obvious place for me to look at. Yes, I should go there. To the shed, I go" in an unskippable cutscene, and she also talks very slowly so it all takes way, way longer than it needs to.On the other hand, the story is really interesting, the graphics are well made, the game is very beautiful and intriguing, and it makes me want to come back for more. And like I said, the gameplay mechanics they got right, they absolutely nailed! It's just that the bad parts are sooooo bad, it's almost undescribable.I don't know if I recommend this game. If you like a game with a fantastic story that keeps you interested and you don't mind a sea full of terrible flaws, then this is a game for you. Otherwise, maybe not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can cope with the heavy subject matter and gruesomeness of some of its brutal segments, Martha Is Dead is a decent horror experience but with some major drawbacks. On the positive side the narrative is really intense and deals with very serious issues, things most horror games are afraid to delve into. It's not for everyone, it's hard to even say you enjoyed a game like this, but the overall message is an important one to hear and I have the utmost respect for the developers. As a video game though, it's mainly a slog unfortunately. Everything is very slow and tedious, you crawl around at a snails pace and there just isn't much there from a gameplay mechanics perspective. Would have liked to see more puzzles such as the morse code bit. The game is also very beautiful but even on top tier hardware(rtx3080,12900k, 32gbb ddr5, m.2 ect) I experienced stuttering and frame drops throughout much of the game, very immersion breaking. The story is strong enough to carry the runtime though, it's that good. The music is also alluring and the atmosphere overall is okay, sometimes though the game is just way too quite like I could hear my button inputs over my headphones, not good. The puppet theatre is prob my favorite part honestly really creepy/disturbing. In the end especially for the kinda steep entry fee, i'm mainly giving this a thumbs up because of the message/subject matter the game brings up. good story but missing the mark otherwise. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game overall. I really enjoyed the story, I kept wanting to continue the game to understand it and learn a bit more about it. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Check the price first. If you find it at a discount or desperately want a psychological horror game that feels very grounded, go for it.I will try not to spoil this one for anyone interested.MiD is about a sister (Giulia) who finds her twin sister (Martha) dead in the lake and, at first, by sheer shock, agrees to say that she is indeed Martha (who was deaf). What slowly unfolds is a tale of psychological horror that sticks with you for one reason or another. The game is set in late 1984, you are part of an Italian family that supports Nazi Germany.Before that though, let's delve into not so serious issues.Gameplay wise, the game is more of a walking simulator, and I mean that in a good way. Your "quests" so to speak are rather rudimentary; Go there, do this, come back. Giulia has a camera at her disposal that allows her to not only document things that she sees in her daily life, but also uncover the truth behind the events that occur throughout the 6 hours it takes to finish the game. The camera manipulation was surprisingly accurate, including different lenses, manipulation of focus, aperture and shutter speed and choosing the right ISO film. The most interactive bit of the game I would say comes from a quest that involves using Morse Code; sending a message is rather easy, but decoding it makes the ordeal much more challenging. In gameplay terms, my biggest gripe is how some of the quests are handed out; you will be given a task that involves say opening a door, but the solution to it is way further ahead within the story, which can lead to frustration. Overall, I think I can describe the gameplay to feel like an artisan craft. Technically, it feels as if it's one scripted scene away from being broken, but never really does.Graphics and sound wise, MiD has its ups and downs. I'd wager the game makes heavy use of photogrammetry to capture some of the landscape, as it all looks and feels great to the eye overall. It's not a technical wonder by any means, but it works well. What doesn't work well however, is performance; the average FPS is not the problem, but rather the stuttering. You would think that using the Unreal Engine for so long, someone would just find a proper solution for it, but it seems not. Add the framedrops, and the abhorrent performance when enabling Ray Tracing (which tbh, I had a hard time finding a proper difference), and you will just have to learn to deal with it. Sound design also has its issues; While the voices are well acted (and I appreciate being able to have the original italian VO with English subs - perfect practice), they would oftentimes get muffled by some other sound in the background, or be played offset to the location that they are in, relative to your perspective. These aspects were not gamebreakers, but they did not help.The story is where MiD shines, yet also trips. The game tells the story of a VERY unreliable narrator, where choices SEEM to matter, but really they do not. What's mostly gripping about the story however is when you realize just how twisted Giulia is, and why that occurs. Sadly though, it resorts to gore and macabre to do so, which I felt was a bit cheap when the story doesn't necessarily need the shock factor to hit home. That said, do be aware that mental illness is at the forefront of this game and pulls no punches in that regard.So, in the end what we have is a game that feels handcrafted, with a slow burner of a story that ends up hitting home when it needed it the most.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really hard game to finish because it made me feel so messed up for most of it! It's a very personal story that touches on family abuse, mental health, child trauma's, human perversions, body gore, symbolism and much more. This game requires you to witness every messed up part that you can imagine and interact with it the whole time making you part of the action like no other game that I've seen or heard of before... What's also interesting is that this game doesn't depict these topics freely or without merit! Everything is done in a very realistic and necessary way that works with the story and it left me speechless and uneasy which is a very hard thing to do because I've gotten used to a lot as a video game consumer. I've played countless horror experiences and nothing came to be as traumatizing and as memorable as this game was and I'm really greatful for it! Another main reason why this game is so effective is because it puts you in plausible scenarios and forces you to do the exact thing that you don't want to do making it scary and uncomfortable where most games would use metaphors or background text describing what happened to ease the experience and therefore making it less impactful. This game will remain in my memory for a long time and, for what it's worth, I believe that its an amazing game in all the right ways! If you're still wondering if this game is for you then I'll ask you one question: If you had to feel and see some of the worst that mankind has to offer, would you be happy that you were able to experience that feeling from the comfort of your home and not by living it as some people have or are currently living it? If your answer is yes than this is probably your kind of psychological horror and you should consider this title. If this question made you uncomfortable or you're looking for any other type or intensity of horror experience than don't play this game! Lastly, if someone offers to show you this game for fun, don't do it! This game can mess you up if you're not a mentally strong person!

_childDocuments_.review: Intensely immersive and thought-provoking psychological horror.I will compare it to two titles. First, this game is superficially extremely similar to LKA's previous release, . Both games explore madness associated with sexual promiscuity and volatile mother-daughter relationships in the context of World War II fascism, and both take place in a building surrounded by rural nature in Italy. In many ways  can be understood as a remake and a rewrite of , a new attempt to tackle the same topic. Indeed it feels quite different: 's plot occurs during the descent, not after it, and is far more visceral and immediate. It wants you to be inside the deeply troubled mind of the protagonist, and not just to observe it as was the case in .I would also compare this game to Guillermo del Toro's film, . There, too, is an attempt at penetrating the trauma of life under fascism through the psychotic fantasies of a young woman. But in this comparison  falls short as it ambitiously forwards an unconvincing equivalence between the Nazis and the Italian Partisans, portraying them as indistinguishable twin siblings emerging from mutual trauma. It's an interesting academic exercise, but it's not unproblematic to portray sympathy towards Nazis. Unfortunately, 's writing isn't deft enough to deal with this challenge and disturbingly dangling questions remain as to what it says or fails to say about Nazism.The writing is also not deft enough to deal constructively with mental illness. It seems that Sony forced LKA to include warnings and triggers, and so like in a lot of "psychological horror" the beams get crossed. On the one hand we are asked to treat sickness with sympathy and respect. On the other hand the game gratuitously sensationalizes and even glorifies it for our entertainment. Let's be honest: horror is not the right genre to tackle mental illness. So, don't even try, because the result is always accompanied by insincerity.Let's talk about what works. The visual design is gorgeous. Play with raytracing if you can and lose yourself in this idyllic, atmospheric countryside cottage by a lake. Much of the game is about taking photos and developing them in a dark room, and the attention to the details of the process is delightful. There are also telegraph decryption and tarot reading mini-games that are likewise satisfyingly detailed without being tedious. What works less well is the quest design. Some poorly placed cues and map bugs make it seem like you're supposed to go looking for things when you can't, or they point you in the wrong direction.  suffered from this, too, so it's definitely something LKA needs to work on.Writing is also hit and miss. Some poorly edited scenes diminish the grandeur of the best ones. And the voice acting, at least in English, is somewhat mediocre. It doesn't seem like the actors were getting proper direction, if at all.Despite the flaws, the sum totality of this game's storytelling is devastating. I won't soon forget what I saw and will continue to second guess myself as to what really happened.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall,  is a fantastic example of a psychological thriller. It achieves horror in clever and sinister ways that linger in the player’s mind, avoiding tropes such as jump scares. The narrative is dark and layered and there is a kind of disturbed pleasure afforded by exploring it that is not found in many other games. Similarly, the visual and audio elements are beautiful and immersive, even in the most unsettling and gory parts.Spanning a range of gameplay and narrative genres, Martha is Dead has wide appeal, it is stunning and horrific and will haunt players long after they finish playing. It will take around 6-8 hours to complete but has some replayability in terms of choices made in-game, missable quests and achievements. As the content warnings suggest, this game may not be for everyone but I heartily recommend this game to fans of dark emotional interactive fiction and cleverly scary horror games.My full review of this game., where I go into detail about gameplay,. narrative and styling can be found on .

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game with a good story. Totally recommended. It is not perfect however, but more on that below.Good:- Story. It is actually a very well-written one with a good ending and good atmosphere. People who say that it is too violent or gross are, probably, people who never experienced things similar to what is displayed in the game - but I did (including self-harm and child abuse), and I think that dialogues, thoughts of the main character and overall presentation are very real and natural. Puppet shows are amazing in terms of how bluntly they express childhood traumas - and I also could relate to this, with the only exception being that I do not need to remember because I never forget.- Some interesting mechanics such as using the telegraph, developing photos, or using camera accessories. They do a great job of immersing yourself into the game.- Little details which show how much attention was put into the game. There are a lot of them, but the one which surprised me the most is the black stain on the front tooth of the main character during just a few of the cutscenes which had a close-up of her face. Might not sound like much, but the game is full of things like this and it really helps with believing the story.Not so good:- Stuttering. I am starting to hate UE more and more, and this game was another example of why. No matter what I did - it stuttered from start to finish, and it would not be such a big deal if it was not accompanied with cases of mouse skipping.- Texture issues. For some reason, the wall textures of the house got broken starting with the second chapter and remained like this until the end of the game. Again, ♥♥♥♥ UE.- Some mechanics which I talked about positively above are not really utilized that often. _childDocuments_.review: While this game is beautiful and has some unique elements to it (the photography and personal journey) it falls flat for me. This is another psychological horror game where a character has a mental illness and is a murderer because of it. I wish we could get horror games that throw away the trope of demonizing mental disorders. (Hellblade is an example of an indie game which took on a huge research effort to accurately portray schizophrenia and mental illness to their players.) The devs try to take the time to illustrate how horrible "mental asylums" were back in the day, and even the medications people were put on, but they don't lend the physical experience to players---it's all done in exposition diary-entry style narration---which is a real missed opportunity.This game really isn't scary. It's a walking simulator with an unraveling narrative given to the player by the protagonist. However, I did not experience any bugs and I feel that the developers did try to have heart in the right places, but the execution focused on high-intensity gore and confusion. If you like spending time in a slower paced environment, this game is worth a try. Otherwise I'd get it on sale or look elsewhere for your tension-string needs.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the performance issues, the story did keep me captivated long enough to finish. While it wasn't a long game, it was indeed performative. Gameplay was indeed minimal and i would be lying if i said otherwise. The gameplay is merely a vehicle for which the developers allow the progression of the story they wished to tell.A story of deceit, sadness, self reflection, and of course realization. The game starts off as quite a mystery, and as the story progresses you are left with more and more questions. By the end everything is seemingly answered. A few are left for subjective interpretation.I will give this games story a solid 8/10. However due to performance issues i will have to give an overall score of 6/10. Still above average and after a couple updates this game will be easily an 8 or 9. Graphics are of course very well detailed and you can tell a lot of work went into it. Sound was fairly well done. Voice acting was done fairly well. Some of the animation could have used a bit of work, but they were so minor that it didn't really detract from the overall experience. This kinda of game isn't really about the gameplay but instead the delivery of a captivating story. They did a fairly good job. The ending was filled with twists and more twists, but kept along a fairly straight and easy to discern path.Should you play this? At the moment it's hard to say yes, but the story is done well enough for one. You will want a decent PC if you wanna run at 4k. I ran the game at 4k ultra 30fps locked with no DLSS no Ray Tracing. Had a Ryzen 5600x and RTX 3060Ti. Something about how the ray tracing is done makes it nearly impossible for a 3060Ti to run about 15fps which is not playable. For a cinematic game like this you can get away with 30fps if it is a mostly constant framerate. Though even then i still had occasional drops to 20fps. Like i said, there are substantial performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is advertised as a "dark first-person psychological thriller" from the creator of The Town of Light. Set in 1944 Italy, and with an Italian language set as default, the game is designed to get into the mind of the player.You play as Giulia, and start off as a young girl, with her grandmother reading a rather unsuitable story to her, the story of a White Lady in a lake, a ghost who lost her partner, trapped in the lake until there is fog upon which she can wonder the surrounding forest, and as is often the case, will murder young women. Lovely bedtime reading. Once the seemingly never-ending intro is finished, you fast forward in time, and get some control of your character, you find yourself setting up a camera by the lake, to try and get photos of wild animals, you then have to go through a rather tedious effort of changing the film on the camera, and since this is 1944, it is one of those very old cameras. After you put the new film in, you check to make sure you have the focus right, but upon doing this you spot a body in the lake. You run down, and by run down, you press one button and the character runs automatically, you dive in, after pressing one button, recover the body and drag to lakeside. But wait the body is your identical twin sister Martha who for some reason is wearing one of Giulia's dresses. Upon this terrible discovery, Giulia takes off Martha's necklace and puts it on herself. Your parents spot you, come to your aid, but your mother who despises you, assumes you are your deaf sister Martha and comforts you. And so, the lie begins, Martha is dead, but now you have become Martha, destined to not only pretend to be her, but also learn more about her mysterious death.Ok that enough spoilers of the game, since that is the opening chapter.The game itself has plenty of warnings on it for disturbing content. The PlayStation release has been censored heavily, and some scenes have been removed completely. Suffice to say this is not a kid's game. For those of you who have played The Town of Light, you might have a general idea of what to expect, but no this is much more disturbing.There are options to skip the disturbing scenes, but then what is the point of playing if you take out the most powerful bits.The rest of the game will have you exploring the woods and the area around the family home, the stunning Italian countryside and of course trying to contact the White Lady.The game can be very disturbing as I mentioned, there are some horrific scenes that not only do you have to watch, but you actively take part in. You will quickly understand why the warnings were needed.Think of the game more as a walking simulator, something that the person sitting next to you watching, will get as much out of it as you would playing, there is a lot of going backwards and forwards between the same locations, which can become tedious too. Giulia moves annoyingly slow, and although the atmosphere of the game is great to start with, it soon loses its impact with repetition.There are a few puzzles to complete in the game, but most of the interactivity involves you collecting things or looking at things. Dolls, Puppets etc which help unlock memory sequences. As this is set in 1944 there are plenty of references to the war, radio news alerts, newspapers and so on.And of course, just as you started, taking and developing photos is a big part of the game.Now I originally played this on Xbox and I was not keen. But I thought I would give it another shot now I knew the general gameplay better, and I must say my opinion has changed a bit.My issues are still there, but I do think there is a story to be told here for you the view to "enjoy" if within the horror realm.Is it perfect? no, but it is not bad either. Better second time around for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD:I initially had heard about this game from my best friend. He told me about how it was going to be censored on PlayStation and about the graphic nightmare close to the beginning where the player is forced to skin the face off of her sister and then proceeds to wear it. I was IMMEDIATELY interested seeing as it's rare that a game has that sort of depiction of violence and I wanted to know more about the story. I personally am a sucker for psychological horror/thrillers and horror all around so this so far has been perfect for me.DISCLAIMER: At this time I've only played about 3 hours so far.Although I've only logged a few hours so far, the graphics run very well on my computer for it being a low-end PC and the soundtrack is absolutely breath-taking. I've adored the gorey symbolism that's taken place so far and the addition of tarot card usage. The atmosphere is very chilling in some spots, like when we head down to the cellar for the first time or tend to our sister's corpse. The music especially is what truly makes it worth everything. There's so much going on in the best way that leaves me wondering what it means and what could happen next. The throw in of puppetry (although not IRL stuff) was so fresh to see and it made me really intrigued to know more about the character, Death, and their role.My only negative to the game is how the bike is practically useless and a bit wonky to control (very stiff). If you do activate the bike pump task, that also was VERY difficult for me to find. That might have been because I haven't rode a bike in years but I wasn't expecting it to be on the other bikes. I do wish our character also ran a bit faster but it's not that big of an issue where it would hinder game play. It also can seem like a lot at times, especially when it comes to new information but once you start using it, it's truly not as bad as I've seen in other games. Mechanically it's a really great game from what I've played so far and I can't wait to delve further into it!
