_childDocuments_.review: Martha Is Dead is a first-person horror game set in 1940’s Italy that manages to be both lovely and horrifying at the same time. I won’t give any spoilers. The only kind of spoiler I’ll say is that “Martha Is Dead” (as the game’s name implies). The protagonist you control is named Giulia and her twin sister is Martha, who is found dead at the beginning of the game. Giulia uses the tools available to her such as her camera to figure out who killed Martha. The premise is simple, but with all of the characters thrown in and without spoiling any plotlines, the plot becomes a lot more complex very quickly.The game is set in 1940’s Italy during World War 2 and Giulia lives with her parents. The game really does showcase the tragedy of war and it’s very respectfully done. It doesn’t glorify war at all. My heart sank when I read through the newspapers in the game, who tried to pin Martha’s murder as something political when it likely wasn’t. It’s not a good idea to rush through this game because Giulia’s house is full of interesting objects to examine and the developers put a lot of creativity into making her house feel like a real house someone would live in for the time period.The graphics of the game are very decent for a game of this scope and the art direction is top-notch. It’s trying to be realistic for the time period and it really does a good job. Another example of a game that did a good job with the art direction in a similar way was A Plague Tale: Innocence, though that was set in 1358 in what would be present-day France. In Martha Is Dead, the nearby forest, the lake, the bridge, the farm and its animals are all beautiful and juxtapose the horror parts of the game that I’ll get more into soon.The gameplay is in first-person view and involves moving Giulia around and examining objects. During certain game segments you’ll need to press combinations of buttons or analog stick directions to proceed, such as through setting up her camera. Some of them are quick-time events where you need to press the sequence of buttons within a few seconds while being chased.There are also scenes where Giulia is flying through the air and has to choose paths with words to complete a sentence for a plot event that happened (it’s like the Psyche Taxi minigame in the Danganronpa series). You’ll restart these sections if you put in an incorrect word, but they’re short and easy for the most part and serve as a good refresher for the plot events that happened.The game has a hint feature that you can activate to highlight all examinable objects in the area. In addition, there’s also a journal to view your objectives. There are both main and optional story objectives in the journal and it does provide hints in the text if you’re stuck in the game.Some of the items needed to progress the game can be a little tricky to find, but if you read the journal and take the game slowly you can find everything without issue. During the early story I had to find a bicycle pump, which was attached on another bicycle by another side of the house’s exits. I was also able to collect scissors and a tripod for Giulia’s camera. If you really get stuck, the journal will provide a hint, such as it explaining that the camera tripod is downstairs.The best thing to remember is that there are 3 elements of the photo you can change, including the exposure, aperture and focus and each of these can be turned up or down by using a control, left analog stick, right analog stick, and left/right directional pad, respectively. You don’t need to change them all at once, you can do it one-by-one and when you get more practice it’s pretty simple, it’s just that it looks intimidating.Sometimes you’ll need to search the house to find special kinds of attachments for the camera such as a flash to allow it to take pictures at night. This does add another layer of complexity because you’ll now have to select your attachments and then take the picture correctly as usual, but it’s not bad at all.I would recommend playing this game with a controller, it makes the game much easier to play and I can’t imagine using the camera with a keyboard. There are scenes where you need to use the camera to take a picture to progress, but you can also use the camera for fun. The house has a farm nearby with many loveable animals and I took a picture of a goat and her kid.The game does a great job of juxtaposing between horrifying moments and happy life moments. I haven’t mentioned it in great detail until now, but horror is certainly present in this game and the game does have very gruesome moments, such as one scene where you play as someone cutting off a human face from a dead body and wearing it. I liked the horror elements of Martha Is Dead because I grew up with slasher movies full of gore, but at the same time I know that it’s not for everyone and I wouldn’t force it on someone who’s not into it. But as someone who has played and watched both horror movies and video games for over 30 years, there is a lot of nasty scenes and the developers aren’t afraid to take risks which I can really appreciate in the modern era. The horror scenes are not distasteful in this game either, they’re meant to convey what it’s like going through a terrible experience and there are significant meanings behind the scenes in the game.The game is organized into days, and progressing the main story mission usually results in major plot events happening and the day progressing, so it’s a good idea to have backup saves because often I’ve accidentally progressed the plot even though I wanted to do side content first.The game is very linear for the first few days, but as you progress you will be able to unlock many side objectives and the world becomes more open. My only criticism is that the days can get repetitive after a while, and as I was finishing my playthrough of the preview build it was getting boring because you’re waking up and exploring the same house again until you do the main mission.One interesting side objective involved finding the pack of tarot cards that was confiscated from you. It’s a really neat game mechanic where once a day Giulia will shuffle her deck, pick 3 random cards, and do a tarot card reading on herself.Eventually you get access to the house’s telephone. There’s a list of contacts your family has written down, such as the police number, family friends, the doctor, etc. You can also keep track of important numbers you come across in the game not present on that list of contacts. When you have free time you can call them and get access to a lot of interesting information. One interesting conversation you can have is actually with a rebel group and it leads to an extremely interesting side quest chain. I’ve explained earlier that Giulia’s father is a German general even though Giulia’s living in Italy. You can help the rebels with their efforts by thwarting the Germans’ plans, or alternatively you can even tell your father about it.I chose to help the rebels, and it lead me sending and receiving their messages in Morse code. It was a very fun side quest and actually taught me how to use Morse code. The game had a translation sheet to convert words to Morse code and back, and that made the process easy even though it looked daunting at first. In fact, I wouldn’t even mind if the whole game was like that because helping the rebels felt like a historical movie.It’s genuinely fun to explore Giulia’s Italian household and learn the rich culture of the 1940’s and when you begin playing I guarantee you’ll want to solve the mystery of what really happened to Martha on that eventful night.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well made. The map, the sound, the characters/objects...everything is fantastic. However, the story is incredibly slow. Incredibly. The story involved in the game is interesting, but progressing through the game is extremely tedious and boring. Having to inspect dozens of items, sometimes to meet an objective (like reading the newspaper every day, letters, etc), or completing objectives that are just really boring in general. There are also bugs in the game that should be addressed as well. I picked up a letter and was unable to put it back down, I was just stuck there; I had to load one of my saves in order to continue. I also thought it was very annoying when I had the lighter in my hand to see around the house, and then if I were to do anything I had to select it from my bag again.The breaking point for me was when the game spawns you in the forest after Martha's funeral, and naturally you think to go down to the lake to meet the White Lady because the main character talked about it. I got down there and realized that I had to walk all the way back to the house to find an item, then go all the way back in order to continue. Very annoying; I just quit the game at that point. It felt more like an open world adventure game rather than a horror.Overall the game was very boring to me, which is disappointing because every other aspect of the game is flawless. I like everything about it except for some small bugs/game mechanics, and how incredibly slow the story is. Sometimes games can be slow, tedious, or boring at certain parts, but I played for 2.5 hours and nothing changed. Sorry devs.Edit: Another major complaint that I have is that the game is not really optimized. I don't have the best computer, but I can play some really resource intensive games on high settings with little to no issues. On this game I had to lower everything to medium, which made the once beautiful-looking game to meh looking, otherwise the lag I got made the game unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: This is yet another title where I would have preferred a middle option. I'm gonna go with not recommended due to its somewhat insensitive handling of mental health and - disorders subject matters.It looks ASTOUNDING though, I love everything visual about it, and some scenes and sections are truly great, like a scene in the woods where the backdrop and setting suddenly hits you in a remarkably poignant way (I don't wanna spoil it as it was the true highlight for me).I enjoyed the photographing and photo development, and sending morse code via the telegraph (a completely optional side quest, but come on, you miss basically half the game not doing it, though I appreciate the option to be more or less active in the war). Several gamers on forums took issue with how the morse code puzzle worked, but I found it actually very smart and realistic, in a gamified way of course. The game does not hold your hand when it comes to coding and decoding these messages but if you figure it out you feel like a champ, and the girl you play as would have had to figure this out the same way you do. Or not, depending.There are several of these little instances where you can opt to take steps to figure things out, like getting hold of numbers to call and pretend to be other people say, to gain information, but the game doesn't outright tell you this is an option as I recall. Then again, you can ignore that completely and bascially never touch the phone at all and go about the games main storyline. I love that.You have all these realistic settings and mechanics in a stunningly beautiful realised world, with superb leading voice actress Annie Warburton, all conveying what could have been a very interesting and engaging story, but then they have to attempt to shock for shock values sake alone. It is pretentious and at the same time insensitive and therefor disingengious to the story they are trying to tell.There was some controversy regarding the game being censored for certain releases, and what it meant was making a cutscene out of a short game play mechanic in which you simply moved the mouse according to prompts. I can't say I understand the reasoning behind that, and also I would stress that the scene in question is meant to be taken metaphorically. The scene didn't bother me and it was a legit part of the story. However, when we later in the game are to believe we can cut a body set in rigor mortis open with normal fricking scissors as if it was made out of butter, I was taken out of it completely and had to laugh to myself. Well I don't know, I'm no expert, maybe dead bodies do turn to butter after a some days, but it came across comedic as presented in game, and I just felt like it was one ”dark for darkness sake” scenario too many and it tips over into splatter farce rather than psychological horror.

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to give a verdict. Many pro's and con's. The setting and time period was a fantastic idea as it has a certain charm that you won't find anywhere else. The protagonist is engaging and you really delve into it all. The journey down the rabbit hole and finding the "truth" was quite thrilling, BUT. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, the graphics in this game are beautiful. If you didn't know it was a horror game, you def wouldn't know by looking at the scenery. There is a morse code part in the game that I highly suggest googling a morse decoder because looking at the chart in the game was like a foreign language. My only BIG complaint is that I would have liked to see loss of a child, child abuse, and animal abuse as part of the warnings. I love gore, and honestly there was a LOT LESS of it than I anticipated. Nothing was really "scary" about the game in my opinion, however, I would have liked a warning about those 3 trigger warnings mentioned. Honestly, I think those few scenes messed with me more than anything. Luckily I was prepared for the loss of a baby because I read a twitter trigger warning. The other two, I was blindsided by. Overall, I do recommend checking out. The graphics and game mechanics alone make it a really interesting game.

name: HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed
detailed_description: HELP SGT. MAX AMMO TO DEFEAT MAJOR EVIL AND SAVE THE HYPERCORE! There was once an ancient line of action figures, who created a magical power source that would allow humans to keep their favourite childhood memories of their toys. This ancient power source is known as the Hypercore. Inside the Hypercore are the beloved memories of our favorite toys. If Major Evil destroys it, these memories will disappear forever. Defend it with everything you've got, or see our cherished toys turn into lost treasures of the past! Key Features 1-4 player online/local co-op. Full split-screen support including online/local. Single player/offline play with player bots. Difficulty scales based on the number of players. Wave-based shooter with story campaign. Classic PvP game modes. (up to eight players) First and third-person camera modes. PLAY CO-OP WITH YOUR FRIENDS Work together as a team to defend the Hypercore. Grab a friend, break out of your toy packaging, and get ready to fight waves of classic toys. Prepare for each wave by searching for weapons, resources, and even hidden secrets. OFFLINE PLAY FOR SOLO PLAYERS Not everybody likes to play online. Hypercharge supports Offline, Split-Screen and Local play. You can progress and unlock everything in-game while playing solo. PLAYER BOTS Don’t have a team to play with? Don’t worry, we’ve got you solo players covered. Player bots listen to your commands, collect resources, and even help to build defences. UNLOCK ACTION FIGURES Earn unlocks the old school way, in-game with hard work! No Pay-to-Win nonsense. PLAYER VERSUS PLAYER MODES Go head-to-head against other action figures as you fight to become top of the scoreboard! Classic PvP modes include Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Battery, Infection, and King of the Hill.

_childDocuments_.review: Hypercharge: Unboxed is a game that reminded me of the Toy Story movies with the references to the Green Army Men from the movie dropping in with their parachutes and tank trucks. It also has that Tower Defense vibe in the adventure mode, but does kind of fall short in the multiplayer department in terms of match making and servers.MY VIDEO  REVIEW LINK: Written Review coming to Weebly soonSCORE: 7/10PROS: - Love the customization option. I just wished there was a little more to it - Reminds me of my childhood with toys beating up other toys - Cool and catchy soundtrack CONS: - Matchmaking can sometimes lead to bot lobbies - Servers created by other players shut down when they shut them down. -I think they could have added other things in gameplayI think the game is worth it for sure when it comes to kids. I like the enemy variety and what they are trying to accomplish, but I just think it needed something to push the score higher, especially in the gameplay / mechanic department. Overall, a 7 out of 10. Do I recommend it? Yes in terms of fun times and nostalgic stuff

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person who enjoyed Small Soldiers, and Toy Story this game will suit you well. If you're the type of person who enjoyed toy stores, arcades, and cartoons in the 90's you'll probably enjoy this game too.Mechanically, this game is crisp. Shooting enemies, and building a defense for your power cores feels rewarding. Graphically, the game is gorgeous. It feels like you're dropped right in the heart of a Pixar scene, and i found myself spending the first few minutes of every new map ignoring the objective and exploring. Just when you think you've found all the hidden nooks, you find a box you didn't know you could jump on, and suddenly an entire area of the map you previously though was inaccessible is made available to you. I'm excitedly waiting this games full release, and to see how other game modes are introduced. I'll be updating this review as the game develops, but for now this game is a wonderfully priced way to spend a few hours a week.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played so far I absolutely love this game, I've been waiting for a silly toy themed game like this for years and the time has finally come.If you're just wanting a "is it worth the price or not", definitely. I got this on sale for £7.74 and feel bad I got it for this cheap, as so much went into this game.I do have some small nit picks that I want to mention to the devs that I feel could improve the game (and just other tiny nit picks that are mostly silly).- The movement.The movement in this game feels a bit off, for example I feel the ledge grabbing is very inconsistent. I feel having the game grab ledges automatically as long as you're in the air and you're going in a forward motion should have the game look for ledges to grab in front of you. Tapping or holding space whilst looking at a ledge to climb over a lot of the time does not work half of the time.I also feel like the game doesn't let you have much air control. A lot of the times I go and try and jump up somewhere, but a lot of the time I'm fighting against the small amount of air control you're allowed to maneuver with, I feel a game like this should definitely allow for some more freedom in movement in terms of air control, but I could just be malding here, as it's just something that bugged me a little when playing.Another thing is I feel that even if toggle sprinting is off, when running you should still be running when letting go off the sprint button by default, it feels a bit clunky when you're expecting your character to still be running, but actually you're suddenly walking and you die from it or you don't make the jump you're trying to make. Toggle sprint is a good counter to this issue, but I feel it still should be a present feature of normal sprinting.The thing that bugged me the most about the movement is just how inconsistent the ledge grabbing felt.- Visual indicators.There were times I had no idea what was hurting me, or that I was being hurt. I feel like the visual indicator on screen that is showing where you got hurt form could maybe be improved slightly, in the form of make it more obvious that it's there or something, because I feel it's hard to notice HUD elements sometimes amongst all the chaos.Now saying this I could just be blind and everyone is fine with how it is, but I know there's people out there who would judge an entire game based off the fact they didn't know where they were getting hit from, so It's just something to keep in mind.- The silly stuff.Now like I said before, I've been waiting for a silly toy game like this of this quality for a long time. That being said, I personally believe there could be a few changes done to make it feel more silly and "toy like".For example, the foot step sounds right now make me feel like i'm playing a super serious world war 2 battlefield game, and the guns sounds (and shoot) like they're real guns. So as a suggestion of something to at least have a think about, is have the foot step sounds sound more "plastic" if that makes sense, so you actually feel like you're an action figure just running around the bed room or whatever, and make the guns feel more "toy like" if that's even possible.Obviously I'm not a developer of this game, maybe all this was already trialed and it just felt like crap, or some other reason, I'm not sure, but again these are just tiny nit picks that I feel would make this game even better and make what it's going for more of a thing. It's just these small tweaks to make what the game is going for be more present, and to just constantly remind you you're playing as an action figure running around the bed room or the garden or whatever doing action figure things.And one last thing, I don't often make a review with much thought into it, it feels funny being a 21 year old doing a serious critique on a game about action figures and toys. Thank you for making a game that is making me a man child.

_childDocuments_.review: hypercharge is a fun tower-defense FPS that's best played in co-op with others, either online or locally. (+) solid variety in weapon types, with all the classic guns present and accounted for (rifle, shotgun, flamethrower, minigun, laser, grenade launcher, etc.)(+) vibrant and colorful visuals, and everything is rendered beautifully in unreal engine 4. overall excellent presentation.(+) well-designed maps with plenty of verticality, and solid platforming to go with it. you'll be searching every corner of these maps to find all the hidden collectibles.(+) lots of attention to detail and easter eggs hidden all over the in-game environments.you'll definitely get a few laughs from all the hidden gags.(-) deathmatch and other PvP modes are available, but aren't really that fleshed out, as the co-op modes are the main attraction here. wouldn't recommend this game to someone who is looking for a competitive online PvP experience.

_childDocuments_.review: You ever played a game and it was just fun? Like not "I have to grind to have fun", not "I have to sweat to have fun", not "I need my friends to carry me to have fun", just actual, raw, unadulterated fun? Hypercharge: Unboxed is just FUN. Its an third-person/first-person shooter that is mechanically sound that is in a world of absolute childish-glee. Remember being a child and walking through the aisles in a toy store? Seeing all the shiny packages and still having a brain that could make dopamine on its own? Remember seeing cheesy commercials between your favorite cartoons for these whacky, out of control toys? Maybe you are even old enough to remember seeing Toy Story on VHS and imagining the fun of toys that come to life? If you fit into any of these nostalgia baiting categories, H:U is for you. You are a toy, fighting to save the other toys from evil toys... how could that possibly be not fun? The game is graphically solid, sounds good, performs well, and has minimal requirements in terms of PC specs. Pick it up on sale and play with some buds, it's 100% worth your time!

_childDocuments_.review: The entire atmosphere is perfectly realized, with impressive details and references throughout every aspect of the game.  FPS bits work well, with weapons that feel distinct and specialized.  Tower defense is good, with many traps and defenses to unlock, but I wish they were buildable beyond just designated spots.  Levels are awesome, with details and areas always making me say "woah, that's cool" in giddy excitement.  They're also huge and very vertical, designed to be explored throughout rounds for items, which is refreshing when paired with the combat and defense.  Think if COD Zombies was also a first-person platformer.  Progression is steady and challenging, with unlocks coming from completing different difficulties and finding collectables, instead of an xp grind.  Cosmetics are great too, with your action figure able to go from G.I. Joe, to dino-men, ninjas, robots, and bug-men.A special note:Not only is this game an incredibly enjoyable mix of FPS and Tower Defense, but the entire release shows just how much the devs care.  On day 1 of release:-Almost no bugs-Full controller support-Online AND splitscreen support, in 2020-A decent sized demo, in 2020-Tons of cosmetics with no microtransactions, in 2020-A quality game for $15-$20, in 2020Day 2, 3, and 5:-Fixed the only bug-Added Steam Trading Cards.-Added more dedicated serversI also need to mention the insane amount of accessibility options:-Separate FOV for game and weapon-Night mode options (disabling blue light)-Screen shake intensity-Weapon sway intensity-Button prompts for Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch controllers-Separate HUD and UI scaling from 50%-150%-Customizable splitscreen options like quality, vertical or horizontal split, and if third screen is top or bottom-Separate control customization between splitscreen players, including KB/MTo top this all off: cheat codes, all of which are yet to be discovered and aren't on the internet yet.  In 2020.  'Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a genuinely terrific game. While it won't have the 4K shine of an AAA title, it looks incredible (especially given it's install size) and has tons of little details to appreciate. The levels are decently varied in terms of size, aesthetics, and design. When playing with friends lower difficulty levels are easy enough, but the harder difficulties can be tough. Players start a level with a set amount of "Build points" (currency) and use those to construct defenses to protect a number of Hypercores (the number varies based on the leval) from swarms of enemy toys that attack in waves. Killing enemy toys provides you with more build points, to build more defenses, to kill more enemies the next wave, etc. Build points are also scattered around the levels for players to run around and collect. This not only provides incentive for exploring each level, but helps teach newer players the layout of the levels and can highlight some good spots to defend from once the attack phase starts. Waves are split into a Build phase and Attack phase.Hypercharge: Unboxed supports four player co-op locally, online, or a combination of the two. While it's more fun (and more fair) to play with friends, it's entirely possible and enjoyable to play single player.Probably my biggest complaint is that I'm not really a fan of the Buildables unlock system. That said, it's a small team, it's still being updated, and what IS there is more or less terrific.If you like FPS, or First Person Tower Defense games Hypercharge: Unboxed is an excellent game overall. It looks great, it sounds great, the weapons feel solid and varied, the platforming is quite good, the levels are diverse, and it feels like playing a war game set inside of Toy Story.

_childDocuments_.review: I played with a friend of mine through all of the levels on casual difficulty and earned gold or higher on each of them.this is by far my favorite game to come to steam in 2020 thus far, i never got the chance to play Toy Soldiers when i was a child but this feels like a way for me to experience it in the modern gaming space while also taking me back to my fantasies while playing with action figures in my childhood home.the graphic fidelity is STUNNING. the attention to detail and the love poured into each miniscule scratch and smudge brings the entire world to life, the subtlest of movement in the animations that show you these are indeed 80s/90s action figures is breathtaking. the batteries have fingerprints on them, the character models have seams in their plastic, the store tiles have scratches and subtle dips from years of wear. every inch of this game world deserves to be admired.It should also be stated. VERY IMPORTANT. I can tell that the artistic portion was so much fun for these devs to work on, because after the first few minutes me and my friend had decided that if there were legible words on objects in the environment.. WE WERE READING THEM! so many fake products that have such incredible meta humor and silliness had us catching our breath for minutes at a time, do yourself a favor and simply walk up to any old box or household object and read the labels. you will not be dissapointed!as for the gameplay, its quick enough to get your blood pumping, but not so fast-paced that it stresses you out, the gun mechanics are more solid than most indie shooters i have seen, with some unique recoil patterns on the automatic powerhouse weapons and some pinpoint accuracy for the sniper options, though it becomes a little obvious this game was not intended to be a hyper-accurate shooter, many starting rifles have very unruly kick to them that make it impossible for newcomers to reliably track targets.the buildable defense mechanics are a lot of fun to play with and strategize, carfully choosing where to place those walls and anti-air turrets to better thwart the waves of incoming toys trying to whack your hyper cores, the more you play a certain stage, the more familiar you become with the best defense strategy to employ.the character customization has consistently put a smile on my face no matter which model of figure i decide to play as, my current favorite being the undead knight figure, Wraith. The name system is also a blast to mess around with, unlocking more titles, nouns, adjectives, etc to mix and match into the perfect pre-2000s action hero name, and the randomization button has given me a ton of laughs as i wonder how my friends might react to seeing what the system has decided to name me.and this may or may not be important to some people, but it sure put the final digital cherry on top when i discovered that each and every one of the customization and buildable card options will be earned through gameplay and skillful challenge completions! no in-game micro-transactions of any kind! it actually blew my mind!this game could have been double the original price and still be far beyond worth the money, please support this wonderful development team, such a small studio deserves your praise and adoration for crafting this plastic-smashing work of art and i cant wait to see what sort of content will become available in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review.  I'd recommend this game to folks now who are looking for a "fun in short bursts" co-op game to play with their buddies.  It's not the best FPS tower defense game out there, but it also has enough charm and does enough right to warrant a purchase - especially on a sale.  It's not something that's going to hold a group's attention for a long time, and the game doesn't have much staying power thanks to forcing you and your friends into replaying the same levels over and over to get your unlocks (since hidden items that give you the unlocks disappear for everyone once one person gets them), but there is fun to be had here in smaller play sessions.The dev fixed all the camera issues that caused extreme nausea, which my first review below touched on, so full props to them for fixing the issues that made the game all but unplayable for quite a few people and as such, I'm adjusting this review to recommend the game now.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------OLD REVIEW HERE---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------If you are prone to any sort of nausea when playing FPS games, you may want to be careful here.I can handle most games, but there are some VR games that put me in a bad state.  This game makes me feel like I played a bad VR game due to the following reasons:- The entire camera shakes when you shoot your gun, instead of just the gun itself.  This may not be so bad if it were subtle, but it's not subtle at all; the whole screen shakes violently.- The camera tilts at an angle when strafing.  This makes it appear like the camera is locked to the player model's head and the player model leans when it strafes.  Can't say for sure, but this is how it appears.  This is also the most nauseating thing... eyes to do not do this when you move side to side in real life or tilt your head.  When you combine this with the camera shake, it's a recipe for that bad VR feel.- Motion blur that cannot be disabled.  This isn't nearly as bad as the other two, but it still sucks.Can't recommend this game in its current state, and since it doesn't look like there's any way to disable all this camera WTFery (it almost seems like the devs have never played a shooter before), I'm probably going to have to refund this.Sucks too, because the premise seems super awesome and tearing out of a toy package as an action figure on a shelf was such a great start.

_childDocuments_.review: is a pretty simple tower-defense FPS with a fantastic "retro toy" aesthetic and decent replay value. Built by a passionate dev team that cares  about the game they're making, it's worth the price of admission (which is usually $15-20). Unfortunately, the community is extremely small, and finding a game with other humans can be hard. Versus modes Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, and Infection are available to play with up to 8 players, but they offer limited entertainment without a full party of human players. Customization options look great, but lack diversity and uniqueness. The retro toy aesthetic shouldn't exclude more varied body shapes and design concepts, but embrace and allow for them instead. I'd like to see this game spread its wings a little bit in that regard. The DLC is reasonably priced, after all. Gimme some Gorgonites for my Commando Elites, you know?While I do recommend it for the fun it's given me,  doesn't seem to have much more than 10 hours of actual game. Unlocks are rewarded through tedious hunts for hidden shinies in each stage. The devs like to call their unlock mechanics "play-to-win," calling back to the gaming days of yesteryear when content was unlocked via gameplay. I don't disagree with the principle (given the pay-to-win MTX addiction grinder  the big-name devs are all dragging us into), but scouring every in' stage for shinies is in' exhausting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bona fide children's wonderland. What a gem; truly, this game will bring you back to playing war with your mismatched assortment of toys as a kid. Though, it's not only the charm of it's characters and settings that elevate this game, but it's variety of play. The maps, guns (plus their modifications), and enemy hordes are unique and numerous, which drastically change the flow of the game and your approach to fighting against the toy invaders. There are a myriad of challenges which will truly test your prowess of the game and it's mechanics, including gathering collectables scattered around each map that require epic parkour to acquire as well as high ranks on the many maps. The rewards are fantastic, too, with some delightful cosmetics that allow you to customize your toy soldier as well as have access to creative new buildable defenses. This game is fantastic and while there is much to praise, I think that the trailer speaks for itself; if you have even an inkling of interest after watching it, then I encourage you to buy. You will not regret it. The only major negative I have is the game's lack of singleplayer content. The game does not scale very well and you quickly feel overwhelmed when playing by yourself, especially on the game's more expansive maps. I almost exclusively play this game with one other friend of mine. And even with that extra support, we've found it near impossible to get anything higher than a gold rank (have all towers still standing on either easy or normal difficulty) on Garden of Evil, the game's largest map. We have put in arduous effort to earn a diamond rank--that is, a perfect score with no damage done to any of the towers on hard difficulty--on a handful of other maps. I've also frequently experienced a bug where my mouse clicks don't always register in the game, so I'll be vigorously clicking and not shooting at all at random points. It's more of a minor annoyance, however, it does become an issue on the air hockey map in particular if you're shooting for that challenging diamond rank, as every shot is crucial. Not everyone experiences this glitch, though I know of some others that have from the game's discord. Thankfully, the singleplayer issue is being addressed in the next major update, which is adding a new game mode (along with a brilliant pirate's playground map) and bots to help pull some weight when low on friends to play with. And yes, the creator's do continue to pour their hearts into this game and are excellent at communicating with the playerbase. I look forward to the future of this game and hope that it gains some more players, as it's well deserving of the attention. It has easily become one of my favorite shooters.9/10 (only gets better with every update)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't generally enjoy leaving reviews, as a matter of fact this is my very first steam review to any of the games that I own. However with this game being in early access I felt that I should at least do my part and tell anyone having doubts whether they should buy this game or wait until its full release - just as I was. And let me tell you that you absolutely should buy it now if this is the type of game that you enjoy. And here is why:CONTENT:The game is full of it - The principle is simple enough, you have to defend your cores. But it's how you do it that will really keep you going - which traps to lay down and in which position, where should you position yourself for quick access to all cores, where should you invest your coins - a trap, a jumping platform or a weapon upgrade. These strategies will lead you to a gold or even platinum medal (standard difficulty) if you are able to use your resources appropriately. tl;dr - If you are concerned with content I can assure you that it isn't lacking and you will have as much fun as any other fully released game in this genera. MAPS: Because the game is in early access and more maps may be added I will not say exactly how many are currently available, but it's the same quantity and size than any other AAA FPS game. The maps are very cleverly laid out and really make you plan and outline a way to get to all cores in time for a quick response.SINGLE V MULTI-PLAYERI have played in both modes and honestly I felt no difference between the two modes, both are very fun and because the game balances the difficult of the level based on you being solo or paying with a friend it never feels unfair.PERFORMANCE: The games runs very smoothly and it never crashed on me once, I run this game at a consistent 144fps and I never had a dip even in intensive battles where a lot of enemies are in one location, if you are especially picky with the performance of your games then I can assure you that this game won't let you down.WILL YOU HAVE FUN?:OBVIOUSLY! If you love fast paced and action filled games then this game is loads of fun!FINALLY:Massive thanks to the devs -  the artwork is absolutely amazing and the game runs buttery smooth and you can tell by a mile that this game had and still has a lot of love put into it. With the amount of crappy games coming out its great to see such a good title being on steam.FINALLY FINALLY - Please to the devs if they are listening - please don't take an epic exclusive for your full release, without steam I couldn't even be writing this review!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from my best friend some time back, and after having gone in to thoroughly play it, it is a demanding title with a variety of fun gameplay modes. Pros: 1: Nostalgia for toy movies such as Toy Story, and Small Soldiers. If you grew up with movies like these, you're gonna start off on a good vibe!2: Classic shooter style gameplay. Nothing fancy, no "slide cancel", no "Advanced techs" or any of that! It's RAW!3: Simplified weapon system! Your entire weapon loadout is 2 weapons, and you can pick them up as you go. They change based on what weapons you pick up in each stage, and each has it's own ammo. 4: Fun character designs. The playable characters and enemies by majority have a humanoid shape. 5: Single Player and Multiplayer modes a plenty! From the campaign/story mode, to the VS modes. 6: Loads of player customization! You unlock a LOT of stuff to work with to make your ideal figure! From base body, to matching heads, to the weapon color, EVEN THE BOX! I was impressed by the attention to detail with the way all of these details came together!7: You can play with up to 7 friends for 8-player online play! This means a fairly light load on your PC if you happen to host a game online!8: Peer to Peer connection: No worry about servers shutting down if the devs decide they're done with this game and move on to their next project if it proves profitable.9: Unique "Tower Defense" action gameplay! It incorporates tower defense mechanics into the game, making it a whole new vibe. Totally different from every other action shooter game I've EVER played to this point!Cons: 1: Only 10 maps (And they're used in both single player and multiplayer)... THIS is a bit crippling to me, as I remember my old FPS and TPS titles having more than 10 maps. The only difference is that the hypercores are not present in most multiplayer modes. I would appreciate some Multiplayer exclusive maps or arena maps designed for multiplayer. Something like an "Overhead display" map, or "Collector's room", or for a MASSIVE map, a Gymnasium from a local High School with stuff like Bleachers as a MASSIVE symmetrical multiplayer map. 2: Bot AI... This is one of those cases where AI bots will start to focus on you if you start to get good or start climbing the heap, even if they're all set to the easiest setting. 3: Limited multiplayer mode options. You have the Campaign/story whhich can be played split-screen, or online, or run a LAN network, which is a big plus for up to 4-players co-op. But the multiplayer modes are the usual batch. Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, and a mode I never thought I'd see outside of free to play garbage First Person Shooters with gross balance issues (Such as overpowered sniper rifles that instant-kill in one shot with explosives nerfed to be useless), the "Infection" mode. There is one more mode, but I forgot what it was... Would be nice if they could make a differentiation between Free For All, and Team modes. 4: Sessions max out up to 8 players in VS modes. I get this is to accommodate players with older PCs, which hits me in nostalgie for old 8-player Starcraft matches. But as an action and shooter game, personally it feels like they could crank up the player and bot numbers. Just a small gripe honestly. I'm used to VS matches with 16 and even 32, sometimes even 64 players at a time killing each other.5: Loadout limitations. Some weapons take 2 slots, and as powerful as they are, the biggest problem with these is the fact that some weapons have substantially more recoil. The minigun for example has crazy high recoil, and you need minigun specific parts to add to your gun.All things considered, despite the cons, the Pros more than outweigh them. I hope this game gets some updates soon to add more to it. It's a good solid game to play, and it could always stand to get more support. A Gymnasium level would be so awesome though.  And a stage where the entire house is a MASSIVE open world including the back yard. An alley map with pipes and lumber situated for a symmetrical map would be cool too. Adding symmetrically designed maps for multiplayer would be a great step forward.

This was due to a few things let me explain.1. Game update was required but I didnt have space in installed drive.2. Used steam tool to move game install drive. - In this process the 'UserSettings1' data is not moved to the new location. (This is the part I didnt not see)3. Updated and Launched the game and the new install made me a new save game. So resolution to this issue is if you do move your install using steam tools to make sure you take that file 'UserSettings1' over to the new install location.

I know there is a "automatic finder"-function, but that's not what I mean, I would like to see a queue-system, where you can optional choose to host the game, and get a bit more XP, or something like that, you could also then easy implement ranked.Score:Graphics - 9/10 - The graphics blend almost perfect with the whole idea of the game.Mechanics (Only played co-op) - 8/10 - Nothing that you haven't seen before, but they took the best parts of other co-op games and blend it together.Sound - 8/10 - Really blends well with the environment, I personally turned down music, but that's just me.Animations/level design - 10/10 - The only thing I miss, which is totally unnecessary for the gameplay, is the possibility to interact with the objects/toys in the surroundings, like moving them or such, everything is just static objects. I'm thinking straight out of the box here, but you could maybe even make it possible to use some of the objects for your advantage. As an example, in the kitchen, there is abit of objects you can interact with, like vegetables and stuff, but what if I could use my grenade launcher to shoot at a carrot which goes into a horde, or push a book down the shelf, to a massive plastic crowd? ---------------Overall: 9/10 - Would easily get a + point if they added queue system and ranked etc. and fixed the progression not being a locale save file, your profile should have some Cloudsync or server hosting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of, if not, the most innovative and fun tower defense game that I ever played. It's very creative and rich in detail with its guns, weapon attachments, map variety, enemy types and game modes.   It functions pretty much like a regular strategic tower defense game, but the strong and unique aspect of this game is the freedom to explore, climb and jump around the map to find collectibles (and very well hidden secrets) and to gather coins to expend on defenses, guns, weapon attachments and even to try your luck on a slot machine.  Depending on your match performance, you'll unlock customization options for your character and buildables for strong and sturdier defenses. It's easier and even in its best when played with friends or by a company of randoms in public matches, but it can be really challenging depending on the difficulty that's being played on, so it requires team synergy and strategic thinking. Really fun and very creative game.tl;dr: It's a tower defense game that's really creative and fun to play with friends, can be really challenging and it's very rewarding, detailed and addicting. Highly Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent most of my playtime in the newly updated single-player campaign/waves mode.- Map Design is astounding. Each map is fun to explore for collectibles, with plenty of jokes and easter-eggs to find. You can spend hours exploring a single map, free roam mode lets you do just that.- The combat tech is very engaging. There's a lot to learn using weapons, from the current gun build you're making to reload swapping.(Swapping weapons/Melee does not cancel previous reload.)- Lots of cosmetic customization. Tons of things to unlock to make your character feel unique.- Versus and other modes are great. No complaints aside from semi-empty lobbies. If you got friends (I don't) it's super fun (I'd think).- The game has incredible charm It's one of the most imaginative and fun games to run around in. Reminds me of the old 3DO Army men games in the best ways possible. They really captured the aesthetic they were aiming for here.- Optimization is insanely great Load times are near instant and framedrops are non-existent. It's amazing how smooth the game runs even with so many toy corpses near the end of a mission.- The devs are devoted and compassionate for their work.Doing free content updates and listening to their fans for so long earns some mad respect from me, no matter what. Excited to see how the game evolves further. Again this is from my personal experience in single-player campaign/waves mode that was released literal days before I installed. - The actual Tower Defense feels limited.The tower-defense part of this game is a bit restricting. Very few placement tiles on early maps and easier difficulties. The turrets are very expensive and feel too situational to rely on. On single-player expect being overrun often, as bots abandon posts frequently, meaning the 1,500 credit defenses gets shredded by 2 meanbots and a spinner cause you were busy with the other 98% of the wave.Trying to juggle defending every hypercore personally makes getting Platinum/Diamond rank (no core damage) a pain on big maps.Batteries drain incredibly fast and sometimes the map spawns too few to sustain a good defense, there's a battery charger you can unlock for build phase to help with this, but it unlocks from Platinum clears, making it obsolete on Casual/Regular.- Some enemy encounters are VERY annoying.There are a few "player hunter" enemies that are too strong, usually killing you before you realize they're there, Brobots and mini-bosses in particular.Drones aren't very tanky but their raw numbers in some maps will demolish you, and they usually kill you in just a few hits. Anti Air is basically required to help mitigate this.Jets are the epitome of annoying. Fast flying, hard to hit enemies that send homing rockets to hit you and your defense. Not terribly lethal to you but it will knock you around (and off high ground) and shred defenses. In my experience, antiair usually miss shots on them because they're just too fast.Dead Army Men sometimes land upright, making you think they're still alive.- Movement feels a bit jankPlatforming is a bit floaty and vaulting is inconsistent. It helps if you have a grenade launcher or jetpack, but I've lost about a half-dozen Platinum games because I couldn't get up to the core from missing a vault and falling down at critical moments.I know I just criticized the game for the past few paragraphs but I had actual, genuine fun while playing. I'd still recommend it even if you'll only ever do the single-player stuff. I know the developers read and respond to reviews so hopefully they use my feedback/complaining however they need. It was a lot of fun to do the campaign and I'll keep trying to solo Diamond rank every level.p.s. flamethrower turrets would be pretty neat, just sayin :^)

_childDocuments_.review: Took a bit to warm up to it, as it felt very simplistic to begin with - but turns out, this simplicity has a lot to offer.In its core, it is a fun coop (or vs) tower defense + FPS shooter mix. _childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game that's very well polished; just needs a little bit of work on certain aspects in regards to bug fixes and tweaks. It's genuinely surreal to be running around in almost identical environments you've likely ran around in as a kid, from toy stores stacked up like military installments I used to make out of dumb Legos and the million assortment of toys/household items around me, to a garden, a garage, and even a familiar bedroom! The customization is super on point too and it genuinely feels like you're making your own action figure. My only gripes with the game are some of the current standing bugs that'll definitely be fixed I'm sure, along with the inability to 'pick' a general starting weapon. It's not a -huge- deal but I do wish you could opt to go into the game with a certain weapon and deal with its drawbacks rather than just having to hope for RNG to give you what you're looking for.Some enemies definitely need tweaking as well, notably the bomber versions of enemies. They feel a little bit cheap when they just plow through an entire line of defenses without issue, then totally nuke one of your points because there's so many of them. Maybe just reduce their rate of spawn a touch? I dunno.This game has a -LOT- of potential though and could go very far with what it has. I genuinely hope to see so much more content for this game, because what's there is genuinely amazing, and is so much fun to play around with. If I had any suggestions as a shot in the dark, maybe an elf action figure or a dwarf, though I know the latter might be more unlikely due to possible funky behavior with the camera and platforming mechanics. New buildables though, new enemies-- honestly just everything the game has now but expanded upon! It has an amazing base to work from, and just generally more of what we've got would be a massive chef's kiss. Thank you guys for the cool game, definitely will be keeping up with it as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very Good First/Third person Tower defense.Pros- Can play single player not just a multiplayer Game! (Though Multiplayer is more preferred) - The graphics are very well done and the art style is great.- The sound track is great and puts you in that retro style mood.- Every toy in the game is just such a throw back to childhood. - Lots of collectables hope to see more!- Good Maps From Small to Large. (There's about 11 Maps I believe so far, which isn't bad but looking forward to seeing more with updates!)- Movement and controls are pretty solid (The climbing up can be a bit tricky with certain secrets but its not overly difficult to get them)- Gun play is pretty well done! (Not to compare with other games but I get a Very "Doom" or "Halo" vibe with it and in my opinion, that's great for this type of game)- The customizing your Gun during Gameplay is pretty cool (Really like that idea Especially when you can switch out to any type of weapon that you need or want quickly. Hope to see more Weapon parts be added!)- split-screen/Local Multiplayer always nice to see in a game like this! Gives a lot of the older multiplayer vibes.- Customization is simple and very pleasing to switch what Action-Figure you want play as and give them a unique title and Symbol. (hope to see more with updates!)- Like that you can have different defense towers and unlocking new ones over time- plenty of replayability and mindless enjoyment (I've Completed most maps on gold and a few on platinum) Haven't done higher difficulty then regular yet so far but plan on doing it all!- Lots of little Easter eggs/references and such, which is fantastic.- So far no bugs or glitches that I have encountered, one crash though, which isn't bad, over the course of my Game Time and its well optimized as well. Cons- There are very little cons with this game which is great but there are improvements that can be done and additions that can be added!- Not alot of PvP or Main Game Modes! (I assume there will be more but it is a bit disappointing there is only the few Main choices you have which is Death match, plague and the Wave based mode. The mini games are cool, Spinners and tanks but I don't count these as main modes because there fairly quick but all modes are decent and have lots of replayability!)- The Bot AI is a bit wonky and simple. (just needs some fixes and tweaks)- Waves do become a bit tedious and no differences between the enemies each wave (at least on regular difficulty) it's usually the same enemies for each map in order then random.- No Campaign is a bummer but it is planned in the future updates.Other Stuff- Unfortnately not a lot of online players and servers so expect to play mostly with friends then random people which isn't a bad thing, you'll probably have a better time with friends then randoms anyway but its personal preference.- Was hoping to see more pvp game modes, maybe a tug of war mode. its a 4v4 and you have to defend your own hyper core while your minion toys attack the other team or something of the sort. Maybe even a capture the flag mode. where the flag is a battery instead and you have to charge your own core or something. Just more other modes in general really. (I just hope too see a few more main modes really, which are planned in the road map and I am very looking forward to.)- Good Design and types of enemies, just hope to see more as well in updates.- Movement is smooth but just needs the slightest tweak with a few things but really it's pretty minor in my opinion and doesn't hinder gameplay at all.-This game has just alot of potential to be better (It's already good) but it can be better and improve with more over time, respectfully in my opinion, of course especially with continuous updates. It is impressive that this is a Fairly Small development team that has made such a good quality game as well so I don't expect things too be pumping out constantly and super fast. So as long as the quality is the same as the game itself with dlc and updates, Im pretty happy with buying this game and the packs to support it.-I don't review a lot of games but this is an under the radar game, and I think this game deserves more attention and notice and believe every review helps to keep this game going and noticed especially when it is a very fun and enjoyable experience, I wish the developers luck and look forward too seeing further updates with this solid game! I hope to see more in the future and look forward to the games that they develop next!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is seriously great, and its criminally underrated. If you want a very polished game to play with friends, definitely try out this game. There's a variety of game modes, including a wave defense mode where you defend structures (called hypercores) from a large amount of different enemies such as toy robots, Beyblades, and toy dinosaurs. A PVP mode that looks pretty sick, although I haven't tried it yet. And a zombie tag type infection mode, where one person starts out as a zombie and they have to try to infect everyone.I don't understand how this game has so few players. Its got some fairly unique building mechanics, the modular weapon system is fun and creative, and the visual style is great. You could probably even play your own game modes in the free roam mode such as hide and seek or hot potato. The game graphically looks great and its one of the most optimized games I think I've ever played. There's even a demo you can try out so you can decide if you want to buy the full game.Right now, the only thing holding this game back is the lack of players. Right now this game has an average player count in the single digits, which is really frustrating.This game is seriously amazing, and I think it is 100% worth the 20 bucks that it's sold for.Oh btw, did I mention that this game is being made by only 6 people?

_childDocuments_.review: The concept and execution of this game is wonderful.  The maps and textures are hyper-detailed.  Progression is excellent and in the 6 hours I've played (half solo, half online) I have unlocked 3 classes, multiple heads, skins, weapons, buildables, with many many many more to go.  This has a lot of potential to be around for a long time.  I typically don't play tower defense but this is different.  Even if the gameplay was terrible (it isn't) I'd still probably stick around for the maps!Map variety is amazing with large, small, and everything in between.  There is only 1 map I don't like (air hockey) but that is because it is difficult.  In addition to tower defense style buildables, you can change larger map subtlyl with different bunkers, towers, and jump points to enable to you camp a hypercore and move around the map more quickly.  Also, there are lots of different weapons to find and/or buy while playing each map (machine gun, sniper, grenade launcher, shotgun, laser, etc).  While playing online, there is also a slot machine in each map to play if you have extra coin.This is an amazing effort that I'm sure we will see copied by the larger less original studios (looking at you Epic) in the very near future, but I don't believe it's possible to have a game with more character.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is well made with a lot of style.--Gameplay--PVE: Pretty much defend the points against waves of enemy toys using map exploration to find weapon attachments and currency to put down traps and bolster your defences. This works very well but does have a level of RNG with drops etc.PVP: I haven't really played much of this but it seems like a simple and effective arena shooter with a few modifier game-modes like zombies which is cool.Freeroam: Exactly what it says on the tin. This mode is mainly to get used to the maps and find collectables for character unlocks which is a good touch and appreciated.--Controls--The controls are pretty standard for an FPS aside from the more floaty feeling during jumps.You have a standard jog and sprint along with a standard jump, double jump and vault/climb when holding down the spacebar to allow for easier traversal. Shooting is a standard sort of FPS thing with damage, recoil, accuracy and reloads that can be slightly buffed through attachments but if you are stuck between reloads you can also melee to deal damage. You have a basic weapon reticle that varies between weapons for aiming and the ability to zoom in with right click (If you have a sniper scope attachment you can scope in proper too).--Graphical design--The whole game reminds me of playing the toy story 2 video game on PS1 or army men on PS2 and I like that a lot!The maps have very good attention to detail even down to the small ones like the trash strewn about on the ground with great modelling, textures and scaling. In a word, the game is very TOYETIC if that's a thing.--Enemies--The base enemies are very well made with their own unique attack/movement animations and variations depending on difficulty. The explosions can be a bit too much at times however.The bosses, be it end of the level or mid wave mini-bosses, are all pretty fun to fight with each having their own designs, abilities and weaknesses. Very nice.--Customisation--The player gets a whole lot of customisation options that are unlocked in various ways on top of 2 payed for DLC packs that add some new character options to chose from which are pretty good.One interesting thing you can give your character a name from a set of unlockable preset words which have a good amount for creativity.The player character starts with a type that has different heads, colour schemes and weapons colours too which gives a pretty good amount of things to tweak and change.There is a bunch more I could say but I'll keep it simple. Overall there aren't really any aspects I HATE at all and the small dev team is constantly working hard to push new content and general updates for the future, props to them.An easy recommend for me and there is also a demo to try for you to check if this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much Hypercharge yet, but I can already tell that this game has the potential to become something very, very special. The developers have done something really difficult here in managing to capture a true childhood-like experience of just playing with our toys and upscaling it into a grand battle that is both beautiful and funny. Kudos.Stuff that I love about this game:- No microtransactions. Thank you for not being evil.- Map design and variety. - Tons of stuff to unlock. Buildables, skins, maps, even new names in the name generator.- The name generator itself is a delight. - The off-brands. Just reading the labels on all of the various props around has been cracking me up. I wish my speed stick had 24 hour Hodor protection.- The music. Great soundtrack with a perfect 80's vibe. I hope more tracks continue to be added!- The level of nostalgia that this game sets off is incredible.- Challenges and Collectibles for added objectives each map. Things that need improvement:- As I write this, only one game mode exists. Coop defense vs waves of enemies. It's fun, but I could see it getting stale after a while, especially once you've collected all of the unlockables. But considering a drop-down menu for game modes exists in the menu, I have to assume that more modes are planned for the future.- The weapon system could use improvement. Attachments are unclear as how they effect you (ex: different optics simply say things like +1 accuracy, but in a game where there is no aiming down sights and only a zoom-in-effect, I have no idea if accuracy means an improved zoom effect, decreased spread, recoil reduction, sway, or what. There's also no indicator for how much +1 is vs nothing or +2, or any comparison with a currently equipped attachment of the same slot). Weapon variety itself is a bit low, but a new weapon was just patched in today, so again my hope is that this is being worked on already.- The machine gun is awful. If it's going to be less accurate and do less damage than the regular rifle, it can't also have a smaller mag. Give that thing at least 60 rounds.- Enemy variety. I absolutely love the enemies that exist (the spinning crossfire death discs might be a bit too strong) but I would love to see more knock-offs of different toys coming in to attack. A bit of randomization to some waves might be nice as well.- Shop inventories. While I love the way that shops are set up as attachments that come in the toy's box, it's a little awkward trying to mouse over every little object to see if it's anything useful or not. I think a shopping menu that you can access at the boxes might be more intuitive. It could also let us sell unwanted attachments for more cash/building coin.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a pure FPS game and this is not a pure Tower Defense game. This is a game that takes a lot of inspiration from these mechanics but integrates them very well in a truly amusing environment.Even the free roaming experience gives moments of pure fun by browsing between toys, books, posters and other items that cames directly from your childhood. One of the best video game setting out there!The care and commitment they put into the sounds and the soundtrack is also impressive.In terms of customization, the game has a lot to offer and asks for nothing but a few hours of commitment and fun. There are action figures for every taste and the pseudo-random generation of battle names is hilarious.As a true psycho child I would have loved to be able to indifferently mount every head on every body but I understand the difficulty in keeping this aspect under control so I keep it as a dream that I know cannot be realized.There's no real singleplayer / adventure mode but from what I've read it should be coming soon and I can't wait. I'd like to see a survival mode in the future as well. Shooting like crazy at hordes of toys until they overwhelm you would be a lot of fun.The fact that I can play it without problems on linux made me buy an additional copy to a friend as a gift. Any linux user should support this developers!

_childDocuments_.review: is an excellent co-op wave shooter, and it evokes fond memories of playing with action figures and toy soldiers as a child.This game has style, and it has it in spades. Every bit of this game is beautifully detailed, down to the fine text on the various products strewn throughout the levels. It's amazing how much they've been able to cram in. It really feels like you're in a store, or a kid's bedroom, or the kitchen, etc. You look like a plastic action figure, and I especially love that your hands are always in a claw grip.This game is pretty challenging, which encourages experimentation with your trap loadout and placement. You'll really have to work for a perfect game on harder difficulties. The guns are satisfying to use.Customization is great. You're able to switch your body type and head, from things like a standard soldier, a bug man, or a kung-fu guy. There are different colors for your body and your guns which you unlock through gameplay and finding secrets in the levels. And, the funniest bit, you get to name your action figure from a list of preset prefixes, adjectives, and nouns.The PvP is lots of fun. There's only a few modes at the time of writing, Team Deathmatch, Free for All, and Plague Mode. (like Infected from Halo)It's amazing, I love it, and I think a lot of people will enjoy this game as much as I do too.

_childDocuments_.review: started off to be a fresh and unique take on the tower defense genre, not necessarily redefining it by any means but it definitely stands out from the crowd. The idea of being a toy soldier defending Hypercores against a multitude of various toys was a charming experience. However the further that you progress into this title, the more obvious it became that some core mechanics were either overlooked completely or restricted compared to other tower defense games.• A variety of different enemies with different variations• Each level is well designed with a lot of attention to detail and secrets• The majority of weapons were decent and fun to use• The idea of being a toy fighting against different enemy toys was quite a charming factor• Lot of replay value if you have a full team• PVP is also available if you’re interested in that• Lacks and restricts basic tower defense mechanics • Games difficulty doesn’t scale with the number of team members, solo players won’t survive• There are fixed positions where you are forced to build towers, with little to freedom• Sometimes the game feels too RNG based, sometimes you’ll get OP weapons that spawn and other times you won’t get anything worthwhile• The range of turrets is represented by a number but it never shows how much a unit is in the map• Sometimes towers to me were damaged but to other players, they weren’t damaged at all• An instance happened where the wave wouldn’t end so we were forced to restartLike any tower defense game your main objective is to protect your base of operation, in this case you’ll be defending Hypercores. Depending on which map you play on, there can be anywhere between one to four Hypercores to protect. It isn’t necessary to protect them all though it does affect your rating on the level which can unlock new towers.Upon starting a level you’ll be given three minutes to explore the map, collect money, build defenses and find batteries. Exploring these maps was always enjoyable the first few times, though some maps were more platform heavy than others, there was still a lot of secrets and collectibles to find as well as references and jokes scattered around the map. Three minutes barely seemed like enough time for a team of two and we usually fell short on time to do all the necessary preparations for the upcoming wave.This title definitely brings new mechanics to the tower defense genre that makes it unique. Whilst your defenses primarily slow down and shoot nearby enemies, the majority of the firepower will come from the weapons that you acquire. There’s a decent amount of weapons that you can find that can mow down most of the enemies, though some were clearly more superior than others. Unfortunately finding these weapons comes down to luck whether they spawn in a shop or around the map.In order to progress through the game you’ll need to obtain medals to unlock other levels. Depending on how many Hypercores you protect will depend on what medal you will get. On expert difficultly, it can be very challenging to get the diamond medal and it got to a point where it felt impossible to progress with just a team of two.As you progress through the game you’ll undoubtedly encounter a lot of different enemies from different toy sets. You’ll be fighting against toy soldiers, robots, spinners, bouncy balls and various other enemies along with different variations of them on the harder difficulties. Some defenses were more effective against specific enemies (for example fire traps were good against spinners) but it was more of a trial and error system to find out which ones were best against what enemy. Spinners were a primary concern if you built walls since the walls were hollow if the spinner could get inside then it would destroy the wall in seconds and leave your Hypercore exposed.However,  seems to overlook some of the most basic tower defense mechanics or make them more restricted. One of the more annoying restrictions is the fixed positions that you build your defenses on, there’s little freedom to where you can place your towers, and although the harder difficulties give you more places to build it still felt rather restrictive.To add more frustration there isn’t any indication as to were your enemies will be coming from. This becomes problematic since you don’t know which Hypercores to protect with more defenses and which ones you don’t have to bother with on that wave. It punishes the player despite not giving information that they need to effectively spend their money and choose which defenses would be the most effective.One of the more noticeable flaws with  is the fact that it doesn’t seem to scale its difficultly depending on how many players are on your team. Solo players will definitely have a hard time getting through the more difficult levels because of the sheer amount of enemies spawning or because of the size of the maps. It seems that  was definitely created with a full team in mind, punishing solo players or teams below four in a number of ways. You can join random people through servers however, you do need a level of communication that doesn’t seem possible when playing with random people.Another overlooked mechanic is yet again more information that is withheld from the player, being able to know what enemies will be attacking on what wave is vital to keeping the Hypercores alive.  doesn’t seem to have this basic feature, on more than one occasion we had to restart because we didn’t have the defenses required to effectively take care of the enemies on that wave. This would usually result in a Hypercore being destroyed or heavily and having no choice but to restart since it would affect our rating for that level.Playing in the perspective of a toy soldier was very appealing, being able to climb the familiar environments of the bedroom, kitchen and gardens was a joy. Every map has a lot of detail both in the textures and references that you’ll find by exploring the maps. Enemies are all designed to be just like classic toys and some are obviously plain knock offs of classic toys from your childhood that adds to the charm of the game. definitely brought some interesting mechanics to the table, its just unfortunate that it forgot about some of the more basic ones. Playing this game solo is practically impossible up to a certain point and even with another friend you won’t be able to get through the entire game without a full team. If you and some friends can team up and play this game together then I would definitely recommend this title. If not then I would wait for an update until it balances some of these issues so it can be possible to play solo or with a friend.
