_childDocuments_.review: After viewing the steam page I was pleasantly surprised by how much I actually enjoy playing this game. It is a similar to a tower defense game, but it encourages/requires exploration between waves of enemies. A timer appears between each wave for you to explore and collect credits or collectibles and build up your defenses. Different strategies are needed for different maps and yes, even different waves. I have played exclusively Co-op so I can't speak for the other game modes, but it is extremely engaging and requires communication and teamwork. Each map brings different challenges. My team and I played several maps, unlocked skins and immediately began customizing our action figures. Then pressed to unlock more. It is fun and addicting and has a lot of playable hours in it making it well worth the money. I can see this as a base game with more maps/unlocks being added in the future as I feel that this game definitely is "beatable" and once all the items are unlocked there won't be much point in playing anymore. The appearance is charming and brings back childhood memories and sparks the imagination in a very Toy Soldier like atmosphere. There are unlock-able characters and skins for your little action figure and your weapon.There is a lot of parkour to collect credits or collectables. These challenges of a different taste than the fast beat shoot'em up during each wave really breaks the game up in a refreshing way. I find it keeps me engaged as basic shooters tend to leave me bored after only a few rounds. I only wish it gave you a little more time during each round for these exploration stages. I end up turning the difficulty to easy for the first few times on each map in order to get all the collectibles as easy mode gives you roughly 4 mins between waves to try to figure out some of the parkour puzzles and try and fail at them a few times while still giving you time to build your defenses. The only thing I found to be disappointing right off the bat was that there were no female versions of each action figure type. It has nothing to do with the game play, just a purely cosmetic thing, but as a girl, its nice to play as a girl character. Especially since the entire game is centered around unlocking customizables for your character. But this doesn't take away anything from this games value or the fun to be had. So i don't see this as a negative, just a little disappointment. There are a few issues I have found. Though none of them are game breaking or even irritating on a level to cause more than a fleeting, mild annoyance.  One of which, is the short tutorial leaves a lot to be desired. I came out of it having no idea how to do a melee attack. Either the words flashed by on the screen too fast for me to catch or I just missed it amidst my panic as I tried to fight little robot action figures.I still have no idea what order the medals are in. I believe it is bronze, silver, gold, platinum, diamond, then emerald? I have also heard rumors that there is a ruby, but I could be wrong and perhaps diamond is the highest? I only know of some of the rewards because the skins require an emerald or diamond score to unlock them. Otherwise, I would have no idea there was even an emerald.And there are options in the host co-op menu that are unclear. There are some things that aren't explained clearly. Navigating the menu can be a little confusing. When first trying to figure out how to play co-op I stumbled around in the menu for a minute as I was expecting a large CO-OP button. Instead, there is a play online and I am still unclear if your friends can just join you as I have had to invite them every time because we can't figure out how to join friends games from the in game menu, so we use steam invites instead. Using the menu I am still unclear and it is a little confusing.In game there are upgrades for your weapons that add to things like accuracy. I have collected a lot of them, but never noticed a difference. I don't know if they do anything at all. If there is a difference, it isn't noticeable during battle.Overall, it is a great game. I enjoy playing and highly recommend it. It is worth the price and I see a lot of potential for dlc's or expansions for this game, continuing the fun. I hope the developers do add new levels, each with their assortment of new maps/challenges. It is really fun. And is some of the most fun I have had with fam/friends on a game in a long time. Seriously, if you are here at the steam page and giving it a look, just buy it. You will get your money's worth and have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game. The devs are great people that care about their game. They've released a slew of free updates and are on top of fixing bugs. The base game looks and runs great, is a unique twist on the genre, and has some fun combat. Still, the game just doesn't have much replay value. You don't have to take my word for it, though; even the reviews that recommend the game only have 5-10 hours in the game on average. If that's all you're looking for, then this game will be a fun time. If you want to be able to play a game for more than an afternoon or two as I do, then this game is not for you.Devs, I know you are working on making that campaign, but I think there are much better uses of your time and energy than something that will most likely only be played once. After you finish that, I think you need to work on making the base game more random and varied as well as some medium to long term goals for people to keep working towards. As of now, each map is basically the same experience each time. Once you find all the collectibles, why play it again? I recommend taking a page from other games that spawn random waves with a rare chance of special waves (like maybe an alien invasion or a ton of green military figures or something). The Gardens and Graveyards game mode of Plants vs. Zombies Garden Warfare does this well. On top of making each session more fun, players need a reason to keep playing/something to work towards. Yes, there already is a ton of different skins to unlock and better versions of placeable defenses, but there is a not a clear path to earning them. It just kinda...happens every once in a while. Players need to be able to target earning what they want to.

_childDocuments_.review: [Disclaimer: I have only played the campaign for 2 hours so my impression *could* change with more play-time]I saw a reel for this game on Instagram and had to buy it!It looked like a realisation of my childhood, playing with action figures with my brothers, in the wake of films like Toy Story and Small Soldiers (from which I'm sure the developers took some inspiration).After my first play-through I can say its great! The nods to all sorts of things from the 90s (from toy stores to the toys themselves) are great and I can't tell you how much I love it when games entice you to explore with the promise of unseen collectables. Something that is often lacking from most modern games.That being said, I can't shake the feeling that as it is it's fallen short of its potential in two critical areas.1. PvE/StoryHaving not played the original, multiplayer mode of the game I can't really comment on it, but from what I've read it appears that the campaign essentially draws completely from it, but adds a string of narrative.I like the route they've gone with the narrative, and the comic strips are really well done, but it feels like a bit of a cop-out for a single player mode to just be a version of MP with bots. They could have done a little more and created a more fully fledged story mode, with some of those MP elements but with a narrative that evolves as you play each level.Like I said before (and has been echoed by many other reviews) the game gives me Small Soldier/Toy Story vibes. It would be great if they capitalised on that more and brought in more of what makes those two special.2. MapsThe maps have been brilliant so far, each further drawing on what it felt like as a child with their favourite action figure in any given environment. The toy stores have been my particular faves, giving you plenty to explore while also providing lots of ways to take out at the enemy...I just wish they were bigger. I know there are limits and what makes sense given the mechanics of the game, but my urge to explore and find other vantage points always lead me to the doors or the end of the aisle where I'm left disappointed to see the (almost) invisible wall. I want to run around the whole house!! I've seen mention of some bigger maps, maybe I've just not got to them yet, but I just feel like there should be more room.(As an aside to the subject of maps, how about this for an idea? A MP mode a bit like Planetside where you have various teams in battle for control of a whole house/store. It could work much like I imagine MP currently does, with points being captured and defended, but each battle contributes to the overall control of the region.)As I previously admitted, I've not played the MP aspect of this game but I think I know what I'm going to say about it based on the little I've read. I'll reserve my judgement on it for now, and come back once I've played it.So yeah, so far I'd give it a 6.5/10, but it could be even better with some more additions.[Edit #1] Oh, and I really wish I could choose to only use 3rd person. The point in this game is to see that you're a toy. you can't do that in 1st and I have to switch camera modes in every level and with every respawn...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is already truly excellent. I've just been seeing adverts for Grounded and getting excited about a game on a small scale, and then this drops into my lap. I've played about 10 hours so far, and myself and my friends that have played it all agree that you can DEFINITELY see that this was made by a group of friends, because it's just... fun, which is the highest compliment I can give any game. The environments are stunning, particularly all the easter eggs; the music is fantastic; the enemy models are perfect; the naming style for your character is GENIUS and not something I would have ever thought of; the controls are intuitive.From reading the developer responses to other reviews, I was very happily surprised to learn that the game is still being updated and changes will still be made. I was already extremely pleased with the game as is, but to hear new game modes might be added in has me very excited. A singleplayer mode would be very useful I think, as some people have mentioned the difficulty is a tad high when there's only 1 of you since you're stretched defending 3 hypercores at once, and depending on the map that can be very difficult to manage. I would add though that I wouldn't want the solution to be what so many games do, whereby you ALWAYS have 4 people on your team, and if there's less than 4 players it just fills the rest with AI. I think one of the dev responses mentioned adding 1 AI bot to help you in singleplayer, which I'd be very happy with, but I wouldn't want the AI to outnumber me 3:1 at that scale.The limitations on where you can build defences makes a lot of sense to me - I would say my only issue so far has been that a lot of the more static defences don't feel dynamic enough to me. Glue traps are fantastic, actively slowing the enemies down and giving you more time to deal with them, but I find walls to end up not being that useful as a couple of solid hits and they're gone. On top of that, it makes them feel like a bad investment as when they're destroyed you have to pay for a brand new one at full price. To use the castle walls as an example in the bedroom map (Dawn of the Toys I think?), I would quite like it if the base price for a wall is something like 15 build credits (or however much it is right now as I recall it being a sensible price), if it's damaged but not destroyed it's 5 to repair, but then if it's destroyed rather than just falling down and vanishing maybe the enemy could bust THROUGH, and then charge you 10 to repair it? That may go against the toy feeling, however, so I would totally get it if that's not the direction artistically the devs wanted to go.One final thing that might help would be either in each level, or maybe only in levels you've already played at least once, before each wave comes maybe it could give you a hint of where the enemies will spawn? I know in some levels, e.g. No 2, you can basically just leave one of the hypercores until later as it won't be attacked directly until wave 3 or 4. Knowing where the enemy will come from, and therefore which hypercores will be most vulnerable in a given wave, might allow players to think more tactically, and maybe destroy defences around 1 core to get the credits to reinforce one that's about to be hit hard.Honestly, if nothing I've said above gets implemented or anything close to it, this would still be one of my favourite games I've played this year. As I've said above, this game is just FUN, I can kick back with a controller and shoot little green army men, and what else do you want in life?Oh, and on a final note, THANK YOU FOR HAVING SPLITSCREEN. I feel like a lot of game developers have forgotten that splitscreen exists over the years, and it sucks because this sort of game is meant for the old days of 4 friends sitting spread across sofas, bean bags and floor in a living room, a few bottles of fizzy drinks, and laughing and yelling as they play together. Kudos to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I’d been watching this game on Steam for some time because I’m big fan of toy games like the original Army Men and the Toy Soldiers games and this looked right up my alley. I think it’s the nostalgia thing that gets me, the fond memories of playing with toys as a kid and setting up big elaborate battle scenes. For some reason I never got around to buying it though, then one day my 10-year-old son saw it on the Nintendo Switch eShop and really liked the look of it and kept asking me to buy it. I thought it would be better on PC, so I stalled him. Fast forward to the 2020 Steam Winter/Summer sale and I noticed it was in sale and showed my son who so excited about it that he used his leftover birthday money to buy it. I’m so glad he did, as we have been having a blast playing it ever since and even my 8 year-old-son has now joined in for 3 player split-screen action. I literally have to stop them from playing as the 3 of us would happily sit there and play it all day if we could, we’re totally obsessed, curse you responsible parenting! I’m using my keyboard and the boys are both using controllers (Xbox One and Xbox 360) and the controls work perfectly. The game’s main mode is a first-person shooter/tower defence hybrid. The levels are a mix of everyday rooms in a house and in a toyshop where you have a set time to explore to collect money to use to build your defences around the “Hypercores” that you need to defend. One of the things that always sucks me into games in unlockable content and goals/achievements and this game has heaps of them. Each level, on top of the hidden coins, coin packs and gear you need to find, there are also well-hidden collectable items. Your money can also be used to buy weapon upgrades in shops or you can take a risk and gamble with a slot machine, which is unlocked after finishing a level over a certain rating for awesome loot (strangely, both my boys get obsessed with these machines and spend far too much money on them). It’s a lot of fun jumping around the level searching for stuff, especially as the developers have added a heap of little details and jokes throughout each level. The level of detail is impressive, for example on the back of some of the toy boxes there’s full readable text. Your character can only build 3 different defence structures at a time, which you can change and customise before you start a game. As with most things in this game your choice of 3 structures is very limited at the start as you need to unlock more as you progress. This also helps when playing co-op to make sure everyone has a good combination of defences at their disposal. The other unlockables in the game are various characters and cosmetics for them. I also like how you unlock a custom title for you character using 4 different slots that have various names you can combine to make you own 3 word title that appears above you in-game, mine is currently: “Sir Mighty Eagle”. There are a couple of other game modes, including a Deathmatch and an Infected style mode, which I have only played briefly. They’re good, but just not as fun as the tower defence co-op mode in my opinion.Everyone starts with a basic rifle weapon, which, depending on the level, will start with one function. You can often find weapon attachments scattered throughout the level and in the in-game shop and slot machine. You are limited to 2 weapon types to change between at once and in some cases with the more powerful and rare weapons like the flamethrower and minigun, only one. The other attachments are items that add accuracy to you weapon, like sights, bipods, and stocks. There is a decent enough variety of weapons, like shotguns, grenade launchers, lasers and machine guns and you soon discover that some weapons are more suited to killing certain enemies that others. This once again comes into co-op strategy as it works well if your team has a good mix of weapons to help take out certain enemies quicker and easier. Speaking of enemies, they are a cool mix of old-school and newer toys that attack you in waves. There’s classic army men, bouncy balls, robots, zombies, and Beyblades just to name a few. They each have different ways of moving and attacking and once you learn their strategies it is a lot easier to dispatch them. And there’s even larger bosses on some levels that take a fair amount of damage before you kill them.You can play this game by yourself and it is still fun, if not a bit harder to defend the cores all by yourself, but this game shines playing co-op with friends without a doubt. The lasting appeal of this game is redoing all the levels and trying to find all the collectables and then increasing the difficulty to try and get some more unlockables. I’m really excited to see what the developers have planned for the future of this game, some more content and DLC packs would be amazing. Great retro theme, awesome level of detail, great couch co-op, tonnes of unlockable content, great for split-screen  Could use some more levels and modes (which it looks like the dev’s will add in at some stage), not as much fun by yourselfEDIT: Since I posted this review the dev's have added so much more free content and they continue to do so, making an awesome game even better!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has never been any fun to play (as you can infer from the fact that I gave up on trying to find a way to enjoy it after only 3 hours) and I don't think it ever will be because rather than listen to player feedback on how to improve the game (namely by adding worthwhile content rather than microtransactions) the devs instead seem to focus on the worst possible form of PR management by attempting to censor negative user-reviews for their microtransactions and banning people who write them.Save your money. I actually gave this game a timid recommendation back when it was still in Early Access because although it wasn't good, I liked the concept and hoped it would eventually become good if the devs could just improve the core gameplay...My sincere apologies to anyone who might have bought the game based on my review because rather than actually make the game good, the devs added MICROTRANSACTIONS in the form of "DLC" skins.After I posted a negative review for a bundle of those, the devs flagged my review with Steam which temporarily resulted in my review being banned. (As you can see above it's back up now because Steam Support found that it was wrongly banned)One of the devs even ADMITTED on discord that they had flagged my review for because it referred to his skin bundles as microtransactions.This is especially absurd since "microtransaction" is literally the same terms used b Eurogamer and other publications to refer to the cosmetic "DLC" in "So Borderlands 3 will indeed have in-game microtransactions, but these will be cosmetic-only..."So to summarize, these devs literally believe that THEY are entitled to decide what the word "microtransactions" means and then flag reviews that use the term in the same way as major gaming publications... Literally minutes after telling me that they flagged my review and WOULD FLAG any other reviews that mentioned their microtransactions, they banned me from the Steam forum literally without even listing a reason, citing an old post that literally read: "Thanks I'm looking forward to it!" in response to one of the devs describing plans for future content.The game works, it looks great, and it's a nice concept.HOWEVER, it isn't nearly as interesting as I hoped it would be because the tower defense aspect is kind of broken (you never actually seem to get enough money to build any of the more interesting defenses) and as a result, the game is kind of dull to play.This game could be great with more dramatic battles and enough money to actually build interesting bases.Timid recommendation because it works and what is here is good but it could be so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is pure fun and a nostalgic overflow.It has several modes. PvE tower-defense with 14 levels and a stylish art-book like story telling campaign. S mall-to-medium replayability factor. (But it will get better when endless mode becomes a thing). PVP modes like Team Deathmatch, Free-for-All and Infection.(Can be played with bots too and friends in private lobbies) Split-Screen mode. 4 difficulty stages.Intuitive gunplay and high level of customization with a little bit of grind required to unlock some parts. (Just like in the 90's!)Flawless performance. Stable FPS, no lag or crashing.Only gets better with friends and family.Recommended with reasonable expectations, as this is an indie team of 5 people.     With a total of 13+ hrs on record, trying to explain how nostalgic this game is , would be an understatement of a century.With every new level you discover or rediscover a part of your childhood and that distant, long forgotten memory that unlocks with an audible 'clink', when you see your favorite toy come to life again. A straight definition of a 'core memory unlocked'. In short, I adore this game. But as anything game-related, I will always try to criticize it without prejudice and provide an actual experience in a form of a review.     First of all, game-play. I would consider it to be good with room for growth. The gunfight is enjoyable and responsive. Each weapon feels as it should feel and packs enough damage as one would expect it to. The idea that you create your own weapon with each session/level, based on your needs at a time, seems like a healthy choice for a tower-defense/shooter. (Although I would like to see an in-game vending machine, where your pre-built weapon could be purchased.) Luckily enough, that is not an issue in almost any level. Throughout said level, you can still create a weapon of your choosing, even when playing with friends.     And perhaps you remember the good old days, when you and your friends gathered at their place and played on a single TV or Screen, using Split-Screen mode? Well, I'm happy to report that this game has this too. One that can be customized to your own preference.    The level design is great with a clear inspiration from Toy Story or Small Soldiers.(From a child's bedroom, where toys come to life to a garden and the toy store.) Presenting a healthy array of jumping-puzzles, collectibles, points of interest and Easter eggs. Almost anyone could find their preferred play style when it comes to weapons. Those few who enjoy a melee based combat, will be disappointed as there are no blades, axes or daggers, just a good old fashioned knuckle sandwich.    Secondly, performance. Geforce RTX 3070 / AMD Ryzen 5/3600 6-core. / 16 gb RAM = 99% 125 FPS. || 200 FPS. I think the result speaks for itself. I have not experienced a drastic dip in FPS or have any lag when playing with friends. Don't remember a single crash either. But again, that is my experience.     And lastly, content. From what I know, the game is being developed by a small indie team. Ever since 2020, the game received several major updates. Introducing campaign, maps, enemies, guns, fixes and more. They are not frequent but they are great. Sometimes there are major updates back to back and sometimes several months pass without much happening. And as of this moment, they are working on an endless tower-defense mode. Which will only enhance the grand experience of this game.     And if you will ever get bored of the campaign and its repetitiveness? The game also offers actual PVP modes such as: free-for-all and Team Deathmach. Infection. (Essentially Zombie survival).Sadly they don't seem to be as populated as one would want them to be. At least in some cases. Some days better than others.One thing is certain. The developers love this game. They love their past and they introduce us to our own nostalgia without looking like greedy corpos thirsting for a quick cash grab. Their DLC's are straightforward. A support package and a couple of action figures.I recommend this game at this stage as it may as well be on par with Deep Rock Galactic, just not as fleshed out. (yet).

It also runs easily at 60 fps on my aging Dell XPS 9550 (with a eGPU GTX 970). There is also 4-player (up to) spit-screen mode - which is in itself a lost art. Playing with my buddies just threw me back 15 years to Halo days. There are modes for all to play - and even little 'party game' style games (Spinners mode and Tank battles).The online mode is solid - there will no doubt be more servers playing up as this launch happens. Hypercharge seriously makes me feel like my 80's kid self. I don't normally 'double-dip' into games on multiple platforms, but something compelled me to just do it. With the 1.0 official launch happening - it's an absolute MUST-HAVE game to own. It's a true sleeper-hit waiting in the wings.

_childDocuments_.review: There is Early Access and then there is development hell Early Access.  Currently this could easily be released today and be 100% better than some other full games out there.  I would put this in the category with Deep Rock Galactic early access run.  The only thing it lacks is more of it. That being said this isn't barebones with ten levels, multiple enemies, and lots of unlockable cosmetics.Short Review: If it looks fun to you I would say get it.  I bought it on a whim (mainly due to the aesthetics) and I have been having fun.  If you like horde/tower defense gameplay as well as exploring huge rooms as an action figure then give it a shot.Gushing Long Review: All I can say, #1 is the art style is 1000% on point.  There is so much attention to detail everywhere!  All of the plastic looks like molded plastic.  I ran into a random garlic clove in the bedroom and I spent a minute just looking over the details.  So many games in the last few years have tried to do the nostalgia of old toys, but they never get the idea right.  Two examples that work so well here is when you spawn in, you burst out of your packaging.  Additional weaponry is even attached to these boxes.  The other example is players don't have player names, they have toy names, like Dr. Punch Man. Which is all selectable in the customization screen.It would be one thing to have a level full of cool details everywhere, but have no reason to look at it.  Some games (I'm thinking of For Honor right now) have loads of detail but all of the gameplay is hyper focused in a small area.  Hypercharge is different because each building round you need to get money that is littered around the room.  So each new round you will want to explore new shelves, around boxes, and in the rafters for all the money and unlockables.  More money means better defenses and more unlockables means more customization.Levels are large, but (as far as I have gotten) not hard to manage. Typically there is one defense point that is out in the open, another one that is slightly less visible, and one that is usually out of the way with less defenses. Most fights start with a focus on the main one, then bump up to the first two, and by the third round you are getting sneaky enemies attacking the third.  I have been playing solo and it's doable but the garage was the first mission I just gave up on one node to focus on the other two.  The game can be soloed but there are definitely advantages to having more players.I'm sort of blathering on at this point so here are my two major highlights so far.  In the second story level the game spawned in green army men.  Here is what I'm talking about with aesthetics.  The army men aren't green soldiers, they are army men with flat mountings on their feet, so to approach you they have to hop!  It's kind of horrifying in a way, even more so because these are the first enemies that have ranged attacks.  So the round starts and I hear a weird diesel engine sound.  Must be an ambient truck noise (I forgot to mention there is some good sound design too).  Then I see one of those classic green tanks that usually come with green army men.  This is followed by out of control green jeeps and finally a huge bomber flying overhead.  The floor is littered with still army men and the bomber is dropping parachute men.  It's chaos, but I'm having a blast.The other moment is just the simple joy that the action playset (with clearly defined "Battle Damage TM" window) is something you can actually use for cover.  Cons: MOAR everything!  The game is great, but more stuff would just make it better. My only other criticism is I think it would be cool if you could interact with the environment.  Like stepping on the keyboard changes the screen or if you step on that plate in the playset the "Battle Damage TM" window blows out.  Maybe things like that could be triggered to do damage to enemies or block paths.Can't wait to see what will be next for HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't put a ton of time into this game, but I can assure you it is worth way more than the 15$ you are going to spend. The update that it recently received could be considered a new game in itself with only the feel of the original lingering in the air.HyperCharge: Unboxed is best played with friends but is completely enjoyable just by yourself.it is an incredibly cool take on the original tower defense games, and while this genre has been done before. The dev team has out done themselves by making this game a unique experience for the player.The graphics are an amazing. first off, while they are pretty realistic you will still get this feeling that you’re just a plastic doll running around the map. a lot of the things you can jump on and identify throughout the map push that art choice. That allows you to get extremely immersed in the game; even before you start the tower defense aspect of it.The defense aspect of it isn't anything too new at least on the surface, each character before playing can select 3 cards to take with them to build with. each card is a defense which will impede or attack enemies before they reach the core. The main difference from other games is that you also get your own weapon which can have at least two different gun types attached to it. this setup allows for a lot of customization between players.this leads into the gameplay, which is an incredible mix of strategy and just plain fun when playing with your friends. For each level there are 3 different difficulties with 3 different medals for each that you can earn. Medals are achieved by how many objectives are left standing by the end. My only grip right now with the gameplay is that it needs a mode where the waves don’t end for each level. that would make playing levels over again more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Big note: My playtime being 37 hours is from me randomly deciding to go back and get SOME stuff, and playing out of boredom. The real playtime, if you're just going once through is probably around 4-6 hours, if you can actually get through it with the bots or get graced with the right online party.Welp... Here we are at campaign's debut, which may as well be 1.0, and... Wow.-The menus have been overcomplicated and downgraded in a previous update (you have to back out from the singleplayer menu with a specific button now in order to get back to the choice screens, tabbing three or four times to go back to be able to choose Online instead of the previous 1-and-set-to-private, but you can also still exit the menu like normal with one button press, leaving you in the menu you wanted to get out of by pressing said button, too, so... was that change really necessary...?)-The maps shown in said menus will bug out and not show you the correct amounts of anything in that level, instead it'll show you the values for the PREVIOUS map you looked at.-Enabling Vsync crashes the game-Hidden collectibles do nothing but give certain awful one-color skins. Objectives also do nothing, unless it's the single one on Adventure Dunes that gets you some more build credits.-All cosmetics are still locked behind random requirements, and buildables are behind medal levels on certain maps. This includes name options, meaning you might have do do all levels on expert and nightmare, then have your hypercores never take any damage before you get the skin or name/adjectives or buildables you like... Except, if you're at that point, you're already about to leave the game anyway due to it being too hard or not playing with friends, so... Why?-The bobbleheads to get different voices/heads for characters are hidden in some really mean spots, I recommend looking up the guides to find them all, cause, no, you're not finding them all on your own. Some can only be shot from exactly 1 angle and it's just plain annoying to get them. Also look up the guide for getting pleb/max ammo, cause, yeah no, you probably didn't even realize they were unlockable til now.-The comics do almost nothing. It basically just shows Max Ammo going through the different areas with no continuity or explanation of what happens to introduced characters, or acknowledgement of the player. In fact, the ending takes the punch out of YOU defeating/exploding Major Evil by saying "oh no! Max Ammo did it, except Major Evil decided to jump off a ledge and a dog actually is just using him as a chewtoy now lol!!!" Basically, we're just stand-ins for Max Ammo the whole time, which would be better if everyone actually started with him, instead of him being unlockable as a super-secret... Oh, and the final bit to the narrator's dialogue is a sequel bait, but, I get the distinct feeling that nothing will come of it...-Bots STILL don't care about hypercores. They can literally all be at the same hypercore, have that hypercore be swarmed by 8 enemies, and they'll shoot something far away from it, so, good luck soloing. They also like to build stuff that doesn't do much of anything helpful.-Online lobbies are practically nonexistant, because everyone else already went through every map, did every difficulty they wanted to, and unlocked everything THEY COULD (remember the earlier point). _childDocuments_.review: This one feels like a hidden gem on Steam. Fun cooperative (or competitive) game based around the realm of toys. Even as an adult this is one fun game, and add the fact its local split screen simply adds the cherry on top. In short, would recommend a purchase on sale (and especially if friends are picking up a copy).HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed (HU)'s  is straight forward and simple. The game allows the player to switch between first person and third person, with a double jump and ledge climbing ability that is integral to the game's mechanics. The movement is smooth and doesn't feel janky. In the defence type game mode player's are challenged to collect a variation of secrets (from gap jumps, finding collectables, and tagging) in addition to collecting coins. As the player collects coins they are allowed to build a preset defence around coloured "towers". Around the map the player can purchase or find weapon upgrades. Two weapons are allowed to be equipped at once (such as shotgun and rifle), but bigger weapons such as a rocket launcher or mini-gun take up both slots. Eliminating enemies also gives the player credit to use towards defence. The enemies themselves are varied, fun, and challenging. From BeyBlades, to toy robots, to drones, to toy planes and jets, to tanks, to jeeps, etc... Each enemy adds a new challenge, and the game throws mini-bosses and large bosses the player's way. The better the player performs in levels means more game unlocks. This is an underrated feature in games as most games require some sort of pay to play. It is rewarding to play and be able to unlock levels, skins, or characters. The  are spot on and absolutely immerse the player into the environment. Being a tiny toy in a giant room and navigating obstacles that a every day room would pose to such a small character is a fun universe to play in. The game does a good job notifying players of possible jumps, and the more familiar a player feels with the level - the more fun it is to jump from location to location. Animations are well done, especially when BeyBlades explode and when the toy robots get punched by the player causing a 360 spin. I also think majority of the level designs were extremely well done. The  are also suitable to the game's environment. Every little sound (from building to moving about the map) is included, and the music switches between some fun themes.Overall, would highly recommend a purchase on sale (and especially with friends). It's a fun simple game I feel anyone can get into - and even appropriate enough if you're playing with kids. One major down side to the game is the inability to throw grenades. Beyond that - well done Devs.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast to play and a awesome nostalgic trip to 80's and 90's toys, beautiful environments, and great gameplay. One feature that this game has that I think is amazing and that is lost from modern games is four-player split screen couch coop. Literally an amazing feature to play with your family or friends. The game itself has platforming aspects that are fun and enjoyable, and for a game with as much freedom as this one in the environments I expected to get a lot of clipping or stuck in weird places, this is not the case here, excellent design. The game is a four player shooter where you defend HyperCores from waves of evil toys, but can be played solo with surprisingly intelligent AI bots. There is the ability to place buildables and turrets, but these are more to complement the shooting than actual tower defense. There are collectables and unlockables in every map and toy solider skins and outfits which are a great progression goal. Also there is quite a bit of extra things to do stuffed in here, with a diorama sets, party games, and multiplayer, more than a lot of triple AAA games. The developers have shown to be absolutely invested into making this a great game and every update makes it even better. For problems with this game, the online seen is hard to find games, but I never had a problem with it as I normally play with bots or my friends locally. I feel like this game was made to be played with families or friends in the same room. Other issues are the occasional  bug, not game breaking but annoying. A good example is the Tank party game included which lets you play as tanks in a top down arena mode, it sadly does not have functioning controls when used with a gamepad controller, but really not a big deal as the party game itself was just a bonus. Overall, 10/10 for games, and with the gradual updates even better. I do wish there was some melee weapons, like a He-man sword or battleaxe, as many of the enemies can overwhelm or group up and I would love to just have a mace and smash those toys! Also more types of guns as well for even more types of shooting (There is a lot already, but I crave MOAR!). The gun modulation is great, attachments are fun and the game is packed full of humor and references (I noticed a certain M41A Pulse scope which was amazing). As you may already tell I love this game, and highly recommend it and hope to see even more from it.But remember!*THIS IS NOT A FLYING TOY* (Unless, of course, you have the Jetpack).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Awesome game for both newcomers and veterans to FPS games. Highly recommended!I got this game because my 7 year old son wanted to play a FPS and I wanted to find something that (1) wasn't gory, (2) wouldn't be too punishing for him, and (3) I could play with him. This game hits all the marks with the added bonus of being a total blast for me, too. My son gets a huge kick out of the fact that we're fighting toys; we have a bucket of the little green army guys so this game has more-or-less brought our play battles to life. The local multiplayer option is great, but I quickly decided to just get a second copy so we could both go full screen and KB+M.The game handles very well and the weapon upgrades and strategy behind placing buildables between waves gives a nice cadence to a round. My son is always psyched to unlock a new character skin and there are plenty of them to go after. The difficulty is such that on the lowest setting, the two of us can do quite well on pretty much any map. There is a good variety there, too, from a frenetic, close-quarters map on an air hockey table to an open kitchen with multiple attack lines.I can tell we'll be playing this for a long time. I have a lot of games in my Steam library but I've never bothered to write a review before -- but I wanted to give a shout out to this small development team. Thanks for making a great game for me and my son!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, do I have much time in this game? No, not yet but I'm on my way.Edit: This game jumped to the front of my mind since it's releasing on Xbox with cross-play to PC soon, and I'm loving it every bit as much as I did before.However, it takes no time at all to see all the tender love and care the developers have put into this game. There are details everywhere that will make you smile. The environments are colorful, vivid, and contain all the details you'd expect to find if you were walking around them in real life. The models of everything from the characters to the weapons to the enemies are so beautifully rendered. The animations are somehow lifelike even though they perfectly match how you'd expect the toys to move. I've seen other reviews mentioning this, but the game feels as though the developers behind the Toy Story 2 Action Game had the budget of a AAA release and the modeling/animation knowhow of modern AAA game devs.I don't have a single complaint I can think of to state against this game because I think it is beyond evident that this game is exactly the game it wants to be, and that is a simply fun game that inherits all the best qualities from the old arcade shooters a lot of people used to play on consoles like the Nintendo 64 and OG Xbox, and it expands upon all of them with the quality of life features you'd want from a game that came out in the past few years while also having gorgeous visuals.The gameplay itself is simplistic, but that's not a bad thing. It's masterfully executed:- the weapons all feel unique and impactful- the attachments make the difference you would expect- enemy types are numerous to the point you think you've seen them all but then realize there's more than you remember- enemy AI is unique between the types, and the AI works fluidly in tandem with the unique animations that fit the toy they appear asHonestly the enemy variety is one of my favorite things about this game. The difference in behavior keeps things fresh between every wave of every match, and this element of the game feels inspired by Doom Eternal, the only other game I can think of where I constantly forget about a specific enemy type and am then pleasantly surprised to be reminded of an enemy I forgot about.Don't be deceived. While the gameplay is and looks simple, it is SOLID, and extremely enjoyable.Do not go into this game expecting Deep Rock Galactic, Evolve, Rainbow Six Siege, or anything else that requires a ton of tactical thought. Go into this game expecting Halo: CE, Army Men: Sarge's Heroes, Toy Story 2: Action Game, and clearly identifiable love for this artistic medium.Should you buy this game? If you want something that's stupid fun and good to play with friends absolutely yes. If you like supporting dedicated artists, absolutely yes. I was initially drawn by the aesthetics in the trailers and gameplay I saw, and then I was floored by the aesthetics I saw when I played it, and then I was hooked by how much fun the game actually turned out to be. I guarantee you'll find something about this game that puts a stupid grin on your face.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve spent over 24 hours of my life playing this game and haven’t even owned it for 4 days. It takes me back to being a kid. Reminds me of Hot Wheels Stunt Track Driver. You’re a toy in a huge house, a kid with a huge imagination. Nostalgia spills from every bit in this game. And not only the feeling of being thrown back to a kid playing with toys in their bedroom, but the gameplay, the PvE and PvP are fun as hell and addicting. Either waves of bad toys trying to destroy nodes you must protect or running into a launch pad and jumping 20 feet in the air as you shoot a grenade at an enemy underneath you as their character explodes into different pieces everywhere. The gameplay sticks, feels like quake but as a toy. Zero micro transactions- the 5 man dev team wanted their game like the old school games. You want something you grind your butt off for it and let me tell you. It’s rewarding as hell. So many secrets hidden all over various maps you have to go back and look for a badass skin or head to show off in game. The soundtrack is a mix of everything. Reminds me of retrowave sometimes and rock at others. It’s all over the place but in a good way with the song suiting what going on. I love it and honestly debating about spending 10 bucks just for the soundtrack alone. Normally I turn the music off in any shooter or grinding game I play to play my own, but this game has me clicking pause on spotify and turning music volume in game all the way up. Some tracks even giving chills at times gripping you in the moment as you shooting down multiple toy planes defending your precious node. This game is a breath of fresh air to me in a era of dying good games riddled with micro transactions and the company’s goal being more for money than the community. This is not the case with hypercharge. I highly recommend this game. Grab a friend, play alone, or play online with randoms cause this game has an amazing community. Join the discord too. This game already has so much to offer in it’s current state and has so much more to offer in the coming future updates. Give it a chance. Whether you’re returning to your childhood memories or want a cool fun co-op/ pvp game to play and chill with. This game is perfect for just that. And at 20 dollars that’s nothing to scoff at. It’s worth so so soooo much more than 20 dollars in my opinion. I played it off my friend’s library and not long after a couple of hours in total I had to own it. Buy it. You won’t regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first "tower-defense" type game, and I'm very glad I started with this. I don't think I would normally be in to this genre, but the design is so tight here it is very enjoyable. This is absolutely dripping with late 80's-90's nostalgia, but not in a lazy, cash-grabby way. It is clear the devs put a lot of love and energy into it's design and have a deep respect for the toys they've represented. This is the perfect manifestation of what we were imagining as kids playing with action figures and it just feels SO DAMNED GOOD to play it out here. There are so many tiny details that no one would have blamed them for not including, but stumbling onto them after your 10th match on a level is so satisfying. And don't let the toy theme fool you - this is not an easy game. Normal difficulty can still throw you some curve balls, and you might breeze through the first and second rounds, and by the last you're just happy you made it out alive. One issue I have is the limited customization options you start out with. Granted they are all unlockable - and you don't have to pay for them - but many of the smaller unlockables are stuck behind very difficult challenges, like perfect scoring some of the levels, which is not easy. I'm happy with this system, I just wish there was a bit more open in the beginning, and perhaps challenges that were a bit more forgiving (read: I need to get good).Overall, this is a small but tight game, made by a small but passionate dev team. There is seemingly endless fun to be had here, and bonus points for local split-screen! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy, got a lot to say about this one! First off, and this is something I truly feel the developers put their main focus on: Attention to detail. There is SO much detail to every little thing you can see in this game. From the single color plastic fortifications, the little missiles you see in missile launching toys (I actually had one of those growing up and its clear these guys did too) from the way the army men move to the way the toys fall apart into glorious messes that poor mom probably has to clean up. You can read those little blurbs they put on the backs of action figure packages that explain the lore and world behind them, and every match starts with you breaking out of your packaging! I could go on, but suffice to say they really nailed the toy acstetic. Its incredible. Now onto the gameplay itself: Its main mode is tower defence, where you have multiple (Some maps just one) Hypercore to defend from waves of enemies. Even the smallest map is huge for a toy, so there is a lot of verticallitity in how you jump, climb and avoid enemy fire. You'll need to jump and climb all over the maps too, since your currency is scattered all over the map as collectables. In between waves thats your cue to get as many collectables, repair, construct defences and upgrade your weaponry. Every map has hidden collectables and hard to find bobbleheads which unlock new customatization parts for your action figure. Every hypercore has a shield and health, and its shield will only recharge if it is powered by a battery, a pickup that can spawn between waves. The battery is essential not only for keeping your hypercores protected, but also powering automated defences like turrets. Plus, to get the highest reward grade post match, all power cores need to have not taken any health damage, which is easier said then done! Teamwork is key in this game, but don't worry, singleplayer lets you play with bots and does not lock you out of any unlockables. I myself managed to do Garden of Evil: The longest biggest map by myself with just one bot (But only after many failed attempts and nailing what defences to pick and where to pick them, plus learning the optimum routes to traverse the map and getting as many credits as I could between rounds.) Last note on this mode, its recommended to clear all maps on regular or casual with Platinum before moving onto expert mode, as getting platinum unlocks the battery charger on a map (where applicable, some maps do not have it) which allows you to recharge your precious batteries and keep them around. The second mode is free roam, which allows you to run jump and climb the maps to your hearts content, and also lets you find each level's secret collectables and bobble heads without any timed pressure. I wish I could speak for the pvp modes, but I'm not huge into pvp so I cannot speak for them sadly. I'll leave you with a tip that will hopefully help: Bots can be very helpful for not making you have to do everything yourself, but remember the more bots you have, the more enemies spawn! Good luck Soldier!

_childDocuments_.review: Great Fun little Arcade Game.... I feel this game could really kick off if some more work was put into it and expanded a bit with more game modes and fine tuning. Customization options are really amazing especially the Glow in the Dark features on some of the skins. Imagine if they put in Actual Licensed Retro Toys in the game (Masters of the Universe, Toy Story, GI Joe, classic Toys) but then again would it be weird if they were shooting toy guns?A Downside i feel is the Name Customization where you pick out a generated name tag for your character which i think is in place to Disguise the bots that most likely always in your match because of the lack of players ( i even played on the weekend)-Plague Mode - which is a variant of a "Infected" game mode which has you scoring points by standing in a zone to capture points and avoiding infected players (you can only score points by being on the zone, most players don't know that). Downside to this mode is if you are not infected you'll be always marked on the HUD with a Red skull so the infected know where you are regardless if you find a great hiding spot or not.-Deathmatch - PVP Free-for-all Game Mode , score points by killing other players where you can pick up weapons off the ground and attatchments.-Waves - PVE Defend zones and collect coins or kill enemies to buy buildables to place around the zone to defend from waves or hordes of enemies which vary from game to game. _childDocuments_.review: An amazing yet small game, Hypercharge: Unboxed gives massive nostalgia for anybody whom fondly remembers the Army Men series or the Small Soldiers movie of the 90's. Playing as your own customizable action figure and battling classic toys of yesteryear's youth, you will scale entire rooms, vault through gardens, and reach the heights of a massive garage in an attempt to find coins, unlock more weapons, and upgrade defenses in order to protect a series of objective 'hypercores'. There's only four things I can imagine that would make this game even better; an open-world level combining the garden and all rooms of the house into one level, toy combat vehicles to help you move around quicker and battle enemies, an in-depth RPG-like skillpoint system to upgrade your weapon profiency, and finally heavy buildables based around real-sized human technology, like desk fans to chop enemies or hair-dryers to melt them or mannable golf-ball shooting turrets (Basically really creative ways small toys would use human-made objects to destroy enemies.)I personally love this game, but for now it's so small and has limited re-playability. I'm eagerly keeping up on the news the Devs are dishing out, and looking forward to the new survival mode they have planned. If they keep up their hard work, Hypercharge is a game that should be mandatory in any game-lovers library!

_childDocuments_.review: In a time long forgotten, there existed an ancient line of action figures imbued with sentience and bound by a sacred purpose: preserving the joy of childhood. These figures, known as the Guardians of Imagination, foresaw a day when humanity's connection to its most precious memories—those of favorite toys and the adventures shared with them—would fade. To prevent this tragedy, they created a magical artifact known as the Hypercore.The Hypercore was no ordinary object. Forged from the purest fragments of nostalgia and wonder, it became a living reservoir of childhood memories. Every child’s laughter, every whispered secret, every epic battle reenacted in bedrooms and backyards was absorbed into its glowing core. It became a source of unending power, ensuring that the bond between humans and their cherished toys could never be broken.But peace would not last. A dark figure arose: Major Evil, a tyrannical force born from forgotten and discarded toys who had grown bitter in their neglect. Fueled by resentment, Major Evil vowed to obliterate the Hypercore, erasing the memories stored within it forever. Without those memories, humanity would lose its connection to the joy and creativity that toys inspire, and the Guardians of Imagination would be reduced to lifeless relics.Now, the fate of the Hypercore—and all the cherished memories it holds—rests in your hands. Major Evil’s armies of corrupted playthings march ever closer, seeking to extinguish the light of the Hypercore. Will you stand with the Guardians of Imagination, wielding the spirit of play and creativity as your weapon?Defend the Hypercore with everything you’ve got, or see the treasures of our past turn to dust. The battle for nostalgia begins now.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good CO-OP tower defense game with interesting FPS elements, this game is also good looking and has great attention to detail in its level design. Some buildables are over-powered while others are under-powered, however, that is to be expected of an early access game.But I would like to bring attention to some serious game/connectivity issues me and a friend have been having online, for example, the game enemies sometimes go very fast and instantly attack the cores within a few seconds and a game over occurs, or they go so slow that it makes an Expert difficulty match extremely easy to complete with a Diamond award.Other game/connectivity issues include randomly not being able to jump, jump pads not being interactive and randomly disconnecting from the server.Another issue is that the Beyblade style enemies are very powerful and hard to stop. When all goes well on a cohesive Expert playthrough of a map, these Beyblade enemies spawn and instantly melt your core's shields and damages health without giving you much of a chance to react. The main problem is that they can glitch through buildable walls and drop from vents directly on top of a core, instantly damaging them before you could even destroy them. They spawn in too many numbers and they are the only enemy in this game that feels truly unfair. Another problem is the dropship, their turrets like to shoot down one particular core, melting their shield down in no time preventing you from getting a Diamond award. This is a problem because you and your friends cannot kill one fast enough before they do that. However the dropships only tend to be a problem on the garden map with the red core.On the plus side though, this game is very fun and completely unique. There is not another game of this kind. If you like rats style maps on CSS/CSGO or TF2 or you have played one of those old Tower Defense flash games, then do yourself a favour and play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever watch Toy Story or Small Soldiers as a kid and think 'man I wish they made a videogame about that but with guns and explosions?' well then Hypercharge is the game for you!Lots of love and detail has clearly been put into this game and it shows in the character of the maps, flavor text and toy designs. Very well optimized, easy to set up a game and play with friends. Lot of cool cosmetics and collectibles to explore and unlock. Love the ability to swap between first and 3rd person mode seamlessly.The generousness of the jumping, double jumping, vaulting and ledge grabbing means you can parkour to some insane and unthinkable places(wink wink).Most of the classic 90s shooter weapon archetypes are represented here. In an amusing twist that I quite like, have for the most part realistic firing sounds but they all launch little plastic bb pellets that, when you reload fall on the floor.Speaking of weapon sounds, the sound design is very good. You can tell special care was taken on weapons. They all sound satisfying to fire and the explosions sound deep and bassy without being too loud. It's a good thing in the normal CoOp modes ammo is unlimited because you'll want to mag-dump just to feel like toy Rambo.The actual original sound track for the game is also pretty good.The building system has a bunch of fun traps, sentries and, I don't know how best to describe them but Crowd control? oriented structures to unlock and experiment with.Has that very 90s early 2000s Saturday morning toy commercial vibe nailed down. A few suggestions I would give for the devs is. 1. Custom maps. You guys have clearly put a lot of effort and love into crafting all the assets in this game, If would be great if you could somehow look into making a in-game custom map making mode where the community could take all those assets and remix and rearrange them to make infinite new maps to play on like one big toy box. These maps don't necessarily need to support all the specially placed collectibles and achievement based cosmetic progression you have baked into the developer made ones, but It would be super cool if we had the tools to make map setups for any room scenario we could imagine.2. A slightly more robust ping system for working with the player bots when playing solo or in a not full multiplayer lobby. Being able see the bots build cards and request they put specific structures on specific build nodes would greatly enhance the experience when playing with them.3. Add are few more weapon types namely a 2 slot Quake/TeamFortress style rocket launcher, kinda slow projectile but with good AOE damage, some sort of auto or semi-auto bolt gun/crossbow than can impale/collateral multiple enemies or pin them to walls, and finally a full sword of some kind for either a full melee or hybrid build would be super cool.My personal wishlist aside, at the end of the day Hypercharge is a very fun, nostalgic coop or pvp toy shooter and it definitely has my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I never review games, like, ever, I play them, and then I talk to them with my friends, but I never feel like my review would be worth it in the sea of other reviews. I have also never really heard of this game before purchasing it. I had the spare cash, I liked the visuals and the trailer, I figured this might be another one of those games I'd play for two hours and then never play again. Boy, was I wrong. This game feels like they took a beloved PS2-era game and slapped modern graphics to it. Other than the "supporter pack" DLC, there is no form of microtransaction in this game, and yet, LOADS of unlockables, all unlocked through normal playthrough in various different ways. The devs have hidden SO many small, funny, cheeky details and references in this game, it just shows this game is a labour of love.On to gameplay, it kind of feels to me like CoD Zombies meets tower defence, you have 3 or 4 nodes to defend through several waves of enemies, each with different ways of attacking you. Speaking of enemies, I expected something similar to CoD Zombies, where there are maybe 2-3 types of enemies, all with similar functions, but nah, there are about a dozen types of enemies in this game, with varying degrees of annoyance and danger, along with a couple "minibosses". Every stage has several difficulties to play it in, and trust me, you don't want to start playing the maps on expert right away, you're going to get your ass kicked. This game relies on the cooperation of every teammate, and it has honestly given me some of the best gaming nights with my buddies.Only downside I can find right now, is that it's almost impossible to get a diamond rank while playing solo in some of the maps, but this game is enjoyed the most with friends anyways. If you do end up getting the game, check out their discord, it's full of helpful people, and it seems like a generally nice place.Oh, and about the DLC, as of right now, there is only one DLC, the "supporter pack" DLC, which gives you more skins and an additional character. It's very much not needed, but it's worth it for the fact that you're giving more money to the devs, who truly deserve it.So yes, I wholeheartedly recommend this game, you get a LOT of content for the small amount they ask for the game.Honestly

_childDocuments_.review: A fun co-op horde shooter. It does have PvP modes, but my friends and I have yet to play those. All of my experience is either single-player or co-op. It's got a good campaign with varied level/enemy design. The core loop is you and three buddies hold off waves of enemy toys advancing to destroy your little battery-powered brains in jars around the map, while trying to find cash and loot along the way. Typically you have 3 OBJs you have to defend and a sizable map with plenty of secrets to help you stand up to the tyrannical toys attacking you. Guns include things like lasers, miniguns, shotguns, grenade launchers, and probably more I don't remember. You can also buy attachments during the level to upgrade stats on your guns. Levels include things like bedrooms, bathrooms, backyards, kitchens, etc. and it makes for a good variety of different environments to fight in with notably more verticality than I expected when going in. All of your progress contributes to your customization options for your character. Maybe my favorite part of the game is to engage with is making my little action figure and assembling an absurd name from unlocked keywords. My friends and I have tons of fun making silly characters between levels, diving in to unlock more options, and doing it all over again. It gives me a feeling of nostalgia similar to walking down the toy isle as a kid and looking at all the various things on the wall my parents would never get me. Action figures were always pretty cheap though, so I got to take one home with me now and again. For 25$ I think you could do a lot worse. If you lack friends to play it with it might be worth considering a sale first. I think the game has a nice and friendly community though it is small. LFG will probably get you better results than matchmaking, but it requires actually interacting with people you don't know. Scary right? Anyways, good game. I do give it the Steam thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: A Nostalgic mood game, based in your childhood home, with a well designed wave-based tower-defense mode that stays fun for hours. An abundance of character customization options that caters to the collector type, unlocked through gameplay, not bs.I consider a games worth, by how many hours I spend enjoying it versus how much I spent. I’m still avidly enjoying, it still is a favorite in my friend group, and the game says I’m 70% through it (all game difficulties, unlocks, etc). I spent $20, well worth it. Or try the free demo. It’s what convinced me!The Waves ModeThere are several game modes to play, but my favorite is the Waves mode. I’ve seen ppl complain that it’s confusing. The tutorial they provide is done in 10 mins, and more than explains all the basics you need to know.Essentially, you defend towers from waves of enemies. In-between waves, you have limited time, to collect weapon upgrades, and credits to spend on defenses. This is the best part. Strategizing your defenses with your friends, unlocking new turrets and traps, failing miserably and then returning with more wisdom to crush the next time. Character CustomizationYou start with several base characters, but as you play you unlock more characters, and a host of different skin options for each of them. The customization menu is so fun to use, and keeps me entertained even when I’m just looking at stuff lol. Because the theme is action figures from your childhood, there’s a satisfying feeling to the fantasy of it all.Level DesignTruly inspired designs to each of their levels. Each level could be somewhere from your home. You can tell that the devs are speaking from their heart when they made each one. Complete with boss levels, special defense modes, and free roam options to give you time to really enjoy it all. For the $20 price tag, they provided a solid base of content to enjoy, with honestly satisfying replayability. Edit: As of April 2023, it seems that the devs are close to finished with the updates on this game. There may be a few more, but most their content seems to be out. This game is a steal. And what's more, most all my gripes with the game have been fixed and/or improved. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this game years ago when it first came out. I was looking for a couch coop fps game and this pretty much ticks all the boxes. When I first played the game it was pretty bare bones, but it showed a lot of potential. It was then put on hiatus for a long time and for a while all hope was lost ( I believe the company went down to one person at one point). But I'm glad they never gave up and have made an amazing game. It has come a long way and all the changes and additions made were all for the better. They deserve recognition and I hope they receive multiple awards for this labour of love, and continue to produce more games.Onto the game itself. In essence it is a tower defence game meets wave shooter set in a world where you play as action figures fighting against weaponised toys. If you have ever watched films like "Toy story", "Small Soldiers" or played with certain toys at one point in your life, this game will bring you so much nostalgia. There is a lot of variety in the enemies and the levels and with the help of pickups and different weapons and mods it can be a little overwhelming at times but it's the nature of 1st/3rd person tower defence games. I would love to see a campaign of some sort but even as it is at the moment I highly recommend playing this game. Well done Digital Cybercherries!

_childDocuments_.review: Probably among the best purchases you could make on this platform. Hypercharge is a fun parody of 80s and 90s toys while also drawing a lot of inspiration from films like Toy Story and Small Soldiers. However, even more than that what it sets out to do it does perfectly. Pros:-The art design is absolutely flawless. Not only does it perfectly replicate the genuine look and design of a toy from the 80s and 90s, the figure designs look like real toys I would have played with as a kid. There is not a single enemy type, player skin, or environmental detail that does not ring a bell with me, I mean even the grenade launcher is a spring loaded missile. Despite none of these toys actually existing there is an amazing amount of thought and detail put into them that makes them feel like toys that would actually be produced.-Sound design is equally good with weapons packing a very satisfying punch despite being BBs.-Weapon variety is wide and very entertaining to swap between different gun combos. Some weapons are admittedly harder to find than others, like the laser or railgun, but when you do manage to get the fun weapons they do not disappoint. It all comes back to that satisfying sound design giving the weapons life and the balancing that makes them feel nice and chunky. You can also add other attachments to your gun such as scopes, stocks, and underslung equipment like a flashlight or stand (the stand is merely cosmetic though, and doesn't setup)-I didn't think much of the music at first, but when I actually paused to take a listen there are some really good tracks in the game's OST. The ones that stood out to me the most were Highway to Heaven, Arcade of Death, and Electrify This just being three that come off the top of my head that could not possibly fit any better in this game. Lots of synthesizers, electric guitars, and every once in a while you'll get more ambient tracks in between all the chaos. This is one of the few games where I'd say picking up the soundtrack is well worth it.-Secrets are sprinkled throughout all of the maps and I could not be any happier with this. They are both challenging to collect without being unfair, and they bring back the novel idea of actually playing the game to unlock cool cosmetics instead of paying for 15 or so DLCs on the storepage. Having to earn those cosmetics provides a true sense of accomplishment for mastering the game's parkour and map layouts, and that accomplishment can then be shown to other players in multiplayer. Really brings back those old memories in Halo 3's multiplayer.-The game pulls no punches, which is why you really need to learn the maps you're playing on and find as many tokens as quickly as possible. The game is challenging, and will get intense, but it never feels unfair or cheap.Cons:-Might be a little entitled, but I don't feel there are still enough unlocks for each figure. Some have less than others, like the space marine or warrior chick. That can be improved through content updates, but that depends entirely on the developers.-The parkour is fine once you get used to it, but it's really jarring figuring out what you can climb on and what you can't. The collision can also be weird so you might think you landed a jump but you bounce off the terrain instead.-Bots can be worse than real players when playing offline. They often wait around the slot machine to take your items, so that jet pack you were throwing precious tokens away for gets snatched up by the bot waiting right behind you. It's incredibly frustrating.-Once again, more more more. I don't feel there are enough maps even with the updates to this game. There are certainly plenty to play on so it's not like you will be bored in the first 4 hours, but variety is never a terrible thing. Maps like a literal sandbox, or a dollhouse, or even kid rooms in different nations would be fun, like in a Japanese kid's room full of Kaiju. There are so many creative ways to play with this concept and I hope the devs run wild with it.Aside from those cons, you can't go wrong buying this game. If you enjoyed tower defense games when those were hitting it big in the mid 2010s, or like wave based shooters the game is for you. It also features other game modes like PVP, but those aren't as heavily populated. If you insist on playing PVP then definitely join the Discord.With all of that said, 10/10, $10 bucks well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short:I can only recommend it. Hypercharge's a real gem, crafted with a high attention to detail.This is the type of game that's worth every cent because of how well-made and replayable it is.What I liked about it:> Fun core gameplay: You start by scavenging through various (human-sized) enviroments as an action-figure and use the resources you find to build defenses against waves of hostile toys. In the action-mode you can switch freely between first person and third person perspective, and start blasting.> Highly detailed environments and characters> Great music and sound design> Lots of unlockables you can earn for your little toy-soldier through gameplay> Single-player friendly thanks to bots (and upcoming SP mode :D)> Free gameplay updates, great support in general> Very friendly and involved dev team!Where I see room for improvement:> Only two weapon slots, power weapons even take up both (I think this is a game which would really benefit from numeral weapon slots, arena shooter style)> Unlocks could use a second "grind" track, so you can keep unlocking things either by a) getting the corresponding achievement (short but harder) or b) accumulating points / in-game currency (long but easier)> Maybe some sort of mini-map / compass / radar for wave-mode, so it's easier to orient oneself and you know where you can find batteries, resources, enemies, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with a lot of detail and effort.To clarify, there are lots of minute details players might miss, each box is incredibly detailed with scuffs, barcodes, writing, postage stamps and various other small details, the floor is covered in scuff marks, shopping cart marks, bits of dirt and everything else you would expect to have been in say a Toys“R”Us store. I wont go into detail about everything that the developers painstakingly added because there's far too much to comment on. Needless to say they added a ridiculous amount of detail to each and every map of the game. So I encourage everyone that plays the game to take a look around the maps and see all the easter eggs and detail the team put in whenever there's a lull between the waves.Gameplay wise it's very fun, the guns feel nice, the enemies are varied (though I think there could be a bit more variation that said it is an Early Access game) I'm not entirely pleased that each map has its own specific loadout with the possibility of finding new weapons across spawns on the map.I'm not entirely thrilled with the buildables either, there's variety there but it feels much too spread out (each buidable has 3 levels and each level is listed in the buildable menu as its own buildable)Another minor issue is that there are secrets on each map, if you're in co-op with a friend and someone claims a secret you cant claim that secret without restarting the map and play it again after having finished it.I think the game is incredibly well made and painstakingly polished and if you're looking for something fun to play with a friend or two it's a very enjoyable experience.Update. PC version has taken a backseat to the nintendo switch version of the gamewith the switch version getting preferential treatment over the PC in terms of updates and supportthe devs have been deleting comments on their discord and banning people who ask for updates on the steam build of the gamethey are also deleting comments on steam and issue community warnings for even mentioning that they're deleting comments they dont agree with
