_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR: HyperCharge: Unboxed is a decent Rat-Map Shooter with a lot of potential in it's ball joints.My friends and I picked this game up a few days ago, and have managed to do all the maps on Regular difficulty, getting Gold or better ranking on all of them. All and all it's a solid, if a bit flawed experience I'd still recommend. The premise is simple; You're a bunch of custom made action figures brought to life Toy Story-style (even a few references to that in game) and tasked with defending several Brain-in-a-jar Hypercores from varying waves of enemies, using a few Tower Defense-Style turrets, traps, and walls.I hasten to say this isn't a Tower Defense game.The idea of a Rat-map always makes for interesting environments to jump and shoot in. Instead of a standard gray military base or an open field, you instead jump around a messy kitchen or a room of a kid who couldn't be bothered to tidy up before he went out. this concept provides colorful and varied maps to explore and fight in.This game is far from perfect, and my friends and I have a handful of things we'd like to see changed. I'm going to note them here, since DCC seems to pay attention to Steam Reviews as well.1: Reloads. A good shooter can be made into a great shooter based simply on how the guns feel to use. Now, I'm not expecting toy guns to feel as powerful as a hand-cannon or anything... But when your reload is simply lowering a gun off screen and bringing it back up again, it doesn't make for satisfying gunplay. We do like that if you start a reload and then swap weapons, reload won't stop. it keeps the pace up and allows for little downtime in a situation where downtime can prove fatal. What I'll suggest instead is maybe giving the player two different moddable guns with Proper reloads. We're already suspending our disbelief over toys going to war, so keeping the reload when holstered mechanic is still fine with two guns.2: Power Consumption: I get the in game joke of the "Ultra-Volt" brand batteries not having nearly enough power to be remotely useful in-world. The problem we've come across, however, is that the turrets, which use the battery's energy to fire, simply cost too much power to be useful. I'd like to see the capacity of the batteries upgraded, or the power costs of the turrets reduced. I'll also voice here my concerns about the Battery Recharger. If you limit access to this station by making sure the player(s) have to have first beaten a map with a Platnium medal (Perfect victory, no health damage to any of the Hypercores), why prevent a player wanting to go back and just have fun with the map from using it on the difficulty they've earned it? Why limit it's use to Expert or Nightmare only? (Edited note: Apparently it is on some maps' Normal and Easy difficulties, just not all of them. It's not on Dawn of the Toy's Normal, for example.)3: The Air Hockey Map: This one's a fun one. Now, A map with no turrets, traps, or map specific defenses is not a bad idea. It challenges the players on their skills with the guns and their own wits. The problem is the choice in enemy type. Beyblades (called Spinners in game) dive at the core relentlessly, and can shove players off the map into the kill zone below. Doing this map perfectly on Expert (Diamond Medal) is the only way to get the upgraded anti-infantry turret, and can seem honestly impossible for any less than 4 players in perfect sync. maybe even with that. I'd like to see the Spinner count cut down by a lot, and add a few more basic melee enemies, like Meanbots, to give some diversity as well as make it more possible for people to win perfectly, if you insist on putting something like a Turret behind that achievement.4: Customization: As I said, the action figures you play as are custom made. This means you can make your own Action figure, name them, and have something that's you. I'd like to see this expanded upon. Being able to swap parts from different types around would be interesting. For example, what I'd personally make is a Knight with a Dino's head, and a Cyborg arm from the Cyber Fury type. Clothing would also be nice, one of my friends would love to have his Dino with Solider style vests, straps and cargo pants over the dinosaur legs.As I said, this is a decent game that has promise. We're likely to keep playing this for weeks to come. More, if the Devs keep updating the game. Maybe give some mod support too. Either way, I hope you all can enjoy this game the way we have.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews but for this game I figured it was warranted. And while I can't speak for every last update that has come out thus far since I've got a ton of other backlog games and my personal life, I can tell that this game is quite the achievement for such a small team to hammer it out and shape it into something amazing. Everything that I've dealt with so far in this game has the polish and care put into it like any triple A title that came out back in the day. This game to me feels like a love letter to the time when gaming was a passion and people wanted to get their ideas out to the world instead of catering to whatever fad is currently out. Games are a form of entertainment for people to escape and unwind from the stresses of their lives, and I for one thoroughly enjoy what this game has to offer. This is a fun game to sink plenty of hours into, and I look forward to what it holds in the future. Thanks for the amazing game so far, Digital Cybercherries~!

_childDocuments_.review: I would never refer to myself as someone who enjoys shooter games. I'm a MOBA player to my core. However, my partner recommended that we get this game to try together, and I've fallen for it hard. Hypercharge: Unboxed is a unique combination of childhood nostalgia + horde shooters that has a beautifully bright atmosphere to set it apart from games like L4D2. As someone who has struggled to get into shooting games for years, I'm captivated by the ability to play as toy defenders in home and store environments, spaces that recall imagery from the Toy Story movies. Unlike most games, Hypercharge: Unboxed allows you to acquire skins and titles by just playing and meeting certain goals on levels - gathering all the coins and collectibles, reaching a particular level rating (gold, plat, diamond...), etc. It also features the ability to switch between first-person and third-person to fit your personal favorite shooter style. Combine this with the extremely satisfying sound of breaking out of your box at the beginning of the level, the building and repair noises, and the overall toy-like sound effects of the players and enemies, and you've got a fantastic game. I hope the devs continue to pour love into this game, because so much of their enthusiasm already shines through. I highly recommend that anyone who is feeling uncertain about this game to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The game deserves a positive recommendation based on the sheer will and genuine determination of the developers. It's also really fun too. I do wish the towers had a little more variability and focus, as having very limited spots to actually place them down is a bit frustrating at points. Think of something like Orcs Must Die, most of the level can have traps and towers placed on it, with decreasing the amount of available spots as the levels progress to give some difficulty and strategy. In this game, there are only a couple of zones you can place towers/traps on all of the levels, and if you're playing solo it's sometimes quite difficult to run back and forth between power cores without the traps and bots carrying their weight. However the focus is clearly the gunplay, and it's good enough to keep the game fun. Multiplayer is fun too, I just wish it was more popular.

_childDocuments_.review: HYPERCHARGE: UNBOXED is  probably the only fps/tower defense hybrid game that has held my interest and I believe could be a couch co-op staple if more people knew about it. Reasons you might like this game:-The game looks pretty impressive and if you like toy story you may feel some nostalgia playing it.-The game has multiple game modes ranging from co-op to vs to a top down tank brawler giving it added replayability with other players although the main gamemode includes singleplayer should you prefer to play alone.-The game heavily encourages and rewards exploration not only by having useful weapons/powerups/parts scattered around the maps but also through  unlockable cosmetics hidden throughout.- There are Several  difficulty levels allowing for players of varied skill levels to play/enjoy the game.- The vast majority of levels can be traversed with no/few invisible walls allowing players to scale the entirety of most maps using skillful use of jumps/ grenade jumps. -The developers are continuing to add new content to the game and are listening to feedback to improve the experience. Reasons you  might not like this game:-Some players dislike the movement in this game and believe it is difficult to respond to threats fast enough(personally I haven't had this issue as I find climbing obstacles to be fairly fluid and allows one to cover ground quickly)- Defenses can only be built in set locations on each map- Most guns are fairly inaccurate making combat at long ranges difficult.For it's price I think HYPERCHARGE is well worth the price and i'd highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys the fps/tower defense genre, people who are looking for a fun co-op game for both offline and online play and really anyone who doesn't find the downsides l've listed dealbreakers as I personally think the game is fantastic. If you're still unsure whether this game is for you be sure to check out the demo and try it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: 21:9 Ultrawide video review: HyperCharge: Unboxed is a Coop First person shooting wave defense game where you take on the role of an action figure and you have to defend your hyper cores from being destroy by an invasion of evil toys. The gameplay is your standard shooter type with the addition of some platforming elements and base building. The game splits between 2 phases, one for building and setting up your defenses like lego barricades, plastic posion ivy, hot glue and more. During the build phase your able to collect coins used for constructing these defenses as well as fine hidden collectibles that require quite a bit of platforming to reach. The second phase is the action phase where you will be fighting of hordes of various toys each with their own strength, weakness, and behaviors. Right clicking allows you to zoom in but there is no aim down sights in this game. There are attachments that appear at random through your mission that can give you an alternate fire or an addon for your gun to provide a stat bonus. At the end of a mission you will be awarded with XP and a rank based on how much health the cores were left with. My only real complaint with the gameplay was that the climbing can act up at times and cause you to work your way back up to where you fell off.Hypercharge Unboxed also features quite a bit outside of native ultra wide support. It has up to 4 player local split screen coop, private matches, a server browser, and tons of customization options to unlock like character skins, gun skins, and different playable action figures. The game is currently in early access and includes a good amount of missions with the promise of more to come, the developers have also stated they plan on adding a PVP game mode and more PVE content down the line.Visually the game is beautiful, the graphics and art style look amazing and I did have someone walk by quickly taking a look at the game thinking it was a toy story trailer. The variety in enemy toys really is a great addition because of the nostalgia factor it gave me, a lot of the toys where things i played with in my child hood. The audio works great and shooting the robots has a very pleasing shut down sound play when they get destroyed. Environments of each level are different and unique with my favorite having to be the toy isle. There's a lot of great jokes and references to be found littered throughout like the pc master race subreddit opened up in the bedroom, or the zerg rush deodorant in the bathroom. Performance wise i had no issues playing and no graphical issues from playing in ultra-wide either. The UI and menus can be scaled but does not have full customization in terms of placementOver all I enjoyed my time with HyperCharge: Unboxed, Its easy to see the developers at Digital Cybercherries put a lot of work into making this game and cared about their product. Its not perfect and could certainly use some more levels but for its asking price I would say it fulfills in giving enough content with the promise of more to come and offers a good amount of replay ability. If you dont take my word for it feel free to check out the stream review section with lots of players who feel the same way. My biggest gripe with the game was not being able to find enough players online off peak hours and thats saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: Hypercharge:unboxed is a fun game. It needs co-op with voice to get the most enjoyment if you want to be successful. There are a range of well designed and ascetically pleasing maps although the Garden of Death needs some work on being able to pick out enemies.On the waves mode which is what I've played the most, you defend 3-4 terminals from attack by AI forces. You gather construction points to build defences, with the type of enemy and defences making some differences e.g. there are airborne enemies in some maps and you can build anti-air defences.For gameplay, some changes I'd like to see are: - another player not being able to destroy your defences- a shorter ready time option, 3:30 minutes between maps is a long time to wait on someone else, as is the construction phase if one player isn't coming out of it but they have no points anyway - more balancing between AI attacks on different terminals, it tends to focus on 1-3 and mostly ignores 4 e.g. the attic level, the players can build a gun turret at green and pretty much leave it while red is under constant attack.- an anti-air weapon that can be carried by playersI hope more players find the game over time and play it, I think some more maps for longevity would help.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for maybe 3 days and already have 10 hours into it. The design is obviously the hook, and it's as good as you think it is. The gameplay is good as well, there are multiple guns and attachments as well as defensive builds you can choose from. The stages themselves might be my favorite, there are so many secret areas to find and little details that make this game really special.For me personally, there is one drawback. I am by no means a completionist. It does not bother me in the slightest that I don't have the highest rank on the hardest difficulty for each stage. If you don't really play with friends like myself, you may feel you've run out of content pretty early on. I've played every stage on normal difficulty, and most on expert. After beating the last couple stages on expert, it will be hard for me to return to Hypercharge very often. This does not make it a bad game- if you are a completionist you'll easily put 50-100 hours into it. I just don't see myself getting over 20. (which, again, is not bad).Overall, the game is a very fair price, and what I have played I have enjoyed. The aesthetic is top tier. I give HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Hypercharge kinda appeared from no where. I saw the reddit post that blew up in December, I looked up the game and it seemed neat. I didn't buy it. Covid had left me a tad stripped of extra gaming money.I got some Steam money for Christmas. My friends still play Titanfall 2 for it's wave defense mode, and I've been unable to play much with them. Our games list don't share as many titles as they used to. Used Christmas money on Titanfall 2. I played with them for two days, on that second day I brought up Hypercharge: Unboxed in conversation as a similar game that looked neat. Well, it seems they liked the toy idea as much as I did, because within an hour of finishing Titanfall 2 for the night, I find it suddenly gifted to me. They all got it, and felt bad I used the money on Titanfall 2, so bought it for me.The next day we start playing Hypercharge, and we all love it. It's easy to think about all the shortcuts they could have taken, but didn't. It's really easy to make a game about toys in cartoon graphics. It's harder to go for an ultra realistic style where the plastic looks like plastic, which they did.. They could have easily made all the levels out of toy props like wooden blocks. It's harder to make a number of unique environments based on real life, they did that too. As someone who worked as an Assistant Manager at a Toys'R'Us over a Christmas season (years ago). I can say they NAILED the toy store levels. The crappy linoleum floor. The shelving. The signs. The lighting. The way the puzzles on shelves are sparse on the bottom rows making mazes but more fully stocked on the higher shelves. The detail on the price gun, the little marks and scratches on it. We joked it would awaken some PTSD. The full backyard level, with grass and gardens and a pond. There is no reason to go in the pond, but they still have underwater effects and minnow swimming around if you do.A long winded way to say a -lot- of care went into this.But that's the tip of the ice burg, because what proved the developer's passion to me was the Tutorial. I've never willingly spent 6 hours in a tutorial before. I had done it the first time, it was informative and didn't waste my time. Over and done, thought nothing more of it, thought I'd never play it again. But every level has a number of hidden collectibles, and I noticed an unlock mentioned finding the collectibles in the tutorial. So, with my morning coffee I decided now was a good time to relax, wake up and explore the nooks of the tutorial for the collectibles. Sure I found a few, even a spare battery, but I found something else. On a back shelf I found a core charger, the thing you put batteries into to power your core. But this wasn't attached to a core. I thought it was odd, it couldn't have been a mistake. So I went back for the extra battery I found, got back to the charger and but it in. In the corner of my screen appeared the text '3 secret chargers remain'. nd a special wave of enemies appeared. What I thought was going to be 20 minutes of exploring with my coffee turned into a few hours of hopping around, exploring EVERYTHING.There was no challenge spelling out all of this was there. The only thing that pointed me back to the Tutorial was a single unlock that said find the collectibles you see in every level there. And yet the developers hide and placed what was hours of content for me (obviously less time if you use guides). That's not even mentioning the secret dev room I learned about even later. It's been a long time since I found something in a game that so clearly proved the developer's passion for their project.If you are somehow still reading this, you might be gripping your armrest wondering when I'll get to game play. The game play is good. The movement and controls feel solid. The jumping is lenient without feeling floaty. The guns overall feel good to use. On the normal difficulty, no level feels unfair. If you play with the newly added bots, they are not perfect by any means, but they're good enough to at least finish levels on hard difficulty.Are there negatives you should be aware of? Yeah. If you don't have friends to play with, the bots will only get you so far. The customization may feel limited and essentially boils down to heads that can only be used on one body type, and color schemes. Hard mode leans a bit too much on enemies that explode instead of more diverse waves or higher numbers of enemies.Despite those however, I'm ready to say it was my game of 2020. Xcom Chimera Squad was good, but doesn't have the same replay value. I waited for Creeper World 4 for years, but it doesn't have me laughing my ass off. Hypercharge is fun, it's something I can replay, it's something I can play with friends, it clearly shows the developer's passion, I love the aesthetic and the name customization is hilarious. I got to be 'Armed Person Lad', with all the powers of a person with arms, will the Hypercore be saved.

_childDocuments_.review: AI dumb as bricks. Co-op mode is actually really good. Visuals are amazing. Love the persistent debris system. No deep gameplay, expect a casual arcade shoot 'em up.The dev stream kept bragging about the great AI that, according to them, allows the bots in this game to very easily be mistaken for real players. So I bought the game, I tried it out in PvP and Plague modes. Those bots have the same intelligence as my Roomba. They kept following the exact same trial and error route to get to my elevated position on a cardboard box. Each time they followed the same exact path over the racks, I would shoot them once with my shotgun and they'd fly back down only to repeat the exact same steps that led to their first fall. The absolutely mindblowing part? There's a jump pad right below me that takes you up to the box. Not a single bot used it. One of them even got lost going in circles under the rack before eventually finding it way back up the path over the racks. Nostalgic in a  way that hearkens back to the days of Counter-Strike's PODBots where you'd have to set waypoints for the "AI". That's not a good thing.Beyond that? Not much depth at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly clean and well executed. It's not hyper-realistic or anything but it's very well done. It's normally very clear what everything is. The only exceptions are items that have been used and fall to the ground, weapon attachments and batteries that have been dropped can easily disappear and lose their colourful glow. The UI is very simple, if a little small on my 1080p monitor, it would be nice to have a UI scale option in the settings.   Tower Defense + FPS. Similar to Sanctum or Orcs Must Die. It's fairly well done, although the game heavily pushes you towards co-op. You're restricted in the number of different towers you can build to 3, which you need to select before starting the match. So if you pick the anti-air turret but then you go into a level without air enemies, you only have 2 useful towers. That along with some of the maps being quite large mean you need to find someone to play with.So far I've only played this game Single Player and while it's doable on Normal, some levels are very difficult on Hard. Features like an Enemy Radar, Build Mode during a wave or AI to act as other players/assistants would help Single Player mode significantly.   I'm not sure if you unlock more as you go along, but I've played almost each level on Normal and a few on Hard. In that time I've only heard the song from the tutorial (Highway to Heaven, an ACDC ripoff that sounds awesome) once, the rest haven't been anything to write home about, and no music plays while you are in build mode, which can be around half the level.   Most of these are spot on, the beyblades sound authentic, the player character makes beeps and buzzes like a Buzz Lightyear or other action figure, it's great. The Colonel character that gives you instructions has some funny lines, although he often repeats himself throughout a battle, including telling the player to rebuild defences during a wave, which cannot be done.I would recommend this game to people who like either FPS or Tower Defense games that can gather a friend or two to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: The guns are simplistic and you can modify them with a couple of modifications to give them slightly different stats. I really like how the guns feel and even though I only tend to use a few that I like, mostly assault rifle, I like that there are possibilities on what to use. In this game you cannot place turrets/traps wherever you want, you have to do it in designated spots in order to protect important objectives. I really like this since it makes you have to think strategically of where to put your objects and what object to place. Between waves and before the first wave, you pick-up coins and collectibles around the map, by use of jumping or building jumping pads around the map. I find this a great and engaging way to get coins for weapon upgrades/objects to place, and creates an interesting and enjoyable thing to do between waves when you're waiting for your slowpoke friends to get finished. Especially because just traversing the map itself is great fun, the maps are really well made. The game really makes you feel like a toy soldier in different environments, fighting off different kinds of toys or enemies that a typical toy soldier would face. Some maps, in particular the maps with heavy grass, can be a bit difficult to see enemies in. But this becomes less of a problem when you get used to the game and what to expect. Overall I'm not a huge graphicsperson, I tend to like whatever, but I really love the attention to detail in every single map. Each map has something unique that you can find, be it an object that looks similar to an object in real life but with different text, or something else.  This is where the game truly shines. Each map feels very different but they all look great and feel great to play on. There are multiple objects and secrets scattered around the map that you will have to traverse the map in order to find. This is not a problem since jumping and getting around in the game is a blast. Most of the collectibles are hidden in hard-to-get-to spots, we had a lot of fun trying to figure out how to get them as a group, or snagging them right before the eyes of a group member! The developers seem great and they do listen to their community. I really like that and you can definitely tell that they really love making this game just by the attention to detail in it. All in all it's among the tower-defense/shooter games that I enjoy the most, especially with some friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself is not bad, clearly is a one of a kind that you could relax and just waste time playing it mindlessly. But the issue I do have with the game is being forced to achieve certain conditions to unlock weapons (I'm not against unlocking new costumes and such because that's how classic games were like before, but playing with the same gun three times and not seeing any variation that you could get is lame).Also noticed that with your weapons at hand (practically your starter rifle and a machine gun/shotgun, if you manage to get one in a match) there aren't enough to hold some types of enemies who will crush easily through your defenses and make you lose your towers/bases (the Hyper Cores). And it's not like you could put strategically in any way walls and traps to create a proper defensive line, the Hyper Cores actually let you build defensive mechanics just around them and that's it. It isn't enough with some specific enemy types and pretty much that was the conclusion one friend of mine and myself reached after three matches of this game.If you want it, get it, but don't expect all that action you are seeing in their store video at first. 6/10--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------(Edit due to respond to the Dev's answer) Hello Joe, your welcome, honestly the idea of your game is cool, that's what I wanted to try it in the first place. I'm gonna respond to the points you made but I'm not gonna unlock the gates of hell (aka allowing comments) so we can keep this as much truthful as possible.1) Well, I didn't saw much in those matches, only 2 guns and some attachments (that don't change much how weapons perform, specially on the starter rifle) and my friend pretty much jumped all around trying to find another weapon but to no avail. So in order to unlock or see random-spawn new different weapons, do I have to force-invest my time into playing other levels with pretty much the same gun? That actually stops me, I can put effort into unlocking costumes or skins but playing with the same weapon and not seeing a real random variation at start, it's quite harsh.2) My point was that you can't build everywhere, you only can build in the designated space the game marks for you (around the objective to protect). You are telling me that it can actually be possible if I do increase the difficulty of the game in order to being able to do it. Why can't you actually be able to do it at first? It would be much fun to have the liberty to place defenses as you see fit and watch if that works or not and leave the difficulty to be set by the player himself/herself. Locking that ability to a certain increased difficulty isn't that fun, plus playing on normal, you can notice how easily some enemy units can pierce your defenses like paper mache, making it frustrating to being forced to set defenses just around the core, when you actually have not one, but three of them to watch at the same time.3) That's funny, I got that trap option you are mentioning, but even setting it around don't stop that much a whole zerg of those spinners. I do agree with some reviews as well that the game feels balanced for a group of 4 people but quite unbalanced for just a solo player or a duo team, the first match felt balanced enough and in the second following map we got, we did saw a sudden zerg of those spinners breaking everything non stop while also having the basic enemy unit (both the normal bot and the advanced fast walking bot) punching the cores directly since nothing could stop that amount of those spinners at the same time. I felt it quite chaotic and I thought "Yea, clearly we need one or two more people to being able to handle this kind of a sudden spawn challenge". It's not a matter of how hard defenses can hold, it felt like it's a matter of how many extra eyes and trigger-fingers you truly need to make the experience enjoyable.4) Well, we both know that first impressions are what really counts with everything, also applied to games as well. And what I saw first, it clearly wasn't what the video was showing. I'm not saying it is false, maybe it is true, but in order to access for it, you have to invest time into it, but what it is real is that you don't get that kind of action at the beginning. Also, honestly, didn't saw the option for a demo, but that's the thing, why would I have to play a demo to have a representation of the game when I actually tried a full version of the game itself, a bought copy no less? That makes me a lot of noise, to say the least.I understand that the game is not perfect, in fact, I would like it to succeed and maybe I could return to try it again but taking into consideration that I didn't saw a demo option for this game (since that we are all used sadly that there are few trials or non trials at all for games these days) I wouldn't risk to exceed the short window of 2 h due to the Steam Refund Policy to try a game and see if it is worth it. I wouldn't risk it as well for an asked vote of trust that the game will become what I expected to be if I continue playing.There are a lot of devs these days that end up releasing cool concepts for games that turn out to be a half completed shell of a game and they all end up asking for this so called "vote of trust": "Trust us, the game will be cool much further away, keep playing, trying to ignore stuff that we know it should be changed". And the problem is that nobody is doing all of this of free charity, and as consumers, we are not getting games as gifts or free, we are paying for a product. I'm not saying that you or your team are incurring in a bad faith behaviour, but other groups and studios are doing that kind of things and that's the current situation we all see, from AAA devs to indie ones. After seeing how easily some shady studios manage to scam people (ruining this line of trust to studios that actually are doing an honest work), leaving them an unfinished project or game and those same people, year after year losing their capacity to defend their rights as consumers, I can't follow something just for someone else asking me a vote of trust when I'm actually paying for it, if it doesn't convince me, I will move forward. It's the least I can do to protect myself and my hard earned cash. I will be keeping an eye on this game and how it keeps evolving, because as I said first of all, the game is not bad, it is attractive to play as the perspective of being a toy, it does reminds me of Small Soldiers. But those specific points are what makes me bail out from the ship, hope you take them as constructive criticism and I do wish you and your team success. Be safe as well!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a toy inspired shooter/tower defence game. You can play it in first and third person. Everything about this game oozes love and passion. it even has split screen support.  .The stages are wonderful. They are colourful in a balanced way. They have nooks and crannies that complement the fact you play as action figures. The fact your starting point is your character getting out of the box is so cool. You roam toy stores and homes; whether you defend the cores in the PvE Tower Defence mode or do the other PvP modes, it's all cool. The details of the halls and places you can jump to are just awesome. Examples include hiding in shelves and going under the covers.All the modes have been made to be accessible for all. For any given mode, you can play it online, with bots, or split screen. You can set the difficulty you want. You can even use cheats if you want. For now, this mostly impacts the Tower Defence mode (and bots). You defend the cores against all sorts of cool toys. They vary from stage to stage. You get to see spinners (Beyblades), army men, UFOs, and even giant robots. The game is extremely fun.The game has 2 mini games you can play locally.The guns are great. You can get two weapons that attach to your gun. The shotgun, rifle, grenade launcher, and other weapons work great. You can get attachment for improving aim, recoil, etc.One of the most coolest aspects in the game is how it keeps improving. At the time of writing this, a survival mode is in the works. I can only look forward to the improvements and additions they bring us. This is the kind of game where you can see the devs care about making a fun game.A very awesome game. If you like toy world games, shooters, or both, this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's been a really fun 3rd person or 1st person wave-based shooter that takes me back to the days of ol' N64 or maybe PS2. It's a really fun shooter that doesn't demand too much of your attention, but certainly requires skills if you want to earn some of the flashier trophies. HYPERCHARGE gives you enough settings to make it as chill or challenging as you desire. If you want to kick back and blast the crap out of some nostalgic toys (if you're a dried up old geez like me - some of these toys date pretty far back), you can cruise around in casual or regular to do just that. If you want to get more unlockables and challenge yourself, all you need to do is tweak the settings. You can also enter free-roam mode so you can explore the maps and find stuff to unlock without the hassle of enemies knocking you about. In this mode, you can also study the environment to improve your strategies for when you choose to tackle the map proper. The only issue I've found with HYPERCHARGE is that your team's AI can be pretty dodgy. If you have no mates available to play (or at all), trying to achieve a platinum or above can be pretty dicey. As an example, some soldiers and tanks were wrecking one of my bases, and all of my AI teammates were jumping around in the same spot, shooting from time to time but not actually properly defending the base. Of course, you can always opt to play with randoms online but I ain't about that life. In saying that, if you do play with randoms online you're more than likely to have a much better experience. There's plenty to unlock, and best of all, you don't need to pay for a damn thing. If you want new skins, heads, titles and maps, you just need to play the game thoroughly. Overall, HYPERCHARGE is brilliant in that it's loads of fun and it respects the players' levels of skill. It's currently super affordable and honestly, you can get more out of this game than a lot of big-budget titles. I hope the devs continue to work on it and bring more new features, but as it stands right now, this is 100% worth your coin.

_childDocuments_.review: I will be adding occasional, concise updates regarding changes significant enough to mention in the comments on this review to keep information up to date without making this review a multi-page essay.HYPERCHARGE: Unboxed is a pleasant surprise. I absolutely love Co-Op wave based survival games and tower defense games so seeing this pop up on Steam's Upcoming was exciting. I decided to just go for it with semi-low expectations and pick it up on release for $15 and I'm honestly glad I did. In it's current state, an early pre-alpha, it doesn't offer a lot in terms of content or replayability but what it has in copious amounts is potential. The visuals are incredible, mechanically it's very solid, combat and movement is polished and fluid, has a great and fitting soundtrack and overall the audio is pretty good. Digital Cybercherries have also heavily emphasized community interaction and personally working with them to make HYPERCHARGE the best it can be. The foundation for an incredible game is here and what you'd be primarily paying for currently is an investment and support in the development team as well as a chance to watch this game and its community grow. I have owned my fair share of Early Access games and a lot of them have been abandoned or failed to become a worthwhile game but based on what HYPERCHARGE has and the commitment promised from the developers I have a lot of faith and excitement for this games future.----------------------------------------------- * Visuals are impressive, almost a bit surreal. They really nailed the toy store aesthetic between the plastics, toy boxes, visual effects, sounds, and overal scale.* Though you are usually confined to the isle of a toy store, there's a whole new level of freedom when you're the size of an action figure. You're able to climb up through all the boxes, racks, and hangars making the toy store feel more like a jungle, adding an unexepected depth to the isles.* A lot of little easter eggs and comedic design hidden throughout the game. Exploring the map and checking out all the various toys on the shelves is pretty entertaining.* The mechanics, movement, and gunplay are really solid and surprisngly well polished. Overall the game feels great to play.* There's a fair amount of customization for your player model and they executed it very well. The models are very well done, from the color schemes to the general design and you can have the color scheme persist to your weapons and turrets.* It runs well. Rarely dip below 60 FPS max settings @1440p with a GTX 780. * Comprehensive settings menu for graphics, controls, audio, and some gameplay.-----------------------------------------------* There's not a lot of content or replayability at the moment. There's  also not a lot of progression yet, mainly consists of upgrading defenses but there is an inactive exp system for future updates. Currently there is only 4 maps with 5 weapons and 5 mostly cosmetic attatchments to choose from.  * There are some bugs.  * Multiplayer can be a bit laggy. Not unplayable by any means but it's inconvenient at times.-----------------------------------------------Should you buy it? Short answer, Yes, if you don't mind the typical Early Access investment of buying an incomplete in development game. HYPERCHARGE does what it sets out to do very well so far and if a Co-Op survival tower defense game is up your alley then this is the game for you. If none of the above applies to you I recommend either skipping this one or keeping an eye on it as it recieves more updates. However, you can tell easily within the first two hours if it's something you'd want to keep, giving you the option to pick it up and refund it if you don't want it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ok but honestly not as good as I was expecting. You get two weapon slots, but no grenade slot. You lose your weapons at the end of each match, and each time you die. This is problematic in deathmatch as the arenas are so small you aren't able to pick anything up before someone is shooting at you. The game was clearly built for the cooperative defense mode where you build defenses against computer enemies; it feels like a missed opportunity to not have PvP for this game mode as the computer enemies are really dumb. Additionally you can only build defenses in very few marked locations; you can't just place them anywhere. And since the arenas are small and have max 4 players you're pretty much just fighting standing in the same spot the whole time and you can see the entire map so there's not really any strategy involved. Lastly, there just aren't that many players and due to the low max players (4) the few servers that have players in them don't have much turnover so they're just always full. I spend more time trying to find a match than I do actually playing. If it were me I would make it max 16 players to ensure more vacancies in populated servers, and make the maps bigger with several defensive points leading back to the base so you can "fall back" as a defensive point gets overrun. If it were PvP, this would allow one team to take over a defensive point held by the other team and then build their own defenses there. And of course, the ability to place defenses anywhere so there is some actual strategy involved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down one of the best fps games I have ever seen come out of such a small team of developers. Bigger companies would struggle to do less.This game is a tower defence game based around toys fighting and defending a "Hyper Core", basically the tower. Enemies come in waves and between waves you can build defences and buy new items such as weapons. If you have played a waved based defence game before, you will feel right at home. You get to hold two weapons at a time but there is a lot of variations you can build with new parts. Which is good because the gameplay and shooting is very strong here. There is platforming, and it is amazing how well the jumping is implemented. In fact I would go so far as to say that jumping around and exploring the levels is one of my favourite past time. That is a probably a first for a fps. The developers obviously knew this would be true so they included a free roam mode where you can explore as much as you like. And explore you will want to do as their are so many collectibles and hidden stuff in each level you can easily lose hours exploring. Side note, you can also play third person if that's your thing. So gameplay is an easy 5/5 for me.Graphics are the next thing worth talking about. And simply put, they are jaw dropping. Whoever worked on the graphics must have worked for Pixar because this is probably the best realization of Toy Story style graphics I have seen in a game to date. The PS2 when it first came out boasted that it could pull off graphics this impressive and of course it couldn't. However it took this long to get a game that truly feels like you are playing in a Pixar universe. The attention to detail is evident everywhere you look and full of jokes. Is that a bottle of Head and Shoulders? Nope, it's a bottle of Elbows and Legs. Unless you look for these types of jokes they are never shoved in your face. I have spent so much time just looking around levels because of this. Graphics is also 5/5Online is so much fun. Besides the co-operative Waves mode, you have Deathmatch and Plague mode. There are some other splitscreen modes which I have yet to play, but they look fun. There is no voice chat, but a radial menu allows you to "speak" to other players and for the most part it works well.I should also mention that if you made it this far, you are going to be surprised when I tell you that everything I have written so far has been about the Nintendo Switch version. I love the game so much that I own it for both PC and Switch. Obviously the PC version is even far more superior to the console version. With free new updates and maps happening all the time you it is actually hard to find anything negative to say about this game.So to sum up: if you want a game that gives you so much bang for your buck, great gameplay and addicting levels full of hidden unlockables, maps and extras, you cannot go wrong with this game. Seriously. It is that good. If you havn't been convinced yet, check out the demo for free. Then go buy the game and I will hopefully fight along side you as we defend our Hyper Cores!

_childDocuments_.review: I think after 200 hours of playtime, I can confidently say that Hypercharge: Unboxed is one of my favorite videogames. It gets so many things right, and it's clear the devs put a ton of work and love into the game. Modern games are rushed out the door and incomplete messes. Hypercharge is well polished and full of diverse maps and unlockables.The graphics are just beautiful and the attention to detail is insane, everything is well modeled + textured and it really shows off what the UE4 can do. You really do feel like a small toy in a big world, which makes exploring the maps more fun. Even after all this time I'm still finding new things to discover!The gunplay is like a mixture of Quake and Halo; the movement is smooth and the guns feel punchy. The main game's mode is co-op wave defense where you must collect money, weapons, and batteries for upcoming waves of enemies. You also can choose pvp style deathmatch and infection mode, all of which support offline bots or you can play online with friends/random people. There's tons of things to unlock such as player models, heads, skins, weapon skins, and names to really make your action figure your own! The sound design is nice as each of the toys sound unique, the guns sound punchy, the music is catchy, and the voice acting is very British. There's nice calm tracks for building time between waves and hype tracks during combat. It seems very 80s/90s inspired mixed with something you'd hear in early 2000s game like Timesplitters.And yeah, I think this game is great!!!!!>Here's a quickstart guide I wrote to help new/returning players alike: >Video review:

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, this is a fun game! I came for the nostalgia, but stayed for everything else. The character/enemy/environment models all look great, and the unlocks/rewards system feels deep and fair. If you don't know, this is a FPS with tower defense mechanics where you try to protect your hyper cores from waves of enemies. Much of the extra content is unlocked from achieving a perfect score on the different difficulties and exploring the maps (finding those bobbleheads be tricky), which begs you to replay the levels and take note about each wave. The humor that is sprinkled around is a good touch as well.This game is better with friends, but I'll play it alone! I don't care, just give me more toys to shoot and traps to lay. Big ups to the devs, I know you are a small team but you've managed to make a very fun, polished game!

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game! Takes me back to the PS One/N64 era. Basic controls that can be mapped any way you see fit. I'm excited that you can play with a controller, since I'm getting ready to have my 7th back surgery and I have nerve damage in my back, neck, legs, arms and hands that sometimes makes it a struggle to play hardcore shooters on a PC so the controller option is great for me. Visually it's stunning. The AI bots (Teammates if you chose to play SP) are fantastic, the music is a blast and the enemies are some of the best. Playing as a toy and being able to play as an action figure is so fun. Thanks for making such a great game.  A+++

_childDocuments_.review: I can finally say after 20 hours of playing this game it is totally worth every penny. Join the Discord, and you'll love this game even more. The Devs are a small team but they REALLY do care. Listening to every piece of feedback and eyeing glitches that are shown, and even interacting with the community itself. They constantly keep everyone updated and welcome people who join the Discord on the daily. Not only does this game have a team that cares but it blends so well with what it DOES present. "Killing Floor Tower Defense" is the best way to put it and DAMN. IT'S AMAZING. The maps are all so unique, and so big. There's always something to explore for batteries, credits or hidden secrets. From defending the bathroom to going outside in the backyard, it's completely action packed to the brim with more content coming too! Gunplay is like Halo and that's not a bad thing. There are multiple modes other than just the base 'Wave' Tower Defense. From Deathmatch to Infection and even some party modes as well as a freemode to explore maps and find secrets, or even just mess around with friends. There is so much love put into this game you just have to play to see. If you're looking for people to play with and online matches. Discord is the best place to go for your needs! Small community, but there are people there who love playing this game just as much if not more than I!
